# S6 — Apply the GitHub mirror lock (repo-level ruleset, deploy-key-only push)

## Why
Enforce that GitHub `main` can ONLY be advanced by the Gerrit replication deploy key. The lock
is a REPO-LEVEL ruleset (navapbc is a free org -> admin-proof ORG-level rulesets need a paid
plan; trusted-admin editability is the accepted risk, recorded in S6-pre's ADR). Applies the
lock that S6-pre prepared (snapshot + ADR + backend/token). Proven empirically (derisk): an
active repo-level ruleset with deploy-key-only bypass REJECTS a repo-admin's direct push
(`GH013`), so "no human/admin bypass" holds.

## What
- **Use the native provider (peer-pattern simplification).** `terraform-provider-github`
  **v6.8.0 (Nov 2025, PR #2726)** added native `DeployKey` bypass support (removed the
  actor_type whitelist; made `actor_id` optional). So the whole prior `null_resource` + `gh api`
  + `ignore_changes` + disabled->active two-phase dance is **dropped** — it existed only because
  the provider rejected `DeployKey`. Pin `integrations/github >= 6.8.0`.
- One `github_repository_ruleset` for the branch lock on `main` (+ any other branch the bot
  pushes), created directly at `enforcement = "active"` in a single apply, with rules
  `update` + `creation` + `deletion` + `non_fast_forward` and a single
  `bypass_actors { actor_type = "DeployKey"  bypass_mode = "always" }` (NO `actor_id` — it's
  optional; GitHub normalizes to `null`, which the empirical spike confirmed is canonical and
  accepted). A SEPARATE `github_repository_ruleset` for tags (`refs/tags/**`, target `tag`) with
  the same rules + the same DeployKey bypass (else tag pushes are rejected).
- **Replace the existing `main-protection` ruleset** (DERISK E5: id 18048287, PR +
  required-status-checks model — incompatible with deploy-key-only push). It is snapshotted in
  S6-pre; S6 deletes it (`gh api -X DELETE` or via the provider after `terraform import`) and
  creates the mirror-lock rulesets. There is no PR/status-check ruleset left once S6 applies.
- Consume S5's deploy key via a `data "github_repository_deploy_key"` (or a remote-state ref to
  S5's `deploy_key_id` output) so the dependency is explicit and S6 cannot apply before S5's key
  exists. (The bypass entry itself carries no actor_id; the data-source lookup is the existence
  gate, failing the apply loudly if the key is absent.)
- **Token scope.** The Terraform identity needs `Administration: write` on `navapbc/rebar`
  (fine-grained PAT scoped to this repo, or classic `repo`), injected at apply time as a
  `sensitive` var from a CI secret, never committed to `.tfvars`.
- **Remote state.** `infra/terraform/github.tf` uses the shared remote backend with state
  locking; `terraform plan` is reviewed before every `apply`.
- Mirror hygiene: turn OFF Pull Requests (Feb-2026 repo setting), disable Issues + Actions; add
  a "mirror — contribute via Gerrit at rebar.solutions.navateam.com" banner to the About +
  README; do NOT archive (archiving freezes the replication bot too).
- Rollback (runnable in ~15 min): set the rulesets `enforcement = disabled` (provider apply, or
  `gh api PATCH .../rulesets/{id} -f enforcement=disabled` for speed), restore `main-protection`
  from S6-pre's snapshot, and re-enable PRs/Issues/Actions.

## Scope
In: the two native ruleset resources (branch + tag) with DeployKey bypass, replacing
main-protection, mirror hygiene, rollback. Out: the snapshot/ADR/token-scope pre-work (S6-pre);
the Gerrit-side replication (S5); the end-to-end push-past-the-ruleset proof (S7).
**Dependency:** apply AFTER S6-pre (snapshot + ADR + backend ready) AND S5 (deploy key exists).

## Files
- `infra/terraform/github.tf` — provider pin (`>= 6.8.0`), remote backend, sensitive token var,
  the two `github_repository_ruleset` resources (branch + tag, `enforcement = active`, DeployKey
  bypass), the `data.github_repository_deploy_key` lookup, and the repo-feature toggles
  (PRs/Issues/Actions off, mirror banner).
- (optional) a small documented step to delete the pre-existing `main-protection` ruleset by id
  (or `terraform import` then replace), referencing S6-pre's snapshot.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A direct `git push` / PR-merge to `main` by a non-bypass identity is REJECTED; force-push
      and deletion of `main` are REJECTED. (Empirically confirmed for the admin-push case.)
- [ ] A tag push by a non-bypass identity is REJECTED by the separate `refs/tags/**` ruleset.
- [ ] The DeployKey bypass is expressed natively as `bypass_actors { actor_type = "DeployKey"
      bypass_mode = "always" }` (no `actor_id`) via `terraform-provider-github >= 6.8.0`, and is
      the ONLY bypass entry on each ruleset; re-running `terraform apply` is idempotent with no
      perpetual diff (provider stores `actor_id = null`, matching GitHub's normalization).
- [ ] The rulesets are created at `enforcement = "active"` in a single apply (NO null_resource,
      NO gh-api bypass step, NO disabled->active two-phase dance, NO `ignore_changes`).
- [ ] S6 obtains the deploy key via a data source / remote-state ref (not a hand-copied ID);
      applying before S5's key exists fails loudly.
- [ ] The pre-existing `main-protection` ruleset (PR + required-status-checks) is replaced/removed
      (snapshot kept in S6-pre); no PR/status-check ruleset remains on `main`.
- [ ] PRs disabled, Issues disabled, Actions disabled; README/About carry the mirror banner;
      repo NOT archived.
- [ ] The Terraform identity's `Administration: write` scope is documented and injected as a
      `sensitive` var from a CI secret (never in `.tfvars`); `github.tf` uses the shared remote
      backend with locking.
- [ ] A rollback runnable in ~15 min is documented (set `enforcement=disabled`, restore
      `main-protection` from the S6-pre snapshot, re-enable PRs/Issues/Actions).

## Plan-review remediation (Round-12, 2026-06-29)
- The Gerrit-only workflow makes the existing GitHub-PR contributor docs stale/misleading. Add contributor-facing docs as part of the mirror cutover.

Added ACs:
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md + README updated for the Gerrit-only workflow (push `HEAD:refs/for/main`, git-review setup, SSH key registration on Gerrit, the LLM-Review gate) so GitHub-PR guidance is no longer presented; the GitHub mirror banner links to it
baseline.summary: infra: S6 — Lock GitHub repo to read-only mirror (repo-level ruleset)

baseline.description:
## Why
The shared `impact = mean(severity attributes)` dilutes a genuinely high-severity plan finding below the 0.70 bar (a critical finding averaged with low axes lands ~0.60-0.69). The mean is the wrong aggregator.

## What
For the plan-review gate, replace the mean with severity-first MAX + hard override + detection amplifier.
- SEVERITY axes (each mapped to [0,1] by the verify pass): AC-unverifiable, DoD-uncertifiable, undecomposed
  (from the deterministic G5 signal), divergent-implementation, internal-conflict, vague-directive,
  irreversible-without-rationale.
- `impact_sev = MAX(axis contributions)` (no averaging).
- HARD OVERRIDE: if ANY of {AC-unverifiable, DoD-uncertifiable, undecomposed, divergent-implementation},
  `impact_sev = max(impact_sev, 0.85)`.
- DETECTION AMPLIFIER: `silent-vs-self-revealing` (silent build-the-wrong-thing -> x1.0, self-revealing
  wall -> x0.8); DoD-uncertifiable forces x1.0. Explicit compose: `impact = min(1.0, impact_sev * detection_mult)`.

## Implementation mechanics (grounded in the current code)
- VERIFY SCHEMA: the shared `verification_model()` in `verify.py` carries only the 5-field `SeverityAttrs`
  (prod_impact, debt_impact, blast_radius, likelihood, reversibility). Add a `plan_review_verification_model()`
  with an extended `PlanSeverityAttrs` adding the 7 axis fields above, EACH defaulting to `'none'`/absent so
  an older or absent verifier abstains (back-compat: a missing axis contributes 0, never inflates).
- PER-GATE DISPATCH (precise): `impact()` is called INSIDE the kernel's `pass3_decide()`, so it is NOT the
  consumer-injected-callable pattern `threshold_for` uses. Add `impact_fn: Callable[[dict], float] | None =
  None` to `pass3_decide()` defaulting to the existing `impact`; `pass3_over_findings` accepts and threads it;
  plan-review's wrapper passes `impact_fn=impact_plan`. The code-review gate later passes its own; the
  plan-review signed-verdict shape stays byte-compatible.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py` (`impact_fn` param + `impact_plan`), `verify.py`
  (`plan_review_verification_model` + `PlanSeverityAttrs`), the plan-review verify prompt (emit the 7 axes),
  and the orchestrator wrapper wiring. Depends on the deterministic G5 signal child. No code-review changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `pass3_decide()` accepts an `impact_fn` (default = existing `impact`); plan-review threads `impact_plan`
      through `pass3_over_findings`; a test asserts the code-review path (no `impact_fn`) is byte-unchanged.
- [ ] `impact_plan = MAX(axes)` with the hard-override list and the detection amplifier (silent x1.0 /
      self-revealing x0.8; DoD-uncertifiable forces x1.0), per the explicit compose above.
- [ ] `plan_review_verification_model()` + `PlanSeverityAttrs` add the 7 axes with abstaining defaults;
      older/absent verifiers do not inflate impact.
- [ ] Offline replay: previously-stranded 0.60-0.69 band findings clear 0.70; verdicts stay stable on
      same-material replicate pairs.
baseline.summary: Plan-review impact redesign: severity-first MAX + hard override + detection amplifier

baseline.description:
## Summary

ROOT CAUSE of the B5 premature-close incident. The plan-review gate reviewed B5 (pout-gloss-hoop) and returned PASS, but did NOT flag a verification-completeness deficiency in B5's acceptance criteria: AC3 ('Integration tests cover claim+close pass/fail through the workflow path with intact signing') was satisfiable ENTIRELY by OFFLINE tests using canned agents that never call resolve_prompt — so the risky new behavior (the workflow plan-review verify/coach steps run against a LIVE model) had NO acceptance criterion requiring it to be exercised end-to-end. B5 shipped + closed (signed completion verdict) with the live plan-review claim gate broken (INDETERMINATE: 'prompt references undefined variable plan'). The completion verifier correctly certified AC-satisfaction-as-written; the gap is that the GATE that reviews PLANS did not catch that the AC could pass without exercising the changed, risky path.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Author a story (like B5) that CUTS OVER a gate/engine to a new code path and DEFAULTS to it.
2. Write an AC that is satisfiable by OFFLINE/mocked tests only (no live / end-to-end exercise of the new path).
3. Run rebar review-plan on the story. 
4. Observe: PASS, with no finding that the AC permits validating the risky behavior without ever running it (no live-verification / end-to-end-DoD requirement).
5. The story ships; the live path is broken; nothing caught it until the path was hit by hand.

## Expected vs Actual

EXPECTED: the plan-review gate's AC-quality / definition-of-done criteria (e.g. E6 ac-text-quality, F1, the T-series acceptance criteria) flag an AC whose verification can pass WITHOUT exercising the actually-changed risky behavior — especially for a cutover/migration that defaults to a new path. The coaching should push 'add a live/end-to-end acceptance criterion for the path you are defaulting to.'

ACTUAL: PASS with no such finding. The verification-completeness gap (offline-only validation of a path that needs live validation) escaped review, enabling B5 to close green while broken.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A plan-review criterion (new or strengthened, e.g. the AC-quality / proxy-validation dimension) flags an AC that can be satisfied WITHOUT exercising the changed risky behavior — i.e. mocked/offline-only verification of a path the story makes the default.
- [ ] An eval/regression case encodes the B5-shaped scenario (a cutover defaulting to a new engine path with an offline-only AC) and asserts the gate surfaces the verification-completeness finding.
- [ ] The coaching for that finding recommends adding a live/end-to-end DoD for the defaulted path.
- [ ] Documented: a gate/engine cutover's DoD must include exercising the new path end-to-end against a live model (green offline tests + a passing completion verdict are necessary but not sufficient).
baseline.summary: plan-review gate passed B5 without flagging that its AC allowed offline-only verification of a path that needed live validation

baseline.description:
## Why

Per-criterion **blocking is already done** (`code_review/registry.threshold_for` + kernel Pass-3 +
detector fail-closed). What is missing is **attestation integration**: a project criterion's
verdict/coverage must fold into the signed (kind-keyed) attestation, and activating/editing/
disabling a criterion must invalidate a prior attestation — but `claim_gate_check` never
re-compares the routing version, and `registry_version()` hashes only the PACKAGED routing
(`attest.py:44`), so an overlay change produces an identical version and does NOT invalidate.

## What

- `registry_version(repo_root=None)` additionally hashes the `.rebar/` overlay when `repo_root` is
  given; thread `repo_root` through **every** caller: `claim_gate_check` → `compute_validity`, and
  also `drift_refresh_candidate` and `remediation_mode_candidate` (which call `registry_version()`
  without it today). So activating/editing/disabling a criterion invalidates a prior attestation at
  claim time.
- A disabled built-in is recorded in a `disabled_builtins: [ids]` field in the verdict `coverage`
  dict (folded into the signed manifest) so the cert reflects reduced coverage; additive/
  expand-contract (absent on old certs → treated as stale → re-review, never a crash).
- Cross-gate: this applies to **any** gate attestation backed by the shared registry — plan-review
  now; code-review once it signs (code-review signs nothing today; the `attest.py` port to
  code-review rides with story `#6`).

## Scope

- Files: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` (registry_version(repo_root), coverage field,
  threading), the claim-gate path.
- Depends on story `#1` (the overlay must exist to hash) and story `#2` (DET blocking).
- Blocking itself is NOT in scope (already shipped via `threshold_for` + kernel Pass-3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `registry_version(repo_root)` hashes the `.rebar/` overlay; threaded through
      `claim_gate_check`/`compute_validity`/`drift_refresh_candidate`/`remediation_mode_candidate`.
- [ ] Activating/editing/disabling a project criterion invalidates a prior plan-review attestation
      at claim time; an unchanged overlay does not churn (regver == today when overlay absent).
- [ ] A disabled built-in appears in `coverage.disabled_builtins` in the signed manifest.
- [ ] Expand-contract: an old attestation lacking the new basis is treated as stale (re-review),
      never a crash.
- [ ] A project criterion's verdict + coverage fold into the signed attestation; it can never
      rebind a built-in.


## compute_validity regver check + disabled_builtins manifest line (remediation, run 1)

### `compute_validity` gains a regver staleness check (clears G6 blocker 1)
Threading `repo_root` into `compute_validity` is necessary but NOT sufficient — its plan-review
branch must ALSO compare the attestation's recorded regver against the current one:
`manifest_regver(manifest) != registry_version(repo_root)` → the record reads as **not valid**
with reason `"stale-regver"` (a new invalidation reason alongside the existing
material/head-sha/reopen checks). So activating/editing/disabling a project criterion (which
changes `registry_version(repo_root)` because it now hashes the `.rebar/` overlay) makes a prior
attestation read stale at claim time. `manifest_regver(manifest)` is a small helper that extracts
the `regver:` line from the signed manifest (mirroring the existing `manifest_material`). An
attestation with NO regver line (pre-this-change) → treated as stale → re-review (expand-contract,
never a crash).

### `disabled_builtins` is a dedicated signed manifest line (clears G6 blocker 2)
`build_manifest()` emits a NEW `disabled_builtins: [id,id,...]` line (sorted, deterministic) WHEN
the verdict `coverage` carries disabled built-ins (from the overlay disabling a built-in via ef7e's
merge) — so the cert reflects reduced coverage rather than silent omission. A `manifest_disabled_builtins(manifest)`
parser reads it back (like `manifest_material`). The line is ADDITIVE/expand-contract: absent on old
certs (parsed as `[]`), present only when non-empty, so a clean run's manifest is byte-identical to
today (attestation-safe). `verify_signature` re-derives the same manifest and checks the HMAC as usual.

## Acceptance Criteria (remediation additions)

- [ ] `compute_validity` (plan-review branch) adds a `manifest_regver != registry_version(repo_root)`
      staleness check returning reason `stale-regver`; a missing regver line → stale (re-review).
      A test proves activating/editing a project criterion invalidates a prior attestation.
- [ ] `build_manifest` emits a deterministic `disabled_builtins: [ids]` line when the verdict
      coverage has disabled built-ins; a `manifest_disabled_builtins` parser reads it; absent/empty
      on a clean run (byte-identical manifest). A test asserts the round-trip + HMAC re-verify.


## No mass re-review + the built-in-disable mechanism (remediation, run 2)

### The regver line ALREADY exists — no mass invalidation (clears T4)
Current signed manifests ALREADY carry a `regver:` line (verified: e.g. `regver: 83e5f63ad06d893a`).
This story adds the CHECK in `compute_validity`, NOT the line. The `registry_version` basis change is
ADDITIVE: for an OVERLAY-ABSENT repo, `registry_version(repo_root)` hashes the same packaged routing
it does today ⇒ the SAME regver value ⇒ existing certs stay valid (zero churn). A repo that has an
overlay is BY DEFINITION new (the overlay feature shipped in ef7e), so it has NO pre-existing certs to
invalidate. The truly-ancient "no regver line at all" case → stale → one re-review, which is the
correct expand-contract behaviour (never a crash). So there is no deployment-wide mandatory re-review.

### The built-in-disable mechanism is part of THIS story (clears G6)
ef7e's MVP implemented overlay RE-TUNE of a built-in (per-key routing merge) but NOT disable. This
story adds disable: an overlay `plan_review` entry for a BUILT-IN id carrying `"disabled": true`
REMOVES that built-in from `effective_criteria(repo_root)` (so its finder never runs) — implemented
in `registry.effective_criteria` (a disabled built-in is excluded from the returned set) +
`effective_routing` (the entry is retained but flagged). The set of disabled built-in ids is exposed
via a small `disabled_builtins(repo_root) -> list[str]` helper. The gate records them in the verdict
`coverage["disabled_builtins"]`, which `build_manifest` folds into the `disabled_builtins:` manifest
line. `_validate_routing_entry` accepts `disabled: bool` only on an un-prefixed (built-in) id (a
`project.` id cannot be "disabled" — it is simply not activated). This keeps the epic's "the overlay
may re-tune OR disable a built-in; a disable is recorded in coverage" AC coherent within this story.

## Acceptance Criteria (remediation additions, run 2)

- [ ] Overlay-absent repos see NO regver change (existing attestations stay valid); the regver line
      already exists, so this adds only the staleness CHECK. A test asserts overlay-absent parity.
- [ ] An overlay `disabled: true` on a built-in id removes it from `effective_criteria`; a
      `disabled_builtins(repo_root)` helper lists them; they flow into `coverage` + the manifest line.
baseline.summary: Blocking policy + attestation integration (registry_version(repo_root), disabled_builtins, invalidation)

baseline.description:
## Context

Bug b636 (landed as 5e7d6e71ba) added deleted-source recovery to fsck. After the module-size split, `restore_deleted_sources` and `rebuild_with_restore` live in `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_restore.py` (:127 and :182) and are re-exported from `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py` (bottom-of-module import at :614).

Only ONE call site actually uses the composed helper — `repair_or_plan` (`fsck_repair.py:580`). The per-ticket repair path `_repair_ticket` (`fsck_repair.py:209`) still calls `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` DIRECTLY at :270-274, so it rebuilds from whatever sources survive and never attempts the restore. That path fails closed rather than corrupting anything, but a ticket whose SNAPSHOT source was dropped by legacy compaction is not recovered when repair runs through `_repair_ticket`.

`rebuild_with_restore`'s own docstring already calls itself "the repair path's single entrypoint", and no ADR or ticket records an intentional divergence between the two paths — this is a residual gap, not a deliberate split.

Discovered while closing story 9f7f (superseded into b636): every other acceptance criterion of 9f7f is implemented, this call site is the residual gap.

## Plan

Route `_repair_ticket`'s rebuild through `rebuild_with_restore` so the two repair entry points behave identically, and surface any restored sources in the `disp` dict the caller already consumes.

### The `no_commit` contract (must be preserved)

`_repair_ticket` takes `no_commit: bool = False` and currently forwards it: `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log(tracker, ticket_id, ticket_dir, no_commit=no_commit)`. `no_commit` gates the git commit in `compact_rebuild.py:234`, and the batch repair loop at `fsck_repair.py:401-408` calls `_repair_ticket(..., no_commit=True)` so commits are deferred until after the whole batch.

`rebuild_with_restore(tracker, ticket_id, ticket_dir) -> tuple[bool, list[str]]` has NO `no_commit` parameter and calls the rebuild with the default `no_commit=False`. Routing naively would make the batch path commit once per ticket — a behavior change.

Worked example of the required contract:

- `rebuild_with_restore` gains a keyword-only `no_commit: bool = False` and forwards it verbatim: `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log(tracker, ticket_id, ticket_dir, no_commit=no_commit)`.
- `_repair_ticket` calls `rebuild_with_restore(tracker, ticket_id, ticket_dir, no_commit=no_commit)` and unpacks `(rebuilt, restored)`.
- The existing `repair_or_plan` call at `fsck_repair.py:580` stays `rebuild_with_restore(tracker, ticket_id, ticket_dir)` — the new parameter defaults to `False`, which is that path's current behavior, so it is unchanged.
- Concretely: `_repair_ticket(tracker, tid, dir, dry_run=False, no_commit=True)` on a ticket with an auto-recoverable orphan restores the deleted source, rebuilds the snapshot, and leaves the tickets worktree DIRTY (no new commit on the `tickets` branch); with `no_commit=False` it commits exactly as it does today.

### Reporting

`_repair_ticket`'s `disp` dict gains a `"restored"` key holding the restored filenames list (empty list when nothing was restored), mirroring what `repair_or_plan` surfaces as "after restoring N deleted event(s)".

### Import cycle

`fsck_repair` imports `fsck_restore` at the BOTTOM of the module (:614) to let the leaf lazily import `snapshot_missing_sources`. `_repair_ticket` therefore uses a function-local `from rebar._commands.fsck_restore import rebuild_with_restore` (the same lazy-import shape the current code uses for `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` at :270) rather than a new module-level import.

### No double-restore

`restore_deleted_sources` skips any name already present on disk as `<name>` or `<name>.retired`, and `rebuild_with_restore` only attempts a restore when `snapshot_missing_sources(ticket_dir)` is non-empty. A second pass over the same ticket therefore restores nothing and reports an empty list — that idempotency is the invariant AC4 asserts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `_repair_ticket` obtains its rebuild through `rebuild_with_restore`, not a direct `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` call.
      Verify: `grep -n "rebuild_with_restore" src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py` shows a call inside `_repair_ticket`, and `grep -n "rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log" src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py` shows no call in `_repair_ticket`.
- [x] `rebuild_with_restore` accepts a keyword-only `no_commit: bool = False` and forwards it to `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log`; `_repair_ticket` passes its own `no_commit` through.
      Verify: `grep -n "no_commit" src/rebar/_commands/fsck_restore.py`.
- [x] `_repair_ticket`'s returned `disp` dict carries a `"restored"` list of restored source filenames.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_repair_restore_08c8.py -q`.
- [x] A held-out test proves a ticket whose SNAPSHOT source was deleted by legacy compaction is recovered when repair runs via `_repair_ticket` (RED before the change).
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_repair_restore_08c8.py -q`.
- [x] A test proves `_repair_ticket(..., no_commit=True)` creates no new commit on the tickets branch while still restoring and rebuilding.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_repair_restore_08c8.py -q`.
- [x] A test proves a second `_repair_ticket` pass over the same ticket restores nothing (no double-restore, empty `"restored"`).
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_repair_restore_08c8.py -q`.
- [x] The `repair_or_plan` call site at `fsck_repair.py:580` is unchanged in behavior and existing fsck repair/restore tests pass unchanged.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/integration/test_b636_rebuild_history_loss.py tests/interfaces/store -q -k "fsck or restore or repair"`.
baseline.summary: fsck _repair_ticket bypasses rebuild_with_restore, so repair never restores deleted SNAPSHOT sources

The release smoke probe reports 3 failures that are NOT engine defects — the probe script tests behavior the engine intentionally changed. Surfaced during the 0.6.0 release smoke test (138 passed, 3 failed).

2. `REBAR_ROOT=<store> PROBE_LIVE=1 bash scripts/probe-rebar.sh`.

      `--set-tags`/`--add-tag`/`--remove-tag` (per CLAUDE.md tag-delta surface).

      that `list` omits by design (don't assert identical key sets).

## 2026-08-08 resolution evidence

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Rebar's CLI facade on current main is 714 lines and reconstructs command identity and policy through 19 overlapping frozensets, an intercept ladder, package-help filenames, a regex-based reference generator, and repeated test censuses. The existing CLI reference is generated, but its syntax authority is not: it embeds 54 hand-maintained help resources plus a curated intercept table, so parser/help drift can pass while the census remains complete.

Twenty-one intercept-only commands lack safe canonical help. `rebar help <command>` reports them unknown, while handler-owned `--help` is inconsistent and can execute work. The maintainer approved normalizing every visible command and approved deriving syntax/options from the same parser definitions used by execution.

## Approved Architecture
Create one stdlib-only immutable lazy route registry. A route records canonical identity, spellings/visibility, lazy handler and parser-factory references, a bounded invocation-adapter kind, generated package-help key, mount/init policy, confirmation/output policy, and possible semantic capabilities. The registry is a routing table, not a plugin system, DI container, or middleware framework.

Every command grammar is built by a side-effect-free stdlib `argparse` factory. Runtime handlers and build-time generation call that same factory. Existing argparse builders are extracted; imperative parsers migrate with accepted/rejected argv, `--` handling, diagnostics, streams, and exit codes pinned by behavioral tests. A narrow shared ArgumentParser subclass/formatter may preserve Rebar diagnostics; no docs-only parser, source-regex grammar, Click dependency, or second parser is introduced.

Generation resolves all parser factories at build/check time using fixed `prog`, width, and formatter policy, then commits package-help and overview bytes. Runtime overview/help, aliases, malformed global syntax, and unknown-command output read only those bytes before RP-04 operation snapshot, config materialization, mount, handler resolution, or optional imports. The lexical top-level selector identifies only the spelling and first-token help/unknown forms; nested argv remains selected-handler-owned.

A separate semantic capability registry maps capabilities to packaging extras and missing postures: `error`, `unavailable`, `abstain`, or intentional `fallback`. Routes advertise possibilities only; checks occur after the selected mode/backend is known, and domain components retain degraded result shapes.

## Compatibility Contracts
Exact aliases reuse canonical grammar/help. `bridge-fsck`, `bridge-probe`, and `jira-onboard` compose canonical argument-definition helpers with alias-specific `prog`/replacement prose; `jira-onboard` keeps its historical spelling. Hidden `bridge-status` is explicitly helpable but undiscoverable. `purge-bridge` remains unknown.

Help/unknown paths never compose an operation or mount. Execution retains central best-effort mount, strict init, confirmation/global-output behavior, legacy JSON shapes, tokens after `--`, and established streams/exit codes. Accepted grammar changes are limited to the separately approved safe-help normalization unless a ticket names another intentional delta. `rebar-mcp` remains a separate entry point.

## Migration and Rollback
Use expand/contract by command family. Add the registry/parser contract and derived compatibility exports; migrate each handler and its runtime parser together; generate authoritative artifacts only after the complete parser/route census passes; then move execution, capabilities, docs/distribution consumers, and finally remove compatibility authorities. No shipped phase may contain a docs-only grammar runtime ignores.

During expansion, rollback selects derived compatibility exports and reverts a parser family with its generated artifacts. After contraction, code revert restores the old router. Ticket, event, bridge, and binding formats do not change.

## Delivery Order
1. Record the architecture decision and prior-art constraints.
2. Establish the parser/registry foundation; migrate core and advanced parser families in parallel; generate canonical package help only after both complete.
3. Migrate lazy execution and semantic capability boundaries.
4. Derive reference/distribution checks from registries and generated parser artifacts.
5. Retire duplicate authorities and complete cutover.

## Testing
Use unit tests for pure registry/parser validation; command-family production-path parity tests for accepted/rejected argv and errors; real subprocess tests for exact committed bytes, streams, exit codes, aliases, and absence of operation/config/mount/handler effects; a clean no-extras wheel for every help form; and a full-extra lane for lazy-reference resolution. Generator `--check` must prove parser-rendered artifacts and `docs/cli-reference.md` are byte-current.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every command's runtime parsing and generated syntax/options come from one side-effect-free argparse factory; no docs-only/manual syntax authority remains.
- [ ] Every visible canonical command appears once in the grouped overview and both top-level help forms return byte-current generated package data before operation/config/store/handler boundaries.
- [ ] Exact, compatibility, hidden, and retired spellings exhibit the approved behavior, including historical `jira-onboard` and unknown `purge-bridge`.
- [ ] Lazy execution preserves mount/init, argv, confirmation, stream, exit-code, and legacy-output contracts except the explicit help normalization.
- [ ] Selected optional modes/backends preserve approved capability postures without eager optional imports.
- [ ] CLI-reference generation, coverage, lean-wheel checks, and full-extra resolution enumerate registries/parser artifacts rather than source regexes or manual command censuses.
- [ ] Duplicate authorities are removed after shadow parity; quality gates pass and no stored-data migration occurs.
- [ ] ADR 0099 and living architecture record the parser, route, capability, migration, compatibility, and rollback boundaries.
baseline.summary: RP-05 — Lazy CLI command and capability registry with canonical help

baseline.description:
## Why
THE security-critical divergence. e165 (change 563, commit 2efdae38f) implemented key validity as an **HLC-epoch** window (ordinal position in the reducer's canonical replay). The APPROVED epic design requires **git-commit-ancestry** validity (tickets-branch commit SHAs). HLC ordering is partly author-assigned, so a malicious clone holding a later-revoked key can write an event with a backdated HLC that sorts BEFORE the revocation and verifies as valid — defeating the feature's "not attacker-controllable" promise. The immutable commit DAG closes that hole. (User rejected the delivered design; see d7c0.)

## Why the DAG is stronger
Commit SHAs chain content+parents, so an event's position in history is a tamper-proof fact — you cannot make a new event an ancestor of an existing revocation commit without forging SHAs. HLC ordering trusts the author-assigned timestamp component; commit ancestry trusts only the DAG.

## Architecture decision — pure reducer + git-aware resolver (READ FIRST)
The reducer (`_processors.py`) is **pure-filesystem** today (no git/subprocess) and MUST stay so (its output is cache-keyed; it runs on plain event-file directories). Commit SHAs are git metadata not in event JSON, so we do NOT store SHAs in reduced state. Instead:

- **Reducer keyring fold (pure):** records each key's lifecycle by **event position** (the
  `{HLC-ts}-{uuid}` filename prefix the reducer already parses) — record shape
  `{public_key, added_at: <position>, revoked_at: <position|None>}`. Drop `added_epoch` /
  `revoked_epoch` / `keyring_epoch`. `state["keys"]` = keys with `revoked_at is None`.
- **Git-aware resolver (new, in `authorship.py`, the attest layer — NOT the reducer):**
  - `resolve_event_commit(position, ticket_dir, *, repo_root) -> str | None`: maps a
    position prefix to the tickets-branch commit SHA that introduced that event file.
    **TYPE is NOT an input** to the resolver, so it globs the position prefix:
    `git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H -- "<ticket_dir>/<position>-*.json"` run in the
    tracker dir, taking the (single) introducing commit. Returns `None` on any git failure
    or no match (fail-closed).
  - `verify_authorship_at_commit(envelope, identity_id, event_commit, event_position, *,
    repo_root) -> Verdict`: builds the trust root from exactly the keys valid at
    `event_commit`. A key K is valid iff **`merge-base --is-ancestor(K.added_commit,
    event_commit)` AND NOT `merge-base --is-ancestor(K.revoked_commit, event_commit)`**,
    where `K.added_commit`/`K.revoked_commit` come from resolving K's `added_at`/`revoked_at`
    positions. This is where the AC's commit-anchored record
    `{pubkey, added_at_commit, revoked_at_commit}` materializes (resolver output). ANY git
    subprocess failure (`git log` / `merge-base` non-zero, timeout, missing repo) resolves
    to a **non-verified** Verdict — the resolver/verifier NEVER raises (fail-closed, mirrors
    `resolve_trust_root`).
- **Intra-commit refinement (N-events-per-commit):** `batch_stage_and_commit` puts N event
  files in ONE commit, and `merge-base --is-ancestor(C, C)` is true, so when a key's
  add/revoke shares the event's commit the DAG cannot order them — refine with the
  **intra-commit position** (`{HLC-ts}-{uuid}` prefix ordering, which is a total order
  within that commit): a KEY_ADD in the same commit counts as added iff its position ≤ the
  event position; a KEY_REVOKE in the same commit counts as revoked iff its position ≤ the
  event position. NOTE this HLC tiebreak is NOT the rejected inter-commit weakness: events
  in one commit were written by ONE author in ONE atomic batch, so an attacker cannot
  insert an event into someone else's already-sealed commit — intra-commit ordering is not
  attacker-exploitable the way cross-commit backdating was.

## What
- Reducer `process_key_event` folds position-based records (no epoch); `make_initial_state`
  seeds `keyring: []` (no `keyring_epoch`); `_rederive_keyring_keys` → keys with
  `revoked_at is None`; remove `keys_valid_at_epoch`.
- **Genesis / bootstrap:** keys carried on a CREATE (`_bootstrap_genesis_keyring`) get
  `added_at` = **the CREATE event's position** (`{ts}-{uuid}` of the CREATE), so their
  added-commit resolves to the CREATE commit (an ancestor of every later event). There is
  NO separate ambiguous sentinel. TOFU genesis (first `KEY_ADD` on a keyless identity)
  records `added_at` = that KEY_ADD's position.
- **Snapshot restore + v4 migration:** `process_snapshot` restores the position-based
  keyring verbatim. A pre-position (e165 v4) SNAPSHOT whose keyring records carry
  `added_epoch`/`revoked_epoch` (no `added_at`) is MIGRATED by re-seeding from the
  identity's static `keys` via `_bootstrap_genesis_keyring` (treated as genesis at the
  CREATE position) rather than trusting the stale epoch fields. Because the stack is
  UNLANDED and lands atomically, no real store holds a v4 epoch snapshot; this migration is
  a defensive floor, not a live path.
- `authorship.py`: add `resolve_event_commit` + `verify_authorship_at_commit` +
  commit-ancestry trust root; **REMOVE `verify_authorship_at_epoch`, `epoch_for_position`,
  `keys_valid_at_epoch`, `_position_prefix`'s epoch use** (the HLC-epoch API).
- `identity.py` key add/revoke seam is unchanged in shape (TOFU genesis self-signed;
  unsigned non-genesis refused; signed add/rotate/revoke); only epoch wording in docstrings
  becomes commit wording.
- Bump `SCHEMA_VERSION` v4→v5 and `_REDUCER_CACHE_VERSION` v5→v6 (both preserve-and-ignore).
- Consumes TS1's in-toto authorship (verify the event's Statement against keys valid at the
  event's commit).

## Stack scoping (why TS2 and TS3 land together)
This story AMENDS Gerrit change 563 = commit 2efdae38f (e165), which touches ONLY `authorship.py`, `reducer/{_processors,_state,_version,_cache}.py`, and `identity.py`. The **consumers** of the era model — `verify_authorship.py` (`_verify_signed` → `epoch_for_position` / `verify_authorship_at_epoch`) and `compact.py` (`_build_authorship_ledger` → `epoch`) — live in commit 721702e91 (3183), so they are rewired to `resolve_event_commit` / `verify_authorship_at_commit` in **TS3 (117b, change 580)**. Because TS2 removes the epoch API from `authorship.py` while TS3 updates its commit-7 consumers, the two are pushed together and land atomically with the whole stack; each is internally green at its own patchset (at commit 563 the verify-gate/compact code does not yet exist). TS2 REPLACES e165's OWN tests (`test_identity_e165*`, which assert the epoch model) with commit-ancestry tests.

## Scope
In: position-based key records, `resolve_event_commit`, DAG-ancestry validity (`verify_authorship_at_commit`) with intra-commit refinement + fail-closed git handling, TOFU/write-gate, reducer fold + snapshot + v4 migration + version bumps, removal of the epoch API, transitioning e165's tests. Out: authorship payload format (TS1); the SNAPSHOT ledger schema + `key_not_valid_at_era` verdict + the verify-gate/compact rewiring (TS3 / 3183, commit 7).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The resolved key record binds `{pubkey, added_at_commit, revoked_at_commit?}`
  (tickets-branch commit SHAs); a test using TWO real fixture commits asserts the resolved
  shape (add key in commit A, revoke in a later commit B; resolver yields A and B).
- [ ] Genesis key-add is accepted ONLY when self-signed (TOFU base case); an unsigned
  NON-genesis key-add is refused (test).
- [ ] Commit-ancestry validity across the revocation boundary: with key K added in commit
  C1 and revoked in a later commit C3, an event signed by K whose commit descends C1 but
  NOT C3 PASSES, and one whose commit descends C3 FAILS (test, both sides of boundary).
- [ ] Validity derives from commit ancestry, NOT event timestamps: an event written AFTER
  the revocation but carrying a BACKDATED `data`/filename timestamp still FAILS, because its
  introducing commit descends the revocation commit regardless of the timestamp (the
  killer test that commit-ancestry beats HLC backdating).
- [ ] Intra-commit refinement: with a KEY_ADD and an event in the SAME commit, a KEY_ADD at
  an earlier intra-commit position → event PASSES; a KEY_ADD at a later position → event
  FAILS; symmetrically a KEY_REVOKE at an earlier position in the same commit → event FAILS
  (test using a batched multi-event commit).
- [ ] Fail-closed git handling: when the position→commit resolution cannot run (git
  failure / no matching commit), verification returns a non-verified Verdict and never
  raises (test, e.g. an unresolvable position).
- [ ] Replay never rejects: a not-yet-valid-key / bad-signature event still folds into
  state (test); the delivered HLC-epoch surface is gone — a grep-assert confirms
  `verify_authorship_at_epoch`, `epoch_for_position`, `keys_valid_at_epoch`,
  `keyring_epoch`, `added_epoch`, `revoked_epoch` are ABSENT from `src/rebar`.
- [ ] The reducer stays pure: a grep-assert confirms `src/rebar/reducer/` imports no
  `subprocess` and runs no git (the resolver lives in `authorship.py`).

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/attest/authorship.py` (resolve_event_commit + verify_authorship_at_commit + commit-ancestry trust root + intra-commit refinement + fail-closed git; remove epoch API)
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` (position-based keyring fold; genesis added_at = CREATE position; remove keys_valid_at_epoch/epoch cursor)
- `src/rebar/reducer/_state.py` (seed keyring, no keyring_epoch)
- `src/rebar/reducer/_version.py` (SCHEMA_VERSION v4->v5)
- `src/rebar/reducer/_cache.py` (reducer cache v5->v6)
- `src/rebar/_commands/identity.py` (docstring epoch->commit wording; seam shape unchanged)
baseline.summary: transition: key validity -> git-commit-ancestry (tickets-branch SHAs, replaces HLC-epoch)

## Why

108 tickets in the store carry `## Success Criteria`. Their criteria are conventionally plain
`- ` bullets, and `_count_ac_items` counts `- [ ]` items ONLY under `## Acceptance Criteria`
(resetting at the next `##`). So those criteria are invisible to the P1 blocking floor, cannot
carry the `[operator-attested]` tag the completion verifier matches on checkbox text, and are
not individually checkable. Migrating them is the substantive half of this epic — the heading
rename is cosmetic by comparison.

## What

Migrate the store tickets carrying `## Success Criteria` so their criteria live under
`## Acceptance Criteria` as `- [ ]` checklist items.

## Scope

The ticket descriptions in the `tickets` branch that match `## Success Criteria` (108 distinct
tickets at time of writing; the migration recomputes the set rather than hard-coding it).

A migration script under `scripts/` performing the rewrite via the rebar library
(`rebar.edit_ticket`) so every change is a normal, auditable ticket event — NOT a direct
rewrite of the git-backed store.

OUT OF SCOPE: closed tickets' historical accuracy is not preserved by rewriting; see Approach
for why closed tickets are migrated too and what that costs.

## Approach

For each matching ticket: locate the `## Success Criteria` block (bounded by the next `## `
heading), convert its `- ` bullets to `- [ ]` items, and merge them into the ticket's existing
`## Acceptance Criteria` block, appending if one exists and creating it if not. Tickets already
carrying both headings merge; the SC heading is then removed.

Editing a ticket's description changes its MATERIAL FINGERPRINT, which invalidates any
plan-review attestation as `stale-material`. That is correct and unavoidable — the plan text
genuinely changed — but it means the migration must not be run blindly across claimed work.
The script therefore processes CLOSED tickets by default and requires an explicit flag to touch
open/in_progress ones, so no in-flight claim is silently invalidated. The count of skipped
in-flight tickets is reported so the remainder can be migrated deliberately.

Run as a dry-run first, with the diff recorded on this ticket before the live run.

## Testing

- Unit tests for the block-rewriting function over fixtures: SC-only, both-headings, SC with
  mixed `- ` and `- [ ]` items, SC as the LAST section (no following `##`), and a ticket with
  no SC block (must be a no-op).
- Dry-run over the real store, with the resulting diff attached as a ticket comment.
- Post-migration assertion that `_count_ac_items` returns >=1 for every migrated ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A script under `scripts/` performs the migration through `rebar.edit_ticket`, with
      `--dry-run` as the default mode and a required explicit flag to modify non-closed tickets.
- [ ] Unit tests cover all five block-shape cases listed under Testing, including the no-op case.
- [ ] After the live run, `git grep -l "## Success Criteria" tickets` matches no ticket
      description outside the skipped in-flight set.
- [ ] Every migrated ticket returns `_count_ac_items >= 1`, verified by a script pass over the
      migrated set.
- [ ] The dry-run diff and the list of skipped in-flight tickets are recorded as comments on
      this ticket.
baseline.summary: Migrate store tickets from Success Criteria bullets to Acceptance Criteria checkboxes

# J4 — Pin a `UserIdentityModel` contract (accountId for Cloud, name for Data Center)

## Context / Problem

User identity is the second real Cloud/DC difference. Jira Cloud identifies users by opaque `accountId` (username and userkey were removed for GDPR); Data Center identifies them by `name`. This leaks into two places in the Cloud adapter: `OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee`, which returns `(value, authoritative, is_account_id)` and encodes the 3-state account-resolution fast-path the core diff consults (ADR 0035 §(d) canonical-comparison corollary), and the transport's create/update assignee payload shape.

PR #120 handled this by copying `resolve_assignee` and hardcoding `is_account_id=False`, and its copy consulted `getattr(self, "_assignee_resolver", None)` — an attribute nothing ever sets, so its entire authoritative branch was unreachable and DC would have returned `authoritative=False` for every assignee. That is not a cosmetic bug: a permanently non-authoritative assignee resolution makes the outbound diff re-emit assignee changes it can never converge, which is the churn class epic `ace2` was created to fix.

## Approach

Define a `UserIdentityModel` Protocol in `adapters/jira_family/` [rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743] with `resolve(local_value, remote_identity)` returning the existing `(value, authoritative, is_account_id)` tuple, and `to_payload(value)` returning the deployment's assignee field shape. Two implementations: `AccountIdIdentity` (Cloud — the current behavior verbatim, `{"accountId": …}`) and `NameIdentity` (DC — resolves through the DC user-search endpoint, `{"name": …}`).

`NameIdentity` performs a **real** lookup against DC's user-search endpoint rather than echoing the local value, so it can return `authoritative=True` and the diff converges. Its resolver is injected at construction from the DC transport [rebar:9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56], not discovered via `getattr`, so there is no unreachable branch.

**Alternative rejected:** DC returns the local value with `authoritative=False` always (PR #120's effective behavior). It compiles and passes shallow tests while guaranteeing assignee-diff churn on every pass.

**Alternative rejected:** normalizing both to a single "user reference" string. The core diff's 3-state fast-path genuinely needs to know whether the value is an accountId, so flattening it would push the branch back into core.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/identity_model.py` (new).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/backend.py` — Cloud constructed with `AccountIdIdentity`.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_user_identity_model.py` (new).

## Testing

Unit tier with a stateful fake resolver for the lookup (the irreducible external boundary), plus a shared contract test over both implementations, since the 3-state contract must hold identically for each.

- shared contract, parameterized over both models: an empty local value yields
  `("", False, <model default>)`; a value that resolves to the SAME identity the remote already has yields
  `(None, True, …)` (converged, nothing to emit); a value resolving to a different identity yields that
  identity with `authoritative=True`.
- Cloud-specific: the resolved value is an accountId and `is_account_id is True`; payload is `{"accountId": …}`.
- DC-specific: the resolved value is a username and `is_account_id is False`; payload is `{"name": …}`.
- failure path: an unresolvable assignee raises `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError` (the neutral base at
  `_backend.py:48`) rather than silently returning a non-authoritative value.
- regression oracle for PR #120's defect: a test asserts that for a resolvable assignee, DC returns
  `authoritative=True` — this test fails against the `getattr`-based implementation.
- contrast case: an unassigned local value yields the documented desired-unassigned state, not a lookup.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] one parameterized contract test covers all three resolution states for both identity models
- [ ] a test asserts DC returns `authoritative=True` for a resolvable assignee (the anti-churn oracle)
- [ ] a test asserts an unresolvable assignee raises `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError` for both models
- [ ] `grep -rn '_assignee_resolver' src/` returns nothing — no `getattr`-discovered collaborator anywhere
- [ ] J1's pinned Cloud assignee behavior is unchanged (`make test` green with those assertions unmodified)
baseline.summary: J4 — pin a UserIdentityModel contract (accountId for Cloud, name for Data Center)

## Context
Planning currently mixes snapshot reads, binding decisions, mode limits, and later handler assumptions. Retry recovery cannot be stable until all decisions derive from one frozen observation.

## Outcome
Define immutable `Observation` and `TicketPlan` values and a pure planner that preserves the existing `Mutation` vocabulary/serialization. This task covers deterministic value construction only, not lifecycle dependency logic or preview output.

## Plan
1. Add frozen provider-neutral observation/version and per-ticket plan types with open payloads.
2. Build pure planner inputs from local snapshot, remote snapshot, binding read view, mode, selection/filter, and limits.
3. Refactor existing differ decisions into plan mutation values without filesystem, provider, subprocess, or clock I/O.
4. Preserve existing mutation serialization and canonical hashes exactly.

## Testing
Feed frozen fixtures twice and compare immutable plans, hashes, diagnostics, and version identity. Poison all I/O seams.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Identical frozen inputs produce equal immutable observations and ticket plans.
- [ ] Plans carry existing mutations, diagnostics, disposition, and observation/version identity.
- [ ] Existing mutation serialization and canonical hashes remain byte-identical.
- [ ] Planner construction performs zero repository saves, ticket writes, Jira calls, subprocess launches, or ambient clock reads.
- [ ] Provider-specific payload extensions remain open without weakening the provider-neutral core fields.

## Out of scope
Lifecycle intents, inter-ticket dependencies, caps ordering, preview rendering, and shadow cutover.
baseline.summary: RP-03 S2 T1 — Build immutable observations and pure ticket plans

## Why
This is the dependency root of the oracle. The three-valued evidence contract, the fail-open execution harness, and the optional-extra scaffolding are shared by every engine — they must exist and be stable before Engine A, T0, or Engine B are built. Getting the contract right here is what makes "one implementation, not two" real.

## What
- The normalized **evidence model**: `resolved | abstained(reason)` with a CLOSED structured reason enum
  (`unsupported_lang | no_tool | parse_error | timeout | ambiguous | private_or_internal_suspected |
  network_error | rate_limited | version_skew | invalid_detector | other`), provenance/tier, and a coverage
  record. `version_skew` (the #1 real failure) and `invalid_detector` (a project detector failing validation)
  are first-class; `other` is the explicit catch-all (no open `…`). Resolution-lane resolved value is `refuted`
  (never an asserted absence). One internal finding shape; SARIF 2.1.0 map at the edges (superset).
- The **fail-open recover/timeout harness** every backend runs inside. OUT-OF-PROCESS tools (ctags, ast-grep,
  OpenGrep, scc/lizard, registry HTTP) use the subprocess reaper (mirror `acli_subprocess`: process-group,
  SIGTERM→SIGKILL, structured timeout). IN-PROCESS bindings (tree-sitter) CANNOT be bounded by a thread/signal
  timeout (it can't interrupt a hung C-extension call, and a segfault would kill the host) — so prefer the CLI
  form of every matcher, and run any unavoidable in-process binding inside a WORKER SUBPROCESS so the same reaper
  applies. A crash/timeout/missing-tool/version-skew becomes a recorded `abstain`, never raises; the visible skip
  IS the coverage record — never a silent no-op. Each backend's version is pinned/recorded.
- **Optional-extra scaffolding**: a new extra in `pyproject.toml`, `_optional.py` guard + `guard_import`, core
  stays import-clean (the existing optionality CI gate), non-adopting clients import nothing.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/grounding/` (new package) — contract + harness + extra wiring only; no backend logic.
- Polyglot/optional by construction; no Python-specific assumptions in the contract.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Evidence model + CLOSED structured reason enum (incl. version_skew, invalid_detector, other) + coverage implemented; `refute`/`abstain` representable; SARIF map both directions.
- [ ] Fail-open harness covers OUT-OF-PROCESS (subprocess reaper) AND IN-PROCESS (worker-subprocess) backends: crash / hang / timeout / missing tool / version-skew → recorded `abstain`, never raises — incl. a segfaulting C-extension parse.
- [ ] Optional extra added; core import-clean (optionality CI gate passes); non-adopting client imports nothing.
- [ ] Unit-tested: harness converts each failure mode to the correct `abstain(reason)` + coverage entry.
baseline.summary: Evidence contract + fail-open execution harness + optional-extra scaffolding (dependency root)

# P1.0 — Unify canonical event-byte serialization + zero-dep structural guard

**Prerequisite for P2.1, P2.2, P2.3.** Every later item that adds, reorders, or
signs event content depends on there being exactly ONE canonical byte format.

## Context (problem + research)

Event serialization is scattered across many writers and only **one** is
canonical — `_store/event_append.py:56-61` emits
`json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":"), ensure_ascii=False)`. Seven
other LIVE writers emit plain `json.dumps(event, ensure_ascii=False)` (unsorted):
reconciler `_engine/event_append.py:123`, `ticket_txn.py:219/351/372`,
`graph/_links.py:145`, `ticket-delete-unlink-scan.py:149`,
`batch_dispatch.py:222`; plus bash heredocs in `ticket-comment.sh:90-91`
(live via `ticket-transition.sh:439` force-close), `ticket-revert.sh:170-174`
(live via `ticket-transition.sh:179` un-archive), `ticket-lib-api.sh:994/1017`
(delete), `ticket-compact.sh:274` (SNAPSHOT). There is **no** byte-parity test —
the one cited in `_store/event_append.py:15`'s docstring does not exist.

**Research / proven art.** The "`json.dumps == jq -S -c`" assumption is unsafe:
`jq` parses numbers as IEEE-754 float64, and rebar's ns `timestamp` is a 19-digit
integer **> 2^53** — jq <=1.6 (default macOS) rounds it on parse, and even jq-1.7
rounds it under arithmetic. The TUF/sigstore ecosystem's hard-won lesson is
"canonicalization across implementations is a footgun; standardize on one / sign
the literal bytes" (RFC 8785 JCS; python-tuf#457; sigstore DSSE). So: collapse to
ONE Python serializer, keep jq out of the event path entirely.

## Evidence (experiments)

- EXP2: `json.dumps(...ensure_ascii=False)` == `jq -S -c` ONLY with
  `ensure_ascii=False` (`世界` diverges otherwise).
- EXP-jq: jq rounds the >2^53 timestamp (`.t+0` -> `...655000`); confirmed.
- EXP-R3 (real code): real `_canonical_bytes` != plain dumps, but parsed dicts are
  identical -> **re-serialization is replay-safe** (reducer reads keys, not bytes).
- EXP-R7 (real code): `python3 -m rebar._store.<submodule>` works and emits
  canonical sorted output -> bash heredocs can call the helper.
- EXP-R9/R9b (real code): the committed stdlib guard
  `docs/experiments/event_write_guard.py` flags **exactly 7 Python + 7 bash** event writers
  with **0 false positives** across 73 read/output `json.dumps` sites.

## What / Implementation detail

1. Factor a **lock-free** `canonical_bytes(event) -> bytes` helper (out of
   `_store/event_append.py:56-61`) importable without the write lock (the txn/LINK
   paths rename+commit inline, e.g. `ticket_txn.py:236-243`).
2. Route every live writer through it: the 5 Python sites import it; the 4 bash
   heredocs call `python3 -m rebar._store.canonical` (pass the event(s) on stdin;
   **batch** multi-event paths — delete writes STATUS+ARCHIVED+N*UNLINK — in ONE
   invocation to avoid per-event subprocess cost).
3. Delete the dead leaf writers (`ticket-create.sh`, `ticket-edit.sh`) and leave
   `ticket-link.sh` (still serves `link --dry-run`, writes no event) /
   `ticket-migrate-*.sh` (one-shot) exempt. Fix the false docstring at
   `_store/event_append.py:15`.
4. Ship the **stdlib** structural guard as a CI test (semgrep/ast-grep/pre-commit
   are ABSENT here — EXP-R9). Python prong = AST (json.dump(s) on a dict carrying
   `event_type`); bash prong = regex scoped to `json.dump` co-occurring with an
   `'event_type'` dict (a bare grep false-positives on ~10 read/output `.sh`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `canonical_bytes()` extracted as a lock-free helper and imported by the 5 Python writers
- [ ] 4 bash heredoc writers call `python3 -m rebar._store.canonical` (multi-event paths batched)
- [ ] dead leaf writers deleted; `_store/event_append.py:15` docstring corrected
- [ ] `tests/scripts/test-ticket-write-commit-event.sh` added (parity + >2^53/non-ASCII fuzz)
- [ ] stdlib structural guard wired into CI (Python AST + scoped bash regex), expected writer set empty
- [ ] reconciler + compaction suites still green (no replay change)

See `docs/remediation-implementation-plan.md` (P1.0) for the full write-up and `docs/experiments/` for the prototypes.
- [ ] All event files (every type) are byte-identical regardless of writer, pinned by
- [ ] The structural guard fails CI on any new raw event serializer; after this epic
- [ ] No reducer/replay behavior change (existing committed data unaffected;
baseline.summary: P1.0 — Unify canonical event-byte serialization + zero-dep structural guard

## Why
Operator direction (2026-08-15): approach chauvinist-subsolar-arctichare (19ea-29af-ebb3-410b) as an EXPERIMENT. The auto-resume design (adolescent-evilminded-locust) re-runs the whole verifier and relies on the verdict cache to skip credited criteria; it passes NO information about WHERE the failed attempt already searched. Question to answer empirically: does handing a resumption the prior attempt's search frontier as an EXCLUSION list ("already searched, found nothing: ...") measurably reduce re-search overlap and steps-to-verdict? Blocker noted at design time: verifier telemetry does not carry argument-level tool-call transcripts — the PoC must capture them harness-side.

## Protocol (rapid PoC — throwaway harness, no production code)
1. Corpus: >=2 real CLOSED tickets with large surfaces (description near the 8000-char cap, many prose ACs/comments). Run read-only (--source local, never signs). Cache lifecycle (one policy, all steps): each (ticket, arm) pair gets an ISOLATED cache namespace — the harness monkeypatches `cache_dir` (src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_verdict_cache.py:59, the single derivation of `.rebar/cache/completion_verdicts/...` from `_resolve_root`) to return a per-arm temp dir, the standard unit-suite technique; nothing under the real store is touched. Attempt 1 (forced exhaustion) runs with cache ACTIVE but EMPTY — banking must fill it, and prior real-store verdicts cannot leak in. Its populated cache is then COPIED once and each resume arm reads its own identical copy.
2. Transcript capture: wrap the verifier's tool executor in-harness (monkeypatch at the workflow seam) to log every tool call with full arguments (file paths read, grep patterns, dirs listed) per criterion.
3. Force exhaustion: a config-level budget cannot go low — the computed floor is AUTHORITATIVE over smaller configured values (src/rebar/llm/completion.py:237 raises max_iterations up to verify_step_floor). The harness therefore monkeypatches `verify_step_floor` to return the reduced budget (e.g. 12-20 steps) for every arm and attempt uniformly — patched at BOTH bindings, since completion_banking.py:38 binds the name at import time: `rebar.llm.completion.verify_step_floor` AND `rebar.llm.workflow.completion_banking.verify_step_floor` (patch-where-used); attempt 1 then FAILs insufficiency-only with a partial bank; keep the transcript.
4. Extract frontier: from the transcript, derive per-criterion searched-set (paths read, patterns tried) and a compact data-shaped frontier block (<=1500 chars, list form, zero imperative sentences).
5. Resume LOOP per arm, same reduced budget every attempt, each arm on its own copy of the attempt-1 cache (per the step-1 policy): repeat the re-run until overall PASS or 3 resume attempts, whichever first; the cache accrues within the arm across attempts (that accrual IS the resume mechanism). (A) CONTROL — plain re-runs, cache-seeded only (locust behavior). (B) TREATMENT — identical, plus a frontier EVIDENCE block spliced into the fenced ticket context, regenerated after each attempt from that arm's cumulative transcript. Seam (mirrors the framework's own evidence precedent): the harness wraps the registered `completion_precheck` step (src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py:48) and inserts the block into its returned `context` inside the `<untrusted_ticket_context>` fence (:229) — exactly how framework-computed child-closure proof (gate_ops.py:226-228 via build_child_closure_evidence) and the epic bug screen land today. The block is DATA-shaped, never directive ("frontier: searched-and-empty: <path/pattern list>" — no instructions), because the fence renders directive text inert by design; the packaged reviewer prompt is NOT edited. This also makes the treatment production-faithful: if it wins, the productized form IS a framework-attached evidence block at this seam.
6. Metrics table (the deliverable): re-search overlap rate per attempt (tool calls repeating any earlier attempt's arguments, same arm) A vs B, newly-banked PASSes per step A vs B, attempts-to-clean-close (or 'not clean in 3') A vs B, token cost delta.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Harness exists in the experiment worktree (throwaway; NOT pushed to Gerrit; no src/rebar changes).
- [x] Argument-level transcripts captured for >=2 large tickets across forced-exhaustion + both resume arms.
- [x] Metrics table posted as a comment on THIS ticket and on chauvinist-subsolar-arctichare: overlap rate, PASS-per-step, attempts, cost.
- [x] Verdict comment applies the PREDECLARED decision rule: GO if, on EVERY corpus ticket, the treatment arm (B) shows (i) re-search overlap rate reduced by >=30% relative to control AND (ii) attempts-to-clean-close <= control; NO-GO if either fails on any ticket; INDETERMINATE if any arm errors environmentally (report raw numbers regardless). Include what telemetry production would need to carry. N is small (2+ tickets) — the rule is a PoC screen for whether a real investment is warranted, not a significance claim, and the comment must say so.
- [x] No store writes beyond ticket comments; no signatures minted (--source local only).
baseline.summary: Experiment: search-frontier exclusion-list resumption (arctichare PoC)

baseline.description:
## Why

Pass-2 (validate each finding) is the strongest reuse candidate: the binary sub-questions
(`is_verifiable`, `evidence_entails_finding`, `path_reachable`, `impact_follows_necessarily`,
`no_viable_alternative_explanation`, `no_existing_mitigation`, `severity_claim_justified` + the
cited-reference veto) and the severity-attribute enums are properties of *a finding*, not of
plans-vs-diffs — so a code-review finding and a plan finding answer the SAME questions. Extracting
it gives one binary vocabulary + one `verification` contract that every gate shares, eliminating
the silent-drift class. The verify orchestration already built for plan-review (token-budget
chunking, merge-by-global-index, the non-frontier verifier-model default) is likewise general and
moves with it.

## What

- Move the Pass-2 verifier into the kernel as `verify_findings(findings, *, context, model,
  headroom) -> verifications`, carrying the chunking + merge-by-index + verifier-model resolution.
- Make the `verification` pydantic/JSON contract the SINGLE registered source of the binary
  vocabulary + severity-attribute enums (one schema, small/flat).
- Reliability: validate with the existing tolerant stack (json-repair + bounded retry +
  pydantic-ai native outputs) and DEGRADE to INDETERMINATE on an unparseable turn — never
  hard-crash a gate. (Reuse `gate_dispatch`'s degrade path; do not add stricter validation.)
- Rewire the plan-review verify step to consume the kernel (the per-gate verify-prompt preamble +
  the plan context are passed in). No behavior change.

## Scope

In scope: the Pass-2 verify function + the `verification` contract + the tolerant-validation
reliability behavior, moved to the kernel; plan-review consumes it. Out of scope: Pass-3 (WS1, on
which this depends), the coach (WS3), the seam doc + behavioral evals (WS4). Touches
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py` (verify builders), `sizing.py` (chunker), `workflow_ops.py`
(verify-inputs op), the verify prompt(s), and the kernel module.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The kernel exposes a `verify_findings` Pass-2 entry that takes a findings list + a domain
      context and returns the per-finding `{severity_attributes, binary}` verifications, with the

## Reproduction Steps

1. Configure local signing (`[identity] signing_key` set; git email resolves to an identity — e.g. 594c).
2. `rebar create task "t"` -> the CREATE event is SIGNED (`author_sig` present).
3. `rebar transition <t> open idea` (or any claim/transition/close) -> the STATUS event is written with `author_id` stamped but **NO `author_sig`** (UNSIGNED).
4. `rebar verify-identity --all --format json` lists that STATUS event as `unsigned` (in-scope, enforceable).

**Expected:** transition/claim/close STATUS (and claim EDIT) events sign like CREATE/COMMENT do. **Actual:** they are attributed but unsigned.

## Root cause

CREATE/COMMENT are written via `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.append_event`, which calls `_apply_authorship` (the signing seam + write-gate). But transitions/claims/closes are written via `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py` (`transition_core` ~L249-268, `claim_core` ~L341-372): these build the STATUS/EDIT event dicts, merge `attribution` (author_email/author_id) but write them directly via `fsutil.atomic_write` + git commit, **never calling `_apply_authorship`**. So the transactional path signs nothing AND bypasses the require_authenticated write-gate.

## Why this blocks the flip (dc09 / pristine-horrible-whapuku)

The CI merge-gate `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yaml` runs `rebar verify-identity` over the whole tickets store with posture/boundary from `rebar.toml`. After `require_authenticated=true` lands, every NEW status transition (post-enforce_since) writes an unsigned in-scope STATUS event that the gate flags -> the gate FAILS -> blocks landing. So enforcement is unsafe across the txn writer until this is fixed. This is a foundational signing gap the epic's 5 stories did not anticipate (they assumed signing worked for all writers).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `transition_core` and `claim_core` in `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py` sign their STATUS (and
      claim EDIT) events via the same signing seam CREATE/COMMENT use (`_apply_authorship` or an
      equivalent), so a transition/claim/close under a configured signing key produces
      `author_sig`.
- [ ] Under `identity.require_authenticated`, an unsignable transition of a non-exempt ticket is
      refused by the write-gate (parity with `append_event`), while gate-exempt types
      (session_log/code_review/identity) are unaffected.
- [ ] A held-out regression test asserts: with a signing key configured, a transition/claim
      STATUS event has `author_sig` and `rebar verify-identity` reports it `verified`; without a
      key + enforcement on, the transition is refused. Proving command: `make test`.
- [ ] No regression to txn atomicity/locking (claim writes STATUS+EDIT in one commit).
baseline.summary: txn.py transitions/claims/closes write UNSIGNED in-scope STATUS/EDIT events (bypass the signing seam) — blocks safe require_authenticated flip

baseline.description:
## Context

Operator-declared serious bug: the review-bot's LLM-Review vote publishes only a COUNT of advisory findings ("PASS. N advisory finding(s) (non-blocking)"), and the finding TEXT is retrievable nowhere on the Gerrit change. Operator impact, verbatim: "if they're invisible it makes it difficult for us to determine which advisory findings should be promoted to blocking." This feeds the pending blocking-lane re-enable work.

## Root cause (AC1 — CONFIRMED, see ticket comment #1 for full evidence)

Premise correction: the behaviour is NOT inconsistent. Advisory text is published on NO change. Change 1636 is not a counter-example — live Gerrit shows `revisions/current/comments` = `{}` and `robotcomments` = "robot comments unsupported" for 1636, 1666 AND 1685 alike, and all three carry the same count-only bot message.

Mechanism, single and deterministic:
1. `src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py:132` `_summarize()`, PASS branch (lines 134-138) renders only
   `len(verdict["advisory"])`. It never itemises the findings.
2. The `"finding"` branch (lines 139-152) itemises BLOCKING findings only — advisory text is
   dropped there too, so a BLOCK vote hides advisories as well.
3. `_translate_findings` (`adapter.py:114`) copies `{severity, dimension, detail}` and DISCARDS
   each finding's `location`, so no file/line anchor ever reaches the Gerrit layer.
4. `voter.py:700` calls `gc.post_vote(change_id, revision, value, message)` — four positional
   args — so `post_vote`'s `robot_comments` parameter (`gerrit_client.py:277-294`) is never
   supplied in production and always falls back to one `/PATCHSET_LEVEL` robot comment carrying
   the same message string. No code path builds a per-file comment map.

Rejected hypotheses: posting failure / auth (the vote POST succeeds — LLM-Review+1 landed on all three) and a size or count threshold (the count is unbounded).

Environmental constraint the fix must respect: robot comments are DISABLED on this Gerrit server, so the review message body is the only surface proven to render. Body enumeration is therefore the guaranteed surface; inline comments are additive.

## Plan

New module `src/rebar/review_bot/finding_publish.py` (keeps `voter.py`, currently 778 LOC, under the 800 cap). It OWNS the enumeration logic that `adapter.py:141-152` currently inlines for blocking findings — that block is EXTRACTED here and both adapter branches call it, so the rendering is defined once, not re-implemented:
- `MAX_DETAIL_CHARS = 240` and `MAX_ITEMS = 10` — the exact limits `adapter.py:145-152` uses
  today, promoted to named constants and imported by `adapter.py`.
- `render_findings_block(findings, kind)` — a header line, then up to `MAX_ITEMS` lines of
  `- (criterion) detail [location]` with `detail` truncated to `MAX_DETAIL_CHARS` (ellipsis
  suffix), then an `"N additional <kind> finding(s) omitted from this summary."` note when
  `len(findings) > MAX_ITEMS`. Byte-identical output to today's blocking block for `kind`
  `"blocking"`.
- `parse_anchor(location)` — split a free-text `location` into `(path, line|None)`, tolerating a
  missing or non-numeric line tail; `None` when there is no usable path.
- `partition_findings(findings, revision_paths)` — anchorable only when the parsed path is a key
  of the revision file map; everything else is anchor-less.
- `build_inline_comments(anchorable)` — `{path: [{line, message, unresolved: false}]}`.
  `unresolved: false` keeps the "no unresolved comments" submit requirement untouched.

`gerrit_client.py`: add `GerritClient.get_revision_files(change_id, revision)` — the plain `GET /a/changes/<id>/revisions/<rev>/files`, valid for ANY revision. The existing `get_merge_files` (`gerrit_client.py:184`) delegates to it so the endpoint call exists once and its merge-specific docstring stays accurate. `post_vote` (`gerrit_client.py:277`) gains an optional `comments` mapping, included in the review body only when non-empty; the `robot_comments` default is unchanged (AC5).

`adapter.py`: `_translate_findings` (line 114) also carries `location` through (additive key; existing consumers of `{severity, dimension, detail}` are unaffected). `_summarize` PASS branch (lines 134-138) keeps its count sentence and appends `render_findings_block(advisory, "advisory")`; the `"finding"` branch (lines 139-152) calls `render_findings_block` for blocking and then appends the advisory block.

`voter.py` (minimal delta at the `post_vote` call site, line 700): call `gc.get_revision_files(...)` inside a `try/except` — ANY failure degrades to an empty path set, i.e. zero anchorable findings and body-only publication, never a failed vote. Partition, then post with `comments=`. On `GerritError` from the comment-bearing POST, retry message-only with an appended notice (AC3) and only then treat a second failure as today's fail-closed error.

Design tradeoff, stated deliberately: EVERY advisory is enumerated in the message body, and anchorable ones are ALSO posted inline. Duplication is cheap; invisibility is the bug, and the body is the only surface this server is proven to render.

## Testing

Run from the worktree venv: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py tests/unit/test_review_bot_finding_publish.py -q`, then `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` and `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`. Each AC4 sub-case is a named test in `tests/unit/test_review_bot_finding_publish.py`, RED-verified by running it against unpatched `main` first.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1 — Root cause identified and recorded as a ticket comment (checked: comment #1 cites the live `GET /a/changes/<n>/revisions/current/comments` and `/robotcomments` responses), with the operator's
  "1636 is a counter-example" premise corrected against live Gerrit API state.
- [x] AC2 — Every advisory finding is retrievable from the Gerrit change: enumerated in the
  review message body on both the PASS and the BLOCK path, and additionally posted as an inline
  comment when its location anchors to a real path in the revision.
- [x] AC3 — A comment-posting failure is never silent: the vote still lands, and its message
  carries an explicit notice naming inline publication as failed and pointing at the durable
  `code_review` artifact (`emit_code_review_artifact` -> `rebar.llm.code_review.sidecar.emit`) as
  the full record. Checked by the AC4(e) test asserting the notice substring in the posted message.
- [x] AC4 — Regression tests pin: (a) advisory findings appear as text in the PASS message
  (the reproduced 1666/1685 condition — RED against current main, which emits a count only);
  (b) advisory text also appears on the BLOCK path; (c) an anchorable finding produces an inline
  comment keyed by path with `unresolved: false`; (d) an anchor-less or off-revision finding is
  still enumerated in the body and produces no inline comment; (e) a `GerritError` on the
  comment-bearing POST falls back to a message-only vote carrying the failure notice.
- [x] AC5 — `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` and `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck` pass; no change to vote semantics — label name,
  vote values, PASS/BLOCK mapping, fail-closed coverage-gap behaviour and the dedup/retry
  bookkeeping are all untouched.
baseline.summary: Advisory review findings sometimes invisible on the Gerrit change
