## Summary

`tests/external/test_ref_lock_ac0_live.py` pushes a throwaway `refs/reconciler/spike-*` ref to the `origin` remote to prove the ref-lock round-trip "against the actual origin". That assumes a **writable** `origin`. In this repo code lands via Gerrit and GitHub `origin` is a **read-only mirror** — the external-integration Actions token is `contents: read` and `github-actions[bot]` gets 403 on push. The test was added 2026-07-04 (after the last green run 2026-06-16) and has therefore **never passed** in this workflow; it was masked by the ALLOW_MODEL_REQUESTS guard until that was fixed.

Its assumption (a writable non-ticket-branch remote) is invalid for this repo, so the test should be removed. The hermetic counterpart `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_ref_lock.py::test_ac0_blob_ref_roundtrips_through_remote` already proves the acquire/release/read CAS mechanics against a local bare remote, so removing the live variant loses no real coverage.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Trigger the external-integration workflow (external job) on main.
2. Observe test_ref_lock_ac0_live fail: `git push ... origin refs/reconciler/spike-* -> exit 128`,
   `remote: Permission to navapbc/rebar.git denied to github-actions[bot]` / 403.

Expected: the external job is green. Actual: the test fails because origin is not writable in this CI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Delete tests/external/test_ref_lock_ac0_live.py.
- [ ] The hermetic unit test (test_ref_lock.py) remains and still covers the CAS mechanics.
- [ ] Verified end-to-end: the external-integration GitHub Action's external job runs green.
baseline.summary: remove stale test_ref_lock_ac0_live: assumes a writable origin remote (invalid in a Gerrit/read-only-mirror repo)

## Context / Problem

Teams running several tracker projects against one codebase cannot use the bridge: it is hard-wired to one project at three points — `JiraConfig.project` is a single scalar (`_config_schema.py`), the inbound fetcher builds its JQL pair from one key and fails closed on an empty one (`fetcher.jqls_for`), and the applier aborts a pass when any outbound mutation targets a key outside that project (`applier.CrossProjectTargetError`). The only escape is the destructive one-way `scripts/retarget_jira_project.py`. Assignee preservation for tracker-unresolvable users is owned by in-progress bug `9b94-af9e-4acf-4dff` and taken as a dependency. (A pre-condensation draft sits in an epic comment; this description supersedes it.)

## Approach

One shared ticket store between N repos and N tracker projects; each ticket records the project it syncs into and the repos it belongs to.

The STORE owns the project set — `.bridge_state/projects.json` on the tickets branch beside `bindings.json`/`prev_snapshot.json`. Mechanical reason: `prev_snapshot.json` is last-known-remote state; two repos fetching different project subsets against one shared snapshot would each diff the other's projects as remote deletions. A store-owned set removes that failure mode by construction.

Built on the provider-neutral `bridge` verb group (epic `2f79-2b32-28c5-4eb3`) and the backend-neutral port — `RemoteRef(vendor, instance, remote_id)`, `Backend.project`/`Backend.query_project`. `Backend.project` is the per-repo default for rebar-created tickets; no new config key.

Migration writes NO events. The ticket project field is tri-state — absent=legacy, explicit-empty= never sync, explicit key=sync there — mirroring `file_impact_scope` (`docs/ticket-model.md`). Absent resolves against the legacy default in the mapping, seeded by an idempotent check-then-act ensure unit (`docs/migrations.md`; the ordered School-A ledger is explicitly not built). A per-ticket EDIT migration was rejected: four-figure event writes under the store lock, and the MCP-boot ensure entry skips under lock contention, so it would silently skip there.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` — mapping store, fetch fan-out, outbound dispatch, cross-project guard.
- `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py`, `_store/init.py` — the ensure unit seeding the mapping.
- `src/rebar/_store/compat.py` — the capability stamp.
- `src/rebar/reducer/`, `schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`, `_commands/composer.py`, `_lib_writes.py`,
  `_mcp_writes.py` — the two new ticket fields and their create-time arguments.
- `src/rebar/_cli/` — the `bridge projects` subcommand.
- `docs/` — the multi-project model, the mapping, an ADR.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `bridge projects` lists, sets and removes project→repos entries on the store mapping, with the
      same operations on the library and MCP surfaces; per-surface test asserts each surface reads
      back an entry written by another.
- [x] A store whose mapping holds two projects fetches both in a single pass and each ingested ticket
      records its source project; reconciler test asserts one JQL pair AND one enrichment pass
      (parent/comment/issuelink maps) per configured project, both projects' enrichment data present
      in the merged snapshot, and the recorded project on each created ticket.
- [x] A ticket whose project is explicitly empty produces no outbound mutation; differ test asserts an
      empty mutation list for it while a sibling with a project produces one.
- [x] A ticket created with an explicit project targets it rather than the repo default; dispatch test
      asserts the create call carries the ticket's project.
- [x] An outbound update inside the configured set proceeds while one outside it still raises
      `CrossProjectTargetError`; paired applier test covers both directions.
- [x] Every ticket in a pre-feature store resolves to the recorded legacy default with zero events
      written; migration test asserts byte-identical event count before/after the sweep.
- [x] A store whose mapping holds more than one project carries `multi-project-bridge` in
      `.store-compat.json` `required_capabilities` and a binary lacking it refuses writes, while a
      single-project store stays writable; store-compat test covers both, including that the
      stamp and mapping mutation land in one tracker commit (asserted on the commit's tree).

## Child decomposition (disjoint file sets)

- **Project mapping store** — `.bridge_state/projects.json` + helpers + ensure seed. Delivers
  migration/legacy-default criteria.
- **`bridge projects` command surface** — subcommand + library/MCP parity per epic `2f79`.
  Delivers criterion 1.
- **Ticket project field** — schema, CREATE data, reducer, create-time args on all three surfaces;
  promote-only rule (cannot change a bound ticket's project). Delivers empty-project criterion.
- **Ticket repos field** — schema, reducer, create-time arg, inbound defaulting from the mapping.
- **Multi-project inbound fetch** — `_build_snapshot` (fetcher.py) iterates the configured project
  set for the base JQL fan-out AND its three enrichment passes — `get_parent_map` /
  `get_comment_map` / `get_issuelinks_map` called once per project, results merged into the shared
  snapshot keyed by issue (single-project enrichment would silently drop parent/comment/issuelink
  data for every project but one); per-query truncation ceiling scoped per project. Delivers the
  two-project fetch criterion incl. enrichment fidelity.
- **Multi-project outbound dispatch** — per-ticket project on create; guard relaxed to set
  membership. Delivers explicit-project + guard criteria.
- **Store-compat capability stamp** — add `multi-project-bridge` to `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`; change
  `_store_compat_unit`'s check-then-act from "blob absent" to "committed `required_capabilities` !=
  desired set from the mapping" (today it never re-stamps a converged store); the `bridge projects`
  set/remove write path writes the re-derived stamp and the mapping mutation in the SAME tracker
  commit (one atomic publish — no observable intermediate state; a crash before the commit leaves
  neither write). Ensure sweeps are convergence backstops for any residual divergence, not the
  trigger. Older binaries cannot create a multi-project mapping at all (they lack the verb), so the
  atomic-commit writer is the only path that can make a store multi-project; `write_compat_record` computes the
  capability list; test covers add (>1) and remove (<=1) transitions plus the synchronous-stamp
  property. Delivers the final criterion.
- **Docs + ADR** — model, mapping, tri-state field, decision record.
- **Live multi-project rehearsal** — LAST child: two live Jira Cloud projects on an isolated
  tickets-branch copy on the encrypted S3 remote (capability from epic `cf3c-1444-863e-49d7`);
  dry-run-gated, all created issues removed. Fixtures cannot reach the cross-project contamination
  this validates.
- **Module-size relief** — files this feature edits sit within ~30 lines of the 800 cap;
  behaviour-preserving extractions along existing seams, ordered ahead of the story needing room;
  they deliver no epic criterion.

## Compatibility and rollback

Additive: absent project = legacy, pre-feature stores behave as today. Single-project stores never receive the stamp, so older binaries keep working; only a genuinely multi-project store fails closed on them — intended (an older binary would see other projects' tickets as unbound and duplicate them). Rollback per-change on Gerrit; deleting `.store-compat.json` returns every binary to implicit-legacy, the ensure re-stamping on the next covered write.
baseline.summary: Many-to-many tracker projects: per-ticket bridge project + repo association over one shared store

## Context
Repository delegation must not blur the boundary between local multi-file persistence and the existing selective tickets-branch publication seam. The ownership and partial-state rules need durable documentation and regression guards.

## Outcome
Finalize the S1 cutover with ADR 0099 and cross-seam tests proving the existing five-file allowlist, unchanged-pass behavior, rotation floor, and retired-first publication semantics remain intact.

## Plan
1. Add failing regressions around selective commit staging, unchanged passes, GET rotation, and retired-state publication.
2. Keep publication in `reconcile_helpers.py`; do not publish each repository checkpoint or broaden staging.
3. Record repository versus publication ownership, ordered partial-state behavior, rollback, and no-journal/no-format-migration decisions in ADR 0099 and its index.
4. Run the full binding-state regression set after removing superseded facade persistence branches.

## Testing
Use existing held-out selective-publication suites plus ADR index checks. Assert repository failures do not cause unrelated tracker staging.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Tickets publication stages only the existing five bridge-state files.
- [ ] An unchanged pass creates no commit.
- [ ] GET rotation and retired-first failure cases preserve the pre-extraction publication and recovery floors.
- [ ] Repository checkpoints never publish independently.

## Out of scope
Lifecycle extraction and new interrupted-retirement recovery remain S2/S3.

# Close-out: empty the allowlist, re-validate pre-seeded noqas, delete dead T201 noqas, final gate

The final ticket — depends on all sweep batches. Verifies the convention is fully enforced with no escape hatches left open, and that the pre-existing suppressions are actually accurate.

## What
- Re-validate the ~96 pre-seeded `# noqa: BLE001` suppressions (written under advisory mode, never gated):
  confirm each still has an accurate reason; fix or remove stale ones.
- Reconcile the `# noqa: T201` annotations (corrected per plan-review G4: all 42 live in
  `_engine/rebar_reconciler/`, NOT the CLI): delete the ones whose `print` migrated to the logger, and
  keep the ones that are legitimate reconciler-subprocess operational stderr prints (covered by the
  reconciler per-file-ignore). Their fate depends on the reconciler sweep (`colder-bugle-rake`).
- **Document the convention durably (plan-review T5e):** capture the error-handling convention (raise-don't-
  catch on the MCP surface, stdout-is-sacred, the named-logger-to-stderr substrate, the observability floor +
  `# noqa: BLE001`-with-reason rule) in `CLAUDE.md` / a contributing doc — so the rationale survives beyond
  the exemplar code + lint (which only enforce blind-except/print, not the reasoning).
- Empty the `per-file-ignores` BLE001/T201 allowlist — all packages are conformant. (`_io/` is now owned by
  the core-leaves sweep `crow-aeon-muck`, so it can actually be removed from the allowlist — closing the
  reachability gap plan-review flagged.)
- **Record the opportunistic-narrowing outcome (epic AC4):** collect from the sweep batches whether any
  opportunistic narrowing surfaced a previously-hidden bug (each fixed with a regression test); if none did,
  record that explicitly here so epic AC4 is not vacuously satisfied.
- Final verification: `make lint` + full test suite pass; run a fresh joe-janitor audit and confirm no
  unguarded blind-except cluster remains.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every remaining `# noqa: BLE001` carries an accurate reason; stale ones fixed/removed.
- [ ] Dead `# noqa: T201` annotations removed; remaining ones are justified reconciler-subprocess
      operational prints (per the T201 G4 correction — they live in `_engine/rebar_reconciler/`, not the CLI).
- [ ] The close-out records whether any opportunistic narrowing surfaced a previously-hidden bug (each with a
      regression test), or states explicitly that none did (epic AC4).
- [ ] The error-handling convention is captured in `CLAUDE.md` / a contributing doc (raise-don't-catch on
      MCP, stdout-sacred, named-logger substrate, observability floor + noqa-with-reason).
- [ ] The BLE001/T201 allowlist is empty (no package exempt — including `_io/`); new unguarded
      blind-excepts / stray prints fail CI.
- [ ] `make lint` + full test suite pass; a fresh joe-janitor audit finds no unguarded blind-except cluster.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Pick a bound ticket with 0 comments on both sides (e.g. REB-5 / local
   0241-c6c1-0a20-491b).
2. Add a LOCAL comment: `rebar comment <local_id> "local-origin"`.
3. Add a JIRA comment to the same issue: `acli jira workitem comment create
   --key <REB-N> --body "jira-origin"`.
4. Run a reconcile pass (`rebar reconcile --mode live`).

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** bidirectional, additive comment sync — both sides end with BOTH
  comments (2 in Jira, 2 in local).
- **Actual:** **Jira = 2 (outbound works), local = 1 (inbound BROKEN).** The
  Jira-origin comment is never mirrored to local. `RECON: inbound_differ total=N
  with_comments=0` — zero inbound comment imports, fleet-wide (not just this ticket).

## Root cause (confirmed in code)

- `inbound_differ.compute_inbound_mutations(jira_snapshot, binding_store,
  local_by_id, outbound_mutations)` takes **no client**.
- `inbound_differ._diff_comments_inbound(jira_fields, local_ticket)` reads comments
  from `jira_fields["comment"]` — but the live **search snapshot does NOT include
  comment data** (Jira search omits comments; documented in `outbound_differ`). So the
  inbound differ sees 0 Jira comments and imports none.
- The OUTBOUND differ DOES fetch comments (`client.get_comments`, for dedup) but that
  fetched data is not shared with the inbound path. So outbound comment sync works and
  inbound does not.

## Fix approach

Give the inbound comment path the Jira comments — e.g. (a) thread the outbound differ's already-fetched comments into the inbound snapshot/`compute_inbound_mutations`, or (b) pass a client to `compute_inbound_mutations` so `_diff_comments_inbound` can fetch via `get_comments` (bounded, mirroring the outbound path), or (c) include comment data on the snapshot entries the inbound differ sees (reuse the absent-alive GET path). Outbound comments carry the `<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->` marker and dedup is by `jira_comment_id`, so our own echoes are already filtered — the fix must not re-import locally-originated comments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A comment created directly in Jira (no reconciler marker, not already in local)
      is mirrored inbound as a local comment on the next pass.
- [x] The simultaneous case converges: 1 local + 1 Jira comment on the same ticket ->
      2 comments in local AND 2 in Jira (no duplicates, no echo re-import).
- [x] Locally-originated comments (carrying the echo marker / matching jira_comment_id)
      are NOT re-imported.
- [x] `inbound_differ ... with_comments` reflects real Jira-side comments (no longer
      structurally 0 when Jira-side comments exist).
- [x] RED->GREEN test: a Jira-origin comment yields an inbound add; an echo does not.
baseline.summary: Inbound comment sync broken: Jira-side comments never mirror to local (inbound differ has no comment data)

RISK 2 (over-cap growth). `src/rebar/llm/prompts.py` crossed the soft cap this window (745 -> 827) and was ADDED to the allowlist rather than split. Split along the front-matter seam so it drops back off the allowlist.

## What / files — careful split along the front-matter seam
- Extract the front-matter I/O cluster to a NEW `src/rebar/llm/prompts_frontmatter.py` (per `docs/architecture.md:219`): `parse_front_matter`, `_split_front_matter_raw`, `write_front_matter`, `_refuse_newer_schema_version`, plus the constants `FRONT_MATTER_KEYS`, `PROMPT_SCHEMA_VERSION`, the module-private regex `_FRONT_MATTER`, and the exception classes `PromptError`, `PromptVersionError`. `PromptVersionError` subclasses `PromptError`, so both MUST move together (leaving the base behind would make the new module import `prompts.py` and cycle).
- The new module depends ONLY on the stdlib (`re`, `warnings`, lazy `yaml`) + `rebar.llm.errors` (for `LLMConfigError`, the base of `PromptError`). It MUST NOT import `prompts.py`, so there is no import cycle.

## Symbol disposition (explicit, to avoid implementer ambiguity)
- MOVE to `prompts_frontmatter.py`: `parse_front_matter`, `_split_front_matter_raw`, `write_front_matter`, `_refuse_newer_schema_version`, `FRONT_MATTER_KEYS`, `PROMPT_SCHEMA_VERSION`, `_FRONT_MATTER`, `PromptError`, `PromptVersionError`.
- STAY in `prompts.py` (they cannot move — they call `resolve_prompt`/`get_prompt`/`load_prompt` or are only used there): `PromptNotFound` (subclass of the now-imported `PromptError`), `ReviewerError`, `EXECUTION_MODES`, `VOLATILE_MARKER`/`_BASE_MARKER`, the cache-split helpers (`split_volatile`/`strip_volatile_marker`/`resolve_prompt_cached`), `get_prompt`, `load_prompt`, `resolve_prompt`, `prompt_override_drift`, the index/catalog helpers, etc.
- `prompts.py` imports the moved cluster back from `prompts_frontmatter.py` (so its own functions — `get_prompt`, `load_prompt`, `prompt_override_drift` raise/parse via the imported names) AND re-exports them for back-compat.

## Re-export shim (preferred over editing call-sites)
Re-export is preferred over rewriting the ~6 call-sites because several callers use lazy/inline `from rebar.llm.prompts import ...` and updating them would scatter the diff across unrelated modules for no correctness gain. The shim MUST cover EVERY name imported elsewhere from `rebar.llm.prompts`, INCLUDING the private `_split_front_matter_raw` (imported cross-module by `prompt_library.py`). Re-export list: `PromptError`, `PromptVersionError`, `parse_front_matter`, `_split_front_matter_raw`, `write_front_matter`, `_refuse_newer_schema_version`, `FRONT_MATTER_KEYS`, `PROMPT_SCHEMA_VERSION`. F401 is satisfied via an `__all__` entry (the repo's facade convention).

## External import sites that must keep working (verified by grep)
`src/rebar/llm/prompt_library.py` (`PromptError`, `_split_front_matter_raw`, `write_front_matter`); `src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor.py` (`parse_front_matter`, `write_front_matter`, `PromptError`); `src/rebar/llm/workflow/prompt_authoring.py` (`PromptError`, `write_front_matter`); `src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py` (`PromptError`); `tests/unit/test_prompt_front_matter.py` (`FRONT_MATTER_KEYS`, `PROMPT_SCHEMA_VERSION`, `PromptError`, `PromptVersionError`, `_split_front_matter_raw`, `parse_front_matter`, `write_front_matter`); `tests/unit/test_execution_mode.py` (`PromptError`). All keep importing from `rebar.llm.prompts` unchanged.

## Docs to update (no stale references after the split)
- `docs/architecture.md` (~line 219): update the `llm/prompts.py` offenders-table remedy row to state the front-matter I/O now lives in `prompts_frontmatter.py` and `prompts.py` re-exports it, and drop `prompts.py` from the "over-cap" set. Remove `src/rebar/llm/prompts.py` from `.github/module-size-allowlist.txt`.
- Grep the tree for any other reference describing `prompts.py` as holding the front-matter cluster and fix it.

## Rollback / expand-contract sequencing (reversible)
1. Create `prompts_frontmatter.py` with the cluster and add the re-export imports to `prompts.py` WITHOUT yet deleting the originals; run the full suite. 2. Then remove the original definitions from `prompts.py` (now provided by the re-exports); run the suite again. If step 2 surfaces a runtime ImportError, revert ONLY the deletion — `prompts.py` with re-exports still behaves as before. The whole change is one commit, revertible wholesale.

## Scope
In: front-matter cluster extraction + re-export shim + the doc/allowlist updates above. Out: changing the prompt schema or resolution logic (byte-for-byte behavior preserved).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `prompts_frontmatter.py` created (>=100 LOC) holding `parse_front_matter`, `_split_front_matter_raw`, `write_front_matter`, `_refuse_newer_schema_version`, `FRONT_MATTER_KEYS`, `PROMPT_SCHEMA_VERSION`, `_FRONT_MATTER`, `PromptError`, `PromptVersionError` — and NONE of these definitions remain in `prompts.py` (only re-export aliases).
- [ ] `prompts.py` drops BELOW 800 LOC and is REMOVED from `.github/module-size-allowlist.txt`.
- [ ] Public AND cross-module-private symbols (incl. `_split_front_matter_raw`) remain importable from `prompts.py` (re-export) — every external import site above still imports unchanged; no caller breakage.
- [ ] `prompts_frontmatter.py` does not import `prompts.py` (no import cycle); `prompts.py` imports the cluster from it.
- [ ] `docs/architecture.md` offenders table updated to the post-split two-file layout; no stale reference to `prompts.py` holding the front-matter cluster survives a grep.
- [ ] The prompt front-matter / drift-gate tests pass (`make lint` + `make test`).
baseline.summary: Risk 2: split prompts.py front-matter cluster (drop off allowlist)

## What
Enrich the tests overlay prompt (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-tests.md`) with the full behavioral-testing standard ported from DSO: BOTH halves — the recall patterns to flag AND the FP-discrimination guards — per the locked principle that the domain rubric lives in the OVERLAY, never in the generic Pass-2 verifier (`code-review-verify.md` stays domain-blind). Base NOT-flag auto-downgrade rules do not apply to test-correctness findings (a test overlay must still judge test quality). DO THIS FIRST to prove the overlay-authoring + eval pattern before the other five specialists (all six are children of da8a).

### Mechanism (resolves plan-review block)
These are NOT new code protocols — they are REVIEW-GUIDANCE PROSE authored into the overlay prompt body (the `<!--volatile-->`-preceding instructions of `code-review-tests.md`), the same way the base
+ existing overlays carry their rubric. The overlay LLM applies them when emitting/withholding
findings; the generic Pass-2 verifier receives NONE of this. The eval (recall + no-fire) is the enforcement: a no-fire case per FP-guard proves the overlay does not over-suppress-or-over-fire.

### RECALL patterns the overlay must flag (test antipatterns)
- change-detector: asserts an internal name/structure/state; would break on a behavior-preserving
  refactor (Rule-4 litmus: "would this break if internals were renamed without a behavior change?").
- tautological: asserts the mock's OWN configured return value (verifies the mock framework, not the
  code). BEFORE flagging, apply the INVERTED-TRACE disproof: mentally invert the condition under
  test; if the assertion would then fail, the test IS catching real behavior — drop the claim.
- over-mocking: mocks a module INTERNAL to the unit under test (asserts internal structure).
- under-mocking: does NOT mock an external boundary (DB/network/clock/third-party) → nondeterministic.
- source-grepping: greps/reads the SOURCE UNDER TEST as an assertion (tests text, not behavior).
- existence-only: a standalone `test -f <file>` with no structural-contract purpose (change-detector).

### FP-GUARDS the overlay must honor (the three named protocols, defined)
1. **Four-Criterion Test** — a test-coupling finding may be raised (as more than a `minor` style
   nit) ONLY when at least ONE defect criterion holds: (a) Refactoring violation — breaks on a
   safe refactor that preserves observable behavior; (b) Tautological assertion — asserts a
   test-configured mock return (subject to the inverted-trace disproof above); (c) Isolation failure
   — cross-test state / fixture pollution / order dependency / network/wall-clock leak; (d)
   Regression blindness — cannot detect a regression in the specific behavior this diff introduces.
   When NONE hold (the assertion targets observable output, exercises real code, survives refactor,
   no isolation issue), it is a philosophy disagreement → suggestion at most, not a defect.
2. **Rule-5 structural-artifact exception** — `grep`/`awk` over a NON-executable INSTRUCTION artifact
   (a `.md` skill/agent/contract/prompt, a workflow YAML, project config, a manifest/index) for a
   required heading, canonical identifier, or section is a STRUCTURAL-BOUNDARY assertion and is
   VALID — it is NOT the source-grepping antipattern (which applies ONLY to grepping SOURCE CODE
   UNDER TEST). Litmus: the grepped token is a contract iff a NON-HUMAN consumer (a parser/validator/
   downstream grep/registry/CI-runner that branches on the exact value) reads it; an LLM is NOT a
   non-human consumer, so prose/heading greps guarding wording ARE change-detectors.
3. **VALID-patterns-not-to-flag** — do NOT raise a finding on any of these (they are valid by the
   standard): (i) observable post-condition assertions (incl. when the unit is the sole producer of
   the post-condition); (ii) Rule-5 structural greps on instruction artifacts; (iii) greps of
   COMMAND OUTPUT (stdout/stderr/exit code of the executed unit); (iv) table-driven / equivalence /
   classifier tests, incl. exact-value assertions on a pure function's output that "look
   tautological"; (v) exit-code / emitted-signal assertions; (vi) mocks at the EXTERNAL boundary;
   (vii) coverage-gap demands (not blocking findings on their own).

## Files
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-tests.md (enrich the overlay prompt body — recall + FP-guards)
- src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-tests.eval.yaml (already exists from f93a; ADD recall cases
  for change-detector / over-mocking / source-grepping / existence-only, and no-fire cases for the
  Four-Criterion philosophy-disagreement, a Rule-5 instruction-artifact grep, a table-driven exact-
  value test, and a boundary mock — each a valid pattern the overlay must NOT flag).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `code-review-tests.md` overlay carries BOTH the recall patterns (change-detector, tautological
      w/ inverted-trace, over/under-mocking, source-grepping, existence-only) AND the three named
      FP-guards (Four-Criterion Test, Rule-5 structural-artifact exception, VALID-patterns-not-to-flag).
- [ ] `code-review-tests.eval.yaml` gains recall cases (new antipatterns) AND no-fire cases (one per
      FP-guard family) and validates offline (`rebar prompt eval code-review-tests` parses/loads);
      the overlay does not over-suppress valid patterns nor over-fire on them.
- [ ] The overlay remains ADVISORY; NO domain test-rubric leaks into `code-review-verify.md` (the
      generic Pass-2 verifier prompt is unchanged by this story).
baseline.summary: tests overlay: full behavioral-testing standard

## Context / Problem

`output_mode` (src/rebar/llm/structured.py:43) blanket-forces PromptedOutput whenever `thinking=True`, and its docstring (:50-56) states the rationale: "pairing extended thinking with a native/forced output constraint is the documented Anthropic 400". E1 (recorded on the selection bug ticket) measured that rationale stale: the historic 400 was tool_choice x thinking; `outputConfig` json_schema + thinking succeeds on the wire today (sonnet adaptive, haiku budget 2048). The blanket guard therefore forces the prompted path — the very path this epic exists to harden — even on cells where native output is measured-safe under thinking.

## Approach

Add a capability field `native_output_with_thinking: bool = False` to the capabilities model in src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py (fail-closed default). Change the guard in `output_mode` to: NativeOutput iff `caps.native_structured_output` AND (`not thinking` OR `caps.native_output_with_thinking`). Rewrite the docstring to the measured facts, including that tools x thinking x native suppresses tool calling (E1: 2/2 skipped) — which is why this function's single call site, src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:181, is the no-tools single-shot path and the agentic runner never consults it; the no-tools scoping is structural, not a parameter. No behavior changes in THIS ticket: every existing capability record keeps the default False, so thinking still forces prompted everywhere until the rows story adds measured cells. That keeps this slice independently landable with pure contrast tests.

## Scope

- src/rebar/llm/structured.py — the guard + docstring in `output_mode`
- src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py — the new field (default False)
- tests/unit/test_structured.py (or the capabilities test file) — contrast tests

## Testing

Unit tier, config-effect contrast through the real read path (shared test-design standard §6):

- caps(native=True, with_thinking=True) + thinking=True -> NativeOutput (new behavior gate).
- caps(native=True, with_thinking=False) + thinking=True -> PromptedOutput (default preserved;
  negative control proving no cell flips in this ticket).
- caps(native=True) + thinking=False -> NativeOutput; caps(native=False) -> PromptedOutput
  (both existing branches pinned unchanged).
- Mutation check: reverting the guard to the blanket `not thinking` form turns the first test
  RED.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The four contrast cases above pass — checked by the new unit tests.
- [x] No existing test changes: the current suite passes unmodified, proving zero behavior
      change at defaults — checked by `make test`.
- [x] The docstring states the measured facts (tool_choice x thinking as the historic 400;
      tool-suppression as the no-tools scoping reason) and cites the E1 evidence location —
      checked in code review.
baseline.summary: Gate output_mode on measured thinking-compatibility per model

# Cloud's three whole-project readers have NO multi-page test — the same class fixed three times on DC

## Claim

`adapters/jira/acli_graph.py`'s `get_parent_map`, `get_comment_map` and `get_issuelinks_map` each paginate a whole project through an opaque `nextPageToken` cursor at `page_size = 100`. **No test exercises more than ONE page.** The only coverage, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_acli_cross_mixin_binding.py:188,200`, feeds payloads carrying `"isLast": True` — a single page, terminating immediately.

This is the SAME defect class that shipped three times on the DC/shared side and was fixed each time only after it was found in production-shaped code:
  * change 1105 — `get_parent_map` advanced by the REQUESTED page size and stopped on a short page;
  * [rebar:9263-b404-cb6c-463f] — `get_issuelinks_map` and `get_comment_map`, the same bug;
  * [rebar:deac-4f5a-856a-49bd] — `fetcher._iter_pages`, which lost 92% of a snapshot when measured.
The Cloud copies of these three readers have never been tested past their first page.

## Why the risk is real rather than theoretical

* The cursor contract is genuinely stateful: `acli_graph.py:271-272` terminates on `isLast` OR on a
  null/absent `nextPageToken`, and the request echoes the token back at `:225`. Nothing asserts the
  cursor ADVANCES, that a second page is fetched and merged, that a null token stops the loop, or
  that a repeated token cannot spin forever.
* A silent truncation here is invisible: these are whole-project READS feeding the differ, so the
  symptom is missing parents / comments / links, not an error.
* DC now has exactly these tests (`test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py:66-128`, recovering 250
  items from a 20-cap client) plus a structural AST guard at `:166`. **That guard scans the DC
  transport source only**, so a fourth unpaginated caller cannot be added silently on DC and CAN be
  on Cloud.
* Live coverage does not compensate: the live Cloud tier exercises a real project, but nothing pins
  the working set above 100 issues, so a passing live run is not evidence the cursor loops.

NOTE the fetcher-level guard is NOT this. `fetch/test_fetcher_truncation_gate.py` covers the FETCHER's search loop (same-token-twice / offset-stall). These three `acli_graph` readers are a separate code path with a separate cursor.

## Provenance

Found by a Cloud-vs-DC test-parity audit commissioned while closing epic e369, not by a failure. The audit's framing is worth keeping: the DC side has been heavily tested recently, so the parity gap runs in BOTH directions — this is the largest instance of Cloud lacking what DC now has.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] a test drives each of `get_parent_map`, `get_comment_map`, `get_issuelinks_map` against a
      fake ACLI client whose working set EXCEEDS one page, and asserts EVERY item is recovered —
      a count comparison against the seeded set, not a `> 0` floor
- [x] the cursor is asserted to ADVANCE: the second request carries the token the first response
      returned, asserted on the recorded request bodies
- [x] termination is asserted on BOTH documented conditions independently — `isLast: True`, and a
      null/absent `nextPageToken`
- [x] a repeated cursor token does NOT loop forever (mirrors the fetcher's same-token-twice guard);
      it either raises or stops, and the test pins which
- [x] each new test is MUTATION-CHECKED: breaking the loop after the first page must turn it RED,
      recorded on this ticket with the verdicts
- [x] the structural anti-regression guard is extended to cover `adapters/jira/acli_graph.py`, so a
      fourth unpaginated whole-project reader cannot be added silently on EITHER deployment
baseline.summary: Cloud whole-project readers (parent/comment/issuelinks maps) have no multi-page test

# The completion-verifier close gate FAILS OPEN on an LLM provider error (via the epic-close bug screen)

## Context / Problem

Closing epic `e369-a449-4773-48fb`, the completion verifier's epic-close bug screen hit a Bedrock `ValidationException` (`LLMUnavailableError`) on every one of its 32 per-candidate calls — and the verifier still returned PASS, exit 0. The screen's `except Exception` degrade coerces EVERY per-candidate failure to verdict `C` ("unrelated"), so a systematic provider outage silently turns the epic's caused_by bug floor into a no-op with no signal anywhere: not in the verdict, not in the sidecar, not in the exit code. Contrast: when the provider package is merely absent, the same gate correctly REFUSES the close. Two failure modes of one dependency, opposite outcomes — and the fail-open one fires exactly when the provider is degraded. (Full RCA in the comments; the original "the outer gate swallows the error" framing was refuted — the outer close gate already fails closed on any exception from `verify_completion`. The real fail-open is the screen-layer degrade.)

The prior RCA's other confirmed defect — `max_tokens` never re-clamped for a smaller model, the source of the 400 itself — is already fixed and merged (commit `e49e7a418a`, Gerrit change 1361).

**Operator-ratified decision (2026-08-04, recorded in the comments): FAIL CLOSED.** A provider error during the completion verifier must BLOCK the close (nonzero exit, error naming the provider failure, ticket stays `in_progress`), consistent with the absent-provider path. The escape hatch is the existing force flag (`--force-close`; its rename to `--force` is story 24f7-1955-bcd8-4f29, out of scope here).

## Approach

Make the epic-close bug screen propagate `LLMUnavailableError` instead of degrading it to `C`, at both layers where it is currently swallowed:

1. `epic_bug_screen.screen_candidates._row` — re-raise `LLMUnavailableError`
   before the broad per-candidate degrade (warm call and fan-out alike; the
   `ThreadPoolExecutor.map` surfaces the first worker exception on iteration).
2. `epic_bug_screen.run_screen` — re-raise `LLMUnavailableError` before the
   outer "the screen is advisory" broad except.

**The exact re-raise predicate at both seams is `except LLMUnavailableError: raise` — the ordinary isinstance catch, which by design also covers its subclass `LLMConfigError` (`errors.py`: `class LLMConfigError(LLMUnavailableError)`).** That is intended, not accidental: both the systemic-outage class (the Bedrock 400) and the absent-provider / missing-extra class fail closed, matching the posture the pinned `test_gate_missing_llm_fails_closed` already asserts at the outer gate seam. Worked example: a screen call raising `LLMUnavailableError("the LLM provider call failed: … ValidationException")` propagates and blocks the close; a screen call raising `RuntimeError("model exploded")` or producing malformed output still degrades that candidate to `C`. Do NOT narrow with `type(exc) is LLMUnavailableError`. Non-systemic failures (malformed output, store read errors, any non-`LLMUnavailableError` exception) keep the documented degrade-open behavior.

Why the FAN-OUT re-raises too, diverging from the `plan_review/pass1.py` container precedent (which aborts only the warm call and degrades a fanned-out worker's systemic error): pass1's fan-out can degrade because the earlier Pass-1 chunk pool re-raises `LLMUnavailableError` before the container stage is ever reached — an upstream tripwire owns the outage signal. The completion screen has NO such upstream tripwire: `produce_completion_verdict` preflights once, but a per-call provider rejection (the motivating 32/32 Bedrock `ValidationException`) is invisible to that single preflight, so the screen's own fan-out is the ONLY place the outage can surface. The alternative (warm-call-only abort) was weighed and rejected — it restores fail-open for exactly the systematic-failure scenario this ticket exists to close. From there the existing machinery already does the right thing with no further change: the workflow interpreter captures the step exception as a failed step, `produce_completion_verdict` raises on a non-succeeded run, and `transition_close._completion_precheck`'s fail-closed handler blocks the close with the standard "completion verification could not run (…) Override with --force-close" message carrying the provider failure text. `--force-close` bypasses the verifier before the screen ever runs, so the escape hatch is untouched. Docstrings/comments that state "the screen never blocks a close" are updated to name the one deliberate exception. This does not regress Gerrit change 1360 (`_legacy_material_ok` grandfathering, the certifiable=False stderr warning, `certifiable` in the PASS sidecar): none of those paths are touched.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/epic_bug_screen.py` — the two re-raise seams + docstrings.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py` — comment/docstring accuracy only.
- `tests/unit/test_epic_bug_screen_4b54.py` and/or a new
  `tests/unit/test_close_gate_provider_error_1019.py` — the RED-first
  behavioral tests below.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py` — a provider-error
  close-refusal case at the gate seam if not already covered.

## Testing

RED first (each fails on current main, for the right reason):

- a screen call raising `LLMUnavailableError` propagates out of
  `screen_candidates` (warm-call and fan-out cases) and out of `run_screen` —
  driving the seam to RAISE, not asserting a mock's call count;
- end-to-end at the close-gate seam: a verifier run that dies with a provider
  error blocks the close — nonzero exit, ticket stays `in_progress`, no
  signature, the error message names the provider failure.

Pinned-unchanged (must stay green):

- non-provider per-candidate failures still degrade to `C`
  (`test_screen_per_candidate_failure_degrades_to_c`,
  `test_run_screen_degrades_open_on_total_failure`);
- absent-provider/missing-extra close still fails closed
  (`test_gate_missing_llm_fails_closed`);
- `--force-close` still bypasses (`test_force_close_skips_verify_and_sign`);
- healthy PASS close still mints the signed attestation per change-1360
  behavior (`test_gate_pass_closes_and_signs_after_close`,
  `test_gate_pass_uncertifiable_warns_on_stderr`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] a completion-verifier run in which the epic-close bug screen raises
      `LLMUnavailableError` REFUSES the close: nonzero exit, ticket stays
      `in_progress`, no signature, the error names the provider failure, and
      the existing `--force-close` escape hatch still applies — checked by the
      new gate-seam test passing.
- [x] a test pins the refusal by driving the screen to RAISE the provider
      error (not by asserting on a mock's call count) — checked by the new
      unit tests in the screen module's suite passing, RED-first.
- [x] non-provider screen failures still degrade open, and the absent-provider,
      force-close, and healthy-PASS close paths are byte-for-byte unchanged —
      checked by the pre-existing tests named in ## Testing staying green.
- [x] the `max_tokens` re-clamp for a smaller model (the source of the original
      400) is merged — checked by commit `e49e7a418a` reachable from `main`.
- [x] epic e369's close disposition is explicitly recorded on this ticket:
      either re-verified once the gate works, or its unsigned close accepted
      with the reason stated — checked by a closing comment on this ticket.
baseline.summary: max_tokens is never re-clamped for a smaller model, so the epic bug-screen silently degraded open (original 'gate fails open' framing REFUTED)

## Why

The migration must be validated WITHOUT trusting LLM output equivalence (the review is LLM-dependent and variable). Epic A shipped a `PlannedTraceRunner` (`workflow/trace.py`) that records each call's INTENDED shape offline. Epic B uses it to prove the workflow and the bespoke implementations issue the SAME plan — the safety net that lets B5 cut over with confidence.

## What

Build a planned-trace parity harness that runs BOTH the bespoke gate and the new engine workflow (B2 plan-review, B3 completion-verification) OFFLINE via the Fake runner over a DIVERSE scenario corpus, and asserts PLANNED-TRACE parity — NOT result parity. The planned trace is the ordered set of intended execution events: `[DET-check-id | (criterion/prompt-id, INTENDED model, call-mode agent|1-shot) | deterministic-step-id]`. Parity is asserted on the PRE-ESCALATION planned trace (tolerating runtime size-ladder escalation divergence), capturing the INTENDED/selected model (not the fake's echoed `model=None`). The harness runs in CI (no live calls, no credentials).

## Scope

- A parity harness + a diverse OFFLINE scenario corpus (varied ticket shapes: container vs leaf,
  with/without overlays, code-grounded criteria, oversize, missing AC, etc.).
- Trace normalization that ignores ordering noise from concurrency but pins prompt-id + intended
  model + call-mode + deterministic step ids, pre-escalation.
- A CI-run test asserting parity for both gates across the corpus.
- Depends on B2 + B3 (both implementations must exist to diff).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A parity harness runs the bespoke and workflow implementations of BOTH gates offline
      (FakeRunner) over a diverse scenario corpus and asserts identical PRE-ESCALATION planned
      traces (prompt-id + intended model + call-mode + deterministic step ids).
- [ ] The harness captures the INTENDED/selected model (not the fake's echoed field) and tolerates
      runtime size-ladder escalation divergence by asserting pre-escalation only.
- [ ] The parity test runs in CI with no live calls / no credentials; the scenario corpus covers
      container/leaf, overlays on/off, code-grounded, oversize, and missing-AC cases.
- [ ] `make lint` + the full test suite pass.

## Problem

GitHub code scanning reports TWO OPEN high-severity alerts — the only open alerts on the repository:

    81  py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization  tests/unit/test_llm_fallback_chain.py:249  high
    82  py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization  tests/unit/test_llm_fallback_chain.py:250  high

Both are this pattern in `test_a_fallback_entry_endpoint_is_built_against_that_endpoint`:

    assert str(model.models[1].base_url).startswith("https://fallback.test")
    assert not str(model.models[0].base_url).startswith("https://fallback.test")

`startswith` on a URL is not a host check. `https://fallback.test.evil.example/` satisfies it, because the attacker-controlled part sits AFTER the prefix the assertion pins. The rule is right about the pattern.

## Honest severity assessment

CodeQL rates these high because the rule cannot distinguish test code from production code. In context the exploitability is nil: the string is a hard-coded constant in a unit test, no untrusted input reaches it, and nothing branches on the result except the assertion itself. So the real defect is not a vulnerability — it is a WEAK ASSERTION. The test means "this model was built against that endpoint" but checks "the base_url starts with these bytes", which would also pass for a different host sharing the prefix. Fixing it makes the test say what it means AND clears the alert, so the two goals coincide and there is no reason to dismiss instead.

Do NOT resolve this by dismissing the alerts, and do NOT add a suppression comment: the assertion genuinely is weaker than intended.

## Approach

Compare the URL ORIGIN exactly rather than by prefix. Parse both sides with `urllib.parse.urlsplit` and compare `(scheme, netloc)` as a tuple — exact equality has no substring semantics for CodeQL to flag and no prefix ambiguity for a reader. `startswith` was presumably chosen because the client normalises the configured endpoint (e.g. appends a trailing slash), which whole-string equality would break; comparing the parsed origin keeps that tolerance without keeping the weakness.

Single-source the endpoint constant so the configured value and the asserted value cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Both assertions compare the parsed URL ORIGIN (scheme + host) by exact equality, and no
      `startswith`/`in` substring check against a URL remains anywhere in the file.
- [x] The test still FAILS if the fallback entry is built against the provider default instead of the
      configured endpoint — the property the test protects is preserved, verified by running it.
- [x] A host that merely shares the configured endpoint as a prefix
      (e.g. `https://fallback.test.evil.example`) does NOT satisfy the assertion, pinned by a test or by
      the construction of the comparison itself.
- [x] After the fix lands and CodeQL re-runs, `gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/code-scanning/alerts` reports
      ZERO open `py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization` alerts.
- [x] No alert is dismissed and no suppression comment is added — the code is changed.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
baseline.summary: CodeQL high: incomplete URL substring sanitization in the fallback-endpoint test

baseline.description:
Integrate mandatory security declarations into brainstorm, preplanning, and implementation-plan so security concerns are addressed at planning time — not discovered at code review.

## Mandatory Declarations

Every planning workflow must verify the following security declarations exist before implementation begins:

### 1. Endpoint Access Level Declaration
Every endpoint must explicitly declare its access level: **public**, **authenticated**, or **internal**. Ambiguity (not intentional public) is a planning failure, not a code review finding.
- **Where enforced:** Implementation-plan task generation — every task creating an API endpoint must include an access_level field in its acceptance criteria
- **Preplanning check:** Security reviewer flags stories involving new endpoints without access classification

### 2. PII Encryption-at-Rest Plan
Every data field touching PII must have an encryption-at-rest plan before implementation.
- **Where enforced:** Brainstorm — during gap analysis, any epic involving user data collection must identify PII fields and their encryption strategy
- **Implementation-plan check:** Tasks creating database models or data stores with PII fields must include encryption acceptance criteria
- **What to declare:** Field name, PII category (name, SSN, DOB, address, etc.), encryption method (column-level, volume-level, application-level), key management approach

### 3. External Integration Threat Model
Every external integration must have a threat model entry before implementation.
- **Where enforced:** Brainstorm — during the scrutiny pipeline, any epic involving external APIs, third-party services, or data exchange must produce a threat model entry
- **What to declare:** Integration name, data exchanged, trust boundary, authentication method, failure mode (fail-open vs fail-closed), data residency implications

### 4. Agent/Sub-Agent Permission Scope
Every agent or sub-agent must have a declared permission scope.
- **Where enforced:** Implementation-plan — tasks dispatching sub-agents must declare permitted tools, file access scope, and network access
- **Preplanning check:** Stories involving multi-agent orchestration must include permission boundaries in done definitions
- **What to declare:** Permitted tools list, file/directory access scope, network access (none/internal/external), credential access (none/scoped/inherited)

### 5. User Input Validation Strategy
Every user input path must identify its validation strategy before implementation.
- **Where enforced:** Implementation-plan — tasks accepting user input must declare validation approach in acceptance criteria
- **What to declare:** Input type, validation method (allowlist/denylist/regex/schema), server-side enforcement (mandatory), max length, encoding/escaping strategy for output contexts (HTML, SQL, shell, etc.)

## Integration Approach

### Brainstorm
- Gap analysis phase should check for PII fields and external integrations in the epic scope
- Scrutiny pipeline should flag epics touching user data or external services that lack security declarations
- Success criteria should include security declarations when applicable

### Preplanning
- Security concern area scan (Phase C) should verify each story has the required declarations based on its scope
- Stories without required declarations should be flagged as incomplete

### Implementation-Plan
- Task acceptance criteria library should include composable security declaration blocks
- The 5 parallel reviewers should include a check: "Does every task with [endpoint/PII/integration/agent/input] have the corresponding security declaration?"
- Tasks missing declarations should fail the plan review gate

## Government Context
These declarations map to federal compliance requirements:
- Access levels → NIST 800-53 AC (Access Control) family
- PII encryption → NIST 800-53 SC-28 (Protection of Information at Rest), NIST 800-122
- Threat models → NIST 800-53 RA-3 (Risk Assessment), FedRAMP requirements
- Permission scopes → NIST 800-53 AC-6 (Least Privilege)
- Input validation → NIST 800-53 SI-10 (Information Input Validation), OWASP Top 10
baseline.summary: improve security criteria used during plan review

## Idea: Human-in-the-loop (HITL) approval gate the agent cannot self-satisfy

### Problem

rebar's start-work and completion gates are enforced in-process by the same runtime the agent drives, and their escape hatches are reachable by the agent itself. In particular, `rebar review-plan --force` bypasses the plan-review claim gate, and it is CLI-invocable by an autonomous agent. Recent real-world drift (session `5eb0` / epic `708d`): an agent, acting on a vague human instruction, rationalized repeated `--force` plan reviews of blocked tickets rather than deferring — each individually plausible, collectively defeating the gate's intent (mint no signed attestation against not-yet-final dependencies). 2026 research frames this precisely:

- *Ambig-DS* (arXiv 2605.09698) — under-specified tasks produce **silent commitments** to
  plausible-but-unintended framings; the bottleneck is recognizing underspecification.
- *Bayesian and Motivated Reasoning in AI Agents* (arXiv 2608.00339) — framing/priors
  "neither specified in the task nor visible in the decision record" silently drive conclusions.
- *Securing Agentic AI: From Per-Action Checks to Trajectory Assurance* (arXiv 2608.01558) —
  "sequences of individually permissible actions may collectively violate system-level
  constraints"; safety must be a **verifiable property of the runtime**, not "an optional
  layer of guidance."

The common thread: any approval an agent can *produce* it can *rationalize producing*. A robust HITL gate must be one the agent structurally **cannot replicate**, only *request*.

### Proposed direction (to be designed via the brainstorm protocol before any build)

Add a HITL approval primitive to rebar that gates a configurable set of consequential / policy-overriding operations (initial candidates: `review-plan --force`, force-close, limit changes to `.github/module-size-limit.txt`, and any future `--force` escape hatch) behind an approval token that:

1. **Is unforgeable by the agent** — the approval is bound to a secret/authority the agent has
   no access to. Sketches to evaluate (prior-art review required, per the brainstorm skill's
   "interrogate novelty" step): a detached signature over the request payload made with a key
   held only by a human/CI identity (mirroring the existing plan-review attestation signing but
   with a *separate, agent-inaccessible* key); a Gerrit-style out-of-band vote by a
   non-agent account; a one-time approval nonce minted by a human-operated command.
2. **Is request/grant-separated** — the agent can only emit a *request* (payload = operation,
   target ticket(s), reason, base SHA). Granting happens in a channel the agent cannot drive;
   the agent then presents the returned token, which rebar verifies against the
   agent-inaccessible authority before allowing the operation.
3. **Is bound and non-replayable** — the token is scoped to the exact operation + target +
   content hash + a short expiry, so a grant for one action cannot be reused for another
   (defeats the "series of individually-plausible forces" pattern; cf. trajectory assurance).
4. **Fails closed and is auditable** — absent/invalid/expired/stale token → operation refused;
   every request and grant is recorded as ticket/session-log events for the decision record
   (directly answering the "not visible in the decision record" finding).

### Explicitly OUT of scope for the primitive itself
- Replacing the existing signing/attestation machinery (this *complements* it with an authority
  the agent cannot hold).
- Deciding *which* operations require HITL — that policy surface is a follow-on decision; this
  idea establishes the mechanism and a minimal initial op set.

### Why an idea, not an open ticket
This needs a full brainstorm pass (purpose / problem / edge cases / implementation) and a prior-art review (existing human-approval / four-eyes / signing-authority patterns, and why OSS agent frameworks do or don't gate self-escalation) before it is claimable work. Promote `idea -> open` and author child stories once the design is settled and the plan-review gate can be satisfied.

### Acceptance criteria (for the eventual design, not this idea)
- A documented threat model showing the agent cannot mint a valid approval token by any
  in-process or CLI path available to it.
- The gated operation set is config-driven and fails closed.
- Request + grant + verification are recorded as durable, queryable events.
baseline.summary: HITL approval gate the agent cannot self-satisfy (unforgeable human approval for --force / policy-overriding ops)

## Context / Problem
The approved Pydantic output, bounded-operation, compatibility, and candidate-tracing children establish the replacement behavior [rebar:serge-monotonous-aruanas] [rebar:amoebaean-hemihedral-vervet]. S2 already converted `_pai_structured` to ONE bounded Pydantic `Agent` run per output mode (native / prompted); this final change makes that one-operation path AUTHORITATIVE for EVERY `mode="structured"` consumer (library, CLI, MCP, and every in-tree caller), proves provider-cache behavior, then removes the obsolete manual retry machinery and any temporary compatibility delegation — WITHOUT breaking patch/import seams and WITHOUT regressing the `structured_retry_limit=0` single-shot fail-safe.

## Approach
Switch every structured `PydanticAIRunner` consumer to the one-operation path through the existing facade. Preserve `ProviderSession`, candidate order, output-mode policy, tool surfaces, timeout/transport limits, provenance, and serialized verdict shapes. `structured_retry_limit` is RETAINED as the output-retry-allowance cap. The single allowance `N = output_retry_allowance(req) = min(OUTPUT_RETRIES, max(0, structured_retry_limit))` (structured_run.py:147) seeds BOTH budgets: the Agent `retries={"output":N}` (apply_structured_seams, :183) AND the CONSTRUCTED request budget — `build_usage_limits` sets `UsageLimits(request_limit=req_limit + allowance)` (structured_run.py:429-431). The RETURNED bare `req_limit` EXCLUDES that addend (it feeds telemetry and `iteration_limit_for`'s `2*B` inverse), so the addend lives ONLY in the constructed `UsageLimits`. Seeding both from one N guarantees the request budget can NEVER trip before the output-retry counter, so `structured_retry_limit=0` → single-shot (zero output-repair retries AND zero addend) — the overlap/judge.py:212 and contracts.py:223 abstain fail-safe. Both branches (`_run_native_output`, `_run_prompted_output`) are ONE `agent.run_sync` with pydantic-ai's IN-Agent `retries`; the prompted path's tolerant-parse+validator failure is fed back via `ModelRetry` INSIDE that single run (NOT a bespoke Python loop), so a bounded retry adds a model request without a second `run_sync`. Run the complete ticket/test oracle and authorized direct Anthropic plus Bedrock cache canaries before deletion. S2 already removed the bespoke scheduler, so no obsolete attempt-loop or compatibility delegation remains to delete (a re-runnable census asserts this); retain deterministic parsing (`structured.py`), the runner facade, and public/re-export paths. Document the retry layers, request budget, complete-or-omit history, trace-not-usage candidates, and the raise-the-limit follow-up policy.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py`, `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py`, `src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py` — authoritative call-site cutover and obsolete-scheduler removal.
- `src/rebar/llm/structured.py` — retain pure repair and stop/refusal policy; remove only dead retry integration.
- ALL in-tree `mode="structured"` consumers (census enumerated in AC-1; incl. computed-mode `fidelity_spot_eval.py` and `scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py`) — compatibility verification, no call-site rewrite needed since all already route through the `get_runner(...).run()` facade.
- `docs/llm-framework.md`, `docs/reuse-surface.md` — documented runtime and library contracts.
- The RP-01 focused runner, structured-output, fallback, usage, failure, cache, plan-review, code-review, and completion suites.

## Testing
- Run the recovered RP-01 behavior matrix and all focused historical ticket regressions.
- Consumer census (AST, not literal-grep): a re-runnable scan over `src/` and `scripts/` constant-folds each `RunRequest(...)`'s effective `mode` (incl. computed `IfExp`s) and asserts no structured consumer bypasses the `get_runner(...).run(...)` facade; paired with a runtime contract test that structured dispatch is single-sourced (one impl, no bespoke scheduler).
- `structured_retry_limit=0` fail-safe: a test asserts the knob still yields zero output-repair retries (single Agent output attempt), preserving overlap/judge.py:212 and the contracts.py:223 batch abstain.
- AC-3 invariant: a test asserts exactly ONE outer Agent run on a well-formed first response, and exactly TWO (native then prompted) only on the bug-895c downgrade — never a third.
- Run lean/full import, lint, typecheck, complexity, and module-size gates.
- Run direct Anthropic and Bedrock same-run retry canaries using environment-provided credentials without printing or persisting secrets; record cache read/write/input counts and complete-versus-omitted wire observations on the ticket.
- Confirm rollback via the pre-removal compatibility commit against the same fixtures; no data migration involved.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The one-operation Pydantic path is the SOLE structured-output implementation reachable through the `PydanticAIRunner` facade, so EVERY `mode="structured"` consumer — library, CLI, MCP, and each in-tree caller in the exhaustive census (`plan_review/{__init__,passes,xcheck,prerequisites,completion_subcall,fidelity_spot_eval}`, `code_review/workflow_ops`, `overlap/judge`, `enrich`, `epic_bug_screen`, `evals/eval_solver`, `workflow/completion_recovery`, `workflow/runs`, `scripts/jira_dc_capability_map`) — necessarily uses it; verified by consumer contract tests, by a mode-resolving AST census (not a literal grep) that fails if any structured `RunRequest` is submitted outside `get_runner(...).run(...)`, and by a runner contract test that structured dispatch is single-sourced.
- [x] The recovered RP-01 behavior matrix passes with only the approved deltas: shared request exhaustion, bounded output-size retry, complete-or-omit failed response, aggregate successful-run usage, exact causal restoration, and candidate tracing outside usage.
- [x] No bespoke fresh-Agent output-attempt loop remains — output repair is the in-Agent bounded retry (`retries={"output":N}`), not a scheduler reconstructing an Agent per attempt. A structured call whose first response is well-formed performs EXACTLY ONE outer model run; the ONLY sanctioned second is the bug-895c native->prompted downgrade. The oracle counts `agent.run_sync` invocations (the outer model runs), NOT `Agent` constructions: exactly one on the happy path, exactly two (native then prompted) on the 895c downgrade, never a third.
- [x] `structured_retry_limit` is retained as the output-retry-allowance cap; `structured_retry_limit=0` yields zero output-repair retries (single-shot), preserving the overlap/judge.py and contracts.py batch abstain fail-safe; verified by a dedicated test.

  provenance: environment=autonomous-session-no-provider-creds; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=narrower; instrument=static-analysis — live Anthropic+Bedrock cache canaries need real creds (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY + AWS) absent here, so NO live call was made and this is NOT self-attested as passed; the retry-layer/cache-accounting contract is pinned offline by the AC-1/3/4 oracle + documented (AC-8). DEFERRED to a credentialed human operator (see tracking comment).
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, the focused suite, module-size gate, and complexity ratchet pass with `runner.py` at or below 800 lines and every new module between 100 and 500 lines.
- [x] The documented retry-layer and accounting contracts match runtime behavior, including the normal plan-reviewed follow-up to raise the shared allowance if legitimate recovery is starved.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The completion-verification close gate chronically fails in ways that leave no verdict: runaway duplicate tool-call loops (one live run repeated an identical search_files call 144x), request-budget exhaustion that dies verdict-less (the --force-close trap: a resource exhaustion is not a verdict, and the gate's only documented exit is --force-close), a recovery path that fans out one isolated evidence run per criterion (operator-ruled unapproved: c9f7's shape is 22 criteria x 20-request budget = 440 requests worst case with ~2.67M context chars re-sent), and a flat 100,000-char recovery context bound (completion_recovery.py:68) that refuses the live 121,147-char ticket c9f7 forever because ticket context is append-only and can only grow. Each failure was patched separately across four exhausted close attempts on epic e369; this epic reworks the verifier's context management as one design so exhaustion is bounded, verified progress survives failures, and every run with progress ends in a scored, signed verdict.

## Approach

Rework along seams that already exist, generalizing only where multiple LLM workflows already share code (the agent_call.py tool-wrapping seam armed for every tool-bearing run, and model_classes.py model knowledge); everything specific to completion semantics — the verdict bank, criterion identity, context assembly, verdict coverage — stays completion-local in the workflow modules. Child responsibilities, each delivered by one child:

- **Context ceilings** — replace the flat recovery char bound with a physical ceiling derived from the resolved verifier model's own context window plus an economic ceiling bounding total re-send spend, preserving the d59e invariants (no elision, zero billable calls on refusal).
- **Duplicate-call damping** — memoize duplicate read-only tool calls at the shared agent-call seam and steer the model off repeats with static nudges; the shipped distinct-ratio runaway actuator stays as the abort backstop.
- **Banked, batched verification** — record per-criterion verdicts incrementally to a run-scoped bank; replace the per-criterion recovery fan-out with batched successor runs over the unverified remainder under a request-denominated budget pool; finalize to a full-coverage verdict whenever any progress is banked, with a deterministic no-LLM fallback so a run with banked progress can never die verdict-less.
- **Context pre-loading** — pre-fetch ranked file_impact contents into the fenced verifier context under a budget clamp with a per-file full/skeleton manifest, cutting agentic read round-trips (live traces show 67-82% of distinct file reads are covered by subtree file_impact).
- **Interim evidence-run insurance** — single-criterion evidence-run survival hardening that ships only while the fan-out it patches still exists.

Sequencing is encoded as dependency edges: ceilings first (smallest change; unblocks re-certifications refused at preflight today), then duplicate-call damping (immediate waste cut for every agentic workflow), then the banked/batched core rework, then pre-loading (its improvement is only measurable against the post-rework baseline).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A completion verification whose primary run dies in a typed failure (budget exhaustion, runaway loop, or token exhaustion) with at least one criterion verdict banked ends in a full-coverage verdict instead of a verdict-less error — delivered by the banked-verification child; checked by its unit suite and a live Bedrock run recorded on that child.
- [x] No completion code path launches one isolated LLM run per criterion — delivered by the banked-verification child; checked by grep over src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py showing the fan-out removed, plus its unit suite.
- [x] The recovery preflight accepts the live c9f7 shape (121,147 chars x 22 criteria) under the two-ceiling bound with the d59e invariants intact — delivered by the context-ceilings child; checked by its held-out unit oracle and a live run recorded on that child.
- [x] Duplicate read-only tool calls inside one agentic run are served from a memo with a static nudge instead of re-executing, with the runaway actuator's window math unchanged — delivered by the duplicate-call damping child; checked by its unit tests and a live Bedrock capture recorded on that child.
- [x] The completion verifier's context pre-loads ranked file_impact contents with a full/skeleton manifest and reduces live request counts by at least 20% with verdict class unchanged versus the post-rework baseline — delivered by the pre-loading child; checked per that child's live A/B acceptance criteria.
baseline.summary: Rework completion-verifier context management: batched AC verification, context ceilings, pre-loading

## Context / Problem

A store write that cannot acquire the write lock in its budget is DISCARDED — no retry, no spool. `acquire()` computes `total_wait = timeout * attempts` into **one** deadline (`lock.py:695-698`), so `attempts` is a silent multiplier, not a retry loop. Both legs non-blocking-poll with jitter (`lock.py:215`, `lock.py:628`), so there is no fairness.

Re-measured 2026-08-11 against an APFS clone of the live 737M tracker (numbers in the AC#1 comment): the 6-writer storm no longer loses writes (6/6, 16/16, 48/48 succeed — 7084's fixes were real), but loss is still terminal and is now driven by HOLDER DURATION. A 70s holder + 3 comments → 3/3 exit 1 with **0 of 3 markers present afterwards**. A 45s holder + one `rebar claim` → fails at exactly **30.30s** (`attempts=1`).

Confirmed since: the live Jira DC CI run recorded here, and TWO of this ticket's own plan-review PASSES, destroyed by 60s timeouts behind 88-163s holders (see comments).


## Approach

**Bounded retry-with-backoff, not fair queueing.** When one holder outlives the whole budget every waiter fails regardless of service order, so FIFO buys nothing here. Bounded re-attempts convert loss into latency with less machinery than a queue.

Retry is safe without the phantom-write semantics that got R6 (spool-and-adopt) declined on 7084, because **the retry lives strictly inside `acquire()`**: it re-attempts only the acquisition, and `LockTimeout` is raised before the caller's write body runs. Once `acquire()` returns the loop is finished and cannot re-enter, so no write is replayed. A retry ABOVE the lock would risk a duplicate append; that boundary is asserted by test.

Checked against the "error surfaced but the write had landed" shape: one `transition` takes up to six acquisitions, five AFTER the STATUS commit (signature `transition_close.py:433`, links, audit, compaction, push). Each is an INDEPENDENT append with its own acquisition, so retrying an acquisition lands *that* event and never replays the STATUS event. Opting `event_append.py` in also makes the completion-signature append survive contention — the direct cause of the "closed WITHOUT a completion signature" warning at `transition_close.py:440`.

1. `acquire()` and `write_lock()` gain **`retries: int = 0`**. The default of 0 reproduces today's
   behaviour exactly, so every caller not listed below is unchanged with no edit.
2. **Why passes rather than one longer budget:** both legs already poll to deadline, so a single
   180s budget would wait as long — but it would hold the won fcntl leg while starving on mkdir,
   and emit nothing until the very end. Discrete passes RELEASE between attempts, giving other
   waiters a window against the lottery-style polling, and give one warning per pass.
3. **Backoff schedule (pinned):** between passes the loop sleeps `_jitter(0.5 * 2**(n-1))` for
   pass *n*, capped at 2.0s — so ~0.5s then ~1.0s for the default 2 retries. Backoff is ADDITIVE
   to, not carved out of, each pass's `timeout*attempts` budget. Ceiling = 3 passes x 60s + ~1.5s
   backoff ≈ **181.5s**, the "~180s" figure below.
4. Opted-in sites pass `_write_path_retries()`, reading env **`REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES`** (int, default
   **2**, clamped `[0,10]`). `REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES=0` restores today's fail-fast.
5. The terminating `LockTimeout` names the **cumulative** wait plus the holder; each exhausted pass
   logs a warning naming it.
6. `txn._acquire_write_lock` (`txn.py:84-86`) discards both by re-raising a generic
   `CommandError("Error: could not acquire lock")`. It propagates `str(exc)` instead.

## Scope

**Edited, opting in to retries** (exactly five call sites):
- `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` — `retries` param, retry loop, backoff, `REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES` helper,
  cumulative-wait message, per-pass warning.
- `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py` — write path, `write_lock()` at **382, 420, 532**.
- `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py` — `_acquire_write_lock` (**84**) plus message propagation.
- `src/rebar/_store/push.py` — **654** (locked commit-and-push) opts in; **361** (advisory merge)
  stays fail-fast.
- `tests/unit/test_lock_retry_zebrafish.py` (new); `docs/concurrency.md`.

**Deliberately NOT edited — every other caller keeps fail-fast via the `retries=0` default:** `compact_txn.py:340`, `compact_rebuild.py:126` (retries would undo 7084's R3 stand-aside and re-create the 48s holder that caused this bug); `fsck_repair.py:241`, `s3_doctor.py:239` (operator-driven repair); `inbound_translate.py:283`; `sync.py:255`, `push.py:361`, `ensures.py:158` (best-effort sweeps).

## Testing

- **Happy path:** an uncontended `acquire(retries=2)` wins on pass 1 and never sleeps.
- **Reproduction (RED→GREEN):** a real subprocess holder held past one budget. With `retries=0` the
  waiter raises `LockTimeout` (today's loss); with `retries=2` it acquires on a later pass and its
  write is present.
- **No double-append:** after a contended acquire succeeding on a later pass, exactly ONE event is
  appended.
- **Exhaustion:** a holder outliving all passes raises `LockTimeout` with the cumulative wait, and
  one warning is logged per exhausted pass.
- **Claim path:** a claim-shaped acquire behind an over-budget holder succeeds on a later pass; its
  `CommandError` carries the cumulative wait and the holder.
- **Fail-fast preserved:** the advisory `push.py:361` merge acquires with `retries=0`.
- **Env override:** `REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES=0` restores fail-fast; out-of-range clamps.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Re-measured post-R1/R3/R5 main and recorded whether writes are still lost — done, numbers in
      the AC#1 comment.
- [x] The retry-vs-fair-queueing decision is recorded in Approach with its selecting evidence.
- [x] A write whose first budget expires is re-attempted, verified by
      `pytest -q tests/unit/test_lock_retry_zebrafish.py -k reproduction` exiting 0.
- [x] The retry never replays the write body, verified by the no-double-append test asserting an
      appended-event count of exactly 1.
- [x] A write exhausting every pass raises `LockTimeout` naming the cumulative wait, verified by
      the exhaustion test's message assertion.
- [x] `claim` succeeds on a later pass behind an over-budget holder, verified by the claim-path
      test.
- [x] `claim`'s error text carries the cumulative wait, verified by asserting the `CommandError`
      message contains it.
- [x] `claim`'s error text names the holder, verified by asserting the `CommandError` message
      contains the holder string.
- [x] Opted-in sites are exactly five, distributed 3/1/1, verified by
      `diff <(grep -rln 'retries=_write_path_retries()' src/rebar --include='*.py' | xargs -n1 sh -c 'echo "$(basename $0) $(grep -c retries=_write_path_retries $0)"' | sort) <(printf 'event_append.py 3\npush.py 1\ntxn.py 1\n')`
- [x] The advisory `push.py:361` merge stays fail-fast, verified by the fail-fast test asserting
      that acquire is called with `retries=0` on that path.
- [x] Each exhausted pass logs a warning naming the holder, verified by a caplog test asserting one
      record per exhausted pass.
- [x] The `retries` default is 0 so unedited callers are unchanged, verified by a test asserting
      `inspect.signature(lock.acquire).parameters['retries'].default == 0`.
- [x] `REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES=0` restores fail-fast, verified by the env-override test.
- [x] Out-of-range `REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES` clamps to `[0,10]`, verified by the clamp test.
- [x] `docs/concurrency.md` documents the ~180s ceiling, verified by
      `test "$(grep -c '180' docs/concurrency.md)" -ge 1`.
- [x] `docs/concurrency.md` documents the override, verified by
      `test "$(grep -c REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES docs/concurrency.md)" -ge 1`.
- [x] `make lint` exits 0.
- [x] `make typecheck` exits 0.
- [x] `tests/integration/test_store_concurrency.py` passes unchanged.
- [x] `lock.py` stays under the 800-line cap, verified by
      `test "$(wc -l < src/rebar/_store/lock.py)" -lt 800`.

## Completed outcome

Merged commit `586357b70996537ac790a82da56fe6e372d0d3e5` implements a rollback-safe, durable bridge pause/resume surface while preserving old readers, old reconcile vocabulary, and existing workflow/environment behavior.

The remote `refs/reconciler/gate` blob remains dual-format: `gated_mode: "reconcile-check"` plus `paused`, `reason`, `who`, and `paused_at`. Pause provenance uses repository `git user.email` and first-pause UTC RFC3339 time. Same-reason pause is idempotent and preserves metadata; different reason, blank reason, missing identity, missing remote, and CAS movement refuse without overwrite. Resume deletes only the observed ref OID and can recover a corrupt blob without decoding it.

A new pause blocks before pass-lock acquisition or ticket mutation and returns rc 0 with one exact, anchored, JSON-decoded `BRIDGE_PAUSED:` line. The scheduled workflow recognizes only that complete rc-0 marker and skips commit-and-push. Ordinary rc 0, malformed/unanchored markers, corrupt rc 1, and legacy gate rc 4 retain their existing behavior. The pre-gate `reconcile-check` early return and old `rebar reconcile --mode` vocabulary remain functional.
