## Context / Problem

The inbound fetcher can only see one tracker project. `_build_snapshot` resolves a single `query_project` and builds one JQL pair — active and recent-done — from it (`fetcher.py:313-406`), then runs its three enrichment passes — parent, comment, issuelink maps — against that one project key (`fetcher.py:408-560`). A store that lists several projects in its mapping still ingests only one of them, and single-project enrichment would silently drop parent/comment/issuelink data for every project but one. Inbound-created tickets also never record which project they came from, so the `bridge_project`/`repos` fields added by cef7 stay unset on inbound tickets.

## Approach

**Fan out per project (fetcher.py).** Replace the single `query_project` with the store's project SET: `projects_store.read_projects(repo_root).keys()`. For EACH project, issue the existing `jqls_for(project)` pair AND run all three enrichment passes (`get_parent_map` / `get_comment_map` / `get_issuelinks_map`) scoped to that project key, merging every result into the ONE shared `snapshot` dict (deduped by the existing `seen_keys`). This reuses `jqls_for` and `_validate_project_key` unchanged, so bug 626d's JQL-injection guard keeps applying to every key with no new interpolation site, and the per-query truncation ceiling (`_ACLI_CEILING`, raising `SilentTruncationError`) stays scoped per project — a busy project cannot exhaust a shared budget on behalf of the others. When the mapping is unseeded (empty), fall back to the single `[query_project]` list so the exact pre-change query pair and single enrichment pass are issued — single-project behaviour is byte-for-byte untouched.

**Failure semantics across the fan-out.** Base-query exceptions (transport/network, malformed response, `SilentTruncationError`) propagate and fail the whole pass, exactly as today — fanning out multiplies failure points but each is fail-closed, so no partial snapshot is written. The three enrichment passes keep their existing per-pass fail-open degradation (log + continue), applied independently per project; a `BackendPaginationStallError` still re-raises past the handlers (a stalled pager is a truncated read).

**Record source project + default repos (apply_inbound_records.py).** Provenance needs NO new channel through the snapshot: the snapshot is keyed by jira key, `_apply_inbound_create` derives `jira_key = mutation.target`, and the CREATE writer `_inbound_create_write_create_event` ALREADY receives `jira_key` and `repo_root`. The source project IS `jira_key`'s prefix (`DIG-123` → `DIG`, the same `rsplit("-", 1)[0]` idiom the fetcher's parent-key derivation uses). A new leaf helper `projects_store.resolve_inbound_bridge_fields(jira_key, repo_root) -> dict` returns `{"bridge_project": <prefix>, "repos": mapping.projects.get(prefix, {}).get("repos", [])}`; the create site stamps both fields in ONE line — `create_data.update(...)` — beside the existing `creation_channel` stamp (`apply_inbound_records.py:221`). No signature change and no `apply_inbound.py` edit are required, and the net addition to `apply_inbound_records.py` (already 797 LOC, near the 800 cap) is the import + the update call — two lines, staying under the cap.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` — fan out the base JQL pair AND all three
  enrichment passes once per configured project into the shared snapshot; per-project ceiling;
  unseeded-mapping fallback to the single configured project.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/projects_store.py` — new `resolve_inbound_bridge_fields`
  leaf helper (derive source project from the jira key, default repos from that project's mapping
  entry).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` — stamp `bridge_project` + `repos`
  at the CREATE write site via the helper (net +2 lines; module is near the size cap).
- tests under `tests/`.

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's external-service row: a stateful verified fake fed production-shaped Jira fixtures. The fake must RECORD the queries and enrichment calls it issues, because "one JQL pair AND one enrichment pass per project" is itself the contract under test and is invisible to a result-only assertion.

- Happy path: a mapping with two projects issues exactly two JQL pairs and one enrichment pass per
  project (parent/comment/issuelink), and the merged snapshot carries issues AND enrichment data
  from BOTH projects.
- Postcondition: each inbound-created ticket records its source project in `bridge_project` and its
  `repos` equal that project's mapping entry; checked on tickets created from a two-project
  fixture.
- Ceiling is per project: one project exceeding `_ACLI_CEILING` raises `SilentTruncationError`
  naming it, while a second under-limit project still ingests — proving the budget is not shared.
- Empty result: a listed project returning zero issues contributes nothing and does not fail the
  pass.
- Single-project regression: an unseeded mapping issues the identical query pair and single
  enrichment pass as before this change; checked by comparing recorded queries/calls.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A two-project mapping issues one JQL pair AND one enrichment pass (parent/comment/issuelink
      maps) per project in a single pass, with both projects' issues and enrichment data present in
      the merged snapshot; checked by a fake transport recording issued queries and enrichment
      calls and asserting the exact per-project counts and contents.
- [x] Each inbound-created ticket records its source project in `bridge_project` and the repos from
      that project's mapping entry in `repos`; checked by asserting both fields on tickets created
      from a two-project fixture.
- [x] The truncation ceiling applies per project, not as a shared budget; checked by a test where
      one project exceeds it (raising `SilentTruncationError`) and a second under-limit project
      still ingests successfully.
- [x] A single-project (unseeded) mapping issues an identical query pair and single enrichment pass
      to the pre-change behaviour; checked by a regression test comparing the recorded
      queries/calls.
- [x] A configured project returning zero issues does not fail the pass; checked by an
      empty-result fixture.
baseline.summary: Multi-project inbound fetch: per-project JQL fan-out and source-project recording

# Child bin-packing for container criteria (pack small children, preserve single-child fallback)

## Why
After merge, the container still makes one call per child. Many children are small — multiple WHOLE children fit
in one call. Packing them reduces calls further, and because G3/G4 are CROSS-CHILD criteria, seeing children
together can IMPROVE consistency detection. Large (parent+child) pairings must keep the single-child path
(ca03 window-fit guarantee).

## What
- Bin-pack whole children into one call up to a token budget = model-window x P8_HEADROOM - output reserve
  (reuse the existing `pair_tokens`/`budget` + P8 machinery). Each child stays WHOLE (never chunked — ca03).
- PRESERVE the single-child path when parent+child strains the window; a child that alone exceeds budget stays
  the existing "too-big -> reduce the ticket" failure finding.
- Structured per-child sections in the prompt + REQUIRED per-child output so per-child attention isn't lost.
- Gate behind an OFFLINE EVAL confirming no per-child attention/accuracy loss vs one-child-per-call.

## Scope
- In: the bin-packer; multi-child container prompt + required per-child output; single-child fallback; the eval.
- Out: merge (S4, dependency); the caching/parallel substrate (S1/S3).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Small children are packed into one call up to the window budget; each child whole (never chunked).
- [ ] A child whose (parent+child) strains the window keeps its own call; a single child exceeding budget yields
      the too-big failure finding.
- [ ] The prompt requires per-child output; an offline eval shows no per-child attention/accuracy loss vs one-per-call.
- [ ] Container call count drops below N for epics with small children; `make lint` + tests pass.

## Remediation (opus review — MAJOR 5, MINOR 10, BLOCKER 3)
- Bin budget reuses `int(largest_window_tokens * P8_HEADROOM) - P8_OUTPUT_RESERVE_TOKENS` (pass1.py:57-59), summed
  over `parent + ALL packed children`; the single-child fallback (`pair_tokens > budget`) still fires for a lone
  oversized child -> the existing too-big failure finding, unchanged.
- Update the sizing.py container-cost projection for <N calls after packing.
- Fidelity gate = the S6 semantic eval harness (DEPENDS ON S6).
- [ ] Bin budget = parent + all packed children <= P8 window budget; a lone child exceeding it yields the existing
      too-big failure finding; each child whole (never chunked).
- [ ] sizing.py projection reflects the reduced (<N) call count after packing.
- [ ] The S6 fidelity harness shows packed-call findings within tolerance of one-child-per-call.

## CI/eval posture (S6)
- The S6 semantic fidelity eval is a HUMAN-REVIEWED development gate run before merge (live, opt-in), NOT a required/blocking CI check (non-deterministic). The offline eval-spec discipline check still runs on every PR.
baseline.summary: Child bin-packing for container criteria (pack small children, preserve single-child fallback)

`_engine_support/reads.py:133-137` and `:151-157` print to stderr and call `sys.exit(1)` when the repo root is not a git worktree. That function is reached from the library gate surface (`_lib_gates.py:42,68,83,109,118,163,210`) and thence from MCP (`_mcp_reads.py:212,218,224`).

Empirically proven during verification: a real in-memory FastMCP client was driven against a tool that exits this way. FastMCP catches `Exception` (`mcp/server/fastmcp/tools/base.py:116`) and `SystemExit` is a `BaseException`, so the whole `anyio.run` dies — the MCP server PROCESS terminates rather than returning a tool error.

Trigger is narrow (REBAR_ROOT unset with a non-repo cwd, or the repo vanishing mid-session), but a leaf helper unilaterally deciding process lifetime for every embedding surface is the defect. The library contract is to raise `RebarError`.

Both remediation proposers converged: convert to a domain exception and map it to exit 1 at the CLI boundary ONLY, so the CLI's observable behaviour is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `tracker_dir()` raises a rebar error instead of calling `sys.exit`
- [x] The CLI maps that error to exit 1 with the same message as today
- [x] A test asserts an MCP tool returns an error payload (not a dead server) with REBAR_ROOT unset in a non-repo cwd
- [x] No `sys.exit` remains reachable from `_lib_*` or `_mcp_*`
baseline.summary: Remove sys.exit from the shared read core

## GHA reconcile-bridge-canary: inject signing key + flip committer email to bot

The canary writes non-exempt tickets via the normal `rebar` CLI (`rebar create bug` / `comment` / `transition` in `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml`), so it will SIGN AUTOMATICALLY through `_seam.append_event` once the identity + key are configured — no code change needed here (unlike the reconciler). The Rebar Bot identity ticket already exists (task bffe: `594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d`), so git-email resolution to the bot works.

- **Secure key injection (concrete):** in a workflow step, `echo "::add-mask::$REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY"`
  first (so it can never surface in logs), then write it to a job-local file — e.g.
  `install -m 600 /dev/null "$RUNNER_TEMP/rebar-bot-signing-key"` then
  `printf '%s' "${{ secrets.REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY }}" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/rebar-bot-signing-key"`
  (mode 0600) — and export `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY` (or set `identity.signing_key`) to that
  path. The runner's `$RUNNER_TEMP` is discarded at job end.
- Set the canary's committer email to `joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com` (from the current bridge
  default) so git-email resolution maps to the Rebar Bot identity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` masks the secret (`::add-mask::`), writes it to a `0600` file under `$RUNNER_TEMP`, sets `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY`/`identity.signing_key` to that path, and sets the committer email to `joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com`; the key is never logged or committed.
- [ ] [operator-attested] A canary run (post-deploy; triggered via `workflow_dispatch` on `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml`) creates a bug/comment/transition whose event is signed as Rebar Bot: capture the created ticket id from the run log and confirm `rebar verify-authorship` (or `rebar verify-identity`) reports it `verified` and attributed to identity `594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d`.
- [ ] No code change is introduced here (the CLI signs automatically via the seam); the key is never logged or committed.
baseline.summary: GHA reconcile-bridge-canary: inject signing key + flip committer email to bot

baseline.description:
Sibling of cabc-7a98-d173-4d7c, found in its Phase-1 sibling sweep (E5). Jira DC's shared pager `_paged_search` loops on `startAt` offsets with no stall guard. A server that ignores/repeats `startAt` (returns the same page) spins forever — measured: 26 calls to the experiment harness cap — instead of terminating loudly. Same defect class as cabc (Cloud acli_graph cursor spin, fixed by ab7f in 30c522cde9) and `fetcher._iter_pages` (guarded since bug deac).

CORRECTED LOCATION: the original description cited `adapters/jira/transport.py:379-416`. Ticket 465d's one-module-per-capability split has since landed and moved the pager verbatim to `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/_base.py:120-157` (`_TransportBase`, the shared pager every capability mixin inherits).

## Proven root cause (runtime-confirmed; full RCA in the ticket comments)

M1 — `_base.py:141-157`: the pager's ONLY loop exit is `if not batch: break`. `start_at` advances locally but nothing verifies the SERVER honoured it, so an offset-blind instance re-serves the same non-empty page forever and the exit is unreachable (`out` grows unbounded). Runtime evidence: a `startAt`-ignoring stub drove 26 calls, requesting offsets [0,3,6,9,12,15,18,21,24,27,...] while receiving page 1 every time; terminated only by the harness cap.

M2 — `_hierarchy.py:91`: `get_parent_map` wraps the drain in a bare `except Exception: warn; return {}` degradation contract, which converts any pager-level abort into a SILENT empty parent map. Runtime evidence: the same stub returned `{}` after 26 calls, raising nothing. So M1's loud signal is neutralised at this caller unless re-raised ahead of the broad clause.

Legitimacy = defect, against cited authority: `fetcher.py:336-344` (the same operation on a parallel surface raises `SilentTruncationError(reason="offset-stall")`, contract stated at `fetcher.py:275-277`), `acli_graph.py:29-46, 79-86` (the Cloud sibling raises `RunawayPaginationError` and its readers re-raise past fail-open at `acli_graph.py:304-306`), and the prior CLOSED `Fixed:` bug cabc for this same class.

## Plan

Scope is deliberately narrow — ticket 465d owns re-architecting the DC transport modules and another stream owns `set_parent`/parent handling — but the EDIT SET IS NOT ONE RE-RAISE. Plan review (T4/T5b/G1G2) correctly found that `_paged_search` feeds THREE whole-project readers and that ALL THREE are consumed by `fetcher.fetch_snapshot` behind broad `except Exception` fail-open handlers (`fetcher.py:610` parent, `fetcher.py:652` comment, `fetcher.py:688` issuelink). VERIFIED: `fetcher.py` names neither stall error (grep for `RunawayPagination` there returns nothing), so a stall raised in the transport is swallowed at the fetcher boundary and the pass writes a silently degraded snapshot. A guard that stops at the transport boundary would therefore NOT resolve the original report. There are FOUR fail-open sites to pierce, not one.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ERROR TYPE (also plan-review advisory A1: do not mint a third bespoke error for one class). `fetcher.py` is CORE and must be able to name the error, but core must never import adapters — verified: `fetcher.py` imports nothing from `adapters/`, while adapters already import `BackendEnvError`/`BackendHTTPError` FROM core (`_links.py:19`, `transport.py:66`). So the error belongs in core's `_backend.py` beside the other `Backend*` errors, where both the DC adapter and `fetcher` can name it with no layering inversion — one canonical type for the class rather than a third bespoke one.

1. `_backend.py` — add `BackendPaginationStallError(RuntimeError)` beside the existing `Backend*`
   errors (`_backend.py:38-60`). Docstring states the invariant: a paged whole-project read whose
   server stopped advancing is a TRUNCATED read, and readers must re-raise it past their fail-open
   handlers rather than degrade around it.
2. `_base.py` — in `_paged_search`, remember the previous page's first issue key; if a page repeats
   it, raise `BackendPaginationStallError`. The server is not honouring `startAt`, so paging can
   never advance. Fires on the SECOND call.
   DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE from `fetcher.py:335-345`: fetcher returns cleanly (no raise) when the
   repeated page is SHORT, reasoning a client that returns fewer items than asked and then repeats
   "has nothing further to give". That does NOT transfer to DC. This pager exists (bug 9263)
   precisely because a hardened DC caps EVERY page below the requested size via
   `jira.search.views.default.max` — so on DC a short page is the NORMAL case WITH more to give, and
   adopting fetcher's short-page branch would silently return 20 of 250: the exact 92%-loss defect
   this pager was built to refuse. `_paged_search` therefore raises on ANY repeated page, short or
   full. It cannot false-positive: a `startAt`-honouring server serves DIFFERENT issues per offset.
3. `_hierarchy.py` — add `except BackendPaginationStallError: raise` immediately ahead of
   `get_parent_map`'s broad `except Exception` (`_hierarchy.py:91`), mirroring `acli_graph.py:304-306`.
4. `fetcher.py` — add `except BackendPaginationStallError: raise` ahead of each of the three broad
   `except Exception` enrichment handlers (`fetcher.py:610`, `:652`, `:688`). This is the boundary
   that decides whether the whole pass fails loudly or writes a degraded snapshot, and a stall must
   fail loudly: consumer confirmed — `fetch_snapshot`'s caller is the reconciler pass, which has no
   `{}`-specific expectation for these enrichments (each is guarded by `hasattr` and merges only
   what it gets), so the propagated error aborts the pass.

   **Instrumentation, stated accurately — an earlier draft of this step was factually WRONG and
   `review-plan` blocked it.** That draft claimed the transport's own `_call_logged` WARNING is
   "already emitted" on this path. It is not: `_call_logged` logs solely inside its
   `except Exception`, and on a stall the wrapped `search_issues` SUCCEEDS — it returns the repeated
   page — so the guard raises AFTER `_call_logged` has already returned, outside its `try`. Verified
   on the merged tree: `_paged_search` contains zero `logger.` calls, and the `get_parent_map` and
   three `fetcher.py` re-raise sites are bare `raise` with no logging.

   So the ONLY signal on the stall path is the raised message — which is self-diagnosing by
   construction: it names the repeated issue key, the `startAt` offset that stopped advancing, and
   the JQL. That is a loud, detailed abort rather than a silent degraded snapshot, which is what
   this step exists to guarantee. A duplicate `logger.warning` before the raise would restate those
   same three facts, so it is recorded as an optional follow-up rather than folded in here.
5. `transport.py` — re-export `BackendPaginationStallError` through the existing `__all__` facade
   (2 lines; no other change to that file, which 465d owns).
6. Tests — the RED oracle (see Verification).

NOT IN SCOPE, ticket to be filed and linked `discovered_from`: Cloud's own `acli_graph.RunawayPaginationError` is swallowed by these SAME three fetcher handlers, so bug cabc's fix (commit 30c522cde9) is itself incomplete at the fetcher boundary. Making Cloud stalls propagate is a behaviour change on the Cloud surface owned by another stream, so it is filed rather than folded in here.

## Verification

RED→GREEN with the oracle held out from the implementing subagent, plus a defect-seeded mutation check (re-remove the guard -> the test must return RED). Oracle lives in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py` and covers: a `startAt`-ignoring stub proving loud self-termination within 2 calls; the error escaping `get_parent_map`'s fail-open; the error escaping all three `fetch_snapshot` enrichment handlers; the facade import; and the unchanged 250/250 recovery for well-behaved page-capping servers through all three whole-project readers. Then `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the DC + fetcher + acli_graph pagination suites.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `_paged_search` raises a dedicated runaway/stall error when `startAt` does not advance
- [x] Fail-open exception handling does not swallow the stall error at ANY of the four sites: the
      transport's own `get_parent_map`, and all three `fetcher.fetch_snapshot` enrichment handlers
- [x] Held-out test with a `startAt`-ignoring stub proves termination within 2 calls
- [x] The stall error is re-exported and importable through the `transport.py` facade
- [x] Existing DC pagination behaviour for well-behaved servers unchanged (250/250 still recovered
      from a page-capping client through all three whole-project readers), and the pre-existing
      `get_parent_map` fail-open contract still returns `{}` for ORDINARY failures
baseline.summary: DC _paged_search lacks offset-stall guard (runaway pagination sibling)

# Outbound CREATE against DC produces no binding: `get_jira_key` returns None after the pass

## Provenance

Surfaced live by harness run **30834117797** (job 91755000385, main @ `25ead49f3e`) by story 5200's NEW row-1-outbound cell (`test_outbound_create_stamps_both_provenance_markers`, landed in change 1283). Its author flagged the create-and-bind SETUP as the likeliest first failure precisely because no prior live cell exercises an outbound CREATE against DC — every other outbound cell mutates an issue that already exists and is already bound. The prediction was correct.

## Evidence — verbatim from the run

> the outbound pass did not create-and-bind '654e-8c11-d632-4a01' (get_jira_key returned None), so
> there is no DC issue to read the provenance markers off. Row 1's markers are written INSIDE the
> create (`dispatch_one.py:306-307`), so a missing binding is upstream of this oracle, not a marker
> finding.

The cell localises the failure itself: this is **not** a provenance-marker defect. The pass did not produce a bound DC issue for the local ticket at all, so the oracle never got as far as reading markers.

## Why this is filed rather than folded into 5200

5200's remaining work was "run the harness and read the verdicts"; this is a product finding the run produced, and burying an unexplained outbound-create failure in a story's comment thread is how a defect of this class survives. It is also the SIXTH instance of the epic's recurring shape — "Cloud has the translation, DC never got its half", every instance a SILENT success where the pass reports OK.

## What is NOT yet established, stated plainly

Whether the create was never PLANNED (the differ emitted nothing for an unbound local ticket), was planned but not DISPATCHED, or was dispatched and the binding write failed. Those are three different defects. The harness output does not separate them, and `dispatch_one.py:571-578`-style warn-and-continue swallowing means a dispatch failure would look identical to a planning gap from the outside.

Note also that this cell is the ONLY live coverage of an outbound create against DC, so there is no prior green run to bisect against — the path may never have worked.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] the failing STAGE is identified — planned / dispatched / bound — with the evidence that
      distinguishes it from the other two
- [x] the root cause is proven, not inferred, and recorded here
- [x] the fix makes `test_outbound_create_stamps_both_provenance_markers` GREEN on a live harness
      run, with the run id recorded
- [x] an outbound create that fails to bind surfaces an operator-visible signal rather than a pass
      that reports OK (consistent with [rebar:39c1-2a32-b564-4b4b] AC4)
baseline.summary: Outbound CREATE against DC produces no binding: get_jira_key returns None after the pass

## Context / Problem

`_REBAR_OVERRIDES` (src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py:282) family-forces `native_structured_output: False` for Claude — a blanket signed-contract posture. E1 (recorded on the selection bug ticket df3a, "EXPERIMENT RESULTS" comment: 39 live Bedrock calls, account 896586841071 / us-east-1) measured native structured output working under extended thinking on specific Bedrock cells. The established mechanism for per-cell measured facts already exists: `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` (capabilities.py:317), an exact-id table that wins over the family default. Enable exactly the measured cells; every other cell stays fail-closed.

Bedrock capability facts are account/region-scoped — this same epic saw a Bedrock fact falsified on re-measurement in the project account — so each enabling row records the E1 account/region it was measured in and a re-measure trigger, and the enablement is scoped to the exact measured ids only.

## Approach

Add `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` rows setting `native_structured_output: True` and `native_output_with_thinking: True` for the cells E1 measured PASS: `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` (adaptive thinking) and `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0` (the dated profile id — the bare haiku alias 400s at request validation; measured E1).

**Plumb `native_output_with_thinking` through EVERY `ModelCapabilities(...)` construction site that feeds `output_mode` (currently inert — this is the load-bearing part of this story, not just the rows).** `output_mode` (src/rebar/llm/structured.py:46) already reads `caps.native_output_with_thinking`, and the field exists on `ModelCapabilities` (introduced by the guard story 0fa4, fail-closed default False), BUT a `ModelCapabilities(` sweep shows THREE live construction sites, and ALL THREE omit the field so it defaults False:

1. `_capabilities_from_profile` (capabilities.py ~:341) — omits it from both its `caps` seed
   dict and its constructor call.
2. The string-fallback path (capabilities.py ~:474-486) — omits it from its `merged` seed dict
   and its constructor call.
3. `_intersect_capabilities` (src/rebar/llm/runner.py:696) — the CONSERVATIVE record for a
   `FallbackModel` chain, fed DIRECTLY into `output_mode`; it intersects every other field with
   `all(...)` across candidates but has no `native_output_with_thinking` line, so a chain of the
   measured cells collapses the field to False and routes PromptedOutput under thinking.

(A `ModelCapabilities(` sweep also finds a fourth occurrence — the module constant `_CONSERVATIVE` at capabilities.py:429 — but that is the intended fail-closed record and must STAY `native_output_with_thinking=False`; the string-fallback seed reads it, so it is set explicitly to False there for clarity, not plumbed from an override.)

So an override that sets `native_output_with_thinking: True` is silently DROPPED on all three override-carrying paths. This story fixes all three: seed the field in the two capabilities.py dicts (profile path: default False; fallback path: from `_CONSERVATIVE.native_output_with_thinking`) and pass `native_output_with_thinking=bool(...)` in both those constructor calls; and add `native_output_with_thinking=all(c.native_output_with_thinking for c in per_candidate)` to `_intersect_capabilities` (the conservative `all` intersection, identical to every sibling field there — a chain claims native-under-thinking only when EVERY candidate is measured to support it). This plumbing is exactly what 0fa4 deferred by leaving the default fail-closed "until the rows story records measured PASS cells" — it is inseparable from the rows and belongs to this story.

Each row's comment cites its measuring run: E1 (df3a "EXPERIMENT RESULTS" — outputConfig json_schema + thinking proven wire-legal, no 400: sonnet-4-6 adaptive, haiku-4-5 budget 2048; account 896586841071 / us-east-1). Client-side Pydantic validators remain mandatory on the native path — Bedrock's schema transform strips `ge`/`le` bounds (measured E1: emitted 1.0 out-of-bounds).

Explicit non-rows, recorded in the table comment: Bedrock opus-4-7/4-8 are rejected server-side by Converse structured output under thinking (provider rollout gap; re-measure trigger: rerun the harness cell when AWS announces support). NOTE these two ids ALREADY carry a `supports_temperature: False` row (ticket 2932/1903) — this story adds NO native-structured-output / native-under-thinking row for them, so they remain fail-closed to PromptedOutput; they are "non-rows" only with respect to the native-output capability. Direct-Anthropic and OpenAI cells gain rows only from a harness matrix run measured PASS (operator-attested artifact); cells without credentials at run time are recorded "unmeasured" and stay prompted.

## Scope

- src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py — the measured-cell rows, the `native_output_with_thinking`
  plumbing through the two `ModelCapabilities(...)` construction sites here (profile +
  string-fallback), and the non-row comment
- src/rebar/llm/runner.py — the third construction site: `native_output_with_thinking` added to
  `_intersect_capabilities`'s `all(...)` intersection (FallbackModel chains)
- tests/unit/ (capabilities test file) — config-effect contrast tests, including a pin that the
  override actually reaches the constructed record

## Testing

Unit tier, config-effect contrast through the real capability read path (resolve model id -> capabilities -> `output_mode`):

- `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` with thinking=True -> NativeOutput.
- The dated haiku id (`us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`) with thinking=True ->
  NativeOutput.
- Plumbing pin (regression pin for the review BLOCK): the constructed `ModelCapabilities` for a
  measured cell has `native_output_with_thinking is True` — a mutation dropping the field from
  ANY of the three constructor calls turns this RED (proves the override is not inert).
- FallbackModel-chain pin: a `_intersect_capabilities` over candidates that ALL support
  native-under-thinking yields `native_output_with_thinking True` (and a chain mixing a
  measured cell with a non-measured one yields False — the conservative `all`) -> output_mode
  routes NativeOutput / PromptedOutput accordingly. A mutation dropping the field from
  `_intersect_capabilities` turns the all-supporting case RED.
- String-fallback coverage: `"bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"` passed as a STRING (not
  an object) also resolves to native_output_with_thinking True -> NativeOutput under thinking,
  so both construction paths are covered.
- `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` (carries only the `supports_temperature: False` row, no
  native/thinking row) with thinking=True -> PromptedOutput (fail-closed negative control).
- An arbitrary unknown Claude id -> PromptedOutput (family default preserved).

All deterministic — no live boundary in this story (the live measurement is the harness story's operator-attested artifact, already recorded; this story only encodes its result).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Both measured Bedrock cells return NativeOutput under thinking through the real read path,
      on BOTH the object and string-fallback construction paths — checked by the new contrast
      unit tests.
- [x] Opus (temperature-row-only) and unknown-id Claude cells stay PromptedOutput under
      thinking — checked by the same tests.
- [x] `native_output_with_thinking: True` set in an override row reaches the constructed
      `ModelCapabilities` (the plumbing is not inert) — checked by a dedicated pin that goes RED
      if ANY of the three construction sites (profile, string-fallback, `_intersect_capabilities`)
      omits the field.
- [x] A `FallbackModel` chain whose candidates ALL support native-under-thinking preserves
      `native_output_with_thinking True` (and a mixed chain collapses to False) — checked by the
      `_intersect_capabilities` contrast test.
- [x] Every enabling row's comment cites its measurement evidence (E1 account/region + the
      wire-legal finding) and the non-row comment records the opus/4-7 re-measure trigger —
      checked in code review.
- [x] [operator-attested] Any non-Bedrock row added under this ticket links its harness matrix
      artifact as a comment here; if none ran (this story adds only the two measured Bedrock
      rows), the non-Bedrock cells are recorded "unmeasured" in the table comment instead.
baseline.summary: Enable native structured output for measured Bedrock model cells

# The `supports_temperature` override table is incomplete — the default model is unguarded

## Context / Problem

Story 2932 landed a MEASURED override so Bedrock models that reject `temperature` have it withdrawn rather than hard-failing (`src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py:95`, consumed at `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:399`). The table has exactly ONE entry:

```python
_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES = {
    "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7": {"supports_temperature": False},
}
```

A fresh measurement sweep shows the behaviour is **family-wide across the opus line and both profile prefixes**, so the single entry leaves rebar's own DEFAULT model unguarded.

## MEASURED — account 896586841071, us-east-1, boto3 `bedrock-runtime.converse`, maxTokens 8

| model id | temp unset | temp=0.0 | temp=0.5 | temp=1.0 | topP=0.9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` | OK | OK | OK | — | — |
| `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` | OK | OK | — | — | — |
| `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` | OK | **400** | **400** | OK | **400** |
| `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` | OK | **400** | — | — | — |
| `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` | OK | **400** | — | — | — |
| `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` | — | **400** | — | — | — |
| `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5` | ValidationException: invalid model identifier | | | | |
| `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5` | ValidationException: invalid model identifier | | | | |

Error text: `ValidationException: \`temperature\` is deprecated for this model.` (and `\`top_p\` is deprecated for this model.`)

## What the data actually says (three corrections to the current model)

1. **`us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` is affected, and it is rebar's `DEFAULT_MODEL`** (`config.py:39` = `claude-opus-4-8`). The table does not list it, so the guard does not fire. This is the single most likely Bedrock Pass-1 model — especially under the operator requirement that Pass-1 run opus (see eb6e) — and it would hard-fail the moment any temperature is configured.
2. **The `global.` prefix is affected too.** The table keys on the full model id, so `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` and `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` are both unguarded even if the `us.` twins are listed. Any fix keyed literally per-id must cover both prefixes, or be matched on the family portion.
3. **It is NOT 'temperature unsupported' — it is 'explicit non-default sampling rejected'.** `temp=1.0` (the API default) SUCCEEDS on opus-4-8 while 0.0 and 0.5 fail. So the deprecation is of the parameter's *tunability*. `supports_temperature=False` still produces correct behaviour (withdraw the parameter → the model uses its default), but the field NAME misdescribes the mechanism, which matters for the next person extending it.

**`top_p` is deprecated on opus-4-8 as well, and there is no `supports_top_p` on the capability record.** This is currently LATENT, not live: rebar never sets `top_p` anywhere in `src/rebar`. But `failure.py:367` already lists `top_p`/`top_k` as sampling parameters rebar 'can send', so the gap becomes live the day anything sets one.

## Why this matters now

- The Pass-2 verifiers deliberately pin `temperature=0` (`code-review.yaml:155`). That is safe ONLY while Pass-2 stays on sonnet, which accepts it. It is the per-pass model split (eb6e) that keeps this from being an outage.
- The production cutover ships with **no fallback**, so an unguarded 400 here is a stuck gate, not a degraded one.
- `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5` and `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5` are NOT invokable in this account at all — worth noting because an earlier note in this epic recorded cache measurements for opus-4-5, and that model id does not resolve here now. Any conclusion resting on it should be re-measured rather than trusted.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` — extend the override table (or match on the family portion of the id so both `us.` and `global.` prefixes are covered by one entry).
- `tests/unit/` — a test per newly-covered id asserting the parameter is withdrawn.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a test asserts `capabilities_for("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8").supports_temperature`
      is False. NOTE the PROVIDER-QUALIFIED form: `_model_id_of` returns None for a bare id with no
      colon, so a bare-string assertion passes VACUOUSLY against the conservative record without ever
      exercising the override table. Production always passes `provider:model` or a model object.
- [ ] a test asserts the same for `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` and for both `opus-4-7` prefixes
- [ ] a test asserts `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` retains `supports_temperature is True` (the guard must not over-apply and silently drop determinism from the model that supports it)
- [ ] the table's comment records the measured matrix above, including that temp=1.0 succeeds, so the next reader does not re-derive it
baseline.summary: Bedrock temperature override table misses claude-opus-4-8 (the DEFAULT model) and the global.* variants

baseline.description:
## The defect

Bug 7e90-233b-3ee9-4f14 fixed the `Git version floor gate` step, which hard-failed every change branched before its data file landed. The same class of defect is still live in `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` on OTHER gate steps that run a repo script with no if-present guard.

The workflow's own "Definition-vs-tree skew guard (ticket ee2a)" note states the rule verbatim: a gate step that runs a repo script must skip (with a log line) when the script is absent from the checked-out tree. Gerrit's Verified lane takes the workflow DEFINITION from the target branch but checks out the CHANGE'S tree, so a step added on main runs against open changes whose base predates its script.

## Unguarded gate steps (swept from the parsed workflow YAML)

In `_build-and-test.yml`, which BOTH the Gerrit Verified lane and branch CI run:

| step | script | script first added |
|---|---|---|
| `comment-hygiene gate` | `scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py` | 2026-08-03 |
| `Config-read gate` | `scripts/check_config_reads.py` | 2026-08-02 |
| `Verified-gate parity gate` | `scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py` | 2026-07-19 |
| `Env-var registry drift gate` | `scripts/gen_env_registry.py` | 2026-07-08 |
| `Docs-index completeness gate` | `scripts/check_docs_index.py` | 2026-07-11 |
| `README quickstart golden-path gate` | `scripts/check_readme_quickstart.py` | 2026-07-11 |
| `CLI-reference drift gate` | `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` | 2026-07-11 |
| `MCP-reference drift gate` | `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` | 2026-07-11 |
| `server.json env-contract drift gate` | `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` | 2026-07-04 |

The two 2026-08-02/03 scripts are the LIVE exposure -- open changes branched before those dates exist today. The older ones are the same latent class and should be guarded for uniformity, so the next reader does not have to re-derive which are safe.

`gerrit-verify.yaml`'s `golden-path` job also checks out the Gerrit patchset and runs `scripts/check_readme_quickstart.py` and `scripts/probe_rebar.py` unguarded -- same class, same lane.

## Confirmed empirically

Running each unguarded step's command in a directory without the script exits 2 with `can't open file '.../scripts/<name>.py': [Errno 2] No such file or directory` -- a hard CI failure indistinguishable from a real gate violation, which is exactly what produced the false Verified -1 in 7e90.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every gate step in `_build-and-test.yml` that runs a repo script carries the ee2a
      if-present guard, skipping with a log line naming the tree-skew cause.
- [x] The `golden-path` job in `gerrit-verify.yaml` is guarded the same way.
- [x] A genuine gate violation still fails when the script IS present -- no gate is weakened.
- [x] A test (mirroring `tests/unit/test_git_floor_gate_tree_skew.py`) executes each guarded
      step against a tree lacking the script and asserts it exits 0 without an `::error::`.
- [x] Consider a structural guard: a check that FAILS when a step in the Verified lane runs a
      repo script without the if-present guard, so the convention stops depending on authors
      remembering the ee2a note.

## Provenance

Found by the Step 7 sibling sweep while fixing bug 7e90-233b-3ee9-4f14.
baseline.summary: Other CI gate steps still hard-fail on the definition-vs-tree skew

baseline.description:
## Context
Recent GitHub Actions runs have remained stuck until another session manually cleared them. Use the repository `rebar-debug` protocol to prove the recurring mechanism and repair every confirmed defect in scope. Do not mutate live GitHub run state during investigation.

## Plan
### Phase 1 — Understand
- Gather a descriptive dossier from authenticated Actions run/job metadata, timestamps, cancellation history, workflow definitions, repository settings, ticket/history evidence, and recent relevant changes.
- Treat this as a chronic incident unless evidence disproves recurrence; generate falsifiable competing hypotheses through the skill-required independent investigation step.
- Run read-only discriminating experiments and require runtime/API evidence of the mechanism before declaring a root cause. Establish defect legitimacy against repository workflow contracts or prior fixed behavior, then sweep callers/dependencies of the artifact proposed for change.

### Phase 2 — Repair (only after Phase 1 proves a defect)
- Read the skill test-design standard, inventory coverage, and create the smallest regression oracle that exercises the proven mechanism. Observe it RED for the expected reason before editing production workflow/code.
- Implement the mechanism-level fix while the RED oracle is held out from the fixer, then restore it and prove GREEN. Seed the exact defect as a mutation and confirm the oracle returns RED before restoring the fix.
- Run relevant workflow validation, lint/tests, and replicate the original stuck-run scenario through a local or read-only-safe equivalent. Sweep for confirmed siblings of the same pattern.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The affected run pattern is identified with URLs and timestamps, checked via `gh run list` and Actions API metadata.
- [ ] A parsimonious root cause is confirmed by discriminating evidence that explains why manual clearing unsticks the queue and rejects competing runner-capacity, concurrency, workflow, and platform hypotheses.
- [ ] Defect legitimacy and the bounded caller/dependency sweep are documented before any production edit.
- [ ] Each confirmed defect has a regression oracle observed RED before the fix, GREEN after it, and RED again under a defect-seeded mutation.
- [ ] Relevant `make lint`, targeted tests, Actions workflow validation, and a safe replication of the original scenario pass after the fix.
- [ ] Findings, experiments, decisions, and final verification are recorded in `rebar comment` updates on this ticket.

## Verification
Use read-only `gh run list`, `gh run view`, and `gh api` queries; inspect `.github/workflows/` and relevant history; then run the exact targeted tests introduced for the confirmed mechanism plus `make lint` and the repository workflow validators. No live run cancellation, rerun, dispatch, or repository-setting change is authorized.
baseline.summary: Diagnose stuck GitHub Actions runs

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Five recurrences of one defect class: rebar's prompted structured-output extraction is schema-blind — `tolerant_parse` (src/rebar/llm/structured.py:121) returns the FIRST parseable JSON object in a reply (fenced blocks first, `_FENCE_RE` at :40, then `_first_json_object` at :82), so any JSON-shaped material the model quotes (tool results, dependency-link records, examples) beats the real payload appearing later. Latest instance: bug child "Completion verifier returns a dependency-link record instead of a CompletionVerdict" blocked a legitimate close. Prior instance-fixes (git 9007f290, 5ed760a1, 1aa90fa5) keep being re-broken by routine model swaps (the Bedrock cutover changed the trigger rate). This epic retires the class, not the instance. All design decisions were derisked by live experiments E1–E4 recorded as comments on the bug child (design-investigation + experiment-results comments).

## Approach

Three coordinated thrusts, each child independently landable via Gerrit, fail-closed throughout:

1. **Harden the prompted path every model shares**: schema-filtered candidate selection with
   last-valid-wins in `parse_structured` (the bug child); an explicit sentinel output channel
   whose directive and extraction land atomically (sentinel child); an opt-in replayable
   raw-reply artifact on parse failure (artifact child).
2. **Provider-native structured output where MEASURED safe**: raise the Bedrock SDK floor
   (SDK child); replace `output_mode()`'s stale blanket thinking guard with measured
   call-property gating (guard child); add exact-id measured-fact capability rows only for
   cells a live measurement passed (rows child). Unmeasured cells stay prompted.
3. **Measure, don't assume**: a reusable provider-matrix raw-output baseline/eval harness
   running as a manual CI job where the API keys already live (harness child).

## Acceptance Criteria

Each criterion is delivered by exactly one child, with no overlapping responsibilities.

- [x] A reply that quotes schema-valid-looking JSON before the real payload parses to the
      correct contract object — delivered by the selection bug child; checked by its corpus +
      property tests passing under `make test`.
- [x] Prompted structured replies carry an explicit sentinel output channel whose extraction
      ships in the same change as the directive — sentinel child; checked by its unit pins and
      recorded before/after eval artifact.
- [x] A final structured-parse failure can leave an opt-in replayable raw-reply artifact,
      default off — artifact child; checked by its config-effect contrast tests.
- [x] The locked Bedrock SDK accepts Converse `outputConfig` client-side (botocore >= 1.43) —
      SDK child; checked by lock resolution and a recorded `uv tree` version proof.
- [x] `output_mode` gates native output on measured thinking-compatibility per model instead
      of blanket-forcing prompted — guard child; checked by its contrast unit tests.
- [x] Every model cell measured PASS runs native structured output and every unmeasured or
      failing cell stays prompted with a recorded reason — rows child; checked by
      config-effect tests through the real capability read path plus the recorded cell table.
- [x] Before/after raw-output distributions for the configured provider matrix exist as
      recorded, deterministically scored artifacts — harness child; checked by the
      workflow_dispatch run's uploaded artifacts referenced on that child.

## Risks

- Trailing-recap schema-valid decoy wins under last-valid-wins — accepted residual; a warning
  marks it; zero of the five historical recurrences show that layout (E3 evidence).
- The sentinel directive changes output distribution (measured: quote-in-prose 0% -> 100%) —
  mitigated by shipping directive+extraction atomically and measuring before/after (harness).
- Bedrock rejects `outputConfig` for opus-4-7/4-8 server-side — those cells stay on the
  hardened prompted path with a recorded re-measure trigger; no workaround exists client-side.
- The botocore floor collides with the `[eval]` -> aiobotocore cap — pyproject.toml's
  `[tool.uv]` conflicts block (~line 261) already forks eval vs bedrock resolution; the SDK
  child must keep those forks resolvable.
baseline.summary: Eliminate the schema-blind structured-output extraction defect class

baseline.description:
Exempt `idea` tickets from the `validate` health checks that punish undesigned, loose work, while keeping the structural checks active.

## Why

An `idea` ticket is captured-but-undesigned and often un-parented, terse, and (for the `idea` command) an empty epic. The health checks that assume a designed, structured ticket would flag every idea, dragging the store health score — the "noisy status" problem migrating into `validate`. The structural checks, by contrast, remain meaningful for a *structured* idea and must stay.

## What

- Exempt `idea` tickets **per-check** (add a `status == "idea"` skip inside each
  exempted check) — do NOT add `idea` to a blanket upstream filter such as
  `normalize_issues`, because that would also suppress the structural checks that
  must stay active. This per-check approach is the mechanism that lets exempt and
  retained checks diverge.
- Exempted checks (skip when status is `idea`): `check_orphaned_tasks` (WARNING
  severity — scored) including its creation-hour cluster finding;
  `check_missing_descriptions`; `check_interface_contracts`; `check_ticket_count`
  (parking-lot tickets are not active load); and `check_empty_epics` (note: it
  emits only `verbose`-severity findings that are never scored, but exempt it too
  so idea-epics don't clutter verbose output).
- Keep these checks active for `idea` tickets: `check_child_parent_deps`,
  `check_cross_epic_child_deps`, `check_duplicate_titles`.
- `check_in_progress_without_notes` needs no change (already status-gated to
  `in_progress`, so it never fires on `idea`).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine_support/validate_checks.py` — add `idea` skips to the
  exempted checks; leave the structural checks untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `validate` emits no `check_empty_epics` finding for an `idea` epic
      (test-verified).
- [ ] `validate` emits no `check_missing_descriptions` finding for an `idea`
      ticket with an empty description.
- [ ] `validate` emits no `check_interface_contracts` finding for an `idea` ticket.
- [ ] `validate` emits no `check_orphaned_tasks` finding for an un-parented `idea`
      ticket.
- [ ] `validate` emits no creation-hour cluster finding for a burst of `idea`
      tickets.
- [ ] `validate` excludes `idea` tickets from the `check_ticket_count` total.
- [ ] `validate` still emits a `check_child_parent_deps` finding for an `idea`
      ticket when that condition holds (test-verified).
- [ ] `validate` still emits a `check_cross_epic_child_deps` finding for an `idea`
      ticket when that condition holds (test-verified).
- [ ] `validate` still emits a `check_duplicate_titles` finding involving an
      `idea` ticket when titles collide (test-verified).
- [ ] `make lint` passes for the changed files.
baseline.summary: Exempt 'idea' tickets from noisy validate health checks

## Why
S2 (68ef) folds `claimed_session` into compiled state, but a folded state key is only useful if it is DISCOVERABLE on the read surface and DURABLE across compaction. This story makes `claimed_session` a first-class, documented read field and proves it survives snapshot/compaction round-trips (incl. the pre-feature snapshot case).

## What
- **MCP outputSchema (`src/rebar/_mcp_models.py`).** Add `claimed_session: str | None = None`
  to `TicketStateOut` so `show_ticket`'s advertised outputSchema enumerates it (the
  compiled-state schema `ticket_state.schema.json` and the generated `types.py` already carry
  it from S2).
- **LLM read format (`src/rebar/reducer/llm_format.py` + `ticket_state_llm.schema.json`).**
  Add `"claimed_session": "csn"` to `KEY_MAP` (and the co-located `Key mapping:` docstring
  table) so `to_llm` renders the value under the compact key `csn` when set (a `None` value is
  omitted, per the existing convention). Enumerate the new alias in the authoritative LLM
  output schema `src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state_llm.schema.json` — its `description` key-map
  list AND its `properties` block — and regenerate `src/rebar/types.py`.
- **Compaction safety (`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py`).** NO active `process_snapshot`
  guard is needed (unlike `managed_refs` which is seeded, or `attestations` which is folded):
  a POST-feature snapshot carries `claimed_session` in `compiled_state` and the generic
  restore loop restores it verbatim; a PRE-feature snapshot simply lacks the key, leaving the
  `make_initial_state` seed (`None`) intact. This story adds a compaction round-trip
  regression test pinning BOTH directions (add only a short clarifying comment at the restore
  loop — no code guard).
- **`show` JSON.** `rebar show` returns the compiled-state dict, which ALREADY includes
  `claimed_session` (it is a state key) — no separate JSON-rendering change is needed; a test
  asserts its presence for a claimed ticket.
- **Docs (`docs/event-schema.md`).** Document `claimed_session`: the STATUS
  `data["session"]` → `state["claimed_session"]` storage, the ordered resolver precedence
  (cross-ref S1 / `docs/config.md`), the fork-winner gating, and the compaction / forward-compat
  behavior (older clones ignore the additive key; pre-feature snapshots default to `None`).

## Scope
- IN: the MCP model field, the `to_llm` `KEY_MAP` entry + docstring + `ticket_state_llm.schema.json`
  (`csn`) + `types.py` regen, a compaction round-trip regression test (both directions, no code
  guard), a `show`-JSON presence test, and the `docs/event-schema.md` section.
- OUT: the `list --session=<id>` filter — DEFERRED to a follow-up ticket (it expands the
  CLI + MCP + `apply_ticket_filters` + `match_predicate` arg surface for optional value, out
  of proportion to this story). Also OUT: multi-harness fields (S5 / c557), capture hooks
  (S4 / S6). The record/fold path is S2 (68ef).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `show <id>` JSON includes `claimed_session` for a claimed ticket. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_claimed_session_read.py -k show_json -q`.
- [ ] MCP `show_ticket` advertises `claimed_session` in its outputSchema. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_claimed_session_read.py -k outputschema -q` asserts
      `"claimed_session" in TicketStateOut.model_json_schema()["properties"]`.
- [ ] `to_llm` renders the session under `csn` when set and omits it when `None`. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_claimed_session_read.py -k to_llm -q`.
- [ ] `csn` is enumerated in `ticket_state_llm.schema.json` (properties + description key-map).
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/test_claimed_session_read.py -k llm_schema -q`.
- [ ] Compaction round-trip preserves `claimed_session` (post-feature snapshot), AND a
      pre-feature snapshot whose `compiled_state` lacks the key restores to `None` (from the
      `make_initial_state` seed) without error. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_claimed_session_read.py -k compaction -q` covers both directions.
- [ ] `docs/event-schema.md` documents `claimed_session` in a DEDICATED section (storage
      `data["session"]` -> `claimed_session`, precedence cross-ref, compaction/forward-compat).
      Proof: a doc-content test that anchors on the section header
      "## Session provenance (`claimed_session`)" and asserts `claimed_session`, `data["session"]`,
      and "compaction" appear WITHIN that section (not merely somewhere in the file).

## Depends on
- S2 (68ef) — the record/fold path; landed in this stack.
baseline.summary: Expose claimed_session on the read surface + compaction-safety guarantee

baseline.description:
# Completion verifier — coach callers to document completion evidence as ticket comments on any FAIL

## Why

When the completion verifier returns FAIL, the only remediation surfaced to the caller is "address the criteria." There is no signposting of the legitimate, low-friction channel for a criterion that is *already satisfied but not discoverable from the code*: recording the supporting evidence as a comment on the ticket. The completion verifier reads a ticket's comments (via its read-only `show_ticket` tool) and the deterministic child-closure gate reads ticket state directly, so documented evidence is genuinely taken into account on the next run — but nothing tells the caller that. The result is callers reaching for the wrong escape hatch instead of the intended evidence channel.

## What

Attach a single, generic remediation-guidance string to **every** FAIL completion verdict, at the one chokepoint both failure paths already pass through (`reconcile_verdict`), and surface it wherever a FAIL verdict is shown to a caller (the close gate and the `verify-completion` text render). The guidance must:

- be generic and broadly applicable (not tied to any one incident);
- coach the caller to record evidence that meets completion requirements as
  ticket **comments** (concrete artifacts: file paths + line ranges, commands and
  their output, links, reasoning connecting the work to the criterion);
- state that the verifier reads the ticket's comments so documented evidence is
  incorporated on the next verification;
- keep the "finish genuinely incomplete work, then re-verify" route;
- NOT mention forcing a ticket closed (steer to the evidence channel only).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` — add a module-level `COMPLETION_REMEDIATION_GUIDANCE`
  constant (exported) and have `reconcile_verdict` set `result["remediation"]` on
  any FAIL verdict. Covers both the agentic FAIL and the deterministic
  child-closure FAIL (`deterministic_child_failure`), which already call
  `reconcile_verdict`.
- `src/rebar/schemas/completion_verdict.schema.json` — document the optional
  `remediation` string field (schema is `additionalProperties: true`, so this is
  contract documentation, not a breaking change).
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — append the verdict's remediation
  guidance to the blocked-close error, leading with the comments-evidence channel.
- `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py` — render the remediation guidance in
  `_render_verdict_text` on a FAIL verdict.
- Tests — assert a FAIL verdict carries `remediation`, that it names the ticket
  comments channel, and that it does not mention forcing closure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `reconcile_verdict` sets a non-empty `remediation` string on every FAIL
      verdict and leaves PASS verdicts without one (no `remediation` on PASS).
- [ ] The guidance text names the ticket **comments** channel and instructs the
      caller to document evidence (paths/commands/results/reasoning) that meets the
      completion requirements; it is generic (no incident-specific wording).
- [ ] The guidance text does not reference forcing a ticket closed.
- [ ] A blocked close (`transition <id> in_progress closed` with a FAIL verdict)
      surfaces the guidance to the caller.
- [ ] `rebar verify-completion <id>` text output shows the guidance on a FAIL
      verdict.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass locally; the change lands on
      `main` through Gerrit with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.
baseline.summary: Completion verifier: coach callers to document completion evidence as ticket comments on any FAIL

## Reproduction Steps
1. Run `pytest tests/unit/test_config_perf.py::test_warm_resolution_is_cheap` on a loaded CI runner (GitHub Actions, py3.11/3.12/3.13).
2. Observe intermittent failure: `assert elapsed < 0.5` trips at ~0.50–0.51s.

Expected: the smoke budget catches a GROSS regression (cache broken → per-resolve filesystem walk, which for 1000×40-deep resolves would take many seconds). Actual: the 0.5s ceiling is only ~1x the warm-cache time under CI load, so it flakes on load variance (observed 0.501/0.505/0.510s across three py versions) even though the cache is working ("typically <10ms" per the test's own comment). Blocked auto-lander-retirement change #666 twice; #665 passed only by luck.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Relax the ceiling to a genuinely generous value (e.g. 5.0s) that still catches a broken-cache regression (orders of magnitude slower) but tolerates CI load variance; keep the test's smoke-regression intent.
- [ ] make test green; the test no longer flakes under load.

baseline.description: Steering an auto-resumed completion verification away from already-searched places (negative frontier, advisory not hard-exclusion to avoid permanent blind spots) and toward where credited evidence was found (positive frontier) requires per-call argument-level transcript telemetry (paths read, search queries run) that the verifier workflow does not currently capture. Two-part capability: (1) transcript capture in the LLM runner telemetry; (2) deterministic frontier-digest extractor + resumption prompt injection, scoped within a single close invocation (same pinned ref), never persisted cross-run. Parent: adolescent-evilminded-locust implements unsteered auto-resume (proven sufficient live via 8d74 re-close 2026-08-14); this idea upgrades it if unsteered resumption proves insufficient at scale.
baseline.summary: Search-frontier handoff for completion-verifier resumptions (needs argument-level tool-call transcript)

baseline.description:
## Why

Enabling `identity.require_authenticated` must break nothing on the Gerrit side. Not every Gerrit-side service writes **in-scope** ticket events, so this story **classifies** them (with file/line evidence) rather than blanket-signing everything, and confirms the one in-scope writer actually signs on the deployed VM (finishing canary 1787, which was force-closed "pending post-deploy run").

## What — enumerate and classify every Gerrit-side store operation

Classification (verified against the code):

- **opcert-service → NON-WRITING.** `src/rebar/opcert_service/jobs.py:11-12` ("The server never
  pushes… runs with `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off`"), enforced at `jobs.py:196-208` (`_sync_push_off`),
  workspace discarded `jobs.py:97-99`; `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:168-169`
  ("STORE-READ-ONLY" / `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: "off"`). Never places an event on the shared store.
- **review-bot `code_review` artifact → GATE-EXEMPT.** `src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py:241-251`
  (`create_ticket("code_review", …)`) + `llm/code_review/sidecar.py:26,143`
  (`REVIEW_RESULT`); `code_review ∈ _GATE_EXEMPT_TYPES` at
  `src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:125`.
- **review-bot reciprocal `relates_to` LINK on the trailer-cited work ticket → IN-SCOPE
  WRITER.** `voter.py:278` `rebar.link(artifact_id, resolved, "relates_to")` where `resolved`
  is a real work ticket; `graph/_links.py:264-267` writes a reciprocal LINK event into the
  work-ticket dir → `_seam.append_event(work_ticket, "LINK", …)`; pushed
  (`docker-compose.yml:93` `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: "always"`). The work ticket is non-exempt, so the
  gate collects this LINK event. Its on-box backfill reconciler (`review_bot/reconcile.py:223`,
  launched `app.py:101`) drives the same voter. (This LINK-write path **refines** the earlier
  "review-bot writes only the exempt `code_review` type" assessment — the reciprocal
  `relates_to` back-link onto the non-exempt work ticket was not accounted for there; the code
  evidence above is authoritative, and is why this story confirms the bot signs rather than
  treating it as fully exempt.)
- **auto-lander → RETIRED** (ADR-0047; `infra/gerrit/project.config:53`), not deployed.
- (For contrast: the Jira→rebar reconciler is a GitHub-side writer — `reconcile-bridge.yml`,
  `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` — covered by story 4dc0, NOT Gerrit-side.)

**Already provisioned to sign:** `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh:98-124` materializes SSM `/rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key` to a `0600` file and exports `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY`; the write seam (`_seam.py:294-315`) signs when a resolvable `author_id` (594c, via the bot git email) + a `signing_key` are present. So the review-bot is equipped to sign its LINK writes as identity `594c`.

## Confirming canary 1787 (the in-scope path signs on the deployed VM)

The in-scope writer is exercised naturally by pushing a change through Gerrit: the deployed review-bot reviews the change and emits a reciprocal `relates_to` LINK onto the change's `rebar-ticket:` work ticket, authored by `594c`. Confirm that LINK event is **signed + verified** — that is the deployed-VM proof. (Fallback: inspect the running review-bot container on the VM via AWS SSM to confirm the key is materialized and `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY` is set.)

## Scope

Gerrit-side operations only: classification + verification. Provisioning only if an in-scope writer is found **unsigned** (it is already provisioned). No enforcement flip here (8d39). No tracked repo-file change (empty `file_impact` is correct); the classification + canary evidence are recorded as comments on this ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Every Gerrit-side store operation is enumerated and classified** non-writing /
      gate-exempt / in-scope-writer, with file/line evidence, recorded on this ticket (the
      table above).
- [ ] **The in-scope Gerrit-side writer produces a signed, verified event.** Capture the
      tickets-branch HEAD before driving the review-bot: `C=$(git -C .tickets-tracker rev-parse HEAD)`.
      After a Gerrit change makes the deployed review-bot emit a reciprocal `relates_to` LINK on
      its `rebar-ticket:` work ticket, confirm **both**: (a) a new LINK event authored by `594c`
      was introduced on that work ticket after `C` — evidenced by the work ticket's
      `rebar show <t> | jq '.authorship.signed'` increasing, recorded as the work-ticket id +
      tickets commit (proves non-vacuous); and (b)
      `rebar verify-identity --all --require-authenticated --since "$C"` exits 0 (every event
      introduced since `C`, including the LINK, verifies — had the bot LINK been unsigned it
      would exit non-zero). Record `C`, the change URL, and the work-ticket id on this ticket.
- [ ] **Confirmed unaffected by enforcement:** the opcert-service (`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off`, never
      pushes) and the review-bot `code_review` artifacts (gate-exempt) are not rejected when
      `require_authenticated=true` — established by the classification evidence above.
- [ ] [operator-attested] Canary 1787 is completed for the in-scope path: the deployed
      review-bot's reciprocal `relates_to` LINK produces an actual **signed, verified** event.
      A materialized key is **not** sufficient — it does not prove the bot signs, and could mask
      a signing malfunction. Required evidence recorded on this ticket: the boundary `C` and
      work-ticket id from AC2, the `rebar verify-identity --all --require-authenticated --since "$C"`
      exit-0 result (confirming the LINK verifies), and a timestamp. Obtain it by driving the
      deployed review-bot with a real Gerrit change — this
      epic's 8d91/8d39 changes naturally produce a review-bot LINK on their work ticket; if none
      is in flight, push a synthetic change. A container/SSM inspection
      (`aws ssm start-session … docker exec … env | grep REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY`) may be
      recorded as *supplementary* diagnostic context only, never as a substitute for the signed
      event.
baseline.summary: Confirm Gerrit-side services sign ticket writes on the deployed VM (finish canary 1787)

## What

Move the strict eval-spec discipline check — currently an inline Python step in the `Prompt Eval` GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml`) — into a unit test that runs in the default pytest suite, and remove the now-redundant inline step.

The check: for every packaged `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/*.eval.yaml`, `validate_eval_spec(spec)` must be clean, and every dataset-bearing spec must additionally pass `validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True)` (registered scorers + balanced dataset + non-empty gold_set).

## Why (necessity)

The `Verified` Gerrit vote is assembled by `gerrit-verify.yaml`, whose `vote` job aggregates `build-and-test`, `optionality`, `golden-path`, and `verify-identity`. It does NOT reference `prompt-eval.yml`, so the strict validation does not gate `Verified` and does not block a Gerrit submit. Concrete evidence: three advisory plan-review specs (asserted-capability, decomp-shape, necessity) each shipped a `dataset` with no `gold_set` and MERGED green (Verified +1) while the standalone Prompt Eval workflow was red — the defect only reddened a non-gating workflow after the fact (fixed in bug d37b). The strict glob-validation lives ONLY in the inline CI script; no unit test covers it (the existing `test_new_eval_specs.py` enumerates a hardcoded 3-spec tuple, so new specs are never checked). The default suite (`pytest -m "not integration and not external"`) runs in both `_build-and-test.yml` callers, so a test there blocks `Verified` pre-merge.

## Scope

- Add a glob-based test to `tests/unit/test_eval_scorers.py` (which already globs all packaged
  specs and runs in the default suite) mirroring the inline CI logic exactly.
- Remove the redundant "Validate every packaged eval spec" inline step from `prompt-eval.yml`
  (the offline job still runs `test_eval_scorers.py`); update the header comment for accuracy.
- No production/library code changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A unit test in `tests/unit/test_eval_scorers.py` globs every packaged eval spec and asserts
      `validate_eval_spec(spec)` is clean, plus `validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True)` clean for
      every dataset-bearing spec; it is collected by the default (non-integration, non-external) suite.
- [ ] The redundant inline validation step is removed from `.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml`.
- [ ] The new test fails if any dataset-bearing packaged spec lacks a gold_set (verified by a
      local red→green check), and passes on current `main`.
- [ ] `make lint` and the eval test suite pass; the `Prompt Eval` and `Verified` gates are green.
baseline.summary: Gate eval-spec strict validation via a unit test (not only the standalone Prompt Eval workflow)

# DC sub-task reparent via `PUT fields.parent` is accepted and IGNORED — the parent never moves

## Provenance

Surfaced live by harness run **30834117797** (job 91755000385, main @ `25ead49f3e`), by TWO independent cells in opposite directions. Not predicted by any ticket; found only because story 5200's repaired cells read the field back instead of trusting the call's return.

## Evidence — two cells, and only one reading survives both

**Outbound (`test_outbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips`)** — verbatim:

> the outbound parent set: fields.parent on RBJUUVX-3 is STILL 'RBJUUVX-1' — the parent it had
> BEFORE the mutation. Expected 'RBJUUVX-2'. This is the silent-no-op signature: `set_parent`
> writes `fields.parent` for a sub-task (`jira_datacenter/transport.py:711-712`) and every core
> caller swallows its failure (`dispatch_one.py:571-578` warns and continues), so an unchanged
> field is the ONLY place the failure is observable.

**Inbound (`test_inbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips`)** — timed out after 90s / 45 attempts waiting for `get_parent_map` to show the reparent; last parent seen was the ORIGINAL.

The inbound cell self-diagnoses as search-index lag ("NOT a bridge defect"). **That reading cannot account for the outbound cell**, which read `fields.parent` back DIRECTLY over raw REST — no search index involved — and still saw the pre-mutation value. A lagging index cannot make a direct field read return stale data. The reading that explains BOTH is that the write itself never took effect.

## Why this matters more than one red cell

`transport.py:688-689` already carries a note that DC may **accept a `PUT {'parent': None}` and ignore it**. This is the same accept-and-ignore shape on the SET path. If it holds, then the sub-task branch of `set_parent` — the branch that exists precisely because it is supposed to be the shape DC accepts — does not work on DC 8.17.1 at all.

That directly undercuts the premise of [rebar:39c1-2a32-b564-4b4b], whose mechanism analysis reads "the one child shape DC accepts (sub-task)". If the sub-task write is also a no-op, then 39c1's AC1 ("the emit gate and DC's accepted child shape overlap for at least one real configuration") cannot be satisfied by the sub-task path, and the Epic Link path added in change 1302 becomes the ONLY candidate rather than a second one.

## What is NOT yet established

Whether DC returns a success status for the ignored write, or an error that `dispatch_one.py:571-578` swallows. The two have different fixes and the harness output does not distinguish them — the swallow is exactly why. 39c1's AC4 alerting change (bridge_alerts entry on every `set_parent` failure arm) will make the difference visible on the next run: an alert present means DC errored and we hid it; no alert means DC returned success and lied.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] the live behaviour is established: does DC 8.17.1 return success, or an error, for a
      sub-task `PUT fields.parent` that does not take effect? Recorded with the run id and the
      raw response.
- [x] N/A — DC does not error; it accepts-and-ignores. Condition never held. ~~if DC errors: the error is surfaced (39c1 AC4) and the caller stops reporting the mutation
      as applied~~
- [x] if DC accepts-and-ignores: `set_parent` verifies the write by reading the field back, or the
      sub-task branch is declined the way the epic branch was, rather than silently claiming success
- [x] a live cell proves the chosen path against the real instance — a unit suite CANNOT settle
      this (changes 1276 and 1288 were both mutation-proven and both wrong in production)
baseline.summary: DC sub-task reparent via PUT fields.parent is accepted and ignored: the parent never moves
