# S7b — Run the LOCAL developer gates on Bedrock (dogfood before the production cutover)

## Context / Problem

S8 (eb6e) cuts the PRODUCTION review bot over to Bedrock with NO fallback — it is the gate that votes on every landing on `main`. Today the first time rebar exercises Bedrock through a real gate will be that cutover, on the shared bot, where a failure stops everyone's landings until a human runs the kill switch.

Local developer gates (`rebar review-plan`, `rebar review-code`, `rebar verify-completion`) run the SAME LLM stack against the SAME provider seam, on a machine where a failure costs one person one command. Pointing them at Bedrock first converts the production cutover from a first contact into a confirmation.

## What is already established — do NOT re-measure

* BEDROCK IS INVOKABLE from this host: account 896586841071, us-east-1, caller
  `arn:aws:iam::896586841071:user/joe_frontier`. AWS CLI credentials are present and working.
* ONLY INFERENCE PROFILES WORK. Plain on-demand ids (`anthropic.claude-*`) are NOT invokable in this
  account at all — they return a ValidationException directing you to use an inference profile
  [rebar:2932-8a98-6d70-4550].
* PROMPT CACHING WORKS on a regional inference profile: `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` measured
  cache_write=4017 then cached on the next attempt; a longer end-to-end run recorded
  cache_read=542,723 / cache_write=6,239 over 19 calls. Caching and inference profiles are NOT
  mutually exclusive, and `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` is the recorded verified caching default.
* `temperature=0` is REFUSED on opus (`ValidationException: temperature is deprecated for this
  model`) and is already handled by the `supports_temperature: False` capability override — the
  withdrawal is MODEL-driven, not provider-driven, and happens identically on both providers.
* PAYLOAD AND TOOL PARITY ARE PROVEN [rebar:0d76-ebbf-ee3a-48ac]: for the same logical call the system
  prompt, messages and tool definitions are byte-identical across providers; the model id is the only
  differing field. Eight envelope differences are enumerated there, seven of them spelling.
* ONE ENVELOPE DIFFERENCE IS SUBSTANTIVE and is the thing most likely to bite here: Bedrock's
  `cachePoint` carries NO TTL where Anthropic's `cache_control` carries `ttl:"5m"`. Latent today
  because rebar sets no non-default TTL — but this story is the cheapest place to find out if that
  assumption is wrong.

## Approach

Configure the LOCAL rebar install to resolve its model classes to Bedrock inference profiles, using the AWS CLI credentials already on the host, and then RUN THE REAL GATES and compare against the Anthropic baseline. Prefer the layered config file (`REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` / the `model_classes` table) over the deprecated bare `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`, so the change is per-class and reversible rather than global.

The deliverable is not the config line — it is the EVIDENCE that a developer's day-to-day gates behave on Bedrock: verdicts still parse, structured output still validates, caching still engages, and the observable cost does not regress.

**Explicitly out of scope:** the production bot, its IAM, its alarms, and its kill switch. Those are S8's. This story must not touch `infra/`.

## Scope

- local LLM configuration only (the config file and/or documented env for a developer machine)
- `docs/local-dev-env.md` — how a developer opts in, and how to revert
- no `src/` behaviour change is expected; if one turns out to be required, that is a finding worth a
  separate ticket rather than silent scope growth

## Testing

Live, because a configuration that only works in a unit test proves nothing here. The oracle is a real local gate run against a real ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [operator-attested] `rebar review-plan` runs end-to-end against Bedrock on a real ticket and
      returns a parseable verdict, recorded with the ticket id, the resolved model ids per pass, and
      the run timestamp.
- [x] [operator-attested] the run's `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` per-call tally shows EVERY call resolved to a
      Bedrock inference profile and ZERO calls to direct Anthropic — the same provider-clean check S6
      applied to its measured arms.
- [x] [operator-attested] prompt caching is observed ENGAGING on the Bedrock path: a run records
      nonzero `cache_read_tokens`, cited from the usage log. A write alone is insufficient — write-only
      is the failure mode bug f81d exists for.
- [x] [operator-attested] `rebar review-code` and `rebar verify-completion` are each exercised once on
      Bedrock and their outcomes recorded. These are the other two gates a developer hits daily; a
      plan-review-only proof would leave them untested.
- [x] Structured output validates on every gate run — no verdict falls back to an unparsed or
      INDETERMINATE shape for a provider-shaped reason. Any that does is recorded with its raw payload.
- [x] Whether the missing Bedrock `cachePoint` TTL causes any observable difference is STATED, with
      evidence either way. "Not observed" is an acceptable answer; silence is not.
- [x] The opt-in and the REVERT are both documented in `docs/local-dev-env.md`, and the revert is
      executed once to prove a developer can get back to Anthropic in one step.
- [x] Nothing under `infra/` is modified — verified by the diff.
- [x] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
baseline.summary: S7b — Run the LOCAL developer gates on Bedrock (dogfood before the production cutover)

## Finding

The verification pipeline intentionally tolerates and repairs provider/model output variations, but a structurally divergent response can currently normalize to an empty result that is treated like a valid review outcome.

## Evidence

- `src/rebar/llm/verify_models.py:143-161` shows tolerant Pydantic parsing can ignore
  unexpected keys and produce an empty model.
- `src/rebar/llm/verify_models.py:26-32` registers the live verification model without
  enabling strict-only parsing.
- `docs/adr/0006-llm-stage-seam-contracts.md:14-35` records the historical risk of malformed
  output yielding misleadingly green reviews.
- `docs/adr/0006-llm-stage-seam-contracts.md:94-154` intentionally adopts tolerant
  expand-contract parsing, telemetry, and staged tightening.

## Definition — "semantically empty" (resolves E2/F1/T8)

A verifier chunk response is **semantically empty** at the finding-index level when, after chunking + reshape, a given finding index has **no verification entry** in the reshaped `verifications` list. Concretely, per `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py::verify_findings`, this happens through either of two paths, and both are already handled but classified into different telemetry buckets:

1. **Raw-empty**: `run_chunk(...)` succeeds but returns an empty list despite a non-empty
   `chunk_indices` — tallied as `outcome_counts["empty_outcomes"]`, and every index in that
   chunk is recorded in `violations["empty_outcomes"]`.
2. **Malformed-to-empty**: `run_chunk(...)` returns a non-empty raw list, but every item is
   dropped by `reshape_verifications` (malformed/duplicate/out-of-range index) — the chunk is
   currently tallied as `outcome_counts["recovered"]` (a violation was recorded and the raw
   output was non-empty), even though zero usable verifications survive for that chunk's
   indices.

**Decision-correctness is unaffected by which of the two buckets a chunk lands in.** `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py::pass3_decide` (~line 505-512) already treats **any** finding with no verification entry as `indeterminate` ("no verification → INDETERMINATE"), regardless of whether that absence came from the raw-empty or malformed-to-empty path. So AC3 ("semantically empty verification results can never produce a valid pass or valid empty review") is already enforced at the decision layer for both paths today — the two-bucket split is a **telemetry classification nuance only** (distinguishing "provider sent nothing" from "provider sent garbage"), not a gap in the pass/fail guard. A `StructuredOutputError` (contract failure surviving retry+repair) is the third, distinct path, tallied as `outcome_counts["unrecoverable"]` and also surfaces as `indeterminate` downstream via the same no-verification rule.

## Audit note — already satisfied by shipped code (resolves E4)

`src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py` (merged via this ticket's own change, commit `8417c4be4` on `main`) already implements: empty-outcome detection (`empty_outcome_indices`, `outcome_counts["empty_outcomes"]`), `StructuredOutputError` handling with loud `logger.error` (`outcome_counts["unrecoverable"]`), the single `reshape_verifications` seam for violation reporting, and all four `outcome_counts` buckets (`clean`/`recovered`/`empty_outcomes`/`unrecoverable`), unit-tested in `tests/unit/test_review_kernel.py` and `tests/unit/test_review_kernel_rules.py`. **ACs 1-5 are satisfied by this shipped kernel function and its tests.**

**AC6 ("Telemetry separately counts...") is satisfied at the kernel-function level only** — `verify_findings()` populates all four buckets and its tests assert this. It is **not yet** called by either live consumer pipeline: `plan_review_decide` and `code_review_decide` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py`, `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py`) each build Pass-2 instructions via the shared `verify_instructions()` prompt helper but then run the model call and `reshape_verifications(...)` inline themselves, without calling `verify_findings` — so neither pipeline's live telemetry stream currently emits `outcome_counts`. This wiring gap is real but is independent surgery on two production step-functions deserving its own review/test cycle; it is tracked as follow-up ticket `c2c5-53a7-2ce0-4d98` (`discovered_from` this ticket) rather than bundled into this ticket's closing scope. This ticket's remaining scope is the kernel function itself (already shipped) plus this clarifying text — no further code change is required to close this ticket.

## Remediation

Preserve flexible parsing, normalization, bounded retries, and provider-independent self-healing. A recovered, semantically non-empty response remains valid. A semantically empty response (either raw-empty or malformed-to-empty, per the definition above) is never a valid verification result; after recovery attempts it must become an explicit indeterminate or contract-failure outcome — already enforced today via `decide.pass3_decide`'s no-verification rule. Telemetry must distinguish clean parses, recovered parses, empty outcomes, and unrecoverable responses — shipped in `verify_findings()`'s `outcome_counts`; pipeline-level wiring is out of scope here (see follow-up ticket above).

Cascade flag: behavior applies across providers and model versions; avoid schema rigidity that converts recoverable format variation into review fragility.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Clean preferred-schema responses continue to validate normally. — shipped:
      `verify_findings`, `outcome_counts["clean"]`.
- [x] Recoverable non-empty responses from supported provider/model variations are normalized
      and accepted. — shipped: `outcome_counts["recovered"]`.
- [x] Semantically empty verification results can never produce a valid pass or valid empty
      review. — shipped: `decide.pass3_decide`'s no-verification → indeterminate rule covers
      both raw-empty and malformed-to-empty paths (see Definition above).
- [x] Empty-after-recovery and unrecoverable responses produce a distinct explicit
      indeterminate or contract-failure outcome. — shipped: `outcome_counts["empty_outcomes"]`
      / `["unrecoverable"]`, both routed to `indeterminate` by `decide.pass3_decide`.
- [x] Bounded retry/self-healing behavior remains provider-independent and deterministic at the
      orchestration boundary. — shipped: `verify_findings`'s chunk/retry loop.
- [x] Telemetry separately counts clean parses, recovered parses, semantically empty outcomes,
      and unrecoverable responses. — shipped at the kernel-function level
      (`verify_findings`'s `outcome_counts`); pipeline-level wiring into `plan_review_decide`
      and `code_review_decide` tracked as follow-up `c2c5-53a7-2ce0-4d98`.
- [x] Tests cover representative alternate wrappers/field shapes, successful recovery, empty
      normalization, retry exhaustion, and provider-version variation. — shipped in
      `tests/unit/test_review_kernel.py` / `tests/unit/test_review_kernel_rules.py`.
baseline.summary: Reject empty verifier outcomes while preserving resilient parsing

# Docs: private-repo credentials, descriptive errors, ref/source semantics, HMAC trust model

## Why

The snapshot model adds an operational requirement the old "read the local checkout" model
did not have — the server must be able to `fetch` from origin, which for private repos means
credentials. Operators and agents need clear guidance and clear failures.

## What

- Update the MCP-server setup docs to state the PRIVATE-REPO FETCH CREDENTIAL requirement:
  the server's clone needs a credential helper / deploy key / token to fetch arbitrary refs.
  Target docs (named so each AC is a deterministic, grep-able check): the MCP-server setup
  section of `README.md` and `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` (and any dedicated MCP setup doc).
- Document the descriptive credential-failure behavior (message + remedy) and that attested
  mode fails closed while local mode still runs.
- Document the `ref` + `source` semantics: attested (default, pinned SHA, SIGNS, records
  `verified_at_sha`) vs local (in-place checkout, NEVER signs); the `origin/main` default.
- Document the HMAC trust model + limits (integrity + intra-domain authenticity only; no
  non-repudiation / public verifiability / transparency) and the in-toto Statement shape.
- Document `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR`, the disk-cap behavior, and the EFS/NFS flock caveat (cross-ref
  alto-fruit-punch).

## Scope

- In: setup-doc credential section, error-behavior docs, ref/source + signing semantics, HMAC
  trust-model doc, the new env/knobs — each pinned to a named doc file.
- Out: code (S1-S5).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `README.md` (MCP-setup section) and `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` state the private-repo
      fetch-credential requirement and how to supply it (grep-able for the credential section).
- [ ] The descriptive missing-credential error (message + remedy) and the fail-closed (attested)
      vs local-still-runs behavior are documented in a named file.
- [ ] `ref`/`source` semantics, the `origin/main` default, AND the signs-vs-never-signs +
      `verified_at_sha` recording are documented for CLI and MCP (named file).
- [ ] The HMAC trust model + limits and the in-toto Statement shape are documented (named file).
- [ ] `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR`, disk-cap behavior, and the EFS/NFS flock caveat are documented
      (xref alto-fruit-punch), each in a named file.
baseline.summary: Docs: private-repo credentials, descriptive errors, ref/source semantics, HMAC trust model

Complete the dogfood: GitHub `main` must only advance via Gerrit's replication identity, so every
change is gated by the `LLM-Review` review-bot (WS6) before it can land. Today the repo still
carries its legacy branch protection and devs still open GitHub PRs; there is also **no dev-facing
guide** for the Gerrit contribution flow (only setup/ops docs). WS7 flips the switch and documents
the new flow.

## Context — CONSUMES d251/S6 (do not rebuild)
`d251`'s S6 (`075f`, closed) already built the mechanism:
- `infra/terraform-github/` — the repo-level ruleset with a **DeployKey-only bypass** (the
  `rebar-gerrit-replication` key from S5) on `main` (+ tags): `update` (which rejects BOTH direct
  pushes AND PR merges by non-bypass actors) + `deletion` + `non_fast_forward`.
- `infra/runbooks/github-mirror-lock.md` — the cutover & rollback runbook.
- `infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json` — a snapshot of the **pre-existing `main-protection`
  ruleset (id 18048287)** for rollback.

WS7 EXECUTES/finalizes that cutover on `navapbc/rebar` and reconciles any legacy protection — it
does not re-author the ruleset or Terraform.

## What
1. **Remove the legacy protection + activate the Gerrit-only ruleset.** Ensure the pre-existing
   `main-protection` ruleset (18048287) and any other human/PR-merge path is removed/superseded so
   the SOLE ruleset governing `main` is the S6 DeployKey-only lock. Reconcile with the S6 Terraform
   so state matches (no drift, no second competing ruleset).
2. **Contributor guide** — a repo-root `CONTRIBUTING.md` (the doc gap): the Gerrit remote setup, the
   `Change-Id` commit-msg hook, `git push origin HEAD:refs/for/main`, how the single `LLM-Review`
   vote gates submit, how to read a `-1` (a real finding vs a `coverage-gap` infra veto — the WS6
   message tags), how to amend + re-push a patchset, submit, and that **GitHub is a read-only
   mirror** (direct pushes / PR merges are rejected). Linked from `README`.
3. **Live cutover apply + proof** (gated on GitHub admin access): apply the ruleset change and
   verify a direct push / PR-merge to `main` is rejected AND a Gerrit-submitted change replicates
   to GitHub `main`.

## Scope
- IN: reconciling/removing the legacy `main` protection to the single Gerrit-only ruleset; the
  `CONTRIBUTING.md` contributor guide; the live apply + verification.
- OUT: re-authoring S6's ruleset/Terraform/runbook (done); the review-bot decision wiring (WS6);
  provisioning Gerrit/replication (d251).

## Rollback / emergency restore (REQUIRED before the live apply)
Making Gerrit the ONLY path freezes GitHub `main` if the Gerrit gate is later unavailable or
misconfigured (no human can push, no PR can merge). The cutover therefore ships with a
documented, tested rollback that CONSUMES S6's rollback assets:
- **Fast un-lock:** re-enable a human push/merge path by either (a) disabling/deleting the S6
  DeployKey-only ruleset via `gh api -X DELETE /repos/navapbc/rebar/rulesets/{id}` (or
  `terraform destroy` of the ruleset resource), or (b) adding a temporary admin/team `bypass_actor`
  to it — restoring the ability to land a fix directly while Gerrit is repaired.
- **Restore prior protection:** re-apply the pre-existing `main-protection` ruleset from the S6
  snapshot `infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json` (id 18048287) so the repo returns to its
  pre-cutover protection, not to "unprotected".
- **Runbook:** the exact commands + the "when to roll back" trigger live in
  `infra/runbooks/github-mirror-lock.md` (S6's cutover & rollback runbook); WS7 verifies that
  runbook's rollback steps are current for the final ruleset and links them from `CONTRIBUTING.md`
  (so an on-call dev knows the escape hatch). Rollback must be exercised (dry-run/PoC) as part of
  the live apply proof, not merely documented.

## Boundary (honest)
The **live apply** needs a token with `Administration:write` on `navapbc/rebar` and is a
high-impact, mirror-locking change. If that access is not available in this session, the config
reconcile plan + the `CONTRIBUTING.md` are still deliverable; the live apply + proof are surfaced
as blocked (do NOT fake the cutover) — analogous to WS6-b's live-env boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria
### Doable now (no live GitHub admin)
- [ ] A repo-root `CONTRIBUTING.md` documents the full Gerrit contribution flow (remote + Change-Id hook + `push …:refs/for/main` + the `LLM-Review` vote semantics incl. finding-vs-coverage-gap `-1` + amend/re-push + submit + GitHub-is-a-mirror); linked from `README`.
- [ ] The cutover plan names the exact legacy ruleset(s) to remove (incl. `main-protection` id 18048287) and confirms the S6 DeployKey-only ruleset is the sole remaining `main` protection; reconciled against the S6 Terraform (no drift / no competing ruleset).
- [ ] A documented, S6-based **rollback / emergency-restore** procedure is captured (fast un-lock via ruleset delete / temporary bypass_actor, AND restore of the `main-protection` snapshot id 18048287), with a stated "when to roll back" trigger, and linked from `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
### Live-gated (needs `Administration:write` on `navapbc/rebar`)
- [ ] The legacy protection is removed and the Gerrit-only ruleset is active on `navapbc/rebar` `main` (+ tags).
- [ ] The rollback procedure is EXERCISED (dry-run/PoC: un-lock then re-lock) so the escape hatch is proven, not just documented.
- [ ] Proof recorded on this ticket: a direct GitHub push / PR-merge to `main` is REJECTED, and a change submitted in Gerrit replicates to GitHub `main`.

## Dependencies
- CONSUMES d251/S6 (`075f`, closed) tooling + the S5 replication deploy key.
- relates_to WS6 (the review-bot must be voting before Gerrit-only enforcement is meaningful).
baseline.summary: WS7: Make Gerrit the only path into GitHub main (cutover) + contributor guide

## Completion state

This story is complete. It removed duplicate workflow-owned CAS delivery loops by moving the behavior behind Python core entrypoints, while preserving best-effort defaults for existing callers. The implementation is merged in the three child tickets and is present at epic ref `694cf894def36241724e7049e3308d782037ef6d`.

## Delivered architecture

`src/rebar/_store/push.py` is the single owner of tickets-branch delivery mechanics:

- `push_tickets_branch(..., strict=False)` owns push-first CAS retry, fetch-and-merge recovery, the five-cycle budget, and the one conditional terminal push.
- Opt-in strict delivery raises `PushDeliveryError` with a stable reason, operational detail, and unpushed-commit count.
- `commit_and_push_tickets_branch(...)` owns the locked stage, commit, and push transaction used by automation.
- The private `python -m rebar._store.push` adapter translates typed core failures into process stderr and nonzero status; core functions remain reusable and never call `sys.exit`.
- Workflow adapters select synchronous strict delivery explicitly. Existing library, CLI, MCP, importer, and ticket-store callers retain best-effort defaults.

The workflows now contain orchestration only:

- `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` invokes `rebar bridge run`; the Python bridge runner performs one locked strict commit-and-push action with the established bot identity and commit subject.
- `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` invokes the Python push adapter once in strict mode.
- Neither workflow contains its own fetch/merge/retry loop.
- Strict workflow failure remains visible to GitHub Actions through a nonzero adapter result after the shared core exhausts delivery.

This is a Python strangler migration, consistent with the projects architecture. YAML remains the workflow declaration layer, while locking, CAS recovery, retry policy, staging, committing, error classification, and diagnostics live in Python. No new shell script or shell-only runtime path was introduced.

## Child ownership and merged evidence

- `953a-d616-52d3-4efe` owns strict push semantics, the corrected CAS retry budget, typed failure reasons, and the initial push-only Python adapter. Merged commit: `a8e0f67c827706525becb9b4d3df8a4da738d44e`.
- `2bc9-75aa-a08a-478a` owns the locked `commit-and-push` entrypoint, dirty-tree handling, commit identity/message, and reuse of the strict push contract. Merged commit: `1532700efd`.
- `742d-54f1-3b6f-4864` owns both workflow cutovers and removal of the stale raw-git/CAS-loop rationale. Merged commits: `11a026540b`, `039fe7bbde`, and `511c339a63`.

All three children are closed and completion-certified by principal `b8a354e0-12c3-4cf2-bbf1-fcc9685d5126` at ref `694cf894def36241724e7049e3308d782037ef6d`.

## Interface, installation, and legacy continuity

The change deliberately preserves the established interfaces:

- Python library: the strict flag is keyword-only and defaults false; existing public imports and write calls keep their return/disposition contract.
- CLI: public commands continue through the same store/library seams; internal automation uses packaged Python entrypoints for strict delivery.
- MCP server: MCP write tools continue through the same Python facade/store path with best-effort defaults, so protocol behavior does not diverge from the library.
- Automated callers: bridge workflows opt into strict delivery; import, claim, transition, delete, compact, and event append remain best effort unless explicitly adapted.
- Dual direction: read behavior and reconciliation input are unchanged; the migration affects outbound tickets-branch delivery only.

Installation behavior also remains continuous:

- brew and pip installations receive the same packaged Python CLI and core modules.
- MCP-server installation receives the same library implementation used by CLI and direct Python callers.
- No workflow depends on a repository-only shell helper, editable-install path, or ambient interpreter behavior.
- Existing workflows and environments that use legacy command vocabulary, status/exit vocabulary, best-effort delivery, bot identity, or commit subjects continue to work. Strictness is explicit at the two workflow boundaries, not silently imposed globally.

No persisted ticket schema or event vocabulary changed.

## Verification evidence

The child changes passed Gerrit LLM review and CI before merge. The combined oracle covers:

- successful delivery after deterministic concurrent non-fast-forward races in real temporary git repositories;
- rejected delivery after the retry budget, with typed core failure and nonzero strict adapter behavior;
- policy-decline versus transport-failure classification;
- lock timeout, store-epoch guards, narrow refspec, working-tree preservation, and stash restoration;
- successful strict commit-and-push with the requested author and subject;
- failed push leaving the local commit recoverable and reporting the unpushed count;
- default best-effort behavior for legacy Python/library and MCP/store callers;
- both workflow entrypoints delegating exactly once with no workflow-local retry loop;
- focused workflow/core tests plus repository lint, typecheck, and full test gates.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Python core is the sole owner of CAS push/retry behavior.
- [x] The locked Python commit-and-push operation stages, commits, and delivers the workflow transaction.
- [x] The bridge workflow delegates delivery once through the strict Python runner.
- [x] The canary workflow delegates delivery once through the strict Python push adapter.
- [x] No workflow-local fetch/merge/retry loop remains.
- [x] Exhausted strict delivery produces a typed core failure and a nonzero automation result.
- [x] Existing Python library callers remain best effort by default.
- [x] Existing CLI callers remain compatible.
- [x] Existing MCP callers remain compatible.
- [x] brew, pip, and MCP-server installations all execute the same packaged Python implementation.
- [x] Legacy vocabulary, environments, bot identity, and commit-subject contracts remain usable.
- [x] Success, contention, and rejected-push paths are covered by observable tests.
- [x] Gerrit review and CI are green for every merged child change.

## Rollback

Rollback is coordinated: restore the previous workflow delivery blocks before reverting the strict Python adapter/core entrypoints. No data migration is required because no persisted schema changed. The local commits produced before a strict push failure remain recoverable and can be delivered after the remote or policy issue is corrected.
baseline.summary: Collapse the duplicated CAS push loop into core

# The two-vote gate cannot see un-applied terraform, so `main` goes red AFTER the change is already in

## Context / Problem

`.github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml` is the only thing that checks committed terraform has actually been applied. It runs a read-only `terraform plan` and FAILS on a non-empty plan (`-detailed-exitcode`, 2 = drift). Its triggers are:

    on:
      pull_request:   paths: ['infra/terraform/**']
      push:           branches: [main]   paths: ['infra/terraform/**']
      schedule:       cron: '17 6 * * *'
      workflow_dispatch: {}

**A Gerrit change is neither a `pull_request` nor a `push` to `main`.** `main` flows through Gerrit and the GitHub mirror rejects PRs, so for every terraform change that lands the normal way, this workflow does not run until AFTER submit — at which point the `push: main` trigger fires and fails. The `Verified +1` a change needs to be submittable therefore carries NO signal about whether its terraform was applied. Applies are manual (`infra/runbooks/provision-restore.md`), and autodeploy does not run terraform (`grep terraform infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` matches only an rsync exclude and a secrets path), so nothing else closes the loop either.

## Evidence — this is not hypothetical, it happened today

Bug 34cd landed `e9d4d390c3` ("34cd: defer autodeploy while a review runs"), which added 70 lines to `infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf` including `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.review_interrupts`. Observed:

* the Gerrit change passed both gates and was submitted;
* the ticket was closed with a passing completion verifier;
* the FIRST terraform-drift run to see the commit was the post-merge `push` run at
  `e9d4d390c3`, and it FAILED — `fmt -check`, `init` and `validate` all passed, only
  `terraform plan (fail on drift)` failed, which is exactly the un-applied signature;
* a read-only `terraform plan` from a clean worktree at `origin/main` reported
  `Plan: 1 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy` — the single pending resource being that alarm.

So the alarm 34cd shipped to make an invisible failure mode visible was itself invisible: declared in HCL, absent from CloudWatch. I applied it (`1 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed`) and the plan is now empty, so `main` is green again — but the process gap that produced it is untouched, and the next terraform change will reproduce it exactly.

**Why this is the epic's own recurring lesson:** the guard shared the change's assumption. The Verified gate proves the code builds and tests pass; it silently does not prove the infrastructure the code depends on exists. A reviewer reading a green `Verified +1` on a terraform change reasonably concludes the infra is live, and is wrong.

## Scope

- `.github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml` — the trigger set, and/or
- whatever dispatches CI for Gerrit changes (the gerrit-to-platform bridge), so a change touching
  `infra/terraform/**` is drift-checked BEFORE it can be submitted rather than after.

## Approach (options, not yet decided)

Two shapes, with a real tradeoff:

1. **Gate it pre-submit** — have the Gerrit CI dispatch include the drift plan for changes touching
   `infra/terraform/**`. Closes the gap properly, but the plan will legitimately be NON-EMPTY for the
   change under review (its resource is not applied yet, and cannot be — it has not landed), so a
   naive reuse of `-detailed-exitcode` would fail EVERY terraform change. The check has to compare
   against the change's own additions, or report advisorily rather than blocking.
2. **Make the post-merge failure impossible to ignore** — keep the check where it is but ensure an
   un-applied landing pages someone, and document the apply as a required step of landing terraform
   (a commit-message checklist item, or a runbook step the author must attest).

Option 1 is the real fix; option 2 is the cheap mitigation. Note the asymmetry that makes this non-trivial: a terraform change is the one category where "CI green" and "the change is done" are genuinely different states, because landing and applying are separate acts.

## Testing

The oracle must FAIL on the exact history that produced this bug. Reconstruct the 34cd landing shape — a change adding a terraform resource, with no apply — and assert the chosen mechanism refuses it (or pages) rather than reporting green. A test that only checks the workflow file's trigger list is a change-detector and does not prove the gap is closed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a change touching `infra/terraform/**` can no longer reach `Verified +1` with an un-applied
      resource WITHOUT that fact being surfaced — either the drift check runs pre-submit, or an
      explicit apply attestation is required to land it. State which mechanism was chosen and why.
- [ ] if the pre-submit option is taken, the check distinguishes "this change's own not-yet-applied
      additions" (expected, not a failure) from "previously-committed HCL that was never applied"
      (the actual defect) — verified by running it against BOTH shapes and observing different
      outcomes.
- [ ] `infra/runbooks/` states that landing a terraform change is not complete until it is applied,
      and names who applies it and how, so the manual step is documented rather than folklore.
- [ ] the 34cd instance is recorded as the motivating case, including that its alarm existed in HCL
      and not in CloudWatch, so the failure mode is concrete for the next reader.
baseline.summary: Terraform drift never gates a Gerrit change, so un-applied infra lands and reds main after submit

# Cluster 1 — consolidate canonical-JSON/content-hash onto the `_store/canonical.py` seam (byte-preserving)

## What

Make `src/rebar/_store/canonical.py` the single home for "sorted-key compact JSON (+ sha256)" and migrate the four real duplicate sites onto it, **preserving every site's exact output bytes** (pure DRY — see the parent epic `civil-marlin-flare` for the no-live-bug analysis).

- Extend `src/rebar/_store/canonical.py` with **purely additive, keyword-only** params (today's
  positional signature `canonical_str(event)` is unchanged, so the existing positional callers stay
  byte-identical):
  - `canonical_str(doc, *, ascii_only=False, default=None)` — defaults reproduce today's exact bytes
    (`ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":")`).
  - `canonical_bytes(doc, *, ascii_only=False, default=None)` and
    `content_hash(doc, *, ascii_only=False, default=None) -> str` (= `sha256(canonical_bytes(...))`).
- The existing `canonical_str`/`canonical_bytes` consumers that must stay **untouched / byte-identical**
  (all call positionally, so the new keyword-only params don't reach them): `_store/event_append.py`,
  `_commands/txn.py`, `_commands/delete.py`, `_commands/compact.py`,
  `_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py`, `_engine/rebar_reconciler/batch_dispatch.py`.
- Migrate each duplicate site to import the seam and delete its local reimplementation, choosing the
  param values that **reproduce that site's current bytes exactly**:
  - `src/rebar/signing.py` `_canonical_payload` → `canonical_bytes({...})` (current `ensure_ascii=False`
    → seam default `ascii_only=False`): byte-identical, zero signature risk.
  - `src/rebar/llm/workflow/schema.py` `canonical_json`/`content_hash` (current `ensure_ascii=False`)
    → delegate to the seam defaults; keep the public names as thin re-exports (preserve
    `llm/workflow/__init__.py` `__all__`).
  - `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/conflict_resolver.py` `_hash_value` → `content_hash(value,
    ascii_only=True, default=str)`. **`ascii_only=True` is REQUIRED**: the current call
    `json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, default=str, separators=(",",":"))` omits `ensure_ascii`, so it
    uses the stdlib default `ensure_ascii=True`; without `ascii_only=True` a non-ASCII provenance value
    would flip from `\uXXXX` to literal UTF-8 and change the stored `value_hash` / echo-suppression
    decision. `default=str` is also load-bearing (provenance values may be non-JSON-native).
  - `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mutation.py` `serialize_manifest` → `canonical_str(items,
    ascii_only=True)` (PRESERVE `ensure_ascii=True`; do NOT normalize — its manifest hash is benign
    and changing it is a gratuitous behavior change).

## Why

Five near-identical canonical encoders have already drifted on `ensure_ascii`; one tested seam removes the duplication and the drift risk while changing **zero** output bytes at any site.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/rebar/_store/canonical.py` exposes `canonical_str`/`canonical_bytes` (with additive,
      keyword-only `ascii_only` + `default` params whose defaults reproduce today's bytes) and
      `content_hash`; the one true encoding is documented in the module.
- [ ] The new params are additive: today's positional `canonical_str(event)` signature is preserved,
      so the six existing importers (`event_append`, `_commands/{txn,delete,compact}`,
      `rebar_reconciler/{inbound_translate,batch_dispatch}`) are untouched and byte-identical.
- [ ] `signing.py`, `llm/workflow/schema.py`, `conflict_resolver.py`, and `mutation.py` import the
      seam; their local `json.dumps(...)`/`hashlib.sha256(...)` reimplementations are deleted.
- [ ] Every retained variant is an explicit, justified param with a cited consumer: `ascii_only=True`
      for both `mutation.py` and `conflict_resolver.py`; `default=str` for `conflict_resolver.py`.
- [ ] `schema.py`'s public `canonical_json` / `content_hash` names still resolve (re-export preserved).
- [ ] A characterization test in `tests/unit/` pins **hardcoded expected bytes captured from the
      pre-refactor code paths** (literal golden constants, so the comparison is non-tautological —
      not re-derived from the new seam).
- [ ] That test exercises each migrated caller by name for byte/digest equality against its golden
      constant: `signing._canonical_payload`, `schema.canonical_json`, `schema.content_hash`,
      `mutation.serialize_manifest`, `conflict_resolver._hash_value`.
- [ ] The golden input set covers non-ASCII, nested, and unicode-key payloads; a non-ASCII value is
      routed specifically through `conflict_resolver._hash_value` to lock its `ascii_only=True` choice.
- [ ] A signing sign→verify round-trip on a fresh manifest still certifies (independently verifiable).
- [ ] `make lint` passes.
- [ ] `make test` passes.
- [ ] `canonical.py` stays under the 800-LOC soft cap; no new module is created.
baseline.summary: Cluster 1: consolidate canonical-JSON/content-hash onto the _store/canonical.py seam (byte-preserving)

## Context and measured baseline

The real-artifact oracle from closed ticket ducal-statuelike-ladybird is valuable, but tests/unit/test_build_provenance.py independently runs git archive plus python -m build in four tests. On the current macOS host the unchanged module took 35.93s. Individually: install-from-sdist 8.40s, wheel-from-sdist 4.69s, sdist-content 4.53s, and empty-env failure 1.81s. Three tests repeat the identical successful clean-tree build with REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT=abc1234; install-from-sdist then performs a distinct second wheel build from the produced sdist.

## OSS consensus and prior decisions

Setuptools builds stable sdist/wheel artifacts once under a session lock and exposes session-scoped readonly fixtures (pypa/setuptools@7d53128, setuptools/tests/fixtures.py#L70-L130). PyPA Build builds a dependency wheel once in a session fixture for downstream tests (pypa/build@bf222f4, tests/test_projectbuilder.py#L427-L438). Closed ticket ducal-statuelike-ladybird requires the real wheel/sdist boundaries but does not require rebuilding an identical prerequisite per assertion. No rejection exists.

## Plan

1. Change only tests/unit/test_build_provenance.py. Create one pytest session-scoped fixture per xdist worker using tmp_path_factory. It performs one git archive of HEAD and one real python -m build with REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT=abc1234.
2. Return only immutable artifact paths from that fixture: the built wheel and sdist. Consumers inspect these archives read-only. No consumer receives the shared extracted source or output directory, preventing mutation of shared state.
3. Wheel-from-sdist and sdist-content tests reuse the corresponding real shared artifacts while retaining their exact archive-content assertions.
4. Install-from-sdist copies/extracts the shared sdist into its function-scoped tmp_path, then performs the distinct real env-unset rebuild there. Empty-env failure keeps its own function-scoped clean tree and real failing build because its environment and observable boundary differ.
5. Strengthen the existing test module with deterministic build-call counting under a subprocess seam or equivalent fixture-level contract: one successful prerequisite build per pytest worker/session plus the retained empty-env and rebuild-from-sdist calls. Timing remains evidence, never a pass threshold.
6. RED first against the current per-test rebuild behavior; hold the counter oracle out from the fixture refactor. GREEN, then seed both defects independently: restore a duplicate successful build and remove/corrupt COMMIT in the shared artifact. The counter/provenance oracles must return RED.
7. Re-run the module serially and with xdist, report individual and total before/after durations, then run lint, typecheck, and the default pytest selection.

## Test contract card

authoritative_contract: ducal-statuelike-ladybird and tests/unit/test_build_provenance.py require real wheel-from-sdist provenance, empty-env build failure, sdist build-info content, and env-unset rebuild-from-sdist preservation. trigger_preconditions: a clean git archive without .git and REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT=abc1234; separate empty env and env-unset rebuild cases. production_path: python -m build through hatch_build.py, with real wheel/sdist archive inspection. test_tier: real subprocess/package builds; a unit tier cannot prove artifact contents or the sdist-to-wheel boundary. observable_postcondition: identical provenance/failure/content assertions; exactly one identical successful prerequisite build per worker/session, while empty-env failure and rebuild-from-sdist remain distinct real builds. negative_control: empty-env failure does not consume the successful artifact; rebuild operates on a function-local extraction and cannot mutate shared inputs. collateral_invariants: fixture lifetime ends with the pytest session; xdist workers share nothing; no cross-session/on-disk cache; no production file changes. ci_gate: default pytest job and full Gerrit Verified gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every existing real wheel/sdist assertion remains and still executes the relevant build boundary.
- [x] One successful clean-source prerequisite build is performed per pytest worker/session; identical prerequisite archive/build work is not repeated per test.
- [x] Shared consumers receive only read-only artifact paths; mutating extraction/rebuild work occurs in function-scoped copies.
- [x] A defect-seeded duplicate prerequisite build fails the deterministic call-count oracle, and a defect-seeded missing COMMIT still fails the provenance oracle.
- [x] Serial and xdist runs pass and report before/after individual durations; timing is evidence, never a gate.
- [x] Packaging tests remain hermetic, add no cross-session cache, and lint/typecheck/default pytest/Gerrit gates pass.
baseline.summary: Reuse build-provenance fixtures while preserving real wheel and sdist coverage

## Context
Once Jira returns a key, local persistence can still fail. The canonical label is the durable remote identity floor; the entity property is optional enrichment. Local confirmation must use RP-02 as the single identity owner.

## Outcome
After create returns a key, attach `rebar-id:<local_id>` first, attempt the optional property second, then persist known key and confirmation through the RP-02 facade. Any failure returns a typed known-key safety abort without remote deletion.

## Plan
1. Require RP-02 repository/lifecycle/recovery facade to be available; do not create a second binding writer.
2. Apply the canonical label before any property or local confirmation. Treat property unsupported/permission failure as visible enrichment failure that cannot erase the label floor.
3. Persist known key and confirmation through named `BindingStore` operations and their unit of work.
4. If label or persistence fails, preserve key, pending/recovery evidence, remote issue, and exact terminal disposition.
5. Execute later lifecycle intents only after their remote postcondition is proven.

## Testing
Fault cuts after returned key, during label, property, known-key save, and confirmation assert remote containment, local bytes, and outcomes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The canonical label is attempted before optional property and local confirmation.
- [ ] Unsupported or forbidden property remains visible and cannot remove a successful label.
- [ ] Known key and confirmation persist only through the RP-02 `BindingStore` facade.
- [ ] Every post-create failure reports the known key and retains recovery evidence.
- [ ] No post-create failure deletes the remote issue.
- [ ] Other lifecycle intents execute only after their remote postconditions are proven.

## Out of scope
Whole-pass crash/restart convergence, dependency release, and production create cutover.
baseline.summary: RP-03 S4 T2 — Contain returned creates and confirm through BindingStore

## Context / Problem

## Context / Problem
Follow-up (fix b) to creatable-foldable-arthropods (fix a, Gerrit 1761). At SEARCH EXHAUSTION, `BOUNDED_FALLBACK_EVIDENCE` banks `met=false` ("criterion unmet") when the run only established "budget ran out before sufficient evidence was found" — misattributing absence-of-evidence as evidence-of-absence, producing false FAIL verdicts on tickets whose evidence exists but was not reached within the window.

## Proposed fix
Distinguish THREE evidence outcomes: met, refuted, insufficient (search exhausted without a determination) — the third carried as a framework-set `evidence_sufficient:false` marker riding alongside `met:false`, per the verdict_obtainable precedent, so every fail-closed consumer stays unchanged. Marker origin — the banking WRITE path:
- `CompletionEvidencePolicy.fallback_record` (completion_tool_policy.py:100-101) passes a literal `False` through the bool-only record tool. Widen the STRUCTURAL contract: the `fallback_record` Callable (:78) gains the marker; completion_banking's wiring supplies a marker-aware bank write. Not the model-facing tool; keeps the no-completion_banking-import independence (:93-96).
- `CriterionBank.upsert` (:441-461) — persists the optional marker alongside bool `met` (docstring updates).
- `record_criterion_verdict` (:539) stays BOOL; its :544 instruction changes semantics: today it banks `met=false` at the bounded-COMMIT boundary for "not demonstrated" — absence-of-evidence banked as refutation. New rule: `met=false` ONLY on positive refutation; not-found records nothing — the bounded fallback (completion_tool_policy.py:187) fires at the boundary and banks the marker. ALL absence-of-evidence flows through the framework's marker path; the marker is never a model-tool input.
- `harvest_structured_into_bank` (:563-591) keeps its bool gate; the model never emits the marker, so harvest sources it by PRESERVATION: overwrite retains the prior entry's marker — only the widened fallback contract sets it; a genuine refutation (bare met=false) replaces it.

**Full consumer graph (changes together):**
- **Schema (completion_verdict.schema.json)**: per the `verdict_obtainable` precedent (schema :14-18, completion.py:516) — a marker alongside {PASS, FAIL}, not a third token. Two OPTIONAL framework-set markers: `criteria[].evidence_sufficient:false` (exhaustion, not refutation) and top-level `evidence_sufficient:false` (derived: no criterion genuinely unmet, ≥1 insufficient). verdict/met vocabularies unchanged; only message renderers read the marker. Both rendering seams validate against this schema (completion_recovery.py:674, :774).
- **`_validate_coverage` (completion_recovery.py:364-368, :717)**: met stays bool → gates unchanged; markers survive validation.
- **`_run_finalizer` (completion_recovery.py:741)**: banked-evidence payload carries the marker so the finalizer sees exhaustion, not refutation.
- **Unbanked/exhausted placeholders** (`assemble_deterministic_verdict` :646-660, `merge_finalizer_with_bank` :715+): a never-banked criterion at exhaustion IS absence-of-evidence — placeholders carry the marker (keeping `exhausted`), not a bare high-severity FAIL.
- **`reconcile_verdict` (completion.py:495-564)**: `:522` normalization UNTOUCHED. As the single chokepoint both verdict kinds pass through (:561) it DERIVES the top-level marker (set iff no criterion genuinely unmet and ≥1 carries the per-criterion marker); the `:564` remediation branch becomes marker-aware (insufficient-evidence remediation, not unmet-criteria guidance). The `:526` fault path is unaffected.
- **Close-gate refusal (close_precheck.py:571-589)**: still gates on non-PASS (fail-closed) — with the marker present it reports "insufficient evidence" + remediation instead of "N unmet criteria".
- **Standalone verb renderer** `_render_verdict_text` (src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:660-693): hard-codes "N unmet criteria" (:672-673) — same marker-aware wording split; exit codes unchanged.
- **Finalizer prompt (completion_verifier_finalizer.md:23-28)**: currently collapses missing/truncated evidence into `met:false` + high-severity FAIL finding. New rule: banked insufficient entries echo as `met:false` with insufficient findings text; `merge_finalizer_with_bank` re-stamps the marker from the bank (stamp = enforcement, prompt = text alignment).
- **Completion sidecar**: the FAIL payload (:355-369) whitelist omits `criteria`; top-level markers ride only via explicit lines (verdict_obtainable :374-375). Add the explicit `evidence_sufficient` line + per-criterion markers to the FAIL payload; round-trip test.
- **Banked-entry rendering** (`assemble_deterministic_verdict` :619-640, `merge_finalizer_with_bank` :705-714): marker-carrying entries emit `met:false + evidence_sufficient:false` with an insufficient-evidence finding, not a bare unmet-criterion FAIL. `merge_finalizer_with_bank` is the authoritative per-criterion RE-STAMP site: the bank (not model output) is the marker's source of truth. Its existing-record branch (:700-704) never consults `bank_entries` — add a bank lookup so the merge overwrites the finalizer's echo (the :705+ fallback already reads the bank). Honesty of message and recorded class, never gate leniency.

## Scope
- Banking WRITE path: `fallback_record` contract + wiring (completion_tool_policy.py); completion_banking.py: `upsert` (persists marker), `record_criterion_verdict` (bool signature unchanged), `harvest_structured_into_bank` (preserve-on-overwrite above), both placeholder branches, `merge_finalizer_with_bank` re-stamp (both branches).
- src/rebar/schemas/completion_verdict.schema.json — optional markers (top-level + per-criterion), verdict_obtainable pattern.
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py — `_validate_coverage` markers survive validation; `_run_finalizer` payload carries the marker (:741).
- src/rebar/llm/completion.py — `reconcile_verdict` derives the top-level marker + :564 remediation branch marker-aware.
- src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py — refusal message keys on the marker (insufficient evidence vs unmet criteria); still refuses both.
- src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py — `_render_verdict_text` marker-aware wording (:672-673); exit codes unchanged.
- completion_verifier_finalizer.md — sufficiency rule (:23-28).
- src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py — explicit marker lines + criteria in the FAIL payload; round-trip test.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] At exhaustion, banked fallback evidence carries `evidence_sufficient:false`, never bare `met=false`; unit test.
- [x] A fallback-banked insufficient entry keeps its marker after a marker-less successor re-harvest (preserve-on-overwrite); genuine refutation (bare met=false) replaces it; model-facing tool stays bool-only; unit tests.
- [x] Genuine refutation still banks bare `met=false` → FAIL; under the new :544 rule not-found records nothing and the bounded fallback banks the marker; guard tests.
- [x] Both rendering seams emit `met:false + evidence_sufficient:false` for insufficient entries, INCLUDING their unbanked/exhausted placeholder branches; per-seam and per-branch tests.
- [x] Schema validates marker-carrying AND all-bool records; `_validate_coverage` passes markers, rejects untyped; `_run_finalizer` payload carries the marker; `merge_finalizer_with_bank` re-stamps from the bank over model echoes; FAIL sidecar round-trips both marker levels; unit tests each.
- [x] Close gate still BLOCKS on insufficient evidence (verdict stays FAIL) but the refusal — and `_render_verdict_text`'s standalone output — reports insufficient evidence + remediation, not unmet criteria; `reconcile_verdict` derives the top-level marker and swaps remediation; gate + reconcile + renderer tests.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1) before close.

## Out of scope
Guard/memo interaction (fix a, landed); retry policy; prompt changes OTHER than the finalizer's evidence-sufficiency rule above.
baseline.summary: Completion verifier banks met=false at search exhaustion — should bank insufficient_evidence (tri-state)

# Spike: verify Claude Code loads AGENTS.md via a `@AGENTS.md` import

## What

De-risk the whole migration by confirming, hands-on, that a `CLAUDE.md` whose body is a single `@AGENTS.md` line actually pulls `AGENTS.md` into Claude Code's context at launch (the mechanism the research identified, but whose live doc page had a fetch bug). Document the observed precedence/nesting behavior. If the import does NOT work in the installed Claude Code version, record the fallback decision (symlink `CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md`, accepting its Windows/tool-clobber tradeoffs) so downstream stories build on a proven mechanism.

## Scope

A throwaway spike in a scratch dir or worktree — no durable code change. Files touched: a temporary `AGENTS.md` + `CLAUDE.md`. Output is a written finding recorded as a comment on this ticket (and, if needed, a correction to the approach in the parent epic).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Confirmed whether `@AGENTS.md` in `CLAUDE.md` loads `AGENTS.md` into context in the
  installed Claude Code build; result recorded as a comment on this ticket with the exact
  version tested.
  - Proving: comment on this ticket stating PASS/FAIL + `claude --version`.
- [ ] If FAIL, the fallback mechanism (symlink vs. content-copy-with-sync-test) is chosen and
  noted so the AGENTS.md story uses it.
- [ ] No stray spike files left in the repo working tree.
  - Proving: `git status --porcelain` clean after the spike.

## De-risking results — SPIKE EXECUTED (PASS, definitive)

Ran headless Claude Code **v2.1.211** in an isolated temp dir: `CLAUDE.md` = `@AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.md` held a canary token. The model returned the canary **verbatim** and with **no approval prompt** → a project-level `@AGENTS.md` import expands into context. Official docs (`code.claude.com/docs/en/memory`) confirm and recommend exactly this: "Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md, not AGENTS.md … create CLAUDE.md [that] imports [it] … add Claude-specific instructions below the import" (literal example: `@AGENTS.md` then `## Claude Code`). Import recursion max depth = 4 hops; same-repo imports need no approval (only imports OUTSIDE the project tree prompt once). **Decision: use the `@AGENTS.md` import — no symlink fallback needed.** KEY NUANCE: imports "load at launch" and do NOT reduce context, so AGENTS.md must itself be lean; the token win comes from de-dup into docs (drives S2). This spike is resolved; implementation is a no-op adopt-the-proven-pattern.
baseline.summary: Spike: verify Claude Code loads AGENTS.md via a `@AGENTS.md` import

## Summary
Reducer cache key is filename+size only, so a same-size in-place rewrite of an event file serves stale state.

## Reproduction Steps
(verified on installed 0.4.0 == HEAD, temp store)
1. rebar comment <id> "AAAA".
2. Overwrite that event file's body so the comment reads "BBBB" (same byte length).
3. rebar show <id> -> still "AAAA" until any other event lands.

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: reads reflect on-disk events.
- Actual: compute_dir_hash (ticket_reducer/_cache.py:38-57) hashes name:size (+ .archived marker) only; the docstring even scopes detection to "same filename, different size".

## Impact
git checkout/rebase of the tickets branch, fsck-recover cherry-picks, or any equal-length rewrite serves stale reads through show/list/search (library, CLI, MCP).

## Source
src/rebar/_engine/ticket_reducer/_cache.py:38-57.

## Fix direction
Include st_mtime_ns in the hash parts (stat is already performed for size; expect ~zero overhead — see validation notes comment for measurement). Content hash is the stronger alternative if mtime granularity worries arise.

## Suggested RED test
Same-size overwrite -> fresh state on next read; cache still hits when nothing changed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Same-size in-place rewrite invalidates the cache (RED test first)
- [ ] No measurable read-path regression (cache still effective on unchanged dirs)
- [ ] Docstring updated to the new invariant
baseline.summary: Reducer cache serves stale state after same-size in-place event rewrite

## Context / Problem

Ticket `d48d-76bd-3d31-47ea` added a fifth validity sub-question (`harm_reachable`) to the rebar-janitor Verification phase and updated the normative scoring formula in `examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/verification.md` to read "graded fraction of the 5 binary sub-answers". Two *secondary prose glosses* elsewhere in the same file still say four, so the file is internally inconsistent about the count:

- the drop-floor parenthetical at line 152: `(low-confidence — <~3-of-4 sub-answers affirm it)`
- the known-fine registry aside at line 191: `it is NOT one of the four validity sub-questions`

Neither is the normative rule (the formula bullet is), so nothing computes from them — but a reader counting sub-questions gets contradictory answers from the same document.

## Approach

Update both glosses to agree with the normative formula. Both replacements are stated verbatim below; there is no implementer discretion.

1. **Drop-floor parenthetical (line 152).** The floor is `validity < 0.75`. Over 5 sub-answers,
   4-of-5 = 0.80 **survives** and 3-of-5 = 0.60 **drops**, so the survive/drop boundary is
   **4-of-5**, not a literal denominator swap to `3-of-5` (which would misdescribe the floor).
   Replace the parenthetical with exactly:
   `(low-confidence — <4-of-5 sub-answers affirm it)`
2. **Known-fine aside (line 191).** Replace `four validity sub-questions` with
   `five validity sub-questions`. No other wording on that line changes.

Line 140 (`**impact** = mean of four terms`) is a *different* count — the four impact terms — and is deliberately left alone.

No rule, threshold, or behavior changes: the normative arithmetic already reads 5.

## Scope

- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/verification.md` — the drop-floor parenthetical in the
  `## The floors` code block and the `matches_known_fine` aside in the `## Known-fine registry`
  section. Nothing else in the file or repo changes.

## Testing

Documentation-only prose edit with no executable path, schema, or test fixture; verification is textual (see Acceptance Criteria). The acceptance criteria assert both the *removal* of the stale text and the *presence* of the exact replacement text, so a wrong replacement cannot pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The drop-floor gloss no longer says `3-of-4`; checked by
      `grep -n '3-of-4' examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/verification.md` exiting non-zero.
- [x] The drop-floor gloss now reads the correct boundary; checked by
      `grep -nF '<4-of-5 sub-answers affirm it' examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/verification.md`
      exiting zero with exactly one match, on the `validity < 0.75` line of the `## The floors` block.
- [x] No `3-of-5` gloss is introduced; checked by
      `grep -n '3-of-5' examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/verification.md` exiting non-zero.
- [x] The known-fine aside no longer says `four validity sub-questions`; checked by
      `grep -n 'four validity sub-questions' examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/verification.md`
      exiting non-zero, and now says the five form; checked by
      `grep -nF 'five validity' examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/verification.md` exiting zero.
- [x] No count-of-four reference to the validity sub-question set survives in the file; checked by
      `grep -nE 'the 4 (binary )?sub|four validity' examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/verification.md`
      exiting non-zero.
- [x] The unrelated `mean of four terms` impact gloss is untouched; checked by
      `grep -nF 'mean of four terms' examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/verification.md`
      exiting zero.
- [x] The change is self-contained: the normative `5 binary sub-answers` formula bullet is already
      present in the file at edit time (`grep -nF '5 binary sub-answers'` exits zero), so this
      ticket depends on no unlanded work.
- [x] `make lint` exits 0 with the repo venv on PATH.

## Symptom
Under `verify.enforce_plan_material_pins=true`, the plan-review CLOSE gate rejects a valid, unchanged **planning-phase** attestation with `incompatible-phase` (`planning -> execution`), even though the plan material never drifted. Closing then requires a fresh execution-phase review that cannot be minted after code drift (the drift-refresh path re-signs the prior planning manifest), so the ticket cannot be closed.

## Root cause — an undocumented override that contradicts the design
The phase mechanism (ticket 5967, "Add planning and execution phases") and the close gate (ticket 2bbd, "Require a separately attested current plan review at close") deliberately make a planning attestation COMPATIBLE with an execution-phase ticket at close. `docs/plan-review-gate.md` §"phase_status compatibility" documents exactly this: `execution | planning or legacy planning | compatible`. 2bbd's stated purpose is to catch a plan that CHANGED during execution — via own-material + pin drift — "without invalidating every implementation because implementation files changed." It never required a fresh execution-phase review.

`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py::compute_validity` contains a later override (added by ticket 145e, "enable ... enforcement for rebar", gated on `enforced`) that forces `phase_status = "incompatible"` when `profile is CLOSE and signed_phase == "planning"`. This directly contradicts the documented table and 2bbd/5967's design, and is documented nowhere. The one concern cited in 145e's trail ("an in-progress self-edit must invalidate close until a fresh execution review") is already covered by own-material-drift invalidation, so the override is broader than any real requirement.

## Fix
Remove the `enforced`-gated CLOSE override (and the paired CLOSE-only `current_phase` promotion to "execution") so the CLOSE profile uses the same documented `review_phase_status` table as DEFAULT/DRIFT_REFRESH. A planning attestation certifies close iff the plan material/pins have not drifted; a drifted plan still invalidates and forces a re-review. The implementation is validated independently by the completion-verifier close gate. (Secondary, out of scope here: the drift-refresh path is reached even under `--force`, contradicting the `__init__.py` comment that `force` bypasses it; noted for a follow-up but not required once the gate accepts either phase.)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Under `enforce_plan_material_pins=true`, `close_plan_review_gate_check` returns
      `ok=true, verdict="certified"` for an unchanged planning-phase attestation.
- [ ] A plan/pin change during execution still invalidates at close (material/pin drift), forcing
      a re-review — unchanged.
- [ ] The `planning`-current + `execution`-signed row stays `incompatible` (base table unchanged).
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` states the CLOSE profile uses the same compatibility table.
- [ ] Tests that encoded the undocumented override are inverted to the documented behavior.

## File impact
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py
- tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_validity.py
- tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_policy_dogfood.py
- docs/plan-review-gate.md
baseline.summary: plan-review CLOSE gate rejects a valid unchanged planning-phase attestation (undocumented override contradicts 5967/2bbd design + docs)

baseline.description:
# Prompt caching writes on every gate call and is never read across calls: the marked prefix is not stable

## Observed — measured, with a control

Two `rebar review-plan` runs executed BACK TO BACK, seconds apart, well inside the ~5-minute cache TTL, on two DIFFERENT tickets (1c39 then 9baf), with REBAR_USAGE_LOG capturing every call. All calls on Bedrock via the project default. Per-call figures:

    pass                                RUN A in / write        RUN B in / write        RUN B read
    plan-reviewer (frontier/opus)        5286 / 2800             5394 / 2908             0
    plan-review-prerequisite-verifier    3809 / 1545             3872 / 1608             0
    plan-review-verifier                 7136 / 4871             7199 / 4934             0
    plan-review-coach                    1999 / 0                2062 / 0                0
    ticket-digest (trivial/haiku)        2131 / 0                2816 / 0                0
    TOTALS                               write 9216, read 0      write 9450, read 0

RUN B WROTE THE CACHE AGAIN INSTEAD OF READING IT. Every read is zero in both runs.

## The mechanism this points at

Each pass's cache-WRITE size tracks its input size almost exactly across the two runs (plan-reviewer 5286 -> 5394 input, 2800 -> 2908 write; verifier 7136 -> 7199 input, 4871 -> 4934 write). A cache prefix that were genuinely stable would produce the SAME marked prefix and therefore a hit on the second run. That the write grows in step with per-ticket input says the MARKED PREFIX ITSELF VARIES PER CALL — i.e. per-ticket content is landing ahead of the cache breakpoint, so the cache key is unique every time and can never be reused.

`capabilities.cache_settings_for` marks the INSTRUCTIONS plus tool definitions, and `structured_run.estimate_marked_prefix_tokens` derives the marked size from the SYSTEM PROMPT. So the hypothesis to test first is that the rendered system prompt/instructions embed per-ticket material (the plan text, the ticket digest, or similar) rather than being invariant across runs.

## What is NOT the explanation — ruled out by evidence

* NOT "caching is off on Bedrock". Three of five passes write thousands of tokens per run, so the
  settings are emitted and the provider accepts them.
* NOT "the read path is broken". Intra-CALL reuse demonstrably works: the production review bot's
  multi-step agentic records read large caches within a single call — e.g. a code-review pass with
  steps=9/125 logged cache_read=386204 against in=430479, and another with steps=17/125 logged
  cache_read=493547. Those are steps 2..N reusing what step 1 wrote inside one conversation.
* NOT the sub-minimum-prefix condition for the three writing passes. That condition explains the
  two passes that write ZERO — coach (whole prompt small) and ticket-digest, where the diagnostic
  fired verbatim: "only 477 tokens sit ahead of the cache breakpoint, below this model's
  4096-token minimum, while 8634 of the 9111 billed input tokens ride AFTER it unmarked". It does
  not explain a pass that writes 4871 tokens and then never reads them.

## Why it costs money rather than being merely untidy

A cache write is billed at a PREMIUM over ordinary input; a read is billed at a steep discount. The current behaviour pays the premium on every gate call and collects the discount only within a single multi-step call. For single-step passes — which is every pass in a plan review, all five records show requests=1 — the write is pure loss: nothing ever reads it. Every plan review on this project pays roughly 9,000-11,000 premium-rate cache-write tokens for zero benefit.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` `cache_settings_for` — where the breakpoints are placed.
- `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` `estimate_marked_prefix_tokens` and the ineffective-cache
  diagnostic — the estimate is the instrument that would have caught this and did not.
- whatever renders the plan-review system prompt / instructions, if that is where per-ticket
  content is crossing the breakpoint.

## Approach — investigate before changing anything

The first task is NOT a fix, it is to identify precisely which bytes sit ahead of the breakpoint and whether they vary per run. Capture the rendered system prompt for the same pass on two different tickets and diff them; the varying region is the defect's location. Only then decide whether the fix is to move per-ticket content behind the breakpoint (into the user message) or to split the instructions into an invariant prefix and a per-run suffix.

Do NOT "fix" this by disabling caching on single-step passes: that trades a real, measurable premium for giving up the cross-call discount entirely, and the cross-call discount is the larger prize once the prefix is stable. Note also that the existing diagnostic's advice — "the changeable thing is where the breakpoint sits, not the size of the prompt" — is exactly right here and was never triggered for the writing passes, so consider whether the predicate should also flag "wrote every call, never read".

## Testing

- an oracle that renders the same pass's marked prefix for two different tickets and asserts they
  are BYTE-IDENTICAL. This is the RED test: it should fail today. Verify RED before any fix.
- a live two-run oracle (the experiment above) asserting cache_read > 0 on the second run for at
  least the frontier pass, run inside the TTL.
- a guard that the ineffective-cache diagnostic fires when a pass writes on every call and never
  reads, so this class cannot recur silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] the bytes that vary ahead of the cache breakpoint are identified and cited, with a diff of
      the rendered marked prefix for one pass across two different tickets.
- [x] the marked prefix for a given pass is byte-identical across tickets, pinned by a test
      verified RED against today's behaviour.
- [x] a second run of the same pass inside the cache TTL records cache_read > 0, evidenced by an
      actual usage-log capture rather than by inspection.
- [x] the diagnostic in `structured_run` also flags the write-every-call-never-read shape, so a
      regression is loud.
- [x] the cost change is stated with figures — premium-rate write tokens per review before and
      after — so the benefit is measured rather than asserted.
baseline.summary: Prompt cache is written on every call and never read across calls: the marked prefix varies per ticket

baseline.description:
Remove the dead `SupportsIncremental` capability and its false docstring, so the reconciler backend port stops asserting a dispatch behaviour that does not exist.

## Context / Problem

`SupportsIncremental` (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py:545-553`) is a `@runtime_checkable` capability Protocol whose docstring asserts, in the present tense, a behaviour that is not implemented:

> Core uses an incremental fetch only when ``isinstance(backend, SupportsIncremental)``;
> otherwise it falls back to a full scan.

It has **zero implementers** and **zero dispatch**: no adapter defines `search_incremental`, and no `isinstance(backend, SupportsIncremental)` check exists anywhere in `src/` (confirmed by `grep -rn "SupportsIncremental" src/` — the only hits are the class itself and the module-docstring inventory at `_backend.py:11-19`). A tested, documented, maintained capability that is never invoked is a false-assurance signal: a reader auditing the backend port finds a "core uses this" promise the code never keeps.

This is the same defect class the sibling ticket `723f-c5b2-d83b-43cb` (closed, this epic) resolved — a docstring that "actively lies" about a zero-caller unit — and it resolved it by **deleting** the dead unit. No consumer needs an incremental fetch: the three tickets that `depends_on` this one (`0743`, `373f`, `fc0c`) are unrelated janitor items, and the reconciler's full-scan fetch (`fetcher.py` `_build_snapshot`) is the only fetch path in use.

## Approach

**Delete the dead declaration** so reality (a backend port with no incremental fetch) no longer needs a claim that contradicts it. This is the minimal, correctness-neutral remedy for a false-assurance finding and matches the epic's established handling of the identical defect class (`723f` deleted `bug_close_reason_ok` and the dead `_attestation` module). Because the capability has no dispatch and no implementers, removing it changes **no** externally observable reconciler behaviour — the full scan already runs unconditionally.

Two negative tests reference the Protocol and must be disposed of; both are safe to remove (removal-rationale, Chesterton's Fence):

- `test_backends_without_incremental_are_detected`
  (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_capability.py:68-69`) guards that the isinstance
  **skip branch** detects a backend lacking a capability. Triggering scenario the fence protects:
  a backend that declines a capability must not be driven through it. That scenario stays covered
  after removal by `FakeBackend` declining `SupportsLinks` — `test_fake_backend_does_not_advertise_links`
  (`:33-34`) and `test_link_sync_is_skipped_for_a_backend_without_the_capability` (`:42-48`) exercise
  the same skip branch — so deleting the incremental-specific case drops **no unique** coverage.
- `test_dc_backend_is_deliberately_not_incremental`
  (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py:85-89`) carries an explicit
  intent marker: its docstring says the assertion exists "to stop it being added by accident."
  With the `SupportsIncremental` Protocol itself removed, there is no capability to accidentally
  opt into, so the fence's purpose is fully subsumed by the deletion; the design rationale it
  recorded (no client need, and incremental fetch has its own correctness surface) is preserved in
  this ticket and in the ADR 0035 amendment below.

ADR 0035 names `SupportsIncremental` in exactly one place — the opt-in-capability prose paragraph `docs/adr/0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md:191-195`, with the symbol on `:192` ("`SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`, `SupportsIncremental`"). That paragraph and the summary at `:259` also assert a "**three** opt-in capability Protocols" **count**, which becomes two once the capability is removed. ADRs are durable records, so this is an **amendment**, not a text deletion, using the repo's established `> **AMENDED by [rebar:<id>]**` convention already present in that file.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py` — delete the `SupportsIncremental` class
  (`:545-553`) and drop `:class:\`SupportsIncremental\`` from the module-docstring opt-in inventory
  (`:11-19`), leaving `SupportsLinks` and `SupportsComments`.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_capability.py` — remove the `SupportsIncremental`
  import (`:16`) and delete `test_backends_without_incremental_are_detected` (`:68-69`); retain the
  `SupportsLinks` skip-path tests unchanged.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py` — remove the
  `SupportsIncremental` import (`:35`) and delete `test_dc_backend_is_deliberately_not_incremental`
  (`:85-89`); retain `test_dc_backend_advertises_its_three_capabilities` (`:78-82`) unchanged.
- `docs/adr/0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md` — amend the opt-in-capability paragraph
  (`:191-195`, symbol at `:192`) and the "three ... capability Protocols" count at `:191` and
  `:259` via the `> **AMENDED by [rebar:1de3-a19f-c4ea-4b28]**` convention.

No adapter or fetcher file is touched: there is nothing to implement.

## Testing

This is a dead-code removal that adds no new runtime behaviour, so the verification is a regression check plus a coverage-preservation check, both at the in-process unit tier against the real Protocols and backends:

- **Regression oracle.** After the edits, the reconciler capability suite is green:
  `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_capability.py tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py`
  collects and passes with the two deleted tests gone and no import error for the removed symbol.
- **Coverage-preservation oracle (the fence).** `test_link_sync_is_skipped_for_a_backend_without_the_capability`
  still collects and passes, proving the isinstance skip branch — a backend declining a capability
  is not driven through it — remains covered by the retained `SupportsLinks` negative case.
- **Absence oracle.** `grep -rq "SupportsIncremental" src/ tests/` exits non-zero, proving the
  declaration and every test reference are gone (the only surviving reference is the amended ADR
  prose under `docs/`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The `SupportsIncremental` class is removed from `_backend.py`
      (verified: `grep -rq "class SupportsIncremental" src/` exits non-zero — no match).
- [x] The `_backend.py` module-docstring opt-in-capability inventory (`:11-19`) no longer names
      `SupportsIncremental` and lists only `SupportsLinks` and `SupportsComments`
      (verified by reading the docstring).
- [x] `test_backends_without_incremental_are_detected` and the `SupportsIncremental` import are
      removed from `test_backend_capability.py`, and the retained skip-path tests
      `test_fake_backend_does_not_advertise_links` and
      `test_link_sync_is_skipped_for_a_backend_without_the_capability` still pass
      (verified: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_capability.py` is green).
- [x] `test_dc_backend_is_deliberately_not_incremental` and the `SupportsIncremental` import are
      removed from `test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py`, and
      `test_dc_backend_advertises_its_three_capabilities` still passes
      (verified: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py` is green).
- [x] ADR 0035's opt-in-capability paragraph (`:191-195`, symbol at `:192`) and its "three ...
      capability Protocols" count at `:191` and `:259` are amended via the
      `> **AMENDED by [rebar:1de3-a19f-c4ea-4b28]**` convention to record that `SupportsIncremental`
      was removed as a zero-implementer, unwired capability (count now two), with a one-line note
      that an updated-since fetch can be reintroduced from vendor support (Jira JQL `updated >`,
      GitHub `since=`, Linear `updatedAt`) if a measured bandwidth need later arises
      (verified by reading the amended ADR).
- [x] No reference to `SupportsIncremental` remains in `src/` or `tests/`
      (verified: `grep -rq "SupportsIncremental" src/ tests/` exits non-zero — no match; the only
      surviving reference is the amended ADR under `docs/`).
baseline.summary: Remove the dead SupportsIncremental capability (zero implementers, false docstring)
