# S6 — Monitoring, back-out, and live E2E proof + docs

Part of epic 1fa8 (CI as a second Gerrit gate vote via gerrit-to-platform → GitHub Actions).

## Why
The PoC's success criterion is proving the two-vote gate end-to-end on the live Gerrit, with the
operability a real gate needs: failure alarms and a tested back-out. This story activates the gate
(after the voter is proven) and demonstrates the whole flow.

## What
Add a CloudWatch alarm for g2p dispatch + `Verified`-vote failures, a tested back-out, activate the
two-vote submit requirement, run the live end-to-end proof, and document the flow + design notes.

## Scope
- Monitoring (Terraform alarm + `infra/scripts/observability.sh` metric), back-out procedure,
  `CONTRIBUTING.md`, design notes. Gated on S1–S5.
- Out of scope: the individual component builds (S1–S5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Add a CloudWatch alarm for g2p hook-dispatch failures and `Verified`-vote failures — publish
      the metric from a journald log pattern via `infra/scripts/observability.sh` (modeled on the
      `voter_errors` metric behind `monitoring_s4b.tf`); name the log source, pattern, and metric.
- [ ] Document and TEST a back-out: disabling the `Verified` submit requirement restores
      single-vote (`LLM-Review`-only) gating if g2p/CI is broken.
- [ ] Activate the two-vote submit requirement (authored in S1) now that the voter is proven.
- [ ] Live E2E on the Gerrit host: a red CI blocks submit; `recheck` re-runs; a green change with
      BOTH votes submits and replicates to GitHub `main`. Record the change URL + both votes.
- [ ] Update `CONTRIBUTING.md` (two-vote flow + `recheck`) and capture design notes (cost / latency
      budget, flaky-test handling, `copyCondition` re-run behavior).
baseline.summary: S6 — Monitoring, back-out, and live E2E proof + docs

baseline.description:
## Why

The plan-review attestation's freshness is currently bound to the exact code HEAD sha (`attest.py` `claim_gate_check` step 3: `result.head_sha != head` → `stale-head`). This is too coarse in BOTH directions:

- **Over-invalidation (child bug `worm-folly-barge`):** ANY commit — even an unrelated file or a
  docs typo — invalidates a freshly-earned, still-correct attestation, forcing a slow (~3-5 min),
  billable re-review for no semantic reason. Especially painful on multi-ticket branches and
  shared-checkout test runs that move HEAD.
- **Under-invalidation (this epic's core goal):** the binding is to the WHOLE commit, not to the
  code the review was actually grounded against, so the design also fails to model "the cited code
  drifted" precisely.

Fix: scope attestation freshness to **what the review depended on, not who/what changed the rest of the tree** — the content of the dependency files — using a content-addressed (Merkle) binding. This matches the consensus of every sound incremental-staleness system (Gerrit `copyCondition` `has:unchanged-files`, Bazel input-hashing, proof-caching dependency checksums). No per-commit attribution, so the "sibling exemption" concern dissolves: a sibling's edit to a shared file is treated exactly like any other edit.

## What

- **Dependency set** = union of the ticket's declared `file_impact` and the files cited in the
  review's findings (whole-file granularity). The cited files are extracted **at sign time from the
  in-memory verdict** — each finding's `citations[]` entries with `kind == "file"` (the
  `CITATION_KINDS` vocabulary in `findings.py`) contribute their `path`. They are NOT read back from
  the persisted `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar, whose `_slim` form drops citation paths; and they are never
  needed at claim time (the claim check reads the signed map, below).
- **Content-addressed binding:** at sign time, compute a `{path: content-hash}` map of the
  dependency set and store it **inside the signed manifest** (`build_manifest` / `sign_plan_review`)
  so drift detection is tamper-evident. (Today `head_sha` is recorded as audit metadata but is NOT
  in the signed payload — this also closes that latent integrity gap.)
  - **Hash algorithm/format:** SHA-256 over the **raw file bytes** (no newline/whitespace
    normalization); binary and large files are hashed the same way (no special-casing). A path in the
    set that does not exist on disk is recorded with a fixed `"absent"` sentinel hash, so a later
    deletion (absent→present or present→absent) is a detectable change.
  - **Content source:** the **working-tree, on-disk** file content (what `review-plan` actually reads
    when it grounds the review), at BOTH sign time and claim time — NOT the committed git-blob at
    HEAD. This is why the binding is HEAD-move/rebase immune: only the bytes the review saw matter.
- **Drift check at claim:** replace the whole-HEAD exact-match (`claim_gate_check` step 3) with a
  per-file content-hash comparison. Any mismatch / deletion / unexpected-creation of a dependency
  file = drift → block the claim (invalidate), prompting re-review. Content-addressing makes this
  ancestry-independent (immune to rebases and shared-checkout HEAD moves — the specific
  `worm-folly-barge` complaint).
- **Empty-set conservative fallback:** when the dependency set is empty (no `file_impact` AND no
  citations — common; this very epic has `file_impact: []`), we cannot scope, so fall back to
  invalidate-on-any-commit (today's safe behavior, but now ONLY for unscopable tickets).
- **New named DET-floor check (`P9` file-impact coverage):** `det_floor.py` currently has P1–P8; P4
  checks only the file-impact UPPER bound (`fi > cap`), not empty. Add a new, explicitly named check
  that, for **leaf tasks only** (`applies_at`), emits an **advisory finding (never blocks)** when
  `file_impact` is empty, advising the caller to specify the `{path, reason}` files this work will
  touch — so the attestation can be scoped to them (otherwise any commit invalidates it) and
  `next_batch` can schedule it conflict-free. Register it in `CANONICAL_DET`, the completeness guard,
  and the module docstring.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` — `build_manifest` / `sign_plan_review` (embed the signed
  `{path: content-hash}` map); `claim_gate_check` (replace step-3 whole-HEAD match with the per-file
  drift check; `head_sha` / `signed_at` remain audit metadata only).
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` — new `p9_file_impact_coverage` advisory check, added to
  the `DET_CHECKS` tuple + the module docstring.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py` — add `"P9"` to the `CANONICAL_DET` tuple and the
  completeness guard (these live in `registry.py`, NOT `det_floor.py`).
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py` — resolve the dependency set at sign time
  (`file_impact` via `get_file_impact` ∪ the verdict findings' `kind=="file"` citation `path`s).
- Tests under the plan-review test suite.

Out of scope (Story 2): the narrowed delta-re-review on drift. This story always falls back to a FULL re-review when drift invalidates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The attestation binds a SIGNED `{path: content-hash}` map of the dependency set
      (`file_impact` ∪ review-cited files); the whole-HEAD exact-match staleness check is removed.
- [ ] Claim SUCCEEDS when an unrelated file changed after signing (fixes `worm-folly-barge`); claim
      is BLOCKED when a dependency file's content changed or was deleted (closes under-invalidation).
- [ ] Empty dependency set → conservative invalidate-on-any-commit fallback.
- [ ] New explicitly named DET check (`P9`) emits an advisory (non-blocking) warning on empty
      `file_impact` at leaf tasks, with guidance text; registered in `CANONICAL_DET` + completeness
      guard + module docstring. (Confirmed P4 does not already cover empty.)
- [ ] The drift check is content-addressed (rebase / HEAD-move immune) and cheap; a **test measures**
      it (times `claim_gate_check`'s drift step over a representative dependency set, e.g. ~30 files,
      and asserts it stays in low single-digit ms) and asserts the claim path makes no LLM/network
      call — the perf claim is verified, not just asserted.
- [ ] The signed manifest serializes the dependency binding as a **per-path `{path: content-hash}`
      map** (NOT a single rolled-up root hash), so Story 2 (`grace-thud-feint`) can attach a
      per-finding code-hash vintage + reuse map on top of it. This payload shape is the contract
      fixed in ADR `0002-code-drift-invalidation.md`.
- [ ] **Claim-path check reads the SIGNED map, not a re-derived set.** At claim time the drift check
      iterates the `{path: hash}` entries IN the signed manifest and re-hashes exactly those paths —
      it does NOT recompute `file_impact ∪ citations` from current ticket state. (Re-deriving would
      let a post-sign `file_impact` shrink silently drop paths from the check and evade drift
      detection; the signed map is the authoritative, tamper-evident set.)
- [ ] **Citation extraction is schema-correct.** The "cited files" half of the dependency set is
      taken from the structured citation `path` (`kind == "file"`) on the **in-memory verdict's**
      findings at sign time (the persisted `REVIEW_RESULT` `_slim` sidecar drops paths, so it is NOT
      the source); a citation with no resolvable `path` is ignored (fall back to `file_impact`)
      rather than guessed. Verify the actual findings/citation schema and
      use the structured field; if none exists, that gap is part of this story's work.
- [ ] Tested: review at X, commit an unrelated file → claim succeeds; commit a dependency file →
      claim blocked; delete a dependency file → blocked; empty-set ticket → any commit blocks; `P9`
      fires on empty `file_impact` and is silent when populated.
baseline.summary: Code-drift detection + invalidation: content-addressed attestation freshness scoped to the review's dependency files (+ P9 empty-file-impact DET warning)

baseline.description:
## Context

During execution-phase plan review, batched overlap-judge calls took 216–311 seconds and returned oversized malformed JSON with runaway candidate_id content. The final catch safely abstained, but only after multiple long generations. Phase 1 proved the overlap call inherits generic 16,000-token, three-structured-attempt, four-transport-attempt, and 600-second-per-request budgets; it declares no overlap-local limits. The original 9022 story and ADR 0086 require a bounded advisory classifier whose timeout/error/malformed output degrades promptly to abstention. Runtime evidence is recorded in `rebar:22da-e9a6-63e7-49e5` comment timestamp 1786251659444495001; the c403 live valid six-candidate/599-output-token evidence is recorded in `rebar:c403-cc3a-2c6d-4b9d` comments.

## Proven root cause

`judge_batch` builds a native structured `RunRequest` without operation-local output, structured-retry, transport-retry, or timeout bounds. Generic runner policy therefore permits three full structured generations and transport retries before the advisory catch executes. A token cap alone still retried three times; schema validation alone acted only after the oversized payload existed. The durable runtime proof is recorded in the Phase 1 RCA comment cited above.

## Repair plan

- Extend the internal `RunRequest` budget contract with lowering-only per-request seams for structured-output retries, transport attempts, and request timeout, preserving current defaults for every existing caller. Keep `output_token_limit` as the existing lowering-only output seam.
- In `runner._effective_config(base, req)`, lower `timeout_s` and `llm_retry_max_attempts` before `run()` calls `_pai_model(cfg)`. The resulting effective `LLMConfig` therefore reaches `anthropic_model.py` / `bedrock_model.py` transport construction, including an injected/shared `PydanticAIRunner`, because that runner reconstructs the model/provider for each `run(req)`.
- Apply the request-local structured-retry seam separately in both native and prompted branches of `_pai_structured`; apply the existing output-token seam through `build_model_settings`.
- Give overlap judge calls explicit advisory budgets: 1,024 output tokens (the c403 live valid six-candidate response used 599), one structured attempt, one transport attempt, and a 60-second request timeout. Any bound hit continues through the existing logged safe-abstention path.
- Preserve valid verdict demultiplexing and aggregation behavior byte-for-byte outside budget metadata.

## Testing

- Unit/contract tier through the real `judge_batch` → `PydanticAIRunner` structured path with a deterministic FunctionModel. Prove the fixture reaches malformed runaway output, the current path is RED by making three attempts/inheriting 16K, and the repaired path makes one bounded attempt then returns exact all-candidate abstention.
- Settings-seam tests prove `_effective_config` lowers timeout/transport policy before model construction, while callers omitting limits retain current settings.
- Negative control: a valid six-candidate verdict under the bounded request retains label-keyed mapping and relation behavior.
- Mutation: remove the overlap-local limits and confirm the held-out oracle returns RED.
- Original-path replication: run an overlap-enabled plan-review scenario and record elapsed time, output size/finish reason, abstention result, and timestamp on this ticket; confirm no fabricated overlap finding.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A runaway overlap response is capped at 1,024 output tokens; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py -k runaway`.
- [x] A malformed overlap response makes one structured generation; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py -k runaway`.
- [x] A failed overlap request makes one transport attempt; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py -k transport_attempt`.
- [x] An overlap request carries a 60-second request timeout; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py -k request_budget`.
- [x] Timeout, truncation, and malformed output each return exact all-candidate abstention; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py -k bounded_abstention`.
- [x] Valid batched verdicts retain label-keyed mapping and aggregation; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py`.
- [x] Callers omitting request-local limits retain existing policy; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_settings_builders_seam.py tests/unit/test_runner_hardening.py`.
- [x] The held-out oracle returns RED when the overlap-local limits are removed; checked by the recorded mutation run.
- [x] Focused tests, `make lint`, and `make typecheck` exit 0.
- [x] An overlap-enabled original-path replication abstains within the declared bound and returns no fabricated overlap finding; evidence recorded on `rebar:22da-e9a6-63e7-49e5` with elapsed time, output/finish diagnostic, result, and timestamp.
baseline.summary: Bound overlap-judge output and latency on malformed candidate-id responses

# The Gerrit review bot cannot invoke Bedrock: LLM-Review fail-closes on every change

Since the eb6e Bedrock cutover went live, the review bot's `base` step dies with a 403 and the bot casts a fail-closed `LLM-Review -1`. **Nothing can land through Gerrit** — the `LLM-Review +1` gate is one of the two required votes and only the bot can cast it.

## Evidence

Change 1331, patch set 1 (2026-08-04 00:45:54Z):

    [LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (llm-unavailable)]
    step 'base' failed: status_code: 403, model_name: us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8
    User: arn:aws:sts::896586841071:assumed-role/rebar-gerrit-instance-role/i-00880b2c7f13527c5
    is not authorized to perform: bedrock:InvokeModel on resource:
    arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1:896586841071:inference-profile/us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8
    with an explicit deny in an identity-based policy

    Automatic retries exhausted (1 attempt(s)) — casting the fail-closed -1.

## It is a regression, and the window is tight

 * change 1330 got `LLM-Review +1` at **00:28:44Z** — the bot was healthy.
 * change 1331 got the 403 at **00:45:54Z**.

The cutover (`eb6e`, merged as `5892134975`) fills `REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL` with `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` in `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:186`. The review gate's `base` step is the `frontier` class, so it is the first thing the cutover re-points and the first thing to hit the deny.

## What I ruled out — the deny is NOT in the role

Read the instance role directly (`joe_frontier`, same account 896586841071):

 * inline `rebar-gerrit-bedrock-converse` **ALLOWS** `bedrock:InvokeModel` on
   `arn:aws:bedrock:*:896586841071:inference-profile/*.anthropic.claude-*`, which matches the
   requested resource, and on `arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/anthropic.claude-*`.
 * the other two inline policies (`rebar-gerrit-cloudwatch-basic`, `rebar-gerrit-ssm-params-read`)
   contain no `Deny` and no bedrock action.
 * the only attached managed policy is `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore`.
 * `PermissionsBoundary: None`.

So there is **no deny anywhere in this role's identity policies**. The explicit deny is being applied from outside the role — an org-level SCP or a similar account-wide guardrail — which is why it cannot be fixed by editing the role.

**CI's Bedrock access is unaffected**, which localises it further: the `external LLM (live bedrock)` arm of run 30857265932 succeeded at 22:04Z under the separate `rebar-external-ci-bedrock` role. Only the Gerrit instance role is denied.

## Two candidate fixes (needs an operator decision — I did not act on production infra)

 1. **Amend the org/SCP guardrail** to permit `bedrock:InvokeModel` on the opus-4-8 inference
    profile for `rebar-gerrit-instance-role`. Requires AWS admin.
 2. **Pull the documented kill switch** — `docker-compose.yml:160-163` records it as purely
    subtractive: delete the three `REBAR_LLM_*_MODEL` lines and recreate the container, and rebar
    resolves the classes back to the direct-Anthropic defaults. Restores reviews immediately;
    reverts the cutover's benefit. Needs SSM/SSH to the Gerrit host.

A third, narrower option if only opus is denied: re-point `REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL` at the sonnet profile that the standard class already uses — but that is unverified, because the deny's source is unknown and may cover every Claude profile for this role. Do not assume it is opus-only without testing.
## Acceptance criteria — VOID (operator ruling: maintenance window)

These were written on the assumption that the 403 was a permissions regression from the eb6e cutover. The operator has since confirmed the review bot was in a planned MAINTENANCE WINDOW, now resolved, so there is no deny to find and no fix to choose. The criteria are void rather than met, and are recorded struck through so the reasoning stays auditable.

- [x] ~~the source of the explicit deny is identified and named~~ [operator-attested] there is no
      explicit deny; the 403 was maintenance, not policy
- [x] ~~a change pushed to Gerrit receives a real LLM-Review verdict~~ [operator-attested] the bot
      is confirmed healthy again by the operator
- [x] ~~whichever fix is chosen, the outcome is recorded here~~ [operator-attested] no fix was
      required and no infrastructure was touched
baseline.summary: Gerrit review bot 403s on Bedrock: LLM-Review fail-closes on every change, nothing can land

## Summary

`rebar criteria eval <project.criterion>` (and the underlying `calibrate_criterion`) cannot run the LIVE calibration of any project criterion whose logical id contains the `project.` namespace dot, because the physical prompt-id → criterion-id round-trip is lossy.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Activate a project criterion via `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` (e.g.
   `project.portability`, `exec: 1-TURN`) with a rubric prompt and an eval fixture
   at `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml`.
2. Run `rebar criteria eval project.portability --runs 1 --output json`.

Expected: the criterion runs live over the dataset and prints calibration metrics.

Actual: exits non-zero with `ValueError: no eval solver for prompt 'plan-review-project-portability'` from `eval_solver.run_case`.

## Root Cause

`rebar.llm.evals.eval.calibrate_criterion` computes `prompt_id = criterion_prompt_id("project.portability")` = `plan-review-project-portability` (the forward map replaces `.`→`-`) to load the eval fixture (correct). But the default `_criterion_solver.solve(prompt_id, case)` passes that DASH prompt-id to `eval_solver.run_case`, which resolves the criterion via `_criterion_id(prompt_id)`: it strips the `plan-review-` prefix to `project-portability` (dash) and checks `cid in registry.by_id(repo_root)`. The registry is keyed by the LOGICAL id `project.portability` (dot), so the dash form is never found → `_criterion_id` returns None → `run_case` raises `no eval solver`. Built-in ids (no dot) round-trip fine; only namespaced `project.<name>` criteria break. Confirmed: `_criterion_id("plan-review-project-portability", root)` → None, while `_criterion_id("project.portability", root)` → "project.portability".

## Proposed Fix (one of)

- `_criterion_solver` / `calibrate_criterion`: resolve the criterion in `run_case` from
  the ORIGINAL logical `criterion_id` (dot), using the dash `prompt_id` only for
  `load_eval_spec`; or
- `eval_solver._criterion_id`: after stripping `plan-review-`, also try mapping a leading
  `project-<name>` back to `project.<name>` (the namespaced project-criterion inverse),
  since `<name>` has no dots.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar criteria eval <project.criterion>` resolves and runs the project criterion's
      Pass-1 finder over its dataset (no `no eval solver` error), for a criterion whose
      logical id contains the `project.` namespace dot.
- [ ] A regression test drives `calibrate_criterion` (or `eval_solver.run_case`) for an
      activated `project.<name>` criterion with an injected/fake runner and asserts the
      criterion resolves (fires/does-not-fire per the fake), proving the physical→logical
      round-trip. File: `tests/unit/test_criteria_eval.py` (or a sibling).
- [ ] Built-in criterion calibration (e.g. `F1`) is unchanged (no regression).
baseline.summary: Live criteria-eval cannot resolve namespaced project criteria (dash/dot round-trip)

baseline.description:
## Why

Both link bugs were invisible in telemetry: the batch outcome reports mutation-level `error=None` and "applied N of N" but never the per-sub-op counts, so a link/comment/label that silently no-ops (or fails non-fatally, logged only to stderr) leaves the pass green. The inbound applier already returns `links_applied`; the outbound batch path does not. Make a silent no-op fail loudly — safely.

## What

- Surface `links_applied`, `comments_applied`, `labels_applied` in the **structured outbound batch outcome** (queryable, not only logged) and the `RECON:` line — parity with the inbound applier's existing `links_applied`.
- Add a **silent-no-op canary**: when a mutation carries N sub-ops of a kind but `applied == 0`, that is a failure condition (`computed > 0 && applied == 0`), surfaced in the outcome/telemetry and asserted by a test that would have caught the link drop.
- **Rollout safety:** the fail-loud invariant lands **warn-first** — emit telemetry + a `WARNING` behind a flag/canary — and is promoted to hard-fail only after a baseline pass that emits zero such warnings. Reverting to warn is a flag flip, no other code change. This avoids hard-failing production syncs on a false positive.
- Sequencing: depends on story D (the single consolidated applier) so the counts come from one path.
- Out of scope (justified): making the threshold itself configurable — the simple `computed > 0 && applied == 0` invariant IS the contract; only enforce-vs-warn is flagged. A configurable threshold is YAGNI.

## Scope

- In: outcome/telemetry plumbing in `batch_dispatch.py` / `applier.py` / `reconcile.py`; the canary test; the warn-first flag.
- Out: the probe wiring (story F); applier consolidation (story D).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The structured outbound batch outcome and the `RECON:` line surface `links_applied`, `comments_applied`, `labels_applied`.
- [ ] A test asserts that a mutation with computed sub-ops > 0 but applied == 0 fails (reproduces what the link drop would have triggered).
- [ ] The fail-loud invariant rolls out warn-first (telemetry + `WARNING`) behind a flag; promotion to hard-fail and reversion to warn are a flag flip with no other code change.
- [ ] Sync semantics are otherwise unchanged (telemetry + guard only); the full reconciler suite is green.
- [ ] The canary asserts the count invariant, not specific log strings (anti-change-detector).
baseline.summary: Surface outbound sub-op telemetry + silent-no-op canary

baseline.description:
## What

Generate `docs/mcp-reference.md` from the MCP server's OWN registrars, correctly classified by gate, and gate it in CI. Mirrors the `gen_env_registry.py` generator + drift-gate pattern.

## Source of truth (verified — registration-time vs call-time gating)
The server (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py` `build_server()`) assembles THREE registrars:
- `register_read_tools` (`_mcp_reads.py`) — 23 tools, ALWAYS registered.
- `register_llm_tools` (`_mcp_llm.py`) — 6 tools, ALWAYS registered; gated at CALL time on
  `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM`.
- `register_write_tools` (`_mcp_writes.py`) — 18 tools, CONDITIONALLY registered: returns
  early when `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` is truthy, so they are ABSENT from `list_tools()` in
  read-only mode. Totals verified: 47 tools (readonly off) / 29 (readonly on).

**Critical:** only `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` changes list membership. `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` and `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC` are call-time only (tools always listed, refuse at call). So a naive single `list_tools()` in ambient env silently produces a PARTIAL reference. The generator MUST enumerate each registrar with `REBAR_MCP_READONLY=0` so writes register.

## Classification rule (deterministic — registrar default + closed 3-entry special-case table)
There is NO per-tool gate attribute, and `readOnlyHint`/`destructiveHint` do NOT map to the env gate. Classify by which registrar registers the tool, then apply the closed override table:
| Group (registrar) | Default gate | Special-case overrides |
|---|---|---|
| READS | none (always available) | `reconcile` -> mutating modes blocked by `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` FIRST, then require `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC` (BOTH gate live mode; dry-run always works); `fsck` -> recover path gated by `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` |
| LLM | `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` (call-time) | `sign_review` -> `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` (HYBRID: in the LLM registrar but write-gated, makes no LLM call) |
| WRITES | `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` (registration-time; absent when readonly) | `run_workflow` -> write-gated by `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` AND, for a non-dry-run workflow that HAS LLM steps, additionally gated at call time by `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` (a second hybrid) |

This special-case table is CLOSED at FOUR entries (`reconcile`, `fsck`, `sign_review`, `run_workflow`); the generator carries them explicitly and a drift check asserts these four names still exist in their expected registrars, so a new hybrid is caught rather than silently misclassified. `sign_manifest` is a WRITE-registrar tool (not the LLM `sign_review` — do not conflate). Gate descriptions come from the `MCP_ENV_VARS` constant (`mcp_server.py`), the same source `rebar-mcp --help` uses, so the doc cannot drift from `--help`.

## Scope
- Add `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` (new): enumerate each registrar onto its own FastMCP
  with `REBAR_MCP_READONLY=0` (writes register); read each tool's name + first-line summary
  (from `.description`); classify via the table above; emit `docs/mcp-reference.md` with a
  generated header and exactly THREE clearly-labeled gate-tier sections:
  **Read-only (always)**, **LLM-gated (`REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM`)**, and
  **Write-gated (`REBAR_MCP_READONLY`)**. The three special cases are inline ANNOTATIONS,
  NOT separate sections: `reconcile` under Read-only annotated "live/mutating modes blocked by
  `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` and require `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC`"; `fsck` under Read-only annotated "recover path gated by
  `REBAR_MCP_READONLY`"; `sign_review` under Write-gated (NOT LLM-gated) annotated "hybrid: in the LLM registrar,
  write-gated"; `run_workflow` under Write-gated annotated "live LLM-step workflows also
  require `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM`". Include the `MCP_ENV_VARS` gate descriptions.
- `--check` drift mode + CI gate in BOTH `.github/workflows/test.yml` AND
  `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` (the actual Verified gate; a parity test
  `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` enforces every `scripts/*.py` in test.yml also
  appears in gerrit-verify.yaml — omitting it breaks `make test`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/mcp-reference.md` is generated (marked generated) from the live registrars and
      lists all 47 tools (23 read + 6 llm + 18 write).
- [ ] Tools are structurally separated into labeled sections by gate tier (NOT prose) — a

## Context
The 884-unit hardening oracle invokes production `_convert` once per unit. `_convert` currently resolves `reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s` on every invocation. A runtime trace on current origin/main d05bf2bc1be observed 100 Pandoc plus 102 `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` subprocesses for 100 conversions; resolving once at the render-pass boundary preserved identical outputs and reduced the trace to 100 Pandoc plus 3 one-time root probes. The prior 884-unit trace observed 1,770 total Popen calls (884 Pandoc + 886 root discovery). This is separate from the copied legacy oracle removed by absolute-diplomatic-snowyowl.

## Contract and prior disposition
- Preserve all real Pandoc calls, corpus units, byte expectations, timeout configurability, per-unit fallback, timeout, and process-group reap behavior.
- absolute-diplomatic-snowyowl approved immutable outputs only for the copied legacy side and retained all 884 real production conversions. harmless-wavy-osprey approved session-scoped sharing that reduced duplicate work, while coercive-paediatric-bug rejected parallelism that does not reduce aggregate runner usage. No tracker ticket rejects render-pass configuration injection.
- Full replacement of product Pandoc calls remains out of scope because ADR 0095 requires the real pinned boundary in every conversion assertion.

## OSS consensus research (2026-08-14)
All three surveyed projects are active, unarchived, and popular: Django (88,426 stars; pushed 2026-08-13) lazily resolves each setting and caches it in `LazySettings.__dict__`; Black (41,804 stars; pushed 2026-08-10) reads pyproject configuration at CLI setup and passes resolved `mode` into multi-file workers; pytest (14,416 stars; pushed 2026-08-12) exposes its resolved Config as a session-scoped `pytestconfig` fixture. Consensus is 3/3 for resolving loop/session invariants once and passing them to repeated work.

## Plan
1. Add a held-out behavioral oracle with three proven renderable units and assert exactly one `_pandoc_timeout()` resolution for the whole render pass.
2. Resolve timeout once in `render_markdown_to_wiki`; pass it through `_render_unit` and `_convert` using optional parameters so direct two-argument callers retain safe default behavior. The direct `_render_unit` caller at test_wiki_render_corpus.py:325 remains valid.
3. Update the two `_convert` monkeypatch stand-ins at test_wiki_render.py:268/278 to accept the optional argument supplied by the public render path.
4. In the 884-unit direct hardening loop, resolve timeout once outside the loop and pass it to `_convert`; keep exact expected bytes and all 884 real Pandoc invocations.
5. Run held-out RED -> fixer -> GREEN, defect-seeded RED, focused hardening/corpus tests, lint, typecheck, and paired subprocess/timing measurement. The fresh-process measurement must observe 884 Pandoc launches, exactly one timeout resolution, and at most 3 one-time Git-root probes.
6. Push through Gerrit; merge only after LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, no unresolved comments, then record CI and runner savings. Back-out is a Gerrit revert restoring per-call timeout resolution.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A render pass with three renderable units calls `_pandoc_timeout()` exactly once.
- [ ] The hardening oracle launches all 884 real production Pandoc conversions.
- [ ] A fresh 884-unit trace launches at most 3 `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` probes.
- [ ] Non-default timeout configuration remains observable between separate render passes.
- [ ] Per-unit timeout fallback behavior remains covered.
- [ ] Pandoc stdin and argv behavior remains covered.
- [ ] Byte-equivalence to all 884 immutable expected outputs remains covered.
- [ ] Whole-process-group reap behavior remains covered.
- [ ] Held-out RED/GREEN and exact defect-seeded RED are recorded.
- [ ] Before/after subprocess counts and wall time quantify savings without claiming more than the evidence.
- [ ] Focused tests, lint, and typecheck pass.
- [ ] LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 pass before merge.
- [ ] Final report cites OSS sources and prior-ticket dispositions.

## Context / Problem

`tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_acli_field_coverage.py` cites "epic 3a03" in short, four-hex form at lines 10, 13, and 414. In this repository `3a03` resolves to `3a03-9863-542e-4ae1`, an unrelated closed bug about the `_no_repo_root_leaks` test-isolation guard. A reader following the citation lands on the wrong ticket, so the provenance of the ACLI contract-regression tests is effectively lost.

The verified source is the pre-extraction DSO epic `3a03-b3f2-b34c-4e4f` (closed, 24 children, "level-triggered reconciler"), recorded in the DSO ticket-data mining report stored on the tickets branch under `63cc-ec94-4792-464b`. Evidence for that attribution:

- The citations arrived verbatim in `b534f47a7f` ("Extract DSO ticket system + Jira reconciler
  into standalone rebar", 2026-06-08), so they name DSO ids, not rebar ids.
- The same file and `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_graph.py` cite
  sibling DSO bug ids in full form (`c916-74a1-ed06-40e4`, `4fa9-0846-519e-4c30`,
  `5010-1c6a-9387-4b5b`); none of them resolve in the rebar store either.
- `3a03-b3f2-b34c-4e4f` is the only DSO-era id beginning `3a03` recorded anywhere in this
  repository's history, and it shares the prefix the author abbreviated.

The earlier hypothesis on this ticket that the source was rebar epic `3006-e198-13db-4e1f` is disproved: `3006` was created 2026-07-03, a month after the citations landed in this repository and six weeks after the 2026-05-24 ACLI audit they describe, and its plan never mentions ACLI. Citing it would substitute one wrong reference for another.

## Approach

Rewrite the three short `epic 3a03` citations to the full DSO id `3a03-b3f2-b34c-4e4f`, labelled as a pre-extraction DSO ticket so no reader mistakes it for the rebar ticket that now owns the `3a03` prefix. This matches the full-id convention the surrounding code already uses for the sibling DSO bug ids, and it needs no new lookup table or doc. The edits are inside a module docstring and a comment banner only, so no test or assertion changes.

## Scope

- `tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_acli_field_coverage.py` — lines 10, 13, and 414: replace
  the short `epic 3a03` citation with `pre-extraction DSO epic 3a03-b3f2-b34c-4e4f`. No
  executable line, fixture, assertion, or test name changes.

No other file changes. The sibling short form `bug c916` on line 409 is left alone: it does not collide with any rebar ticket and its full id is already given on line 422.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `grep -n "3a03" tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_acli_field_coverage.py` returns three
  lines, each containing the full id `3a03-b3f2-b34c-4e4f` and none containing a bare `3a03`
  short-form citation.
- [x] Each of the three corrected citations identifies the id as a pre-extraction DSO ticket,
  verified by reading lines 10, 13, and 414.
- [x] `git diff` for the change touches only comment and docstring lines in that one file,
  verified by inspecting the diff.
- [x] `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_acli_field_coverage.py`
  passes with the same collected test count as before the edit.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass in the worktree.

## Not the same bug as [rebar:895c-3eb2-043a-4de1] — do not fold them together

While proving 895c's root cause (Bedrock rejecting an over-complex structured-output grammar), a **second, distinct** LLM failure mode surfaced in the same logs and must not be attributed to it.

### The two are separable on three independent axes

| | 895c (schema complexity) | THIS bug (overlap-judge) |
|---|---|---|
| step | `plan-review-prerequisite-verifier` | `overlap-judge` |
| duration | 180.6-185.9s (tight, 27 samples) | **312-381s** (different band) |
| `requests` recorded | **0** — no model request ever completed (pre-response 400) | **3** — real requests completed |

A pre-response 400 and a failure after three completed requests are different mechanisms. The duration bands do not overlap.

### What is known

* Recorded via the usage instrumentation landed by [rebar:aec1-76e7-bb95-4c86]: 5 occurrences,
  312-381s, `requests=3`. Overall failure rate across that sample was 64 ok / 9 failed = 12.3%.
* Separately observed in `/tmp/03ef-review6.out`: `llm call [overlap-judge] ... model=anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6 FAILED in 0.4s: status_code: 401 ... 'API key is invalid.'` — a DIFFERENT overlap-judge failure again (direct-Anthropic auth), tracked separately.
* 895c's original report also noted `UnexpectedModelBehavior: Exceeded maximum output retries (2)`
  from the overlap judge — consistent with an output/validation failure rather than a request
  rejection.

### Why it matters

`overlap-judge` deduplicates findings across reviewers. When it fails the review still proceeds, so this degrades silently — the failure is not visible in the verdict.

## Resolution (premise resolved by the fix — closed `duplicate`)

Re-measured 2026-08-11 across all 17 local `usage.jsonl` logs (1638 `overlap-judge` records, 2026-08-06T20:35Z -> 2026-08-12T01:29Z). **The 312-381s / `requests=3` failure mode no longer occurs and is now structurally unreachable.** Commit `7fa8102477` (2026-08-08, ticket [rebar:22da-e9a6-63e7-49e5]) bounded the live `judge_batch` path with `output_token_limit=1024`, `structured_retry_limit=0`, `transport_attempt_limit=1`, `request_timeout_limit_s=60`.

Splitting failures by `output_tokens` separates two disjoint populations:

| population | n | `requests` | duration | last seen |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `output_tokens`=48000 (unbounded, this bug's signature) | 135 | 3 | 186.0-465.4s | **2026-08-10T17:39:48Z** |
| `output_tokens`=1024 (bounded by 7fa8102477) | 295 | 1 | **1.5-29.8s** | 2026-08-12T01:29Z |

Bounded-path failures above 120s: zero. In the 312-381s band: zero. Of the 149 `overlap-judge` calls after 2026-08-11T18:07Z, all 67 failures are bounded and the maximum duration across every call is 24.0s. The 2026-08-09/08-10 occurrences were stale checkouts and long-lived processes still running pre-fix code — independently confirmed by [rebar:3939-d68c-6e99-498d], which reached the identical 2026-08-10T17:39 cutoff from different data.

**The original Acceptance Criteria are void with the premise**, and are recorded here rather than left as unreachable checkboxes:

- **AC1/AC2 (mechanism, by measurement) — ANSWERED.** Output-retry exhaustion, not a provider-side
  timeout and not transport retry. Every long failure carries `finish_reason=length` and exactly
  48000 output tokens = 3 attempts (pydantic-ai `OUTPUT_RETRIES=2` default) x the 16000-token
  default cap; successful calls on the same path show 16091/16036/16323/16102/32035 output tokens,
  confirming the 16k-per-request ceiling. `model=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` throughout,
  so distinct from the [rebar:2876-7958-8dee-4882] direct-Anthropic 401 misroute (0.2s) and from
  [rebar:895c-3eb2-043a-4de1]'s pre-response 400 (`requests`=0).
- **AC3 (effect on the verdict) — ANSWERED.** `judge_one` and `judge_batch` both swallow any
  exception and return `_ABSTAIN`, so an overlap-judge failure never fails a review: it silently
  disables cross-reviewer dedup for the affected pairs and duplicate findings survive into the
  verdict with no signal that dedup did not run. On the batch path the whole batch abstains
  together. The fix changed the cost of that failure (~$132 measured waste -> ~$0.02 each), not its
  semantics.
- **AC4 (regression test) — VOID.** `7fa8102477` landed its own coverage of the bounds
  (`tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py` +141 lines, plus `test_runner_hardening.py` and
  `test_settings_builders_seam.py`). A test written for this ticket would pin the same seam.

Residual, non-blocking (inherited from 3939): a batch whose legitimate verdict exceeds 1024 output tokens now abstains — an overlap-recall loss worth revisiting only if drain-abstain rates grow. The live follow-on is [rebar:b273-e0ba-f719-4f1c] (a gate run does not warn when its running build is behind the base ref), which is what made these stale-build failures read as current.

## Testing

    python -m rebar.llm.usage_log summarize .rebar/usage.jsonl   # the recorded evidence
    pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q
baseline.summary: overlap-judge LLM calls fail at 312-381s with requests=3 — a SECOND failure mode, distinct from the schema-complexity 400

baseline.description:
Split from silvern-dewy-damselfly (f4cf-60b2-41c0-4843) during its plan review.

## Problem

After a close whose completion-signature append failed, a later reader cannot reliably tell that ticket apart from one closed with the gate off. Damselfly makes the loss machine-readable in the RETURNED PAYLOAD of the call that suffered it, but that payload is ephemeral and never persisted. An agent that was not the caller, or the same agent in a later session, has no durable discriminator.

## Premise verified in code — PARTIALLY true, narrower than first written

The original draft claimed all three states are indistinguishable. That overstates it: verification found one existing discriminator, **the `COMPLETION_VERDICT` PASS sidecar** (`llm/completion_sidecar.py:202` `latest_pass_record`), emitted on EVERY completion PASS at `_commands/close_precheck.py:577-580`, before signing and before the close commits:

| state | `attestations["completion-verifier"]` | PASS sidecar |
|---|---|---|
| (a) closed, attestation valid | present | present |
| (b) closed, signature failed to persist | absent | **present** |
| (c) closed, gate OFF | absent | absent |

(b) is therefore already distinguishable via `audit/read.py:113-123`. Three caveats keep that from being a real answer: the sidecar is **reducer-ignored** (`completion_sidecar.py:10-16` — not in `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES`, so it never reaches compiled state and `rebar show` cannot see it, only the audit surface); its emit is **best-effort**, dropped with only a stderr warning (`close_precheck.py:349-355`); and `prune()` deletes it after `RETAIN_PER_TICKET = 10`.

**(c) has no discriminator at all, and that is the sharper bug.** The gate's on/off state at close time is nowhere in the store — it is read from config and discarded (`_commands/close_precheck.py:410-416`; key `verify.require_completion_verification_for_close` at `_config_schema.py:159`, default False). So "closed with no attestation" collapses these into ONE indistinguishable state:

* gate genuinely off (`close_precheck.py:416`)
* `--force` close (`close_precheck.py:417`)
* config unreadable → `gate_enabled` **fails OPEN** (`_commands/gates.py:79-87`)
* `source == "local"` unattested close (`close_precheck.py:585-586`)
* `certifiable is False` withholding (`close_precheck.py:589-600`)
* a dropped PASS sidecar

Worse, `txn.transition_core` **accepts `force_close_reason` and never uses it** (`_commands/txn.py:198` — one occurrence, silently discarded though `transition_close.py:474` passes it), so a force close leaves no durable reason. Tracked separately as defiant-orthoclase-buck. The close STATUS event records only `status`, `current_status`, `parent_status_uuid` and present-only `close_class` (`txn.py:277-296`; `docs/event-schema.md:47`).

## Direction

Record, on the close STATUS event, WHY a completion signature was or was not expected — in the same locked write that already commits the close (`txn.transition_core`), so NO additional lock acquisition is needed. That is the whole point: an audit comment or a second event would append through the same `event_append` -> `write_lock` path whose 60s timeout causes the failure being recorded, and would be missing exactly when it matters.

**It must be an ENUM, not a boolean.** A single bool cannot separate the states the ACs demand. The field is `completion_expectation`, total over the close path:

| value | meaning at close time |
|---|---|
| `required` | the gate ran and a completion signature was expected |
| `disposition` | a bug closed `duplicate`/`not_a_bug`/`escalated` naming a live replacement: `_completion_precheck` returns a DISPOSITION verdict (`close_precheck.py:441-446`) that IS signed, but is not a completion PASS and must not read as one |
| `gate_off` | `verify.require_completion_verification_for_close` was false |
| `gate_unreadable` | the config could not be read and `gate_enabled` **failed OPEN** (`_commands/gates.py:79-87`), skipping the gate with only a stderr warning — a FAULT, and recording it as `gate_off` would launder it into a policy choice |
| `force_bypassed` | `--force` skipped the gate by operator approval |
| `local_source` | unattested local-source close (`close_precheck.py:585-586`) |
| `not_certifiable` | `certifiable is False` withholding (`close_precheck.py:589-600`) |
| `not_applicable` | `idea -> closed`: a REJECT/DROP, not a completion |

**The event records the EXPECTATION only, never the outcome.** The outcome is not knowable at that point: the STATUS event commits BEFORE signing is attempted, which is the ordering that causes this whole bug family. A reader derives the three states by combining the durable expectation with the durable attestation:

* `required` + completion attestation present -> closed and signed
* `required` + attestation absent -> **closed with the signature LOST** (the state damselfly
  can only report ephemerally)
* `disposition` + attestation present -> closed and signed as a DISPOSITION, not a verified
  completion (the manifest's first line carries `DISPOSITION <class>`)
* `disposition` + attestation absent -> a disposition close whose signature was lost
* anything else -> not expected, and the value says exactly why

**How the value is computed and threaded.** It is NOT `verified_result`. That is `None` for a `--force` close even though a signature WAS expected, and `None` for gate-off, so it conflates the very states this ticket separates. `close_precheck` already distinguishes all six cases at the points cited above but discards the distinction, returning only a verdict-or-`None`. So: `_completion_precheck` returns the expectation alongside its verdict, `close_ticket` passes it into `txn.transition_core`, and `transition_core` — which today accepts no such parameter — gains one and writes it into the STATUS event `data` next to the present-only `close_class` (`txn.py:287-288`), following that field's present-only precedent.

**Reduced state, not just the event.** AC2 requires a reader to work from reduced state, so the field must be folded and declared, not merely written: `close_class` is folded by `_fold_close_class` at BOTH `*->closed` sites in `reducer/_processors.py` (the fork-winner edge and the plain edge), and declared in `schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`. `completion_expectation` follows that same path in the same change — an event field with no fold would leave AC2 unsatisfiable.

Damselfly's ephemeral `completion_signature.cause` is NOT the same vocabulary: it reports an OUTCOME to the caller, where this records an EXPECTATION durably. Where they overlap (`force_bypassed`) the spelling is deliberately shared. The field is present-only, so a reader that does not know it degrades safely — the precedent `COMPLETION_VERDICT` already follows.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `completion_expectation` is written into the close STATUS event in the SAME locked write
      as the close, taking no additional write-lock — verified by a test asserting the lock is
      acquired exactly once
- [ ] A later reader, holding no lock and reading only reduced state, separates
      closed-and-signed (`required` + attestation) from closed-with-signature-lost (`required`,
      no attestation) from closed-with-gate-off (`gate_off`) — verified by a test closing one
      ticket each way and asserting all three read back distinctly
- [ ] Each of `force_bypassed`, `local_source` and `not_certifiable` is recorded as ITSELF and
      never as `gate_off` — verified by a test per value
- [ ] `idea -> closed` records `not_applicable`, matching damselfly's rule that a REJECT/DROP
      is not a completion — verified by a test
- [ ] The expectation is computed independently of `verified_result`, so a `--force` close
      records `force_bypassed`, not gate-off — verified by a test
- [ ] The field is documented in `docs/event-schema.md` and is present-only, so a reader that
      does not know it degrades safely — verified by a test
baseline.summary: Closed-without-signature is not distinguishable from gate-off on read

## Context
Record the approved RP-04 architecture before implementation. The completed research and probes live on `relevant-liberal-xantus` and in `.joe-janitor/rp04-secrets-research.md`, `.joe-janitor/rp04-composition-readback.md`, and `.joe-janitor/rp04-adr-research-critique.md`. This child is documentation-only and must not start RP-04 implementation.

## Deliverable
Create ADR 0098, `docs/adr/0098-operation-scoped-config-and-provider-composition.md`, using this repository's ADR format and generator. The ADR records one coherent decision: Rebar composes immutable non-secret operation configuration with separately owned provider-auth/runtime bindings at application boundaries. The slug avoids the generic word `bindings`, which would incorrectly classify the application-wide decision under the reconciler workstream. The generator has no generic operation-config keyword, so its current deterministic fallback is `Other decisions`; changing that classifier is outside this documentation-only ticket.

## Plan
1. Work from a fresh worktree at current `origin/main`; reserve ADR 0098 with the generated `.numbers/0098` marker.
2. Cite the completed primary-source and maintained-OSS research for Pydantic/PydanticAI, OpenAI, Anthropic, boto3/AWS, Git credential helpers/SSH, Jira integrations, CI secret injection, subprocess environments, and Rebar's current probes. Claims about dependency behavior must point to the exact source consulted.
3. Describe the current split authorities, trust boundaries, behavioral regressions, and why configuration and authentication are related at composition time but remain separate data/capability models.
4. Record the approved decisions: operation snapshot precedence/root rules and lifecycle; CLI/MCP/Python/service composition ownership; subsystem projections; provider-native pre-client auth/session injection into Rebar-owned factories; provider-specific `SecretStr`/`SecretBytes` static carriers; no universal secret broker/keyring/cloud-secret retrieval; subprocess environment rules without global mutation; restart/redeploy static rotation; SDK-owned refresh; fail-closed decision-bearing auth; and the optional observability exception.
5. Record op-cert startup composition: exactly one path or multiline value, validation before service work, process-owned 0700/0600 copy, context-local signer/principal/push policy, no application runtime SSM/boto3/region coupling, and deployment freedom to retain SSM-at-rest before injection. Amend only ADR 0049's per-job retrieval/composition detail; preserve its algorithm, trust-root/era, producer, and deployment storage choices.
6. Explain alternatives and rejection grounds: current ambient/per-consumer loading; one secret-provider/string lookup; application-owned SSM/keyring layer; aggressively restricted child environments; global `os.environ` overlays; public constructed-client/runner replacement; per-job op-cert retrieval; and hot rotation owned by Rebar.
7. State security limits/non-goals, migration and rollback, compatibility effects, explicit behavior changes, observability/provenance constraints, and implementation verification obligations. Relate ADRs 0008, 0014, 0041, 0046, 0049, 0050, 0059, and 0083 without claiming to supersede their unaffected decisions.
8. Regenerate `docs/adr/README.md` and `.numbers/0098`; make the minimal `docs/architecture.md` update appropriate for a proposed decision under this project's conventions.
9. Run ADR-number/index/docs checks. Then perform and publish the required numbered Draft Critique: uncited claims, internal inconsistencies, missing constraints, and conflicts with existing ADRs. Resolve any mechanical/document defects, but stop before HOLD/MERGE and request explicit maintainer approval.

## Verification
- `python scripts/gen_adr_index.py --check`
- `python scripts/check_adr_numbers.py`
- The repository's documentation/lint checks applicable to changed files.
- Deterministic searches confirm no placeholder sections or merge-conflict markers in the changed ADR artifacts.
- Read the rendered diff against the approved research and every related ADR named above.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] ADR 0098 exists in project-native format and accurately records the approved operation-snapshot, provider-auth/runtime-binding, subprocess, rotation, failure, observability, and op-cert decisions.
- [x] Every external dependency/OSS behavior claim has a specific primary or repository research citation; Rebar probe claims cite the recovery artifacts or durable research ticket.
- [x] Alternatives, consequences, security limitations/non-goals, explicit behavior changes, migration, rollback, and post-cutover compatibility are concrete enough that implementation stories need not invent architectural policy.

- [x] `docs/adr/README.md` and `docs/adr/.numbers/0098` are generator-produced, collision-free, and pass their checks; `docs/architecture.md` points readers to the proposed decision without overstating implementation status.

baseline.description:
## The assertion cannot pass, even when the code is correct

`test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance` (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py:317-319`) creates an issue directly on the DC harness, runs a `bootstrap-strict` pass, then asserts:

    tickets = rebar.list_tickets(repo_root=str(dc_rebar_repo))
    matched = [t for t in tickets if remote_key in json.dumps(t)]
    assert matched, f"no local ticket was created from DC issue {remote_key}; ..."

`remote_key` is the RAW Jira key (`RBJNAZV-1`). Two facts make the match impossible:

1. **The local id is LOWERCASED.** `_jira_key_to_local_id` (`inbound_translate.py:120-124`) returns
   `"jira-" + jira_key.lower()`, so the created ticket's id is `jira-rbjnazv-1`. The `in` test is
   case-sensitive.
2. **The ticket payload carries NO raw Jira key.** `_inbound_create_write_create_event`
   (`apply_inbound_records.py:183-212`) builds `create_data` from id / ticket_type / title /
   description / parent_id / tags / priority / assignee / creation_channel. The Jira key appears only
   as a TITLE FALLBACK (`fields.get("summary","") or jira_key`), so it is absent whenever the issue
   has a summary — as it does here ("J7 provenance oracle"). The binding is recorded separately, in
   the binding store (`_inbound_create_record_binding`), which `list_tickets` does not return.

Verified directly against the payload shape the inbound path writes:

    remote_key : RBJNAZV-1
    local_id   : jira-rbjnazv-1
    ticket json contains raw remote key? False

## Why this matters more than a broken test

Observed in GitHub Actions run 30651750699 (job "jira DC harness smoke"), where it is the ONLY failure — 1 failed, 14 passed — on the first run in which the harness got far enough to reach it (the PAT-cap fix [rebar:f391-806b-938f-45d8] unblocked it).

The run reported `invariants: scanned=1` and `OK: applied 1 of 1 mutations`. The pass SAW the DC issue and applied a mutation. So the observable evidence is consistent with the inbound create having worked perfectly and the ORACLE being unable to see it.

**The consequence is that epic e369's headline acceptance criterion — "an issue created in DC appears in the local store after an inbound pass" — is UNPROVEN, not disproven.** This test is the only thing currently asserting it, and it cannot distinguish "the ticket was created" from "the ticket was not created". Whichever the truth is, the oracle has to be fixed before the epic can make a claim either way. Do NOT read this failure as evidence that inbound is broken, and do NOT read a future green as evidence that it works until the assertion actually targets something the inbound path writes.

This is the THIRD oracle-that-cannot-pass found in this epic, after `_envelope()` being asserted on writing-mode passes (which emit no JSON — corrected under bda8). The pattern is consistent: the live tests were authored against an assumed output shape rather than the one the code emits, and the defects stayed invisible because an earlier failure aborted the run before the assertion was reached.

## Approach

Assert against what the inbound path ACTUALLY produces, and assert the binding too, so a pass is evidence of the round-trip rather than of a string appearing somewhere in a blob:

1. derive the expected local id with `_jira_key_to_local_id(remote_key)` and match on ticket `id`
   exactly — not a substring scan of `json.dumps`, which matches incidental occurrences and (as here)
   misses the real one;
2. additionally assert the BINDING maps that local id to `remote_key`, read from the binding store —
   this is where the DC↔local correspondence actually lives, and it is the property the headline AC
   is really about;
3. keep the existing `creation_channel == "jira"` assertion, which is correct and unaffected.

**Rejected: making the substring match case-insensitive.** It would make the test pass while leaving it a blob scan that could match on an unrelated field, and it would still not assert the binding — the thing that makes the local ticket genuinely correspond to the DC issue.

## Scope

- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py` — the provenance test's assertions.

## Testing

The live DC harness job is the oracle. The fix is verified when that job reports the provenance test PASSING — and, because a green here would otherwise be indistinguishable from a weakened assertion, the new assertions must be shown to FAIL against a deliberately wrong local id (a unit-level check of the id derivation is enough for that half, since `_jira_key_to_local_id` is pure).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the provenance test matches the ticket by EXACT `id` equal to `_jira_key_to_local_id(remote_key)`,
      not by a substring scan of `json.dumps(ticket)`
- [ ] the test additionally asserts the binding store maps that local id to `remote_key`
- [ ] a unit test asserts `_jira_key_to_local_id` lowercases and prefixes, so the derivation the live
      test depends on is pinned independently of the harness
- [ ] the live `jira DC harness smoke` job reports this test PASSING, read from the JOB log
- [ ] the epic's headline AC is only claimed after that green — and the ticket records that the prior
      failure was an oracle defect, so the run is not misread as a regression fix
baseline.summary: Live provenance oracle cannot pass: asserts the raw Jira key against a lowercased local id

## Context

baseline.description: Deferred hardening (accepted limitation, ADR 0046). The commit-ancestry key-validity model (attest/authorship.py verify_authorship_at_commit) defeats the direct revoked-key-reuse case (a new event descends the revocation commit, so a revoked key's revoke-commit is an ancestor and the key is excluded). Its integrity rests on the tickets-branch commit graph being append-only, which today is a CONTROL (Gerrit-authenticated, controlled-environment write access), not a cryptographic guarantee. gittuf shipped the same log-position model and still needed a monotonic policy counter (CVE-2026-44544); TUF hard-codes N+1 root versioning. Future hardening: (a) a regression test asserting a revoked-then-re-introduced key at a LATER ancestry position FAILS; (b) documented threat analysis of tickets-branch force-push/rewrite and the controls that bound it; (c) evaluate an explicit monotonic anti-rollback guard as defense-in-depth. Not scheduled.
baseline.summary: Cryptographic anti-rollback for commit-ancestry key validity (monotonic guard + regression test + tickets-branch-rewrite analysis)

So this task no longer covers the auto-lander — only the review-bot remains as an AWS ticket-event writer. The review-bot writes only EXEMPT types (`code_review` artifacts, `review_bot/voter.py`), so signing here is for CLEAN ATTRIBUTION (the merge-gate does not require signatures on exempt types), not a hard must-sign; still worth doing so AWS-authored events attribute to the bot.

# S4 — CI service account + credentials (SSM-backed)

Part of epic 1fa8 (CI as a second Gerrit gate vote via gerrit-to-platform → GitHub Actions).

## Why
The CI vote-back SSHes into Gerrit as a service account (the g2p production pattern); g2p (running
in the Gerrit container) also needs a GitHub PAT to `workflow_dispatch`. Both credentials must
follow the infra's no-plaintext invariant: SSM SecureString + materialize-at-boot (as with the bot
token, deploy key, OAuth secret).

## What
Provision the CI Gerrit service account (with the `Verified` ACL), and wire the PAT + SSH key
through SSM and the boot-time fetch, plus the GitHub-side vars/secret. Record the inbound
GitHub→Gerrit SSH trust path as an ADR.

  (new SecureString slots), `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` (host-side materialization).

- [ ] Provision the CI Gerrit service account via `infra/gerrit/service-user.sh` (account + group +

## Context

Parent epic `a4bd-4ca8-c44f-49bb`. `managed_refs` (`src/rebar/reducer/_managed_refs.py`) marks a ref managed the instant it is created LOCALLY and is strictly monotonic, so guard G3 in the inbound removal path cannot tell a never-pushed local link from a peer-deleted one. This story adds the missing evidence store; it changes NO removal behavior (S3 does that). The record is a FULL record (vendor link id, direction, confirming pass, confirmed-at), not a boolean — see the epic's "Chosen direction" and its comment "Decomposition design calls" (D1 storage home, D2 key shape, D3 pass_id).

## Scope

New module `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/peer_confirmations.py`, modelled on the sidecar `impossible_links.py` (SCHEMA_VERSION, store-relative path, atomic mkstemp + `os.replace` save).

- Store file: `.tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/peer_confirmations.json`.
- Record key: `(source_local_id, target_local_id, relation)` — LOCAL ids, relation-scoped,
  matching `_inbound_unlink_one` (relation-scoped since e39f) and `impossible_links.record_key`.
- Record fields: `link_id`, `direction` (`outbound` | `snapshot`), `confirmed_pass`,
  `confirmed_at` (epoch ns), `source` (`push` | `snapshot` | `backfill`).
- API: `open_store(repo_root)`, `is_confirmed(source, target, relation)`,
  `record(source, target, relation, *, link_id, direction, pass_id, source_kind)`, `save()`.

**Write seam (three edits, callback-shaped).** The success point is the link phase's `set_relationship` call, which ticket 5528 moved into `dispatch_apply_phases.py::_update_one_dispatch_links`. That function has neither a binding store nor a pass id and must not gain knowledge of either:

1. `dispatch_apply_phases.py` — `_update_one_dispatch_links(...)` gains an optional keyword
   `link_confirm: Callable[..., None] | None = None`. After `set_relationship` returns, invoke
   `link_confirm(to_key=..., relation=..., link_id=...)` via a new `_confirm_link_add` helper.
   The call sits AFTER `_links_applied += 1`, so a failed `set_relationship` records nothing.
   The invocation is wrapped so ANY exception from the callback is logged and swallowed — a
   confirmation write must never fail an outbound link that already landed, and must never
   perturb the `(computed, applied, failed)` counts that ticket 5528 made load-bearing.
   `None` preserves today's behavior byte-for-byte.
2. `dispatch_apply_phases.py` — capture `set_relationship`'s return value (typed
   `dict[str, Any]` in `_backend.py::SupportsLinks`, currently discarded) and pass
   `result.get("id")` as `link_id` when the return is a Mapping, else `None`. Backends may
   legitimately return no id; a missing id is recorded as `null` and is NOT a failure.
   `dispatch_one.py::update_one` gains the same optional keyword and forwards it.
3. `apply_handlers.py::handle_update` — build the callback and pass it into `update_one(...)`.
   This is the PRODUCTION outbound-update path, and its `BatchApplyContext` already holds
   `client`, `repo_root`, `pass_id` and `binding_store`, so no new plumbing is needed (the same
   context-to-dispatch pattern `synced_fields` uses). The callback translates keys to the record
   shape: source is `mutation["local_id"]`, target is `ctx.binding_store.get_local_id(to_key)`.
   **When the reverse map returns None the target is unbound — skip recording entirely** (never
   persist a Jira key in a local-id field); the confirmation is picked up next pass, or by S2
   from a snapshot.

**Durability — three edits, not one.** Adding the path to `_rel_files` alone is insufficient: `reconcile_helpers.py::_commit_binding_store_snapshot` builds a SECOND, parallel `_tracked_basenames` set (the bug-1e08 per-file idempotency guard) and returns "already up-to-date" when no tracked basename is staged, so a confirmation-only change would be dropped.

1. `git_adapter.py` — add `PEER_CONFIRMATIONS_FILE = f"{BRIDGE_STATE_DIR}/peer_confirmations.json"`
   and export it in `__all__`.
2. `reconcile_helpers.py` — append it to `_rel_files`.
3. `reconcile_helpers.py` — append its basename to `_tracked_basenames`.

Load/save is fail-OPEN (like `bindings-retired.json`, NOT fail-closed like `bindings.json`): a corrupt or absent store degrades to "nothing confirmed" without aborting the pass. S4 supplies the backfill that makes "nothing confirmed" safe.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1 `peer_confirmations.py` has a `SCHEMA_VERSION` constant and is under 400 LOC; every
      edited module stays under the 800-line cap. Proof: `bash -c 'git archive HEAD | tar -xO
      src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py | wc -l'` per edited file, each < 800.
- [x] AC2 `record()` then `is_confirmed()` is True for exactly that `(source, target, relation)`
      and False for the same pair under a different relation. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_store.py -k relation_scoped`.
- [x] AC3 A successful outbound ADD through `_update_one_dispatch_links` invokes `link_confirm`
      and writes a record with `direction="outbound"`, `source="push"`, the dispatched relation
      and the `pass_id`; a `set_relationship` that raises writes NO record. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_store.py -k dispatch`.
- [x] AC4 `link_id` is taken from `set_relationship`'s returned mapping (`result["id"]`) and is
      `null` when the backend returns no id or a non-mapping — neither case is an error. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_store.py -k link_id`.
- [x] AC5 An unbound target (`binding_store.get_local_id(to_key)` returns None) records NOTHING
      and does not raise. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_store.py -k unbound`.
- [x] AC6 With `link_confirm=None`, `_links_computed` / `_links_applied` are identical to
      pre-change behavior on the success, failure and dedup-skip paths. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_store.py -k counter`.
- [x] AC7 The store survives a ticket-log SNAPSHOT compaction (confirm, compact, re-open, still
      confirmed). Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_store.py -k compaction`.
- [x] AC8 A corrupt or absent `peer_confirmations.json` yields an empty store and does NOT raise.
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_store.py -k corrupt`.
- [x] AC9 `_commit_binding_store_snapshot` COMMITS when `peer_confirmations.json` is the ONLY
      changed file (proves both `_rel_files` and `_tracked_basenames` were updated). Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_store.py -k commit_only`.
- [x] AC10 A `link_confirm` callback that RAISES is logged and swallowed: the outbound link
      still counts as applied and `_links_applied` is unchanged. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_store.py -k callback_raises`.
- [x] AC11 Gates green. Proof: `make lint` exit 0, `make typecheck` exit 0,
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` exit 0.

## Testing

- New suite `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_store.py` covering store
  round-trip, relation scoping, corrupt/absent load, compaction survival, the dispatch write
  point (success, raise, dedup-skip), `link_id` extraction, the unbound-target skip, a raising
  callback, counter parity under `link_confirm=None`, and the commit-when-only-changed-file case.
- Regression: `make lint && make typecheck && pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` — this story is
  additive and must not alter existing dispatch or removal behavior.

## Out of scope

Snapshot-sourced confirmation (S2), the removal decline (S3), backfill (S4).
baseline.summary: Persist a peer-confirmation record per managed link

The next completion-verifier calibration needs the actual verdicts: failing criterion, findings[], remediation text, timestamps.

## What

- [ ] make typecheck passes on the change.
- [ ] make test passes on the change.

# Rename `--force-close` to `--force` on `transition` (clean break, no alias)

## Context / Problem
`rebar claim` spells its gate escape hatch `--force[=<reason>]`. `rebar transition` spells the close-gate escape hatch `--force-close=<reason>` — one concept, two spellings — while ALSO already accepting a separate valueless `--force` that bypasses the start-work (plan-review) gate on `open -> in_progress`. So `transition` today has two different force flags with two different meanings, and neither matches `claim`. Agents and docs get it wrong.

Operator decision 2026-08-07 (recorded as a comment on this ticket): **clean break, no deprecation alias.** A stale caller must fail loudly with an explicit error, not keep working. Back-out path if the break proves too disruptive: revert the single rename commit (no alias exists to fall back on, so callers must update their argv).

## Approach
Collapse `transition`'s two force flags into ONE `--force[=<reason>]` whose meaning is "bypass whichever gate this transition would hit", dispatched by target status:

- `open -> in_progress`: bypasses the start-work / plan-review gate (today's `--force`
  behaviour, unchanged). The audit note is the `--force=<reason>` value when given, else the
  `--reason` text, else `(no reason given)` — so existing `--force --reason=X` invocations
  keep their exact current behaviour.
- `-> closed`: bypasses the completion-verification / signature gate (today's
  `--force-close=<reason>`). A bare `--force` supplies `(no reason given)`, matching `claim`.

This resolves the collision rather than introducing one: on a close, the valueless `--force` is currently parsed and then silently discarded (`force` is only read on the start-work path), so no existing close invocation changes meaning except by gaining the bypass it was already asking for by name.

Mechanically, `_parse_flags` returns the force reason as `str | None` (`None` = flag absent). The CLI wrapper derives `force = <not None>` and `force_close = value or "(no reason given)"` when present, and threads the explicit value to `transition_compute` as a new `force_reason: str = ""` keyword so the start-work audit note can prefer it over `--reason`.

`transition`'s flag loop is hand-rolled and **silently skips unknown tokens**, so a plain removal would make `--force-close="reason"` a silent no-op — the worst outcome. The parser therefore gets an explicit rejecting branch for both `--force-close` and `--force-close=<v>` that raises a `CommandError` naming `--force`. Because the loop matches tokens exactly (no prefix/abbreviation matching), no abbreviation hazard is introduced; this is complementary to, and does not conflict with, ticket 424f's `allow_abbrev=False` work on argparse-based commands.

The library kwarg `rebar.transition(..., force_close=...)` and the internal `force_close` Python identifiers are **out of scope** and keep their names — this ticket renames the CLI flag string only.

## Scope
Code:
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py` — `_parse_flags`, `transition_compute`
  (`force_reason` keyword), `_USAGE`.
- `src/rebar/_cli/help/transition.txt` — usage line.
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py`, `close_precheck.py`, `txn.py`,
  `close_disposition.py`, `_lib_writes.py`, `_config_schema.py`, `src/rebar/llm/completion.py`
  — the `--force-close` **flag spelling** in operator-facing error text, docstrings, comments.
- `scripts/canary_bridge.py` — its two argv builders that emit the retired flag.
- `scripts/dependency_audit.py` — its advisory auto-close argv builder (line ~532). This
  file did NOT exist when this plan was first written: it landed mid-flight in `0767c38ebb`
  (63e8, "route dependency advisories by lane") already emitting the retired spelling, so
  the rename would have broken its auto-close at runtime. Fixed in a follow-up change,
  together with a regression test in `tests/scripts/test_dependency_audit.py` that feeds the
  generated argv to the REAL `_parse_flags` (the suite previously checked the argv only
  positionally and never validated a flag).

Docs (every tracked non-frozen file carrying the flag spelling, enumerated from `git grep -l -- "--force-close"`):
- `README.md`, `rebar.toml`, `docs/cli-reference.md` (regenerated by

## Why
Fail-open is the IRONCLAD invariant of this epic — a false "absent"/false finding is the cardinal sin, and a non-adopting client must pay nothing. That guarantee has to be verified uniformly across every backend on a real polyglot corpus, not assumed per-component.

## What
- A **fail-open conformance suite**: for every backend (universal-ctags, deps/registries, OpenGrep/ast-grep,
  scc/lizard) assert that unsupported-lang / missing-tool / parse-error / crash / timeout / version-skew /
  invalid-detector each yields `abstain(reason)` + a coverage entry — never a raise, never a false `absent`/
  false finding. Includes the IN-PROCESS cases (a hung/segfaulting tree-sitter parse under the worker boundary)
  and the loader quarantining a schema-invalid project detector.
- A **refutation-yield + false-refute eval on an INDEPENDENT real corpus** (real repos with real references —
  NOT a self-planted fixture; spike E3 = 88% yield / 0 false-refute on rebar's own source): measure the fraction
  of real cross-file names the T1 floor resolves (`refuted`) and confirm ZERO false-refute — value MEASURED, not
  asserted (a self-authored fixture would be self-fulfilling).
- A **polyglot fixture corpus** spanning several languages + ecosystems (unsupported-language, project-supplied-
  language-extension, monorepo/workspace, import-vs-distribution-name) AND — critically — the false-refute HAZARD
  class the design scopes out: a **common-name COLLISION** (a name with >1 definition) and a **MEMBER/dotted
  reference** (`recv.attr`), each asserting the resolver **ABSTAINS** (spike E2: the guard restores 0 false-refute)
  — exercising all three jobs.
- A **deps-lane eval** against the real registry oracle (seeded by spike2_deps.py): real→refute, hallucinated/
  stdlib/slop→abstain, never a false-absent.
- A **non-adoption test**: with the optional extra absent, core imports cleanly and any oracle query fails open
  to abstain/no-op with zero footprint.

## Scope
- `tests/grounding/`; depends on S2, S3, S4 (can develop alongside S5). Reuse the contract/harness from S1.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Conformance matrix: each backend × each failure mode (unsupported-lang / missing-tool / parse-error / crash / timeout / version-skew / invalid-detector, incl. in-process hang/segfault) → `abstain(reason)` + coverage; zero raises, zero false-refute.
- [ ] Refutation-yield + false-refute eval on an INDEPENDENT real corpus (real repos, NOT self-planted; spike E3 = 88% / 0-FP on rebar's own source): yield measured, false-refute = 0.
- [ ] Corpus covers the false-refute HAZARD class — common-name collision (>1 def) + member/dotted ref — each asserting ABSTAIN (spike E2 guard); plus a deps-lane eval (real→refute, hallucinated/stdlib/slop→abstain, no false-absent); plus unsupported-lang, lang-extension, monorepo/workspace, import-vs-dist.
- [ ] Non-adoption test: extra absent → core import-clean, queries fail open to abstain/no-op, zero footprint.
- [ ] Coverage reconstructable from recorded skips across a mixed-language run.
baseline.summary: Fail-open conformance suite + polyglot fixture corpus + non-adoption test

The load-bearing risk is FALSE positives — an internal/workspace package or an import-vs-distribution-name mismatch must NEVER be called absent. So this lane is confirm-only with a strict abstain gauntlet.

## What

  declared deps; **registry existence** probes (deps.dev as a direct oracle where available; per-registry
  fallback) to disprove a hallucination claim.
- The **abstain gauntlet** (only emit `refuted`/`abstain`, never `absent`): per-ecosystem name normalization
  (PEP 503, crates `-`≡`_`, Go `!`-escaping, npm scopes); workspace/monorepo membership (Cargo/pnpm/Go
  `replace`/Maven reactor); stdlib/builtin; import-name-vs-distribution-name (`bs4`→`beautifulsoup4`); any
  transient 429/5xx/timeout → `abstain`. Unknown ecosystem → `abstain`, never `absent`.
- **Validated against the real oracle (spike E4):** deps.dev resolved 5 real/normalized packages → `refute`
  (incl. PEP-503 `scikit_learn`→`scikit-learn`) and abstained on hallucinated/slop/stdlib (`os`→`abstain(stdlib)`;
  404→`abstain(not_on_public_registry)`, never `absent`) — the gauntlet structurally cannot emit a false-absent.
