# DC segmenting Markdown-to-wiki renderer

## Problem
DC stores wiki while rebar authors Markdown and sends Markdown literally. Whole-body pandoc 3.6.1 escapes arrows, erodes tables, and deletes `<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->`.

Add an unwired pure renderer. `WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound` retains 32,767-character truncation; its other methods, `OutboundFieldMapper`, CREATE, `normalize_rich_text`, and live sends stay unchanged. Story 3388 owns cutover/echo/codec convergence; 5c0e owns timeout/process/GPL/SBOM hardening.

Pandoc's maintained pair produced 98.4% eligible-character coverage; md-to-jira, mistune-jira, and md-jira lack equivalent fidelity. ADR 0083 governs imports. ADR 0095 plus `.numbers/0095` records invariants, pin provenance, alternatives, platform, and deferrals.

## Corpus
Commit a deterministic, fixed-seed scrubbed sample from `scripts/build_dc_wiki_corpus.py`: 29 code-arrow, 29 table, 120 prose (178); shards below 500 KB. Per-stratum targets are PINNED so a growing store cannot silently change the corpus. Change `scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py`'s filter to skip `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/`; the scrub also maps vocabulary other repo-wide guards reject (retired bridge spellings, `--force-close`). Reject emails, tenant hostnames, URLs.

Eligible means a classifier-6 unit dispatched to pandoc. Body ratio = bodies whose rendering changed / 178; character ratio = characters of changed bodies / all corpus characters. Measuring characters over ELIGIBLE-UNIT source instead is unachievable: 98,214 of 296,511 eligible characters are unmarked prose pandoc returns byte-identical, capping it at 0.669. Pin measured 0.916/0.969; require >=0.90/>=0.95 plus a non-vacuous dispatched-and-changed check.

## Renderer contract
Add `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` with `render_markdown_to_wiki(markdown: str) -> str`.

Two-phase left-to-right lexer:
1. Lock complete `{noformat}` spans, HTML comments from `<!--` through the next `-->`, backtick/tilde fences, and four-space-indented blocks, including internal blank lines. Locked HTML comment spans pass exactly even when adjacent to prose.
2. Split intervening text into blank-line blocks plus list items; preserve separators/order.

Classify, in order:
1. Locked blocks and units beginning `h1.`-`h6.`, `{code}`, or `{noformat}` pass exactly.
2. An inline-Jira scanner masks code, then recognizes `[label|target]`, `{color:name}...{color}`, and `{{monospace}}` as UNAMBIGUOUS (these settle a unit alone, even inside a bullet), and `*strong*` (never `**`) / `_emphasis_` as AMBIGUOUS (they settle only a unit with no CommonMark-only heading/quote/list/fence/backtick/`**`/image/`[label](target)`). Without that split a rendered bullet re-renders and oscillates. ADR records the tradeoff.
3. ASCII table = >=2 pipe-bearing lines with a pipes/colons/hyphens/whitespace delimiter row. Wrap exact bytes once in `{noformat}`.
4. HTML tag matching `<[/!]?[A-Za-z][^>]*>` passes exactly; HTML comments were already locked in phase 1.
5. Prose outside extracted code containing `(?`, `\b`, `\d`, `\s`, `\w`, or a bracket class followed by `*`, `+`, `?`, or `{n,m}` passes exactly.
6. Remaining headings, quotes, list items, and prose render via pypandoc `commonmark -> jira` with `--wrap=none`.

Code fragments are fences, four-space blocks, and inline spans with matching backtick runs; mask them before classifiers and arrows. One regex pass ordered `<!--`, `-->`, `<->`, `->`, `<-`, `=>` maps arrows to ↔/→/←/⇒ and delimiters to themselves. Inline code copies exactly.

Every extracted fragment must appear byte-identically in order after conversion or that unit falls back. Strip content-free `{anchor:}` after headings. Five-pass tests start from Markdown and prove passes 2-5 byte-identical. Use real pandoc outputs for bold, italic, links, and monospace; NO monkeypatch anywhere. A probe observed `*b*`, `_i_`, `[l|http://x]`, and `` `mono` `` -> `{{mono}}`, so monospace needs no synthetic shape. The same probe established the jira writer NEVER emits `{color:...}` (a color span is stripped to plain text under both readers), so color is not a pandoc output to pin -- it is only pre-existing markup the inline scanner passes exactly, covered by the pre-existing-wiki fixtures.

Missing pypandoc returns the body and warns `wiki_render_fallback` with only `reason="pandoc_absent"`; conversion/preservation failure returns the unit and debugs the same event with `"conversion_failure"`/`"preservation_failure"`. Never log bodies. Module state is immutable.

## Dependency/CI
Add `wiki = ["pypandoc-binary==1.15"]` plus wiki in dev, register its pypandoc probe, and lock. Optionality adds `wiki:wiki`, removes stale `eval:eval`, and changes the union to `agents,tracing,wiki`. Dynamic tests `test_optionality_loop_covers_every_declared_extra` and `test_eval_extra_is_gone` plus full suite prove parity.

A clean-environment probe established `pypandoc.__version__ == 1.15`, pandoc `3.6.1`, `# Heading` → `h1. {anchor:}Heading\n`, `` `mono` `` → `{{mono}}\n`, and no `{color:...}` form; ADR 0095 records that provenance. A non-skipping test hard-imports pypandoc and asserts those exact values. It gates Linux/macOS CI; Windows wheels exist, and a platform without one falls back to identity. Wiki tests never importorskip.

Changed paths: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py`; `scripts/build_dc_wiki_corpus.py`; `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/`; `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render.py`; `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_corpus.py`; `pyproject.toml`; `uv.lock`; `src/rebar/_optional.py`; `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml`; `scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py`; `docs/adr/0095-dc-segmenting-wiki-renderer.md`; `docs/adr/.numbers/0095`.

## Verification
Author the oracle RED-first without skip/xfail. Run `make lint`/`make typecheck`/`make test` with worktree `.venv` on PATH. Stateless: no store/retry/cache contention.

CLI/MCP/API/facade: out of scope, this is unwired. Dual direction: story 3388. Cloud: ADF child.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Classifier-6 units render through real pandoc in order; `test_dc_segmenting_passthrough`.
- [x] Tables preserve exact bytes once; table passthrough and five-pass tests.
- [x] HTML/regex-dangerous units preserve exact bytes; passthrough tests.
- [x] Specified arrows convert prose; `test_arrow_substitution_cases`.
- [x] Code arrows and prose/code `-->` stay exact; arrow tests.
- [x] 29 code-arrow fixtures retain protected excerpts; corpus test.
- [x] 29 tables keep exact bytes inside one noformat wrapper over five passes.
- [x] HTML comments survive exactly; corpus HTML test.
- [x] Block and inline Jira forms stay byte-identical for five passes.
- [x] Real-pandoc bold/italic/link/monospace outputs stabilize after pass one.
- [x] Pre-existing `{color:name}` markup passes exactly; pandoc emits no color form.
- [x] Missing pandoc returns exact body and content-free `wiki_render_fallback:pandoc_absent`.
- [x] Conversion failure returns exact unit and logs only `conversion_failure`.
- [x] Preservation failure returns exact unit and logs only `preservation_failure`.
- [x] wiki locks pypandoc-binary 1.15; packaging test.
- [x] wiki installs alone and jointly without eval; uv sync and optionality lane.
- [x] Real binary reports pandoc 3.6.1; non-skipping pin test.
- [x] Real jira heading conversion equals `h1. {anchor:}Heading\n`; pin test.
- [x] Body ratio >=0.90 and character ratio >=0.95, with eligible units dispatched and changed.
- [x] Cardinality is 29+29+120=178; pinned cardinality test.
- [x] Fixtures contain no email, tenant hostname, or URL; secrets test.
- [x] Heading output has no content-free anchor; passthrough test.
- [x] ADR marker passes `scripts/check_adr_numbers.py`.
- [x] ADR has Decision/Invariants/Pin/Alternatives/Platform/Deferrals; ADR test.
- [x] Existing WikiTextCodec tests stay unmodified; full suite.
baseline.summary: DC one-way segmenting wiki renderer

## Reproduction Steps
1. Land commit 10837ca88 (adds external volume gerrit_reviewbot_tickets to infra/compose/docker-compose.yml) WITHOUT updating the provisioning loops in infra/scripts/compose-up.sh.
2. Every rebar-autodeploy tick that sees a new main SHA rebuilds the review-bot image, then `docker compose up -d review-bot` aborts: external volume "gerrit_reviewbot_tickets" not found. Backoff resets on each new main SHA, so a busy push day compresses many multi-GB docker builds into a tight window.
3. Around 2026-07-10 03:15–03:52 UTC the 30G root disk transiently filled (pip Errno 28 in the autodeploy builds, journal); concurrent review clones then failed (VOTER_ERROR "No space left on device"), fail-closing changes 452/461/462 with [LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (review-error)].

**Expected:** autodeploy converges after every main advance; reviews never veto for infra reasons. **Actual:** deploys failed on every attempt for ~41h (fail #21 by Jul 10 00:00); transient ENOSPC fail-closed live reviews.

## Resolution (applied on-box 2026-07-10 ~04:45 UTC, supervised)
- Pruned builder/image caches (~3.5G), verified RED via `docker compose up -d --dry-run review-bot` (reproduced the volume error).
- Created the missing bind volume exactly matching sibling spec: `docker volume create --driver local --opt type=none --opt o=bind --opt device=/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets gerrit_reviewbot_tickets` (+ mkdir of host dir); dry-run then GREEN.
- One supervised autodeploy run: "review-bot redeployed + healthy", deployed-sha now d1e4cd5c; Gerrit container untouched; disk 20% used.
- The repo-side fix for infra/scripts/compose-up.sh (and hardening) is child/discovered work.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Autodeploy converges (deploy complete) after volume creation; no bot-build-failed since.
- [ ] Review-bot posts a real (non-coverage-gap) LLM-Review vote post-deploy (functional probe on change 461).
- [ ] Stale coverage-gap veto on change 452 cleared via /rerun.
- [ ] Discovered follow-up defects filed and linked discovered_from this ticket.
baseline.summary: incident: review-bot fail-closed LLM-Review vetoes — root disk exhaustion from a 41h autodeploy failure loop (missing gerrit_reviewbot_tickets volume)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py` measures **796 lines** against the repository's hard 800-line module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), which CI enforces with no allowlist escape hatch. Four lines of headroom is not enough for the sibling story that makes the outbound create path target a per-ticket project, so that story cannot land until this file has room.

## Approach

Extract the entire `update_one` sub-tree — lines **432-796** — into a new `dispatch_update.py`. This is a pre-existing call-graph seam, not a mechanical cut: `update_one` (`:447`) calls `_update_one_apply_parent` (`:497`), `_update_one_scalar_update` (`:500`), `_update_one_dispatch_labels` (`:506`) and `_update_one_dispatch_links` (`:510`), and `_update_one_scalar_update` is the sole caller of `_is_illegal_transition_400`. Nothing above line 432 calls into the block; the only dependency runs downward, through `_call_with_retry` (`:71-143`), which stays put.

The repository has already made this exact split twice: `dispatch_apply_phases.py` (226 lines) holds three other `update_one` phases, and `batch_dispatch.py` (148 lines) is the stable re-export facade. This extraction follows the pattern rather than inventing one.

**The import edge the new module must carry.** `update_one` does not only call the four helpers that move with it — it also calls `_update_one_apply_reporter` (`:498`), `_update_one_filter_fields` (`:499`) and `_update_one_dispatch_comments` (`:507`), which already live in `dispatch_apply_phases` and are imported at `dispatch_one.py:53-55`. Those three imports move to `dispatch_update.py` with their caller; `dispatch_one` drops them, since nothing left in it uses them. This is what makes the extraction land in the module that already owns the other `update_one` phases.

**The one hazard, and how it is avoided.** `dispatch_one.py` must **not** re-export `update_one` back for convenience — that would create `dispatch_one → dispatch_update → dispatch_one`, because `dispatch_update` imports `_call_with_retry` from `dispatch_one`. Instead `batch_dispatch.py`'s import block (`:31-40`) is re-pointed at `dispatch_update` for `update_one` and `_is_illegal_transition_400`. That is the only production re-point needed: `applier.py:122-130` already imports both symbols **from `batch_dispatch`**, not from `dispatch_one`, so its `__all__` at `:329` keeps resolving with no edit.

`batch_dispatch` is the established public surface. Its import block at `:31-38` currently takes six names from `dispatch_one` — `_call_with_retry`, `_find_link_id`, `_index_existing_links`, `_is_illegal_transition_400`, `create_one` and `update_one`. (`delete_one` is **not** among them; it is defined in `batch_dispatch` itself at `:54`.) After the move that block splits three ways: `_call_with_retry` and `create_one` still come from `dispatch_one`; `_is_illegal_transition_400` and `update_one` come from `dispatch_update`; and `_find_link_id` / `_index_existing_links` are taken directly from `dispatch_apply_phases`, where they are actually defined (`:206` and `:180`) and from which `dispatch_one` only re-exports them. Every edge then points from `batch_dispatch` downward and from `dispatch_update` to `dispatch_one`, never back, so the direction stays acyclic.

**The new module's complete import inventory**, derived by scanning the moved range rather than by inspection:

- stdlib: `json`, `subprocess`, `sys`, `urllib` — and only these four. `logging`, `time`, `os`,
  `random` and `pathlib` are imported by `dispatch_one` but unused inside `432-796`, so they stay.
- `typing`: `Any`, `cast`.
- from `rebar_reconciler._errors`: `JiraAPIError`, `http_status`.
- from `rebar_reconciler.dispatch_apply_phases`: `_update_one_apply_reporter`,
  `_update_one_filter_fields`, `_update_one_dispatch_comments`, `_find_link_id`,
  `_index_existing_links`.
- from `rebar_reconciler.pass_io`: `record_parent_divergence` only. That module is imported at
  `dispatch_one.py:57` alongside `_write_mapping_atomic`, which the moved range does **not** use, so
  `dispatch_one` keeps its own `pass_io` import for that name.
- from `rebar_reconciler.dispatch_one`: `_call_with_retry`.

**One CI gate keys on the symbol's file.** `.github/complexity-baseline.json` records per-symbol ceilings keyed as `<file>::<symbol>`, and two of its keys name this module — `dispatch_one.py::_update_one_dispatch_links` and `dispatch_one.py::create_one`. The first symbol moves, so its key must be re-pointed to `dispatch_update.py::_update_one_dispatch_links` or the complexity gate fails on a file that no longer defines it; `create_one` stays and its key is untouched. This consumer lives outside the source tree and is invisible to any symbol- or import-level search, which is why it is called out explicitly.

**One consumer does need an edit.** `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_synced_fields_reporting_e6e9.py:36` imports `update_one` **directly** from `dispatch_one`, so it breaks the moment the symbol moves and the no-re-export rule forbids papering over it. That import is re-pointed at `batch_dispatch`, which is where every other consumer already gets it. This is the single test edit this story makes, and it is enumerated rather than discovered during implementation — an earlier draft of this plan wrongly claimed no test changes were needed.

This is a behaviour-preserving move: no logic is rewritten.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_update.py` (new) — the moved sub-tree, ~405 lines
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py` — drops to ~431 lines
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/batch_dispatch.py` — the `:31-38` import block split across
  `dispatch_one`, `dispatch_update` and `dispatch_apply_phases`; the only production re-point
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` — the `_update_one_dispatch_links` ceiling re-keyed to the new
  file
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_synced_fields_reporting_e6e9.py` — its direct
  `from ... dispatch_one import update_one` at `:36` re-pointed at `batch_dispatch`

`applier.py` is deliberately **not** in scope: it already imports the moved symbols from `batch_dispatch` (`:122-130`), so it needs no change.

## Testing

No new behaviour, so no new behavioural tests: the oracle is the existing suite passing **unchanged**, which is what proves the move preserved behaviour. Two specific hazards are verified rather than assumed:

- Monkeypatch survival: there are **five** module-attribute patch sites on `dispatch_one`, across
  three test modules — `apply/test_applier_identity_write.py:156,195`,
  `test_cloud_rate_limit_sweep_heldout.py:258,279` and `test_error_taxonomy.py:61` — and every one of
  them patches the same attribute, `dispatch_one.time`. All five stay safe: `time` is consumed by
  `_call_with_retry` and `create_one`, both of which remain resident, and `dispatch_update` reaches
  the retry helper by importing `_call_with_retry` from `dispatch_one`, so the sleep call still
  resolves against `dispatch_one`'s globals where the patch is applied. Confirm all five pass
  unedited — this is the assertion that proves the split did not silently defeat a patch.
- Import-cycle check: importing `dispatch_one` and `dispatch_update` in either order must succeed,
  asserted directly so a future re-export cannot silently reintroduce the cycle.
- Direct-importer coverage: the one re-pointed test
  (`test_synced_fields_reporting_e6e9.py`) passes after its import is changed, and a repository-wide
  grep for `from rebar_reconciler.dispatch_one import update_one` returns no remaining hit. The grep
  is part of the oracle because this consumer was missed by symbol-level analysis and only a string
  search surfaced it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `dispatch_one.py` and `dispatch_update.py` are each at or below 650 lines; checked by running
      the module-size gate and recording both counts.
- [ ] The full existing test suite passes, with exactly one existing test file edited —
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_synced_fields_reporting_e6e9.py`, whose direct import
      is re-pointed — and one file added,
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dispatch_update_split.py`, which holds this story's
      structural assertions; checked by the gating test command plus confirming the diff under
      `tests/` touches only those two paths.
- [ ] All five `dispatch_one.time` patch sites pass unedited; checked by running the three named
      test modules.
- [ ] `dispatch_update.py` carries the full import inventory named in the Approach and `dispatch_one`
      no longer imports what it stopped using; checked by asserting both modules' import lists.
- [ ] The complexity gate passes with `_update_one_dispatch_links` re-keyed to
      `dispatch_update.py::_update_one_dispatch_links` and `create_one`'s key unchanged; checked by
      running the complexity-baseline gate and inspecting both keys.
- [ ] `batch_dispatch` resolves all six previously-imported names after its block is split; checked
      by importing each from `batch_dispatch` and asserting no `ImportError`.
- [ ] No `from rebar_reconciler.dispatch_one import update_one` remains anywhere in the tree; checked
      by a repository-wide string grep returning zero hits.
- [ ] `dispatch_one.py` does not import from `dispatch_update.py`; checked by a test that imports the
      two modules in both orders and asserts no `ImportError`.
- [ ] `update_one` and `_is_illegal_transition_400` remain reachable through `batch_dispatch` **and**
      through `applier`'s existing re-export; checked by asserting both resolve from each module
      after the move, which confirms `applier.py` needed no edit.
- [ ] No behaviour change: checked by confirming the moved functions' bodies are identical to their
      pre-move text apart from import lines.
baseline.summary: Size relief: extract the update_one sub-tree from dispatch_one.py into dispatch_update.py

baseline.description:
## Why

The reconciler concentrates the codebase's accidental complexity. This story reduces it where the value clearly exceeds the regression risk — pure-refactor changes to working, well-tested, high-blast-radius sync code must clear that bar.

## What

Two behavior-preserving wins (named REST budget; inbound scalar-field transform table). Two further candidates (create_one DispatchContext; compute_mutations flatten) were evaluated and deliberately deferred — see outcome.

## Scope

- `_engine/rebar_reconciler/batch_dispatch.py` (named budget constant).
- `_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound.py` (`_apply_inbound_update` field table).
- Out of scope: `reconcile_once` (essential orchestration spine — untouched).

## Outcome (honest scoping)

- **Done — named budget:** `_REST_CALL_BUDGET = 200` replaces the bare literal in the
  guard + docstring.
- **Done — inbound field-map table:** the scalar-field if-ladder
  (description/priority/assignee/ticket_type/parent_id) is now a declarative

# Settle 049e's one documentary claim with a live measurement

## Context

Bug `049e-9fac-a821-4ea2` made the DC comment ceiling configurable (`[tool.rebar.reconciler].comment_max_chars`, default 32767) and DROPPED the idea of auto-discovering the ceiling from `/rest/api/2/application-properties`, on the grounds that the `/advanced-settings` sub-resource where `jira.text.field.character.limit` is actually exposed requires the global "Administer Jira" permission, while rebar authenticates as an ordinary user's PAT.

**That conclusion is DOCUMENTARY, not measured.** 049e's agent tried to probe live and could not: the `tests/external/live_jira_dc` harness image is linux/amd64 only and its README records three measured attempts where Jira never became usable within an hour on the arm64 workstation. So no 403 was ever captured. 049e's AC asked for an EMPIRICAL determination and got a documentary one; rather than tick that box on inference, the limitation was recorded and the probe deferred here.

## Why this is worth doing rather than dropping

The probe is genuinely runnable — just not on that host. The `jira-dc-harness` job in `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` runs the same harness on GitHub Actions' amd64 runners, where the image works. So this is a deferred measurement, not an impossible one.

## What it does NOT change

049e's remedy stands either way. Configuration is the correct fix whether or not the endpoint is readable: a readable endpoint would enable an OPTIONAL auto-discovery convenience on top of the config key, not invalidate it. So this ticket cannot regress 049e — it can only add an enhancement or confirm the drop. That independence is why 049e was closeable with this leg outstanding.

## Approach

Add a single cell to the live DC suite that requests `/rest/api/2/application-properties` (and the `/advanced-settings` sub-resource) with the harness's ordinary non-admin PAT and RECORDS the outcome — status code and body shape — asserting only that the outcome is one of the two documented possibilities, so the cell reports a fact rather than pinning a guess.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] a live DC cell requests `/rest/api/2/application-properties` with a NON-ADMIN PAT and records
      the observed status code, run id, and job name on this ticket
- [x] the `/advanced-settings` sub-resource is probed separately, because that is where
      `jira.text.field.character.limit` is exposed and its permission requirement may differ
- [x] the cell distinguishes 403 (permission, the documented expectation) from 404 (endpoint absent on
      8.17.1) from 200 (readable) — a bare non-200 assertion does NOT satisfy this
- [x] the outcome is written back onto `049e-9fac-a821-4ea2` so its documentary claim is either
      confirmed or corrected in the record
- [x] if the endpoint IS readable, a follow-up is filed for optional auto-discovery; 049e's config key
      remains the supported mechanism either way

## Measured and closed (run 30944241768) — see MEASURED-275E-A

    GET /rest/api/2/application-properties                    non-admin PAT: 403 | admin: 200 (72)
    GET /rest/api/2/application-properties/advanced-settings  non-admin PAT: 403 | admin: 200 (33)

Both paths are PRESENT but PRIVILEGED. The admin leg in the same run is what distinguishes that from "absent on 8.17.1"; three controls (the PAT authenticates as the new user, that user lacks ADMINISTER, and the admin comparison) are asserted rather than assumed, which is what the "no bare non-200" criterion required.

049e's documentary claim is CONFIRMED and its remedy stands: `comment_max_chars` remains the mechanism. The final criterion's conditional does not fire — the endpoint is NOT readable by rebar's PAT, so no auto-discovery follow-up is filed.
baseline.summary: Probe empirically whether /rest/api/2/application-properties is readable by rebar's non-admin PAT on DC

## The fallback chain cannot rescue a Bedrock failure in this environment

Observed while proving [rebar:895c-3eb2-043a-4de1]. When Bedrock rejects a call, rebar's fallback arm to direct Anthropic fails immediately with an auth error, so the chain provides **no** redundancy.

### Evidence

`/tmp/03ef-review6.out`:

    llm call [plan-review-prerequisite-verifier] mode=single_turn model=anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6
    FAILED in 0.4s: status_code: 401, model_name: claude-sonnet-4-6,
    body: {'type': 'error', 'error': {'type': 'authentication_error', 'message': 'API key is invalid.'}}

Same shape recorded for `overlap-judge` (8 occurrences, `status_code: 401`).

The 0.4s duration confirms it fails at authentication, not on the request.

### Why this matters

Two independent guards were assumed to exist and only one does:

1. rebar falls back from the primary provider to a secondary on failure.
2. That secondary is reachable.

(2) is false here. So any primary-provider failure is terminal, and the fallback machinery gives a **false sense of resilience** — the more dangerous state, because the design implies coverage that is not there. It also means the 895c grammar failures had no chance of being rescued at runtime.

### Open questions for whoever takes this

* Is the direct-Anthropic arm INTENDED to be configured in this environment? `rebar.toml` documents
  that the bedrock arm "deliberately blanks ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" for the provider matrix — if that is
  also true for normal local/CI operation, then the fallback is intentionally unreachable and the
  defect is that it is still ATTEMPTED (burning a call and emitting a misleading 401) rather than
  skipped with a clear message.
* If it is meant to work, the credential is simply absent/invalid and this is a configuration fix
  plus a guard that detects it early.

Deciding which of those two it is IS the first task; do not assume.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] it is established whether the direct-Anthropic arm is intended to be reachable in this
      environment (cite the configuration authority, not an assumption)
- [ ] if it is NOT intended: an unreachable fallback candidate is detected and skipped (or refused
      at config time) rather than attempted, so the logs stop showing a misleading 401
- [ ] if it IS intended: the credential resolution is fixed and a startup/preflight check reports a
      missing-or-invalid fallback credential BEFORE a gate run depends on it
- [ ] either way, the operator-visible message distinguishes 'fallback not configured' from
      'fallback failed', because those need different actions

## Testing

    pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q
baseline.summary: The direct-Anthropic fallback arm is non-functional (401 invalid API key), so a Bedrock rejection cannot be rescued

# `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` is at exactly 800/800 LOC

## Context / Problem

Surfaced while reworking the fsck cluster on `defaceable-icy-antelope`. With `fsck.py` taken off the cap, `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` is now the largest file in `src/rebar` at **exactly 800** — the hard cap in `.github/module-size-limit.txt`, enforced by the CI module-size gate with no allowlist. The next change to it of any size, including a one-line bug fix, cannot land.

This is the fourth instance of the pattern (`valiant-balladic-willet` did `passes.py`, `splurgy-witless-flamingo` did `_ref_lock.py`, `defaceable-icy-antelope` did `fsck.py`), and several more files are within a handful of lines:

| file | LOC |
|---|---|
| src/rebar/_lib_writes.py | 800 |
| src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_banking.py | 799 |
| src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py | 799 |
| src/rebar/_store/push.py | 799 |
| src/rebar/signing.py | 798 |
| src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py | 798 |

## Approach

Follow the pattern set by `defaceable-icy-antelope`: take an architectural view rather than a mechanical split. Identify the actual concerns in the module, then extract along a call-graph seam that already exists — a helper family with a single internal call site is the seam a prior author cut and stopped at. Name each new module for its concern. Target 200-500 LOC per file; never create a module under 100 LOC (if a candidate concern is smaller, it belongs with its nearest collaborator). Behaviour-preserving: identical behaviour, identical exit codes.

Read the architectural-analysis comment on `defaceable-icy-antelope` first — it records the concern-map method, the re-export compatibility constraint for module-attribute callers, and the complexity-ratchet re-keying that any move requires.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` is at most 500 lines — verified by
      `[ "$(wc -l < src/rebar/_lib_writes.py)" -le 500 ]` exiting 0.
- [ ] AC2: each new module is at least 100 lines — verified by `wc -l` on each.
- [ ] AC3: no `src/rebar` file exceeds the hard cap — verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` exiting 0.
- [ ] AC4: no test file is edited — verified by `git diff --stat origin/main -- tests/`
      producing no output.
- [ ] AC5: `make lint`, `make typecheck` and `scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
      each exit 0.
baseline.summary: _lib_writes.py sits at exactly 800/800 LOC — the next file pinned at the cap

## Context / Problem
S1 proves one atomic update executor and S2 produces pure plans, but legacy batch dispatch still replays compound methods, conflates deferred and applied work, and uses a rolling breaker that cannot distinguish physical attempts from exhausted logical outcomes. One ticket-local or permanent failure can distort batch behavior.

## Outcome
Make the typed coordinator authoritative for non-create plans: update, delete, probe, clean-label, repair-property, and conflict handling. Execute atomic desired postconditions in dependency order; after partial success, re-observe and plan only remaining drift. Produce exact ticket/pass outcomes and apply the approved endpoint/provider finite-pass fuse only to normalized exhausted logical failures.

## Plan
1. Add a coordinator that consumes immutable plans, enforces dependencies, and calls adapter atomic operations through S1s budget. Preserve successful earlier postconditions and never replay the whole compound mutation after a late failure.
2. Normalize auto-healed, success, deferred, permanent, commit-unknown, exhausted transient, and skipped dispositions with ticket/endpoint/tenant/provider/global scope.
3. Replace the rolling 5-of-10 breaker. Endpoint scope opens after three consecutive eligible exhausted logical outcomes across at least two tickets; provider scope additionally spans two endpoint families. A matching success resets consecutive state.
4. Exclude physical attempts, recovered warnings, permanent failures, ticket-local 404, and opaque diagnostics from inferred fuse counters. Retain direct authoritative credential, configuration, quota, rate, issue, endpoint, tenant, and global behavior.
5. When a fuse opens, defer remaining matching plans with reason/scope/retry metadata while independent scopes continue. Preserve exact applied/failed/deferred/skipped tallies and nonzero degraded-pass signaling.

## Testing (RED → GREEN)
- Coordinator tables cover dependency success/failure, partial compound update, idempotent already-gone delete, ticket-local 404 isolation, permanent 4xx, auth/quota/rate scopes, and mixed endpoint families.
- Fuse sequences assert threshold, two-ticket/two-family requirements, success reset, exclusions, and independent-scope continuation.
- Replay fixtures derived from historical GitHub Actions outcomes assert zero premature stop in the completed 1,200-run slice; raw warning/grep text is never classified as a terminal outcome.
- Verified-fake Cloud/DC batches assert wire order, maximum calls, exact tallies, logs, and exit status.

## Compatibility / rollback
Cut over by non-create operation family and never dual-send. Before legacy removal, an operation-family flag can select the old dispatcher. Rollback preserves successful Jira effects and resumes from re-observation. The intentional differences are three-call shared budgeting, explicit deferral, exact partial outcomes, and replacement of the rolling breaker.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Non-create plans execute atomic postconditions once in dependency order; a late failure preserves earlier success and re-observes only remaining drift within the same logical budget.
- [ ] Ticket-local/permanent failures isolate the ticket, authoritative broad scopes stop only their declared scope, and independent tickets/endpoints continue.
- [ ] Endpoint fuse opens only after three consecutive eligible exhausted logical outcomes across two tickets; provider fuse additionally requires two endpoint families; matching success resets state.
- [ ] Physical attempts, recovered warnings, permanent failures, ticket-local 404s, and opaque diagnostics never increment inferred fuse counters.
- [ ] Remaining matching work is explicitly deferred with reason/scope/`retry_not_before`; applied, failed, deferred, skipped, and recovered tallies plus exit status are exact.
- [ ] Historical replay fixtures and verified-fake Cloud/DC batches show no premature termination of observed successful/partially successful work.
baseline.summary: RP-03 S3 — Coordinate non-create operations with deferral and the scoped fuse

## Context / Problem
At plan authoring (commit 0f5dbc88b) Ruff ASYNC emitted zero diagnostics across `src/rebar` and Ruff DTZ emitted three diagnostics: DTZ006 for `datetime.fromtimestamp()` and DTZ007 for `datetime.strptime()` in `src/rebar/_engine_support/validate_checks.py`, plus DTZ011 for `date.today()` in `src/rebar/grounding/detectors/security_pin.py`. Those are dated observations; the authoritative set is whatever `ruff check --select ASYNC,DTZ src/rebar tests` reports against the **current** `origin/main` tip. The approved ratchet lands only after every ASYNC/DTZ site live on current `origin/main` has explicit, tested timezone semantics.

**Live observation @ `origin/main` ff4c56007a (drift since authoring):** `ruff check --select ASYNC,DTZ src/rebar tests` reports **6** diagnostics — the 3 src sites above (validate_checks.py:65 DTZ006, validate_checks.py:68 DTZ007, security_pin.py:94 DTZ011) **plus 3 drift-introduced sites in the test tree**: tests/unit/test_jira_onboard.py:146 DTZ001 (`datetime.datetime()` without tzinfo), tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:1423 ASYNC110 (`asyncio.sleep` in a `while True` loop), and tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:1611 ASYNC251 (`time.sleep` in an async function). Because the ratchet gates ASYNC/DTZ across `src/rebar tests`, all 6 — src and test — must reach zero before ASYNC/DTZ are selected. The authoritative set remains whatever the live command reports at implementation time; this figure is a dated observation.

## Dependencies and Ownership
This story has an ordering-only `depends_on` edge to `d9f5-baa5-9fc3-451d` because both stories edit `pyproject.toml`; the Mypy strictness configuration lands first to avoid sibling merge conflicts. No runtime behavior in this story depends on the Mypy change. This story creates and owns `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py`; `125d-ee6f-7af0-4200` depends on this story and extends that same file later.

## Approach
1. Create `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` as the owner of the shared Ruff configuration contract. This test separately asserts ASYNC selection, DTZ selection, absence of the exact Ruff security selector `S`, absence of `.semgrep.yml`, `.semgrep.yaml`, and `.semgrep/`, and absence of the literal `datetime.UTC` token from production Python files under `src/rebar`.
2. Define validation timestamp semantics as UTC. Change `validate_checks.py` to use the datetime module. Integer epoch seconds are converted with `datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(created, tz=datetime.timezone.utc)`. Persisted timestamp strings without an offset are interpreted as the event store's UTC wall time with `datetime.datetime.strptime(...).replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)`. Both paths produce the same UTC hourly cluster key.
3. Prove timezone invariance on supported POSIX/macOS platforms by running the validation behavior under at least two `TZ` values with `time.tzset()`. The test is explicitly skipped when `time.tzset` is unavailable; Windows is not a declared supported platform in `pyproject.toml`. Rejected: adding a production timezone-injection seam solely for this test, because the explicit timezone argument is directly testable and an extra API would add unused production complexity.
4. Preserve security-rule cadence as a host-local calendar-date decision. Obtain an aware current instant with an explicit `tz` argument, convert it to the host timezone, then extract its date. The implementation may use an equivalent helper or expression; the contract is the host-local date semantics plus DTZ005 compliance, not a particular line spelling. Boundary tests cover age equal to `cadence_days` and age greater than `cadence_days`.
5. Add ASYNC and DTZ to the gated Ruff selection after the tests fail against current configuration.
6. Run the focused, default, and integration pytest tiers.

The spelling `datetime.UTC` is prohibited because Ruff `target-version` remains `py310`; all production UTC construction uses `datetime.timezone.utc`. Rejected: blanket DTZ ignores.

## Scope
- `pyproject.toml`
- `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` (required; created and owned by this story)
- `src/rebar/_engine_support/validate_checks.py`
- `src/rebar/grounding/detectors/security_pin.py`
- `tests/unit/test_validate_idea_exemptions.py`
- `tests/unit/test_code_review_ws5.py`
- `tests/unit/test_jira_onboard.py` (resolve live DTZ001 drift)
- `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py` (resolve live ASYNC110/ASYNC251 drift)

## Testing / Verification
- Configuration and negative assertions: `pytest -q tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py`
- Focused behavior: `pytest -q tests/unit/test_validate_idea_exemptions.py tests/unit/test_code_review_ws5.py`
- Ruff families: `ruff check --select ASYNC,DTZ src/rebar tests`
- Canonical lint: `make lint`
- Default tier: `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q`
- Integration tier: `pytest -m integration -q`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` asserts ASYNC is selected by the global Ruff configuration.
- [x] `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` asserts DTZ is selected by the global Ruff configuration.
- [x] `ruff check --select ASYNC,DTZ src/rebar tests` exits 0.
- [x] Tests prove integer epoch timestamps produce the same UTC hour cluster under at least two distinct process `TZ` settings on platforms providing `time.tzset`.
- [x] Tests prove timezone-less persisted timestamp strings are assigned `datetime.timezone.utc` before clustering.
- [x] A source-level AST assertion verifies the UTC-producing calls in `validate_checks.py` use `datetime.timezone.utc`; `pytest -q tests/unit/test_validate_idea_exemptions.py` executes that assertion.
- [x] Behavioral validation tests prove the numeric and timezone-less timestamp paths produce the expected UTC cluster keys; `pytest -q tests/unit/test_validate_idea_exemptions.py` exits 0.
- [x] `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` recursively scans `src/rebar` Python files and fails if the literal `datetime.UTC` token is present.
- [x] Security-pin tests prove the implementation obtains an aware current instant with an explicit timezone, converts it to the host timezone, and uses the resulting local date; `pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_ws5.py` exits 0.
- [x] `ruff check --select DTZ005 src/rebar/grounding/detectors/security_pin.py` exits 0.
- [x] Security-pin tests prove `age_days == cadence_days` is not stale.
- [x] Security-pin tests prove `age_days > cadence_days` is stale.
- [x] `make lint` exits 0.
- [x] `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q` exits 0.
- [x] `pytest -m integration -q` exits 0.
- [x] `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` asserts the exact Ruff security selector `S` is absent.
- [x] `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` asserts `.semgrep.yml`, `.semgrep.yaml`, and `.semgrep/` are absent.

<!-- green-on-origin-main AC -->
- [x] After `git fetch origin`, `ruff check --select ASYNC,DTZ src/rebar tests` and `make lint` exit 0 against the **current** `origin/main`; any pre-existing ASYNC or DTZ diagnostic on current `origin/main` (including drift-introduced since the measured commit) is resolved before ASYNC/DTZ are landed.

## Context / Problem
FP verification over all 348 historical G7 findings (recorded on ticket 696a-82a4-47c5-4e54, research round 3 + operator decisions): at priority >= 0.85, 0 clearly-incorrect findings (22 CORRECT / 7 UNCLEAR across >= 0.75), with direct evidence authors revised plans in the demanded direction within minutes. The 0.80-0.85 band is empty (priorities quantize), so 0.85 selects the same historical set as 0.80 with less future exposure. G7 has never blocked because its routing entry carries default_posture "advisory" @ 0.95 (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json, "G7") — a configuration artifact, the same shape the bfa8 T3/T10 enablement (commit e3962d21e) and the c97a T5c enablement (commit 623d68c4a) corrected. Two noise shapes must be fixed in the same change: an unresolvable parent is emitted as a finding instead of an abstain (observed on ticket 18f9), and same-issue duplicates stack (ticket 76d2 carried 3 findings for one contradicted parent clause). Only 3 historical findings carry plan-v4 kind grades yet — see the Monitoring note (deliberately not an AC).

## Approach
Follows the landed bfa8/c97a pattern exactly: a routing flip + rubric guidance, no pass3_decide changes, no new machinery.

(1) Routing (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json, "G7" entry): block_threshold 0.95 -> 0.85, default_posture "advisory" -> "blocking". Plan-review blocking derives ONLY from default_posture == "blocking" plus block_threshold — src/rebar/llm/criteria/model.py:73-77 (threshold_for, gate="plan_review"); the blocking_enabled field is the code-review gate's convention and is inert in plan review. A finding then blocks in Pass-3 when priority = validity x impact >= 0.85 (src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py:588, pass3_decide), threaded through the plan-review wrapper src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:756-771 (impact_fn=impact_plan).

(2) Kind scoping — provided by the EXISTING plan-v4 grading, stated exactly; no per-grade Pass-3 gate exists and none is added. G7 maps its severity onto the divergent_implementation axis (src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G7.md, kind-mapping paragraph), which impact_plan grades by DIVERGENCE KIND (src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py:350-357 DIVERGENCE_GRADE01/_DIVERGENCE_FLOOR_GRADES; ADR 0054, commit 7d846e0c9): contradicts_reality and omits_required_site score 1.0 and hard-floor impact at 0.85 (decide.py:407-409); incomplete_enumeration contributes 0.55 (DIVERGENCE_INCOMPLETE_CONTRIB, pinned strictly below every blocking block_threshold by tests/unit/test_divergence_grade_split.py:142 — note decide.py's inline comment misattributes this pin to test_impact_plan.py, which pins only UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB; the plan cites the real pin) and NEVER floors, so a cosmetic divergence cannot reach the 0.85 bar through this axis. Consequence, stated as the mechanism actually behaves: blocking @ 0.85 admits BOTH floor-grade kinds — contradicts_reality AND omits_required_site — at validity >= 0.85; an incomplete_enumeration-graded finding cannot block via the divergence axis. Restricting blocking to contradicts_reality alone (this ticket's original framing) would require per-grade gating that pass3_decide/threshold_for do not have; that machinery is REJECTED because (a) the landed precedents scope by guidance not machinery, (b) the FP evidence is kind-blind — 0 clearly-incorrect across ALL 348 historical findings at >= 0.85, so it supports blocking the whole band, and (c) ADR 0054 deliberately gives omits_required_site the floor (an omitted required site is the exact harm class the grading exists to catch), while the rubric fixes in (3) remove the known omission-side FP shapes (sibling handoff, closed parent). A one-sentence rubric guidance (the bfa8 T10 pattern) reinforces the kind mapping: only a genuine contract contradiction or a provably required omission is a floor kind; cosmetic/wording mismatches are incomplete_enumeration — coached, never auto-blocked.

(3) Rubric fixes (src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G7.md):
- FAIL-OPEN (abstain-with-coverage), the T13/T14 pattern (see src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T14.md FAIL-OPEN paragraph): a parent that cannot be resolved via show_ticket ABSTAINS with a covered-but-unverified note — never a finding.
- CLOSED parent: its contract is checked against its FINAL (as-closed) state, and scope the parent explicitly handed to sibling tickets is NOT a leaf violation (consistent narrowing remains a non-finding).
- DEDUP-AT-SOURCE, the c97a T5c pattern (src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T5c.md "DEDUP-AT-SOURCE"): emit at most ONE finding per contradicted parent clause; additional manifestations fold into that finding's evidence. Rubric-only: the deterministic discovery-stage dedup (src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py:252-284, dedup_key/suppress_and_dedup) collapses only identical (criteria, location, body) triples and cannot recognize same-clause paraphrases, and no LLM-free same-clause detector is feasible — so decide.py is deliberately NOT touched (dropped from this ticket's earlier scope).

(4) Tests and pins: all THREE pinned blocking-set assertions gain G7 — tests/unit/test_threshold_recalibration.py EXPECTED_ROUTING ("G7": (0.85, "blocking")) and the blocking-set assertion at test_only_the_approved_and_prerequisite_criteria_are_blocking — G7 enters via a NEW `G7_BLOCKING = {"G7": 0.85}` constant added to the set-union expression (`... | set(PILOT_BLOCKING) | set(G7_BLOCKING) | ...`); G7 is deliberately NOT added to PILOT_BLOCKING because test_routing_posture_blocking_at_090 parametrizes over that dict asserting block_threshold == 0.90 — and tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py _PLAN_REVIEW_APPROVED_BLOCKING. Additionally tests/unit/test_plan_review_g7.py::test_g7_posture_is_advisory_at_0_95 hard-asserts the OLD posture (default_posture 'advisory', block_threshold 0.95) and is renamed/updated to test_g7_posture_is_blocking_at_085 asserting the new (0.85, 'blocking') pair. New tests/unit/plan_review/test_g7_blocking.py follows tests/unit/plan_review/test_criteria_blocking.py: findings driven through the REAL orchestrator.pass3_over_findings wrapper with the REAL impact_plan (no impact monkeypatch — the kind grades themselves produce the impact).

(5) Regenerate docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md via `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` and commit the output.

Alternatives rejected: 0.80 threshold (admits future validity-0.80 findings with no historical quality evidence; the 0.80-0.85 band is empty so 0.85 loses nothing); per-grade Pass-3 gating (new cross-gate kernel machinery for a restriction the evidence does not demand — see (2)).

Monitoring note (explicitly NOT an acceptance criterion): re-run the FP classification once >= 20 kind-graded G7 findings have accumulated in the REVIEW_RESULT corpus; the zero-LLM criterion-effectiveness recorder already tracks blocking outcomes (same monitoring stance as the bfa8 pilot). Record the recheck on this ticket's close notes.

## Scope
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json (G7 entry only), src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G7.md, tests/unit/plan_review/test_g7_blocking.py (new), tests/unit/test_threshold_recalibration.py, tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py, tests/unit/test_plan_review_g7.py (posture pin updated), docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md (regenerated). NOT touched: src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py, src/rebar/llm/criteria/model.py, the verifier prompts.

## Testing
`.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/plan_review/test_g7_blocking.py tests/unit/test_threshold_recalibration.py tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py tests/unit/plan_review/test_criteria_blocking.py tests/unit/test_impact_plan.py tests/unit/test_divergence_grade_split.py tests/unit/test_plan_review_g7.py -v`, then the full `tests/unit` suite. Cases: threshold_for(["G7"], registry.by_id(), gate="plan_review") == (0.85, True); a G7 finding graded contradicts_reality with an all-yes graded binary BLOCKS (impact 1.0, priority 1.0); the same finding marked self_revealing floors to impact 0.85 -> priority 0.85 -> BLOCKS (exact-boundary case, priority >= block_threshold); omits_required_site all-yes BLOCKS (floor kind, pinned deliberately); incomplete_enumeration all-yes lands impact 0.55 / priority 0.55 -> ADVISORY; a floor-kind finding at validity 0.8889 with self-revealing impact 0.85 -> priority 0.7556 -> ADVISORY (the validity guard); rubric-text assertions for the abstain-with-coverage, closed-parent + sibling-handoff, one-per-clause dedup, and floor-kind guidance sentences.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] criteria_routing.json "G7" carries default_posture "blocking" with block_threshold 0.85 (checked: test_g7_blocking.py asserts threshold_for(["G7"], registry.by_id(), gate="plan_review") == (0.85, True)).
- [ ] Through the real plan-review Pass-3 wrapper with the real impact_plan, a contradicts_reality-graded G7 finding at validity 1.0 BLOCKS (checked: test_g7_blocking.py).
- [ ] Through the same wrapper, an omits_required_site-graded G7 finding at validity 1.0 BLOCKS (checked: test_g7_blocking.py).
- [ ] Through the same wrapper, an incomplete_enumeration-graded G7 finding stays ADVISORY at priority 0.55 (checked: test_g7_blocking.py).
- [ ] The G7 rubric contains each of the four new rule sentences: abstain-on-unresolvable-parent (never a finding); closed-parent-final-state + sibling-handoff; one-finding-per-contradicted-parent-clause; floor-kind guidance (checked: one rubric-text assertion per sentence in test_g7_blocking.py).
- [ ] The pinned routing table, the pinned blocking-set union (via the new G7_BLOCKING constant), the _PLAN_REVIEW_APPROVED_BLOCKING set, and the test_plan_review_g7.py posture pin each reflect G7 at (0.85, "blocking") (checked: test_threshold_recalibration.py, test_impact_model_versioning.py, test_plan_review_g7.py all pass).
- [ ] docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md is regenerated (checked: `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` produces no diff on the committed tree).
baseline.summary: G7 floor-grade divergence blocking at 0.85 plus abstain and dedup fixes

## Summary
REBAR_MCP_READONLY=TRUE (or True/YES) silently disables the readonly gate — the membership test is case-sensitive.

## Reproduction Steps
(verified on installed 0.4.0 == HEAD)
1. REBAR_MCP_READONLY=TRUE; build_server().
2. list_tools() -> all 14 write tools exposed.

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: common truthy spellings enable the gate; an operator setting TRUE believes the server is read-only.
- Actual: mcp_server.py:115-116 tests membership in ("1","true","yes") without .lower(); TRUE fails open (the dangerous direction).

## Source
- src/rebar/mcp_server.py:115-116 (_readonly)
- src/rebar/mcp_server.py:271-273 — REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE uses the same parse; its failure direction is safe (stricter) but fix both for consistency.

## Fix direction
.strip().lower() before the membership test in one tiny _env_truthy helper used by both checks.

## Suggested RED test
Parametrize TRUE/True/YES/Yes/1/yes/true -> all readonly (write tools hidden); ""/0/no -> not readonly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Case-insensitive truthy parse for REBAR_MCP_READONLY and REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE
- [ ] RED parametrized test first
- [ ] Documented accepted values in README/CLAUDE.md

## Why

`verify.require_signature_for_close` (default False, OFF in this project) is the "signature close gate" — it requires an HMAC signature BEFORE closing a work ticket. It is documented as the ALTERNATIVE to `require_completion_verification_for_close`, which is what THIS project actually uses (enabling both deadlocks a non-force close). It has never been used here and is a retired alternative. Remove it and the close-gate code reachable ONLY through it.

## What

Delete (reachable only via this gate):
- `resolve_signature_gate` — `_commands/gates.py:58-80` (whole function).
- `_signature_gate` — `_commands/txn.py:311-410` (whole function) + its two CommandErrors
  ("requires a certified signature (verdict: …)" and the "made at a different commit"
  HEAD-binding error).
- `transition_core` plumbing: the `sig_require`/`sig_config_error` locals + the
  `resolve_signature_gate` call (`txn.py:182-187`) and the story/epic close-gate block
  (`txn.py:250-260`).
- Config field + validator (`_config_schema.py:210`, `:485`).
- True-path tests: `test_signature.py:312`, `test_close_gate_story_epic.py:38,116`,
  `test_idea_close_bypass.py:27` (rewrite — bypass logic changes); trim flag-specific
  assertions in `test_config_typed.py`, `test_config_perf.py`, `test_config_backcompat.py`;
  regenerate golden CLI help (`transition__*help.out`).

## Scope — MUST PRESERVE

The entire shared HMAC signing/attestation substrate: `signing.py` (`signing_key`, `verify_record`, `most_recent_attestation`, `head_sha`, `verify_signature`), the `attestations` map, `sign_manifest`/`verify_signature` MCP tools, and the completion-verifier close path (`transition_close.py`) + plan-review claim gate — all share this machinery and must keep working. `--force-close` and `--verdict-hash` are NOT owned by this gate — keep both. Docs handled by the doc-sweep story.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `require_signature_for_close` removed from schema, parser, and any docs/help (coordinated with the doc-sweep story).
- [ ] `resolve_signature_gate` and `_signature_gate` deleted; the story/epic close path no longer references a signature gate.
- [ ] Shared signing machinery intact: plan-review claim gate and completion-verifier close gate both still function (prove with their existing tests green).
- [ ] `--force-close` / `--verdict-hash` unaffected; true-path tests removed/rewritten; golden help regenerated.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The `rebar-root-disk-pressure` CloudWatch alarm (root `/`, 30G, threshold 85%) sat in ALARM for ~39 hours on 2026-08-04/06: the review-bot host's root disk filled from ~48% to ~95% during an autodeploy build burst, then stayed pinned at 92-96% until the next real deploy finally reclaimed it. Root cause: `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` reclaims docker garbage via `prune_docker_caches()` (builder prune `--keep-storage 5GB` + image prune) ONLY on the deploy and backoff paths. When `main` is quiescent, every ~2-min `rebar-autodeploy.timer` tick hits the "up to date … no-op" early exit (autodeploy.sh:228) and returns WITHOUT pruning, so nothing reclaims disk between deploys. This extends closed bug 7a41-95f4-c38c-4b5a (added the deploy-path prune) to cover the quiescent-main gap it left.

## Approach

Add a pressure-triggered, throttled reclaim to the autodeploy no-op path — the ideal hook because it fires every ~2 min exactly when no deploy is reclaiming, already holds the single-flight `flock` (autodeploy.sh:191), and already has `prune_docker_caches()` in scope. Reuse the exact root-disk-% computation from observability.sh:79 (`df --output=pcent /`).

1. Add tunables near `BUILD_CACHE_KEEP` (autodeploy.sh:~87): `DISK_PRESSURE_PCT` (default 80 — below the 85% alarm for hysteresis), `PRESSURE_PRUNE_MIN_INTERVAL` (default 600s throttle), `PRESSURE_PRUNE_TS_FILE` (default under `STATE_DIR`).
2. **Relocate `prune_docker_caches()` above the no-op exit.** It is currently defined at autodeploy.sh:245, which is AFTER the line-228 no-op exit; bash only makes a function callable once its `funcname() { … }` definition line has executed, so calling it from line 228 would fail with "command not found". Move the entire `prune_docker_caches()` definition up into the helper block near line ~150 (immediately below the new helpers in step 3), so it is defined before its FIRST use. Its existing callers stay valid because they all run later than line 150: `record_backoff_failure` (autodeploy.sh:261), the deploy-success path (autodeploy.sh:379), and the new line-228 call. Concrete resulting order: helpers/`prune_docker_caches`/`reclaim_under_pressure` at ~142-160 → single-flight + fetch (~191-224) → line-228 no-op exit calling `reclaim_under_pressure` → backoff/deploy paths (245+) that also call `prune_docker_caches`. `prune_docker_caches`' own body is unchanged (it uses only `docker`, `timeout`, `log`, `BUILD_CACHE_KEEP`, all available at that point).

3. Add two helpers in that same block (autodeploy.sh:~150): `root_disk_pct()` (the `df --output=pcent /` one-liner) and `reclaim_under_pressure()` which returns early unless `root_disk_pct >= DISK_PRESSURE_PCT`, enforces the min-interval throttle via the persisted timestamp file (atomic tmp+mv write), emits a countable `AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE` journal marker via the existing `marker()`, calls `prune_docker_caches` (now defined above it), and logs the before/after percentage. A prune failure only logs (never alters control flow), matching the deploy-path guarantees.
4. Call `reclaim_under_pressure` on the no-op early-exit line (autodeploy.sh:228), before the `log "up to date"; exit 0`.

Default threshold 80% with a flat floor plus the 10-min throttle (not a derivative/trend) is chosen deliberately: the throttle prevents per-tick churn and `prune_docker_caches` keeps a 5GB warm cache so back-to-back prunes are cheap no-ops; an absolute floor is simpler and less flappy than slope tracking. All new behavior is opt-outable via env overrides sourced from `/etc/rebar/autodeploy.env` (already sourced by the script), so no host redeploy is required to tune it.

## Scope

- `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` — add the three tunables; relocate the existing `prune_docker_caches()` definition from line ~245 up into the helper block (~150) so it precedes the new line-228 call site (its body and its two existing call sites are otherwise unchanged); add the `root_disk_pct()` + `reclaim_under_pressure()` helpers; and add the single new call site on the no-op exit path (line 228). No change to the deploy/backoff prune BEHAVIOR, the drain/defer logic, or any journal-marker token except the new `AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE`.
- `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_disk_pressure.py` — new test module (new testable behavior): assert the reclaim fires when simulated disk% is at/above the threshold and no-ops below it, that the throttle suppresses a second prune inside the interval, and that a prune failure does not change the script's exit code. Stub `df` and `docker` via PATH shims / injected fakes, matching the existing `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_*` harness style.

The new `AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE` marker is intentionally NOT wired to a new CloudWatch metric in this story (autodeploy still exits 0; the existing `root_disk_used_percent` alarm already covers the outcome). Wiring an observability delta metric for it is deferred as out of scope.

## Testing

- Happy path: with a `df` shim reporting 90% and a `docker` shim that records calls, running the no-op path invokes `prune_docker_caches` once and writes the timestamp file.
- Throttle/edge path: a second invocation within `PRESSURE_PRUNE_MIN_INTERVAL` does NOT invoke prune; an invocation with `df` reporting 70% (below threshold) does NOT invoke prune.
- Failure path: a `docker` shim that exits non-zero leaves the script's overall exit status at 0 (prune failure is non-fatal), and the pressure marker is still emitted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] On the autodeploy no-op tick, when root `/` usage is >= `DISK_PRESSURE_PCT` (default 80) and the throttle window has elapsed, `prune_docker_caches` runs — verified by `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_disk_pressure.py` happy-path assertion (docker-shim call recorded).
- [x] When root usage is below the threshold, or within the throttle window of the last pressure-prune, no prune runs — verified by the below-threshold and throttle assertions in the same test module.
- [x] A prune failure on the pressure path does not change autodeploy's exit code (stays 0) and only logs — verified by the failure-path assertion.
- [x] A countable `AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE` marker line (prefix `AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE ` followed by the `marker()` JSON) is emitted to stderr exactly once per triggered pressure prune and zero times on the below-threshold and throttled paths — asserted by capturing the script's stderr in the test module and counting matches.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the new and existing `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_*` tests pass under the repo venv.
baseline.summary: autodeploy: pressure-triggered docker prune on the no-op tick to prevent root-disk-pressure

baseline.description:
Add an atomic `idea` command on all three surfaces (CLI, MCP, library) that creates an `epic` in status `idea` in a single genesis CREATE event.

## Why

Capturing an idea must be one race-free operation. A create-then-transition path would momentarily leave the ticket in `open` (claimable by a parallel agent, the anti-pattern `claim` already forbids), so the idea must be born in `idea` via a single CREATE event. The command is intentionally light: title plus an optional description only.

## Prerequisite (depends on S1, 81b4-985e-b3e8-4026)

This story requires the status-vocabulary story to land FIRST: `idea` must be a recognized status value (added to the `TicketStatus` literal and to `_VALID_STATUSES`) before this command is coherent. Without S1, a created idea-status ticket is inconsistent with the type surface, and the transitions exercised by the end-to-end smoke test below (`transition idea open`, `transition idea closed`) are rejected by the existing `_validate_status` guard. A `depends_on` link to S1 is already recorded. This story's own deliverable — the command emitting a single CREATE event carrying `status=idea` for an `epic` — does not itself modify the status vocabulary; it consumes what S1 establishes.

## What

- Have `process_create` honor an optional `status` on the CREATE event, defaulting
  to `open` when absent — completing the one CREATE field the reducer does not
  currently read. The `idea` command is the sole producer of a non-`open` genesis
  status; no general `create --status` flag is added.
- Add the CLI command `rebar idea "<title>" [--description=…]` creating an `epic`
  in status `idea`.
- Add the MCP write tool `create_idea` with the same behavior.
- Add the library entry point `rebar.idea(...)` with the same behavior.
- Suppress the create-time "non-bug ticket lacks file_impact" stderr warning for
  idea-created epics.
- Document `rebar idea` / `create_idea` / `rebar.idea` in the command/tool
  references and note in `docs/event-schema.md` that a CREATE event may carry
  `status`.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` — `process_create` honors optional `status`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/idea.py` — new atomic CLI command.
- `src/rebar/__init__.py` — `rebar.idea(...)` library entry point.
- `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` — `create_idea` MCP write tool.
- `docs/event-schema.md` and command/tool reference docs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `process_create` sets `status` from the CREATE event data when present.
- [ ] `process_create` defaults `status` to `open` when the CREATE event omits it.
- [ ] `rebar idea "<title>"` creates a ticket of type `epic`.
- [ ] The ticket created by `rebar idea` has status `idea`.
- [ ] The ticket created by `rebar idea` is produced by a single CREATE event with
      no intervening STATUS event (test inspects the event log).
- [ ] `rebar idea "<title>" --description=TEXT` records TEXT as the description.
- [ ] The MCP `create_idea` tool creates an `epic` in status `idea` in one CREATE
      event.
- [ ] The library `rebar.idea(...)` creates an `epic` in status `idea` in one
      CREATE event.
- [ ] No surface gains a general `create --status` flag.
- [ ] The create-time file_impact stderr warning does not fire for a ticket created
      by `rebar idea`.
- [ ] `docs/event-schema.md` states that a CREATE event may carry `status`.
- [ ] The command/tool reference lists `rebar idea`, `create_idea`, and
      `rebar.idea`.
- [ ] After S1 (status vocabulary) and S2 (close-bypass) have landed, an
      end-to-end smoke test demonstrates the user-facing flow: `rebar idea`
      creates a ticket absent from `ready`/`next-batch`; `transition idea open`
      promotes it to claimable work; `transition idea closed` succeeds with no
      completion-gate error. (This AC is gated on the S1/S2 prerequisite above.)
- [ ] `make lint` passes for the changed files.
baseline.summary: Add atomic 'idea' command (CLI/MCP/library) creating an epic in status idea

baseline.description:
## Report

`scripts/canary_bridge.py:26` does a bare `import alert_dedup`. That only resolves when `scripts/` is already on `sys.path`. Running the affected test file on its own fails:

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/test_reconcile_bridge_canary_class.py -q
ERROR ...::test_every_bug_close_carries_valid_class[heartbeat-alert-_heartbeat_recovery_env]
  - ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'alert_dedup'
ERROR ...::test_every_bug_close_carries_valid_class[binding-drift-alert-_drift_recovery_env]
  - ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'alert_dedup'
1 passed, 2 errors
```

Reproduced on `origin/main` with the repo venv on PATH.

## Provenance — introduced today, not pre-existing

`scripts/alert_dedup.py` was ADDED by `0767c38ebb` (ticket 63e8, "route dependency advisories by lane"). That change correctly EXTRACTED the dedup helpers out of `canary_bridge.py` rather than duplicating them — the extraction was the right call — but it left the consumers importing the new module by bare name.

## Why it matters even though CI is green

CI's full run passes because `tests/scripts/conftest.py:32-38` inserts repo-root `scripts/` on `sys.path` at collection time, and that process-wide side effect leaks into every later-collected module in the same session — including `tests/unit/`, which has no such insert of its own. The failure only appears when the file is run as a SUBSET — which is what developers and agents do constantly while iterating. A test that passes in CI and fails when you run it directly trains people to distrust the suite.

## Chosen mechanism (AC2 decision, stated up front)

**An explicit `sys.path` insert of the script's own directory, immediately above the sibling import** — the pattern already established in this repo by `scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py:46-51`. Rationale, and why the two alternatives are rejected:

- *Package-relative import* — rejected. These modules are executed as standalone scripts by
  workflow YAML (`python scripts/canary_bridge.py heartbeat-alert …`,
  `scripts/dependency_audit.py gate`). A relative import raises
  `ImportError: attempted relative import with no known parent package` under that
  invocation, so it would trade a test-only failure for a production-canary failure.
- *Making `scripts/` a real package* — rejected. Adding `scripts/__init__.py` changes how
  every script in the directory is resolved by every existing caller (workflows, Makefile,
  pre-commit), which is a far larger blast radius than the defect, and is not
  behavior-preserving.

The chosen insert is invocation-independent: it derives the directory from `__file__`, so it holds under `python scripts/x.py`, `python -m pytest`, bare `pytest`, and `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` alike. It is idempotent (guarded by a membership check) and does not reorder any path entry that is already present.

## Sweep of sibling call sites (AC3)

Every bare import under `scripts/` of a module that lives in `scripts/` or `tests/`:

| Site | Status |
|---|---|
| `scripts/canary_bridge.py:26` `import alert_dedup` | **UNGUARDED — fix here** |
| `scripts/dependency_audit.py:50` `import alert_dedup` | **UNGUARDED — fix here** |
| `scripts/calibrate_completion_floor.py:24` `from gold_set_completion import …` | SAFE — line 22 explicitly inserts `tests/unit` derived from `__file__` immediately above it |
| `scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py:51` `import jira_dc_field_readiness` | SAFE — lines 46-48 insert `scripts/` from `__file__`; this is the precedent pattern |
| `scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py:59` `from _engine_path import engine_dir` | SAFE — lines 57-58 insert `tests/` from `__file__` |

The sweep is valid as of the sha it runs against and is re-run against merged `main` before push.

## Guard (AC4/AC5) — closing the other half of the class

Ticket `a371` (merged `1db88c92d7`) landed `tests/unit/test_tests_import_convention.py`, which AST-scans for `tests.`-rooted imports **under `tests/`**. It does not look at `scripts/`, so the class is only half-guarded. This adds the companion: `tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py`, same AST-scan shape, asserting that every bare import under `scripts/` naming a module that is only resolvable via a directory insert is preceded by that insert in the same file — plus a subprocess check that the affected test module collects when run alone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1 — the reported repro passes standalone.**
  Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_reconcile_bridge_canary_class.py -q` exits 0 with
  0 errors (repo venv on PATH, no wrapper).
- [x] **AC2 — the import is resolved by an explicit, invocation-independent mechanism.** Both
  fixed sites derive the directory from `__file__` and insert it idempotently above the
  import; neither relies on ambient `sys.path` ordering.
  Verify (asserts the insert itself, not merely the token `__file__`):
  `python -c "import sys; bad=[p for p in ['scripts/canary_bridge.py','scripts/dependency_audit.py'] for w in [open(p).read().split('import alert_dedup')[0]] if not ('sys.path.insert' in w and '__file__' in w)]; print(bad); sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)"`
  exits 0 and prints `[]`.
- [x] **AC3 — sibling call sites swept and classified.** The table above enumerates all five
  bare sibling-import sites and states which are safe and why.
  Verify (AST scan that distinguishes sibling imports from stdlib/third-party by resolving
  each imported top-level name against a real file under `scripts/` or `tests/**`, then
  compares the resulting set to the five documented rows — exits 0 and prints `OK` only on
  an exact match):
  `python -c "$(cat <<'PY'
import ast, pathlib, sys root = pathlib.Path('.') sib = {p.stem for p in root.glob('scripts/*.py')} | {p.stem for p in root.glob('tests/**/*.py')} found = set() for p in sorted(root.glob('scripts/*.py')):
    tree = ast.parse(p.read_text(), filename=str(p))
    for n in ast.walk(tree):
        names = [a.name for a in n.names] if isinstance(n, ast.Import) else (
            [n.module] if isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom) and n.level == 0 and n.module else [])
        for m in names:
            if m.split('.')[0] in sib and m.split('.')[0] != p.stem:
                found.add(f"{p}:{n.lineno}:{m}")
expected = {
 'scripts/canary_bridge.py:__L__:alert_dedup',
 'scripts/dependency_audit.py:__L__:alert_dedup',
 'scripts/calibrate_completion_floor.py:__L__:gold_set_completion',
 'scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py:__L__:jira_dc_field_readiness',
 'scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py:__L__:_engine_path'}
norm = {':'.join([a, '__L__', c]) for a, _, c in (f.split(':') for f in found)} print(sorted(norm - expected) or 'OK'); sys.exit(1 if norm - expected else 0) PY )"`
  (line numbers are normalized out so the check survives the insert shifting them).
- [x] **AC4 — the a371 guard has a companion covering `scripts/`.**
  Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py -q` exits 0, and the
  new file exists.
- [x] **AC5 — the guard is proven RED against the defect.**
  Verify: reverting the `sys.path` insert in `scripts/canary_bridge.py` and re-running
  `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py -q` FAILS naming
  `scripts/canary_bridge.py`; restoring it makes it pass. Run this before landing and record
  the output in a ticket comment.
- [x] **AC6 — no behavior change and no regression.**
  Verify: `make lint && make typecheck && python -m pytest tests/unit tests/scripts -q`
  all pass.

## Out of scope

Any change to what `canary_bridge.py` or `dependency_audit.py` DO — this is an import- resolution repair only. No CLI surface, no argv, no output text changes.
baseline.summary: canary_bridge's bare 'import alert_dedup' resolves only when scripts/ is on sys.path; subset test runs error
