# Refresh exact-pinned dev tooling: zizmor + ruff

Bump two exact `==` pins in `pyproject.toml`'s `[dev]` extra to current, un-yanked releases.

## Why
- **zizmor 1.27.0 is YANKED** for GHSA-f42p-wjw5-97qh (Moderate, CWE-532): 1.27.0 prints
  GitHub tokens (`GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`/`ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN`) to stderr under `-v`/debug
  logging. Only 1.27.0 is affected; the fix is 1.28.0. rebar's `make lint` invokes `zizmor
  release.yml` with no verbose flag, so there is no live exposure, but pinning exactly to a
  security-yanked release is fragile (a stricter resolver / pruned cache can fail installs).
- **ruff 0.15.19 -> 0.15.22**: routine patch refresh to stay current on the format/lint pin
  (exact-pinned for local<->CI parity). No yank/security; grouped here as a low-risk sibling.

## Plan
1. `pyproject.toml`: change the pin line `zizmor==1.27.0` -> `zizmor==1.28.0`.
2. `pyproject.toml`: change the pin line `ruff==0.15.19` -> `ruff==0.15.22`.
3. Reinstall the dev extra so the worktree venv has the new tools.
4. Run `make lint`; if the newer ruff reformats anything, apply `ruff format` and include the
   diff so CI format-check stays green. Run `make typecheck`.
5. One commit, `rebar-ticket` trailer + DCO sign-off; push to Gerrit; land after
   `LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1`.

Note: the pin comment block above zizmor does not mention a specific version string, so no
comment edit is required — only the pin line itself changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` pins `zizmor==1.28.0` — verify: `grep -c 'zizmor==1.28.0' pyproject.toml` returns 1 and `grep -c 'zizmor==1.27.0' pyproject.toml` returns 0.
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` pins `ruff==0.15.22` — verify: `grep -c 'ruff==0.15.22' pyproject.toml` returns 1 and `grep -c 'ruff==0.15.19' pyproject.toml` returns 0.
- [ ] `make lint` exits 0 in the worktree venv (ruff check + format-check + zizmor + actionlint).
- [ ] `make typecheck` exits 0 in the worktree venv.
- [ ] `git diff --name-only origin/main` lists only `pyproject.toml` (plus any file ruff-format rewrote), no unrelated files.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The change is merged to `main` via Gerrit with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` (evidence: the merged change's Gerrit vote record; out-of-session).
baseline.summary: Bump zizmor 1.27.0->1.28.0 (yanked/GHSA) and ruff 0.15.19->0.15.22

The rule "a plan review that PASSED but whose attestation failed to persist is RETRYABLE, not success" exists only in the CLI: `_cli/_llm_commands.py:129-171` inspects `result["signature"]`, discriminates `plan_review_generation_changed` vs `plan_review_sign_aborted` vs transient, and returns exit 11.

`_mcp_llm.py:227-229` returns `rebar.llm.review_plan(...)` raw, with no such inspection. Verified end-to-end: an MCP agent sees `verdict: PASS`, proceeds to `claim`, and the claim gate refuses because the signature the gate consumes was never written.

The surface most used by autonomous agents has the weaker implementation. The recovery (`sign_review`) IS already exposed over MCP — the agent simply is not told to use it. This is a presentation gap in the seam, not a missing capability.

Both proposers converged on extracting the classifier below both front-ends.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The retryable/cause discrimination lives in one place below CLI and MCP
- [x] The CLI still maps it to exit 11 with byte-identical stderr
- [x] The MCP result carries a structured retryable flag and names `sign_review` as the recovery
- [x] A test covers the passed-but-unsigned state on both surfaces

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Pydantic deliberately counts one Agent-visible model turn even when `FallbackModel` tries multiple candidates inside it. The approved RP-01 decision follows maintained-project practice: keep that request budget authoritative and make candidate activity operationally visible as tracing, not as `candidate_requests` in usage. `Agent.instrument_all()` (already called by `setup_tracing`, `src/rebar/llm/tracing.py:54`) instruments only the Agent's OUTER model — for a fallback run that is the `FallbackModel`, yielding ONE model-request span whose internal candidate iteration is invisible. Candidate construction is centralized in `model_classes.build_fallback_model` (`src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:414+`); `runner.PydanticAIRunner` already records ordered candidate provenance (`src/rebar/llm/runner.py:372-465`). This story is purely additive instrumentation and does NOT change the S2 `_pai_structured` control flow, whose one bounded operation already preserves the bug-895c native-to-prompted fallback (S2 AC-7).

## Approach
Make each candidate visible by wrapping every already-built concrete candidate model (inside `build_fallback_model`) in a thin subclass of pydantic-ai's own `pydantic_ai.models.wrapper.WrapperModel`. Its `request` override opens ONE rebar-owned child span — via `opentelemetry.trace.get_tracer(...).start_as_current_span(...)` on the SAME `TracerProvider` that `setup_tracing`/`instrument_all` already configures (not a parallel tracer) — around `super().request(...)`. It reuses the library's wrapping primitive but does NOT use `InstrumentedModel` directly, because `InstrumentedModel` owns its request-span lifecycle with no public hook to attach rebar's per-candidate `order`/`outcome`; a rebar-owned child gives that control. Nesting is by ambient OTel context: `instrument_all`'s outer `InstrumentedModel` span is current when `FallbackModel.request` calls each candidate, so the child span parents to it automatically — and because `instrument_all` does NOT re-wrap inner candidates, exactly one rebar span is emitted per candidate (no duplication). A short SPIKE confirms both the child-under-parent nesting and the no-double-wrap property before implementation.

Each candidate span records: zero-based `order`, provider-qualified model identity, an `outcome` from the closed vocabulary {`returned`,`raised`}, and provider-reported usage only when the SDK response exposes it (else omitted, never inferred). Any error text on a `raised` span is placed under the allowlisted `message` key and taken back out sanitized — `sanitize_diagnostic({"message": reason})["message"]` — so no prompt, response, credential, endpoint, or unsanitized body reaches the span. The bug-895c native-to-prompted downgrade needs NO code change here: both the native and prompted `agent.run` route through the SAME wrapped candidates, so the downgrade is already legible as the native attempt's span `raised` (sanitized reason) then the prompted attempt's span `returned`. Instrumentation is best-effort: any exception in candidate wrapping or span emission — tracing enabled or disabled, exporter present or absent — is swallowed at the wrapper boundary so the fallback result, `RunUsage`, and the propagated exception/`FallbackExceptionGroup` are identical to tracing-off. Do not alter `FallbackModel` selection, `ProviderSession` lifecycle, `RunUsage`, `UsageLimits`, pricing, JSONL, or the S2 `_pai_structured` control flow. Provider SDK/HTTP retries stay outside this candidate layer and are never inferred.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py` — wrap concrete candidate models in the `WrapperModel` subclass at construction, without changing order or fallback predicates.
- `src/rebar/llm/tracing.py` — define the `WrapperModel`-based candidate-span helper: the shared-tracer accessor, the bounded rebar attributes (`order`, model identity, `outcome`, optional usage), and the best-effort swallow.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — thread candidate order/provenance into the wrapper without adding retry policy.
- `tests/unit/test_llm_fallback_chain.py`, `tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py` — candidate order, outcome, provenance, and usage non-interference.
- `tests/unit/test_candidate_tracing.py` — new focused module using an in-memory OTel span exporter, plus the lean-import and tracing-ON span-failure contracts.

## Testing
- Primary 503 then fallback success: one Agent model-request span parenting two ordered candidate spans (`raised` then `returned`).
- All candidates fail: one `raised` span per attempted candidate; the existing ordered `FallbackExceptionGroup` unchanged.
- Bug-895c downgrade: native attempt span `raised` (sanitized reason) then prompted attempt span `returned`, with no `_pai_structured` change.
- Secret-canary: a candidate whose error carries an API key/email yields a `raised` span whose reason is redacted and which holds no prompt/response/endpoint body.
- Tracing ENABLED with a span-emission/exporter failure: result, usage, and propagated exception identical to tracing-off (span error swallowed).
- Tracing disabled: identical result, usage, imports, and exception behavior.
- Lean-import subprocess: base install without the tracing extra imports and runs with no span dependency error.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Each attempted fallback candidate emits exactly one rebar OTel span, ordered zero-based, with no duplicate from `instrument_all`; verified by an in-memory exporter test.
- [x] Every candidate span parents to the single Agent model-request span (ambient-context nesting); verified by parent-span-id assertions.
- [x] Each candidate span carries provider-qualified model identity; verified by attribute assertions.
- [x] Each candidate span carries an `outcome` drawn only from {`returned`,`raised`}: the answering model `returned`, each earlier failed candidate `raised`; verified by attribute assertions.
- [x] The existing ordered `FallbackExceptionGroup` and resolution classification are unchanged by instrumentation; verified by fallback-chain tests.
- [x] The S2-preserved bug-895c native-to-prompted fallback is legible as a native attempt `raised` then a prompted attempt `returned`, with no change to the `_pai_structured` control flow; verified by a downgrade trace test.
- [x] A `raised` span reason is redacted through `sanitize_diagnostic` (keyed under `message`) and contains no prompt, response, credential, endpoint secret, or unsanitized exception body; verified by secret-canary assertions.
- [x] A span-emission or exporter failure while tracing is ENABLED leaves the fallback result, `RunUsage`, and propagated exception identical to tracing-off; verified by a tracing-ON span-failure test.
- [x] `_usage`, `UsageLimits`, pricing, and durable usage JSONL are identical with tracing on and off and contain no candidate counter; verified by paired-result assertions.
- [x] The base install without the tracing extra imports and runs with no span dependency error; verified by a lean-import subprocess test.
baseline.summary: RP-01 S4 — Trace fallback and downgrade candidates without redefining usage

# rebar's hardcoded Jira vocabularies disagree with a real DC instance in four places

## Provenance

Found by the capability-map job (run **30863672922**, ticket 259b) on its first execution — Jira DC 8.17.1, Server + Software licensed, a Scrum-template project. Every item below is a direct comparison of a rebar constant against what the instance actually offers, with the raw REST request/response recorded in that run's `evidence.json`.

None of these would surface as a test failure today. Three are silent by construction.

## The four defects

**1. Status `IDEA` does not exist.** `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA['idea'] = 'IDEA'` (`jira_family/value_maps.py`), but no status of that name exists in ANY workflow bound to ANY issue type on the instance. Every SCRUM type uses "Software Simplified Workflow for Project SCRUM", whose only statuses are To Do / In Progress / Done. **A local `idea` ticket can therefore never sync its status** — the mapped value matches nothing. Silent: the transition simply never resolves.

**2. Label limit is 254, not 255.** `JIRA_LABEL_MAX_CHARS = 255` (`value_maps.py:58`) is INCLUSIVE, but the instance REJECTS a 255-character label. The effective ceiling is 254. So a label of exactly 255 chars is fitted to the limit and then rejected by Jira — and per bug 6afc, ACLI exits 0 on that class of rejection, so it fails silently and re-emits. (`JIRA_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS = 254` was checked in the same pass and IS correct.)

**3. Two distinct issue types are both named `Task`** (ids 10003 and 10004). Any name-based type resolution is ambiguous and may bind to the wrong one, non-deterministically. rebar's `LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA` maps by NAME.

**4. Three link relations are unrepresentable on stock Jira** — `supersedes`, `discovered_from`, `caused_by` have no corresponding link type. `RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK` maps only `blocks`, `depends_on` and `relates_to`, so those three silently do not sync. Whether that is intended is not recorded anywhere; it should be a documented decision rather than an accident.

## What the same pass CONFIRMED as correct, so it is not re-litigated

Issue types Bug/Story/Task/Epic all present; all five priorities (Highest..Lowest) present; link types Blocks and Relates present; **and the link DIRECTIONS verified end-to-end** — `blocks` and `depends_on` are true inverses of the single `Blocks` type, `relates_to` symmetric, all three confirmed by creating real links and reading both endpoints. That was the highest-risk vocabulary (a direction error inverts a dependency silently) and it is correct.

Transition names also equal their destination status names on this workflow, so bug 7f93's name-vs-destination hazard does not currently bite here — but that is a property of THIS workflow, not a guarantee.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] each of the four is triaged: fixed, or recorded as an accepted limitation with a reason
- [x] the `idea` status gap has a decision — map it to an existing status, or state that `idea`
      tickets deliberately do not sync status
- [x] the label limit is corrected to the enforced value, with a test that would catch an
      off-by-one against the instance rather than against a constant
- [x] the duplicate `Task` name is handled by resolving types by ID where available, or the
      ambiguity is documented as harmless with evidence
- [x] the three unmapped relations are documented as deliberate, or mapped
- [x] the declared environment contract (3fe5) asserts these so a future instance change fails loudly

## Criteria dispositions (operator, 2026-08-04) — Gerrit 1375 + 1381

**AC1 / AC2 / AC5 — MET.** All four findings triaged; see the TRIAGE-2E47-A comment. `idea` is a documented operator prerequisite (unchanged, deliberately). The unmapped relations are now DATA (`UNSYNCED_RELATIONS`, four of them with per-relation reasons) with a test asserting the synced and unsynced sets exactly partition `rebar.types.Relation`, so a new relation with no sync decision fails loudly instead of silently never syncing.

**AC3 — AMENDED, because the criterion as written prescribes an outcome that is WRONG.** It says to correct the label limit "to the enforced value". Doing that turns four characterization oracles red: `sanitize_label` RAISES above the ceiling rather than truncating, so a shared 254 makes the live-validated CLOUD path reject a 255-char label that Cloud accepts — trading a silent DC defect for a loud Cloud regression, which is the one thing this epic was built to prevent. Same class of amendment as the epic's own AC5 note ("prescribes an outcome that would be WRONG if achieved").

What this ticket delivers instead, and what moves:
* DELIVERED — the TEST half of AC3, which is the part that was actually missing: a live cell posts 254
  and 255-character labels to the real instance and reads them back, with 254 as a control leg, so the
  off-by-one is measured against the INSTANCE rather than against a constant agreeing with itself.
  Unit pins now use literal 255/256 for the same reason.
* MOVED — the per-deployment ceiling itself, to [rebar:2c93-ce1c-127e-4d58], which also records the two
  decisions it needs (raise-vs-truncate, and whether Cloud's documentary 255 is even real — if Cloud
  also rejects 255 the divergence collapses and a shared 254 becomes correct, so that measurement
  comes first).

**AC4 — the measurement is in place; it needs one harness run to report.** Resolving types by ID is a change to the DC create path, and "documented as harmless with evidence" needs evidence I did not have: whether the PROVISIONED PROJECT's issue-type scheme exposes `Task` once or twice. A create posts `issuetype: {"name": ...}` scoped to a project, so that — not the instance-wide duplicate — is what can actually reach rebar. The 3fe5 declared-environment contract now asserts project-scoped issue-type name uniqueness and prints the instance-wide entries as evidence (Gerrit 1381). It FAILS provisioning if a name is offered twice, which is the condition under which a create could bind non-deterministically.

**AC6 — satisfied by the same contract change**, for the items that belong there: issue-type name uniqueness is asserted at provisioning time where a future image change fails loudly and attributably, and the label ceiling is asserted against the instance by the live cell.
baseline.summary: rebar's hardcoded Jira vocabularies disagree with a real DC instance in four places

# Elevate trust-boundary crossing to an explicit framing in the T5c plan-review security overlay

## Context
Follow-up to a278 (container/leaf scrutiny + T10 endpoint-auth). Research on how mature
security / LLM-review projects avoid false positives converged on **trust-boundary crossing** as
the scope gate: a security concern is in scope only when a component is reachable by a LOWER-trust
actor (STRIDE Spoofing↔authn; OWASP ASVS 1.4.1 enforcement points; Semgrep/Anthropic
exploitability-over-category). Today T5c uses this idea only implicitly. Making it an explicit,
first-class framing (a) generalizes beyond auth to T5c's other dimensions and (b) sharpens the
reachability judgement — while keeping rebar's own local/in-process work false-positive-free.
Scope note: this is for **T5c only** — T10's `endpoint_access_contract` stays focused on infra
contract-completeness and must NOT be re-scoped to the general framing (approved: don't blur T10).

Files: `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T5c.md` (rubric), `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` (T5c checklist if needed).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `plan_review_T5c.md` leads with an explicit TRUST-BOUNDARY scope gate: a security finding is in
      scope only when the plan introduces/exposes a component reachable by a lower-trust actor
      (public internet, another tenant, an untrusted network, an unauthenticated user); in-process /
      local-CLI / loopback-only surfaces PASS as not-applicable.
- [ ] The framing GENERALIZES beyond auth: the same gate governs T5c's existing dimensions
      (authn/authz, encryption-in-transit, least-privilege, secret lifecycle) — each fires only where
      a boundary is actually crossed.
- [ ] Preserves the positive-pass carve-out (pure library / in-process module / single-user local CLI /
      loopback-only → PASS, no auth demanded) so rebar's own local work stays FP-free.
- [ ] Zero-trust caveat encoded: a single-tenant / private network is LOWER severity, not exempt.
- [ ] T10 `endpoint_access_contract` is left unchanged (no blurring); a test/asserts T10 still fires
      only on infra intent.
- [ ] Validation: recalibrated T5c run against `d251` (or an equivalent networked-service plan)
      surfaces the security surface via the trust-boundary gate; run against a local no-network
      negative (`8a1c`/`4702`) PASSes as not-applicable — old-vs-new documented.
- [ ] `validate-routing` + plan-review unit tests + `make lint` green.
baseline.summary: Trust-boundary framing for the T5c plan-review security overlay (generalize the scope gate; keep T10 focused)

## Why
Epic 88ab (elfish-chair-lug) S3. R3 requires BOTH votes on every feature-branch change and on the merge change. The design EXPECTED g2p dispatch to be branch-agnostic; this story VERIFIES that and, per the verified finding below, REMEDIATES the gap it exposes. ASSUMES epic 1fa8 (smoky-flare-slug) is complete (g2p installed, gerrit-verify.yaml exists, two-vote submit active).

## VERIFIED FINDING (drives the revised scope)
g2p does NOT branch-filter dispatch (source: lfit/releng-gerrit_to_platform@44d5d46 patchset_created.py / github.py / helpers.py — event->workflow mapping is filename-substring based, no branch keys in gerrit_to_platform.ini). BUT g2p dispatches via GitHub `workflow_dispatch(ref=refs/heads/{GERRIT_BRANCH})`, which REQUIRES that ref to EXIST on the GitHub mirror to resolve the workflow file. `replication.config` replicates only refs/heads/main + refs/tags/* + refs/changes/* — NOT refs/heads/feature/*. So a feature/* change's dispatch targets a non-existent GitHub ref -> 422/no-op -> the change gets LLM-Review but NEVER Verified and can never satisfy the two-vote gate. Proven live: change 198 on feature/s3-ci got LLM-Review+1 and zero CI. This is the exact failure the story exists to catch.

## What (REVISED — includes the remediation)
- **AC1 (verified statement):** record the g2p branch-filtering finding above (config or no-op) with source citation in the ini spec / a short g2p-dispatch note.
- **FIX (new, required for the story's CI-coverage evidence):** `infra/gerrit/replication.config` — add `push = refs/heads/feature/*:refs/heads/feature/*` to `[remote "github"]`, scoped to feature/* (NOT a wildcard, never refs/meta/*), so the workflow_dispatch ref resolves. Documented tradeoff: feature branches become transiently visible on the mirror (deleted after merge-back; teardown handled by S6 inventory + merge-back cleanup). **Deploy** to the running Gerrit via the gerrit_etc volume; `autoReload = true` in replication.config means the plugin re-reads on change with NO Gerrit restart (verified). Back-out: remove the line; a `.bak-s3` of the prior config is kept on the box.
- Verify `checkout-gerrit-change-action` fetches a MERGE refspec so CI builds the actual merge tree (get_change_refspec computes refs/changes/NN/NNNN/P identically for merge + normal commits — the patchset ref IS the merge tree; run-log evidence).
- Prove with run-log evidence: (a) a feature/* patchset-created triggers gerrit-verify.yaml and casts Verified (POST-FIX); (b) a merge change into main gets CI on the merge tree; (c) Verified RE-RUNS (does not carry) on a re-merge (MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE); (d) `concurrency: cancel-in-progress` behaves sanely across concurrent branch + merge changes.

## Scope
g2p config + workflow verification + evidence, PLUS the replication.config feature/* fix + its live deployment (the prerequisite that makes feature/* CI possible — without it none of the run-log ACs can be produced). No label/ACL config (S1), no bot code (S2), no doc prose beyond the ini/dispatch spec (S4). The replication change is the minimal remediation, not new gate behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Verified statement on g2p branch filtering recorded (config or no-op), with source/doc citation, in the ini/dispatch spec
- [ ] replication.config replicates feature/* (committed) AND deployed live via autoReload (no restart); a newly-created feature branch auto-replicates to the GitHub mirror (proven)
- [ ] Run-log evidence: feature/* patchset triggers gerrit-verify.yaml and casts Verified (post-fix)
- [ ] Run-log evidence: merge change gets CI on the actual merge tree via the merge refspec
- [ ] Run-log evidence: Verified re-runs on a re-merge; no carry observed
- [ ] Concurrency behavior across branch + merge changes documented with a run example
baseline.summary: S3: CI (Verified) coverage on feature branches + merge changes — g2p dispatch verified

## Reproduction Steps
1. Close a work ticket with the completion-verification gate enabled (verify.require_completion_verification_for_close=true).
2. For certain inputs (observed deterministically on ticket b593, a tiny pyproject metadata diff), the verify-step model emits its structured output as a top-level JSON **array** (a bare list of findings) rather than the completion_verdict **object**.
3. src/rebar/llm/structured.py validate_to() raises StructuredOutputError('structured output must be a JSON object, got list'); the workflow step 'decide@then/verify' fails and the close is blocked fail-closed.

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: verifier tolerates/normalizes a single-verdict wrapped in a list (or the verify prompt/schema forces an object), producing a PASS/FAIL verdict.
- Actual: deterministic parse failure (5/5 attempts); the ticket cannot earn a signed completion attestation and must be --force-closed (left uncertified).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] tolerant_parse/validate_to in src/rebar/llm/structured.py robustly handles a top-level array carrying one verdict object (unwrap), OR the completion verify step constrains output to an object.
- [x] A regression test reproduces the 'got list' input and asserts a verdict is produced.
- [x] Closing a previously-affected ticket earns a signed completion-verifier PASS.

## 2026-08-08 resolution evidence

Exact former list-shaped verifier payloads now return real verdicts through validate_to/parse_structured; 3 targeted tests passed. Canonical implementation: 6f0a-0c1e-cdf8-4a8d.

## Why

The T2 semantic-resolution tier (epic `850f`) was deferred out of the v1 code-grounding floor as a
placeholder with three candidate backends and unresolved security/determinism tradeoffs. Before any
code lands, the selection and the confirm-only policy must be recorded as a durable decision, and the
IaC grounding lane (a different domain) must be split out so it is not silently folded into this epic.
This story produces that record; S2/S3 implement against it.

## What

- Add an ADR at `docs/adr/00NN-code-grounding-t2-semantic-resolution.md` (next free ADR number) that
  records:
  - **Decision:** v1 T2 backend = one-shot compiler/checker-CLI diagnostics, first language Python via
    `pyright --outputjson`. LSP-client-library and containerized/hermetic tiers are **deferred** (with
    their cost/security/determinism tradeoffs stated: LSP multiplies per-language server/runtime/config
    surface; containerized needs an egress-locked single-tenant microVM sandbox because building
    untrusted client repos is arbitrary code execution).
  - **Confirm-only mapping:** a T2 `refuted` is emitted only when the checker ran to completion (file has no
    import-resolution diagnostics = environment built) and there is no diagnostic at the reference;
    every other case (tool-absent / unsupported-lang / no-file / parse-error / timeout / crash /
    env-not-built / diagnostic-present) is `abstain` with a closed structured reason. T2 never asserts
    an absence and never sits on a deterministic blocking path.
  - **Minimal-seam decision (Rule-of-Three):** with one concrete backend, no `T2Backend` Protocol +
    plugin registry — S2 ships a single `refute_semantic()` dispatch function selected by config. A
    future backend adds a name + a branch.
  - **Consumers unchanged:** T2 records reuse the existing three-valued contract and closed
    vocabularies (`TIER_T2` already exists), so `5fd2`/`9da1` consumers need no edit.
- Reference the ADR from `docs/grounding.md` (a one-line pointer under the tiers section) so the design
  is discoverable from the grounding doc.
- Create a **sibling epic** for the IaC grounding lane (`terraform validate` = IaC T1, Registry
  provider/module existence = IaC T0, `terraform plan` = IaC T2) and `link <iac-epic> 850f relates_to`
  so the split is recorded in the graph.

## Scope

In scope: the ADR document, the `docs/grounding.md` pointer, and the sibling IaC epic + link. Out of
scope: any `src/` change (that is S2/S3) — this is a design/doc-only story.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/adr/0030-code-grounding-t2-semantic-resolution.md` exists and follows the repo's ADR
      format (Status/Date/Context/Decision/Consequences headings, matching a sibling ADR's structure).
- [ ] The ADR records the backend-selection decision (pyright compiler-CLI diagnostics for v1).
- [ ] The ADR records the confirm-only mapping (`refuted` only on a completed run with no
      import-resolution diagnostics and no diagnostic at the reference; every other case `abstain`).
- [ ] The ADR records the minimal-seam (no-registry) rationale and the LSP/containerized deferral with
      their stated tradeoffs.
- [ ] `docs/grounding.md` links to the new ADR from its tiers/T2 section.
- [ ] A sibling epic for the IaC grounding lane exists, linked `relates_to` epic `850f`, with a
      description scoping the IaC T0/T1/T2 tiers.
- [ ] `make lint` exits 0.
- [ ] The change touches only files under `docs/` (no `src/` edits).
baseline.summary: T2 grounding S1: ADR — select pyright compiler-CLI diagnostics backend + split IaC lane to sibling epic

## Dependencies (STACKED — review with --ref HEAD)
Builds on **ddbe** (identity + mappings) and **264f** (`resolve_mapping`), committed on this branch, not yet on origin/main. Review with `--ref HEAD`.

## Context
An inbound external user (e.g. a Jira assignee/reporter with an `accountId` + `displayName`) that has NO local identity mapping mints a PLACEHOLDER identity storing the raw `(provider, external_id, display_name)`. Re-running resolution after a real mapping appears UPGRADES the placeholder in place — idempotently, one identity not two — keyed on the provider's stable opaque id (Gitea's OriginalAuthorID discipline).

## Why
When rebar pulls a Jira ticket, its assignee/reporter/comment authors are external Jira users we may not yet know. Minting a durable placeholder (keyed on the stable accountId) preserves attribution without guessing an email, and lets a later real mapping enrich the SAME identity rather than forking a duplicate.

## What
### 1. Resolve-or-mint seam (`src/rebar/_commands/identity.py`)
`ensure_identity_for(provider, external_id, display_name, *, repo_root=None) -> str`:
- IDEMPOTENT resolve-first: call `resolve_mapping(provider, external_id, repo_root=...)`
  (264f). If it returns an existing identity id, RETURN it (do NOT create a second) —
  this is what makes a re-run yield ONE identity. Optionally UPGRADE: if that identity
  is still a placeholder and `display_name` is non-empty and differs from its current
  title, update the title in place (`edit_ticket`) — the upgrade path.
- Else MINT a placeholder: `create_identity(name=display_name or external_id,
  email="", mappings=[{"provider":provider, "external_id":external_id}], ...)` marked
  as a placeholder via a `placeholder` tag set ATOMICALLY at mint: extend
  `create_identity_core` / `create_identity` with an optional `tags` list that is
  forwarded to `create_core(..., tags=...)` (create_core already accepts `tags`), so
  the CREATE event carries `tags=["placeholder"]` in one event (no separate tag() call,
  no tagless window). `is_placeholder` checks the `placeholder` tag in compiled state
  (the reducer surfaces CREATE tags). Return the new id.
- Never raises for a lookup problem (a resolve failure falls through to mint).
- `is_placeholder(identity_id, *, repo_root=None) -> bool` helper (the `placeholder`
  tag is present).
- The mapping key is ALWAYS the provider's opaque `external_id` (never email), so the
  resolve/upgrade is provider-neutral (works for jira/github/gitea alike).

### 2. Placeholder → real upgrade
When a real mapping/identity is later established for the same `(provider, external_id)` — either a subsequent `ensure_identity_for` with a better `display_name`, or an operator enriching the identity (email/keys) and removing the `placeholder` tag — the SAME identity id is reused (resolve-first keys on `external_id`). A test adds a real name/email to the placeholder, re-runs `ensure_identity_for(same provider/external_id, ...)`, and asserts exactly ONE identity exists for that mapping (not two) and it is the upgraded record.

### 3. Inbound reconciler wiring (`apply_inbound_records.py`)
Where the inbound apply reads the inbound Jira ASSIGNEE (the only inbound user field today — `_extract_name(fields["assignee"])` at ~lines 113/258, which pulls the `displayName`), ALSO resolve the inbound user through `ensure_identity_for("jira", <accountId>, <displayName>)` so an unmapped inbound user mints/reuses a placeholder identity and the local attribution references a stable identity. Keep the existing name extraction as the human-readable fallback; the identity minting is additive and best-effort (a missing accountId falls back to the name-only behavior without failing the inbound apply).

## Scope
In: `ensure_identity_for` + `is_placeholder` (idempotent resolve-or-mint, keyed on external_id, placeholder tag, in-place upgrade) and the inbound-apply wiring. Out: outbound mapping (264f), enforcement (3183). Concurrency: minting is idempotent for SEQUENTIAL re-runs (resolve-first); the reconciler applies inbound records single- writer, so no concurrent double-mint of the same accountId is expected.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `ensure_identity_for("jira", <accountId>, <displayName>)` on an accountId with
  no existing mapping creates a placeholder identity whose title is the displayName,
  whose `mappings` contains `{"provider":"jira","external_id":<accountId>}`, and which
  `is_placeholder` reports True (test).
- [ ] Re-running `ensure_identity_for` with the SAME `(provider, external_id)` returns
  the SAME identity id and does NOT create a second — a test asserts exactly ONE
  identity maps that accountId (list/search count == 1) after two calls, even when the
  second call supplies a different display_name (which upgrades the title in place).
- [ ] The mapping key is the provider's opaque `external_id` (not email), so an
  upgrade for a different provider/id is independent — a test with two different
  `external_id`s yields two distinct identities, and the same `external_id` under a
  different `display_name` still yields one.

- [ ] Inbound wiring (best-effort): given an inbound Jira assignee field with an
  `accountId` + `displayName` and no existing mapping, applying the inbound record
  mints/reuses a placeholder identity for that accountId (test drives the inbound
  apply path with a fixture record and asserts a placeholder identity exists for the
  accountId); a record missing an `accountId` falls back to name-only behavior WITHOUT
  failing the inbound apply.

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/_commands/identity.py` (ensure_identity_for + is_placeholder)
- `src/rebar/__init__.py` + `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` (export ensure_identity_for/is_placeholder)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` (resolve inbound Jira user via ensure_identity_for, additive/best-effort)
baseline.summary: identity: inbound ghost/placeholder + idempotent auto-upgrade

baseline.description:
The plan-review gate's **Pass-2 verifier returns an empty `verifications` list**, so every Pass-1 finding reaches `pass3_decide` with no verification → `decision: indeterminate, reason: "no-verification"`. When ALL findings are no-verification (zero resolved), the verdict is forced INDETERMINATE, which is NOT signable → the plan-review claim gate blocks the ticket. This blocked epic 5ca8's children (clay-cake-act: 0 blocking, deterministic floor all PASS, 4 findings all no-verification → INDETERMINATE across multiple plan-hardening passes). It affects ANY `mode="structured"` prompted LLM op (the same json-repair path).

## Root cause (proven via joe-debug, runtime evidence)
The structured-output reliability stack (story 1268) has two paths in `_pai_structured` (`src/rebar/llm/runner.py`): a NATIVE path (`Agent(model, output_type=mode_obj)` — schema enforced) and an Anthropic PROMPTED path that generates FREE TEXT then tolerantly parses (json-repair). `structured.output_mode` returns `PromptedOutput(model_cls)` for Anthropic (which would inject the schema into the prompt), BUT the prompted branch built `Agent(model, **kwargs)` with `output_type=str` and **discarded `mode_obj`** — so the JSON schema was NEVER conveyed to the model. The model, knowing fields only from the verifier prompt's PROSE ("severity ATTRIBUTES", "BINARY sub-answers"), emitted plausible-but-divergent keys — captured live:

```
{"findings": [{"index": 0, "attributes": {...}, "sub_answers": {...}}]}
```

instead of the `plan_review_verification` contract shape `{"verifications": [{"index", "severity_attributes", "binary"}]}`. `VerificationOutput` ignores unknown keys, so tolerant parsing produced `VerificationOutput(verifications=[])` — a VALID, EMPTY object, no error raised. Instrumented run: `verify-step … verifs_per_chunk=[0] merged_verifs=0` → `decide: findings=4 raw_verifs=0` → all 4 no-verification.

## Reproduction Steps
1. `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=50 rebar review-plan <a-task-with-code-grounded-findings> -o json`.
2. Inspect `indeterminate` findings — all carry `reason: "no-verification"`; `blocking`/`advisory` empty; verdict INDETERMINATE despite the deterministic floor passing.

- **Expected:** the verifier emits schema-conforming `verifications` (keyed by 0-based `index`); `pass3_decide` resolves each finding to advisory/dropped; the verdict reaches PASS/BLOCK.
- **Actual:** the verifier emits a divergent JSON shape (schema never conveyed) → empty `verifications` → all findings no-verification → INDETERMINATE.

## Fix
- `src/rebar/llm/structured.py`: add `schema_directive(model_cls)` rendering the model's JSON Schema with a "use these EXACT keys; JSON only" directive.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` `_pai_structured` PROMPTED path: append `schema_directive(model_cls)` to the initial prompt AND the bounded-retry prompt, so the model is told the exact output shape (restoring the schema-conveyance that `PromptedOutput` provides and the json-repair refactor dropped). NativeOutput path unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The prompted structured path conveys the output JSON schema to the model (a unit test with a schema-aware FunctionModel proves a `mode="structured"` run yields non-empty, correctly-keyed structured output only because the schema reached the prompt; mutation-checked).
- [ ] An OFFLINE unit test (a schema-aware `FunctionModel`, the repo's standard way to test LLM behavior without a billable call) proves the prompted structured path conveys the schema so a `mode="structured"` run yields non-empty, correctly-keyed output — RED before the fix, GREEN after, mutation-checked (`tests/unit/test_runner_structured_schema.py`). The end-to-end live `rebar review-plan` going INDETERMINATE → PASS (4 no-verification → 0 indeterminate, 2 resolved advisories) is recorded as the replication in PR #74 (not an in-repo test, since a real review-plan requires a live LLM).
- [ ] No regression: the runner-hardening / structured / pydantic-ai runner suites pass; `make check` clean.
baseline.summary: Plan-review verifier returns empty verifications (schema not conveyed in prompted structured path)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Bug 828a found that `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` told authors to name a rejected alternative, while the authoritative G6 criterion (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G6.md`) explicitly says NOT to require one because it primes implementers. The drift survived a month.

The packaged prose guides cite criterion ids inline as if authoritative — 15 distinct ids in the plan guide alone (`G6` on lines 77/130/289, `F1`, `E2`, `COH`, `ISF`, …), in both bare (`(G6)`) and backticked (`` (`G6`) ``) form — yet nothing couples them to the criteria registry. `validate_criteria_guide()` (`plan_review/registry.py:652`) is scoped by `_GUIDE_RELPATH` to the GENERATED `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` only. `tests/unit/test_guides.py` couples the guides to `coach_moves.MOVE_REGISTRY` only. So a criterion's rubric can be rewritten and every prose paraphrase of it silently becomes a lie.

## Approach — a citation PIN manifest (the prose is never regenerated)

A gate cannot mechanically judge whether prose accurately paraphrases a rubric; that is a semantic call. What it CAN do is refuse to let a cited criterion change **silently**. So the gate converts an invisible semantic drift into a visible, forced re-verification:

For every criterion id a packaged guide cites, pin a digest of that criterion's authoritative registry text. When the criterion's text changes, the pin no longer matches and the gate fails, naming the guide, the criterion, and the remedy: re-read the criterion, confirm the guide's claim about it still holds, then re-pin.

This reuses the existing **regenerate-in-place + parity-diff** contract exactly — but the regenerated artifact is a DERIVED PIN MANIFEST, not the guide body. The hand-authored prose is never rewritten by a generator, so the objection that prose guides "cannot be regenerated the way `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is" does not apply: nothing regenerates them here. `regenerate_guide_criterion_pins()` writes the manifest; `validate_guide_criterion_pins()` diffs it — the same shape as `regenerate_criteria_guide()` / `validate_criteria_guide()` and as the `reviewers/index.json` drift gate.

### The interface the checker depends on

The extractor keys ONLY on the registry's **closed criterion-id vocabulary** (`CANONICAL_LLM`), matched at word boundaries against the guide text. It depends on NO structure or markup in the guides — no heading convention, no section layout, no fence — so ordinary prose edits (rewording, reordering, adding sections) cannot break it, and a guide restructure is not a gate failure. Both citation forms are matched by construction, since backticks are not word characters. Digests are computed over `_guide_section_body(criterion)` — the same rendering `rebar explain <id>` serves — so scenario text, checklist, posture, exec tier, and facet are all inside the pin.

The manifest is generated over the PACKAGED built-ins only (`load_criteria(repo_root="")`, as `regenerate_criteria_guide` already does), so a project's `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` overlay can never rotate the shipped pins.

### What the gate reports

1. **unknown citation** — a guide cites an id absent from the registry (renamed/removed
   criterion): the guide must be updated.
2. **stale pin** — a cited criterion's digest differs from its pin: its text changed, so the
   guide's claim about it must be re-verified and re-pinned.
3. **orphan pin** — a pin exists for an id no longer cited: prune it.
4. **missing manifest** — the pin file is absent: run the regenerator.

## Scope

- **NEW** `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/guide_parity.py` — extraction, digesting,
  `regenerate_guide_criterion_pins()`, `validate_guide_criterion_pins()`, and the
  `regenerate` / `validate` `_main`. It is a NEW module, not an append to
  `plan_review/registry.py`: that file is 755 LOC against the LOCKED hard cap of 800 in
  `.github/module-size-limit.txt`, so appending it would fail the CI module-size gate.
- **NEW** `src/rebar/_guides/criterion-pins.json` — the generated manifest, packaged
  alongside the guides it pins so it ships and is diffable in review.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py` — one line: fold
  `validate_guide_criterion_pins()` into the `validate-routing` composition at `:744`
  (`validate_packaged_routing() + validate_criteria_guide()`), which
  `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:386` already runs. No new CI step is needed.
- `tests/unit/test_guides.py` — the gate's tests.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — a short subsection telling guide authors and criterion authors what the
  gate enforces and how to clear a failure (`regenerate` after re-verifying the claim), so the
  new constraint is discoverable rather than only surfacing as a red build.

## Testing

- Mutating a cited criterion's registry text makes `validate_guide_criterion_pins()` report a
  stale pin naming that criterion and the guide that cites it (the 828a class).
- A citation of an id absent from `CANONICAL_LLM` is reported as an unknown citation.
- A pin whose id is no longer cited is reported as an orphan.
- An absent manifest is reported with the regenerator command.
- Regeneration is idempotent and canonical (byte-identical on a second run).
- The committed manifest is in sync with the registry (the drift gate itself).
- A prose-only edit that adds no new citation does NOT fail the gate (no false positive on
  ordinary guide edits).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A criterion-text change that contradicts a claim in a packaged prose guide fails a gate;
      verified by mutating a criterion in a test and asserting the gate reports the divergence
      naming the criterion and the citing guide.
- [ ] The gate covers every guide in `AUTHOR_GUIDES`, not just the plan guide; verified by a
      parameterized test over `AUTHOR_GUIDES`.
- [ ] The gate runs in CI without a new workflow step, by composition into `validate-routing`;
      verified by a test asserting the composed `_main` surfaces a pin problem.
- [ ] Regeneration is idempotent and the committed manifest is in sync; verified by tests.
- [ ] A guide edit that changes prose without changing citations does not fail the gate;
      verified by a test.
- [ ] No `src/rebar` file exceeds the 800-LOC cap.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default suite exit zero.
baseline.summary: Gate parity between packaged prose guides and the criteria registry

## Problem
The layered defenses against the attestation-laundering anti-pattern — tagging a CODE-VERIFIABLE acceptance criterion `[operator-attested]` so the completion verifier accepts a ticket comment instead of repository proof — failed to reject a live instance.

## Reproduction (today, epic fb8a-7363-e406-4e36 close)
1. Epic close failed: completion verifier hit its step budget (request_limit=24) and reported AC-19 unmet — though its proof is repo-resident (tests/unit/test_scan_scoping.py::test_fsck_default_skips_archived_and_flag_restores et al., merged 39de64871c).
2. The operator retagged AC-19 `[operator-attested]` (the anti-pattern; a misclassification — the evidence is an exact path/symbol repository fact).
3. `rebar review-plan fb8a-7363-e406-4e36` → PASS. Expected: the evidence-kind criterion (criteria_routing.json "FIRE on … a tagged repository fact grounded by exact path/symbol evidence") fires; also the AC carried NO `provenance:` continuation line, which det_measurement_provenance (plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py) is supposed to require on every tagged AC.
4. Close succeeded: the completion verifier accepted the tag at face value — correct per its prompt (completion_verifier.md "How you classify a criterion: SOLELY from an author tag"; ADR-0043 makes the tag a trust escape hatch), which is exactly why the REVIEW-side guards must be the rejection point.

## Suspected defects (investigate all)
- Evidence-kind criterion did not fire on a tagged repo-provable AC at re-review time (routing overlay not applied? criterion advisory instead of blocking? re-review of an in_progress ticket skips it?).
- det_measurement_provenance did not flag the missing `provenance:` line (same questions; det_floor.py wiring says ADVISORY — if so, advisory is insufficient for this class).
- Consider a deterministic pre-close guard: a criterion whose text cites an exact repo path/symbol (or whose evidence comment does) but carries the tag is auto-rejected before any LLM runs.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Root cause identified for why the plan-review evidence-kind guard passed a tagged repository fact (with the failing review run cited).
- [x] A mistagged code-verifiable AC (repo path/symbol evidence exists) is REJECTED before close: reproduced RED with a fixture ticket, then GREEN after the fix.
- [x] A tagged AC missing its `provenance:` continuation line is rejected (or the advisory is promoted to blocking for close-path reviews), with tests.
- [x] Legitimately external ACs (deploy/vote/console evidence with provenance) still pass: guard test.
- [x] [operator-attested] `make lint`/`make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
  provenance: environment=rebar.solutions.navateam.com (Gerrit) + GitHub Actions CI; principal=session operator via authenticated Gerrit REST (git-credential identity); privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — GET /a/changes/1791/detail read LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 before submit; change now MERGED, merge f9cfefa5b9 reachable from origin/main.

## Completion state

This epic is complete. It replaces the fragmented Jira-specific operator surface with one provider-neutral, Python-first bridge surface while retaining every live legacy contract needed by existing workflows and environments. Twenty descendants are closed; their code is merged, including final Gerrit change 1595, and the completed tree is present at ref `694cf894def36241724e7049e3308d782037ef6d`.

## Product and compatibility decisions

- The canonical noun is `bridge`; the design is intentionally tracker-neutral.
- `bridge preview` and `bridge sync` are primary. `reconcile` remains an explicit compatibility adapter with its historical safe dry-run default.
- Canonical verbs are setup, check-access, fsck, status, preview, sync, pause, and resume.
- `bridge-status` remains a compatibility entrypoint. The audited-dead `purge-bridge` spelling remains removed.
- Canonical exits are 0, 1, and 2. Legacy adapters retain historical 3, 4, and 75 translations where older workflows and environments depend on them.
- Canonical operational selection uses `--max-changes`, `--only`, `--except`, and `--max-age`, with user-facing help that does not expose engine internals.
- Pause state is remote-persisted, includes a reason, and remains readable by mixed-version fleets.
- Destructive repair and normal bridge operation no longer require the GitHub-specific `gh` CLI.

The default inversion is deliberate and covered through real entrypoints: argument-less `reconcile` remains non-mutating, while argument-less `bridge sync` is the canonical mutating command. Compatibility is implemented as explicit adapters rather than a naive alias.

## Three interfaces

All supported interfaces expose the bridge functionality through shared Python services:

- Python library: public imports provide the bridge operations and preserve legacy reconcile behavior.
- CLI: `rebar bridge ...` is canonical; retained commands and flags normalize through compatibility adapters.
- MCP server: MCP tools expose the same bridge capabilities and route through the same library/core contracts.

Automated workflows use the same Python core. Reads, preview, and status remain compatible while outbound sync/delivery selects its intended strictness explicitly. No surface has a private reimplementation of bridge semantics.

## Three install paths

The feature works from all supported installation routes:

- brew installs the packaged `rebar` CLI and Python implementation.
- pip installs the same library and console entrypoints.
- MCP-server installation runs the same bridge library/core through `rebar-mcp`.

No supported path depends on an editable checkout, repository-only helper, ambient Python, or a newly introduced shell script. Runtime ownership is Python; YAML, Jenkins, and GitLab files remain thin declarative wrappers.

## Portable automation and delivery

The bridge is runner-neutral across local execution, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, and bare environments. Provider wrappers share code-derived exit behavior, secrets vocabulary, and timeout policy. Full-depth execution succeeds; shallow history fails with a named diagnostic. Jenkins secret use avoids Groovy interpolation. GitLab configuration is validated offline against its vendored pinned schema. Required shellcheck coverage validates the unavoidable provider shell bodies as test artifacts; shellcheck is not a runtime dependency and bridge behavior is not implemented in shell.

Tickets-branch delivery is also Python-owned:

- `src/rebar/_store/push.py` owns CAS retry, fetch-and-merge recovery, strict failure classification, and the terminal push budget.
- The locked Python `commit-and-push` entrypoint owns staging, commit identity/subject, and delivery.
- The bridge workflow invokes `rebar bridge run`; the canary invokes the Python push adapter once.
- Workflow-local CAS loops and the stale raw-git exemption rationale are absent.
- Existing Python, CLI, MCP, importer, and ticket-store callers remain best effort unless explicitly adapted.

## ADR numbering and indexing

ADR 0092 records the bridge-primary vocabulary and explicit compatibility-adapter decision. It complies with the current ADR convention:

- the filename is `docs/adr/0092-bridge-primary-vocabulary-compatibility-adapters.md`;
- the heading uses the same unique four-digit number;
- `docs/adr/README.md` contains the matching 0092 index entry;
- the repository ADR collision/index gate recognizes the file;
- later changes updated ADR 0092 and the older ADR 0027/0070 references without creating a duplicate or out-of-index decision.

## Verification evidence

The merged descendant changes passed Gerrit LLM review and CI. The combined RED-first and held-out coverage includes:

- real CLI entrypoint parity for canonical and legacy defaults;
- Python-library and MCP facade parity;
- canonical 0/1/2 and legacy 3/4/75 exit behavior;
- pause/resume persistence, reason handling, and mixed-version reads;
- local, GitHub, Jenkins, GitLab, bare, full-depth, and shallow-history contracts;
- successful, contended, and rejected tickets-branch pushes in real temporary git repositories;
- strict workflow failure and best-effort legacy caller controls;
- documentation/help/schema/release-note stale-vocabulary sweeps;
- ADR uniqueness and index coverage;
- repository lint, typecheck, full tests, module-size, packaging, and workflow gates.

The former broken user-guide `--dry-run` example has regression coverage. The CLI whitelist is gone. Current workflows and documentation use canonical bridge vocabulary while compatibility tests keep older environments working.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The canonical CLI exposes setup, check-access, fsck, status, preview, sync, pause, and resume under `rebar bridge`.
- [x] Argument-less legacy `reconcile` remains dry-run.
- [x] Argument-less canonical `bridge sync` remains live.
- [x] Legacy `bridge-status` remains usable.
- [x] Canonical exit codes are 0, 1, and 2.
- [x] Historical 3, 4, and 75 translations remain available through legacy adapters.
- [x] The Python library exposes the bridge surface.
- [x] The CLI exposes the bridge surface.
- [x] The MCP server exposes the bridge surface.
- [x] brew installation executes the packaged bridge implementation.
- [x] pip installation executes the packaged bridge implementation.
- [x] MCP-server installation executes the packaged bridge implementation.
- [x] Pause state is durable and mixed-version safe.
- [x] Core operations have no required `gh` dependency.
- [x] Local, GitHub, Jenkins, GitLab, and bare environments use the same runner-neutral core.
- [x] Python core owns tickets-branch CAS delivery.
- [x] No workflow-local CAS retry loop remains.
- [x] ADR 0092 has a unique convention-compliant number.
- [x] ADR 0092 is indexed in `docs/adr/README.md`.
- [x] All 20 descendants are closed.
- [x] Every merged code change passed both Gerrit review gates before submission.

## Rollback and residual gaps

The migration is additive and has no persisted-schema backfill. Rollback must restore a workflow delivery implementation before reverting its Python strict adapter, and retained legacy adapters provide the operational fallback. Persistent pause readers accept old and new records, so downgrade remains safe.

Residual-gap sweep: no interface, install path, provider environment, legacy vocabulary, held-out test tier, escalation compromise, or deferred blocking review finding remains undispositioned. Shell snippets remain only where provider configuration requires them and are validated test artifacts; application behavior remains Python-owned.
baseline.summary: Bridge redesign: one portable command surface for tracker sync

# The ticket store must be mutated through rebar, never through git stash

`_store/push.py` performs a stash -> merge -> pop dance inside the tickets worktree (module docstring, bug 12a6), with `_resolve_conflicted_pop` (push.py:167-200) to repair a pop that applies with conflict (bug 6818). It ends by dropping the stash (push.py:200).

## Why the design is unsound
Its stated assumption is that "the stashed working-tree edits live on reconciler-REGENERABLE files" (push.py:170-176). That assumption does not hold, because **git's stash stack is shared across every worktree of a repository**. `.tickets-tracker` is a LINKED WORKTREE of `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.git`, and this machine currently has ELEVEN worktrees on that repo. A `git stash pop` executed in the tickets worktree can therefore pop a stash created in a SOURCE worktree.

## Observed incident
A stash created on branch `fix-c5b3-scc-byfile` was popped into the tickets worktree:

    stash@{0}: On fix-c5b3-scc-byfile: RECOVERED measurement-provenance work
    (ADR 0061 / det_measurement_provenance) displaced into worktree fix-c5b3-scc-byfile
    by a shared-stash race; backup at /tmp/RECOVERED-stash-race

Its contents are exactly the two paths that kept conflicting in the tracker:
    .rebar/criteria_routing.json            +23
    src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py  +9
Neither is reconciler-regenerable; both are source. Effects:
- SOURCE files (src/, docs/, tests/, .rebar/) appeared in the tickets worktree, which tracks
  no source tree at all — origin/tickets is clean, so this is purely local corruption.
- The index was left with unmerged (DU) entries and NO MERGE_HEAD — a stranded state that
  blocks EVERY ticket write. It oscillated (4 unmerged -> 0 -> 4) as concurrent rebar
  operations popped and re-stashed, so manual cleanup did not hold.
- It blocked the close of bug beb1 whose completion verification had already PASSED, and
  caused two COMPLETION_VERDICT sidecars to be lost ("could not be written").
- The stash message records that this race had ALREADY displaced work once before.

## Principle
The ticket system is an event-sourced store with its own API. It must be mutated through rebar, not by direct filesystem/git manipulation of the tracker worktree. `git stash` in particular is a REPO-GLOBAL operation being used for worktree-local intent, which is the category error here.

(For the record: agents have also been doing direct git in the tracker — this session used `git add -A` / `commit` / `merge` / `push` / `rm` there during a remediation. That is the same violation from the other direction and should also be designed out, e.g. a locked commit-and-push entrypoint that agents use instead.)

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] rebar performs NO `git stash` operation in the tickets worktree. Replace the
      stash->merge->pop dance with a mechanism that cannot touch a shared, repo-global stack —
      e.g. commit-then-merge on the tickets branch, a worktree-scoped temporary ref, or a
      `git -c stash.useBuiltin` free path that stages into a dedicated ref.
- [x] If any stash-like step is unavoidable, it must be provably scoped so it can never apply
      a stash entry created by another worktree/branch (assert the stash's branch-of-origin
      before popping, and refuse otherwise).
- [x] Held-out test: with an unrelated stash created on a DIFFERENT branch of the same repo,
      a tickets-store write that hits the push-retry path must not apply it and must not
      strand the index.
- [x] `_resolve_conflicted_pop`'s regenerable-files assumption is either enforced or removed.
- [x] fsck (or the store write path) reports a tickets worktree containing tracked-source
      paths, since origin/tickets legitimately has none.
baseline.summary: rebar must not use git stash in the tickets worktree — the stash stack is shared across all worktrees

baseline.description:
# Asymmetric attestation foundation — DSSE envelope + SSHSIG scheme + pluggable-scheme substrate

## Context
rebar signs its attestations (plan-review, completion-verifier verdicts) with a **symmetric HMAC** keyed on a per-environment secret (`src/rebar/signing.py`; `.signing-key` / `REBAR_SIGNING_KEY`). Two upcoming capabilities — per-person **authorship** signing (the identity epic) and third-party-verifiable **operation certificates** (the op-cert epic) — both need **asymmetric** signatures (verify-by-anyone, forge-by-none) over attestation bytes, verified offline. Building that signing layer twice would duplicate security-critical code and worsen the namespace collision already forming on the `SIGNATURE` event type / `signature` / `key_id` fields. **Beneficiary:** the two consumer epics (and their end users) — they get one hardened, standards-based signing substrate instead of two divergent stacks.

## Approach (and why)
Reuse established standards rather than hand-roll crypto:
- **DSSE (Dead Simple Signing Envelope)** as the envelope, signing `PAE(payloadType, body)` over
  exact opaque bytes. PAE eliminates the JSON re-serialization / canonicalization attack class (we
  never re-serialize parsed JSON to verify) and carries **no in-band `alg`** the verifier trusts —
  closing the JWT `alg`-confusion class (RFC 8725). DSSE is the Sigstore/in-toto/SLSA standard;
  ~30 lines, offline, scheme-agnostic.
- **SSHSIG via OpenSSH `ssh-keygen -Y`** (stdlib `subprocess`, **no new core dependency**) as the
  first asymmetric scheme — reuses the reference implementation and developers' existing SSH keys;
  verified offline against an `allowed_signers`-format trust input. Fail-closed was confirmed
  experimentally (wrong namespace / unknown principal / substituted key / tampered bytes / expired
  window all exit non-zero; `-Y check-novalidate` is structure-only and is never used for authz).
- **Pluggable scheme registry + per-kind policy table** (`kind → {scheme, namespace, trust-root}`),
  pinned out-of-band; the verifier **never** selects the scheme from record data. The existing
  **HMAC is registered as a legacy scheme** so current attestations keep verifying unchanged (this
  is the expand phase; the HMAC→asymmetric cutover for operation-certs is the op-cert epic's
  contract phase).

Alternative considered and rejected: `securesystemslib` for signing — it has **no SSH signer** (so it would not cover the authorship path) and pulls `cryptography` (heavy) for Ed25519; core stays stdlib-only.

## Scope
- **In:** a new attestation-substrate module (DSSE envelope + PAE; scheme registry; SSHSIG scheme
  via subprocess; per-kind policy table; verify-dispatch with domain separation); registration of
  the existing HMAC as a legacy scheme; an ADR; unit/behavioral tests.
- **Out:** any identity entity or authorship kind (identity epic); any change to operation-cert
  behavior / actor / enforcement (op-cert epic); **removing** HMAC (op-cert epic's contract phase).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A new module (e.g. `src/rebar/attest/`) exposes `sign(kind, body_bytes) -> envelope` and
      `verify(kind, envelope, trust_root) -> verdict`, where `kind` selects `{scheme, namespace,
      trust-root}` from an out-of-band policy table (not from the envelope). A unit test asserts a
      record whose in-band scheme field is tampered still verifies under the policy-pinned scheme
      (no `alg` confusion).
- [ ] DSSE PAE is implemented per the v1.0.0 spec
      (`PAE(type,body)="DSSEv1" SP len(type) SP type SP len(body) SP body`), proven by a unit test
      against the spec's worked example; a test with duplicate/re-ordered JSON keys demonstrates
      verify operates on the exact stored bytes and does not re-serialize.
- [ ] The SSHSIG scheme signs and verifies via `ssh-keygen -Y` in a subprocess using argv arrays
      (no shell), branches only on exit code, and allowlist-validates namespace + principal. A test
      matrix asserts fail-closed on: tampered bytes, wrong namespace, unknown principal, substituted
      key, and expired validity window.
- [ ] The existing HMAC signer is registered as a legacy scheme; a plan-review/completion-verifier
      attestation created before this change still returns verdict `certified` (regression test).
- [ ] `ssh-keygen` availability/version (>= 8.9 for validity intervals) is detected; its absence
      fails closed with a clear error (test asserts no silent pass).
- [ ] An ADR under `docs/adr/` records the substrate: DSSE envelope, pluggable scheme, per-kind
      policy table, domain separation, HMAC-as-legacy.
- [ ] One signing substrate exists that both consumer epics import; no consumer needs its own crypto.
- [ ] Signatures are produced/verified over DSSE-PAE bytes; verification never re-serializes parsed JSON
- [ ] The SSHSIG scheme signs/verifies offline via `ssh-keygen` with **no new core runtime dependency**
- [ ] Existing plan-review / completion-verifier attestations still verify (HMAC as a registered legacy

## Intended decomposition (children)
1. DSSE envelope + PAE module (+ spec-example + duplicate-key tests).
2. Scheme registry + per-kind policy table + verify-dispatch (domain separation; alg-confusion test).
3. SSHSIG scheme via `ssh-keygen` (fail-closed subprocess contract + test matrix).
4. Register existing HMAC as a legacy scheme (regression test).
5. ADR + docs.

## Prior art / grounding
DSSE protocol v1.0.0 (secure-systems-lab/dsse); in-toto attestation; OpenSSH PROTOCOL.sshsig + `allowed_signers`; git SSH commit signing (`gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile`); RFC 8725 (JWT BCP); RFC 8785 (JCS, considered and rejected in favour of DSSE PAE). Fail-closed behavior of `ssh-keygen -Y verify` confirmed by direct experiment in this environment (OpenSSH 10.2).
baseline.summary: Asymmetric attestation foundation — DSSE envelope + SSHSIG scheme + pluggable-scheme substrate

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Every recurrence of the schema-blind extraction class was diagnosed from a lucky console capture; when the reask loop in src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py (the prompted branch of `_pai_structured`, the `for _ in range(structured.OUTPUT_RETRIES + 1)` loop that ends in `raise last`) exhausts `OUTPUT_RETRIES` today, the raw reply is discarded and the failure is not replayable. The store's posture is that durable records carry no response text (usage-log precedent), so capture must be opt-in and local — never a default, never in ticket events.

## Approach

On the FINAL structured-parse failure of the prompted reask loop (immediately before the terminal `raise last` in `_pai_structured`, after the bounded retries are exhausted), when the new config key `llm.parse_failure_artifact_dir` resolves to a non-empty path, write one timestamped file into that directory containing the raw reply text (the last attempt's `str(result.output)`), the model id, the contract (response-model) name, and the attempt count; then append the artifact path to the raised error's message. Key unset (the default) → behavior is byte-for-byte today's `raise last`.

**Config plumbing — `llm.*` is a RESERVED section resolved in `src/rebar/llm/config.py`, NOT core `src/rebar/config.py`.** `llm.*` keys are fields on `LLMConfig` (src/rebar/llm/config.py), resolved in `LLMConfig.from_env` off the file table from `_read_llm_file_table` (which calls `_root_config.read_reserved_section("llm", …)`), with the standard CLI > env > file > default precedence provided by the `_llm_str` helper. So the key is added as a new `parse_failure_artifact_dir: str | None = None` field on `LLMConfig`, resolved in `from_env` via `_llm_str(table, cli, "REBAR_LLM_PARSE_FAILURE_ARTIFACT_DIR", "parse_failure_artifact_dir", None)` — exactly the pattern the file's other string knobs use (e.g. `base_url`). The failure hook in `structured_run.py` obtains the resolved value on the failure path via `rebar.llm.config.resolve_gate_config(...)` (the active gate config if a gate is running, else a fresh `LLMConfig.from_env`), which is how the other helpers in that module already read config.

**Why this approach (rationale).** It reuses the one config-resolution path every other `llm.*` knob uses (no new loader, no core-config coupling — importing `rebar.llm.config` is already on the failure path), and it fails CLOSED and LOCAL: the default-None key means zero behavior change and nothing is ever written unless an operator opts in on their own host, honoring the usage-log "no durable response text" posture. The write is confined to the prompted branch because the NativeOutput branch never runs the reask loop (constrained decoding validates in-SDK), so that is the only reask-exhaustion seam. The write is BEST-EFFORT: it is wrapped so any I/O error (missing/unwritable dir it cannot create, full disk) is swallowed and the ORIGINAL `last` validation error is still raised unchanged — a debugging aid must never convert a parse failure into a different, misleading failure. The directory is created if absent (`mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`). Rotation is by count: after writing, prune oldest-by-mtime so at most 20 artifacts remain per directory, so an unattended host cannot grow unbounded; concurrent writers racing the prune is acceptable (best-effort, local debugging only). A successful parse takes the `return` path and never reaches the hook, so it writes nothing.

Alternatives considered: (a) threading the dir down as a new `_pai_structured` parameter — heavier signature churn across callers for a value only the failure path needs; (b) capturing in the generic `interpret_failure` enricher — wrong seam, it handles typed provider errors, not the prompted-parse-exhaustion path. The chosen in-branch resolve is the smallest correct change.

Document the key (name, default None = off, `REBAR_LLM_PARSE_FAILURE_ARTIFACT_DIR` env alias, rotation-keeps-newest-20) in docs/config.md alongside the other `llm.*` keys.

## Scope

- src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py — the failure hook in `_pai_structured`'s prompted branch,
  before `raise last`; reads the dir via `resolve_gate_config`, writes the artifact best-effort,
  appends the path to the error message.
- src/rebar/llm/config.py — the new `parse_failure_artifact_dir: str | None` field on
  `LLMConfig` and its `_llm_str` resolution in `from_env` (the RESERVED-`llm`-section path;
  core src/rebar/config.py is deliberately NOT touched — it does not own `llm.*`).
- docs/config.md — key documentation (default + env alias + rotation).
- tests/unit/test_structured_run.py — new contrast tests (fault injected at the parse seam).

## Testing

Unit tier with config-effect contrast (shared test-design standard §6), fault injected at the parse seam (a reply fixture that fails all candidates, forcing retry exhaustion), the model driven by the `fake` runner / a stubbed agent so no live call is made:

- Key set + forced final failure → exactly one artifact exists containing the reply bytes and
  metadata (model id, contract name, attempt count); the raised error names the path.
- Key unset + same failure → no artifact, error byte-for-byte unchanged (negative control).
- Key set + successful parse → nothing written (success negative control).
- Rotation: writing a 21st artifact evicts the oldest (by mtime).
- Best-effort: an unwritable configured dir still raises the ORIGINAL parse error (the artifact
  write never masks it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Forced final parse failure with the key set writes exactly one artifact with reply +
      model id + contract name — checked by the new unit test.
- [x] With the key unset the failure path is byte-for-byte unchanged and writes nothing —
      checked by the contrast test.
- [x] A successful parse writes nothing even with the key set — checked by the negative
      control test.
- [x] The key is documented with its default and rotation behavior — checked by the
      docs/config.md section existing and naming both.
baseline.summary: Opt-in raw-reply artifact when structured parsing fails
