## Context
Remediation epic for the comprehensive quality audit recorded on ae1b-b2a0-a080-4b4e. Scope is deliberately narrowed to three buckets the audit flagged: (1) the CI default-suite reliability flake, (2) the assignee/user-facing documentation bug, and (3) the LOW-RISK, NON-OVERLAPPING slice of the file-size, complexity, and typing findings.

## Architectural principle (avoid recurrence, not just the instance)
The near-cap modules and high-CCN functions in scope share one root cause: **flat units that mix responsibilities/layers, plus duplicated infrastructure that every new call-site re-hand-rolls**. The shrink-only ratchets prevent *regression* but not *creep toward the cap*. So each child fixes the cause structurally rather than cutting lines to a number:
- Decompose by **responsibility/layer with a one-way dependency direction**, so future code has an obvious small home instead of re-inflating a god-file: run-mechanism vs. diagnostics vs. failure-interpretation (structured_run); CLI-facade vs. transaction vs. snapshot-rebuild (compact); public-API vs. recovery vs. git-primitives (event_append).
- **Centralize duplicated infrastructure WITHOUT changing node-set semantics**: the graph child promotes the 15-line _loader.py shim into a real loader+traversal layer (a `load_indexed_states` applied only where the reduce/index policy is provably identical — _blockers & _compute_dep_graph — plus a pure shared `bfs` skeleton the raw-reduce BFS functions reuse while keeping their exact traversal), removing the duplicated loop that drives the CCN without altering any function's result set.
- **Preserve public import paths** (re-export moved public symbols) so every extraction stays behavior-identical and touches only non-contended files.

Splits follow existing call-graph seams (AGENTS.md module-size policy); new modules are >=100 LOC; complexity baselines move downward only.

## Scope selection (why these and not others)
Non-overlap computed against the file_impact of all 212 in-progress tickets (audit ticket excluded); every NEW child touches only zero-contention files. Deliberately EXCLUDED:
- High-risk complexity orchestrators next_batch.compute (CCN 42) and import_ndjson.import_tickets (CCN 45) — core scheduling/import logic, not low-risk.
- The typing ratchet FLIP in pyproject.toml (contended x9) and the near-cap files runner.py/_config_schema.py/signing.py/_ref_lock.py/init.py (all contended).
- Already-tracked, out-of-requested-scope findings: mutmut lane (521b-04c3-572f-4514), repo-wide package DAG (44ea-43c6-b351-4d81), test-env hardening (def1-9c3c-6802-48bd).

## Recommended systemic follow-up (out of scope here)
The ratchets fire only AT the 800 cap / at the recorded CCN. A genuine recurrence guard is an EARLY-WARNING margin (advisory surfaced in the metrics lane at, e.g., ~650 LOC / CCN ~15) so creep is visible before it reaches the cap. That changes enforcement policy and touches the (contended) gate/CI config, so it belongs in its own proposal, not these non-overlapping stories.

## Children
- Adopted existing open tickets: fade-ea90-7564-4715 (CI flake bug) and 879f-5549-91e3-4d6f (user-facing doc drift incl. the assignee example).
- New non-overlapping tasks: split near-cap modules structured_run.py / compact.py / event_append.py; centralize graph loader/traversal to cut blocker-subsystem complexity; annotate the attest package to be typing-ratchet-ready.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] CI flake fade-ea90 resolved (or root-caused with a durable fix) so the Python 3.11 xdist worker no longer dies in test_opcert_service_app.
- [x] User-facing assignee example teaches a Jira-resolvable identity consistent with docs/config.md.
- [operator-attested] [x] The three named near-cap modules are split by responsibility along existing call-graph seams with public import paths preserved, and each ends with real headroom under the 800 cap: structured_run.py and compact.py reach the ≤500 target, and event_append.py drops to ≤640 (its git-primitive leaf extracted; recovery kept with the API to preserve the monkeypatch/test seam that couples their shared `_git_add` patch point).
- [operator-attested] [x] The graph loader/traversal duplication is centralized and the four flagged functions drop to their target CCN with graph outputs unchanged.
- [operator-attested] [x] The attest package is clean under mypy src/rebar/attest --disallow-untyped-defs (ratchet flip deferred to when pyproject.toml contention clears).
- [operator-attested] [x] Every new child edited only non-in-progress-contended files.
baseline.summary: Remediation (audit ae1b): CI-flake, assignee doc bug, and low-risk non-overlapping size/complexity/typing debt

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
When a compaction sweep holds the store write lock, a blocked session cannot tell what is holding it or whether interrupting it is safe. Both facts are already known to the code and neither reaches the operator.

Live incident 2026-08-13 (`vigilant-erasable-pony`): a sweep held `.tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock` for 24+ minutes at 0.0% CPU. The blocked session saw:

    flock: could not acquire lock after 181s (holder: host=... pid=... held=47s)

A bare pid. Identifying it as compaction required `lsof`/`ps`. The blast radius is host-wide across worktrees, so "check your own checkout" does not help.

The answer is already documented: `compact_trigger.run_sweep` guarantees "a skipped sweep is a no-op for correctness (the events stay live and the next trigger folds them)". An operator holding that guarantee can safely SIGTERM the holder. Looking at an unattributed pid, the safe response is to wait — which is exactly wrong here. One sweep was killed manually (pid 98440, 26 minutes) to unblock three agents.

## Approach
Say what the holder is, and that it is interruptible — at the two places a blocked writer already looks.

**1. Label the lock holder, ambiently.** `lock_owner._owner_stamp` writes the v2 ownership line (`rebar-lock v2 host=... ns=... pid=... start=...`) that `describe_lock_holder` renders into every `LockTimeout`. That stamp is written by `_acquire_mkdir` (`lock.py`), reached only through `lock.acquire`. Add an optional operation label so the timeout reads `... pid=98440 held=181s op=compact-sweep` instead of a bare pid.

The label must reach `_owner_stamp` WITHOUT editing the acquisition call site: the sweep's store-write-lock acquisition is `lock.acquire()` in `compact_txn._compact_locked` (`compact_txn.py:358`), invoked per ticket, and `compact_txn.py` is deliberately OUT of scope (it carries the just-landed sweep-perf change `mesodermic-vaporish-seaslug` and must not be re-touched). The satisfying mechanism is an AMBIENT label, not a new `acquire` parameter:

- `lock_owner.py` gains a process/thread-local label — a `contextvars.ContextVar` plus an
  `operation_label(label)` context manager that sets it on enter and resets on exit.
  `_owner_stamp()` reads that contextvar and, when set, appends a single colon-free `op=<label>`
  field. Unset (every ordinary writer) ⇒ the stamp is byte-identical to today's.
- The sweep sets that contextvar around its whole body at its two entry points
  (`compact_trigger.run_sweep`, `compact.py`'s sweep loop). Every `lock.acquire` beneath that
  `with` block — including the per-ticket `lock.acquire()` inside `_compact_locked`, which this
  ticket does NOT modify — writes its stamp with `op=compact-sweep`. Data flow: sweep-entry →
  contextvar → `_owner_stamp`; the label reaches the stamp ambiently and `compact_txn.py` needs
  no change. `contextvars` is the right carrier because the label is read synchronously in the
  same process/thread that later calls `acquire`: the sweep folds inline (`_sweep_one_ticket` →
  `compact_cli` → `_compact_locked`), so the ambient value is in scope at the acquisition.

The v2 format's forward-compat contract is preserved exactly: the line is COLON-FREE so an older rebar splitting on `host, sep, pid = stamp.partition(":")` finds no separator and declines to act (bug castoff-tigerseye-ammonite). A new `key=value` field keeps that (the label value is sanitized to strip any `:`, `=`, or whitespace, staying one colon-free token), and `_parse_v2_stamp` already ignores unknown fields. The label is descriptive only — `_stamp_is_stale` / `stamped_file_is_stale` never read `op=`, so reclamation is unaffected.

**2. State the remedy in the error.** `describe_lock_holder` renders the `op=` field into the holder string; `LockTimeout` recognises the known interruptible label (`compact-sweep`) in that string and appends a remedy line — that the holder is a compaction sweep, interrupting it loses no data, and the next trigger re-folds. An ordinary (unlabelled) holder gets no remedy line.

Deliberately NOT here: auto-killing a long sweep. That is a separate pre-emption policy; the reported incidents were all resolved by a human given the right information. Inform first.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_store/lock_owner.py` — an ambient operation-label contextvar + `operation_label`
  context manager; `_owner_stamp` appends an optional colon-free `op=` field (sanitized to one
  token) when set; a helper mapping a known interruptible label to its remedy text. Never
  consulted by staleness logic.
- `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` — render the `op=` label in `describe_lock_holder`; extend the
  `LockTimeout` message with the safe-to-interrupt remedy when the holder string names a known
  interruptible operation.
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py` — wrap `run_sweep`'s body in
  `lock_owner.operation_label("compact-sweep")` (the ambient carrier — not an edit to any
  acquisition call), so the store-lock acquisitions it drives via `_compact_locked` stamp it.
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` — wrap the sweep loop (`compact_all_cli`/`_run_sweep`) in the
  same `operation_label("compact-sweep")`, so a direct `rebar compact-all` is also labelled.
- `tests/unit/test_lock_holder_labelling.py` — new tests.

Portability: the mechanism is a colon-free `key=value` field in the lock stamp file plus an in-process `contextvars` label — no CI provider, external service, or platform facility — so it works identically anywhere rebar runs, with or without CI.

## Testing
- A labelled holder appears in `describe_lock_holder` and in the `LockTimeout` message
  (asserting `op=compact-sweep`, not only a pid).
- The remedy text is PRESENT for a labelled optional holder, ABSENT for an ordinary writer.
- An UNLABELLED holder renders byte-identically to today's `describe_lock_holder` output.
- The stamp stays colon-free with the label; a label containing `:`/`=`/whitespace is sanitized.
- `_parse_v2_stamp` accepts a stamp carrying an unknown extra field (forward compat).
- Reclamation is label-blind: a labelled and unlabelled stale lock adjudicate identically.
- End to end: with `operation_label("compact-sweep")` active, a real `lock.acquire` writes an
  owner stamp carrying the label — the ambient contextvar reaches `_owner_stamp` through the
  actual acquisition path `_compact_locked` uses.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A blocked writer's `LockTimeout` names the holder as a compaction sweep — a test asserts
      the message contains the operation label rather than only a pid.
- [x] The remedy text (safe, lossless) is present for a labelled optional holder — a test
      asserts it.
- [x] The remedy text is absent for an ordinary writer — a test asserts it.
- [x] An unlabelled holder's rendering is byte-identical to today's — a test pins the format.
- [x] The stamp remains colon-free with a label present — a test asserts it.
- [x] `_parse_v2_stamp` ignores an unknown extra field — a test asserts it.
- [x] Staleness/reclamation ignore the label — a test asserts a labelled and unlabelled stale
      lock adjudicate identically.
- [x] The label reaches the stamp through the real acquisition path via the ambient contextvar —
      a test drives `lock.acquire` under `operation_label(...)` and asserts the written stamp
      carries `op=compact-sweep`.
- [x] The full local gate set passes. [operator-attested]
- [x] CI's pytest tiers pass. [operator-attested]
baseline.summary: Lock timeouts name a bare pid, not the compaction sweep holding it

Remove a stale backup directory carried in the tickets tree at HEAD. Immediate working-tree win, no history rewrite, and a prerequisite for the reclaim. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
Confirmed present at HEAD: `.bridge_state.bak-retarget/prev_snapshot.json` **33,025,572 bytes** + `bindings.json` **15,186 bytes**, from a single static revision (`b3475f0e`, 2026-07-08). It is materialized by **every worktree checkout** and walked by every GHA `git add -A`.

It contributes ~0 MB/day, so it does not explain the ongoing growth — this is a one-off 33 MB of dead weight. It must land **before** epic 0303-692c's reclaim: the strip removes the directory from history, and the reclaim's re-add commit restores only the live `.bridge_state` files, so the tree-identity assertion depends on this already being gone.

Note the tickets `.gitattributes` glob is `.bridge_state/*`, which does **not** match `.bridge_state.bak-retarget/*` — so no merge-driver consideration applies.

## Plan-defect correction during execution
The original third criterion said `rebar fsck` must be absolutely clean. The live store already had 561 diagnostics before this deletion, including intentional permanent `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED` audit evidence that fsck and its integration tests are designed to surface. Absolute zero would require deleting audit history or changing unrelated fsck semantics. The scoped proof that this deletion did not corrupt the store is an unchanged before/after diagnostic multiset plus a green read-only reconciler pass. This correction was made only after the completion verifier rejected the literal wording; the rejection and exact counts remain recorded in comments and session log dc9a-ea86-ecba-40a0.

Execution-phase plan review also found a now-dead exact-name entry and scrub comment in the live-Jira store-copy fixture. Remove those two references so the repository no longer carries current-store logic for a path deleted from tickets HEAD. This is a test-harness cleanup only; the glob scrub still removes every `.bridge_state*` sibling and preserves fixture isolation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `.bridge_state.bak-retarget` is absent from `git ls-tree -r HEAD` on the tickets branch. Tier:
      **repo assertion**.
- [ ] Working-tree size of a fresh checkout drops by **>=33 MB**. Tier: **repo measurement**.
- [ ] `rebar fsck` reports the identical diagnostic multiset before and after deletion (zero new
      diagnostics), and a read-only reconciler pass completes green afterwards, proving nothing read
      the backup. Tier: **CLI subprocess** with before/after count-by-kind comparison.
- [ ] `grep -rn 'bak-retarget' src/ .github/` returns no production consumer. Tier: grep assertion.
- [ ] The live-Jira store-copy fixture no longer hard-codes the deleted backup name; its `.bridge_state*`
      glob scrub and store-copy isolation tests remain intact. Tier: **test-harness unit/static check**.

## Files
Tickets-branch `.bridge_state.bak-retarget/`; `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_store_copy_isolation.py`.

Rollback: revert tickets commit f2837f0a8 to restore the two files, and revert the paired Gerrit test cleanup commit. No history rewrite or force push is required.

Scope: XS. No dependencies.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

An orphaned store write-lock froze the review-bot's startup on the Gerrit host for over an hour on 2026-07-31, causing seven consecutive autodeploy failures (CloudWatch alarm `rebar-autodeploy-errors`, 18:21 UTC onward). The lock could never be reclaimed, by design, and would not have self-healed.

`src/rebar/_store/lock.py`:
- `_owner_stamp()` (:152-154) writes `f"{socket.gethostname()}:{os.getpid()}"` into the lock dir.
- `_mkdir_lock_is_stale()` (:171-190) returns `False` unless `host == socket.gethostname()` (:184).

Inside a container `socket.gethostname()` is the **container id**, and docker assigns a NEW one on every `compose up -d` recreate. So a lock orphaned by the SAME host's previous container is classified as a **foreign-host** lock — the shared-filesystem case the guard was written for — and is never reclaimed. There is no age-based ceiling, so the orphan is permanent.

The conservatism itself is deliberate and correct in its intended setting; the docstring says "never reclaim on anything short of proof (bug yaw-gravel-linen)". The defect is that **hostname is not host identity inside a container**, so the foreign-host branch misfires for what is actually the same host.

## Observed (production, 2026-07-31)

- Lock dir `/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets/.ticket-write.lock.d/`, created 18:30:49, owner stamp
  `1e0fab75d5bd:3085`. Container `1e0fab75d5bd` ran 18:03:46-18:30:55 and was SIGKILLed mid-store-write
  when a deploy recreated it (it logged a completed code_review artifact link and `Shutting down` in
  the same second).
- Every later container has a different id, so `_mkdir_lock_is_stale` returned False forever.
- `run_ensures()` (`_store/ensures.py:158`) calls `write_lock()` with the defaults
  `_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT=30` x `_DEFAULT_ATTEMPTS=2` = a 60s budget, then swallows `LockTimeout`. Startup
  therefore took ~62s instead of <4s, exceeding autodeploy's `HEALTH_TIMEOUT=30`, so every deploy was
  rolled back to `:prev`.
- Journal evidence (spans 2026-07-03 -> 2026-07-31): 197 `is a writable rebar store` lines vs 183
  `ensure env-id` lines = 14 lock-timeout boots, ALL on 2026-07-31 from 18:30:49 onward, zero in the
  preceding four weeks. `.ensure-applied` remained stamped at the last successful sweep, 18:03.
- Cleared manually by removing the orphaned lock dir; this ticket is the durable fix.

## Approach

Make the owner stamp stable across container recreates on one host (e.g. boot_id + pid, or a start-time-qualified pid) so a same-host orphan is provably reclaimable, and/or add an age-based reclaim ceiling so a lock that cannot be proven live is reclaimable after a bounded interval. Keep the existing refusal-without-proof behaviour for the genuine shared-filesystem case.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` — `_owner_stamp`, `_mkdir_lock_is_stale`, `_reclaim_mkdir_lock`.
- Tests for the container-recreate scenario and the shared-filesystem scenario.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A lock orphaned by a dead process on the SAME host is reclaimable even when the recorded
      hostname differs because the process ran in a since-recreated container; verified by a test that
      simulates a changed `gethostname()` with a dead pid.
- [ ] A lock owned by a LIVE process is still never reclaimed, and a genuinely foreign-host lock is
      still not reclaimed on the strength of hostname alone; verified by tests (no regression of
      bug yaw-gravel-linen).
- [ ] An unprovable lock does not block indefinitely: either an age ceiling applies or the failure is
      surfaced rather than silently swallowed into a 60s stall.
- [ ] make lint, make typecheck, and the default suite exit zero.
baseline.summary: Store mkdir lock is permanently unreclaimable inside a container: gethostname() is the container id, so a same-host orphan looks foreign-host

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Plan review LLM calls run at the flat DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS (16000, src/rebar/llm/config.py:269) with no output-budget raise anywhere in the plan-review call sites. A structured response that exceeds the ceiling raises UnretryableOutputError (src/rebar/llm/structured.py; runner.py:628-651 degrades to INDETERMINATE) — observed live on epic a492's container review: one bin over 17 children failed after 333s, and the S7-landed exhaustiveness directive (enumerate every independent defect in one run) deliberately increases per-call finding output, widening this exposure. Truncation here has only bad outcomes: a full-cost re-review or silent loss of critical findings. The completion verifier was remediated for the same family by RAISING the output token budget (completion_recovery.py raises max_tokens, :207/:222); plan review needs the comparable remediation. Operator goal: allow effectively unlimited output tokens for plan-review calls — output is naturally bounded by the model's actual findings, and unspent max_tokens costs nothing.

## Approach
Operator scope extension: the remediation covers ALL review workflows and ALL their LLM passes — plan review (Pass-1 chunks/AGENT/container/ISF/prerequisite, Pass-2 verify + novelty + completion sub-calls, Pass-4 coach, xchecks), the four-pass code review (base finder, Round-A/Round-B overlays, Pass-2 verify, Pass-4 coach — which the Gerrit review-bot inherits), the completion verifier's PRIMARY call (its recovery path already raises; the main call must get the same model-max floor), and review_ticket. scan_spec and the overlap judge are out of scope (not review gates; their outputs are small and schema-bounded). Raise every covered call's output budget to the RESOLVED MODEL'S MAXIMUM output capacity (the API requires a finite max_tokens, so model-max IS the unlimited setting). Mechanism: the runner already lets a request raise the config floor (runner.effective_max_tokens — a request may only raise, and req.output_token_limit still clamps down where bounded recovery needs it). Add a per-model max-output lookup — check first whether the just-landed ModelProfile capabilities seam (change 1014, f184: read capabilities from ModelProfile) exposes max output tokens and use it; otherwise a small table beside sizing.largest_window_tokens with a conservative fallback to the current default for unknown models. Apply it at the plan-review request builders: Pass-1 finder chunks and AGENT criteria, container bins, ISF finder/summarizer, prerequisite finder, and the verify/coach workflow steps (whichever do not already scale via output_tokens_per_item — the verify agentic arm's existing per-item scaling and 64000 ceiling may be replaced by or reconciled with model-max; state the final rule uniformly). Bounded-recovery paths that intentionally clamp via output_token_limit are untouched. Verify timeout interaction: larger max_tokens must not trip request timeouts (cfg.timeout_s; the SDK's streaming requirement for long requests is handled at the transport — confirm by reading anthropic_model.py). Alternative rejected: per-bin child-count scaling (this ticket's earlier draft) — still an arbitrary ceiling; any finite budget below model-max re-creates the truncation class the operator ruled out.

## Scope
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py and src/rebar/llm/plan_review/prerequisites.py (request builders), src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py (or the ModelProfile seam: model max-output lookup, shared by all workflows), src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml, src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml, src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/completion-verification.yaml (step budgets reconciled to the one model-max rule), src/rebar/llm/completion.py (primary verifier call floor), src/rebar/llm/operations.py (review_ticket), code-review step builders under src/rebar/llm/code_review/ as needed, tests/unit/workflow/test_review_output_budget.py (new, covering every workflow's request fields), tests updated where they pin request max_tokens.

## Testing
Unit with a recording FakeRunner: every plan-review request carries max_tokens equal to the resolved model's max output (per the lookup) and never below DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS; unknown model falls back to the default; output_token_limit clamps still apply where set; the verify arm's budget follows the stated final rule; existing plan-review workflow tests pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every LLM request in the plan-review, code-review, and completion-verification workflows plus review_ticket carries the resolved model's maximum output budget, floor-raised through the existing runner contract (checked: `pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_review_output_budget.py` asserting request fields per workflow and per pass, including code-review overlays and the completion verifier's primary call).
- [ ] Unknown/unmapped models fall back to the current default without error (checked: unit test).
- [ ] Bounded-recovery output_token_limit clamps are unaffected (checked: existing recovery tests pass).
- [ ] A synthetic oversized-findings container fixture that previously raised UnretryableOutputError at 16000 completes under the raised budget (checked: unit test with a FakeRunner that enforces the request ceiling).

## 2026-08-08 duplicate consolidation

Duplicate reports: `4e6f-1a2d-482c-435e` and `b54e-9a31-30ff-486b`.

Fresh resolution experiment on current `origin/main`: the complete review-output-budget suite passed `23` tests. baseline.description:
# Attested signing: pin verified_at_sha via the signed manifest channel

## Why

A signed verdict is only worth anything if it is reproducible and bound to specific content. Today the verdict signs a manifest and stores git `head_sha` as AUDIT METADATA ONLY (signing.py) — nothing cryptographically pins WHAT code was verified. Attested mode must resolve->pin->record->sign the immutable SHA. (Claim-gate ref-resolution coherence is a sibling story; this slice is the attested-signing pin only.)

## What

- Bind the SHA through the EXISTING MANIFEST CHANNEL, NOT a new signed-payload field.
  `signing._canonical_payload` signs exactly `{v, algorithm, ticket_id, manifest}` and
  `sign_manifest`/`compute_signature` already sign the full `manifest: list[str]`. Carry the
  pin as a MANIFEST STEP (`verified-at-sha:<sha>`): it enters the signed bytes (bound +
  reproducible) WITHOUT touching `_canonical_payload` or bumping `PAYLOAD_VERSION` — so NO
  invalidation of prior certified closures. The manifest-vs-payload signing decision is
  recorded in the architecture ADR.
- Record `verified_at_sha` as a queryable ticket field (convenience metadata; the trust anchor
  is the manifest step). Keep the existing `head_sha` audit field AS IS (additive).
- Resolution boundary: resolve the client `ref` (default `origin/main`) to an immutable SHA;
  an UNRESOLVABLE ref in attested mode fails closed (no sign).
- Atomicity MECHANISM (named, not just asserted): the combined manifest pin + `verified_at_sha`
  ticket write is serialized through the ticket's existing event-append / optimistic-concurrency
  boundary (compare-and-set on the current SHA), so concurrent retries / races between two
  verifications against different SHAs cannot interleave (no check-then-act TOCTOU). Set-once
  per SHA; re-verifying a DIFFERENT SHA overwrites (no stale/double pin).
- verified_at_sha lifecycle: on REOPEN/abandon the pin is retired (cleared/invalidated) so a
  stale SHA never outlives its closure; local-mode runs never set it.
- Bar signing in `local` source mode: verify + report, NO signature.
- Shape the manifest pin so a future move to DSSE + asymmetric + transparency log is an envelope
  swap, not a rewrite (KEEP HMAC now; limits documented in S6).

## Scope

- In: manifest-channel SHA binding (no payload-version bump), `verified_at_sha` field +
  lifecycle, resolution boundary + fail-closed, atomic/idempotent/overwrite pin with a named
  serialization mechanism, local-mode signing bar, in-toto envelope shape.
- Out: claim-gate ref-resolution coherence (sibling story); snapshot/cache (S1/S2); HMAC-trust
  docs (S6, dependency).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An attested PASS adds a `verified-at-sha:<sha>` MANIFEST STEP covered by the signature;
      verifying certifies the SHA. No `_canonical_payload` change, NO `PAYLOAD_VERSION` bump
      (regression test: pre-existing signatures still verify). The decision is recorded in the ADR.
- [ ] `verified_at_sha` is a queryable ticket field; re-running against the same SHA reproduces
      a verdict + manifest over identical content; `head_sha` audit field preserved (additive).
- [ ] The pin + field write is serialized via the ticket's event-append/optimistic-concurrency
      (compare-and-set) — proven by a concurrency/retry test (two writers racing, and a re-verify
      against a different SHA overwrites with no stale/double pin); NOT verified by inspection.
- [ ] On reopen/abandon the `verified_at_sha` pin is retired (no stale SHA outlives the closure);
      a `local`-mode run (dirty allowed) never sets it and never emits a signature.
- [ ] An unresolvable ref in attested mode fails closed (no signature).
- [ ] The manifest pin is shaped as an in-toto-style statement so the HMAC envelope can be
      swapped for DSSE/asymmetric later without changing the pin's data shape (covered by a test/contract).
baseline.summary: Attested signing: pin SHA, record verified_at_sha, in-toto-shaped HMAC, claim-gate coherence

baseline.description:
Classify every LLM failure into the closed resolution-disposition enum paired with a sanitized diagnostic (verbatim within a field allowlist), delivered as a PURE, total library function — the vocabulary + mapping the later stories wire in, without changing any exception the runner raises today.

## Why
`src/rebar/llm/runner.py` flattens auth, 429, 529, timeout, and content-filter into one `LLMUnavailableError` — no caller can tell "retry" from "buy quota" from "fix config" from "the agent is looping." Gates, exit codes, messaging, and telemetry need a typed disposition plus the raw truth for troubleshooting. This story delivers that CLASSIFICATION as a side-effect-free function; the per-seam wiring, the exit-code bifurcation, and any NEW raised error types are story authorial-hated-blackbear's (2eca) — it is the named owner of runner.py reconciliation and the only story that changes control flow.

## The multi-seam reality (why this is metadata-only)
The RED baseline (story arawana, committed a63ae39c) empirically pins that failures do NOT all pass through one `except`:
- `UsageLimitExceeded` is intercepted at a DEDICATED prior arm (`runner.py:335`) and re-raised as `LLMRunnerError`, BEFORE the generic `except Exception` (`runner.py:353-365`).
- `content_filter`/`length` `finish_reason` never raise from the model layer — the structured path's `structured.check_stop_reason` raises `UnretryableOutputError` (`structured.py:243`).
- rebar's own typed errors pass through unchanged at `runner.py:351` (`except LLMError: raise`).
- `sizing.is_context_limit_error(exc)` (sizing.py:171) matches on the exception MESSAGE to drive the model-escalation ladder; `pass1_with_ladder` (sizing.py:229) branches on `LLMUnavailableError` vs other.
So this story changes NO raised type anywhere; it adds a classifier + a metadata object. A pure classifier CAN classify a `UsageLimitExceeded` even though the generic seam never receives one — because callers (the RED suite; story drake; blackbear's future wiring) invoke the function DIRECTLY with any signal.

## What — five constructs, all in `src/rebar/llm/failure.py`
- `class ResolutionClass(str, Enum)` — the closed 8-class vocabulary: WAIT_AND_RETRY, RETRY_NOW, INCREASE_PROVIDER_LIMITS, CHANGE_SETTINGS, CHANGE_INPUT, CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL, FIX_AGENT_DESIGN, NEEDS_INVESTIGATION.
- `@dataclass(frozen=True) class LLMOutcome{resolution_class, diagnostic: dict, retryable: bool}` — only `retryable` (True iff class in {WAIT_AND_RETRY, RETRY_NOW}) is behaviour-critical; the class is the messaging/telemetry hint.
- `@dataclass(frozen=True) class ClassifyContext{model, provider, attempts, trace_id, finish_reason}` — all optional; `classify_llm_failure(exc)` works with none. `finish_reason` lets the structured seam classify a content-filter/truncation signal that raised no exception.
- `def classify_llm_failure(exc, ctx=None) -> LLMOutcome` — the pure, TOTAL classifier (never raises; an unmatched failure or an internal/sanitizer error degrades to NEEDS_INVESTIGATION with a minimal diagnostic).
- `def sanitize_diagnostic(fields) -> dict` — the allowlist + redactor (below).

NO new exception classes are introduced in this story (that is blackbear's, alongside the raise-site + exit-code changes). `errors.py` is NOT edited here. Back-compat is therefore trivial and total: this story raises nothing new, so every existing `except LLMUnavailableError` and every exit-code consumer is unaffected — asserted by a test that classifies each RED signal and confirms `classify_llm_failure` is additive (it returns metadata; it does not raise).

### Signal → resolution_class mapping (the classifier's COMPLETE vocabulary — every row a CONCRETE, matchable artifact)
Callers invoke the function directly with any of these; the RED suite pins each row by direct call, independent of where the classifier is wired.
| Concrete signal (exception type / status+body / finish_reason) | resolution_class | retryable |
|---|---|---|
| `ModelHTTPError` status 429 (body code NOT `insufficient_quota`); 529; 500/502/503/504 | WAIT_AND_RETRY | yes |
| `httpx.ReadTimeout` / other `httpx.TimeoutException` (read/pool/write) | WAIT_AND_RETRY | yes |
| `httpx.ConnectError`; `httpx.ConnectTimeout`; `ModelAPIError` with no `status_code` | RETRY_NOW | yes |
| `ModelHTTPError` 429 body code `insufficient_quota`; status 402 | INCREASE_PROVIDER_LIMITS | no |
| `ModelHTTPError` 401/403; malformed 400 (no context-length hint); `UserError` | CHANGE_SETTINGS | no |
| `ModelHTTPError` 400 with context-length hint (`is_context_limit_error` phrasing); 413; `finish_reason=="content_filter"` (via ctx); `ContentFilterError` | CHANGE_INPUT | no |
| `FallbackExceptionGroup` (provider/model fallback chain exhausted) | CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL | no |
| `UsageLimitExceeded` (diagnostic records request- vs tool-call-limit); `IncompleteToolCall` | FIX_AGENT_DESIGN | no |
| anything else | NEEDS_INVESTIGATION | no |

- Matching is by concrete type / `status_code` / body `error.type|code` / `finish_reason` ONLY — no vague "blip"/"exhausted" prose triggers. rebar's OWN `StructuredOutputError`/`UnretryableOutputError` (validation-exhaustion, truncation) are NOT this classifier's inputs — they are handled at the structured seam and pass through `runner.py:351` unchanged.
- **Unwrap `tenacity.RetryError` FIRST** (`RetryError.last_attempt.exception()`) before matching, so an exhausted-retry `httpx.ReadTimeout`/`ConnectTimeout` maps correctly (regression-tested). `import tenacity` is GUARDED (`try/except ImportError`) → a safe no-op in wave 1 (tenacity arrives with story arcticduck/95a5).
- Discriminate `UnexpectedModelBehavior` subclasses (`ContentFilterError`, `IncompleteToolCall`) rather than the base.

### The single metadata-only runner touch (this story)
At the generic `except Exception` seam (`runner.py:353-365`) ONLY, call `classify_llm_failure(exc)` and attach the `LLMOutcome` to the raised `LLMUnavailableError` as an attribute (e.g. `err.outcome`), WITHOUT changing that it raises `LLMUnavailableError`. The `UsageLimitExceeded` arm, the `except LLMError` passthrough, the structured `UnretryableOutputError` path, and `is_context_limit_error` are LEFT EXACTLY AS-IS. Wiring the classifier at the other seams + onto verdict/coverage + exit codes is blackbear's job.

### Diagnostic sanitization (concrete mechanism, not just an ADR)
The diagnostic is built from an ALLOWLIST (exception type, status_code, provider error `code`/`type`, finish_reason, Retry-After, attempts, trace_id, model, provider, request/tool-call-limit flags) — the raw provider body is NEVER dumped wholesale. Any captured free-text passes through a single pure redactor masking `Authorization`/`x-api-key`/`api-key`/`cookie` values, bearer tokens, key-shaped tokens (`sk-...`, `sk-ant-...`, long hex/base64), and emails. Unit-tested against a planted secret. The ADR is RECORDED by blackbear (2eca, sole ADR/docs owner).

## Scope
- The five constructs above, all in `src/rebar/llm/failure.py` (stable path; story drake imports from here — a layout change is a breaking inter-child contract coordinated via blackbear).
- The single metadata-only runner touch (attach `LLMOutcome` at the generic seam; change no raised type).
- Best-effort provider-body inspection for the terminal-vs-transient 429 split (behind the reliable `retryable` core; a misread wastes <= N bounded retries, never a safety issue).
- NOT in scope: any NEW exception classes / raise-site changes / `errors.py` edits (blackbear); the retry mechanism (arcticduck); exit-code mapping, verdict/coverage plumbing, gate posture (blackbear).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `classify_llm_failure` maps every row of the table above to the correct `resolution_class` + `retryable`, pinned by a test that calls it DIRECTLY with each concrete signal (including `UsageLimitExceeded` and `finish_reason=="content_filter"`); an unrecognized exception -> NEEDS_INVESTIGATION.
- [ ] Catches `httpx.*` directly (ConnectTimeout is NOT a ConnectError — asserted); discriminates `ContentFilterError`/`IncompleteToolCall`; unwraps `tenacity.RetryError` first (a test wraps an `httpx.ReadTimeout` in a `RetryError` and asserts WAIT_AND_RETRY), with the `import tenacity` guarded so wave-1 (no tenacity) still passes.
- [ ] This story raises NO new exception type; a test asserts `classify_llm_failure` is additive metadata and that the existing `except LLMUnavailableError` catches + exit-code consumers are unchanged (nothing new is raised, `is_context_limit_error` still True for context-length, `check_stop_reason` still raises `UnretryableOutputError`).
- [ ] The diagnostic is sanitized (a test injects a fake API key / auth header in a provider body and asserts it is scrubbed before any sink), and a `sanitize_diagnostic` failure does not make the classifier raise (degrades to a placeholder).
- [ ] The classifier is total and never raises (property test over arbitrary exceptions, incl. one whose `__str__` raises).
- [ ] The metadata-only runner touch attaches the `LLMOutcome` at the generic seam without altering the raised type; the arawana RED assertions and the sizing/structured tests stay green; `make test`/`make lint`/`make typecheck` green.

Files: `src/rebar/llm/failure.py` (new — all five constructs), `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` (attach `LLMOutcome` at the generic seam only), `tests/unit/test_llm_failure_classifier.py` (new — table + sanitizer + totality + preservation tests).

## Verified library behavior (experiment log — pydantic-ai 1.107.0, tenacity 9.1.4, httpx 0.28.1, offline)
Run offline (ACTUAL captured output; no billable call). Confirms the symbols the classifier discriminates and the tenacity unwrap the design pins:
```
[1] pydantic_ai.exceptions MROs:
    ModelHTTPError           OK   ['ModelAPIError', 'AgentRunError', 'RuntimeError']
    ModelAPIError            OK   ['AgentRunError', 'RuntimeError', 'Exception']
    ContentFilterError       OK   ['UnexpectedModelBehavior', 'AgentRunError', 'RuntimeError']
    IncompleteToolCall       OK   ['UnexpectedModelBehavior', 'AgentRunError', 'RuntimeError']
    UsageLimitExceeded       OK   ['AgentRunError', 'RuntimeError', 'Exception']
    UserError                OK   ['RuntimeError', 'Exception', 'BaseException']
    FallbackExceptionGroup   OK   ['ExceptionGroup', 'BaseExceptionGroup', 'Exception']
    ContentFilterError <: UnexpectedModelBehavior: True
    IncompleteToolCall <: UnexpectedModelBehavior: True
    FallbackExceptionGroup MRO: ['ExceptionGroup', 'BaseExceptionGroup', 'Exception']
[2] ModelHTTPError.status_code=429 body-error-type='insufficient_quota'  (terminal-vs-transient 429 reads body)
[3] httpx: [ConnectError, ConnectTimeout, ReadTimeout]; ReadTimeout <: TimeoutException: True (caught directly)
[4] tenacity.RetryError.last_attempt.exception() -> httpx.ReadTimeout: read timed out  (the unwrap)
[5] tenacity reraise=True -> httpx.ConnectTimeout (NOT RetryError: True)  (normal transport path)
[6] UsageLimitExceeded <: UnexpectedModelBehavior: False | <: AgentRunError: True  (separate FIX_AGENT_DESIGN bucket)
```
These are pydantic-ai/httpx/tenacity LIBRARY symbols, not rebar symbols — a code-grounding pass restricted to the rebar snapshot must not read their repo-absence as non-existence (bug succinct-formable-kite). The RED baseline (story arawana, committed) already pins the CURRENT collapse these cases flip: HTTP/timeout/refusal/incomplete -> LLMUnavailableError today.
baseline.summary: Classify LLM failures into the resolution-disposition enum + verbatim diagnostic

# T2 — NDJSON export: rebar export / rebar.export_tickets() + export.schema.json

## Context

P1.2 epic rule-swamp-pupil (ab74-b205-72af-4ce1). A flat, tool-friendly NDJSON projection (one full ticket object per line) for reporting/data-mining AND as the artifact T3 import consumes. Lossy interop projection, NOT a backup. Streaming via `reduce_ticket` (NEVER `reduce_all_tickets` — it materializes all states, `reducer/_api.py:179-245`). Independent of T1: a normal store has no source_* fields; export emits them only when present.

## What

- New `src/rebar/_io/__init__.py`, `src/rebar/_io/export_ndjson.py`, `src/rebar/_io/_strip.py`.
- `rebar.export_tickets(...)` library fn: iterate ticket ids cheaply (dir listing, no full
  reduce) → `reduce_ticket(id)` → `public_state()` → write one NDJSON line → release.
  Each line carries `schema_version`. Run metadata (`exported_at`, `source_env`, counts)
  to stderr/log, never to a stdout data line.
- `_strip.py` — provider-neutral `strip_external()`: removes `jira_comment_id` on comments,
  `bridge_alerts`, `SYNC`-derived linkage, and any future provider id. This is the only
  seam the GitHub follow-on inherits.
- `rebar export` CLI (`src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` dispatch + handler in `_io` or
  `_commands`): flags `--status`, `--type`, `--parent`, `--strip-external`/`--no-jira`,
  `--include-session-logs` (default EXCLUDE session_log), `--exclude-archived` (default
  INCLUDE archived with `archived:true`), `--include-deleted` (default EXCLUDE deleted),
  `-o <file>` (default stdout), `--output`. Help text `_cli/help/export.txt`.
- `src/rebar/schemas/export.schema.json` (per-line shape) + register in `schemas/__init__.py`.

## Scope

In: export path + strip + schema + CLI/lib surface. Out: import (T3), idempotency/perf (T4).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar export` / `rebar.export_tickets()` emit NDJSON, one full ticket per line, each
      with `schema_version`; every stdout line validates against `export.schema.json`.
- [ ] Streaming: uses `reduce_ticket` per id (NOT `reduce_all_tickets`); a memory-sanity
      test over a large synthetic store confirms bounded memory.
- [ ] Scope defaults correct: session_log excluded (opt-in), archived included+marked
      (opt-out), deleted excluded (opt-in); `--status`/`--type`/`--parent` filter.
- [ ] `--strip-external`/`--no-jira` leaves no external-tracker linkage in output.
- [ ] Run metadata goes to stderr, not stdout; `-o` writes to file.
- [ ] Tests: schema-validity, strip-external, scope filters, streaming memory; `pytest` green.

baseline.description:
# Gate blindness to world-grounded evidence: force measurement provenance into the record

## Context / Problem

A `/rebar-implement` run of epic `061c-ecd1-8967-4a76` landed five changes through every gate. **The gates performed to their design envelope.** Plan-review blocked infeasible mechanics (a tenacity-transport claim that cannot wrap boto3; an `isinstance` against a botocore-dependent class; a live canary path that would have made billable AWS calls on every CI run). The completion-verifier twice refused a close whose stated criteria had no test. Full-suite pre-flight caught cross-module regressions `tests/unit` missed.

Every one of those catches shares a property: **the ground truth lived in the repo**, where the reviewer's read/grep tools could reach it.

Four escapes got through, and they are one defect wearing different clothes — **a green signal whose measurement could not have observed the failure it claims to rule out**:

1. **Wrong environment.** Bedrock caching and model-availability measurements were taken in account
   `579718921998` / `us-east-2` and recorded as settled fact; the project runs in `896586841071` / `us-east-1`
   (named by the Terraform backend `rebar-tfstate-896586841071`). No gate compares a claim's observation
   context against the project's environment. A human caught it by asking "is that this project's account?"
2. **Instruments that cannot observe the failure — twice, in the same investigation.** This escape is the
   epic's sharpest example precisely because the *first correction was also wrong*.

   **2a.** Live `bedrock:Converse` calls validated a *scoped* IAM grant while running under an identity
   holding `bedrock:*`. Evidence generated under broader privilege than production is structurally unable to
   fail, so its success carries **zero information**.

   **2b.** The prescribed remedy — `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` against the role — then produced a
   confident, recorded, and **wrong** conclusion: that `bedrock:Converse` was the action to grant. The
   simulator answered exactly the question asked ("would this policy permit the action *named*
   `bedrock:Converse`?", legitimately no, since that action genuinely exists) but **not** the question that
   mattered ("which action does the Converse API actually *check*?"). Only a real call FROM the instance
   revealed the truth — `AccessDeniedException ... not authorized to perform: bedrock:InvokeModel` — meaning
   the ORIGINAL plan was right and the "fix" broke it, on a role feeding `eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a`, a cutover
   with no fallback.

   The pair is the lesson: a wildcard identity could not fail, and a simulator could not fail *for the reason
   that mattered*. **Evidence is only as good as its ability to have come out the other way for the reason
   you care about** — and swapping one instrument for a more rigorous-sounding one does not establish that.
3. **Tests that cannot fail** — the code-side form of the same defect: a contrast case whose discriminating
   conjunct was never exercised, and an oracle asserting on an object where production passes a string.
   **Both WERE caught** (mutation testing; the LLM reviewer) precisely because they are repo-checkable. That
   contrast is the evidence for this epic's thesis.
4. **Confidence outrunning method**: "verified by reading" was a hand-picked grep that missed a dependency;
   "18/18 green" was reported while typecheck was red.

## Why 1 and 2 are structural, not a calibration miss

`verified_at_sha` pins the code world completely and the outside world not at all. Plan-review runs **before** the evidence exists, so it cannot audit a measurement not yet taken; the completion-verifier accepts `[operator-attested]` evidence **on trust by design** (ADR-0043). One gate cannot audit it, the other is designed not to. The in-flight T5c rewrite pushes grounding toward current code and IaC state but still cannot observe a live cloud account — nothing in the current design can, and nothing should try.

## Approach

Do **not** make a gate observe the world. Force the measurement's context into the record as text, then let the existing repo-grounded machinery find contradictions in it. Detail lives in the child story; the shape is:

1. Extend the attested-evidence contract with measurement-provenance fields — environment, principal, and
   privilege posture relative to production.
2. Enforce their **presence** deterministically, zero LLM, mirroring
   `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py` (DET-first doctrine).
3. Let an LLM criterion judge the *declaration* against repo facts — once provenance is text, "plan attests
   account X, IaC names account Y" becomes a **repo-checkable contradiction**, which is exactly what the
   gate's strongest criteria already do well.
4. Land the generalized rule as an **advisory** criterion per ADR-0054; corpus replay decides promotion.

## Prior art considered, and why this schema diverges

Established provenance vocabularies exist and were weighed rather than ignored: **in-toto attestation predicates**, **SLSA provenance**, and **W3C PROV**. This schema deliberately does NOT align to them.

They model **artifact-build provenance** — who produced an artifact, from which materials, with which builder — and answer "can I trust this binary came from that source?". The question here is different: **measurement provenance** — where an observation was taken, under what privilege relative to production, and with what kind of instrument — answering "could this measurement have come out the other way for the reason I care about?". Privilege posture and instrument kind have no counterpart in a build predicate, and they are the two fields that catch this epic's actual escapes.

The second reason is the carrier. This declaration must be written BY HAND, by a human or agent authoring a markdown acceptance-criteria checklist, and read back by a reviewer scanning that same list. A JSON predicate document is the wrong shape for that surface: it would not survive being typed into a checkbox continuation line, and the deterministic floor that enforces presence is a line-oriented text check by design (DET-first doctrine, zero LLM). A four-field `key=value` line is writable, greppable and diffable where a nested predicate is not.

What we DO borrow is the underlying principle those standards encode — that evidence without recorded context is unverifiable — applied to measurements instead of builds. If this schema ever needs to interoperate with a build-provenance toolchain, the mapping is a separate piece of work and the ADR-0061 contract is the thing that would be extended.

## Explicitly rejected

- **Making the completion-verifier re-run world measurements.** Expensive, flaky, recursive — the verifier's
  own credentials carry the same privilege-masking problem, so it would validate using the instrument under
  suspicion.
- **Escape 4 as gate scope.** Reported-green-while-red is *reporting discipline*, already covered by the
  orchestration rule that agents report gate output faithfully rather than narrating success. Filing it as a
  gate gap would be mis-attribution.
- **Wording changes alone.** The contract was followed and still failed; emphasis is not the defect. This is
  the same lesson as epic `9109-2ad9-2477-4cf6` (Serena tool-choice), which is why that epic's structural
  framing is the model here rather than its subject matter.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] an `[operator-attested]` criterion lacking measurement provenance is flagged by a DETERMINISTIC check
      (no LLM) — `det_measurement_provenance.py`, surfaced advisory through `p6_ac_quality`, landed in
      change 1423 with a mutation-tested oracle (breaking the binding rule, placeholder detection or enum
      membership each kills tests)
- [x] the new criterion ships **advisory** (ADR-0054) and rides the `.rebar/` project overlay, leaving the
      shipped default criteria set unchanged for other rebar clients
- [x] an ADR records the amended evidence contract, citing ADR-0043 as the shape it changes
- [x] the completion-verifier is NOT made to re-run world measurements — the rejected alternative stays
      rejected, and a test or grep demonstrates it

## Descoped to `98df-3528-9b1f-405a` (ridiculous-expert-mouse), filed as an `idea`

AC-1 originally also required the wrong-account escape to be **reproduced as a regression fixture** from the real `579718921998` vs `896586841071` case. That clause is NOT delivered and is NOT claimed as done.

Reproducing it means exercising the AGENT criterion's rule (a) semantically, which needs an eval corpus (`.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.eval.yaml`) plus a live run — the same behavioural half descoped from story `f161`. Both moved to `98df`, which also carries the rule (b)/(c)/(d) fixtures and the ADR-0054 corpus-replay false-positive rate that would justify promoting the criterion from advisory.

This epic therefore closes on its MECHANISM being delivered and proven — provenance is now forced into the record as text, deterministically enforced, and judged by a tool-enabled criterion — not on that criterion's firing behaviour having been calibrated. The distinction is safe because the criterion ships **advisory**: it cannot block any claim or close, so an uncalibrated advisory criterion is inert-but-useful rather than risky. Promotion is a separate ADR-0054 decision nobody has committed to, which is why `98df` is an `idea`.
baseline.summary: Gate blindness to world-grounded evidence: force measurement provenance into the record

# Project-supplied review criteria + project-invariant compliance (unified cross-gate registry)

## Context

rebar's review gates ship a fixed, built-in set of criteria. Client projects have their own
standards and invariants — naming, layering, banned APIs, architectural rules — the built-in
set can't express. This epic lets a **project supply its own review criteria** and declare
**architectural invariants** the gates check, **beyond** the built-in set.

**Cross-cutting:** it must serve **plan-review, code-review (`b744`), and any future
criteria-based gate** through **one shared registry**. (Spun out of `5fd2` as follow-on F8;
config-UX sibling `55de`/F5.)

**Posture (from `5fd2`, binding):** coach-not-block, advisory-by-default, **fail-open
(ironclad)**, polyglot / broad client base, convergent-by-construction, **reuse existing
machinery — no plugin system, no new DSL**.

## Design decisions (settled in brainstorm; see rationale comment)

1. **Unified criterion data model + shared registration/discovery/schema/eval plumbing;
   per-gate application** (gate-scoped routing inside the shared record; postures do NOT
   converge).
2. **Two authoring forms, no project code in the gate:** DET "invariants" = declarative
   pattern rules via the existing grounding scan facade; LLM criteria = prompt files.
3. **Any criterion (DET or LLM) may block** — `--force`-escapable, folds into the signed
   (kind-keyed) attestation coverage, can never rebind a built-in.
4. **Blocking is project-owned policy.** rebar surfaces the same eval/calibration instruments
   it uses on its built-ins; the maintainer decides blocking + threshold. Trust is theirs.
5. **Reuse existing formats** (prompt front-matter, the `criteria_routing.json` schema,
   Inspect-AI fixtures, the scan facade). No new formats.
6. **Explicit activation; presence != active.** Routing/threshold in a `.rebar/` overlay
   (§ Overlay schema); namespaced + additive; the overlay may re-tune or **disable** a
   built-in (recorded in coverage).
7. **Eval tooling in scope** = fixture/discrimination harness + calibration/agreement view.
   **Out** = REVIEW_RESULT FP-replay (F1; gate-agnostic, inherited later).
8. **An "invariant" is just a blocking criterion** (usually DET). One mechanism.
9. **Visual editor extended** to author project criteria (reuses `/library/create`).

## Overlay schema, activation & caching (clears E2/G6/T8)

- **File:** `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`, reusing each gate's packaged `criteria_routing.json`
  schema, keyed by gate:
  `{"plan_review": {"<id>": {…routing…}}, "code_review": {"<id>": {…}}, "activate": ["project.<name>", …]}`.
- **Per-criterion routing** reuses existing keys: plan-review `{exec, applies_at, block_threshold,
  default_posture, facet, checklist}`; code-review `{exec, applies_to (globs), block_threshold,
  blocking_enabled}`. (Note the deliberate posture divergence — plan-review derives blocking
  from `default_posture`; code-review uses an explicit `blocking_enabled`; the shared
  `threshold_for` must honor BOTH — do not "fix" the divergence.) **DET criteria also carry
  `fail_mode: open|closed`** (default `open` for project invariants; `closed` for the built-in
  security class) — see § DET-invariant scan scoping.
- **`exec` vocabulary:** `1-TURN` / `2-STEP` / `AGENT` (LLM tiers) or **`DET`** (pattern-rule
  invariant; code-review already uses `DET` inline). A **DET criterion has no prompt** — descriptor
  assembly must treat prompt resolution as OPTIONAL for `exec: DET` (today `_descriptor_from_prompt`
  unconditionally calls `get_prompt(...)` and raises if absent). A DET criterion's "rubric" is its
  detector rule id (`.rebar/detectors/`), not a `.md`; only its routing entry is required.
  **DET fallback descriptor shape** (a `_descriptor_from_prompt` DET branch that skips
  `get_prompt`): `name` = routing `name` or id; `scenario` = the detector rule's `message`/
  description from its `.rebar/detectors/<id>` envelope; `facet` = routing `facet` (default = id);
  `checklist` = empty. This is an expand-contract change (add the DET branch; existing prompt-backed
  callers unaffected).
- **Namespace / collision (load-time, located error):** a net-new project criterion id MUST be
  `project.<name>`-prefixed. An overlay entry keyed by an **un-prefixed built-in id** is a
  **re-tune/disable** of that built-in (allowed, §Design 6). A `project.`-prefixed id equal to a
  built-in id, or a duplicate project id, is **rejected at load** (a project id can never rebind
  a built-in).
- **Activation:** a criterion runs only if listed in `activate` (presence in the file ≠ active).
- **Discovery — `effective_criteria(repo_root)`** = `CANONICAL_LLM`/`OVERLAY_IDS` ∪ activated
  project ids (each resolved via `get_prompt(id, repo_root)` for its rubric + the overlay routing
  entry). Route it through **every** vocabulary site: plan-review `load_criteria`,
  `check_registry_coverage`, and the **workflow Pass-1 assemble op** (`workflow_ops` emits a
  sanitized `include_project_<name>` boolean — `.`→`_` — per activated project id as the
  coverage/routing record). **LANDED-DESIGN NOTE (ef7e):** the v3 `batch` schema is IMMUTABLE and
  the gate self-validates, so project criteria do NOT fan out via a new workflow field; instead the
  rebar-specific `ProductionBatchRunner` appends the `project.` subset of `route_criteria` to the
  finder set (built-ins keep their static YAML `criteria:` slots, unchanged). Code-review sites
  (`OVERLAY_IDS`, `routing_index`, `threshold_for`) are unified later, after b744 (story 5065).
- **Caching (clears G6 cache bug) — LANDED (ef7e):** `_routing_index()` stays `@lru_cache`d for the
  **packaged** index (immutable per binary); `effective_routing(repo_root)` / `load_criteria` are
  `@lru_cache(maxsize=128)` keyed by `(repo_root, sha256(overlay-bytes))` — a CONTENT signature
  (not mtime), so an overlay edit self-invalidates and cross-repo leakage is impossible;
  `prompt_library._invalidate_caches()` clears them. A RED cross-repo-leak test proves it.

## Attestation & invalidation (clears G6/COH/E1; reuses kind-keyed attest infra)

- **`registry_version(repo_root=None)`** additionally hashes the `.rebar/` overlay when
  `repo_root` is given; thread `repo_root` through **every** caller — `claim_gate_check →
  compute_validity`, and also `drift_refresh_candidate` and `remediation_mode_candidate` (which
  call `registry_version()` today without it) — so activating/editing/disabling a criterion
  **invalidates a prior attestation at claim time** (today it hashes packaged routing only — the
  change does not invalidate).
- **Disable recorded in coverage:** a disabled built-in is listed in a `disabled_builtins: [ids]`
  field in the verdict `coverage` dict (and folded into the signed manifest) so the cert reflects
  reduced coverage rather than silent omission; the field is additive/expand-contract (absent on
  old certs).
- **Cross-gate:** applies to **any gate attestation backed by the shared registry** (plan-review
  now; code-review once it signs — see Migration; code-review signs nothing today).
- **Expand-contract / back-compat:** the new regver basis is additive; an existing attestation
  lacking it is treated as **stale → re-review**, never a crash. Overlay absent ⇒ regver == today
  (no invalidation churn).

## DET-invariant scan scoping & fail-open (clears COH)

- A DET invariant runs as a **whole-repo content scan** via the shared `grounding.engine_b.scan`.
  The **oracle always fails open** (engine binary absent / parse-error / timeout → `abstain`). The
  **consumer** then applies the criterion's **`fail_mode`**: `open` (default for project invariants)
  turns an abstain into a skip = PASS; `closed` (the built-in security class, via the existing
  `apply_failclosed`) turns an abstain into a BLOCK. So generalizing `code_review/detectors.py` =
  making its currently-hardcoded fail-closed behavior a per-criterion `fail_mode` that **defaults
  open** — the two behaviors are one code path parameterized by `fail_mode`, not a contradiction.
  Matches are **gate-scoped**: code-review filters matches to the **diff** (as
  `code_review/detectors.py` already does); plan-review has no diff, so a DET invariant checks the
  plan's declared intent and repo context — an invariant that inherently needs a diff is **N/A at
  plan time (fail-open)** and belongs to code-review.
- Because matches are gate-scoped (diff / plan), pre-existing whole-repo violations are **not**
  surfaced as new work — this is why **no baseline/grandfathering** is needed (reconciles the
  Out-of-scope note).
- **LLM fail-open:** an LLM criterion configured to block whose call errors/times out **fails
  open** (skipped, does not block) — same rule as DET.

- **`apply_failclosed` → `fail_mode` expand-contract (clears T4; story `7f0d`).** The generalization
  is backward-compatible, no flag-day: `apply_failclosed(...)` is KEPT as a thin wrapper that calls
  the new `apply_fail_mode(..., fail_mode="closed")` — so its **default stays `closed`** and every
  existing caller (`code_review/detectors.py`, the built-in security class) is byte-identical until
  explicitly migrated. `detectors.py` is then migrated to call the new function with the
  criterion's routing `fail_mode` (project invariants default `open`, security class `closed`); the
  old wrapper is deprecated and removed only after all callers pass an explicit `fail_mode`.
  **Rollback** = revert callers to the `apply_failclosed` wrapper (still `closed`). No caller's
  behavior changes silently.

## What exists vs. what we build (grounded to file:line, 2026-06-30; incl. b744 worktree)

**Already built (reuse):**
- **Shared three-pass kernel** `review_kernel/` (verify/decide/coach) — **both** gates already
  consume it (code-review via `code_review/workflow_ops.py`); the divergence-risky core is
  already unified.
- **A DET pattern-rule → finding consumer already exists:** `code_review/detectors.py` calls the
  shared `grounding.engine_b.scan` + `load_registry` (which already unions `.rebar/detectors/`) +
  `apply_failclosed` (consumer-side fail-CLOSED; oracle stays fail-OPEN). Generalizable — the only
  hardcoded bits are the `rebar.builtin.security.` prefix + 2 criterion mappings.
- **Per-criterion blocking is DONE:** `code_review/registry.threshold_for` + kernel Pass-3 +
  detector fail-closed.
- **Project extension points:** `.rebar/prompts/` (rubric override), `.rebar/<gate>_moves.json`
  (additive coach moves), `.rebar/detectors/` (project pattern rules), `.rebar/evals/` (fixtures).
- **Kind-keyed attestation infra** (`plan_review/attest.py`); Inspect-AI eval seam; discrimination
  scorers + Cohen's κ + parity metrics.

**Net-new (build):**
- **Open the closed criterion vocabularies** (`CANONICAL_LLM`, `OVERLAY_IDS`) via
  `effective_criteria(repo_root)` — THE precondition; a project criterion is silently skipped
  today regardless of overlay.
- **`.rebar/` routing overlay + activation + cache isolation** (§ Overlay schema).
- **A shared descriptor abstraction:** code-review has only `routing_index()` (raw routing), no
  `load_criteria`-style merged descriptor and no `facet/checklist/…`; unification introduces/
  generalizes one and reconciles the `blocking_enabled` vs `default_posture` postures + exec-tier-
  polymorphic (prompt-less DET vs LLM) criteria.
- **Generalize the DET-scan consumer** beyond the security prefix (data-driven criterion↔detector
  map) so arbitrary project invariants route; make the fail-open/closed behavior a per-criterion
  `fail_mode` (today `apply_failclosed` is hardcoded closed; default project invariants to open);
  expose to plan-review too.
- **Per-criterion eval runner** — `eval_solver.run_case` is a closed 3-id dispatch (raises
  otherwise) + a validate-only CLI; add a criterion-aware runner + a live CLI + the
  **calibration/agreement view** (rendering is net-new; κ/parity metrics exist).
- **Attestation port to code-review** + `registry_version(repo_root)` + disable-coverage +
  claim-gate invalidation (§ Attestation).
- **Editor live must-fire/must-not-fire preview** — a new **synchronous** editor endpoint
  `POST /criterion/preview` `{criterion_id | inline(prompt+routing), fixture}` →
  `{verdict: "fire"|"no-fire", finding?: <findings.py finding shape>, rationale: str}`, reusing
  the per-criterion eval runner behind the `agents` extra + credentials, with a **configurable
  timeout (default 60s)** (no prompt-execution endpoint exists today — the editor's `POST` set is
  `/save`, `/prompt/save`, `/validate`, `/library/create`). **Spike gate:** if a single sync
  preview does not return within the timeout on the reference model, fall back to an async
  job+poll shape rather than blocking the editor's `ThreadingHTTPServer` handler.
- **Routing derivation/validation pipeline** (`criteria_routing.json` is hand-maintained; no
  generator/drift gate).

## Migration & compatibility

- **Callsites** to route through `effective_criteria`: plan-review `load_criteria`,
  `check_registry_coverage`, `attest.registry_version`, `workflow_ops` vocab; code-review
  `OVERLAY_IDS`, `routing_index`, `threshold_for`.
- **Preserve the `review_code` / `code_review/shim.py` `review_result` return shape** — it is a
  back-compat surface consumed by MCP `review_code`, CLI `rebar review-code`, and the Gerrit
  `review_bot/adapter.py`.
- **Rollback = fail-open to packaged:** overlay absent ⇒ both gates behave exactly as today. The
  unification is expand-contract; a misbehaving unified registry falls back per-gate. The
  `registry_version` code change is itself expand-contract (old certs → stale, never crash).
- **Docs deliverable:** an ADR under `docs/adr/` (LANDED: `docs/adr/0015-project-supplied-criteria.md` for the plan-review slice) + a `CLAUDE.md` "project-supplied criteria"
  section document the unified registry contract, the overlay merge/activation semantics, and the
  attestation-invalidation protocol, plus a how-to for authoring/activating/eval'ing/blocking on a
  criterion (the concrete target for the docs AC).

## Build order (risk-ordered MVP; clears G5 thin-slice)

Prove the full loop on the riskiest piece first, then fan out:
1. **MVP slice — ✅ DONE (story `ef7e`, PR #103).** `effective_criteria`/`effective_routing`
   (content-hash cache isolation) → activate ONE project LLM criterion from the `.rebar/` overlay →
   `ProductionBatchRunner` fans it into Pass-1 → surfaces its finding; CI parity gate + ADR 0015.
   (The `registry_version`-reflects-the-overlay + attestation-invalidation half is split into story
   `08af`, step 6 below — this slice proved author→activate→run→surface.)
2. Generalize the DET-invariant scan consumer (data-driven map).
3. Per-criterion eval runner + calibration view.
4. Editor live-preview + authoring extension.
5. **Unify** plan-review + code-review registries into `rebar.llm.criteria` (after `b744` lands).

## Dependency

**Blocked on `b744`** (code-review; WS1–WS5 landed on `worktree-code-review-capability`, WS6 =
Gerrit voter pending). The `review_kernel` is already shared; the remaining fork is the
registry/descriptor + posture + vocabulary layer, unified after b744 lands (temporary
duplication accepted).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `effective_criteria(repo_root)` opens the closed vocabularies (`CANONICAL_LLM` +
      `OVERLAY_IDS`) so an activated project criterion is loaded/run by the gate; routed through
      every vocabulary callsite (see Migration).
- [ ] `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` overlay per the § Overlay schema: gate-keyed, namespaced,
      explicit `activate` list, load-time collision/rebind rejection (a located error).
- [ ] Overlay merge is cache-isolated per repo (packaged index stays cached; overlay is not); a
      RED test proves no cross-repo routing leakage.
- [ ] The overlay may re-tune or disable a built-in; a disable is recorded in attestation coverage.
- [ ] Project DET pattern-rule invariants run through the generalized (data-driven)
      `engine_b.scan` consumer and surface as blocking-capable findings; fail-open on
      engine-binary-absent / parse-error / timeout per the criterion's `fail_mode` (default `open`
      → skip = PASS; security-class `closed` → block).
- [ ] Project LLM prompt criteria run through the shared registry with gate-scoped routing; an
      LLM-block criterion that errors fails open. … [truncated by reconciler]
- [ ] A project can add its own criteria (DET pattern-rules + LLM prompts) that run in plan-review,
- [ ] A project can declare architectural invariants (blocking DET criteria) the gates check.
- [ ] The project **owns blocking/threshold policy** per criterion, informed by the same
- [ ] **No project code executes in the gate**; unsupported stacks fail open.
baseline.summary: Project-supplied review criteria + project-invariant compliance (unified cross-gate registry)
