## Why

Two regexes key on the `## Success Criteria` heading and one scope extractor lists it. They are the only code that READS the heading to make a decision, so until they change the heading remains load-bearing and the store migration cannot be verified. (One further site, `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:308`, WRITES the heading into generated eval fixtures; that is a producer, not a reader, and belongs to the eval-specs story — this story does not depend on it and its AC greps deliberately do not cover it.) `_count_ac_items` already counts `- [ ]` items ONLY under `## Acceptance Criteria`, so criteria written under SC never reach the P1 blocking floor and can never carry the `[operator-attested]` tag — collapsing the two TIGHTENS the gate.

## What

Point the heading-reading code at `## Acceptance Criteria`, and update the test fixtures that embed `## Success Criteria` in ticket descriptions.

## Scope

Code:
- `src/rebar/_engine_support/gates.py:136` — the epic branch of `_clarity_score`, currently
  `+2` for `^##\s+Success Criteria`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:227` — the deliberate copy of that heuristic used for
  P1 coverage (non-blocking); the two must stay in lockstep, which the module comments require.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/assemble.py:253` — `_SCOPE_HEADINGS`, which lists
  `"## success criteria"` alongside `"## acceptance criteria"`; drop the SC entry.

Test fixtures embedding the heading:
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_gate_rubric_consistency.py:4,36`
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py:48`
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_gate_subtree.py:28`
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_gate_subtree_heldout.py:22`
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_gate_story_epic.py:29`
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_completion_verifier.py:219,293,356,407,425,465`
- `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py:108`

OUT OF SCOPE: removing `clarity-check` entirely (separately planned). This story only stops it keying on the SC heading.

## Approach

In both `_clarity_score` copies the epic branch REPOINTS its `+2` from `^##\s+Success Criteria` to `^##\s+Acceptance Criteria`. Because AC is already a universal blocking floor, the bonus becomes automatic and the epic branch stops discriminating. That is accepted deliberately: clarity-check is a dead metric already slated for removal, and the alternative is worse.

The arithmetic, measured against the real `_clarity_score` rather than estimated. The epic fixture in `test_gate_rubric_consistency.py` scores 6 today (heading +1, len>=200 +1, len>=500 +1, bullet +1, SC +2 ... minus length, netting 6 at 440 chars). With the SC block removed and the bonus DROPPED it scores 4 at 412 chars — below the default threshold of 5, so `test_clarity_pass_implies_check_ac_pass[epic]` goes RED and would need the fixture padded past 500 chars to compensate. With the bonus REPOINTED it scores 6, unchanged.

Dropping the bonus would also lower every real epic in the store by 2, risking a live clarity-check regression across the 108 migrated tickets for the sake of a metric being deleted. Repointing avoids both the fixture fragility and that regression, so it is the chosen route.

`_SCOPE_HEADINGS` loses `"## success criteria"`; `"## acceptance criteria"` already covers the collapsed vocabulary.

Fixtures that carry BOTH headings drop the SC block; fixtures carrying SC as their only criteria block have it renamed to `## Acceptance Criteria` with its bullets converted to `- [ ]` items so they still satisfy the P1 floor.

## Testing

- `test_gate_rubric_consistency.py` is the invariant that a clarity-PASS implies a check-ac
  PASS; it must stay green with the epic fixture no longer carrying SC.
- `pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle tests/interfaces/store tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py` green.
- A new case pinning that an epic carrying `## Acceptance Criteria` plus `## Context` (the two
  remaining epic signals) passes BOTH `clarity-check` and `check-ac`. The fixture deliberately
  keeps `## Context` so the case tests the AC repoint rather than the degenerate
  zero-heading-signal path.
- An assertion of the score itself (`_clarity_score(fixture, "epic") == 6`), so a future change
  to the weights fails loudly here instead of silently drifting the epic fixture under the
  threshold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -rn "Success Criteria" src/rebar/_engine_support/gates.py src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py src/rebar/llm/code_review/assemble.py` returns no matches.
- [ ] The two `_clarity_score` copies remain textually in lockstep (verified by diffing the two
      epic branches), preserving the invariant their comments assert.
- [ ] No *fixture* under `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/`, `tests/interfaces/store/` or
      `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py` still describes a ticket using
      `## Success Criteria`. Verified by
      `grep -rn '## Success Criteria' <those paths> --exclude=test_criteria_heading_collapse.py`
      returning no matches. AMENDED during implementation: as originally written this was a
      blanket string prohibition, which is unsatisfiable alongside the epic's own design —
      sibling story 5f4d requires the reintroduction guard be "proven by a test that injects
      one", so the epic MUST contain a file carrying the literal heading. This story's new
      contract test `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_criteria_heading_collapse.py` is that
      file: every occurrence is a negative-case probe demonstrating the heading is inert
      (one of them, L144, asserts its ABSENCE from the code-review scope context). The
      criterion's intent — no fixture corpus carries SC as live plan vocabulary — is met in
      full. 5f4d's allowlist must cover that file; a note is recorded on 5f4d.
- [ ] A new test asserts an epic whose description carries `## Acceptance Criteria` and
      `## Context` passes both `clarity-check` and `check-ac` (exit 0 each), and that
      `_clarity_score(fixture, "epic")` equals 6 — the same score the fixture earns today, so
      the repoint is proven score-neutral rather than assumed.
- [ ] The epic fixture in `test_gate_rubric_consistency.py` needs NO length padding to stay
      green, confirming the repoint (not a drop) was implemented.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the full pytest suite pass.
baseline.summary: Point heading-detection code and its test corpus at Acceptance Criteria

## Finding

Canonical contributor guidance hardcodes a specific maintainer/bot DCO identity even though project contribution policy requires contributors to sign with their own real configured identity.

## Evidence

- `AGENTS.md:124-169` documents the Gerrit workflow and currently prescribes `Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart <joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com>`.
- `.agents/rules/rebar.md:28-34` repeats the same personal bot identity.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md:198-214` requires a real contributor name and email for DCO sign-off.

## Remediation

Make the canonical guidance identity-neutral: contributors and agents use the real name and email configured for the actor performing the commit (`git config user.name` / `git config user.email`). Retain Joe Oakhart's bot identity only in narrowly scoped automation guidance for a workflow that actually runs as that bot.

Cascade flag: documentation-only contract change; verify all imported/copied agent guidance (`AGENTS.md`, `.agents/rules/*.md`, and any other contributor-facing guidance under `docs/`) so contradictory instructions do not remain. Automation-owned paths (`infra/`, `.github/workflows/`, `tests/fixtures/`) and experiment corpora (`docs/experiments/`) legitimately reference the bot identity and are explicitly out of scope for the sweep and for the consistency check below.

Add a deterministic consistency check: a `make lint`-integrated grep step (e.g. a target in the `Makefile`, or a script under `scripts/` invoked from `make lint`) that runs `git grep -nE 'joeoakhart\+bot@navapbc\.com|Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart' -- AGENTS.md '.agents/rules/*.md' CONTRIBUTING.md ':(glob)docs/**/*.md' ':(exclude)docs/experiments/**'` (the `:(glob)` pathspec magic makes `**` recurse into subdirectories under `docs/`; the `:(exclude)` pathspec drops `docs/experiments/` from the scan) and fails the build if it finds any match. `infra/`, `.github/workflows/`, and `tests/` are excluded by construction because they are not passed as pathspecs. Document, next to the check, which file owns it and that `infra/`/`.github/workflows/`/`tests/`/`docs/experiments/` are the intentional exclusions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `AGENTS.md` tells contributors and agents to verify `git config user.name` and `git config user.email` and to sign off with that configured real identity. Verify: `grep -q 'git config user.name' AGENTS.md && grep -q 'git config user.email' AGENTS.md`.
- [ ] `.agents/rules/rebar.md` and any derived guidance no longer instruct every actor to use Joe Oakhart's bot identity. Verify: `! git grep -nE 'joeoakhart\+bot@navapbc\.com|Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart' -- '.agents/rules/*.md' AGENTS.md`.
- [ ] Any retained Joe-specific identity is explicitly scoped to the automation that owns it (e.g. `infra/`, `.github/workflows/`, `CLAUDE.local.md`) and is not presented as general contributor guidance. Verify: `git grep -nE 'joeoakhart\+bot@navapbc\.com|Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart'` returns matches ONLY under `infra/`, `.github/workflows/`, `tests/`, or `docs/experiments/`; any match outside those prefixes fails the check.
- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md`, canonical agent guidance, and generated/imported guidance describe one consistent DCO contract, defined concretely as: all three name "the committer's own configured git identity (`git config user.name`/`user.email`)" as the sign-off source, and none of them names a specific third party (Joe Oakhart or otherwise) as the required sign-off for general contributions. Verify: `for f in CONTRIBUTING.md AGENTS.md .agents/rules/rebar.md; do grep -q "configured git identity" "$f" || exit 1; done` exits 0 (each file must contain the phrase, or the loop exits non-zero on the first miss), AND `git grep -l 'Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart' -- CONTRIBUTING.md AGENTS.md '.agents/rules/*.md'` returns no results.
- [ ] A deterministic consistency check exists and fails the build on a reintroduced hardcoded personal sign-off: implemented as a `make lint`-integrated grep step (script or Makefile target) running `git grep -nE 'joeoakhart\+bot@navapbc\.com|Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart' -- AGENTS.md '.agents/rules/*.md' CONTRIBUTING.md ':(glob)docs/**/*.md' ':(exclude)docs/experiments/**'` (the `:(glob)` magic recurses into `docs/adr/`, `docs/design/`, `docs/migrations/`, `docs/calibration/`, etc.; `:(exclude)` drops `docs/experiments/`; `infra/`, `.github/workflows/`, `tests/` are excluded by not being passed as pathspecs) and fails the build (non-zero exit) if `git grep` finds any match. Verify: the new check's script/target exists, running it against the post-change guidance files exits 0, and running it against a scratch copy with the hardcoded string reinjected exits non-zero.
baseline.summary: Make contributor sign-off guidance identity-neutral

## Context / Problem
In `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`, the `golden-path` job executes `sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq && jq --version` unconditionally on every run. On standard GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest` runners, `jq` is already pre-installed out of the box, making the 15–30s `apt-get update` call redundant overhead.

## Approach
Use a conditional check `type jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || (sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq) && jq --version`. This evaluates `type jq` in <0.001s and skips `apt-get update` when `jq` is present, while safely falling back to package installation if executed on a minimal runner environment lacking `jq`.

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` (`golden-path` job step)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` uses a conditional fallback check for `jq` installation in the `golden-path` job step.
- [x] `make lint` (ruff + actionlint + zizmor) passes.
- [x] `make typecheck` passes.
- [x] `python scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py` passes.
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` passes all 17 tests.
baseline.summary: Avoid redundant apt-get update in gerrit-verify golden-path step when jq is present

baseline.description:
## Summary

Sibling sweep of bug 5546 (rebar-debug Step 7). 5546's root cause is a repeatable pattern, not a one-off: **a bare `git fetch <remote> <branch>` whose result is then consumed as `<remote>/<branch>`.** A bare fetch always writes FETCH_HEAD but only *opportunistically* writes `refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>` — and only when the remote's CONFIGURED refspec covers that branch. Under a narrow refspec (`+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`, which is what `git clone --single-branch` AND `actions/checkout` produce by default) the ref is never written, or — worse, when it already exists — never UPDATED, so the consumer silently reads a missing or STALE ref.

5546 fixed the `sync.py` instance. Two live instances remain; both were confirmed semantically (read in context), not by string match.

## Sibling 1 — `src/rebar/_store/push.py:182`

```python
_git(base_path, "fetch", remote, branch)          # :182  bare fetch
...
merge = _git(base_path, "merge", remote_ref, ...) # :202  consumes f"{remote}/{branch}"
```

This is the non-fast-forward retry loop. Under a narrow refspec the merge target is missing or stale, so the merge cannot absorb what actually rejected the push and **every retry re-pushes the same rejected history until the budget is exhausted.**

## Sibling 2 — `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:286,309` (and the canary at :424,:436)

```sh
git fetch origin tickets || true                      # :286
ahead=$(git rev-list --count origin/tickets..HEAD ...) # :287  consumes origin/tickets
...
git fetch origin tickets 2>&1 || ...                  # :309  inside the retry loop
```

Note the SAME workflow already uses the correct explicit form at line 115 (`git fetch origin '+tickets:refs/remotes/origin/tickets'`), as does `verify-identity.yml:55` — so these sites are internally inconsistent, which is good evidence they are an oversight rather than a deliberate choice.

**This is a strong candidate root cause for bug 449f-f9bf-be90-47fe** (and for the Reconcile Bridge push-rejection evidence recorded in 5546's own comment thread: 4 runs on 2026-07-30 exhausting a 5-retry budget with `! [rejected] HEAD -> tickets (fetch first)`). Because line 115 creates `refs/remotes/origin/tickets` earlier in the job, the later bare fetches at :286/:309 leave it STALE rather than absent — so `rev-list origin/tickets..HEAD` and the reconcile merge both operate on a snapshot that never advances, and the retry loop provably cannot converge no matter how large the budget. That mechanism has NOT yet been experimentally confirmed against a real runner; it is a cited hypothesis, and confirming or rejecting it is the first task here.

## Deliberately NOT siblings (checked and cleared)

- `src/rebar/opcert_service/workspace.py:70,87` — bare fetch, then consumes
  `review/<branch>` / `tickets/<branch>`. Same shape, but the workspace is built by
  `git init` + `git remote add`, which installs the DEFAULT WILDCARD refspec, so the
  branch is always covered. Not reachable.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:347`, `review_bot/gerrit_client.py:335`,
  `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:115`, `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:86`,
  `verify-identity.yml:55` — already use an explicit refspec. Correct as written.
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py:375` — a genuine instance, but bug 01e8-302b-ab8f-4220
  already owns and fixes it. Excluded to avoid a conflicting edit.

## Why filed rather than folded into 5546

5546's authorized surface was `src/rebar/_store/sync.py` + its tests. `push.py` and the CI workflows are separate blast radii — the workflow change in particular needs a real runner to verify — so they get their own reviewable change rather than riding along.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The 449f hypothesis above is experimentally confirmed or rejected against a real
      narrow-refspec checkout; if confirmed, 449f is linked to this ticket.
- [ ] `push.py`'s retry-loop fetch uses an explicit refspec, with a test proving the
      non-fast-forward retry loop converges under a narrow clone refspec (it currently
      cannot).
- [ ] The reconcile-bridge workflows' bare `git fetch origin tickets` sites use the
      explicit refspec already used at line 115 of the same file.
- [ ] A guard (lint rule, test, or reviewer-facing note) prevents the bare-fetch form
      from being reintroduced.
baseline.summary: sibling sweep of 5546: bare git fetch leaves <remote>/<branch> missing or stale in push.py and the reconcile-bridge workflows

# Gerrit change descriptions show line breaks at fixed-width intervals

## Context / Problem

Reported alongside bug 4e21 (Jira descriptions rendering a break at the end of every soft-wrapped line). The reporter observes a similar-looking line-break problem on Gerrit change descriptions.

## What has already been ruled out

Bug 4e21's fix does NOT address this. That fix changes `text_to_adf` in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/adf.py`, which lives in the Jira adapter and is reachable only from the Jira REST v3 payload builders (`adapters/jira/acli.py:201`, `adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py:369`) plus the three description compare sites. Nothing under `src/rebar/review_bot/` or the Gerrit client imports it. A search of `src/rebar/review_bot/` and `src/rebar/llm/` for `textwrap` or any reflow helper found no matches, so rebar does not appear to be injecting these breaks in code.

## Working hypothesis (NOT yet confirmed — this is the work)

A Gerrit "change description" is the git commit message. Gerrit renders commit messages as preformatted fixed-width text and preserves the author's newlines verbatim. Commit-message bodies are conventionally hard-wrapped at ~72 columns (git's own norm), so the breaks may be authored rather than injected, which would make this intended behavior rather than a defect.

## Acceptance criteria

- Obtain a concrete example Gerrit change whose description renders wrongly, and record the change number.
- Determine whether the newlines are present in the commit message object itself (`git cat-file commit <sha>`) or introduced by a rebar/review-bot code path.
- Classify explicitly: defect vs intended-behavior vs authoring convention. If intended, close as not-a-bug with the citation and, if useful, document the commit-message wrapping convention instead.
- Only if it is a genuine injection defect: fix under RED->GREEN discipline.

## Notes

Filed at the reporter's request during the 4e21 session and deliberately scoped OUT of that session. Not yet reproduced or confirmed as a defect.
baseline.summary: Gerrit change descriptions show fixed-width line breaks (investigate; may be authoring convention)

baseline.description:
## Context
Operation certificates become asymmetric on the foundation substrate (namespace `rebar.opcert.v1`), signed by an environment's Ed25519 key and verifiable by anyone against its public key, binding the ticket/state so they cannot be replayed. New module `src/rebar/attest/opcert.py`, mirroring `attest/authorship.py`, registers `rebar.opcert.v1` in the `registry.py` `POLICY` table pinned to the `sshsig` scheme, and is wired in `attest/__init__.py`.

**Environment-key era rotation (folded in from former task 5893) — explicit-SHA model.** Env keys live **out-of-band** (`.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml`, on the code branch, NOT the tickets branch — see the epic's "Trust config & era-validity protocol"), so the identity epic's tickets-branch resolver (`authorship.resolve_event_commit` / `_keyring_for`, which glob `<ticket_dir>/<position>-*.json`) **cannot be reused verbatim**. Instead each key record carries explicit `added_at_commit`/`revoked_at_commit` **git SHAs on `main`**. What is reused is the era-validity **rule** — the `git merge-base --is-ancestor` ancestry comparison and the shared `key_not_valid_at_era` verdict — factored so authorship (position→commit) and op-cert (explicit-commit) share one ancestry predicate.

**Two-phase verdict (matches `verify_authorship.py`).** Like authorship, the substrate's era check returns a non-verified `Verdict` (`unknown_principal`) when no key is valid at the era; the `key_not_valid_at_era` reclassification is done by the **op-cert verifier** (the analog of the gate-layer two-phase check): first verify against ANY historical key for the env; if that passes but the era-scoped check fails, emit `key_not_valid_at_era`; otherwise emit `mismatch` (all verdicts are canonical `verify_signature_result.schema.json` enum members).

**Material fingerprint = the existing canonical gate fingerprint (opaque to the substrate).** The `material_fingerprint` bound in the subject is exactly the string the gates already compute today in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py::material_fingerprint`: the 16-hex-char truncation of `sha256(json.dumps({ticket_id, description, file_impact, children}, sort_keys=True))` (tags / comments / links / assignee are NOT material). The op-cert substrate (`opcert.py`) treats this fingerprint as an **opaque string**: `sign_opcert`/`verify_opcert` bind and byte-compare it exactly, and the caller (the plan-review / completion-verifier gate) supplies it — so the substrate does not depend on `PlanContext`. Replay/mutation defense is therefore: the verifier is given the ticket's CURRENT fingerprint and rejects any cert whose bound fingerprint differs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Op-certs are produced/verified via the foundation substrate (`src/rebar/attest/opcert.py`,
      `register_opcert_policy()` pinning `rebar.opcert.v1` → `sshsig` in `registry.POLICY`,
      registered in `attest/__init__.py`) with an Ed25519 environment key; a test asserts a cert
      signed by env E verifies against E's public key and fails against a different key.
- [ ] The certificate subject is an in-toto v1 Statement binding
      `{ticket id, material fingerprint, merged-log position (a `main` commit SHA)}`, where the
      material fingerprint is the existing canonical gate fingerprint
      (`plan_review.pass1.material_fingerprint`, 16-hex sha256 over
      `{ticket_id, description, file_impact, children}`) supplied by the caller and treated as an
      opaque bound string by the substrate; a test asserts a cert cannot be replayed onto a
      different ticket or onto a mutated material fingerprint.
- [ ] Environment-key rotation uses the **explicit-SHA** era model: a key is valid at the cert's
      bound `main` commit `P` iff `is-ancestor(added_at_commit, P)` and not
      `is-ancestor(revoked_at_commit, P)` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`), reusing the shared
      ancestry *rule*, NOT `resolve_event_commit`. The op-cert verifier does the two-phase check
      (verify against any historical key; if that passes but the era check fails → the shared
      `key_not_valid_at_era` verdict; else `mismatch`). All three verdicts (`certified`,
      `key_not_valid_at_era`, `mismatch`) are in the canonical `verify_signature_result.schema.json`
      enum — no new verdict string is introduced. A test asserts a cert from a key valid
      at its era verifies while one past its rotation surfaces `key_not_valid_at_era`.
baseline.summary: op-cert: asymmetric environment-signed kind + subject binding

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Every other story in this epic is validated against fixtures and a stateful fake transport — the right tier for each. But a fake cannot reach the failure modes that only appear against a real tracker: real JQL over several projects, real per-project key allocation and issue creation, and the one that matters most — whether a pass scoped to one project can contaminate another. It is the justified live canary the shared test-design standard allows for external-service mapping.

A first live-Cloud draft (against the shared REB + DIG projects) surfaced two flaws the fake had masked, making live Cloud the wrong tier:

1. Non-existent project keys parse-ERROR, they do not return empty. The draft modelled the
   "configured but empty" and "unknown to the tracker" paths with keys that live only in the mapping,
   never in Jira. Real Jira rejects `project = REBEMPTY` (`the value 'rebempty' does not exist for the
   field 'project'`), acli exits non-zero, and because the inbound fetcher fans a per-project query
   out with no per-project try/except (`fetcher.py` `_build_snapshot`), that aborts the ENTIRE pass.
   The fake returned empty, so nothing caught it. No contract says a mapped-but-absent project is
   tolerated; the inbound search is deliberately fail-closed, the safe posture for a bridge.
2. Only two real Cloud projects exist. Modelling three repo shapes (one/two/zero repos), an empty
   project, and an unknown-project fail-closed path needs more isolated projects than two shared
   production projects supply, and throwaway Cloud projects are not available here.

## Approach

Rehearse against the ephemeral Jira Data Center instance the existing DC harness (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/`) already stands up in CI, where we hold admin rights and create and destroy throwaway projects per run. This dissolves both flaws and makes the rehearsal a reproducible, CI-verified green run on every build (the `jira-dc-harness` job) rather than a manual attested live-Cloud step. The isolated store copy is the harness's existing local/file-based copy (`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off`); no S3 remote is involved.

A per-run fixture provisions four scratch projects via the harness's bug-3fe5-hardened provisioning (pinned `_PROJECT_TEMPLATE`; `_assert_project_capabilities` verifies issue types/fields first, no silent degrade), each a random `RBJ`-prefixed key, and tears them all down on every exit path: P_ONE -> one repo, P_TWO -> two repos, P_ZERO -> zero repos, P_LEGACY -> the legacy default. "Configured but empty of issues" is now a REAL project that simply returns `[]` in a pass, never a non-existent key. "Unknown to Jira" is modelled as its true product behaviour: a key never created is configured and the harness asserts the pass FAILS CLOSED (the per-project search raises, the pass writes nothing).

Dry-run gating is the contamination control: each mutating scenario runs `bridge preview` first and asserts the previewed mutation set contains ONLY targets in the intended project (empty intersection against every other configured project) before `bridge sync` runs — every mutating pass, including any binding setup sync, is preview-gated first. The per-mutation target project each intersection is computed against is read from the preview plan: the Jira key prefix for an outbound UPDATE, and the `_bridge_target_project` field for an outbound CREATE (which has no key yet).

Cleanup runs on every exit path: session-scoped finalizers DELETE each scratch project (`/rest/api/2/project/{key}`, poll-until-404), which removes its issues; per-run random keys mean no run touches another's data, and a session guard refuses to start if a prior `RBJ*` project leaked.

## Scope

- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py` (edit) — add a session-scoped `scratch_projects` fixture
  that yields N verified scratch projects, REUSING the existing in-conftest provisioning
  (`_create_scratch_project` / `_assert_project_capabilities` / `_random_project_key` / `_request`),
  and tears them all down. Nothing is relocated: ccf6 and
  `test_live_jira_dc_conftest.py::test_the_monkeypatched_surface_is_still_defined_in_conftest` require
  `_request` and the provisioning helpers to stay DEFINED in conftest (two unit tests monkeypatch
  `_request` in conftest's namespace, and moving them fails open to live HTTP), so the cluster is
  reused in place, never moved. The module-size cap applies only to `src/rebar`, so this test file
  may grow.
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_multi_project_rehearsal.py` (new) — the scenarios and per-run
  fixtures (four scratch projects, isolated DC store copy mapped for them, DC-pointed bridge config).
- `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` (edit) — runbook: the rehearsal now runs against the ephemeral DC
  instance in CI (and locally via `make jira-dc-up`), replacing the live-Cloud section.
- `tests/external/live_multi_project/conftest.py` (delete) and
  `tests/external/live_multi_project/test_multi_project_rehearsal.py` (delete) — the flawed
  live-Cloud-only draft, replaced by the DC rehearsal.

## Testing

Tier: a live end-to-end rehearsal against a real Jira DC instance — permitted by the shared standard for external-service mapping when a fake cannot reach the mechanism (genuine cross-project isolation, real JQL over several projects). Gated to the opt-in external suite (`REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1`, the DC-readiness sentinel) and run in the `jira-dc-harness` CI job (`pytest -m external tests/external/live_jira_dc`) on a native-amd64 runner; a new file there is collected automatically. The nine scenarios are the Acceptance Criteria below, each preview-gated then applied.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The rehearsal provisions its throwaway scratch projects with the hardened pinned template and
      verifies their capabilities before any scenario runs; checked by asserting each created project
      reports the required issue types/fields (a degrade fails provisioning, not a later scenario).
- [x] Issues created in two scratch projects are both ingested in one pass with the correct source
      project and repos recorded; checked by querying both projects and asserting both tickets' fields.
- [x] Rebar-created tickets targeting each project land in that project only; checked by querying the
      projects and asserting each issue exists in exactly one.
- [x] A ticket with an explicit empty project creates no issue in any project; checked by a post-run
      query of every scratch project finding no issue for it.
- [x] All three repo configurations (one/two/zero repos) produce the expected repos on inbound
      tickets and correct routing on outbound ones; checked per configuration.
- [x] An outbound update targeting a project outside the configured scope is surfaced in `bridge
      preview`'s planned mutation set and, on `bridge sync`, raises `CrossProjectTargetError` from the
      write-path guard and changes nothing; checked by comparing the projects' issue state before and
      after the refused sync.
- [x] A project key never created in the DC instance, when configured in the mapping, makes a bridge
      pass fail closed and write nothing; checked by asserting the pass errors and a post-run query of
      the real projects shows no change.
- [x] Every scenario's preview contained only targets in its intended project; checked by asserting an
      empty intersection against every other configured project for each preview.
- [x] The whole rehearsal runs green in the `jira-dc-harness` CI job against the ephemeral DC instance;
      checked by the job passing (not skipped — the fail-on-all-skip canary enforces at least one live
      scenario executed).
- [x] Every scratch project the run created is deleted on teardown and a read of each returns 404,
      including when a scenario fails mid-run; checked by injecting a post-creation failure into one
      scenario and asserting all scratch projects are gone (404) after teardown.
baseline.summary: Live multi-project rehearsal against throwaway projects on the ephemeral Jira DC instance

baseline.description:
# RC2b: snapshot-horizon-safe replay (no silent sub-horizon drop)

## Why
When two clones write at once, one can compact and delete the events it folded before seeing the other's event. After merge, that event sorts BEFORE the snapshot and replay's positional skip drops it regardless of `source_event_uuids` -> silent data loss. Live store holds ~11 such orphans.

## Decision (ACCEPTED): Option 1 (rebuild-on-stray) + Option 3 (conservative horizon)
Option 2 (per-field LWW-by-timestamp) deferred.

## Concrete rules
- SETTLED (Option 3): compaction folds an event only if `hlc.physical_now() - event_ts >= COMPACTION_HORIZON_NS`.
  `COMPACTION_HORIZON_NS` is a NEW `CompactConfig` field (default `1_800_000_000_000` = 1800 s in HLC nanosecond
  ticks — HLC uses `time.time_ns()`); ALSO add its coercer entry to `_SECTIONS['compact']` in `_config_schema.py`
  and an env-var alias in `config.py` (the established pattern). Younger "hot-edge" events stay live `.json`.
- REBUILD (Option 1): fsck detects a merged-in pre-snapshot orphan (KNOWN-type `.json` sorting before the SNAPSHOT,
  uuid absent from `source_event_uuids`) and rebuilds that ticket's snapshot from the full ordered log INCLUDING
  `.retired`. This needs a NEW `include_retired: bool = False` param on `reduce_ticket` (`reducer/_api.py`) +
  `prepare_event_files` (`reducer/_cache.py`, both listing paths ~97/~102) + `scan_for_latest_snapshot` seeing the
  same set. CACHE (resolved): the rebuild path BYPASSES the `compute_dir_hash` cache and reads the full file set
  directly (avoids a stale `*.json`-only hash ignoring `.retired`). Rebuild uses `fsutil.atomic_write` (the existing
  helper — do not hand-roll tmp+rename); the old snapshot goes to `<snap>.bak`, deleted only after a clean replay
  round-trip in the same run. `.bak` CRASH RECOVERY (resolved): if `<snap>.bak` exists at rebuild start, RE-REBUILD
  from the full log (authoritative) and overwrite — do not "restore from .bak". Log (WARN) each detected orphan +
  rebuild; a rebuild counter lives as a module-level metric in fsck. Concurrency: a single-writer guard (the store
  write-lock) serializes fsck rebuild vs compaction on a ticket.

## Dependencies
- A1 (tricolour-head-ratfish) ADDS `RETIRED_SUFFIX`/`is_active_event`/the `.retired` rename (NOT in the codebase
  today) — depends_on A1 landing first (wired). A3 (entitled-unsweet-nutria) REUSES this `include_retired` rebuild.

## Scope
`reducer/_processors.py` (process_snapshot + positional skip ~648-702), `reducer/_api.py` + `reducer/_cache.py` (`include_retired` + cache bypass), `_commands/fsck.py` (orphan-detect + rebuild + counter), `_commands/compact.py` (horizon fold guard), `_config_schema.py` (`CompactConfig.COMPACTION_HORIZON_NS` + `_SECTIONS['compact']`), `config.py` (env alias). `reducer/_sort.py` read-only. NOT the reconciler code.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `COMPACTION_HORIZON_NS` on `CompactConfig` (default 1_800_000_000_000 ns), coercer in `_SECTIONS['compact']`, env alias in `config.py`; ADR records the rule. Test: an event younger than the horizon is NOT folded.
- [ ] `reduce_ticket`/`prepare_event_files`/`scan_for_latest_snapshot` gain `include_retired`; default False preserves behavior; the rebuild path bypasses the cache. Test: rebuild does not return a stale cached state.
- [ ] Rebuild uses `fsutil.atomic_write`; `.bak` written + deleted only after a clean round-trip; if `.bak` exists at start, re-rebuild (test covers the interrupted-rebuild restart); rebuild counter incremented + WARN logged.
- [ ] A merged-in pre-horizon orphan is no longer silently dropped. Two-clone sub-horizon-append regression test: RED before, GREEN after.
- [ ] Determinism proof: `reduce_ticket` twice on the same file set (incl. shuffled `os.listdir` order) -> equal compiled_state. Proof: `python -m pytest tests/scripts/reducer/ -k determinism -q`.
- [ ] Decision + design recorded in an ADR.
baseline.summary: Snapshot-horizon-safe reconciliation (RC2b): no silent sub-horizon drop

baseline.description:
Six subsystem agents triaged every substantial comment in `src/rebar` (439 files) against the maintainer's destination taxonomy: history belongs in tickets, architecture in ADRs, logic in code, contracts in schema, and comments carry only proximate just-in-time context in concise language.

Total recoverable: **~2,033 lines**. Per shard: reconciler ~970, plan_review+workflow ~230, store/reducer ~230, llm core ~218, commands/CLI ~205, root/services ~180.

The largest single category is self-referential: **prose explaining the 800-LOC cap**, occupying the budget it describes. 28 sites in the reconciler alone carry variants of "RELOCATED VERBATIM out of transport.py; this module changes no behaviour. The move is forced by the LOCKED 800-line cap." The loop closes at `outbound_differ.py:164`, which records that a fix had to "buy its lines back from real duplication instead of from comments" because the module sat at the cap.

Headroom recovered where it is tightest: `runner.py` 3 → ~48 lines (the repo's #1 hotspot, 88 commits, whose 371-line method sits at its C901 ceiling); `_ref_lock.py` 1 → ~21; `dispatch_one.py` 14 → ~57; `inbound_differ.py` 18 → ~66; `fetcher.py` 29 → ~80.

Honest counterweight, and it must not be lost: **comment triage cannot fix three files.** `_store/event_append.py` (791) recovers ~10 lines; `reducer/_processors.py` (777) recovers ~3; `signing.py` (798) recovers ~5-8. Their comments ARE the replay-compat and security invariants. Each shard identified the real call-graph seam instead, and those splits are out of scope here.

Every shard produced a `do_not_move` list — blocks that look relocatable but are load-bearing. Those lists are the protection record and must be preserved (appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md`) so a future sweep does not re-flag them. Examples: "on DC 8.17.1 the `fields.parent` write answers HTTP 204 and is silently ignored. Do not 'simplify' that extra round trip away"; "ACLI's `--out`/`--in` are INVERTED relative to the naive reading"; "READ FROM `exc.response.headers`, NOT `exc.headers`".

Verified-stale comments found along the way (correctness, not verbosity): six sites say the deterministic floor is "P1-P9" while `DET_CHECKS` has 11 entries and runs P1..P11; three sites in `llm/` assert an Anthropic constraint that `structured.py:228-238` explicitly calls "a stale rationale" and "a relic" 210 lines below one of them; `_backend_registry.py:3` says "STUB: signatures pinned, bodies to be implemented" while `select_backend` is imported by 13 modules; `_io/__init__.py:14` says the import side "lands in a later sub-task" six lines above the line that imports it; `reducer/llm_format.py:1-28` documents a key map that omits four keys present directly below it and cites a module path that does not exist.

~13 new ADRs are proposed across the shards, each consolidating an argument currently restated 4-8 times. The largest: "one idempotent transform, applied fit-then-normalize, on the local side only" — the same four-paragraph argument at 8 sites, warning that "Swapping the two re-introduces a diff that never converges."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] All six shards complete, each landing separately
- [x] Each shard's `do_not_move` list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` before that shard's edits land
- [x] History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a ticket filed first
- [x] Proposed ADRs are written and the inline blocks reduced to citations
- [x] Verified-stale comments are corrected, not deleted, where they document a live invariant
- [x] No file's comment density is reduced by deleting a load-bearing invariant

## CORRECTION (plan-review BLOCK, criteria E1/E2/F1)

Two ACs were unmeasurable: the ~2,033-line recovery headline had no covering criterion, and "Proposed ADRs are written" named no specific ADR set. Superseded below. The line-recovery criterion is deliberately framed as a MEASURED-AND-RECORDED outcome, not a fixed target — this is the same correction the 9ce8 shard's own plan-review already blessed ("the number is an output of the work, not an input to it"); mandating a fixed >=2,000-line floor would contradict that and incentivise manufactured relocations.

## Disposition vocabulary (what the ACs measure against)

A **unit** is one contiguous comment block (a run of adjacent comment lines, or a single docstring). Every in-scope unit gets exactly one disposition:

- **RELOCATE** (non-KEEP) — the prose moves to its taxonomy destination (history -> ticket,
  architecture -> ADR, contract -> schema) and the inline block is reduced to a one-line
  citation. Recovered lines = block minus citation.
- **DELETE** (non-KEEP) — redundant/obsolete prose with no destination worth keeping; removed
  outright. Recovered lines = whole block. Only after confirming it is not load-bearing.
- **KEEP** (KEEP-class) — proximate just-in-time context that belongs exactly where it is;
  untouched, not counted as recovered.
- **DO_NOT_MOVE** (KEEP-class) — looks relocatable but is load-bearing (measured external-API
  fact, anti-refactor warning, or a lint/type-checker pragma); retained VERBATIM and recorded on
  the shard's `do_not_move` list. Not counted as recovered.
- **CORRECT-IN-PLACE** (KEEP-class) — a verified-stale comment documenting a LIVE invariant;
  the text is corrected where it sits, not moved. Not counted as recovered.

"non-KEEP unit" in the ACs = the RELOCATE and DELETE classes only. KEEP, DO_NOT_MOVE and CORRECT-IN-PLACE are KEEP-class: retained (corrected in place where stale) and never counted as recovered lines. Completeness is verified by confirming every in-scope unit carries exactly one of these five labels.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above)

- [x] All six shards complete, each landing as a separate stacked change in the dependency order
      9ce8 -> 4fc1 -> 4b94 -> ad16 -> da4c -> ab77.
- [x] Each shard MEASURES and RECORDS on its own ticket the actual comment lines it recovered (by
      diff line-count), and this parent records the net total across shards. Per the 9ce8
      correction the ~2,033 / per-shard figures are OUTPUTS to be measured, NOT targets: no
      relocation is manufactured to reach an estimate, and a shard recovering fewer lines than
      estimated is not a failure provided every non-KEEP unit in scope was correctly
      dispositioned.
- [x] Every ADR enumerated in the shard tickets (the new ADRs and the amendments to ADR
      0028/0055/0031/0035) EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it is
      collapsed -- destination first, then the relocation. This AC is met per-shard against that
      shard's own enumerated ADR set.
- [x] History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a
      ticket filed first.
- [x] Each shard's `do_not_move` list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` before that shard's
      edits land.
- [x] Verified-stale comments are corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only
      where obsolete.
- [x] No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings
      stay verbatim.
- [x] No behaviour change: the full test suite AND `make lint` / `make typecheck` pass
      unchanged across every shard. Inline pragma comments (`# noqa`, `# type: ignore`,
      `# ruff:`, `# tickets-boundary-ok`) and any docstring a test reads via introspection
      are load-bearing by definition and go on every shard's `do_not_move` list -- they are
      never treated as relocatable prose.
baseline.summary: Comment triage: relocate history, rationale and contracts out of src

baseline.description:
# A per-pass model configuration seam (one env var cannot express four passes)

## Problem

rebar's gates deliberately run different model classes per pass. On the direct-Anthropic path this works today and is MEASURED: a real `rebar review-plan` made 41 calls on `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` (Pass-1, which escalates up from the YAML `model_ladder`) and 1 on `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6` (the Pass-2/Pass-4 verifier downgrade). The operator requirement is exactly that shape: Pass-1 on opus for most criteria, Pass-2/Pass-4 on sonnet.

There is no way to express that on any non-default provider, because the whole selection collapses onto ONE knob:

- ~~**The verifier downgrade inverts.**~~ **RESOLVED — retained only so the record shows what changed.**
  This bullet argued that `review_kernel/verify.py:269`'s `verifier_default if model == default_model
  else (model or verifier_default)` would read ANY Bedrock id as an explicit operator choice, so the
  sonnet downgrade would stop applying and Pass-2/Pass-4 would follow Pass-1 onto one model. That
  mechanism is now UNREACHABLE: `resolve_verifier_model` has ZERO callers under `src/rebar`, pinned by
  `test_the_superseded_equality_rule_has_no_production_consumers` (172e). The verifier paths resolve the
  `standard` CLASS instead, so the inversion cannot occur. What remains is narrower and is the real
  subject of this ticket: four code-review steps declare no class at all.
- ~~**Pass-1's ladder routes to the wrong provider.**~~ **RESOLVED — this problem no longer exists, and
  the claim is retained only so the record is honest about what changed.** This section originally read
  that `plan-review.yaml:62-65` sets `model_ladder: [claude-haiku-4-5, claude-sonnet-4-6,
  claude-opus-4-8]` as BARE names, and that since `config.py` maps the `claude` prefix to provider
  `anthropic`, a Bedrock run would send its Pass-1 finders to DIRECT ANTHROPIC — a split brain. VERIFIED
  AT HEAD: that ladder now reads `[trivial, standard, frontier]`, i.e. CLASS terms (story 7761 landed
  it), so the bare-name provider inference no longer applies to plan-review's Pass-1. The split-brain
  risk this ticket was partly created to fix is already closed for plan-review; what REMAINS is the
  code-review gate, below.
- **Code review is only PARTLY split — this is the remaining problem and the reason this ticket is still
  needed.** CORRECTED against HEAD: an earlier version said `code-review.yaml` "declares no `model:` and
  no `model_ladder:` on any step", which is no longer true — `verify` (`:143`) declares `model: standard`
  at `:156` (story 172e landed it). The four steps that still inherit `cfg.model` implicitly are `base`
  (`:67`), `round_a` (`:77`), `round_b` (`:109`) and `coach` (`:182`). So the gate has a Pass-2 split and
  no Pass-1/Pass-4 split. Note the four undeclared steps do NOT fall back to `resolve_verifier_model` either — nothing under
  `src/rebar` calls it. They simply inherit the run's single resolved `cfg.model`, having declared no
  per-step model for the interpreter to override with.

## Why this blocks two stories

- **eb6e (production cutover)** scopes itself to "the bot service's `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`" — one env var
  for four passes. Both single-model outcomes are wrong: opus-everywhere hard-fails Pass-2, which
  pins `temperature=0` (MEASURED: `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` returns 400 `temperature is
  deprecated for this model`; see [rebar:1903-868c-b704-4a80]), and sonnet-everywhere silently
  downgrades Pass-1 with no test to catch it.
- **0d76 (parity bar)** compares v1=Anthropic against v2=Bedrock. Without per-pass control the arms
  differ in TWO variables (provider AND per-pass model class), so any criterion failure is
  unattributable and any pass is unrepresentative of production. A full corpus run is ~3,200 model
  calls; spending that on an unattributable comparison is the expensive way to learn this.

## Approach (the mechanism EXISTS — this ticket is the CONSUMER)

**THE EXACT CLASS EACH STEP DECLARES — stated here so no executor has to guess.** A review round blocked twice on this being unspecified.

| step | `code-review.yaml` | pass | declares |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base`    | `:67`  | Pass-1 finder (single-shot) | `model: frontier` |
| `round_a` | `:77`  | Pass-1 finder (**batch**)   | inside `batch:` -> `model_ladder: [frontier]` |
| `round_b` | `:109` | Pass-1 finder (**batch**)   | inside `batch:` -> `model_ladder: [frontier]` |
| `verify`  | `:143` | Pass-2 verifier             | `model: standard` — ALREADY LANDED (172e) |
| `coach`   | `:182` | Pass-4 coach                | step-level `model: standard` |

This matches the criterion above — opus-family for Pass-1, sonnet-family for Pass-2/Pass-4 — because `frontier` and `standard` resolve to exactly those families via `_DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_CLASS`.

**WHY THE BATCH STEPS MUST USE A LADDER KEY, AND WHY IT HAS EXACTLY ONE RUNG.** A step-level `model:` on a `batch:` step is a SILENT NO-OP — `interpreter.py:384-395` builds `BatchRunRequest` from the `batch:` sub-dict only (`model_ladder=tuple(batch.get('model_ladder') or ())`) and never passes the enclosing step's `model:`, while `runners.py:128-130` computes `resolve_model_string(ladder[0]) if ladder else None` and comments that an empty ladder means "no per-step model, NOT a resolved class". Because `model` IS a legal step key (`schema.py` `_STEP_ORDER`), such a declaration VALIDATES and is then discarded — and a test asserting only that the YAML carries a class token would PASS while runtime behaviour was unchanged. An earlier version of this very table made that mistake. ONE RUNG, not plan-review's three: `plan-review.yaml:62-65` declares its finder batch as `model_ladder: [trivial, standard, frontier]`, so copying that precedent here is the obvious move — and it is the WRONG one for this ticket. A ladder escalates per criterion, so the model that actually answers a given criterion is NOT determinate: a cheap criterion may be resolved at `trivial` and never reach `frontier`. This ticket's first criterion requires a TEST asserting "the RESOLVED model for each pass ... is the intended class", and that assertion is not writable against a non-deterministic resolution. Flat classes keep the criterion falsifiable. Adopting the ladder for cost reasons is a legitimate FOLLOW-UP optimisation, but it is a different change with a different oracle, and bundling it here would make the per-pass guarantee untestable — which is the whole point of the ticket.

**PASSES vs STEPS — two different counts, both correct, stated so they are not read as a contradiction.** "Four passes" is the plan-review PASS model (Pass-1 finder, Pass-2 verifier, Pass-3 decide, Pass-4 coach) and is what this ticket's title means. "Five LLM-calling steps" is the CODE-REVIEW gate's step count in `code-review.yaml`. One pass can be implemented by MORE THAN ONE step — which is precisely how the batch steps `round_a`/`round_b` escaped an earlier count. Neither number is wrong; they measure different things.

**REWRITTEN: an earlier draft called this a "candidate, not a decision" and sketched a mapping still to be designed. Stale — epic eb58 has since shipped it.** `model_classes.py` provides the trivial/standard/frontier slots, the nine `REBAR_LLM_<CLASS>_<FIELD>` overrides, per-class fallback chains and class-aware resolution; the batch runners and verifier paths already consume it; and `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is deprecated, fanning out to all three classes. This ticket does NOT design a mapping — it makes the remaining gate steps DECLARE their class.

Make the per-pass model resolvable per provider rather than inferred from one string. Sketch: express the mapping (Pass-1 finder ladder, Pass-2/Pass-4 verifier) as configuration keyed by provider, so a Bedrock run names Bedrock inference-profile ids for each pass instead of inheriting bare `claude-*` names. Note `bedrock_model_id` is NOT the answer — a single scalar cannot express a mapping, which is part of why it was deleted [rebar:281f-3336-c668-4979].

**STALENESS AUDIT of this section, run against source at HEAD 18ecd9709 rather than accepted wholesale from a review finding:**
* STALE, fixed: `plan-review.yaml` no longer names bare `claude-*` ids — `:62` declares a `model_ladder`
  in CLASS terms (7761).
* STALE, fixed: "no per-provider class mapping exists" — `model_classes.py` exists and is consumed.
* **RETRACTED — I DEFENDED THIS CLAIM AND IT WAS WRONG.** An earlier revision asserted that
  `review_kernel/verify.py:263-269`'s equality test (`verifier_default if model == default_model else
  ...`) is OPERATIVE, and that steps without a declared class "still inherit the equality rule". The
  function body does still contain that expression — which is all I actually checked — but it has
  **ZERO production call sites**: `resolve_verifier_model` appears under `src/rebar` only as its own
  definition, one docstring mention in `model_classes.py:279`, and two re-export lines in
  `review_kernel/__init__.py`. `tests/unit/test_code_review_verifier_class.py:171`
  (`test_the_superseded_equality_rule_has_no_production_consumers`, landed by 172e) ENFORCES that
  nothing calls it, and instructs "do not relax the assertion". So the rule is superseded and
  unreachable, not live. I verified EXISTENCE and inferred REACHABILITY, which is not the same thing.
* **THE REAL MECHANISM, corrected:** the four undeclared steps inherit the run's single resolved
  `cfg.model` because they declare no per-step model at all — the interpreter simply has nothing to
  override with. That single-knob inheritance is what this ticket removes. `resolve_verifier_model` is
  NOT part of the story and must not be cited as the defect; if anything, a NEW caller of it would
  reintroduce the 172e defect and break the guard test.

This ticket does NOT touch `verify.py:269`. An earlier revision said the chosen shape "must also fix" that equality test; that instruction rested on the retracted claim above. The helper is superseded and callerless, a guard test pins it that way, and ADDING a caller would reintroduce the defect 172e removed. Leave it alone.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a test asserts the RESOLVED model for each pass under a Bedrock configuration is the intended
      class (opus-family for Pass-1, sonnet-family for Pass-2/Pass-4)
- [ ] a test asserts no bare `claude-*` model id is resolved to provider `anthropic` during a run
      configured for another provider
- [ ] a test asserts the Pass-2/Pass-4 downgrade still applies when the operator has NOT explicitly
      chosen a model, on a non-default provider
- [ ] the code-review gate expresses its per-pass models explicitly. RE-MEASURED against the shipped YAML — and this CORRECTS AN ERROR AN EARLIER PASS OF THIS PLAN
      INTRODUCED. That pass wrote "the gate has THREE prompt steps, not four", which is WRONG: it
      counted only the single-shot prompt steps and MISSED THE TWO BATCH STEPS. The gate has FIVE
      LLM-calling steps — `base` (:67), `round_a` (:77), `round_b` (:109), `verify` (:143) and `coach`
      (:182). Only `verify` declares `model: standard` (:156, landed by 172e). The remaining work is
      therefore FOUR steps — `base`, `round_a`, `round_b`, `coach` — all still inheriting `cfg.model`.
      Correcting "four" DOWN to "three" made this plan worse than its original wording, and would
      have shipped two batch steps silently unclassed
- [ ] [operator-attested] a real gate run on the non-default provider shows the per-pass model ids
      actually used, cited from the run's usage log in a comment
baseline.summary: Per-pass model configuration seam: one env var cannot express four passes

## Observability gap

`rebar audit show <id> --output json` surfaces the **completion** attestation/sidecar, but its `plan_reviews[]` entries do **not** expose whether each plan-review was cryptographically **signed**. The per-entry keys are: `coaching, coverage, findings, impact_model_version, material_fingerprint, metrics, model, regver, runner, schema, ticket_id, ticket_type, verdict, verified_at_sha` — there is no `signed` / `signature` / `signer` / `key_id` field.

Consequence: a PASS that was signed is **indistinguishable in the audit** from a PASS produced with `--no-sign` (or one whose signing step failed to persist). The plan-review **claim gate** depends on a valid signed attestation existing, yet the audit trail — the natural place to confirm gate-readiness — cannot answer "is this plan-review signed, by whom, and at what SHA?".

To confirm signature persistence today you must bypass the audit and read the raw `*-SIGNATURE.json` events on the `tickets` branch (`git show tickets:<id>/<...>-SIGNATURE.json`) and check the latest SIGNATURE is newer than the latest EDIT. That is not a supported/ergonomic verification path.

## Suggested fix

Add plan-review signature metadata to each `plan_reviews[]` entry in the audit projection — e.g. `signed: bool`, `signer` (author id / email), `key_id`, and the attestation `material_fingerprint` + `verified_at_sha` it covers — mirroring how the completion attestation is already surfaced. Optionally a `signature_current: bool` (no EDIT newer than the SIGNATURE).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `rebar audit show <id> --output json` `plan_reviews[]` entries include a signature block
  (signed flag + signer + key_id + covered fingerprint/sha) when a `SIGNATURE` event exists.
- [ ] A signed PASS and a `--no-sign` PASS are distinguishable in the audit output.
- [ ] Text output (`--output text`) notes signed/unsigned per plan-review.
baseline.summary: audit show does not surface plan-review signature status (signed PASS indistinguishable from --no-sign)

# Rebase-If-Necessary submits a tree CI never validated, so `main` can violate a LOCKED gate while every landed change was green

## What is broken on `main` right now

`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` is **803 LOC on `gerrit/main`**, over the LOCKED 800-LOC module-size cap. The gate scans every `src/rebar` file, so **any change whose patchset tree contains that file fails `Verified`**:

```
##[error]src/rebar file(s) over the 800-LOC hard cap (split them — there is no allowlist):
803 src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py
```

It crossed the cap in `339262b990` ("af11: silence unrelated ambiguity in close scan"), merged 2026-08-04 16:28Z.

## The mechanism — how a green change landed a red tree

Change **1367** merged AFTER af11 and its merged commit carries the 803-line file. It nonetheless has a legitimate `Verified +1`. Its module-size gate reported:

    Module-size gate: OK (no src/rebar file exceeds the 800-LOC hard cap; limit locked at 800).

Because the gate ran on the **patchset**, and the patchset was based on a commit predating af11:

```
tested patchset  refs/changes/67/1367/3
  base                929ba5d66940        transition_close.py = 800   -> gate OK
  af11 an ancestor?   NO
submitted commit    313b4e9fcf21
  parent              0d1c92a1027e        transition_close.py = 803   -> gate would FAIL
```

`main` is **Rebase-If-Necessary**, so Gerrit rebased at submit and landed a tree that **CI never ran against**. The `Verified +1` was earned on a different tree than the one that merged.

**Three changes have landed this way since af11** — 1366, 1364, 1367 (16:53Z, 17:37Z, 17:39Z) — each green on a pre-af11 base, each landing the 803-line file forward.

## Why this is a hole in the gate, not just an accident

The module-size limit is deliberately LOCKED: `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is single-sourced and a normal contributor changing it fails CI, because "an administrator must override this gate to land a limit change". The intent is that the cap cannot be crossed without an explicit administrative act. Server-side rebase defeats that intent **without anyone overriding anything**: no administrator acted, no gate was forced, and yet `main` now violates the locked invariant.

It also inverts the incentive. A change branched from CURRENT main is BLOCKED; a change sitting on a stale base sails through and pushes the violation forward. The stalest branches are the ones that can still land.

## Blast radius, and why it will get worse

Every change branched from af11 or later is blocked until the file is split. Epic `e369-a449-4773-48fb` has **eight** such changes queued (1370, 1371, 1372, 1373, 1375, 1378, 1380, 1381), all `Verified -1` solely on this. As the pre-af11-based changes drain, the blocked set becomes everything.

## Candidate remedies (a CI-policy decision, recorded not taken)

1. **Re-verify after rebase.** Make submit-time rebase re-trigger CI, or forbid Rebase-If-Necessary
   when the rebase changes any gated invariant. Correct but slows every submit.
2. **Evaluate the file-size gate against the MERGE RESULT** rather than the patchset tree, the way a
   conflict check already looks at both sides.
3. **Accept the window and detect it**: a post-merge job on `main` that fails loudly the moment a
   locked invariant is violated, so the breach is attributed to the merge that caused it instead of to
   the next contributor who happens to branch from it.

(3) is the cheapest and would have caught this at 16:28Z rather than leaving it to be diagnosed by an agent whose unrelated changes it blocked.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `transition_close.py` is under the cap on `main` (immediate unblock; owned separately)
- [ ] a decision is recorded on whether submit-time rebase must re-verify, or whether the gate moves
      to the merge result
- [ ] `main` gains a check that fails when a LOCKED invariant is violated post-merge, attributing it
      to the merge commit
- [ ] a test pins that a patchset based on a stale base cannot land a tree violating the module-size
      cap — the specific hole demonstrated above

## Method note

I first told the operator "nothing can land until this is split". **That was too strong**, and the evidence above is what corrected it: changes based on a pre-af11 main still pass and still land. The accurate statement is that any change whose PATCHSET TREE contains the over-cap file is blocked. I also briefly concluded the opposite — that those three had been force-submitted — from post-rebase parents, which are not the tested tree; fetching `refs/changes/67/1367/3` directly is what settled it.
baseline.summary: Rebase-If-Necessary submits a tree CI never validated, so main violates the LOCKED module-size cap while every landed change was green

## Context / Problem

Agents and contributors struggle to discover *how to write a plan that passes the plan-review gate*. The existing material is either gate-mechanics (`plan-review-gate.md`) or a generated, reviewer-facing criterion registry (`plan-review-criteria-guide.md` / `rebar explain <id>`) — there is no concise, author-facing on-ramp, and AGENTS.md mispoints authors at the criterion registry for the "description template". The same discoverability gap exists for the code-review (`LLM-Review` + `Verified`) gate.

## Approach

Add two hand-written, prose on-ramp docs — `docs/writing-a-passing-plan.md` and `docs/passing-code-review.md` — kept short and distinct from the generated registry (so the registry stays the single source of truth for the reviewer). Make them discoverable from the CLI/MCP by extending the existing `rebar explain` seam with author-guide names (`rebar explain plan` / `rebar explain review`) via the one shared `registry` lookup that already backs the CLI, the MCP `explain_criterion` tool, and the library. Fix the AGENTS.md pointers. Rejected alternative: generating these from the registry (rejected — the on-ramp is prose, not a per-criterion rubric, and would fight the parity gate).

## Scope

- docs/writing-a-passing-plan.md (new), docs/passing-code-review.md (new)
- docs/README.md (link both new docs — the docs-index CI gate requires every top-level
  docs/*.md to be linked from the index)
- AGENTS.md (fix pointers; add code-review on-ramp reference)
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py (AUTHOR_GUIDES + explain_guide)
- src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py (_explain routes guide names)
- src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py (explain_criterion routes guide names)
- tests/unit/test_plan_review_explain.py (cover the guide path)

## Testing

Unit tests over the new `explain_guide` path across all three surfaces (library, CLI, MCP): success for every registered guide, unknown-name → `unknown-id`, missing-file → `missing-file`. Pure in-process logic (no live boundary), so offline unit coverage exercises the real path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/writing-a-passing-plan.md` exists and states the description template + the
      blocking-criteria checklist; verified by reading the file and `rebar explain plan`
      printing it (exit 0).
- [ ] `docs/passing-code-review.md` exists covering the commit checklist, LLM-Review dimensions
      (blocking vs advisory), and vote responses; `rebar explain review` prints it (exit 0).
- [ ] `rebar explain <criterion-id>` still works unchanged; an unknown topic exits 1 with a
      structured `unknown-id` error.
- [ ] AGENTS.md points authors at both new docs; no pointer claims the template lives in the
      criterion registry.
- [ ] Both new docs are linked from `docs/README.md`, so the docs-index CI gate stays green;
      verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_check_docs_index.py::test_current_repo_index_is_clean`.
- [ ] `make lint` and the explain unit tests pass.
baseline.summary: Author-facing plan-review & code-review on-ramp docs + rebar explain plan/review

# S1 — Optional Streamable-HTTP transport for rebar-mcp + transport hardening

## Why
Authentication in MCP is an HTTP-transport concern; the spec says stdio servers must not authenticate. rebar-mcp is stdio-only today (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py`, `build_server().run()` with no transport arg). Before any verifier can exist there must be an HTTP transport to authenticate against. This story adds that transport and its network hardening — the foundation every auth story builds on — with stdio unchanged as the default. It also owns the SDK version pin, because it is the first story to construct the SDK's HTTP transport / `TransportSecuritySettings`.

## What
Add an **optional Streamable-HTTP transport** to rebar-mcp, selected by config, using the official `mcp` SDK's native support:
- **Pin the SDK here:** set `mcp>=1.28.1,<2` in `pyproject.toml` — in BOTH places it appears: the
  `[project.optional-dependencies] mcp` extra AND the `[dev]` extra (both currently `mcp>=1.9`). The
  v2-alpha renames the surface; 1.28.1 is at/above the DNS-rebinding fix GHSA-9h52-p55h-vw2f. All
  later stories build on this pin.
- Extend the existing **flat** `McpConfig` dataclass and the flat `_SECTIONS['mcp']` key→coercer
  dict in `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` (the one-level `coerce_sparse` architecture — NO nested
  sub-tables) with flat scalar keys: `transport` (`stdio` default | `http`), `http_host` (default
  `127.0.0.1`), `http_port` (default `8000`), `http_path` (default `/mcp`), `http_allowed_hosts`
  (comma-separated), `http_allowed_origins` (comma-separated), and `allow_unauthenticated_http`
  (bool, default `false`). Each is one dataclass field + one flat coercer entry, auto-deriving its
  `REBAR_MCP_*` env var. This story registers these keys in `MCP_ENV_VARS` + `server.json` and
  regenerates `docs/mcp-reference.md`/`docs/env-vars.md` for its slice (the CI drift gate
  `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` must pass). NOTE — both doc generators currently miss
  dynamically-derived MCP env vars and must be adjusted (all later key-adding stories rely on these
  fixes): (a) `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` **hardcodes** the gate-env-var table (line ~208, the
  static tuple `("REBAR_MCP_READONLY","REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM","REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC")`) instead of
  iterating `MCP_ENV_VARS` → change it to iterate `MCP_ENV_VARS`; (b) `scripts/gen_env_registry.py`
  (which generates `docs/env-vars.md`) AST-scans for literal `os.environ`/`os.getenv` calls, so it
  will NOT see the `REBAR_MCP_*` names the flat coercer derives dynamically → teach it to also ingest
  `MCP_ENV_VARS`. `MCP_ENV_VARS` + `server.json` (drift-gated by `scripts/check_server_manifest.py`)
  remain the authoritative registration; the two generators are made to reflect it.
- In `build_server`/`main`, when `transport=http` construct `FastMCP("rebar", host=…, port=…,
  transport_security=TransportSecuritySettings(...))` and run via `run(transport="streamable-http")`;
  the stdio path is unchanged.
- **Explicit transport-security defaults:** DNS-rebinding/Origin protection **on**. For a loopback
  bind, set explicit loopback allowlists (`127.0.0.1:<port>`, `localhost:<port>`, `[::1]:<port>` and
  the matching `http://…` origins) rather than empty lists (empty + protection-on either 421s
  localhost or degrades protection). Construct `host`/`port`/`transport_security` at `FastMCP(...)`
  time, NOT via late attribute assignment (the documented "421" late-host bug).
- **Non-loopback bind fail-closed gates:** a non-loopback `http_host` requires BOTH
  `http_allowed_hosts` AND `http_allowed_origins` to be non-empty, AND an explicit TLS-at-edge
  acknowledgment `REBAR_MCP_HTTP_TLS_AT_EDGE` (a flat `http_tls_at_edge` bool key) — because bearer
  tokens and proxy secrets must never cross the network in cleartext; without it the server refuses
  to start.
- **Unauthenticated-HTTP guard:** `allow_unauthenticated_http` (env `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP`)
  read through the flat coercer (a resolved config field, NOT a bespoke `os.environ` read). Starting
  `transport=http` with auth disabled refuses to start unless `allow_unauthenticated_http` is true.
  (Auth config lands in S2; until then "auth enabled" is treated as false, so HTTP requires the ack.)

## Approach & rationale
Use the SDK's built-in Streamable-HTTP transport and `TransportSecuritySettings` rather than hand-rolling an ASGI server — the SDK provides both, keeping this a thin wiring change on a blessed seam, consistent with peer servers (GitHub/Grafana/Neon). Keep every config key flat to fit rebar's existing `coerce_sparse` architecture (adding scalars alongside `readonly`/`allow_llm`/ `allow_jira_sync`).

## Scope
The transport + transport-security + the two fail-closed startup gates (non-loopback and unauthenticated-HTTP) + the SDK pin only. It ships **no** token verifiers and validates **no** token (that is S2+). A subset of the epic.

## Security
Crosses a trust boundary (opens a network listener). Mitigated here by: DNS-rebinding/Origin allowlisting on by default with explicit loopback defaults; loopback-only bind by default; a non-loopback bind requiring both allowlists AND the explicit TLS-at-edge ack; and the fail-closed unauthenticated-HTTP refusal. TLS is terminated at an edge proxy (documented in S7); rebar binds HTTP behind it and never advertises or serves bearer auth in cleartext.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` pins `mcp>=1.28.1,<2`; `make typecheck` resolves the SDK imports used here.
- [ ] `McpConfig` exposes the flat `transport`/`http_host`/`http_port`/`http_path`/
      `http_allowed_hosts`/`http_allowed_origins`/`http_tls_at_edge`/`allow_unauthenticated_http`
      keys as fields + `_SECTIONS['mcp']` coercer entries; unset → stdio, byte-identical to today
      (observable: existing `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp.py` stdio suite passes).
- [ ] Integration test (tier: integration — an in-process ASGI HTTP client, e.g. httpx
      `ASGITransport`, driving the SDK's Streamable-HTTP ASGI entrypoint within its lifespan/session
      context; concrete entrypoint resolved against the pinned `mcp>=1.28.1,<2` at implementation
      time; a unit test cannot cross the Starlette transport/middleware seam) boots with
      `transport=http` (and `allow_unauthenticated_http=true` set for this auth-off boot) and asserts
      a baseline MCP request succeeds (observable oracle: HTTP 200 + valid `initialize` response).
- [ ] Integration test asserts a disallowed `Host` → **421** and a disallowed `Origin` → **403**,
      while an allowed loopback request passes (negative control in the same test), confirming the
      explicit loopback defaults work with protection ON.
- [ ] Unit/integration test asserts a non-loopback `http_host` refuses to start when either
      allowlist is empty OR `http_tls_at_edge` is unset, and starts when both allowlists AND the ack
      are supplied (observable oracle: process exits non-zero / raises a clear message vs boots).
- [ ] Unit/integration test asserts `transport=http` with auth off and no
      `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP` refuses to start, and starts when the ack is set.
- [ ] `MCP_ENV_VARS` + `server.json` include the new keys; `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` iterates
      `MCP_ENV_VARS` (not the hardcoded tuple) and `scripts/gen_env_registry.py` ingests `MCP_ENV_VARS`,
      so the regenerated `docs/mcp-reference.md` AND `docs/env-vars.md` include every new `REBAR_MCP_*`
      key; and `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` passes (observable oracle: both regenerated docs
      contain the new key names and the drift tests are green).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.

## Compatibility
Additive: stdio remains default; all new keys default to today's behavior when unset. The only cross-cutting change is the `mcp` pin, backward-compatible with existing installs. No change to the existing 48 tools or the stdio path.
baseline.summary: S1 — Optional Streamable-HTTP transport for rebar-mcp + transport hardening

# Data Center refuses to null a sub-task's `fields.parent` (HTTP 400)

## Provenance

Filed to satisfy [rebar:88d9-fe42-e50f-4067]'s AC11, which pre-authorised this exact outcome:

> UNLESS it reports its explicit `SETUP FAILED` message, which means Data Center refused to null a
> sub-task's `fields.parent`. That is a PLATFORM finding, not this fix failing; record it and file
> it separately rather than weakening the cell.

Observed on harness run **30834117797** (job 91755000385, main @ `25ead49f3e`).

## Evidence — verbatim

> SETUP FAILED (not a rebar defect): Data Center REFUSED to clear the parent of sub-task RBJYRMS-2 —
> BackendHTTPError: HTTP Error 400: JiraError HTTP 400 url:
> http://localhost:2990/jira/rest/api/2/issue/10029

The message came from `test_inbound_clear_parent_round_trips`'s SETUP, not its assertion: the cell could not get Data Center into the precondition state it needed, so it never exercised the code under test. The cell was deliberately built to report this case DISTINCTLY rather than as an ambiguous red, and it did.

## What this does and does not establish

**Does:** DC 8.17.1 rejects a `PUT` that nulls a sub-task's `fields.parent`. A sub-task on DC must have a parent — the field is structurally required — so there is no "detached sub-task" state for the fixture to create.

**Does not:** say anything about whether rebar's inbound parent clear works. That path's evidence is the discriminating trio recorded on 88d9 (measured RED against both wrong states, GREEN against the fix) plus the full 2079-passing suite. The live cell simply cannot reach it on a sub-task.

## Consequence — the inbound clear has no live coverage on DC

This is the honest statement of the gap, and it should not be papered over: the ONLY live cell for the inbound parent clear is blocked by a platform constraint, so on Data Center that path is proven by unit evidence alone. Given that this epic has twice shipped mutation-proven code that was wrong in production (1276, 1288), unit-only coverage of a data-affecting path is a real risk, not a formality.

## Options for restoring live coverage, none yet chosen

 1. Use a NON-sub-task child whose parent is an Epic Link, and clear the epic link instead — a
    different write path (greenhopper sentinel epic `"none"`), so it tests the clear the production
    code would actually take for a non-sub-task.
 2. Assert the refusal itself as the contract: pin that DC rejects the null so a future DC version
    that starts accepting it fails loudly and tells us the coverage gap can be closed.
 3. Accept unit-only coverage for the sub-task clear and record it as a known limit.

Option 1 is the only one that yields real coverage, and it is closest to what a rebar deployment would actually do, since [rebar:1a9f-50c0-e7a5-4fda] casts doubt on the sub-task write path working at all on this version.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] the refusal is confirmed against the target DC version with the raw response body recorded
      (the current evidence is the status code and URL only)
- [x] one of the three options above is chosen, with the rejected ones and the reason recorded
- [x] if option 1 or 2: the cell lands and is GREEN on a live harness run, with the run id recorded
- [x] N/A — option 2 was chosen, not option 3. Condition never held. ~~if option 3: the limitation is documented where a DC operator will see it, not only on a ticket~~
baseline.summary: Data Center refuses to null a sub-task's fields.parent (HTTP 400): the inbound-clear live cell cannot reach its precondition

baseline.description:
`rebar transition --help` advertises `[--reason=<text>]` on every transition, but on a plain close the value is parsed, threaded through two call layers, and then discarded. A user closing a ticket with `--reason="..."` reasonably believes the rationale was recorded. It was not.

Evidence:

- `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:197` — `transition_core(..., close_reason: str = "", ...)`. The name
  appears three times in the file (`:154` is a different symbol, `:197` and `:199` are signatures)
  and is **never read in any body**.
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:130-136` parses `--reason`; `:293-294` shows its only live use
  on a non-force path is `force_reason = (reason or "(no reason given)") if force else ""`, i.e. it
  is meaningful **only** under `--force`. `--force-close=<reason>` carries its own separate value.

## Scope: make the flag honest — do NOT add persistence

An earlier framing of this finding proposed persisting the close reason via the existing comment mechanism. That is rejected. `txn.py:253-259` records the governing decision:

> Bug-close CLASS guard (ticket ed13): a bug closing from a non-idea status now REQUIRES a bounded
> `--class <value>` from the closed vocabulary — REPLACING the old free-text `--reason` (which was
> validated then discarded).

ed13 deliberately replaced free-text close rationale with the bounded `CLOSE_CLASSES` vocabulary, which IS folded onto the `*->closed` STATUS edge and is single-sourced against `common.schema.json#/$defs/close_class`. Re-introducing free text — in any form — reverses a recent, intentional move toward machine-readable close data, and no evidence was found that the decision was wrong. The "why this specific ticket" capability is not missing: `rebar comment <id>` already provides it, it simply is not compulsory, and making it compulsory is what ed13 undid.

Related, already tracked elsewhere — do not duplicate: `bug_close_reason_ok` (`txn.py:154`) is dead with a docstring falsely claiming two consumers; its deletion is covered by ticket `723f-c5b2-d83b-43cb`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `close_reason` is removed from `transition_core`'s signature and every call site that passes it
- [x] `--reason` is documented as applying to the force paths only, in `transition.txt` help, the
      `transition.py` usage string, and any overview/docs line that advertises it more broadly
- [x] Passing `--reason` on a plain (non-force) close either has a documented effect or is refused —
      it must not be silently accepted and dropped
- [x] No change to `--class` / `CLOSE_CLASSES` behaviour, and no new free-text field on any event
- [x] `--force` and `--force-close=<reason>` behaviour is unchanged
baseline.summary: Make transition --reason honest: drop the discarded close_reason, scope the flag to force paths
