baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
A container ticket (epic/story with children) rarely declares its own `file_impact`, so its plan-review attestation's signed dependency set is empty and the code-drift gate falls back to whole-HEAD invalidation (ADR 0002 decision 5): ANY commit — however unrelated — invalidates the container's attestation, forcing a re-review or drift-refresh on every merge. This is the container-scale form of the over-invalidation ADR 0002 was written to fix, and a real gate-economics drag under the parallel epic/child workflow where the base ref moves constantly.

The scope a container plan actually reasons about is its children's declared scope. The invalidation lattice for inheritance already exists: `material_fingerprint` (pass1.py:551) hashes a ticket's description + file_impact + child ids, and a container review pins each DIRECT child's material fingerprint into the signed manifest — so a child editing its file_impact (or a child being added/removed) already invalidates the container's attestation via pin/material drift, forcing a re-review that recomputes any inherited union. Inheritance therefore cannot go silently stale one level deep. It does NOT hold for grandchildren (a child's fingerprint covers grandchild IDS only, not grandchild file_impact), which is why inheritance is DIRECT CHILDREN ONLY — deeper drift is covered by the deeper tickets' own attestations, mirroring the review model (reviews pin direct dependencies; dependency-order review covers each tier).

Depends on 72d9-8fbd (athletic-esthetical-polecat) landing first: before that fix, scoped dependency sets are inert in attested mode, so giving containers a non-empty set would move them OFF the only working invalidation (whole-HEAD) onto a broken path.

## Approach
1. In `dependency_hashes` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py): when the reviewed ticket
   has children, compute the candidate union = own `file_impact` ∪ review citations ∪ the
   union of DIRECT children's `file_impact`. Apply the POISON RULE: if any non-closed direct
   child has an empty `file_impact`, do NOT inherit — keep the pre-change set (own ∪
   citations; empty ⇒ whole-HEAD fallback), preserving fail-closed for undeclared scope.
   Closed children neither contribute files nor poison (their work is delivered; ADR 0024's
   completion floor deliberately stops re-litigating it, and their files' later churn belongs
   to other tickets). NO new store reads: the orchestrator already fetches every direct
   child whole (`orchestrator.assemble_context` -> `ctx.children`, each carrying status and
   file_impact), so thread that list through as an optional parameter —
   `_run_plan_review` passes `ctx.children` to `attest.sign_plan_review(children=...)`,
   which forwards to `dependency_hashes(children=...)` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py
   and attest.py gain the threading; manifest.py consumes it). This also avoids any
   tickets-root ambiguity in attested mode (the child states were read from the pinned
   ticket snapshot by the same review run). `children=None` (default — e.g. the resign
   recovery path, which has no assembled context) means NO inheritance: the dep set stays
   the pre-change own-impact ∪ citations, which is the conservative direction (an empty set
   falls back to whole-HEAD invalidation), and the drift-refresh path re-hashes the PRIOR
   signed dep set so an inherited scope survives refresh unchanged.
2. Extend P9 (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py, `p9_file_impact_coverage`): containers
   currently auto-pass. Keep passing when inheritance is effective (every non-closed direct
   child declares file_impact, and there is at least one). Surface an ADVISORY (never
   blocking) on a container whose inheritance is poisoned, naming the children with empty
   file_impact, so authors see exactly why the epic stays on whole-HEAD invalidation. Leaf
   behavior unchanged.
3. Document: docs/plan-review-gate.md (scoped-drift paragraph: containers inherit direct
   children's declared impact under the poison rule) and a short amendment note in
   docs/adr/0002-code-drift-invalidation.md decision 5.
Rejected: recursive (whole-subtree) inheritance — the pin lattice only self-heals one level deep, so a grandchild file_impact edit would leave a recursively-computed union silently stale. Rejected: inheriting a partial union when some children lack file_impact — that flips the empty-set fallback from fail-closed to fail-open for exactly the undeclared portion.

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py (dependency_hashes + a small child-union helper)
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py and src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py (thread
  ctx.children through sign_plan_review into dependency_hashes; no new store reads)
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py (P9 container extension)
- tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py
- tests/unit/test_plan_review.py (the existing P9 unit tests pin the old container auto-pass
  and must be updated to the new container semantics)
- docs/plan-review-gate.md, docs/adr/0002-code-drift-invalidation.md

## Testing
Interface tests in tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py against a tmp repo with the suite's attested/ref=HEAD default, committing drift via the existing `_commit_all` helper: container+children fixtures asserting the signed manifest's `dep` paths (inherited union, poison rule, closed-child exclusion), claim-gate outcomes (unrelated commit keeps the claim open; a committed change to a child-declared file blocks the claim naming drift), the child-file_impact-edit → container pin invalidation property, and DET-floor unit assertions for the P9 container advisory. In tests/unit/test_plan_review.py, replace test_p9_not_applicable_for_container (which asserts the old unconditional container pass) with three container cases: effective inheritance passes, a non-closed impact-less child yields the poisoning advisory naming the child id, and a closed impact-less child does not poison; leaf cases unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A container whose non-closed direct children all declare non-empty file_impact signs a
      dependency set equal to own file_impact ∪ citations ∪ the children's union — asserted
      by parsing `dep` lines from the signed manifest in an interface test.
- [ ] Poison rule: if any non-closed direct child has empty file_impact, the signed set is
      unchanged from pre-change behavior (empty ⇒ whole-HEAD fallback applies) — asserted by
      manifest inspection plus a claim blocked after an unrelated commit.
- [ ] Closed children neither contribute paths nor poison the union — asserted with a fixture
      containing one closed impact-less child.
- [ ] With inheritance effective: an unrelated committed change does NOT invalidate the
      container attestation (claim succeeds); a committed change to a child-declared file
      DOES (claim blocked, reason names drift) — both asserted via rebar.claim.
- [ ] A child editing its file_impact after the container review invalidates the container's
      attestation (pin/material drift) — asserted via claim_gate_check.
- [ ] P9: a container with poisoned inheritance yields an advisory naming the offending
      child id(s); a container with effective inheritance passes; leaf behavior is unchanged —
      asserted in DET-floor tests.

# Close the Cloud <-> Data Center reconciler test-parity gaps

## Why this exists

Two Jira adapters now sit behind one backend port, and they were hardened at different times by different means:

* **Cloud** (`adapters/jira/`, ACLI-based) is the historically battle-tested path. Years of
  production incidents produced byte-for-byte characterization pins, ADF depth tests, comment and
  description length-convergence suites, and a large applier/differ corpus.
* **Data Center** (`adapters/jira_datacenter/`, pycontribs-based) was written and tested intensively
  during epic [rebar:e369-a449-4773-48fb], which drove it against a real Dockerized instance. That
  work produced things Cloud never had: multi-page pagination proofs, a 429/`Retry-After` matrix,
  TLS and credential validation, a live 49-cell harness suite, and a structural anti-regression
  guard.

**The gaps therefore run in BOTH directions, and that is the point of this epic.** A parity audit commissioned while closing e369 found Cloud-only coverage that DC lacks AND DC-only coverage that Cloud lacks — and the second direction contains the single highest-risk finding, because Cloud's whole-project readers have never been tested past one page while DC's have.

## The governing insight

Every defect e369 found in the DC adapter was an OPERATIONAL EDGE that only appears against a differently-configured instance: index lag, server-side page caps, admin-toggled rate limiting, screen configuration, workflow transition naming. None was an architectural flaw. The same class of edge exists on Cloud and is simply untested there, because Cloud's coverage grew from *incidents that happened* rather than from *configurations that differ*.

So this epic is not "make the two suites look alike". It is: **for each behaviour the two adapters share, the harder-won test should exist on both sides**, and where a SHARED module is exercised through only one adapter, a regression must not be able to reach production for the other.

## Scope

Test-tier work plus the small production changes that untested duplication forces (one map is genuinely duplicated and must be single-sourced before it can be guarded). No behaviour change to either adapter is intended; where a test reveals one is needed, that becomes its own bug ticket rather than being folded in silently.

## Out of scope

Adding coverage for behaviours only one adapter HAS (Cloud's ADF codec depth, DC's TLS/PAT handling) — those are legitimate asymmetries, not gaps. Promoting `_engine` through the mypy strictness ratchet. Any change to the backend port's shape.

## Provenance

Commissioned during epic e369's closeout. Every finding below was verified against the tree before being written down — the audit was treated as a lead, not as evidence.

## PRIORITY FRAMING (operator direction, 2026-08-02) — READ THIS BEFORE PICKING UP A CHILD

The top priority is **shipping defect-free Jira Data Center functionality.** This epic is a *related* priority precisely because parity is what gives confidence that the DC feature is defect-free — it is instrumental to the goal, not adjacent to it.

That ranks the two directions differently, and the ranking should drive which child you take:

* **DC-DIRECTION GAPS COME FIRST.** `cedc` (DC characterization) and `79d5` (DC length convergence
  + the comment ceiling) are the ones that directly buy confidence in what is being shipped. DC's
  values have never been pinned; its contract test asserts SHAPE only and would pass with every
  value wrong. Until those land, "the DC adapter is defect-free" rests on the live harness alone,
  and the live harness only covers the configurations that one default-configured instance happens
  to have.
* **BOTH-DIRECTION items rank with them** where they touch DC: `bd9e` (the duplicated ticket-type
  map is read by DC's create path) and `2944` (several of the tests that cannot fail are DC tests,
  so they are confidence we do not actually have).
* **CLOUD-DIRECTION GAPS RANK BELOW.** `0fad` and `2127` harden the mature, live-exercised Cloud
  path. They are real and worth doing — `0fad` in particular is a genuine latent truncation risk —
  but they do not serve the DC-confidence goal, and they must not gate it. `0fad` was moved out of
  epic e369 for exactly this reason and dropped to P2 under this framing.

**Do not read "parity" as "make the two suites symmetrical."** The goal is confidence in the DC feature. Where an asymmetry is legitimate (Cloud's ADF depth, DC's TLS/PAT handling) closing it buys nothing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `cedc-58d1-f6d1-428e` is closed: DC's create-path field values, both sanitizer boundaries,
      the identity label form, and all four probe branches are pinned BY VALUE, and the shared
      `map_fields_to_remote` body is exercised through `WikiTextCodec` as well as `AdfCodec`
- [x] `79d5-63c7-5f31-48a7` is closed: an oversized DC comment AND an oversized DC description each
      converge across TWO passes (pass 2 plans nothing for that ticket), and the DC comment
      ceiling's PROVENANCE is cited in the source at the `max_chars=WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` binding
      — naming `jira.text.field.character.limit` and JRASERVER-28519 — so the constant reads as a
      decision rather than an assumption. (The ceiling is no longer unknown: it was established from
      Jira's `jpm.xml`, whose property description covers Comments as well as Description; that it
      is admin-configurable is tracked separately as `049e-9fac-a821-4ea2` and does NOT gate this
      epic.) Verified by reading the cited comment in the diff
- [x] `bd9e-0740-1b47-47f8` is closed: exactly ONE dict literal defines the local->Jira ticket-type
      map within `adapters/`, and `test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py` carries an assertion that
      fails the build if a second copy appears — the same guard shape the status and priority maps
      already have
- [x] `2944-dd3f-e982-4359` is closed: each of the five enumerated vacuous tests either asserts the
      contract its own docstring names or is renamed to what it actually pins; none is merely
      deleted, because the docstring's intent is the valuable part
- [x] [operator-attested] every pin or rewrite added under this epic is MUTATION-CHECKED — the
      mutation applied and the resulting verdict recorded as a comment on the owning child ticket. A
      pin nobody has seen fail is not evidence. Copied terminal output showing the mutated code and
      the resulting FAIL, pasted as a child-ticket comment, satisfies this criterion; it is attested
      rather than CI-checkable because a mutation is applied and reverted in a working tree and
      therefore leaves no repo artifact to inspect
- [x] where the two adapters CORRECTLY diverge, the expectation carries a DIFFERENT value per
      vendor rather than asserting sameness. Checked positively rather than as a negative property:
      the parametrized characterization suite must contain at least one case for EACH known
      divergence — (a) rich text, ADF vs wiki markup, and (b) identity form, Cloud `accountId` vs
      DC `name` — in which the Cloud and DC parameters carry DIFFERENT expected values, and both
      cases pass. Verifiable by reading the parametrize table in the diff and by running those
      cases; a reviewer can confirm it without re-deriving which behaviours diverge, because the
      two are enumerated here
- [x] `test_backend_characterization.py`'s pre-existing Cloud assertions still pass UNEDITED, so
      Cloud's incident-hardened safety net is intact rather than loosened to fit DC
baseline.summary: Close the Cloud<->DC reconciler test-parity gaps

# Container eval fixtures without a `children` payload cannot be run by `run_case`

## Problem

`eval_solver._run_criterion_case` raises for a CONTAINER criterion (G3 / G4 / decomp-shape) whose case carries no non-empty `children` list — the criterion runs `pass1_container` over a (parent, children, sibling-roster) decomposition, not inline text. ALL 12 cases in `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-container.eval.yaml` carry only `input` (the parent plan) and no `children`, so none can be executed through `run_case`. `plan-review-decomp-shape.eval.yaml` cases DO carry `children` and are the working precedent.

## Evidence (measured, story 0d76)

In the live provider-parity run, `G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar` and `G3-FP-covered-by-named-consumer-rebar` raised `ValueError: container criterion 'G3' needs a non-empty children list in the eval fixture` on BOTH arms at ALL 3 epochs, before any model call, on both class slots. They contributed nothing but error counts. `provider_parity._runnable` now excludes them, so the parity corpus is 28 items rather than 30. (Only those two surface because `select_corpus` takes the FIRST gold-block and FIRST gold-advisory case per spec; the other ten are equally unrunnable.)

## The decision, and why it is already settled by the project's own record

The original AC asked whether to add `children` payloads or to document the cases as runnable only through `pass1_container` directly. The repo already answers this, so this ticket does NOT re-open it:

- `eval_solver._run_criterion_case` states the contract in its own comment: *"A container
  criterion with no `children` payload is a **fixture error**, not a silent pass."* The raise is
  deliberately loud precisely so the fixture gets fixed.
- `plan-review-decomp-shape.eval.yaml` is the same kind of spec with the payload present, and
  documents the shape in its header: *"Container criteria run over a (parent, children)
  decomposition, so each case carries the parent plan as `input` and the children as a
  `children:` list."*
- `_run_criterion_case` drives the SAME `pass1_container` fan-out the real gate uses, so a
  `children`-carrying fixture IS the "runnable through `pass1_container`" path — the second
  option is not a different capability, only a decision to leave the corpus smaller.

So: add the payloads. No new capability, no contract change, no code change.

## Approach

Add a `children:` list to each of the 12 cases in `plan-review-container.eval.yaml`, each entry `{ticket_id, title, description}`, matching the decomp-shape shape exactly.

The children are **transcribed, not invented**: every case's existing `input` prose already names its child set (e.g. `G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar`: "Its children cover the importer, the API, and the UI — but NO child addresses idempotency"; `G4-R-ordering-violation-snap`: "Child A deletes the legacy payments column; child B still reads it"). Each `children` list makes exactly those children explicit and adds nothing the `input` does not already assert, so the gold label (`expect`) of every case is unchanged by construction.

`sibling_roster` is deliberately NOT pinned per case: `_run_criterion_case` falls back to `build_sibling_roster(children)`, the ONE shared builder, so eval fixtures see the same roster shape production does.

No source change: `provider_parity._runnable` already admits any container case with a non-empty `children` list, so `eligible_cases` picks the fixed cases up unchanged.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-container.eval.yaml` — add `children:` to all 12 dataset
  cases. `prompt`, `model`, `epochs`, `gate`, `scorers`, `tolerance`, every `input`, every
  `expect`/`criterion`/`corpus`/`note`/`mode`, and the whole `gold_set` are UNCHANGED.
- `tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py` — `test_container_cases_without_a_children_payload_are_excluded`
  ends with `assert all(i.spec != "plan-review-container" for i in pp.eligible_cases())`, using
  the container spec as the witness that the exclusion rule is non-vacuous. Once the fixtures are
  fixed that witness is false. The RULE stays pinned (the `_runnable` unit assertions in the same
  test already prove it non-vacuously on synthetic cases); only the stale witness line is
  replaced by its inverse — that the container spec is now eligible.

## Testing

- The load-bearing assertion is that every container case in `eligible_cases()` carries a
  non-empty `children` payload AND that the container spec is now represented — i.e. the ticket's
  own AC becomes an executable test rather than a manual check. This is added to
  `tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py` in place of the stale witness line.
- A fixture-shape test in `tests/unit/test_plan_review_evals.py` pins that EVERY dataset case in
  `plan-review-container.eval.yaml` carries a non-empty `children` list whose entries each have
  `ticket_id`/`title`/`description` — so a future case added without a payload fails CI instead
  of silently dropping out of the corpus (which is exactly how this bug went unnoticed).
- No live model call is needed: `_runnable` / `eligible_cases` / spec loading are all offline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every dataset case in `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-container.eval.yaml` carries a
      non-empty `children:` list whose entries each have `ticket_id`, `title` and `description`;
      pinned by a new test in `tests/unit/test_plan_review_evals.py` that fails if any case lacks
      one.
- [x] `provider_parity.eligible_cases()` picks the container cases up with NO change to
      `src/rebar/llm/evals/provider_parity.py` or `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py`; verified
      by `git diff --stat` showing neither file modified, and by a test asserting
      `any(i.spec == "plan-review-container" for i in pp.eligible_cases())`.
- [x] The container spec contributes its first gold-block and first gold-advisory case again, so
      `select_corpus(eligible_cases())` grows by exactly 2. MEASURED on this base: eligible
      128 -> 140, corpus 26 -> 28. (The recorded "28 -> 30" totals predate unrelated changes to
      the spec set; the +2 delta is the invariant, and is what the test asserts. See the ticket
      comment recording this measurement.)
- [x] Every container item in `eligible_cases()` satisfies `item.case["children"]`; the existing
      exclusion RULE remains pinned by the `_runnable` assertions
      (`not _runnable("G3", {"input": ...})`, `_runnable("G3", {"children": [...]})`).
- [x] Each case's `expect` label is unchanged and each `children` list is entailed by that case's
      existing `input` prose (no new scenario invented); reviewable by diffing that no `input`,
      `expect`, `criterion`, or `gold_set` line changed.
- [x] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green with the worktree venv on PATH.
baseline.summary: container eval fixtures lack the children payload run_case needs

## Why

The GitHub mirror is the public discovery point, yet it lacks the standard
community-health files contributors and security researchers expect. There is no
`SECURITY.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, issue templates, PR template, or
`SUPPORT.md`. Their absence reads as "not ready for outside contribution" and
leaves vulnerability reporters with no documented channel.

## What

Add GitHub-native community health files that meet contributors where they are
while preserving the Gerrit merge gate:

- `SECURITY.md` — primary reporting via **GitHub private vulnerability reporting**
  (Security tab / advisories); fallback contact `hello@navapbc.com`; a supported-
  versions note and a coordinated-disclosure statement.
- `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` — **Contributor Covenant 2.1** verbatim, enforcement
  contact `hello@navapbc.com`.
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml` + `feature_request.yml` — GitHub
  **issue forms**, plus `config.yml` with `blank_issues_enabled: false` and
  contact links to `CONTRIBUTING.md` (the Gerrit flow) and `docs/`.
- `.github/pull_request_template.md` — a **redirect** template stating GitHub PRs
  are not merged here and pointing to the Gerrit review flow in `CONTRIBUTING.md`
  (NOT an auto-mirror bot).
- `SUPPORT.md` — where to get help (issues for bugs/features; docs links; code
  contributions go through Gerrit).

## Scope

Docs/meta files only. No code changes. The redirect PR template is the
deliberate substitute for the out-of-scope PR->Gerrit mirror bot. `hello@navapbc.com`
is used per maintainer decision; add a code comment noting it should be confirmed
to route before the first public release.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `SECURITY.md` exists with GitHub private vuln reporting as the primary
  channel, `hello@navapbc.com` fallback, supported-versions + disclosure policy.
- [ ] `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` is Contributor Covenant 2.1 with the enforcement
  contact filled in.
- [ ] `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` has bug + feature issue forms and a `config.yml`
  that disables blank issues and links to CONTRIBUTING/docs.
- [ ] `.github/pull_request_template.md` redirects contributors to the Gerrit flow.
- [ ] `SUPPORT.md` exists and links docs + CONTRIBUTING.
- [ ] GitHub's community-standards checklist shows these files detected.
baseline.summary: Add GitHub community health files (SECURITY, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, issue/PR templates, SUPPORT)

baseline.description:
## Reproduction Steps

1. On origin/main with `[identity] require_authenticated = true` (Gerrit change 759 / commit 8bb261c19), push any commit.
2. The `verify-identity` merge-gate (`.github/workflows/verify-identity.yaml`, post-merge on the GitHub mirror) runs `rebar verify-identity` over the whole store.
3. Observe: `verify-identity: FAIL — 182 enforced in-scope event(s) are not verified` — every push to main goes red.

**Expected:** with write-signing rolled out, the whole store verifies clean under enforcement. **Actual:** 182 enforced events fail: 2 unsigned `COMPLETION_VERDICT` sidecars + 180 `key_not_valid_at_era`.

## Root cause (both experimentally confirmed)

- **Source 1 — reducer-ignored sidecars are wrongly in the gate's scope.** `COMPLETION_VERDICT` (and siblings `REVIEW_RESULT`/`TICKET_DIGEST`/`ENQUEUE_ENRICH`) are NOT in `reducer.KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES` (non-state-bearing observability), yet `verify_authorship._event_from_file` classifies them. Emitted best-effort-unsigned when no signing key resolves, they become enforced failures. This is a mechanism-2 artifact (completion verification) whose store event fell into mechanism-1 (identity write-signing) scope.
- **Source 2 — compaction persists `commit_sha: null`.** `compact._build_authorship_ledger` records `null` when `resolve_event_commit` returns None at fold time and retires the raw file; the gate can't re-resolve the null, fail-closes it to ENFORCED, and mis-classifies validly-signed, era-valid events as `key_not_valid_at_era` (`verify_authorship.py` :206-220,:249-270).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `verify_authorship._event_from_file` skips events whose `event_type` is not in `reducer.KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES` (reducer-ignored sidecars), proven by a test where a `COMPLETION_VERDICT` on a work ticket is NOT an enforced failure while a KNOWN unsigned `STATUS`/`CREATE` still IS. (`src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py`)
- [ ] The gate re-resolves a LEDGER entry whose recorded `commit_sha` is null via `authorship.resolve_position_commit(position, tracker)` before the era/enforcement decision, proven by a test that a null-commit, era-valid signed ledger entry classifies `verified` not `key_not_valid_at_era`. (`src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py`)
- [ ] `compact._build_authorship_ledger` never persists `commit_sha: null` when the position is resolvable — it falls back to `resolve_position_commit`; proven by a monkeypatched unit test. (`src/rebar/_commands/compact.py`)
- [ ] Regression tests added under `tests/unit/` and the full suite passes; `make lint` clean.
- [ ] [operator-attested] `verify-identity` is added as a pre-merge job in the Gerrit `Verified` gate (`.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`) so the whole-store enforcement check runs BEFORE merge, not only post-merge (mitigates the prior epics' gap).

## Follow-on (separate change; NOT an acceptance criterion of this bug)

Re-enabling `identity.require_authenticated = true` on main (with a freshly pinned `enforce_since`) is the deployment step this fix ENABLES, tracked as its own change. It is deliberately not gated on this bug's closure: its safety is proven by that change's OWN pre-merge whole-store `verify-identity` gate (added here), which reports 0 enforced-not-verified before it can merge — the self-correcting whole-store measurement the previous rollout lacked.

## Context

Remediation of the incomplete identity-signing rollout (epics e68d built, dc09 rolled out). Prior epics verified via a producer-side window scan + force-closes and never ran the whole-store-under-enforcement check; this bug fixes the two escaped defect classes and hardens the process. Rollback of the premature flip landed as Gerrit change 767.
baseline.summary: verify-identity false-rejects reducer-ignored sidecars + null-commit ledger entries — blocks safe require_authenticated enforcement

# Establish a consistent, observable error-handling convention (remediation-led) + enable BLE001

## Context

A codebase-health audit (joe-janitor, 2026-06-24) found ~199 `except Exception`/`except BaseException` sites in `src/rebar` (~96 already `# noqa: BLE001`-justified, ~100 unguarded), ~104 scattered `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` diagnostics, and `logging` used in only a handful of modules with **no handler configured anywhere**. Each agent session invented its own swallow style (`pass`, silent fallback, ad-hoc stderr print), so unintended swallows hide real failures with no operator signal — a cross-session-inconsistency smell.

**This epic is remediation-led: the primary deliverable is remediated code that SETS the pattern, not a design-decision document.** The convention is established by an exemplar remediation (working code other batches copy) plus a CI lint gate, not by prose. This was decided after researching rebar's actual peers (basic-memory, the `modelcontextprotocol/servers` reference servers, mcp-atlassian) and the MCP framework itself — the chosen convention is deliberately boring and uses no novel/rarely-used elements.

## The convention (demonstrated by the exemplar, enforced by lint)

- **MCP surface:** don't catch-and-return error dicts — just `raise`; the MCP framework converts a raised
  exception into an `isError` tool result and keeps the connection alive. Use `ToolError` for intentional,
  clean client-facing messages (e.g. `ConcurrencyError`, validation).
- **CLI surface:** a base `RebarError` caught at the boundary maps to an exit code (already in place;
  `ConcurrencyError` -> exit 10).
- **Library:** named `logging.getLogger(__name__)` under the `rebar` root + a `NullHandler` in
  `__init__.py`; the CLI and MCP entrypoints each install a **stderr** `StreamHandler`.
- **Best-effort case:** inline narrow-and-log — **no shared helper** (peers don't have one; a helper would
  be novel). `try/except <type>: logger.warning(..., exc_info=True)`.
- **Terminal state = observability floor:** every broad catch must either log with `exc_info` OR carry a
  justified `# noqa: BLE001` (reason string required). Narrowing is opportunistic, with tests; fail-open /
  body-inspecting / public-API sites stay broad-but-logged.
- **Enforcement:** ruff **BLE001** (blind-except) and **T201** (print, scoped: banned in library/core/MCP,
  allowed in the CLI presentation layer) enabled in CI, gated behind a *shrinking* `per-file-ignores`
  allowlist (the existing `.github/module-size-allowlist.txt` strangler pattern).

## stdout is sacred (the load-bearing constraint)

CLI *data* `print(json.dumps(...))` on stdout is a machine contract (the reconciler `json.loads` it at `reconcile.py:472`) and MCP-over-stdio reserves stdout for JSON-RPC framing. Only **stderr diagnostics** migrate to the logger; stdout data prints stay.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The logging substrate exists (named loggers + `NullHandler` + stderr handler at both entrypoints) and
      a stdout-purity contract test guards the CLI data contract.
- [ ] An exemplar package (`llm/plan_review/`) is fully remediated to the convention and is the reference
      others copy; BLE001 + scoped T201 are enabled with a shrinking allowlist.
- [ ] The ~100 unguarded broad-except sites are remediated to the observability floor in batches (log with
      `exc_info` or justified `# noqa: BLE001`); no silent `except ...: pass` remains without justification.
- [ ] Where opportunistic narrowing surfaced a previously-hidden bug, it is fixed with a regression test;
      if no batch surfaced one, the close-out records that explicitly (so AC4 is not vacuously satisfied).
- [ ] The convention is durably documented in `CLAUDE.md` / a contributing doc (not only in the exemplar
      code + lint), so the rationale (raise-don't-catch on MCP, stdout-sacred, noqa-with-reason) survives.
- [ ] The allowlist is emptied; `make lint` + the full test suite pass; child tasks are parented here with
      file-impact set.
- [ ] One observable, lint-enforced way to do error handling across rebar's library / CLI / MCP surfaces.
- [ ] Failures that used to vanish silently are now observable on a stderr logger; `KeyboardInterrupt` /
- [ ] A future joe-janitor audit finds no unguarded blind-except cluster; new unguarded blind-excepts / stray
baseline.summary: Consistent error-handling pattern + eliminate unguarded except Exception

# The DC harness project has NO 'Epic' issue type, so the epic-parent path cannot be tested live

## Evidence

Harness run **30857265932** (main @ `b301e7513d`, i.e. WITH change 1311), `test_outbound_epic_parent_round_trips_via_the_epic_link`:

    SETUP FAILED (not a rebar defect): project RBJSXPQ offers no 'Epic' issue type
    (has ['Sub-task', 'Task'])

`collected=58`, 6 failed / 51 passed / 1 xfailed.

The cell reported SETUP FAILED distinctly rather than as an ambiguous red — that branch was written for exactly this case — so the diagnosis cost nothing. But the consequence is real.

## What this blocks

The scratch project is created from whichever template the DC image ships, and that template offers only `Sub-task` and `Task`. **No Epic issue type means no Epic Link relationship can be created**, so on this harness:

 * [rebar:39c1-2a32-b564-4b4b] **AC1 cannot be arbitrated.** Change 1311's Epic Link write is
   unexercised live — the cell cannot reach the code. This is the THIRD distinct reason that AC has
   gone unproven (first the emit/apply gates were disjoint, then the greenhopper route 404'd, now
   the fixture cannot build the fixture).
 * [rebar:9bb9-56a3-e9c0-46e9] **AC3 likewise** — the read side cannot be proven for the epic case
   either, for the same reason.

Both changes are unit-proven and neither is live-proven. Given 1276, 1288 and 1302 each shipped mutation-proven and wrong, that is exactly the gap this epic exists to close.

## Why this is a harness defect, not a product one

Nothing about rebar is implicated. `_seed_epic` correctly discovers the project's issue types rather than hardcoding `Epic` (the same discipline `_subtask_type_name` follows), and correctly reports SETUP rather than blaming the transport. The gap is that the harness provisions a project which cannot express the relationship under test.

## Candidate fixes, cheapest first — none yet verified

 1. **Create the scratch project from a Jira SOFTWARE template** rather than whatever the image
    defaults to. Epic ships with the Software templates; the Core/Business ones do not carry it.
    `conftest.py:359` already records a prior attempt at pinning a template
    (`com.pyxis.greenhopper.jira:gh-simplified-kanban-classic`), so the machinery and the prior art
    both exist — check why that pin is not in force.
 2. **Add the Epic issue type to the project's issue-type scheme** after creation, via REST.
 3. **Provision a second project** from a Software template solely for the epic cells.

Option 1 is the obvious first try given the existing comment, but the template list an image offers is version-specific and must be READ from the instance, not assumed — the same lesson `_seed_epic` already encodes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] the harness project (or a project the epic cells use) offers an `Epic` issue type, discovered
      from the instance rather than assumed
- [x] `test_outbound_epic_parent_round_trips_via_the_epic_link` EXECUTES — it reaches its assertions
      instead of reporting SETUP FAILED — on a harness run, with the run id recorded
- [x] whichever template or scheme change is made is discovered/verified at runtime, so a future DC
      image that ships a different template set fails loudly rather than silently reverting to a
      project without Epic
- [x] the canary line still shows `skipped` at its expected baseline — this must not be "fixed" by
      skipping the cell
baseline.summary: DC harness project has no Epic issue type, so the epic-parent path cannot be tested live

## Why

The compaction fold claims an all-or-none contract (invariant I1): snapshot written first, sources renamed to `*.retired`, and on failure every completed rename reversed and the snapshot removed. But in `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` (~lines 235-247) the rollback path only *logs* a failed reverse-rename and continues, then unconditionally removes the snapshot and returns failure. Because normal replay excludes `*.retired` (`src/rebar/reducer/_cache.py`), a source that failed to restore becomes invisible with no snapshot left to carry its folded effect — silent, undetectable data loss that violates the stated contract.

## What

Chosen approach (committed — not "retain OR sentinel"): **retain the snapshot.** The snapshot already carries the folded effect of every source, so keeping it is the minimal change and needs no new on-disk artifact. On any reverse-rename failure during rollback, skip the `os.remove(snapshot)` step, emit an explicit `rollback incomplete; run fsck` diagnostic, and return failure.

Key realization from the fsck code: with the snapshot retained, the residual mixed state is **already detectable and repairable by existing fsck** — no new issue kind is needed:
- A source that WAS reversed back to an active `.json` is a UUID in the snapshot's
  `source_event_uuids` whose active file "still exists" → the existing
  `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT` check (`src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:302`) fires, and it is
  already in the `--repair-snapshots` rebuild trigger (`fsck.py:191`).
- A source that failed to reverse stays `*.retired` and folded in the snapshot — i.e. the
  normal healthy compacted state; no false positive (crucially, this means the detection
  does NOT fire on healthy fully-compacted tickets).
So this story's only production change is: **do not delete the snapshot** in the rollback-failure branch (plus the diagnostic). The existing `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT` + `--repair-snapshots` path already reconciles the mixed state (confirmed against `fsck.py`), so **no fsck code change is expected**.

Two correctness facts, confirmed against the code (correcting earlier drafts):
- **Repair mechanism is REBUILD, not retire-only.** `--repair-snapshots` routes a
  `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT` finding to `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log`
  (`src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:193-195`, `compact.py:289`), which WRITES A NEW SNAPSHOT
  from the full ordered log and retires the live raws. So the repair test must assert a
  new `*-SNAPSHOT.json` IS written and the formerly-active source IS renamed to
  `*.retired`, and a follow-up `fsck` exits 0 — NOT "no new snapshot written."
- **Reads are already safe in the mixed window (no double-count).** The reversed-to-active
  source keeps its ORIGINAL (old) filename, so it sorts BEFORE the retained snapshot;
  normal replay short-circuits on the snapshot and skips all pre-snapshot events
  (`src/rebar/reducer/_api.py`, `_cache.py:110-113` positional skip), so the folded event
  is not re-applied. The mixed state is therefore read-correct BEFORE repair; the
  `rollback incomplete` diagnostic tells the operator to run `fsck --repair-snapshots` to
  NORMALIZE the hygiene inconsistency (`SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT`), not because reads are
  wrong.
- **Durability of the decision.** Add an architectural comment at the retained-snapshot
  branch in `compact.py` explaining WHY the snapshot is intentionally not removed (so a
  future refactor doesn't "fix" it back into the data-loss hazard), and note the
  compact→fsck recovery contract in the concurrency docs.

- Add fault-injection tests (currently the negative suite injects only at
  `compact.lock.acquire` and `compact._git`, never in the rename loop).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` (rollback-failure branch: retain snapshot + diagnostic)
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py` (verify the existing `_check_snapshot`/`_scan` +
  `--repair-snapshots` rebuild covers the mixed state; extend only if a gap is found)
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_negative.py` (new fault-injection tests)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Forward-rename fault test: inject `OSError` on the 2nd/3rd forward `os.rename`;
      assert nonzero exit, no active snapshot, every original filename restored, no
      stray `*.retired`, reduced state deep-equal to pre-compaction, clean `fsck`, and
      an idempotent re-compaction.
- [ ] Reverse-rename fault test: inject a forward failure AND a reverse-rename failure
      (so at least one source is reversed-to-active and at least one stays `*.retired`);
      assert the snapshot is NOT deleted, a recoverable diagnostic is emitted, and no
      source data is lost.
- [ ] In the mixed state BEFORE repair, a read is correct: the reducer's event-UUID set +
      payloads deep-equal the pre-compaction reduced state (the snapshot's positional skip
      excludes the reversed-to-active source; no double-count). The `rollback incomplete`
      diagnostic directs the operator to run `fsck --repair-snapshots`.
- [ ] `fsck` (no flag) reports `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT` for the reversed-to-active
      source in that mixed state (existing detection), and does NOT flag a healthy
      fully-compacted ticket.
- [ ] `fsck --repair-snapshots` reconciles by REBUILDING via
      `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log`: assert a NEW `*-SNAPSHOT.json` is written, the
      formerly-active source is renamed to `*.retired`, a follow-up `fsck` exits 0, and
      the reduced state is unchanged (deep-equal to pre-repair).
- [ ] An architectural comment in `compact.py` documents why the snapshot is retained on
      rollback failure, and the compact→fsck recovery contract is noted in
      `docs/concurrency.md`.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: Fix compaction rollback-failure atomicity hazard + rename fault-injection tests

## Why
Epic AC1 requires a **write-time guard that rejects private-key material in an identity event**. The delivered `identity` create path (ddbe / change 558) passes `keys` straight onto the CREATE event with no check, so a user could accidentally commit an SSH PRIVATE key into the always-readable, replicated tickets store — a real (if narrow) footgun. The epic completion-verifier flagged this as unmet. (Remediation of epic gnu-whale-ichor to full AC coverage; see session_log fanatical-gentling-bushbaby.)

## What
Add a shared guard `reject_private_key_material(values: list[str])` in `src/rebar/_commands/identity.py` that raises `CommandError` if any value contains a private-key PEM/OpenSSH header — matching (case-insensitive) any of: `-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----`, `-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----`, `-----BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY-----`, `-----BEGIN DSA PRIVATE KEY-----`, `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----`, `-----BEGIN ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY-----` (i.e. the generic `BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY` family). Call it:
- in `create_identity_core` on the `keys` list BEFORE `create_core` appends the CREATE
  event (no event written on rejection);
- in `add_identity_key` on the `public_key` BEFORE the KEY_ADD event is appended.
A legitimate authorized-keys public line (`ssh-ed25519 AAAA…`) passes unchanged.

## Scope
In: the `reject_private_key_material` guard + its two call sites (identity CREATE keys[] and KEY_ADD public_key). Out: any other behavior. The guard function lives in the ddbe commit (558); the `add_identity_key` call site lives in the e165 commit (563) — both are amended (the guard fn is defined in 558, so 563 can call it).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `create_identity(name, email, keys=[<a string containing "BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE
  KEY">])` raises (CommandError/RebarError) and appends NO event (store unchanged); a test
  asserts the raise and that no identity was created.
- [ ] `add_identity_key(identity, <a private-key string>)` raises and appends no KEY_ADD
  event (test).
- [ ] A normal authorized-keys public line (`ssh-ed25519 AAAA…`) is accepted by both
  `create_identity(keys=[…])` and `add_identity_key` (test).
- [ ] The guard matches the common private-key header family case-insensitively
  (parametrized test over the RSA/EC/DSA/OPENSSH/PKCS8/ENCRYPTED headers).

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/_commands/identity.py` (reject_private_key_material guard + create/key-add call sites)
baseline.summary: identity: reject private-key material at the identity write-gate (epic AC1)

## The gap AS FILED — refuted before implementing

`scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` was reported to match wrapper calls only by bare callable name, so that `core._git("commit", ...)` — an attribute on a module object passed in as a parameter — would escape it. **That is not the case.** `_ScopeLinter._wrapper_name` has carried an `ast.Attribute` branch (`func.attr in WRAPPER_NAMES`) alongside the `ast.Name` branch since the gate's first commit, 6739ea54fa ("d37e: lint gates raw git writes to seams"), confirmed by `git log -S'isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr in WRAPPER_NAMES'`.

A synthetic probe (`/tmp/rebar-4073-9d4f-c644-44a9/probe`, `--report`) shows `core._git(root, ["commit", ...])`, `mod.run_git(root, ["add", "-A"])`, `core._git(root, *argv)`, `core.sub._git(...)` and `self._git(...)` ALL firing, `check` exiting 1, and `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` silencing the attribute form exactly as it silences the bare form. Full evidence is in the ticket comment.

`_ref_lock_push.py` has no hits for a different reason: its one wrapper call (`push_lease_cas`, line 116) passes `push`, which is not in `MUTATION_VERBS` (`{add, commit, rm, mv, reset, update-ref, checkout, clean}`). The gate saw the call and resolved its argv — it correctly declined to fire. `src/rebar/_store/push_recovery.py` does not exist yet anywhere in the tree.

## What is actually wrong

The BEHAVIOUR is right; the EVIDENCE for it is missing. All 8 R2 tests in `tests/unit/test_raw_git_write_lint.py` use the bare-name form (`test_wrapper_literal_mutation_verb_fires` through `test_sibling_wrapper_names_not_in_name_set`); not one exercises an attribute receiver, and the module docstring says only "BY NAME". Untested, undocumented coverage is coverage that reads as absent — which is how this bug came to be filed. Left alone it will be re-filed, and worse, a future refactor of `_wrapper_name` can delete the branch with every test still green.

## Change

Two files, no detection-logic change (a detection change would be wrong — the detection is correct):

1. `tests/unit/test_raw_git_write_lint.py` — a new R2 sub-section pinning the attribute form:
   - `test_wrapper_attribute_form_mutation_verb_fires` — `core._git(...)` / `core.run_git(...)`
     with a literal mutation verb each fire `wrapper-git-mutation`.
   - `test_wrapper_attribute_receiver_shape_does_not_matter` — `self._git(...)`, a nested
     receiver `core.inner._git(...)`, and an imported-module receiver `_ref_lock._git(...)` all
     fire, proving the match is on the attribute and not on any particular receiver shape.
   - `test_wrapper_attribute_form_opaque_argv_fires_and_marker_silences` — `core._git(root,
     *args)` fires the fail-closed `unresolvable-argv-wrapper`, and the SAME line with
     `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` is clean. This is the ACs' "existing exemption mechanics must keep
     working" requirement, on the attribute form.
   - `test_attribute_form_push_lease_cas_shape_does_not_fire` — the real `push_lease_cas` argv
     shape plus an attribute-form read (`rev-parse`) stay clean, pinning the disposition so the
     absence of a marker on `_ref_lock_push.py` reads as resolved rather than as a blind spot.
2. `scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` — the module docstring's R2 bullet gains the explicit
   statement that the name comes from the CALLABLE, so an attribute call is matched by its
   attribute whatever the receiver, and names the late-binding `core`-passing idiom as the
   reason that matters. Docstring only; `_wrapper_name`, `MUTATION_VERBS`, `WRAPPER_NAMES`,
   `_check_wrapper_call` and every marker path are untouched.

## Deliberately NOT done

Adding `push` to `MUTATION_VERBS` would make `_ref_lock_push.py` fire. That is a real but DIFFERENT question — what "mutation" means for a gate whose stated policy is local store writes (`git add/commit/rm`) — and it would flood every legitimate `git_adapter` and sync push site. Recorded in the ticket comment rather than smuggled in under a detection-blind-spot premise.

## Verification

- Mutation check (already run): deleting the two-line `ast.Attribute` branch from
  `_wrapper_name` turns exactly the three new detection tests RED (31 passed, 3 failed);
  restoring it returns 34 passed. The new tests therefore pin the branch rather than merely
  co-exist with it.
- Whole-repo re-run of the gate after the change: `python scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py`
  exits 0 and `--report` yields the same 123-hit inventory as before, so no new hits need
  triage and no legitimate site needs a new marker (the change adds no detection).
- Full local gate set before push: every `scripts/check_*.py`, the generators' no-diff check,
  `make lint`, `make typecheck`, the CI pytest selection
  (`-m "not integration and not external" -n 3 --dist worksteal --timeout=300`), and
  `tests/integration` explicitly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1 — Attribute-form calls whose attribute is in `WRAPPER_NAMES` resolve: confirmed
      already true, with the reason and the probe evidence recorded on the ticket, and the
      coverage stated in the gate's own module docstring so it is no longer implicit.
- [x] AC2 — `_ref_lock_push.py` is explicitly dispositioned (seen, argv resolved, correctly
      not fired because `push` is not a mutation verb; no marker warranted) and the
      `push_recovery.py` half is recorded as moot (the file does not exist).
- [x] AC3 — Four tests in `tests/unit/test_raw_git_write_lint.py` pin attribute-form detection,
      receiver-shape independence, fail-closed opaque forwarding, and marker sanctioning; three
      of them are shown to fail when the `ast.Attribute` branch is removed.
baseline.summary: check_raw_git_writes misses attribute-form git wrapper calls

## Why

Epic `850f` needs a place for a T2 semantic backend to plug in and be reported, without touching the
deterministic T1 lane or any consumer. Today `TIER_T2` exists in the closed tier vocabulary but is
never emitted, and member/dotted references abstain inline in `resolve.refute_absence`. This story
adds the opt-in, default-off seam and wiring; S3 adds the actual pyright backend behind it. Shipping
the seam separately keeps the seam change regression-safe and independently reviewable.

## What

- New module `src/rebar/grounding/semantic.py` (stdlib-only, import-clean) exposing:
  - `T2_BACKENDS: tuple[str, ...] = ()` initially — the closed set of selectable backend names. (S3
    adds `"pyright"`.) An unknown/empty selection fails open to disabled.
  - `refute_semantic(reference, *, repo_root, config, timeout=None, cache=None) -> dict | None` —
    returns a normalized `TIER_T2` evidence record (`refuted`/`abstain`) or `None` meaning "T2 declined
    to run; keep the caller's T1 record". With no registered backend it returns `None` (default-off).
    `cache` is a **caller-owned** optional mapping (mirrors T1's `index` param) for reusing one
    backend invocation across many references in a single review — no module-global mutable state, so
    no cross-thread concern.
  - `available_backends() -> list[dict]` — `[{name, available, version}]` for each name in
    `T2_BACKENDS`, each probed fail-open (empty while `T2_BACKENDS` is empty).
- Extend `GroundingConfig` + `load_config` in `resolve.py` with three `.rebar/grounding.toml`
  `[grounding]` keys (all default-off / safe):
  - `t2_enabled: bool = False`, `t2_backend: str | None = None`, `t2_timeout_seconds: float = 30.0`.
    Invalid types/values fail open to the default (never a raise), consistent with the existing loader.
- Wire escalation in `oracle.refute_absence` (the single consumer entry): after the T1/deps lane
  returns, if the record is an `abstain` on a `member`/dotted reference or a not-found bare
  `symbol`/`import`, call `semantic.refute_semantic(...)`; a returned `refuted@T2` replaces the T1
  abstain, otherwise the T1 record is returned unchanged. `resolve.refute_absence` is **not** modified
  (T2 stays out of the deterministic T1 lane).
- Extend `oracle._backend_availability()` to append `*semantic.available_backends()` so
  `grounding_info` reports T2 backends.

## Scope

In scope: `semantic.py`, the config keys, the `oracle` escalation + availability wiring, and unit
tests. Out of scope: the pyright backend itself and its extra/docs (S3). While `T2_BACKENDS` is empty
the seam is fully inert.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/rebar/grounding/semantic.py` exists exposing `refute_semantic`, `available_backends`, and
      `T2_BACKENDS`.
- [ ] `semantic.py` is stdlib-only: `tests/unit/grounding/test_non_adoption.py` still passes
      (the import-purity guarantee holds).
- [ ] `GroundingConfig`/`load_config` expose `t2_enabled` (bool, default False), `t2_backend`
      (str|None, default None), and `t2_timeout_seconds` (float, default 30.0).
- [ ] Each new config key fails open to its default on malformed input (a test feeds a malformed
      `.rebar/grounding.toml` and asserts the defaults, with no raise).
- [ ] `oracle.refute_absence` escalates member/dotted and not-found-symbol abstains to
      `refute_semantic`.
- [ ] `oracle.refute_absence` returns `refute_semantic`'s `refuted@T2` when produced, otherwise the
      unchanged T1 record.
- [ ] `resolve.refute_absence` is unmodified (verified by diff review — the T1 lane stays out of T2).
- [ ] `oracle._backend_availability()` includes the T2 backends reported by `available_backends()`.
- [ ] `grounding_info()` output validates against `grounding_info.schema.json` after the change.
- [ ] Default-off regression: a test in `tests/unit/grounding/` asserts that with `t2_enabled=False`
      (empty `T2_BACKENDS`) `oracle.refute_absence` returns the pre-change evidence for a member/dotted
      reference (still `abstain` at `TIER_T1`).
- [ ] A seam-dispatch test using an in-test fake backend (monkeypatched into `T2_BACKENDS` +
      `refute_semantic`) shows a `refuted@T2` record replaces the T1 abstain.
- [ ] That `refuted@T2` record validates against `grounding.schema.json`.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/grounding/` exits 0.
- [ ] `make lint` exits 0.
baseline.summary: T2 grounding S2: pluggable semantic seam (refute_semantic + config + oracle escalation, default-off)

# WS6 — Rewire the Gerrit review-bot to the four-pass code review

## Why
Epic `d251` (AWS Gerrit + rebar MCP) **shipped and merged** — including S4b's complete review-bot:
`src/rebar/review_bot/` (receiver `app.py`, `voter.py`, `gerrit_client.py`, `dedup.py`,
`reconcile.py`) plus the **verdict→label seam `adapter.code_review_decision(diff_text, repo_root,
ref) → {decision, message, findings}`**. That seam is currently implemented over the OLD
single-pass `rebar.llm.review_code(...)` + a blocking-severity heuristic — a deliberate "proven
pipe" placeholder. `adapter.py`'s own docstring says: *"b744-WS6 will REIMPLEMENT this same
signature over `gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict` — drop-in, with no caller change."*

WS6 is exactly that swap: make Gerrit's `LLM-Review` vote driven by **our new four-pass code
review** (the deterministic Pass-3 blocker), not the single-pass demo.

## Realignment (2026-06-30) — supersedes the earlier standalone-package plan
The pre-merge WS6 plan (a NEW `src/rebar/gerrit/` voter package + REST client + patchset handler)
is **retired as redundant**: d251 already ships all of that in `src/rebar/review_bot/`. WS6 must
NOT build a parallel package — it CONSUMES the shipped receiver and swaps only the decision engine
behind the existing seam. The live dogfood is split out to WS6-b (`0da5`); the GitHub cutover to
WS7.

## What
- **Rewrite `src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py`'s `code_review_decision`** over
  `gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict` (the typed `PASS`/`BLOCK`/`INDETERMINATE` verdict):
  - keep the signature + return shape (`{decision, message, findings}`, plus an additive
    `coverage_gap` flag) so `voter.py` is unchanged;
  - map the verdict fail-closed (below); the four-pass gate's own Pass-3 thresholds
    (`criteria_routing.json`) decide PASS vs BLOCK, so the adapter no longer applies the
    `blocking_severities` severity heuristic (it becomes vestigial for this path);
  - review the receiver's cloned working tree by passing `repo_root` (the security detectors scan
    the changed files there) + the fetched `diff_text`.
- **Add an `enabled: bool | None = None` override to `produce_code_review_verdict`** so the adapter
  can pass `enabled=True` (force-enable): the code-review gate is OFF by default
  (`verify.enable_code_review`), but voter activation is itself the authoritative gate, so the
  per-repo flag would otherwise leave every change with the inert disabled verdict. (ADR 0015.)
- **Update `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py`** adapter tests to drive the four-pass verdict (mock
  `produce_code_review_verdict`) instead of `review_code`.
- **ADR 0015** records the seam reimplementation + the force-enable rationale + the fail-closed
  vote mapping + the coverage-gap message distinction.

## Vote mapping (fail-closed; the gate's Pass-3 owns PASS/BLOCK)
`produce_code_review_verdict` emits three verdicts (PASS/BLOCK/INDETERMINATE) plus an inert
disabled verdict. The adapter collapses them to the receiver's PASS/BLOCK (the voter then casts
`llm_review_max_value` / `llm_review_block_value` from `ReceiverConfig`):

| verdict / state | adapter decision | note |
|---|---|---|
| PASS + full coverage | PASS | advisory findings are surfaced in the message, non-blocking |
| BLOCK (blocking findings) | BLOCK | real finding (`coverage_gap=False`) |
| INDETERMINATE (LLM outage) | BLOCK | fail-closed coverage-gap |
| PASS but `coverage.enabled==false` (inert) | BLOCK | fail-closed coverage-gap (`gate-disabled`) — defense-in-depth |
| fail-closed security-scanner abstain | BLOCK | fail-closed coverage-gap (`scanner`) |
| ANY exception / bad shape | BLOCK | fail-closed coverage-gap (`review-error`) |

## Distinct coverage-gap message (infra vs code)
The vote comment (`ReviewInput.message`, posted by the receiver's `post_vote`) begins with a
machine-parseable tag so an INFRA `-1` is unmistakable from a real-finding `-1`:
`[LLM-Review: PASS]`, `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]`, and
`[LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (<gate-disabled|llm-unavailable|scanner|review-error>)]`. The
`coverage_gap` sub-reason is derived deterministically from `verdict.coverage`
(`enabled==false` → gate-disabled; `llm_unavailable` → llm-unavailable; a `security_detectors`
note with `reason=='fail-closed-abstain'` → scanner). A real secret MATCH
(`reason=='detector-finding'`) is a finding, NOT a coverage gap.

## Scope
- IN: the `adapter.py` reimplementation, the `produce_code_review_verdict` `enabled` override, the
  updated `test_review_bot.py` adapter tests, ADR 0015.
- OUT: the receiver/voter/gerrit_client/reconciler (d251 shipped them — unchanged); the live
  end-to-end dogfood (WS6-b, gated on the deployed env); the GitHub cutover (WS7).

## Dependencies
- CONSUMES d251's shipped `review_bot` package + the provisioned `LLM-Review` label / value
  mapping (`ReceiverConfig`). depends_on WS4 (98ff, closed) for `produce_code_review_verdict`.
- No live env needed: the adapter is fully verifiable offline (mock the verdict; the receiver's
  own tests already stub Gerrit).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `review_bot/adapter.py`'s `code_review_decision` is reimplemented over `produce_code_review_verdict` with `enabled=True`; the signature + `{decision, message, findings}` return shape are unchanged (the voter is not touched).
- [ ] Vote mapping is exhaustive + fail-closed over PASS / BLOCK / INDETERMINATE / inert-disabled / scanner-abstain / exception; a test asserts each → the correct decision, and that an inert-disabled verdict never yields PASS.
- [ ] `produce_code_review_verdict` gains an `enabled: bool | None = None` override (default None = read config); a test asserts `enabled=True` forces the gate to run even when `verify.enable_code_review=false`.
- [ ] The vote message distinguishes a coverage-gap `-1` (sub-reason gate-disabled / llm-unavailable / scanner / review-error) from a real-finding `-1`, via the documented first-line tag; a test asserts the PASS tag, the finding tag, and each coverage-gap sub-reason.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py` adapter tests are updated to the four-pass verdict (mock `produce_code_review_verdict`); the full `pytest -k review_bot` suite passes; ruff + mypy clean.
- [ ] ADR 0015 records the seam reimplementation, the force-enable rationale, the fail-closed vote mapping, and the coverage-gap message vocabulary.
baseline.summary: WS6: Rewire the Gerrit review-bot to the four-pass code review

baseline.description:
## Silent data loss in the store under concurrent write + in-flight review

**Evidence is SECONDHAND** — reported by the session working [rebar:aec1-76e7-bb95-4c86], not reproduced by the filing session. Filed anyway because it is silent DATA LOSS in the ticket store, which is the system of record for every agent.

### What was observed

1. A `rebar edit --description` succeeded and was **verified by read-back at 14,997 chars**.
2. A subsequent `rebar show` returned **10,582 chars** — an OLDER revision. Nothing reported an
   error; no conflict, no `ConcurrencyError`, no exit 10.
3. The agent's next read-modify-write then grafted new edits onto that stale text, **corrupting an
   acceptance criterion** by splicing two unrelated fragments:

       - [ ] a gate run persists `finish_reason` (recorded for triage, deliberately not rendered) (the windowed distinct-ratio that
             rebar ticket 70bc establishes is computable from the record)

4. Only a further read-back caught it. The agent rebuilt from a saved good revision and verified
   the restore (15,666 chars, all markers present).

### The reporter's hypothesis (unproven)

The ticket was being edited **while its own `rebar review-plan` was running**, and a review emits its own `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar events (`sidecar_emitted: true`). Store reconvergence between the two writers is the suspected cause. Corroborating signal: a later write to the same ticket with **no review in flight** stayed intact.

### Why this is worth a ticket rather than a note

* **Optimistic concurrency did not fire.** The documented protection is a `ConcurrencyError`/exit 10
  on a conflicting write. Here the write reported success, verified on read-back, and was then
  silently rolled back — which is the one failure mode the concurrency design is supposed to make
  impossible.
* **Read-back verification is not sufficient**, which invalidates the standard mitigation every
  agent is told to use. The read-back PASSED and the data was still lost afterwards.
* The practical rule that emerged ("never write to a ticket while its own review is running") is an
  undocumented landmine, and it conflicts with the normal remediate-then-review loop the plan-review
  gate asks authors to perform.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the interaction is REPRODUCED deterministically (concurrent `rebar edit` + an in-flight
      review emitting sidecar events on the same ticket), or the hypothesis is falsified and the
      real trigger identified — the current evidence is a single secondhand observation
- [ ] it is established why optimistic concurrency did not reject the losing write; a silent
      last-writer-wins rollback on a ticket description is either a bug in the conflict detection
      or an undocumented property of sidecar reconvergence
- [ ] a write that will be discarded FAILS LOUDLY (`ConcurrencyError`/exit 10) rather than
      reporting success and reverting afterwards
- [ ] a regression test drives the concurrent-writer path and asserts the losing write is rejected,
      not silently dropped
- [ ] if the 'do not edit during a review' constraint is genuine and must stand, it is DOCUMENTED
      where authors will hit it (the plan-review gate docs describe exactly the revise-then-review
      loop that triggers it)

## Testing

    pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q
baseline.summary: A verified ticket description write was SILENTLY REVERTED to an older revision while that ticket's own plan-review was in flight

## Summary

The `langfuse tracing round-trip (ephemeral self-hosted)` job of the `external-integration` workflow has been broken since the d6d1 cutover (2026-06-22) and tests behavior that no longer exists. Two independent breakages:

1. **Readiness probe imports an uninstalled SDK.** `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml:128`
   runs `from langfuse import get_client; assert get_client().auth_check()`, but the `langfuse`
   Python SDK was dropped from `[agents]` in c282b2950. `pip install -e '.[dev]'` no longer
   installs it, so all 24 readiness iterations raise `ModuleNotFoundError` — hidden by
   `2>/dev/null`, masquerading as "Langfuse project did not initialize in time".

2. **Test asserts a removed trace_id round-trip.** `tests/external/test_llm_trace.py:100` asserts
   `result["trace_id"]` is truthy and fetches `GET /api/public/traces/{id}`. The runner now
   hardcodes `trace_id=None` (src/rebar/llm/runner.py:391); the SDK trace-id capture was deleted
   in 2e9bd4205 when tracing became write-only OTLP export (src/rebar/llm/tracing.py). Also the
   job never installs `[tracing]`, so `setup_tracing` no-ops and no spans are exported at all.

## Decision (user, 2026-07-09)

Rewrite the job to validate CURRENT behavior (write-only OTLP span export to Langfuse), not the removed SDK trace_id round-trip.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Trigger the `external-integration` workflow (langfuse-trace job).
2. Observe "Wait for Langfuse to be ready" time out after 120s ("project did not initialize in time").

Expected: readiness passes; a review run's OTLP spans land in Langfuse and the test confirms it. Actual: readiness fails on a hidden ModuleNotFoundError; the test would fail on the None trace_id anyway.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Readiness probe no longer imports the langfuse SDK; uses a REST check (e.g. `curl -fsS -u pk:sk .../api/public/projects`) and does not mask stderr.
- [ ] The langfuse-trace job installs the `[tracing]` extra so OTLP export actually fires.
- [ ] `tests/external/test_llm_trace.py` asserts OTLP spans for a review run are ingested by Langfuse (fetched via REST), with no reliance on a runner-surfaced `trace_id`.
- [ ] Verified end-to-end: the rewritten test passes against the docker-compose.langfuse.yml stack with a real review call, and the external-integration GitHub Action's langfuse-trace job runs successfully.
baseline.summary: langfuse-trace job tests removed behavior + readiness probe imports uninstalled SDK

baseline.description:
## Context

A documentation audit (final unified report, evaluated at commit `2272d68ca` = `origin/main`) surfaced front-door defects and factual drift in rebar's docs. Every finding was re-validated against `origin/main` before filing this epic; one audit finding (that `docs/config.md` mis-describes the config-file format) was **REFUTED** — the loader matches the doc exactly — and is deliberately excluded.

Our audiences are human clients, LLM clients, human contributors, and LLM contributors. The two highest-leverage moves are (a) fixing the immediate defects that break onboarding/trust, and (b) adding cheap **drift-proofing** so the same class of staleness cannot silently return — the true lever on maintenance burden.

### Validated findings this epic remediates
- P0: README `session-log` syntax is invalid (missing subcommand); README quickstart
  is not actually one ticket end-to-end (hard-coded `reel-lot-tea`, separate Python
  ticket, MCP shows config only).
- P1: dependency count + `mcp` floor wrong in README and `docs/config.md` (truth: 3
  base deps, `mcp>=1.9`); `docs/output-schemas.md` points at a moved source path and
  describes a removed bash shell-out; stale bash-engine language in CI comments +
  `leaf.py`.
- P2: `docs/README.md` index is incomplete (4 unlinked living docs) and mixes living
  references with historical evidence.

### Reuse note (avoids duplicate work)
- `scripts/probe-rebar.sh` already implements the full install→…→close golden path;
  it just is not wired into CI.
- `scripts/gen_env_registry.py` + its CI drift gate is a proven **generator +
  drift-gate** pattern to template for new generated references.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All child tickets are closed (each with green CI / `Verified +1`).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass on the assembled stack. This
      aggregate integration check is owned at the EPIC level (not any single child):
      the executor runs it on the full assembled stack before landing, as the
      parent-level close gate.
- [ ] The refuted config-format finding is NOT acted on (no spurious change).
- [ ] Lower-value inventory work (Python-API / config-key) is captured as an `idea`,
      not shipped speculatively.
- [ ] The golden-path CI gate runs the **literal commands extracted from the README quickstart fenced block** (not merely an independent probe with its own syntax), so a wrong command *printed* in the README — e.g. the `session-log` missing its `append` verb — fails the build. This is the mechanism that makes command *text* rot (not just executability) a hard CI failure, and doubles as the end-to-end new-user onboarding validation (CI follows the README exactly as a cold reader would).
- [ ] Docs-index completeness/drift fails the build (docs-index CI gate `f088`): every
      living/normative `docs/*.md` is linked from the index, and the relative links
      the remediation touches (index entries + inbound links to docs relocated under
      `docs/archive/` by `9d81`) resolve. Scope is bounded to index completeness and
      the links this epic manages — it is the enforcement arm of the P2 finding, not a
      general site-wide linter.
- [ ] Generated CLI + MCP references drift-gate against their live registries.

### Drift-proofing mechanism — how command *text* rot fails the build (closes G6/F4)
The audit gap is that testing command *executability* (running `probe-rebar.sh`, which uses its own internally-correct syntax) does NOT catch a wrong command *printed in the README*. So the golden-path gate (ticket `contained-dendritic-angora`/0435) is scoped to **extract the fenced command block(s) from the README quickstart and execute those exact lines** in a throwaway repo. A stale/invalid README command then exits non-zero and fails CI. This is both the text-accuracy drift guard (G6) and the concrete end-to-end onboarding validation (F4): a new user copy-pasting the README is exactly what CI now does.

### Shared-file edit ordering (closes P5)
Several children edit `README.md` (session-log fix `a41f`, quickstart repair `b55f`, dep-count `319a`, catalog-trim `b5a4`). These are **serialized through the review stack in dependency order** — each change is built on the prior one (a41f → b55f → 319a → … → b5a4), so there is no concurrent same-file edit; `b5a4` additionally `depends_on` the generated-reference tickets (`e866`, `235a`) it links to. The stack order IS the observable ordering proxy: a later change rebases on the earlier landed change, never races it.

The SAME single-linear-stack serialization covers the other shared files: `.github/workflows/test.yml` (edited by `0435`, `e205`, `e866`, `235a`, `f088`) and `docs/README.md` (edited by `9d81`, `6755`) are each modified by exactly one change at a time in stack order — every change is built on the prior landed one, so there is never a concurrent same-file edit to reconcile. Execution is a single agent driving one relation-chain, so the dependency order and the stack order are the same total order.
- [ ] Every validated defect above is corrected against `origin/main`.
- [ ] New CI gates make quickstart-command rot and docs-index drift fail the build
- [ ] The docs index is complete and clearly separates living reference from historical
- [ ] Volatile command/tool surfaces move toward generated references so they cannot go
baseline.summary: Documentation remediation: fix front-door defects, drift-proof the docs, clarify taxonomy
