## Why
Tier E is the LAST tier of the bash->Python strangler-fig migration (story adult-oxide-slave, 8784-c2d7-c395-4478). Tiers A-D are DONE/retired; Python is the sole live impl for reads, leaf writes, compute, and the write/sync core. The story's end-state AC is literally "no _engine/*.sh": one implementation + three facades (lib/CLI/MCP), zero standalone shell tests, no embedded heredocs.

Grounding against the live tree (2026-06-12) shows this requires porting ~20 STILL-LIVE bash commands the dispatcher routes to (init, fsck, fsck-recover, transition, reopen, claim, compact, compact-all, scratch, clarity-check, check-ac, quality-check, summary, exists, resolve, format, list-descendants, delete, get-file-impact, get-verify-commands, bridge-status, purge-bridge) -- not just deleting dead wrappers -- plus rewiring the reconciler off the compat shims + engine_env, relocating ticket_txn.py off the bare _engine/event_append.py, deleting the dispatcher + compat shims, and translating all 107 .sh test files to pytest. Plan reviewed by opus subagent (REVISE->APPROVE).

## What
Execute the approved cluster plan, ONE COMMAND AT A TIME (the established §2 per-command protocol: characterize -> port reusing rebar.reducer/graph/_commands/_store/_engine_support -> byte-parity goldens -> cut library+argparse to in-process -> dogfood soak -> delete bash + translate suite), each in a clean green commit. Tier E has NO kill-switch; rollback is git revert. Clusters:
- E0: argparse cli.py skeleton + help/usage/error goldens (byte-identical to the bash dispatcher via a
  golden-as-package-data help action) + the auto-init/freshness middleware (port _ensure_initialized).
  Transitional subprocess fallback for not-yet-ported commands. NO deletions.
- E1: cut the console_scripts entrypoint over to argparse (dispatcher still exists for fallbacks).
- E2: port read-ish/quality cmds (clarity-check, check-ac, quality-check, summary, exists, resolve,
  format, list-descendants, get-file-impact, get-verify-commands, delete).
- E3: port write/lifecycle cmds (transition, reopen, claim, compact, compact-all, scratch).
- E4: port init / fsck / fsck-recover (highest risk; isolated soak each).
- E5: port bridge-status / purge-bridge.
- E5b: rewire rebar_reconciler off ticket_reducer/bare event_append/engine_env.
- E5c: relocate ticket_txn.py; delete the bare _engine/event_append.py.
- E6: rewire remaining compat-shim importers; delete the shims; assert-gone tests.
- E7: delete the dispatcher _engine/rebar + engine_env/PYTHONPATH machinery + engine_dir zipimport
  assertion + jq prereq + flock(1)/mkdir discovery; retire machinery tests in the same commit.
- E8: translate the 107 .sh suites to pytest; delete suite-engine.sh/assert.sh/collector.
- E9: docs (architecture.md offender table -> empty; bash-migration.md §7 DONE) + exhaustive
  live-dogfood validation + soak-evidence comment + close adult-oxide-slave.

## Scope
The whole remaining bash engine, one command/cluster at a time over multiple sessions; each cluster independently green + revertible. NOT in scope: store/locking/event-schema changes (ratified sound); dropping the dual-leg mkdir lock (release-level follow-up, see Tier D note).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] cli.py is a real argparse CLI over rebar._commands/_reads/_engine_support (three facades, one impl)
- [ ] Help/usage/error output byte-identical to the bash dispatcher (goldens pinned before cutover)
- [ ] All ~20 live commands ported in-process; library no longer subprocesses the dispatcher
- [ ] reconciler + ticket_txn.py rewired off compat shims / bare event_append / engine_env
- [ ] Zero _engine/*.sh; compat shims deleted with assert-gone tests; dispatcher + machinery deleted
- [ ] Zero standalone shell tests (tests/**/*.sh == 0); suites translated to pytest, suite green
- [ ] Exhaustive live-dogfood validation passed; soak-evidence recorded; adult-oxide-slave closed
baseline.summary: Tier E: delete the bash dispatcher -> argparse cli.py + port ~20 live cmds + zero _engine/*.sh

baseline.description:
# Rotate the compromised GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN — BLOCKED on deploying the 66af fix to prod first

## Why this exists
66af (Gerrit 1384, MERGED) fixes the review-bot logging the webhook token in plaintext. Its AC5 mandates the already-leaked token be rotated AND that the rotation be "TRACKED SEPARATELY AND EXPLICITLY". This ticket is that record.

## Decisive finding (do NOT rotate before deploying)
The 66af code is merged to main but NOT deployed to the prod box (i-00880b2c7f13527c5). Verified inside the running container `compose-review-bot-1` (image built 2026-08-04T11:07Z, BEFORE 1384 merged ~12:47):
  - review_bot/config.py: TokenRedactingFilter  -> 0 (absent)
  - review_bot/app.py:    X-Rebar-Token          -> 0 (absent)
  - review_bot/app.py:243  token = request.query_params.get("token", "")  <-- still URL-sourced
So the bot still takes the token from `?token=` and uvicorn access-logs it in clear text. Rotating now would re-leak the NEW token the moment Gerrit's webhook/`/rerun` next calls it — exactly the runbook's forbidden precondition ("the code fix must land BEFORE rotation").

## Also: the token is a SHARED secret (ADR-0014)
`/rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token` is simultaneously (a) the bot's Gerrit HTTP basic-auth password (outbound REST/voting), (b) the inbound webhook `?token=`/`X-Rebar-Token` secret, and (c) the container `GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN` env. A bare `aws ssm put-parameter` DESYNCS these and breaks the LLM-Review gate. The canonical atomic tool is `infra/gerrit/service-user.sh` (gerrit set-account new password + SSM overwrite + re-render/push webhooks.config to refs/meta/config).

## Correct sequence (coordinated deploy-then-rotate; brief review-bot bounce)
1. Deploy current origin/main (with 66af) to the box: rebuild the `compose-review-bot` image
   from current main + `docker compose up -d` recreate; re-render webhooks.config to the
   X-Rebar-Token HEADER form via the updated service-user.sh. This removes the leaky URL path.
2. Rotate: run `infra/gerrit/service-user.sh` -> new 256-bit token set as the bot's Gerrit HTTP
   password, overwritten into SSM, and substituted into webhooks.config (pushed to
   refs/meta/config).
3. Restart the review-bot container so it loads the new GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN (fetch-secrets.sh ->
   .env -> compose up -d).
4. Verify end-to-end: inbound webhook triggers a review (or `/rerun`), AND an outbound
   LLM-Review vote succeeds (outbound basic-auth works). Update any operator-local git
   credential caches to the new token.
5. Prefer a quiet window AFTER in-flight changes 1376 (9305) and 1386 (1dbe) have landed — both
   depend on the LLM-Review bot and would be disrupted by the bounce.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] [operator-attested] 66af code deployed to the prod box; running container confirmed to source the token from
      the X-Rebar-Token header and to carry TokenRedactingFilter (no `?token=` URL read).
- [ ] [operator-attested] Token rotated via service-user.sh: new value is the bot's Gerrit HTTP password, in SSM,
      and in the pushed webhooks.config; old (compromised) value no longer accepted.
- [ ] [operator-attested] review-bot restarted and verified: an inbound webhook/`/rerun` triggers a review AND an
      outbound LLM-Review vote lands with the new credential.
- [x] [operator-attested] Rotation recorded as DONE here (not assumed), and 66af AC5 checked off / closed.

## Security note
Until step 2 completes, the previously-logged token remains COMPROMISED and valid. Treat as an open credential exposure.
baseline.summary: Rotate compromised GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN (deploy 66af first)

## Context
Discovered while debugging grindable-deviant-angwantibo. `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py::_collect_node_ids` launches a real nested pytest collection subprocess without `--basetemp`. The confirmed sibling mechanism is pytest session shutdown traversing the shared numbered temp root in `cleanup_numbered_dir`/`rmtree`, which can delete or stall on another run temp tree. The fixed `_store_isolation` helper does not cover this independent caller.

## Plan
- Add a RED regression that gives the nested collection subprocess a poisoned shared numbered temp root and proves a pre-existing sentinel survives unchanged.
- Pass a caller-owned private `--basetemp` directory to `_collect_node_ids` without changing its collection selection, stdout parsing, return-code contract, or timeout.
- Prove GREEN, seed the omitted-basetemp mutation back to RED, and run focused plus repository gates.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The regression fails on the current implementation because nested collection removes or traverses the shared numbered-root sentinel.
- [x] `_collect_node_ids` runs nested pytest with a private basetemp owned by the caller.
- [x] The held-out regression passes and the exact-defect mutation returns it to RED.
- [x] Existing workflow-parity tests pass.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `make test` pass.
baseline.summary: Give parity collection subprocess a private pytest basetemp

baseline.description:
## Summary
When a synced local ticket is archived or moved to status `deleted`, its bound Jira issue is left live (e.g. "To Do") indefinitely. The reconciler's outbound diff never sees these tickets, so no transition/close/unbind is ever emitted. Proven on REB-464/456/465/466/457 (bound to locally archived/deleted test tickets), all still "To Do" in Jira.

## Root Cause (two filter layers, an unintended gap)
- Layer 1 (archived): the reconciler builds its local snapshot via `rebar list --full` (`reconcile.py:455`) with no `--include-archived`; `reducer/_api.py:234` drops `archived=True`. Archived tickets never enter the diff.
- Layer 2 (deleted): deleted-status tickets survive the snapshot but are skipped in the differ loop (`outbound_differ.py:537-540`, `excluded_statuses={archived,deleted}`).
- Smoking gun: `outbound_fields.py:94` maps `"deleted" -> "Done"` (propagation is INTENDED) but the `:539` skip fires before that mapping runs (`:636`) — intended behaviour rendered dead code. `OutboundMutation` declares a `"delete"` action (`outbound_differ.py:245`) but nothing ever constructs one. Not a deliberate "never mutate Jira" policy: `closed -> Done` propagates normally.
- Runtime proof: `rebar list --full` returns 0 for the archived id vs 1 with `--include-archived`; a `reconcile --mode dry-run` (249 mutations over 606 issues) plans nothing for any of these keys.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Sync a local ticket to Jira (binding confirmed).
2. Archive it, or transition it to `deleted` locally.
3. Run `rebar reconcile --mode dry-run`.

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: local archival/deletion of a bound ticket drives its Jira issue to a terminal status (Done) and/or retires the binding, within one pass.
- Actual: no mutation is planned; the Jira issue is stranded live forever.

## Proposed design (perf-safe, binding-driven)
Drive terminal-transition detection from the BINDING STORE, not a full archived-ticket scan, so cost scales with the number of *synced* tickets (~606), never with the total number of archived tickets:
- Each pass compute `missing = bindings.keys() - active_snapshot_ids` (synced tickets that fell out of the active view = just archived/deleted). Cheap set-diff over ~606 bindings.
- For only those ids, do a targeted state read and emit the already-wired terminal transition (`deleted`/`archived -> Done`) via `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` + `_diff_fields`.
- Idempotency: once Jira == Done the field-diff is empty (near-zero steady-state cost); optionally retire the binding after the terminal transition so it leaves the working set. Per-pass cost = O(newly-archived-since-last-pass), shrinking to zero — never O(all-archived). Do NOT switch the full snapshot to `--include-archived`.
- Unifies with the class-C binding GC (same binding-store iteration).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A locally archived or deleted ticket bound to a Jira issue drives that issue to a terminal Jira status (Done), or unbinds it, within one reconcile pass.
- [ ] Detection is bounded by #bindings / #newly-archived, not total archived-ticket count (no full `--include-archived` snapshot per pass); documented with a perf note/test.
- [ ] The dead `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS["deleted"]="Done"` mapping becomes reachable (or is replaced by an explicit terminal-transition path).
- [ ] A test binds a ticket, archives/deletes it locally, runs a pass, and asserts the Jira issue transitions to Done (RED before fix).
- [ ] The concrete drift (REB-464/456/465/466/457) reconciles after the fix.

## Notes
Discovered comparing Jira REB vs the local store. All current instances are "delete me" test tickets, but the mechanism affects any real archived (or closed-then-archived) ticket. `bridge_fsck` does not detect this (see the class-D ticket). Files: `outbound_differ.py`, `outbound_fields.py`, `reconcile.py`, `reducer/_api.py`.

## Guardrails (must-preserve — prior-art + archaeology; folds in the corrected plan)
Approved policy: local archive/delete drives the Jira issue to a terminal status (Done). But:
- [ ] Drive the terminal transition from the per-binding BASELINE + binding-store walk, NOT from snapshot membership; act only on a CONFIRMED terminal/404 (grace-counted), never on snapshot-absence (L13/L16/L17).
- [ ] Close the bidir loop: add `archived` to the reverse status map AND the single-pass bidir suppression, so inbound reading Jira `Done` does not flip local `archived -> closed` (L21/L3; `inbound_translate.py:121`). Today `archived` maps nowhere on the reverse path.
- [ ] Gate the whole class behind the circuit breaker (refuse a pass that would terminal-transition/retire > N% of bindings) [prior art: Argo `allowEmpty`].
- [ ] Preserve `note_absent` grace + reversible retirement (L14/L15); a local-archive retirement must not corrupt the `absent_404_count` machinery.
- [ ] Unify with class C (13eb): one binding-store loop heals terminal transitions and GCs dead bindings.
- [ ] Parity is proven by the CONVERGENCE property (re-reconcile after the heal yields zero actions), not by an enumerated case.

## Implementation contract (foundation-first — read before coding)
DEPENDS ON amiss-bun-wince (baf7): do NOT hand-roll a detection path. This bug is the `TERMINAL_TRANSITION` Decision cell of `classify()` (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/classify.py) plus its apply handler.
1. Detection: the level-triggered binding-store walk (all_bindings()) classifies each bound pair; a pair whose LOCAL ticket is archived or status=deleted while ObservedJira=PRESENT with Jira status != Done yields `TERMINAL_TRANSITION`. Read the local ticket's true state with a targeted read (`rebar show`-equivalent library call), NOT by adding --include-archived to the snapshot (see the perf note: 120 archived tickets exist, only 6 are bound).
2. Apply: emit the already-mapped transition via `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` ("deleted"->"Done"; add "archived"->"Done") through the existing outbound mutation dispatch (typed_dispatch/apply_outbound) — construct a normal status-transition mutation; do NOT invent a new mutation type.
3. ADR 0029 #2 is a HARD PREREQUISITE in this ticket: add `archived` to the reverse status map (inbound_translate.py `_status_maps` region) so inbound Jira `Done` on a locally-archived ticket KEEPS local archived (never flips it to closed), and add the archived case to the L3 single-pass suppression map (inbound_differ.py). RED test first: archive locally -> 1 pass -> Jira Done -> next inbound pass -> local STILL archived; assert stability over 3 simulated passes.
4. Circuit breaker: TERMINAL_TRANSITION is an acting kind — it is automatically counted by check_blast_radius (foundation); no extra work beyond NOT bypassing the apply-path breaker.
5. Live acceptance cells: REB-464/456/465/466/457 (verified still 'To Do' on 2026-07-03) transition to Done; census on the following pass shows 0 acting for this class.
Files: classify.py (cell), outbound_fields.py (status map + reachability of the dead deleted->Done mapping), inbound_translate.py + inbound_differ.py (reverse map + L3), apply_outbound.py/typed_dispatch.py (handler), tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/classify/ + diffing/.
baseline.summary: Reconciler never propagates local archive/delete to the bound Jira issue (stranded live issues)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
A top-level command cannot truthfully declare one required package extra. Optionality varies by nested mode, workflow contents, analyzer, renderer, or selected provider. Enforcing extras during route discovery would hide stable verbs and break lean diagnostic paths; converting every missing dependency to an error would regress intentional unavailable, abstain, and fallback behavior.

## Approach
Create a stdlib-only semantic capability registry independent of the command registry. Each immutable record names a semantic key, packaging extra, and missing posture. The initial complete runtime census is:

- `agent_runtime → agents/error`, `audit_ui → ui/error`, `bedrock_provider → bedrock/error`, `jira_datacenter → jira-datacenter/error`, and `s3_remote → s3/error`;
- `metrics_lizard → metrics/unavailable` and `pricing → pricing/unavailable`;
- `grounding_structural → grounding/abstain` and `grounding_t2 → grounding-t2/abstain`;
- `cloud_adf → adf/fallback`, `datacenter_wiki → wiki/fallback`, and `trace_export → tracing/fallback`;
- separate-entrypoint `mcp_server → mcp/error` and `review_bot → reviewbot/error`, reusable without adding CLI verbs.

`dev` is packaging/development metadata and is not a runtime capability. Validate that every capability references a declared packaging extra, every route's possible capability name exists, and no probe imports the optional package.

Expose a narrow shared error helper for `error` capabilities. Invoke it only after existing handlers/factories parse the selected mode/backend: `audit show` before `audit serve`; status/check/dry-run paths before live agent work; provider selection before Bedrock/Jira DC/S3 client construction. For `unavailable`, `abstain`, and `fallback`, domain components retain control of result payloads and logging; they may consult registry metadata/install hints but the registry never manufactures their domain result.

## Compatibility and Rollback
Preserve existing exact install guidance, exit/error types, and degraded output shapes. Stable verbs and top-level help never depend on installed extras. Existing `_optional.require_extra` and `guard_import` remain compatibility surfaces during expansion and delegate to the new semantic seam where applicable. Rollback restores those direct calls; no persisted data changes.

## Testing
Use unit tests for capability validation and shared error text. Use clean no-extras subprocess/production-path tests for each posture and contrast mode: lean `audit show` versus selected `audit serve`; review/workflow diagnostics versus live agent construction; unselected versus selected Bedrock/Jira DC/S3; metrics/pricing unavailable; grounding abstain; ADF/wiki/tracing fallback. Block heavy modules in `sys.modules` and import hooks during registry/help construction. Separate `rebar-mcp` and review-bot entrypoint smoke tests assert their packaging capabilities without adding CLI routes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every initial semantic capability above validates against one declared packaging extra and one typed missing posture without importing its probe module.
- [ ] Stable commands and top-level help remain present in a no-extras wheel; only the selected capability boundary emits an actionable error for `error` postures.
- [ ] Lean diagnostic/read/dry-run modes execute without requiring sibling live capabilities, including `audit show` and non-agent review/workflow paths.
- [ ] Metrics/pricing unavailable, grounding abstain, ADF/wiki/tracing fallback, and selected provider errors retain their existing domain output, exception, stream, and exit contracts.
- [ ] `rebar-mcp` and review-bot remain separate entry points and can consume capability metadata without appearing in the top-level route registry.
baseline.summary: RP-05 S4 — Enforce semantic capabilities at selected execution boundaries

baseline.description:
## Summary

The `Reconcile Bridge` workflow fails in production on a recurring basis — **22 failed runs between 2026-07-23T20:29Z and 2026-07-30T22:14Z** — and **7 of those failures landed AFTER the most recent reconciler-bridge bug fix**, including two in the very `refs/reconciler/lock` subsystem that fix repaired.

Individual failures are self-healing (a later scheduled run succeeds), which is why they have never been ticketed: the heartbeat canary only files a ticket when staleness exceeds its 2h threshold (it did so once, `4b5c`). The remaining failures are invisible.

## Timing investigation vs commit history

**Most recent reconciler-bridge bug fix:** `7c763f1a7` — *"a4b2: prune an orphaned local pass-lock ref"*, authored 2026-07-27 23:20:41 -0700 = **2026-07-28T06:20:41Z**. Ticket `a4b2` (*Stranded local refs/reconciler/lock wedges every local reconcile pass permanently*) is a **bug** and its fix is specifically about the pass-lock ref lifecycle.

Every later commit touching `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` is J-series Jira Data Center *story* work (`62d9`, `0a94`, `aac8`, `9fd4`), not a bug fix. `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge*.yml` has no commit since `5623a2496` (`0e15`, 2026-07-19); `src/rebar/_store/push.py` / `sync.py` have none since `27e1165cd` (2026-07-17).

**Failures after that fix (7):**

| When (UTC) | Run | Failing step |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-07-29T15:27:11Z | 30465914822 | Run reconciler |
| 2026-07-30T00:45:55Z | 30503669644 | Commit reconciler events back and push to origin/tickets |
| 2026-07-30T03:06:34Z | 30510284129 | Commit reconciler events back and push to origin/tickets |
| 2026-07-30T05:02:44Z | 30515516036 | Commit reconciler events back and push to origin/tickets |
| 2026-07-30T19:46:26Z | 30576272914 | Run reconciler |
| 2026-07-30T20:29:25Z | 30579382013 | Run reconciler |
| 2026-07-30T22:03:07Z | 30585738860 | Commit reconciler events back and push to origin/tickets |

**Rate before vs after the fix** (same workflow, contiguous windows):

```
PRE-FIX  2026-07-23T20:29 -> 2026-07-28T06:20 : 955 runs, 815 success,  15 failure, 124 cancelled  (1.57% fail)
POST-FIX 2026-07-28T06:20 -> 2026-07-30T22:14 : 549 runs, 460 success,   7 failure,  81 cancelled  (1.28% fail)
```

The failure rate is essentially unchanged, and the lock/lease failure mode recurs after a lock-specific fix. `a4b2` addressed a *local* stranded ref wedging local passes; it did not address CI-side lease loss under contention. **This bug is therefore NOT a regression of `a4b2` and not a claim that `a4b2` is wrong — it is the residual, separate problem `a4b2` did not cover.**

## Three distinct failure modes observed post-fix

**(1) Pass-lock lease lost mid-pass** — 2 runs (30576272914, 30579382013):

```
ref-lock renew: refs/reconciler/lock CAS rejected — lease lost/stolen
  (held 52b2181c53bacdfc7c6d4623afbd5d5ec6f6b0ff)
ERROR: reconcile heartbeat lost the lease (pass_id='2026-07-30T19-50-55') — aborting pass
ERROR: reconcile_once raised: pass lock lease lost mid-pass (pass_id='2026-07-30T19-50-55') — aborting
```

Aborting on lease loss is correct-by-design (`2711`: "heartbeat loses lease mid-pass -> pass aborts, no double-run"), but the abort surfaces as a hard workflow failure (exit 1) rather than a benign skip.

**(2) Push to `origin/tickets` rejected after 5 retries** — 4 runs:

```
Push rejected (attempt 4):
 ! [rejected]            HEAD -> tickets (fetch first)
error: failed to push some refs to 'https://github.com/navapbc/rebar'
hint: Updates were rejected because the remote contains work that you do not have
Push failed after 5 retries. Last stderr: ...
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

Concurrent writers keep advancing `origin/tickets` faster than the retry budget.

**(3) Unhandled `HTTP Error 404` from the reconcile pass** — 1 run (30465914822, 2026-07-29T15:34:55Z):

```
ERROR: reconcile_once raised: HTTP Error 404: Not Found
```

Preceded in the same run by repeated (non-fatal) warnings:

```
WARNING rebar_reconciler.apply_inbound_records: _apply_inbound_update: rebar.link failed for
  761e-5af2-ed57-408a -> 119f-63e3-34b7-4f96 (blocks): RebarError('rebar link failed (exit 1):
  Error: ERROR: redundant link — ... are in a direct parent-child relationship')
```

A bare 404 escaping as an unhandled exception is the least explained of the three and may be a genuine gap rather than contention.

## Adjacent signal: cancellation volume

124 pre-fix + 81 post-fix runs were **cancelled** (~15% of all runs), consistent with heavy schedule/dispatch overlap. High overlap is the plausible common driver behind both mode (1) and mode (2), so it is included here as evidence rather than as a separate ticket.

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** contention between overlapping reconciler runs is absorbed
  (backoff, longer retry budget, or a clean no-op exit), so a run that loses a
  race does not turn the workflow red; genuinely unhandled errors (mode 3) fail
  loudly and distinguishably.
- **Actual:** ~1.3% of runs fail, in three different ways that are
  indistinguishable at the workflow level, none individually tracked.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each of the three modes is classified as either *benign contention*
      (should exit non-red / be absorbed) or *a real fault* (should stay red),
      with the decision recorded.
- [ ] Mode (1): losing the pass lock to a legitimate concurrent holder no longer
      produces a red run; a genuine lock fault still does.
- [ ] Mode (2): the `origin/tickets` push either succeeds under normal
      contention (adequate retry/backoff, or fetch-rebase-retry) or exits
      non-red when it has provably lost a benign race.
- [ ] Mode (3): the `HTTP Error 404` path is root-caused and either handled with
      a specific error or reported with enough context to identify the
      failing request.
- [x] Post-fix verification. The `>= 500 runs` population gate originally written
      here is **WAIVED by operator decision (2026-07-31)**: at ~215 Reconcile Bridge
      runs/day it is wall-clock-bound at ~2.3 days, and it adds no evidence about the
      MECHANISM beyond what the oracles already prove. Replaced by, and satisfied by:
      (a) each fixed mode proven RED-first against an oracle held out from the
          implementing agent, then mutation-checked by re-seeding the exact defect —
          mode 1 returns `assert 1 == 75`, mode 3's create/delete 404 escapes again;
      (b) the post-fix sample that actually exists at close, recorded plainly:
          **7 Reconcile Bridge runs** since the fix landed (6 success, 1 cancelled,
          0 failures). Seven runs is a small sample and is explicitly NOT claimed as
          proof the failure has stopped — it is on the record so the number is stated
          rather than implied. Sustained-absence evidence, if wanted, needs the
          wall-clock this waiver declines to spend.
- [ ] Cancellation rate is either explained as expected or reduced.
- [ ] File paths: `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`,
      `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` (pass lock / reconcile_once error
      handling).

## Investigation provenance

Found during a cross-source audit of AWS, Gerrit and GitHub Actions logs for errors not tracked as bugs (2026-07-30). Run inventory: 2,598 Actions runs over 2026-07-23 → 2026-07-30 pulled via the Actions API; failure classification from per-job step conclusions and job logs.
baseline.summary: Reconcile Bridge fails ~1.3% of runs in three modes (lock-lease loss, tickets push rejected, unhandled 404) — 7 recurrences after the a4b2 pass-lock fix

## Why

The concurrency contract promises compaction is recoverable if the process dies after the snapshot is written and partway through source retirement. Existing tests only monkeypatch Python exceptions (which still run `except`/cleanup code) or construct orphan states by hand — none kill an actual compactor process. `SIGKILL` runs none of the rollback, lock-release, cache-cleanup, or git-staging code, so the real process-death durability contract (including lock reclamation and a dirty tracker worktree left between snapshot write and commit) is unproven.

## What

- Add a deterministic subprocess test that kills a real `rebar compact` process
  mid-retirement and verifies recovery from a fresh CLI process.
- Use a test-only failpoint / filesystem barrier to pause after the first source
  rename, rather than a timing-based race window.

## Scope

- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/` (new process-death test)
- Possibly a small test-only failpoint hook in `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py`
  (guarded so it is inert in production).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Test seeds foldable events, launches `rebar compact` in a subprocess, pauses after
      the first source rename via a barrier, and `SIGKILL`s it.
- [ ] From a fresh CLI process: the write lock is recoverable, the ticket reads at its
      exact pre-crash semantic state, no source UUID is lost, `fsck` returns the
      documented clean/repairable result, and re-running compaction is idempotent or
      performs the documented repair (after which `fsck` is clean).
- [ ] The test is deterministic (no reliance on a narrow timing window).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: Add real compactor process-death (SIGKILL) recovery test

baseline.description:
## Context

Bug 8185-2d4b-d2bf-4282 proved that physically deleting committed ENQUEUE_ENRICH, CLAIM_ENRICH, DONE_ENRICH, and TICKET_DIGEST UUID events breaks the event store's append-only union invariant. Independently valid stale clones can then produce delete/modify conflicts instead of reconverging without history loss.

Gerrit change 989, commit be8a0c059571b340cd7705191769a4a64998643d, removed queue and digest pruning and added a real two-clone regression proving both histories survive and merge cleanly. That was the required correctness and recovery fix.

Removing pruning creates a deliberate long-term retention problem. Each successful enrichment cycle normally appends ENQUEUE_ENRICH, CLAIM_ENRICH, DONE_ENRICH, and TICKET_DIGEST events; retries or claim races can append more. At the 2026-07-27 measurement, the live tickets tree contained 1,198 such files totaling about 1.23 MB: roughly 5.5% of tracker files and 0.5% of tracker bytes.

Queue reduction reads accumulated per-ticket event history, pending-work discovery scans every ticket directory, and latest-digest lookup enumerates the ticket directory. Without retention, live file/inode counts and these O(history) scans grow linearly, increasing clone, checkout, index, merge-tree, and operational costs. The former deletion scheme bounded only the live tree; deleted blobs remained in earlier Git history, so it never truly bounded repository storage.

Existing follow-up task 475e-9b99-9085-4b2d records the initial retention design work. This epic preserves the broader architectural context and is intentionally out of scope for the current session.

## Long-term objective

Design and land merge-safe retention, compaction, or archival semantics that bound hot/live tracker cost while preserving cross-clone convergence, crash recovery, auditability, and every independently committed event or a lossless compacted representation. Physical deletion or rename of committed UUID events is not an acceptable solution.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Current queue and digest growth rates and read/clone/index costs are measured with deterministic benchmarks.
- [ ] The chosen design bounds hot/live event lookup and working-tree growth without rewriting or deleting independently committed UUID events.
- [ ] Real two-clone stale-history tests prove independent retention operations reconverge cleanly and preserve all logical state.
- [ ] Crash recovery, claim leasing, latest-digest selection, auditability, and migration/rollback behavior are documented and tested.
- [ ] Operational rollout includes monitoring and a safe migration for existing unbounded histories.
- [ ] The relationship between live-tree retention and Git object/history storage is documented so the design does not claim storage reclamation it does not provide.

## Related evidence

- Closed root-cause bug: 8185-2d4b-d2bf-4282
- Existing retention-design task: 475e-9b99-9085-4b2d
- Correctness fix: Gerrit change 989 / commit be8a0c059571b340cd7705191769a4a64998643d
baseline.summary: Bound tracker growth without deleting committed event history

# `binding_store.py` is at 787/800 — extract the last-synced-peer-state cluster

Raised by the operator while reviewing change 1296 (ticket 88d9): "We're adding a lot to binding_store.py. Should we split that out to preemptively avoid the 800 LOC cap?" Measured rather than estimated: the file was **749** LOC, 1296 takes it to **787**, and the cap is **800**. Thirteen lines of headroom, and the CI module-size gate fails the build when ANY `src/rebar` file exceeds the cap — so the next contributor to touch this file breaks the build, having added nothing wrong.

Deliberately NOT done inside 1296: that change is a data-loss fix that needed to land promptly, and bundling a structural refactor into it would have made it slower to review and harder to reason about. The docstrings added there were tightened instead (795 -> 787) to buy immediate headroom.

## The seam, which already exists

`binding_store.py` holds two distinct concerns:

1. **binding lifecycle** — bind / confirm / unbind, absence + rekey handling, GC/retire grace, the
   immutable numeric Jira id (bug 7c26). This is the bulk of the file.
2. **last-synced PEER STATE** — the ADR-0026 three-way-merge baseline (`get_baseline`, `set_baseline`,
   `seed_baselines_from_snapshot`, `_BASELINE_FIELDS`) plus the peer-parent evidence channel added by
   1296 (`get_peer_parent`, `set_peer_parent`). Together ~130 LOC with docstrings — comfortably over
   the policy's 100-LOC floor for a new module, and a genuine cohesive concern: "what did the peer
   look like the last time we successfully looked".

Concern 2 has its own ADR, its own absence semantics ("an ABSENT baseline is VALID and degrades to local-wins"), and its own advance site in the pass (`reconcile._advance_baselines` / `_advance_peer_parent`). Its consumers are `outbound_field_diff`, `binding_walk` and now `inbound_fields` — none of which touch binding lifecycle.

## What makes this non-trivial, stated honestly

These are METHODS on `BindingStore`, not free functions, so this is not a file move. Extraction means either module-level helpers taking the entry dict (the store keeps thin delegating methods, so no caller changes) or a mixin. The first is preferable — it keeps the public surface identical, so every existing call site and every test double stays valid, and it makes the peer-state functions directly unit-testable without constructing a store.

Per the module-size policy this must be split ALONG THE SEAM ABOVE and not mechanically to hit a number, and the new module must not fall under 100 LOC.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `binding_store.py` is under 700 LOC, and the new module is over 100
- [x] `BindingStore`'s public surface is UNCHANGED — no call site and no test double is edited to
      accommodate the split, asserted by the fact that the reconciler suites pass untouched
- [x] the peer-state functions are directly unit-testable without constructing a `BindingStore`, and
      at least one new test does so (otherwise the extraction bought nothing)
- [x] `_BASELINE_FIELDS` moves WITH the cluster, and `outbound_field_diff` / `binding_walk` /
      `inbound_fields` still resolve their reads (a grep-backed consumer list recorded on this ticket)
- [x] the absence semantics survive the move verbatim: absent baseline degrades to local-wins, absent
      peer parent degrades to NO CLEAR. A test pins each, because these are the properties that make
      the cluster safe and a refactor is exactly when they get quietly dropped
- [x] the module-size gate passes, and the full reconciler unit + integration suites pass
baseline.summary: binding_store.py is at 787/800: extract the last-synced-peer-state cluster

## Context / Problem
Automated bug filers can spam duplicates, file on single flakes, or silently break when create args/gates change (0e15/376d class: gate changes broke automated surfaces). The audit surface is the THREE existing filers — no new filer is built; this ticket HARDENS what exists and documents the contract for future filers: the heartbeat-alert filer (scripts/canary_bridge.py cmd_heartbeat_alert ~:197) and the binding-drift-alert filer (cmd_binding_drift_alert ~:350) — canary_bridge.py has exactly these two create sites, verified by inventory —, plus `_file_conflict_bug_ticket` in the reconciler applier (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py:135, called at :522), which today files one bug per unresolved (local, Jira) conflict with no dedup key, no template contract, and no empty-detail abort.

## Approach
Per OSS practice (PyTorch DISABLED-test bot, Flutter flake bot, Sentry fingerprinting, Alertmanager 'for:'): dedup via a stable per-check TAG searched with has-tag (one open ticket per check); file only after N>=2 consecutive reds; max one accumulation comment/day; templated body (check name, first-red time, run URL, failing-output tail, workflow path) with abort-if-empty-detail; recovery comment on green with close left to agents is documented in the CONTRACT as the default for future filers whose bugs carry investigation value; it is NOT retrofitted anywhere in this ticket. The two canary_bridge filers ALREADY auto-close their alert ticket on green via `rebar transition open closed --force-close` (cmd_heartbeat_alert ~:247-262, cmd_binding_drift_alert ~:398-410) — that existing recovery contract is KEPT AS-IS (pure state alerts, nothing to investigate once green); the audit records this divergence and its rationale in the table rather than retrofitting agent-close onto them. Pattern elements apply per-site by SEMANTIC FIT, recorded in the audit table: the N>=2 consecutive-red threshold applies only where a derivable red/green run signal exists: the HEARTBEAT filer only — its stale check fails the canary run (the 'Fail job on stale' step), so the workflow's previous run conclusion carries the signal. The BINDING-DRIFT filer gets NO threshold, with rationale recorded: its oracle never fails the run (conclusion carries no drift signal), and drift is PERSISTENT state, not a flake — it cannot self-heal between runs, so first-observation filing is correct and dedup + daily accumulation already bound spam; the conflict filer has no cycle semantics, so it gets dedup (stable tag derived from the conflict identity: local id + jira key), template, abort-if-empty, and detected_by — not the threshold. CONSECUTIVE-RED STATE STORE: no new state store — the workflow's own run history is the durable state. On red, the filer queries the same workflow's previous completed run conclusion (gh api repos/{repo}/actions/workflows/{file}/runs?status=completed&per_page=2, excluding the current run); previous-also-red => threshold met; previous-green-or-absent => first red, no ticket. Dedup search runs FIRST: an existing open tagged ticket always takes the accumulate-comment path regardless of threshold. ACCUMULATION DEDUP ('max one accumulation comment/day'): derived from the target ticket's OWN comment history — the accumulation comment opens with a stable marker line; the filer reads the ticket (rebar show --output json), finds the newest marker-bearing comment, and skips if it is <24h old. The ticket store IS the durable state; no new store, and the */20 cron cannot spam. First-red time in the template = the previous red run's timestamp. WORKFLOW THREADING (scope): the consuming alert steps in .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml today pass only STALE/RUN_URL/DRIFT_* env; the heartbeat alert step's run-history query additionally needs GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} (already used by other steps in that workflow), the repo (github.repository), and the workflow file id (the literal filename) threaded as step env — enumerated as workflow edits in scope, heartbeat step only. The contract doc records the same recipe for future filers with run-conclusion signals. LIFECYCLE: green with no open tagged ticket (single flake that never crossed the threshold) => recovery path no-ops on the empty has-tag search — stated as an invariant and unit-tested. USER-REQUIRED ADDITIONS: (a) audit ALL existing auto-bug-creation sites and retrofit the fitting pattern elements; (b) document the bug-creation contract for automation — exact rebar create args, exit codes, dedup search command, REBAR_DETECTED_BY env var — so auto-filers always fire a well-formed create.

## Scope
- canary/heartbeat/binding-drift filer scripts or workflow logic (coordinate with Tier-3 migration child if concurrent)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py `_file_conflict_bug_ticket`: dedup tag + template + abort-if-empty + detected_by (no threshold — no red/green cycle)
- docs: bug-creation contract page
- audit table of every auto-file site in the change description, with a per-site row: which pattern elements apply and why

## Testing
Heartbeat-filer unit tests: first red -> no ticket; second consecutive red -> one ticket with template fields; third red same day -> accumulation comment, not a new ticket; second accumulation within 24h -> skipped (marker-line dedup); green with open ticket -> existing auto-close path preserved (transition open closed --force-close, unchanged); green with NO open ticket -> no-op, exit 0; empty detail -> abort with loud log, no hollow ticket; previous-run query failure -> treated as first red (fail toward not filing, loud log). Binding-drift tests: first observed drift -> one ticket (no threshold, rationale in table); repeat drift -> accumulation not duplicate; green -> existing auto-close preserved. Conflict-filer tests: same conflict twice -> one ticket + one accumulation comment; distinct conflicts -> distinct tickets; empty conflict detail -> abort.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] All three audited auto-file sites use the fitting dedup+template pattern elements (audit table enumerates sites x elements with rationale, including the kept auto-close divergence and the binding-drift no-threshold rationale).
- [x] Heartbeat consecutive-red threshold implemented via workflow run-history query; no new state store introduced; single flake files nothing.
- [x] Bug-creation contract documented and referenced by every filer.
- [x] Filer behavior covered by the unit tests above, including the green-with-no-ticket no-op and the query-failure arm.
- [x] detected_by stamped by all automated filers (env var from the detected-by child).
baseline.summary: Auto-bug-filer hardening: dedup pattern, all-site audit, contract doc

## Summary
rebar's LLM runner inherits `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` from the environment, so when a local
Claude-Code payload-optimizing proxy (headroom, `http://127.0.0.1:8787`) is enabled, ALL
of rebar's agentic LLM calls are routed through it. That proxy corrupts rebar's **agentic
tool-loop** requests (Pass-2 plan-review verifier, completion-verifier), producing an empty
provider stream. The empty stream surfaces as `UnexpectedModelBehavior("Streamed response
ended without content or tool calls")`, is caught at `runner.py:333` as a terminal
`LLMUnavailableError` (no retry), and fail-closes the plan-review verdict to INDETERMINATE —
which writes no attestation, so **every code-grounded ticket becomes un-claimable**.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Enable headroom (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787`).
2. `rebar review-plan <code-grounded-epic>` (e.g. ac1b-cef3-35c8-415f).
3. Observe `coverage.verify_failed=True`, `coverage.metrics.verify_requests=0`,
   `coverage.verify_error` = "Streamed response ended without content or tool calls",
   verdict INDETERMINATE.

Expected: verify completes; verdict PASS/BLOCK on the plan's merits.
Actual: verify makes 0 requests; verdict INDETERMINATE; claim refused ("attestation stale").

Discriminating proof: `env -u ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL rebar review-plan <same>` → verify_requests=20,
verify_error=None, verdict PASS. Single-turn and simple/large tool-use streams pass through
headroom fine; only the multi-turn agentic tool-LOOP breaks. RTK (bash hook) is not involved.

## Fix
rebar's internal agent must not route through a local (loopback) Claude-Code payload optimizer.
When the resolved model is Anthropic and `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points at a loopback host, build the
Anthropic model with a provider pinned to the direct public API (bypassing the local proxy).
Respect non-loopback gateways (untouched). Opt out with `REBAR_LLM_ALLOW_LOCAL_PROXY=1`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` set to a loopback host, rebar's runner builds an Anthropic model
      whose provider base_url is the direct public API (`https://api.anthropic.com`), not the loopback.
- [ ] A non-loopback `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` (a real gateway) is respected (passed through unchanged).
- [ ] `REBAR_LLM_ALLOW_LOCAL_PROXY=1` opts back in (no bypass) for users who intend the local proxy.
- [ ] Non-Anthropic providers and the test model_override path are unaffected.
- [ ] Unit test covers loopback-bypass / non-loopback-passthrough / opt-out; existing runner tests pass.
- [ ] Replication: with headroom running, `rebar review-plan ac1b-cef3-35c8-415f` yields a determinate
      verdict (verify_requests>0), not INDETERMINATE.
baseline.summary: runner routes agentic LLM calls through local headroom proxy -> empty stream -> INDETERMINATE

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Operator directive (verbatim, 2026-08-13): 'you're authorized to configure our bridge to run hourly instead of continuously for this project in order to free the runner.'

The config half is done: `RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS` was flipped true -> false at 2026-08-13T14:59Z, so the self-re-dispatch chain stops after its in-flight pass and the runner slot frees. The bridge now runs solely on `reconcile-bridge.yml`'s cron, which change 1726 (f59a-2d16-68c5-450c) just set to a uniform 40-minute three-entry schedule. Operator intent here is HOURLY, so that block is now wrong and over-elaborate — the three-entry spelling existed only because cron cannot express 40 minutes in one entry.

## Approach
1. **The schedule** — replace the three entries in `reconcile-bridge.yml` with the single entry `23 * * * *`. Off-:00 deliberately: GitHub's scheduler is best-effort and most contended at the top of the hour, so an on-:00 entry is likeliest to be delayed or dropped. `workflow_dispatch` stays (manual runs); AC1's "no other trigger" is about automatic firing.
2. **The cadence test** — `test_bridge_backstop_fires_on_a_uniform_40_minute_cadence` (added by 1726) derives the day's fire times from the cron entries and asserts every consecutive gap, wrapping past midnight. Keep that machinery — it catches what a literal pin cannot — and retarget it: rename to `..._on_a_uniform_hourly_cadence`, assert the gap set is exactly `{60}`, and add two assertions the hourly form makes meaningful: exactly ONE schedule entry (the three-entry workaround must not survive as dead weight) and a non-zero minute (the off-:00 hygiene, otherwise unenforced). `_cron_field_matches` is unchanged.
3. **Pinned literals** — `_UNCHANGED_CRONS`, `test_reconcilers_keep_their_own_schedules_and_never_cancel`, and `test_github_schedule_and_continuous_redispatch_remain_compatible` each pin 1726's three-entry list; all take the single hourly entry. The canary's `0 */2 * * *` pin is unchanged — it stays 2-hourly per pittabird.
4. **Jenkinsfile** — the three-line `cron('''…''')` block collapses to `cron('23 * * * *')`, its 40-minute comment rewritten.
5. **Canary staleness arithmetic** — the canary header derives its window as "3x cadence". At 40 min the floor was 2h against a 4h window; hourly it becomes 3h, still inside 4h, so **the window does not change** — only the sentence naming 40 minutes. `canary_bridge.py`'s alert body "bridge cadence: 40 minutes" becomes "hourly". This is the one place the change could silently create false alarms, so it is checked, not assumed.
6. **The CloudWatch alarm — a real break, not a comment** — `monitoring_bridge.tf`'s `bridge_run_failures` alarm is `Sum`, `period = 3600`, `threshold = 1`, `GreaterThanThreshold`: "two failed passes in one hour" (its comment still says the bridge "runs every ~20 minutes"). Hourly, at most ONE pass falls in a bucket, so the Sum can never exceed 1 and **the alarm becomes structurally unfirable** — the silent monitoring regression it exists to prevent (the 2026-08-12 token expiry that produced no signal). Retune to keep the intent (a blip stays quiet, a sustained failure pages): keep `period = 3600`, set `threshold = 0`, `evaluation_periods = 2`, `datapoints_to_alarm = 2` — two CONSECUTIVE hourly buckets each with a failed pass. A healthy pass publishes 0, failing `> 0` and breaking the streak, so single flakes stay quiet. Detection latency ~40 min -> ~2h; update the description and both cadence comments.
   **Apply consequence, stated not discovered:** `terraform-drift.yml` runs `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` on `infra/terraform/**` changes and FAILS on a non-empty plan, so this leaves Terraform Drift red until an operator applies it — called out on the ticket at landing so the apply is sequenced, not discovered as a mystery red.
7. **Comments and docs** — every remaining "40-minute"/"40 min": the bridge header, schedule comment, re-dispatch backstop references and `::warning::` string; the `test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py` and `test_ci_tickets_push_policy.py` docstrings; and `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` — cadence table, the "…40-minute floor" heading plus its three anchor links, its bullets, and the latency note recording the new **1 hour** worst case.

1726's chain-pacing step stays: gated on `RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS`, now false, so it is inert here — but this file is a client-copied TEMPLATE and an adopter may still opt in. Deleting a working opt-in mechanism is not what "run hourly for this project" asks for.

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` — single hourly cron + comment rewrites.
- `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` — staleness arithmetic sentence only.
- `Jenkinsfile` — single hourly cron.
- `scripts/canary_bridge.py` — alert-body cadence string.
- `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` — cadence table, heading + anchors, 1h latency note.
- `infra/terraform/monitoring_bridge.tf` — retune `bridge_run_failures` to stay firable hourly.
- `tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_push_policy.py` — retargeted cadence test, literal pin, docstring.
- `tests/unit/test_ci_main_push_policy.py`, `tests/unit/workflow/test_bridge_provider_wrappers_heldout.py` — pins.
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py` — docstring.

## Testing
- **Happy path:** the retargeted cadence test derives fire times from the workflow's own cron and asserts the gap set is exactly `{60}` — a property, not a literal echo. The three pins assert the single-entry list.
- **Edge / regression:** the same test asserts one schedule entry and a non-zero minute, so neither a reintroduced multi-entry block nor an on-:00 drift passes silently. Both are checked by mutating the workflow locally (a second entry; minute 0) and confirming the test fails before reverting.
- **Alarm arithmetic:** confirm by hand that one failed pass in an hour does NOT breach (one bucket, two consecutive required) and two consecutive failing hours DOES — so the retune preserves the quiet-on-a-blip intent, not merely firability.
- **False-alarm check:** confirm the canary arithmetic still holds — 3 x 60 min = 3h floor inside the unchanged 4h window — and that `tests/scripts/test_canary_bridge*.py` and `test_reconcile_bridge_canary_class.py` pass unchanged (they set `ALERT_WINDOW_HOURS` explicitly).
- **Gates:** the `check_*` gates, generator no-diff, `make lint` (actionlint parses the workflow), `make typecheck`, the CI unit selection, and `tests/integration`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `reconcile-bridge.yml` has exactly one `schedule:` entry, `23 * * * *`, and no other automatic trigger; `workflow_dispatch` remains for manual runs.
- [x] The cadence test derives the schedule and asserts a uniform 60-minute gap, a single entry, and a non-zero minute; the mutation checks in Testing confirm it fails on a second entry and on an on-:00 minute.

## What
When `rebar create` makes a work ticket whose type is **not** `bug`/`session_log`
(i.e. `task`/`story`/`epic`), print a **stderr warning** that no `file_impact` was
recorded, nudging the author to run `set-file-impact` before the plan-review gate.
This surfaces the plan-review **file-impact-coverage (P9)** requirement *early*, at
create time, instead of only when `review-plan` runs — so it can be fixed before a
full review round (the churn seen on ticket f112, re-reviewed after file_impact was added).

## Why
`file_impact` cannot be supplied at create time (only via a later `set-file-impact`),
and the P9 detector (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:645`, `applicable = not
ctx.children`) flags any leaf work ticket lacking it. `bug`/`session_log` are gate-
exempt upstream (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:540`), so the warning mirrors that exemption.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py` `create_cli()`: after a successful create, if
  `ticket_type not in ("bug", "session_log")`, emit
  `print("Warning: no file_impact recorded ...", file=sys.stderr)` (matches existing
  `Warning:`-to-stderr convention in transition.py/txn.py/unlink.py).
- Keep stdout pure (created alias/id line unchanged); warning goes to stderr only.
- Not in scope: a `--file-impact` create flag or MCP structured warning (follow-ups).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar create task "x"` with no file_impact prints a `Warning:` line to **stderr** naming the id and pointing at `set-file-impact`; stdout stays pure (alias/id line only).
- [ ] `rebar create bug "x"` and `rebar create session_log ...` print **no** such warning.
- [ ] A test in `tests/integration/test_stdout_purity.py` (or equivalent) asserts the stderr warning for `task` and its absence for `bug`.
- [ ] `make lint` and the touched tests pass.
baseline.summary: create: warn on stderr when a non-bug ticket is created without file_impact

## Why

The floor must key on VERIFIED delivery, never bare `closed` status — otherwise a force-closed or
abandoned child would launder un-validated work past scrutiny, and a stale closed ticket can hard-
block the epic review (observed in practice).

## What

Add a `delivered_now(child, epic, repo_root)` helper (in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py`,
reusing the `compute_validity(sig, child_state, 'completion-verifier')` validity-on-read check used INSIDE `_child_closure_findings` in `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` — note that fn is a DEFICIT detector (returns findings for children LACKING delivery), so we reuse its validity CALL applied to children whose status IS closed, NOT the fn itself) that returns True iff
the child is `closed` AND holds a completion-verifier attestation that is VALID on read
(`compute_validity(..., "completion-verifier")` — so drift-stale / force-closed / unsigned all read
false), OR child B is superseded by a SIBLING A (same parent; direction B superseded_by A) that is itself a live vehicle (delivered-now OR open/in_progress, not force-closed/abandoned) (read the
`supersedes`/`duplicates` links via `src/rebar/__init__.py`; verify shared parent so work that left
the epic does not count as delivered). Recomputed each run. In-progress / abandoned / force-closed
children return False -> stay in scope.

## Scope

- IN: the `delivered_now` predicate + its sibling-supersede check + validity-on-read reuse.
- OUT: the Pass-3 wiring (separate story); the Pass-2 sub-call (separate story).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `delivered_now` is True for a closed child with a VALID completion attestation; False for force-closed, unsigned, drift-stale, in-progress, and abandoned children.
- [ ] `delivered_now` treats B as delivered-elsewhere ONLY when a SIBLING A (same parent) supersedes B (direction: B superseded_by A) AND A is a live in-epic vehicle (delivered-now OR active open/in_progress); False when A is not a sibling or is itself force-closed/abandoned (closes the supersede-direction + replacement-not-done gap).
- [ ] The predicate reuses the `compute_validity(..., 'completion-verifier')` validity-on-read call (NOT the deficit-detector `_child_closure_findings` itself), applied to closed children, and is recomputed per run (no persisted state).
- [ ] Unit tests cover attested / force-closed / drift-stale / supersede-sibling / supersede-nonsibling / in-progress cases.

## Supersede mechanism (concrete artifact)

The supersede relationship is the structured `supersedes` LINK RELATION (one of rebar's six link
relations) — an auditable, event-sourced graph edge in the ticket's deps, NOT a free-text note,
tag, or naming convention. `delivered_now` reads it via `rebar.show`/`ticket_deps`: child B is
delivered-elsewhere iff a SIBLING A (same `parent_id`) has an `A supersedes B` edge (equivalently B
`superseded_by` A) AND A is a live in-epic vehicle (delivered-now OR open/in_progress). Because the
edge is a structured graph relation (not unsigned prose) AND the superseding sibling A stays in
review scope, this is NOT the unsigned/gameable suppression the Alternatives reject: no coverage is
removed (A is still reviewed), and the security/contract preserve-set (T5c/T10) is never dropped
regardless of supersede — so a manipulated edge cannot launder a security finding.

## Acceptance Criteria (mechanism)

- [ ] The supersede signal is the structured `supersedes` link relation read from the child's deps (named artifact), not a note/tag/convention.
- [ ] A test asserts the security/contract preserve-set is never dropped even when a supersede edge is present (no laundering).

## Acceptance Criteria (reopen semantics)

- [ ] A PARENT epic reopen does NOT un-deliver its closed children: ADR 0009 keys on each ticket's OWN `last_reopened_at`, so only a CHILD's own reopen invalidates that child's completion attestation. Closed children remain `delivered-now` across a parent reopen; a reopened child flips to not-delivered and its findings resurface.
baseline.summary: delivered-now predicate: reuse completion attestation (validity-on-read) + in-epic sibling supersede

## Context / Problem
After Gerrit 1796, `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` sits at 800 LOC (the absolute CI module-size cap) and `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py` at 799. Any edit to either must extract first or the module-size gate fails. Each module carries several distinct concerns. Operator direction: remediate BOTH architecturally — separate concerns into modules with clear contractual boundaries, not a mechanical split to duck under the cap.

## Concern map (from the real call graph, verified by Serena refs + grep string sweep)
`completion.py` (800) holds four concerns: (1) operation orchestration — `verify_completion`/`_verify_completion_inner`/`_verifier_model_for_completion`/`verify_step_floor` (consumers: `src/rebar/llm/__init__.py:38`, `workflow/completion_banking.py:38`, `workflow/gate_dispatch.py`); (2) deterministic child-closure gate — `child_closure_findings`/`_uncertified_child_ids`/`build_child_closure_evidence` (consumer: `workflow/gate_ops.py:61,224`); (3) epic-close bug-screen deterministic layer — `EPIC_BUG_SCREEN_CEILING`, `_epic_subtree_states`, `_open_bugs`, `_first_in_progress_ns`, `epic_bug_floor_findings`, `epic_bug_candidates` (consumers: `gate_ops.py:64`, `epic_bug_screen.py:267-275`, whose docstring already describes these as the screen's DET stages 1-2); (4) verdict reconciliation — remediation constants, `reconcile_verdict` + fault/insufficiency helpers, `deterministic_child_failure`. `completion_recovery.py` (799) holds three: (5) criteria surface + admission bounds + coverage contract — `explicit_completion_criteria`, `physical_context_ceiling`, `_validate_recovery_inputs`, `_validate_coverage`, the checkbox regexes and `_MAX_*` bounds; (6) failure taxonomy — `_normalized_finish_reason`, `_is_token_exhaustion`, `_bounded_diagnostic`, `raise_completion_workflow_failure`; (7) recovery orchestration — `CompletionAgentStep` (primary run + banked successors + finalization).

## Approach — target modules and their contracts
Behavior-preserving moves along the existing seams above; no signature or logic changes. Keep documented public seams stable via re-export; move internal consumers to the new homes.
- `rebar/llm/completion.py` (~250 LOC): OWNS the completion-verification operation (entry `verify_completion`, model/budget tuning `verify_step_floor`/`_VERIFY_STEP_FLOOR_MAX`/`_verifier_model_for_completion`) and REMAINS the stable public seam its `__all__` documents: re-exports `child_closure_findings`, `build_child_closure_evidence`, `deterministic_child_failure`, `reconcile_verdict`, `COMPLETION_REMEDIATION_GUIDANCE`, and `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE_REMEDIATION` (imported by name at `tests/unit/workflow/test_insufficient_evidence_marker.py:315`) — so `gate_ops` imports and `monkeypatch` strings on `rebar.llm.completion.*` (e.g. `tests/unit/test_ticket_description_limit.py:209`) stay valid unchanged.
- NEW `rebar/llm/completion_child_gate.py` (~210): OWNS the deterministic child-closure invariant + evidence block (concern 2). Exposes `child_closure_findings`, `build_child_closure_evidence`.
- NEW `rebar/llm/completion_reconcile.py` (~290): OWNS verdict normalization + remediation (concern 4): `reconcile_verdict`, `_findings_from_criteria`, `_is_no_verdict_fault`, `_insufficiency_only`, `NO_VERDICT_CRITERION`, both remediation constants, and `deterministic_child_failure` (the no-LLM FAIL verdict).
- `rebar/llm/epic_bug_screen.py` (297 → ~460): ABSORBS concern 3 so the entire epic bug screen (DET floor, DET candidate filter, LLM screen) is one module; `gate_ops.py:64` and `epic_bug_screen.py:267-275` switch to local/`epic_bug_screen` imports. The epic_bug_* symbols are NOT re-exported from completion.py, so EVERY `completion.epic_bug_*` reader in `tests/unit/test_epic_bug_screen_4b54.py` repoints to `epic_bug_screen`: direct attribute-call sites at lines 79, 94, 103, 112, 120, 129, 136, 238 AND monkeypatch targets at 230 (`EPIC_BUG_SCREEN_CEILING`) and 450 (`epic_bug_floor_findings`) — import/alias switch only.
- NEW `rebar/llm/workflow/completion_criteria.py` (~240): OWNS concern 5 — what counts as a completion criterion, the recovery admission bounds, and the full-coverage contract.
- NEW `rebar/llm/workflow/completion_failures.py` (~230): OWNS concern 6 — typed exhaustion classification, bounded allowlisted diagnostics, and workflow-failure finalization.
- `rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py` (~420): keeps `CompletionAgentStep` + finalizer constants; re-exports `explicit_completion_criteria`, `raise_completion_workflow_failure` (its documented `__all__`) AND `physical_context_ceiling` — so `gate_dispatch.py:669`, `completion_prefetch.py:214`, the patch string `test_completion_prefetch.py:120`, and every `_cr.physical_context_ceiling` module-alias read (`test_close_gate_bound_remedy_db1c.py:66`, `test_completion_token_recovery.py:312`, `test_completion_recovery_context_product_bound.py:94-97`, `test_completion_recovery_oversized_d59e.py:57,220`) stay valid unchanged. Underscore-helper module-alias reads repoint to `completion_criteria`: `_validate_recovery_inputs` (`test_completion_recovery_contract.py`, `test_completion_recovery_context_product_bound.py:112-137`), `_validate_coverage` (`test_completion_recovery_contract.py`, `test_completion_banking.py:219-239`, `test_insufficient_evidence_marker.py:288-296`), `_MAX_TOTAL_CRITERIA_CHARS` (`test_completion_recovery_oversized_d59e.py:190-191`).
Caller updates: `completion.py:758` prelude imports and doc cross-references. Tests get import-path and monkeypatch-target updates ONLY; zero assertion changes. Riskiest assumption: every moved symbol stays patchable where its runtime caller reads it. baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Existing stores — including client deployments — have no `.bridge_state/projects.json` and no `bridge_project` on any ticket. Without a migration they read every ticket as absent-project with no recorded legacy default for the resolver to fall back to, so a store that syncs today stops syncing on upgrade.

## Prerequisites (substrate, from cited deps — already `depends_on` edges)

- `[rebar:c927-0a68-4465-42a2]` — the projects-mapping store `projects_store.py`: the
  `.bridge_state/projects.json` record (`{version, legacy_default, projects}`), `load_mapping`, the
  `Mapping` dataclass, the tri-state resolver `resolve_project` (absent field → `legacy_default`;
  `""` → `None`; key → verbatim), and `set_project`/`read_projects`.
- `[rebar:67f9-4a07-9667-446a]` — registers `multi-project-bridge` in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`
  (`src/rebar/_store/compat.py`), so
  a store may stamp it and still pass its own compat gate.

`Backend.project` (`_backend.py:598-605`, the effective write/create scope) is pre-existing.

## Approach

Ship the migration as ensure units on the idempotent registry (`src/rebar/_store/ensures.py`, `REGISTRY_IDS` `:66`, `_registry()` `:82`) — rebar's sanctioned seam (`docs/migrations.md:40-56`; the ordered School-A ledger is deliberately not built, `:14-16`). Units run at init/re-init, `fsck --repair`, and MCP boot (`:57-65`), so a client store converges with no operator action.

**No ticket events.** An EDIT-per-ticket migration would be a four-figure event write under the store lock, and MCP-boot runs the sweep on a short lock budget and skips when contended (`:63-65`) — so it would silently skip at one entry point and converge unpredictably. Instead the unit records `legacy_default` once, and `resolve_project` `[rebar:c927-0a68-4465-42a2]` treats every absent-field ticket as belonging to it. One small write migrates the whole store.

Two units, both check-then-act and safe to re-run:

1. **Seed the mapping.** If `.bridge_state/projects.json` `[rebar:c927-0a68-4465-42a2]` is absent, write it with
   `legacy_default` and a single `projects` entry from `Backend.project` (`_backend.py:598-605`); if
   present, return `ok` and write nothing. Tree-check the committed
   `tickets:.bridge_state/projects.json` blob before committing so a converged store makes zero commits
   (`docs/migrations.md:45-46`).
2. **Converge the capability stamp (backstop, NOT the trigger).** Per the parent epic 0e68, the
   *authoritative* `multi-project-bridge` stamp is written by the `bridge projects` set/remove write
   path — the stamp and the mapping mutation land in the SAME tracker commit (one atomic publish). This
   ensure unit is only a **convergence backstop for residual divergence**: when the mapping already
   holds more than one project but `.store-compat.json`'s `required_capabilities` lacks
   `multi-project-bridge` (a legacy store, or a crash between the write path's two writes), it adds the
   token; a single-project store is never stamped and stays usable by older binaries. It is
   level-triggered on the mapping state and decoupled from *how* the store became multi-project, and is
   never the primary trigger — the seed above only ever makes a **one-project** mapping, so this unit
   never fires from the same sweep's seed. The token is registered in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES` by
   prerequisite `[rebar:67f9-4a07-9667-446a]` (`src/rebar/_store/compat.py`, the `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`
   frozenset), so a stamped store still passes `check_store_compat` on this binary — this story makes
   **no** `compat.py` edit, and a test asserts a two-project stamped store passes the gate.

Ids are new and never reused (`docs/migrations.md:50-51`).

**Unit bodies live in a new `src/rebar/_store/project_ensures.py`**, not `init.py` (where the six existing units live, e.g. `_store_compat_unit` `:509`). `init.py` is **758 lines** — ~42 under the 800-line gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), so this is a **cohesion** choice, not size-forced: the projects migration is distinct from init's `.gitignore`/`.gitattributes` constants. `ensures.py` (257 lines) gains only its two registry entries.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/project_ensures.py` (new) — both unit bodies
- `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py` — two `REGISTRY_IDS` entries + two `_registry()` mappings
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_ensures.py` — update the hardcoded `expected` id-set literal in
  `test_registry_id_set_is_frozen` (`:57`, the six existing ids) to add the two new ids so the
  registry-agreement test passes
- `docs/migrations.md` — document the two units and the `multi-project-bridge` token's meaning for
  other binaries/operators (it gates `.store-compat.json` compatibility)
- `tests/integration/test_ensure_project_mapping.py` (new) — the behavioural oracle below

## Testing

Real temp git repos and refs (the shared standard's git row) — the units commit to `tickets` and the zero-commit-when-converged property is only observable against real refs.

- Happy path: sweeping a no-mapping store creates one whose `legacy_default` equals the backend
  project, and every ticket resolves to it via `resolve_project`.
- Load-bearing: the sweep writes **zero ticket events** — assert the event-file set is identical before
  and after (distinguishes this from an EDIT-per-ticket migration).
- Idempotence: a second sweep returns `ok` for both units and the tickets-branch tip SHA is unchanged.
- Conditional stamp (contrast pair): one-project → `required_capabilities` empty; two-project → exactly
  `multi-project-bridge`. The one-project half proves the stamp is genuinely conditional.
- Compat-gate safety: a two-project stamped store still passes `check_store_compat` on this binary.
- Failure path: a raising unit is recorded `failed` and does not abort the sweep or caller.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A no-mapping store gains one whose `legacy_default` equals the configured backend project;
      real-git test reads the seeded record.
- [x] Every absent-`bridge_project` ticket resolves to that default via `resolve_project`
      `[rebar:c927-0a68-4465-42a2]`; same test.
- [x] The sweep writes zero ticket events; the event-file set is identical before and after.
- [x] A second sweep returns `ok` for both units.
- [x] A second sweep leaves the tickets-branch tip SHA unchanged (compared across two sweeps).
- [x] A one-project mapping leaves `required_capabilities` empty; real-git test.
- [x] A two-project mapping adds exactly `multi-project-bridge`; real-git test.
- [x] A two-project stamped store still passes `check_store_compat` on this binary; test invokes the
      gate.
- [x] The two new ids are added to `REGISTRY_IDS`.
- [x] The two new ids are mapped in `_registry()`.
- [x] The two new ids are added to the `expected` literal in `test_registry_id_set_is_frozen`
      (`test_ensures.py:57`) so that test passes.
- [x] A raising unit is recorded `failed` and does not abort the sweep or caller; test monkeypatches a
      raising unit into `_registry()`.
- [x] `docs/migrations.md` documents the two ensure units and the `multi-project-bridge` token's
      compat meaning for other binaries/operators (that it gates `.store-compat.json` compatibility).
baseline.summary: Legacy-store migration: ensure units seeding the project mapping without writing ticket events
