## Summary
After bug ad39 fixed reconcile-check's local-ticket loader, running `rebar reconcile --mode reconcile-check` against the healthy live store (627 bindings, all now checked, 0 orphaned) reports `in_sync: 0` with **3660 discrepancies** — i.e. EVERY binding shows some field mismatch. The authoritative real differ (dry-run) dispatches ~0 inbound changes over the same store, so these are representational diffs (status-name mapping, description/priority format, label normalization), not actionable drift.

## Reproduction Steps
1. `rebar reconcile --mode reconcile-check` on a healthy store post-ad39.
2. Observe `bridge_state/reconcile-check.json`: checked=627, orphaned=0, in_sync=0, discrepancies=3660.

Expected: in_sync ~= checked for a store the real differ considers converged.
Actual: in_sync=0; every binding flagged with field discrepancies.

## Root Cause (hypothesis)
`_compare_pair` in reconcile_check.py compares local vs Jira fields WITHOUT the same normalization the differs use (reverse status map, description ADF/markdown normalization, priority/label canonicalization). Latent until ad39 made the loader actually load tickets.

## Impact
Diagnostic-only (reconcile-check is read-only; does not act). But in_sync=0 makes the go/no-go read alarming/unusable for the class-D consumer. Should reuse the differ's field-normalization so reconcile-check's discrepancy set matches what the differ would actually dispatch.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] reconcile-check's field comparison reuses the differ's normalization so a store the real differ considers converged reports in_sync ~= checked (few/zero discrepancies).
- [ ] Unit test: a binding whose normalized fields agree (but raw representations differ, e.g. status open/To Do) counts in_sync, not discrepant.
- [ ] Landed on main via Gerrit.

baseline.description:
## Why

The plan-review `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar is the only durable record of a review's four passes, but its `_slim` step drops the pass-1 `evidence` and `scenarios` fields, and it does not persist the numeric `block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled` each finding was judged against (these are resolved from the criteria registry at decision time and then discarded). Without them an auditor cannot see a finding's grounding quotes or the exact decision boundary that was applied.

## What

Extend the plan-review sidecar to a new schema version `plan_review_result_v2` that additionally persists, per finding: the pass-1 `evidence[]` and `scenarios[]`, and the resolved `block_threshold` (float) and `blocking_enabled` (bool) that pass-3 used. All existing fields and the all-buckets pooling (blocking + advisory + overflow + indeterminate + dropped) are unchanged.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py` — bump `SCHEMA` to `plan_review_result_v2`; stop stripping
  `evidence`/`scenarios` in `_slim`; thread the resolved `block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled` from
  the pass-3 decision into each persisted finding; `latest_review_result` accepts both `v1` and `v2`.
- `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py` — expose the resolved `block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled`
  on each finding's decision output (the `ThresholdResolver` result is currently used then dropped).

## Approach rationale

Bump the schema and widen the payload rather than write a parallel record, so the single existing emit/prune/read path carries the richer data unchanged in shape. The resolved threshold is captured at the exact point pass-3 applies it, which is the only place it is knowable without re-reading the registry (avoiding historical drift).

## Compatibility & rollback

`v1` sidecars remain valid and are read with the new fields absent (readers treat missing threshold/evidence as "not recorded"). No backfill. Reverting restores the `v1` payload; already- written `v2` events remain readable by the tolerant reader. Adding fields to the payload does not change the reducer-ignored status or the event type, so older clients keep skipping the event.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Running `review-plan` emits a `REVIEW_RESULT` event whose `schema` is `plan_review_result_v2`
      and whose every persisted finding carries `evidence`, `scenarios`, `block_threshold`, and
      `blocking_enabled`. Oracle: an in-process integration test drives a review with a stub LLM
      runner and asserts on the emitted event JSON via the real sidecar emit path (test-design §3
      producer/consumer shape).
- [ ] `pass3_decide`/`pass3_over_findings` expose the resolved `block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled`
      on each finding. Oracle: a unit test against the real decide functions asserting the fields
      are present with the resolved values.
- [ ] `latest_review_result` reads both a `v1` and a `v2` sidecar file without error, reporting the

- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.

# Jira descriptions render a line break at the end of every soft-wrapped source line

## Context / Problem

Tickets synced into Jira are hard to read: a visible break appears at the end of each fixed-width line of prose. Confirmed live on REB-1581, whose stored description is 27 top-level ADF nodes, ALL of type `paragraph` — a single prose paragraph is split across four consecutive paragraph nodes of 102/108/106/111 chars.

Root cause: `text_to_adf` (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/adf.py:239-251) splits the description on `\n` and wraps EVERY source line in its own ADF paragraph node. Rebar descriptions are authored hard-wrapped at ~95-110 columns, so each soft-wrapped continuation line becomes a separate Jira paragraph.

## Acceptance criteria

- A blank-line-delimited block of soft-wrapped prose renders in Jira as ONE paragraph, with the wrapped lines joined.
- Intentional structure is preserved: blank-line paragraph separation still produces separate paragraphs, and list items / headings stay on their own lines rather than being joined into a run-on.
- No description re-sync churn: the differ must not re-emit a description update on every pass. The identical normalization must be applied to the local value at ALL THREE compare sites (outbound_fields.py:566, inbound_differ.py:209, reconcile_check.py:180-189), following the existing `fit_text_to_adf_limit` precedent.
- Verified live against Jira with a probe ticket, which is then removed from both Jira and rebar.

## Design notes / risks

- Joining soft-wrapped lines is inherently lossy, so the documented round-trip invariant `adf_to_text(text_to_adf(t)) == t` (adf.py:9, pinned by tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_adf.py:694-699) must be restated as idempotency on already-normalized text. This is a deliberate contract change, not test weakening.
- Grouping shrinks the ADF (~8432 -> ~7977 chars on a real ticket), moving where `fit_text_to_adf_limit` truncates. That converges but causes a one-time re-emit for currently-truncated descriptions; check against test_inbound_differ.py:484 and test_reconcile_roundtrip.py:221 (the tarry-amble-bugle clobber class).
- Churn history this must not regress: bug 626d, bug 85a1, and the DIG-4175 plateau (339 outbound updates across batches 7-20 from a trailing `\n\n`).
- Emitting `hardBreak` instead of joining WOULD preserve invertibility (`_handle_hard_break` decodes to `"\n"`), but does not fix the report — a hardBreak is still a per-line break. Rejected.
baseline.summary: Jira sync injects a line break at the end of every soft-wrapped description line

`bridge_fsck` reads `prev_snapshot.json` off disk as its offline Jira oracle and uses the **field values**, so narrowing prev to a key-set (A4-2) would silently degrade its drift classification. Fence it first. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why first
`bridge_fsck.py:306-308` loads the file as `jira_snapshot` and passes `fields=jira_snapshot[key]` into `ObservedJira.PRESENT` at `:344` and `:380`. With `{}` entries, membership still works but every field-based classification degrades. This is an **out-of-band consumer of the file itself**, not of `ctx.prev_snapshot`, so no test that exercises `reconcile_once` would catch it. It reads the **working tree**, so it is unaffected by clone filters.

## Approach
Make the field-dependence explicit: classify on membership where that is sufficient, and where a field value is genuinely required, report the classification as **indeterminate** rather than inferring from an empty dict. Do not silently treat absent fields as absent values.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Against a **key-set** prev fixture (`{jira_key: {}}`), `bridge_fsck` drift classification is
      identical to its classification against the equivalent full-payload fixture for every case that
      does not require a field value, and reports **indeterminate** (never a false drift) for cases
      that do. Tier: **unit** with paired fixtures.
- [x] Against a full-payload prev, behaviour is byte-identical to today (no regression for the
      pre-A4-2 world). Tier: **unit** golden comparison.
- [x] `rebar bridge-fsck` exit code and JSON shape are unchanged for both fixtures. Tier: **CLI
      subprocess**.

## Files
`src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge_fsck.py`, `src/rebar/schemas/bridge_fsck.schema.json`, tests

Scope: S. No dependencies (independent of A1/A2/A3).
baseline.summary: A4-1: fence bridge_fsck's offline drift oracle before prev_snapshot is narrowed

## Summary

The plan-review gate's Pass-2 **agentic verify** step (`verify_branch → verify`, prompt `plan-review-verifier-agentic`, `mode: structured`) truncates its output on finding-rich / complex plans: the model hits the per-call **output** token cap (`finish_reason=length`) before emitting the complete `plan_review_verification` structured result. The truncation aborts the verify step, so every finding it was verifying degrades to **indeterminate** and the whole review returns **verdict = INDETERMINATE** (`verify_failed=true`) instead of a real PASS/BLOCK — even when the find pass produced legitimate, actionable findings.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Take a finding-rich plan — reproduced live on epic `6c9c-811f-6dc4-40e7` (7 ACs, multi-file) and
   task `2711-21bf-ab71-4136` (the reconciler cutover child). Both are in the store.
2. Run `rebar review-plan <id> --output json`.
3. Observe in the result:
   - `coverage.verify_failed = true`
   - `coverage.verify_error = "step 'review@then/verify_branch@then/verify' failed: the model hit
     the token cap before finishing (finish_reason=length) — its output is TRUNCATED; raise
     max_tokens or split the step"`
   - `verdict = INDETERMINATE`, `counts.indeterminate` large (e.g. 30–35), `counts.blocking = 0`.

Frequency: reproducible on complex plans (container epics, multi-file cutover tasks). Smaller plans verify fine, so it scales with finding count / verification output size.

### Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** the verify step completes and returns a full `plan_review_verification`, yielding a
  decisive PASS/BLOCK; a plan is only INDETERMINATE for genuine ambiguity, not because the verifier
  ran out of output budget.
- **Actual:** the verifier's structured output is cut off at the per-call `max_tokens`
  (`finish_reason=length`), the step fails, and the review collapses to INDETERMINATE with all
  candidate findings unverified.

## Root-cause pointers

- The error text is emitted by `src/rebar/llm/structured.py:193-194` (the `length` finish-reason
  guard) via the stop-reason check at `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:456`.
- The step is defined at `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml:130-146`. It already scales
  its **turn/tool-call** budget with `step_budget_per_item: 25` (from bug 59bc), but that governs
  agent turns, **not** the per-call output `max_tokens`.
- The per-call output cap is `cfg.max_tokens` → `model_settings["max_tokens"]`
  (`src/rebar/llm/runner.py:252-259`), defaulting to `DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS`
  (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:266,471,535`). This is exactly the class of bug the find pass already
  hit and fixed — see the comment at `runner.py:254-255`: the default "4096 default — far too small
  for a multi-child container review, whose output truncated (stop_reason=max_tokens)". The verify
  step needs the analogous treatment: scale its output cap with finding count, or split the step.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The agentic verify step no longer truncates on finding-rich plans: re-running
      `rebar review-plan 6c9c-811f-6dc4-40e7` and `rebar review-plan 2711-21bf-ab71-4136` completes
      the verify step (`verify_failed` absent/false) and returns a decisive PASS/BLOCK.
- [x] The verify step's per-call output `max_tokens` scales with the verification workload (e.g.
      derived from finding count / `step_budget_per_item`, mirroring the find-pass fix at
      `runner.py:252-259`) — or the step is split so each sub-call stays under the cap.
- [x] When the output cap is genuinely hit despite scaling, the failure is surfaced distinctly
      (e.g. a dedicated "verifier truncated" signal) rather than silently degrading every finding to
      indeterminate, so operators can tell a truncation from real ambiguity.
- [x] A regression test exercises a synthetic finding-rich verify input and asserts the step
      completes (no `finish_reason=length`) with the scaled cap.
- [x] Non-integration suite green.

## 2026-08-08 resolution evidence

The full review-output-budget suite passed 23 tests, including oversized output above the former default cap and all review gate call sites. Canonical implementation: 30a2-4f2a-dd5a-45a0.
baseline.summary: Plan-review agentic verify step truncates (finish_reason=length) on finding-rich plans -> whole review degrades to INDETERMINATE

baseline.description:
## Context

The plan-review "Pass-2 verify" pass takes the findings the finder raised and makes a decisive
per-finding "is this real?" judgment. There are two problems with how it chunks and where it lives,
and this epic resolves both together with a clean sequencing.

**Problem 1 — token-naive chunking.** The bespoke verifier chunks the findings list by a HARD-CODED
count (`pass2_verify(batch_size=12)`, `passes.py`; `range(0, len(findings), 12)`). It is an arbitrary
mechanical guardrail (introduced in the original plan-review epic 5fd2, commit 2873a916), never
config-driven, token-naive. The workflow-engine gate (the sole verdict producer since the B-RETIRE
cutover, commit 68dc9713) instead does ONE aggregate verify call over all findings — correct for the
common case, but a pathological huge-findings ticket could exceed the model context window where the
count-12 chunk would not. The principled fix is TOKEN-BASED chunking (estimate the verify request vs
the selected model's window — like the Pass-1 finder `sizing.py` machinery already does), splitting
only when needed, NOT a magic count.

**Problem 2 — a surviving second code path.** The B-RETIRE cutover deleted the bespoke full-review
orchestrator (`run_review`, the `gate_engine` flag, the B4 parity harness, `pass4_coach`), but
`pass2_verify` / `verifier_cfg` / `_run_passes` are NOT dead: they back the opt-in **progressive
drift-refresh** probe (`verify.progressive_drift_refresh`, default off → `orchestrator.drift_refresh`
→ `_run_passes` → `pass2_verify`). So there are still TWO verify call sites, which is exactly the "no
two divergent batching rules" hazard. Rather than maintain a shared chunker across both, we **migrate
drift-refresh onto the workflow engine FIRST**, collapsing to a single verify path; the chunking work
then becomes a single-site change.

**Decision — verifier model downgrade becomes a declarative per-step `model:` key.** The bespoke
`verifier_cfg` downgrades the verify pass from the default frontier model (Opus) to a decisive
non-frontier model (Sonnet) UNLESS the operator explicitly chose a model. The workflow verify step
does NOT apply this today (it uses the runner default). We reproduce the downgrade declaratively via
the existing per-step `model:` key (`resolve_model`, WS-D3: step > workflow > cfg) so the workflow
verify step pins Sonnet-by-default with operator override preserved. NOTE: the two historical call
sites sizing against possibly-different models is NOT a blocker for chunking — each site sizes against
its own resolved model and both are correct; and after the migration there is only one site anyway.
Because this makes a per-step `model:` key first-class on a shipped gate workflow, the change must be
reflected in the **visual workflow editor UX**: the per-step model must be editable in the properties
panel and must round-trip through BPMN export/import (today only the workflow-level model is carried,
so editing the workflow in the visual editor could silently DROP a step's model).

## Workstreams (sequenced)

**WS1 — Migrate drift-refresh onto the workflow engine (FIRST), delete the bespoke pipeline.**
- Add a "probe mode" to the plan-review workflow: run find→verify→decide over a restricted criteria
  subset (`_PROBE_CRITERIA = E4, G1G2`) instead of the full registry (a `criteria` allowlist input on
  the finder op, or a dedicated `drift-probe.yaml` reusing the same ops/prompts).
- Expose per-finding decisions + citations in the workflow return shape so the escalation gate can
  inspect `decision` and `citations[].path` against the drifted-file set.
- Rewrite `drift_refresh` to wrap the workflow call; keep the non-LLM orchestration in Python
  (candidate detection, dep re-hash, escalation gate, `refresh_attestation`, synthetic PASS verdict).
- **Pre-deletion parity gate (expand→contract):** before deleting any bespoke code, run BOTH the
  workflow probe and the bespoke `_run_passes` probe over a fixture corpus and assert verdict parity
  (escalate-vs-refresh decision agrees). The deletion is the LAST step of WS1, gated on that parity
  test passing; until it does, the bespoke path stays behind the (already default-off) drift flag as
  the back-out.
- Only after parity holds, DELETE the now-dead bespoke orchestration: `_run_passes`, `pass2_verify`,
  `verifier_cfg`. Keep the genuinely shared helpers (`pass3_decide`, `pass3_over_findings`,
  `verify_instructions`, `coach_instructions`, `render_coach_notes`, `load_move_registry`).

**WS2 — Verifier model downgrade as a per-step `model:` key + visual-editor UX.**
- Pin the workflow verify step's `model:` to the decisive non-frontier verifier (Sonnet) by default,
  preserving operator override (mirrors `verifier_cfg` semantics declaratively via `resolve_model`).
- Surface the per-step `model` field in the visual editor properties panel (a select over the known
  model ladder) and make it round-trip through BPMN export/import so the visual editor never drops a
  step's model on save.
- **BPMN back-compat:** import of a pre-existing BPMN document that lacks the per-step model attribute
  must default gracefully to "no per-step override" (the step falls back to the workflow/cfg model via
  `resolve_model`), never error — legacy exports stay importable.
- Document the per-step `model:` knob in the workflow-authoring + editor docs.

**WS3 — Principled token-based chunking for the (now single) verify path.** (Depends on WS2: WS3
sizes against the per-step `model:` window that WS2 pins/resolves.)
- Replace any count-based batching with a token estimate vs the verify step's resolved model window,
  reusing `sizing.py` `largest_window_tokens(model)` + the `est_tokens` (chars/4) estimator rather
  than a new magic constant or a new tokenizer dependency.
- **Budget formula (explicit):** `budget = floor(largest_window_tokens(model) * HEADROOM)` where
  `HEADROOM` is a named, config-driven knob (`verify.verify_window_headroom`, default `0.8`) — NOT a
  hardcoded literal (so we don't replace `batch_size=12` with a different magic number). A chunk fits
  when `est_tokens(system_prompt + verify_instructions(chunk)) + projected_output(chunk) <= budget`.
- **Projected output (explicit):** `projected_output(chunk) = len(chunk) * PER_FINDING_VERIFY_TOKENS`,
  a named constant sized from the `plan_review_verification` schema's per-finding object (a small
  reserve, ~256 tokens/finding, documented and adjustable) — output scales with finding count, so it
  is reserved per finding, not as a flat constant.
- `<= budget` findings → ONE aggregate verify call (unchanged behavior). `> budget` → minimal
  principled splits that preserve GLOBAL finding enumeration and re-merge by finding `index` (the
  existing merge contract).
- **Single-oversized-finding edge case** (one finding alone exceeds the budget): escalate up the ladder
  starting from the verify step's RESOLVED model — `models_at_or_above(resolved_verify_model)` where
  `resolved_verify_model` is the WS2 per-step `model:` after any operator override (the same value the
  budget is computed against), so the escalation base is unambiguous. If it still does not fit at the
  top of the ladder, mark that finding INDETERMINATE (non-blocking, surfaced) — never silently drop.

**WS4 — Coach-call parity nit (separate task).**
- Bespoke `pass4_coach` returns `[]` with NO LLM call when there are 0 surviving advisories; the
  workflow ALWAYS runs the `coach_notes` prompt step (1 wasted coach call on a clean PASS). Gate the
  workflow `coach_notes` step on `surviving > 0` (a `when:` condition) to match bespoke.

## Design decisions (resolved)

- **Sequencing + dependencies:** WS1 (migration) lands first so chunking is a single-site change and
  "no two divergent batching rules" holds by construction. **WS2 → WS3:** WS3 sizes against the
  per-step `model:` window that WS2 pins, so WS2 lands before WS3. Riskiest slice first: the WS1
  migration (verdict-parity risk) and the WS2 BPMN round-trip (serialization-format risk) are the two
  evidence-gated slices; each ships behind its own parity/round-trip test before the dependent work.
- **Model downgrade = per-step `model:` key** (declarative, operator-overridable); each verify site
  sizes against its own resolved model — no cross-path model reconciliation is required.
- **Editor parity is in scope:** a per-step `model:` on a shipped gate workflow MUST be editable and
  round-trip-safe in the visual editor (properties panel + BPMN), or editing the workflow there would
  regress the gate. Legacy BPMN without the attribute imports gracefully (no per-step override).
- **Token estimator:** reuse `est_tokens` (chars/4) + `largest_window_tokens`; no new dependency. The
  `> budget` test empirically grounds the chars/4 safety margin (asserts estimate + headroom keeps a
  real request under the actual window), so the margin is measured, not assumed.
- **Headroom is a config knob** (`verify.verify_window_headroom`, default `0.8`), not a literal.
- **Merge semantics:** preserve global enumeration; re-merge by finding `index` (existing contract).
- **Oversized single finding:** escalate from the resolved verify model, else INDETERMINATE — never
  silent-drop.
- **Decomposition:** this epic is a parent; WS1–WS4 become child stories/tasks (WS1 the riskiest
  vertical slice), each separately plan-reviewed before it is claimed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **WS1:** `drift_refresh` produces its probe verdict via the workflow engine (find→verify→decide
      over `E4, G1G2`), not `_run_passes`.
- [ ] **WS1:** The drift non-LLM orchestration (candidate detection, dep re-hash, escalation on a
      blocking finding or a finding citing a drifted file, `refresh_attestation`) is preserved.
- [ ] **WS1:** A parity test asserts the workflow probe and the bespoke probe reach the same
      escalate-vs-refresh decision over a fixture corpus BEFORE any bespoke code is removed.
- [ ] **WS1:** The workflow return shape exposes per-finding `decision` + `citations[].path` at the
      granularity the drift escalation gate requires.
- [ ] **WS1:** Once the parity test passes, `_run_passes`, `pass2_verify`, and `verifier_cfg` are
      deleted; no dead bespoke orchestration remains.
- [ ] **WS1:** The shared helpers (`pass3_decide`, `pass3_over_findings`, `verify_instructions`,
      coach/move helpers) remain present and are still imported by the workflow ops.
- [ ] **WS2:** The workflow verify step pins the decisive non-frontier verifier model (Sonnet) by
      default, resolved via the existing per-step `model:` / `resolve_model` path.
- [ ] **WS2:** An explicit operator model override is honored on the verify step (parity with the old
      `verifier_cfg`).
- [ ] **WS2:** The visual editor properties panel lets a user view/edit a step's `model`.
- [ ] **WS2:** A per-step `model` survives a BPMN export → import (visual-edit → save) round-trip
      unchanged; a regression test asserts the round-trip.
- [ ] **WS2:** Importing a legacy BPMN document that lacks the per-step model attribute succeeds and
      falls back to the workflow/cfg model (no error, no per-step override).
- [ ] **WS2:** Authoring + editor docs document the per-step `model:` knob.
- [ ] **WS3:** A token estimate (no magic `batch_size` constant) decides verify chunking, reusing
      `largest_window_tokens` + `est_tokens`.
- [ ] **WS3:** The fit test is `est_tokens(request) + projected_output <= floor(window * HEADROOM)`,
      where `HEADROOM` is the config knob `verify.verify_window_headroom` (default 0.8) and
      `projected_output = len(chunk) * PER_FINDING_VERIFY_TOKENS` (a named per-finding reserve).
- [ ] **WS3:** `<= budget` findings → one aggregate verify call (unchanged behavior).
- [ ] **WS3:** `> budget` findings → minimal principled splits that preserve global enumeration and
      re-merge verifications by finding `index`; a test (via a deterministic window-shrink seam)
      asserts principled splitting, NOT count-12.
- [ ] **WS3:** The `> budget` test also asserts the chars/4 estimate plus headroom keeps a real
      request under the actual model window (the estimator safety margin is grounded, not assumed).
- [ ] **WS3:** A single finding larger than the budget escalates from the resolved verify model via
      `models_at_or_above`; if still too large at the top of the ladder it is marked INDETERMINATE
      (non-blocking, surfaced) — never silently dropped; a test covers this path.
- [ ] **WS4:** The workflow `coach_notes` step is gated on `surviving > 0`; a PASS with 0 surviving
      advisories makes no coach LLM call; a test asserts the call count.
- [ ] Each of WS1–WS4 is a child ticket of this epic, separately plan-reviewed before it is claimed.
- [ ] `make lint` + `make check` + the full test suite pass.
- [ ] Drift-refresh runs entirely through the workflow engine; the bespoke `pass2_verify` /
- [ ] The workflow verify step applies the Sonnet-by-default verifier model (operator override preserved),
- [ ] The workflow verify chunks findings into multiple calls ONLY when the estimated request would exceed
- [ ] No magic `batch_size` constant remains anywhere (the headroom fraction is a named config knob).
- [ ] A PASS with 0 surviving advisories makes no coach LLM call.
baseline.summary: Workflow Pass-2 verify: migrate drift-refresh off bespoke, add per-step model key (editor-surfaced) + principled token-based chunking

# The typed no-region error names AWS_REGION as a fix, and it is not one — MEASURED

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py` raises a typed `LLMConfigError` when no AWS region resolves, and its message instructs the operator to set "a standard AWS region source (AWS_REGION / AWS_DEFAULT_REGION / the active profile's config)". The surrounding docstring says the same. **`AWS_REGION` alone does not work**, so an operator who follows the error message exactly gets the identical error again, with nothing to indicate why.

MEASURED in the production review-bot container (compose-review-bot-1 on i-00880b2c7f13527c5), on **botocore 1.43.62 / boto3 1.43.62** — a NEWER version than the 1.43.58 the original finding was made against, so this is not a stale observation:

    AWS_DEFAULT_REGION genuinely UNSET (env -u), AWS_REGION=us-east-1
      -> boto3.session.Session().region_name is None
    both genuinely UNSET
      -> boto3.session.Session().region_name is None
    AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1, AWS_REGION empty
      -> boto3.session.Session().region_name == 'us-east-1'

So only `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` (or a profile) resolves. This is exactly why `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` sets BOTH `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` and `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` for the review-bot, and its inline comment already records the asymmetry correctly — the compose file is right and the module docstring/error message are wrong, so the two disagree in-tree.

The blast radius is operator time during an outage, on a path that is fail-closed by design: the Bedrock provider refuses to construct without a region, so this message is precisely what a first-responder reads while the LLM-Review gate is not voting. Discovered while verifying the region story for the production cutover [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a].

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py` — the `LLMConfigError` message and the module/function docstring
  that both list `AWS_REGION` as a working source.

Nothing else: no behaviour change, no config change. The pre-check that produces the error is correct as written — it tests boto3's own resolution rather than inventing a default — and must not be altered.

## Approach

Correct the text to name `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` (and rebar's own `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION`) as the sources that resolve, and state explicitly that `AWS_REGION` alone does NOT, with the botocore version the claim was measured against so a future reader can tell whether to re-measure rather than assuming. Do not silently delete the `AWS_REGION` mention: an operator who has already set it needs to be told it is insufficient, which a bare omission does not do.

## Testing

A test asserting the error message does not offer `AWS_REGION` as a standalone remedy would be a change-detector on prose. The oracle worth having instead is the behavioural one this ticket rests on: assert that with only `AWS_REGION` set, region resolution yields nothing and the typed `LLMConfigError` is still raised — so if a future botocore makes `AWS_REGION` work, the test goes GREEN in a way that flags the docstring as re-checkable rather than leaving it quietly wrong.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] the `LLMConfigError` message no longer presents `AWS_REGION` as a sufficient fix, and names
      `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` / `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` as the sources that do resolve.
- [x] the message or docstring states that `AWS_REGION` alone does not resolve, naming the botocore
      version the behaviour was measured on, so the claim is falsifiable rather than folklore.
- [x] the module docstring and the error message agree with each other AND with the existing
      `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` review-bot comment, which already states the asymmetry
      correctly — the in-tree contradiction is gone.
- [x] a test pins the BEHAVIOUR (only-`AWS_REGION` still fails to resolve and still raises the typed
      error), not the prose, and is verified RED by mutating the pre-check away.
baseline.summary: bedrock_model.py tells operators to set AWS_REGION, which does not resolve a region

## Summary

The `external integration (live services)` job of the `external-integration` GitHub Action fails at the pytest step. Every live LLM call raises immediately (0.1s, before any network I/O): `Model requests are not allowed, since ALLOW_MODEL_REQUESTS is False`, surfacing as `test_execution_mode_live.py:44 AssertionError: assert 'failed' == 'succeeded'`.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Trigger the `external-integration` workflow (or run `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1 pytest -m external tests/external`).
2. Observe the live tests fail with the `ALLOW_MODEL_REQUESTS is False` RuntimeError.

Expected: the external tier makes REAL model calls and the live tests pass. Actual: the tier's model calls are blocked before any network I/O; the job fails.

## Root Cause

`tests/conftest.py::_no_live_model_requests` (session-scoped autouse, added 2026-06-29 in commit 9450d0462 / PR #85) sets pydantic-ai's global `models.ALLOW_MODEL_REQUESTS = False` as a CI safety net against accidental billing. The opt-in external tier never re-enables the switch, so all its live calls raise.

Confirmed by guard-commit ancestry vs run outcome: last success (sha aa3ae84ab, 06-16) had the guard ABSENT; both failing runs (07-06, 07-09) have it PRESENT.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The external tier re-enables `ALLOW_MODEL_REQUESTS` (only when opted in via `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL`), guarded for the lean lane where pydantic-ai is absent.
- [ ] The default suite's session safety-net remains intact (non-external tests still see the switch False).
- [ ] A RED->GREEN test in `tests/external/` proves the switch is on for the tier and makes no billable call.
- [ ] `make lint` passes on the change.

# S5 — Gerrit -> GitHub one-way replication (core plugin, non-force, deploy key)

## Why
Make Gerrit the sole writer of GitHub `main`. The core, Apache-2.0, WAR-bundled `replication`
plugin (push) is the right tool — the GerritForge BSL re-license (2025-09-30) touched only
`pull-replication`/multi-site, not this plugin. The non-force / `mirror=false` / deploy-key
choices form a one-way-door replication contract (Gerrit is the only writer; GitHub history is
append-only/fast-forward), captured as an ADR (## Files).

## What
- `replication.config` (`infra/gerrit/replication.config`):
  - `url = git@github.com:navapbc/rebar.git` (scp-style SSH).
  - **`projects = rebar`** (peer-pattern correction — REQUIRED). Because the URL
    hardcodes the single repo and uses no `${name}` interpolation, WITHOUT a `projects =`
    filter the remote matches **every** Gerrit project and tries to push each one's `main`+tags
    into the one GitHub repo. Bind it to exactly the `rebar` project.
  - `push = refs/heads/main:refs/heads/main` + `push = refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*` (NON-force — no
    leading `+`).
  - `mirror=false` (true does a destructive prune of remote refs absent/invisible locally).
  - `replicatePermissions=false` (don't leak `refs/meta/config`); explicit refspecs so
    `refs/changes/*` is never pushed.
  - finite `replicationMaxRetries = 3`; `timeout = 60` (seconds). Values are concrete; they may
    be tuned but must remain finite/bounded — unlimited retries are forbidden (see AC).
- **Crash-safe queue (peer-pattern correction).** Set `[replication] eventsDirectory =
  data/replication` in the plugin's own `replication.config` (NOT `gerrit.config`, where the
  replication plugin silently ignores it) so pending replication
  events survive a Gerrit restart. Without it, the push queue is in-memory and a restart
  mid-queue silently drops pending pushes, leaving the GitHub mirror stale.
- Identity: a single-repo, write-enabled, passphrase-less GitHub deploy key on `navapbc/rebar`
  (currently **0 deploy keys** — S5 adds exactly one; GitHub-side bypass-listing is S6's job).
  Private key from **SSM Parameter Store** at `/rebar/prod/github-deploy-key` (SecureString).
  The replication plugin's SSH client runs as the **Gerrit OS user** (`gerrit2`), so the key +
  SSH config live in `/home/gerrit2/.ssh/`, not root's.
- Provisioning is **as-code and idempotent**: the GitHub deploy-key registration + SSM parameter
  are managed by IaC (Terraform `github_repository_deploy_key` + `aws_ssm_parameter`, or an
  equivalent checked-in idempotent script), and an init/entrypoint hook materialises the key from
  SSM + seeds `known_hosts` **before** the replication plugin can fire its first push.
- **SSM->disk materialisation + ordering (the most common failure mode):** an entrypoint step,
  run as/writing to `gerrit2` and ordered **before** Gerrit's main process starts, must: (1)
  `aws ssm get-parameter --name /rebar/prod/github-deploy-key --with-decryption` -> write
  `/home/gerrit2/.ssh/id_ed25519` owned by `gerrit2`, mode `0600`; (2) `ssh-keyscan github.com
  >> /home/gerrit2/.ssh/known_hosts` (non-interactive first connection); (3) write `~/.ssh/config`
  `Host github.com` with `IdentityFile` pointing at that key. This step **MUST hard-fail
  (fail-closed):** on ANY `aws ssm get-parameter` failure (throttle, IAM-propagation lag,
  network-not-ready) or a missing/empty key value it **exits non-zero and ABORTS Gerrit startup**
  — never continue and let Gerrit start without the deploy key, since that yields silent
  replication failure rather than a loud one.
- **Lifecycle / rotation (one-way-door — in the ADR):** rotation = generate new keypair -> add
  the new GitHub deploy key -> update SSM -> reload the replication plugin -> remove the old key
  (no outage gap). Reproducible from checked-in IaC.
- **Observability:** a persistent alert (not just the one-time check) on `replication_log`
  ERROR / max-retry-exhaustion / `REJECTED_NONFASTFORWARD` — a log-based metric + alarm so
  operators are notified when replication stalls (revoked key, network partition, non-FF
  rejection) instead of GitHub silently going stale.
- **Rollback / kill-switch:** replication disabled in <5 min without a full redeploy by renaming
  the config + reloading the plugin (`mv replication.config replication.config.disabled && ssh
  -p 29418 <gerrit> gerrit plugin reload replication`); if the key is suspected compromised,
  revoke the GitHub deploy key + rotate SSM.

## Scope
In: replication plugin config (incl. `projects=` + crash-safe `eventsDirectory`) + the
deploy-key identity (SSM->disk, `~/.ssh/config`, `known_hosts`) + as-code provisioning + push of
`main`+tags + replication-failure alerting + a documented rollback/kill-switch + the ADR. Out:
the GitHub-side lockdown that makes the mirror read-only (S6). **S5->S6 ordering (do not
ignore):** S5 turns on non-force push **before** S6 forbids direct GitHub writes, so a direct
push to GitHub `main` in that window would diverge it and cause every subsequent non-force
replication to be rejected `non-fast-forward`. Mitigate by (a) deploying S6 in the same
change-set or promptly after, AND (b) the pre-activation prerequisite + non-FF alert below.

### Pre-activation prerequisite
Before enabling replication, verify GitHub `main` is fast-forwardable from Gerrit's HEAD:
`git ls-remote https://github.com/navapbc/rebar refs/heads/main` HEAD must be an ancestor of (or
equal to) Gerrit's `main` HEAD. If GitHub is already ahead, resolve the divergence first.

## Files
- `infra/gerrit/replication.config` — push refspecs, `projects=`, `mirror=false`,
  `replicatePermissions=false`, finite retries, timeout.
- `infra/gerrit/replication.config` — holds the ENTIRE replication config: `[remote "github"]` (url, non-force push refspecs, `replicatePermissions=false`), `projects=rebar`, AND `[replication] eventsDirectory = data/replication`. (NOT `gerrit.config` — the plugin reads only its own `replication.config`.)
- `infra/gerrit/entrypoint.sh` (or init hook) — SSM->disk key materialisation + `ssh-keyscan`
  known_hosts + `~/.ssh/config`, run as `gerrit2` before Gerrit starts.
- `infra/` deploy-key provisioning as-code — Terraform `github_repository_deploy_key` +
  `aws_ssm_parameter` (SecureString at `/rebar/prod/github-deploy-key`) or a checked-in
  idempotent script; includes teardown.
- `infra/` replication-failure alert definition (log-based metric + alarm on `replication_log`
  ERROR / max-retry / `REJECTED_NONFASTFORWARD`).
- `docs/adr/0010-gerrit-github-replication.md` — ADR: plugin choice + BSL rationale, non-force /
  fast-forward-only policy, `mirror=false`, `projects=` single-repo binding, crash-safe
  `eventsDirectory`, deploy-key rotation lifecycle, and the pointer to S6.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A change submitted in Gerrit replicates `main` to `navapbc/rebar` (non-force, fast-forward)
      and tags replicate, verified by `replication_log` exit-0 + `git ls-remote` reflecting the SHA.
- [ ] The remote is bound via `projects = rebar` so ONLY the rebar project replicates
      to the GitHub repo (no other Gerrit project is pushed there), verified by config + log.
- [ ] `refs/changes/*` and `refs/meta/config` are NOT pushed to GitHub (explicit refspecs +
      `replicatePermissions=false`), verified by inspecting GitHub refs after replication.
- [ ] `mirror=false` (no destructive pruning) and `replicationMaxRetries` is finite (e.g. 3,
      never unlimited) with a bounded `timeout`.
- [ ] `[replication] eventsDirectory` is set so the replication queue is crash-safe across a
      Gerrit restart (a restart mid-queue does not silently drop pending pushes).
- [ ] **Non-force is enforced end-to-end:** given a GitHub `main` that cannot be fast-forwarded,
      the push is **rejected** — `replication_log` records `non-fast-forward` (exit non-zero) and
      GitHub history is **unchanged** (guards against a stray `+`).
- [ ] The replication identity is a single-repo write deploy key whose private key is from SSM
      (no plaintext in VCS); on the host `/home/gerrit2/.ssh/id_ed25519` exists owned by
      `gerrit2` mode `0600`, `~/.ssh/config` routes `github.com` to it, `known_hosts` pre-seeded.
- [ ] **The entrypoint SSM-materialisation step hard-fails (fail-closed):** simulating an `aws
      ssm get-parameter` failure (or a missing/empty key) causes the step to exit non-zero and
      Gerrit **does not start** — Gerrit never comes up without the replication deploy key.
- [ ] A pre-activation SSH smoke-test passes before go-live: `sudo -u gerrit2 ssh -T
      git@github.com` returns GitHub's "successfully authenticated" banner (no host-key prompt).
- [ ] Deploy-key + SSM provisioning is reproducible as-code (re-run on a clean host recreates
      key + SSM param + on-disk key + known_hosts, no manual steps); teardown documented.
- [ ] A persistent replication-failure alert fires (in a test) on an ERROR / max-retry /
      `non-fast-forward` entry in `replication_log`, so a silent stall in the S5->S6 window is caught.
- [ ] A rollback/kill-switch works: replication disabled in <5 min via `mv replication.config
      replication.config.disabled` + `gerrit plugin reload replication`, with deploy-key
      revocation as the compromise path.
- [ ] `docs/adr/0010-gerrit-github-replication.md` captures the replication-contract decisions.

## Round-7 remediation
- **Concrete project name (E2):** `projects = rebar` (the project S3 creates on the Gerrit instance) — not a placeholder.

## Round-8 remediation
- **eventsDirectory location (G6):** `[replication] eventsDirectory = data/replication` belongs in `replication.config` (the replication plugin's OWN config file), NOT `gerrit.config` (Gerrit silently ignores the unknown stanza there). Place it in `infra/gerrit/replication.config`.

## Plan-review remediation (Round-11, 2026-06-29)
- BSL scope RESOLVED (Round-12): GerritForge's 2025-09-30 re-license (gitenterprise.me/2025/09/30/re-licensing-gerritforge-plugins-welcome-to-gerrit-enterprise) moved the **pull-replication** and **multi-site** GerritForge plugins to BSL (their Apache-2.0 versions deprecated). The **core `replication` (push) plugin used here ships with Gerrit Core under Apache-2.0** — GerritForge explicitly keeps the widely-used/core plugins Apache-2.0. This epic uses push `replication`, NOT pull-replication or multi-site, so it is unaffected. No legal review needed at build; ADR-0010 records this citation + a 1-line LICENSE-string check of the bundled `replication` jar in the pinned 3.14.1 image as the mechanical confirmation.

Added ACs:
- [ ] ADR-0010 cites the BSL re-license scope (or records the LICENSE-in-image verification) confirming the `replication` push plugin used here is Apache-2.0, not BSL-restricted
baseline.summary: infra: S5 — Gerrit->GitHub one-way replication (core plugin, non-force, deploy key)

baseline.description:
## Reproduction Steps

1. On a CI leg where actionlint is not pre-installed (Linux tiers), `make lint` runs
   `make actionlint-bin`, which downloads `actionlint.tar.gz` from GitHub releases.
2. The download transiently fails (GitHub network blip); `curl` writes no file.
3. Observe: the recipe prints `actionlint: installed …` (FALSE SUCCESS) and returns exit 0
   despite no binary; `make lint` then runs the missing binary → exit 2.

- Expected: a failed/corrupt download aborts `make actionlint-bin` NON-ZERO with a clear
  error (and transient failures are retried), so CI is reliable and the sha256 gate holds.
- Actual: the failure is masked as "installed" (exit 0), turning a transient blip into a
  confusing hard CI failure; the pinned-sha256 verification never actually gates.

## Root cause (proven, /rebar-debug)

`actionlint-bin` (Makefile) chains its `curl` download / `sha256sum -c` verify / `tar` extract with `;` and ends in an unconditional `echo "…installed"`, so any step's failure is ignored and the recipe returns 0. Deterministically reproduced: a forced 404 → recipe exit 0, no binary. Two coupled defects: (1) no `curl` retry (the transient flake trigger); (2) no `set -e`/fail-fast (masks the failure and defeats the sha256 gate).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `make actionlint-bin` exits NON-ZERO and installs no binary when the download fails
      (nonexistent version → HTTP 404). Proving command:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_ci_actionlint_install.py` (RED on the pre-fix recipe).
- [ ] A successful download still verifies (sha256) and installs the binary (exit 0).
- [ ] Transient network errors are retried (`curl --retry`).
- [ ] Fix confined to the `actionlint-bin` recipe (+ the guard test).

Observed: Gerrit-verify run 29619392619, job 88011385914 (py3.12 tier); other tiers passed.
baseline.summary: CI flake: make actionlint-bin masks a failed download as 'installed' (exit 0) — no fail-fast / no retry

## Context
Stamp denormalized author identity (name + email) plus an OPTIONAL `author_id` (referencing a ddbe `identity`) onto EVERY mutating event's envelope, without breaking replay of pre-change events. Substrate for authorship attestation (bde5) and enforcement (3183). Hard-depends on ddbe (identity entity + resolver).

## Why
Authorship certification needs each event to record who wrote it in a replication- and compaction-durable form (denormalized), with an optional link to the rich `identity` entity when one resolves (identity is opt-in).

## What
### 1. Shared attribution helper (`src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py`)
- Extract `_git_config(key, fallback="") -> str` from the existing `author()`;
  reimplement `author()` on it; add `author_email()` = `_git_config("user.email","")`.
  Strip; return fallback on unset / OSError / non-zero exit / timeout; NEVER raise.
- Add `attribution_fields(repo_root=None) -> dict` returning
  `{"author_email": author_email()}` plus `{"author_id": <id>}` ONLY when
  `identity.resolve_current_identity(repo_root=repo_root)` is non-None (ddbe ships
  this keyword-only `(*, repo_root=None)` signature; 4e9d depends on ddbe). Omit
  `author_id` when None.
- CACHE: a module-level dict `_ATTRIBUTION_CACHE: dict[str, dict]` keyed by the
  CANONICAL repo_root string `os.path.realpath(str(repo_root or config.repo_root()))`
  — so `None` (the append_event default) and an explicit path to the SAME physical
  repo resolve to the SAME key (AC5's 'at most once' cannot be split). NOT `lru_cache(maxsize=1)` — a single slot poisons
  multi-repo tests). First call per repo_root does exactly ONE git-email lookup and
  ONE `resolve_current_identity` scan; subsequent calls for that repo_root return the
  cached dict. (Process-scoped; never persisted. A test helper may clear it.)

### 2. Stamp at ALL FOUR envelope-composing sites (verified complete list)
Every site that COMPOSES an event envelope stamps `author` (name) next to `env_id`. Add an optional `attribution: dict | None = None` parameter to each composer and do `if attribution: event.update(attribution)` immediately after the `author` key, so `author_email`/`author_id` land in the envelope. Callers pass `attribution_fields(repo_root)` computed WHERE they already compute/hold `author` and have `repo_root`/tracker in scope. The four sites:
- `_seam.py::append_event` (lines ~219-220) — the majority path (create/edit/link/
  comment/tag/sign/...). Compute `attribution_fields(repo_root)` inline (it already
  receives `repo_root`); include it BEFORE the batch-sink branch so buffered events
  are byte-identical.
- `_commands/txn.py` — `transition_core` (STATUS ~280) and `claim_core` (STATUS ~449,
  EDIT ~468). Add an `attribution: dict | None = None` kwarg to BOTH cores (mirroring
  how `author`/`env_id` are already threaded); the callers `transition_close.py` and
  `claim.py` (which hold `repo_root`) compute it and pass it. Do NOT add a bare
  `repo_root` to the core signatures — thread the ready-made `attribution` dict.
- `_commands/delete.py` — `_write_unlink` (~116) and `_write_event` (~206). Add an
  `attribution: dict | None = None` param to both AND to the intermediate
  `scan_and_write_unlinks` (which sits between `delete_cli` and `_write_unlink` and
  already threads `author`) so the dict reaches `_write_unlink`. The top caller
  (`delete_cli`, which holds repo_root) computes `attribution_fields(...)` once and
  threads it down alongside `author`.
- `_commands/compact.py` — SNAPSHOT composition in `_compact_locked` (~198) and
  `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` (~364), which use `_git_author()`. Compute
  `attribution_fields(repo_root)` alongside and merge it, so SNAPSHOTs carry
  attribution too (otherwise a compacted ticket's fold loses it).

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE (5th composer, deliberately excluded): the inbound Jira reconciler composes its OWN envelopes via `_write_event_file()` /`_event_meta()` in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py` (~214, called by `apply_inbound.py`/`apply_inbound_records.py`/`applier.py`). Inbound events attribute to the EXTERNAL Jira author, NOT the local git user/identity — applying local `attribution_fields` there would be semantically WRONG. External-author attribution is the job of the provider-mapping stories (264f outbound, 2f13 inbound ghost). 4e9d covers the four LOCAL-write composers only.

### 3. Replay back-compat (reducer surfaces PRESENT-ONLY, matching where `author` lives)
Surface present-only (mirrors `source_*`) at the SAME structural location each processor already puts `author` — verified sites:
- `process_create` (_processors.py:59) → TOP-LEVEL `state["author_email"]`/
  `state["author_id"]` present-only (the ticket-author attribution bde5 reads).
- `process_comment` (:248) → on the per-comment `_entry` dict.
- `process_revert` (:374) → on the per-revert record.
- `process_signature` (:494) → on the signature record.
(`process_edit`/`process_status` do NOT stamp author; NOT touched.) A pre-change event (no author_email/author_id) reduces BYTE-IDENTICAL — no new keys anywhere. SNAPSHOT restores compiled_state verbatim (additive; older reducers ignore unknown keys) — no special handling.

## Scope
In: helpers + repo-keyed cache; stamping at the 4 composer sites via the `attribution` param; reducer present-only surfacing at the 4 processors; back-compat
+ every-path + cache tests. Out: signing/verifying (bde5), key lifecycle (e165),
enforcement (3183). `author_id` is populated, NOT verified/required here.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] EVERY LOCAL mutating path stamps `author_email` into the raw stored event
  (inbound Jira-reconciler events are excluded by design — see scope note; their
  author is the external Jira user, handled by 264f/2f13): a test
  exercises `create` (append_event), `comment` (append_event), a `claim`/`transition`
  (txn.py), a `delete`/archive (delete.py), and a `compact` SNAPSHOT exercising BOTH
  compact.py paths (a threshold `_compact_locked` compaction AND a
  `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` rebuild), asserting each resulting event JSON
  contains `author_email` — proving all four
  composers stamp it, not just append_event.
- [ ] With a current identity set (`rebar identity use <id>`): a CREATE carries
  `author_id == <id>` in the raw event AND top-level reduced state surfaces
  `author_id`/`author_email`. With NO identity resolved: `author_id` is ABSENT from
  both the raw event and reduced state (test both branches).
- [ ] Back-compat: a hand-authored event stream WITHOUT author_email/author_id reduces
  without error to compiled state containing NEITHER key anywhere (top-level or
  sub-records) — byte-identical to pre-change — asserted by diffing the reduced dict.
- [ ] `author_email()` returns `""` (never raises) when `git config user.email` is
  unset or the git call errors — tested by forcing the subprocess to fail.
- [ ] Caching: across N>=3 sequential writes in one process for one repo_root, BOTH
  the git-email lookup AND `resolve_current_identity` run at most once each (NOT
  vacuous: N must be >=3 so 'at most once' is a real reduction from N) — asserted with
  TWO independent call-counters.

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py` (_git_config + author_email + attribution_fields + repo-keyed cache + append_event stamping)
- `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py` (attribution kwarg on transition_core + claim_core)
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` (caller: compute attribution_fields(repo_root), pass to transition_core)
- `src/rebar/_commands/claim.py` (caller: compute attribution_fields(repo_root), pass to claim_core)
- `src/rebar/_commands/delete.py` (attribution param on _write_unlink + _write_event + scan_and_write_unlinks passthrough)
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` (stamp SNAPSHOT envelopes in _compact_locked + rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log)
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` (present-only surfacing: top-level at process_create; per-entry at comment/revert/signature)
baseline.summary: identity: event attribution (name+email + optional author_id) + replay back-compat

baseline.description:
## Context

`project.review-phase-boundaries` runs advisory. `.rebar/criteria_routing.json:82-87` holds `"default_posture": "advisory"`, `"block_threshold": 0.9`, `"blocking_enabled": false`.

The sampling already recorded on this ticket (2026-08-05) covered 51 in-scope reviews and found 6 findings with a maximum author impact of **0.5**, against a 0.90 block threshold. That measurement settles one thing decisively: **flipping `blocking_enabled` at the current 0.90 threshold would change nothing** — no observed finding has ever come within 0.4 of the line. So "enable blocking" and "keep advisory" are not the real choice; the real choice is what threshold, if any, makes this criterion load-bearing without punishing authors.

**Operator direction (2026-08-09):** do not pick a posture from the current sample. First assess the HISTORICAL IMPACT of lowering the threshold — i.e. counter-factually replay what would have been blocked at candidate thresholds — and choose from that evidence.

A caveat carried forward from the existing sampling comment, which the analysis must resolve rather than inherit: the 6 findings were never confirmed against false positives. A threshold chosen from a finding set that includes false positives would block authors on reviewer noise.

Related and directly instructive: ticket `f391`'s analysis of the `undecomposed` axis showed that this codebase's persisted `*-REVIEW_RESULT.json` sidecar stream under `.tickets-tracker/` supports exactly this kind of counter-factual replay at **zero LLM cost**, and that an impact floor applied without regard to grade silently makes a low-graded finding block like a high-graded one. Use the same replay instrument here, and check for the same failure mode.

## Plan

Replay the persisted review corpus and, for each candidate `block_threshold`, compute what WOULD have blocked: how many changes, on which tickets, and with what author-visible impact scores. Then audit the findings that a candidate threshold would newly make blocking — every one of them — for false positives, since those are precisely the cases that would have stopped an author.

Report the trade-off curve rather than a single number, then record a posture decision (threshold value and `blocking_enabled`) justified by that curve.

Do NOT change `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` in this ticket. Landing a routing/posture change is a separate reviewable change, and coupling the analysis to the config edit would make the evidence hard to review on its own merits.

## Testing

This is an analysis ticket: its deliverable is a recorded readout, not code. Verification is that the numbers are reproducible — state the corpus location, the replay method, and the exact denominator, so a second reader can re-derive the curve. Never estimate a rate whose denominator is not reachable from the checkout; say so instead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The counter-factual replay is recorded: for each candidate `block_threshold`, the number of
      reviews and distinct tickets that would have been blocked, with the corpus size and the exact
      denominator stated.
- [ ] Every finding that a candidate threshold would newly make BLOCKING is audited for false
      positives, and the false-positive rate among them is reported.
- [ ] The readout states whether impact is applied grade-independently for this criterion (the
      failure mode `f391` found on the `undecomposed` axis), since a grade-independent floor would
      make any threshold choice misleading.
- [ ] A posture decision is recorded — threshold value and whether `blocking_enabled` flips —
      justified by the curve and the false-positive audit, not by the 51-review sample alone.
- [ ] The readout has a Limits section separating verified observations from what the reachable
      corpus could not answer.
- [ ] `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` is UNCHANGED by this ticket; any posture change is filed as a
      separate follow-up ticket linked `discovered_from`.
baseline.summary: Assess historical impact of lowering the project.review-phase-boundaries block threshold

## Summary
edit --title="" silently clobbers the title; the identical clobber class was already fixed for --description (bug e78f-9f79) and --parent, but not --title.

## Reproduction Steps
(verified on installed 0.4.0 == HEAD, temp store)
1. T=$(rebar create task "real title" | tail -1)
2. rebar edit $T --title="" -> exit 0
3. rebar show $T | jq .title -> ""
4. Contrast: rebar create task "" -> Error: title must be non-empty (exit 1); rebar edit $T --description="" -> Error (citing e78f-9f79).

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: empty --title rejected like empty --description (and like create's title validation).
- Actual: empty title accepted, producing "" titles that break list/search ergonomics.

## Source
src/rebar/_engine/ticket-edit.sh — description guard :122-127 (the model), parent guard :156; no equivalent in the --title arm.

## Fix direction
Mirror the e78f-9f79 guard for --title (validated diff in the implementation-notes comment).

## Suggested RED test
edit --title="" -> exit 1, title unchanged; edit --title="new" still works.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Empty --title rejected with a clear error naming the rule (RED test first)
- [ ] Non-empty title edits unchanged
- [ ] Sweep ticket-edit.sh for any other empty-value clobber arms (tags? assignee has legit clear semantics — document which empties are intentional)

## Context
The completed Gerrit Verified latency RCA optimized the macOS completion path, but Ubuntu jobs still occupy scarce org-wide runners for 11-14 minutes and contribute to queue contention. Follow-up questions identify three candidate levers: replace repeated Pandoc corpus rendering with static expected results plus a smaller boundary test, remove redundant work from the exhaustive 1,440-minute bridge cadence proof, and determine whether expensive Jira DC-oriented default-tier tests can move out of the per-change hot path while retaining fast unit coverage. The genuinely live tests/external/live_jira_dc suite is already excluded from Gerrit Verified by the `not external` selector and runs in its dedicated harness; moving that suite again would save zero. This work must preserve behavioral coverage and must not use extra parallel jobs or unchanged aggregate runner usage.

## Plan
- Build a dated Ubuntu runner-time dossier from final post-remediation run 31752047186, pytest duration logs, workflow routing, and focused local runtime experiments.
- For Pandoc and render_unit, map every current assertion to the code boundary it exercises. Include both full-corpus consumers: test_wiki_render_corpus.py (~884 pass-1 subprocesses plus additional passes) and test_wiki_render_hardening.py (~1,768 subprocesses for byte-equivalence). Compare static golden fixtures, a bounded real-Pandoc contract sample, and full-corpus external execution using defect-seeded experiments to detect any coverage loss. Treat the pinned Pandoc-version-to-output coupling as an explicit external boundary. Any accepted golden fixture must identify its Pandoc version and binary fingerprint, provide a documented regeneration command, and include a fast drift assertion that fails when the installed Pandoc version differs. The full real-Pandoc corpus must remain in the scheduled external-integration workflow as the revalidation destination, including after pin changes.
- For the bridge cadence test, discriminate between the cost of the 1,440 arithmetic checks and invariant workflow YAML I/O; prefer hoisting invariant I/O if it preserves the exhaustive proof.
- Confirm the live Jira DC suite routing, then inventory the Jira DC-oriented harness-free tests that actually execute in the default tier. Identify which, if any, exercise a genuine external boundary rather than our code, and map any proposed lane move to faster existing or new unit contracts before implementation.
- Compare each candidate with current practice in at least three named, popular, actively maintained OSS projects. Consensus means at least two-thirds of the surveyed projects, rounded up, use the practice and no surveyed project documents rejecting it for coverage or reliability; otherwise route the proposal to operator disposition.
- Search tracker history for prior acceptance or rejection of every proposal.
- Measure deterministic savings with paired before/after runs under the same environment. Report per-cell elapsed-time delta, sum the deltas across the three Ubuntu Python cells as runner-minutes freed per Verified run, and report the baseline-normalized Ubuntu occupancy reduction as `sum(cell deltas) / sum(baseline cell durations)`. This occupancy metric is the queue-pressure capacity effect; do not infer queue-wait reduction from one run. If GitHub job records expose queued/start timestamps for a multi-run sample, report the observed wait distribution separately with sample size and confidence, without attributing causality.
- Record a confirmed RCA and measured runner-time/wall-time savings. Create linked implementation tickets only for remediations that preserve coverage; under the operator standing approval, implement those meeting the defined OSS-consensus bar through Gerrit. Back-out for any merged CI behavior change is a Gerrit revert restoring the prior full per-change execution; the scheduled full-corpus lane remains available as the coverage oracle during diagnosis.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every Ubuntu operation or test phase over 30 seconds in the final sample is attributed to a specific mechanism and measured with a focused baseline.
- [x] The Pandoc corpus proposal covers both full-corpus consumers and has an assertion-level coverage map plus A/B runtime estimate.
- [x] The render_unit proposal has an assertion-level coverage map and A/B runtime estimate.
- [x] The bridge-cadence proposal has an assertion-level coverage map and A/B runtime estimate.
- [x] [operator-attested] The live Jira DC routing is recorded with workflow citations.
  provenance: environment=production repository workflow definition and GitHub Actions logs; principal=RebarBotNava under operator authorization; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=static-analysis — committed selectors and dedicated external-workflow routing were inspected without invoking Jira DC.
- [x] The default-tier Jira DC-oriented proposal has an assertion-level coverage map and A/B runtime estimate.
- [x] Each proposal cites tracker history.
- [x] Each proposal cites at least three named popular actively maintained OSS projects and applies the defined consensus rule.
- [x] No accepted remediation removes an assertion, behavioral equivalence class, OS/Python cell, or external boundary.
- [x] Every moved coverage boundary has an explicit destination and schedule.
- [x] Every accepted golden fixture identifies the exact Pandoc version and binary fingerprint that produced it.
- [x] Every accepted golden fixture includes a documented runnable regeneration command.
- [x] Every accepted golden fixture has a fast automated version-drift assertion and a scheduled full real-Pandoc revalidation lane.
- [x] Runner-minute savings are quantified without counting parallel matrix time as critical-path wall time.
- [x] Queue-pressure capacity savings are reported as runner-minutes freed per run and baseline-normalized Ubuntu occupancy reduction; any observed queue-wait distribution is reported separately and not presented as causal.
- [x] Every consensus-backed remediation is implemented on a linked ticket.
- [x] Every implemented remediation passes repository gates and Gerrit LLM-Review +1 plus Verified +1 before merge.
- [x] Every implemented remediation merges before this task closes.
- [x] Non-consensus or coverage-risking proposals are summarized with evidence and left for operator disposition.
- [x] The back-out path for each merged remediation is recorded as a Gerrit revert restoring full per-change execution.
baseline.summary: Reduce Ubuntu CI runner occupancy without losing test coverage

baseline.description:
# Context

Discovered while fixing 79d6 (financial-maroon-toucan, Gerrit 1658), which unguarded the region env so every live-LLM matrix arm resolves a Bedrock region.

`tests/external/test_completion_banking_behavior_0707.py` sets `_live_llm_ready = _live_llm.live_llm_ready()` — a probe that answers "is the credential present for the provider THIS ARM resolves from the standard model class". But the module bypasses model-class resolution and pins `_MODEL = "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"`. On the anthropic and openai arms the probe says READY (an Anthropic/OpenAI key exists) while every cell actually calls Bedrock — an arm that carries no AWS credential, because the OIDC step is gated `if: matrix.provider == 'bedrock'`.

A module's readiness sentinel must agree with the model it pins. Here it cannot.

It is the ONLY bedrock-pinned module in the `llm_live` lane: `test_bedrock_cache_live.py` is also bedrock-pinned but carries no `_live_llm_ready` sentinel (plain `external` + its own `REBAR_LIVE_BEDROCK` opt-in), so it runs in the complement job and is unaffected.

# Disposition — option (b) is REJECTED; do not re-litigate

**Un-gating the OIDC step to all arms is rejected**: it hands AWS credentials to arms holding third-party API keys (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`), widening the blast radius of the scoped Bedrock CI role for ZERO coverage gain — it would call the same model from three arms and learn the same fact three times. The OIDC step stays gated to `matrix.provider == 'bedrock'`.

Also rejected: un-pinning `_MODEL` so the eval follows each arm. The pin exists to hold the model fixed while reproducing bug 0707; unpinning turns a single-model regression reproduction into a 3x-spend cross-provider eval, which is a different test with a different purpose.

**Approved: option (a) — a provider-aware readiness sentinel.** Test-harness correctness with zero credential-surface change.

# Plan

1. `tests/external/_live_llm.py`: give `live_llm_ready()` an optional `required_provider`
   argument. When supplied, readiness additionally requires the arm's `configured_provider()`
   to MATCH it, so a module that pins a provider is ready only on the arm that runs it.
   Add a `skip_unless_provider(provider)` mark factory whose reason names the mismatch
   (module pins X, arm resolves Y) so the skip is VISIBLE, not silent. Purely additive:
   the no-argument call and the module-level `skip_without_live_llm` are unchanged, so the
   seven modules that do not pin a provider keep their exact current behaviour.
2. `tests/external/test_completion_banking_behavior_0707.py`: pass the pinned provider to the
   sentinel and apply `skip_unless_provider("bedrock")` on both tests.
3. Regression test for the invariant.

Canary-safe: the all-skip canary fires only when collected>=1 and executed==0. On a non-bedrock arm the other `llm_live` modules still execute, so the arm stays green for the right reason.

# Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1 — A module that pins a provider is `_live_llm_ready` only on the arm that resolves
  that provider; on other arms it skips with a reason naming both the pinned provider and the
  arm's resolved provider.
- [x] AC2 — `tests/external/test_completion_banking_behavior_0707.py` uses that gate for
  `bedrock`, and modules that pin nothing are behaviourally unchanged.
- [x] AC3 — A test pins the invariant (a pinned-provider module is not ready on a mismatched
  arm, and is ready on the matching arm when its credential is present), and the rejection of
  option (b) is recorded on this ticket.
baseline.summary: Bedrock-pinned live-LLM modules lack AWS credentials on non-bedrock arms

## Summary
The store's `git commit` path (`_git_commit`, `_git_commit_paths`, and the UU-recovery commit in `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`) lacked the object-DB transient retry that `_git_add` has. A `git commit` WRITES new tree + commit loose objects via git's same `create_tmpfile` path as `git add`; on a CI-runner FS that intermittently fails ("unable to create temporary file"). `_git_commit` retried only index.lock + "could not parse HEAD", so this transient surfaced as a hard StoreError, dropping a concurrent locked `append_event` write.

This is the intermittent failure of `tests/interfaces/store/test_enrich_drain_prune_concurrency.py::test_enrich_queue_prune_never_drops_concurrent_locked_writes` (swallowed_write_raises=1, lost=1). ~4% reproduce rate locally; seen on CI ubuntu py3.12.

## Root Cause (proven)
`_git_add` composed an object-DB retry (`_TRANSIENT_ADD_MARKERS` loop); `_git_commit` / `_git_commit_paths` / UU-recovery commit did not — asymmetric coverage left when the object-DB add retry was added (edf7/vocal-dip-robin). Proven by injection: injecting the object-DB signature into the FIRST `git commit` makes `stage_and_commit` RAISE (no retry) and lose the event; the same signature into `git add` self-heals; index.lock into `git commit` self-heals.

## Fix
Factor the object-DB retry into a shared `_with_transient_add_retry(run_once)` helper and apply it to `_git_commit`, `_git_commit_paths`, and the UU-recovery commit (and refactor `_git_add` to use it). Add a live RED test (`test_single_write_retries_transient_commit_odb_failure`) that injects the object-DB signature on the first commit and asserts self-heal.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_git_commit`, `_git_commit_paths`, and the UU-recovery commit retry the object-DB
  transient (via `_with_transient_add_retry`). Proof: `pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_event_append_transient_retry.py`.
- [ ] A RED test asserts a commit object-DB transient self-heals; it fails if the retry is
  removed from `_git_commit` (mutation-checked).
- [ ] The concurrency test passes across repeated runs (post-fix failure rate ~0 vs ~4% pre-fix).
- [ ] make lint + typecheck pass; no existing test weakened.
baseline.summary: Store git commit drops a concurrent locked write on an unretried object-DB FS transient (enrich-prune flake)

Largest cluster, unanticipated: the bash dispatcher is GONE (no `*.sh`, no `ticket_txn.py`) yet ~16 module docstrings still narrate 'Ports ticket-X.sh', 'byte-parity with the dispatcher arm', 'Tier E cutover', 'until E7'. ~126 lines, confirmed stale rather than merely historical. `docs/bash-migration.md` is the existing home.

Verified stale and confirmed individually: `_commands/txn.py:3-8` cites a shim that does not exist; `_engine_support/reads.py:15-19` states a false reason for the module's location; `_commands/leaf.py:9-12` says tag/untag/archive are 'tracked as child tickets' while all three are defined in that same file; `_engine_support/__init__.py:7-9` cites compat shims that do not exist; `_io/__init__.py:14` says the import side 'lands in a later sub-task' six lines above the line importing it; `_cli/_help.py:3-8` is truncated mid-clause (introduced by 3a53e202a7).

`_engine_support/reads_cli.py` explains the same unknown-option rule in five near-identical blocks — a ->CODE fix (extract one helper) rather than a comment edit.

Headroom: `_commands/init.py` 799 -> ~782 (18 lines of margin), `_cli/_llm_commands.py` 789 -> ~778 (22) — both WITHOUT any code extraction. The module-size pressure in these two files is partly caused by comments explaining previous module-size splits.

New ADR proposed: 'Explicit init over silent-implicit tracker creation' — a prior-art survey (git-bug/git-appraise vs git-issue/bugs-everywhere/Fossil) stated in four places.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination
- [x] The shard's do_not_move list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands
- [x] Verified-stale comments are corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only where obsolete
- [x] No load-bearing invariant is lost

## CORRECTION (plan-review BLOCK, criteria F1/E6)

AC3/AC4 rested on a subjective correct-vs-delete judgment with no decision rule or observable check. Superseded below with the parent 373f disposition vocabulary and a recorded-reason rule for every deletion.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above)

- [x] Every substantial in-scope comment unit is dispositioned into exactly one of the parent
      373f labels: RELOCATE (to docs/bash-migration.md, an ADR, or a ticket, reduced to a
      one-line citation), DELETE, KEEP, DO_NOT_MOVE, or CORRECT-IN-PLACE.
- [x] Decision rule for CORRECT-vs-DELETE: a stale comment that documents CURRENT runtime
      behavior / a live invariant is CORRECTED in place; a comment is DELETED only when the thing
      it describes no longer exists (referenced artifact removed, or the statement is superseded).
      For each DELETE, the reason (referenced-artifact-gone / superseded) is stated in the commit
      body or a ticket comment, so no comment documenting current behavior is removed without a
      recorded reason.
- [x] The dead bash-dispatcher narration (~16 module docstrings citing 'Ports ticket-X.sh',
      'byte-parity with the dispatcher arm', 'Tier E cutover', 'until E7' — the bash dispatcher
      and ticket_txn.py no longer exist) is relocated to docs/bash-migration.md where still
      useful, or deleted as stale with the reason recorded.
- [x] The individually-confirmed stale comments are CORRECTED or DELETED per the rule above:
      `_commands/txn.py:3-8` (cites a non-existent shim), `_engine_support/reads.py:15-19`
      (false location reason), `_commands/leaf.py:9-12` (tag/untag/archive defined in-file, not
      'tracked as child tickets'), `_engine_support/__init__.py:7-9` (non-existent compat shims),
      `_io/__init__.py:14` (contradicted 6 lines below), `_cli/_help.py:3-8` (truncated clause).
- [x] The `_engine_support/reads_cli.py` five near-identical unknown-option blocks are collapsed

      lint/type pragmas (`# noqa`, `# type: ignore`, `# ruff:`, `# tickets-boundary-ok`) and
      test-introspected docstrings are DO_NOT_MOVE.
- [x] Any new ADR (e.g. 'Explicit init over silent-implicit tracker creation') EXISTS and is
      committed before any comment citing it is collapsed.

- [x] No behaviour change: the full test suite AND `make lint` / `make typecheck` pass unchanged.
