## Context

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py` is the shared Jira-family inbound mapper. Story J7 seals `adapters/jira/` and `adapters/jira_datacenter/` against importing one another, while the Data Center backend deliberately delegates to the same mapper as Cloud. Keeping the mapper at the reconciler package root is therefore what preserves the bidirectional adapter seal.

The neutrality sweep in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py` exempts this one file because it necessarily carries the Cloud ADF lazy-load literal. The existing wording presents the exemption as temporary relocation debt, which is no longer the intended architecture.

## Operator decision

Do not move or split `inbound_fields.py`. Keep the J7 adapter seal strict and retain the single sweep exemption as a documented architectural cost.

Rejected:
- Moving to `adapters/jira/` would create a Data Center-to-Cloud adapter import.
- Moving to `adapters/jira_family/` would violate the mirror rule because root-core consumers cannot import that layer; routing the ADF dependency through a path-string would evade rather than satisfy the gate.
- Giving Data Center a separate mapper would duplicate behavior.
- Relaxing J7 or splitting the module adds a seam without removing the underlying constraint.

## Plan

Rewrite the exemption comment, test docstrings, and failure diagnostic in `test_backend_neutrality.py` so they state the durable reason: the root location allows both Jira adapters and the root-core consumers to share one mapper without opening a sibling-adapter edge or laundering the Jira-family boundary. Remove the obsolete claim that ticket 556a will relocate the module.

This is a static explanatory correction only. Production code, imports, and gate behavior remain unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The neutrality sweep explains why `inbound_fields.py` is deliberately rooted and exempt: Data Center and Cloud share it while J7 forbids sibling-adapter imports.
- [x] The explanation states why `adapters/jira_family/` is not a compliant destination for the current module and consumers.
- [x] The sweep diagnostic no longer describes the exemption as temporary follow-up work.
- [x] The existing neutrality tests pass unchanged in behavior.
- [x] No production file, import path, or sweep membership changes.
baseline.summary: Keep inbound_fields.py rooted; correct the neutrality-sweep exemption rationale

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
The bounded Agent operation [rebar:kingsize-unfair-blackbird] changes two observable compatibility seams by design: successful retries now expose whole-run usage, and Pydantic wraps retry exhaustion in broad `UnexpectedModelBehavior`. Rebar consumers require one truthful operation row, typed resolution behavior, consumed-so-far diagnostics, and complete final-failure artifacts (`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:362-381`, `src/rebar/llm/run_failure.py:48-157`, `src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:491-642`).

## Approach
Treat the Pydantic Agent run as the accounting unit. Project its aggregate `RunUsage` once through `_extract_usage`, `agent_call`, gate aggregates, and the durable JSONL row; never subtract rejected output attempts or emit per-attempt rows. On exhaustion, walk the standard Python cause chain of the terminating `UnexpectedModelBehavior` (empirically grounded against pydantic-ai 1.107.x in the grounding comment): a VALIDATION-failure exhaustion reaches the identical Rebar `StructuredOutputError` at `UnexpectedModelBehavior.__cause__` -> `ToolRetryError` -> `ModelRetry.__cause__`, because S2's `pai_output.output_function` raises `ModelRetry(str(err)) from err` so that exact object survives on the chain — S3 re-raises THAT identical object, preserving its subtype. A repeated-truncation/concision exhaustion carries NO Rebar object (S2's `concision_guard` raises a bare `ModelRetry(CONCISION_INSTRUCTION)` with no `__cause__`), so the DEFINED chain-absent fallback constructs a fresh `UnretryableOutputError`. Leave an unrelated `UnexpectedModelBehavior` (no 'Exceeded maximum output retries' marker) unchanged. Capture the complete final provider response only at terminal failure through the existing opt-in artifact policy; retry-wire omission never mutates stored messages.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` — whole-run usage extraction and compatibility result.
- `src/rebar/llm/run_failure.py`, `src/rebar/llm/failure.py` — exact cause-chain restoration and sanitized consumed counters.
- `src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py`, `src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py` — one-row success/failure recording and complete final artifact timing.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py`, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` — verify existing aggregates retain the complete operation counters without a parallel attempt field.
- Focused usage, failure-matrix, hardening, artifact, and plan-review tests.

## Testing
- Successful invalid-then-valid output with attempt usage 5 and 7 reports requests=2 and output_tokens=12 in memory, aggregate telemetry, and one JSONL row.
- Validation and output-size exhaustion restore their exact Rebar objects; an unrelated upstream exception remains untouched.
- Terminal failure preserves consumed requests/tokens and stores only the complete final response when artifact capture is enabled.
- Historical rows and pricing remain compatible because no new core usage field is introduced.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A successful two-attempt Agent run reports the sum of both attempts in `_usage`, Pass-1 aggregate telemetry, and exactly one durable JSONL row; verified by focused usage and plan-review tests.
- [x] Validation exhaustion re-raises the IDENTICAL Rebar `StructuredOutputError` object (same `id()`, found by walking the terminating `UnexpectedModelBehavior` cause chain); a repeated-truncation/output-size exhaustion — whose concision `ModelRetry` carries no Rebar object — surfaces a freshly-constructed `UnretryableOutputError` (the defined chain-absent fallback); and an unrelated `UnexpectedModelBehavior` remains untranslated; verified by identity, chain-absent-fallback, and negative-guard tests.
- [x] Failure diagnostics retain consumed requests, tool calls, and provider-reported tokens without creating a fictional usage value for a call that reported none; verified by the failure-matrix suite.
- [x] When parse-failure artifacts are enabled, only terminal failure writes an artifact and that artifact contains the complete final provider response even when the retry wire omitted an earlier response; verified by artifact-content and file-count tests.
- [x] Existing pricing and usage reports remain byte-compatible apart from the approved higher counters after successful retry; verified by historical-row and pricing fixtures.
- [x] `_usage` and usage JSONL contain no `candidate_requests` or other competing request-budget field; verified by schema assertions.
baseline.summary: RP-01 S3 — Preserve usage, failure, and artifact contracts at the Pydantic boundary

baseline.description:
## Observation

Found while proving the root cause of bug 4bf4 (jscpd live-clone fixture below the token floor). Not a blocker for 4bf4 — filed so the observation is not lost.

`rebar.metrics.analyzers._jscpd.run_jscpd` reads `statistics.total.{clones,percentage}` and returns them verbatim. When **no file in the scanned tree clears jscpd's `--min-tokens` floor (default 50)**, jscpd 5.0.14 returns:

    {"clones": 0, "percentage": 0.0, "sources": 0, "lines": 0, "tokens": 0}

That is byte-identical in the two fields rebar reads to a tree that genuinely has no duplication. So `rebar metrics` would report "0% duplication" for a tree jscpd never actually examined.

## Why it may matter

The project already holds the invariant that jscpd failing to answer must surface as `Unavailable` rather than zero — see `tests/unit/metrics/test_jscpd_dup_heldout.py::test_failed_jscpd_is_unavailable_not_zero`, and 4bf4's own AC3: "a metric that reads 0 when it means 'I cannot tell' is worse than `unavailable`". `sources == 0` is arguably that same case, and is currently reported as a confident zero.

## Why it was NOT fixed under 4bf4

It needs a judgment call rather than a bugfix, and 4bf4's proven root cause was solely the test fixture. Options:

1. **Treat `sources == 0` as unavailable.** Honest, matches the existing invariant. But it
   turns a legitimately-tiny or empty tree from "0% duplication" into "unavailable", which
   some callers may find noisier. Note `statistics.total.sources` is absent from the minimal
   report shape used by `tests/unit/metrics/test_jscpd_dup.py::test_parse_statistics_total`,
   so the check must be `.get("sources")` and fire only on an explicit `0`.
2. **Leave as-is.** On any real repository at least one file clears a 50-token floor, so
   `sources > 0` in practice and the ambiguity never materializes.
3. **Surface `sources` alongside the totals** so callers can decide, without changing the
   current availability semantics.

No option is obviously correct without a product view on what the duplication metric should say about a tree too small to measure. Recommend option 1 or 3 if picked up.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A decision is recorded on which of the three options applies.
- [x] If option 1 or 3: duplication over a tree where no source clears the token floor is
      distinguishable from genuine zero duplication, with a regression test.
- [x] `tests/unit/metrics/test_jscpd_dup.py::test_parse_statistics_total` continues to pass
      unmodified (its report fixture omits `sources`).

## Duplicate resolution evidence

This ticket duplicates dental-catty-dorado. That closed ticket selected option 1: an explicit statistics.total.sources == 0 result is Unavailable, while a report that omits sources preserves the existing genuine-zero behavior. Merged commit aeb4e036a6ba431e85837acec9d47188f4df0038 contains the exact guard and held-out regression test. Its recorded experiments distinguish an unmeasured tree (sources: 0) from a measured no-duplication tree (sources: 2, clones: 0, percentage: 0.0), and the mutation check reintroduced the ambiguous confident-zero result. Current origin/main contains that commit and behavior.
baseline.summary: jscpd duplication reports 0% when no source clears the token floor, indistinguishable from genuine zero

baseline.description:
## Client report
While one rebar gate invocation was running, a sibling agent executed `uv tool install --force`. uv garbage-collected the release directory backing the active process, and the gate later crashed with `ImportError` / `FileNotFoundError`. Expected behavior: an invocation resolves one installed release and keeps all code/resources it needs reachable for its entire lifetime, even when another process force-reinstalls the tool.

The reported explanation is a hypothesis until reproduced and traced. Investigation must distinguish uv installation semantics, Python import timing, subprocess/module resource lookup, and any rebar-controlled launcher or snapshot seam.

## Plan
- Reproduce with two synchronized real processes: pause an invocation after startup but before a late import/resource read, force-reinstall from the sibling process, then release the gate.
- Trace the exact path removed and the first late read/import that reaches it; compare against a no-reinstall control and uv upstream behavior.
- Establish the authoritative lifecycle contract and bounded caller/deployment impact before repair.
- After confirmed RCA, create a held-out parent/child subprocess RED oracle and implement lifetime pinning at the narrowest owned seam; prove GREEN and exact-defect mutation RED.
- Sweep CLI, library, MCP, review-bot, and spawned gate-worker entry paths for parity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A deterministic synchronized-process reproduction proves the changeable root cause and rules out unrelated import/cache races.
- [ ] A cited contract defines which release/resources remain valid for one invocation.
- [ ] A real parent/child subprocess test is observed RED before repair, GREEN afterward, and RED under exact-defect mutation.
- [ ] A force reinstall during an active gate cannot cause that invocation to raise `ImportError` or `FileNotFoundError` from its resolved release.
- [ ] The next invocation uses the newly installed release; lifetime pinning does not permanently retain obsolete releases.
- [ ] CLI, library, MCP, automated gate callers, and child-process parity are dispositioned.
- [ ] Cleanup behavior and operator setup documentation are updated where the proven mechanism requires it.
baseline.summary: Concurrent uv tool reinstall can delete the active rebar release during a gate invocation

baseline.description:
## Why

Blocking is project-owned policy; rebar's job is to surface the same eval/calibration instruments
it uses on its built-ins so a maintainer can decide informed. Today `eval_solver.run_case` is a
**closed hardcoded dispatch** (only `completion-verifier` / `ticket-quality` / `spec-alignment`;
raises otherwise) and the CLI is validate-only — so a project criterion cannot be run through the
eval harness at all.

## What

- A criterion-aware runner extending `eval_solver.run_case` so an arbitrary (built-in or project)
  criterion prompt_id is runnable — reconcile the invocation model (the criterion runs as its
  Pass-1 finder against a fixture); resolve the T3 advisory (the existing solver's invocation model
  vs a per-criterion prompt).
- `rebar criteria eval <id>` — a live CLI (not validate-only) that runs the criterion's
  must-fire/must-not-fire + discrimination fixtures from `.rebar/evals/<id>.eval.yaml` (discovery
  already exists) with N-run stability.
- A calibration view over the existing κ/parity primitives: per criterion print **recall**
  (=fraction of must-fire fixtures it fires on), **false-accept** (=fraction of must-not-fire it
  wrongly fires on), **Cohen's κ** and **agreement %** (verdict vs the fixture's labeled expect).
  Reconcile the preview/eval `verdict` vocabulary with the fixture `expect` vocabulary.

## Scope

- Files: `src/rebar/llm/eval_solver.py` (criterion-aware dispatch), `src/rebar/llm/eval.py` /
  `eval_scorers.py` (reuse discrimination scorers, κ, parity), `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py`
  (`rebar criteria eval`), calibration rendering.
- Depends on story `#1` (a criterion must be loadable/activatable to eval it).
- Out: REVIEW_RESULT FP-replay (F1) — gate-agnostic, deferred; project criteria inherit it later.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `eval_solver.run_case` runs an arbitrary criterion prompt_id (built-in or project), not the
      closed 3-id set; the invocation model is documented.
- [ ] `rebar criteria eval <id>` runs must-fire/must-not-fire + discrimination fixtures live from
      `.rebar/evals/` with N-run stability.
- [ ] The calibration view prints recall, false-accept, Cohen's κ, agreement % per criterion, with
      each metric defined; the eval `verdict` vocabulary is reconciled with the fixture `expect`.
- [ ] FP-replay (F1) is explicitly out of scope.


## Invocation model & implementation contract (remediation, run 1)

### Criterion arm of `run_case` (clears G6/T1/T8 blocker)
The existing `run_case` branches (`case_store` + a disposable git repo + `create_ticket`) are the
AGENTIC store-reader ops — structurally inapplicable to a plan-review criterion, which is a
single-turn/agentic **finder over inline text**. The criterion arm therefore does NOT use
`case_store`. Concrete path:
- `run_case(prompt_id, case, *, runner, graph=False, repo_root=None)` gains a `repo_root=None`
  param (default `config.repo_root()`; back-compat for existing callers). If `prompt_id` resolves to
  a criterion — bare id or `plan-review-<id>`, present in `registry.by_id(repo_root)` — take the
  criterion arm; else the existing 3-id dispatch (unknown non-criterion still raises `ValueError`).
- The arm: `desc = registry.by_id(repo_root)[cid]`; `cfg = resolve_gate_config(repo_root)`;
  `findings = passes.pass1_chunk(runner, cfg, plan=case["input"], chunk=[desc],
  agentic=registry.exec_tier(desc)=="AGENT")`; return `{"findings": findings}`. No store, no ticket.
  (Container G3/G4 + ISF need a graph/log, not inline text — OUT of scope here; a criterion whose
  fixtures require them errors with a clear message.)

### Verdict ↔ expect vocabulary reconciliation (clears T8/AC3)
`_fired(verdict) = len(verdict.get("findings") or []) > 0`. A case's expected fire is derived from
its `expect` via the EXISTING sets: `FIRE_EXPECTS = {"finding","fail"}` → expected-fire;
`NOFIRE_EXPECTS = {"pass"}` → expected-no-fire. Only fire/no-fire cases feed the calibration
(validity/impact/novelty axis cases are skipped, not miscounted). Two-category labels `"fire"` /
`"no_fire"` feed `cohens_kappa` + agreement.

### Calibration metrics (clears AC3 metric defs)
`calibrate_criterion(criterion_id, *, repo_root=None, runner=None, runs=1, solve=None)` in eval.py:
- `recall` = fired / total must-fire fixtures; `false_accept` = wrongly-fired / total must-not-fire
  fixtures; `agreement` = fraction of cases where observed == expected; `kappa` =
  `cohens_kappa(expected_labels, observed_labels)`.
- Injectable `solve` (mirrors `run_eval`) so tests compute metrics deterministically without a model.

### N-run stability (clears E2/T5e/G6 — N is configurable)
`runs` (CLI `--runs`, default **1**) is N. Each case runs N times; its observed verdict is the
MAJORITY fire/no-fire across the N runs, and per-case `stability` = fraction of the N runs agreeing
with that majority (1.0 = fully stable). The view prints the min/mean stability so a flaky criterion
is visible. N=1 ⇒ stability trivially 1.0.

### CLI error states + sequencing (clears T6/E5/G5)
`rebar criteria eval <id>` errors clearly (non-zero exit, no traceback) on: missing/empty id; a
criterion id absent from the registry (`unknown criterion`); an absent `.rebar/evals/<prompt_id>.eval.yaml`
fixture (`no eval fixtures for <id>`); a fixture with zero fire/no-fire cases (`empty calibration
dataset`). Thin-slice sequencing: (1) `run_case` criterion arm + a unit test with a fake runner;
(2) `calibrate_criterion` + a deterministic-`solve` test; (3) CLI wiring + error-path tests.

## Acceptance Criteria (remediation additions)

- [ ] The criterion arm of `run_case` calls `passes.pass1_chunk` directly (no `case_store`), with a
      documented `repo_root` param; a fake-runner unit test asserts fire (non-empty findings) and
      no-fire (empty) map correctly.
- [ ] `calibrate_criterion` computes recall / false-accept / κ / agreement / stability with an
      injectable `solve`; a deterministic test asserts the metric math (no live model).
- [ ] `rebar criteria eval <id>` errors clearly (non-zero, no traceback) on unknown id / absent
      fixture / empty dataset; each has a test.
baseline.summary: Per-criterion eval runner + calibration view (rebar criteria eval)

baseline.description:
## Context
Plan-review, code-review, and completion sidecar emit paths automatically prune older committed UUID-named event files through delete_events. This repeats the destructive-retention mechanism proven to wedge the review-bot tracker in bug 8185-2d4b-d2bf-4282.

## Evidence
- The two-clone experiment for 8185 proved that deleting a shared base sidecar while each stale clone appends a replacement makes Git infer rename conflicts.
- plan_review/sidecar.py, code_review/sidecar.py, and completion_sidecar.py each call delete_events from automatic retention.
- The store concurrency contract requires independent UUID events to reconverge by append-only union.

## Plan
- Build real two-clone RED reproductions for each automatic emit/retention path.
- Remove or replace automatic physical deletion only where the runtime experiment proves conflict.
- Preserve latest-result readers, audit history, reducer behavior, and clean tracker state.
- Verify each path RED to GREEN with mutation checks and the full concurrency tier.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Real two-clone tests prove each affected automatic sidecar path reconverges cleanly.
- [ ] Automatic sidecar writes do not physically delete committed UUID event files.
- [ ] Latest-result readers still select the newest valid sidecar.
- [ ] Focused, default, integration, lint, and typecheck gates pass.
baseline.summary: Automatic LLM sidecar retention can diverge independent tracker clones

## Context
The review gates expose real configuration — risk posture, chunking, budget caps, per-criterion advisory-vs-
blocking, and a global enable/disable kill-switch. A project needs a coherent way to read, set, and validate
that config rather than hand-editing scattered keys. (Spun out of `5fd2` as a separate epic; was follow-on F5.)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A validated config schema covering risk posture, chunking, budget caps, per-criterion blocking, the global enable/disable, and the ADVISORY SURFACING CAP (top-N advisory findings; default 10; NEVER applies to blocking findings).
- [ ] A CLI/MCP surface to read/set/validate the config with shipped defaults.
- [ ] Invalid config is a located error, not a silent no-op.
- [ ] A single, validated configuration surface for the review gates with sensible shipped defaults.
- [ ] A tool/UX to view and set it (per-criterion posture, chunking, budgets, the enable/disable switch) with
baseline.summary: Review-gate project configuration tool + UX (risk posture, chunking, budgets, per-criterion blocking, enable/disable)

## Purpose

This story is the quiet-window handoff added to epic `0303-692c-55dc-4a18`. It does not define an alternative reclaim. The epic owner executes it in the same window as in-progress story `6981-d937-bce7-4497` (A6-1), using the already-landed A6-0c/A6-0d helpers and every A6-1 safety gate. Its additional responsibility is to execute bug `30d3-eaf0-c7a4-497a` before the history rewrite so the authoritative store is clean before it is repacked.

The primary reclaim is the proven length-aware `git fast-export --no-data | filter | git fast-import` history strip from A6-0c. Repack/gc is follow-on compaction only. Repack alone cannot reclaim the reachable scattered `.bridge_state` history: the measured 12.79 KB/version result was already measured after `--window=250 --depth=50`.

No operational step in this story begins until the operator explicitly confirms zero active sessions plus all `rebar-mcp` servers stopped. Claiming this story after plan-review PASS only reserves the work; it is not permission to mutate the tracker, repair diagnostics, remove pins, rewrite history, or publish.

## Preconditions and ordering

1. Revalidate the A6-1 quiet-window gates immediately after operator confirmation: both GitHub workflows remain disabled; no run is in progress; review-bot `/health` reports `in_flight: 0`; every open current Gerrit patchset has a nonzero current-patchset `LLM-Review` vote from `DETAILED_LABELS`; `refs/reconciler/lock` plus `refs/reconciler/gate` are absent; the AWS timer plus both host LaunchAgents remain paused. If `main` advanced, refresh the host runtime again from current `main`, record its path/version/source SHA, then repeat the exact-runtime epoch-mismatch refusal probe.
2. Converge the shared local tracker only after the quiet-window checks: fetch `origin/tickets`, reset the dedicated tracker to that exact tip, prove the tracker is clean plus zero commits ahead. Do not touch the shared main checkout.
3. Before any store mutation, create a pre-repair off-repo bundle with `infra/scripts/prepare_reclaim_backup.py`; verify it with `git bundle verify`; restore it into a throwaway repository; compare the restored old-tip/pin OIDs to the manifest. Retain this checkpoint until the whole window closes.
4. Claim and execute `30d3-eaf0-c7a4-497a` under its signed plan. Record each diagnostic-class repair, before/after counts, plus the interleave on both tickets. Require `rebar fsck` to report zero repairable diagnostics and exactly the four intentional `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED` records on `4214-ac28-d19c-41b9`, `72d5-79ec-9e2e-4a2b`, `b043-9490-32ca-4548`, and `fc9e-8c2e-cb2f-465f` before starting the rewrite.
5. Because the repair can advance `origin/tickets`, create a fresh final off-repo bundle at the post-repair tip using new artifact paths. Verify/restore it exactly as above. This final bundle tip must equal the `old-tip` used by the rewrite lease. It is the forward-publication rollback artifact; do not reuse the A6-0d rehearsal artifact.
6. From fresh live ref enumeration, remove only the ref pins documented by A6-0d, and only after the final bundle is verified. Run `infra/scripts/reclaim_bridge_history.py` in a fresh unfiltered clone. The script rewrites to a scratch output ref, dynamically re-adds the current `.bridge_state/` tree, then performs its graph/tree/count/pack-bound assertions; it does not push, repack, or gc. Run operator-controlled `git repack -ad --window=250 --depth=50` followed by `git gc --prune=now` only after both verified off-repo bundles exist. This separate compaction/prune makes the stripped unreachable history release disk bytes.
7. Before publication, require all A6-0c/A6-1 assertions: rewritten `HEAD^{tree}` equals the recorded old-tip tree; commit count is unchanged; merge-commit count is unchanged; `.bridge_state.bak-retarget/` has no residual historical commits; fresh unfiltered clone size is at most 150 MB; pre/post identity-report summary counts match; the multiset of `(event_uuid, verdict, grandfathered)` matches while ignoring rewritten commit SHAs; the synthetic post-rewrite writer leaves old-tip ancestry false plus incremental `size-pack` growth below 1 MB.
8. Re-read the live remote tip immediately before publication. Publish only with exact `--force-with-lease=<old-tip>:<new-tip>`. Any lease failure aborts the publication path and requires a fresh unfiltered clone, new measurements, plus a new final backup for the advanced tip.
9. Verify the published tree/count/size/identity results. Require `git merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip> origin/tickets` to exit nonzero. Enumerate every ref fetched by a default clone and require none to have the old tip as an ancestor.
10. Converge the persistent review-bot clone over SSM. Land the `rebar.toml` `identity.enforce_since` re-pin through normal Gerrit review using the commit map, with `LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`, then Submit.
11. Before allowing the deterministic first post-rewrite write, set `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN=off` in the review-bot execution environment and prove no eligible process can opportunistically drain the inherited enrichment queue. Keep the override active through the first-write fetch, ancestry, and size receipt; record the prior setting for restoration.
12. Use the re-pin review-bot vote as the deterministic first live post-window write. Require it to be the sole writer-produced canonical review-artifact sequence (exactly CREATE, REVIEW_RESULT, code-review-to-work link, and reciprocal work-to-code-review link; no unrelated commit interleaves) between the immediate post-rewrite baseline and the receipt. Record its change/patchset/vote timestamp. Re-fetch `origin/tickets`; require old-tip ancestry to remain false; require growth from the immediate post-rewrite baseline to remain below 1 MB.
13. Restore the prior overlap-drain setting, then re-enable both workflows, the AWS timer, plus both LaunchAgents. Require a green reconciler pass plus final `rebar fsck` with zero repairable diagnostics and exactly the four intentional `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED` records on `4214-ac28-d19c-41b9`, `72d5-79ec-9e2e-4a2b`, `b043-9490-32ca-4548`, and `fc9e-8c2e-cb2f-465f` before notifying the operator that sessions may resume.

## Rollback

Rollback is an explicit second quiet window. Re-establish every writer pause plus operator confirmation, verify the final off-repo bundle, restore it into a fresh unfiltered clone, then restore the recorded old tip with `--force-with-lease=<rewritten-tip>:<old-tip>`. Revert `rebar.toml` `identity.enforce_since` through normal Gerrit review to the recorded pre-rewrite boundary, then require the old-store identity summary plus `(event_uuid, verdict, grandfathered)` multiset to match the pre-window receipt before writers are enabled. Apply the same temporary `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN=off` guard through the rollback first-write receipt, then restore its prior setting. Re-converge the shared tracker, persistent review-bot clone, plus ephemeral workflow worktrees before re-enabling writers. Never bypass an epoch mismatch inside application merge paths.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [operator-attested] The operator zero-session/stopped-MCP confirmation is recorded on this ticket before tracker convergence.
- [x] [operator-attested] The pre-repair bundle passes `git bundle verify`.
- [x] [operator-attested] The pre-repair bundle restore reproduces every manifest OID.
- [x] [operator-attested] Ticket `30d3-eaf0-c7a4-497a` closes with a zero-repairable-diagnostic `rebar fsck` receipt plus exactly the four intentional `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED` records on `4214-ac28-d19c-41b9`, `72d5-79ec-9e2e-4a2b`, `b043-9490-32ca-4548`, and `fc9e-8c2e-cb2f-465f` before rewrite start.
- [x] [operator-attested] The execution order is recorded on both maintenance tickets.
- [x] [operator-attested] The final off-repo bundle passes `git bundle verify`.
- [x] [operator-attested] The final bundle restore reproduces every manifest OID.
- [x] [operator-attested] The final bundle old tip equals the exact rewrite lease old tip.
- [x] [operator-attested] Live remote ref enumeration is recorded before pin removal.
- [x] [operator-attested] Only the A6-0d-documented pre-rewrite pins are removed.
- [x] [operator-attested] Rewritten `HEAD^{tree}` equals the recorded old-tip tree.
- [x] [operator-attested] Rewritten commit count equals the pre-rewrite count.
- [x] [operator-attested] Rewritten merge-commit count equals the pre-rewrite count.
- [x] [operator-attested] No rewritten commit retains `.bridge_state.bak-retarget/`.
- [x] [operator-attested] A fresh unfiltered clone of rewritten `tickets` is at most 150 MB.
- [x] [operator-attested] Pre/post identity-report stderr summary counts are identical.
- [x] [operator-attested] Pre/post identity-report `(event_uuid, verdict, grandfathered)` multisets are identical when `commit` is ignored.
- [x] [operator-attested] The synthetic post-rewrite writer leaves old-tip ancestry false.
- [x] [operator-attested] The synthetic post-rewrite writer increases incremental `size-pack` by less than 1 MB.
- [x] [operator-attested] The exact `--force-with-lease=<old-tip>:<new-tip>` publication succeeds.
- [x] [operator-attested] No ref fetched by a default clone has the old tip as an ancestor.
- [x] [operator-attested] The persistent review-bot clone converges to the published epoch.
- [x] [code-verifiable] Landed `rebar.toml` `identity.enforce_since` equals the mapped post-rewrite SHA.
- [x] [operator-attested] Opportunistic enrichment is disabled for the deterministic first post-rewrite write and its prior setting is restored after the receipt.
- [x] [operator-attested] The re-pin review-bot vote is the sole writer-produced canonical review-artifact sequence (exactly CREATE, REVIEW_RESULT, code-review-to-work link, and reciprocal work-to-code-review link; no unrelated commit interleaves) between the immediate post-rewrite baseline and the receipt.
- [x] [operator-attested] The re-pin review-bot vote leaves old-tip ancestry false.
- [x] [operator-attested] The re-pin review-bot vote increases post-rewrite `size-pack` by less than 1 MB.
- [x] [operator-attested] Both reconciler workflows are re-enabled.
- [x] [operator-attested] The AWS `rebar-autodeploy.timer` is enabled plus active.
- [x] [operator-attested] Both host LaunchAgents are loaded.
- [x] [operator-attested] Post-enable reconciliation is validated by either a green reconcile-bridge.yml run or, during a GitHub Actions outage, an operator-approved production-equivalent signed CLI sequence: pre-live dry-run with zero mutation/recovery failures; live pass(es) exit 0 with every Jira batch error=None and silent_noop=[]; persisted state is pushed; final dry-run has zero mutation/recovery failures; and the canary classifier reports drift_total=0.
- [x] [operator-attested] Final `rebar fsck` reports zero repairable diagnostics and exactly the four intentional `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED` records on `4214-ac28-d19c-41b9`, `72d5-79ec-9e2e-4a2b`, `b043-9490-32ca-4548`, and `fc9e-8c2e-cb2f-465f`.

## Evidence and scope

Record command exits, exact SHAs, bundle paths/checksums/sizes, before/after pack bytes, run/SSM/Gerrit identifiers, timestamps, plus the actual interleave on this ticket and on A6-1 where the evidence is shared. Operational scope uses `infra/scripts/prepare_reclaim_backup.py` plus `infra/scripts/reclaim_bridge_history.py`; the only repository file changed during the window is `rebar.toml` for the normal Gerrit re-pin. No `src/` change belongs to this story.

baseline.description:
# Thread the probe allowlist into project-criterion routing

## Problem (verified at origin/main cc69cc1179)

`ProductionBatchRunner.run` fans activated `project.<name>` criteria into the Pass-1 set via `_project_criteria(ctx, exclude)` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py:112`, defined at `:257`). That helper calls `orchestrator.route_criteria(ctx)`, which has NO probe notion.

Under PROBE MODE (the drift-refresh tripwire), the built-in set is forced to the tiny allowlist `E4`+`G1G2` — `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:254-263` does `included = {cid for cid in effective if cid in probe}`. But built-ins reach the runner through `req.criteria` while project criteria are re-routed independently, so an activated project criterion is ALSO evaluated during a probe: extra billable LLM calls on what is meant to be the cheap probe. Harmless to the verdict today (the drift comparison keys off E4/G1G2 only), and the existing caveat at `production_batch_runner.py:265-269` names this ticket as the follow-up.

## Approach

The probe allowlist already reaches the workflow as gate input `probe_criteria` (`gates/plan-review.yaml:24`, threaded to the `assemble` step at `:54`). Deliver it to the batch step through the EXISTING generic seam — a batch step's `with:` is resolved once by the interpreter (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/interpreter.py:376-396`) into `BatchRunRequest.with_inputs`, which this runner already reads three keys from (`:155`, `:166`, `:173`). So NO change to the generic `BatchRunRequest` dataclass, and no plan-review concept leaks into the seam: a runner that ignores the key (e.g. `DefaultBatchRunner`) is unaffected.

Suppression semantics MIRROR `workflow_ops`: keep only ids present in the allowlist. Since a `project.` id is never in the E4/G1G2 probe set, that is suppression in practice, but the filter — rather than a blanket "return nothing when probing" — stays correct if the allowlist ever grows.

## Changes

1. `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml:60-62` — add
   `probe_criteria: ${{ inputs.probe_criteria }}` to the `finders` batch `with:`.
2. `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py:257` — `_project_criteria` grows a
   third parameter `probe` (an id collection, default empty). When non-empty, the returned
   project criteria are filtered to ids in `probe`.
3. `production_batch_runner.py:112` — pass `req.with_inputs.get("probe_criteria")`.
4. `production_batch_runner.py:265-269` — replace the caveat paragraph with a description of
   the implemented behaviour (the ticket reference goes away with the caveat).

## Tests

- `tests/unit/test_criteria_overlay.py:234-238` (existing project fan-in test) — extend: with a
  probe allowlist of `E4`/`G1G2`, `_project_criteria` returns `([], [])` for the same activated
  `project.no-print` overlay that fans in when NOT probing. Same-fixture pair, so it fails
  before the change and passes after. Its two existing calls pass `exclude=` by KEYWORD, so a
  defaulted new parameter leaves them working.
- **Monkeypatch stub population.** `_project_criteria` is stubbed in tests via
  `monkeypatch.setattr`, which Serena cannot see; grepping the symbol as a STRING
  (`grep -rn '_project_criteria' tests/`) enumerates the WHOLE population — exactly TWO
  2-positional-arg stubs, both `lambda ctx, seen: ([], [])`:
  `tests/unit/test_pass1_finder_model.py:103` AND `tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py:143`.
  Once the call site at `production_batch_runner.py:112` passes a third argument, EITHER
  un-updated stub raises `TypeError`. Both are updated to accept it. (The remaining `tests/`
  hits are unrelated: docstring mentions in `test_bug_blast_radius_escalation_ad0d.py:16,174`
  and code-review's separate `_validated_project_criteria`.)
- A YAML-level assertion that the `finders` batch `with:` carries `probe_criteria`, so the
  wiring cannot regress silently while the unit test still passes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] With a non-empty `probe_criteria`, `_project_criteria` returns no activated project
      criterion whose id is outside the allowlist. Worked example: the
      `project.no-print` overlay fixture + allowlist `["E4","G1G2"]` yields `([], [])`.
- [x] With an empty/absent `probe_criteria`, the fan-in is byte-identical to today: the same
      fixture yields `project.no-print` in the single-turn set (normal full review unchanged).
- [x] `gates/plan-review.yaml`'s `finders` batch `with:` passes `inputs.probe_criteria`.
- [x] `BatchRunRequest` (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/runners.py:61`) is UNCHANGED — no
      plan-review-specific field on the generic seam.

baseline.description:
## Summary
Ticket write operations fail hard on git `index.lock` contention and NEVER self-heal: a single interrupted/crashed commit leaves a stale `.git/worktrees/<tracker>/index.lock` that wedges **every** subsequent ticket write (`comment`, `edit`, `create`, `link`, `tag`, …) until a human manually removes it. Even *transient* contention (two clones committing at once) surfaces as a hard error with no retry. Locks should be transient and ticket operations should retry + reclaim provably-stale locks to be self-healing.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Drive any ticket write through `rebar._store.event_append.stage_and_commit` (e.g.
   `rebar comment <id> "..."`).
2. Simulate an interrupted commit by leaving a stale git index lock:
   `touch "$(git -C <tracker> rev-parse --git-dir)/index.lock"` (no git process holds it).
3. Run `rebar comment <id> "anything"` again.

Observed in the wild: after an interrupted `rebar comment`, a ~15-minute-old `/Users/.../.git/worktrees/-tickets-tracker/index.lock` (0 bytes, no owning process per `lsof`) blocked five consecutive `rebar comment` retries; the store only recovered after a manual `rm` of the lock file.

## Expected vs Actual
- **Expected:** a transient `index.lock` contention is retried with bounded backoff and
  succeeds once the peer releases; a *provably stale* `index.lock` (no live owning git
  process / older than a threshold) is detected and reclaimed automatically — mirroring the
  stale-lock reclamation rebar ALREADY does for its own mkdir write-lock
  (`_store/lock.py::_mkdir_lock_is_stale` / `_reclaim_mkdir_lock`). Ticket writes are
  self-healing in the common case; only a genuinely-held lock (live peer) waits/fails.
- **Actual:** `stage_and_commit` (`src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:145-175`) shells out to
  `git add`/`git commit` and raises `StoreError("Error: git commit failed while holding
  lock: … Unable to create '<gitdir>/index.lock': File exists. Another git process seems to
  be running …")` on the FIRST failure — no retry, no backoff, no stale detection. The
  rebar `_store/lock.py` write lock is held around this, but that lock only reclaims its OWN
  mkdir lock; the git-owned `index.lock` created transiently by `git add`/`git commit` is
  not covered by any retry or staleness check, so one dead commit wedges all writes.

## Context / root cause
Two lock layers exist and only one self-heals:
- `_store/lock.py` (rebar write lock: fcntl + mkdir) — ALREADY reclaims a provably-stale
  mkdir lock (owner stamp `<host>:<pid>`, dead-pid probe).
- git's `index.lock` (created per `git add`/`git commit` inside `stage_and_commit`) — NOT
  covered. Interrupted/killed commits (CI cancellation, `^C`, OOM, a crashed peer) strand it.

The `edf7`/`6818` history in the surrounding comments shows related git-race hardening (surfacing stderr, healing UU/unmerged paths), but transient/stale `index.lock` itself is still fatal-on-first-try.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `stage_and_commit` (and the sibling inline committers `txn.py::claim_core`/
      `transition_core`, `compact.py`) retry a git `index.lock` "File exists / Another git
      process seems to be running" failure with bounded exponential backoff (small, capped
      total wait) before surfacing an error
- [ ] A *provably stale* `index.lock` (no live owning git process AND/OR older than a
      configurable threshold) is detected and reclaimed automatically, reusing/mirroring the
      staleness logic in `_store/lock.py` (`_mkdir_lock_is_stale` / `_reclaim_mkdir_lock`);
      a genuinely-held lock (live peer within the window) is NOT stolen
- [ ] A concurrency test: two processes committing to the same tracker serialize and BOTH
      succeed (no spurious hard failure from transient `index.lock` contention)
- [ ] A stale-lock test: a pre-created `index.lock` with no owning process is reclaimed and
      the ticket write succeeds without manual intervention
- [ ] The retry/reclaim is fail-safe: a lock genuinely held by a live peer still waits within
      budget then surfaces a clear, actionable error (never silently drops the write, never
      corrupts the index)
- [ ] No regression to the existing `edf7` stderr-surfacing and `6818` unmerged-path healing
      behavior
baseline.summary: Ticket writes fail hard on git index.lock — add retry + stale-lock reclamation (self-healing)

## Context / Problem
`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` is 796 LOC — 4 under the 800 hard cap enforced by the CI module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), so any addition turns the build red. It grew because a single module accreted THREE distinct responsibilities: the run mechanism, cache-effectiveness *diagnostics*, and *failure interpretation*. Zero in-progress file_impact contention. Flagged by audit ae1b.

## Approach
Decompose by responsibility (not by line count) into three cohesive modules with a one-way dependency direction — the recurrence-preventing fix: future cache-warning or failure-classification logic then lands in its own module instead of re-inflating the orchestrator.

1. Extract the **cache-effectiveness diagnostics** cluster → new `src/rebar/llm/cache_diagnostics.py` (~230 LOC): `warn_if_cache_ineffective` (structured_run.py:533), `cache_write_never_read` (:645), `warn_if_cache_write_never_read` (:675), `estimate_marked_prefix_tokens` (:704), `_warn_if_zeroed_usage` (:740).
2. Extract the **failure-interpretation** cluster → new `src/rebar/llm/run_failure.py` (~180 LOC): `FailureContext` (:45), `interpret_failure` (:59), `_write_parse_failure_artifact` (:304).
3. `structured_run.py` retains the run mechanism (`_pai_structured` :186, `build_model_settings` :342, `build_usage_limits` :420, `effective_max_iterations` :461, `_known_model_output_ceiling` :470, `effective_max_tokens` :489, `_extract_usage` :499, `_import_pydantic_ai` :764, `_pai_check_config` :775) → ~390 LOC.

Rationale (G6): responsibility-based seams are stable, so the split does not need to be redone as code evolves; the two extracted modules are pure/observability code with no back-edge into the orchestrator. **Preserve every public import path** by re-exporting the moved names from `structured_run.py` (`from .run_failure import FailureContext, interpret_failure` etc.) — external importers `llm/runner.py`, `llm/usage_report.py`, `llm/capabilities.py` docs, and the tests are then untouched, keeping the edit-set non-overlapping. The re-export also keeps `test_structured_run_seam.py::test_moved_symbols_are_importable_from_the_new_module` (which asserts `hasattr(structured_run, "_warn_if_zeroed_usage")`) green with no test edit.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` — remove the two extracted clusters; add re-export shims.
- `src/rebar/llm/cache_diagnostics.py` — NEW (cache-effectiveness diagnostics).
- `src/rebar/llm/run_failure.py` — NEW (failure interpretation + parse-failure artifact).

## Verification (behavior-preserving refactor — no new behavior)
- Moved code is byte-identical; only imports are adjusted. No test edits.
- `mypy`, ruff, and the module-size gate stay green; `structured_run.py` ≤ 500 LOC; both new modules ≥ 100 LOC.
- Existing oracle tests pass unchanged: `tests/unit/test_structured_run_seam.py`, `tests/unit/test_interpret_failure_seam.py`, `tests/unit/test_cache_floor_warning.py`, `tests/unit/test_cache_floor_per_model.py`, `tests/unit/test_cache_prefix_breakpoint.py`, `tests/unit/test_settings_builders_seam.py`, `tests/unit/test_max_tokens_model_ceiling_1019.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `wc -l src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` ≤ 500; each new sibling ≥ 100 LOC.
- [x] `cache_diagnostics.py` and `run_failure.py` contain exactly the named symbols; neither imports back from `structured_run.py`, and neither imports `runner` at runtime.
- [x] All prior external import paths still resolve (verified: `python -c "import rebar.llm.structured_run as s; s.interpret_failure; s.FailureContext; s.build_model_settings; s.warn_if_cache_ineffective; s.warn_if_cache_write_never_read; s._warn_if_zeroed_usage; s.estimate_marked_prefix_tokens"`).
- [x] The full default suite and the module-size/complexity/type/lint gates are green with no test edits required.

## Context
The grounding worker harness hard-codes POSIX `fork`. CPython 3.12 warns when this runs in a multithreaded host because the child can deadlock; Python 3.14 no longer defaults to fork. Runtime experiments confirmed `multiprocessing/popen_fork.py -> os.fork()` is the warning source, while spawn preserves 46/47 existing lifecycle tests. The one failure is a test fixture that attaches an unpicklable local closure to a Process. No production caller exists in-repo, but `run_in_worker` is publicly re-exported.

## Approved API contract
- Default to the cross-platform `spawn` context.
- Accept an optional caller-supplied multiprocessing context for informed legacy/frozen-executable compatibility; callers explicitly selecting fork own its thread-safety risk.
- Require worker callables to be importable module-level names and args, kwargs, and return values to be pickleable. Future C-extension bindings construct parser/query state inside the child from plain-data arguments.
- Preserve the documented never-raise/fail-open contract: process start and pickling failures, plus parent receive/unpickling failures, return an abstaining `RunResult`.
- Do not add cloudpickle/loky without a demonstrated production caller requiring dynamic callables.

## Plan
- Add held-out behavioral coverage proving the default worker completes under a live background thread with the fork warning promoted to error.
- Add contract coverage for explicit context injection and non-pickleable start/receive failures mapping to fail-open results.
- Switch the default context to spawn, expose optional context injection, and make start/receive cleanup exception-safe.
- Replace the spawn-incompatible reap-lag test mutation with a parent-only proxy while preserving the crash-vs-timeout oracle.
- Document the public callable/serialization contract and explicit fork escape hatch.
- Run the grounding lifecycle/conformance matrix, mutation checks, lint, typecheck, and repository gates.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Default `run_in_worker` completes under a live background thread with the fork deadlock warning treated as an error.
- [x] An explicitly supplied multiprocessing context is used.
- [x] Non-importable or non-pickleable worker inputs return `RunResult(abstain_reason="other")` without raising.
- [x] Parent receive/unpickling failures return `RunResult(abstain_reason="other")` without raising.
- [x] Timeout, large-result drain, exception, signal-crash, cleanup, and reap-lag contracts remain green under spawn.
- [x] The documented public contract states importability/pickleability requirements and the explicit fork risk.
- [x] Focused grounding tests, lint, typecheck, and repository tests pass.
baseline.summary: Grounding harness tests fork from multithreaded workers and warn about deadlock risk

## Context / Problem
Parity sibling of the reconverge merge-abort recoveries (loris/1757 variant (a), wolverine/1767 variant (b)): the push non-fast-forward recovery path has the SAME untracked-overwrite wedge. `rebar._store.push_recovery._recover_dirty_merge` sets a dirty tree aside with a stash COMMIT OBJECT (`_stash_create`, never refs/stash), clears TRACKED changes via `git reset --hard` (untracked files are deliberately left alone, matching `stash push` semantics), then merges the remote ref. When an UNTRACKED local file collides with a file the merge wants to create — exactly the compaction-leftover class (`*-SNAPSHOT.json`, `*.retired`) that wedged reconverge — the merge aborts ("untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge"), and today's code gives up: `merge --abort`, restore stash, warn/strict-raise. Every push retry then re-fails the same way: the push path cannot self-heal the store class we already heal in reconverge.

## Approach
Extend `_recover_dirty_merge` (and its `_merge_remote_under_lock` sibling seam if the abort surfaces there) with the SAME recovery shape sync.py's reconverge uses: on merge failure, parse the paths git names with the parser in `rebar._store.sync` — today `_untracked_overwrite_paths` (sync.py:226), being generalized by prerequisite Gerrit change 1767 (ticket dozing-trophied-wolverine) into a shared `_merge_abort_named_paths`; use whichever name is on main at implementation time — move the named UNTRACKED colliding paths into the shared quarantine directory (`<git-common-dir>/reconverge-quarantine/<utc-ts>/`, the dir `_quarantine_untracked`/sync.py:248 established — move, never delete), retry the merge ONCE; any other failure keeps today's behavior exactly (abort, restore stash, warn or strict-raise). Reuse boundary, respecting each module's git seam: the pure PARSER is imported from sync (no subprocess in it), but the MOVER is not — sync's `_quarantine_untracked` shells through sync's module-level `_git`, whereas every push_recovery function deliberately late-binds `core._git` so push's ~25-site test monkeypatch keeps working (push_recovery.py:10-27). So implement the quarantine move locally in push_recovery through `core._git`/os.rename against the same quarantine directory path (share the dir-path helper if 1767 exposes one), rather than calling sync's mover across the seam. The stash restore ordering is preserved: quarantine + retry happen between the failed merge and any `_restore_stash`, so the stash commit object is restored exactly once on every exit path.

Sequencing: depends on change 1767 (wolverine) being merged — it lands the shared parser/quarantine helpers this reuses.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_store/push_recovery.py — untracked-overwrite recovery (quarantine + single retry) in the dirty-merge and locked-merge recovery paths; reuse sync's shared helpers.
- tests/unit/test_push_recovery_untracked.py (new; or extend the existing push_recovery test module if one covers `_recover_dirty_merge`) — RED-first coverage.

## Testing
- RED first: fixture store where the worktree holds an untracked file that the remote ref's merge wants to create; assert today's `_recover_dirty_merge` fails (merge aborted, stash restored, no merge commit).
- GREEN: same fixture after the fix — the colliding untracked file is moved into the quarantine dir (bytes preserved, byte-for-byte), the retried merge completes with both parents, and the stash-recorded tracked edits are restored.
- Guard: a genuine content conflict still aborts, restores the stash, and warns/strict-raises (unchanged behavior); paths git does not name are untouched; the quarantine dir is only created when something is moved.
- Stash-safety: the stash commit object is restored exactly once on both the retry-success and retry-failure paths (no lost tracked edits).
- Mutation check: skipping the quarantine move or the retry returns the RED assertion; retrying more than once is killed by a call-count assertion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A push recovery whose merge aborts ONLY on untracked-overwrite collisions completes after quarantining the named paths and retrying once, with no event bytes lost (quarantine holds the moved files); checked by the RED-to-GREEN test.
- [x] Tracked edits set aside in the stash are restored on every exit path (success, retry-failure, non-recoverable abort); checked by the stash-safety tests.
- [x] Genuine conflicts and unnamed paths keep today's behavior exactly; checked by the guard test.
- [x] The recovery reuses the shared sync parser/quarantine helpers (no duplicated recovery mechanism); checked by review of the diff.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1) before close.
baseline.summary: Parity sibling: push non-fast-forward recovery (_store/push_recovery.py) has the same untracked-overwrite wedge as reconverge — resets tracked-only, leaves colliding untracked leftovers

# Workflow engine: conditional overlays (via if:) + delegating batch step

## Context

Split out of soupy-spool-revel (6f2d) per the brainstorm (session logs boom-demon-jug ad3f + woody-meat-seize). The e6d9 engine (declarative IR + thin worklist interpreter, run-state on the git event log; step kinds uses/prompt/branch/loop/map + bounded-concurrent map fan-out) is closed. To express a reusable 4-pass LLM-review pipeline ON the engine (epic B migrates plan-review + completion-verification), the engine needs support for (1) conditional criterion INCLUSION and (2) budgeted BATCH orchestration. This epic adds ONLY that, engine-only (no plan-review coupling). A prior-art survey (Argo/Step Functions/dbt/LangGraph/Airflow/Dagster/Temporal) + a code investigation grounded the design.

## The two concepts (one already exists, one is genuinely new)

1. **Conditional overlay = the EXISTING `if:` skip-guard (do NOT add a new field).** Code investigation
   found the engine ALREADY does per-step conditional inclusion: the v1 `if:` skip-guard (retained in
   v2; interpreter.py _guard_scoped) evaluates a predicate over run-start-journaled inputs + recorded
   prior outputs, is replay-deterministic (no live-store access), records a durable `skipped` event,
   and fails closed. So overlays ADOPT `if:`. The deliberately-CLOSED expression grammar (lint_refs.py
   _ALLOWED_EXPR; pinned by the v2 schema `expression`  — no operators/regex/functions) is the only
   gap: it can branch on a boolean in scope but cannot COMPUTE one. The clean design (keeping the grammar
   tiny + injection-safe) is a DETERMINISTIC scripted PRECOMPUTE step that turns each overlay trigger
   (has-children, has-linked-session-log, keyword/trigger match over a text input) into a boolean output
   the criterion's `if:` references; plus optionally journaling the resolved included-set at run-start
   for coverage. NO new IR field is added.

2. **Batch orchestration = a THIN delegating step (genuinely new).** No surveyed engine makes adaptive
   cost-budgeted batching first-class — it is app code everywhere — and encoding it in the IR would break
   the replay invariant (batch composition depends on a runtime token estimate + which call hit a context
   limit, so its control state is a recorded DECISION-TREE, not a function of outputs). So the IR gains a
   thin `batch` step declaring only params (group, usd_budget, model_ladder); a batch-RUNNER (behind a
   seam) does the adaptive packing / token-estimation / context-limit fallback / model-escalation /
   shed-to-INDETERMINATE / fingerprint-checkpoint and JOURNALS its batch-plan + fallback as OPAQUE events
   the interpreter stores but never interprets. Epic A ships the seam + a reference default runner; epic
   B supplies the production runner (extracting the gate's sizing.py) behind this seam.

## Scope (engine-only)

- Overlay-via-`if:`: a deterministic trigger-precompute scripted step + a documented precompute-then-`if:`
  pattern + optional run-start journaling of the resolved included-set. The expression grammar is UNCHANGED.
- The `batch` step kind: schema/JSON Schema + the batch-runner SEAM + a reference default runner + the
  journaled batch-plan/fallback event vocabulary + interpreter wiring (store the opaque plan, do not interpret).
- A THROWAWAY demo workflow exercising an `if:`-gated (overlay) step + a `batch` step end-to-end (dry-run
  via FakeAgentRunner), removed by epic B; retained meanwhile as the visual-editing refinement sample.
- VISUAL EDITING in the workflow editor for the batch step (NEW) and the `if:` overlay predicate (EXISTING
  — confirm/extend the editor renders + edits `if:` and supports add/remove of a conditionally-included prompt).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Overlays adopt `if:` (no new IR field): a deterministic precompute scripted step computes overlay-
      trigger booleans (has-children, has-linked-session-log, text/keyword trigger match) as step outputs;
      a criterion gated by `if: ${{ steps.<triggers>.outputs.<name> }}` is included when truthy and skipped
      (durable event) when falsy; the expression grammar is NOT extended. (A1)
- [ ] Replay determinism for inclusion: a mid-run store edit does not change the included/skipped outcome
      (read from the run-start journal, not live state); the resolved included-set is observable for coverage
      (journaled at run-start OR documented as recovered from skip statuses — decide + record). (A1)
- [ ] A `batch` step kind exists with declarative params (group/usd_budget/model_ladder), a batch-runner
      SEAM + a reference default runner; the runner journals its batch-plan + fallback as OPAQUE events the
      interpreter STORES but never branches on (a test asserts this); replay reads the recorded plan. (A2)
- [ ] The Burr-tripwire stays green (no asyncio/threading leaks outside the confined fan-out). (A2)
- [ ] A throwaway demo workflow exercises an `if:`-gated overlay step + a `batch` step end-to-end under the
      FakeAgentRunner (offline, no live calls), with a test; it is clearly labeled disposable. (A3)
- [ ] The workflow visual editor renders/edits the `batch` step and the `if:` overlay predicate, and
      supports add/remove of a conditionally-included prompt. (A4)
- [ ] make lint + the full test suite pass.
- [ ] The engine expresses conditional criterion inclusion (via `if:` + a precompute pattern) and budgeted
- [ ] A demo proves both offline; the batch step + the `if:` overlay are visually editable.
baseline.summary: Workflow engine: first-class conditional overlays + delegating batch step (engine-only; + throwaway demo + visual editing)
