## Why
The epic 88ab feature-branch flow (S3) replicates refs/heads/feature/** (all nesting depths) to the GitHub mirror so g2p's workflow_dispatch(ref=refs/heads/feature/<name>) resolves. Side effect: test.yml, eval.yml, optionality.yml all trigger on push: branches: ['**'], so every replicated feature/* branch-head push fans out 3 extra CI runs on the mirror. These runs cast NO Verified vote (gerrit-verify workflow_dispatch is the sole Verified source), so they are pure cost/noise, not part of the gate.

## What
- Scope feature/** OUT of the push triggers of test.yml, eval.yml, optionality.yml (e.g. push: branches-ignore: ['feature/**'], preserving main + pull_request), so replicated feature branches do not trigger redundant mirror CI.
- Verify the gerrit-verify (Verified) path is unaffected.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] test/eval/optionality no longer run on pushes to refs/heads/feature/** (all nesting depths) on the mirror — evidence: after the change lands + replicates, push a test feature/<x> branch head and confirm the GitHub Actions run list shows zero push-triggered test/eval/optionality runs for it (gh run list --branch feature/<x>)
- [ ] main + PR triggers unchanged; gerrit-verify Verified path unaffected
- [ ] A feature/** branch push produces zero push-triggered mirror runs (evidence)
baseline.summary: Scope feature/** out of push-triggered mirror workflows (test/eval/optionality) — avoid CI fan-out from feature-branch replication

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The `rebar-implement` skill (`examples/agent-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md`) dispatches an implementation subagent in Phase 4d but never specifies a model tier. In both Claude Code and Codex CLI an unset model inherits the orchestrator's (expensive) model, so the subagent silently runs on the strongest tier — the anti-pattern that erases any token saving. The skill also lacks guidance on which work is safe to delegate to a cheaper model and how to escalate when a cheap implementer is insufficient.

## Approach

Add a `## Model tiering` operating principle and targeted amendments to Phases 3, 4a, 4d, plus a new `### 4e-bis` escalation ladder. Frame tiers as *capabilities* (strong / standard / cheap) with Claude Code and Codex CLI example mappings, rather than hardcoding product names — the skill is cross-harness (`AGENTS.md`-class prose read by non-Claude harnesses) and model names drift across releases. The held-out-TDD invariant is preserved: test-authoring (4b) and held-out validation (4e, already in the file) stay strong-tier, and a *separate* implementer always exists, so a green result still means the implementer could not tailor code to the full oracle. The design was pressure-tested across five adversarial review rounds before this change.

Rejected alternative: naming Opus/Sonnet/Haiku directly — simpler but breaks portability to Codex and rots as models are renamed.

## Scope

- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md` — the only file changed; prose-only
  (~+111/-2 lines). No source code, no behavior, no tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `## Model tiering` section exists with a capability-tier table naming both a Claude Code
      and a Codex CLI example per tier — checked by `grep -n 'Model tiering' && grep -c '^| '`.
- [ ] Phase 4d states a standard-tier default, a cheap-tier-only-for-transcription rule, and a
      constraints-in-brief requirement — checked by reading section 4d.
- [ ] A `### 4e-bis` escalation ladder exists that distinguishes normal held-out iteration
      (no escalation) from the model-weakness escalation triggers — checked by reading it.
- [ ] No hardcoded module-size number is introduced; the brief cites
      `.github/module-size-limit.txt` (which contains `800`) as the source of truth — checked by
      grep for the filename in SKILL.md.
- [ ] Phase 3 dispatch-by-kind includes a seam note directing research/discovery/grep-shaped
      non-code leaves to the cheap/fast tier — checked by grep for "tier" within the Phase 3
      non-code-leaf bullet.
- [ ] Phase 4a carries an explicit annotation that the existing-coverage search is cheap-shaped
      but spec derivation stays strong-tier by choice — checked by reading Phase 4a.
- [ ] Change is docs-only and `make lint` passes — checked by `git diff --stat` showing only the
      SKILL.md path and a clean lint run.

No `## Testing` section: this is a prose/docs change with no new testable behavior. "Transcription" in AC2 means a leaf whose happy-path test fully pins the code (1–2 files), so implementing it is mechanical transcription rather than design.
baseline.summary: rebar-implement skill: capability-tiered model delegation (strong orchestrator / cheaper subagents)

baseline.description:
## What
Adopt the B1 batch primitive (`_store.batch_stage_and_commit`, ticket 890d-4733-1c88-4976 — **hard prerequisite; this ticket `depends_on` B1**) on the NDJSON importer's independent passes so a bulk import commits far fewer commits than one-per-event.

## Why
`src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py` already has idempotency-by-`source_id` and deferred-push, but each pass funnels through a per-event commit. Every write in the importer — CREATE (`composer.create_core`), parent/edit (`composer.edit_core`), comments and file-impact/ verify (`_commands/leaf.py`), links (`graph._links.add_dependency`) — ultimately calls the ONE sink `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py::append_event`, which composes the event and commits it via `event_append.write_and_push`. That single sink is where the commit happens.

## Deferred-commit sink (mechanism — a contextvar at ONE boundary, NOT kwarg-threading)
Introduce the compose/commit split at the SINGLE `_seam.append_event` boundary via a module-level `contextvars.ContextVar` `_batch_sink` (default `None`):
- **`_batch_sink is None` (default):** `append_event` composes AND commits per-event exactly
  as today. Every existing caller — interactive and library — is unchanged, with NO kwarg
  threaded through `create_core`/`edit_core`/`leaf.*`/`_lib_writes`/`_lib_gates`. This is why
  the edit surface is tiny and guardrail-1 (interactive writes stay one-commit-per-event) is
  structurally guaranteed: nothing sets the contextvar outside the importer.
- **`_batch_sink` set to a buffer (a `list[tuple[str, dict]]`):** `append_event` still lets
  the caller's state-reading guards run (they execute BEFORE it) and still composes the
  canonical event, but APPENDS the composed `(ticket_id, event_dict)` to the buffer instead
  of committing. The importer owns the buffer, sets the contextvar around one pass, then
  flushes via `batch_stage_and_commit` and resets the contextvar.

## Flush-boundary failure semantics
The existing importer wraps each per-row write in a `try/except` that `warn()`s and continues (fail-open at row granularity). That is PRESERVED for row-level problems by moving them earlier: a malformed row that fails to COMPOSE (bad field, validation) is `warn()`-skipped at compose time and simply never enters the buffer — same observable behavior as today. The batch FLUSH itself (`batch_stage_and_commit`) is all-or-nothing: a git-level flush failure aborts the import with a clear error rather than silently dropping a chunk. This is safe because the import already runs `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off`, is idempotent-by-`source_id`, and is crash-resumable — a failed/partial flush leaves whole-commit-or-none and a re-run re-scans committed `source_id`s and resumes.

## Scope (edit surface)
- `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py` — add the `_batch_sink` contextvar + a small helper
  (`batch_sink(buffer)` contextmanager) and the "append to sink vs commit" branch in
  `append_event`. This is the ONLY write-path source file changed.
- `src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py` — for the independent, append-only passes **Pass 1
  (CREATE), Pass 2a (parents), Pass 2c (file-impact/verify-commands), Pass 2d (comments)**,
  wrap each pass in `batch_sink(buf)` and flush `buf` through `batch_stage_and_commit` in
  chunks (default 256, hard-coded — no new config key). Passes run sequentially and each
  pass's buffer is flushed (committed) before the next, so a later pass reads the prior
  pass's committed state.
- **Pass 2b (links) and Pass 2e (statuses) stay per-event (do NOT set the contextvar):**
  2b because `add_dependency` does read-after-write within the pass (it emits TWO
  `_write_link_event` calls for a reciprocal `relates_to` and calls `_is_active_link`, an
  idempotency check that READS committed link state — buffering would make a later link in
  the chunk unable to observe an earlier one, a TOCTOU); 2e because it is STATEFUL
  (children-before-parents, `cascade=False`).

## Commit-count math
Per-pass flush -> total NEW commits = `sum_over_batched_passes(ceil(pass_events/256))` + (per-event commits from Pass 2b links and Pass 2e statuses). For a synthetic import of N=3000 tickets where each ticket has 1 CREATE + 1 comment and **NO parents, file-impact, verify-commands, links, or status transitions** (so Pass 1 and Pass 2d each carry 3000 events and Passes 2a/2b/2c/2e carry zero), that is `ceil(3000/256) + ceil(3000/256) = 12 + 12 = 24` batch commits vs ~6000 per-event (>=10x fewer). The benchmark asserts the DELTA (commits after − before; baseline `init_repo` commits excluded). A synthetic file that also exercises parents/file-impact adds `ceil(pass_2a/256) + ceil(pass_2c/256)` more batch commits.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_batch_sink` contextvar + `batch_sink()` contextmanager in `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py`; `append_event` appends the composed `(ticket_id, event_dict)` to the active sink and skips the commit when a sink is set, else commits per-event exactly as today (default path byte-for-byte unchanged)
- [ ] Guardrail 1 preserved: only the importer ever sets the contextvar; interactive writes (`create`/`edit`/`transition`/`claim`/`link`/`comment`) still commit one-event-per-commit (a unit test asserts a normal `create`/`comment` still makes one commit each)
- [ ] Importer Passes 1, 2a, 2c, 2d run under `batch_sink(buf)` and flush via `batch_stage_and_commit` in 256-event chunks; Pass 2b (links) and Pass 2e (statuses) remain per-event
- [ ] Equivalence PROVEN by a pytest that imports the same NDJSON into two trackers (per-event vs batched) and asserts equal replayed state via a concrete normalizer: for each ticket id, load `rebar.show_ticket(tid, repo_root=t)` (the reducer's replayed dict) from both stores, delete the volatile keys (`created_at`, `updated_at`, `env_id`, and every event/comment `uuid`+`timestamp`), and assert the two normalized dicts are equal for every ticket (a raw `git ls-tree` diff is NOT valid because event filenames embed per-run `uuid`/`timestamp`). Concretely: a test helper `_state(t) = {tid: _normalize(rebar.show_ticket(tid, repo_root=t)) for tid in rebar.list_tickets(repo_root=t)}` with `_normalize` deleting the volatile keys, and `assert _state(t_per_event) == _state(t_batched)`
- [ ] Benchmark: a synthetic N=3000 import where each ticket has only 1 CREATE + 1 comment (no parents/file-impact/verify/links/statuses, so only Pass 1 and Pass 2d carry events) makes the commit-count delta = `2*ceil(3000/256)` (=24), >=10x fewer than the ~6000 per-event commits. Commit count is read via `int(subprocess.run(["git","-C",tracker,"rev-list","--count","HEAD"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout)` before and after the import
- [ ] Idempotent re-import test: run the same NDJSON import twice into one tracker; assert the second run adds ZERO commits (`rev-list --count HEAD` unchanged) and `rebar.list_tickets` returns the same ids/count (source_id re-scan skips all already-imported events)
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && python -m pytest tests/ -k import -q` all green
baseline.summary: B2: route the NDJSON importer's independent passes through the batch primitive

baseline.description:
## Archaeology: the gate EXISTS — the gap is sanction granularity
`scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` (policy d37e-4f64-3265-4f30 / empirical-inhuman-urus, landed 6739ea54fa, wired in `_build-and-test.yml:172`) already gates raw git writes: AST layer P over src/+scripts, workflow layer W, inline `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` sanction, fail-closed opaque-argv. It passes CLEAN on the current tree — so the hand-rolled reconciler operations a parallel session found are NOT violations under its policy.

Why it missed them: the policy sanctions the reconciler seam at MODULE granularity — all of `git_adapter.py` and `_ref_lock.py` are "write seam internal". `git_adapter` exports low-level PRIMITIVES (`add`, `commit`, `commit_email`, `commit_tree`) as sanctioned wrappers, so any caller may COMPOSE them into a hand-rolled non-atomic sequence and the gate approves every call. Proven instance: `reconcile_helpers.py:226` (`git_adapter.add`) + `:246` (`git_adapter.commit`) — inline stage+commit against the tickets tracker with no lock and no atomic commit+push transaction. The gate enforces the MECHANISM rule ("no raw subprocess git") but not the PROTOCOL rule ("tracker mutations go through the atomic locked commit+push transaction"), so bypasses of the atomic seam are invisible to it by design.

## Fix: add a composition rule (R3) to the existing checker — not a new checker
1. In `check_raw_git_writes.py`, add rule R3: a call to a sanctioned git-wrapper module's MUTATION PRIMITIVES (`add`, `commit`, `commit_email`, `commit_tree`, ref-planting writes) from OUTSIDE the atomic-transaction functions fires, unless the call site carries `# raw-git-ok:` with a reason. The sanctioned entry points become the atomic transaction seams themselves (the locked write-transaction functions in `_store` and the reconciler's `_ref_lock` transaction), not every export of the wrapper modules.
2. Enumerate today's out-of-transaction composition sites from the new rule's first run; sanction each with an inline reasoned marker referencing the parallel session's remediation ticket, so the debt is visible in-tree and drains as that session lands (marker removed with each fix).
3. Keep the existing marker/fail-closed semantics — no allowlist file, reason mandatory.
4. Tests in `tests/unit/test_raw_git_write_lint.py`: composed add+commit outside a transaction fires R3; the same calls inside the sanctioned transaction functions do not; marker-with-reason sanctions; marker-without-reason fails.

## Non-goals
Remediating the existing composition instances (the parallel session owns those; our markers reference their ticket); changing git_adapter's API; runtime interception.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] R3 exists in `scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py`: out-of-transaction calls to sanctioned wrapper mutation primitives are flagged; sanctioned-transaction internals are not.
- [ ] Today's composition sites are enumerated by the rule and carry reasoned inline markers referencing the remediation ticket (no silent allowlist).
- [ ] Unit tests cover: R3 fires on composed add/commit outside a transaction; does not fire inside sanctioned transaction functions; marker semantics (reasoned passes, reasonless fails).
- [ ] Checker passes on the current tree with the markers in place; CI wiring unchanged (`_build-and-test.yml` already runs it).
- [ ] `make lint` / `make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
baseline.summary: Gate: shrink-only ratchet forbidding tracker git mutations outside the _store seam

baseline.description:
# A committed lock turns any future advisory on a transitive dep into a build-stopping CI failure

## Why this exists

Closing `e47e-a33d-b9cf-4421` surfaced a `caused_by` edge to `ce5d-d352-9511-47bc` ("go uv-canonical with a committed lock"), and the edge is accurate. It is NOT a defect in ce5d — committing a lock is the right call for reproducibility — but it has a consequence nobody has a standing answer for:

**Before the committed lock, each install floated and a fixed upstream version was picked up silently. Now a transitive dependency is frozen, so the moment an advisory is published against the pinned version, the GATING `pip-audit` job fails on every change in flight, with no code change and nothing the authors of those changes did wrong.**

That is exactly what happened with `click 8.2.1` / PYSEC-2026-2132: six changes from five different work streams all went red simultaneously, and each author independently began diagnosing it.

## Why it will recur

Nothing about the click case was special. The preconditions are structural:
* uv's universal resolution locks every extra jointly, so ONE capping dependency (there, `inspect-ai`)
  holds the whole project on a vulnerable version;
* `pip-audit` is gating and correctly refuses to distinguish "reachable in this project" from
  "present in the environment" — `click.edit()` was never called anywhere in rebar;
* the retry logic in the job only retries DB-UNREACHABLE failures, so a real finding is not
  recheckable — which is the single most time-wasting property, because `recheck` is the first thing
  everyone tries.

## The knowledge that must not be rediscovered under time pressure

This is the substance of the ticket. It took several wrong turns to establish, including one confidently-recorded wrong conclusion:
* `constraint-dependencies` can only NARROW an existing constraint set. Testing feasibility with it
  returns UNSATISFIABLE **as its expected output**, which reads as proof that the upgrade is
  impossible. It is not proof of anything. `override-dependencies` REPLACES the offending requirement
  and is the correct instrument.
* `uv lock --upgrade-package <pkg>` is a NO-OP against an upstream cap for the same reason.
* Overriding a cap is only safe when the cap is STALE rather than a real incompatibility, and that
  needs evidence (upstream issue/PR showing the incompatibility was fixed; the capped package
  importing and running under the newer version).
* An override must carry a REMOVE-WHEN condition, or it outlives its justification silently.
* `override-dependencies` is a workspace directive, NOT published in wheel metadata — so it changes
  this repo's lock only, and downstream consumers are unaffected.

## Out of scope

Changing the pip-audit job to be non-gating, or adding blanket suppressions. The gate did its job here — it found a real advisory in the shipped environment. The problem is response latency, not the gate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] a short runbook exists (in `docs/`, discoverable from the pip-audit job's own failure output or
      a comment beside it) covering: how to tell a real finding from a DB-unreachable flake, that
      `recheck` cannot clear a real finding, the `override-dependencies` vs `constraint-dependencies`
      distinction, and the evidence required before overriding an upstream cap
- [x] the runbook states the verification set for any lock intervention: `uv lock --check` under the
      uv versions in use, `uv sync --locked --extra dev`, and `pip-audit` over the whole resulting
      environment to confirm the old pin was masking nothing else
- [x] a mechanism exists to notice an override whose REMOVE-WHEN condition has been met, rather than
      relying on someone happening to re-test — either a periodic check or a documented review trigger
- [x] the runbook is linked from the pip-audit step so a person hitting the failure finds it without
      knowing it exists
- [ ] [operator-attested] the runbook is validated by walking the click/PYSEC-2026-2132 case through
      it and confirming it would have led to `override-dependencies` without the detour, with that
      walkthrough recorded on this ticket
baseline.summary: Committed lock turns transitive-dep advisories into build stoppages

baseline.description:
## Problem (parity sibling of the tickets-branch invariant violation)
`alert_store._atomic_write` (`alert_store.py:84`) hand-rolls `tempfile` + `os.replace` instead of the shared `rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write` seam — the same hand-rolled-vs-shared-seam class as `projects_store` (ticket `fea4-f98c-f1a2-4168`, LANDED). This ticket converts that one writer to the authoritative shared seam.

## Scope note — binding-snapshot conversion was ATTEMPTED and REVERTED (behavior-preserving boundary)
The original plan for this parity sweep also proposed routing `reconcile_helpers._commit_binding_store_snapshot` through `push.commit_and_push_tickets_branch` (which stages with `git add -A`). That conversion is **intentionally NOT part of the landed change.** A first patchset that did it FAILED CI: `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_reconcile_idempotency.py::test_unchanged_second_pass_preserves_binding_store_bytes_and_head` went red — on an unchanged second reconcile pass the binding bytes are byte-identical and `mutation_count == 0`, yet git HEAD advanced. Root cause: the seam's `git add -A` widening sweeps in OTHER per-pass `.bridge_state` state files (rotation / last-pass / peer_confirmations markers) that the original selective 5-file staging deliberately excluded, so a redundant commit is created and reconcile idempotency is broken. That is a real behavioral change, which falls OUTSIDE the approved scope ("call the authoritative seam AS-IS, only where it is behavior-preserving"). The binding-snapshot path therefore keeps its original selective-staging raw-git implementation unchanged. Only the `alert_store` conversion (below), which is genuinely behavior-preserving, landed.

## Use the EXISTING seam (NO new facade, NO redesign) — same as ticket fea4
`rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write` — the shared crash-atomic write.

## Approach — alert_store._atomic_write -> fsutil.atomic_write (RESIDENCY = LOCAL SCRATCH)
`alert_store` writes to `repo_root/bridge_state/bridge_alerts` (NO dot), which `.gitignore` (`bridge_state/`) ignores and which is NOT tracked on the tickets branch (only the dotted `.bridge_state/*` is). So the alert files are local scratch: `fsutil.atomic_write` ALONE is correct — NO publish/commit path is added.
- The current `_atomic_write` does `parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` before writing;
  `fsutil.atomic_write` does NOT create the destination directory. KEEP an explicit
  `path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` immediately before the call, then
  `fsutil.atomic_write(path, content, permissions=0o600, fsync=True)` to preserve exact
  serialized bytes, mode `0o600` (mkstemp default, no chmod today), and fsync-before-replace
  durability.

## Constraints — BEHAVIOR-PRESERVING
No functional change beyond seam adoption: same on-disk alert bytes/mode, same missing-parent handling. Reuse the existing seam ONLY; add no helper.

## Testing / Verification
- RED-first byte-identity test that `fsutil.atomic_write` produces the same file contents and
  `0o600` mode as the removed hand-rolled path, and that the write succeeds when the parent dir
  does not pre-exist (guards the retained `mkdir`).
- Reconcile idempotency remains green (proving the binding-snapshot path was left unchanged):
  `python -m pytest tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_reconcile_idempotency.py -q`.
- Proving commands (all must pass): `make lint`; `make typecheck`;
  `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ -q` (modulo the known-unrelated
  `state/test_ref_lock.py::test_ac0_blob_ref_roundtrips_through_remote` flake).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `alert_store._atomic_write` is replaced by `fsutil.atomic_write` with a retained
      `parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`; residency determined = local scratch
      (documented); no publish path; exact bytes + `0o600` mode + fsync preserved.
      Verified by `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_alert_store_atomic_write.py -q`.
- [x] The binding-snapshot commit path is left UNCHANGED (raw selective-staging), so reconcile
      idempotency is preserved (no redundant commit on an unchanged second pass).
      Verified by `python -m pytest tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_reconcile_idempotency.py::test_unchanged_second_pass_preserves_binding_store_bytes_and_head -q`.
- [x] No functional/behavioral change beyond the alert_store seam adoption.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ -q`
      all pass (modulo the known-unrelated `state/test_ref_lock.py` flake).

## Sequencing
Depends on fea4 (LANDED). Edits `alert_store.py` (+ its test) only — disjoint from A/C/D.
baseline.summary: Parity: migrate binding-store snapshot + alert_store onto shared locked commit+push / atomic_write seams (behavior-preserving)

baseline.description:
## Why
A lean runtime must run workflows without authoring/eval tooling; since extras can only ADD deps, optionality must be CI-enforced or the base silently grows heavy.

## What
- Wire the extras taxonomy ([agents]; net-new [eval], [tracing]); add a `rebar llm setup` wizard.
- CI: AST import-linter (no heavy top-level imports in core); a clean core-only wheel job; per-
  extra + a union job; guard_import error messages naming the exact extra.

## Scope
- In: extras, wizard, optionality CI.
- Out: tracing backend choice (operator). The [tracing] sink is write-only -- OTel is never read
  back into a rebar decision (oracle-discipline rule, enforced when P3 tracing lands).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Extras taxonomy wired; `rebar llm setup` interactive flow validates with a FakeRunner dry-run.
- [ ] Import-linter + clean-core-wheel CI + per-extra and union jobs.
- [ ] guard_import points users at the exact `pip install nava-rebar[...]` to run.
- [ ] [tracing] documented as a write-only sink (OTel never an input to a rebar decision).
baseline.summary: WS-J: Dev/prod extras split + setup wizard + optionality CI

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Gerrit review of change 1874 observed that `docs/event-schema.md` lists six canonical LINK relations but omits the already-supported `caused_by` relation. The packaged CLI overview lists `caused_by`, and closed task `isogonal-wedded-catfish` is the design/implementation authority adding it as the seventh directional, non-blocking, non-cycle-inducing relation.

## Investigation and repair plan

- Reproduce the maintained-documentation mismatch against current `origin/main` and cite the authoritative implementation/design surfaces.
- Under rebar-debug, prove whether the omission is a stale inventory rather than a runtime defect.
- Add a held-out documentation contract that parses the LINK/UNLINK row and requires set equality with `rebar.graph._links.CANONICAL_RELATIONS`, preventing any future relation omission; retain an explicit `caused_by` semantics assertion as this bug's RED anchor.
- Repair only the proven documentation omission, run exact-defect mutation, focused documentation gates, lint, and typecheck.

## Testing / Verification

- Run `pytest tests/interfaces/contracts/test_event_schema_relations.py` before the repair and require set equality to fail specifically with `caused_by` missing from the documented inventory.
- Run the same command after the repair and require it to pass.
- Remove `caused_by` from the repaired event-schema row, rerun the focused test, require RED, then restore the repair.
- Run `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the focused documentation-contract suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/event-schema.md` includes `caused_by` in the canonical LINK relation inventory.
- [ ] The parsed event-schema LINK inventory equals `CANONICAL_RELATIONS` as a set.
- [ ] The event-schema relation prose states `caused_by` is directional.
- [ ] The event-schema relation prose states `caused_by` is non-blocking and non-cycle-inducing.
- [ ] `pytest tests/interfaces/contracts/test_event_schema_relations.py` is RED before repair with `caused_by` as the sole missing canonical relation.
- [ ] The same focused test is GREEN after repair.
- [ ] The exact omission mutation returns the focused test to RED.
- [ ] `make lint` passes.
- [ ] `make typecheck` passes.
baseline.summary: Document caused_by in the event-schema relation inventory

baseline.description:
## Why

A re-fired container review re-litigates delivered AC (false BLOCKs / stale coaching). We need a
deterministic gate that drops those findings without hiding anything live — mirroring the novelty
floor (ADR 0008) and drift-refresh (ADR 0002).

## What

Add a third Pass-3 floor in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py` (`pass3_decide`) that, using the
completion sub-answers (story: Pass-2 sub-call) and the delivered-now predicate (story:
delivered-now), DROPS a finding iff ALL hold: attribution = a delivered-now child AND
containment = limited-to-closed AND layer = plan-semantics AND priority (validity x impact) < floor
AND the criterion is NOT in the always-preserve set (config-backed `verify.completion_preserve_criteria`; default the registered security overlay T5c + contract criterion T10). Recompute every run (never persist a drop). Record each
drop to the `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar (`sidecar.py`) joinable by finding id. Gate behind a
`verify.completion_floor_active` evidence-gate flag + a `verify.completion_priority_floor` in
`src/rebar/config.py` (VerifyConfig), defaulting inert — the total back-out, exactly like the
novelty flags.

## Scope

- IN: the Pass-3 drop predicate; the config keys; sidecar `floored` recording; the deterministic
  aggregation of the three sub-answers + priority + structural criterion class.
- OUT: the sub-questions themselves (separate story); the delivered-now predicate (separate story).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pass3_decide` drops iff attribution=delivered-now AND containment=limited-to-closed AND layer=plan-semantics AND priority<floor AND the finding's criterion is NOT in the always-preserve set; all other combinations keep.
- [ ] Suppression is inert unless `verify.completion_floor_active` is true; `verify.completion_priority_floor` is configurable (mirrors `novelty_priority_floor`).
- [ ] Every drop is written to the `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar (joinable by finding id) and is recomputed each run (no persisted suppression).
- [ ] The always-preserve set is CONFIG-BACKED (`verify.completion_preserve_criteria`) referencing REGISTERED criterion IDs — default {T5c security overlay, T10 endpoint/interface contract}; adding privacy/compliance is a config change, not code (T8/T5e).
- [ ] Completion drops carry a distinct `drop_reason="completion"` in the `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar (vs novelty `"novelty"` / normal), so `plan_review_result_v1` offline joins never collide (G6).
- [ ] A finding on a preserve-set (T5c/T10) criterion is never dropped regardless of the other axes.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the truth table (each single-condition flip preserves the finding).

## Worked example (suppression boundary)

Epic mid-flight; child X = closed+attested, child Y = open.
- "X's AC wording for step 3 is ambiguous" -> attribution=X(delivered-now), containment=limited-to-closed, layer=plan-semantics, priority<floor, criterion=COH -> DROPPED (settled plan text).
- "X's step-3 mechanism conflicts with Y's planned approach" -> containment=spans-open -> KEPT.
- "X's delivered contract omits an error field consumers rely on" -> layer=delivered-functionality -> KEPT.
- "X's endpoint has no auth" (T5c) -> criterion in {security} veto -> KEPT regardless of the other axes.
- If X was force-closed (not attested) -> delivered-now=False -> every finding on X KEPT.

## Acceptance Criteria (durable record + invariants)

- [ ] A durable ADR `docs/adr/0024-completion-aware-container-plan-review.md` codifies the contracts: the three-field sub-answer schema + closed enums, the `delivered-now` predicate, the completion-floor drop rule + config knobs, and the sidecar `drop_reason` field (inline AC + session log are not the durable record).
- [ ] The Pass-3 floor consumes the exact enum value `containment=="limited-to-closed"` (no value drift vs the sub-call).

## Acceptance Criteria (sidecar schema + ADR cross-refs)

- [ ] `_slim()` in `sidecar.py` gains a `drop_reason` field (enum {`null`, `"completion"`, `"novelty"`}): `null` for surfaced/normal findings, `"completion"` for completion-floor drops, `"novelty"` for novelty-floor drops; it lives in the per-finding slim payload and is the join key that disambiguates the two floors offline.
- [ ] ADR 0008 (novelty floor) and ADR 0002 (drift-refresh path) are updated with a cross-reference to ADR 0024 so the three Pass-3 floors/paths are documented as one coherent set (no standalone/misleading floor reference).
baseline.summary: Pass-3 completion floor: deterministic drop of delivered re-litigation + config evidence-gate

baseline.description:
## Refuted premise (as originally filed)

Filed as: current `origin/main` fails the locked complexity gate because `close_ticket` in `transition_close.py` reports 19 against a recorded ceiling of 17, to be fixed by extracting along a seam.

**That is false, and the suggested remedy would have changed working code without unblocking anyone.** Verified:

* main tip `07e76a1ce3`: ruff reports `close_ticket` at **17**, and
  `.github/complexity-baseline.json` records **17**. `--check` on a clean checkout returns
  `active=60 new=0 increased=0 stale=0`.
* the sha in the report, `104dc4e10a`: code **19**, recorded ceiling **19**.

Neither tree contains a 19-vs-17 mismatch. There is nothing in `close_ticket` to extract.

## The real defect

CI runs `--lock`, not `--check`. `lock_against_base` (`scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:455`) compares the CHANGE's baseline against **main TIP**: a REMOVED entry or a LOWERED ceiling is allowed; a RAISED ceiling or a NEW entry is a violation needing an administrator.

Change 1673 (merged `8f6b6c9356`) extracted the signing tail from `close_ticket`, taking it 19 -> 17, and drained the stale baseline entry 19 -> 17. Lowering is allowed, so it passed. But every OPEN change whose tree still carries the pre-1673 baseline now presents ceiling 19 against main's 17 — which the lock reads as RAISING it.

**Verbatim reproduction.** Feeding main-tip ceilings as `base` and `104dc4e10a`'s as `branch` into `lock_against_base` returns exactly one violation:

```
ceiling RAISED for 'src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py::close_ticket': 17 -> 19 —
an administrator must override the gate to raise a ceiling
```

That is the reported symptom, verbatim. The same call with a rebased branch returns ZERO.

So the gate cannot distinguish "this branch RAISED a ceiling" from "main LOWERED it underneath an un-rebased branch". It blames the branch for a change main made. This is not specific to 1673: **every future ceiling reduction on main will break the fleet identically**, so the shrink-only ratchet currently punishes the shrinking it exists to reward. A change that never touches the baseline is still hit, because it still carries the old FILE.

Immediate operational unblock (no code, no admin): affected changes REBASE onto current main.

## Direction

Compare the branch against **`merge-base(main, HEAD)`** rather than main tip, so only entries the BRANCH itself changed can violate.

* `_fetch_base_ceilings_from_main` (`:494`) currently fetches `--depth=1`, which is too
  shallow to compute a merge base. Fetch main with enough history, and if the local checkout
  is shallow (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository`) deepen it before retrying.
* Read the baseline at the merge-base commit and use it as `base`. `lock_against_base`'s rules
  are unchanged — only the base it is given changes.
* **Fallback direction matters.** If a merge base still cannot be computed, fall back to
  today's main-tip comparison with an explicit note. That fallback is STRICTER, never looser:
  it can only over-report, so an unavailable merge base can never let a genuine ceiling raise
  through. Fail-closed posture is preserved.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] An un-rebased branch carrying the pre-reduction baseline PASSES the lock after main
      lowers a ceiling — verified by a test reproducing exactly that scenario
- [x] A branch that genuinely RAISES a ceiling relative to its merge base still FAILS —
      verified by a test
- [x] A branch that adds a NEW entry still FAILS — verified by a test
- [x] A ceiling LOWERED or an entry REMOVED by the branch still passes — verified by a test
- [x] When no merge base can be computed the gate falls back to the main-tip comparison and
      says so, never silently passing a genuine raise — verified by a test
baseline.summary: complexity lock compares against main tip instead of merge base, so ceiling reductions on main break every un-rebased branch

## Why
The "select prompts AND scripted ops / author in place" half of the vision: compose by selecting from a typed palette, and author new prompts in the UI.

## What
- TYPED PALETTE / INSERTION: insert a new step by selecting EITHER a scripted op OR a prompt from a
  typed palette (grouped by category/contract), surfaced via editor endpoints
  (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor.py`, `editor_assets/`). Selecting a scripted op sets `uses:`;
  selecting a prompt sets `prompt:`. (This delivers the success-criterion's "scripted ops from a typed
  palette", not only the prompt library.)
- PROMPT LIBRARY: dropdown listing built-in + project prompts (from the derived index + project dir).
- CREATE a new prompt and EDIT prompt text in the UI. On Save, write-back AUTO-DETECTS a writable
  `nava-rebar` source checkout (pyproject `[project].name == nava-rebar` AND a writable
  `src/rebar/llm/...` path -> edit the packaged `.md`) else writes a `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md` project
  override; SHOW the resolved target path before Save. Writes are ATOMIC (write-temp + rename) through
  S2's canonical writer, and creating/editing a prompt REGENERATES the derived index.
- NON-HAPPY PATHS (explicit): refuse + clear error when NEITHER a writable source checkout NOR a
  writable project dir exists; id COLLISION on create-new (refuse/confirm-overwrite); discarding
  unsaved edits; an empty/invalid prompt id.
- Round-trip golden tests prove no corruption on authored/edited prompts.

## Scope
In: typed palette (op+prompt insertion) + library + create/edit + atomic write-back + non-happy-paths + index regen + tests. Out: properties-panel structured fields (S8).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The typed palette inserts a scripted op (sets `uses:`) AND a prompt (sets `prompt:`); the prompt dropdown lists built-in + project prompts.
- [ ] Create-new + edit-text persist via S2's writer with an ATOMIC write; write-back target auto-detected and the resolved path shown; packaged write refused when read-only.
- [ ] Non-happy paths handled: neither-location-writable error, id collision, discard-unsaved, invalid id — each surfaces a clear error (no silent corruption); round-trip tests pass.
- [ ] Authoring/editing a prompt regenerates the derived index (no stale index).
- [ ] A browser e2e exercises palette insert (op + prompt) / create / edit / Save.
- [ ] The palette groups by the CLOSED category vocabulary from the prompt model (review/verifier/transform/code/exploration); the insertion mechanism is specified (a bpmn-js palette/context-pad entry or a custom insertion panel) and inserts a valid `uses:`/`prompt:` step.
baseline.summary: Editor prompt library + authoring/write-back (select + create + edit in place)

## Context / Problem
The workflow editor currently presents authored YAML/BPMN configuration without a trustworthy view of the effective criteria policy derived from built-ins plus project overlays. RP-06 adds an immutable derived policy and an explicit project applicability rule; exposing derived state as if it were editable topology would create a second policy authority and make misconfiguration difficult to diagnose.

## Approach
Extend the workflow-editor server to obtain the S1 `CriteriaSnapshot` for the selected repository and expose a narrow, read-only Effective Policy view. Keep Authored Workflow as the only editable YAML/BPMN topology. The effective view shows snapshot digest/source, criterion id, gate, execution tier, effective posture/threshold, applicability summary, enabled/disabled state, and a concise derived reason. It never serializes edits back into workflow or project routing.

At authoring/save validation, a new `project.*` code-review LLM criterion must have a non-empty list of non-empty repository-relative `applies_to` globs. The editor rejects an empty/missing selector with the exact `["**"]` repository-wide remedy. Built-in entries, project DET criteria, and plan-review criteria retain their distinct trigger authoring controls and are not forced through this field.

Keep stored execution trace and per-call debugging detail out of the editor response. The Effective Policy panel is configuration provenance, not a review-result/status viewer. Repository or validation errors fail the save or mark the effective view unavailable with a located, actionable message; they do not silently display packaged defaults as effective policy.

## Rationale and Compatibility
A read-only projection makes the centralized pattern visible while preserving one authored source of topology. Older workflow files remain readable. The UI and server add fields without rewriting saved YAML/BPMN, and rollback removes the panel/endpoint while leaving authored artifacts unchanged.

## Testing
Use server contract tests with real overlay/snapshot compilation and focused editor DOM/state tests. The oracle is the serialized authored document remaining byte-equivalent while the read-only view changes with project policy. Negative controls cover built-in empty trigger semantics, project DET, and plan review. Error fixtures prove unavailable policy is explicit and save validation is fail-loud.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The editor renders distinct Authored Workflow and read-only Effective Policy sections, and no action in the effective section mutates or serializes YAML/BPMN.
- [ ] Effective Policy data comes from the repository-bound `CriteriaSnapshot` and displays digest/source plus concise criterion gate, tier, posture, applicability, and enabled/disabled provenance.
- [ ] Creating or saving a project code-review LLM criterion with missing, empty, non-list, or blank globs is refused with the criterion location and `use ["**"] for repository-wide` remedy.
- [ ] Built-in secondary triggers, project DET selector controls, and plan-review `applies_at`/`trigger` authoring remain valid negative controls and are not subjected to the project-LLM glob rule.
- [ ] A snapshot load/validation failure marks Effective Policy unavailable with an actionable located error and never substitutes packaged defaults or permits an invalid save.
- [ ] Server and editor tests prove policy changes update only the derived view while authored workflow round-trips byte-equivalently.
- [ ] Editor payloads contain no per-unit discovery trace, raw prompt/context body, provider response, or secret.
baseline.summary: RP-06 S6 — Separate authored workflow from effective review policy

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`outbound_field_diff.py` wires the live account-search resolver into the outbound mapper by **setting an attribute on it**:

    outbound_mapper._assignee_resolver = lambda lv: assignee_resolver(lv, jira_key)

wrapped in a `try/except (AttributeError, TypeError): pass`. Consumers then **discover** it with `getattr(self, "_assignee_resolver", None)` and silently fall back to a non-authoritative result when it is absent.

This is a collaborator passed by side-channel rather than by contract, and it has three concrete costs:

1. **It fails silently.** If the injection ever stops happening — a mapper that forbids attribute assignment
   hits the bare `except ...: pass` — every assignee resolution degrades to `authoritative=False`. That is not
   cosmetic: a permanently non-authoritative assignee makes the outbound diff re-emit an assignee change it can
   never converge, the churn class epic `ace2` exists to fix.
2. **It hid a real bug in review.** GitHub PR #120's proposed Data Center adapter copied the `getattr` line
   into a class where nothing ever set the attribute, so its ENTIRE authoritative branch was dead code and DC
   would have returned `authoritative=False` for every assignee. A typed constructor parameter makes that
   failure impossible to write.
3. **It is invisible to the type checker.** Each assignment needs `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` because the
   attribute is on no Protocol, so mypy cannot see the dependency at all.

## The FULL live site list (re-enumerated against this tree)

The Data Center adapter has since MERGED, so the blast radius is wider than "one injection + one getattr". `grep -rn '_assignee_resolver' src/` currently matches, in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`:

| # | site | role |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `outbound_field_diff.py:270` | core injection (`try/except`, per-`jira_key` closure) |
| 2 | `adapters/jira/backend.py:111` | Cloud `_JiraOutbound.resolve_assignee` getattr discovery |
| 3 | `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:118` | **DC** `_DCOutbound.resolve_assignee` getattr discovery |
| 4 | `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:331` | **DC** `JiraDataCenterBackend.__init__` injection onto `self.outbound`, `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` |
| — | `adapters/jira/backend.py:105,115`, `jira_datacenter/backend.py:115,324`, `jira_datacenter/_people.py:50` | docstrings that describe the attribute |
| — | `outbound_differ.py:384` | an UNRELATED local function that happens to share the name; leave it (renaming it is churn, and it is a nested `def`, not an attribute) |

Two implementers of the neutral `OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee` therefore have to change, not one: `adapters/jira/backend.py:92` (Cloud) and `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:109` (DC).

The two injections have DIFFERENT lifecycles, which is the one thing that needs a decision rather than a transcription:

- the core injection (#1) is built per remote key inside `compute_update_fields` and is the resolver the
  differ means to use;
- DC's (#4) is bound once in the backend constructor to the `jira.JIRA` client
  (`lambda name: _search_users_by_username(client, name)`), with no `jira_key`.

Today the core injection **overwrites** DC's constructor one whenever the differ runs, so "core wins, constructor is the fallback" is not a new policy — it is exactly the current behaviour, and the explicit form must preserve it.

Also note the call site is NOT where the injection is: `resolve_assignee` is invoked at `outbound_field_diff.py:398` inside `diff_canonical_fields`, a function that today receives no resolver. `compute_update_fields` (the injection point) calls it at line ~271, so the resolver has to be threaded through that hop as well.

## Approach

Thread the resolver **explicitly** instead of by attribute:

1. Widen the neutral port `OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee` in `_backend.py` with a keyword-only,
   defaulted `assignee_resolver` parameter, so the dependency appears in the contract and is typechecked.
2. Widen BOTH implementers to accept and forward it:
   - Cloud `adapters/jira/backend.py` → `AccountIdIdentity(resolver=assignee_resolver)`, deleting the getattr;
   - DC `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` → `NameIdentity(resolver=...)`, deleting the getattr.
3. Give DC's `_DCOutbound` a declared, typed constructor parameter for its client-bound resolver, and have
   `JiraDataCenterBackend.__init__` pass it there — deleting the `self.outbound._assignee_resolver = ...`
   assignment and its `# type: ignore[attr-defined]`. `resolve_assignee` prefers the explicit parameter and
   falls back to the constructor-supplied one, which reproduces today's overwrite semantics exactly.
4. Thread the resolver from `compute_update_fields` through `diff_canonical_fields` to the
   `resolve_assignee` call, and delete the attribute-injection block (and its `try/except ... : pass`).
5. Update the four/five docstrings that describe the attribute, and the test doubles that implement
   `resolve_assignee` so they accept the new keyword.
6. Keep every observable resolution outcome identical — this is plumbing.

### What "resolver absent" means, explicitly

The new parameter's default is `assignee_resolver=None`, and `None` keeps its CURRENT documented meaning: "no live account search is available on this path", which the identity models already define as the permissive, non-authoritative string match — `AccountIdIdentity(resolver=None).resolve("a@x.com", {"account_id": "acct-9"}) == ("a@x.com", False, False)`, pinned today by `test_user_identity_heldout.test_cloud_with_no_resolver_keeps_the_permissive_fallback`. The change is not the VALUE but its provenance: absence becomes a **declared default on the contract** that a caller chooses, instead of the invisible outcome of an injection that silently did not happen. Nothing raises, and no outcome moves.

## Why this is a separate ticket

Discovered while implementing story J4 [rebar:0a94-e104-7304-4d85], whose plan asserted the attribute was never set (true of PR #120, not of this tree) and whose AC4 asked for `grep -rn '_assignee_resolver' src/` to return nothing. Satisfying that literally means changing the **backend-neutral port signature**, which affects every backend — a materially wider blast radius than J4's three-file scope, and precisely the kind of core-risking change epic e369 deliberately sequenced away from the Data Center delivery path. J4 instead guarantees the property where it matters (the new identity models take the resolver as an explicit parameter and contain no `getattr` discovery at all) and defers this core cleanup here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `grep -rn '_assignee_resolver' src/` matches nothing except the unrelated local function in
      `outbound_differ.py`, and no `getattr(..., "_assignee_resolver", ...)` remains anywhere — in
      particular all four sites above are gone
- [x] the resolver is a declared parameter on the neutral `OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee` contract in
      `_backend.py`, and on BOTH implementers (Cloud and DC)
- [x] no `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` remains at either wiring site, and `make typecheck` passes
- [x] the six-state parity oracle in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_user_identity_heldout.py`
      (`_CLOUD_STATES` × `test_account_id_identity_matches_the_live_cloud_backend_state_for_state`)
      still passes and still compares the live backend against the live identity model. Its ONE line
      that builds `expected` by attribute-injection (`backend.outbound._assignee_resolver = ...`,
      line ~148) necessarily becomes the explicit parameter pass — that seam is what this ticket
      deletes, so the oracle cannot be literally byte-unmodified. Its six states, its expectations,
      and its live-vs-live construction stay exactly as they are; only the injection line changes
      form. Every OTHER assertion about `resolve_assignee`
      (`state/test_canonical_mapper_surface.py`, `test_backend_characterization.py`,
      `test_dc_backend_characterization.py`) passes UNMODIFIED
- [x] a test proves the degradation path is gone: with the resolver absent, the behavior is the documented
      explicit default rather than a silent non-authoritative fallback
- [x] a test proves DC still resolves authoritatively through its constructor-supplied resolver, and that a
      core-supplied resolver takes precedence over it (today's overwrite semantics, preserved)
baseline.summary: Replace the outbound mapper's _assignee_resolver attribute-injection with explicit parameter passing

## Context

Placeholder epic for R-4 from the DSO gap analysis (~/dso_rebar_plan_review_gap_report.md, R-4), REFRAMED during design review from 'cite bug history in rubrics' into a first-class, extensible mechanism.

DSO anchors its reviewer prompts with concrete worked examples from its own bug history (e.g. the --label vs --labels flag-mismatch defect; a false-positive from a 20-ticket calibration record). Concrete failures calibrate an LLM reviewer far better than abstract instructions. rebar has a BETTER source than DSO for this: the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar accumulates real per-criterion findings and false-positive signal.

## The concept (converged reframe)
A CALIBRATION-EXAMPLE LIBRARY for plan review:
- A CORE set of examples ships with rebar (per criterion: a sharp good/bad worked example).
- Projects can add their OWN project-specific examples -- mirroring the existing extension seam (.rebar/criteria_routing.json overlay + .rebar/prompts/ overrides). An absent overlay fails open to the core set.
- This makes rebar LEARN OVER TIME: it increases its effectiveness based on accumulated experience in a SPECIFIC project (a false positive seen once becomes a calibration anchor that prevents its recurrence).

This is the natural evolution of R-4 + the sidecar's per-criterion FP record + the existing project-overlay architecture.

## Open design questions (for the brainstorm session)
- [ ] WHERE in the four-pass pipeline is example context injected? (Pass-1 finder rubrics? Pass-2 verifier? both? Injecting into the verifier risks anchoring the FP-filter; injecting into the finder shapes what gets surfaced. Decide deliberately.)
- [ ] HOW are examples CURATED to prevent unbounded growth? (A per-criterion cap? Relevance/recency scoring? Dedup by norm_id? Promotion from sidecar -> curated library needs a gate so the prompt doesn't bloat and bust the cache.)
- [ ] Sourcing: hand-authored core vs auto-mined from sidecar corpus vs human-curated promotion of sidecar findings.
- [ ] Interaction with the CI prompt/routing drift-parity gate and prompt-cache efficiency (examples are prompt weight).
- [ ] Format/contract: how examples attach to a criterion (prompt front-matter? a sibling examples file keyed by criterion id?).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] This epic holds the reframed concept + open design questions from the review discussion
- [ ] Sequenced AFTER the G-series rubric enrichments (no point anchoring rubrics about to be rewritten)
- [ ] Placeholder only pending a dedicated brainstorming session
- [ ] A decision on injection point(s) in the plan-review pipeline
- [ ] A curation mechanism with a bounded-growth guarantee
- [ ] A core example set + a project-extension seam consistent with the existing overlay architecture
- [ ] A promotion path from observed sidecar findings/FPs into curated examples
baseline.summary: Plan-review calibration-example library (core + project-extensible, learns over time) (R-4)

## What

`transition <id> open in_progress` currently bypasses the plan-review claim gate that `claim` enforces. Starting work via a plain transition should apply the SAME validation (require a certified plan-review attestation, or `--force` with an audit note). The gate logic, today living in `src/rebar/_commands/claim.py::_plan_review_precheck`, must be consolidated into a single shared method that both the claim path and the transition path call — so the two cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The plan-review gate validation lives in ONE method (consolidated out of `claim.py` into a shared home, e.g. `src/rebar/_commands/gates.py`).
- [ ] `claim_compute` calls the consolidated method (behavior unchanged; existing claim-gate tests still pass).
- [ ] `transition_compute` calls the consolidated method when transitioning `open -> in_progress`, blocking (fail-closed) on a missing/stale attestation when the gate is enabled, and exempting bug/session_log.
- [ ] `--force` (with audit comment) bypasses the gate on the transition path, mirroring claim.
- [ ] New tests cover the transition open->in_progress gate (blocked / force-bypass / bug-exempt / earned-attestation-succeeds).
baseline.summary: Apply plan-review gate to open->in_progress transition; consolidate claim/transition gate logic

## Why
A senior-SDET-quality review of the test suite, run as an iterative loop, is the closing quality gate for the post-migration hardening.

## What
- Run an opus subagent primed as an SDET to review the project's testing (coverage adequacy, assertion quality, isolation, flakiness, fixture design, seam organization, contract coverage across the 3 interfaces, CI wiring).
- Remediate every important/critical finding.
- Repeat the review→remediate loop until a review returns NO important/critical findings.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] At least one opus SDET-primed review performed and its findings recorded
- [ ] All important/critical findings remediated (with tests/changes referenced)
- [ ] Review loop repeated until a clean pass (no important/critical findings)
- [ ] Suite green locally + CI after remediation
baseline.summary: Opus SDET review loop: review tests, remediate important/critical findings, repeat until clean

# Create canonical AGENTS.md (rebar dev guide) + reduce CLAUDE.md to a thin @AGENTS.md pointer

## Why

`AGENTS.md` is read natively by Codex, Cursor, Copilot's coding agent, Zed, Windsurf, Amp, Factory, Jules, Devin, RooCode, and Cline — so one canonical `AGENTS.md` covers the ecosystem, and Claude Code is bridged by a one-line import. This also fixes the size/duplication anti-pattern: sections that duplicate a `docs/` file become one-line pointers.

## What

Author a lean `AGENTS.md` at the repo root that keeps rebar-INTERNAL developer specifics inline and replaces every already-documented topic with a one-line `docs/…md` pointer. Then reduce `CLAUDE.md` to a single `@AGENTS.md` import plus an optional `## Claude Code` section.

- **INLINE (kept in full):** intro; the record-work/claim-before-you-work operating rules; the
  parallel-agent loop; env bootstrap (`make install`/`make hooks`); module-size policy; Serena
  navigation; a **condensed** Git/Gerrit section; a 6-line library snippet.
- **POINTER (one line each), to EXISTING docs:** gate protocols → `docs/plan-review-gate.md`;
  quality gates + ticket template + project criteria → `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md`; MCP
  tool set → `docs/mcp-reference.md`; store-shares-writes + parent-first cascade →
  `docs/concurrency.md`; ticket model → `docs/ticket-model.md` (created by S1); session logs →
  `docs/event-schema.md` + `docs/user-guide.md`; library reference → `docs/reuse-surface.md`; the
  LLM agent-operations topic → `docs/llm-framework.md`; the completion close-gate →
  `docs/plan-review-gate.md`. These are POINTERS only — this story writes no content into those
  docs (their content already exists; the two "stowaway" topics currently mixed into CLAUDE.md's
  Session-logs heading are simply not carried into AGENTS.md).

## Scope

In: new `AGENTS.md`, rewritten `CLAUDE.md`. No writes to any `docs/*` file (pointers only). Out: `CLAUDE.local.md` (S3), the shim/reference sweep (S6), and code. **Depends on S1** (already linked `depends_on`): `docs/ticket-model.md` must exist before `AGENTS.md` points at it. Rollback is a plain `git revert` (docs/text only).

## Design decisions (spike-validated)

- The `@AGENTS.md` import is PROVEN in Claude Code 2.1.211 (headless canary + official docs
  recommend exactly `@AGENTS.md` + `## Claude Code`); no symlink fallback.
- Imports "load at launch" and do not reduce context, so the token win comes from de-dup into docs
  and **AGENTS.md must itself be lean.** A grounded estimate puts a complete lean file at ~152
  lines and ≤ 200 only if the Git/Gerrit section is condensed to agent-actionable rules and defers
  the full recipe to `CONTRIBUTING.md` (verbatim Gerrit → ~215-230, which misses the target).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `AGENTS.md` exists at repo root and is ≤ 200 lines.
  - Proving: `test -f AGENTS.md && [ "$(wc -l < AGENTS.md)" -le 200 ]`
- [ ] The Git/Gerrit section is condensed (≤ ~55 lines) and defers the full recipe to
  `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
  - Proving: `rg -q 'CONTRIBUTING.md' AGENTS.md`; reviewer confirms the section ≤ 55 lines.
- [ ] Each already-documented topic is a one-line pointer, not a restated section.
  - Proving: `rg -n 'docs/plan-review-gate.md|docs/mcp-reference.md|docs/ticket-model.md|docs/concurrency.md|docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md|docs/llm-framework.md' AGENTS.md`
- [ ] Every `docs/…md` path that `AGENTS.md` points at resolves to a real file (no dangling
  pointer; targets created by S1 are in place by then).
  - Proving: `for p in $(rg -o 'docs/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.md' AGENTS.md | sort -u); do test -f "$p" || { echo "MISSING $p"; exit 1; }; done`
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` is a single `@AGENTS.md` import + optional `## Claude Code` section, ≤ 30 lines.
  - Proving: `[ "$(rg -c '@AGENTS.md' CLAUDE.md)" = 1 ] && [ "$(wc -l < CLAUDE.md)" -le 30 ]`
- [ ] `make lint` passes.
  - Proving: `make lint`
baseline.summary: Create canonical AGENTS.md (rebar dev guide) + reduce CLAUDE.md to a thin @AGENTS.md pointer

## Context / Problem

With the port defined (S2 [rebar:ce4d-c3ca-5412-4798]) and selection wired (S3 [rebar:94f9-a9a0-7475-4e75]), the backend-neutral core still named Jira concretely — both by constructing the Jira transport inline AND by importing the vendor field mappers directly. This story routes the **transport-construction** sites through the `Backend` port so the core stops building an `AcliClient` inline, and de-hardcodes the provider-identity `"jira"` literals.

## Scope split (recorded at implementation time)

The original story bundled TWO kinds of rewiring. They were split because the second requires a dependency-injection refactor that fights the standalone `spec_from_file_location` test-loader convention and is independently reviewable:

- **Landed here (this change):** the four transport/construction sites, the provider-identity
  literals, and the `apply_handlers` exception-class import — a behaviour-preserving change proven
  by the full reconcile suite staying green.
- **Split to follow-up [rebar:4af8-2d88-719e-4478]:** routing the core *importer* sites
  (`outbound_differ`/`inbound_differ`/`apply_inbound`/`outbound_comments`/`inbound_translate`) off
  the vendor mappers via injection, and single-sourcing the leak-fix constants
  (`outbound_links._RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK`, ADF-sizing, value-maps) under `adapters/jira/`.

## Scope (landed)

Transport/construction sites routed through `select_backend(load_config()).transport`:
- `applier._load_acli` and `fetcher._load_acli` now return the backend transport directly.
- `run_differs.py`'s outbound-diff client and `_attestation.build_acli_client_from_env()`
  obtain the transport from the selected backend (fail-fast env behaviour preserved).
- The jira factory builds the `AcliClient` with `resolve_jira_settings(project_default="DIG")`
  so the transport carries the project for every consumer.
- `apply_handlers.py` catches `AssigneeNotFoundError` via a direct import (not `ctx.acli.…`).
- `apply_inbound_records.py`'s two provider-identity `"jira"` literals flow from the selected
  backend's `vendor` (the `validate_creation_channel("jira")` vocabulary key is retained).
- ~34 `_load_acli` test doubles migrated module-shaped → transport-shaped (assertions unchanged).

## Testing

## Context

When the plan-review claim gate re-fires on a CONTAINER ticket (epic/story with children) that is
mid-execution, it reviews the plan as if FRESH — blind to which children are already delivered. It
then re-litigates acceptance criteria already shipped by closed+attested children: false BLOCKs and
coaching to tighten AC that is done, plus a slow whole-context review of settled work.

Re-fires are legitimate but infrequent — a paused epic reopened (ADR 0009 invalidates an
attestation signed before the reopen), or a material course-correction to the epic plan
(material-fingerprint invalidation). The claim CASCADE is not the driver (it only fires while the
parent is `open`). Code-drift invalidation is INTENTIONAL and unchanged (a container's plan is
reviewed against codebase state — G6 runs at container scope): this epic changes only what a
re-fired review DOES, not when it fires.

## What we build

A deterministic Pass-3 "completion floor" (third floor beside the novelty floor ADR 0008 and the
drift-refresh path ADR 0002), fed by a separate `plan_review_completion` Pass-2 sub-call (mirroring
`plan_review_novelty`) that answers three atomic orthogonal sub-questions per finding: ATTRIBUTION
(which closed child), CONTAINMENT (limited vs spans open), LAYER (plan-semantics vs
delivered-functionality). Pass-1 stays completion-blind (full recall); the coach is unchanged.

## Scope

- IN: the Pass-2 completion sub-call + three sub-questions; the Pass-3 completion floor + config
  evidence-gate + priority floor; the delivered-now predicate (attestation reuse + in-epic sibling
  supersede); sidecar recording; calibration gold-set + tests.
- OUT (deferred, separate epics): partial-completion attestation for in-progress children; a
  structured `resolution` enum on `close`; the sidecar re-injection queue; an optional second LAYER
  binary. In-progress children stay FULLY in scope in v1.

## Alternatives considered

- (a) Exempt epics from the claim gate — REJECTED: discards the container security review ADR 0016
  added (a container epic that stands up infrastructure would go unreviewed).
- (b) Completion-aware container review — CHOSEN; hybrid = (b) + keying on VERIFIED delivery
  (completion attestation) + in-epic sibling supersede.
- Decomposition-drift-only freshness (never invalidate a container on code drift) — REJECTED:
  code-drift invalidation is intentional; a container's plan IS reviewed vs codebase state (G6 runs
  at container scope).
- A single composite predicate instead of three sub-questions — REJECTED: attribution / containment
  / layer are orthogonal (identity / spatial scope / artifact layer); folding them loses the
  distinctions and re-couples model category + severity error.
- Hide delivered children / review only open children — REJECTED: blinds coherence + security to
  delivered<->open interactions; we FREEZE delivered children as visible context, not hide them.
- Tag- or progress-note-based suppression — REJECTED: unsigned + gameable (prompt-injection surface
  into a security-sensitive gate); we key on the signed completion attestation.
- Run the completion-verifier to drive scoping — REJECTED: FAIL-by-construction mid-flight + signing
  ambiguity (needs a third attestation kind); we READ the attestation closed children already carry.
- Reuse the novelty sub-answer mechanism (add the three completion questions to NOVELTY_SUBANSWERS)
  instead of a parallel sub-call — REJECTED: completion keys on a DIFFERENT context input (the
  delivered-children manifest) than novelty (prior findings), so a separate sub-call preserves the
  Pass-1 independence invariant by construction; they share the kernel sub-answer machinery, not context.

## Acceptance Criteria

Decision (recorded, not a forward deliverable): option (b)/hybrid chosen — see the decision comment, '## Alternatives considered', and the completion session log.
- [ ] A separate `plan_review_completion` Pass-2 sub-call (mirroring `plan_review_novelty`) emits, per finding, {attribution, containment, layer} with fail-safe values (insufficient/n/a/spans-open/delivered-functionality all keep).
- [ ] Pass-3 completion floor drops a finding iff attribution=delivered-now-child AND containment=limited AND layer=plan-semantics AND priority<floor AND criterion not in {security,contract}; gated behind an evidence-gate flag + configurable priority floor (mirroring the novelty floor).
- [ ] `delivered-now` = valid completion attestation (validity-on-read, reusing the `_child_closure_findings` predicate) OR superseded by a sibling under the same parent; force-closed/abandoned/in-progress children are NOT delivered and stay in scope.
- [ ] Drops recorded to the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar (joinable, observable) and recomputed every run (a reopened/un-delivered child auto-resurfaces its findings).
- [ ] A durable ADR (`docs/adr/0020-completion-aware-container-plan-review.md`) codifies the new contracts (sub-call schema + closed enums, delivered-now predicate, completion floor + config, sidecar drop_reason) — inline AC + session log are not the durable record.
- [ ] Tests: a partially-complete epic review drops delivered plan-semantics findings yet preserves (a) a delivered child's delivered-functionality/security finding, (b) a finding spanning an open sibling, (c) all findings on a force-closed child; plus a calibration gold-set of must-never-suppress cases.
- [ ] A re-fired container review does not re-litigate delivered AC: findings limited to a
- [ ] Suppression is deterministic in Pass-3, keyed on VERIFIED delivery (completion attestation or
- [ ] No change to WHEN a review is invalidated (code-drift stays), no `close`-op change, no new
baseline.summary: Completion-aware plan-review for container tickets (epics/stories with children)

# The shared webhook/rerun secret is written to journald in every access-log line

## Context / Problem

The review-bot receiver is a uvicorn app, and uvicorn's default access log records the full request line INCLUDING THE QUERY STRING. Both authenticated endpoints take their secret as a QUERY PARAMETER (`?token=...`), so every request writes the secret to stderr -> journald in clear text:

    INFO:  127.0.0.1:34184 - "POST /rerun?token=<the actual secret>&change=1323 HTTP/1.1" 202 Accepted
    INFO:  172.21.0.4:33070 - "POST /webhook?token=<the actual secret> HTTP/1.1" 202 Accepted

Observed directly in the production container's journal (`journalctl CONTAINER_NAME=compose-review-bot-1`).

## Why it matters

* **The secret is the auth for both endpoints.** `config.py:239` is
  `webhook_token = os.environ.get("WEBHOOK_TOKEN", "").strip() or bot_token`, and this
  container sets no `WEBHOOK_TOKEN`, so the webhook token IS `GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN` — the
  review bot's Gerrit credential. Anything that can read the journal therefore learns a
  credential that can both drive reviews AND act as the bot against Gerrit.
* **The blast radius is wider than the box.** journald content flows into anything that reads
  it: `infra/scripts/observability.sh` greps the same journal, operators paste log excerpts into
  tickets and chat, and any future log-shipping would carry the secret off-host. It also means
  the secret cannot be treated as unexposed after any incident that involved sharing logs.
* **It is a fail-open exposure, not a fail-closed one:** nothing errors, nothing alarms, and the
  endpoint keeps working — so there is no signal that would ever surface it.

DISCOVERED the hard way: an agent grepping the journal for `/rerun` activity while working [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a] surfaced the token into a session transcript. That is the failure mode — the secret is sitting in the most-grepped log on the box.

**This ticket does not fix the exposure that already happened.** The token in the journal (and anywhere journal excerpts have been shared) must be treated as compromised and ROTATED independently of the code fix. Rotation alone is also not sufficient: without the fix, the new token is logged the moment it is first used.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py` — the `/webhook` and `/rerun` handlers and/or the uvicorn
  logging configuration (`configure_logging`).
- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot` — the `uvicorn` invocation, if the access-log format or
  its disabling belongs there.
- `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` — the `/rerun` recipe currently instructs the operator to
  put the token in a URL, which is what puts it in the log; and a rotation note.

## Approach (options, with the tradeoff stated)

1. **Move the secret out of the query string** — accept it as a header (e.g. `X-Rebar-Token`) or
   in the POST body. Cleanest: access logs record the request line, not headers. But
   `/webhook` is called BY GERRIT, so the Gerrit-side webhook configuration must be able to
   send it — check what the `webhook` plugin supports before assuming a header is expressible.
   `/rerun` is operator-driven and can move to a header immediately regardless.
2. **Scrub the access log** — install a uvicorn log filter that redacts `token=[^&]*`. Keeps the
   URL shape, protects the value, and covers BOTH endpoints even if Gerrit cannot send a header.
   Weaker in principle (the secret still transits a URL, so it can leak via any other component
   that logs URLs) but it is the only option that works without a Gerrit-side change.
3. Do both: header for `/rerun`, redaction filter as the backstop for `/webhook`.

Do NOT simply disable the access log — it is load-bearing for debugging and for the `observability.sh` greps.

## Testing

The oracle must assert on the EMITTED LOG LINE, not on the handler's behaviour, because the handler is already correct — it is the logging that leaks:

- drive a request carrying a known sentinel token through the app with `caplog` (or a captured
  uvicorn handler) and assert the sentinel does NOT appear in any emitted record, while the
  route and status DO;
- verify RED by reverting the fix and observing the sentinel reappear;
- if a header is adopted, a second test that a query-string token is REJECTED (or at least not
  logged), so the old path cannot quietly persist.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] the webhook/rerun secret no longer appears in any log record the receiver emits, proven by
      a test that asserts on the emitted log line with a sentinel value and is verified RED by
      reverting the fix.
- [x] the mechanism is stated in the code where the choice is made (header vs redaction filter),
      including WHY — so a future change does not reintroduce the query-string form as a
      convenience.
- [x] `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md`'s `/rerun` recipe no longer instructs the operator to
      put the token in a URL, and carries a note that the previous token must be treated as
      compromised and rotated.
- [x] the access log still records route and status for both endpoints (the observability greps
      and debugging value are not sacrificed to fix this).
- [x] ROTATION IS TRACKED SEPARATELY AND EXPLICITLY: the currently-logged token is rotated, and
      that rotation is recorded as done rather than assumed, since the code fix does not
      un-leak what is already in journald.
baseline.summary: Review-bot logs the webhook token in plaintext on every /webhook and /rerun request
