Keep verbose `session_log` bodies out of the dependency-graph and store-health hot paths, and out of default `list`, while keeping them in `search` and `show`.

## Why

`reduce_all_tickets()` compiles full bodies with no lazy-loading and backs `ready`, `next_batch`, `deps`, `validate`, and `list`. Verbose logs must not tax those. The requester chose "searchable, hidden from list": logs appear in keyword `search` and `show` but nowhere that would slow the constant graph/health work.

## What

- Add an `exclude_ticket_types` (or `exclude_session_logs`) parameter to
  `reduce_all_tickets()` in `src/rebar/reducer/_api.py`, mirroring the existing
  `exclude_archived` / `exclude_deleted` pattern.
- Default it on for graph/health callers: `src/rebar/graph/_ready.py`
  (`find_ready_tickets`), `src/rebar/graph/_graph.py` (`build_dep_graph`),
  `src/rebar/_engine_support/next_batch.py` (`compute`), and
  `src/rebar/_engine_support/validate.py` (`validate_state` health checks).
- Exclude `session_log` from default `list` (surface only on explicit
  `--type=session_log`) in `src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py` /
  `src/rebar/reducer/_filters.py`.
- Keep `session_log` in the `search` corpus (`src/rebar/reducer/search.py`) and in
  `show` (single-ticket reduce path unchanged).

## Scope

Read-path visibility and graph/health isolation only. The recent-logs command is a separate story.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ready`, `next_batch`, `deps`, and `validate` never include `session_log`
      tickets and their timings are unaffected by log count/size (asserted).
- [ ] Default `list` omits `session_log`; `list --type=session_log` returns them.
- [ ] `search <keywords>` matches `session_log` bodies; `show` returns a
      `session_log` fully.
- [ ] `validate` does not flag `session_log` tickets as orphaned/empty/etc.
- [ ] Tests assert both the exclusions and the inclusions.
baseline.summary: Isolate session_log from graph/health compile paths and default list

baseline.description:
# op-cert: AWS IaC + deploy of the trusted gate service (zero fixed-cost: existing VM + API Gateway SigV4) + live authenticated integrity test

## Why
The trusted gate service (the sibling service story) is only a trust anchor once it runs in the controlled environment with SigV4-authenticated access and a key nobody else can read. This story declares that as code, **actually deploys it** (an authenticated AWS CLI is provided — the deploy is in scope), and proves the deployed endpoint end-to-end. Deployment decisions are settled in the epic's "Producer-signing & compute-runtime design resolution", **cost-verified against the live account**: rebar's entire AWS footprint is the one t4g.large `rebar-gerrit` box (+ Route 53 + free SSM parameters), so the binding constraint is **zero increase in fixed monthly cost** — the service rides the existing box (the compose slot freed by the autolander's retirement, ADR 0047) behind an API Gateway HTTP API (pay-per-request, no fixed fee), with the key in free SSM Parameter Store. A dedicated Fargate/NLB/Secrets-Manager/KMS-CMK stack was rejected (~$50+/mo new spend for isolation ADR 0046 L4 does not require).

**Hard dependency (not yet on `main`):** the sibling service story provides `src/rebar/opcert_service/` and `infra/compose/Dockerfile.opcert` — neither exists on `main` yet; this story starts only after that story lands (enforced by the `depends_on` link).

## What
- **Terraform — extend the existing `infra/terraform/`** (the module that already declares the
  Gerrit EC2, its IAM instance profile, and the data volume):
  - an **API Gateway HTTP API** (v2) whose routes set `authorization_type = "AWS_IAM"` (SigV4
    — a ROUTE attribute; HTTP API v2 has NO separate `aws_apigatewayv2_authorizer` resource for
    IAM), over TLS. The integration URI is **`https://` to the box's HOST-nginx TLS origin**
    (nginx + certbot run as HOST services on the box — `infra/scripts/compose-up.sh` header —
    with TLS on 443 at the Elastic-IP-bound hostname; NOT `http://…:80`, which the existing
    config 301-redirects and would break the integration) for the `/opcert/` routes, injecting a shared origin-guard header. Caller restriction is
    identity-policy-based (an HTTP API has no resource policy): `AWS_IAM` auth requires SigV4,
    and the IaC CREATES the admin role it restricts to — `aws_iam_role` **`rebar-opcert-admin`**
    (no such role pre-exists in `infra/terraform/`), trust policy limited to the principal ARNs
    supplied via a new variable `opcert_admin_principal_arns` (set at deploy to the operator's
    IAM principals), with an inline policy granting `execute-api:Invoke` scoped to exactly this
    API's execution ARN — and no other principal/policy in the IaC grants Invoke;
  - an **SSM Parameter Store SecureString** `/rebar/prod/opcert-ed25519-key` (declared with a
    placeholder `value` + `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [value] }`, so the out-of-band-seeded
    key is never reverted or clobbered by a later `terraform apply`) holding the
    **passphrase-free Ed25519 private key**. NO new IAM
    grant: the parameter lives under `/rebar/prod/`, which the instance profile's existing
    `rebar-gerrit-ssm-params-read` policy (`infra/terraform/iam.tf`) already covers — and
    nothing broader is added;
  - the **origin-guard header provisioning path**: Terraform generates the guard value with
    `random_password` — the `hashicorp/random` provider is ADDED to
    `infra/terraform/versions.tf` `required_providers` (today it pins only `hashicorp/aws
    ~> 5.0`; `terraform init` refreshes `.terraform.lock.hcl`) — stores it as SSM SecureString
    `/rebar/prod/opcert-origin-guard` (also under the existing grant), and maps it as a static
    request-header parameter (`X-Opcert-Guard`) on the API Gateway integration. Unlike the KEY
    parameter, the guard parameter is fully Terraform-managed and carries NO
    `lifecycle ignore_changes` (its value IS `random_password.result`; rotation =
    `terraform apply -replace=` on the random resource, which updates the SSM value and the
    integration header together) — the `ignore_changes = [value]` guard applies ONLY to the
    operator-seeded Ed25519 key parameter;
  - NO new fixed-monthly-cost resources: no Fargate/ECS service, no load balancer/VPC link, no
    Secrets Manager secret, no customer KMS CMK, and no `kms:Sign` anywhere (SSHSIG signing is
    performed by the service itself; AWS KMS has no Ed25519 signing).
- **Compose — extend `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`**: an `opcert` service on
  `infra/compose/Dockerfile.opcert` (sibling story) with env `REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID` and the SSM
  parameter names; an nginx route `/opcert/` → the service that rejects requests whose
  `X-Opcert-Guard` header does not match. On the box the guard value is materialized from its
  SSM parameter by `infra/scripts/materialize-opcert-guard.sh` into a HOST-nginx map entry
  (nginx runs as a host service, not a container) with NAMED files and NO install-step
  ownership problem: `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template` — which today has NO `/opcert/`
  location — gains, IN THE TEMPLATE ITSELF, the guard map with a fail-closed default and a
  GLOB include (`map $http_x_opcert_guard $opcert_guard_ok { default 0; include
  /etc/nginx/opcert-guard*.conf; }` — nginx accepts a zero-match glob include, unlike a
  missing literal include) plus the `location /opcert/ { if ($opcert_guard_ok = 0) { return
  403; } proxy_pass … }` block routing to the compose service. The DENY-ALL default is
  therefore STRUCTURAL in the template: a fresh boot with no materialized file serves 403 on
  /opcert/ and nginx starts cleanly — no separate default-file install step exists to own.
  `infra/scripts/materialize-opcert-guard.sh` writes only the one-line map entry
  `/etc/nginx/opcert-guard.map.conf` (`"<value>" 1;`) from the SSM parameter and reloads
  nginx; the guard value also lands in the service env. It is WIRED INTO the boot orchestrator
  `infra/scripts/compose-up.sh` alongside the existing materialize/.env-regeneration calls,
  running BEFORE `docker compose up` (the precedent ordering), and it finishes with
  `nginx -s reload` so a guard rotation re-run takes effect (at first boot the reload is a
  no-op-safe refresh). Rotation hazard closed explicitly; (b) ROTATION — the documented
  runbook is two steps in order: `terraform apply -replace=random_password.opcert_guard`
  (updates the SSM value + the API Gateway static header), then re-run
  `materialize-opcert-guard.sh` (rewrites the nginx map + `nginx -s reload`); between the two
  steps /opcert/ serves 403 — fail-closed, a brief and acceptable rotation window following the existing
  precedent (`infra/gerrit/materialize-deploy-key.sh` / `materialize-g2p-config.sh` — SSM →
  file). It is WIRED INTO the boot orchestrator `infra/scripts/compose-up.sh` alongside the
  existing materialize/.env-regeneration calls, running BEFORE `docker compose up` (the
  precedent ordering), and it finishes with `nginx -s reload` so a guard rotation re-run takes
  effect on the host nginx (at first boot the reload is a no-op-safe refresh) — the same value Terraform maps onto the API Gateway integration, closing
  the loop.
- **Deploy + prove** (authenticated AWS CLI): `terraform apply`; generate the key locally
  (`ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N ""`) and seed the SecureString (the key exists nowhere else).
  **Key-loss recovery runbook (documented in the story's deploy notes):** if the SSM parameter
  is deleted or state is lost, the trust anchor is NOT recoverable and is not meant to be —
  recovery = mint a NEW keypair, re-seed the parameter, and pin the new public key as a NEW
  era entry in `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` (`added_at_log_position` = current tickets
  tip) while the lost key's entry is revoked with a grandfather pin at the loss point — certs
  already stored under the lost key stay valid (the era-anchor model), and only new certs
  require the new key. No historical re-certification is needed;
  deploy the compose service on the box; pin the environment's public key + `env_id` into
  `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` per the epic's "Authoritative era anchor" resolution
  (`added_at_log_position`, operator-stamped at the current tickets tip); then the live checks — a
  SigV4-signed job round-trip (submit → poll → terminal status), an unsigned request rejected
  (401/403 at API Gateway), and a direct-to-origin request without the guard header rejected.
## Scope
- In: the Terraform extension, compose/nginx wiring, key generation + SSM seeding procedure,
  the real deploy, the live round-trip evidence, the trusted-env pinning.
- Out: the service code and Dockerfile (sibling story); any change to rebar library code; the
  merge-gate consumer (shipped, 4214); resizing or re-homing the existing box.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `infra/terraform/` declares: the API Gateway HTTP API (v2) with
      `authorization_type = "AWS_IAM"` on its routes over TLS,
      `execute-api:Invoke` granted only to the IaC-created `rebar-opcert-admin` role (trust policy
      from `opcert_admin_principal_arns`; the assertion method is STRUCTURED and SELF-FAILING —
      the literal command the test runs exits non-zero on any violation:
      `terraform plan -out=tf.plan && terraform show -json tf.plan | jq -e
      '[.planned_values.root_module.resources[] | select(.type == "aws_iam_role_policy" or
      .type == "aws_iam_policy") | {label: .name, s: (.values.policy | fromjson | .Statement[])}
      | select([.s.Action] | flatten | any(. == "execute-api:Invoke"))] | length == 1 and
      .[0].label == "opcert_admin_invoke"'` — where `.name` in `terraform show -json` is the
      Terraform RESOURCE LABEL, so the invoke policy is declared with the pinned label
      `aws_iam_role_policy.opcert_admin_invoke` on the `rebar-opcert-admin` role; exactly one
      statement grants Invoke and it is that resource, else the command exits non-zero), the `hashicorp/random` provider in `required_providers`,
      the box-origin integration with the static `X-Opcert-Guard` request-header mapping; and
      the two SecureString parameters (the key parameter guarded by
      `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [value] }`)
      (`/rebar/prod/opcert-ed25519-key`, `/rebar/prod/opcert-origin-guard`) under the existing
      `rebar-gerrit-ssm-params-read` path grant with NO new/broader IAM grant. EVERY AC1 sub-claim is asserted with its own literal `jq -e` query against the one
      `terraform show -json tf.plan` output, each exiting non-zero on violation:
      (a) https URI — `.planned_values.root_module.resources[] |
      select(.type=="aws_apigatewayv2_integration") | .values.integration_uri |
      startswith("https://")`;
      (b) guard header — `... select(.type=="aws_apigatewayv2_integration") |
      .values.request_parameters | has("append:header.X-Opcert-Guard")`;
      (c+d) parameters — `[.planned_values.root_module.resources[] |
      select(.type=="aws_ssm_parameter") | {n:.values.name, t:.values.type}] | (map(.n) |
      contains(["/rebar/prod/opcert-ed25519-key","/rebar/prod/opcert-origin-guard"])) and
      all(.t=="SecureString")`;
      (e) route auth — `[.planned_values.root_module.resources[] |
      select(.type=="aws_apigatewayv2_route") | .values.authorization_type] | length > 0 and
      all(. == "AWS_IAM")` (aggregated with `all()` — a per-route stream would let `jq -e`
      pass on the last route alone);
      (f) key-param `lifecycle.ignore_changes` — `.configuration.root_module.resources[] |
      select(.address=="aws_ssm_parameter.opcert_ed25519_key") |
      .lifecycle_meta_arguments.ignore_changes? // empty | length > 0` (in `terraform show
      -json`'s `configuration` section lifecycle meta-arguments nest under
      `.lifecycle_meta_arguments`, not `.lifecycle`, and are absent from `planned_values`);
      (g) provider — `.configuration.provider_config | has("random")`.
- [ ] `terraform fmt -check` and `terraform validate` pass (asserted by a test or CI step);
      `terraform plan` against the provided account succeeds.
- [ ] `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` + nginx config gain the `opcert` service and the
      guarded `/opcert/` route; a test asserts the service entry, the env wiring
      (`REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID`, parameter names), that the nginx route requires the
      `X-Opcert-Guard` header, and that the materialize script (per the `infra/gerrit/materialize-*.sh`
      precedent) renders the guard value from its SSM parameter — tested hermetically with a
      stub `aws` executable prepended to `PATH` that returns a fixture value (no live SSM or
      account access in unit tests). The test also asserts `infra/scripts/compose-up.sh` calls
      the materialize script before `docker compose up`, that the script ends with
      `nginx -s reload` (host nginx), that the TEMPLATE itself contains the fail-closed guard
      map (`default 0;` + the zero-match-safe glob include) and the guarded `/opcert/`
      location, and that the Terraform integration URI uses the `https://` scheme.
- [ ] The deployed environment's public key and `env_id` are pinned in
      `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` (with `added_at_log_position` per the epic's SUPERSEDING "Authoritative era anchor" resolution — the tickets-branch log-position era fields, not the superseded `added_at_commit` main-SHA form); a
      test asserts the entry parses and the `env_id` matches the compose service's
      `REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The service is deployed from `infra/` via the authenticated AWS CLI
      and the live checks pass: a SigV4-signed job round-trip succeeds; an unsigned request is
      rejected at API Gateway; a direct-to-origin request without the guard header is rejected —
      evidence: a comment recording the `terraform apply` outputs (API endpoint id/URL) and the
      captured round-trip + both rejections.
baseline.summary: op-cert: AWS IaC + deploy of the trusted gate service (zero fixed-cost: existing VM + API Gateway SigV4) + live authenticated integrity test

# `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py` is at exactly 800/800 LOC

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py` is at **exactly 800** lines — the hard cap in `.github/module-size-limit.txt`, enforced by the CI module-size gate with no allowlist. Any change to fsck of any size, including a one-line bug fix, cannot land today. This is the third instance of the same pattern (`valiant-balladic-willet` did `passes.py`, `splurgy-witless-flamingo` did `_ref_lock.py`), so the remediation is framed as an architectural rework of the fsck cluster rather than a mechanical split: the file is pinned because four concerns are fused in it, and each new check grows the fused whole.

The full concern map, the recurrence mechanism and the rationale for each cut are recorded as the architectural-analysis comment on this ticket. This description states the resulting plan.

## Approach

Separate `fsck.py` by concern along call-graph seams that already exist. `fsck.py` today holds four concerns; two of them already have a single internal call site, which is the seam a prior author cut and stopped at.

1. **Enumeration + per-ticket validators** move to a new `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_scan.py`:
   `_scan` (the store walk — JSON validity, CREATE presence, stale index.lock, snapshot
   consistency, forward-compat event types, and the advisory ensures/authorship tallies) and
   `_check_snapshot`, which `_scan` is the only caller of. This is the cluster that grows with
   every check added.
2. **Tracker-level health** moves to a new `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_tracker_health.py`:
   `_tracker_health` and the four checks it fans out to — `_tracker_sync_status`,
   `_branch_mismatch`, `_foreign_store_paths`, `foreign_store_path_list` — plus the
   `_FSCK_GIT_TIMEOUT` watchdog they share. `_tracker_health` is already the single entry
   point, called once from `_scan`; these checks share a shape the per-ticket checks do not
   (each inspects the tracker as a whole via git/config, each yields at most one line, each
   decides for itself whether that line is counted).
Within `fsck_scan.py` the per-check separation is carried through rather than stopping at the file boundary: `_scan` becomes a thin orchestrator over one function per check (`_check_json_validity`, `_check_create_events`, `_check_index_lock`, `_check_ticket_snapshots`, `_check_forward_compat`, `_advisory_lines`), and `_check_snapshot` sheds its filename-parsing loop to `_active_event_map`. This is required as well as cleaner: the complexity ratchet (`scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py`) keys accepted debt by `path::symbol`, and its CI `--lock` mode refuses **any** new key — so moving the two baselined functions wholesale would read as newly added debt needing an administrator override. Decomposing them under the C901 threshold instead means `.github/complexity-baseline.json` **loses** both fsck entries and gains none, retiring 43 points of recorded debt rather than relocating it.

3. **Report shaping + command driver** stay in `fsck.py`: `_transform_json` /
   `_STRUCTURED_KINDS` plus `fsck_cli`, `_repair_cli`, `_run_live_repair`,
   `_missing_tracker_result`. Report shaping is roughly 45 LOC on its own, so extracting it
   would create a sub-100-LOC module, which the module-size policy forbids; it is also the
   output half of the same command surface the driver owns. `fsck.py` therefore becomes what
   its name should mean — the fsck **command**: parse argv, drive scan or repair, render.

Dependency direction is strictly one-way and matches the existing call graph: `fsck.py` -> `fsck_scan.py` -> {`fsck_tracker_health.py`, `fsck_repair.py`, `fsck_authorship.py`}. No new edges, no cycles.

The change is **behaviour-preserving**: identical findings, identical text and JSON output, identical exit codes. No check logic, message string, or counted/informational classification is altered — code moves, and imports are rewired.

`fsck.<symbol>` attribute access is load-bearing outside the module: `_store/gitutil.py` and `_commands/fsck_recover.py` import `_resolve_tracker_git_dir`, `_commands/tracker_maintenance.py` imports `foreign_store_path_list`, and tests call `fsck._check_snapshot`, `fsck._scan`, `fsck._tracker_sync_status`, `fsck._foreign_store_paths`. Every one **calls** the symbol; none monkeypatch it, so `fsck.py` keeps re-exports for all of them and those callers stay untouched. The two symbols that ARE monkeypatched on `fsck` (`_reconciler_in_flight`, `owned_repair_pause`) are consumed by `_run_live_repair`, which stays in `fsck.py` — so the trap flamingo recorded, a moved function resolving a patched dependency from the wrong module's globals, does not arise.

Out of scope: `_engine_support/bridge_fsck.py` (a different command, no call edge here) and `fsck_repair.py` (already a clean single-concern extraction).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py` — becomes the command driver + report shaping; keeps
  re-exports for external `fsck.<symbol>` callers.
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_scan.py` — new; `_scan` + `_check_snapshot`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_tracker_health.py` — new; `_tracker_health`, `_tracker_sync_status`,
  `_branch_mismatch`, `_foreign_store_paths`, `foreign_store_path_list`, `_FSCK_GIT_TIMEOUT`.
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` — drops the two `fsck.py` entries the decomposition retires.

No other file changes. Tests are not edited: their behavioural assertions and their `fsck.<symbol>` bindings must keep passing unchanged, which is the primary evidence that the refactor preserved behaviour.

## Testing

No new testable behaviour is introduced — this is a pure structural refactor, so the existing suite is the oracle and is run unmodified:

- The fsck suites under `tests/interfaces/store/` plus
  `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_creation_channel_compaction.py` pass unchanged, covering both
  output formats, the repair paths, and the direct `fsck._check_snapshot` / `fsck._scan` bindings.
- `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` passes.
- The full CI selection `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` passes, catching any
  caller whose `fsck.<symbol>` binding the move broke.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py` is at most 400 lines — verified by

baseline.description:
## Summary
Session logs "bleed" between sessions: a new agent session appends to the previous
session's `session_log` ticket instead of starting a fresh one, producing a single
enormous log that combines multiple unrelated sessions.

## Root cause (suspected)
The "current session log" is tracked by a **local, git-ignored pointer**,
`.rebar/current_session_log`. `append_session_log` / `log_session` / `session-log append`
create a log on first use and then append to whatever the pointer names. The pointer is
**never scoped to the actual session/agent** and is never auto-rotated at session
boundaries — so once written it persists across sessions, and every later session's
appends land on the same old log ticket until someone manually runs
`session-log start`. rebar has no session identifier of its own (see related epic
`crust-fetch-stump`), so it cannot detect that a new session has begun.

## Reproduction Steps
1. In session A: `rebar session-log append "work on thing A"` (creates a log, writes the pointer).
2. Finish session A without ever calling `session-log start`.
3. In an unrelated session B (same checkout): `rebar session-log append "work on thing B"`.
4. Inspect the log: `rebar session-logs --limit 5` / `rebar show <log-id>`.

- **Expected:** session B's entry is in its own new `session_log` (or at least clearly
  attributable to session B); logs stay per-session and reasonably sized.
- **Actual:** session B appends to session A's log via the stale
  `.rebar/current_session_log` pointer; the single log grows without bound and mixes
  entries from multiple unrelated sessions, making retrieval-by-keyword noisy and the
  bodies huge.

## Impact
- Session logs become extremely long and mix unrelated work, defeating their purpose as
  durable, per-session, keyword-retrievable records.
- Large combined bodies are exactly what the `session_log` type was designed to keep out
  of the hot paths; a giant shared log undermines that intent.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A new session does not silently append to a prior session's `session_log`; the
      first `append` in a new session writes to a fresh log (auto-rotation) or the pointer
      is scoped so cross-session bleed cannot happen.
- [ ] The rotation/scoping mechanism is documented (CLAUDE.md session-logs section +
      `docs/` as appropriate) and does not require agents to remember `session-log start`.
- [ ] Backward compatible: existing pointer/log behavior for a single continuous session
      is unchanged; absent any session identifier the behavior degrades safely.
- [ ] A regression test demonstrates that two distinct sessions produce distinct logs
      (or the same log only when genuinely the same session).
baseline.summary: Session logs bleed between sessions — pointer never rotates, producing one giant multi-session log

baseline.description:
Add a `session_log` ticket type so agents can store verbose, durable session logs in the rebar store and surface them later via keyword search — without the verbose bodies degrading the dependency-graph / health hot paths that run constantly during the parallel-agent workflow.

## Context

rebar has one compile path (`reduce_all_tickets()` in `src/rebar/reducer/_api.py`) with **no lazy-loading**: it folds the full body (description + every comment) of every ticket into memory. That path backs `search`, `list`, `ready`, `next_batch`, `validate`, and `deps`. A verbose log stored as an ordinary ticket would therefore tax every graph/health operation. The design intent is that `session_log` tickets are compiled from JSONL **only for query operations** (`search` / `show` / the new recent-logs command) and are **excluded** from the operations that compile all tickets to build the dependency graph and run store-health checks.

Ticket types are enumerated in `src/rebar/schemas/common.schema.json` (the `enum`) and `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py` (`_TYPES`), with type-aware behavior in `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py` (tiers) and `src/rebar/_engine_support/gates.py` (clarity heuristics). Jira sync has no per-type exclusion today but already filters by status in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py`. All three interfaces (CLI / MCP / library) funnel reads through the single shared impl in `src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py`, so one library function auto-flows to CLI and MCP. Every compiled state carries `created_at` (ns) for recency ordering.

## Decisions (locked with the requester)

- **Query visibility — searchable, hidden from `list`.** Included in keyword
  `search` results and the recent-logs command + `show`; **excluded** from default
  `list` (surfaced only via explicit `--type=session_log`) and from all
  graph/health ops.
- **Content model — two approaches in scope.** (1) the type plus normal
  `create` / `edit` / `comment`; (2) a convenience capture helper that creates a
  log on first use and appends entries, via the shared write path. An automatic
  per-session hook was considered and **explicitly removed from scope** (no honest
  cross-interface trigger exists — the CLI has no long-lived process — and it adds
  write amplification).
- **Linking — non-blocking only.** No `blocks` / `depends_on` (and excluded from
  the dependency graph), but `relates_to` / `discovered_from` permitted so a log
  can reference the work it documents.
- **Gates & lifecycle — exempt, no transitions.** Skipped by
  `clarity_check` / `check_ac` / `quality_check` and by `validate`'s orphan/health
  checks; cannot be `claim`ed or `transition`ed. `show`, `comment`, and `edit`
  work as normal.
- **Title guidance — documented, not enforced.** Titles should carry a short
  summary of the work (not merely date / time / session id); this lives in the
  ticket docs but is never validated.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `session_log` is a valid ticket type accepted by `create` across schema +
      `_TYPES`, and rejected nowhere it should be accepted.
- [ ] Session logs are excluded from `reduce_all_tickets()` for graph/health
      callers (`ready`, `next_batch`, `deps`, `validate`) and from default `list`,
      but included in `search` and `show`.
- [ ] `claim` / `transition` on a `session_log` are refused with a clear message;
      `blocks` / `depends_on` links are refused while `relates_to` /
      `discovered_from` succeed.
- [ ] `clarity_check`, `check_ac`, and `quality_check` treat `session_log` as
      exempt, and `validate` does not flag session logs as orphans/empty/etc.
- [ ] A "last 5 session logs" capability (ordered by `created_at` desc, default
      limit 5) is reachable identically from the library, the CLI, and an MCP tool
      with a documented `outputSchema`.
- [ ] `session_log` tickets are never emitted to Jira by `reconcile` (outbound
      filter + absent from the local→Jira type map) and never appear in
      `bridge_fsck` output.
- [ ] A capture helper can create/append a session log from all three interfaces,
      and `CLAUDE.md` + `docs/` document the type, its exemptions, and the
      title-summary convention.
- [ ] Tests cover the type across all three interfaces and assert the graph/health
      performance isolation; full suite passes.
- [ ] A `session_log` ticket type exists end to end (schema, validation, all three
- [ ] Session logs are discoverable via `search` keywords and a "last 5 session logs"
- [ ] Graph/health operations (`ready`, `next_batch`, `deps`, `validate`) are provably
- [ ] Session logs are gate- and lifecycle-exempt, support non-blocking links only,
- [ ] A capture helper lets agents record verbose logs without hand-assembling
baseline.summary: Add a session_log ticket type for verbose, queryable session logs

# Pass-1 ladder expressed in classes

## Context / Problem
`workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml:62-65` sets `model_ladder` to BARE names (`claude-haiku-4-5`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-opus-4-8`). `production_batch_runner.py:87-93` assigns `model_ladder[0]` to `cfg.model`, and `config.py:333-341` maps the `claude` prefix to provider `anthropic`. So during a run configured for another provider, the Pass-1 finders still resolve to DIRECT ANTHROPIC — a split-brain in the pass that does most of the work (MEASURED: 41 of 42 calls on a real review). `code_review/batch_runner.py:55` has the same shape.

## Approach
Express the ladder as CLASS names (`trivial`, `standard`, `frontier`) rather than model ids, resolved through the class config at run time. The ladder keeps its meaning — escalate through capability tiers — and becomes provider-portable by construction rather than by convention.

**Alternative rejected — provider-qualifying the ladder entries in YAML.** Hard-codes one provider into the gate definition, which is what makes today's ladder non-portable.

## Scope

CORRECTED: the original list omitted the two files this ticket's OWN mechanism and ACs require. Verified in source at b4b475b04.

- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — **REQUIRED, was missing.** `resolve_model` at config.py:362 is
  literally `return step or workflow or cfg.model`. The MECHANISM section below names this as "the
  ONE funnel", so the reserved-word resolution lands here. Its only caller is
  `workflow/runs.py:154`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py` — **REQUIRED, was missing.** `models_at_or_above` is
  defined at sizing.py:312 and is the subject of the AC about a BEDROCK primary returning
  Bedrock escalation targets. Callers: `prerequisites.py:257`, `sizing.py:371`, and an alias at
  `orchestrator.py:72`.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml` — the ladder entries. MEASURED: lines 62-65
  currently hold the literal ladder `claude-haiku-4-5` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` / `claude-opus-4-8`,
  which is what the `grep -n "claude-"` AC targets.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py` and
  `src/rebar/llm/code_review/batch_runner.py` — resolve a class name to a model.
- `tests/unit/` — resolution and no-cross-provider tests.

### The resolver ALREADY EXISTS — this ticket wires it, it does not build it

`model_classes.resolve_model_string` is delivered and tested by f844: `test_model_classes.py:329` asserts `resolve_model_string("standard") == "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"` and :342 asserts a literal id round-trips unchanged. So this ticket's job is to route `resolve_model` and the ladder THROUGH that existing function, not to reimplement class resolution.

### Existing couplings to keep green (measured, so nobody assumes zero)

- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites_model_log.py:43` does
  `monkeypatch.setattr(sizing, "models_at_or_above", ...)`. A rebind target: if this ticket moves
  or renames that function, re-importing it elsewhere will NOT fix that patch.
- `orchestrator.py:72` holds `_models_at_or_above = sizing.models_at_or_above`, a module-level
  ALIAS bound at import time, and `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:1145,1150` assert through it
  with LITERAL ids. Those must keep returning the same bare ids byte-for-byte — the plan's
  "a literal id keeps working byte-for-byte" guarantee is what makes them safe.
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_scoped_ticket_tool.py::test_resolve_model_precedence` pins
  `resolve_model`'s step > workflow > config precedence. Adding class resolution must not disturb
  the precedence ORDER; it resolves the WINNER after precedence is applied.

## Testing
Contract tier: the observable is the model id the batch runner assigns to `cfg.model`.
- a ladder of class names resolves to the configured models, in order.
- with classes configured for a non-default provider, the entry rung does NOT resolve to an
  anthropic-inferred bare id (the split-brain regression).
- the escalation order is unchanged.


## MECHANISM (parent eb58 comment 4 — the CORRECTED decision; do not re-derive)

**A workflow step names a class by using the class name as its `model:` value.** The three class names are RESERVED VALUES in the EXISTING model-string space. There is no new `class:` key and no schema change — the v3 step schema stays closed; its VALUE space gains three reserved words.

    model: standard                                  # instead of: model: claude-sonnet-4-6
    model_ladder: [trivial, standard, frontier]      # instead of three literal ids

### ONE FUNCTION, SEVERAL CALL SITES — there is NO single funnel

An earlier version of THIS section said resolution happens at "the ONE funnel every step model already passes through: config.resolve_model". **That was wrong and is repudiated.** Parent eb58 comment 4 records the correction ("My 'ONE funnel' keystone claim was WRONG"), and the shipped code says it too: `model_classes.py:238` — "THERE IS NO SINGLE INTERCEPTION POINT ... `model_ladder` never reaches `rebar.llm.config.resolve_model` (the batch runners copy `model_ladder[0]` straight onto `cfg.model`), and neither do the verifier paths".

The reserved vocabulary lives in ONE function, which **f844 already delivered and tested** (`test_model_classes.py:329` proves `resolve_model_string("standard")` -> `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`; :342 proves a literal id round-trips unchanged):

    model_classes.resolve_model_string(value) -> str
        value in {trivial, standard, frontier} -> resolve via load_class_slots()
        anything else                          -> returned UNCHANGED

This ticket WIRES that function; it does not build it. The call sites it must wire:

  a. `config.resolve_model` (`config.py:362`) — the workflow-step path, sole caller
     `workflow/runs.py:154`. **The import MUST be lazy, inside the function body.**
     `model_classes` imports `config` at module scope and its own docstring forbids the reverse, so
     a module-level import here closes an import cycle. eb58 comment 4 calls this out as the exact
     cycle the earlier draft proposed after prohibiting it one ticket earlier.
  b. the ladder expansion in `production_batch_runner.py:93`
     (`cfg = dataclasses.replace(cfg, model=req.model_ladder[0])`) and
     `code_review/batch_runner.py:55` (`model = req.model_ladder[0] if req.model_ladder else None`).
  c. **`workflow/runners.py:120`, `DefaultBatchRunner.run()` — a THIRD ladder consumer with the
     identical `req.model_ladder[0]` split-brain.** Not enumerated by eb58 comment 4 and not
     previously in any ticket's scope; found by this ticket's plan review and verified in source.
     A class name reaching it unresolved would be handed to the runner as the literal string.

  (The verifier paths — `resolve_verifier_model`, `_verifier_cfg` and its callers at
  `xcheck.py:198`/`:336` — are the FOURTH consumer group. They belong to task 172e, not here.
  172e and this ticket SHARE call site (a): whichever lands first wires it and the other consumes
  it. That is a shared prerequisite, not a one-directional block.)

REJECTED — a new `class:` key: forks a step schema `runs.py` documents as closed, forces every consumer to handle two mutually exclusive keys, and makes `model: standard` vs `class: standard` a silent ambiguity. Reserved values keep ONE resolution path.

REJECTED — resolving at YAML load time: the class -> id mapping depends on process-scoped env/CLI layers, so load-time resolution would freeze the wrong value in a long-lived process and would be invisible to `provider_provenance` (343b).

## The escalation ladder is a SECOND split-brain (measured)

`sizing.MODEL_LADDER` (`sizing.py:99-103`) hardcodes the three BARE Anthropic ids with their context windows, and `models_at_or_above()` (`sizing.py:312`) returns those bare names for runtime escalation. Its lookup is a SUBSTRING match, so it happens to match a Bedrock id — but it RETURNS the bare Anthropic name. MEASURED:

    models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6")
      -> [("claude-sonnet-4-6", "anthropic"), ("claude-opus-4-8", "anthropic")]

So a Bedrock run that hits a context limit silently escalates to DIRECT ANTHROPIC: a hard failure in a Bedrock-only container with no key, or silent Anthropic billing where a key exists. This is DISTINCT from the entry-rung split-brain this ticket already names (`model_ladder[0]` -> `cfg.model`) and must be fixed in the same change, or the cutover leaks cross-provider on every escalation.

### MODEL_LADDER HAS TWO JOBS — DECOUPLE THEM; DO NOT PUT CLASS NAMES IN THE TABLE

MEASURED at `sizing.py:99-103`, `MODEL_LADDER` is a table of `(BARE_NAME, WINDOW_TOKENS)` pairs:

    ("claude-haiku-4-5", 200_000), ("claude-sonnet-4-6", 1_000_000),
    ("claude-opus-4-8", 1_000_000)

It drives TWO different things:
  * escalation ORDER, via `models_at_or_above` (`sizing.py:312`);
  * P8's context-window budget, via `largest_window_tokens` (`sizing.py:137-146`), which matches
    with `if name in model` — a SUBSTRING test against the BARE name.

An earlier draft of this ticket said the ladder's "rungs become CLASS names". **DO NOT DO THAT.** `"standard" in "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"` is FALSE, so every lookup would miss and `largest_window_tokens` would fall through to `return MODEL_LADDER[-1][1]` — the ladder maximum — for EVERY model, silently changing P8's budget with no error raised. The substring match works today precisely because the table holds bare names and a qualified id CONTAINS its bare name.

REQUIRED SHAPE:
  * `MODEL_LADDER` stays EXACTLY as it is — bare names and windows. It remains the sizing table.
  * `largest_window_tokens` is UNCHANGED, byte-for-byte. Its behaviour is a regression target, not
    a thing this ticket edits.
  * `models_at_or_above` keeps using the existing substring match to find the START RUNG (so an
    already-resolved `provider:model` string still positions correctly), then MAPS each at-or-above
    rung through the class config before returning: haiku -> `trivial`, sonnet -> `standard`,
    opus -> `frontier`, each resolved via `resolve_model_string`. With NO classes configured,
    `resolve_model_string` returns the name unchanged, so the current bare-id return value is
    preserved byte-for-byte and every existing caller keeps working.

That decoupling is what lets escalation become provider-correct WITHOUT touching P8's budget maths.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] a test asserts the Pass-1 entry rung resolves through the class config, not a bare model id
- [ ] a test asserts no ladder rung resolves to provider `anthropic` when classes are configured for
      another provider
- [ ] a test asserts the ladder's escalation ORDER is unchanged by the change
- [ ] `grep -n "claude-" src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml` returns no model_ladder entry

- [ ] a test asserts `model_ladder: [trivial, standard, frontier]` in a workflow resolves each rung
      through the class config, and that a ladder of literal ids still resolves to those ids unchanged
- [ ] a test asserts `models_at_or_above()` on a BEDROCK primary returns escalation targets that stay
      on BEDROCK — it currently returns bare Anthropic ids that infer to provider `anthropic`, so
      this criterion fails against the current implementation and cannot pass vacuously
- [ ] a test asserts the Pass-1 entry rung comes from the class config rather than
      `model_ladder[0]` being copied into `cfg.model` by the batch runners
- [ ] `sizing.MODEL_LADDER` is UNCHANGED (still bare names + windows) and `largest_window_tokens`
      is byte-for-byte unchanged. A test pins the window returned for a provider-qualified id
      (e.g. `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`) so the substring match cannot silently start
      missing. This criterion FAILS if the implementer puts class names in the table
- [ ] a test asserts `models_at_or_above` returns the SAME bare ids as today when NO classes are
      configured — the back-compat control that stops a "resolve always" implementation passing
- [ ] `workflow/runners.py:120` (`DefaultBatchRunner.run`) resolves a class-named ladder rung too;
      a test drives it with `model_ladder: [standard]` and asserts the runner receives the
      configured model id, not the literal string `standard`
- [ ] `config.py` does NOT import `model_classes` at module level (the import cycle guard):
      `python -c "import ast,sys; m=ast.parse(open('src/rebar/llm/config.py').read()); print(any(isinstance(n,(ast.Import,ast.ImportFrom)) and 'model_classes' in (getattr(n,'module','') or '')+''.join(a.name for a in n.names) for n in m.body))"`
      prints False
baseline.summary: Pass-1 ladder expressed in classes

## Context / Problem
GitHub code-scanning alert #88 (`py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization`, Security/quality) flags the upstream-URL assertion in `test_notice_names_pandoc_its_version_and_its_licence` in `tests/unit/test_notice_records_pandoc_gpl.py` (currently line 51):

```python
assert "pandoc.org" in text or "github.com/jgm/pandoc" in text, (...)
```

This is not real URL sanitization — there is no untrusted input; the test checks that NOTICE mentions upstream so the GPL source-availability obligation is actionable. But the finding is still worth fixing: bare substring containment accepts a NOTICE that only contains a lookalike host — prefix-style (`https://notpandoc.org`) or suffix-style (`https://pandoc.org.evil.com`) — which does NOT actionably point at upstream. The same rule class was fixed before in `test_llm_fallback_chain.py` (ticket revealable-ungracious-billygoat, alerts 81/82) with parsed-origin netloc equality.

## Approach
Replace the two substring checks with a single scheme+host-anchored regex whose host ends with an explicit end-of-host boundary (a negative lookahead), so BOTH lookalike classes are rejected:

```python
_UPSTREAM_RE = re.compile(
    r"https?://(www\.)?pandoc\.org(?![\w.-])|https?://github\.com/jgm/pandoc(?![\w-])"
)
assert _UPSTREAM_RE.search(text), (...)
```

`(?![\w.-])` after `pandoc\.org` refuses to end the host before a dot, letter, digit, or hyphen, so `https://pandoc.org.evil.com` is rejected (unlike a `\b` anchor, which matches before a literal dot) while `https://pandoc.org`, `https://pandoc.org/`, and `http://www.pandoc.org` all match. `(?![\w-])` after the github path rejects `https://github.com/jgm/pandoc-extras` (a different repo) while allowing a trailing `/`, whitespace, or end of text. This handles arbitrary subdomain sequences per the CodeQL guidance, matching the strictness of the parsed-origin prior art without urlparse machinery — appropriate because the subject is a whole document, not a single URL to validate. Alternative weighed: extracting every URL from NOTICE and comparing parsed netlocs exactly, as `test_llm_fallback_chain.py` does — rejected as over-engineering for a one-line document-content assertion; the lookahead-anchored regex achieves the same rejection set here.

RED-first demonstration (already executed): the old expression accepts both `https://notpandoc.org.evil.com` (prefix) and `https://pandoc.org.evil.com` (suffix); the anchored regex rejects both and still accepts the real NOTICE.

## Scope
- `tests/unit/test_notice_records_pandoc_gpl.py` — only the upstream-URL assertion in `test_notice_names_pandoc_its_version_and_its_licence` (plus the module-level compiled regex it uses). Do NOT touch the pandoc version pin strings or NOTICE content (a parallel agent is bumping pypandoc-binary in the same file; anchoring the change to the assertion, not a line number, keeps the two changes rebase-clean).

Sibling sweep (already executed): alert #88 is the only open code-scanning alert repo-wide; grep for URL/hostname substring-`in` checks found no other same-class occurrences in scope (remaining matches are scheme-anchored full-URL literals or error-message assertions).

## Testing
Test-only change. Happy path: `pytest tests/unit/test_notice_records_pandoc_gpl.py -x -q` stays green against the real NOTICE. Failure path: the RED demonstration shows the anchored regex rejects `https://pandoc.org.evil.com`, `https://notpandoc.org`, and a bare schemeless `pandoc.org` mention, all of which (except the last two prefix forms partially) satisfied the old expression.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The upstream-URL assertion in `test_notice_names_pandoc_its_version_and_its_licence` no longer uses bare substring containment; it matches via a scheme+host-anchored regex with an explicit end-of-host boundary. Verify: read the diff.
- [x] The new assertion rejects a suffix-style lookalike: `_UPSTREAM_RE.search("https://pandoc.org.evil.com")` is None. Verify: run the expression in Python.
- [x] The new assertion rejects a prefix-style lookalike: `_UPSTREAM_RE.search("https://notpandoc.org")` is None. Verify: run the expression in Python.
- [x] The new assertion accepts the real NOTICE, preserving the test's intent that NOTICE actionably points at upstream. Verify: `pytest tests/unit/test_notice_records_pandoc_gpl.py -x -q` passes.
- [x] The diff touches only the upstream-URL assertion and its supporting regex; version pins and NOTICE content are unchanged. Verify: read the diff.
- [x] `make lint` passes. Verify: run it.
- [x] `make typecheck` passes. Verify: run it.
- [x] The change is pushed to Gerrit for review. Verify: a Gerrit change exists for the commit.
- [x] [operator-attested] After the fix lands and CodeQL re-runs, alert #88 clears without dismissal. Verify: `gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/code-scanning/alerts` shows no open alert #88.
  provenance: environment=github.com/navapbc/rebar code-scanning (live GitHub API); principal=operator session via authenticated gh CLI; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — `gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/code-scanning/alerts/88 --jq .state` returned "fixed" on 2026-08-15 12:25 PT: cleared by default-branch re-analysis after the merged fix, not dismissed.
baseline.summary: code-scanning #88: anchor upstream-URL assertions in NOTICE test (incomplete URL substring sanitization)

## Why

The two model sub-questions (containment, layer) must be calibrated so suppression never hides a
severe / cross-sibling / delivered-functionality / security finding. Per G-Eval, freeze wording and
calibrate to a gold set (kappa ~0.8) whose anchors are the must-never-suppress cases.

## What

Build a gold-set fixture + an end-to-end partially-complete-epic review test. The gold set encodes
labelled findings: pure re-litigation (drop) vs must-never-suppress anchors — a delivered child's
delivered-functionality/security finding, a finding spanning an open sibling, a finding on a
force-closed child, and a delivered child that opened a security boundary. Add the calibration
record under `docs/calibration/` (a LIVE run, since the changed artifact is a prompt) and the test
module under `tests/plan_review/`.

## Scope

- IN: the gold-set fixture; the end-to-end partially-complete-epic test; the calibration doc.
- OUT: the floor/predicate/sub-call implementations (their own stories).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A gold-set fixture labels drop vs must-never-suppress findings, including the four anchor cases above.
- [ ] An end-to-end test builds a partially-complete epic (delivered + open + force-closed children) and asserts: delivered plan-semantics findings dropped; delivered-functionality/security, cross-sibling, and force-closed-child findings preserved.
- [ ] A calibration record (LIVE LLM run) is written under `docs/calibration/` reporting agreement against the gold set.
- [ ] The suite runs green with the completion floor active and is byte-identical with it inactive.

## Acceptance Criteria (ordering + invariants)

- [ ] Calibration runs only AFTER 94fd's prompt is frozen (explicit `depends_on` 94fd); a later prompt revision retriggers recalibration (the calibration record notes the prompt hash it was run against).
- [ ] A non-regression test asserts the epic's success-criteria invariants: NO `close`-operation change, NO new attestation kind, and code-drift / fire-timing invalidation unchanged (only what a re-fired review DOES changes).

## Acceptance Criteria (gold-set scope)

- [ ] The gold-set has >=5 labelled cases per anchor category (pure re-litigation -> drop; delivered-functionality -> keep; security/contract T5c/T10 -> keep; cross-sibling spans-open -> keep; force-closed child -> keep), >=25 total, and 'complete' = every category represented across the G3/G4, coherence, and overlay criterion provenances.

## Acceptance Criteria (reopen invariant)

- [ ] A test covers the reopened-child auto-resurface invariant: a delivered child whose findings were dropped, once reopened, is no longer `delivered-now` (recomputed that run) so its findings resurface — asserting the recompute-every-run / no-persisted-drop behaviour end to end.
baseline.summary: Calibration gold-set + partially-complete-epic tests (must-never-suppress anchors)

# The pass that GENERATES blocking findings moves to the cheapest model the moment b690 lands

## Severity framing

This is not a cost or consistency issue. **Pass-1 of plan-review is the finder** — it produces the findings that become blocking and gate every `claim`. Moving it to a weaker model makes the gate QUIETLY MORE PERMISSIVE, and there is no alarm for "the review was weaker than it should have been". `b690`'s change is `LLM-Review +1 / Verified +1` and green on every offline test, because **none of this risk is test-detectable**: the offline suite substitutes `FunctionModel`/`FakeRunner` for exactly the thing that changes, which is WHICH MODEL a live gate calls.

## The mechanism, verified end to end

Under this repo's actual config there is **no `model_classes` table anywhere** (no `[llm]` in `rebar.toml`, no `[tool.rebar…]` LLM keys in `pyproject.toml`, no `.rebar/config.conf`, no `REBAR_LLM_*` in shell rc / LaunchAgents / CI), so classes take built-in defaults:

    trivial -> anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5   standard -> anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6
    frontier -> anthropic:claude-opus-4-8   LLMConfig.from_env().model -> claude-opus-4-8

**Crucially, plan-review's runner floor is NOT `cfg.model`.** `plan_review/__init__.py:609` calls `produce_plan_review_verdict(ctx, _verifier_cfg(cfg), …)`, so the whole run's `runner._config.model` is `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`. Then:

1. `gate_dispatch.py:163` builds `ProductionBatchRunner(runner=get_runner(_verifier_cfg(cfg)))`
   → floor = sonnet.
2. `production_batch_runner.run` does `cfg = replace(cfg, model=resolve_model_string(req.model_ladder[0]))`
   → `plan-review.yaml:62-65` rung 0 is `trivial` → **haiku**.
3. `pass1.py:484` → `sizing.pass1_with_ladder` → `passes.pass1_chunk` builds
   `RunRequest(..., config=cfg)` (`passes.py:319-330`).
4. **PRE-b690** the runner opened `cfg = self._config` and DISCARDED `req.config` → Pass-1 actually
   ran on **sonnet**. **POST-b690** it honours the declaration and runs on **haiku**.

Measured:

    gate runner floor model  : anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6
    Pass-1 batch cfg.model   : anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5
    PRE-b690  effective model: anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6
    POST-b690 effective model: anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5

**The smoking gun that this was never intended-and-tested:** `origin/main`'s own `_verifier_cfg` docstring asserts "The Pass-1 finder is unaffected: it runs the YAML `model_ladder` via the ProductionBatchRunner, not `cfg.model`." **That comment is FALSE on main**, and `b690` is what makes it true. `git log -L62,66` on `plan-review.yaml` shows Pass-1 has declared the cheapest rung since the workflow was born (originally the literal `claude-haiku-4-5`) and has **never once actually run on it**.

## Why the ladder does not save it

`pass1_with_ladder` escalates on a **context-limit signal** — it is a SIZE ladder, not a quality ladder (its own docstring says so). A plan that fits haiku's 200k window stays on haiku forever. Some Pass-1 chunks also run `execution_mode="agentic"` (code-grounding with tool calls), where the drop from sonnet to haiku is a large capability change, not a marginal one.

Secondary effect on the prerequisite finder (`registry.py:361-367` gives it `"default_posture": "blocking"`): `pack_prerequisite_bins(..., model=cfg.model)` now packs for haiku's 200k instead of sonnet's 1M, so context-limit escalation genuinely fires where it previously could not. Escalation does work (`models_at_or_above('claude-haiku-4-5')` → `['claude-haiku-4-5','claude-sonnet-4-6','claude-opus-4-8']`), but the first attempt is a real downgrade and every attempt burns tokens.

## Why it is silent rather than loud

The gates fail CLOSED on errors — `attest_gate.py:112-125` blocks a claim on a missing/stale attestation, and an LLM outage degrades to INDETERMINATE → no signature → claim blocked. That is the loud path and it is fine. **This is the other kind:** a haiku Pass-1 that surfaces fewer grounded findings yields a **PASS**, which gets signed, and the claim proceeds. The sidecar records only the VERIFIER's model (`data.model`), never Pass-1's, so it is invisible in the artifacts too.

## An asymmetry worth deciding on

Code-review's Pass-1 finder declares **`frontier`** (`code-review.yaml`, landed by 3768). Plan-review's Pass-1 declares **`trivial`**. Both are finders that generate blocking findings. That asymmetry may be deliberate, but it has never been effective, so it has never been evaluated.

## The decision, made by the operator and confirmed by archaeology

**Pass-1 (the finder) runs on `frontier`/opus. Pass-2 verify and Pass-4 coach run on `standard`/sonnet.** That split is what `_verifier_cfg` was written to express, and its own docstring already asserts it ("The Pass-1 finder is unaffected"). The docstring has simply been false since 2026-06-27.

This is a RESTORATION, not a new preference. The sidecar record shows 115 plan reviews generating findings on opus up to 2026-06-27, then zero ever since — a total changeover one day after `4beec08a4` introduced the verifier downgrade and accidentally applied it to the whole run. See the archaeology comment for the day-by-day table.

**b690 is the ENABLER.** Until it landed, `PydanticAIRunner.run` discarded `req.config`, so NO ladder rung could influence Pass-1 at all. With b690, the declaration is finally reachable — and it says `trivial`, which is why the regression would deepen rather than heal on its own.

**The change:** `plan-review.yaml`'s `model_ladder` entry rung `trivial` -> `frontier`. `standard` would freeze the regression; `trivial` would deepen it.

Note that with rung 0 at `frontier`, `models_at_or_above(opus)` returns just `[opus]`, so model escalation becomes a no-op. That costs nothing: sonnet and opus share the same 1M window, so the only size-meaningful step was ever haiku->sonnet, and the size handling that matters (batch -> one-criterion-per-call -> the P8 too-big finding) is independent of the model rungs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `plan-review.yaml`'s Pass-1 `model_ladder` entry rung is `frontier`, so findings generate on
      opus as they did before 2026-06-27
- [ ] Pass-2 verify and Pass-4 coach remain on the verifier model (`standard`/sonnet) — this ticket
      must not disturb the downgrade that `_verifier_cfg` correctly applies to them
- [ ] a test asserts the EFFECTIVE model of Pass-1 at the seam that decides it
      (`ProductionBatchRunner` -> `run_pass1` -> `pass1_chunk`, i.e. the model reaching the runner),
      so a future change cannot silently move the finder again. Asserting the YAML text is NOT
      sufficient — the YAML has said `trivial` for five weeks while sonnet actually ran
- [ ] a test asserts Pass-1 and Pass-2 resolve to DIFFERENT models under the default config, since
      the defect was precisely the two collapsing onto one
- [ ] `_verifier_cfg`'s docstring claim that "the Pass-1 finder is unaffected" is either true after
      this change or corrected — it must not remain a false assertion in the code
- [ ] [operator-attested] a real plan-review run after the change records opus for the Pass-1 finder,
      cited from `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` per-step attribution (which story b690 made possible)
- [ ] the prerequisite finder's bin packing is checked against opus's window, since
      `pack_prerequisite_bins` sizes to `cfg.model`

## Notes

Found by an independent landing-safety assessment of the epic stack, NOT by the offline suite — which is green at the stack tip and cannot see this. `b690` itself is closed and correct in its own terms: it made declarations effective. This ticket is about one declaration that turns out to be wrong.
baseline.summary: b690 silently downgrades the plan-review Pass-1 finder from sonnet to haiku, weakening the claim gate that generates blocking findings
Tier C: retire bash compute (delete ticket-next-batch.sh + validate-issues.sh + REBAR_COMPUTE switch + dual-run wiring)

# S2 — Deploy Gerrit + review-bot receiver (docker-compose) behind nginx + TLS

## Why
Run Gerrit and the **review-bot webhook receiver** as the two containers on the box, reachable
over HTTPS at `rebar.solutions.navateam.com`. Gerrit needs a `%2F`-safe reverse proxy — the
community uses nginx/Apache, NOT Caddy (Caddy URL-decodes paths by default with no global
switch, which breaks Gerrit's change/project screens; no confirmed Caddy+Gerrit recipe exists).
This is the bottom layer of the d251 "proven pipe": Gerrit serving, the receiver reachable over
HTTP, TLS terminated, secrets from SSM. NOTE (peer-pattern correction): Gerrit POSTs webhook
JSON, not MCP protocol — so the right component is a thin HTTP **webhook receiver that IMPORTS
the review kernel as a library**, NOT the stdio rebar-MCP server exposed over HTTP (a FastMCP
HTTP transport would reject a Gerrit webhook by spec; `streamable-http` is a red herring here).

## What
- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`:
  - official `gerritcodereview/gerrit` pinned to a PATCH tag (e.g. `3.14.1`) with persistent
    volumes (git/index/cache/etc/db on the data volume) + the two-step init. DERISK NOTE (E4):
    bare minor tags `3.14`/`3.13` do NOT exist on Docker Hub; pin a published patch tag
    (`3.14.1`/`3.13.7`/`3.12.8`), all of which publish arm64 manifests.
  - the **review-bot container** (signing key + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY sourced from SSM into the boot
    `.env` — see secrets bullet; write-gating as needed); both `restart: unless-stopped`, pinned
    tags. The receiver calls the `rebar.llm` library functions DIRECTLY, so the LLM review path is
    enabled simply by `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` being present + the `[agents]` extra being installed —
    there is NO separate allow-flag for direct library calls (`REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` gates only the
    stdio MCP server's tool wrappers, which this receiver does not use, so it is intentionally not
    set).
  - the Gerrit data volume is declared **`external: true`** (created once, outside compose) so a
    stray `docker compose down -v` cannot destroy git/NoteDb/index state. S2 only DECLARES this
    external data volume; volume snapshotting + retention is owned by **S7's DLM daily-snapshot
    policy** (see S7), and the restore procedure is in the runbook. Freeze-and-restore (the d251
    recovery posture, no break-glass v1) operates against the snapshots S7 manages.
- **Review-bot webhook receiver (in-scope S2 deliverable).** The second container is a thin
  **webhook->review->vote receiver** (an ASGI/FastAPI service under `src/rebar/review_bot/`)
  that IMPORTS the review kernel as a library and exposes a plain HTTP endpoint Gerrit's
  `webhooks` plugin POSTs to. This is deliberately NOT the stdio rebar-MCP server over HTTP
  (Gerrit speaks webhooks, not MCP JSON-RPC; an MCP HTTP transport would reject the request).
  The stdio MCP server is unchanged and remains for agent use only. The receiver binds
  `0.0.0.0:<PORT>` (default `8000`); nginx routes
  `location /review/ { proxy_pass http://review-bot:<PORT>/; }`. Decision recorded in
  `docs/adr/0007-review-bot-receiver.md`.
- `gerrit.config`: `container.heapLimit=2g` with `core.packedGitLimit` budgeted INSIDE the heap
  (~512m-1g), NoteDb, `canonicalWebUrl=https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/`, sshd/httpd thread
  caps + `sshd.batchThreads` to avoid parallel-clone OOM.
- nginx + certbot (Let's Encrypt) terminating TLS on 443: route Gerrit (`%2F`-safe: `proxy_pass`
  with no path) and the receiver (`location /review/`) behind the one cert; Gerrit SSH on 29418.
- **certbot renewal lifecycle.** Initial issuance AND renewal: a systemd timer (or cron) runs
  `certbot renew` twice daily with a deploy-hook that reloads nginx; nginx serves an
  `/.well-known/acme-challenge/` location (webroot) so HTTP-01 renewal succeeds. Installed by
  the bootstrap script.
- **secrets bootstrap (SSM -> ephemeral `.env`).** `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` runs
  `aws ssm get-parameter --with-decryption` for the signing key + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (via the
  **instance role**, no static keys) and writes a root-only (`0600`) `.env` that compose reads,
  BEFORE `docker compose up`. The `.env` is gitignored + ephemeral (regenerated each boot, never
  committed); the script is idempotent and **aborts** if SSM is unreachable (never reuses a
  stale `.env`). Recorded in `docs/adr/0008-secrets-source-ssm.md`.
- **IAM instance role (least privilege).** Grants `ssm:GetParameter`/`GetParameters` scoped to
  the project parameter-path prefix only (e.g.
  `arn:aws:ssm:us-east-1:896586841071:parameter/rebar/prod/*`) plus `kms:Decrypt` on the
  SecureString key — no wildcard. Defined in the infra IaC.
- **observability (minimal).** Both containers log via `journald`; a health probe hits `/` and
  the receiver `/review/` health path; a disk-usage alarm guards the Gerrit data volume.

## Scope
In: containers, the external Gerrit data volume DECLARATION, base `gerrit.config`,
nginx+TLS+certbot renewal, the review-bot receiver HTTP surface + hosting, SSM->.env secrets
bootstrap, the SSM IAM instance role, minimal logging/health/disk observability. Out: Gerrit
project/label/submit-req (S3); the bot identity + event wiring + the receiver's review/vote
LOGIC (S4 — S2 stands up the *service*, S4 wires its behavior); replication (S5); the data
volume's snapshot + retention policy (S7's DLM daily-snapshot policy owns it — S2 only declares
the volume).

## Files
- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`, `infra/compose/gerrit.config`, `infra/nginx/*.conf`
  (incl. the `/.well-known/acme-challenge/` location and the `location /review/` upstream)
- `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` (SSM -> ephemeral `.env`), bootstrap scripts under `infra/`
  (install the certbot-renew timer, the health/disk checks)
- `src/rebar/review_bot/` (the webhook-receiver ASGI service — skeleton/health endpoint in S2;
  review+vote behavior in S4)
- `docs/adr/0007-review-bot-receiver.md`, `docs/adr/0008-secrets-source-ssm.md`
- `.gitignore` (ensure `infra/compose/.env` is ignored)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Gerrit is reachable at `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/` with a valid Let's Encrypt cert.
- [ ] A Gerrit change screen / a project path containing `%2F` renders correctly (encoded-slash round-trip verified end-to-end through nginx).
- [ ] certbot renewal is automated: the timer/cron is installed + enabled, the nginx `/.well-known/acme-challenge/` location serves the HTTP-01 challenge, and `certbot renew --dry-run` succeeds and reloads nginx via the deploy-hook.
- [ ] Gerrit SSH clone works on 29418 and the admin account is bootstrapped.
- [ ] Gerrit data persists across `docker compose down/up` and an instance reboot; the data volume is `external: true` so `docker compose down -v` does not destroy it. (Snapshot + retention of this volume is owned by S7, not S2.)
- [ ] The review-bot webhook receiver (a plain HTTP service importing the review kernel as a library, NOT the stdio MCP over HTTP) is reachable through nginx at `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/review/` — a POST reaches the receiver process (not a 502); the decision is recorded in `docs/adr/0007-review-bot-receiver.md`.
- [ ] The review-bot container's signing key + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY are sourced from SSM at boot by `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` into a `0600`, gitignored, ephemeral `.env` (never baked into the image/compose, never committed); the script authenticates via the instance role, is idempotent, and aborts if SSM is unreachable. The receiver's LLM review path is enabled by `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` + the `[agents]` extra alone (no `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` flag, which gates only the stdio MCP server, is set).
- [ ] The SSM IAM instance role grants `GetParameter`/`GetParameters` scoped to `parameter/rebar/prod/*` only (no wildcard), verified against the attached policy.
- [ ] Both containers log to `journald`; a health probe covers `/` and `/review/`, and a disk-usage alarm covers the Gerrit data volume.
- [ ] Gerrit runs a supported version at an EXISTING arm64 patch tag (e.g. `gerritcodereview/gerrit:3.14.1`; a bare minor tag like `3.14` is NOT used — it doesn't exist), with `heapLimit=2g` and `packedGitLimit` budgeted within it.

## Round-12 plan-review remediation (2026-06-30 — recalibrated gate BLOCK + critical advisories)

**Blocking — internal sequencing (phased build, each phase verified before the next):**
- **Phase 1 (riskiest first):** Gerrit `gerritcodereview/gerrit:3.14.1` (arm64) container up with the external data volume + base `gerrit.config`; reachable over plain HTTP through nginx (no TLS yet); `%2F`-encoded path round-trips. Proves the arm64 image + the `%2F`-safe proxy before anything else is layered on.
- **Phase 2:** nginx TLS via certbot (Let's Encrypt) on 443 + the `/.well-known/acme-challenge/` webroot + the twice-daily `certbot renew` timer with the nginx-reload deploy-hook; `certbot renew --dry-run` green.
- **Phase 3:** `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` (SSM->ephemeral 0600 `.env`) via the instance role + the scoped IAM policy attachment (S2's separately-named inline policy on the S1-owned role).
- **Phase 4:** the review-bot receiver container reachable through nginx at `/review/` (skeleton + health only — review/vote LOGIC is S4b).
- **Phase 5:** observability (journald, `/` + `/review/` health probes, data-volume disk alarm).

**Critical advisories folded in:**
- **`webhooks` plugin is NOT bundled in the official image (seam to S4a):** S2 stands up the *service* only. The Gerrit site's `plugins/` dir is a bind-mount/volume path so a version-matched (3.14.1) `webhooks` + `events-log` plugin jar can be dropped in; ACTUAL plugin install + wiring is **S4a**. S2 verifies only that the site supports dropping plugin jars (the plugins dir is writable + on the persistent volume). No S2 AC depends on webhooks delivering events.
- **Receiver framework dependency (was absent):** add a `reviewbot` optional extra to `pyproject.toml` = `fastapi` + `uvicorn[standard]`. The receiver container builds via `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot` (`pip install .[agents,reviewbot]`). The stdio MCP server is untouched.
- **Dockerfile added** to Files: `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot`.
- **`core.packedGitLimit` is OFF-HEAP (correction):** JGit's `core.packedGitLimit` is the mmap'd packfile budget, sized against TOTAL RAM, NOT inside the Java heap. Config: `container.heapLimit=2g` (on-heap) + `core.packedGitLimit` ~1g budgeted against the ~8 GB box RAM ALONGSIDE (not within) the heap, leaving headroom for the OS + the receiver container.
- **`fetch-secrets.sh` explicit SSM-leaf -> env mapping** (the 7 params S1 created): `/rebar/prod/gerrit-admin-password`->`GERRIT_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `gerrit-ssh-host-ed25519-key`->`GERRIT_SSH_HOST_ED25519_KEY`, `github-replication-deploy-key`->`GITHUB_REPLICATION_DEPLOY_KEY`, `mcp-hmac-signing-key`->`MCP_HMAC_SIGNING_KEY`, `anthropic-api-key`->`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `alert-endpoint`->`ALERT_ENDPOINT`, `gerrit-bot-token`->`GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN`. (Same contract as S1's user_data.sh; S2 sources only the subset the containers need.)
- **LLM path enablement:** the receiver's LLM review path is enabled by `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` + the `[agents]` extra ALONE — `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` (which gates only the stdio MCP server) is intentionally NOT set.
- **External volume creation step:** the Gerrit data volume is a Docker `external: true` volume backed by the `/var/gerrit` EBS mount; `infra/scripts/compose-up.sh` (the boot orchestrator) runs `docker volume create --driver local --opt type=none --opt o=bind --opt device=/var/gerrit gerrit_data` (idempotent) BEFORE `docker compose up`, so a stray `docker compose down -v` cannot destroy it.
- **Port single-source:** the receiver port is one env var `REVIEW_BOT_PORT` (default 8000) in the `.env`; compose and the nginx upstream both read it (nginx via an envsubst-templated conf at boot), so the two can't drift.

**Added / updated ACs:**
- [ ] The build is phased (Phase 1 Gerrit+HTTP -> 2 TLS -> 3 secrets/IAM -> 4 receiver -> 5 observability); Phase 1 reachability is proven before TLS is layered on.
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` declares a `reviewbot` extra (fastapi + uvicorn); `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot` builds the receiver via `.[agents,reviewbot]`.
- [ ] `gerrit.config` sets `container.heapLimit=2g` (on-heap) and `core.packedGitLimit` as a SEPARATE off-heap budget (~1g) sized against box RAM, NOT inside the heap.
- [ ] `fetch-secrets.sh` maps the enumerated `/rebar/prod/*` leaves to the documented env-var names, writes a 0600 ephemeral `.env`, authenticates via the instance role, is idempotent, and aborts if SSM is unreachable.
- [ ] The Gerrit data volume is created as an `external` bind volume on `/var/gerrit` by `compose-up.sh` before `docker compose up`; `docker compose down -v` does not destroy it.
- [ ] The receiver port is single-sourced (`REVIEW_BOT_PORT`) and consumed by both compose and the nginx `/review/` upstream.
- [ ] The Gerrit site `plugins/` dir is on the persistent volume + writable (so S4a can drop version-matched webhooks/events-log jars); no S2 AC depends on event delivery.
baseline.summary: infra: S2 — Deploy Gerrit + rebar MCP (docker-compose) behind nginx + TLS

baseline.description:
## Context
The completed Gerrit Verified latency RCA optimized the macOS completion path, but Ubuntu jobs still occupy scarce org-wide runners for 11-14 minutes and contribute to queue contention. Follow-up questions identify three candidate levers: replace repeated Pandoc corpus rendering with static expected results plus a smaller boundary test, remove redundant work from the exhaustive 1,440-minute bridge cadence proof, and move genuinely live Jira DC coverage out of the per-change hot path while retaining fast unit coverage. This work must preserve behavioral coverage and must not use extra parallel jobs or unchanged aggregate runner usage.

## Plan
- Build a dated Ubuntu runner-time dossier from final post-remediation run 31752047186, pytest duration logs, workflow routing, and focused local runtime experiments.
- For Pandoc and render_unit, map every current assertion to the code boundary it exercises; compare static golden fixtures, a bounded real-Pandoc contract sample, and full-corpus external execution using defect-seeded experiments to detect any coverage loss.
- For the bridge cadence test, discriminate between the cost of the 1,440 arithmetic checks and invariant workflow YAML I/O; prefer hoisting invariant I/O if it preserves the exhaustive proof.
- Inventory expensive Jira DC/default-tier tests, identify which require a real Jira or external binary, and map them to faster existing or new unit contracts before proposing any lane move.
- Compare each candidate with current practice in popular actively maintained OSS projects and search tracker history for prior acceptance or rejection.
- Record a confirmed RCA and measured runner-time/wall-time savings. Create linked implementation tickets only for remediations that preserve coverage; under the operator standing approval, implement those matching OSS consensus through Gerrit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every Ubuntu operation or test phase over 30 seconds in the final sample is attributed to a specific mechanism and measured with a focused baseline.
- [ ] Pandoc corpus, render_unit, bridge cadence, and Jira DC lane-move proposals each have an assertion-level coverage map and an A/B runtime estimate.
- [ ] Each proposal cites tracker history and practices from popular actively maintained OSS projects.
- [ ] No accepted remediation removes an assertion, behavioral equivalence class, OS/Python cell, or external boundary; moved coverage has an explicit destination and schedule.
- [ ] Runner-minute and expected queue-pressure savings are quantified without counting parallel matrix time as critical-path wall time.
- [ ] Every consensus-backed remediation is implemented on a linked ticket, passes repository gates and Gerrit LLM-Review +1 plus Verified +1, and merges before this task closes.
- [ ] Non-consensus or coverage-risking proposals are summarized with evidence and left for operator disposition.
baseline.summary: Reduce Ubuntu CI runner occupancy without losing test coverage
