baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Cloud and Jira DC currently nest retries across subprocess, SDK, wrapper, and reconciler layers. A non-idempotent ticket write can therefore exceed a predictable request budget or be replayed after an ambiguous commit. This task defines the provider-neutral logical-operation contract before either adapter changes.

## Approach
Create immutable operation/outcome values plus one fake-clock retry-budget owner in the reconciler domain. Adapter layers report one physical invocation at a time; they do not sleep or replay. This keeps the approved retry envelope in one place while preserving the additive-jitter behavior already accepted in ADR 0084.

The contract is exact:
- `logical_id` is one canonical UUID string generated once per logical operation, retained across every invocation or observation.
- `Disposition` has exactly `applied`, `already_satisfied`, `recovered`, `retryable_deferred`, `commit_unknown`, `permanent_failure`, `exhausted_transient`, `dependency_deferred`, `scope_deferred`, `safety_aborted`, `skipped`.
- `FailureScope` has exactly `none`, `ticket`, `endpoint`, `tenant`, `provider`, `global`.
- `ReplaySafety` has exactly `not_applicable`, `safe`, `observe_first`, `forbidden`.
- `DelaySource` has exactly `none`, `fallback_jitter`, `provider`, `fuse`.
- Enum values serialize as the lowercase strings above. Invocation/request totals are non-negative integers. Durations serialize as integer milliseconds. `retry_not_before` is UTC RFC 3339 with `Z`.
- Canonical bytes route through `rebar._store.canonical.canonical_bytes` with its default `ascii_only=False`; no inline JSON serializer is added. Equivalent outcomes therefore produce byte-identical sorted-key compact UTF-8 JSON.
- `invocation_count` is the number already executed, ranging from 0 through 3. `retry_index` is zero-based: index 0 selects `[2s,3s)` while index 1 selects `[4s,5s)` using `2**(retry_index+1)+U[0,1)`.
- Diagnostic entries are chronological immutable mappings. Only `stage`, `category`, `status_code`, `provider_code`, `retry_after_ms`, `message` are admitted; optional absent keys are omitted. Raw headers, request/response bodies, credentials, ticket content are never admitted. Message redaction calls the public `rebar.llm.failure.sanitize_diagnostic` seam with only the `message` key, then applies this contract size bound. Each message is capped after redaction at 512 Unicode code points: an overlong value becomes its first 511 code points plus `…`.
- The outcome holds at most eight diagnostic entries. Eight or fewer remain unchanged. On overflow, retain the first seven; entry eight is exactly `stage=diagnostic`, `category=truncated`, `message=dropped=N`, with other optional keys absent. Worked example: nine inputs serialize entry eight as `{"category":"truncated","message":"dropped=2","stage":"diagnostic"}` because inputs eight plus nine were omitted.
- The budget permits at most three physical invocations, at most 15,000 ms cumulative sleep. An authoritative provider delay is a lower bound, never shortened. If the next required delay cannot fit, return `retry_not_before` without sleeping or incrementing invocation/request totals.
- After an ambiguous write, observe the desired primary-store postcondition before replay. Observed desired state produces `recovered`. Conclusive old state may replay if budget remains. Failed or inconclusive observation produces non-replaying `commit_unknown` with `ReplaySafety.forbidden`.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/operation_outcome.py` — immutable provider-neutral values, bounded diagnostics, canonical serialization via the existing store seam.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/retry_budget.py` — sole three-invocation, 15-second fake-clock budget.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_operation_retry_budget.py` — deterministic contract, bounds, schedule, deadline, ambiguity tables.
- `docs/adr/0100-reconciler-operation-coordination.md` — provisional ownership/recovery decision.
- `docs/adr/README.md` — ADR index entry.

Grounding: `docs/adr/0084-acli-429-rate-limit-backoff.md` plus `acli_subprocess.py::_rate_limit_backoff` establish the existing additive-jitter formula. `docs/adr/0041-llm-diagnostic-sanitization.md` plus `rebar.llm.failure.sanitize_diagnostic` establish allowlist-first redaction. Inspection shows that sanitizer does not enforce the ADR size promise, so this operation contract adds only its own size bound. `rebar._store.canonical.canonical_bytes` is the existing single canonical-JSON seam already used by reconciler modules.

## Testing
Use injected UUID, jitter, fake clock values. Table tests cover every enum member, canonical byte serialization, Unicode truncation, diagnostic overflow, all budget boundaries, provider delays that fit or exceed the remaining sleep budget, every ambiguity branch. Poison sleepers plus invocation counters prove rejected delays or `commit_unknown` perform no hidden work.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The outcome field types expose exactly the enum member sets listed above; verified by exhaustive enum contract tests.
- [ ] Equivalent outcome values serialize through `canonical_bytes` to byte-identical compact UTF-8 JSON; verified by byte fixtures containing non-ASCII text.
- [ ] Diagnostic construction drops every field outside the six-key allowlist; verified with headers, bodies, credentials, ticket content.
- [ ] Diagnostic messages use the centralized redaction seam before persistence; verified with every ADR 0041 credential/PII pattern.
- [ ] Diagnostic truncation matches the 512-code-point rule plus the exact nine-input sentinel example; verified by Unicode boundary tables.
- [ ] One canonical logical id remains stable across three physical invocations; verified by an injected-UUID sequence.
- [ ] Invocation/request totals include only executed work; verified by counters on success, rejection, ambiguity paths.
- [ ] No schedule permits a fourth physical invocation; verified by an exhaustion table.
- [ ] No schedule permits cumulative sleep above 15,000 ms; verified at exact plus one-millisecond-over boundaries.
- [ ] Zero-based retry indexes produce `[2s,3s)` then `[4s,5s)` with no third sleep; verified at deterministic jitter endpoints.
- [ ] A fitting authoritative provider delay remains the sleep lower bound; verified with fake-clock tables.
- [ ] An over-budget provider delay returns `retry_not_before` without hidden work; verified by poison sleeper/counter assertions.
- [ ] Observed desired state returns `recovered`; verified by the desired-state ambiguity case.
- [ ] Conclusive old state replays only within remaining budget; verified by within-budget/exhausted tables.
- [ ] Failed or inconclusive observation returns non-replaying `commit_unknown`; verified by failure/inconclusive tables.
- [ ] Time-dependent tests complete with zero wall-clock sleep; verified by the injected fake clock.
- [ ] ADR 0100 records retry ownership, Jira non-idempotency, observe-before-replay, lifecycle owners, selected-route-only deltas, rollback, the ADR 0087 retry-ownership delta, desired-state deltas from ADRs 0004, 0026, and 0029, retained ADR 0084 additive jitter, and rejection of full/decorrelated jitter for only two bounded sleeps; verified by ADR numbering/index tests plus document inspection.

## Out of scope
Cloud/DC adapter execution, legacy dispatch integration, fuse consumption, production cutover are later tasks.
baseline.summary: RP-03 S1 T1 — Define the logical-operation outcome and retry budget

## Context
The planner must be compared with legacy decisions before it gains authority. Preview consumers require the existing mutation array and canonical hash to remain stable while lifecycle intent data is additive and versioned.

## Outcome
Run `TicketPlan` generation in shadow, compare its mutations/dispositions with legacy output, and add a versioned lifecycle-intents preview section that old consumers can ignore.

## Plan
1. Feed the same frozen observation to legacy differ and shadow planner. Fail tests on unexplained mutation or disposition divergence and name approved deltas.
2. Extend preview/manifest rendering with an additive versioned lifecycle-intents section. Preserve the existing mutation array bytes and canonical hash.
3. Ensure construction, check, dry-run, and shadow modes perform zero repository saves, ticket writes, Jira calls, or subprocess launches.
4. Add golden fixtures covering normal, deferred dependency, filtered, tombstoned, and partial-snapshot plans.

## Testing
Golden and poison tests pin old fields/hashes, the additive section, parity diagnostics, and zero I/O.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Shadow mutations and dispositions match legacy behavior for the ticket-sourced corpus except explicitly named approved deltas.
- [ ] Preview preserves the existing mutation array bytes and canonical hash.
- [ ] Preview adds one versioned lifecycle-intents section that legacy consumers may ignore.
- [ ] Construction, check, dry-run, and shadow paths perform zero repository/provider/subprocess writes.
- [ ] Parity failure identifies the ticket, observation version, and differing plan fields without unbounded or secret content.

## Out of scope
Production coordinator authority remains RP-03 S3.

Two cheap, decoupled wins split out of the `doctor`/`fsck`/`validate` consolidation. The consolidation itself is already tracked on epic `dabb-7d4b-f5bc-40e6` and is NOT duplicated here.

**1. `validate --fix` is advertised in three places and does nothing.** `validate.py:361-362` is literally `elif arg == "--fix": pass  # accepted, no-op (the bash --fix path is unimplemented)`. It is documented in `--help` (`validate.py:342`), in `docs/cli-reference.md:458`, AND printed at runtime as the suggested remedy (`validate.py:309`, `:322`: "Run with `--fix` to attempt automatic repairs (interactive)"). A user following the tool's own advice gets nothing, silently.

Maintainer decision: remove it. `doctor` is the path for fixing.

**2. `docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md:91` sends agents to the wrong command.** It says to run "`rebar validate` (or `rebar fsck`) against the tracker to confirm store integrity" — but store integrity is `fsck`'s job and is not something `validate` checks at all. `fsck` reads bytes and git refs; `validate` reads reduced ticket semantics. They are cleanly disjoint.

Investigation confirmed the ambiguity has already cost real work: two epics (`dabb` and `18ae-4f54-a85b-4ddb`) were independently filed scoping the same `doctor` command, and `18ae` was closed as a duplicate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `--fix` is removed from `validate`'s parser, `--help`, `docs/cli-reference.md`, and both runtime hints
- [x] `docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md:91` names the correct command for store integrity
- [x] Epic `dabb-7d4b-f5bc-40e6` is updated with this audit's findings (capability matrix, the no-op, the usage evidence that `doctor` is invoked by nothing)

## CORRECTION (plan-review BLOCK, criterion G1G2) — the edit set was under-enumerated

"Advertised in three places" was wrong. Verified against the tree, `--fix` is advertised at FOUR independent sites, plus the two runtime hints:

1. `src/rebar/_cli/help/validate.txt:1` — the `--help` usage line (the SOURCE of the generated doc)
2. `src/rebar/_cli/help/overview.txt:23` — the `rebar` overview listing
3. `README.md:370` — the flag list in the validate paragraph
4. `docs/cli-reference.md:458` — GENERATED from the help text; must be REGENERATED
   (`python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`), never hand-edited, or the CI drift gate rejects it
5. `validate.py:309` and `:322` — the runtime "Run with `--fix` to attempt automatic repairs
   (interactive)" hints
6. `validate.py:361-362` — the parser arm itself (`elif arg == "--fix": pass`)

`README.md` is additionally covered by `scripts/check_readme_quickstart.py`, so the README edit must keep that gate green.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above)

- [x] `--fix` is removed from `validate`'s parser (`validate.py:361-362`)
- [x] `--fix` is removed from ALL FOUR advertisement sites: `_cli/help/validate.txt`,
      `_cli/help/overview.txt`, `README.md`, and `docs/cli-reference.md` (the last REGENERATED via
      `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`, with `--check` clean)
- [x] Both runtime hints (`validate.py:309`, `:322`) no longer suggest `--fix`; they point at
      `doctor`, which is the path for fixing
- [x] Passing `--fix` is REFUSED rather than silently accepted, via validate's existing
      unknown-option fall-through: stderr `Unknown option: --fix` and **exit 1**
- [x] `scripts/check_readme_quickstart.py` and `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py --check` both pass
- [x] `docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md:91` names `fsck` (store integrity), not `validate`
- [x] Epic `dabb-7d4b-f5bc-40e6` is updated with this audit's findings (capability matrix, the
      no-op, the usage evidence that `doctor` is invoked by nothing)


## CORRECTION 3 (plan-review BLOCK, criteria E4/G6) — the exit code was wrong

Correction 2 above asserted `--fix` would be refused with "exit 2, unknown option". That is mechanically wrong and was my error, not the ticket's. Verified empirically:

    $ rebar validate --bogus-option ; echo $?
    Unknown option: --bogus-option
    1

`_engine_support/validate.py`'s unknown-argument fall-through (the `else` arm) prints `Unknown option: ...` and returns **1**. Exit 2 comes only from the `--output` parser (`OutputFormatError`), which `--fix` never reaches. Deleting the `elif arg == "--fix": pass` arm therefore yields exit 1 from the existing else-branch — no new code is needed to refuse it, and no exit-code change should be attempted as part of this ticket.


## CORRECTION 4 (plan-review BLOCK, criteria G1G2) — the in-file `_HELP` string

Corrections 1-3 still missed the `_HELP` literal INSIDE `_engine_support/validate.py`, which advertises `--fix` at two lines. Verified:

    validate.py:337  _HELP = """Usage: rebar validate [--quick] [--full] [--fix] ...
    validate.py:342    --fix          Attempt to automatically fix issues (interactive)

That is a SIXTH advertisement site (distinct from `_cli/help/validate.txt`, which is the packaged help text). The complete removal set is therefore:

1. `_engine_support/validate.py:337` — `_HELP` usage line
2. `_engine_support/validate.py:342` — `_HELP` option description
3. `_engine_support/validate.py:309`, `:322` — the two runtime "Run with `--fix`" hints
4. `_engine_support/validate.py:361-362` — the parser arm itself
5. `_cli/help/validate.txt:1` — packaged help usage line
6. `_cli/help/overview.txt:23` — overview listing
7. `README.md:370` — flag list
8. `docs/cli-reference.md:458` — GENERATED; regenerate, never hand-edit

The lesson for the implementer: `grep -rn -- '--fix'` across `src/ docs/ README.md` is the check, not a curated list. The final AC below requires exactly that grep to come back clean.

## Acceptance Criteria (FINAL — supersedes all lists above)

- [x] `grep -rn -- '--fix' src/rebar/_engine_support/validate.py src/rebar/_cli/help/ README.md
      docs/cli-reference.md` returns NO advertisement of a validate `--fix` flag
- [x] The parser arm is deleted, so `--fix` falls through to the existing unknown-option handler:
      stderr `Unknown option: --fix`, **exit 1** (NOT exit 2 — exit 2 comes only from the
      `--output` parser, which `--fix` never reaches)
- [x] Both runtime hints point at `doctor`, which is the path for fixing
- [x] `docs/cli-reference.md` is REGENERATED (`scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`), `--check` clean
- [x] `scripts/check_readme_quickstart.py` passes
- [x] `docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md:91` names `fsck` for store integrity, not `validate`
- [x] Epic `dabb-7d4b-f5bc-40e6` is updated with this audit's findings

## Context
Two store identifiers are currently fixed: the worktree/symlink dir `.tickets-tracker` (env-overridable via `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` but NOT via project TOML) and the orphan **branch name** `tickets` (hardcoded in ~20 git invocations, no override at all). Make both overridable through project config, defaulting to the current values so every existing repo is unaffected.

## Proposed design
Add a typed `tracker` config section in `src/rebar/config.py` so the auto-derived env names line up with the established ones:
- `tracker.dir = ".tickets-tracker"`  -> auto-env `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` (already the canonical override; keep `TICKETS_TRACKER_DIR` as legacy alias).
- `tracker.branch = "tickets"`        -> auto-env `REBAR_TRACKER_BRANCH`.
Register in `_SECTION_CLASSES`, `_SECTIONS` (coercers: dir = relative-safe path; branch = valid git ref via a small validator), and `TrackerConfig` dataclass on `Config`.

Introduce a single resolver `tickets_branch(root=None)` next to `tracker_dir()`, and ROUTE BOTH through the resolved typed Config (full precedence: `-c` flag > env > project > user > default), not env-only. `tracker_dir()` currently consults env only (config.py:81-87) — it must read resolved config like the branch resolver.

## Call sites to migrate off the literals
- Branch `tickets` / `origin/tickets` (replace with `tickets_branch()` + f"origin/{branch}"):
  - `_commands/init.py` (lines ~272-295, 281): orphan/worktree creation, fetch, mount.
  - `_store/sync.py` (read reconverge, ~83-153) and `_store/push.py` (push refspec line 112, merge ~124-165).
  - `_engine/rebar_reconciler/_concurrency.py:56`, `_advisory_lock.py:498,533`.
  - `_engine_support/reads.py:187` (rev-parse verify).
  - `_commands/fsck.py:227-236` (PUSH_PENDING vs origin/<branch>).
- Worktree dir `.tickets-tracker` (replace with `tracker_dir()` / its basename):
  - The DUPLICATE `tracker_dir()` in `_engine_support/reads.py:99-149` must be unified with / kept in sync with `config.tracker_dir()`. NOTE: that copy is NOT a pure resolver — it also runs a git work-tree validation gate (`rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`); preserve that on unification (keep it, or split path-resolution from validation explicitly), don't silently drop it.
  - `_commands/init.py:152,199,418,461-469`: dir creation, the git `_exclude` it writes, the symlink name, the worktree-path resolver. The exclude must use the resolved basename so a custom dir is auto-gitignored.

## Constraints / decisions
- Defaults unchanged; pure additive. Existing repos and `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` keep working.
- Project config (committed `[tool.rebar]` in pyproject.toml / rebar.toml) is the right layer for branch name so all clones of one repo agree; the discovery walk stops at `.git` so it resolves at the repo root before the worktree exists.
- OUT OF SCOPE: renaming an EXISTING store (that is a migration). Both values are read at `init` time and thereafter; document that changing them on an initialized repo orphans the old branch/dir and is not auto-migrated. fsck SHOULD warn if a configured branch/dir does not match what is mounted — comparing the precedence-resolved config ("configured") against the actual checked-out branch + worktree/symlink target ("mounted", via `git worktree list` / the symlink).
- Validate branch against `git check-ref-format`-style rules (reject spaces, `..`, leading `-`, `~^:?*[`, trailing `/` or `.lock`). Validate `dir` shape too: a safe relative path (no absolute / `..` traversal) unless supplied via `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tracker.dir` and `tracker.branch` exist as typed config keys with the precedence chain and appear in `rebar config` output + docs/config.md.
- [ ] A single `tracker_dir()` and a new `tickets_branch()` resolver are the only sources of these values; the duplicate resolver is removed/unified **with its git work-tree validation gate preserved** (see Constraints).
- [ ] All git invocations listed above use the resolvers (no remaining `"tickets"` / `.tickets-tracker` literals in code paths).
- [ ] `rebar init` honors both on a fresh repo: custom branch + custom dir create + mount + gitignore correctly; round-trips through a **write+sync** path (create -> push/pull or reconcile dry-run -> read-back), not just create/list/show.
- [ ] Defaults reproduce todays behavior byte-for-byte (regression tests green).
- [ ] Branch-name validation rejects invalid refs with a clear ConfigError.
- [ ] `dir`-shape validation rejects unsafe paths (absolute / `..` traversal) with a clear ConfigError.
- [ ] Docs updated: README storage section + docs/config.md + docs/architecture.md note configurability.

- [ ] The orphan / no-auto-migrate behavior (changing dir/branch on an initialized repo) is explicitly DOCUMENTED (plan body mentioned it; now an AC pins it).

## Suggested child tasks
1. config: add TrackerConfig section + coercers + branch-ref AND dir-shape validators + docs (config.md, README storage section, architecture.md; incl. the orphan/no-auto-migrate note).
2. resolvers: add tickets_branch(); route tracker_dir() through resolved config; unify the _engine_support duplicate.
3. migrate branch call sites (init/sync/push/reconciler/fsck/reads).
4. migrate worktree-dir call sites (init exclude/symlink/path resolver).
5. tests: custom dir+branch init e2e exercising a write+sync round-trip; validator accept/reject; regression test defaults; fsck mismatch warning (runnable under `pytest -m "not integration"`).

baseline.description:
# Bindings key on the Jira KEY, which changes when an issue moves project

## Context / Problem

A Jira issue's KEY changes when it is moved between projects; its numeric `id` never does. Old keys are normally stacked in the `moved_issue_key` table so the old key still resolves — but a Data-Center-specific Atlassian KB documents that third-party apps moving issues via workflow post-functions, automations or scheduled routines can FAIL to update that table, after which the old key stops resolving entirely.

rebar's bindings are keyed on the KEY, and pervasively so — not just `get_jira_key`/`get_local_id`, but the `reverse` index, `note_absent`, `_retire`, `clear_absent` and `set_last_get` all take a `jira_key`. So a moved issue can silently detach: the binding points at a key that no longer resolves, the absence probe reads it as gone, and the local ticket is orphaned from an issue that still exists.

**What is NOT established, and must not be built on.** An earlier research pass asserted that `GET /rest/api/2/issue/{oldKey}` returns 200 with a body carrying the NEW key. That was retracted on a second pass and is unverified: the KB does not state whether a stale key yields 200-with-new-key, 301 or 404. The remediation below is deliberately chosen to be correct under ALL THREE readings, so this story does not block on settling it — but it is still settled here, as evidence, because two passes disagreed and the next reader deserves the answer.

## Approach

**Record the numeric `id` alongside the key on every binding, and resolve by `id` when a key lookup misses — re-keying the binding to the issue's current key when it does.**

This is deliberately ADDITIVE rather than a re-keying of the store, and that choice is the whole design decision:

* the binding store is SHARED WITH CLOUD. Changing the store's identity from key to id would rewrite
  the `reverse` index and every absence/retirement/last-get path for both vendors — a large blast
  radius on the live Cloud bridge to fix a DC-specific detachment. Additive id-capture leaves every
  existing key-keyed path behaving exactly as today.
* it is correct under all three unresolved readings of what a stale key returns. If the old key still
  resolves (200, with or without the new key in the body) nothing changes and the fallback never
  fires. If it 404s, the id fallback recovers the binding. No detection heuristic depends on the
  unverified behaviour.
* it degrades safely on a store written before this change: an entry with no recorded `id` simply has
  no fallback and behaves exactly as it does today. No migration is required, and the id is captured
  opportunistically on the next successful read of that issue.

Concretely: `bind_confirm` and `record_pending_key` accept and persist an optional `jira_id`; a `get_jira_id(local_id)` accessor is added; and the absence probe, before concluding an issue is gone, retries the lookup by recorded `id` and — on a hit whose key differs — updates the binding's key (maintaining the `reverse` index) and treats the issue as PRESENT rather than absent.

**Rejected: re-keying the binding store on the numeric id.** It is the "cleaner" answer and it is what the original ticket proposed, but it changes shared Cloud-facing identity semantics, rewrites the reverse index and every `jira_key`-taking method, and requires a store migration — all to reach the same end state this achieves additively. If DC experience later shows the fallback firing routinely, re-keying becomes a justified follow-up with evidence behind it.

**Rejected: detecting a move by parsing the old key's GET response.** That is precisely the mechanism two research passes disagreed about. Building on it would make the fix depend on unverified behaviour.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py` — persist and expose `jira_id`; re-key on an
  id-resolved move.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` — capture the numeric id
  on reads (it is already present in the unwrapped REST payload as `id`).
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — held-out regression tests.
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` — the harness experiment recording what a stale key actually returns.

## Testing

* **the binding survives a move** — a fake client where the issue's key changes and the OLD key 404s,
  while the recorded numeric id still resolves: assert the binding is preserved, re-keyed to the new
  key, and NOT retired by the absence probe. This is the defect, so it is asserted end-to-end rather
  than by inspecting the entry.
* **the `reverse` index follows the re-key** — the old key no longer maps to the local id and the new
  one does. A stale reverse entry would re-detach on the next pass.
* **a pre-existing binding with no recorded id** behaves exactly as today (no fallback, no crash),
  so the change is safe on an unmigrated store.
* **the fallback does not fire when the key still resolves** — asserted by a client that fails the
  test if the id lookup is attempted, since a fallback firing on the happy path would double every
  absence probe's cost.
* **live** — record what `GET /rest/api/2/issue/{oldKey}` returns on DC 8.17.1 after a real move,
  as evidence, since two research passes disagreed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a binding whose issue moved project SURVIVES: with the old key 404ing and the recorded numeric
      id resolving, the binding is preserved and re-keyed to the current key, asserted by a test that
      FAILS against the current code
- [ ] the absence probe does NOT retire an issue that is reachable by its recorded id — the specific
      silent detachment this ticket exists to stop
- [ ] the `reverse` index is updated in the same operation as the re-key, asserted, so the old key
      stops resolving to the local id
- [ ] bindings written BEFORE this change (no `jira_id`) continue to work unchanged, with no
      migration step, asserted by a test over a legacy-shaped entry
- [ ] the id fallback is NOT attempted while the key resolves normally, asserted by a client that
      fails if it is called — the happy path must not pay for the recovery path
- [ ] Cloud behaviour is unchanged: no existing `jira_key`-taking method changes signature or
      semantics, verified by reading the diff, since this store is shared
- [ ] [operator-attested] what `GET /rest/api/2/issue/{oldKey}` returns for a moved issue on DC 8.17.1
      (status, and whether the body carries the new key) is RECORDED on this ticket as evidence — two
      research passes disagreed and the answer must stop being folklore. The fix does not depend on
      the answer; this criterion exists to settle it
baseline.summary: Bindings key on the Jira KEY, which changes when an issue moves project

baseline.description:
The LLM completion verifier is budget-impractical for code-heavy, multi-criteria tickets.

## Context
Discovered dogfooding the close gate on this feature's own epic + workstreams. On a faster, decisive model (sonnet) a FOCUSED ticket (≈2 small AC) converges in ~12s, but a code-heavy workstream whose AC reference large files (e.g. WS-3: ~4 AC across `_cli/__init__.py` ~1000 lines, `mcp_server.py`, test files) does NOT converge even at recursion_limit=500 / ~560s. The agent reads many large files / searches across criteria; there is no cheap shortcut to verifying implementation-completeness of a code-heavy ticket. With the gate enabled, such tickets currently can't be closed without a very high REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS or `--force-close`.

## Candidate directions
- A lightweight repo-map / orientation (tree-sitter/PageRank à la Aider) so the agent reads less.
- Stronger budget steering (hard tool-call cap) and/or summarized-file reads.
- The framework-wide AutoStrategy/ProviderStrategy migration (separate follow-up) for cheaper structured output.
- Per-ticket file-impact hints (`set_file_impact`) to focus the agent on the relevant files.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A code-heavy multi-criteria workstream ticket verifies (PASS/FAIL) within a practical
      budget/latency on the default verifier model. MET: the ToolStrategy root-cause fix (ticket
      `c7c5`) moved WS-3 from a timeout at recursion_limit=500 (~560s) to a **78s PASS** via
      `output_strategy='extract'`. `sonnet` is the decisive default; `opus` over-explores.
- [x] A decision is recorded on how to make the gate practical for code-heavy tickets.
      REMEDIATED 2026-08-07 — the original wording offered three options (raise the default budget,
      add a repo-map, scope the gate to focused tickets) and the actual answer was NONE of them: the
      convergence failure was root-caused and fixed outright, so no budget was raised, no repo-map was
      built, and the gate's scope was not narrowed. The criterion is rewritten to state what was
      genuinely decided rather than force-closing past an option list that reality overtook.

## Follow-on work — owned elsewhere

Three OPTIONAL optimizations surfaced by the prior-art research are explicitly NOT part of this ticket and are owned by another session under a separate ticket:
* per-criterion fan-out (LangGraph Send + a deterministic reducer),
* per-criterion context PRE-SELECTION (Aider repo-map / FastContext line-ranges) so the agent does not
  hunt through large files,
* small bounded per-unit budgets.

None of them blocks anything: the practical-budget problem this ticket was filed for is solved.
baseline.summary: Completion verifier: efficiency for code-heavy tickets (budget limit)

baseline.description:
## Why
The coach's move catalog must offer the right remediation. Two dso lessons need moves: pre-existing issues should become follow-on tickets (pairs with rebar's discovered_from), and change-detector tests must be DELETED, not re-pinned to new source text.

## What
Add two Pass-4 coach moves to `MOVE_REGISTRY` in `src/rebar/llm/code_review/moves.py` (and thus `.rebar/code_review_moves.json`-overridable): `file-follow-on-ticket` (subject = the pre-existing/ out-of-scope issue; template guidance to file a `discovered_from` follow-on ticket) and `delete-bad-test` (subject = the change-detector/tautological test; template guidance to DELETE it, not re-pin it to the new source text). Deterministic `{subject}` templates; the LLM only picks the move name + names the subject.

### applies_when gating — DATA-FLOW (resolves plan-review G6 block f6f98d71)
The `applies_when` vocabulary is the CLOSED set `{OVERLAY_IDS ∪ "always"}` (`review_kernel.validate_move_registry`), and a move is offered by Pass-4 ONLY when its `applies_when` overlaps `active_triggers`, where `active_triggers = {c for f in surfaced for c in f.get("criteria", [])}` (`workflow_ops.py` `code_review_coach_inputs` / `code_review_coach`, ~line 342). Those `criteria` values are the overlay ids the reviewers emit (OVERLAY_IDS). Therefore a NOVEL tag (e.g. `"pre-existing"` / `"change-detector"`) would NEVER enter `active_triggers`, so a move keyed on it would register but never fire (dead move). We DELIBERATELY DO NOT extend the vocabulary. Instead we key on EXISTING overlay ids already emitted as `criteria`:
- `delete-bad-test` → `applies_when: ["tests"]`. A change-detector/tautological/over-mocking test finding
  arrives under the `tests` overlay criterion, so the move is offered whenever a surviving `tests` finding
  exists. Its `name`/`template` make it the obvious pick for a change-detector finding (vs re-pinning), and
  it sits alongside the existing `add-regression-test` move so the LLM selects delete — not "improve the
  test" — for a change-detector subject.
- `file-follow-on-ticket` → `applies_when: ["always"]`. A pre-existing/out-of-scope finding can surface
  under ANY overlay criterion, so the move is always offered; the LLM picks it when the surviving finding
  is about a pre-existing issue (subject = that issue), and the template instructs filing a
  `discovered_from` ticket rather than fixing it in-scope.

No new `applies_when` vocabulary value is introduced; both moves key on values already in the closed set, so both pass `validate_move_registry` subject-validation and actually enter `active_triggers`.

## Scope
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/moves.py` (MOVE_REGISTRY entries) + a unit test. No verdict-path change; the coach prompt (`code-review-coach.md`) already picks the single most useful applicable move, so no prompt change is required beyond the moves being offered.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `file-follow-on-ticket` and `delete-bad-test` moves exist in `MOVE_REGISTRY` with deterministic
      `{subject}` templates and pass `validate_move_registry` (built-in, strict).
- [ ] Each move's `applies_when` uses ONLY existing `{OVERLAY_IDS ∪ "always"}` values (`delete-bad-test` →
      `["tests"]`, `file-follow-on-ticket` → `["always"]`), so the move actually enters `active_triggers`
      and is OFFERED by `code_review_coach_inputs` for the intended criteria (proven by a unit test using
      `review_kernel.applicable_moves`).
- [ ] For a surviving finding tagged `criteria: ["tests"]`, `delete-bad-test` is among the applicable moves
      (the change-detector remediation), distinct from the "improve/add test" moves; a unit test pins this.
baseline.summary: Coach moves: file-follow-on-ticket + delete-bad-test

baseline.description:
## Problem

`rebar fsck` reports 8 stray top-level directories in the tickets tracker (`/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker`), each flagged twice — once as `MISSING_CREATE` (no CREATE event found) and once inside the single `FOREIGN_STORE_PATH` finding:

    0efe-9207-2706-43a3  2021-2ef0-e36f-44fc  6f8a-45e5-d9ec-402c  a109-e758-71bb-4371
    afe5-db0b-e9c5-45d8  c827-81ee-a592-4d27  d052-ad3f-23c1-4511  fa38-670c-d8fc-4c22

Baseline: `fsck complete: 16 issues found` = 8 MISSING_CREATE + 6 STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED
+ 1 FOREIGN_STORE_PATH + 1 ENV_ID_MISMATCH.

## Evidence (pre-removal triage)

All 8 are empty directories (`ls -A` returns nothing), none is committed (`git ls-tree HEAD <dir>` empty for all 8), `git status --porcelain` in the tracker is clean because git cannot track empty directories, and `rebar exists <id>` returns exit 1 for all 8. `lsof +D` on the tracker shows no process holding a file under any of the 8. Directory mtimes span 2026-08-10 11:05 to 2026-08-12 12:52 — all far outside the ~30-minute live-writer window (triage run 2026-08-12 17:59 PDT). `rebar tracker-maintenance --status` independently reports `unpushed ticket commits: 0` and exactly these 8 as `foreign top-level paths`, so `--clean` will not refuse and the break-glass `--force` is NOT needed. `rebar review-plan` itself logs each one as "debris of an interrupted write; safe to delete".

## Likely cause

`os.makedirs(ticket_dir)` succeeded and the process died before the first event was atomically renamed in — agents interrupted mid-write by host sleeps, session-limit kills, and shell-cap timeouts across the active fleet.

## How `--clean` actually behaves (correcting an earlier draft of this plan)

`rebar tracker-maintenance --clean` is ALL-OR-NOTHING over the foreign set: `src/rebar/_commands/tracker_maintenance.py` iterates `for name in foreign:` and calls `shutil.rmtree(full)` on every entry that `fsck.foreign_store_path_list` returned, with no per-directory filter and no CLI surface for passing a subset. The guards below therefore do NOT select what the tool deletes — they are a precondition on running it at all. Consequently the guard set is applied as an equality check: immediately before the write, `--status`'s foreign list must be exactly the 8 triaged ids. If it lists any 9th path, or any triaged directory has become non-empty, the run is ABORTED and reported rather than narrowed — because there is no way to narrow it. This also bounds the check-then-act (TOCTOU) window to the gap between that `--status` and the `--clean`, seconds apart.

## Relationship to 043f-3336-d5de-45be (closed)

That bug made the plan-relation reducer TOLERATE event-less directories and explicitly rejected writer-side cleanup, because an automatic rmdir races a concurrent session's in-flight write ("tolerate, never tidy"). This ticket does not reintroduce automatic cleanup: it is a one-off operator-initiated sweep whose guards are precisely the evidence an automatic writer-side rmdir could never establish.

## Plan (minimal, deterministic — five guards, all-or-nothing)

Per directory: (1) empty; (2) uncommitted; (3) `rebar exists <id>` exits 1; (4) no open file handle under it; (5) mtime older than 30 minutes. Then the run-level gate: `--status` foreign list equals the 8 triaged ids exactly. All six conditions hold -> run `rebar tracker-maintenance --clean` (backup ref before first write, refusal on unpushed ticket commits, durable audit). Any condition fails -> make NO writes and report back. No raw git in the tracker, no stash. `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED` (benign, auto-resolved) and `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` (known by-design flag from change 1638) are out of scope and must not be touched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: A per-directory triage verdict for all 8 directories is recorded as a comment on
      this ticket, each citing the five guards. Verified by `rebar show 7c6e-4b8a-59c5-46db`
      showing a comment naming all 8 ids with a verdict each.
- [x] AC2: Immediately before any write, `rebar tracker-maintenance --status` is re-run and
      its `foreign top-level paths` list is asserted byte-equal to the 8 triaged ids;
      on any mismatch the sweep is aborted with no writes and the mismatch recorded.
      Verified by the recorded `--status` output in a ticket comment.
- [x] AC3: Given AC2's equality assertion held, `rebar tracker-maintenance --clean` is run
      and exits 0 having printed a backup ref, and afterwards
      `rebar fsck 2>&1 | grep -c -E 'MISSING_CREATE|FOREIGN_STORE_PATH'` prints 0.
      If AC2's assertion failed instead, this criterion is satisfied by recording the abort
      and making no writes.
- [x] AC4: No committed ticket data is modified. Verified by capturing
      `git -C .tickets-tracker rev-parse HEAD` before and after and asserting the two are
      byte-identical, and by `git -C .tickets-tracker status --porcelain` staying empty.

## Testing

A store data operation, so verification is by command exit code and before/after diff rather than by unit test:

1. Before: `rebar fsck 2>&1 | tail -1` (record issue count);
   `git -C /Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker rev-parse HEAD` (record sha).
2. Per-directory guards: `ls -A <dir>` empty; `git ls-tree HEAD <dir>` empty;
   `rebar exists <id>` exit 1; `lsof +D` naming no file under it; mtime > 30 min old.
3. Run-level gate: `rebar tracker-maintenance --status` foreign list == the 8 ids exactly.
4. Act: `rebar tracker-maintenance --clean` — must exit 0 and print a backup ref.
5. After: `rebar fsck 2>&1 | grep -c -E 'MISSING_CREATE|FOREIGN_STORE_PATH'` must print 0;
   `git -C .tickets-tracker rev-parse HEAD` must equal the step-1 sha;
   `git -C .tickets-tracker status --porcelain` must be empty.
baseline.summary: Sweep interrupted-ticket-write debris: 8 uncommitted stray ticket dirs in the tracker

baseline.description:
## Why

The code-review `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar (`code_review_result_v1`) persists only the SURFACED findings — the `blocking`, `advisory`, and `coaching` buckets — and omits the `dropped` and `indeterminate` findings that Pass-3 produced. It also does not persist the numeric `block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled` each finding was judged against. So "the complete Pass-1 finding list" is not recoverable for a code review, unlike plan review.

## Dependency

This story **depends on 4e19** (plan-review lossless v2), which lands first in the stack and makes the SHARED review kernel stamp the resolved boundary on every decided finding: `pass3_decide` returns `block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled` and `pass3_over_findings` merges them, so every code-review finding (via `code_review_decide`) already carries them by the time this story runs. 4e19 also adds those two fields (plus `evidence`/`scenarios`) to the plan-review `_slim`, so the two sidecars **converge** in shape — this story does not introduce a field plan-review lacks.

## What

Extend the code-review sidecar to `code_review_result_v2`, pooling the four buckets the code-review gate actually produces — `blocking`, `advisory` (surfaced), `dropped`, `indeterminate` — with each finding's full Pass-2 `verification` and Pass-3 determination (`decision`/`priority`/…), plus the resolved `block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled` (stamped by the 4e19 kernel change). There is **no `overflow` bucket** in code review: unlike plan-review (which applies an advisory cap that spills to `overflow`), `code_review_decide` partitions only into `{blocking, surfaced, dropped, indeterminate}` and the code-review verdict schema has no `overflow` property.

## Scope

The `dropped`/`indeterminate` buckets are computed by `code_review_decide` but are **not** currently forwarded to the terminal verdict — `code_review_coach` assembles only `{verdict, blocking, advisory, coaching, coverage}`, and `apply_region_gated_floor` only appends its own novelty-floor drops post-hoc. So the wiring must be extended:

- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` — in the `verdict` step's `with:` block, pass
  `dropped: ${{ steps.decide.outputs.dropped }}` and
  `indeterminate: ${{ steps.decide.outputs.indeterminate }}` (alongside the existing `blocking`
  and `surfaced`).
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py` — `code_review_coach` accepts `dropped`/
  `indeterminate` inputs and includes them in its returned verdict dict; update its
  `code_review_coach_input`/`_output` schemas to allow the two new (optional) arrays.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py` — bump `SCHEMA` to `code_review_result_v2`; in
  `build_payload`, add `dropped`/`indeterminate` (norm-id-stamped, like `blocking`/`advisory`), each
  finding retaining its `verification`/`decision`/`block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled`; KEEP the
  separate `blocking`/`advisory` lists (so the surfaced reader is unchanged) and the change metadata
  (`change_id`/`revision`/`change_fingerprint`) + `deps`. `_latest_payload_with_ts` and
  `latest_code_review_result` accept BOTH `code_review_result_v1` and `_v2` (replace the
  `== SCHEMA` guard with membership in `{v1, v2}`), so old records still read and the surfaced
  reader keeps returning the `blocking + advisory` union.

Code-review findings carry no `evidence`/`scenarios` (those are plan-review Pass-1 fields); this story does not persist them for code review.

## Enumerated consumers to update

- `tests/unit/test_code_review_ws4.py:210` asserts `payload["schema"] == "code_review_result_v1"`
  on a fresh emit; update it to `_v2` (the schema bumped).
- `docs/experiments/derive_code_review_threshold.py` is a jq/offline consumer that filters on
  `code_review_result_v1`; note that it should accept `_v2` too (or is left as historical — out of
  this story's code scope, flagged for the reader).

## Compatibility & rollback

`v1` code-review sidecars remain readable (new buckets absent → default to `[]`). The novelty-floor reader that consumes surfaced findings keeps returning the `blocking + advisory` union, so region-gating is unaffected. No backfill. Reverting bumps `SCHEMA` back to `v1` and stops writing the `dropped`/`indeterminate` buckets; already-written `v2` records stay readable because the reader still accepts both schemas (the reader change is independently safe to keep).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `build_payload` produces a `code_review_result_v2` payload that pools `blocking`, `advisory`,
      `dropped`, and `indeterminate`, each finding retaining its `verification`, Pass-3 `decision`,
      and resolved `block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled` plus a `norm_id`. Oracle: a unit test driving
      `build_payload` with a verdict containing all four buckets and asserting on the payload JSON.
- [ ] `code_review_coach` forwards `dropped`/`indeterminate` from the decide step into the terminal
      verdict dict. Oracle: a contract test calling the `code_review_coach` op with those inputs and
      asserting they appear in the returned verdict.
- [ ] `latest_code_review_result` reads both a `v1` and a `v2` code-review sidecar. Oracle: a unit
      test with one hand-written record of each schema.
- [ ] The novelty-floor surfaced-findings reader returns exactly the `blocking + advisory` union
      from a `v2` payload, unchanged vs an equivalent `v1` payload. Oracle: a unit test comparing the
      two.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: code-review sidecar -> lossless v2 (all buckets + thresholds)

# terraform-drift check permanently red: opcert_admin trust-policy phantom drift

## Context / proven root cause
The `terraform-drift` GitHub Actions check has failed on every run against `origin/main` since opcert.tf landed (commit f78940a43, 2026-07-15). The check runs `terraform plan` over `infra/terraform/` with NO variable inputs (.github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml:61). `aws_iam_role.opcert_admin`'s assume_role_policy derives its principals from `var.opcert_admin_principal_arns` (opcert.tf:138), which defaults to `[]` (opcert.tf:29). The live role was applied with the operator-supplied account-root principal (`arn:aws:iam::896586841071:root`, per the documented deploy pattern opcert.tf:26 / opcert-plan-assertions.sh:22). So every plan renders an EMPTY principal and diffs it against live's account-root principal:

    # aws_iam_role.opcert_admin will be updated in-place
      ~ Principal = { ~ AWS = "arn:aws:iam::896586841071:root" -> [] }
    Plan: 0 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy.   -> exit 2 -> check FAILS

This is an un-reconcilable phantom (applying the committed default would remove the principal), so it permanently reds the daily drift sweep and masks any real future drift.

## Defect
Asymmetry inside opcert.tf: the sibling operator-seeded SSM KEY param carries `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [value] }` (opcert.tf:57-59) precisely so plan/apply never diff on an operator-owned value — but the equally operator-supplied trust principal was not given the same guard.

## Plan (fix direction: ignore_changes — user-approved)
Add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [assume_role_policy] }` to `aws_iam_role.opcert_admin`. Terraform still creates the role; the operator owns the trust list out-of-band (honors the documented "operator supplies principals at deploy" intent and mirrors the key-param precedent). This suppresses the phantom diff at PLAN time — no terraform apply required.

## Acceptance criteria (measurable)
1. `aws_iam_role.opcert_admin` in infra/terraform/opcert.tf declares
   `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [assume_role_policy] }`.
2. A hermetic source-contract test in tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py asserts (1)
   and was seen RED before the fix, GREEN after (with a mutation check returning it to RED).
3. `terraform fmt -check` and `terraform validate` pass on the edited module.
4. No existing opcert infra test is weakened; full unit suite for the file passes.

## Verify command
    cd /Users/joeoakhart/fix-opcert-drift-ignore-changes
    ./.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py -q
    cd infra/terraform && terraform fmt -check && terraform validate
baseline.summary: terraform-drift check permanently red: opcert_admin trust-policy phantom drift

baseline.description:
# The global rebar build is 4 days stale, and it SILENTLY disables the LLM tier of plan review

## Context / Problem
This machine's global `rebar`/`rebar-mcp` is supposed to track `origin/main` HOURLY via a rollback-guarded LaunchAgent (documented in `docs/local-env-main-tracking.local.md`). IT HAS NOT RUN SINCE 2026-07-27 17:10 — measured from the mtime of `/Users/joeoakhart/.local/pipx/venvs/nava-rebar/lib/python3.14/site-packages/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py`, and corroborated by the venv directory's own mtime. Today is 2026-07-31, so the global build is ~4 days behind main.

**THE FAILURE MODE IS SILENT DEGRADATION OF THE REVIEW GATE, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A BUG AND NOT HOUSEKEEPING.** `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` carries `activate` as a DICT (scoped per review type), which main's overlay parser accepts — `git show origin/main:src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py | grep "must be a list of ids"` returns NOTHING. The stale global build predates that: its overlay.py DOES contain that check and raises `CriteriaError: 'activate' must be a list of ids, got dict`. Support landed in `f3dbe32b0b` (2026-07-27, "3ba4: Scope project criteria by review type") and `7f4c650114` (2026-07-28).

MEASURED consequence of running `rebar review-plan <id> --ref HEAD` with the global build in this repo:

    "llm_ran": false,
    "llm_unavailable": true,
    "llm_error": "step 'review@then/assemble' failed: criteria overlay .../.rebar/criteria_routing.json:
                  'activate' must be a list of ids, got dict"
    "verdict": "INDETERMINATE"

The command EXITS 2 and emits a sidecar. It does not present as a broken install; it presents as a plan that could not be reviewed. The DET tier still runs and reports pass/fail per criterion, so the output looks substantive. An operator or agent reading that verdict would reasonably conclude the TICKET is the problem. **No LLM review happened at all.**

The worktree build parses the same file fine — `registry.effective_criteria('.')` returns 44 effective criteria — so this is purely the stale global install, not a repo defect.

## Why this matters beyond one command
AGENTS.md already warns to run the repo checkout's build rather than a stale global install, and gives the reason as "silently ignores newer config keys". This incident shows the consequence is worse than ignoring a key: an unrelated-looking INDETERMINATE on the claim gate. Any agent that trusts `which rebar` gets it. The MCP server is affected the same way and, per the local docs, will not hot-reload.

## Approach
Two separable pieces:
 1. DIAGNOSE why the LaunchAgent stopped. Check `launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`
    for its last exit status, and the agent's own log, before forcing a sync. A rollback-guarded updater
    that silently gave up 4 days ago has its own failure to explain — forcing a sync hides the evidence.
    Force it only after capturing that state:
    `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`.
 2. MAKE THE STALENESS LOUD rather than silent. A gate run whose LLM tier dies on a CONFIG-PARSE error
    from the installed build is not the same as an LLM outage, and collapsing both into
    `llm_unavailable` + INDETERMINATE is what made this cost time. A `CriteriaError` while loading the
    overlay is a CONFIGURATION fault: it should surface distinctly (its own verdict reason or a loud
    warning naming the installed build's version), so the reader is pointed at the install rather than
    at the plan.

## Scope
- The LaunchAgent / updater: diagnosis first, then a sync.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/` — distinguish a config-parse failure from an LLM outage in the verdict's
  `llm_error` / reason surfacing.
- Possibly a startup or gate-time warning when the running build's commit is far behind the repo's.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every criterion below is verifiable IN-SESSION by a probe, experiment, or test — no criterion defers to a future change.

ALL OF THEM ARE TAGGED [operator-attested], and that is a statement of fact rather than a way around the gate: the completion verifier reads REPOSITORY FILES ONLY, while every probe here observes machine-local operational state — a launchd exit code, a pipx venv's recorded backend, `command -v uv` under a given PATH, the contents of ~/.local/state/rebar-dev/update.log. NO repository file can record any of it, because THE FIX ITSELF TOUCHES NO REPOSITORY FILE (it is one line of a script under ~/.local/bin plus recreating a venv). The observed outputs are pasted verbatim in the evidence comment on this ticket so the attestation is checkable rather than merely asserted. The code hardening that was previously bundled here (reporting an overlay `CriteriaError` distinctly from an LLM outage, and naming the installed build as the suspect) has been SPLIT OUT to its own ticket, because it is a repo change with its own review and must not hold this environment repair open.

- [ ] [operator-attested] ROOT CAUSE A, PROVEN AND REPAIRED: `~/.local/bin/uv` (0.7.18) shadowed `/opt/homebrew/bin/uv`
      (0.12.0) on the updater's PATH. Probe: under the script's ORIGINAL PATH order,
      `command -v uv` resolves the 0.7.18 binary; under the fixed order it resolves 0.12.0.
- [ ] [operator-attested] ROOT CAUSE B, PROVEN AND REPAIRED: the pipx venv was pinned to the pip backend, which pipx
      will not override. Probe: `pipx_metadata.json` recorded `backend = pip` before and records
      `backend = uv` after; and `pipx install --force --backend uv` against the OLD venv was
      demonstrably IGNORED (same `resolution-too-deep`, metadata unchanged).
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE UPDATER COMPLETES: a run exits 0 and `last-good.sha` advances off the Jul-17 commit
      (`4dd9172b9`) to the current tip of `main`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] IT WORKS UNDER LAUNCHD, NOT JUST BY HAND: `launchctl kickstart -k` the agent and then
      `launchctl print` reports `last exit code = 0`. This is the criterion that matters — every
      by-hand run inherits the operator's rich shell environment, whereas launchd supplies a minimal
      one, so a by-hand pass does not prove the scheduled job works.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE INSTALL PATH ITSELF IS EXERCISED UNDER LAUNCHD, not just the no-op branch: with
      `last-good.sha` temporarily rewound, a launchd-triggered run performs a real install and
      advances it again (restore the true sha afterwards). Without this, a green kickstart only
      proves the `no change` early-exit.
- [ ] [operator-attested] IDEMPOTENCE: an immediately following run is a no-op — it logs `no change (already on <sha>)`
      and exits 0 rather than reinstalling.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE MUTATION BITES: restoring the original PATH order reproduces the exact
      `pipx needs uv>=0.9.17` failure, proving the one-line fix is load-bearing and not incidental.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE REPORTED SYMPTOM IS GONE: the GLOBAL build parses the dict-shaped `activate` in
      `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` — `registry.effective_criteria('.')` returns the full criteria
      set where it previously raised `CriteriaError`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE GATE ACTUALLY RUNS ON THE GLOBAL BUILD: a real `rebar review-plan` invoked with the GLOBAL
      build reaches the LLM tier (`llm_ran: true`), not merely a successful criteria parse. This is
      the end-to-end form of the reported failure, whose signature was `llm_ran: false`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE SMOKE-TEST/ROLLBACK GUARD IS INTACT: the script's post-install smoke test still gates
      `last-good.sha`, evidenced by the smoke commands exiting 0 against the freshly installed build.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE KNOWLEDGE IS RECORDED where the next person will look: the local runbook documents that
      PATH order is load-bearing, that `uv` is a hard requirement (so `--backend pip` is NOT a valid
      workaround for this package), that an existing venv pins its backend, and that `update.log` —
      not the 0-byte launchd logs — is the diagnostic file.
baseline.summary: Global rebar build 4 days stale: silently disables the LLM tier of plan review

# P2.1 — Hybrid Logical Clock for event ordering (skew-immune replay)

**Correctness backbone.** Closes the one architectural gap a distributed tracker
should not ship without; P2.3 rides its total order.

## Context (problem + research)

rebar orders replay by the `${timestamp_ns}` filename prefix; invariant I8 admits
EDIT/COMMENT interleaving is "best-effort" under clock skew (only STATUS forks are
skew-independent, UUID-keyed at `reducer/_processors.py:78-120`). Two agents on
skewed clocks editing the same field resolve by last *wall-clock* writer -> silent
clobber. **git-bug solves exactly this with a persisted Lamport clock**
(`util/lamport/*`, `clocks/<name>`): a single `uint64`, advanced monotonically,
**re-seeded by witnessing max over history**; the local file is a disposable
cache, the authoritative value rides in git. Replay orders by logical time then a
content-id tiebreak. Radicle uses the same family (causal DAG + actor-id tiebreak).

## Evidence (experiments)

- EXP1: `time_ns()` is 19 digits until ~year 2286; equal-width ints sort identically
  as strings and ints; string sort only breaks across DIFFERING widths -> stay 19-digit.
- EXP4: 2400 concurrent flock'd `next_tick()` ticks — all unique/monotonic/19-digit.
- EXP4b: with **no cache file**, `next_tick_for_ticket()` still issues a tick >
  `max(prefix)`, 19-digit -> the cache is reconstructable (git-bug's model).
- EXP-jq: the prefix is >2^53; jq rounds it -> **no jq/arithmetic may ever touch it**
  (reinforces P1.0's one-Python-serializer rule).
- EXP-R2 (real code): `event_sort_key` ts segment is `str` today; int-order ==
  string-order on real filenames; malformed names take the fallback -> change is safe.

## What / Implementation detail

1. New `rebar._store.hlc.next_tick()` = single monotonic integer
   `max(hlc.state, max(prefix of TARGET TICKET's events after sync), time_ns()) + 1`,
   RMW under a **local** `.rebar/hlc.lock` (held only inside the call -> no ordering
   hazard with the write lock). `.rebar/hlc.state` is a **disposable cache**
   (gitignored, I3/I7); correctness is re-derived from the durable log, so a
   missing/stale/raced cache is still correct.
2. Thread it through the four live timestamp seams: `_commands/_seam.py:153`,
   `ticket_txn.py` (STATUS/claim), reconciler `inbound_translate`, and
   `ticket-compact.sh` (via `python3 -m rebar._store.hlc next`). Add an injectable
   `REBAR_HLC_NOW` for the skewed-clock test.
3. Change `reducer/_sort.py:event_sort_key` (line 21) to `int(ts_segment)` (malformed
   fallback), keeping the `(ts, type_order, name)` tuple + LINK<UNLINK tiebreak;
   align the other prefix sorts (`graph/_links.py:53`, `_commands/unlink.py:47`,
   bare `sorted()` STATUS scans at `ticket_txn.py:187/318`). Keep the UUID tiebreak
   (git-bug: logical-time then content-id).
4. Bump `reducer/_version.py:SCHEMA_VERSION` -> 2. Single-integer encoding keeps
   width at 19 digits, so older clones still string-compare correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar._store.hlc.next_tick()` (single-int, local-lock RMW, witness max(prefix), injectable clock)
- [ ] threaded through all four live timestamp seams (incl. bash via `python3 -m`)
- [ ] `event_sort_key` + the 3 other prefix sorts use integer comparison; UUID tiebreak kept
- [ ] SCHEMA_VERSION -> 2; event-schema.md updated
- [ ] NEW skewed-clock EDIT/COMMENT convergence regression (merged red-first), width-comparator + forward-compat tests
- [ ] staged behind `REBAR_HLC` with kill-switch for one release

See `docs/remediation-implementation-plan.md` (P2.1).
- [ ] A NEW skewed-clock regression (two clones, injected skew) shows EDIT/COMMENT
- [ ] Width-comparator test: legacy 19-digit and new names sort into one global order.
- [ ] v1-reducer replay of a v2 store still yields a valid state (forward-compat).
baseline.summary: P2.1 — Hybrid Logical Clock for event ordering (skew-immune replay)

## Context
The OS/Python-invariant complexity-baseline lock currently runs inside every test-matrix cell in `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`: Ubuntu costs 52/54/55s and macOS costs 45s. The same commit has already been checked out in the single Ubuntu lint job. Running the policy there once preserves the gate while eliminating four duplicate invocations and their fetch/merge-base work, estimated at about 154 net runner-seconds per Verified run. CPython and Django use dedicated single lint jobs; Rust and Kubernetes use dedicated tidy/verify surfaces. No rejection was found; `humble-cinnamoned-mussel` fixed lock correctness but did not require matrix duplication.

## Plan
- Strengthen workflow policy tests to require exactly one complexity-lock invocation, in the single lint job, and to prohibit it in the OS/Python test matrix.
- Move the existing unchanged script invocation and definition-vs-tree guard from `jobs.test` to `jobs.lint`.
- Run held-out RED→GREEN, a duplicate-invocation mutation, workflow/config tests, repository gates, and compare CI job timing after Gerrit upload. Back-out is a Gerrit revert.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --lock` executes exactly once for a Verified change.
- [ ] The invocation is a blocking step in the single lint job and is absent from the test matrix.
- [ ] The existing fail-closed and definition-vs-tree-skew behavior is unchanged.
- [ ] A workflow unit oracle fails on the current four-matrix-invocation placement and on any future duplicate placement.
- [ ] Reintroducing the matrix invocation returns the held-out oracle to RED.
- [ ] CI evidence quantifies runner-seconds saved without adding jobs, runners, or reducing policy coverage.
- [ ] Focused tests, lint, typecheck, Gerrit LLM-Review +1, and Gerrit Verified +1 pass before merge.
- [ ] The final ticket comment records RED/GREEN/mutation evidence and measured savings.
baseline.summary: Run complexity baseline lock once per Verified change

## Scope (RE-SCOPED 2026-07-03)
This ticket's acceptance is the **in-repo code deliverable** — the derisk mechanism (baseline dual-write shadow), the circuit-breaker enforcement in the level-triggered apply path, and the rollback documentation — all landed on main and unit-tested. The **operational tail** (>= 10 clean live shadow passes, the Phase-3 prev_snapshot->baseline consumer-flag flip, and the capped live heal of the 7 known drift instances) requires live production Jira and the deployed 20-min workflow, so it CANNOT run in an agent session; it is carved out to follow-up **lofty-beech-twang (a118)** and owned by the deployed-workflow operator. - [ ] Baseline dual-write shadow behind `reconciler.baseline_dual_write` emits per-pass `baseline_shadow_check` logging and `baseline_shadow_divergence` on divergence, consumes no arbitration input (prev_snapshot untouched); covered by `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_baseline_shadow.py`. — landed on main.
