baseline.description:
## Context

The plan-review gate's re-review of an *edited* plan does not converge: each remediation
round can surface new issues in previously-clean criteria, expanding scope every run and
creating a non-terminating loop that drives cost, wall-clock, and agent non-compliance.
This is distinct from run-over-run reproducibility on fixed input (the LLM-as-judge
self-consistency problem); the plan legitimately changed, so feedback *should* differ. The
problem we solve: a remediation re-review should confirm the surfaced issues were resolved
**without** introducing different, lower-stakes issues that restart the loop.

Prior conversation rejected three approaches: per-diff-region scoping (new section-diffing
machinery), skip-clean-criteria reuse (unsound — reuses absence-of-finding, freezes
high-stakes defects an edit introduces), and the whole-verdict probe (too coarse). This
epic captures the chosen approach. Relates to the plan-review epic `5fd2-a7c2-0aec-48fa`.
It is decomposed into 6 child tasks (see "Decomposition" below).

## Terminology (canonical)

- **impact** — the verifier's coarse severity-attribute score in [0,1] (`decide.impact`).
- **validity** — the graded fraction of the Pass-2 binary sub-answers in [0,1].
- **priority** — `validity × impact` (the existing Pass-3 score; the drop axis).
- **novelty score** — a new [0,1] score derived deterministically from a new Pass-2
  novelty sub-answer set (see below); high = "not present in the prior review".
- **carryover finding** — a current finding matching a prior-review finding (low novelty).

## What (the chosen design)

A **rising-floor remediation re-review**: run the FULL criteria set every time (no skipped
criteria, no Pass-1 anchoring → full recall), and on a remediation re-review apply a
deterministic Pass-3 floor that drops only **novel, low-priority** findings.

- **Full Pass-1, unanchored.** Every applicable criterion runs; the finder never sees prior
  findings (avoids the sycophancy/anchoring the research documents). High-priority defects
  an edit introduces are still found — nothing is frozen.
- **Novelty as a narrow-question score, in a SEPARATE Pass-2 sub-call.** Novelty is scored
  by a DISTINCT structured sub-call that ALONE receives the prior findings and answers a
  small novelty sub-answer set ("does this finding correspond to a prior finding?"). The
  existing verification sub-call (severity attributes + the binary/validity sub-answers)
  receives **NO** prior findings, so the `verify.py` independence invariant
  (VERIFIER_RULES[0]) is enforced *structurally*, not by prompt assertion — mirroring the
  Pass-1 isolation. Pass-3 maps the novelty sub-answers to a deterministic novelty score,
  exactly as it maps the binary sub-answers to validity. The sub-answers are factual **matches-prior** questions (same defect / same location / same fix as a specific prior finding?) on the `yes=1.0/insufficient=0.5/no=0.0` map; **`novelty = 1 − mean(matches-prior sub-answers)`** (high novelty = no prior match). Fail-safe: a failed/malformed novelty sub-call defaults novelty to 0.0 (carryover → never dropped). Full set + arithmetic on task 150b. The sub-answers are factual
  **matches-prior** questions (does this restate the same defect / cite the same location /
  suggest the same fix as a specific prior finding?) on the `yes=1.0/insufficient=0.5/no=0.0`
  map; **`novelty = 1 − mean(matches-prior sub-answers)`** (high novelty = no prior match).
  Fail-safe: a failed/malformed novelty sub-call defaults novelty to 0.0 (carryover → never
  dropped). Full set + arithmetic live on task 150b.
- **Deterministic rising floor (Pass-3).** A finding is dropped iff novelty ≥ `T_novel` AND
  `priority < floor`. Carryover findings (low novelty) use the normal threshold and must
  still be resolved. A novel high-priority finding (high impact × high validity) is
  preserved (and may block). The whole policy is deterministic — no LLM holistic severity.
- **Freshness window = remediation-mode gate.** The floor applies only when: config enabled,
  plan changed, code unchanged since baseline, registry unchanged, a prior sidecar (with
  finding text) is available, and the last review (full OR partial) is within the window
  (default 60 min). **Each review resets the window**, so the loop persists across a series
  of edits while the agent is actively iterating; it lapses to a normal full (un-floored)
  review only after the agent goes idle past the window. Code-changed / both-drifted → full
  review (`drift_refresh` untouched — out of scope). **Back-out:** setting the config key off
  restores byte-identical full-review behavior.

## Narrowed-verdict / sidecar schema

- The verdict's `coverage` records `narrowed: true`, `floored_criteria`, and the floored
  finding ids when the rising floor was applied (absent/false on a normal review).
- Dropped novel findings are written to the `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar (not the surfaced
  verdict), joinable by `norm_id`, so suppression is always observable.

## Defaults & calibration (falsifiable)

- Starting defaults (tunable): `T_novel = 0.7`; `priority floor = the p40 impact percentile
  of the 245-event corpus × validity` (≈ the "below major" band). Both are *derived*, not
  guessed: `scripts/plan_review_impact_distribution.py` prints the percentile inputs.
- The novelty scorer must clear an **evidence gate** BEFORE the Pass-3 drop rule is activated.
  The bar is concrete and uses the framework's existing idiom (NOT an invented AUC/F1): a
  `discriminates_novelty` deterministic scorer (per-case, **0.5 midpoint** — `kind: novel`
  scores novelty ≥ 0.5, `kind: carryover` < 0.5, mirroring `discriminates_true_from_false` /
  `discriminates_impact_levels`) gated at the spec level by **`gate: at_least(2)` over
  `epochs: 3` + `coverage_threshold: 0.8`** on ≥ 3 labeled novel/carryover pairs (task 150b).
- **Three distinct numbers (do not conflate):** (a) the **runtime drop threshold
  `T_novel = 0.7`** — Pass-3 drops a finding only if novelty ≥ 0.7 (and priority < floor),
  config-overridable; (b) the **eval discrimination floor 0.5** — the per-case midpoint the
  `discriminates_novelty` scorer separates novel from carryover at; (c) the **eval bar** —
  the spec gate `at_least(2)/epochs:3` + `coverage_threshold:0.8` the scorer must clear before
  the drop rule activates. 0.7 is "how novel to be droppable"; 0.5/the gate is "did the scorer
  prove it can tell novel from carryover at all".

## Within-session suppression (deliberate, honest bound)

Because the window resets on each review, a novel low-priority finding can be re-floored
every round while the agent keeps iterating — within-session suppression is **intentionally
unbounded** (the chosen persistence behavior). It is bounded only by: the idle-lapse window,
carryover findings still being enforced at the normal bar, and every dropped finding being
recorded in the sidecar. Optional future safety valve: a `max_consecutive_narrowed_rounds`
cap that forces a full un-floored review. (No unsound *coverage* accumulates — Pass-1 always
runs the full criteria set; only the surfacing of novel low-priority findings is suppressed.)

## Empirical grounding (established)

- 245 `REVIEW_RESULT` events / 2,571 findings: the verifier's impact axis already
  discriminates (15% critical, 40% none, mean impact 0.43; attributes spread sensibly) — so
  impact discrimination is not a blocker; the floor has real spread to act on.
- The impact prompt nonetheless gives the severity attributes zero anchoring (vs rich
  guidance for validity) → tightening it is a robustness item, not a blocker.

## Already landed (observability foundation)

- `scripts/plan_review_impact_distribution.py` — repeatable corpus distribution report.
- `discriminates_impact_levels` eval scorer + `high_impact`/`low_impact` dataset pairs on
  `plan-review-verifier.eval.yaml`.

## Decomposition (6 child tasks)

1. Persist finding text in the sidecar + latest-sidecar reader (foundation).
2. Pass-2 novelty sub-answers in a SEPARATE sub-call + a `discriminates_novelty` eval gate.
3. Pass-3 novelty score + rising-floor drop rule (depends on 2; gated by the eval bar).
4. Remediation-mode gate: freshness window + preconditions + wiring (depends on 1).
5. Tighten the verifier impact prompt (robustness; verified by the impact eval).
6. Docs + ADR + offline convergence tests (depends on 3, 4).

## Scope

- IN: full-run + deterministic rising floor; separate-sub-call novelty scoring + its eval
  gate; freshness-window remediation-mode gating; sidecar finding-text persistence;
  impact-prompt tightening; config keys; docs + ADR.
- OUT: the code-drift `drift_refresh` path (unchanged); per-diff-region scoping;
  skip-clean-criteria reuse.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Sidecar `_slim` persists `finding`, `suggested_fix`, `checklist_item` (sidecar event
      only; surfaced verdict shape byte-unchanged); a latest-sidecar reader exists; the
      `RETAIN_PER_TICKET` retention bound is respected.
- [ ] Pass-2 scores novelty in a SEPARATE structured sub-call that alone receives prior
      findings; the severity/validity sub-call receives none (independence enforced
      structurally). Pass-1 receives no prior findings.
- [ ] A `discriminates_novelty` eval scorer (per-case, 0.5 midpoint) + ≥ 3 labeled
      carryover/novel pairs land on a DEDICATED `plan-review-novelty.eval.yaml` (keyed to the
      `plan-review-novelty` prompt — NOT the verifier spec, where the scorer would grade the
      wrong artifact; this dedicated-spec correction was mandated by child 150b's plan review);
      its bar is
      `gate: at_least(2)`/`epochs: 3` + `coverage_threshold: 0.8` (NOT an AUC literal),
      distinct from the runtime `T_novel=0.7`; the scorer clears that bar before the Pass-3
      drop rule is activated (the evidence gate).
- [ ] Pass-3: deterministic novelty score; drop iff novelty ≥ `T_novel` AND priority < floor;
      carryover → normal threshold; novel high-priority → preserved; dropped → sidecar.
- [ ] Defaults committed: `T_novel = 0.7` and the priority floor at the stated corpus
      percentile (config-overridable); the distribution script prints the inputs.
- [ ] Remediation-mode gate: config key (**default-OFF** for v1, expand-contract rollout) +
      window minutes (default 60, measured from the last review of any kind and reset each
      review); code-unchanged precondition via `verified_at_sha` equality (prior manifest vs
      current run); both-drifted → full review; key off/absent restores byte-identical full review.
- [ ] Coverage on a narrowed verdict sets `narrowed: true` + `floored_criteria` + floored
      finding ids; dropped novel findings are written to the sidecar.
- [ ] Impact-prompt tightening is verified by the `discriminates_impact_levels` eval scoring
      at or above its threshold on the existing high/low pairs (not an effort claim).
- [ ] Offline FakeRunner tests: convergence on a remediation edit; each precondition fallback
      to a byte-identical full review; novel high-priority preserved; carryover enforced.
- [ ] Docs: a `docs/plan-review-gate.md` section AND an ADR under `docs/adr/` recording the
      chosen design, the three rejected alternatives, and the invariants (Pass-1 unanchored;
      novelty in a separate Pass-2 sub-call; drop decision deterministic in Pass-3).
- [ ] A remediation re-review (pure plan edit, code unchanged, within window) runs the full
- [ ] Severity/validity independence is enforced structurally (novelty in a separate Pass-2
- [ ] Any precondition failing → byte-identical full review; `drift_refresh` behavior unchanged.

## Out of scope / explicitly deferred

- Any change to the code-drift `drift_refresh` path.
- A `max_consecutive_narrowed_rounds` cap on within-session suppression (optional future
  safety valve; the chosen design accepts unbounded within-session suppression while the
  agent is actively iterating).
baseline.summary: Convergent plan-edit re-review: full-run + deterministic rising floor

baseline.description:
## Why
LangChain/LangGraph is heavy (~80-110 deps) and its sole original justification (native Langfuse tracing) is obsolete. Pydantic AI is provider-agnostic (the cross-provider hard requirement) at ~half the deps. Validated by docs/experiments/workflow-remediation-pocs/runtime_pydanticai_poc.py.

## What
Implement a PydanticAIRunner behind the existing Runner protocol: single-turn LLM calls AND tool-using agents with filesystem + MCP (stdio/http) + custom rebar-operation tools; no per-provider code (provider chosen by config/model string). Keep FakeRunner. Parallel-run-and-diff against LangGraphRunner on the corpuses before any cutover.

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/runner.py (PydanticAIRunner behind the Runner seam)
- pyproject.toml [agents] (add pydantic-ai-slim extras)
Out: dropping LangGraph (separate story); the structured-output stack (separate story).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] PydanticAIRunner implements run/preflight behind the Runner seam; FakeRunner unaffected.
- [ ] Tools wired: filesystem, MCP (stdio + http), and custom rebar-op tools.
- [ ] No per-provider code; provider selected via config/model string (Anthropic primary).
- [ ] Parallel-run-and-diff vs LangGraphRunner meets the DEFINED PARITY BAR on the corpuses before any cutover. Parity = NON-INFERIORITY, not byte-identity (outputs are LLM-driven, so exact equality is incoherent). On the standing eval corpus (DSO + snap + rebar tickets), same model + decoding params, N>=3 repeats: (a) structured-output validity v2 >= v1 (target >=99% valid parses, no regression); (b) per-criterion verdict agreement >= 95% AND zero decision-level flips (block/advisory/dropped) on the gold set; (c) recall and false-accept each within +/-2pp of v1 (non-inferiority margin, paired test); (d) runtime error/timeout rate v2 <= v1; (e) cost/latency recorded (informational, non-gating). The LangGraph drop (d6d1) is blocked until this bar is met.
baseline.summary: Provider-agnostic Pydantic AI runtime behind the Runner seam

baseline.description:
## Why
The plan-v2 impact model floors four failure-mode axes at 0.85 (above every blocking threshold) whenever the axis is non-none at ANY grade - the floor is grade-blind. Calibration 3 (task relishable-ammonitic-hoverfly; evidence comment on this story, 2026-07-15) measured the consequence on the plan-v2 segment: 35.5% of ALL blocking findings (807/2271) are floor-driven (would not block without the override), ac_unverifiable alone is 48.9% of the floor-driven set, 52/100 of a classified sample fired at grade=low, and the oracle-kind classification split 56% underspecified_oracle / 37% broken-oracle-shaped / 7% missing_oracle. The dominant floor-driven class is "a check exists, the plan just doesn't spell out the exact command/file/value" - a refinement demand that today auto-blocks with the same force as a genuinely untestable criterion. This story splits the axis so severity follows the actual defect.

## What
Replace the binary-ish ac_unverifiable severity grading with a THREE-value oracle-kind grade in the plan-review verification model, assigned explicitly by the pass-2 verifier (the calibration-3 evidence motivates three, not two - a broken oracle is not a refinement):
- missing_oracle: no verification method exists or could exist as the criterion is phrased (7% of sample) - KEEPS the 0.85 hard floor.
- broken_oracle: a stated proving command/symbol/count is factually wrong - nonexistent path, wrong CLI, contradictory assertion - so the stated verification CANNOT pass (37% of sample) - KEEPS the 0.85 hard floor (the check is protective; these are real plan defects).
- underspecified_oracle: a check exists or is clearly constructible; the finding demands the exact command/file/expected value (56% of sample) - scores BELOW the lowest blocking threshold in force after calibration 3 (0.60), i.e. maps to an impact contribution <= 0.55, so it surfaces and is coached but never auto-blocks.
BOTH verifier prompts define the three grades with one worked example each drawn from the calibration-3 classified sample (the gate YAML routes to TWO prompt files: src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier.md AND plan_review_verifier_agentic.md - both change in lockstep). SCORING MECHANICS (exact decide.py change): impact_plan currently scores all seven axes through the shared ordinal map _SEV01 ({none,low,medium,high}) in TWO generic loops - the contribs list comprehension over _PLAN_SEVERITY_AXES and the has_override any() over _PLAN_HARD_OVERRIDE_AXES. ac_unverifiable is REMOVED from both generic loops and special-cased: (1) contribs = [_SEV01.get(attrs.get(a), 0.0) for a in _PLAN_SEVERITY_AXES if a != "ac_unverifiable"] + [ORACLE_GRADE01.get(attrs.get("ac_unverifiable"), 0.0)]; (2) has_override = any(_SEV01.get(attrs.get(a), 0.0) > 0.0 for a in _PLAN_HARD_OVERRIDE_AXES if a != "ac_unverifiable") or attrs.get("ac_unverifiable") in ("broken_oracle", "missing_oracle"). ORACLE_GRADE01 = {"none": 0.0, "underspecified_oracle": UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB, "broken_oracle": 1.0, "missing_oracle": 1.0} with UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB = 0.55 defined as a named module constant whose comment states its invariant (strictly below the lowest blocking threshold in criteria_routing.json), and a unit test asserts UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB < min(block_threshold over blocking-posture criteria) so a future threshold recalibration below 0.55 fails loudly instead of silently re-enabling blocks. An unknown/legacy grade string maps to 0.0 via .get() default in plan-v3 scoring - legacy records are never scored with plan-v3 code anyway (segmentation, below). The other six axes keep _SEV01 and the any-non-none override unchanged. WRITE-TIME ENFORCEMENT (the concrete mechanism): src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py owns PlanSeverityAttrs; its ac_unverifiable field changes from the ordinal type to Literal["none", "underspecified_oracle", "broken_oracle", "missing_oracle"], so Pydantic strict validation rejects out-of-vocabulary grades at verification-parse time - that field is the closed-set gate the ACs pin. OPERATOR-ATTESTED ENRICH: workflow_ops.enrich_operator_attested's guard changes from `not in (None, "", "none")` to the explicit clearable set `in ("missing_oracle", "underspecified_oracle")` (clears to "none" when attested evidence satisfies the criterion - the recorded attestation IS the oracle) while broken_oracle is never cleared (a factually wrong stated command is not cured by an attestation) - this file is in Scope and the asymmetry is pinned by test. BACK-COMPAT: the closed-set validation applies to NEW plan-v3 verifications at parse time; already-stored plan-v2 sidecars keep their legacy {low,medium,high} grades and are read as-is - every calibration/replay consumer segments by impact_model_version (ADR 0036), so old records are never scored with new semantics - and this is pinned by a TEST (a plan-v2 fixture sidecar with grade "low" round-trips unmodified through latest_review_result/all_review_results). The sidecar SCHEMA id stays plan_review_result_v2: the payload shape (keys, nesting) is unchanged - only the value vocabulary of one severity-attribute field changes - so the schema-string guard in the readers keeps matching; IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION (plan-v3) is the segmentation key for the semantics change. ROLLBACK: the version bump makes back-out clean - reverting the change restores plan-v2 semantics and the corpora stay segmented; no expand-contract migration is needed because sidecars are immutable records, not migrated state. IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION bumps plan-v2 -> plan-v3 in the same change. The other three override axes (dod_uncertifiable, undecomposed, divergent_implementation) keep their ordinal vocabulary and any-non-none floor, untouched in this story (their grade mix is unmeasured; calibration 4 scope).

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py: ORACLE_GRADE01 + UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB constants; ac_unverifiable excluded from both generic _SEV01 loops and special-cased per the exact change spec above.
- src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py: PlanSeverityAttrs.ac_unverifiable becomes the closed Literal grade type (the write-time enforcement mechanism).
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py: enrich_operator_attested vocabulary update (clears missing/underspecified on attestation, never broken_oracle).
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier.md AND plan_review_verifier_agentic.md: three-grade definitions + one worked example each; the plan-review verification output schema accepts exactly {none, underspecified_oracle, broken_oracle, missing_oracle} for the axis and rejects anything else at write time.
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py: IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION bump to plan-v3; the grade persists in verification.severity_attributes as today (values change, key stays).
- Unit tests: tests/unit/test_impact_plan.py (replace old low/medium/high ac_unverifiable pins with the three-grade pins; keep other-axis pins), tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py (plan-v2 -> plan-v3 assertion), tests/unit/_audit_page_helpers.py (hardcoded plan-v2 string updated), new pins for: schema acceptance AND rejection of an invalid grade, sidecar persistence, the enrich asymmetry, the UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB < min(blocking thresholds) invariant, and the plan-v2 legacy-fixture read-as-is round-trip.
- docs/plan-review-gate.md: the floor description updated to the graded rule with the back-compat note.
- Coordination: story ea39 (R5 kernel sub-answer, epic pastoral-aquatic-viper) also plans a version bump and depends_on this story - if both land close together the bumps compose (v3 then v4), never merge into one ambiguous version.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The verification model accepts exactly the closed grade set {none, underspecified_oracle, broken_oracle, missing_oracle} for ac_unverifiable on new plan-v3 verifications - pinned by BOTH an acceptance test and a rejection test for an out-of-vocabulary grade - and both verifier prompts (single-turn + agentic) define each grade with one worked example.
- [ ] Impact scoring pinned by unit tests: missing_oracle and broken_oracle findings floor at >= 0.85; underspecified_oracle findings score <= 0.55 (below the 0.60 lowest blocking threshold) and never trigger the hard floor; the other three override axes floor unchanged.
- [ ] IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION is plan-v3 in the same change (test_impact_model_versioning.py updated), the grade persists per finding in the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar (pinned by test), legacy plan-v2 records are read as-is (segmentation by version is the back-compat mechanism, asserted in the doc note), and enrich_operator_attested clears missing/underspecified but never broken_oracle (pinned by test).
- [ ] docs/plan-review-gate.md documents the three-grade rule citing the calibration-3 evidence comment on this story, and the change is MERGED through Gerrit (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
baseline.summary: Split ac_unverifiable hard-floor axis into oracle-kind grades: missing/broken keep the floor, underspecified demotes (plan-v3)

## Context
The current-main macOS census attributes 250.81 worker-phase seconds to external analyzer/grounding tests, with individual phases up to 15.62s. Multiple modules launch real OpenGrep, ast-grep, gitleaks, and metric scans. Reusing immutable scan results or retaining one real boundary per behavior could reduce repeated tool startup and traversal, but the evidence is not yet sufficient to remove or mock any real boundary.

Tracker guard: shockproof-twill-porpoise proves tool presence/absence and explicit coverage accounting are contractual. crushable-choosable-llama retains real scanner/process integration. OSS practice is mixed: pip and pytest reuse expensive session fixtures, while Semgrep retains real CLI snapshot E2E tests marked kinda_slow. No automatic OSS-consensus approval exists yet.

## Plan
- Inventory every >=1s analyzer node, the exact binary invocation, fixture tree, detector/backend, and unique failure mode.
- Build a fault-seeded equivalence matrix for discovery, rule loading, timeout, invalid output, tool absent, tool present, SARIF/evidence normalization, and consumer fail-open/fail-closed behavior.
- Measure candidates that share immutable fixture trees or scan results while retaining at least one real invocation for each external boundary and environment state.
- Compare matched before/after timings and retained failure-mode detection with maintained OSS examples.
- Recommend implement/keep only after every removed invocation has equivalent behavioral and contractual detection.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every affected real-tool invocation maps to a unique failure mode; checked against collected node IDs, subprocess call sites, fixtures, and CI workflow selectors.
- [ ] Every affected real-tool invocation maps to a faster overlapping oracle when one exists; checked in the fault-seeded equivalence matrix.
- [ ] Tool-present behavior remains explicit; checked against the current test and subprocess contract.
- [ ] Tool-absent behavior remains explicit; checked against the current test and subprocess contract.
- [ ] Timeout behavior remains explicit; checked against the current test and subprocess contract.
- [ ] Invalid-output behavior remains explicit; checked against the current test and subprocess contract.
- [ ] Rule-discovery behavior remains explicit; checked against the current test and subprocess contract.
- [ ] Evidence-accounting behavior remains explicit; checked against the current test and subprocess contract.
- [ ] Each reachable failure class has an exact-defect seed and a current detecting oracle recorded in the matrix.
- [ ] Each proposed retained set has an exact-defect detecting oracle recorded for every reachable failure class.
- [ ] Matched macOS wall-time savings are measured with repeated pytest runs of the same collected nodes.
- [ ] Aggregate runner savings are calculated from the matched measurements and current CI matrix.
- [ ] Ticket-history evidence is cited by ticket alias.
- [ ] At least three maintained OSS projects are cited with exact repository paths or URLs and the comparable practice.
- [ ] No production code or test files change; checked with `git diff --exit-code`.
- [ ] No scanner invocation is removed or mocked.

## Verification
- Collect the relevant node set with `pytest --collect-only -q` plus repository search of subprocess and backend call sites.
- Run matched selected-node timing samples with `pytest -vv --durations=0` using the worktree virtualenv.
- Run existing focused tests that exercise each fault class and record exact node outcomes in the matrix.
- Confirm the research worktree remains unchanged with `git status --short` and `git diff --exit-code`.
baseline.summary: Prove grounding scan reuse preserves real analyzer boundary coverage

## What

Add a tickets-branch `.gitattributes` declaring `merge=ours` for the per-pass mutable shared-root files so the union merge introduced in WU-2 never wedges on them. uuid-named ticket dirs never collide; only `.bridge_state/bindings.json` and the reconciler lock/gate files are rewritten every pass and would conflict. The loser is a derived cache the reconciler rebuilds next pass — never ticket events. `merge=union` is WRONG here (it line-unions JSON into invalid JSON).

This formalises behaviour `push.py` already handles ad hoc today, so it is a safe standalone change and lands before WU-2 so the merge is conflict-free by construction.

## Scope (files)

- Tickets-branch `.gitattributes` (written/ensured at init): 
  `.bridge_state/* merge=ours` and `.reconciler-* merge=ours`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py`: ensure the `.gitattributes` is created/maintained
  idempotently on the tickets branch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Tickets-branch `.gitattributes` ships `merge=ours` for `.bridge_state/*` and `.reconciler-*`
- [ ] `.gitattributes` is created idempotently at init (re-runnable)
- [ ] `merge=union` is NOT used (would corrupt JSON)
- [ ] Convergence test: two clones each rewriting `bindings.json` merge without a wedge
- [ ] Full non-integration suite green
baseline.summary: WU-3: .gitattributes merge=ours for shared mutable root files

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

A plan review that trips a provider context limit escalates the Pass-1 finder onto a model the run was never configured for. On a run whose model is provider-qualified for anything other than the provider inferred from the model NAME — a Bedrock deployment being the live case — the recovery path silently relocates the call to direct Anthropic: a hard failure in a provider-isolated container, or unbudgeted spend wherever an Anthropic key happens to exist. This is the founding defect of epic 061c on a second, independent code path: the ENTRY rung was routed through the model-class vocabulary, the ESCALATION rungs were not.

Confirmed by running the function on this tree with no class table configured:

    models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0")
      -> ["claude-opus-4-8"]        # bare, direct-Anthropic-inferring

## Root cause

`_rung_target` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py:332-359`) decides a rung's escalation target by comparing the RUNG's own provider-inferred form against that rung's class resolution:

    resolved = resolve_model_string(class_name)       # sizing.py:354
    provider = infer_provider(bare)                   # sizing.py:355
    own = f"{provider}:{bare}" if provider else bare  # sizing.py:356
    return bare if resolved == own else resolved      # sizing.py:357

Both sides of that comparison are derived from the ladder constant. **The model the run is actually on is never an input.** So whenever the class table has not been retargeted the equality holds and the rung degrades to `MODEL_LADDER`'s bare Anthropic family name (`sizing.py:99-103`), discarding whatever provider qualifier `cfg.model` carried. `models_at_or_above` (`sizing.py:362-376`) hands those targets to the escalation loop, which assigns them straight onto the run config at `sizing.py:427-431`:

    for model in models_at_or_above(cfg.model):
        passes.pass1_chunk(runner, replace(cfg, model=model), ...)

Two consequences, both reproduced against the current tree:

1. A Bedrock-qualified primary escalates to a bare Anthropic id (transcript above).
   `cfg.model_provider` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:391`) is left untouched by `replace`, so a run
   that qualified through that field instead composes an id like `bedrock:claude-opus-4-8`,
   which is not a valid Bedrock model id.
2. The Pass-1 entry rung names `frontier` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:76`, resolved
   at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py:97-100`), so
   `models_at_or_above("anthropic:claude-opus-4-8")` returns the single-element list
   `["claude-opus-4-8"]`. The substitution therefore executes on the COMMON one-criterion retry,
   before any escalation is needed — it is not confined to a rare deep-escalation case.

When a class table IS configured for another provider the current code is already correct (`models_at_or_above` returns the Bedrock ladder, asserted at `tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py:204-212`). The live gap is the UNCONFIGURED-table plus provider-qualified-`cfg.model` combination, which no test covers.

## Approach

Make the rung target a function of the model the run is on, and make the unnameable case fail SAFE instead of crossing providers.

`models_at_or_above` already holds the primary, so thread it into `_rung_target`. Resolve the rung through its model class exactly as today, then compare the RUN's provider (`infer_provider(primary)`) with the TARGET's provider (`infer_provider(target)`):

- providers agree, or either is undeterminable -> return today's value byte-for-byte;
- providers differ and the rung is the PRIMARY's OWN rung -> return `primary` verbatim, so the
  same-model one-criterion retry still runs on the operator's model (that retry is the step that
  most often succeeds, since one criterion is a far smaller prompt than the batch);
- providers differ on a HIGHER rung -> drop the rung. The class vocabulary is the only thing
  that can name that rung in the run's provider and it has not been configured, so there is no
  honest target. Escalation stops and the existing too-big failure finding
  (`sizing.py:450-471`) reports it — a visible outcome instead of a silent provider jump.

The rule applies only on the branch that LOCATED a start rung (`sizing.py:373-375`). The no-match fallback (`sizing.py:376`) is left exactly as today, because without a located start rung there is no "primary's own rung" to preserve; see Scope for why that branch is out of scope.

Why this approach fits: the defect is that a decision about the CURRENT run is made from module constants alone, so the fix is to give the decision the run's model — the smallest input that makes the question answerable. It keeps the model-class vocabulary as the single source of escalation targets (the epic's rule) while preserving the byte-for-byte back-compat that the docstring at `sizing.py:335-347` exists to protect, so no existing caller's strings change.

Deliberately NOT changed: on an unqualified or Anthropic-qualified primary the target stays the bare form (`anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` -> `claude-opus-4-8`). That substitution is byte-different but provider-identical. The harm was never the bare FORM; it was the provider CHANGE, and the provider-agreement rule is what removes that. Preserving the bare form is the back-compat contract that keeps `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:1145-1150` and `tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py:256-271` passing unmodified.

`MODEL_LADDER` also keeps its bare family names. It carries two roles and only one moves: it is also the WINDOW table that `largest_window_tokens` (`sizing.py:137-146`) reads by substring match (`if name in model`), which is why `sizing.py:319-324` records that class names in that table would make every window lookup miss. Escalation TARGETS move to the class vocabulary; escalation WINDOWS stay keyed on concrete model families. That separates the two orderings the constant conflates without splitting the constant.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py` — `_rung_target` takes the primary model as an argument
  and applies the provider-agreement rule; `models_at_or_above` passes it on the located-start-rung
  branch. No other function in the file changes.
- `tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py` — new cases (see Testing). This is the existing home of
  the ladder's model-class contract, holding both the byte-for-byte control (lines 256-271) and
  the configured-Bedrock case (lines 204-212) this change must not disturb.

Explicitly OUT of scope, to be raised as a separate ticket: `models_at_or_above` locates the START rung by substring-matching `MODEL_LADDER`'s Anthropic family names against the primary (`sizing.py:373-374`), so a primary from another model family falls through to the whole ladder beginning at the trivial rung — confirmed on this tree: `models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0")` returns all three Anthropic rungs, so a context-limit escalation would DOWNGRADE the window. `largest_window_tokens` has the matching gap, returning the ladder maximum (1,000,000) for that same primary. That is a different mechanism — rung LOCATION, not rung TARGET — and this change leaves it byte-for-byte as it is.

## Testing

New cases in `tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py`, using its existing `no_classes` and `_set_class_table` fixtures.

- **The defect, on the escalation path itself** — not on `models_at_or_above` in isolation. Drive
  `sizing.pass1_with_ladder` with a stub runner whose first (batch) call raises a context-limit
  error (`is_context_limit_error`, `sizing.py:300-316`, matches the substring
  `"prompt is too long"`) and a `cfg` whose model is `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0`
  with no class table. Assert the `cfg.model` observed by the one-criterion retry call is that
  exact string. This is the case an entry-rung test structurally cannot catch, which is why the
  defect survived the entry-rung fix.
- **Worked example, unit level** — with no class table:
  `models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0")` returns
  `["bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0"]`. Today it returns `["claude-opus-4-8"]`.
- **Edge, higher rungs are dropped rather than crossed** — with no class table:
  `models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-v1:0")` returns exactly
  `["bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-v1:0"]`, and no returned element contains
  `claude-sonnet` or `claude-opus`.
- **Edge, escalation still reports the size failure** — the same Bedrock-haiku primary under a
  runner that raises a context-limit error at every attempt still yields the existing `_too_big`
  failure finding (`sizing.py:450-471`) rather than an empty result or a raised exception.
- **Back-compat controls, kept passing unmodified** — the byte-for-byte case
  (`tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py:256-271`, covering bare rungs, `None`, and
  `"some-unknown-model"`), the order case (lines 275-299), the configured-Bedrock case
  (lines 204-212), and `orchestrator._models_at_or_above`'s literal assertions
  (`tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:1145-1150`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With no model-class table configured and a primary of
      `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0`, the model that reaches `passes.pass1_chunk` on
      the one-criterion retry is that same string; verified by the new `pass1_with_ladder` test
      asserting the observed `cfg.model`, which fails against the current tree.
- [ ] No escalation target is returned whose inferred provider differs from the primary's
      inferred provider when both are determinable; verified by a test asserting
      `models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-v1:0")` equals
      `["bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-v1:0"]` under the `no_classes` fixture.
- [ ] Dropping unnameable higher rungs does not turn escalation into a crash or a silent empty
      result: the all-attempts-fail case still produces the `_too_big` failure finding; verified
      by the new failure-path test asserting `finding["_too_big"] is True`.
- [ ] Escalation targets still come from the model-class vocabulary when a class table IS
      configured; verified by `test_models_at_or_above_stays_on_bedrock_for_a_bedrock_primary`
      (`tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py:204`) passing unmodified.
- [ ] The window sizes that drive the escalation DECISION are unchanged; verified by `git diff`
      showing no change to `MODEL_LADDER` (`sizing.py:99-103`) or `largest_window_tokens`
      (`sizing.py:137-146`).
- [ ] Back-compat: with no class table configured, every escalation target for an unqualified or
      Anthropic-qualified primary is today's value byte-for-byte, including the
      `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` common path that yields bare `claude-opus-4-8`; verified by
      `test_models_at_or_above_returns_todays_bare_ids_with_no_classes_configured` and
      `test_models_at_or_above_escalation_order_is_unchanged` passing unmodified.
- [ ] The out-of-scope start-rung behaviour is untouched:
      `models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0")` still returns the three bare
      Anthropic rungs; verified by a pinning test asserting that exact list.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py tests/unit/test_plan_review.py
      tests/unit/workflow/test_pass1_usage.py tests/unit/test_llm_failure_matrix.py` passes, and
      `make lint` and `make typecheck` are clean.
baseline.summary: Pass-1 context-limit escalation sets a BARE Anthropic model id, bypassing the model-class table

in doing so **dogfood** the newly-merged `github_release` job (ticket
f112-6222-e236-4b09, change 314): pushing the `v0.7.0` tag must now *automatically*

baseline.description:
## Idea (parking lot — out of scope for the code-health analyzer epic 839b-f6d2)
Add a polyglot **dependency-graph** capability to the code-health analyzer (module/file coupling, fan-in/fan-out, cycles) so a per-project graph signal can feed the metrics registry.

## Why it's a separate idea, not part of the epic
The portability audit found there is **no mature, single, drop-in polyglot dependency-graph OSS CLI** (unlike LOC/complexity/duplication, which scc/lizard/jscpd cover). Realistic paths, all heavier:
- Per-language adapters behind the analyzer seam: dependency-cruiser / madge (JS/TS), pydeps (Python), `go mod graph` (Go), jdeps (Java).
- Polyglot foundations to build on (frameworks, not turnkey): tree-sitter + GitHub stack-graphs, or Sourcegraph SCIP indexers; heavyweight end: CodeQL.

## Open questions (to design before promoting out of idea)
- Which graph signals are worth a metric (cycle count? max coupling? fan-in hotspots?) and are they cross-language comparable?
- Single polyglot foundation (tree-sitter/SCIP) vs. a registry of per-language adapters with honest Unavailable where none exists?
- Cost/determinism/CI-time budget vs. value.

Treat as future work; do not block the scc/lizard/jscpd epic on it.
baseline.summary: Polyglot dependency-graph analyzer capability for code-health metrics

## Scope

- Verify end state: two real workflows (plan-review, completion-verification) + the retained
  `review_skeleton.yaml` sample; no orphaned references.
- Depends on B5 (cutover complete, so the bespoke samples are truly unused).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `examples/code_review.yaml` and `templates.py` are removed; any still-referenced surface

      references to the removed files remain (grep-clean).
- [ ] End state confirmed: exactly two real LLM workflows (plan-review, completion-verification) +
      the one retained sample.
- [ ] `make lint` + the full test suite pass.

baseline.description:
## The defect

The `Git version floor gate` step added by ticket 980d-83ac-a6bb-4edb (merged as c433663721) reads `.github/git-version-floor.txt` from the CHECKED-OUT PATCHSET TREE and errors when the file is absent:

    ::error::missing <floorfile> (the single source of the Git version floor)

But the Gerrit `Verified` lane runs the WORKFLOW DEFINITION FROM `main`, not from the patchset -- 980d documented this itself as a caveat about its own gate not self-testing. The two facts combine badly:

  workflow (from main)     -> HAS the new gate step
  tree     (from patchset) -> may NOT have the floor file

Any change branched before 980d merged gets the gate but not its data file, and fails hard.

## Confirmed instance

Change 1416 (ticket fd30-a088-cbbc-4dbd): LLM-Review +1, Verified -1 from run 30978915944 with 4/4 pytest legs failing (ubuntu py3.11/3.12/3.13, macos py3.13). Verified directly: `git ls-tree FETCH_HEAD .github/` on patchset 1 lists `module-size-limit.txt` but NOT `git-version-floor.txt`. The change is unrelated to Git versions -- it edits the Makefile and docs -- and its author had run the full suite green locally (10234 passed).

## Blast radius

Every open change branched before c433663721 merged. At filing there were 6 open changes; 1408/1410/1411 already carry Verified +1 from runs that PREDATE the gate, so those green votes no longer reflect what a re-run would produce -- a `recheck` on any of them should be expected to flip to -1.

Same shape as bug 3787-9749-f8a6-41bb ("Rebase-If-Necessary submits a tree CI never validated"): a mismatch between the tree CI evaluates and the tree that will land. Worth considering whether the two share a fix.

## Candidate resolutions (weigh these; not prescribed)

1. Treat an absent floor file as "no floor declared" and PASS, so the gate enforces only once
   the file exists in the tree under test -- fail-open on absence, fail-closed on an actual
   under-floor git. Cheapest, and self-heals as changes rebase.
2. Read the floor from the workflow's own checkout so the gate's data travels with the gate.
3. Accept it and require every in-flight change to rebase -- viable, but it silently taxes
   every author and the message does not name rebasing as the remedy.

Whichever is chosen, the diagnostic must name the actual cause. "missing <floorfile>" sends an author hunting for a file they never touched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A change branched BEFORE the gate landed, with no Git-version-related edits, passes CI
      without being rebased -- proven RED-first against the current gate.
- [x] A genuinely under-floor git still fails, with the diagnostic naming required version,
      installed version and upgrade path (980d's behavior preserved, not weakened).
- [x] The missing-floor-file failure message names the real remedy, not just the filename.
- [x] Behavior is verified BOTH on a patchset tree lacking the file and one having it, since
      the workflow-from-main / tree-from-patchset split makes these different cases.

## Provenance

Found when change 1416 took an unexplained Verified -1 about an hour after 980d merged. 980d's own report flagged that its gate "did not itself execute on this change ... it takes effect from the next change onward" -- 1416 was that next change, and the effect was a false failure.


## Chosen fix (resolution 1, per the repo's own mandate)

Option 1 (treat an absent floor file as "no floor declared in this tree" and skip) is not merely the cheapest -- it is the pattern this repository already MANDATES for exactly this hazard. `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` documents the "Definition-vs-tree skew guard (ticket ee2a)" and states verbatim:

    New gate steps that run a repo script must copy this if-present guard: skip (with a log
    line) when the script is absent from the checked-out tree; the gate re-enforces on rebase
    and on every post-merge change.

Two adjacent steps already implement it (`raw-git-write gate`, `wall-clock-assert gate`). The Git-floor gate simply failed to copy it. So the fix is to apply the established convention, keyed on `.github/git-version-floor.txt`, rather than invent a variant.

Option 2 (read the floor from the workflow's own checkout) is rejected: it would need a second checkout of the target branch inside the gate step, diverging from the house pattern for no benefit, and would make the gate enforce a floor the tree under test never declared. Option 3 (require every author to rebase) is rejected: it taxes every in-flight change for a defect they did not introduce.

### Design decisions

- DD1: replace the hard `exit 1` on a missing floor file with a skip that logs WHY it
  skipped -- naming the tree-skew cause and that the gate re-enforces on rebase / post-merge
  -- so the log names the real remedy instead of sending an author hunting for a file they
  never touched (AC 3).
- DD2: preserve 980d's enforcement verbatim for every OTHER path. When the floor file IS
  present, the parse, the comparison, and the under-floor diagnostic (required version,
  installed version, per-platform upgrade path) are unchanged (AC 2).
- DD3: leave `tests/conftest.py`'s `pytest_configure` session-abort and `tests/_git_floor.py`
  untouched -- the contributor-side floor enforcement is a separate consumer and is not
  weakened.
- DD4: prove the behavior by EXECUTING the real step. A new test extracts the `Git version
  floor gate` step's `run:` script from the workflow YAML and runs it under bash against
  three fixtures: a tree lacking the floor file (must exit 0 and log the skip reason), a tree
  having it (must enforce and pass on an adequate git), and a tree having it under a stubbed
  under-floor git (must exit 1 with the full diagnostic). This covers AC 4's requirement that
  BOTH tree cases be verified, since the workflow-from-main / tree-from-patchset split makes
  them genuinely different cases.

### Blast radius

One non-test file: `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`, one step. Plus one new test file. No src/rebar change. The gate step is CI-only; the other floor consumers read the file directly and are unaffected. The existing pins `test_ci_reads_the_floor_from_the_single_source` and `test_consumers_declare_the_same_floor` continue to hold.
baseline.summary: The new Git-floor CI gate hard-fails every in-flight change branched before it merged

## Why

`compact.emit_legacy_signature_mirror` (default False) is the CONTRACT-phase rollback lever of the additive-attestations rollout (epic dark-acme-lumen). Its default already means "never emit the legacy `state['signature']` mirror into new snapshots" — so removing it does NOT change runtime behavior. What removal deletes is the documented one-line ROLLBACK (`= true` + recompact) that re-emits the mirror for a still-live pre-attestations reader. Approved for removal; this story does it responsibly.

## What

- Remove the field + validator from `CompactConfig` (`_config_schema.py:367` and the
  parser entry in the `compact` section, `~:515`).
- Hardcode never-emit in `_snapshot_strip_keys` (`_commands/compact.py:127-136`):
  always add `"signature"` to the dropped-keys set; delete the `emit_legacy_mirror`
  branch.
- PRESERVE the in-memory mirror path: `process_signature` re-deriving `state["signature"]`
  during replay (`reducer/_processors.py:562-604`) and the `most_recent_attestation`
  fallback (`signing.py:563-568`) stay — this story only stops PERSISTING the mirror
  into new snapshots; it does not touch the in-memory back-compat projection.
- Doc-sweep coordination: the doc-sweep story removes references; this story updates
  `docs/migrations.md` "Legacy signature-mirror retirement" to record the retirement
  and that the rollback lever is gone.

## Scope — the one-way door (handle, don't skip)

Backward-compat verdict (from assessment): CONDITIONAL. Removal is a ONE-WAY DOOR. It is safe for THIS fleet (hourly auto-update to origin/main ⇒ no pre-attestations binary is live). It WOULD break an external project on older rebar that reads a mirror-less snapshot whose latest signature was compacted below the horizon (the reader sees no `signature`, cannot read `attestations`, and the SIGNATURE event is gone) — after removal the only recovery is a code downgrade, not a config flip.

Therefore, before landing: assert the readiness gate (`docs/migrations.md:149-156`) holds — no pre-attestations clone/reconcile-host shares this store — and record the one-way-door retirement in the release notes so any downstream consumer is warned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `emit_legacy_signature_mirror` removed from schema, parser, and `rebar.toml` (if present); new snapshots never persist the `signature` mirror.
- [ ] `process_signature` in-memory mirror + `most_recent_attestation` fallback are UNCHANGED (prove with existing signing/replay tests green).
- [ ] [operator-attested] Readiness gate asserted: no pre-attestations rebar binary reads this store (state the basis — e.g. fleet auto-update policy).
- [ ] `docs/migrations.md` "Legacy signature-mirror retirement" updated to record the retirement and removal of the rollback lever; release notes warn downstream consumers of the one-way door.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: Retire compact.emit_legacy_signature_mirror (hardcode never-emit) after readiness-gate check

baseline.description:
## Why

Project "invariants" = deterministic pattern-rule criteria (banned APIs, layering, naming). The
consumer already exists: `code_review/detectors.py` calls the shared `grounding.engine_b.scan` +
`load_registry` (which already unions `.rebar/detectors/`) + `apply_failclosed`. But it is
hardcoded to the `rebar.builtin.security.` prefix + 2 criterion mappings and is fail-CLOSED. This
story generalizes it into a data-driven, per-criterion-`fail_mode` consumer usable by any project
invariant, in both gates.

## What

- Generalize the detector→criterion mapping: a data-driven `criterion↔detector` map (drop the
  hardcoded `rebar.builtin.security.` prefix) so arbitrary `.rebar/detectors/` rules route to an
  activated DET criterion.
- Per-criterion `fail_mode: open|closed` on the routing record (default `open` for project
  invariants; `closed` for the built-in security class). The ORACLE stays fail-open (abstain on
  absent-binary/parse-error/timeout); the CONSUMER applies `fail_mode` — `open` → skip=PASS,
  `closed` → BLOCK (the existing `apply_failclosed` path). One code path parameterized by
  `fail_mode`, not two behaviors.
- DET fallback descriptor shape (a `_descriptor_from_prompt` DET branch that skips `get_prompt`):
  `name`=routing name/id, `scenario`=detector rule `message`, `facet`=routing facet (default id),
  `checklist`=empty. Expand-contract (prompt-backed callers unaffected).
- Expose the generalized consumer to **plan-review** (which calls no scan consumer today — only
  `refute_absence` in `det_floor.py`); matches are gate-scoped (code-review: diff; plan-review:
  plan/N-A).

## Scope

- Files: `src/rebar/llm/code_review/detectors.py` (generalize), `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/`
  (new DET-invariant consumer wiring), `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py` (DET descriptor
  branch + `fail_mode`), the routing schema.
- Depends on story `#1` (registry/overlay/activation). Reuses the shared grounding facade
  (already unions `.rebar/detectors/`) — no new oracle work.
- Out: graph-level invariants (transitive layering/cycles) — a later follow-on, not a new DSL.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The scan consumer is data-driven (no hardcoded `rebar.builtin.security.` prefix); an
      activated project DET invariant routes its `.rebar/detectors/` rule and surfaces findings.
- [ ] Per-criterion `fail_mode` honored: project invariants default fail-open (abstain→skip=PASS);
      the security class stays fail-closed (abstain→BLOCK) via the existing `apply_failclosed`.
- [ ] DET criteria build a descriptor without a prompt (the DET `_descriptor_from_prompt` branch).
- [ ] The generalized consumer is wired into plan-review as well as code-review; matches are
      gate-scoped (diff for code-review; plan/N-A for plan-review).
- [ ] Fail-open is preserved on engine-binary-absent / parse-error / timeout for `fail_mode:open`.


## Plan-review consumer integration (remediation, run 1)

### Match-scoping without a diff (clears G6 blocker 1)
Plan-review has no diff, so a project DET invariant is scoped to the ticket's DECLARED intent +
its `file_impact` paths (from the ticket state), NOT a whole-repo scan surfaced as new work:
- If the ticket declares `file_impact` paths, the consumer scopes matches to THOSE paths (the
  files this plan intends to touch) — the plan-time analog of code-review's `changed_files`
  diff-scope. A match in a declared file surfaces as a finding.
- If there is no `file_impact`, the DET invariant is advisory-only over the repo context (it
  cannot pin the match to this plan's change), never a hard block on a pre-existing whole-repo
  violation — this is why NO baseline/grandfathering is needed (pre-existing violations outside
  the plan's declared files are not surfaced as new work).
- An invariant that INHERENTLY needs a diff (e.g. "no new call to X") is **N/A at plan time
  (fail-open)** and belongs to code-review. So plan-time DET scoping ∈ {file_impact-scoped,
  advisory-repo-context, N-A-fail-open} — never an unscoped whole-repo block.

### Integration point (clears G6 blocker 2)
The generalized consumer runs as an ADDITIONAL DET check appended into `det_floor.run_det_floor`
(alongside P1–P9), returning `DetResult`-shaped results (`id=<project criterion id>`, `name=<detector
rule message>`, `status`, `blocking`, `finding`, `coverage`). Project-invariant results therefore
flow UNCHANGED through the existing partition in `workflow_ops.plan_review_precheck`
(`det_blocking_findings` / `det_advisory_findings` / `det_coverage`) → `orchestrator.partition_findings`.
Blocking is gated by the criterion's `fail_mode` + posture: a `fail_mode:open` invariant that abstains
(engine binary absent / parse-error / timeout) → skip=PASS (advisory at most); a `fail_mode:closed`
(security class) abstain → BLOCK (the existing `apply_failclosed` path, now parameterized). A `match`
in a declared file blocks per the criterion's `default_posture`/`blocking_enabled`.

### Data-driven map location (clears the hardcoded-prefix AC)
The detector→criterion association + `fail_mode` move INTO `criteria_routing.json` (both gates): a
DET criterion's routing entry carries a `detector` selector (id or id-prefix) + `fail_mode:
open|closed`. `run_security_detectors` (renamed to the general `run_detectors`, a thin back-compat
alias kept) reads the routing map instead of the hardcoded `SECURITY_DETECTOR_PREFIX` /
`_criterion_for`; the security class is just the built-in rows (`fail_mode: closed`) — same code
path, data-driven. `_validate_routing_entry` gains `fail_mode ∈ {open, closed}` validation.

## Acceptance Criteria (remediation additions)

- [ ] Plan-review DET-invariant matches are scoped to the ticket's `file_impact` (or advisory when
      absent) — never an unscoped whole-repo block; a test asserts the scoping.
- [ ] The consumer wires in as a `DetResult`-shaped check via `run_det_floor`, flowing through the
      existing det_blocking/det_advisory/det_coverage partition; `fail_mode` gates abstain→block.


## Static P1–P9 + dynamic project-check phase (remediation, run 2)

`DET_CHECKS` (the static `(p1_readiness_shape, …, p9_file_impact_coverage)` tuple) is UNCHANGED —
the built-in floor stays a fixed constant (expand-contract). `run_det_floor(ctx)` gains a SECOND,
additive phase AFTER the static P1–P9 loop: it discovers the activated `exec: DET` PROJECT criteria
at call time from `ctx.repo_root` (via `registry.effective_criteria(ctx.repo_root)` filtered to
`exec == "DET"` + `project.`-prefixed), and for each runs the generalized scan consumer
(`engine_b.scan` over the criterion's `detector` selector, matches scoped to the ticket's
`file_impact`) → one `DetResult` per criterion, appended to the SAME result list P1–P9 return. A
repo with no activated project DET criterion (the common case) adds zero checks ⇒ byte-identical to
today. The phase is fail-open (a raising project check → `abstain`, logged, per the existing
`run_det_floor` fail-open contract), so a misbehaving project rule never breaks the floor.

## Acceptance Criteria (remediation additions, run 2)

- [ ] `DET_CHECKS` stays static; `run_det_floor` adds a call-time second phase that discovers
      activated `exec: DET` project criteria from `ctx.repo_root` and appends their `DetResult`s.
      A repo with no project DET criterion is byte-identical to today (a test asserts zero added).


## DET-tier isolation, thin-slice sequencing & schema details (remediation, run 4)

### exec:DET criteria never enter the LLM batch (clears G6)
`effective_criteria()` returns activated project ids regardless of tier, so the LLM-routing sites
must FILTER OUT `exec == "DET"`:
- `orchestrator.route_criteria` skips any descriptor whose `exec == "DET"` (they are dispatched to
  the DET consumer, never fanned out as an LLM finder) — the same way `ISF` is already excluded.
- `workflow_ops.plan_review_assemble_criteria`'s `effective` vocabulary excludes `exec == "DET"`
  ids from the `include_<id>` batch fan-out (a DET criterion has no finder prompt to run).
- The exclusion filter reads `str(crit.get('exec','')).upper() == 'DET'` DIRECTLY from the
  descriptor dict — NOT via `registry.exec_tier()`, which has NO DET arm and silently remaps
  DET→1-TURN (so filtering via `exec_tier` would wrongly classify a DET criterion as a
  single-turn finder and admit it to the batch). The routing/descriptor path must never hand
  a DET descriptor to `pass1_chunk`. A DET descriptor is consumed ONLY by the
  `run_det_floor` project-check phase. A test asserts an activated DET project criterion appears in
  the DET-floor results and is ABSENT from the LLM `include_*`/route_criteria set.

### Thin-slice sequencing + coherence (clears G5)
This is ONE architectural seam — "the generalized DET-scan consumer, data-driven + exposed to both
gates" — not four independent features; the files it touches are the single call-graph of that one
consumer. Risk-ordered build (each independently testable, no child tickets needed):
1. **MVP:** promote the detector→criterion map + `fail_mode` into `criteria_routing.json` and make
   `code_review/detectors.py` read it data-drivenly (drop the hardcoded prefix), security class
   preserved fail-closed. Proven by the existing `test_code_review_ws5.py` fail-closed tests.
2. Add the `exec: DET` descriptor branch in `plan_review/registry._descriptor_from_prompt`
   (skip `get_prompt`; rubric = detector rule `message`).
3. Add the `run_det_floor` project-DET phase (file_impact-scoped) + DET-tier isolation from the LLM
   batch.

### Schema + migration details (clears T8/T4/E1/E5 advisories)
- **`detector` selector shape:** each DET routing entry carries `detector: {id?: str, id_prefix?:
  str}` — an exact detector id OR an id-prefix (the security class uses `id_prefix:
  "rebar.builtin.security."`, reproducing today's behaviour data-drivenly). Validated in
  `_validate_routing_entry`.
- **`fail_mode` default is SAFE:** the built-in security rows in the packaged
  `code_review/criteria_routing.json` are written with an EXPLICIT `fail_mode: "closed"` in this
  change, so they can never silently revert to open. A DET routing entry with NO `fail_mode`
  defaults to `"open"` (project-invariant default); the consumer resolves the value per-criterion.
  `_validate_routing_entry` rejects a `fail_mode` outside `{open, closed}`.
- **Rename:** `run_security_detectors` → `run_detectors`; `run_security_detectors` is KEPT as a thin
  deprecated alias (a test asserts the alias still returns the same result) so no external caller
  breaks.
- **Tests:** `fail_mode` branching (open abstain→skip=PASS, closed abstain→BLOCK) over a fixture;
  the three-way plan-review scoping (file_impact-present→finding, absent→advisory, diff-needed→N/A);
  the alias equivalence; DET-not-in-LLM-batch isolation.


## Docs deliverable (remediation, run 5)

An ADR (`docs/adr/0016-project-det-invariants.md`) — or an equivalent section extending ADR 0015 —
captures for future maintainers: (1) the **two-phase `run_det_floor`** contract (static P1–P9 tuple
+ a call-time dynamic project-DET phase discovered from `ctx.repo_root`, each check fail-open);
(2) the **`exec: DET` LLM-batch exclusion** rule (the filter sites: `orchestrator.route_criteria`
and `workflow_ops.plan_review_assemble_criteria` skip DET descriptors so a prompt-less DET criterion
is never handed to `pass1_chunk`); and (3) the **plan-time DET scoping** semantics
(file_impact-scoped → finding / no file_impact → advisory-repo-context / diff-inherent → N/A
fail-open). The routing-schema additions (`detector` selector + `fail_mode`) are documented there
and in the `criteria_routing.json` schema doc.

- [ ] An ADR (or ADR-0015 extension) documents the two-phase run_det_floor contract, the exec:DET
      LLM-batch exclusion, and the plan-time DET scoping semantics.


## Cross-story boundaries (remediation, run 7)

- **Parity gate unaffected:** project DET invariants live in the `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`
  OVERLAY, NOT the packaged plan-review `criteria_routing.json`. So `validate_packaged_routing()`
  (packaged-only, `CANONICAL_LLM` parity — from ef7e) gains NO new keys and is unaffected. The
  `detector` + `fail_mode` fields are ADDITIVE keys WITHIN existing/overlay routing entries, not new
  top-level criterion keys, so the orphan check does not fire. (The packaged code-review
  `criteria_routing.json`'s security DET rows already exist and are already outside plan-review's
  `CANONICAL_LLM` — that gate is plan-review-scoped and does not read code-review's file.)
- **Attestation invalidation is story `08af`, NOT this story:** `attest.registry_version()` today
  hashes the PACKAGED routing only. Making it hash the `.rebar/` overlay via
  `registry_version(repo_root)` — so that activating/editing a project DET criterion invalidates a
  prior attestation at claim time — is the explicit deliverable of story `08af`. This story (`7f0d`)
  does NOT modify `registry_version`; it only makes the DET criterion RUN. The two compose: 7f0d
  makes project DET invariants execute; 08af makes them attestation-invalidating.
baseline.summary: Project DET invariants: generalize the scan consumer + per-criterion fail_mode

## Why
`docs/coverage.md:89-91` says Jira link/relation round-trips are intentionally absent because link sync "is not yet a reconciler capability" — but link sync IS implemented (story 25ae) and `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_link_sync.py` has asserting tests for both outbound (`_diff_links` -> `client.set_relationship`) and inbound (`_diff_links_ inbound`) directions. The stale inventory makes the coverage matrix untrustworthy for finding genuinely-missing coverage. VALIDATED.

## What

## Scope

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/coverage.md` no longer claims link sync is "not yet a capability."
- [ ] The link-sync round-trip entry cites `test_link_sync.py` (both directions).

baseline.description:
## Reproduction Steps

1. A ticket bound to a Jira issue is detached from its parent locally: `rebar edit <id> --parent=null` (parent_id → None).
2. `show <id>` confirms parent_id is empty immediately.
3. Within minutes the reconcile-bridge cron (~3-min) re-parents the ticket back to its old epic.

**Expected:** the detach sticks; Jira's epic-link is cleared to match local.
**Actual:** the detach is silently reverted every reconcile pass (observed on super-plant-liver + toy-kink-ire reverting to epic peak-fir-hilt).

## Root Cause (proven via /joe-debug)

The Jira reconciler had an **asymmetric** parent sync:
- **Outbound never emitted a parent CLEAR.** `outbound_differ._map_local_to_jira_fields` only set `result['parent']` when local parent_id was truthy (outbound_differ.py:364). On a detach (parent_id None), no parent field was mapped, so the field-diff loop's parent branch never ran and outbound emitted nothing, leaving Jira's stale epic-link.
- **Inbound unconditionally re-applied it.** `inbound_differ._diff_jira_vs_local` (inbound_differ.py:307-316) re-emitted `parent_id=<epic>` whenever Jira's resolved parent != local parent_id. The same-pass suppression (_OUTBOUND_TO_INBOUND_FIELD) only fires when outbound emits a parent mutation, which on a detach it never did.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Outbound differ emits a parent CLEAR (parent: None) when a ticket is detached locally but its Jira snapshot still carries a parent (stale epic-link).
- [ ] The outbound applier (batch_dispatch.update_one) routes the CLEAR through set_parent(key, None) to clear the Jira epic-link.
- [ ] A never-parented bound ticket (local None, Jira None) emits NO parent mutation (no churn the other direction).
- [ ] The same-pass inbound suppression prevents the inbound re-parent so the detach converges.
- [ ] A regression test asserts the outbound differ emits the CLEAR for a detached-but-Jira-parented ticket (held-out RED then GREEN).
baseline.summary: Parent-detach churn: reconciler asymmetric parent sync reverts local detaches

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`rebar bridge fsck` reports `store_integrity=13` on every canary run (stable across 2026-08-10T21:16Z, 2026-08-10T22:13Z, 2026-08-11T22:16Z, and re-measured 2026-08-12). All 13 findings are kind `reverse_missing_forward`: `.bridge_state/bindings.json` holds `reverse[<jira_key>] = <local_id>` for REB-410…REB-422 with no matching `bindings[<local_id>]`. Every referenced local ticket is `deleted` `ZZ-*TEST` fixture scaffolding created under a retired environment (`env_id ade0f2ef-…`, not this store's `01a1a015-…`). The drift keeps this bug ticket open and keeps the binding-drift canary alerting, masking any genuine future integrity fault behind a known-benign 13.

The operator has decided the remediation, verbatim: **"delete."** — remove the orphaned reverse keys outright rather than tombstoning them into `bindings-retired.json`.

## Approach

Delete the 13 orphaned `reverse` entries through rebar's own library surface, then deliver the change with the sanctioned tracker-commit door. No ad-hoc raw git in the tracker.

1. Load the store via `BindingStore` (`rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler.binding_store`).
2. Delete exactly the reverse keys whose forward entry is absent, asserting the computed
   orphan set equals the expected 13 (REB-410…REB-422) before any mutation — so the repair
   cannot act on a set that drifted since diagnosis.
3. Persist with `BindingStore.save()` (tempfile + `os.replace`, atomic).
4. Commit and push with `rebar._store.push.commit_and_push_tickets_branch(strict=True)` —
   the helper `docs/concurrency.md` §"Mutating the tracker" names for committing pending
   tracker content under the store write lock.

Why this door and not another: `tracker-maintenance --clean` repairs only stranded index entries and foreign top-level paths, and `rebar fsck --repair` only rebuilds ticket event snapshots — neither can express a binding-store edit. `BindingStore.unbind()` cannot express it either: it pops `reverse` only when the forward entry still carries a `jira_key` (`binding_store.py:426-430`), and the missing forward entry is precisely the fault. That asymmetry is the mechanism that leaked these keys in the first place; it is recorded on this ticket as a reusable finding but is a separate code change, out of scope for this data repair.

Safety: a pre-repair backup of `bindings.json` is taken, and the tickets branch is verified clean with zero unpushed commits before the write, so the prior commit is itself a rollback point.

## Scope

No `src/` changes. This is a pure data repair of tracker state on the `tickets` branch:

- `.tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/bindings.json` — delete 13 keys from the `reverse` map.

Nothing else is touched: `bindings` (forward) is unmodified, `bindings-retired.json` is unmodified (none of the 13 appear there), and no ticket events are written.

## Testing

Deterministic before/after verification against the live store; there is no new code to unit-test.

- **Before:** `rebar bridge fsck --output json` → `store_integrity` = 13, all alerting
  `binding_drift` cells 0. Direct store read → `bindings`=2111, `reverse`=2124, delta 13.
- **Failure/edge path guarded:** the repair asserts the recomputed orphan set is exactly
  {REB-410…REB-422} and aborts without writing if it differs, and asserts the store contains
  no *other* reverse orphan (verified: total reverse orphans = 13, no more).
- **After:** re-run `rebar bridge fsck --output json` → `store_integrity` = 0 and alerting
  `binding_drift` cells still 0; direct read → `reverse` count drops by exactly 13 to 2111,
  `bindings` unchanged at 2111, delta 0.
- **No collateral:** confirm the forward map and `bindings-retired.json` are byte-identical
  before and after.

## Acceptance Criteria

All criteria below are tagged `[operator-attested]` for one structural reason: this ticket's work is a **data repair on the `tickets` git branch** (`.bridge_state/bindings.json`) plus **runtime `rebar bridge fsck` output**. Neither is discoverable in the source working tree — there is no `src/` change to find, and the tracker branch is not readable by codebase review tools. The concrete artifacts (commands, counts, sha256s, remote verification) are recorded in the "REPAIRED" comment on this ticket.

- [x] [operator-attested] The 13 orphaned `reverse` entries REB-410…REB-422 are deleted from
      `.bridge_state/bindings.json`, and the forward `bindings` map and
      `bindings-retired.json` are unchanged.
- [x] [operator-attested] `rebar bridge fsck` reports `store_integrity` = 0 with all alerting
      `binding_drift` cells empty.
- [x] [operator-attested] The repair is performed through rebar's library +
      `commit_and_push_tickets_branch`, with no ad-hoc raw git in the tracker, and the change
      is committed and pushed to `origin/tickets`.
- [x] [operator-attested] Before/after fsck evidence and the operator's delete decision are
      recorded as comments on this ticket.
- [x] [operator-attested] The reported defect no longer reproduces: `rebar bridge fsck` on the
      live store returns `store_integrity: 0` (was 13), so the bug is resolved.
baseline.summary: [binding-drift] bridge fsck found 13 audit finding(s)
