# The step-budget repetition diagnostic is computed, then dropped

## Context / Problem

Discovered while root-causing [rebar:bf31-fd55-d28d-4b7a]. The reported symptom was "the gate cannot be tuned because it cannot be observed" — no partial verdict, no count of anything, just a bare budget number. The diagnostic that answers it **already exists** and is thrown away one frame from the surface.

`interpret_failure` (`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:75-103`) builds `budget_diag` via `usage_log.failure_usage`, which reduces every tool call to a `(tool_name, sha256(args)[:8])` signature and summarizes it — `tool_calls_distinct`, `max_consecutive_repeat`, `top_repeated_tool_calls`. That is precisely the loop-vs-explore discriminator, and it is attached as `budget_err.diagnostic`.

It then goes nowhere. `emit_gate_error` is only called by `raise_completion_workflow_failure` when `failure_diagnostic` is truthy (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:373-403`), and `failure_diagnostic` is set ONLY inside `CompletionAgentStep._recover` — which a budget exhaustion never reaches (the sibling [rebar:fd84-92b4-01ba-4911] fixes reachability). So **no `gate_error_v1` sidecar is written** and the CLI message carries none of it. In the instrumented reproduction the propagated exception reached the caller with `diagnostic: null`.

Two operators burned ~50 minutes each escalating the budget 480 -> 1600 against a constraint that was never a budget (and ticket 46a2-9c1a-d855-4706 records a third: 480 -> 1200, same result). The measurement that would have said so in one line was computed on the first run and discarded.

## Approach

Wire the already-computed diagnostic through the two drops. First, `CompletionAgentStep` records the caught exception's `.diagnostic` onto `self.failure_diagnostic` when it enters recovery (fd84 adds the budget entry edge; this ticket makes the diagnostic it carries survive), so `raise_completion_workflow_failure` — whose sidecar emission and `CompletionRecoveryError` path already exist and are keyed on a truthy `failure_diagnostic` — emits the `gate_error_v1` sidecar carrying the repetition counters. The carry path is NOT automatic: the caught exception's `.diagnostic` is filtered through `_bounded_diagnostic` (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py`), whose `allowed` allowlist strips `tool_calls_distinct`, `max_consecutive_repeat`, `top_repeated_tool_calls` and `distinct_ratio_window` today — and whose scalar-only merge guard would drop the list-valued `top_repeated_tool_calls` even if allowlisted. This ticket widens that allowlist with those four repetition keys and relaxes the scalar-only guard for exactly `top_repeated_tool_calls` (a bounded list of `{signature, count}` dicts — hashed signatures, no prompts or arguments), so the summary survives both the recovery-exception merge and the primary-exception merge ([rebar:fd84-92b4-01ba-4911], landed, established that carry). On the budget path the counters ride the PRIMARY exception, and every primary-diagnostic key is re-prefixed `aggregate_` before landing on `failure_diagnostic` — so the sidecar carries them as `aggregate_tool_calls_distinct`, `aggregate_max_consecutive_repeat`, `aggregate_top_repeated_tool_calls`, `aggregate_distinct_ratio_window`. `format_repetition` reads the BARE key names, so `raise_completion_workflow_failure` builds its render input by projecting the prefix off first — `{k.removeprefix("aggregate_"): v for k, v in diag.items() if k.startswith("aggregate_")}` — and passes that projection to `format_repetition`; the sidecar itself keeps the `aggregate_`-prefixed names unchanged. Second, the operator-facing close-gate failure message renders the distinct-vs-total counts (via the existing `usage_log.format_repetition` renderer, which already formats exactly these fields) so "it looped" is distinguishable from "it ran out of room" without reading a log. No new computation: every value is already produced by `usage_log.failure_usage`; this ticket widens the diagnostic filter to stop dropping it and renders it.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py` — `_bounded_diagnostic`: extend the `allowed`
  allowlist with `tool_calls_distinct`, `max_consecutive_repeat`, `top_repeated_tool_calls`,
  `distinct_ratio_window`, and permit the list-typed `top_repeated_tool_calls` through `merge()`
  (all other keys stay scalar-only); in `raise_completion_workflow_failure`, project the
  `aggregate_`-prefixed keys back to bare names and render that projection through
  `usage_log.format_repetition` into the raised message.
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_token_recovery.py` — the tests below.

Out of scope: making budget exhaustion reach this code at all ([rebar:fd84-92b4-01ba-4911], landed: budget exhaustions now enter `_recover` and set `failure_diagnostic`); computing the detector's new field ([rebar:70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0], landed: `failure_usage` now emits `distinct_ratio_window`). This ticket carries both through the `_bounded_diagnostic` filter that currently strips them.

## Testing

    pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_token_recovery.py -q

Happy path: a budget exhaustion whose recovery also fails emits a `gate_error_v1` sidecar populated with the repetition counters. Edge: a failure with NO diagnostic (the pre-existing bare path) still raises `LLMError` exactly as today (regression-pinned). Privacy: the sidecar payload carries no prompts, tool arguments, or response text.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] a step-budget exhaustion whose recovery also fails writes a `gate_error_v1` sidecar carrying
      the repetition summary under the `aggregate_`-prefixed names the primary-exception merge
      produces (`aggregate_requests`, `aggregate_tool_calls`, `aggregate_tool_calls_distinct`,
      `aggregate_max_consecutive_repeat`, `aggregate_top_repeated_tool_calls`,
      `aggregate_distinct_ratio_window`) — i.e. the `_bounded_diagnostic` allowlist passes these
      keys and the list-valued `top_repeated_tool_calls` survives the merge; verified by a test
      asserting the sidecar is emitted and those keys are populated
- [x] the operator-facing close-gate failure message includes the distinct-vs-total tool-call counts
      rendered from the `aggregate_`-prefix-stripped projection (so `format_repetition`'s bare-key
      lookups resolve to the actual numbers, never `None`), making "it looped" distinguishable from
      "it ran out of room" without reading a log; verified by a test asserting the raised error's
      message contains the concrete counts (e.g. `30 distinct / 253 calls`), not `None`
- [x] the sidecar payload stays free of prompts, tool arguments and response text (the existing
      privacy contract in `usage_log.failure_usage` is preserved); verified by a test asserting only
      hashed signatures and counters appear
- [x] a failure without any diagnostic still raises the current bare `LLMError` unchanged (no
      manufactured empty sidecar); regression-pinned by a test
baseline.summary: Step-budget repetition diagnostic is computed then dropped: no gate_error_v1 sidecar, no counters in the operator message

baseline.description:
## Symptom

2026-08-12T23:07:07Z rebar-gerrit-voter-errors and 23:07:18Z rebar-review-bot-merge-change-errors both went OK -> ALARM, each on exactly 1 datapoint in the 23:06Z probe minute, and both returned to OK at 23:13Z.

NO voter error and NO merge-change error occurred. Both counts came from a SINGLE journal line at 2026-08-12T23:02:26Z which is the review-bot's own LLM code-review analysis prose, verbatim (CONTAINER_NAME=compose-review-bot-1):

    ...mits matching markers for every target (VOTER_ERROR, MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR, AUTODEPLOY_ERROR,
    AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED, gerrit_to_platform error, both interrupt reasons) and REPL_LOG is
    populated. The rolled-up review_interrupts per_interval=2 arithmetic is consistent
    (total 14 seeded, next run +2)

The reviewer was reviewing a change to infra/scripts/observability.sh itself (the cold-start seeding fix for widespread-zealous-narwhal / e2a6-9ee4-8d5c-4290), so it enumerated the marker tokens as prose. The probe then counted that prose as two errors.

## Mechanism

infra/scripts/observability.sh section 4 and section 4c count markers with an UNANCHORED grep over the review-bot container's journal:

    vtotal=$(journalctl CONTAINER_NAME="$VOTER_CONTAINER" --no-pager -o cat | grep -cE 'VOTER_ERROR')
    mtotal=$(journalctl CONTAINER_NAME="$VOTER_CONTAINER" --no-pager -o cat | grep -cE 'MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR')

The pattern matches the token ANYWHERE in a line. The review-bot writes its LLM output to the same journal stream, so any review whose text mentions a marker name is counted as an occurrence of that marker. The probe cannot distinguish its own alarm vocabulary from an actual error.

## Evidence that the counted line is not a real marker

Full-journal counts, real markers are emitted at line start under -o cat:

    VOTER_ERROR        line-start (real): 221    substring-anywhere: 222   offset file: 222
    MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR line-start (real):   0    substring-anywhere:   1   offset file:   1

So exactly one of the 222 counted voter errors is the false match, and the merge-change counter has NEVER seen a real error in the entire retained journal — its only count in history is this false positive, which is what fired its alarm.

Review-bot health across the window contradicts any real failure: voter_voted events at 23:05:08Z, 23:13:04Z and 23:19:38Z, i.e. the bot was voting normally before, during and after. There is no Gerrit 4xx/5xx, no 409 and no conflict of any kind in the window.

## Classification

FALSE POSITIVE, and the alarm is not at fault: both alarms are correct to fire on a nonzero count. The count was fabricated by the probe. Do not tune the alarms.

## Why this recurs and is getting worse

The trigger is a review that discusses observability.sh or the marker vocabulary. The fleet is actively landing changes to observability.sh right now (the narwhal cold-start fix), so every further review of that file is likely to re-fire these two alarms. It is self-referential: the observability code's own review trips its own alarms. It also silently corrupts the offset files (voter offset is now 222 against 221 real markers), so the counters permanently carry the inflation.

Same false-positive FAMILY as widespread-zealous-narwhal (probe publishes counts for non-events) but a DISTINCT mechanism: that one is an absent-offset cold start, this one is an over-broad pattern matching the token as data. Both live in infra/scripts/observability.sh.

## Suggested fix direction (not prescriptive)

Anchor the match to the marker's actual emission shape rather than a bare substring. Evidence says real markers begin the message (221/221 line-start under -o cat), so '^VOTER_ERROR' / '^MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR' would exclude the prose case. A structural match on the emitted record would be sturdier still. Whatever is chosen must be applied to every marker counter that reads a stream the LLM also writes to, and the same question should be asked of the AUTODEPLOY_* counters, whose journal is not currently LLM-written but which share the unanchored shape. Consider also whether the inflated offsets should be corrected or simply left to age out.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A journal line containing a marker token as prose (not at the emission position) is NOT counted. Verify: test feeding the verbatim 23:02:26Z line to the voter and merge counters yields 0.
- [x] A genuine marker line is still counted. Verify: test with a real-shaped VOTER_ERROR and MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR line yields 1 each.
- [x] The tightened pattern is applied to every counter reading an LLM-written stream (sections 4 and 4c at minimum), and the AUTODEPLOY_* counters are audited for the same shape.

## Verification

Discovered by ops sweep of AWS alarm firings; full evidence trail on childsafe-bizarre-lorikeet (b902-18af-14ed-4da1). All investigation read-only (CloudWatch describe/get + SSM read-only journalctl); nothing mutated in AWS or on the box.
## Implementation plan (on top of the narwhal cold-start fix, change 1686)

### Anchor to the marker's emitted RECORD shape, not the bare token

Every countable marker is emitted as `<TOKEN> {json}` at the START of the journal message — `voter.py` (`"VOTER_ERROR " + json.dumps(record)` printed to stderr, same for `MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR`) and `autodeploy.sh` `marker()` (`printf '%s %s\n' "$1" "<json>" >&2`). Under `journalctl -o cat` that is line-start, a space, then `{`. So the pattern becomes `^<TOKEN> \{` — the ticket's "structural match on the emitted record", which excludes prose naming the token both mid-line AND at line start. Evidence agrees the anchor keeps every real marker: line-start count 221 == real count 221 (bare substring counted 222).

Sites in `infra/scripts/observability.sh`:
- §4 `voter_errors`: `'VOTER_ERROR'` -> `'^VOTER_ERROR \{'`
- §4c `review_bot_merge_change_errors`: `'MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR'` -> `'^MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR \{'`
- §4d `deploy_errors`: `'AUTODEPLOY_ERROR'` -> `'^AUTODEPLOY_ERROR \{'`
- §4e the four `publish_autodeploy_marker_delta` call sites: `^AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED \{`,
  `^AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT \{`, and the two reason-scoped patterns gain the same prefix.
  The anchor goes at the CALL SITES; the helper's first argument stays a plain ERE.

### Audited, deliberately NOT anchored

§3 `replication_errors` (Gerrit's `replication_log`) and §4b `g2p_dispatch_errors` (Gerrit container journal): neither stream is LLM-written, and both match free-form phrases (`Giving up`, `[ERROR]`, `failed to dispatch`) that are not line-anchored records, so an anchor would drop real failures. Recorded as a comment at each site.

### Tests — tests/scripts/test_observability_marker_anchor_8c2f.py

Same stub harness as `test_observability_interrupt_reasons.py` (journalctl stub cats a file).

1. `test_prose_naming_a_marker_is_not_counted` — journal holds the VERBATIM 2026-08-12T23:02:26Z
   review-bot line naming `VOTER_ERROR` / `MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR` / `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` /
   `AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED` / both interrupt reasons as prose. Every marker metric publishes 0.
2. `test_real_markers_are_still_counted` — one genuine `<TOKEN> {json}` line per marker publishes 1
   (2 for the rolled-up `review_interrupts`, which matches both reason lines).
3. `test_line_start_prose_without_a_record_is_not_counted` — line-start prose publishes 0.
4. `test_inflated_offset_self_heals` — offset 222 against 221 real markers publishes 0 and re-bases
   to 221, showing the false counts already banked need no manual correction (bug
   2dc7-31b7-ecbb-4cd2's clamp).

RED-verified against the current tree first.

### Deploy and residue

No manual box action: autodeploy.sh watches `OBS_PATHS`. The inflated offsets (voter 222 vs 221 real, merge 1 vs 0) self-heal on the first probe run after this lands — the count drops, the negative-delta clamp publishes 0, and the offset re-bases.

### Out of scope

Alarm thresholds (correct as written); autodeploy.sh's `capture_bot_logs` redaction.
baseline.summary: observability.sh counts UNANCHORED marker substrings in the review-bot journal, so the bot's own LLM review text naming VOTER_ERROR / MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR fires false alarms

# J8 — ADR amending 0035: the Jira-family sub-seam, shared provenance, and the DC horizon

## Context / Problem

ADR 0035 §6 states that "the first real second backend is out of scope for this ADR and is tracked separately by epic `be74-7832-03a8-48ac`" — the GitHub adapter. This epic lands a different second backend first, and it introduces a structure ADR 0035 does not describe: a `jira_family` layer between the neutral core and a concrete adapter, with two contracts (`RichTextCodec`, `UserIdentityModel`) parameterizing it. It also makes a provenance decision — that the Jira family shares one `jira` creation channel and `jira-` id prefix, with deployments distinguished by `RemoteRef.instance` — which is precisely the decision PR #120 would have made silently by inheriting the hardcoded literal `validate_creation_channel("jira")` — today at `apply_inbound_records.py:211`, not :163 as an earlier draft of this plan said. Story J9's identity fix shifted it, and line 163 now holds an unrelated tag list-comprehension. CITE THE SYMBOL, not a line number: this plan has already gone stale against this exact file once. And it adds rebar's first third-party runtime dependency in the reconciler, confined to an extra.

Left unrecorded, each of these gets re-litigated the next time a Jira-like tracker appears.

## Approach

Write one ADR that amends 0035 rather than replacing it, recording: the `adapters/jira_family/` layer and why the seam is now two levels for one vendor family; the two parameterizing contracts; the shared-`jira` provenance decision and explicitly what it defers to epic `be74` (generalizing `jira_key`, the `jira-` prefix, and the channel vocabulary when a genuinely different vendor lands); the `pycontribs/jira` dependency, why it is extra-gated, and why the Cloud ACLI path was deliberately not migrated onto it; and the Docker harness as the verification oracle given that DC trial licenses ended in March 2026 and no official DC OpenAPI spec exists.

The ADR states the **horizon** plainly: Data Center goes read-only on 28 March 2029 and receives no new features today, so this is a deliberately time-boxed investment for existing self-hosted clients, and the durable asset is the family seam rather than the DC adapter. That framing is what tells a future maintainer whether to extend this code or retire it.

The ADR must ALSO record two findings this epic produced by execution, both already evidenced on this ticket's comments — they are properties of the SEAM, not of the DC adapter, so epic `be74` (GitHub Issues) inherits them:

* **The port did not state what the core requires.** `TicketTransport` declares SIX members while the
  core reaches for TWENTY-ONE distinct transport members (an earlier draft said fifteen — that was a
  call-form-only AST scan; counting EVERY attribute access on a `client`/`transport` receiver finds
  six more, because the reconciler routinely passes methods as values, e.g.
  `_call_with_retry(client.delete_issue_link, link_id)`); TWELVE were absent from the DC transport and
  declared on no Protocol at all. The consequence was measured, not theorised: a DC writing reconcile
  pass crashed (`set_entity_property`) while `isinstance(backend, Backend)`, the backend contract
  suite, and 1636 reconciler unit tests were all green. So ADR 0035's "the contract suite certifies a
  backend" holds ONLY as far as the port is complete — and, per [rebar:cc77-8120-bcc6-47e8], only as
  far as the transport parameters are TYPED, since an unannotated `client` makes the gap invisible to
  mypy. State that conditionality plainly. Tracked by [rebar:a357-b747-ece9-4cf5] and
  [rebar:bda8-370d-23ad-4e36]; the exception half is [rebar:bb8c-8283-80c6-4052].
* **`RemoteRef.instance` is NOT built.** The ADR must NOT assert that deployments *are* distinguished
  by it as though that were existing reality. `RemoteRef` is never constructed in production code —
  `src/` holds only the frozen dataclass definition and docstrings; the only constructions in the repo
  are two test helpers. State it as the INTENDED design with the gap named and tracked
  ([rebar:6a91-7429-e521-4a2e]), or a future reader will build on a field nothing populates.

**Alternative rejected:** documenting only in `docs/architecture.md`. rebar's ADR set is where rejected alternatives live; without them the fork-per-deployment and hand-rolled-client options get re-proposed.

## Scope

- `docs/adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md` (new — 0055 is the next free number; 0054 is taken by
  `0054-data-driven-calibration-no-costly-llm-assessments.md`).
  **Numbering caution:** THREE existing files share the number 0035 —
  `0035-rc2b-snapshot-horizon-safe-replay.md`, `0035-code-review-two-lane-tier-tagged-impact.md`, and
  `0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md`. This story amends the THIRD. Every reference must cite the
  FILENAME; a bare "ADR 0035" is ambiguous in this repo.
- `docs/adr/0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md` — a pointer noting the amendment and correcting §6's
  "first real second backend" statement.
- `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/user-guide.md` — the `reconciler.backend` choice and the DC extra.
- `docs/env-vars.md` — regenerated for `JIRA_PAT`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/user-guide.md` states the DC least-privilege expectation: a dedicated service account whose PAT is
      scoped to only the reconciled projects (Browse Projects / Create Issues / Edit Issues / Add Comments /
      Link Issues), never an admin token — and documents `allow_insecure` as cleartext-only-if-you-must, the
      `ca_bundle` key for internal-CA certificates, and `resolved_statuses` for workflows that do not use the
      conventional Resolved/Done/Cancelled state names (epic AC13)
- [ ] the ADR exists, is `Accepted`, and records each rejected alternative (fork-per-deployment, hand-rolled
      stdlib client, generalizing the store vocabulary now, migrating Cloud onto pycontribs) with its reason
- [ ] ADR 0035 carries a pointer to the amendment, and **all THREE stale statements** are corrected —
      not just Decision item 6. The claim that the first real second backend is out of scope appears
      at `:111` (layout-diagram comment `<backend-x>/  # future second backend`), `:204-205` (prose),
      and `:236-237` (Decision item 6). All three are falsified because this epic landed Jira Data
      Center AHEAD of the GitHub adapter `be74` was reserved for; correcting only one leaves two
      readers misinformed
- [ ] the ADR records the OSS-comparison finding [rebar:558e-55ce-d9f1-4fa9]: the seam ARCHITECTURE
      converged with what mature Jira integrations do (a maintained client library rather than
      hand-rolled REST, PAT bearer auth, an ephemeral containerised instance as the oracle), and every
      gap found was instead in OPERATIONAL EDGES that only appear against a differently-configured
      instance — index lag, server-side pagination caps, admin-toggled rate limiting, screen
      configuration, project moves. State that pattern, because it tells the next backend author where
      to look
- [ ] the ADR states the March 2029 DC read-only date and what it implies for future investment in this adapter
- [ ] `docs/user-guide.md` documents selecting the DC backend and installing the extra, and the documented
      commands have been executed against the J5 harness
- [ ] `docs/architecture.md` documents the `reconciler.backend` choice and the `jira-datacenter` extra
      (it mentions neither today) — it is a Scope deliverable and was previously uncovered by any AC
- [ ] the ADR records that ADR 0035's "the contract suite certifies a backend" claim is CONDITIONAL on
      the port being complete and typed, citing the measured evidence (6 declared vs TWENTY-ONE called, 12
      absent, a live crash while every static signal was green). The figure is 21, not 15: a
      call-form-only AST scan finds 15 and misses six members the reconciler reaches for as VALUES
      (e.g. `_call_with_retry(client.delete_issue_link, link_id)`). An earlier draft of this AC
      carried the stale 15 while the Context above already said 21
- [ ] the ADR describes `RemoteRef.instance` as INTENDED design with its gap named and ticketed, NOT as
      an existing mechanism — `grep -rn "RemoteRef(" src/` returns nothing, and the ADR must not
      contradict that
- [ ] `docs/env-vars.md` regenerates with no diff
baseline.summary: J8 — ADR amending 0035: the Jira-family sub-seam, shared provenance, and the DC horizon

## Context

Observed 2026-07-10 during the adept-hedge-stain epic close-out: `rebar fsck` reported 14 issues (later 17 after more write activity) — MISSING_CREATE + ORPHAN_EVENT ('pre-snapshot event not captured in source_event_uuids'). This ticket's original open question was whether those were (a) false positives from binary/store version skew (an older binary misreading newer ENQUEUE_ENRICH-era events) or (b) genuine faults.

## RESOLVED (2026-07-11)

The ENQUEUE_ENRICH-introducing change has **already merged to main** (current binary = main 2d1524ad8; `rebar fsck` prints `ensures: 5/5 applied` with NO "store contains events newer than binary" WARN), so AC1's gate is satisfied and the classification can be made from the current binary. Re-running fsck from that binary, the faults **persist** — so they are **NOT version-skew false positives**. They are real, but BENIGN, artifacts (full forensic classification recorded as a comment on this ticket and on 115b):

- **13 ORPHAN_EVENT** — benign snapshot-staleness from a distributed compaction-vs-reconciler
  write race (the Jira reconciler writes an assignee EDIT; a compaction in a different clone
  snapshots before observing it; the reconciler re-emits an identical EDIT after the snapshot
  which drives live state). Live status/assignee verified correct for all 13.
- **4 MISSING_CREATE** — local-only phantom dirs (0 tracked files, not in HEAD, no structural
  refs); 110e is a local duplicate of the tracked epic 6d0d.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [operator-attested] Re-run `rebar fsck` with the ENQUEUE_ENRICH-era binary against the live store and record
  the counts on this ticket. (DONE: 13 ORPHAN_EVENT + 4 MISSING_CREATE, `ensures: 5/5 applied`.)
- [ ] [operator-attested] Classify each fault as version-skew artifact vs real. (DONE: none are version-skew — they
  persist under the current binary; classified real-but-benign per the forensic comment.)
- [ ] [operator-attested] Remediate the real faults with A3-safe tooling (NOT `fsck --repair-snapshots`, which
  rebuilds from the full log and previously corrupted 11/13 statuses): retire each orphan EDIT
  file (`.json` -> `.json.retired`, which fsck skips) and delete the 4 local phantom dirs, then
  confirm `rebar fsck` reports zero ORPHAN_EVENT + zero MISSING_CREATE with no ticket's
  status/assignee changed. (This is the shared remediation tracked jointly with 115b.)

## Notes

- Root cause of the recurring orphan race (compaction snapshotting before observing a remote
  reconciler write) is a separate durable-fix follow-up, out of scope for this classify-and-
  remediate-to-zero ticket.
baseline.summary: Re-audit live-store fsck once ENQUEUE_ENRICH-era code lands: 13 ORPHAN_EVENT + 1 MISSING_CREATE reported by main's binary against a newer store

# S1 — Gerrit gate config: `Verified` label + two-vote submit requirement

Part of epic 1fa8 (CI as a second Gerrit gate vote via gerrit-to-platform → GitHub Actions).

## Why
The gate today is a single vote (`LLM-Review` only). Adding an independent CI vote requires a
`Verified` label plus a submit requirement that demands it, mirroring the existing `LLM-Review`
label/SR pattern in `infra/gerrit/project.config`.

## What
Add the `Verified` label + submit-requirement + voting ACL, and record the gate-architecture
change (two independent votes) as an ADR superseding/amending ADR-0013.

## Scope
- `infra/gerrit/project.config` (label + submit-requirement + `label-Verified` ACL).
- New ADR superseding/amending ADR-0013; update the gate section of `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md`.
- **The submit-requirement ACTIVATION is deferred** until the voter is proven (done in S6) — this
  story authors the config; S6 flips it on. Out of scope: the workflow, g2p, credentials.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Add `[label "Verified"]` (function `NoBlock`, values -1/0/+1, `defaultValue = 0`,
      `copyCondition = changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE`) to `infra/gerrit/project.config`, mirroring the
      `LLM-Review` label block.
- [ ] Add `[submit-requirement "Verified"] submittableIf = label:Verified=MAX` and grant the CI
      service-account group `label-Verified = -1..+1` (Service Users only; devs cannot self-vote).
- [ ] The intended final gate is `label:LLM-Review=MAX AND label:Verified=MAX AND -has:unresolved`;
      the `Verified` submit-requirement is left inactive/enforcement-deferred until S6 proves the
      voter (avoids blocking all submits during rollout).
- [ ] Write an ADR that supersedes/amends **ADR-0013** documenting the two-independent-vote gate.
- [ ] Update the gate section of `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` to describe both votes.

## Context

An assessment of rebar's config surface (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py` vs this project's `rebar.toml`) identified settled rollout flags and retired alternatives to prune, one settled feature to activate by dogfooding, and an authenticated-identity rollout to stand up. Each decision is backed by a code-level investigation recorded on the relevant child. This epic delivers all of it plus a doc-accuracy sweep.

## Workstreams

- **Prune (removal approved):** `reconciler.baseline_dual_write` +
  `baseline_consumer_swap` (→ always-on); the three settled verify defaults
  `progressive_drift_refresh` / `remediation_mode` / `novelty_drop_active` (→ always-on);
  `verify.require_signature_for_close` (retired alternative); and
  `compact.emit_legacy_signature_mirror` (a one-way door — landed behind a readiness-gate
  check). That is **seven** config keys grouped into four removal stories.
- **Activate by dogfooding:** `verify.completion_floor_active` — assessed as fully
  implemented AND already calibrated (gold-set 30/30, κ=1.0, zero must-never-suppress
  anchors dropped; docs/calibration/completion_floor.md). Enable it in THIS project.
- **Authenticated-identity rollout (setup only):** stand up signing identity for every
  ticket-event writer (local dev; AWS review-bot + auto-lander; GitHub Actions reconciler
  + canary), AWS/GitHub sharing the Rebar Bot identity. The `require_authenticated` flag
  flip is OUT OF SCOPE (setup only). **The signing seam** is `_seam.append_event` /
  `_apply_authorship` (`src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py`), which stamps `author_id` /
  `author_email` / `author_sig`. The reconciler's inbound writer `_write_event_file`
  (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py`) bypasses it today. **The fix
  is to stamp+sign author fields inline** (reuse `_apply_authorship`'s stamping logic on the
  event dict before `_write_event_file` persists it), NOT to route through
  `_seam.append_event`: `append_event` calls `write_and_push` which commits+pushes eagerly,
  whereas `_write_event_file` intentionally writes files WITHOUT committing so the
  reconciler's own orchestration can batch-commit later — routing through the seam would
  break that batch-commit design and thread `repo_root`/`tracker` through 12+ call-sites.
  Inline stamping keeps the deferred-commit orchestration intact and is additive to the
  event dict (older readers ignore the new author keys).
- **Doc-accuracy sweep** for every removed key + overall config-doc correctness.

## Secret delivery mechanism (per environment)

SSHSIG signing needs a private-key FILE PATH (`identity.signing_key: str | None`; `sshsig.sign(key_path=...)`). Each writer environment delivers that path as follows (the private key is never committed; actual secret provisioning in AWS/GitHub is an operator/escalation step, the design is fixed here):

- **Local dev / agent clone:** the developer's own OpenSSH private key under `~/.ssh/`;
  set `identity.signing_key` in local config (or export `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY`) to
  that path. Per-machine, git-ignored, never committed.
- **AWS review-bot + auto-lander:** a new SSM SecureString
  `/rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key` (add to `rebar_secret_params` in `infra/terraform/ssm.tf`).
  A multi-line OpenSSH PEM private key CANNOT be delivered via the container `.env`
  (`fetch-secrets.sh` writes only single-line `KEY=VALUE` env pairs — the
  `GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` pattern is for single-line tokens only). Instead
  it MUST be materialized to a standalone `0600` FILE at boot, following the
  `ci-gerrit-ssh-key` / `g2p-github-pat` precedent (`infra/gerrit/materialize-g2p-config.sh`,
  fail-closed): a dedicated boot step (or an extension of `fetch-secrets.sh`) writes the SSM
  value to e.g. `/run/secrets/rebar-bot-signing-key` (0600), and the reviewbot/autolander
  containers set `identity.signing_key` (or `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY`) to that file path.
  `sshsig.sign()` consumes it as `ssh-keygen -Y sign -f <key_path>`.
- **GitHub Actions reconciler + canary:** a GitHub Actions encrypted secret
  `REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY`; a workflow step writes it to a `mktemp` file, `chmod 0600`, and
  exports the path as `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY` (and sets the committer email to
  `joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com` so git-email resolution maps to the bot identity). The key
  is never logged or committed.

## KEEP (assessed, not touched)

Nothing on the original KEEP list survives as keep: the signature-mirror is now a removal (readiness-gated) and the completion floor is now an activation. There are no remaining keep-dormant decisions in this epic's scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All child stories are closed.
- [ ] `rebar` runs clean against this project's `rebar.toml` (a grep of `rebar.toml` for each removed key name returns zero hits; no `unknown key … ignored` warnings).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass on the landed result.
- [ ] A repo-wide grep confirms no committed doc/help/release-note references any removed config key.
- [ ] Each ticket-event-writing environment (local, AWS auto-lander/review-bot, GHA reconciler + canary) has a named, documented signing-key delivery path per the "Secret delivery mechanism" section; actual secret provisioning that requires AWS/GitHub access is recorded as an operator step where it cannot be completed in-repo.
- [ ] All **seven** approved removals (`baseline_dual_write`, `baseline_consumer_swap`,
- [ ] `completion_floor_active` is enabled in this project's `rebar.toml`, with a documented
- [ ] Every ticket-event-writing environment can sign as its intended identity (bot for
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass on the landed result.
baseline.summary: Prune settled/stale config values + authenticated-identity enablement + doc-accuracy sweep

## Why

The default test suite runs serially with branch coverage — the dominant cost of the `build-and-test` job (~22 min pytest). Measured `pytest -n4 --dist worksteal` on the same selection is ~5× faster (1700s→~350s) with byte-identical outcomes (5877P/14S/same 1 known-Py3.14 fail), proving the suite's per-test isolation holds under parallel workers.

## What

Introduce pytest-xdist to the gating test runs, pinned to the runner's real core count.

- Add `pytest-xdist` and `pytest-split` to the `[dev]` extra in `pyproject.toml`, pinned
  exactly (both are ABSENT today; used ad hoc in experiments only).
- `gerrit-verify.yaml` + `test.yml`: change the default-suite command to
  `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n <N> --dist worksteal …` where N is the
  runner's real vCPU count — pin `-n4` (ubuntu-latest, 4 vCPU) / `-n3` (macos arm, 3 vCPU),
  NOT `-n auto` (18-worker local runs over-subscribe and hit a coverage SQLite combine race).
- FIX COVERAGE UNDER XDIST (prereq — proven): add `parallel = true` to
  `[tool.coverage.run]` in `pyproject.toml`. Without it, `-n4 --cov` fails to combine
  worker data (reports ~37% vs the true 80%, below `fail_under=70` → red build, and leaks
  `.coverage.*` files). With `parallel = true` the combined TOTAL matches serial exactly.
- Integration tier: parallelize only NON-live tests. `pytest -m "integration and not live
  and not jira_live" -n4` is xdist-safe (64P/1S identical serial vs -n4, 1.6× faster).
  Live tests (`[integration, live]`, e.g. `test_reconcile_live_e2e.py`) share one live Jira
  project and flake under parallel load (eventual-consistency); keep them serial or confine
  to one worker via `@pytest.mark.xdist_group` + `--dist loadgroup`. In CI's integration job
  they self-skip without Jira creds, but the command must not assume that.
- Update `docs/coverage.md` to document that coverage collection under pytest-xdist REQUIRES
  `parallel = true` in `[tool.coverage.run]` (else the combined TOTAL is silently deflated,
  e.g. ~37% vs the true 80%, tripping `fail_under`), so anyone adding a new coverage-bearing
  workflow keeps the combine correct. This satisfies the parent epic's AC-3.

## Scope

- Files: `pyproject.toml` (`[dev]` deps, `[tool.coverage.run] parallel`),
  `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`, `.github/workflows/test.yml`, `docs/coverage.md`.
- Verify runner vCPU with an in-workflow `nproc` echo (belt-and-suspenders) before pinning N.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pytest-xdist` + `pytest-split` added to `[dev]`, pinned exactly.
- [ ] `parallel = true` added to `[tool.coverage.run]`; a `-n4 --cov` run reports a combined
      TOTAL equal to the serial value and ≥ `fail_under=70`, with no `.coverage.*` files left
      in the checkout.
- [ ] gerrit-verify + test.yml default-suite step runs with `-n <real-cores> --dist worksteal`;
      test outcomes are identical to the pre-change serial run (same pass/skip counts, no new
      isolation/leak-guard failures).
- [ ] Non-live integration tier runs under `-n4`; live tests are kept serial or xdist_group-confined.
- [ ] `docs/coverage.md` updated to document the xdist + `parallel=true` coverage-combine
      requirement (satisfies parent AC-3).
- [ ] Change passes CI (`Verified +1`) and lands via Gerrit.

baseline.description:
## Why

Enforcement is the epic's goal; it must land **only after** every writer signs (79da local, 4dc0 CI, 1a51 Gerrit) and grandfathering is proven (8d91). Flipping early turns every push red by construction (bug `27ae-8322-9278-4a7c`): with 0 signed events store-wide today, the gate would reject everything. This is the final, atomic switch — and the **only** change that writes both the flag and `enforce_since`.

**Depends on bug `0ba4-6a28-7a88-47b2` (txn signing).** The transactional write path (claim/transition/close, and delete) previously wrote UNSIGNED in-scope STATUS/EDIT/ARCHIVED events (they bypassed the signing seam). 0ba4 centralizes signing in a shared `finalize_event` choke point every write routes through. The flip is unsafe until that fix is **landed AND live across every active writer build** (local auto-updates hourly; CI/Gerrit deploy from `main`) — otherwise a still-old writer keeps emitting unsigned events that the merge-gate rejects. Hence the pre-flip validation AC below: prove no active process is still writing unsigned non-SNAPSHOT events before flipping.

## What

- In `rebar.toml`, in **one** change, set `[identity] require_authenticated = true` **and**
  `enforce_since = <the anchor SHA documented by 8d91>` (replacing the current rollout-prep pin
  `ce3f8bcbe13d37e93a0758f7f73cb3ebeac3b043`). No earlier child modifies `enforce_since`; its
  value equals the exact anchor SHA from 8d91.
- **Demonstrate enforcement is real** without polluting the shared store:
  (i) the **merge-gate** fails on a synthetic post-boundary forged/unsigned in-scope event in an
  isolated temp store (`rebar verify-identity --all --require-authenticated` exits non-zero) —
  reusing 8d91's harness; and (ii) the **local write-gate** refuses an unsignable write when the
  signing key is unset (with `require_authenticated=true`, a non-exempt write with no resolvable
  signing key is refused, exit non-zero) — proving the flag is live, not advisory.
- **Confirm each writer surface still passes under enforcement**: a representative signed write
  on local and CI verifies; the Gerrit-side in-scope writer (the review-bot LINK, per 1a51)
  verifies. No red pushes on `main`.
- **Provide a documented fast-revert (rollback) path**: how to revert
  `identity.require_authenticated` to `false` in a single change if a writer surface unexpectedly
  fails post-flip.

## Scope

The single atomic config change (flag + boundary) + under-enforcement verification + a rollback procedure. Depends on 79da, 4dc0, 1a51, 8d91. `file_impact`: `rebar.toml` (the flag + `enforce_since`); plus a runbook/rollback note.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **PRE-FLIP GATE — no active process writes an unsigned non-SNAPSHOT in-scope event.**
      Before flipping, validate over a window in which EVERY active writer operates — a fresh
      local session write, a `reconcile-bridge` CI run, a Gerrit review-bot write (its
      `relates_to` LINK on a work ticket), the **enrich drain**, and the **reconciler** — that
      no active process is still emitting unsigned in-scope events. Method: capture
      `C0 = git -C .tickets-tracker rev-parse origin/tickets`; let the writers run (or trigger
      each); fetch `origin/tickets`; then enumerate every event file introduced in
      `C0..origin/tickets` and assert **every in-scope event carries `author_sig` EXCEPT
      `*-SNAPSHOT.json`** — SNAPSHOT is the sole permitted unsigned type (a compaction artifact
      the merge-gate re-verifies via the snapshot's `authorship_ledger`, not the SNAPSHOT event).
      Proving commands (both must hold):
      (a) `rebar verify-identity --all --require-authenticated --since C0` exits 0 (every
      enforced event since `C0` verifies); and
      (b) no unsigned non-SNAPSHOT event exists in the window — e.g.
      `git -C .tickets-tracker diff --name-only --diff-filter=A C0..origin/tickets | grep -E '/[0-9].*\\.json$' | grep -v -- '-SNAPSHOT.json'`
      yields only files whose JSON has a non-empty `author_sig`.
      This confirms bug `0ba4`'s signing fix is LIVE across every writer build (local/CI/Gerrit,
      incl. the enrich drain + reconciler) so the flip breaks nothing. Record `C0`, the window,
      and the per-writer signed events observed. If ANY active process still emits an unsigned
      non-SNAPSHOT event, DO NOT FLIP — remediate that writer first.
- [ ] **The flip is atomic and pins the 8d91 anchor.** `identity.require_authenticated = true`
      **and** `enforce_since = 8dcef776c3dd9e68935b74b82137e1ffd8f04f10` land in **one** change; `enforce_since` is written here
      for the first time (no earlier child modifies it) and its value **equals the exact anchor
      SHA documented by 8d91**. Proving command:
      `python -c "import rebar._config_schema as c, rebar.config as cfg; k=cfg.load_config('.').identity; import sys; sys.exit(0 if (k.require_authenticated and k.enforce_since=='8dcef776c3dd9e68935b74b82137e1ffd8f04f10') else 1)"`
      exits 0 (and `git show HEAD:rebar.toml` contains both on the flip commit).
- [ ] **Enforcement is real, not advisory.** After the flip, `rebar verify-identity
      --all --require-authenticated` returns **non-zero** on a new in-scope unsigned/forged event
      (demonstrated in an isolated temp store via 8d91's harness), and the local write-gate
      **refuses** an unsignable non-exempt write with the signing key unset. Both exits recorded.
- [ ] **Under enforcement, every in-scope writer surface passes.** A representative signed write
      on **local** and **CI** shows `authorship: {signed: >=1}` and verifies (its event uuid is
      absent from `rebar verify-identity --all --format json`); the **Gerrit-side** writer passes
      iff 1a51 classified one (it did — the review-bot LINK). Evidence (ticket ids + event uuids)
      recorded on this ticket. No `main` push goes red.
- [ ] **A documented rollback path exists.** The runbook records the single fast-revert change
      (set `identity.require_authenticated = false`, land through Gerrit) to use if a writer
      surface unexpectedly fails post-flip. [operator-attested] the rollback step is captured in
      the runbook (recorded as a comment on this ticket with the exact revert diff + procedure).
baseline.summary: Flip identity.require_authenticated=true with pinned enforce_since in one change

baseline.description:
The inbound UPDATE path never mints an identity for an inbound assignee: it hands the mint a bare STRING, and the mint's first line requires a dict. The mint returns immediately and silently, because it is best-effort by contract. The inbound CREATE path is unaffected, which is exactly why this has gone unseen.

FOUND BY: J11's live cell `test_the_inbound_assignee_mints_a_jira_family_identity` (tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py) on harness run 30767546938, job 91548842532, main @ d72c4777d3 — the first run in which that cell's precondition held and it reached its real assertion. 48 passed / 1 failed, `[jira-live-canary] collected=49 executed=49 skipped=0`.

    AssertionError: THE PASS MINTED NOTHING: jira/'admin' still resolves to no identity in the
    store copy after an inbound pass that carried that assignee.

MECHANISM — PROVEN, NOT INFERRED. Each link is cited, and the chain is reproduced harness-free in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_inbound_update_assignee_mint_5200.py` (4 cells, green):

  1. `inbound_fields._map_jira_to_local_fields:223-225` maps the Jira user object to TWO
     canonical keys — the scalar `assignee` (a bare string from `_extract_jira_field_value`:
     `name`, else `displayName`) and the fixed-shape `assignee_identity`
     ({display, email, account_id}), whose `account_id` ALREADY carries Data Center's username
     (`_identity_of:154-179`, the precedence 5f48 established).
  2. `inbound_differ._diff_jira_vs_local:185-188` emits ONLY the scalar:
     `changed["assignee"] = jira_mapped.get("assignee")`. `assignee_identity` is not in
     `field_map` (`:170-176`), so it never reaches the mutation.
  3. `apply_inbound_records._inbound_update_write_edit_event:333-340` states that these fields
     ARE the differ's local-keyed shape, and `:369` passes `fields["assignee"]` — that string —
     into `_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity`.
  4. `_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity:100-101` opens with
     `if not isinstance(assignee, dict): return`. A string returns before any key is read.
     Nothing is minted and nothing is logged: `:83-102` documents the function as
     "ADDITIVE + best-effort ... any mint failure is swallowed".

  The CREATE path at `:200-203` passes the RAW user object out of the snapshot, which IS a
  dict, so an inbound create mints correctly. Every identity the J11 harness has ever produced
  came from that path — including the one that made this cell's ORIGINAL precondition fail.

WHY THIS IS NOT A SETUP ARTIFACT OF THE CELL. The suspicion was that the cell's unassign/sync step leaves the pass with no assignee CHANGE to act on. It does not: cell 1 of the reproduction runs the real `_diff_jira_vs_local` with a local ticket that is unassigned and a Jira issue assigned to admin — precisely the state the cell arranges — and the differ DOES emit `changed["assignee"]`. So the mint is reached; it declines the value it is given.

WHY IT IS NOT A REGRESSION OF 5f48-244c-7063-42d0. That bug fixed the KEY SELECTION inside the mint (`for key in ("accountId", "name")`) so a DC user object resolves. This defect is upstream of that guard: on the update path the function returns at line 100 before any key is read, so 5f48's fix is never reached. It is a case 5f48 never covered.

SCOPE. The differ and the applier are deployment-neutral, so Cloud has the same gap on the update path; DC ships it, which is why it belongs to this epic (e369's standing precedent for defects in paths DC ships). Its practical effect: a user first seen on an inbound EDIT (rather than on the issue's inbound create) never gets a ghost identity, so a later outbound pass has nothing to key on — the exact failure mode 2f13's ghost-minting exists to prevent.

PROPOSED FIX (NOT YET IMPLEMENTED — needs sign-off; no src/ change has been made). Plumb the identity through instead of loosening the guard:
  * `inbound_differ._diff_jira_vs_local` — when it emits an `assignee` change, ALSO forward
    `jira_mapped["assignee_identity"]` (the mapper already computes it, at no extra extraction);
  * `apply_inbound_records:369` — key the mint on that canonical identity's `account_id` /
    `display` rather than on the scalar.
DO NOT "fix" this by making `_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity` accept a bare string. On Data Center the scalar happens to be `name` (== the external id), so it would look correct here; on Cloud the scalar is the DISPLAY NAME, and minting keyed on it would register every Cloud user under the wrong external id — a silent data defect strictly worse than the missing mint. The reproduction's 4th cell pins the contract a correct fix must meet.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
  * An inbound pass that carries an assignee CHANGE (not only an inbound create) mints/reuses a
    placeholder identity under the shared `jira` family, keyed on the deployment's external id
    (accountId on Cloud, username on DC), and NOT under `jira-datacenter`.
  * `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_inbound_update_assignee_mint_5200.py` is updated so the
    update path is proven to mint and the differ is proven to forward the identity, and cell 3
    stays green so the create path is shown not to regress. CRITERION AMENDED AFTER
    IMPLEMENTATION, and the reason matters: this originally read "cells 2 and 4 invert". Cell 4
    (`test_the_mapper_already_carries_everything_the_mint_needs`) DID invert. **Cell 2
    (`test_the_mint_is_a_no_op_on_the_shape_the_update_path_hands_it`) MUST NOT INVERT**, because
    inverting it would mean asserting that `_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity` ACCEPTS a bare
    string — the one fix this ticket explicitly prohibits, since on DC the scalar is `name`
    (== the external id) and looks right, while on Cloud it is the DISPLAY NAME and would
    register every Cloud user under the wrong id. The implemented fix keeps the mint's dict guard
    untouched and repairs the CALLER instead, so cell 2 correctly keeps its polarity and now
    serves as the regression guard against that wrong fix. The forward behaviour is proven by
    NEW cells (5-7) plus the Cloud accountId guard below. The original wording prescribed a
    mechanism that would have introduced the defect it was meant to prevent; the intent — "the
    update path mints; the differ forwards the identity" — is unchanged and is met.
  * A Cloud-shaped payload ({accountId, displayName} with displayName != accountId) mints keyed
    on the accountId — the guard against the wrong fix above.
  * The J11 live cell `test_the_inbound_assignee_mints_a_jira_family_identity` goes green on a
    harness run WITHOUT any weakening of its assertions.
baseline.summary: inbound UPDATE never mints an assignee identity: the mint gets a string

baseline.description:
## Problem
The verifier's step budget routinely exhausts on legitimate validation, failing criteria as "unmet" that are merely unproven-within-budget (fb8a: request_limit=24, 2 false unmets; pony: repeated exhaustion, 5 then 1 false unmets). The pressure drives operators toward attestation-laundering.

## Design intent (operator-stated)
The budget's ONLY goal is preventing runaway tool use. For valid tool use the floor must be GENEROUS with ample scaling; we never artificially limit authorized validation.

## Current mechanics
`verify_step_floor(c) = clamp(steps_per_criterion x c, step_floor_min, 480)`, defaults 8/48; structured_run halves steps into request_limit (6-AC epic: 48 steps = 24 requests). Defects: (1) story-calibrated cost model — epic criteria traverse child tickets (show_ticket + comments + repo reads, 5-10 requests each) plus fixed overhead, no evidence-surface term; (2) runaway is ALREADY separately guarded (tool_calls_limit, loop detection, the clamp), so a small budget adds no safety, only false FAILs; (3) no cross-run carryover — every re-verify re-proves all criteria (~10 min/cycle).

## Plan
1. Raise defaults: completion_verify_steps_per_criterion 8 -> 24, completion_verify_step_floor_min 48 -> 160 (supersedes the interim operator-machine config mitigation). Raise the 480 clamp to 960 so 24/criterion scales past 20 ACs — the clamp is a runaway ceiling, not a validation cap.
2. Evidence-surface scaling: budget = per_criterion x c + child_traversal x direct_children + fixed_overhead, with defaults child_traversal = 16 steps/direct child and fixed_overhead = 16 steps (mid-band of observed 5-10 requests/child at the 2x steps halving; initial show_ticket+parse sizes the same). Both are new config keys: typed VerifyConfig fields (defaults 16) in _config_schema.py (:249-250 area) AND validators in _config_sections.py:35-36 style. Children counted from the ticket graph at budget-sizing time; any enumeration/read error at the completion.py:780 site fails OPEN to direct_children=0, preserving its "enumeration must not raise" invariant (criteria_count already fail-closes to 0 there, keeping the lean-install typed missing-extra LLMError path). The child term lands INSIDE `verify_step_floor` (new `direct_children: int = 0` param), NOT at the sizing call — its exactly-two consumers, primary sizing (completion.py:780) and `plan_recovery_pool` (completion_banking.py:224), stay on one formula. `plan_recovery_pool` gains a pass-through `direct_children` param (default 0) forwarded by its sole caller (completion_recovery.py:625); its docstring oracle pins (c=8 -> floor 64, N 32, global 48, successor 16; clamp-max) update to 24/160/960 mechanics with childless + childful rows.
3. Cross-run PASS-verdict cache — a NEW ticket-scoped store; the run-scoped `CriterionBank` (completion_banking.py:396-435) stays as designed (run-unique dir = concurrent-close isolation). Cache at `.rebar/cache/completion_verdicts/<ticket>/<criterion-hash>.json`, written ONLY on a validated PASS at finalize (atomic tmp+rename; last-write-wins safe). Invalidation: NOT the whole-repo HEAD tree sha (`_resolve_tree_sha` :358-373 — any unrelated commit rotates it); key each entry by (criterion-text hash, scoped content fingerprint).The scoped fingerprint is NET-NEW code (BankStamps' material_fingerprint hashes PLAN TEXT, not file bytes): a new helper resolves each file_impact path to its git BLOB SHA (batch `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>`) and hashes the sorted (path, blob-sha) pairs; absent path -> sentinel; git failure disables reuse for the run (fail-open to re-verification); when own file_impact is empty but the ticket has children (the epic case), the fingerprint unions direct-child file_impact blobs (DIRECT children from the ticket graph, the same list budget sizing uses) — NOT `_subtree_impacts` (completion_prefetch.py:257; whole-subtree BFS, {path:count} frequencies not blobs, excludes root). Whole-tree sha is the fallback ONLY for childless tickets with empty file_impact. Cache entries store the FULL banked record (met, evidence, citations); at run start (completion_recovery.py:487 `CriterionBank.for_run`) still-valid entries are SEEDED into the run's bank, stamped `seeded: true`. Seeded ids are EXCLUDED from the primary's work surface twice over: (a) `primary_criteria_manifest` (DEFINED completion_banking.py:193, signature (expected, id_by_text); recovery.py:540 is its call site in `_primary_manifest_contract`) gains a `seeded_ids` frozenset param threaded through _primary_manifest_contract and omits those ids; (b) since the manifest is data-only, the primary context ALSO annotates each seeded criterion's prose with an "already credited — do not re-verify" directive, so the primary (launched first, :495) actually skips them. Finalizer interaction: `merge_finalizer_with_bank` today PRESERVES the finalizer's met on echoed records (only the evidence_sufficient marker re-stamps via `_restamp_marker`), so this plan SCOPES A CHANGE: `seeded: true` records bypass finalizer judgment — an echo (incl. a met:false downgrade) is replaced by the bank's validated-PASS record, an omission appended from the bank. Same-run (non-seeded) downgrade preservation unchanged — the rule keys strictly on the seeded flag. RED test: an echo that drops OR downgrades a seeded criterion still yields the credited verdict; a same-run downgrade is still preserved. Exhaustion converges across runs. (Marker semantics from 1d71-a76c: cached entries are PASS-only; insufficiency never cached.)
4. Runaway guards stay authoritative: tool_calls_limit + loop detection unchanged; document at verify_step_floor that the budget exists ONLY for runaway prevention.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Defaults raised (24/160; clamp 960), rationale documented at verify_step_floor; a 6-AC epic sizes to >=80 requests, a 15-AC epic to >=180; formula unit tests, INCLUDING updating the hard-coded pins in tests/interfaces/contracts/test_completion_budget.py (verify_step_floor(1)==48, (8)==64, (40)==320, (100)==480, captured max_iterations==48, _VERIFY_STEP_FLOOR_MAX==480) to the new mechanics.
- [x] Budget sizing adds a child-traversal term inside verify_step_floor (new direct_children param, default 0) so BOTH consumers — completion.py:780 primary sizing and plan_recovery_pool (completion_banking.py:224, forwarded by completion_recovery.py:625) — share the formula; new VerifyConfig fields + _config_sections validators for the two keys; epic-fixture test (childful sizes strictly larger than childless at equal criteria count, primary AND recovery pool; enumeration failure -> direct_children=0, no raise); plan_recovery_pool docstring pins AND the hard-coded pins in tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_banking.py:53-67 (floor/N/global/successor) updated to the new mechanics plus a childful row.
- [x] A re-verify after exhaustion credits still-valid cached PASS verdicts (same scoped fingerprint + criterion text) by seeding them into the run-scoped CriterionBank with the seeded flag; the primary manifest omits seeded ids AND the primary context marks each seeded criterion "already credited — do not re-verify" (both tested); the merge path credits seeded records verbatim (finalizer echo/omission cannot downgrade them) while same-run finalizer downgrades stay preserved; invalidation RED->GREEN on fingerprint or text change, INCLUDING an in-scope content edit (a file under file_impact changes, ticket text unchanged -> blob sha rotates -> cached PASS invalidated); an unrelated commit outside file_impact does NOT invalidate; run-scoped bank concurrent-close isolation regression-tested.
- [x] Runaway protection regression-guarded: tool_calls_limit and loop detection unchanged; a looping-tool fixture still trips the backstop under the larger budget.
(trimmed for admission cap)
baseline.summary: Completion-verifier budget: generous runaway-only floor, evidence-surface scaling, cross-run bank persistence

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Gerrit 1704 (bug knavish-stimulated-bluebottle, merged as f8e6a2507f) gave the enrichment drain lock an owner stamp and a bounded stale-reclaim. The LLM code review passed it +1 but raised four ADVISORY findings on the new code. They are non-blocking and were deliberately not folded into that change, but three are cheap quality gaps in code that shipped and one needs a design decision, so they should not simply evaporate.

## Approach
Take the three cheap ones directly; decide the first one explicitly rather than by default.

1. **Reclaim TOCTOU (needs a decision, `enrich_drain._acquire_advisory_lock`).** There is no
   exclusion between `stamped_file_is_stale` and the `os.unlink`, unlike the mkdir leg, which
   is safe only because its caller already holds the fcntl leg. Two drainers can both condemn
   the same orphan and the loser's unlink can remove the winner's fresh lock, so mutual
   exclusion is defeasible and two drains can run at once. Harm is bounded — the lock only
   prevents redundant WORK and the queue claim is separately optimistic and lease-bounded —
   so this is not a correctness hazard, and it is strictly better than the permanent wedge it
   replaced. Closing it properly means giving the drain lock a kernel leg (`flock`) or an
   atomic create-and-rename, i.e. changing the locking MECHANISM. Decide: accept and document
   the window, or adopt a mechanism. Do NOT leave it undocumented.
2. **Torn-stamp vocabulary (`_describe_drain_lock_holder`).** It collapses an incomplete v2
   stamp into "an unstamped drain lock", while doctor's `_existence_report` distinguishes
   "unknown (incomplete ownership stamp)". Two surfaces describing one artifact should agree.
3. **Untested doctor branches (`doctor_locks._existence_report`).** The drain row's
   "unrecognised ownership stamp" and "incomplete ownership stamp" descriptions have no test.
4. **Untested stamp-write failure (`_acquire_advisory_lock`).** The branch where `os.write`
   raises, logs the unattributable-lock WARNING, and still returns the fd is untested; its
   contract is that the lock stays ceiling-bounded.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` — item 1's outcome (comment or mechanism) and item 2.
- `tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py` — item 4.
- `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor_locks.py` — item 3.

## Testing
A test forcing `os.write` to raise asserts acquisition still succeeds, the WARNING fires, and the resulting unstamped lock is still reclaimable once past the ceiling. Two doctor tests plant a non-v2 stamp and a truncated v2 stamp and assert each `holder_description`. If item 1 adopts a mechanism, a concurrency test drives two acquirers across the reclaim window.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The reclaim window is resolved explicitly: either a code comment states the window and
      why it is acceptable, or a mechanism removes it — verified by reading the diff.
- [ ] `_describe_drain_lock_holder` distinguishes an incomplete v2 stamp from an unstamped
      lock, using the same wording as doctor — asserted by a test on a truncated stamp.
- [ ] The drain row's "unrecognised ownership stamp" description is asserted by a test.
- [ ] The drain row's "incomplete ownership stamp" description is asserted by a test.
- [ ] The stamp-write-failure branch is covered by a test asserting the fd is still returned
      and the WARNING is logged.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and CI's pytest invocation are green.
baseline.summary: Close out the drain-lock code-review advisories

baseline.description:
# op-cert: producer signing seam — gates mint Ed25519 op-certs with the environment key (expand phase)

## Why
The gate producers still sign verdicts with the legacy per-clone HMAC secret via the `signing.sign_manifest` seam. The epic's "Producer-signing & compute-runtime design resolution" settles fork A — **uniform producer signing**: the producers mint `rebar.opcert.v1` DSSE certs with the ambient environment's Ed25519 key, so a local run and a trusted-server run produce the same artifact and there is exactly ONE signature per verdict (no double-signing; the remote handler never signs separately). This story is the expand phase: write-new (Ed25519 op-certs), read-both (envelopes + legacy HMAC records).

**Hard dependency (not yet on `main`):** the storage keystone e4df (Gerrit change 660, in review on the 649←650←660←664 stack) provides `signing.sign_opcert_manifest()` (the envelope-bearing `SIGNATURE` event) and `opcert.opcert_from_record()`. Neither exists on current `origin/main` — this story MUST NOT start until that stack lands, and its first AC pins a mechanical import pre-check so the dependency is enforced, not assumed.

## What
- **The seam is `signing.sign_manifest` itself — a global repoint, not per-site edits.**
  `signing.sign_manifest(ticket_id, manifest, kind=…)` internally mints a `rebar.opcert.v1`
  DSSE op-cert (via the e4df `sign_opcert_manifest` machinery), deriving bound values when the
  caller does not supply them: material fingerprint from the canonical manifest (the kind's
  existing material where present), bound commit from the manifest's `verified-at-sha` line,
  else current `HEAD`. Every existing caller inherits Ed25519; the full blast radius is
  enumerated and each site gets a test:
  - `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:333` (`sign_plan_review` — the plan-review producer);
  - `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:538` (`refresh_attestation` — the drift-refresh
    producer; MUST re-sign as an op-cert so a refresh never downgrades a certified op-cert back
    to an HMAC record in the last-writer-wins attestations map);
  - `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/resign.py:126` (`resign_plan_review`);
  - `src/rebar/signing.py:637` (the `rebar sign` CLI);
  - `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:638` → `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:245` (the MCP `sign_manifest`
    tool).
  After this story no caller HMAC-signs these kinds; the contract story (HMAC removal) then
  deletes the dead HMAC branch.
- **Environment key genesis** (`src/rebar/signing.py`): on first signing use, auto-generate a
  **passphrase-free Ed25519 keypair** at `<tracker>/.opcert-key` / `.opcert-key.pub`
  (`ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N ""`, key file 0600, git-ignored) — mirroring the HMAC
  `.signing-key` genesis it replaces. Genesis is atomic + race-safe with `ssh-keygen`'s two-file
  reality (`ssh-keygen -f <path>` always writes `<path>` AND `<path>.pub`; it cannot write to
  an fd): generate into a private `mkdtemp` 0700 staging dir (`ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N "" -f
  <staging>/key`), then `os.link` the PRIVATE key to `<tracker>/.opcert-key` as the SINGLE
  exclusive-create commit point (`os.link` fails with `EEXIST` if a concurrent first-signer
  won; never `os.replace`, which is not exclusive): the loser ADOPTS the winner's key by
  re-reading the existing file. `.opcert-key.pub` is DERIVATIVE, never a commit point — written
  from the committed private key (`ssh-keygen -y`) and re-derivable any time it is missing.
  The staging dir is removed in a `finally`. DSSE principal/keyid defaults to the
  environment's existing `env_id`; `REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID` overrides (deployment config).
  Verify-side key resolution never creates a key.
- **Key-loss pre-mortem:** a deleted/unreadable key file is regenerated on the next sign (a
  fresh keypair under the same `env_id`); certs signed by the lost key then read as
  not-certified on verify and are re-earned on the next gate run — the same lifecycle as any
  stale attestation, no operator ceremony. Only when regeneration itself is impossible
  (`ssh-keygen` unavailable, tracker directory unwritable) does signing take the degrade path
  below. (Pinned trusted-environment keys are different:
  rotation there follows the epic's era protocol in `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml`.)
- **Close-gate producer**: the completion-verifier sign call in
  `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` rides the same repointed seam; the never-sign
  structural guards (non-PASS, degraded coverage), the material-drift recheck, and the
  `certifiable: false` / `source=="local"` withhold rules are all preserved unchanged.
- **Read path (expand) — the dispatch rule is explicit.** `signing.verify_record` (the single
  verify chokepoint `verify_signature` and `compute_validity` sit on) dispatches on the RECORD
  SHAPE. Mechanically, the dispatch lives in a shape-aware wrapper (e.g.
  `verify_attestation_record(record, ticket_id, *, repo_root)`), because the existing
  `verify_record(record, ticket_id, key)` takes the raw HMAC secret and cannot carry an op-cert
  trust root: legacy `signature`-bearing records route to the UNCHANGED
  `verify_record` + HMAC secret; `envelope`-bearing records route to
  `attest.registry.verify(OPCERT_KIND, envelope, trust_root)` — matching `registry.verify(kind,
  envelope, trust_root)` — under the substrate's OWN kind (the `Policy(SshsigScheme,
  namespace=OPCERT_NAMESPACE)` entry `opcert.register_opcert_policy()` registers;
  `OPCERT_KIND = OPCERT_NAMESPACE = "rebar.opcert.v1"`, the constants in `attest/opcert.py`,
  giving domain separation from `rebar.authorship.v1`), with `trust_root` built from the
  environment's own public key via `authorship.allowed_signers_from_keys([own_pub],
  principal)`. EVERY `verify_record` caller moves to the wrapper — the complete inventory (grep-verified):
  `signing.verify_signature` (signing.py:675), `signing.verify_attestations` (signing.py:692 —
  the all-kinds iterator), and `_engine_support/validate.py:117` (`signature_findings`). The
  wrapper's translation rule for envelope records is a LITERAL table (downstream readers see
  the existing contract unchanged; `key_id` carries the record's `principal`, which keeps
  `drift_refresh_candidate`'s provenance read — `llm/plan_review/attest.py:529`,
  `result.get("key_id")` — working as-is):
  - `record.principal != own env_id` → the WRAPPER returns `verdict: "foreign_key"`,
    `certified: false` WITHOUT invoking the scheme (there is no key to verify with — exactly
    today's HMAC `foreign_key` semantics; `SshsigScheme` itself never emits `foreign_key`);
  - `record.principal == own env_id` → `registry.verify(OPCERT_KIND, envelope, root)` and the
    `Verdict` maps `verified → certified`, `verdict → verdict` (pass-through), `reason →
    reason`. The strings this path can emit, verbatim from the code: `"certified"`,
    `"mismatch"`, `"invalid"` (malformed principal/namespace), `"unavailable"` (ssh-keygen
    missing — `sshsig.py:110`), plus the registry's defensive `"unknown_kind"` /
    `"unknown_scheme"`. (`"key_not_valid_at_era"` is emitted only by the merge-gate era path,
    `opcert.verify_opcert`, and is already in the schema enum.) The attestation kind's
  legacy POLICY pins are NOT touched: `POLICY["plan-review"]` / `POLICY["completion-verifier"]`
  remain HMAC-pinned through the expand phase and are removed by the contract story (8f1d). The
  envelope is verified against the environment's own public key
  (`.opcert-key.pub`) for same-environment verification — a cert whose `principal` is another
  environment is classified `foreign_key` BY THE WRAPPER per the translation table below (the
  scheme is never invoked for it); a record carrying
  the legacy `signature` (HMAC hex) field routes to the unchanged HMAC path (removed later by
  the contract story). The event/record plumbing is the e4df dependency's CONTRACT — consumed here, not
  re-built, and asserted BEHAVIORALLY at story start by the dependency-gate AC (rather than
  taken on faith): the envelope-bearing `SIGNATURE` event, the reducer passthrough of
  `envelope`/`principal`/bound fields into `attestations[kind]`, and `opcert_from_record`
  read-back. The envelope-bearing record RETAINS the `manifest` list exactly as the
  legacy record carries it (envelope and manifest coexist on the e4df record), so
  `compute_validity`'s manifest-derived checks (`manifest_deps` / `manifest_material` /
  `manifest_regver` / `signing.verified_at_sha_from_manifest`) read it unchanged.
  Validity-on-read lifecycle rules (reopen, code drift,
  material drift) apply to envelope attestations identically. Worked example of the shape:
  `attestations["plan-review"]` holds `{algorithm: "sshsig", envelope: "<encoded DSSE>",
  material_fingerprint: "<hex>", merged_log_commit: "<sha>", principal: "<env_id>"}` (no HMAC
  hex), where `merged_log_commit` is the commit the gate verified against — the manifest's
  `verified-at-sha` line (the seam's bound-commit derivation above; the e4df event already
  carries the field) — and `verify_signature(ticket, kind="plan-review")` returns its existing
  result shape with `certified: true` and the op-cert verdict string (`certified`) — the exact
  field contract is pinned by the existing `verify_signature_result.schema.json`.
- **Downstream `signature`-field consumers are enumerated and updated** (they would otherwise
  break or mis-report on envelope records):
  - `src/rebar/signing.py:648` — the `rebar sign` text-mode report hardcodes
    `record['signature'][:16]`; updated to render the envelope digest + principal for op-cert
    records (no `KeyError`);
  - `src/rebar/_engine_support/validate.py` `signature_findings()` — checks
    `record.get('signature')` and would report envelope-bearing records as `unsigned`; updated
    to route through the same `verify_record` shape dispatch.
- **Output-schema contract** (`docs/output-schemas.md` seam): `sign_result.schema.json` — and
  the `SignResultOut` Pydantic model that the MCP `sign_manifest` tool validates against
  (`src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:245`) and that `rebar sign --output json` conforms to — currently
  REQUIRES a `signature` (HMAC hex) field; the op-cert record carries `envelope` instead. `verify_signature_result.schema.json`'s CLOSED `verdict` enum (currently `["unsigned",
  "foreign_key", "certified", "mismatch", "key_not_valid_at_era"]`) is widened with EXACTLY the
  four strings the op-cert dispatch path can newly emit — `"invalid"`, `"unavailable"`
  (`SshsigScheme.verify`, sshsig.py:110/125), `"unknown_kind"`, `"unknown_scheme"`
  (`registry.verify`, registry.py:100/107); `certified`/`mismatch`/`key_not_valid_at_era` are
  already present — a backward-compatible enum extension, with the schema-drift test
  regenerated. The sign-result
  shape is updated in ALL THREE of its artifacts together: `sign_result.schema.json`,
  `_mcp_models.py::SignResultOut` (`signature` required → optional alongside `envelope`), and
  the `types.py::SignResult` TypedDict (lines 215-224; `signature: str` becomes
  `NotRequired`). Expand-phase, the schema admits BOTH result shapes (the legacy HMAC shape
  and the envelope shape `{algorithm: "sshsig", envelope, principal, material_fingerprint,
  merged_log_commit, …}` with `signature` no longer required); the contract story (8f1d) later
  tightens it to envelope-only.
- **Degrade, never wedge**: if `ssh-keygen` (OpenSSH ≥ 8.9, `sshsig.ensure_available()`) is
  unavailable or the key is unreadable and cannot be regenerated, signing records the existing
  in-band `{signed: false, error: …}` outcome; no local operation is blocked by signing itself.
  A project whose claim/close gate requires the signature then blocks at that gate with a clear
  install-OpenSSH remediation message.

## Scope
- In: the global `sign_manifest` seam repoint + the five enumerated call sites; key genesis +
  principal resolution; expand-phase read path; the `sign_result.schema.json` / `SignResultOut`
  contract update; tests below.
- Out: HMAC removal (the contract story, 8f1d); the remote service and its client command
  (ee0b); AWS IaC (the deploy story); any change to gate YAMLs or verdict schemas.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Dependency gate (behavioral): on the branch this story builds on (the e4df stack has
      landed), the import check `python -c "from rebar.signing import sign_opcert_manifest; from rebar.attest.opcert import opcert_from_record"`
      succeeds AND a round-trip passes — `sign_opcert_manifest` on a fixture ticket yields a
      reduced state whose `attestations[kind]` carries `envelope`/`principal`/bound fields and
      `opcert_from_record` returns the envelope; recorded as the story's first verification
      step (this asserts e4df's reducer/event contract instead of claiming it).
- [ ] First signing use in a fresh environment generates `<tracker>/.opcert-key`(+`.pub`),
      passphrase-free Ed25519, mode 0600, git-ignored, via the body's exclusive-create mechanism (0700 staging dir, `os.link` of
      the private key as the sole commit point, derivative `.pub` — never `os.replace`); a test
      asserts genesis, permissions, exclusive-create under a concurrent first-sign race (exactly
      one keypair survives; the loser adopts it — no overwrite), and that verify-side resolution
      never creates a key.
- [ ] A passing plan review produces an envelope-bearing `SIGNATURE` event (no HMAC hex) whose
      DSSE subject binds `{ticket_id, material_fingerprint, verified-at sha, kind="plan-review"}`;
      a test asserts `verify_signature(kind="plan-review")` certifies it in the same environment
      and that the never-sign guards (non-PASS / degraded coverage) still refuse to sign.
- [ ] Drift-refresh and resign re-sign as op-certs: tests drive `refresh_attestation` and
      `resign_plan_review` and assert the resulting record still carries a DSSE envelope (a
      refresh never downgrades an op-cert to an HMAC record).
- [ ] The MCP `sign_manifest` tool and the `rebar sign` CLI emit envelope-bearing events via the
      same seam; a test drives each end-to-end and asserts the DSSE envelope is present.
- [ ] A gated close produces an envelope-bearing `SIGNATURE` event (kind `completion-verifier`)
      via the same seam; a test asserts the material-drift recheck still withholds signing on
      drift and `certifiable: false` still closes unsigned.
- [ ] Expand-phase read-both: a test asserts a legacy HMAC attestation written before this change
      still verifies/reads as today, alongside a new envelope attestation on the same ticket
      (kind-keyed coexistence per the additive attestations model).
- [ ] `REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID` overrides the DSSE principal; absent, the principal equals the
      environment's `env_id`; a test asserts both.
- [ ] With `ssh-keygen` unavailable (patched `ensure_available`), or the key file unreadable
      AND regeneration impossible (unwritable tracker dir), a
      plan-review PASS records the in-band `{signed: false, …}` outcome and the operation exits
      successfully; a test asserts the claim gate then reports the missing-attestation block
      with a remediation that names OpenSSH ≥ 8.9.
- [ ] `sign_result.schema.json` and `SignResultOut` admit the envelope-bearing result shape
      (and, expand-phase, still admit the legacy HMAC shape); a test validates a real op-cert
      sign result against the schema, and the MCP `sign_manifest` tool returns it without
      validation error.
- [ ] Read-path dispatch: a test asserts the shape-aware wrapper (`verify_attestation_record`)
      routes an envelope-bearing record to the op-cert verifier and a `signature`-bearing record
      to the unchanged `verify_record` HMAC path, on the same store.
- [ ] Consumer regressions: tests assert `rebar sign` text-mode output renders an op-cert
      record without error, and `_engine_support/validate.py` `signature_findings()` does not
      report a certified envelope-bearing record as unsigned.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green.
baseline.summary: op-cert: producer signing seam — gates mint Ed25519 op-certs with the environment key (expand phase)
