# The DC harness errored all 62 cells at setup: an ORDERING DEADLOCK in the Epic-field readiness gate

## CORRECTION: this ticket's original root cause was WRONG

**Originally filed (by me) as "9790's field-readiness budget is too short".** That diagnosis was false, and `review-plan` blocked the plan for it. Recorded here rather than quietly rewritten, because the wrong version is the more instructive artifact.

I took the decision rule out of 9790's own `not_ready_message` — *"if the inventory contains no `customfield_*` entries whatsoever the plugin is still starting and the budget is too short"* — and treated it as a measurement. **That rule is wrong AND self-confirming**: an empty custom-field inventory is exactly what a Jira instance with no project returns, so it "confirms" itself under the one condition it cannot distinguish. It misdiagnosed 9790's own author, then me, then this ticket, and it cost a 50-minute harness run. I made it worse by instructing the implementing agent not to re-derive it. The agent verified first anyway and refuted it.

## The PROVEN root cause: an ordering deadlock

**GreenHopper provisions `Epic Link` / `Epic Name` when the FIRST Jira Software project is created.** 9790's gate waited for those fields at SESSION START — before any project exists — so it waited for a capability that only the action it was blocking could create. No budget can satisfy it.

Discriminating experiment, GitHub Actions run **30981084637** (run on the ~15-min probe workflow, not the ~50-min harness):

    before any project                    27 fields,  0 customfield_*,  Epic Link False
    after 180s QUIET, still no project    27 fields,  0 customfield_*,  Epic Link False
    0.05s AFTER project create (HTTP 201) 55 fields, 13 customfield_*,  Epic Link TRUE

The quiet-settle leg is what makes it discriminating: it supplies **time without the action**, and time did nothing. That single cause explains every symptom — both the 600s and the 1800s budgets failing with byte-identical inventories, the container sitting idle (`Startup is complete` at 05:40:58, `Plugins upgrades completed successfully` at 05:41:53, then ~29 minutes of silence), run 30964805133 passing 62/62 before the gate landed, and both probe runs failing the same way since 1387.

## Evidence of the failure

Harness run **30975323866** at `31f352d535`: **1 xfailed, 62 ERRORS in 606.98s** — every cell errored at fixture setup, none ran. The preceding run **30964805133** at `c3fb869ab5` (before the gate landed) was **62 passed, 1 xfailed, 0 failed**.

## The fix — the budget went DOWN, not up

Check the Epic fields **after** provisioning, not at session start. Because provisioning is measured at **0.0512s** (run 30981084637; confirmed 0.032-0.058s, always 1 poll, 57 times in run 30982731669), the budget was **lowered 600s -> 120s** — ~2400x the measurement, still bounded so a genuine degrade fails in two minutes instead of ten. Raising it, which the original plan proposed, would have made every failure slower without making any of them pass.

9790's misleading message text is rewritten as part of this fix, so the refuted rule cannot mislead the next reader.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] the readiness check runs where the capability can actually exist — after provisioning — and the
      ORDERING is the fix, not the budget
- [x] the budget is sized from a MEASURED provisioning time with the measurement recorded (run id +
      observed delay) as a cited constant, not guessed
- [x] the harness run is GREEN end to end (0 failed, 0 errored cells) on `main`, with the run id
      recorded
- [x] the wait still FAILS loudly on a genuine degrade (custom fields present but not the Epic ones),
      pinned by a test whose fixture varies that axis
- [x] `JIRA_DC_FIELD_READY_TIMEOUT`'s default and override path are documented where an operator
      hitting a timeout will find them

## Verification

* **Green on `main`:** harness run **30986591446** at `0df44dcbc9` — `62 passed, 1 xfailed`, canary
  `collected=63 executed=62 skipped=1`, **0 failed / 0 errored**, no FAILED or ERROR lines in the log.
  This is epic [rebar:e369-a449-4773-48fb]'s exit-bar evidence.
* **Degrade path still loud:** `test_a_degraded_image_still_fails_the_capability_check_loudly`
  (`tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_conftest.py:382`), with five mutations each returning RED — including
  `ready=True` on expiry (the exact blindness 9790 removed) and restoring the deadlock itself.
* **Measurement cited in code:** `scripts/jira_dc_field_readiness.py` names run 30981084637 and
  `elapsed_after_create=0.0512` as a constant, specifically so the next reader does not re-derive it.

## Testing

    gh workflow run "Live External Integration" --ref main
    pytest tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_conftest.py -q
baseline.summary: The DC harness errored all 62 cells at setup: an ordering deadlock in the Epic-field readiness gate

# ACLI subprocess 429 handling: bounded backoff, honor Retry-After if available

## Context
All ACLI calls go through `_run_acli` (`acli_subprocess.py`), which retries all non-zero exit codes (except 401/assignee) with a uniform 2s/4s sleep. `_call_with_retry` (`dispatch_one.py:100-144`) adds 429/5xx classification and already raises the EXISTING `RetryExhaustedError` (`_errors.py`). `_call_with_backoff` (`acli_subprocess.py:236-292`) is dead code (no production call sites; it wraps `urllib`, NOT the subprocess `CalledProcessError` domain). ACLI is a subprocess, so Jira `Retry-After` availability is UNVERIFIED.

## What (minimal, contract-preserving — a plan, not an implementation)
1. PROBE FIRST: against a rate-limited/staged endpoint, record (a) whether `Retry-After` is parseable in stderr,
   (b) the exit code ACLI returns on HTTP 429, (c) whether ACLI retries 429 internally. Record on the ticket.
2. Add 429-aware jittered exponential backoff with a BOUNDED max-retry/total ceiling to the LIVE `_run_acli` retry
   loop (so continuous 429s cannot hang the subprocess). Honor `Retry-After` IFF the probe confirmed it; else
   backoff without it. If ACLI retries 429 internally, no Python-layer change for 429 (documented).
   CONTRACT-PRESERVING: the ceiling only BOUNDS attempts — on exhaustion `_run_acli` raises exactly what it raises
   today (`CalledProcessError`). Do NOT introduce or surface a new exception type from `_run_acli`; the 9 call
   sites' contract is unchanged. (`RetryExhaustedError` stays where it is, in the app-layer `_call_with_retry`.)
3. Retryable-code scope: ADD-ON (recommended) — the 429 branch REPLACES the uniform sleep for that attempt (no
   double-sleep); all other exit codes keep their current retry behavior (zero caller impact). NARROW to
   {429,502,503} would break other non-zero codes and is OUT OF SCOPE unless separately decided.
4. `_call_with_backoff` (dead) is OPTIONAL cleanup only, NOT required by this ticket. If a follow-up removes it,
   that follow-up also drops its `acli.py:57` import, its `__all__` entry, and the `test_error_taxonomy.py`
   reference — but this ticket leaves it untouched.
5. PRESERVE the non-idempotent-write guard (`AcliTimeoutError` is not a `TimeoutError`).
6. Observability: log rate-limit detection, backoff trigger, Retry-After honored-vs-unavailable, ceiling reached.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Probe recorded: Retry-After availability, the 429 exit code, whether ACLI retries 429 internally (+ the Python outcome for the internal case).
- [ ] Bounded jittered exp-backoff added to the live `_run_acli` loop; honors Retry-After IFF probe-confirmed; add-on mode does not double-sleep; on exhaustion the EXISTING `CalledProcessError` contract is unchanged (no new exception surfaced to the 9 callers).
- [ ] Other non-zero exit codes retain current retry behavior (ADD-ON); NARROW is explicitly out of scope.
- [ ] No-blind-retry-on-timeout guard preserved; new backoff covered by a case in `tests/.../test_acli_subprocess_timeout.py`.
- [ ] Rate-limit/backoff/Retry-After/ceiling events logged; the retry policy is captured in an ADR/design note.
baseline.summary: Align ACLI bulk-path 429 handling with the REST path (honor Retry-After)

## Why

Offline fixtures can establish the rubric's discrimination, but the epic succeeds only when the deployed Gerrit review bot loads the criterion from the reviewed rebar repository and carries it through the real four-pass pipeline. The first rollout must collect evidence without blocking contributors.

A live Gerrit probe is required because only the deployed bot's webhook-to-checkout-to-prompt path can prove end-to-end project-criterion execution; an offline replay would mock or bypass the repository-resolution behavior this story is intended to dogfood.

## What

Run an advisory-only Gerrit dogfood probe after the seam repair and project criterion land. Use one Gerrit change with four sequential patchsets against the review-system prompt surface:

1. A positive control adds this exact discovery/evidence refinement: `Before emitting, isolate
   the shortest changed clause that directs a review phase to act. Name the instructed phase, the
   assigned action, and the phase that owns that action. If the changed text does not identify all
   three, abstain instead of inferring an ownership violation.` The boundary criterion emits no
   finding.
2. Preserve the historical severity-only probe unchanged: `For each candidate finding, assign
   severity as high, medium, or low.` Record that it abstains because it does not identify the
   instructed and owning phases; this is evidence about stimulus limits, not criterion execution.
3. Use the predeclared balanced-corpus FIRE control RP-F2: `Pass 1 sets severity, confidence,
   blocking status, and remediation for every finding.` Capture the project-attributed advisory
   finding and its Pass-2/Pass-3 data.
4. A final patchset removes the FIRE sentence, retains only the valid positive-control refinement,
   and is the sole revision submitted to `main`.

## Preconditions

Before the probe, an operator confirms the configured `gerrit` remote targets rebar's Gerrit and that the deployed review bot posts `LLM-Review` results for this repository. Record the remote URL, change id, patchset SHA, UTC timestamp, and bot vote/message on this ticket. If the bot is absent or misconfigured, do not substitute an offline run: create an operational bug linked `discovered_from`, mark this story blocked, and resume only after the live prerequisite is restored. Allow 60 minutes after each patchset upload for its `LLM-Review` message; after that window, follow the same operational-bug and blocked-story path.

For this story, an acceptable review trace is the `code_review_result_v2` payload from the ambient ticket-store artifact titled `code-review: <change-id> @ <revision>`, pasted into a ticket comment. It must contain the reviewed `revision`, `coverage.llm_ran: true`, and the `blocking`, `advisory`, `dropped`, and `indeterminate` lists. The predeclared RP-F2 FIRE probe provides direct project-criterion execution proof: its finding must carry `reviewer_id: code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries` and `criteria: [project.review-phase-boundaries]`. The positive control is deliberately a comparative observation—same Gerrit change, unchanged routing/bot, LLM coverage present, and no project-criterion entry in any verdict list—not a claim about unavailable per-criterion forwarding counters.

## Scope

- Keep `blocking_enabled: false` for the entire probe. `block_threshold: 0.90` is recorded but
  inert; no change in this story enables blocking.
- Record Gerrit change id, each patchset SHA, UTC timestamp, vote/message, project criterion finding,
  Pass-2 validity/impact attributes, Pass-3 priority/decision/threshold/posture, and final amended
  patchset outcome as ticket comments.
- Confirm the project-only physical prompt id ran against the RP-F2 FIRE-control patchset SHA using
  its stamped `reviewer_id`; compare the positive and cleaned revisions using the same artifact
  schema without claiming a nonexistent execution-count field.
- Leave the repository with only valid review instructions. Threshold calibration and a future
  `blocking_enabled: true` decision require a separate ticket backed by accumulated real-review
  data; this story neither selects a lower threshold nor promotes the criterion.

This story is observational: it does not change the rubric in response to probe results. A rubric or seam defect discovered by the probe is captured as a new ticket linked `discovered_from` and is fixed only through that separately reviewed work.

If the historical severity-only directive abstains, preserve that patchset and trace unchanged. Use only the already-committed RP-F2 balanced-corpus FIRE case as the discriminating follow-up; do not tune or improvise a new probe. If RP-F2 does not produce the project-attributed finding, record the unexpected trace, create a rubric/seam bug linked `discovered_from`, and mark this story blocked.

After the final patchset, post a calibration handoff comment on this ticket with the exact labels `Priority distribution:` and `Blocking promotion: deferred`; the latter must name a future, separately reviewed, data-backed posture ticket as the only path to enabling blocking.

Out of scope: changing the rubric, collecting multi-day adoption metrics, changing the impact model, or enabling blocking.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [operator-attested] The Gerrit remote and review-bot precondition is recorded with remote URL,
  change id, patchset SHA, UTC timestamp, and bot vote/message before either probe is evaluated.
- [ ] Before and after all probe patchsets, project routing remains `block_threshold: 0.90` and
  `blocking_enabled: false`; verify with
  `.venv/bin/python -c 'import json; r=json.load(open(".rebar/criteria_routing.json"))["code_review"]["project.review-phase-boundaries"]; assert r["block_threshold"] == 0.90 and r["blocking_enabled"] is False'`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] A positive-control Gerrit patchset is recorded with change id, patchset
  SHA, UTC timestamp, and an acceptable artifact payload with `coverage.llm_ran: true`. Routing and
  bot deployment are unchanged across the four patchsets, and no entry in `blocking`, `advisory`,
  `dropped`, or `indeterminate` names `project.review-phase-boundaries` for this valid
  discovery/evidence refinement; entries from unrelated criteria do not affect the comparison.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The historical severity-only patchset is recorded unchanged with change id,
  patchset SHA, UTC timestamp, sentence, and acceptable artifact payload. Its repeated abstention
  and absence from every project-attributed verdict bucket are recorded as a stimulus limitation,
  not treated as proof.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The predeclared RP-F2 FIRE-control patchset is recorded with change id,
  patchset SHA, UTC timestamp, exact corpus sentence, and an acceptable artifact payload. Its
  grounded `advisory` finding carries `reviewer_id: code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries`
  and `criteria: [project.review-phase-boundaries]`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The ticket comment records the project-attributed advisory entry's
  observed Pass-2 `validity`, `impact`, and at least two named `verification.binary` answers from
  the persisted artifact. These are observations from the run, not predeclared invariant values.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The ticket comment records the entry's observed Pass-3 `priority` and
  the deterministic routing outcome `decision: advisory`, `block_threshold: 0.90`, and
  `blocking_enabled: false`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] All negative directives are absent from the final submitted patchset, the
  project criterion emits no phase-boundary finding on that revision, and the recorded final
  revision contains only phase-compliant instructions. This fourth patchset of the same Gerrit
  change is the only probe revision submitted to `main`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] A ticket comment contains the exact labels `Priority distribution:` with
  the observed Pass-3 values and `Blocking promotion: deferred` with an explicit handoff to a future,
  separately reviewed, data-backed posture ticket.
- [ ] The final cleaned dogfood change is landed on `main`; verify with
  `.venv/bin/python -c 'import subprocess; commits=subprocess.check_output(["git", "log", "origin/main", "--format=%H", "--grep=rebar-ticket: 9447-b31c-e0b7-446d"], text=True).split(); assert commits, "dogfood commit is not on origin/main"'`.

## Dependencies

Depends on the landed repository-root seam repair `3ba4-c0d1-1813-44a5` and the project-criterion authoring story `225a-323c-a9f6-436b`. The former umbrella `2c14-fa5f-1228-4e02` and child bug `8a4b-e8b6-1bf9-48d8` were superseded and closed.
baseline.summary: Dogfood the review-phase-boundaries criterion in advisory Gerrit reviews

## Summary
The reducer's strategy layer is dead code: reduce_ticket accepts/defaults LastTimestampWinsStrategy but never calls strategy.resolve, and replay performs NO UUID dedup — duplicate-UUID event files double-apply.

## Reproduction Steps
(verified on installed 0.4.0 == HEAD, temp store)
1. Create a ticket; rebar comment <id> "only-once".
2. Copy the COMMENT event file to a new filename (same uuid in payload, ts+1s).
3. rebar show <id> -> comments == ["only-once","only-once"].

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected (documented at ticket_reducer/_api.py:31-44): "dedup by UUID (first occurrence wins), sort by timestamp".
- Actual: _processors.py:347-416 replays raw files in FILENAME order, no UUID dedup (only snapshot-source-uuids skipped), sorted by filename timestamp not event timestamp. MostStatusEventsWinsStrategy equally unreachable. Verified: no .resolve( call site in ticket_reducer/.

## Impact
Merge-as-union convergence leans on UUID-level determinism; duplicate-UUID files (recovery cherry-picks, manual copies, fsck-recover paths) silently double-apply comments/edits/links.

## Source
- src/rebar/_engine/ticket_reducer/_api.py:197-244 (unused strategy param/default)
- src/rebar/_engine/ticket_reducer/_processors.py:347-416 (replay loop)

## Fix direction
Decide: (a) wire the strategy into replay (load -> strategy.resolve -> process), or (b) delete the dead strategy classes/param and add a minimal seen-UUID skip in replay_events, documenting filename-order replay. See validation notes comment for measured blast radius of each (incl. test_ticket_reducer_conflict.py interactions) before choosing.

## Suggested RED test
Duplicate-UUID event under a second filename -> applied exactly once; existing conflict-resolution tests stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Duplicate-UUID events apply once (RED test first)
- [ ] Decision recorded: wire-strategy vs minimal-dedup + dead-code deletion
- [ ] tests/scripts/test_ticket_reducer_conflict.py and reducer suites green
- [ ] _api.py docstring matches the actual replay semantics afterward
baseline.summary: Reducer strategy is dead code: no UUID dedup on replay (duplicate-UUID events double-apply)

## Context / Problem

Three agents on 2026-08-05 reported contradictory answers to "does ticking an AC checkbox invalidate a plan-review attestation?". The contradiction is a DIAGNOSTIC defect, not a behavioral one, and the empirical answer is now settled (see Findings). Every attestation staleness message today names a fixed, partly-fictional list of inputs, so a reader cannot tell which input actually changed and hunts for an edit that could never have been the cause. The operator has approved fixing this broadly: wherever rebar reports an attestation error, it must say WHAT CHANGED. That approval covers this ticket's whole scope, including the additive manifest change described below.

## Findings that fix the scope (verified in this checkout)

- The material basis is a SINGLE composite sha256, built in
  `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` `material_fingerprint()` over exactly four keys —
  `ticket_id`, `description`, `file_impact`, `children` — plus `file_impact_scope` when the
  scope is `none`. Verified by reading `pass1.py:750-777`.
- AC checkbox STATE is normalized out of that basis by
  `pass1.py::_normalize_checkbox_state` (`pass1.py:741-747`, bug 330c). Ticking `- [ ]` to
  `- [x]` therefore does NOT invalidate an attestation. Confirmed by running
  `material_fingerprint` over a tick-only description pair: the hashes are equal.
- "AC" is NOT a basis component. Acceptance criteria live inside `description`. Every current
  message says "description/AC/file_impact/children", naming an input that does not exist.
- A pre-330c attestation hashed the RAW description, so after a tick neither the normalized
  recompute nor the `attest.py::_legacy_material_ok` grandfather (`attest.py:614-631`) can
  match, and it reads `stale-material` with no component actually edited. This is the residual
  cause the current message hides, and it reconciles observation 3 in the original report.
- `children` is derived from OTHER tickets' `parent_id` at read time
  (`relation_snapshot.py::live_material_children`), not from this ticket's own event log.
- The signed manifest ALREADY carries per-child/prerequisite pins —
  `plan-material-pin: <role> <id> <fingerprint>` parsed by `manifest.py::manifest_pins`
  (`manifest.py:428-457`) — so the signed child-id set is recoverable from any pinned
  attestation without any schema change.

## Approach

Add per-component fingerprints to the signed manifest and diff them component-wise on read.

Concretely:

1. New module `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/material_diff.py`. It owns the basis
   (`material_basis(ctx)`, which `pass1.material_fingerprint` now calls, so the composite and
   the per-component view cannot disagree) and `material_components(ctx)`, which returns
   `{name: (hash16, size)}` for each basis key. The `size` is a plain integer count of that
   component — characters for `description`, entries for `file_impact` / `children` — and it is
   load-bearing, not decoration: a 16-char hash is one-way, so without a recorded count the
   message could say only "description changed", never "4210 -> 4396 chars". A count discloses
   no content. `explain_material_change(attestation, ticket_id, repo_root)` returns the compact
   human clause naming the components that differ.
2. `manifest.py::build_manifest` emits one additive, deterministic line per component:
   `material-part: <name> <hash16> <size>`, sorted by name — exactly four whitespace-separated
   tokens including the prefix. `manifest.py` gains `manifest_material_parts()` to parse them
   back into `{name: (hash16, size)}`. The lines are additive, so an existing verifier ignores
   them and a pre-change manifest simply parses to `{}`. The prefix cannot collide with
   `manifest_material()`, which matches `startswith("material:")`.
3. `attest.py::compute_validity` calls `explain_material_change` for BOTH `stale-material`
   returns (plan-review at `attest.py:588-601` and completion-verifier at `attest.py:527-538`)
   and puts the named components in `reason`. It also names the reopen timestamp on
   `stale-reopened` and keeps the already-specific `stale-code` / `stale-head` wording (both
   already name the drifted paths / the two SHAs).
4. `attest_gate.py::claim_gate_check`'s `unsigned` message (`attest_gate.py:121-126`) states
   both remedies, because rebar cannot distinguish "never reviewed" from "review PASSed but
   signing aborted": run `rebar review-plan <id>`, or `rebar sign-review <id>` if a review
   already passed. `claim_gate_check` already forwards `compute_validity`'s `reason` verbatim,
   and `_commands/transition_close.py::_raise_plan_review_close_gate_error` and
   `_commands/claim.py` render that same string, so fixing the source fixes the claim gate, the
   close gate and `review-plan --status` together.
5. The sites that re-word or drop the reason instead of forwarding it are pointed at the same
   helper or made to carry the data they already hold:
   - `generation.py:265-269` and `resign.py:198-208` — replace the fixed list with the named
     components.
   - `generation.py:270-273` — "a dependency's plan material changed since the review" names no
     dependency, although the changed pin set is in hand; `resign.py:262-270` already names the
     ids, so this one is brought to parity.
   - `completion.py:178` — a child's closure-validity detail is currently
     `f"signature: {sig.get('verdict')}"`, dropping the reason that explains it; it forwards the
     reason too.
   - `_cli/_llm_commands.py:118-141` — a signing failure whose reason is a relation-snapshot
     READ failure currently renders the generic "run `rebar sign-review`" advice, which is
     wrong: a re-sign re-collects the same generation and hits the same unreadable read. It
     gets its own branch naming the reason and the real remedy. The branch is keyed on the
     REASON, not the event: `plan_review_sign_aborted` is the base-class event that also covers
     arbitrary terminal signing errors, for which `sign-review` remains the correct recovery.
     The discriminator is membership in `PlanRelationSnapshotError.REASONS` (the existing
     closed vocabulary at `relation_snapshot.py:26-33`: `store-read-failure`, `missing-target`,
     `ambiguous-reference`, `malformed-reference`, `reducer-error`, `canonical-id-mismatch`);
     every other abort keeps today's `sign-review` advice unchanged.
   - `attest_gate.py:166-167` — the docstring's verdict vocabulary omits `not-closed`,
     `malformed-phase`, `incompatible-phase` and the `stale-pin-*` values; corrected so the
     documented list matches what `compute_validity` can actually return.

   These were found by an exhaustive sweep of every attestation refusal surface. Surfaces
   deliberately left unchanged because they already forward the reason verbatim:
   `_commands/gates.py::_claim_gate_reason`, `_commands/transition_close.py`, and
   `llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py`. `attest/opcert.py` and `signing.py` are also left
   alone: their verdicts are cryptographic (`mismatch` / `foreign_key`), not staleness, and
   already name the two keys or ids that differ.

Why this approach: the composite hash is one-way, so naming a changed component requires the old per-component values, and the only trustworthy source for them is the SIGNED manifest — anything reconstructed at read time could disagree with what the reviewer actually saw. The alternative of replaying the event store to `signed_at` is rejected: `children` comes from other tickets' state, so it would need a whole-store replay, and compaction squashes exactly the old events where legacy attestations live. Adding the parts to the manifest is additive, authenticated by the existing HMAC, and deterministic (no timestamps), so re-signing stays reproducible.

Attestations signed before this change carry no `material-part:` lines. For them `explain_material_change` degrades in two useful steps rather than falling back to the old fixed list: it uses the signed `plan-material-pin:` child ids to report a `children` add/remove diff when one exists, and when no component difference can be named it says so plainly and points at the pre-330c normalization basis as the likely cause, with the remedy.

No gate outcome changes: every edit is inside the `reason` string of an already-failing branch, or is a new additive manifest line. No branch condition, threshold or verdict value is touched.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/material_diff.py` (new) — the material basis, component hashing,
  and the diff/explain helpers.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` — `material_fingerprint` delegates its basis to
  `material_diff.material_basis` so the composite and the per-component view cannot diverge.
  This also moves 24 lines out of a file sitting at 776 of the 800-line cap.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/relation_snapshot.py` — extract `current_plan_context` from
  `current_material_fingerprint_impl` so the composite and the component view read the same
  state.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py` — emit and parse `material-part:` lines.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py` and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py` — record
  the same per-component fingerprints on the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar so `sign-review` can name
  the component too.
- `src/rebar/schemas/plan_review_verdict.schema.json` and
  `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — the two places that document the basis as
  "description/AC/..."; corrected to the real key list.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` — component-named `stale-material` reasons (both
  kinds); timestamp-named `stale-reopened`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest_gate.py` — actionable `unsigned` message.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/generation.py` — replace the fixed-list wording.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/resign.py` — replace the fixed-list wording.
- `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` — forward the child-closure validity reason, not just the
  verdict.
- `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py` — a dedicated render branch for a `plan_review_sign_aborted`
  signing failure that names the reason and the correct remedy.
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — state plainly that ticking a checkbox is attestation-safe, and
  document the component-named staleness reasons.
- `tests/unit/plan_review/test_94a3_material_diff.py` (new) — the tests below.
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_sidecar_heldout.py` — its fake `sidecar.emit` gains the new
  keyword argument so the pinned emit signature stays accurate.

`pass1.py` sits at 776 of the 800-line cap, so the new hashing code lands in `material_diff.py`; `pass1.py` is edited only to DELETE its inline basis construction and call `material_diff.material_basis` instead, which leaves it smaller than before.

## Testing

- Happy path: an attestation whose `file_impact` changed reports a reason containing
  `file_impact` and NOT `description` or `children`; likewise a description-only edit and a
  children-only edit, one test each.
- Checkbox pin (330c): an attestation over a description whose boxes are then ticked reports
  `certified`, not `stale-material` — pinning the normalization that is currently only implicit.
- Legacy/grandfather regression: a pre-330c attestation (raw-description basis) over an
  unchanged ticket still reports `certified`, and one that cannot be grandfathered reports the
  "no component differs" wording rather than a spurious component name.
- Edge: an attestation with no `material-part:` lines and no pins still produces an actionable
  reason and never raises.
- Gate-outcome invariance: for each of the stale verdicts, assert `valid is False` and the
  `verdict` value is unchanged from the current code — the same inputs are still refused.
- The full existing suites `tests/unit/test_compute_validity.py`,
  `tests/unit/test_legacy_material_grandfather_96d1.py`,
  `tests/unit/test_attestation_invalidation.py` and `tests/unit/test_plan_material_pins.py`
  pass unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `material_diff.material_components(ctx)` returns `{name: (hash16, size)}` whose keys are
      exactly the `material_fingerprint` basis keys; verified by a test that asserts the key set
      matches and that changing one component changes only that component's hash.
- [x] `build_manifest` emits sorted `material-part: <name> <hash16> <size>` lines that
      `manifest_material_parts()` round-trips; verified by a round-trip test.
- [x] A manifest carrying no `material-part:` line parses to `{}`, and a malformed one is
      skipped rather than raised; verified by two tests.
- [x] A `stale-material` reason from `compute_validity` NAMES the differing component(s) and
      does not contain the string `description/AC/file_impact/children`; verified by one test
      per component, plus a repo-wide grep asserting that literal survives only in
      `material_diff.py`, which documents its removal.
- [x] Each named component carries its before -> after count in a fixed shape,
      `<name> (<old> -> <new> <unit>)`, where the unit is `chars` for `description` and
      `ticket_id`, `paths` for `file_impact`, `children` for `children`, and `fields` for
      `file_impact_scope`; a component whose count is unchanged but whose hash moved renders
      `<name> (<n> <unit>, contents edited)`, and one present on only one side renders
      `added`/`removed`. Verified by a test asserting `1 -> 3` appears for a file_impact
      change.
- [x] Ticking checkboxes only leaves the verdict `certified`; verified by a test that signs over
      an unticked description, ticks every box, and asserts `compute_validity` returns
      `verdict == "certified"`.
- [x] A pre-330c (raw-description) attestation over an unchanged ticket still returns
      `certified`; verified by a test.
- [x] An un-grandfatherable pre-component attestation returns a reason saying the component
      cannot be named, rather than naming one; verified by a test.
- [x] `stale-reopened` names both the sign and the reopen timestamp; verified by asserting both
      appear in the reason.
- [x] The claim gate's `unsigned` message names both the `review-plan` and the `sign-review`
      remedy; verified by asserting both substrings in the reason.
- [x] A signing failure whose reason is in `PlanRelationSnapshotError.REASONS` renders that
      reason and does NOT advise `sign-review`; verified by a test feeding
      `store-read-failure` to the renderer.
- [x] Any other `plan_review_sign_aborted` failure still advises `sign-review`; verified by a
      test feeding an arbitrary error string to the renderer.
- [x] A dependency-material change from `generation.py` names the changed dependency ticket
      ids, matching `resign.py`'s existing wording; verified by asserting the ids appear in the
      raised message.
- [x] No gate outcome changes: for every branch touched, a test asserts the same
      `(valid, verdict)` pair as before, and `pytest tests/unit tests/integration` passes.
- [x] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` states plainly that ticking an AC checkbox is
      attestation-safe; verified by a grep for that statement in the file.

## Provenance

Three independent agent reports on 2026-08-05, recorded in the original description above. Related: bug 858c-786a-13be-4332 (the close gate cannot express an N/A criterion).

## Why this idea exists

Operator decision 2026-08-05: the inert `CodeHealthConfig.analyzers` knob is being DELETED (bug dce2-b93d-4112-451c) rather than wired up, because it advertises a capability that does nothing today. This idea preserves the capability's intent so the deletion is not a loss of information.

## What a real implementation would need

The analyzer FRAMEWORK already exists and shipped -- the interface plus hard Unavailable fallback (story 3b30-2168-ba16-41fc), and adapters for size/LOC via scc (18f9), complexity via lizard (21fb), and duplication via jscpd (3ba0). What never existed is per-project SELECTION: `_config_schema.py` grew an `analyzers` field and a coercion row, but `_commands/metrics.py` only ever consumed scan_roots / size_cap / size_near_fraction and never read it.

So the work is not "build analyzers", it is "let a project choose which analyzers run".

## The operator's explicit condition on doing this

Do NOT re-introduce the selection knob as configuration alone. It must ship together with DOGFOODING: at least one project-specific analyzer that rebar itself selects and runs through the knob, proving the seam end-to-end on a real analyzer rather than on config plumbing. That condition is the whole reason the previous attempt rotted into an inert field.

## Suggested acceptance shape when this is promoted out of idea

- A project can select which analyzers run, and the selection is actually read by the metrics
  pipeline (a test proves a deselected analyzer does not run).
- At least one project-specific analyzer exists, is selected via the knob, and produces a
  real metric for this repository.
- An inert-config guard covers the new field so it cannot silently regress to zero read sites
  (this is the 281f / 9d7a inert-config family, and the 6754 gate's read-via marker).
baseline.summary: Per-project analyzer selection, shipped with at least one dogfooded project-specific analyzer

# S3 — OIDC / JWKS JWT verifier

## Why
JWKS-backed JWT validation is the "OAuth" half of the confirmed floor and the generic "plug into any OIDC provider" path — one verifier covers AWS Cognito, Microsoft Entra ID, Auth0, Okta, Keycloak, WorkOS, Google ID tokens, and GitHub Actions OIDC (all publish a JWKS and issue standard JWTs). It is the highest-leverage verifier for the "wide variety of environments" goal.

## What
Add a **`JWKSTokenVerifier`** to `src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py`, selected by the `jwt` token in `mcp.auth_strategies`, with flat config keys it registers: `auth_jwt_jwks_uri`, `auth_jwt_issuer`, `auth_jwt_algorithms` (default `RS256,ES256`), `auth_jwt_leeway` (seconds, default 60), `auth_jwt_jwks_refetch_cooldown` (seconds, default 30), `auth_jwt_jwks_timeout` (seconds, default 10), `auth_jwt_expected_typ` (default **unset**), and `auth_jwt_allow_private_jwks_host` (bool, default `false`). It does **not** take a per-verifier audience — it validates `aud == auth_resource_server_url` (the single resource from S2). Implemented with PyJWT (`jwt.PyJWKClient` + `jwt.decode`); add `pyjwt[crypto]` to the `[mcp]` extra (the SDK pin lives in S1). It validates the signature (pinned algorithms), `iss`, `aud`, `exp`/`iat`/`nbf`, optionally the header `typ` (when `auth_jwt_expected_typ` is set — see Security), maps `scope`/`scp`→scopes, sets `expires_at` from `exp` (a real positive value), and stamps `resource=auth_resource_server_url` so the composite audience check passes. This story registers its keys in `MCP_ENV_VARS`/`server.json` + regenerates the reference docs.

## Approach & rationale
Use PyJWT's `PyJWKClient` (JWKS fetch + in-process key cache + `kid` lookup) and `jwt.decode` with an explicit pinned `algorithms` allowlist — PyJWT's documented JWKS path and the same shape FastMCP's `JWTVerifier` uses, giving provider-generic OIDC validation in a small module on the SDK seam. PyJWT is already a transitive of `mcp`; `pyjwt[crypto]` makes the `cryptography` backend explicit for RS/ES verification. **PyJWKClient's `lifespan` is a cache TTL, not an unknown-`kid` flood guard**, so this verifier implements the unknown-`kid` refetch cooldown itself (see the concurrency-safe design in Security) rather than relying on the library for it.

**Async-safety of the blocking JWKS fetch.** `PyJWKClient.get_signing_key_from_jwt()` (and its underlying JWKS HTTP fetch) is **synchronous/blocking**, but the verifier's `verify_token` runs on FastMCP's async event loop. The verifier therefore offloads every key lookup / JWKS fetch to a worker thread via `asyncio.to_thread(...)` so it never blocks the event loop, and it serializes the cooldown check-and-update with an `asyncio.Lock` (see Security) so the "at most one fetch per cooldown window" guarantee holds under concurrent requests.

## Scope
The JWKS/JWT verifier only, on the S2 seam. Not introspection/proxy/custom. Subset of the epic. Depends on S2.

## Security
Boundary-crossing. Hard requirements (RFC 8725 JWT BCP):
- **Algorithm pinning:** reject `alg:none`; never derive the algorithm from the token header. Also
  **refuse to start** if any **symmetric** algorithm is configured in `auth_jwt_algorithms` together
  with a JWKS source (asymmetric-only on the JWKS path) — this blocks the RS256↔HS256 confusion
  attack (signing HS256 with the public key as the HMAC secret). The symmetric set that triggers the
  startup refusal is the closed, explicitly-enumerated family **`{HS256, HS384, HS512}`** (case-
  insensitive); anything outside the asymmetric families `RS*/PS*/ES*/EdDSA` on a JWKS source is
  likewise refused.
- Mandatory `aud == auth_resource_server_url` (RFC 8707), `iss == auth_jwt_issuer`, and `exp`/`nbf`
  with bounded `leeway`.
- **Cross-JWT-confusion `typ` check (configurable, because OIDC providers vary):** when
  `auth_jwt_expected_typ` is set, the JWT header `typ` MUST equal it (RFC 8725 §3.11 — e.g.
  `at+JWT` per the RFC 9068 access-token profile), so an ID token or other same-issuer/same-aud JWT
  cannot be replayed as an access token. It defaults **unset** (check skipped, relying on
  `aud`+`iss`+`scope`) because many IdPs do not stamp `typ` on access tokens; S7 documents that
  operators SHOULD set `auth_jwt_expected_typ=at+JWT` for RFC 9068-compliant IdPs.
- **SSRF-safe JWKS fetch:** `jwks_uri` is fixed at construction from trusted config (never the token
  — no `jku`/`x5u`), **HTTPS-only** (an `http://` URI is rejected at construction), with a bounded
  HTTP timeout given by the named key **`auth_jwt_jwks_timeout` (seconds, default `10`)**, passed as
  the `timeout=` argument to `PyJWKClient` so a slow/hung JWKS endpoint cannot stall the verifier.
  Private/link-local hosts (e.g. `169.254.169.254`, RFC 1918, loopback) are **rejected by default**;
  an operator with a legitimate internal IdP sets `auth_jwt_allow_private_jwks_host=true` to opt out.
- **Key rotation without DoS (concurrency-safe):** the JWKS is cached with a bounded TTL; the verifier
  caps refetch on an unknown `kid` to **at most one refetch per `auth_jwt_jwks_refetch_cooldown`
  seconds (default 30)** (implemented by the verifier itself, not PyJWKClient's `lifespan`). Because
  `verify_token` runs concurrently on the async event loop, the cooldown's read-check-then-update of
  the last-refetch timestamp is a check-then-act (TOCTOU) hazard; it is therefore made **atomic under
  an `asyncio.Lock`** that serializes the check-and-update, so two coroutines seeing the same
  unknown `kid` cannot both trigger a refetch. Result: an attacker flooding random `kid`s cannot force
  more than one JWKS fetch per cooldown window even under concurrency, while a legitimate rotation
   still refetches after the cooldown.
  **Timestamp-on-failure policy:** the last-refetch timestamp is updated on every fetch *attempt* (success OR failure), not only on success, so a JWKS endpoint that errors cannot be used to bypass the flood guard by making fetches fail. The cost is bounded: a transient JWKS outage delays a legitimate refetch by at most one `auth_jwt_jwks_refetch_cooldown` window (default 30 s), and during that window a fetch failure raises → the composite denies (the request fails regardless), so no invalid token is admitted; operators seeing persistent outages lengthen the endpoint's availability, not this guard.
- A JWKS-fetch failure raises (composite treats as non-acceptance → deny); a definitively invalid
  token returns None. All verify-path errors go through the S2 redaction helper so no token/secret
  substring is ever logged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` adds `pyjwt[crypto]` to `[mcp]`; `make typecheck` resolves the imports.
- [ ] The `auth_jwt_*` flat keys (including `auth_jwt_jwks_timeout`) are registered in
      `MCP_ENV_VARS`/`server.json`, appear in the regenerated reference docs, and
      `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` passes.
- [ ] Unit test (tier: unit against the real verifier; the irreducible boundary — the JWKS HTTP
      fetch — is a stateful fake serving a locally-generated key set) asserts: a JWT with correct
      `iss`/`aud`(=resource) → an `AccessToken` with the expected scopes AND
      `resource==auth_resource_server_url` and an `expires_at` **equal to the token's `exp` claim**
      (observable oracle: returned `AccessToken.expires_at` == the exact `exp` used to mint the JWT,
      not merely a positive value).
- [ ] Unit tests assert rejection for: wrong `iss`; `aud` ≠ `auth_resource_server_url`; expired
      `exp`; `nbf` in the future; `alg:none`; and an `HS256` token signed with the RSA public key as
      the HMAC secret — each a distinct negative control.
- [ ] Unit test asserts that with `auth_jwt_expected_typ=at+JWT` set, a token whose header `typ` is
      absent/mismatched is rejected while a matching one is accepted (observable oracle: accept vs
      reject); and that with `auth_jwt_expected_typ` unset the typ check is skipped.
- [ ] Unit test asserts the verifier **refuses to start** when `auth_jwt_algorithms` includes a
      symmetric algorithm (`HS256`/`HS384`/`HS512`) alongside a JWKS source (observable oracle:
      startup raises).
- [ ] Unit test asserts construction-time SSRF guards: an `http://` `jwks_uri` is rejected; a
      private/link-local host is rejected by default and accepted only with
      `auth_jwt_allow_private_jwks_host=true`; and the JWKS client is constructed with
      `timeout=auth_jwt_jwks_timeout` (default `10` s) (observable oracle: for the SSRF rejections,
      construction raises; for the timeout, the test patches `jwt.PyJWKClient` and asserts it was
      called with keyword `timeout=10` — the concrete default value — so the assertion is exact and
      unambiguous, not merely 'a timeout is passed').
- [ ] Unit test asserts a JWKS **fetch failure raises** (→ composite non-acceptance/deny), distinct
      from a definitively-invalid token which returns None.
- [ ] Unit test asserts unknown-`kid` cooldown is concurrency-safe: a burst of concurrent requests
      with distinct unknown `kid`s within one cooldown window triggers **exactly one** JWKS fetch
      (observable oracle: the stateful JWKS fake's request count == 1 for the burst — not 0, which
      would mean the lock wrongly blocks all fetches, and not >1, which would mean the TOCTOU
      double-fetch was not prevented), while a token signed by
      a rotated key validates after the cooldown elapses (a legitimate rotation still refetches).
- [ ] Integration test (httpx `ASGITransport`) asserts a valid JWKS-issued token → 200 and a
      garbage bearer → 401 end-to-end through the transport.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.

## Compatibility
Additive verifier, opt-in via the `jwt` strategy. The `pyjwt[crypto]` add is backward-compatible; the SDK pin already lives in S1.
baseline.summary: S3 — OIDC / JWKS JWT verifier

# Live credentials were written into a rebar ticket comment; the tickets branch has been unable to push for ~8 hours

GitHub **push protection** is rejecting every push of the `tickets` branch because one ticket comment contains real secrets. No secret value is reproduced here.

## What was found

    commit  0a09e51c9f   "ticket: COMMENT 129e-2d88-cce2-492c"
    author  RebarBotNava <joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com>
    when    2026-08-03 19:13:25 -0700
    path    129e-2d88-cce2-492c/<timestamp>-<uuid>-COMMENT.json

GitHub's scanner names two distinct credential types in that one blob:

  * an **Anthropic API Key**
  * a **GitHub Personal Access Token**

The parent ticket is `129e-2d88-cce2-492c` — "Bedrock cutover silently removed server-side web search from blocking criterion" — which belongs to the review-bot / Bedrock workstream, not to the Jira DC epic. The comment appears to have pasted a live environment or provider configuration verbatim.

## Blast radius

**The secrets did NOT reach GitHub.** `git merge-base --is-ancestor 0a09e51c9f origin/tickets` is false — push protection blocked the branch before the commit was ever published. That is the one piece of good news, and it is luck bought by a platform control rather than by anything rebar did.

They ARE in local git history on the `tickets` branch, on any machine that has fetched or created it.

**122 ticket commits are stuck behind the blocked one** and cannot reach `origin`. Everything written to the store from this host since 19:13 is invisible to CI and to every other agent session. Two concrete consequences already observed:

 * Gerrit change 1343 fails the `require resolvable rebar ticket` gate — its ticket
   (`339a-57ac-e5f3-4718`) exists locally but is not on the `tickets` branch CI reads, so the
   change cannot land.
 * Comments recorded on the Jira DC epic's children tonight are local-only, so the close gates
   and other sessions cannot see them.

This also explains why the store's auto-push has been failing silently: rebar writes, commits, attempts to push, and the push is rejected — with nothing surfaced to the agent doing the write.

## What must NOT be done

**Do not use the GitHub "unblock secret" URL.** It resolves the push by PUBLISHING the credentials to the repository, which is the outcome the control exists to prevent.

## What needs an operator decision

 1. **Rotate both credentials.** They were written into a store whose whole design is to
    auto-push to a remote; treat them as compromised regardless of the block holding.
 2. **Remove the comment from the `tickets` branch history.** This is a history rewrite on a
    shared, auto-pushed branch used by every agent session, so it is not a change any single
    session should make unilaterally.
 3. **Consider a store-side guard.** rebar runs `gitleaks` as its code-review secret gate, but
    nothing scans ticket EVENT payloads on write. A comment is the one place an agent routinely
    pastes raw environment output, which makes this failure mode likely to recur.
 4. **Surface a failed auto-push.** The silent failure is arguably the more dangerous defect:
    the store reported success to every writer for eight hours while diverging from the remote.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] both credentials rotated (operator attestation, 2026-08-04)
- [x] the offending comment removed from `tickets` history and the branch pushing again
- [x] push-rejection surfacing tracked in e7a9-35fa-1d58-4095 (linked depends_on) — AC re-scoped by operator decision 2026-08-04; original text: "a rejected auto-push surfaces to the writing agent instead of failing silently", now owned by e7a9
- [x] a decision recorded on whether ticket event payloads are scanned on write
baseline.summary: Live credentials in a rebar ticket comment are blocking every tickets-branch push (122 commits stuck)

## Context / Problem

With the `Backend` interface defined (S2 [rebar:ce4d-c3ca-5412-4798]), the reconciler still has
no way to *choose* a backend: the vendor is implicit in which module is imported. This story
adds the **selection infrastructure only** — a `reconciler.backend` config key, an in-tree
registry, and a `select_backend()` entry point that returns the `Backend` for the configured
key. It deliberately does **not** rewire any existing consumer (the `_load_acli` seams, the
`AcliClient` construction sites, or the differ/apply leaks) — that is S4
[rebar:6673-7636-a116-4f90], which routes *all* consumers through the port at once. Keeping
selection and rewiring in separate stories avoids the trap the first draft hit: `_load_acli()`
returns the acli **module** (callers do `acli_mod.AcliClient(...)`), so it cannot be quietly
"delegated to `select_backend`" without changing its contract and the tests that patch it —
that contract change belongs with the coordinated rewire in S4.

**Grounded config mechanism.** The reconciler is *not* configured by
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/config.py` (that module is flat domain constants —
`EXCLUDED_FIELDS`, status-mapping dicts — with no settings namespace). Runtime settings come
from the **app-level typed config**: `rebar.config.load_config()` returns a `Config` dataclass
with a first-class `[reconciler]` section (`ReconcilerConfig` at
`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:475`, field `jira_cli_timeout` at `:476`), already consumed by the reconciler at
`acli_subprocess.py:71` as `load_config().reconciler.jira_cli_timeout`. So the backend selector
is a **new field on `ReconcilerConfig`**, read as `load_config().reconciler.backend` — mirroring
the existing `jira_cli_timeout` field exactly. `select_backend(config)` takes that app-level
`Config` object.

Edit-set:
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — add `backend: str = "jira"` to the `ReconcilerConfig`
  dataclass (class def `:475`; add the field beside `jira_cli_timeout` at `:476`), and register a **constrained coercer** for it
  in the `"reconciler"` coercer table (the `"reconciler": {...}` block opening at `:653`) using the
  existing `_as_choice(v, k, {"jira"})` pattern (`:117`) — the same mechanism `sync.push`/`pull`
  (`:609`–`:610`) and `mcp.transport` (`:617`) use. This gives **config-load static validation**
  (an unknown key raises `ConfigError` naming the allowed choices) and a free
  `REBAR_RECONCILER_BACKEND` env override (auto-derived by the env layer, `_config_sources.py`).
  The static choice-set (`{"jira"}` today) is the config-load guard; the *registry* below does
  the authoritative runtime object lookup. A second backend adds its key to **both** the
  `_as_choice` set and the registry.
- New `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend_registry.py` — a `register(key, factory)`
  decorator, a `select_backend(config)` resolver (takes the app-level `Config`, reads
  `config.reconciler.backend`), and a **test-only reset** helper
  (`_reset_registry_for_test()` context manager), since the registry is process-lifetime module
  state.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/backend.py` — decorate `JiraBackend` with
  `@register("jira", …)` (the `JiraBackend` class itself is introduced by S2, a prerequisite;
  this story only adds its registration).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/__init__.py` — **currently comment-only (zero
  imports)**; add `from .jira import backend as _jira_backend  # noqa: F401` so importing the
  `adapters` package fires each shipped adapter's `@register` side-effect. This is the import
  trigger the registry depends on (the earlier draft wrongly said this file already imports each
  adapter — it does not).

*No `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/config.py` change and no new
`rebar_reconciler/_config_schema.py`* — the earlier draft named both in error; the real config
home is the app-level `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` above.

## Approach

The registry is a module-level dict populated by an idempotent `register` decorator (the
in-tree decorator-registry style rebar uses elsewhere — no setuptools entry-points; a second
backend is added in-tree under `adapters/<x>/`). `select_backend(config)` reads
`config.reconciler.backend` off the passed app-level `Config`, looks up the factory, and
constructs the `Backend`; an unknown key (one that somehow bypassed the `_as_choice` load-time
guard) raises a registry error naming the registered keys. Registration happens as a
side-effect of importing `adapters/jira/backend.py`. To make that deterministic regardless of
caller import order, `select_backend` **lazily imports `rebar_reconciler.adapters` inside the
function** (before resolving the key), and `adapters/__init__.py` is edited to
`from .jira import backend` — so the first `select_backend` call is guaranteed to populate the
registry. The lazy in-function import also avoids a circular import
(`adapters/jira/backend.py` imports the registry to use `@register`, so the registry module must
not import the adapters at *its* module top). The reset helper lets the teeth test
register a `FakeBackend` and tear it down without leaking process state. **No consumer is
rewired here** — `select_backend` is proven equivalent to today's construction in isolation;
S4 changes the call sites.

## Scope

- The `reconciler.backend` field on `ReconcilerConfig` + its `_as_choice` coercer (static-key
  validation) + default `"jira"`, in `src/rebar/_config_schema.py`.
- The registry module (`register` + `select_backend` + `_reset_registry_for_test`) and
  `JiraBackend`'s registration.
- **Out of scope:** rewiring `_load_acli` / the `AcliClient` construction sites / the
  differ/apply leaks (all S4); physically relocating vendor modules (S5
  [rebar:dfb9-d2d1-455d-48d9]); the `Backend`/`JiraBackend` interface itself (S2, prerequisite);
  a doc note in ADR 0035 that selection is config-driven (a one-line S1/ADR follow-up, tracked
  there, not blocking here).

## Testing

- **Tier:** unit, RED-first (each test authored and seen failing for the right reason before
  the code exists).
- **Config-schema unit** (app-level typed config — `pytest tests/unit/test_config_typed.py`
  plus a new focused `tests/unit/test_config_reconciler_backend.py`; NOT the engine-side
  `rebar_reconciler/state/test_config.py`, which covers the flat domain constants):
  `load_config()` on a default config yields
  `reconciler.backend == "jira"`; a `rebar.toml` with `[tool.rebar.reconciler] backend = "nope"`
  is rejected at **config-load** by the `_as_choice` coercer with a `ConfigError` naming the
  allowed keys (independent of the registry); `REBAR_RECONCILER_BACKEND=jira` env override
  resolves.
- **Registry unit** (`pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_registry.py`, a new
  file): `select_backend(load_config())` returns a `JiraBackend` for the default; `register` is
  idempotent (same key+factory = no-op; a conflicting factory for the same key raises);
  `_reset_registry_for_test` round-trips (state after exit == state before enter).
- **Equivalence:** `select_backend(load_config())` returns a `Backend` whose `TicketTransport`
  is an `AcliClient` constructed from the **same** `resolve_jira_settings()` values as today's
  direct construction (asserted against the resolved `JiraSettings` fields
  url/user/api_token — not a live Jira call).
- **Teeth:** via `_reset_registry_for_test`, register a `FakeBackend` under a test key, point a
  `Config` at it (`reconciler.backend` set to that key with the choice-set temporarily widened
  in the test), and assert `select_backend` returns the fake — then confirm reverting the
  registration makes the same lookup raise. Confirms selection is honored, not hard-coded.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ReconcilerConfig.backend` exists in `src/rebar/_config_schema.py`, defaults to `"jira"`,
  and a value outside the `_as_choice` set is rejected at config-load with a `ConfigError`
  naming the allowed keys — verified by
  `pytest tests/unit/test_config_typed.py tests/unit/test_config_reconciler_backend.py`
  (valid default resolves + unknown value raises), exit 0.
- [ ] `select_backend(config)` accepts the app-level `Config` (`rebar.config.load_config()`
  return type), reads `config.reconciler.backend`, and returns a `Backend`; the default returns
  a `JiraBackend` whose transport is an `AcliClient` built from the same `resolve_jira_settings()`
  values as today — verified by `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_registry.py -k equivalence`, exit 0.
- [ ] `register` is idempotent (same key+factory = no-op; conflicting factory raises) and
  `_reset_registry_for_test` round-trips registry state — verified by
  `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_registry.py -k "idempotent or reset"`, exit 0.
- [ ] **Teeth:** with `_reset_registry_for_test`, a `FakeBackend` registered under a test key and
  a `Config` pointed at it makes `select_backend` return that fake (selection is honored, not
  hard-coded to Jira), and reverting the registration makes the same lookup raise — verified by
  `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_registry.py -k "teeth or fake or dispatch"`,
  exit 0.
- [ ] No existing consumer (`_load_acli`, the `AcliClient` construction sites, the differ/apply
  modules) is modified — verified by `git diff --name-only origin/main` listing only
  `src/rebar/_config_schema.py`, `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend_registry.py`,
  `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/__init__.py`,
  `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/backend.py`, and files under `tests/`
  (no other `src/` path present — in particular no `_load_acli`/differ/apply module).
- [ ] Every `src/rebar/**/*.py` stays within the 800-LOC cap — verified by
  `pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`, exit 0.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` all green.
baseline.summary: Backend selection infrastructure: reconciler.backend config + in-tree registry + select_backend() + JiraBackend registration (no consumer rewiring)

## Why

Non-structural findings (coherence and other plan-semantics criteria) re-litigate closed children
too, and carry no `_container_child`. Without a finding<->closed-child association we cannot tell a
live signal from noise, and cannot distinguish plan-semantics from delivered-functionality.

## What

Add a SEPARATE Pass-2 sub-call `plan_review_completion` in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py`,
mirroring the `plan_review_novelty` sub-call (its own contract + prompt), that ALONE receives the
delivered-children manifest (their own AC text) and emits, per finding, three atomic sub-answers:
ATTRIBUTION (closed child id or none; structural pass-through for G3/G4 `_container_child`),
CONTAINMENT (`limited-to-closed | spans-open-or-system | n/a`), LAYER
(`plan-semantics | delivered-functionality | n/a`). Write the rubric prompt at
`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_completion.md`, register the contract, and add it to the
derived prompt index. Bounded/validated outputs; every ambiguous value fails toward keep. Frozen
wording (not regenerated per run) per G-Eval guidance.

## Scope

- IN: the sub-call + contract registration + the prompt + output parsing/validation + prompt-index
  entry.
- OUT: the Pass-3 drop decision (separate story); the gold-set calibration (separate story).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `plan_review_completion` sub-call exists, registered like `plan_review_novelty`, receiving ONLY the delivered-children manifest (Pass-1 independence preserved).
- [ ] Per finding it emits {attribution, containment, layer} with the closed enums above; malformed/insufficient answers coerce to the keep-safe value.
- [ ] G3/G4 attribution is taken structurally from `_container_child` (not re-asked); a None/unattributed finding is never force-attributed.
- [ ] The rubric prompt `plan_review_completion.md` exists, is in the prompt index, and passes the CI drift gate; wording is frozen.
- [ ] Unit tests cover parsing + the fail-safe coercions for each sub-answer.

## Sub-call contract (fully specified)

Closed enums (each a closed set; fail-safe value in brackets):
- `attribution`: `<closed-child-ticket-id>` | `none` [none]. `none` = not about any closed child
  (open child, the container itself, or cross-cutting). For G3/G4 findings the value is taken
  STRUCTURALLY from `_container_child` (deterministic, not LLM-asked); for all other criteria it is
  LLM-emitted and VALIDATED against the delivered-children id set (an id not in the set -> none).
- `containment`: `limited-to-closed` | `spans-open-or-system` | `n-a` [spans-open-or-system].
- `layer`: `plan-semantics` | `delivered-functionality` | `n-a` [delivered-functionality].
Only `containment=limited-to-closed` + `layer=plan-semantics` + a delivered-now attribution can
enable a drop; every other value keeps.

Output contract: a `CompletionSubAnswers` model {attribution:str, containment:Literal[...],
layer:Literal[...]} per finding, registered as the `plan_review_completion` contract via
`register_contracts()` (mirroring `novelty_model` -> `plan_review_novelty`, passes.py:147), prompt
`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_completion.md`.

Determinism: Pass-3 is deterministic GIVEN the sub-answers — attribution is deterministic for
container-coverage findings (`_container_child`) and LLM-emitted+validated otherwise, exactly as
Pass-2 severity is LLM-emitted while Pass-3 decide is deterministic.

Manifest assembly (OWNER: this story, in `orchestrator.py`): iterate the epic's children, call
`delivered_now` per child, collect each delivered child's own AC text into the delivered-children
manifest handed to the sub-call (the sub-call ALONE receives it, mirroring novelty's prior-findings).

Degrade path: total sub-call failure (LLM error / parse failure / timeout) -> emit NO completion
sub-answers -> the completion floor drops NOTHING that run (all kept), mirroring `novelty()`==0.0
(carryover, never dropped). Fail toward keep.

## Acceptance Criteria (contract hardening)

- [ ] Each of `attribution` / `containment` / `layer` is a CLOSED enum exactly as listed above; the parser coerces any unknown/missing value to the bracketed fail-safe (which keeps).
- [ ] `containment=limited-to-closed` is the exact value the Pass-3 floor checks (no `limited` vs `limited-to-closed` drift across stories).
- [ ] The `plan_review_completion` contract + `CompletionSubAnswers` model + prompt file exist and are registered like `plan_review_novelty`; a test asserts registration.
- [ ] The delivered-children manifest assembler (in `orchestrator.py`) is implemented and unit-tested; the sub-call receives ONLY that manifest (Pass-1 independence).
- [ ] Total sub-call failure degrades to zero drops (floor inert that run), with a test.
baseline.summary: plan_review_completion Pass-2 sub-call: attribution + containment + layer sub-questions

## Completion state

This prerequisite is implemented and merged in commit `a8e0f67c827706525becb9b4d3df8a4da738d44e` (`store: add strict tickets push delivery`). The current tree, not the pre-migration workflow YAML, is the source of truth: `src/rebar/_store/push.py` owns the CAS retry budget, and both bridge workflows now delegate delivery to Python/core entrypoints.

## Delivered contract

- `push_tickets_branch(base_path, *, strict=False)` remains push-only and preserves best-effort behavior for every existing caller by default.
- The shared core performs five push-first retry cycles. Only a retriable non-fast-forward rejection enters fetch-and-merge recovery. If the fifth rejection produces a clean merged HEAD, exactly one terminal sixth push spends it; an earlier successful push returns without a terminal push.
- Opt-in strict delivery raises the reusable `PushDeliveryError` in core. Core does not call `sys.exit` or own process streams.
- The private Python module adapter, `python -m rebar._store.push push --tracker ... [--strict]`, is the process boundary that translates `PushDeliveryError` into stderr plus a nonzero exit. Child `2bc9-75aa-a08a-478a` extends the same Python adapter with `commit-and-push`.
- Stable reasons introduced and pinned by this change are `push-disabled`, `async-delivery-unobservable`, `invalid-destination`, `remote-not-found`, `push-policy-declined`, `push-transport-failed`, `merge-recovery-blocked`, `store-epoch-pre-merge`, `store-epoch-during-recovery`, `final-push-rejected`, and `lock-timeout`. The current core also has the later `push-multi-bundle-conflict` strict reason for the git-remote-s3 heal path; it is preserved and is not misrepresented as part of this changes original eleven-reason oracle.
- Policy declines remain distinct from transport failures. Strict errors carry underlying git/config detail and the current unpushed-commit count.
- Strict failure writes no ticket event and does not emit `BRIDGE_ALERT`.
- Dirty-tree staging and committing remain outside `push_tickets_branch`; that behavior is owned by dependent child `2bc9-75aa-a08a-478a`.

## Caller and compatibility coverage

The completed caller-contract inventory covers event append, batch append, NDJSON import, transition close, both delete paths, both compact paths, and claim. Each legacy caller omits strict delivery or reaches the shared core with `strict=False`, retaining its warning-and-return disposition while inheriting the corrected retry budget.

This preserves continuity across all supported surfaces and install paths:

- Python library callers keep the additive keyword-only API and the unchanged `strict=False` default.
- Public CLI commands that write through the store keep their established best-effort behavior; the strict module action is an internal adapter for automation.
- MCP write tools continue through the same library/store seams with best-effort defaults.
- brew, pip, and MCP-server installations use packaged Python entrypoints; no shell-only runtime implementation or install-path-specific behavior was introduced.
- Existing workflows and environments that depend on the legacy vocabulary and disposition remain valid. Strict workflow adapters opt in explicitly and fail loud only at their delivery boundary.

No persisted schema changed. The reusable Python core is authoritative; workflow-local retry loops are no longer required.

## Verification evidence

The merged change was reviewed and CI-verified before submission. Its RED-first oracle and final tests cover:

- deterministic contention in real temporary git repositories, pinning five rejected in-loop pushes plus exactly one successful terminal push;
- absence of a terminal push after earlier success and absence of duplicate terminal pushes;
- strict policy rejection versus strict transport failure with distinct stable reasons, git detail, unpushed count, and nonzero adapter exit;
- paired best-effort controls for the strict branches;
- the complete legacy caller matrix through its existing seams;
- narrow refspec, stash/pop, epoch guards, rejection classification, working-tree preservation, and no event or alert emission;
- focused pytest coverage plus repository lint, typecheck, and full test gates.

The merged epic ref `694cf894def36241724e7049e3308d782037ef6d` contains this commit and the dependent workflow migrations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Core owns five CAS retry cycles plus exactly one conditional terminal push.
- [x] Strict delivery is additive, catchable, reasoned, and translated to process failure only by the Python adapter.
- [x] Best-effort remains the default for all pre-existing library, CLI, MCP, importer, and store-write callers.
- [x] Caller-contract, contention, strict-failure, best-effort-control, and working-tree invariants are covered by tests.
- [x] The implementation is Python-owned and functions from brew, pip, and MCP-server installs without workflow-local shell retry logic.
- [x] Documentation distinguishes default best effort from explicit strict delivery.
- [x] No persisted schema, ticket event, legacy vocabulary, or existing environment contract is broken.

## Rollback

The API addition is keyword-only and defaults false. Reverting the strict adapter and retry-budget commit before dependent workflow cutover would not require data migration. In the completed epic, rollback must restore the prior workflow delivery implementation together with the core revert so strict workflows do not lose their delivery boundary.
baseline.summary: Add strict CAS push semantics and complete the retry budget

# Remediate CLAUDE.local.md to machine/operator-local content only

## Why

`CLAUDE.local.md` (155 lines) currently mixes two things: genuinely machine/operator-local content (this host's hourly `origin/main`-tracking LaunchAgent; the Gerrit credential identities `RebarBotNava`/`JoeOakhartNava` and keychain specifics) and generally-applicable project rules that are duplicated from `CLAUDE.md` (worktree discipline, activate-the-venv, plan-review signing, CI-before-close, the rebar tracking loop, a restatement of the Gerrit workflow). The generally-applicable rules belong in the shared, checked-in guidance so every agent gets them; the local file should hold only what is specific to THIS machine/operator.

## What

Strip `CLAUDE.local.md` down to only machine/operator-local content, having first confirmed (via the AGENTS.md story) that every generally-applicable rule removed now lives in `AGENTS.md` or `docs/`. Keep: the local main-tracking LaunchAgent note and the Gerrit auth identities / credential-pinning guidance. Optionally note that Anthropic now deprecates the `CLAUDE.local.md` name in favor of importing a gitignored file via `@` — record whether we adopt that or keep the current name (a coherence decision, not required by this story).

## Scope

In: `CLAUDE.local.md` only (git-ignored, local). Out: adding new content to `AGENTS.md`/`docs` (that is the AGENTS.md and re-home stories — this story only removes what they already re-homed). Depends on: the AGENTS.md story (the generally-applicable rules must have a home before removal).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `CLAUDE.local.md` contains only machine/operator-local content (main-tracking LaunchAgent
  + Gerrit identities/credential pinning); no duplicated project-workflow guidance remains.
  - Proving: reviewer confirms; `rg -c 'worktree|plan review|Track all work' CLAUDE.local.md`
    trends to 0 for the generally-applicable rules.
- [ ] Every rule removed has a verified home in `AGENTS.md` or `docs/` (no guidance lost).
  - Proving: for each removed rule, cite the `AGENTS.md`/`docs` location in the change description.
- [ ] Decision on the `CLAUDE.local.md`-name-vs-gitignored-`@import` modernization is recorded.
baseline.summary: Remediate CLAUDE.local.md to machine/operator-local content only
