## Why

Epic A must EXPERIMENTALLY PROVE the new constructs and DE-RISK the epic-B plan-review migration — finding flaws in our implementation and resolving them as A-scope, so B is a migration, not a discovery. A trivial smoke test does not do that; a realistic vertical slice of the actual B pipeline does.

## What

Author a throwaway but REALISTIC 4-pass review SKELETON workflow (the shape B migrates onto) and run it OFFLINE under FakeAgentRunner — no live calls — to surface integration flaws now:
- overlay_triggers (A1) precompute -> a `batch` finder over a `criteria` list (each criterion a
  prompt-library-backed entry with an optional `when` overlay; A2 shape) -> ONE aggregate verify
  prompt -> a `uses` decide step.
- Capture a PLANNED-TRACE from the run — the ordered [criterion/prompt-id, intended model, call-mode
  (agent|1-shot), deterministic-step-id] — proving epic B's parity-validation mechanism is actually
  emittable from the engine BEFORE B depends on it (the single biggest B risk).
Treat discovered flaws (can the criteria list express conditional inclusion? does the runner journal a usable plan? is the planned-trace capturable? does replay hold?) as work to FIX here. Label the workflow DISPOSABLE — epic B removes it, retaining it meanwhile as the visual-editing sample.

## Scope

- src/rebar/llm/workflow/examples/<demo>.yaml (clearly labeled throwaway): the realistic skeleton.
- A test (tests/unit/workflow/) running it under FakeAgentRunner: asserts conditional criteria are
  included/skipped, the batch-plan is journaled, the aggregate verify + decide run, and a PLANNED
  TRACE is captured — all offline, zero live calls.
- Record the flaws found + how they were resolved (the de-risking outcome).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A realistic offline 4-pass skeleton (overlay_triggers -> batch finder over a prompt-backed
      criteria list with per-criterion `when` -> aggregate verify -> decide) runs end-to-end under
      FakeAgentRunner with zero live calls.
- [ ] A PLANNED-TRACE is captured from the run (criterion/prompt-id + intended model + call-mode +
      deterministic steps), demonstrating epic B's validation mechanism is emittable from the engine.
- [ ] The experiment surfaces + the ticket records any construct flaws found, and they are FIXED as
      part of epic A (not deferred to B).
- [ ] The workflow is labeled disposable (removed by epic B; meanwhile the visual-editing sample);
      make lint + the workflow test suite pass.
baseline.summary: Throwaway demo workflow exercising overlay + batch end-to-end (offline dry-run)

baseline.description:
Close the silent-success gap on the NativeOutput structured path (parity with PromptedOutput) plus two proven output self-heal tweaks on rebar's already-strong structured.py ladder. Small, cohesive, fully offline-verified.

## Why
A truncated / refused turn never raises at the model layer — it comes back as a complete-looking but unusable response — so exception classification can't see it; it needs a stop-reason check on the RESULT. rebar's PromptedOutput path already does this (`structured.check_stop_reason`, runner.py:519). But the **NativeOutput path (runner.py:497-502) returns `run_result.output` DIRECTLY with NO stop-reason check** — a truncated/refused NativeOutput response is returned as a hollow verdict. Separately, `structured.py` already implements almost the whole self-heal ladder (tolerant parse, deterministic json-repair before reask, error-fed reask, fast-fail on truncation, bounded `OUTPUT_RETRIES`) — it needs two cheap, proven additions.

## What
- **NativeOutput stop-reason parity (the core fix):** add `structured.check_stop_reason(getattr(run_result.response, "finish_reason", None))` on the NativeOutput branch (runner.py:497-502) BEFORE returning. A `length`/`max_tokens`/`content_filter`/`refusal` finish_reason then raises `UnretryableOutputError` (⊂ `StructuredOutputError` ⊂ `LLMError`) — exactly as the PromptedOutput path already does — so the gate degrades to an unsigned INDETERMINATE via `gate_dispatch`, never a hollow PASS/BLOCK. This REUSES the existing raise-based degrade path; it adds NO new routing, NO coverage-field change, NO truncation-vs-parse conjunction (the check runs BEFORE any parse, so truncation is always caught as the exception — there is no "parses-but-truncated" case). NOTE Anthropic (rebar's provider) uses PromptedOutput today; NativeOutput is the OpenAI-strict-schema path, fixed for correctness/parity.
- **Self-heal tweak 1 — schema-guided json-repair:** `structured.py:161` currently calls `repair_json(cand, return_objects=True)` WITHOUT a `schema=` arg. Add `schema=model_cls` (json-repair 0.61.2 accepts a pydantic v2 model directly; default `schema_repair_mode='standard'`) for schema-guided deterministic repair BEFORE any LLM reask, wrapped in a `try/except` that falls back to today's schema-less `repair_json` if the schema-guided call raises (never regresses current behavior). Requires threading `model_cls` into the tolerant-parse helper. Bump the `pyproject.toml` pin `json-repair>=0.30` → `>=0.61` (0.61.2 already installed — a floor raise, not a runtime change) so `schema=` is guaranteed.
- **Self-heal tweak 2 — faulty prior output in the reask:** `runner.py:530`'s reask sends instructions + schema_hint + the validation error, but NOT the model's raw faulty reply. Add a bounded snippet `str(result.output)[:_FAULTY_OUTPUT_SNIPPET_CHARS]` (named constant = 2000, truncated with an ellipsis marker) so the model can diff its own mistake (the LangChain RetryWithErrorOutputParser / Instructor pattern).
- **Deferred (follow-on, NOT here):** the #5221 case — a refusal returned as NON-EMPTY content with a NORMAL finish_reason and only an out-of-band `provider_details` signal — is NOT detected here; its exact Anthropic `provider_details` shape can't be characterized without a live refusal, so it is deferred IN FULL to a `discovered_from` follow-on ticket. This story adds NO speculative provider_details parsing. (Anthropic refusals today normalize to the finish_reason the parity fix already catches.)

## Scope
- The NativeOutput stop-reason parity fix + the two `structured.py`/`runner.py` self-heal tweaks + the pin bump. Cohesion: all are small, same-theme changes to the same structured-output reliability seam (`_pai_structured` + `structured.py`), share tests, and none is independently land-worthy — kept together to minimize integration overhead.
- NOT in scope: a second-interpreter "fixer" LLM (`structured.py` rejects it — keep that stance); verdict-schema edits (blackbear owns those); the deferred #5221 refusal-as-content case.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The NativeOutput path runs `check_stop_reason`, so a truncated/refused NativeOutput response raises `UnretryableOutputError` → INDETERMINATE (parity with PromptedOutput), not a hollow verdict — test `test_native_output_path_checks_stop_reason`. A zero-finding CLEAN NativeOutput/PromptedOutput review still passes untouched — test `test_zero_finding_clean_review_passes`.
- [ ] `repair_json` is called with `schema=model_cls`, with a `try/except` fallback to the schema-less call — tests `test_repair_json_receives_schema` and `test_repair_json_falls_back_when_schema_call_raises`.
- [ ] The targeted reask includes the bounded faulty prior output (`_FAULTY_OUTPUT_SNIPPET_CHARS`) — test `test_reask_prompt_includes_bounded_prior_output`.
- [ ] No second-LLM fixer; no verdict-schema files edited. The deferred #5221 follow-on is created during the work (not a close-gate criterion).
- [ ] `make test`/`make lint`/`make typecheck` green.

Files: `src/rebar/llm/structured.py` (schema-guided repair; thread model_cls), `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` (NativeOutput check_stop_reason; bounded faulty output in reask), `pyproject.toml` (json-repair pin), `tests/unit/test_silent_success.py` (new); read-only on `src/rebar/schemas/*`.

## Verified library behavior (experiment log — pydantic-ai 1.107.0, offline)
ACTUAL captured output (no billable call):
```
ModelResponse fields: [parts, usage, model_name, timestamp, kind, provider_name, provider_url,
                       provider_details, provider_response_id, finish_reason, run_id, ...]
  -> finish_reason present (truncation/refusal signal, read by structured.check_stop_reason)
  -> provider_details present (the STRUCTURED out-of-band filter signal drake keys on, NOT a regex)
rebar structured.check_stop_reason(stop_reason: str | None) -> None   (reused for the truncation conjunction)
```
json-repair schema-guided repair, VERIFIED offline:
```
json-repair 0.61.2: repair_json params = [json_str, return_objects, skip_json_loads, logging, json_fd,
    chunk_length, stream_stable, strict, schema, schema_repair_mode, json_dumps_args]  -> schema + schema_repair_mode present
```
The current pin `json-repair>=0.30` predates the `schema=` arg; this story bumps it to `>=0.61` (0.61.2 is already installed, so the bump is a floor-raise, not a runtime change). So the refusal-as-content detection keys on the structured provider signal (finish_reason + provider_details), never a regex over answer text; and the truncation conjunction reuses the existing check_stop_reason. A detected silent-success is routed through story mamba's shared LLMOutcome (resolution_class=CHANGE_INPUT + sanitized diagnostic) — one routing path, not a second. These are pydantic-ai LIBRARY response fields, not rebar symbols (bug succinct-formable-kite: repo-absence != non-existence). RED baseline (arawana, committed) pins today: canned content_filter/length finish_reason -> UnretryableOutputError; text mode does NOT read finish_reason (the silent-success gap drake closes).
baseline.summary: Silent-success detection + output self-heal (schema-guided repair, faulty-output reask)

baseline.description:
# The live-DC readiness gate (`serverInfo` 200) is too weak for the contract 3fe5 asserts, so a timing flake would be misattributed to an image degrade

## The gap

Both live-DC workflows gate on the same signal — poll `/rest/api/2/serverInfo` until 200:

* `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml:526-536`
* `.github/workflows/jira-dc-epic-link-probe.yml:50-60`

But `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py::_assert_project_capabilities` then asserts the instance exposes the **Jira Software (GreenHopper) custom fields** `Epic Link` and `Epic Name` (`_REQUIRED_FIELDS`). **`serverInfo` answering 200 does not imply those fields are registered.**

## Proof, measured on the probe workflow

Run 30944211742 shares the harness's readiness gate and queries the field inventory immediately after it passes:

```
Wait for Jira DC to become ready : 19:39:01 -> 19:47:33   (8m32s, serverInfo polling)
Run the Epic-Link clear probe    : 19:47:33 -> 19:47:34   (1 second later)

field 'Epic Link' absent from an inventory of 27 field(s); names present:
  ['Archived','Archiver','Attachment','Comment','Created','Creator','Images','Key','Last Viewed',
   'Log Work','Original Estimate','Progress','Project','Remaining Estimate','Resolved','Status',
   'Sub-Tasks','Time Spent','Time Tracking','Updated','Votes','Watchers','Work Ratio',
   'Σ Original Estimate','Σ Progress','Σ Remaining Estimate','Σ Time Spent']
```

27 fields, **every one a system field, zero `customfield_*`**. The read was authorised and well-formed; the plugin had simply not registered its fields one second after `serverInfo` went green.

## Why the harness has not failed on this — and why that is luck, not safety

The harness is not more careful than the probe; it is just **slower afterwards**. It installs dependencies and then runs a ~41-minute suite, so by the time the first test's fixture reaches `_assert_project_capabilities`, minutes have elapsed and GreenHopper is up. The probe asks in the first second and sees the real state.

So the harness's margin is incidental. If a run reached that fixture faster (dependency cache warm, fewer collected tests, a reordering) or the plugin initialised slower, `_assert_project_capabilities` would raise **`PROVISIONING FAILED: this instance exposes no ['Epic Link', 'Epic Name'] field(s)`** and its own message would tell the reader to *"Re-run the capability map against the current image and update `_REQUIRED_FIELDS` if the instance genuinely renamed them"* — i.e. it would be diagnosed as the **3fe5 image degrade** when the true cause is timing. A misattributing flake, and an expensive one: it points the next reader at the image and the declared contract instead of at readiness.

This is the same family as 3fe5 itself. 3fe5's lesson was that an unverifiable contract must not pass vacuously; this is the mirror — a contract asserted **too early** fails loudly for the wrong reason.

## Fix

Gate on the CAPABILITY, not a proxy. After `serverInfo` goes green, poll `/rest/api/2/field` until every name in `_REQUIRED_FIELDS` is present, under its own bounded budget, and fail with the inventory dump when it never arrives. `serverInfo` is the wrong predicate for anything depending on a plugin's fields.

Best placed in the readiness helper both tiers share (`conftest.wait_for_jira_dc_ready`) so the workflow step and the fixture cannot diverge, with the workflow-level curl loop kept as the cheap first gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] readiness for the live-DC tiers requires every `_REQUIRED_FIELDS` name to be present in
      `/rest/api/2/field`, not merely a 200 from `serverInfo`
- [x] the wait has its own bounded budget, and on expiry fails with the observed field inventory in the
      message so the failure is self-diagnosing
- [x] `_assert_project_capabilities`'s message no longer attributes a missing Epic field to an image
      degrade without first distinguishing "not registered yet" from "not offered by this image"
- [x] the probe workflow and the harness workflow share one readiness definition, so they cannot drift
- [x] a test pins that a field-inventory response containing only system fields is treated as NOT ready
      rather than as a degraded image

## Testing

    pytest tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_provisioning.py tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_conftest.py -q
    make lint && make typecheck

The load-bearing assertion is the negative one: a system-only inventory must read as "not ready". Without it this stays a latent flake that only appears when a run happens to be fast.
baseline.summary: Live-DC readiness (serverInfo 200) is too weak for 3fe5's declared field contract; a timing flake would be misattributed to an image degrade

Operator-approved early removal (pre-1.0 breaking pass #3), 2026-08-12. Source: the DEPRECATION REMOVAL-READINESS SURVEY, comment #11 on childsafe-bizarre-lorikeet (b902-18af-14ed-4da1), Tier 2 item 2 — "strongest candidate for the next breaking window". Operator ruling (verbatim): "The two best candidates and the one ready now are all approved for removal."

## What

Remove the three deprecated single-pass review PUBLIC entry points (story 316a, deprecated 31f352d535, shipped v0.11.0):

- CLI verb `rebar review` — intercept `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:50,512-514` + handler `_review` at `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:133-207`.
- Library `rebar.llm.review_ticket` — the warn-and-delegate wrapper `src/rebar/llm/operations.py:135-183`, its `__all__` row at `:33`, and the re-export at `src/rebar/llm/__init__.py:54,119`.
- MCP tool `review_ticket` — `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:60-95`.

Replacements: `rebar review-plan` / `rebar.llm.review_plan` / the `review_plan` MCP tool.

## What STAYS (do not touch)

The single-pass ENGINE `rebar.llm.operations._review_ticket_impl` (`src/rebar/llm/operations.py:185+`) STAYS — it has live internal consumers at `src/rebar/llm/review_workflows.py:86` and `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:348`. The third consumer (`src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:92,95`) disappears with the MCP tool, taking it from 3 to 2. `src/rebar/schemas/review_result.schema.json` also STAYS — `review_result` is still produced by `review-code` and the workflow path.

## Known hazards (found by inventory; each is a drift-gated set that must move in ONE commit)

1. **CLI ladder parity** — `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py:74-79` (`INTERCEPT_COMMANDS["review"]`), the intercept ladder in `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`, and `tests/unit/test_gen_cli_reference.py:43` (`_LADDER`). The script self-checks its curated key set against the ladder at `gen_cli_reference.py:144-156`.
2. **MCP manifest mirror** — the `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` description string at `src/rebar/mcp_server.py:128-129` is mirrored verbatim into `server.json:33` and into generated `docs/mcp-reference.md:46,52,94` (gated by `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` + the mcp-reference drift gate).
3. **Schema wiring** — `src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py` loses `"review": PLAN_REVIEW_VERDICT` (:345) and `"review_ticket": REVIEW_RESULT` (:350). The latter is currently the ONLY key keeping `review_result.schema.json` visible to the every-schema-file-is-wired guard, so it must be RE-POINTED (to the surviving `review-code`/workflow producer), not merely deleted, or the guard reports the schema orphaned.
4. **MCP outputSchema coverage** — `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_output_schema_coverage.py:121` holds the `NO_SCHEMA_EXEMPT["review_ticket"]` entry (the tool advertises no outputSchema); it must go with the tool or the coverage test fails on an unknown tool name.

## Deprecation-registry treatment (mirrors the two prior pre-1.0 passes)

# P1.4 (rev) — Bounded git growth via stock gc + non-destructive (union) recovery

> Supersedes `seek-algae-reign` (a240-d692-a86f-411c). The original epic proposed a
> bespoke operator `rebar gc` with hand-tuned reflog/prune windows to protect a
> reflog-only recovery net. Critical evaluation + 7 git experiments + two Opus
> reviews (principal-engineer + peer-comparison) showed that design is an outlier:
> no comparable tool builds it, and it treats a symptom (a recovery path that
> orphans commits into the reflog) instead of the cause. This epic implements the
> peer-aligned design instead. Full design trail: session_log (see relates_to).

## Context (problem + why the rewrite)

Every ticket mutation is a committed file on the orphan `tickets` branch. The write path forces `gc.auto=0` (`_store/event_append.py:74-84 _ensure_gc_auto_zero`, also `compact.py:61`, `txn.py:217/413`, `init.py:182`) for ONE reason: to keep git's reflog alive, because `_store/sync.py` `_do_reconverge` does `git reset --hard origin/tickets` in the "unrelated histories" path (~71-85), which **orphans local-only commits** and relies on the reflog to recover them (the warning at `sync.py:81` literally says "recoverable: git reflog"). No durable ref is saved before the reset. Cost: unbounded loose-object/pack growth with no safe reclaim, and a recovery net that depends on an ephemeral, gc-governed structure the operator cannot see.

## Validated facts (our experiments — see session_log)

- Reachable commits survive even `git gc --prune=now`; only `reset --hard` orphans
  + reflog-expiry can lose data (EXP-A/B).
- On the append-only branch `git gc` is ~96% repack/delta (2.5M -> 104K, 600 objects
  intact) and `--prune` reclaims ~nothing; "deleted"/compacted blobs stay reachable
  from history so `--compact-first` reclaims nothing for gc (EXP-E/G).
- `git gc` produces cruft packs by default on git >= 2.41 (EXP-F).
- A durable ref makes an orphaned commit survive a FULL reflog wipe + `gc --prune=now`
  (EXP-H) — i.e. reachability, not the reflog, is the durable guarantee.

## Prior art (verifiable references — the patterns we follow)

- **git-bug** — leaves `gc.auto` on, ships NO gc command, recovers by DAG **union
  merge (fast-forward-only, both parents kept), never `reset --hard`**; batches many
  ops into one blob/commit (operationPack):
  https://github.com/git-bug/git-bug/blob/master/entity/dag/entity_actions.go ,
  https://github.com/git-bug/git-bug/blob/master/entity/dag/operation_pack.go
- **git-appraise** — git-notes unioned via `cat_sort_uniq` (never drops); before its
  one rewrite path it **archives the old head to a ref "to keep history from being
  garbage collected"** (ref-reachability, not reflog):
  https://github.com/google/git-appraise/blob/master/repository/git.go ,
  https://github.com/google/git-appraise/blob/master/review/review.go
- **git-issue** — one-commit-per-change, stock gc, no bespoke maintenance:
  https://github.com/dspinellis/git-issue
- **jujutsu (jj)** — recovery net is the op log materialized as real `refs/jj/keep/`
  refs; gc (`jj util gc`) is safe because it only collects objects unreachable from
  retained refs => "gc reachability == recovery guarantee" co-design:
  https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/operation-log/ ,
  https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/technical/architecture/
- **git itself** — `gc.auto` default (6700 loose) is the normal posture; cruft packs
  default since 2.37/2.41; `--prune=now` risks corruption under concurrent writers;
  `git maintenance` is the scale-up scheduler (disabling gc.auto WITHOUT out-of-band
  maintenance is the anti-pattern, cf. Scalar/GitLab):
  https://git-scm.com/docs/git-gc , https://git-scm.com/docs/git-maintenance ,
  https://github.blog/open-source/git/highlights-from-git-2-37/ ,
  https://devblogs.microsoft.com/devops/introducing-scalar/

## Design + the safety invariant

Adopt the universal peer pattern: **trust stock `git gc`, and make recovery non-destructive so the reflog is never load-bearing.**

> INVARIANT: after union recovery, every commit rebar cares about is ref-reachable;
> therefore stock `git gc` is safe by construction — it only ever collects truly
> unreachable objects.

This is jj's co-design lesson achieved for free: if commits are never orphaned, gc has nothing unsafe to collect.

## Implementation plan (work units)

- **WU-1 Re-enable stock gc.** Delete `_ensure_gc_auto_zero` (`event_append.py:74-84`)
  + its call (`:124`); drop the four `git config gc.auto 0` writes (`txn.py:217`,
  `txn.py:413`, `compact.py:61`, `init.py:182`). Set `gc.autoDetach=true` explicitly
  at init so a forked background gc never serializes a foreground write. Migration:
  idempotent `git config --unset gc.auto || true` at init/fsck.
- **WU-2 Union, don't discard.** Replace the `reset --hard origin/tickets` in
  `sync.py` Path 1 (unrelated histories) with
  `git merge --allow-unrelated-histories origin/tickets --no-edit`, **reusing the
  existing diverged-Path-3 conflict -> `merge --abort` -> keep-local -> hint
  handling** (extend proven code, do not invent). Keep `reset --hard` only for the
  ff-adopt path (discards nothing).
- **WU-3 Conflict policy for mutable shared root files.** uuid-named ticket dirs
  never collide, but `.bridge_state/bindings.json` and the reconciler lock/gate
  files are rewritten per pass and would conflict. Add a tickets-branch
  `.gitattributes` with `merge=ours` for `.bridge_state/*` and `.reconciler-*`
  (the loser is a derived cache the reconciler rebuilds next pass — never ticket
  events). `merge=union` is WRONG (line-unions JSON into invalid JSON). NOTE:
  push.py already handles these conflicts today, so this only formalizes it.
- **WU-4 Docs + invariant.** Rewrite `docs/concurrency.md:165-196` and the `sync.py`
  module docstring (both assert the old reset+reflog design). State the safety
  invariant; note `git maintenance run` as the scale-up posture and that git's own
  30d-unreachable reflog window remains as a free backstop we no longer depend on.

## What this supersedes / drops from the old epic

- DROP the bespoke `rebar gc` command, `reflog expire --expire=<14d>`, the 14-day
  window rationale, `--compact-first` (reclaims nothing — EXP-G), and the
  `check_no_rebase_in_progress`-as-gc-guard (recovery is `reset --hard`, atomic, no
  marker — the guard cannot see it). None of this machinery exists in `src/` yet;
  this epic ensures it never gets built.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] WU-1: `_ensure_gc_auto_zero` + all four `gc.auto 0` writes removed; `gc.autoDetach=true` set at init; idempotent `--unset gc.auto` migration
- [ ] WU-2: `sync.py` Path 1 uses `git merge --allow-unrelated-histories` (reusing Path 3 conflict handling); ff-adopt path unchanged; no `reset --hard` that orphans local commits remains
- [ ] WU-3: tickets-branch `.gitattributes` with `merge=ours` for `.bridge_state/*` and `.reconciler-*`; convergence test for two clones racing `bindings.json`
- [ ] WU-4: `docs/concurrency.md` + `sync.py` docstring rewritten to the invariant; `git maintenance` noted as scale-up
- [ ] Tests: union-recovery loses no tickets; `gc --prune=now` loses no reachable data; bindings.json race converges
- [ ] Full non-integration suite green
- [ ] `gc.auto` is re-enabled; stock background `git gc` reclaims loose/pack growth with
- [ ] Unrelated-history sync MERGES (never discards) local tickets; two clones each
- [ ] Docs assert the safety invariant; the reflog is no longer load-bearing.
baseline.summary: P1.4 (rev) — Bounded git growth via stock gc + union recovery

## Context / Problem

Ticket 4af8 injected the vendor mapper entrypoints, but four core modules still reach the Jira adapter for *scalar* concerns: `applier.py:603-605` (imports `adapters.jira.acli_subprocess` and calls `resolve_jira_settings(project_default="DIG").project` for the cross-project safety guard), `fetcher.py:379-381` and `fetcher.py:441-443` (`resolve_jira_settings().project`, un-defaulted, for JQL scoping and parent enrichment), `_attestation.py:65-79` (`resolve_jira_settings(project_default="DIG")` + the JIRA_URL/JIRA_USER/JIRA_API_TOKEN fail-fast), and `apply_handlers.py:39` (`from …adapters.jira.acli_subprocess import AssigneeNotFoundError`). Epic bbf1 AC3 requires zero `adapters.jira` imports in core.

An earlier version of this ticket also moved the vendor-shaped field-diff helpers (`diff_fields`/`extract_field`/`assignee_matches`/`local_type_to_remote`) onto the Backend port; plan review blocked that (correctly) because those helpers are parameterized on Jira snapshot dicts, violating ADR 0035 §(d) ("core owns diff/apply; the port only translates"). That concern is now owned by the sibling canonical-shape differ stories under epic bbf1 — this ticket is re-scoped to the scalar, translation-only port surface that the block never applied to.

## Approach

Extend the `Backend` Protocol in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py` with scalar, read-only members — none parameterized on vendor shapes:

- `project` — the project/scope key with the applier's default semantics (Jira:
  `resolve_jira_settings(project_default="DIG").project`), consumed by the `applier.py:601`
  cross-project guard.
- `query_project` — the un-defaulted variant (Jira: `resolve_jira_settings().project`),
  preserving the fetcher's fail-closed behavior when unset, consumed at `fetcher.py:379-381`
  and `fetcher.py:441-443`.
- `assert_env_ready()` — raises a new neutral `BackendEnvError(RuntimeError)` (also defined in
  `_backend.py`) listing the missing connection essentials; JiraBackend carries the current
  `_attestation.py:72-79` JIRA_URL/JIRA_USER/JIRA_API_TOKEN check.
- A neutral `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError` exception defined in `_backend.py`;
  `adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py`'s `AssigneeNotFoundError` subclasses it, and
  `apply_handlers.py` catches the neutral base (soft-fail semantics unchanged).

All three accessors sit on the `Backend` facade Protocol itself (not a new capability sub-protocol): every backend has *some* scoping/readiness story, and a project-less backend (e.g. a flat-list GitHub backend) returns its configured scope key (repo slug) or raises `BackendEnvError` from `assert_env_ready()` — the fail-closed semantics the consumers already have. Update the S2 contract suite and the test-only `FakeBackend` in the same change so every in-tree Backend implementor satisfies the widened Protocol (structural typing breaks loudly at typecheck otherwise — that IS the expand step; there are no out-of-tree implementors yet, per ADR 0035).

Route the four modules through the backend instance already in scope where one exists, otherwise through the registry seam (`select_backend(load_config())` — the exact pattern already proven at `outbound_differ.py:450-454`), and delete their `adapters.jira`/`acli_subprocess` imports. Extend `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py` with a NEW full-tree AST walker: the existing `_module_level_imported_names` helper walks only `tree.body` (top-level nodes), but all four vendor-import sites being removed are function-nested lazy imports (`fetcher.py:379`, `fetcher.py:441`, `applier.py:603`, `_attestation.py:65`) — so the new case uses `ast.walk` over the whole tree, collecting every `ast.Import`/`ast.ImportFrom` at any nesting depth, and asserts none resolves under `adapters.jira`/`acli_subprocess` for the four modules. (`inbound_probe.py:65-67` uses the same `resolve_jira_settings()` pattern but is deliberately NOT in this ticket's scope: it is owned whole — REST mechanics and all — by sibling story `aff0-b0d9-e11c-4b6a` under the same epic, which relocates it behind a `SupportsAbsenceProbe` capability; splitting the file between two tickets would create an edit-set overlap.)

ADR 0035 §(d)'s pinned-interface table gains a row documenting the new scalar members and `BackendEnvError`/`BackendAssigneeNotFoundError`, so future backend implementors have a canonical reference for what the port now mandates.

Rejected alternative: extending the port with the vendor-shaped diff helpers — blocked by plan review as an ADR 0035 §(d) violation (a GitHub backend would have to implement `extract_field(jira_fields, …)`); the differ is made neutral by the canonical-shape sibling stories instead. Salvage note: Gerrit change 920 (worktree `impl-4af8-differ-di`) implemented a superset of this ticket and passed LLM-Review +1 / Verified +1; cherry-pick only the scalar subset from it, dropping the port field helpers.

## Scope

- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py (port: project/query_project/assert_env_ready + BackendAssigneeNotFoundError)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/backend.py (JiraBackend implements the new members)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py (AssigneeNotFoundError subclasses the neutral base)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py, applier.py, apply_handlers.py, _attestation.py (rewire; drop vendor imports)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py (full-tree AST gate for the four modules)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ (S2 contract suite + FakeBackend updated to the widened Protocol)
- docs/adr/0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md (§(d) interface table: new scalar members + neutral exceptions)

## Testing

- Happy path: `JiraBackend.project` returns the DIG-defaulted project; `query_project` returns
  the configured project; `assert_env_ready()` passes with all three JIRA_* set.
- Failure/edge: `query_project` preserves today's un-defaulted fail-closed behavior when the
  project is unset; `assert_env_ready()` raises naming exactly the missing JIRA_* vars;
  `apply_handlers` catches `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError` when the Jira subclass is raised
  (assignee soft-fail preserved).
- Gate: the new AST neutrality case fails if any of the four modules re-grows an
  `adapters.jira` import (module-level or nested).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `fetcher.py`, `applier.py`, `apply_handlers.py`, `_attestation.py` contain NO
      `adapters.jira`/`acli_subprocess` import at ANY nesting depth — verified by the new
      full-tree `ast.walk` case (not the top-level-only `_module_level_imported_names`
      helper) in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py`.
- [ ] The Backend port exposes `project`, `query_project`, `assert_env_ready()` (raising
      `BackendEnvError`), and `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError`; `JiraBackend` implements them
      by delegating to `resolve_jira_settings`; the S2 contract suite and `FakeBackend` are
      updated to the widened Protocol; behavior is identical (DIG default in the applier
      guard, fail-closed fetcher JQL scoping, `_attestation` JIRA_* fail-fast, assignee
      soft-fail) — verified by the unit tests named in Testing.
- [ ] ADR 0035 §(d)'s interface table documents the new scalar members and both neutral
      exceptions — verified by the amended ADR text in the change.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green; whole test tree collects with 0 errors.

## Landed

Implemented and merged to `main` as Gerrit change 926 (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
baseline.summary: Backend port scalar surface: project scope, env-readiness fail-fast, neutral assignee error (fetcher/applier/apply_handlers/_attestation)

Split out of task 77e1-7f82-98e6-4fed (dominant-northbound-blackrhino) so that ticket can close honestly against the scope it actually delivered.

## BLOCKED — do not start until bug 01e8-302b-ab8f-4220 closes

Bug 01e8 ("rebar init bootstrapped a fresh empty tracker while origin/tickets already existed") is IN PROGRESS in another session covering store/init/sync divergence, and has already modified `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` and the fsck path. 01e8 declares NO `file_impact`, so the overlap with the two call sites below cannot be verified precisely. Rather than guess and risk a conflicting edit to a file another session holds, the operator deferred these two sites into this ticket.

**Unblock condition:** 01e8 reaches `closed`. Re-read both call sites at that point — 01e8 may have moved, rewritten, or already bounded them, exactly as it turned out for `_ref_lock.py` under 77e1 (see below).

## The two deferred sites

- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` — `fetch <remote> <branch>` (~line 375)
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py` — `push origin HEAD:tickets` (~line 338)

Both are network-capable git subprocess calls that can block indefinitely on a stuck remote or a hung credential helper. Line numbers are from the 77e1 sweep and may have drifted — locate by command, not by line.

## Precedent to follow (already established; do not invent a new mechanism)

- `src/rebar/_store/push.py:57` and `src/rebar/_store/sync.py:58` — `_GIT_TIMEOUT = 30`, for INCREMENTAL ref-sized ops against an already-warm clone.
- `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py` — `_GIT_TIMEOUT = 300` (added by bug 747f, merged as `96a0d5c3f`), for a COLD materializing fetch that is legitimately minutes.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py` and `src/rebar/opcert_service/workspace.py` — bounded under 77e1 itself; read that change as the nearest reference implementation.

Pick the value by call profile, not by habit: `fsck_repair`'s `push origin HEAD:tickets` is an incremental push of ticket events against a warm clone, so the 30s `_store` precedent fits it. `init`'s `fetch <remote> <branch>` is a cold first fetch into a freshly-initialised store and can legitimately take minutes, so the 300s `_snapshot` precedent fits it. Justify whichever you choose.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Both call sites above pass an explicit timeout, with a comment justifying the value against the cited precedent.
2. A timeout surfaces as an ACTIONABLE error naming the git operation that timed out and the bound it exceeded — never a bare `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` and never a hang. Follow the `_store/push.py` synthetic-`CompletedProcess(124)` precedent or the module's own existing error type, whichever fits the call site.
3. A held-out RED->GREEN test proves the timeout is passed AND that a timing-out call produces the descriptive error rather than propagating `TimeoutExpired`.
4. `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default suite exit zero.
baseline.summary: Bound the two _commands/ network-capable git call sites with an explicit timeout

## Context and confirmed defect

Merged main at d2dea317ec fails every Gerrit Verified matrix cell before pytest: `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` is 808 LOC against the locked 800-LOC cap. Change 1730 reproduced the same failure on Ubuntu Python 3.11/3.12/3.13 and macOS Python 3.13 in run 31726058931. The importer patch never executed. This is distinct from deferred repo-wide sweep cinderlike-lucky-akitainu: it is the narrow main-is-red regression blocking all changes.

## Root cause

Two individually reviewed config additions accumulated through Gerrit's server-side main history without preserving module-size headroom. The monolithic `_SECTIONS` coercion registry remains colocated with dataclasses despite already being an import-independent table over `_config_coercion` helpers, leaving the schema module above its enforced hard cap.

## Plan

- Extract the complete `_SECTIONS` registry, unchanged, to a new `src/rebar/_config_sections.py` leaf that imports only the coercion helpers it calls.
- Import `_SECTIONS` back into `_config_schema.py`; preserve every key, coercer, validation bound, and public behavior.
- Prove structural equivalence with the config tests and full lint/typecheck gates; seed a mutation that removes one registry entry and confirm existing config-surface coverage catches it.
- Do not raise or alter the 800-LOC limit and do not broaden into the deferred repo-wide sweep.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` is below 800 LOC and the new module is at least 100 LOC, following the existing registry seam.
- [x] Every `_SECTIONS` section/key and coercer is preserved exactly; config-surface and focused config tests pass.
- [x] The module-size gate, lint, and typecheck pass.
- [x] A defect-seeded missing-registry-entry mutation is observed RED, then the final implementation is restored GREEN.

## File impact

- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — replace the inline coercion registry with an import.
- `src/rebar/_config_sections.py` — hold the unchanged coercion registry in its independent leaf module.

## Context / Problem
Four `graph` functions carry moderate cyclomatic complexity in the checked-in ratchet (`.github/complexity-baseline.json`), re-measured on this base and unchanged: `_blockers.py::_find_direct_blockers` (18), `_graph.py::_get_all_blocked_by` (20), `_graph.py::check_cycle_at_level` (16), `_unblock.py::detect_newly_unblocked` (22). LOW-RISK: pure logic, `graph.*` is in the mypy strictness ratchet, extensive existing tests, zero in-progress contention. The high-risk orchestrators `next_batch.compute` (CCN 42) and `import_ndjson.import_tickets` (CCN 45) are deliberately EXCLUDED. Flagged by audit ae1b.

## Root cause (architectural)
`graph/_loader.py` is a 15-line shim that stops at raw `reduce_ticket`/`reduce_all_tickets`, so higher-level query logic is hand-rolled per call-site. TWO distinct patterns recur and drive the CCN:
1. The **exact** "reduce_all → drop `error`/`fsck_needed` → index by id" loop is duplicated verbatim in `_find_direct_blockers` (`_blockers.py:33-40`) and `_compute_dep_graph` (`_graph.py:65-72`) — identical policy (`reduce_all_tickets(exclude_archived=False, exclude_session_logs=True)` + drop error/fsck).
2. `_get_all_blocked_by` (`_graph.py:127`) and `check_cycle_at_level` (`_graph.py:223`) each re-implement an FS-walking BFS skeleton (queue/visited + per-node `reduce_ticket` + try/except + dep-scan).

## Approach (conservative, behavior-preserving — reconcile divergent node-sets, do NOT unify them)
Add exactly two shared helpers and refactor onto them WITHOUT changing any function's node-set or traversal results:

1. `graph/_loader.py`: add `load_indexed_states(tracker_dir) -> dict[str, dict]` reproducing pattern (1) EXACTLY (`reduce_all_tickets(exclude_archived=False, exclude_session_logs=True)` via the `reducer` module attribute so the existing `_loader_module.reducer.reduce_all_tickets` patch point still works, then drop `error`/`fsck_needed`, index by `ticket_id`). Apply it at ONLY the two identical-policy sites: `_blockers.py:33-40` and `_graph.py:65-72`.

2. `graph/_relations.py` (already hosts `build_blocked_by`): add a shared **accumulator** BFS skeleton, `bfs(starts, neighbors_fn) -> set[str]`, where `neighbors_fn(node, visited) -> Iterable[str]`. **Contract (stated explicitly because the two call-sites' outputs differ structurally):**
   - `bfs` owns ONLY queue/visited bookkeeping: pop, skip if visited, mark visited, call `neighbors_fn`, add every yielded id to an **accumulator** set and enqueue it when not already visited. All I/O, reduce calls, exception-swallowing and filtering stay in each `neighbors_fn`; `bfs` has no policy.
   - The returned set is the **accumulator**, NOT `visited`: a start node is absent unless a real edge yields it, and a yielded id is present even when no ticket dir backs it (never dequeued). That is exactly `_get_all_blocked_by`'s `blocked` set (`_graph.py:151` adds every `blocks` target before any existence check). A `visited`-returning bfs would wrongly include the seed and break `check_would_create_cycle`'s `target_id in _get_all_blocked_by(source_id)` test.
   - `visited` is passed to `neighbors_fn` (read-only) because both loops consult it when deciding what to yield (`_graph.py:160-161`, `:266`); without it the accumulator would differ.
   - `_get_all_blocked_by` becomes `return bfs([ticket_id], neighbors)`, `neighbors` reproducing its per-node behavior verbatim (dir-exists → `reduce_ticket` → yield `blocks` targets unconditionally; then `os.listdir` → skip visited/hidden/non-dirs → `reduce_ticket` → yield entries whose `depends_on` targets `current`).
   - `check_cycle_at_level` becomes `return source_id in bfs([target_id], neighbors)` after its existing `not level` / self-loop early returns. Its mid-loop `if current == source_id: return True` is equivalent: the seed cannot be `source_id` (self-loop already returned), so `source_id` is dequeued iff some `neighbors_fn` yielded it, iff it is in the accumulator. Dropping the early return changes only how far the walk goes, never the boolean; the walk is bounded by the level-filtered dep component reachable from `target_id`, not by tracker size, and no perf test covers this function.
   - Both keep raw `reduce_ticket` (NO error/fsck filter, NO session-log exclusion) — NOT routed through `load_indexed_states`, so their node-set is unchanged.

3. `_find_direct_blockers`: use `load_indexed_states` for the load branch; extract the two blocking sources named in its own docstring into `_own_depends_on_blockers` / `_blocks_targeting` helpers to cut branching.

4. `detect_newly_unblocked`: extract its inline scandir+tombstone loader (`_unblock.py:53-80`) into a named module-level helper `_load_states_with_tombstones` (kept in `_unblock.py`; NOT merged with `load_indexed_states` — its tombstone semantics differ); keep the readiness logic and the existing `build_blocked_by` reuse.

OUT OF SCOPE (divergent semantics): `_ready.py` (dependency-light — must NOT import the heavy `_loader`), `_status.py::_get_ticket_status` (a status *predicate* mapping error→closed, not a loader), `_unblock.py::batch_close_operations`.

Rationale (G6): centralizing only the provably-identical loop (site 1) plus one accumulator-BFS skeleton lowers CCN and removes the growth-driving duplication, while leaving each function's node-set/traversal identical — so the change is behavior-preserving and the next graph query has a loader/bfs to reuse instead of hand-rolling a fifth copy.

## Scope
- `graph/_loader.py` add `load_indexed_states`; `graph/_relations.py` add accumulator `bfs`.
- `graph/_blockers.py`, `graph/_graph.py`, `graph/_unblock.py` — refactor the four functions onto those helpers as described above.
- `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_cycles.py` — ADD one characterization test (below).
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` — regenerate (`python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --update-stale`), shrink-only.

## Verification (behavior-preserving refactor)
- **The behavioral oracle is the whole `tests/scripts/graph/` directory (notably `test_graph_cycles.py`, `test_graph_traversal.py`, `test_graph_unresolved_blocker.py`, `test_graph_perf.py`) plus `tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py`** — the suites that actually import the four functions. They pass UNCHANGED (no edits to existing tests).
- **One NEW characterization test** is required because no existing test pins the accumulator-vs-visited distinction: assert `_get_all_blocked_by` still returns a `blocks` target whose ticket dir does NOT exist (unconditional add), and that the seed id is absent from the result. Write it RED-first against `origin/main` (it must pass there, proving it characterizes current behavior) before the refactor.
- Complexity gate green with the four ceilings regenerated downward; `mypy src/rebar/graph` + `make lint` green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `.github/complexity-baseline.json` records `_find_direct_blockers` ≤ 8, `_get_all_blocked_by` ≤ 8, `check_cycle_at_level` ≤ 8, `detect_newly_unblocked` ≤ 12 (verified: `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` exits 0).
- [x] The inline "reduce_all → drop error/fsck → index" loop is gone from `_find_direct_blockers` and `_compute_dep_graph`; both call `load_indexed_states` (verified by reading the two functions).
- [x] `_ready.py`, `_status.py::_get_ticket_status`, and `_unblock.py::batch_close_operations` are unchanged (verified: `git diff origin/main` touches none of those three symbols).
- [x] `_get_all_blocked_by` and `check_cycle_at_level` return results identical to origin/main (verified: `tests/scripts/graph/` and `tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py` pass with no edits to existing tests).
- [x] The new characterization test asserts `_get_all_blocked_by` includes a `blocks` target with no backing ticket dir and excludes the seed id (verified: it passes on origin/main AND after the refactor).
- [x] `mypy src/rebar/graph` is green.
- [x] `make lint` is green.
baseline.summary: Reduce cyclomatic complexity of the graph blocker subsystem (CCN 16-22, low-risk)

## Context
Cut the next minor release, 0.11.0, from reviewed main using docs/releasing.md. The current package and latest tag are 0.10.1/v0.10.1. PyPI is immutable; publication must use the dispatch-from-main workflow and its required pypi environment approval. The release date is 2026-08-06. Closed ticket 5ac8-96d1-4691-49a5 is the 0.10.1 release precedent, not active duplicate work.

Post-publication rebar-debug investigation proved that docs/releasing.md currently prescribes the wrong provenance verifier: gh attestation verify queries GitHub Artifact Attestations for SLSA provenance, while pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish uploads a PEP 740 publish/v1 bundle to PyPI. The observed CLI surface is `uvx pypi-attestations verify pypi PYPI_FILE --repository REPOSITORY`; running it against the downloaded 0.11.0 wheel and https://github.com/navapbc/rebar returned OK. Follow-up bug 13b4-c597-200b-4e31 owns the runbook and workflow-comment correction.

## Plan
- Work in a fresh worktree based on current origin/main and confirm release prerequisites, identity, recent Gerrit history/rights, and channel state.
- Bump pyproject.toml and every version in server.json to 0.11.0; regenerate uv.lock so the root project version remains locked at 0.11.0; generate and hand-curate the 0.11.0 CHANGELOG section dated 2026-08-06 and its compare links.
- Run version-lockstep and proportional release preflight: release-specific tests/guards, lock-currentness, lint, typecheck, full tests, build, and twine checks.
- Commit with DCO, Change-Id, and rebar-ticket trailer; send through Gerrit and wait for LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 with no unresolved comments, then Submit.
- After the bump lands on main, dispatch release.yml from main with version=0.11.0 and obtain the required pypi environment approval; monitor the entire workflow to a terminal result.
- Verify PyPI 0.11.0 plus PEP 740 provenance, the v0.11.0 GitHub tag/release and artifacts, MCP Registry 0.11.0, and the Homebrew tap bump (trigger autobump if useful).
- Install nava-rebar[mcp]==0.11.0 from PyPI in the distribution-channel environment and run the packaged post-publication probe.
- Record receipts and results on this ticket, then close it only after all acceptance criteria are met.

## File impact
- pyproject.toml — package version bump
- server.json — MCP manifest/package version bump
- uv.lock — root package version lockstep with pyproject.toml
- CHANGELOG.md — curated 0.11.0 release notes and compare links

## Rollback / failure policy
Before publish, stop on any failed guard, review, or CI vote and remediate through a new Gerrit patchset. After publish, PyPI cannot be replaced: if the artifact is bad, yank 0.11.0, de-list its GitHub Release, and cut a fixed patch version; do not overwrite artifacts or retag published content.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [operator-attested] `python -m twine check dist/*` exits 0 for the built artifacts.
- [x] [operator-attested] The release commit contains DCO sign-off, a Gerrit Change-Id, and this rebar-ticket trailer.

- [x] [operator-attested] Gerrit records Verified +1 on the release change.
- [x] [operator-attested] Gerrit has no unresolved comments on the release change.

## Context

Canonical bridge operations use conventional statuses: 0 for success or benign no-work/yield/paused states, 1 for operational failure, and 2 for invalid invocation/configuration. Legacy reconcile routes historically emit 3 for another live pass, 4 for the phase gate, and 75 for reschedule. The merged implementation centralizes semantic classification while retaining every legacy translation required by older workflows and environments.

Canonical rebar bridge preview/sync and legacy rebar reconcile or direct python -m rebar_reconciler routes consume one typed disposition and differ only at the outer numeric adapter. Python and MCP bridge facades use the same core result; legacy Python rebar.reconcile and MCP reconcile continuity remains.

## Exact contract

Canonical preview/sync map converged, paused, in-flight, reschedule, and historical phase-gate states to 0; invalid invocation/configuration to 2; and operational failure to 1. Their state markers remain stable.

Legacy CLI and direct-engine adapters map the same dispositions to the established 0/3/4/75/1/2 results with legacy messages and defaults. Older checked-out workflows, systemd/Jenkins units, scripts, and probes therefore continue to work. Retirement of the legacy codes is a separate future deprecation.

The production workflow uses the canonical route and no numeric whitelist. Preview remains non-mutating; sync preserves its existing mutation semantics; paused state still skips commit-and-push.

## Verification

Repository proof at merged ref 694cf894def36241724e7049e3308d782037ef6d:
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py defines one disposition and separate canonical and legacy exits.
- docs/exit-codes.md lines 29-54 and docs/release-notes.md lines 29-46 publish canonical 0/1/2, retained 3/4/75, and rolling-deployment continuity.
- test_reconcile_main.py, test_bridge_cli_heldout.py, test_lock_steal.py, and test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py cover canonical/legacy subprocess and workflow behavior.
- Public library and MCP contract suites cover both new bridge and retained reconcile facades.
- The numeric-consumer census found no unclassified production 3/4/75 consumer; intentional uses remain only in legacy adapters, compatibility tests, and dual-contract documentation.

No new contention harness is required because the change classifies a result after existing lock/CAS seams and introduces no retry, cache, or composed write.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Canonical preview/sync emit only 0/1/2; benign dispositions exit 0 and no canonical adapter emits 3/4/75.
- [x] Legacy reconcile CLI and direct-engine mode routes retain historical 3/4/75 translations, messages, and defaults.
- [x] Canonical and legacy adapters consume one typed disposition, run the pass once, and preserve repository/ref effects.
- [x] Python and MCP bridge and legacy consumers use the shared result boundary without a divergent whitelist.
- [x] The production workflow uses canonical 0/1/2, has no old case whitelist, and preserves paused commit-skip behavior.
- [x] Deployment, workflow, script, and probe consumers of 3/4/75 are migrated or explicitly classified as compatibility.
- [x] Exit-code and release documentation publish both contracts and the rolling-migration guarantee.
- [x] [operator-attested] Gerrit change 1595 and GitHub Actions run 31300543302 passed LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, and the focused subprocess, workflow, library, and MCP continuity suites at merged ref 694cf894def36241724e7049e3308d782037ef6d.
baseline.summary: Make 0/1/2 canonical while preserving legacy exit compatibility

# Live-validate the Jira Data Center adapter against the real client instance

## Context / Problem

Epic `e369` verifies the Data Center adapter against a Dockerized Jira from the Atlassian SDK, because
Atlassian stopped issuing DC trial licenses on 30 March 2026 and publishes no official DC OpenAPI spec. That
harness proves REST v2 semantics, but it cannot prove behavior specific to the client's actual deployment:
their Jira version, workflow/transition names, custom fields, permission scheme, link types, and user-directory
configuration.

## Approach

When sandbox access to the real self-hosted instance exists (a scratch project on the client's Jira, or a
developer license generated from their existing commercial license via my.atlassian.com), run rebar's
live-validation harness pattern from ADR 0037 — guaranteed bilateral teardown, deterministic matrix — against
it, and record the deltas from the Dockerized baseline.

This is filed as an idea rather than a child story of `e369` because its precondition is access rebar does not
control, and a ticket that cannot be finished in-session would fail the plan-review gate's measurability
criterion. Promote it to a story once access is confirmed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a scratch project on the real instance is reachable and its Jira version recorded
- [ ] the reconcile convergence + idempotence pass from `e369` runs green against it
- [ ] every delta from the Dockerized baseline (transition names, custom fields, permission errors, link types)
      is recorded as a comment and, where it changes behavior, filed as a follow-up ticket
baseline.summary: Live-validate the Jira Data Center adapter against the real client instance

# Merge G3+G4 into one container call per bin (2N -> N)

## Why
G3 (child-coverage) and G4 (child-consistency) share the identical (parent, child, roster) context and are
disjoint audits the container prompt already describes together. Evaluating both in one call halves container
calls (2N -> N).

## What
- Evaluate G3 AND G4 in ONE call per (child/bin): present both rubrics over the shared context (`passes.py` +
  `plan_review_container.md`). Keep per-criterion attribution in the output (findings tagged G3 vs G4).
- Gate behind an OFFLINE EVAL confirming combined-call findings match separate-call findings within tolerance
  (two rubrics in one turn must not dilute either).

## Scope
- In: the merged G3+G4 container call + attribution + the offline eval.
- Out: parallelization (S3, dependency); bin-packing (S5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] G3 and G4 are evaluated in one call per bin; findings are correctly attributed to G3 vs G4.
- [ ] An offline eval shows no accuracy regression vs separate G3/G4 calls (within tolerance).
- [ ] Container call count halves (2N -> N) for an epic; `make lint` + tests pass.

## Remediation (opus review — MAJOR 5/7, BLOCKER 3)
- Attribution flips from code-assigned (`passes.py:276` hardcodes `[cid]`) to model-self-reported. VALIDATE the
  returned `criteria` against {G3,G4} and DROP out-of-set tags (mirror passes.py:222-224); preserve the
  `_container_child` provenance (passes.py:288).
- Update the sizing.py container-cost projection from `2N` to `N` calls (it currently hardcodes 2*children).
- Fidelity gate = the S6 semantic eval harness (DEPENDS ON S6), not a vague "offline eval".
- [ ] Merged-call findings with `criteria` not in {G3,G4} are dropped (not mis-tagged); `_container_child` preserved.
- [ ] sizing.py container-cost projection reflects N calls (post-merge); shedding stays calibrated.
- [ ] The S6 fidelity harness shows merged-call findings within tolerance of separate G3/G4 calls.

## CI/eval posture (S6)
- The S6 semantic fidelity eval is a HUMAN-REVIEWED development gate run before merge (live, opt-in), NOT a required/blocking CI check (non-deterministic). The offline eval-spec discipline check still runs on every PR.
baseline.summary: Merge G3+G4 into one container call per bin (2N -> N)

# Eval corpus + ADR-0054 calibration for `project.measurement-provenance`

## Context

Story `f161-c70a-1a69-4ed1` landed the measurement-provenance mechanism: the deterministic presence/shape check (`det_measurement_provenance.py`, advisory via `p6_ac_quality`), the `.rebar/` overlay routing entry (advisory, `exec: AGENT`, `[operator-attested]` trigger), the `execution_mode: agentic` rubric stating decision rules (a)-(d), and ADR-0061.

What it did NOT deliver is any proof that the AGENT criterion actually FIRES or STAYS SILENT as the rubric specifies. The rubric states the rules; nothing exercises them. Every sibling project criterion ships a `.rebar/evals/<prompt-id>.eval.yaml`; this one has none.

This was descoped from f161 deliberately: the criterion ships **advisory**, so the mechanism is correct and useful without calibration, and the ADR-0054 promotion decision it feeds is not being made yet. Filed as an **idea** because promotion is a judgement call nobody has committed to.

## Approach

Follow the `project.engine-layer-enforcement` pattern exactly (`.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-engine-layer-enforcement.eval.yaml`
+ its offline shape test + a live semantic run recorded as attested evidence).

**1. `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.eval.yaml`** — a BALANCED corpus, `epochs: 3`, `gate: at_least(2)`, a deterministic `emits_valid_findings` scorer. Each entry needs a `note` naming the causal mechanism and observable effect, not just a label. Minimum fixtures:

| Rule | Fixture | expect |
|---|---|---|
| (a) environment contradiction | declares `579718921998`, repo Terraform backend names `896586841071` | finding |
| (a) contrast | declared account MATCHES the IaC | pass |
| (b) no-anchor fallback | non-AWS cluster/tenant id with no in-repo counterpart | pass |
| (c) privilege posture | scoped-permission criterion declaring `privilege_posture=broader` | finding |
| (c) contrast | same criterion declaring `production-equivalent` | pass |
| (d) instrument vs claim | AUTHORIZATION claim + `instrument=simulation` **at** `privilege_posture=production-equivalent` | finding |
| (d) contrast | same claim with `instrument=live-call` | pass |

The (d) must-fire case is the load-bearing one: it is the ONLY fixture that proves `instrument` is judged INDEPENDENTLY of `privilege_posture`. Both fields read 'fine' in it, and it must still fire — that is escape 2b (`simulate-principal-policy` returning a confident WRONG authorization answer that only a live call refuted). If this fixture passes when it should fire, the fourth field epic 3147 mandated is decorative.

**Fixture quality is the actual work.** A must-fire plan so obviously broken that any criterion would flag it proves nothing. Each must-fire case should differ from its contrast case in ONE declared field, so a fire/pass split isolates the rule under test.

**2. `tests/unit/test_measurement_provenance_eval.py`** — offline shape checks, no LLM, CI-safe: fixture parses, ids unique, `criterion` matches, both polarities present, every rule covered.

**3. Live semantic run** — `rebar criteria eval project.measurement-provenance --runs 3`, recorded on this ticket as `[operator-attested]` evidence. Dogfood this epic's own contract: the attestation must itself carry a `provenance:` line (environment / principal / privilege_posture / instrument), which doubles as the cheapest possible test that the new four-field contract is writable in practice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the eval corpus exists with BOTH polarities for each of rules (a), (c) and (d), plus the
      rule-(b) no-anchor pass case, each carrying a `note` naming the causal mechanism
- [ ] the rule-(d) must-fire fixture declares `privilege_posture=production-equivalent` AND
      `instrument=simulation` on an authorization claim, proving `instrument` is judged
      independently rather than as a proxy for privilege
- [ ] each must-fire fixture differs from its contrast fixture in exactly ONE declared field, so
      the fire/pass split isolates the rule under test
- [ ] an OFFLINE shape test passes with no LLM call: `pytest tests/unit/test_measurement_provenance_eval.py -q`
- [ ] [operator-attested] the live run `rebar criteria eval project.measurement-provenance --runs 3`
      is recorded on this ticket with its per-fixture outcomes and the measured FALSE-POSITIVE RATE,
      and that comment itself carries a `provenance:` line declaring environment, principal,
      privilege_posture and instrument (dogfooding ADR-0061)
- [ ] the promotion decision is RECORDED either way: advisory -> blocking with the FP rate that
      justifies it, or 'stays advisory' with the reason — ADR-0054 requires the evidence, not a
      particular outcome
baseline.summary: Eval corpus + ADR-0054 calibration for project.measurement-provenance

## Problem (resolved during this ticket's lifetime — this ticket now verifies the fix)

Epic `0e68-41eb-5782-4336` (outrageous-uncultured-wildebeast) had a 10,135-character description, over the 8,000-char review admission cap (`7cf80009d9`). `review-plan` on the epic returned a single blocking P4 admission finding without running the LLM, so the epic could not earn a plan-review attestation — and the parent-first claim cascade therefore blocked EVERY child of the epic (discovered when `bloated-shadeful-lamprey`'s claim failed with "Parent error: no certified plan-review attestation").

## State at planning time

The epic's description has ALREADY been condensed by the session owner: the description field now measures 7389 characters (under the cap), and the full 10,135-char original is preserved verbatim as an epic comment dated 2026-08-13. Editing the epic changes only the epic's OWN material fingerprint — children's attestations bind their own material (material_diff.material_basis), not the parent's, so no sibling attestation was invalidated by the edit.

## Remaining work (verification only; no further edits prescribed)

Run the epic's plan review to earn the certified PASS the cascade requires, then prove the cascade is unblocked with a child claim.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `0e68-41eb-5782-4336`'s description field measures at most 8,000 characters; checked by reading the field and reporting the measured length.
- [x] `rebar review-plan 0e68-41eb-5782-4336` admits the plan — no P4 admission finding in the result; checked by inspecting the review output's blocking list.
- [x] `rebar review-plan 0e68-41eb-5782-4336` returns a certified PASS with zero blocking findings and a persisted, signed plan-review attestation (checked with `--status`; if a PASS fails to persist, `rebar sign-review` is the recovery), before the claim check below.
- [x] A child of the epic can be claimed without the parent cascade failing; checked by `rebar claim bloated-shadeful-lamprey` exiting 0 (its own plan-review attestation is already certified and its material unchanged).
baseline.summary: Oversized epic description blocks the parent-first claim cascade

# WS4 — Gate dispatch entry + source separation

## Why
The capability must be OFF by default and SOURCE-SEPARATED so it is inert when disabled, while preserving the existing public surface. This story adds the dispatch entry (parallel to plan-review) and isolates the code into its own optional package, retiring the throwaway single-pass route.

## What
- `gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict(ctx, cfg, *, target_ticket=None, runner=None, repo_root=None)` running WS3's `gates/code-review.yaml` in-memory (parallel to `produce_plan_review_verdict`), wiring the `CodeReviewBatchRunner` (constructed with the assembled diff context) + a `RunnerAgentStep` + a `MemoryRecorder`, and returning the typed `code_review_verdict`.
- Source-separate into the optional `rebar.llm.code_review` package (already created in WS1-WS3); PRESERVE the public surface — `rebar.llm.review_code(...)`, the MCP `review_code` tool, and `rebar review-code` keep names/signatures and `review_result` output — via the re-export shim in `code_review/__init__.py`.
- RETIRE the single-pass `evidence + aggregate_findings`-only route (the gate replaces it); record the one-way-door removal in an ADR. When `single_pass.py` is retired, `code_review/__init__.py` is REWRITTEN so the public `review_code`/`select_code_reviewers` are provided by the GATE-backed shim (translating `code_review_verdict → review_result`), NOT lazily re-exported from `single_pass`: drop `"single_pass"` from `_SUBMODULES`, replace the `__getattr__` single-pass re-export with the gate shim, and a test asserts `review_code` still resolves + returns a `review_result` after retirement.

## Implementation sequencing — thin vertical slice first (resolves the G5 "too many concerns" BLOCK)
WS4 lands as ordered slices, each independently testable, smallest-risk-first:
1. **Slice 1 (MVP — the vertical slice):** register `code_review_verdict.schema.json` + `produce_code_review_verdict` (the ENABLED path) + the offline enabled-state test (FakeRunner → a schema-valid verdict for a sample diff). This proves the gate produces a verdict end-to-end before any surface change.
2. **Slice 2:** the `[code_review] enabled` flag + the disabled no-op path + the ZERO-LLM-call disabled test.
3. **Slice 3:** the `review_code` shim translation (`code_review_verdict → review_result` via `finalize_findings`) preserving the library/CLI/MCP surface + their tests.
4. **Slice 4:** retire `single_pass.py` + rewrite the `__init__` shim (drop it from `_SUBMODULES`) + the ADR + the docs/CLI-help stale-reference audit.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` — `produce_code_review_verdict`.
- `src/rebar/schemas/code_review_verdict.schema.json` — the NEW typed verdict schema (registered + wired into OUTPUT_SCHEMAS or CONTRACT_SCHEMAS).
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/` — the verdict finalizer + the disabled-path shim; `single_pass.py` is retired (the gate path supersedes it).
- `src/rebar/mcp_server.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py` — public surface unchanged.
- `docs/adr/` — ADR for retiring the single-pass demo; `docs/`/CLI-help stale-reference audit.
- OUT OF SCOPE: detectors (WS5), Gerrit (WS6).

## Sidecar mechanism (resolves the G6 BLOCK + the T1/T3/T8 sidecar advisories)
Plan-review's `sidecar.emit()` anchors on `verdict['ticket_id']` (the event-store key) and builds a plan-review-specific payload — code review reviews a DIFF, which has no ticket. So WS4 does NOT call `plan_review.sidecar.emit()` directly. Instead:
- The typed `code_review_verdict` (the return value) is the PRIMARY artifact — always produced.
- A sidecar EVENT is emitted ONLY when `produce_code_review_verdict` is given a `target_ticket` (e.g. a ticket-scoped review, or WS6's Gerrit path that associates a change with a ticket): a thin `code_review` sidecar emit reuses the `REVIEW_RESULT` event TYPE (not a new format) anchored on that ticket, with a code-review payload (verdict/blocking/advisory/coaching/coverage). Mirrors plan-review's emit but takes the anchor explicitly rather than reading `verdict['ticket_id']`.
- The diff-only path (the `rebar review-code` CLI / MCP `review_code` on a `(base,head)`/diff, no ticket) emits NO event — the verdict dict is the sole artifact. This is the v1 default; the sidecar event is the ticket-scoped extension.

## Prerequisite (WS3, CLOSED — shipped artifacts this story builds on)
WS3 already shipped (closed) the gate's runtime; WS4 wires the dispatch over it, it does NOT re-build it:
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` — the v3 workflow: `assemble_diff → triggers → base → round_a(batch) → union → round_b(batch) → merge → verify → decide → coach → verdict`; its terminal step (`code_review_coach` op) returns `{verdict, blocking, advisory, coaching, coverage}`.
- `code_review.batch_runner.CodeReviewBatchRunner(context: str)` — the `BatchRunner` (parallel to `ProductionBatchRunner`) that runs each included overlay's own prompt with the injected diff context; `produce_code_review_verdict` constructs it with the assembled diff context and passes it as `run_workflow(..., batch_runner=...)` (the `BatchRunRequest` seam is unchanged — the interpreter builds the request; the runner just executes per-overlay).
- `code_review.workflow_ops` scripted ops + the `code_review_findings`/`code_review_coach`/`code_review_base_output` contracts are registered.

## Re-export shim translation contract (resolves the G6 shim data-flow BLOCK)
`review_code()` must keep returning a `review_result` (its public contract), but the gate produces a `code_review_verdict` (a different shape). The shim's data-flow is pinned:
- **ENABLED:** `review_code(...)` assembles the diff context, calls `produce_code_review_verdict`,
  then TRANSLATES the `code_review_verdict` → `review_result` (reusing `findings.finalize_findings`
  so the result is schema-valid). Field mapping per blocking/advisory kernel finding →
  `common.finding`: `severity` ← the Pass-3 `severity`; `dimension` ← `criteria[0]` (else
  `"code-review"`); `detail` ← the `finding` claim text (+ any `merged_from` appended); `citations`
  ← a single best-effort file citation `{kind:"file", path, line_start}` parsed from `location`
  via the assembler's location parser (the `evidence` strings are folded into `detail`, since
  `common.citation` is a structured object, NOT a free string). Top-level: `summary` ← a one-line
  `"<verdict>: N blocking, M advisory"`; `reviewers` ← the distinct `reviewer_id`s carried on the
  findings (the overlays/base that produced them — available on each finding, not a separate
  verdict field); the raw `code_review_verdict` (incl. `coaching`/`coverage`) is attached under a
  `verdict` key. So `review_code()` does NOT keep the old single-pass path — it is a thin
  translator over the gate.
- **DISABLED:** `review_code()` returns a valid EMPTY `review_result` (`findings: []`) + a
  `summary`/note "code-review capability disabled", never an error/stub, and makes ZERO LLM calls.

## Feature flag (resolves the T8 flag advisories)
The capability is gated by `[code_review] enabled = false` in `rebar.toml` (default OFF), overridable by `REBAR_CODE_REVIEW_ENABLED` (same truthy parsing as the other env gates). When disabled, `produce_code_review_verdict` returns the inert disabled result (see back-out) WITHOUT running the workflow (ZERO LLM calls).

## code_review_verdict schema (resolves the T8/T3/E1 schema advisories)
A NEW registered schema `code_review_verdict.schema.json` (parallel to `plan_review_verdict`): `{verdict: "PASS"|"BLOCK", blocking: [finding], advisory: [finding], coaching: [note], coverage: {det_ms, llm_ms, total_ms, llm_calls, llm_ran}}`. `finding`/`note` reuse the shared `common.schema.json` shapes; `additionalProperties: true`. Wired into the schema registry (the every-schema-file-is-wired guard) and pinned by a test.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `produce_code_review_verdict` runs `gates/code-review.yaml` on the v3 engine (CodeReviewBatchRunner + RunnerAgentStep + MemoryRecorder) and returns the typed `code_review_verdict`; OFF by default (`[code_review].enabled` / `REBAR_CODE_REVIEW_ENABLED`), inert when disabled.
- [ ] ENABLED-state offline test: with the flag ON + a FakeRunner, `produce_code_review_verdict` returns a well-formed `code_review_verdict` (validates against the schema) for a sample diff.
- [ ] DISABLED-state test: with the flag OFF, `produce_code_review_verdict` returns the inert disabled result and makes ZERO LLM calls (FakeRunner call-count == 0); and `review_code()` returns a valid EMPTY `review_result` (+ a 'capability disabled' note), never an error/stub.
- [ ] Sidecar: a `target_ticket`-scoped call emits a `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar on that ticket; a diff-only call emits NO event (the verdict is returned). A test exercises both.
- [ ] `code_review_verdict.schema.json` is registered + wired into the schema registry; a test validates a real verdict against it.
- [ ] The public surface is preserved: `rebar.llm.review_code(...)`, MCP `review_code`, and `rebar review-code` keep names/signatures/`review_result`; a test exercises each (enabled→gate path, disabled→empty result).
- [ ] The single-pass GATE PATH is unreachable (no `evidence + aggregate_findings`-only route runs when enabled); an ADR records the removal.
- [ ] Stale references to the single-pass `code_review.py`/`single_pass.py` flow in docs / CLI-help / `docs/` are audited + updated.
- [ ] `make lint` + `make typecheck` + the test suite pass.

## Back-out (one-way door — resolves the E1/T4/T7/COH contradiction)
The single-pass code is DELETED, so reverting the feature-flag default does NOT restore single-pass behavior — it makes the gate INERT. When OFF, the preserved `review_code()` surface returns a valid empty `review_result` (zero findings + a 'capability disabled' note), NEVER an error/stub. The ADR states honestly that retirement is a one-way door and the flag-default is the INERTNESS control, NOT a behavior-restore. (This supersedes any earlier "reverting the flag restores prior behavior" phrasing — that phrasing is removed as incorrect.)

## Rationale (resolves the G6 approach-rationale advisory)
A dedicated `rebar.llm.code_review` package (vs inlining in `llm/__init__` or reusing plan-review's dispatch) is chosen because: (a) source-separation is an explicit AC (inert + isolated when disabled); (b) it mirrors the shipped `plan_review` package structure (registry/contracts/workflow_ops), so the two gates are symmetric and the kernel-consumer pattern is one shape; (c) it lets WS4 retire `single_pass.py` without touching unrelated modules. Sequencing within WS4: register the schema → add the verdict finalizer + dispatch (enabled path) → wire the flag + disabled shim → retire single_pass + audit docs.
baseline.summary: WS4: gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict + source-separation (re-export shim, retire single-pass, ADR)

baseline.description:
Supersedes bug e983 (config_manual fire-and-forget) by generalizing it into an infra-health readiness gate for the review/landing pipeline.

PRINCIPLE: an unhealthy infra precondition (unapplied/invalid config, LLM-provider outage, GitHub outage, env error) makes LLM Review UNSOUND. Treat these as INFRA-CLASS conditions (per Zuul RETRY_LIMIT/NODE_FAILURE): block fail-closed, do NOT cast a content vote, and AUTO-RECOVER (re-run blocked reviews) when the signal returns healthy — no human recheck (author changed nothing; only the environment did).

DESIGN (OSS-grounded):
- Health registry: named checks, each tri-state healthy/unhealthy/unknown (never conflate 'check errored' with 'healthy'). Signals: config-applied (live-vs-desired refs-meta/replication probe), config-valid, llm-provider (Anthropic reachable/quota), github (API/Actions/mirror), deploy-host/replication, environment.
- Aggregator: per-signal blocking vs advisory severity; fail-closed on any blocking-unhealthy. (cf. Argo health assessment; K8s readiness gate.)
- Consumption points, one health source: (a) REVIEW boundary — review-bot ABSTAINS (casts no LLM-Review content vote) when infra unhealthy, instead of erroring/false-voting; (b) LANDING boundary — dedicated bot-cast Infra-Ready submit-requirement blocks submit with an explicit per-signal message. Keeps env-readiness OFF the code-content labels (avoids the 'environment masquerading as a review vote' anti-pattern).
- Recovery = infra-class retry loop: on signal recovery, auto-re-run blocked reviews + re-eval gate; bounded (RETRY_LIMIT), windowed (thundering-herd), same-patchset re-vote that cleanly REPLACES the stale -1, terminal alert on exhaustion. (cf. Zuul infra-class auto-retry.)
- Reliability: independent tri-state observation (Ansible/Puppet lesson: apply exit-0 != converged; only a zero-diff re-read proves it); Terraform-style tri-state so a probe ERROR never false-clears; marker bound to the config revision it was computed against (Terraform stale-plan rejection).
- Waiver + break-glass: audited per-signal/global override; guard-the-guard on who may waive (Gatekeeper); a guaranteed break-glass reachable when the gate itself is wedged.
- Rollout: WARN/detect-only first (emit signals, do not block) until detection proven reliable, THEN flip to fail-closed. Staged config-first.

CONTEXT: closes the e983 root cause properly (durable reconciled status, not a fire-and-forget event) and also turns today's ad-hoc LLM/GitHub-outage failures into one loud, self-healing, auditable signal. Related: 0e15 (--class propagation), and the plan-review calibration miss on epic 86ac/ed13 that let consumer-migration advisories ship sub-threshold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A health registry exposes each named infra check in tri-state (healthy / unhealthy / unknown) and never reports a probe error as healthy; verified by a unit test that feeds an errored probe and asserts the aggregate is unknown, not healthy.
- [ ] When any blocking signal is unhealthy the review-bot casts no LLM-Review content vote (abstains) and the Infra-Ready submit-requirement blocks submit with a per-signal message; verified by an offline test asserting no content vote is emitted and submit is blocked.
- [ ] On signal recovery a blocked review is automatically re-run under a bounded retry (RETRY_LIMIT) with windowed replay, replacing the stale vote without human recheck; verified by a test that drives unhealthy then healthy and asserts exactly one bounded re-run.
- [ ] Each health observation is bound to the config revision it was computed against and a stale observation is rejected rather than allowed to false-clear; verified by a test that presents a stale-revision observation and asserts rejection.
- [ ] Rollout ships in WARN/detect-only mode (signals emitted, submit not blocked) until a config flip enables fail-closed; verified by a test asserting detect-only emits signals without blocking and the flip enables blocking.
- [ ] An audited break-glass override can waive per-signal or global blocking and remains reachable when the gate itself is wedged; verified by a test exercising the waiver path and asserting the audit record is written.
baseline.summary: Infra-Ready health gate: fail-closed review/landing gate over infra-health signals with infra-class auto-recovery
