## Outcome: NOT A BUG (mechanism disproved)

Originally filed on the hypothesis that the completion verifier attributes a suppressed governed call's COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE to repository file content, corrupting its verdict. Under operator decision B5 (test-and-approve only if the mechanism is proven) the hypothesis was tested first. It did not reproduce. No contract change was implemented.

## Original hypothesis

The completion wrapper returns COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE to every losing governed call in a same-response batch (src/rebar/llm/completion_tool_policy.py:151-154). The claim was that the model treats that synthetic result as the read_file payload and concludes the target file itself is the notice, as suspected during the close of bug 0707-59ae-7db6-489b.

## What was done

Four independently designed held-out oracles, 22 live runs total, on a disposable fixture repo containing a real tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py; the unmodified shipped system prompt src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md; real pai_tools.filesystem_tools; bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 pinned at temperature 0.0. Where arms were compared, the only varied variable was the text of the synthetic result given to a losing governed call.

- Oracle 1, message-level injection, 8 runs: model re-issued the read, got real content,
  recorded met=true; under persistent read_file suppression it routed around via search_files
  and still recorded met=true.
- Oracle 2, the REAL wrap_completion_evidence_policy with no injection, 5 runs: genuine
  batching occurred and a read_file genuinely lost the batch at run_step 1 in every trial. No
  misattribution in any recorded evidence.
- Oracle 3, starved condition, 6 runs: the notice was the only thing returned for the target
  file. The verifier reported this accurately rather than as file content.
- Oracle 4, realistic worst case, 3 runs: all three recorded met=true with correct citations,
  one stating explicitly that the steering text was untrusted data and was disregarded.

## Findings

1. The claimed attribution mechanism did not occur in any of the 22 runs. The verifier
   consistently classifies the steering string as a tool-scheduling message, not as content.
2. The incident wording in 0707 is best explained as a paraphrase. The verifier's true
   statement that its calls "returned only a COMMIT steering message with no actual file
   content" reads, when summarised, as a claim about the file. The 0707 record preserved the
   conclusion, not the verifier's verbatim evidence string.
3. The proposed remedy was measured to regress. An affirmative, cannot-be-scored-as-content
   steering result raised suppressed-call counts from 6 to 12 and 49 across matched trials, and
   one trial died with UsageLimitExceeded having recorded no verdict at all.
4. A real, different defect was identified: a false unmet caused by evidence starvation when a
   suppressed governed read is never recovered. Filed as dd41-239d-6e09-4a86
   (rutile-massive-spoonbill), linked discovered_from this ticket, left open for operator
   approval because the indicated fix is a behavior change.

Evidence artifacts are preserved at /Users/joeoakhart/.claude/jobs/6f8df6b5/tmp/waterdogs-artifacts/ (oracle.py, oracle2.py, oracle3.py, oracle4.py, results*.json, fixture/). The full reproduction record is the first comment on this ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [operator-attested] The attribution hypothesis is tested against the real completion policy, not only by
      inspection, and the result is recorded on this ticket with the exact rig, model,
      temperature and run counts.
- [x] [operator-attested] The recorded evidence shows a governed evidence call genuinely losing a same-response
      batch, establishing that the hypothesis was tested under its own precondition.
- [x] The outcome is recorded as disproved, with the alternative explanation for the original
      incident wording stated.
- [x] [operator-attested] The counter-evidence against the proposed notice-rewording remedy is recorded, so the
      change is not reattempted blindly.
- [x] [operator-attested] The genuine defect found during the investigation is filed as its own ticket and linked
      discovered_from this one.
- [x] No production code, prompt, schema, or public surface is changed by this ticket.
baseline.summary: Completion verifier can mistake COMMIT steering for repository file content

baseline.description:
# Cloud's `RunawayPaginationError` is swallowed by `fetch_snapshot`'s three enrichment fail-opens

## Claim

Found in ticket 18a4's Phase-1 parity census (the fetcher-boundary axis).

DEFECT. Bug cabc's fix (ab7f, commit 30c522cde9) added `RunawayPaginationError` to Cloud's `adapters/jira/acli_graph.py:29` and made its three readers re-raise it past their OWN fail-open handlers (`acli_graph.py:304, 394, 477`). That re-raise gets the error out of the transport — and straight into `fetcher.fetch_snapshot`'s three broad `except Exception` enrichment handlers (parent `fetcher.py:625`, comment `:672`, issuelink `:712`), which log a warning and degrade.

## Proven root cause (runtime-confirmed; see the RCA comment)

`RunawayPaginationError` subclasses `RuntimeError`, NOT the core stall type. Live MRO:

    (RunawayPaginationError, RuntimeError, Exception, BaseException, object)
    issubclass(RunawayPaginationError, BackendPaginationStallError) == False

The three fetcher re-raise clauses match on the CORE type (`except BackendPaginationStallError: raise` at `fetcher.py:621, 668, 708`), so they MISS Cloud's error and control falls to the broad `except Exception` beneath each. Driving the real `fetch_snapshot` with a stub whose `get_parent_map` raises `RunawayPaginationError` produced `WARNING ... parent enrichment failed (RunawayPaginationError(...)); snapshot written without parent data (degraded)` and a written snapshot — no propagation. A stalled Cloud cursor therefore still yields a silently degraded snapshot that the differ treats as authoritative (missing parents read as parentless; missing issuelinks read as "no links", so link removals become undetectable).

Intended behaviour is stated authoritatively at `_backend.py:49-70` ("Readers must re-raise this PAST their fail-open handlers", naming bug cabc as an instance of the class), `acli_graph.py:29-38`, and `fetcher.py:511-516`. cabc's fix is incomplete at the layer above the transport.

## Fix

Ticket 18a4 fixed exactly this hole on the DC side and built the mechanism this ticket needs: `rebar_reconciler._backend.BackendPaginationStallError` (core, so `fetcher` can name it without importing `adapters/`), plus `except BackendPaginationStallError: raise` clauses already in place ahead of all three fetcher enrichment handlers.

One-line change: make Cloud's error subclass the core one — `class RunawayPaginationError(BackendPaginationStallError)` in `acli_graph.py`. The three fetcher re-raise clauses then cover Cloud automatically. Keeping the Cloud-specific name preserves every existing `except RunawayPaginationError` site and its tests unedited; `BackendPaginationStallError` itself subclasses `RuntimeError`, so `except RuntimeError` sites are unaffected too. Adapters importing core is the established direction (`jira_datacenter/_base.py:19` already does it).

NOT folded into 18a4 deliberately: this changes observable behaviour on the CLOUD surface (stalls that previously degraded now abort the pass), which another work stream owns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A stalled Cloud cursor propagates out of `fetch_snapshot` instead of degrading: a
      token-repeating Cloud stub driven through the REAL `fetch_snapshot` raises, for each of the
      three enrichment readers (`get_parent_map`, `get_comment_map`, `get_issuelinks_map`).
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_acli_graph_pagination_heldout.py`
- [x] `issubclass(RunawayPaginationError, BackendPaginationStallError)` is `True`, and
      `RuntimeError` remains in its MRO so existing `except RuntimeError` sites still catch it.
      Proof: asserted in the same test module.
- [x] Existing `except RunawayPaginationError` sites and their tests pass UNEDITED.
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` with no edits to the pre-existing test bodies.
- [x] Ordinary (non-stall) enrichment failures still fail open and write a degraded snapshot
      (negative control: a plain `RuntimeError` from an enrichment reader must NOT propagate).
      Proof: negative-control case in the same test module.

## Testing

- RED-first held-out test added to
  `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_acli_graph_pagination_heldout.py`: a token-repeating Cloud
  REST stub driven through the real `fetcher.fetch_snapshot` (loaded from source, `_load_acli`
  patched), parameterized over all three enrichment readers, asserting the stall escapes. Verified
  failing before the fix and passing after; mutation-checked by restoring the `RuntimeError` base.
- Negative control in the same module: an ordinary `RuntimeError` enrichment fault still degrades
  and writes a snapshot carrying the base scan's issues.
- Regression: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/`, plus `make lint` and `make typecheck`.
baseline.summary: Cloud RunawayPaginationError is swallowed by fetcher's three enrichment fail-opens

## Impact, stated first

The scheduled **Reconcile Bridge** workflow failed 12 times in 6 days. An evidence pass over all 12 failed runs (see the pinned comment) split them cleanly: **6 runs died on an ACLI authentication failure**, and 6 died on **git delivery** faults that the original sweep misattributed to ACLI. When the bridge stalls, only the Reconciler Heartbeat Canary notices.

This ticket now covers **the ACLI auth failure and how it is reported**. The other faults are filed as separate linked tickets — they are unrelated causes in a different subsystem.

## Confirmed signature (6/12 runs)

Runs 31481490100, 31358521998, 31350775907, 31263067299, 31222668500, 31179770156. Identical:

    ACLI stderr: ✗ Error: unauthorized: use `acli [product] auth login` to authenticate
    ERROR: reconcile_once raised: Command `[acli, jira, workitem, search, --jql, ...]`
        returned non-zero exit status 1
    Reconcile failed (exit 1)

It fails on the **very first** ACLI call, 15–20s in, with no reconcile work preceding it. The `acli jira auth login` workflow step **succeeded** earlier in the same job. So the token is rejected **at first use, not at login**.

## The code defect this ticket fixes

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py` fast-aborts on auth via:

    _AUTH_FAILURE_CODE: int = 401
    ...
    if cpe.returncode == _AUTH_FAILURE_CODE:
        raise cpe

ACLI is a **subprocess** and exits **1**, never 401 — that branch is **dead code**. So a deterministic auth failure:

1. burns the full 3-attempt retry budget with 2s+4s backoff, and
2. surfaces as the generic `reconcile_once raised: ... exit status 1`, indistinguishable from
   a data/operational failure.

Nothing in `rebar_reconciler/` matches the `unauthorized` / `auth login` stderr string.

## Explicitly OUT of scope (and why)

**Automatic credential renewal.** The token is rejected at first use, so re-running `acli jira auth login` with the same `JIRA_API_TOKEN` cannot succeed. Renewal requires **rotating the secret value** — an ops action needing a new secret, not a code change. No new auth flow is invented and no credential is stored anywhere new. Rotation is flagged to the operator, not automated here.

**The git-delivery failures** (TLS `server certificate verification failed`; rejected ref pushes on `refs/reconciler/last-pass` and `refs/heads/tickets`; `HTTP 422` re-dispatch onto a disabled workflow) and **the swallowed `command cancelled` noise** in the link-apply loop are filed as separate linked tickets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] An ACLI failure whose stderr carries an authentication/authorization marker (the
      `unauthorized` / ``use `acli ... auth login` `` text) is detected **from stderr**, not from
      a subprocess exit code of 401 that ACLI never returns. Unit test asserts a
      `CalledProcessError` with `returncode=1` + that stderr is recognised as an auth failure.
- [x] Such a failure **aborts on the first attempt** without consuming the retry budget —
      retrying a rejected credential is deterministic and cannot succeed. Unit test asserts the
      subprocess was invoked exactly **once** (today: 3 times).
- [x] The failure raises a **distinct typed error** (not a bare `CalledProcessError`) carrying
      the failing command, so callers can `except` it specifically. Unit test asserts the type.
- [x] A pass failing this way emits an **operator-facing message that names the credential as
      the cause**, distinguishable from the generic `reconcile_once raised: ...` used for
      data/operational failures — so a credential problem is tellable from a data problem
      without opening the log. Unit test asserts the classifier's message/disposition.
- [x] **Non-auth** ACLI failures keep their existing retry-and-backoff behaviour unchanged.
      Regression test asserts a non-auth non-zero exit still makes 3 attempts.
- [x] The Mode 1 / Mode 2 relationship is **determined and recorded** on this ticket: they are
      independent (`unauthorized` count is 0 in all six `command cancelled` runs; the two
      signatures never co-occur). Recorded in the evidence comment.
- [x] The misattributed git-delivery faults and the swallowed `command cancelled` noise exist as
      **separate tickets linked `discovered_from`** this one.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the reconciler test suite pass.

## Notes

Originally filed by an automated ops error sweep, which hypothesised that `command cancelled` was a mid-pass abort caused by the credential expiring. The evidence pass **refuted** that: the string is non-fatal noise bracketed by successful `batch_outcome ... error=None` lines, and those runs actually failed in git delivery. The original AC about a "partially-applied reconcile" left by such an abort is therefore **moot** — no pass is aborted by that string.
baseline.summary: Reconcile Bridge reports ACLI auth failure as a generic error: the fast-abort is dead code keyed on a 401 exit ACLI never returns

baseline.description:
Encode the agent-build invariants that guard against silently-disabled safeguards as tests plus a one-time construction check — not per-call runtime blocking. Every mechanism below is a CONCRETE, verified pydantic-ai 1.107.0 signal.

## Why
Several dangerous silent failures are static properties of rebar's OWN agent construction, not per-call events: tools silently stripped when a hook returns None (#5177), tools silently ignored on a non-tool-calling provider (#6186), `usage_limits` silently ignored if set on the `Agent(...)` constructor instead of `run*` (#1987), and usage silently zeroed on some provider adapters (#5360). Asserting these per-call wastes work and risks false-blocking a healthy run — they belong in tests + a one-time check.

## What (concrete mechanisms)
- **Construction-time provider tool-calling check.** VERIFIED signal: a pydantic-ai model exposes `model.profile.supports_tools` (a bool). The check is gated on `self._model_override is None` (the SAME guard as the anthropic model construction) — so the `model_override` test double is NEVER checked, concretely and by construction (no `.profile`-inspection heuristic to exclude it). It applies where rebar constructs an explicit model OBJECT (the anthropic path via `_build_retrying_anthropic_model`, the primary path in practice). Guard: FOR A TOOL-USING op (`tools` non-empty) where `model` is a model OBJECT exposing the capability — read defensively as `supports = getattr(getattr(model, 'profile', None), 'supports_tools', None)` (so a missing/None profile is a safe skip, never an AttributeError) — assert that when `supports is False` it raises (a `True`/`None` value passes); else raise `LLMConfigError` (fail fast). It is a NO-OP for the string-model paths (OpenAI/Gemini pass a model STRING to `Agent`, which pydantic-ai builds + validates internally — rebar has no object to introspect there) and for `model_override` (a test double). So the check bounds the path rebar actually owns without false-positiving on provider-string paths. CACHE: a module-level `set()` `_TOOL_CAPABILITY_CHECKED` keyed by the resolved model string — the check runs ONCE per unique model per process (not per call), so a hot loop pays nothing.
- **Tests — tools actually offered.** rebar builds the agent's tools as `pai_tools.filesystem_tools(cfg.repo_path)` (callables `read_file`, `list_directory`, `search_files`) + `pai_tools.rebar_tools(cfg.repo_path, allow_comment=…)` (`show_ticket`, and `comment_ticket` when allowed). A test asserts these builders return callables whose `__name__`s are exactly the expected set (so a #5177 hook-returns-None regression that strips a tool is caught).
- **Tests — `usage_limits` on `run*`, not the constructor.** A spy on `Agent`/`run_sync` asserts (a) `run_sync` IS called with `usage_limits=`, and (b) the `Agent(...)` constructor kwargs do NOT include `usage_limits` (the #1987 mis-placement). Confirmed: `Agent.run_sync` accepts `usage_limits`; the constructor does not honor it.
- **Usage-plausibility telemetry WARNING (never a block).** After a successful REAL run (`self._model_override is None` — offline test doubles report zero usage and must never warn), if `_extract_usage` reports BOTH `input_tokens == 0` AND `output_tokens == 0` while `requests > 0` (a request was actually made), log a WARNING (`llm usage looks zeroed/implausible …`) — an observability signal for the #5360 zeroed-adapter cluster. It NEVER blocks a gate (usage is observability, not load-bearing); a genuinely tiny run is at worst a benign warning.

## Scope
- Tests + the construction-time capability check + the telemetry warning. NO per-call runtime blocking for these invariants.
- NOT in scope: changing the tool surface or provider adapters themselves; a per-call usage assertion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test: `pai_tools.filesystem_tools`/`rebar_tools` offer exactly the expected tool names — fails if a tool is stripped (`test_expected_tools_offered`).
- [ ] Test: `run_sync` is called with `usage_limits=` and the `Agent(...)` constructor is NOT — fails on the #1987 mis-placement (`test_usage_limits_on_run_not_constructor`).
- [ ] Construction-time check: a model OBJECT with `profile.supports_tools == False` used for a tool-using op raises `LLMConfigError`; a string-model path is a NO-OP (test asserts no raise); the check is cached in a module-level `set()` `_TOOL_CAPABILITY_CHECKED` (invoked once per model string; `test_capability_check_cached` spies on the `model.profile` access — or a counter in the check helper — asserting a repeated same-model run reads the profile only once) — `test_capability_check_fails_fast`, `test_capability_check_noop_for_string_model`, `test_capability_check_cached`.
- [ ] Usage-plausibility emits a WARNING (asserted via caplog) on an all-zero-usage successful run and NEVER blocks (`test_usage_plausibility_warns_never_blocks`).
- [ ] `make test`/`make lint`/`make typecheck` green.

Files: `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` (the cached construction-time capability check + the usage-plausibility warning), `tests/unit/test_agent_build_invariants.py` (new).

## Verified library behavior (experiment log — pydantic-ai 1.107.0, offline)
ACTUAL captured output (no billable call):
```
FunctionModel.profile.supports_tools == True; AnthropicModel("claude-sonnet-4-6").profile.supports_tools == True (bool)
  -> VERIFIED on the ACTUAL AnthropicModel type rebar constructs (offline, no API call — just the model object)
model.profile also exposes: supports_json_schema_output, supports_json_object_output, supports_thinking, ...
Agent.__init__ has tools/toolsets: True         (tools offered via the constructor; introspectable)
Agent.run_sync accepts usage_limits: True       (#1987: usage_limits belongs on run*, NOT Agent(...))
rebar tool builders: pai_tools.filesystem_tools -> [read_file, list_directory, search_files];
                     pai_tools.rebar_tools -> [show_ticket, (comment_ticket when allow_comment)]
_extract_usage returns a dict with input_tokens/output_tokens (both 0 => the zeroed-adapter signal)
```
These are pydantic-ai LIBRARY symbols (`model.profile.supports_tools` etc.), not rebar symbols (bug succinct-formable-kite: a code-grounding pass must not read repo-absence as non-existence).
baseline.summary: Agent-build invariants as tests + one-time capability check

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

A `caplog` assertion whose records never arrive DOES NOT FAIL — it passes vacuously. `assert not [unexpected]` is trivially true against an empty list, and even a positive `assert any(...)` only fails if someone wrote it that way. So a test can lose 100% of its coverage and stay GREEN, permanently and silently, with nothing in the run output distinguishing it from a test that genuinely verified something.

This is not hypothetical. It is happening in this repository right now.

## The live instance

`src/rebar/review_bot/config.py:145-146` (`configure_logging()`) sets

    lg = logging.getLogger("rebar")
    lg.propagate = False

process-globally, and never restores it. pytest's `caplog` captures through a handler on the ROOT logger, so once propagation is off NO `rebar.*` record can reach it again for the remainder of the process. Every later `caplog` assertion on a rebar logger silently sees zero records.

Proven on a clean tree by a two-test probe: identical assertion, passes before `configure_logging()` and fails after; `caplog.at_level()` does not help because it adjusts LEVELS, not propagation. Full mechanism, both entry points, and the reproduction are on ticket b718-fb7f-b1a4-4feb — including that `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:202` calls `configure_logging()` at MODULE IMPORT time, so merely importing the app poisons the process (inert in this checkout only because `fastapi` is absent).

b718 fixes THE POISONER. This ticket is about the far larger problem it exposed: THE SUITE CANNOT TELL THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A PASSING ASSERTION AND AN UNREACHABLE ONE.

## Blast radius — measured, though the precise void count is unknown

    54 test files contain `caplog`
    255 total `caplog` occurrences

How many of those are currently void in a full run is NOT established, and establishing it is the first job of this ticket. The count depends on run order and on which logger each assertion targets, and `-n 6 --dist worksteal` distributes tests across workers nondeterministically — so the SAME assertion may be live in one run and void in the next, on the same commit. That non-determinism is itself part of the defect: coverage is not reproducible.

## Why this is severe rather than untidy

* IT FAILS OPEN. Every other gate in this repo fails closed. This one silently reports success.
* IT IS INVISIBLE. Nothing in the output marks a void assertion. Reviewers, CI and agents all see
  green.
* IT SURVIVED DETECTION. It was found only as a side effect of debugging an unrelated ticket, by an
  agent that noticed one victim test and traced it. Nobody was looking for it.
* IT IS ORDER-DEPENDENT, so a test can be genuinely verifying in isolation — which is how it was
  written and reviewed — and verify nothing in the suite that actually gates merges.
* THE VICTIM IS NEVER THE CULPRIT. The one test that DID go red pointed at
  `test_agent_call_seam.py`, nowhere near `review_bot/config.py`.

## Approach

Fixing the current poisoner (b718) removes today's instance but not the class — any future code that touches logger propagation, handlers or levels reintroduces it, with the same silence.

The durable fix is to make an unreachable log assertion FAIL LOUDLY instead of passing. Candidates to weigh, not yet decided:
  * an autouse fixture that asserts `logging.getLogger("rebar").propagate` is True at test setup, so
    the poisoning is caught at the point of damage rather than at a random later victim;
  * a `caplog` wrapper/fixture used by rebar tests that fails when zero records were captured for an
    assertion that expected some;
  * making `configure_logging()` scoped/restorable so no test can leak it in the first place (overlaps
    b718 — coordinate rather than duplicate).
The first is the smallest change that converts a silent fail-open into a loud fail-closed, and it protects against future reintroduction rather than just this instance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The number of `caplog` assertions currently void in a full default-selection run is ESTABLISHED
      and recorded — not estimated. The 54-file / 255-occurrence figures above are the search space,
      not the answer.
- [x] An unreachable log assertion FAILS rather than passing vacuously, and a test proves it: with
      propagation deliberately disabled, a previously-green assertion must go RED.
- [x] The guard catches the poisoning AT ITS SOURCE, not at a random later victim — a test asserts the
      failure names the code that disabled propagation, not an unrelated downstream test.
- [x] Any assertion found to be void is either restored to working coverage or deleted; none is left
      passing vacuously. Deleting is acceptable where the assertion no longer earns its place, but
      leaving a green no-op is not.
- [x] Coordinated with b718 so the poisoner fix and the class guard do not implement overlapping
      mechanisms.
- [x] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
baseline.summary: Unreachable caplog assertions pass vacuously: the suite cannot distinguish verified coverage from zero coverage

## Summary

There is no ongoing per-test performance signal in CI: slow tests are invisible until someone profiles by hand. Add lightweight, always-on per-test timing to the gate so the slowest tests surface in every run, and (optionally) persist a durations file usable for future cross-runner sharding (pytest-split). `--durations` and `pytest-split --store-durations` are both verified working on this suite.

## What

- Add `--durations=25` to the default-suite pytest invocation in `gerrit-verify.yaml`
  and `test.yml` so every gate run prints its 25 slowest tests (setup/call/teardown).
  Confirmed compatible with `-q`, coverage, and xdist.
- OPTIONAL (behind this task): add a scheduled/post-merge step that runs
  `pytest --store-durations --durations-path .test_durations` and uploads `.test_durations`
  as an artifact, so timing data is tracked over time and available if the team later shards
  across runners with pytest-split. Verified: `--store-durations` writes a valid JSON map
  (`{"<nodeid>": <seconds>, …}`).
- `.test_durations` must be gitignored (or artifact-only) so it never leaks into the
  checkout and never trips the repo-leak guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `--durations=25` added to the default-suite pytest command in
      `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` and `.github/workflows/test.yml`.
- [ ] A gate run's log shows the 25 slowest tests.
- [ ] If a `.test_durations` store step is added, the file is artifact/gitignored (never
      committed, never leaks into the working tree).
- [ ] Change passes CI (`Verified +1`) and lands via Gerrit.
baseline.summary: Bake per-test performance logging (--durations) into the gate

# S5 — The `gerrit-verify.yaml` workflow (reuse `test.yml`)

Part of epic 1fa8 (CI as a second Gerrit gate vote via gerrit-to-platform → GitHub Actions).

## Why
This is the workflow g2p dispatches — it runs the SAME checks as `.github/workflows/test.yml` and
casts the `Verified` vote. It follows the fixed 3-job g2p production shape (clear-vote →
build-and-test → vote), keeping checks drift-free by reusing the existing steps.

## What
Author `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` with `workflow_dispatch` + the nine `GERRIT_*`
inputs and the three jobs, all third-party actions SHA-pinned.

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` (and optionally converge with `test.yml`).
- Depends on S4 (the GitHub vars/secret) and references the `Verified` label from S1.
- Out of scope: g2p host install (S3), the gate activation (S6).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Author `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` triggered by `workflow_dispatch` with the nine
      `GERRIT_*` inputs; `concurrency` keyed on the change with `cancel-in-progress: true`.
- [ ] `clear-vote` job: `lfreleng-actions/gerrit-review-action` `vote-type: clear` (resets
      `Verified→0`; verified semantics) + a short `sleep` for replication.
- [ ] `build-and-test` job: `lfreleng-actions/checkout-gerrit-change-action` (fetch the exact
      `GERRIT_REFSPEC`) then the existing `test.yml` steps (lint / typecheck / test matrix + the

      vote-type: ${{ WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION }}` → `Verified` +1/-1, with the run URL in the vote message.

baseline.description:
# A change can be permanently blocked by a stale LLM-Review -1

When `LLM-Review` votes -1 for a reason that is later RESOLVED OUTSIDE the diff — the `bugfix-size-attestation` finding is the concrete case: it blocks on the ticket lacking a plan-review attestation, which is earned by running `rebar review-plan`, not by editing code — there is no reliable way to get the vote recomputed. The change cannot land even though the finding no longer holds.

## The copy condition swallows every re-trigger
    copy condition: "changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE OR changekind:MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE
                     OR changekind:TRIVIAL_REBASE"

Observed on change 1577 (bug 85fa), four attempts, all copied the stale -1 rather than re-reviewing:
  1. `git commit --amend --no-edit` + push  -> same tree AND message -> NO_CODE_CHANGE -> copied
  2. commit-MESSAGE-only amend + push      -> still NO_CODE_CHANGE (tree unchanged) -> copied
  3. `recheck-review` comment (documented in docs/review-policy.md:47) -> the review bot did
     not respond; it also CANCELLED the in-flight CI run, leaving a spurious Verified -1
  4. rebase onto current main + push       -> TRIVIAL_REBASE -> copied

CI behaves differently and correctly: `Verified` re-ran on patch sets 3 and 4. Only the LLM review is stuck, which makes the asymmetry easy to miss.

The remaining levers per docs/review-policy.md are a maintainer re-trigger or a genuine content change. Manufacturing a code edit purely to defeat vote-copying is a bad incentive: it adds unreviewed churn to satisfy a mechanism, not a reviewer.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than working around
The gate stack already taxes small fixes. On 85fa: a ~70-line correctness fix hit the 800-line module cap, which forced a module extraction, which pushed it to 321 non-test lines, which tripped the 150-line bugfix floor, which required an LLM plan review to clear — and then the resulting -1 could not be recomputed once the attestation existed. Three gates compounding, with no exit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] ~~ A blocked author can cause LLM-Review to re-evaluate the CURRENT patch set without~~ — SUPERSEDED, not delivered here
      changing code — e.g. `recheck-review` actually re-runs the reviewer, mirroring what
      `recheck` does for CI.
- [x] ~~ If `recheck-review` is the intended mechanism, it works and is tested; if it is not,~~ — SUPERSEDED, not delivered here
      docs/review-policy.md stops naming it.
- [x] ~~ A re-trigger comment does not CANCEL a running CI job (observed: posting~~ — SUPERSEDED, not delivered here
      `recheck-review` cancelled run 31349189893 and produced a Verified -1 that reflected
      cancellation, not a real failure).
- [x] ~~ Consider narrowing the copy condition: a finding whose evidence lives OUTSIDE the diff~~ — SUPERSEDED, not delivered here
      (attestation state on the ticket) should not be copied forward across patch sets, since
      the world it described can change without the tree changing.

## DUPLICATE — superseded by bug 6a81
Filed before finding the existing tickets. The acceptance criteria above are NOT delivered by this ticket; they are struck through and carried by:
  6a81  recheck-review should accept a bugfix-size-attestation block once the ticket
        has the attestation  (the primary issue; my findings are recorded there)
  0d78  Prevent recheck-review from retriggering CI  (the cancellation side effect)
  b0f5  /rerun and recheck-review are fire-and-forget into a volatile queue  (why the
        re-trigger produced no reviewer response at all)
baseline.summary: A resolved LLM-Review -1 cannot be re-evaluated: every re-trigger path hits a vote copy condition

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The completion-verification close gate dies verdict-less when its agentic verify step falls into a tool-call loop: the step budget exhausts, the run surfaces a bare `LLMError` with `diagnostic: null`, and the only documented exit is `--force-close` (an unattested close). Four exhaustions on epic e369; three of four instrumented runs LOOPED, wasting 40-70% of each pathological run (measured on ticket c827-2a23-cd00-473e). Six prior attempts adjusted budgets or added reporting; none acted at the layer where the loop happens.

## Approach

Fix the causal chain end to end, in dependency order. First give the repetition detector a signal that separates a k-cycle from healthy breadth (a windowed distinct-ratio produced in `usage_log._repetition_summary` — the existing headline metric is provably inverted on real traces). Independently, replace the provider-broken forced-landing primitive: the `tool_step_limit` empty-filter rewrite in `src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py` causes a Bedrock/Anthropic 400 (`toolConfig` must be defined while history holds `toolUse` blocks — live-proven) — keep tools advertised and steer with synthetic tool results instead. Make bounded recovery reachable for a step-budget exhaustion (`CompletionAgentStep.run` currently catches only `UnretryableOutputError`), and surface the already-computed repetition diagnostic in the `gate_error_v1` sidecar. Then wire the detector to ACT during the run: a typed runaway error classified ahead of the provider-outage fallback in `interpret_failure`, routed into the shipped bounded recovery + tool-free finalizer so the verdict is built from fresh per-criterion evidence, never the poisoned history. Finally, record per-run request/tool-call usage durably by default so the gate can be tuned from data. This fits the problem because every piece wires or repairs a mechanism that already exists and was measured failing — nothing parallel is introduced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] a runaway tool-call cycle in the completion gate's verify step is detected DURING the run, aborted at that point, and routed to a verdict built from fresh per-criterion evidence — never a bare `LLMError` with `diagnostic: null`; checked by the actuator child's end-to-end test
- [x] no code path empties the advertised tool surface mid-run after a tool call has occurred, so the Bedrock/Anthropic toolConfig 400 cannot recur; checked by a regression test asserting tool definitions persist for the whole run
- [x] every budget exhaustion or runaway leaves an operator-actionable diagnostic (a `gate_error_v1` sidecar carrying the repetition counters) distinguishing "it looped" from "it ran out of room"; checked by the diagnostic child's sidecar test
- [x] gate runs record request and tool-call usage durably by default, including the loop-vs-breadth axis; checked by the instrumentation child's tests
- [x] a healthy high-breadth run is never truncated or aborted by any of the above — budgets remain failure bounds, not workload ceilings; checked by tests replaying the healthy-run profile (0.922 distinct ratio, minimum 24-window ratio 0.833) and asserting no abort

## Child decomposition

Children by responsibility (dependency order): the detector signal (`distinct_ratio_window`, window 24, trip <= 0.50, single-sourced in `usage_log`) delivers criterion 5's discriminator and is a prerequisite of the actuator and the instrumentation; the protocol-safe forced landing (steering toolset replacing the empty-filter cutoff) delivers criterion 2; recovery reachability (catch extension in `CompletionAgentStep.run`) is a prerequisite of the actuator and the diagnostic surfacing; diagnostic surfacing (sidecar + close-gate message) delivers criterion 3; the actuator (typed runaway error routed to bounded recovery) delivers criterion 1; default-on usage recording delivers criterion 4.
baseline.summary: Completion gate loop breaker: detect runaways during the run, act, and land a verdict

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Operator directive (verbatim, 2026-08-13): 'add standing guidance for the project: flaky tests get debugged using rebar-debug, not retried until they pass. a flaky CI pipeline is a failure that slows development, wastes tokens, and decreases our trust in CI as a regression oracle.'

Tonight's evidence: the order-dependent leaked-logger flake (future-fibroid-hammerkop) cost four `Verified -1`s across changes 1715/1716/1717/1720, multiple recheck cycles, and hours of queued rebases before it was root-caused (deterministic RED via a two-file pytest invocation) and fixed class-wide in change 1721. Root-causing it once was cheaper than every recheck combined.

The guidance today points the other way. `AGENTS.md` says "A `Verified -1` is a CI failure (open the run; comment `recheck` if it is a flake)", and `CONTRIBUTING.md` §6 says "**`Verified -1` but the failure looks transient/flaky.** Comment **`recheck`** to re-run CI on the same patchset." Both read as licence to retry a nondeterministic test until it passes. Adding the new rule without narrowing these two would leave the repo self-contradicting.

## Approach
One authoritative wording in `AGENTS.md` (the canonical agent guidance, read by every harness); the two existing recheck lines are narrowed to point at it rather than restate it.

1. **The rule, in `AGENTS.md`** — replace the parenthetical on the existing "The gate" bullet and add ONE sibling bullet in the same Git-workflow list, in that list's bolded-lead style. It must carry three things and no more: (a) a test that fails intermittently is a **bug to root-cause**, not a retry — debug it with the `/rebar-debug` workflow (hypothesis-driven, isolated worktree, deterministic RED before any fix) and fix the class, not the instance; (b) the one-sentence rationale — a flaky pipeline slows development, wastes tokens, and erodes CI as a regression oracle; (c) the narrow carve-out — `recheck` is for **provably environmental** faults (a TLS/promisor cert flake, a missing CI dispatch, a runner outage) and the recheck comment must state that reasoning. AGENTS.md's keep-it-lean rule caps this at the bullet plus the one-clause edit above it.
2. **Reconcile `CONTRIBUTING.md` §6** — rewrite the "`Verified -1` but the failure looks transient/flaky" bullet so it splits the two cases explicitly: an environmental fault is recheckable with stated reasoning; a nondeterministic **test** is a bug and gets debugged, with a pointer to the AGENTS.md rule. The adjacent "CI didn't run / no run appeared" bullet is already an environmental case and stays as-is — it is the carve-out's worked example, so it is left alone deliberately rather than overlooked.
3. **Cross-link, don't duplicate** — `docs/dependency-advisory-runbook.md` already states the same shape for its own gate ("Only a DB-unreachable failure is recheckable. `recheck` can NEVER clear a real finding"); it is consistent with the new rule and needs no edit. No new doc is created: `CONTRIBUTING.md` §6 remains the CI-triage home and now points at the rule instead of contradicting it.

**Out of scope.** No change to the `recheck` trigger mechanism, the review bot, or `gerrit-verify.yaml` — this ticket changes guidance only. No quarantine/auto-retry tooling is added; the directive is explicitly that flakes are debugged, so building a retry facility would contradict it.

## Scope
- `AGENTS.md` — the rule bullet plus the narrowed clause on the existing "The gate" bullet.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — §6's transient/flaky bullet, reconciled and cross-linked.
- `tests/unit/test_flaky_test_guidance.py` — new; pins the rule and the reconciliation.

## Testing
This is guidance, so the testable behavior is that the rule is present AND that the old retry-until-green licence is gone — the second half is what a plain "text exists" test would miss.
- **Happy path:** a new `tests/unit/test_flaky_test_guidance.py` asserts `AGENTS.md` carries the rule's load-bearing phrases (intermittent failure is a bug to root-cause, the `/rebar-debug` pointer, the three-part rationale, and the environmental-only carve-out) and that `CONTRIBUTING.md` §6 names both branches.
- **Failure/regression path:** the same test asserts the **contradiction is gone** — neither file still tells a reader to `recheck` because a failure "looks transient/flaky" without qualifying it as environmental. Verified by restoring the old sentence locally and watching the test fail before reverting.
- **Gates:** `make lint`, `make typecheck`, the `check_*` gates, generator no-diff, and the CI unit selection (`test_codex_agent_guidance.py` and `test_agents_claim_assignee_guidance.py` already pin other AGENTS.md content, so they prove the edit did not disturb neighbouring guidance).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `AGENTS.md` carries the rule as concise agent guidance with the rationale compressed to one sentence naming all three costs (slows development, wastes tokens, erodes CI as a regression oracle).
- [x] The guidance names the deterministic-reproduction expectation via the `/rebar-debug` workflow and the narrow legitimate-recheck carve-out (provably environmental faults, reasoning stated in the recheck comment).
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` §6 no longer offers `recheck` for a failure that merely "looks transient/flaky", and cross-links the AGENTS.md rule instead of restating it; `AGENTS.md`'s own "`recheck` if it is a flake" clause is narrowed the same way.
- [x] `tests/unit/test_flaky_test_guidance.py` pins both the new rule and the absence of the old licence, and passes; `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the CI unit selection are green.
baseline.summary: Guidance: flaky tests get debugged, not retried

baseline.description:
## Reproduction Steps

1. Sync a rebar store to Jira (e.g. the REB cutover) where local tickets have
   assignees that are not Jira users (agent names like `claude`, `claude-opus`).
2. Run `rebar reconcile --mode dry-run` after the initial create pass.

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** once a ticket is created+bound and its synced fields match, the
  reconciler emits no further mutations for it (convergence).
- **Actual:** ~323 of 355 bound tickets emit an `assignee` update every pass. The
  local assignee (e.g. `claude`) is not a Jira user, so the applier soft-fails the
  assign (`assignee 'claude' cannot be assigned — retrying without assignee`),
  Jira stays unassigned, and `_assignee_matches("claude", None)` is False — so the
  differ re-emits the same assignee update on the next pass. Perpetual churn (passes
  still succeed; the canary stays green — this is noise/inefficiency, not failure).

## Root cause

`outbound_differ._diff_fields` + `_assignee_matches`: a local assignee that cannot
be resolved to a Jira account never matches Jira's (unassigned) state, and there is
no "unresolvable assignee → don't re-emit" suppression after the applier soft-fails.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A bound ticket whose local assignee cannot be assigned in Jira does NOT
      re-emit an assignee update every pass (converge or suppress-after-soft-fail).
- [ ] Decide the intended semantics: skip assignee sync for non-Jira-user
      assignees, map agent identities to a service account, or record an
      unresolvable-assignee marker so the differ stops re-emitting.
- [ ] A dry-run after convergence shows 0 perpetual assignee-only updates.
baseline.summary: Reconciler churns assignee updates for non-Jira-user assignees (never converges)

# Two CloudWatch alarms have NO actions, so they fire into an empty room

## Context / Problem

`rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` is the alarm the review-bot's fail-closed path depends on: `voter.py`'s `_voter_error()` writes a greppable `VOTER_ERROR` marker, `infra/scripts/observability.sh` §4 publishes `rebar/host:voter_errors`, and `infra/terraform/monitoring_s4b.tf` alarms on it. The chain is real and the metric genuinely publishes (~22 datapoints over 2h, consistent with the 5-minute probe).

**But the alarm declares no actions, so nothing tells a human when it fires.** Verified on both sides: `grep -nE "actions" infra/terraform/monitoring_s4b.tf` returns NOTHING, and live `describe-alarms` returns `AlarmActions: []`, `OKActions: []`, `ActionsEnabled: true`. The alarm transitions `OK -> ALARM` correctly and silently — discoverable only by someone already looking in the CloudWatch console, i.e. precisely the person who does not need an alarm.

**Why it matters.** The `LLM-Review` vote gates every landing on `main` (ADR-0013). When the voter fails closed, changes become unsubmittable — a failure that is *silent to Gerrit by design* (no vote rather than a wrong one), and now also silent to the operator. Discovered while working the Bedrock production cutover [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a], whose ORDERING criterion treats this alarm as the safety net that must be proven before the model flip.

## The defect is cited, not asserted

Two authoritative in-repo statements establish that an actionless alarm is a defect here, so this is not merely the reporter's expectation:

1. `infra/terraform/monitoring.tf:205-207` — of a previously-adopted alarm: *"created
   out-of-band with an EMPTY alarm_actions list (so it never notified). Bringing it under IaC
   also WIRES it to the SNS topic, **closing the silent-alarm gap**."* Empty `alarm_actions` is
   named, in this repo's own IaC, as a gap to be closed.
2. `infra/terraform/monitoring_s4b.tf:19-21` — this alarm's own header states its purpose is that
   it *"surfaces a persistently broken voter to an operator instead of letting unsubmittable
   changes stack up unnoticed."* The resource does not do what its own contract says.

**Counter-evidence considered and rejected:** `monitoring_1fa8.tf:38-42` says it *"mirrors S4b's voter_errors alarm; UNLIKE S4b it WIRES SNS ... because a broken CI dispatcher silently blocks ALL submits."* That reads as if S4b's silence were deliberate — but the stated rationale for wiring 1fa8 ("silently blocks ALL submits") is *equally* true of S4b by ADR-0013, and S4b's own header claims operator notification. So 1fa8's author observed the omission and rationalized it rather than fixing it; it documents the convention FROM the one instance that does not follow it. This is a defect, not intended behavior.

## No operator decision is needed — the target is the established convention

This was queued as "needs the operator to pick a notification target". It does not. An audit of all **13** `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` blocks in `infra/terraform/` shows **eleven** set BOTH `alarm_actions` AND `ok_actions` to the shared `aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn`:

    HAS-ACTIONS  g2p_dispatch_errors             monitoring_1fa8.tf:74-75
    HAS-ACTIONS  review_bot_merge_change_errors  monitoring_88ab.tf:62-63
    HAS-ACTIONS  deploy_errors                   monitoring_autodeploy.tf:57-58
    HAS-ACTIONS  review_interrupts               monitoring_autodeploy.tf:128-129
    HAS-ACTIONS  root_disk_pressure              monitoring_autodeploy.tf:180-181
    HAS-ACTIONS  bedrock_invoke_client_errors    monitoring_eb6e.tf:121-122
    HAS-ACTIONS  mirror_out_of_sync              monitoring_ws7.tf:52-53
    HAS-ACTIONS  gerrit_gate_down                monitoring.tf:88-89
    HAS-ACTIONS  ec2_system_check                monitoring.tf:135-136
    HAS-ACTIONS  ec2_instance_check              monitoring.tf:161-162
    HAS-ACTIONS  gerrit_data_disk_high           monitoring.tf:239-240
    NO-ACTIONS   voter_errors                    monitoring_s4b.tf:35   <-- this ticket
    NO-ACTIONS   replication_errors              monitoring_s5.tf:30    <-- SIBLING

The fix is to follow the existing pattern, not to choose a target. (A prior comment recorded an operator ruling naming `joeoakhart@navapbc.com`; that is the existing email subscription ON `aws_sns_topic.alerts`, so wiring the shared topic satisfies it — no new destination resource.)

## SCOPE — fix BOTH alarms in this one change

`replication_errors` (`infra/terraform/monitoring_s5.tf:30`) has the IDENTICAL defect, the identical shape, and no ticket of its own. These two are the ONLY alarms in the repo lacking actions. Fixing one and leaving the other guarantees rediscovery later, and would mean two terraform applies for one line each. **This ticket's scope is expanded to cover both.**

In scope:
- `infra/terraform/monitoring_s4b.tf` — add `alarm_actions` + `ok_actions`.
- `infra/terraform/monitoring_s5.tf` — same, for `replication_errors`.
- a new regression guard test (below).

Out of scope: `observability.sh` (the publishers are correct and working), and the alarms' thresholds (`period = 300`, `evaluation_periods = 1`, `threshold = 0` are deliberate and fine).

## Approach

1. Add `alarm_actions = [aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn]` and `ok_actions = [aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn]`
   to BOTH resources, matching `monitoring_autodeploy.tf`. Wire OK as well as ALARM so a recovery
   is visible and the alarm does not read as stuck-firing.
2. Correct `monitoring_1fa8.tf`'s now-false "UNLIKE S4b it WIRES SNS" comment.

## The guard is the point, not just the two fixes

Two instances that both survived review means the convention is not checkable. Add a **test that parses every `resource "aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm"` block under `infra/terraform/` and FAILS on any block lacking `alarm_actions`**, so alarm number 14 cannot ship mute.

Guard requirements:
- **Anti-vacuity assertion (mandatory).** The test MUST assert the parser actually found the
  alarms — `assert len(alarms) >= 13`. A guard that silently parses zero blocks is the exact
  failure class this session has been fixing all night (bugs 34c2, 8a5e, 1909); without this the
  guard is a tautology that passes forever after any parser or layout drift.
- **Explicit opt-out, never silence.** If some future alarm legitimately should not notify, the
  guard must require a documented marker comment (e.g. `# rebar:allow-actionless-alarm: <reason>`)
  inside that resource block. Absence of actions must never pass by default.
- Offline text-contract test, following the existing precedent
  `tests/unit/test_mirror_lock_terraform.py`. New file: `tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py`.

## Testing

The guard is RED before the fix (it fails naming `voter_errors` and `replication_errors`) and GREEN after — that ordering is the proof. Anti-vacuity is verified by mutation: point the parser at an empty directory and confirm the test FAILS rather than passes.

Note the alarm wiring itself cannot be unit-tested end-to-end; live confirmation is an apply-time observation, recorded below as a residual.

## REMEMBER THE APPLY — landing is not applying

Committing this does NOT create the notification. Applies are manual and [rebar:1c39-96d4-8f9e-4d38] records that the Terraform drift check does not gate a Gerrit change, so un-applied infra lands and reads as done. Whoever works this MUST state explicitly whether the change was APPLIED or merely MERGED. If no AWS credentials are available, say so plainly and record the un-applied state as an open residual rather than implying the alarms now notify anyone.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `voter_errors` (`monitoring_s4b.tf`) declares `alarm_actions` AND `ok_actions` pointing at
      `aws_sns_topic.alerts`, matching `monitoring_autodeploy.tf`.
- [x] `replication_errors` (`monitoring_s5.tf`) does the same, in the SAME change.
- [x] a guard test parses every `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` block in `infra/terraform/` and
      fails on any lacking `alarm_actions`; it was seen RED before the fix and GREEN after.
- [x] the guard carries an anti-vacuity assertion (`>= 13` alarms parsed) that itself fails when
      the parser finds nothing.
- [x] the guard requires an explicit documented opt-out marker for any intentionally silent alarm.
- [x] `monitoring_1fa8.tf`'s "UNLIKE S4b it WIRES SNS" comment is corrected.
- [x] the report and the ticket state PLAINLY whether the change is APPLIED or only MERGED. If
      only merged, the un-applied apply is recorded as an explicit open residual and the ticket
      does NOT claim the alarms notify anyone in production.
baseline.summary: The voter_errors alarm notifies nobody: rebar-gerrit-voter-errors has no alarm_actions

## Context / Problem
Gerrit change 1869 patch set 1 (revision dcb219a7408e2ebeb68d3a17c97df4907b28ba2d) failed its sole macOS/Python 3.13 job in GitHub Actions run 32187810048. The failed test was tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py::test_session_finish_fails_explicitly_when_porcelain_times_out: its nested pytest subprocess exceeded the test harness's 12-second outer deadline even though captured stderr showed the intended internal git status --porcelain watchdog raising subprocess.TimeoutExpired after 5 seconds. The rest of the run passed (13,880 passed, 65 skipped); Ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13 all passed.

This ticket is intentionally separate from change 1869. The observed 5-second internal watchdog plus 12-second outer deadline is only a lead: investigate dynamically whether macOS teardown/scheduling overhead, product liveness, or unrelated infrastructure explains the failure.

## Plan
- Reproduce the real nested-pytest harness under controlled scheduling/teardown delays and capture the runtime path from the five-second Git watchdog through pytest session-finish cleanup.
- Generate and run falsifiable experiments that distinguish harness-budget exhaustion from a product watchdog failure and from unrelated runner infrastructure.
- After a proven RCA, encode the final observable timeout contract with a held-out RED oracle, repair via an independent fixer, then prove GREEN, exact-defect mutation RED, and original-report replication.
- Sweep sibling nested-process deadline tests for the same budget-coupling pattern.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Runtime evidence proves a specific, changeable root cause and rules out product-watchdog and unrelated-infrastructure alternatives.
- [ ] A final-form held-out regression test is observed RED before repair and GREEN afterward.
- [ ] Reintroducing the exact defect returns the oracle to RED, then restoring the repair returns it to GREEN.
- [ ] The original nested-pytest blocking-Git scenario completes reliably with the intended explicit watchdog failure under controlled macOS-equivalent teardown overhead.
- [ ] Relevant focused tests plus lint and typecheck pass.
- [ ] Sibling timing-contract occurrences are swept and every confirmed sibling is fixed or ticketed.

- tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py

# DC parent sync is ONE-WAY: outbound writes the Epic Link, inbound never reads it

## The asymmetry

After Gerrit **1311** (ticket 39c1), `JiraDataCenterTransport.set_parent` writes a non-sub-task's parent to the instance-discovered "Epic Link" custom field. Nothing reads it back.

`get_parent_map` (`transport.py:515-546`) — the ONLY inbound parent read — searches with `fields="parent"` and extracts `fields.parent` alone:

    for issue in self._paged_search(query, fields="parent", rate_limit_retry=True):
        parent = fields.get("parent") if isinstance(fields, dict) else None
        out[key] = parent.get("key") if isinstance(parent, dict) else None

Repo-wide, `Epic Link` / `_epic_link` appears ONLY in `transport.py`'s outbound path.

**So a parent rebar sets on Data Center is invisible to rebar on the next inbound pass.** On DC, inbound can only ever see a SUB-TASK's parent — and [rebar:1a9f-50c0-e7a5-4fda] gives reason to doubt even that path takes effect.

## Why this is the epic's signature class, again

"Cloud has the translation, DC never got its half" — d067, 8d68, 751e, 2b16/88d9, 39c1. This is a fresh instance, created by the fix for the sixth one. Not a regression (nothing read the Epic Link before), and 1311 is not wrong — its scope was the outbound half, and the emit gate only ever emits an EPIC parent, so the Epic Link is the correct target. But the ROUND TRIP is open, and epic e369's headline criterion is BIDIRECTIONAL reconcile.

## The unproven risk that makes this more than cosmetic

If outbound writes a parent the next inbound pass cannot see, the differ may re-emit the SAME parent mutation every pass — the perpetual re-emission bug 8b25 was filed for (~230 steady-state `fields=['parent']` mutations on Cloud). **Explicitly NOT asserted here**: it depends on how the outbound differ decides a parent is already synced. The live cell that would show it is `test_a_repeat_pass_over_a_converged_pair_plans_nothing`, which is currently GREEN — so either the churn does not occur or that cell does not cover this shape. Settle it before assuming either.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `get_parent_map` returns a non-sub-task's parent from the instance-discovered "Epic Link"
      field, in addition to `fields.parent` for sub-tasks — field id discovered BY NAME, never
      hardcoded, reusing the discovery+cache the outbound side already has rather than a second copy
- [x] the two shapes do not collide: a sub-task's `fields.parent` still wins where both exist, and a
      test pins which takes precedence
- [x] the round trip closes: a parent WRITTEN by outbound is SEEN by the next inbound read, asserted
      against a real DC instance on a harness run (run id recorded). A unit suite does NOT settle
      this — changes 1276, 1288 and 1302 were all mutation-proven and all wrong live
- [x] idempotence is proven, not assumed: repeated passes over a converged epic-parent pair emit NO
      further parent mutation — this is the churn risk above
- [x] `get_parent_map`'s degradation contract is preserved: a failure still logs a WARNING and
      returns `{}` so the inbound pass falls back to parentless rather than aborting
- [x] `transport.py` stays under the 800-LOC cap (it is ~781 after 1311; the discovery helper
      already exists, so this should reuse it rather than grow a parallel one)
baseline.summary: DC parent sync is one-way: outbound writes the Epic Link, inbound never reads it

## Summary

Discovered while validating bug 751a's review_ticket retarget via a live 'Live External Integration' workflow_dispatch (run 31856166064). The 'external LLM (live bedrock)' lane failed on ONE test, unrelated to the review_ticket retarget:

    tests/external/test_completion_banking_behavior_0707.py::test_dense_completion_banks_and_terminates_in_two_of_three_trials

with:

    rebar.llm.errors.LLMError: completion verification workflow did not produce a verdict: step 'decide@then/verify' failed: the LLM provider call failed: _observe_trial.<locals>.observed_upsert() got an unexpected keyword argument 'evidence_sufficient'

Same run: 17 passed, 1 failed on the bedrock arm; the anthropic and openai LLM arms and the langfuse round-trip lane were fully GREEN.

## Root cause (CONFIRMED)

This is a TEST-HARNESS signature drift, NOT a production bug. The symbols `_observe_trial` and `observed_upsert` exist ONLY in the test file `tests/external/test_completion_banking_behavior_0707.py` (`_observe_trial` at line 51, the nested `observed_upsert` closure at line 78); `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py` contains neither.

The test monkeypatches `banking.CriterionBank.upsert` with `observed_upsert`, whose signature is `(self, criterion_id, met, evidence, *, source='tool')`. The REAL `CriterionBank.upsert` (src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_banking.py:459) has since gained two keyword-only params: `evidence_sufficient: bool | None = None` (~line 466) and `seeded: bool = False` (~line 467). Production legitimately passes them:
- `record_insufficient()` -> `upsert(..., source='fallback', evidence_sufficient=False)` (completion_banking.py:515-516), reached via the bounded-fallback path (completion_tool_policy.py:105);
- the finalizer `upsert(..., evidence_sufficient=...)` (completion_banking.py:662-667);
- the cache seed `upsert(..., seeded=True)` (completion_verdict_cache.py:286).

When `verify_completion` runs under the monkeypatch and hits the bounded-fallback path, `upsert(..., evidence_sufficient=False)` reaches the narrow `observed_upsert` closure, which raises TypeError. The anthropic/openai arms gathered sufficient evidence and never entered the fallback, so upsert was only ever called with `source=` (which the narrow stub accepts) — hence bedrock-only. Deterministic TypeError, not flakiness. `evidence_sufficient` (and `seeded`) carry a real signal into the banked entry, so they MUST be preserved, not dropped.

## Decided fix

Thread ALL keyword arguments through the test's `observed_upsert` stub so it stays signature-faithful to the real `upsert`: keep `source` (used for the write-bookkeeping) and forward every other kwarg (`evidence_sufficient`, `seeded`, and any future kwarg) unchanged to the original upsert via `**kwargs`. Do NOT make the caller stop passing `evidence_sufficient` — production is correct and its signal must be preserved. No change to completion_recovery.py or completion_banking.py.

Extract the bookkeeping stub into a shared, live-dependency-free helper `tests/_bank_observer.py` (`make_observed_upsert`) so the live eval and a fast unit regression share one wrapper, and add a unit regression `tests/unit/test_completion_bank_observer_forwarding.py` driving `CriterionBank.record_insufficient` (evidence_sufficient=False) and a seeded upsert through the wrapper to prove the TypeError is gone and the kwargs are forwarded (no live creds).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The test stub `observed_upsert` forwards `evidence_sufficient` (and `seeded`) through to the real `CriterionBank.upsert` (via `**kwargs`), preserving the signal, so `decide@then/verify` produces a verdict. Production code is unchanged.
- [x] A fast unit regression (no live creds) drives `record_insufficient`/`seeded` through the shared wrapper and fails RED (the exact TypeError) before the fix, GREEN after.
- [x] The evidence_sufficient/seeded kwarg TypeError is eliminated on the bedrock arm — the completion verifier runs to a verdict (live run 31870102530: all 3 trials error=None, verdict=PASS; the prior LLMError is gone). [operator-attested] A separate, pre-existing behavioral assertion (_bounded_bank_gaps) still fails on the bedrock-pinned oracle (model bulk-banks); tracked as discovered bug 3bfc-b16c-c3c4-4e55.

## Testing

- ruff check + format-check + mypy on changed files.
- pytest tests/unit/test_completion_bank_observer_forwarding.py (RED->GREEN) + the completion-verifier unit subset.
- A workflow_dispatch of 'Live External Integration' (bedrock arm) for authoritative live confirmation.
baseline.summary: External bedrock lane: completion verifier observed_upsert() got unexpected kwarg 'evidence_sufficient'
