## Context / observed warning
Tracker writes repeatedly emit:

`WARNING rebar.llm.enrich_drain: enrich drain gate check took 300–500 ms (> 20 ms budget)`

A closed ticket (`verymad-hard-weaverbird`) recorded the same observation at 300–800 ms but explicitly left it separate. No open bug owns this warning. The warning occurs on ordinary write paths where the feature gate is intended to be cheap.

## Investigation and repair protocol
- Use `rebar-debug` in a fresh worktree from current `origin/main`.
- Reproduce the latency with deterministic instrumentation or a bounded measurement that isolates the gate check from unrelated tracker work.
- Build an evidence dossier, propose falsifiable causes, and confirm the runtime mechanism before changing production code.
- Establish defect legitimacy against the documented 20 ms budget and run the caller-dependency gate.
- If a defect is proven and remediation does not require a behavioral/design decision, repair via physically withheld RED-oracle TDD, run the relevant and full gates, send through Gerrit, and close only after both votes are green and the change lands.
- If remediation changes when enrichment runs, its consistency guarantees, or another user-visible behavior, stop with a decision brief for operator approval.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The warning is reproduced and its root cause is proven with runtime evidence and exact citations.
- [ ] The ticket records whether the behavior is a defect against the 20 ms contract or needs an operator decision.
- [ ] For an autonomous defect repair, a mechanism-level regression test is observed RED before the fix, physically withheld from the fixer, GREEN afterward, and shown to fail under a defect-seeded mutation.
- [ ] The original warning scenario is replicated after remediation and meets the documented budget without weakening enrichment correctness.
- [ ] Construct and surface-parity siblings receive explicit dispositions.
- [ ] Any code change passes local gates, Gerrit LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1, lands, and only then is the ticket closed.
baseline.summary: Enrich drain cheap gate exceeds its 20 ms latency budget

baseline.description:
## Context
rebar has no general mechanism to apply an idempotent setup/config change to an ALREADY-EXISTING install. Init-time `_migrate_*`/`_ensure_*` functions (e.g. `_migrate_gc_config`) run only at `init`/re-init, so a fix shipped after a store was initialized never reaches it unless someone re-inits — the gap the `gc.auto=0` legacy-store issue exposed. Discovered from the gc discussion (e3d0).

**School B (desired-state / convergent), not School A (ordered ledger).** Idempotent, safe-to-re-run, drift-correcting (Ansible/Puppet/Chef check-then-act `changed`/`ok`; K8s level-triggered reconcile). We do NOT build an ordered version ledger (Alembic/Flyway/Rails are for irreversible, unsafe-to-rerun migrations). The A-tier ledger (committed store-format version, ordered, fail-closed on too-new) is future work (docs/migrations.md + doctor idea dabb).

## Design (corrected against origin/main via two plan-review passes)
**Ensure-registry (`ensures.py`).** A registry of ensure units, each `{stable, immutable id, callable(tracker) -> EnsureOutcome}` where the callable is check-then-act (no-op when converged) and `EnsureOutcome` is a small dataclass `{id, status: Literal["ok","changed", "failed"], detail}`. `run_ensures(tracker)` runs ALL units unconditionally under the STORE write lock (`_store/lock.py` write_lock — init_core does NOT currently hold it), catches a raising unit (skip-and-continue → `failed`), returns the outcome list, and rewrites `.ensure-applied` to the ids of the NON-failed (ok/changed) units only.

**The exact 5 re-init idempotent steps migrated** (init.py:209-213 — the already-initialized path that reaches existing stores): `env-id`, `gc-config`, `merge-ours driver`, `gitattributes` (COMMIT), `gitignore` (COMMIT). **Two units commit** (gitattributes AND gitignore) → check-then-act (tree-check before commit) required for BOTH. These same units also appear on the fresh-init path (init.py:242-248) and `_ensure_env_id` is additionally called from `_init_via_symlink` (init.py:564, 582); the migration wires `run_ensures()` at all init entry points and removes the hand-listed calls from each, with no double-execution. The fresh-init-only bootstrap (`_commit_precommit`, `_gen_local_files`, `_exclude_scratch_in_tracker`, `_ensure_branch_user_config`) are NOT ensures and stay.

**Entry points (non-hot):** init/re-init/symlink-init (always), `rebar fsck --repair` (opt-in), MCP server startup (best-effort — log-and-continue, never abort boot; under write lock). The sweep never runs on the hot write path or on pure reads.

**fsck reconciliation (origin/main ALREADY has `fsck --repair`).** `fsck --repair` is the existing A3 data-remediation verb (rebuild snapshots, retire orphans; requires mutation; `--dry-run`/`--limit`). We do NOT add a new `--fix` flag — we FOLD the ensure-sweep into the existing `--repair` path (one "drive to healthy" verb, both data + config). Plain read-only `rebar fsck` gains an `ensures: N/M applied` line derived WITHOUT calling run_ensures: M = count of registry ids, N = count present in `.ensure-applied`. The pending-hint points to `rebar fsck --repair`.

**Concurrency.** run_ensures runs under the store write lock so concurrent sweeps serialize; check-then-act makes the second sweep a no-op. gitattributes/gitignore use `merge=ours`. `.ensure-applied` is a full atomic rewrite (temp+rename) of the current non-failed id set — no read-modify-write.

**Applied-set marker + write-path pending-hint (Rails CheckPending, hardened).**
- `.ensure-applied` (WS1-owned: format+write) and `.ensure-hinted` (WS2-owned) — both git-ignored
  (ADD BOTH to `_GITIGNORE`, init.py:38-48), atomic; `.ensure-applied` = JSON array, absent/garbage
  → empty set; `.ensure-hinted` = last-hinted timestamp.
- Hook the COMMON mutation paths via `_seam.append_event` / `event_append.write_and_push`
  (create/edit/link/comment/tag/set_*/sign/transition/claim), lazy import. Best-effort, NOT
  universal: `compact.py`, `txn.py`/`transition_close.py`, `delete.py` commit inline and are
  intentionally NOT hooked (acceptable — a rate-limited nudge, not correctness).
- `pending = registry ids − parsed .ensure-applied`, computed ONCE per process (cached boolean;
  registry static in a process). Converged store adds ≤1 read/process; reads untouched.
- Emit a WARNING → `rebar fsck --repair` only when pending AND `.ensure-hinted` older than the
  interval; then atomically update it. Interval + suppression are typed config (`EnsureConfig`
  in `_config_schema.py`: `ensure.hint_interval_secs`=86400, `ensure.hint_enabled`=true), Interval + suppression live in the `[ensure]` config section (`ensure.hint_interval_secs`=86400, `ensure.hint_enabled`=true); the env override is auto-derived per rebar's standard mechanism — no edits to any generated file.
- Hook swallows ALL its own exceptions incl. lazy-import ImportError/SyntaxError (debug log) — a
  write NEVER fails on the nag. Rare double-hint under concurrency accepted.
- Marker gates the HINT ONLY, never the repair. Fresh auto-init'd worktree converges at init → never hints.

**Accepted trade-offs:** long-lived MCP server converges at boot, does not re-sweep mid-life (drift caught at next `fsck --repair`) — WS4 documents it; a permanently-failing unit stays out of the set and is named in the rate-limited hint. Post-rollback: old code simply ignores the git-ignored `.ensure-applied`/`.ensure-hinted` files (no schema coupling).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `ensures.py` registry generalizes the 5 re-init units; each is check-then-act with a stable/immutable id + `EnsureOutcome` result; BOTH commit units (gitattributes, gitignore) tree-check (second run → zero commits)
- [ ] `run_ensures()` runs unconditionally under the store write lock at all init entry points, `fsck --repair`, and MCP startup (best-effort at startup); NEVER gated on the marker
- [ ] Migration removes the hand-listed calls from BOTH re-init and fresh-init paths (and handles `_ensure_env_id`'s `_init_via_symlink` callers) with no double-execution
- [ ] The ensure-sweep is folded into the EXISTING `fsck --repair` (no new flag); plain `fsck` prints `ensures: N/M applied` read-only (M=registry ids, N=in `.ensure-applied`, without calling run_ensures)
- [ ] `fsck --repair` heals and is git-level idempotent (twice → zero new commits); the pending-hint points to `rebar fsck --repair`
- [ ] Best-effort write-path pending-hint on the common mutation paths (inline committers acknowledged out); pure reads untouched; ≤1 read/process; never fails a write (incl. lazy-import errors)
- [ ] Hint rate-limited via `.ensure-hinted` + typed-config interval (86400s) + `[ensure]` config-section suppression (`ensure.hint_enabled`; env auto-derived); fresh auto-init'd worktree never hints
- [ ] `.ensure-applied` (JSON array, atomic full rewrite of non-failed ids) + `.ensure-hinted` are added to `_GITIGNORE`; absent/garbage → empty set (no crash)
- [ ] `run_ensures()` has a typed `EnsureOutcome` + partial-failure contract (skip-and-continue; init logs failures, never aborts)
- [ ] Hot-path regression test: mutation ops may hint but never invoke `run_ensures` (no git-config subprocess; ≤1 marker read/process)
- [ ] `docs/migrations.md` documents reuse, marker-gates-hint-never-repair, hot-path contract, long-lived-MCP trade-off, post-rollback file-ignore, and A-tier future; gc-config is the reference unit
baseline.summary: First-class migration pattern: idempotent per-environment ensure-registry (B tier)

baseline.description:
Scope: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/**` (95 files, 27,284 LOC, 42% comment density). ~970 lines leave — the largest shard.

Dominant category: 28 sites carrying 'RELOCATED VERBATIM ... forced by the LOCKED 800-line cap' (~75 lines), already single-sourced in `.github/module-size-limit.txt`, AGENTS.md and ADR 0058.

Four new ADRs proposed, each consolidating an argument restated 4-8 times: field-convergence fit-then-normalize (8 sites); pagination-stall aborts past fail-open handlers (3 independent arguments, 3 prior incidents); unmapped relations skipped not approximated; core owns the value maps. Plus amendments to ADR 0028, 0055 §(g), 0031, 0035.

Verified stale: `_backend_registry.py:3` 'STUB: signatures pinned, bodies to be implemented' while `select_backend` is imported by 13 modules; the S3/S4-not-landed notes in `_backend.py` and `adapters/jira/backend.py`.

Headroom: `_ref_lock.py` 1 -> ~21, `dispatch_one.py` 14 -> ~57, `inbound_differ.py` 18 -> ~66, `binding_store.py` 18 -> ~33, `fetcher.py` 29 -> ~80.

This subtree's comments are overwhelmingly measured external-API facts that cannot be re-derived from code. The do_not_move list is the most valuable output of the shard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination
- [ ] The shard's do_not_move list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only where obsolete
- [ ] No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured-fact and anti-refactor warnings stay verbatim

## CORRECTION (plan-review BLOCK, criteria E4/G1G2/G6)

### 1. The dominant-category count was wrong — re-measured

The body claims "28 sites carrying 'RELOCATED VERBATIM ... forced by the LOCKED 800-line cap' (~75 lines)". That is not borne out by the tree. Measured over `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`:

    $ grep -rn "RELOCATED VERBATIM" src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler | wc -l
    6                       # 6 sites, ALL under adapters/jira_datacenter/
    $ grep -rniE "800-line|LOCKED 800|module-size cap" src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler | wc -l
    6                       # a SEPARATE, smaller set (transport.py, retry.py, transitions.py)
    $ grep -rliE "RELOCATED VERBATIM|800-line|LOCKED 800|module-size cap" ... | wc -l
    10                      # 10 distinct files carry EITHER marker

No single site carries the quoted combined marker. The two families are disjoint, and neither is close to 28. The real figure is **~12 occurrences across 10 files**, not 28.

**Consequence for the shard's headline yield.** The "~970 lines leave" estimate was built on the inflated count for its largest single category. That estimate is therefore UNRELIABLE and must not be treated as a target. The implementer MEASURES the actual recoverable total and records it on this ticket; the number is an output of the work, not an input to it. Do not manufacture relocations to reach ~970.

### 2. Write-ordering must cover the ADRs, not just `do_not_move`

The plan requires the `do_not_move` list to be appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands, but says nothing about ordering for the four proposed new ADRs (field-convergence fit-then-normalize; pagination-stall aborts past fail-open handlers; unmapped relations skipped not approximated; core owns the value maps) or the amendments to ADR 0028/0055/0031/0035.

Those ADRs are the single-source DESTINATIONS for the arguments currently restated 4-8 times. If a comment citing "see ADR NNNN" is collapsed before ADR NNNN exists, the citation dangles and the argument is simply LOST — which is the opposite of relocation and is not recoverable from the diff by a later reader.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above)

- [ ] The shard's `do_not_move` list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands
- [ ] Each new ADR and each amendment EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it
      is collapsed or deleted — destination first, then the relocation
- [ ] Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination; nothing is deleted
      without a destination that already exists
- [ ] The ACTUAL recoverable line count is measured and recorded on this ticket, replacing the
      unreliable ~970 estimate. The measured marker counts (6 RELOCATED VERBATIM, 6 cap mentions,
      10 files) are the corrected baseline
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are CORRECTED where they document a live invariant, deleted only
      where obsolete — specifically `_backend_registry.py`'s "STUB: signatures pinned, bodies to be
      implemented" (false: `select_backend` is imported by 13 modules) and the S3/S4-not-landed
      notes in `_backend.py` and `adapters/jira/backend.py`
- [ ] No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings
      stay VERBATIM (this subtree's comments are overwhelmingly measured facts that cannot be
      re-derived from code — the do_not_move list is the most valuable output of the shard)
- [ ] No behaviour change: the reconciler's tests pass unchanged
baseline.summary: Comment triage: reconciler subtree

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
normalize_ci_conclusion.sh is a pure function in shell — trivially portable, currently tested only via a subprocess-driving contract test. Its REAL contract is two-input: f(CONCLUSION, FAILURE_OBSERVED) -> vote in {success, failure, cancelled} (never out-of-domain), consumed by .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml.

## Approach
Port to a small stdlib-only Python entry point with unit tests; the workflow call site swaps to the Python invocation. The existing contract test tests/scripts/test_normalize_ci_conclusion.py drives the SHELL script via subprocess — it is the porting oracle: first re-point its subprocess invocation at the Python entry point (proving CLI-level behavior parity env-var-for-env-var), keep its full case table, and add direct in-process unit tests of the function. The shell file is deleted in the same change, so no test ever references a missing script. The workflow currently fetches the script via sparse-checkout of exactly 'scripts/normalize_ci_conclusion.sh' (gerrit-verify.yaml:323) and calls it at :340 — update the sparse-checkout path to the new .py file (cone-mode: false so a single-file pattern works) and keep the entry point dependency-free so the single-file checkout still runs without the package installed. Opportunistic priority (lowest tier).

## Scope
- scripts/normalize_ci_conclusion.sh (deleted) -> new stdlib-only Python entry point
- tests/scripts/test_normalize_ci_conclusion.py: subprocess target swapped to the Python entry point, case table preserved
- .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml: sparse-checkout path at :323 AND the run invocation at :340
- new direct unit tests for the function

## Testing
The ported subprocess contract test keeps its full table (env-driven CLI parity). Direct table-driven unit test over f(CONCLUSION, FAILURE_OBSERVED):
- success -> success; failure -> failure; cancelled -> cancelled (FAILURE_OBSERVED irrelevant for these — assert both values)
- skipped x FAILURE_OBSERVED=false -> success (benign im-open fallback)
- skipped x FAILURE_OBSERVED=true -> failure (fail-closed)
- empty CONCLUSION -> failure; unrecognized value (e.g. 'timed_out') -> failure (fail-closed anomaly rows)
- FAILURE_OBSERVED unset defaults to false
Outputs asserted to always be in {success, failure, cancelled}.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Python entry point reproduces the shell mapping exactly as f(CONCLUSION, FAILURE_OBSERVED), including skipped-fallback rows and fail-closed empty/unknown rows.
- [x] tests/scripts/test_normalize_ci_conclusion.py drives the Python entry point via subprocess with its case table preserved (no orphaned reference to the deleted .sh), plus direct unit tests cover the full contract (both FAILURE_OBSERVED values for pass-through rows included).
- [x] gerrit-verify.yaml sparse-checkout fetches the new .py path (cone-mode: false) and the run step invokes it; entry point is stdlib-only so the single-file checkout works; shell file deleted.
baseline.summary: Shell-to-Python Tier 1: normalize_ci_conclusion.sh

baseline.description:
Each plan-review workflow op independently re-assembles the entire ticket graph from the store, so one gate run does ~4×(1 + 1 + K children) `show_ticket`/`list_tickets` reads. On an epic with many children this is the latency the observability commit (`08cd4c325`) was added to explain — "a slow epic review looks like a hang" — a client-facing reliability/perceived-performance issue.

## Why
The B-RETIRE migration decomposed the review into pure `uses` ops but gave them no shared context, so each re-reads + re-derives the graph (`orchestrator.assemble_context` is itself an N+1 read: `show_ticket` + `list_tickets(parent=)` + one `show_ticket` per child).

## What / files
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:66,147,212,235` — the precheck/assemble/verify_inputs/coach_inputs ops each call `orchestrator.assemble_context(...)`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py:85` and `__init__.py:108` — assemble again.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:77-110` — `assemble_context` (the N+1 read).
Approach: assemble `PlanContext` ONCE in `plan_review_precheck`, serialize its `state`/`children` into the precheck step outputs, and have downstream ops reconstruct `PlanContext` from those outputs (as `plan_review_coach` already does at `workflow_ops.py:342`). Alternatively memoize on `(run_id, ticket_id)`.

## Scope
In: eliminate the redundant re-reads within one gate run; preserve verdict bytes exactly. Out: changing the verdict/finding shape or the workflow YAML's op sequence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A single plan-review gate run assembles the ticket graph at most once (assert via the observability step counts / a read-counter spy).
- [ ] Verdict output is byte-identical to pre-change for a fixed fixture (characterization test).
- [ ] Measured store reads for an epic-with-K-children review drop from ~4×(2+K) to ~(2+K).
- [ ] Existing plan-review tests pass.
baseline.summary: Eliminate redundant ticket-graph re-assembly in plan-review gate

baseline.description:
## Context and evidence

The remaining macOS critical path is filesystem-heavy. The N=3000 import long pole reproduces at 20.19-21.63s on the same macOS host with 15.39-16.65s system CPU versus 4.59-5.67s user CPU. cProfile attributes 13.69s to 24 required git-add/git-commit pairs, while the full default suite creates thousands of temporary Git stores below pytest --basetemp. The workflow deliberately uses runner.temp rather than /tmp because the macOS tmp cleaner previously deleted live test trees.

Maintained OSS precedent matches this mechanism. Apple Git CI creates a 4GB APFS RAM disk for test output and documents greater-than-2x test speedup from avoiding slow storage for many small writes (apple-oss-distributions/Git src/git/.gitlab-ci.yml lines 82-88 at 6b2f9bfe). Aeron creates a macOS APFS RAM disk in GitHub Actions for its temporary test filesystem (aeron-io/aeron .github/workflows/ci.yml lines 62-68 at 092f184a). Git t/perf/README says putting test roots on tmpfs can massively speed the suite. Tracker search found no prior RAM-disk/tmpfs proposal or rejection. This changes storage placement only: no test, worker, platform, behavioral assertion, coverage, mutation work, or runner is removed or added.

Operator direction: do not land a control-only patchset, because an extra full-matrix run would create the contention this work is intended to reduce. Use the next full Verify run initiated by another session as the timing control. Storage sizing comes from the stable local full-suite temp tree or one local explicit-basetemp reproduction; only an implementation change may trigger another Gerrit run.

## Plan

1. Watch the next unrelated full Gerrit Verify run for ambient context without modifying it, and use a no-extra-run trusted-workflow control only when its selectors and collection/pass/skip counts match the treatment. Capture macOS default/integration/job and Ubuntu job wall times, slow-duration tail, queue delay, run conclusion, checked-out patchset, and collection counts. The primary control ultimately captured as 31868300174 used runner.temp and matched the first treatment at 13,397 passed / 65 skipped default and 158 passed / 11 skipped integration; unrelated-run timings remain contextual rather than causal proof.
2. Measure retained temp allocated bytes and file count from a stable local full-suite run using the same selectors and distinct explicit basetemps. Size the RAM disk with at least 50% headroom while keeping it below 40% of detected runner physical memory. If the requirement cannot fit, stop and report infeasibility rather than risk memory pressure or a full volume.
3. In the existing build/test matrix job, create an APFS RAM disk only when runner.os is macOS, after setup/gates and immediately before pytest. Publish its exact device and /Volumes/RebarTests mount path through step outputs; /Volumes is outside the /tmp and /var/folders locations subject to the macOS tmp cleaner. Non-macOS cells continue using runner.temp byte-for-byte. Route both unchanged pytest selectors to separate basetemps below that mount.
4. Always report filesystem type, allocated bytes, file count, and capacity, then detach the exact device created by setup after both pytest tiers, including failure/cancellation paths where GitHub permits cleanup. Do not use a broad disk target, persistent mount, cache, extra runner, or extra job.
5. Add static workflow contract tests proving macOS-only creation, measured bounded sizing, unchanged selectors/xdist worker counts/timeouts/coverage flags, distinct default/integration basetemps, and always-run exact-device cleanup. Explicitly re-run the existing workflow consumers tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py, tests/unit/test_gate_step_tree_skew.py, tests/unit/test_extra_coverage_guard.py, and tests/unit/test_worktree_python_pin.py; these consumers should remain unchanged unless an existing invariant truly changes. Run actionlint and zizmor.
6. Push the implementation through Gerrit immediately. Compare matched selector/collection-count treatments primarily with exact no-RAM control 31868300174 and secondarily with recent green runs; report absolute/percentage savings and Ubuntu non-regression. Retain only if the full matrix is green and both macOS default-suite and job wall times improve by at least the larger of 5% or the observed recent-green range. Worked 5% floor from the exact 17m26s default / 20m36s job control: treatment must be at most 16m33.7s default and 19m34.2s job before any larger observed-range requirement; otherwise revert the lifecycle.

## Test contract card

authoritative_contract: .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml executes the unchanged default and integration pytest selectors on Ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13 and macOS 3.13, with coverage once on Ubuntu 3.13. trigger_preconditions: macOS matrix cell reaches the pytest steps after all existing gates. production_path: GitHub Actions creates an ephemeral APFS RAM device, pytest tmp_path/basetemp writes real Git repositories there, then cleanup detaches only that device. test_tier: static workflow contract tests plus the actual full Gerrit Verify matrix. observable_postcondition: identical collection/pass/skip counts and gates, lower macOS pytest/job wall time, bounded RAM use, no mounted device after cleanup. negative_control: every Ubuntu cell keeps runner.temp and existing behavior; a RAM-disk setup/sizing failure fails loudly before tests rather than silently changing coverage. collateral_invariants: no test selection, assertion, marker, worker count, timeout, coverage, mutation shard, Python/platform cell, or runner concurrency changes. ci_gate: actionlint, zizmor, workflow contract tests, full Gerrit Verify, LLM-Review.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The next unrelated full Verify run records control macOS default/integration/job wall times, Ubuntu job times, queue delay, slow tail, and conclusion without a control-only patchset.
- [ ] Local retained-temp evidence yields at least 50% RAM-disk headroom below 40% of detected physical memory.
- [ ] The selected outcome is platform-safe: if retained, only macOS creates and uses the APFS RAM disk while Ubuntu retains runner.temp; if rejected by the AC7 retention oracle, the RAM-disk lifecycle is absent and every cell uses runner.temp.
- [ ] Default and integration selectors, markers, xdist counts/distribution, timeouts, coverage-once behavior, collection/pass/skip counts, and all platform/Python cells remain unchanged.
- [ ] If the RAM-disk outcome is retained, cleanup runs under always(), reports final filesystem usage, and detaches only the exact device created by setup; if rejected by AC7, no RAM-disk cleanup lifecycle remains.
- [ ] Static workflow tests, actionlint, zizmor, focused/full pytest, LLM-Review, and Gerrit Verified are green.
- [ ] Against a no-RAM control with matching selectors and collection/pass/skip counts, both macOS default-suite and job wall times are lower than control by at least the larger of 5% or the observed recent-green range, with no Ubuntu regression; otherwise the experimental lifecycle is fully reverted. For the captured 17m26s default / 20m36s job control, the 5% floor is at most 16m33.7s default and 19m34.2s job before applying any larger observed-range requirement.
baseline.summary: Use a measured macOS RAM disk for Git-heavy pytest temp trees

baseline.description:
## Context
The 2026-07-12 calibration analysis (session logs remarkable-hydrated-nightjar / tainted-continuing-queensnake / shaggy-linoleum-gavial) found: (1) code review is too loose — 0 'BLOCK — finding' votes across 162 post-recalibration changes while confirmed must-fix findings sailed through as advisories (change #529's untested-degradation advisory scored impact 0.0 and went red on main 57 minutes after merge; #518's importlib code-execution findings at 0.54; #539's correctness findings at 0.60 — against a 0.95 threshold no real finding ever reached); (2) plan-review advisory load is protocol-inflated — CLAUDE.md mandates remediating ALL valid advisories (~13/round, 95% of remediation edits mint new findings), and with the convergence floors now default-ON (change 562) we want to observe organic agent behavior instead of mandated remediation; (3) completion-verifier defects are structural, not admissibility: FAIL verdicts persist nowhere, FAILs ratchet piecemeal (3b4e took 2 extra CI cycles), and 'children closed (signed)' epic ACs defeat the certifiable:false escape hatch (bf50/5f39 contagion, bug 02a3); and (4) leaf plans DRIFT from their parent's plan as leaves are claimed and edited — by epic close a leaf's ACs can describe a materially different deliverable than the parent declared, and no plan-review criterion checks a leaf's scope against its PARENT (drift is caught only at epic-close completion verification, far too late). The review that gates the CLAIM is the right moment to catch drift ticket-by-ticket. This 4th finding motivates child d4cf (the new G7 leaf-plan parent-containment criterion).

## Definitions & Sequencing
- **"serious-tier" (Success Criterion 1):** the code-review criteria whose findings map to the SERIOUS (0.9) consequence binaries in `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py` — prod-lane `data_loss_without_recovery`, `security_bypass_not_enforced_elsewhere`, `silent_wrong_feeding_a_decision`; maint-lane `unversioned_published_contract_break`, `safety_net_removal_without_replacement` — plus the `security` criterion. Child b9c0 enumerates the exact enabled set and pins it in a test; everything else stays advisory at 0.95.
- **code-v2 vs code-v3 cohort ordering (f32e vs 9f25/b9c0):** 9f25 derives, and b9c0 enables, a block threshold over the existing **code-v2** finding cohort — valid for code-v2 sidecars only. f32e adds a new maint binary and bumps `IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION` to **code-v3**, which per ADR-0036 starts a FRESH calibration cohort. Re-deriving/enabling any threshold over code-v3 is explicitly a FUTURE follow-up, NOT part of b9c0 — no threshold in this epic consumes code-v3. The two workstreams are independent by design; there is no ordering dependency between f32e and 9f25/b9c0, and b9c0's threshold governs code-v2 findings regardless of f32e's landing order.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All child tickets (the epic's work items) are closed, each with its change landed on main.

## Context
Three genuine Gerrit Verify runs assign an almost identical setup duration to tests/unit/workflow/test_editor.py::test_server_binds_loopback_only: 35.06s before static Pandoc replay and 35.09s in both post-static-corpus patch sets. Focused test/module runs are subsecond/2.44s; targeted editor setup instrumentation was below 4ms; a 10,000-directory APFS tmp_path benchmark stayed below 3.4ms. Recurrence after removing complete Pandoc subprocess replay rejects the prior generic worker-starvation account. CPython ThreadingHTTPServer construction synchronously calls socket.getfqdn(host), which performs reverse DNS even for numeric 127.0.0.1, making a fixed macOS resolver timeout the leading dynamic hypothesis. Existing pytest durations identify only the aggregate setup phase, so one organic CI observation needs nested timing before changing behavior.

## Plan
- Add a thresholded pytest fixture-setup observer that emits worker id, node id, fixture name, and monotonic elapsed time only for fixture spans above one second.
- Add transparent, semantics-preserving timing around the editor server constructor, TCP bind, and socket.getfqdn call during the _server fixture; emit only spans above one second and preserve original arguments, return values, and exceptions.
- Keep output quiet outside CI/explicit opt-in and avoid any new dependency or external call.
- Prove locally that the observer names the correct nested span using deterministic delayed fakes, then run the focused editor and observability tests.
- Land through Gerrit and use the first organic macOS/Ubuntu full-route run as the discriminating experiment. H1 predicts ~35s in getfqdn(127.0.0.1) on macOS with bind milliseconds; H2 predicts the inverse; H3 predicts the time belongs to _no_repo_commits rather than _server.
- Record the confirmed mechanism and create a linked RED/GREEN fix ticket only after runtime evidence discriminates the hypotheses. Back out with a Gerrit revert if instrumentation changes test semantics or produces noisy routine logs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Fixture spans above one second identify worker, node, fixture, and elapsed seconds.
- [x] Editor server setup separately measures constructor, TCP bind, and getfqdn without changing their behavior.
- [x] Instrumentation is silent below threshold and outside CI/explicit opt-in.
- [x] Deterministic tests prove each discriminating span is attributed correctly.
- [x] Focused editor tests and broader test-observability guards pass.
- [x] Lint, typecheck, action/workflow policy gates pass as applicable.
- [x] Gerrit LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 are recorded before merge.
- [x] The first organic post-merge macOS/Ubuntu observation is recorded.
- [x] A confirmed root cause or explicit inconclusive experiment result is written back before close.
baseline.summary: Instrument recurring 35-second macOS editor setup long pole

## Summary
MCP reconcile tool runs Jira-MUTATING bootstrap modes with zero gating, even under REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1. Verified LIVE (incident, remediated): a reconcile call with mode=bootstrap-strict from a sandboxed temp store, readonly server, executed against real Jira and created 19 real issues (DIG-5615..DIG-5633; all deleted, deletion verified by JQL).

## Reproduction Steps
(verified on installed 0.4.0 == HEAD)
1. Export REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1 and build the MCP server (build_server()).
2. Call tool reconcile with {"mode": "bootstrap-strict"} (acli installed + credentialed).
3. Observe the pass runs and applies real Jira mutations (OK: applied 10 of 993).

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: any Jira-mutating mode requires REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE=1; a readonly server exposes at most reconcile-check/dry-run.
- Actual: bootstrap-strict/bootstrap-throttle mutate real Jira ungated under readonly; only mode=="live" is checked.

## Source
- src/rebar/mcp_server.py:271-276 — gate checks only the literal string "live".
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mode.py:106-112 — MODE_CAPS: BOOTSTRAP_STRICT=10, BOOTSTRAP_THROTTLE=100 APPLIED mutations/pass; only RECONCILE_CHECK/DRY_RUN are cap-0.
- Note dry-run is not a pure read either: it writes bridge_state/ and the invariants path files local bug tickets.

## Fix direction
Gate by capability, not string: parse the mode via the Mode enum and require the env var for any mode whose MODE_CAPS != 0; under _readonly(), restrict reconcile to cap-0 modes (or hide it). Correct docstrings + CLAUDE.md ("'live' mutates Jira" is dangerously incomplete — also __init__.py:404-409, tracked with bug frog-oryx-strut).

## Suggested RED test
Parametrize all five modes x {readonly, non-readonly} x {with, without REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE} with a fake acli on PATH that fails loudly if executed; assert only cap-0 modes pass without the env var and that readonly blocks mutating modes before any acli invocation. Never real credentials in tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] bootstrap-strict/bootstrap-throttle (and live) require REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE=1 over MCP
- [ ] Under REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1 no Jira-mutating reconcile mode is callable
- [ ] Invalid mode strings produce a clean tool error (not a crash)
- [ ] RED test matrix above lands first and goes GREEN with the fix
- [ ] Docstrings/CLAUDE.md updated to name all mutating modes
baseline.summary: MCP reconcile: bootstrap modes mutate real Jira ungated, even under REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1

## Reproduction Steps
The rebar review bot (compose-review-bot-1 on the rebar-gerrit EC2 host) clones each change into /tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots to review it. These snapshots are never garbage-collected, so the 30G root disk fills to 100%.

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: review workspace is bounded / cleaned per review.
- Actual: /tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots grew to 14G; root fs hit 100%; clone_change_ref failed with 'No space left on device', which the voter surfaces as [LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (review-error)] on EVERY change (observed on 452, 458, 461, 462). This fail-closed vetoes unrelated changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The review-bot's per-change clone/snapshot workspace is bounded or cleaned after each review (e.g. rm the snapshot on completion, or a periodic prune).
- [ ] A disk-usage guard/alarm so the host does not silently reach 100%.
- [ ] Document the manual recovery (docker builder prune + clear /tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots) in an infra runbook.

## Discovered
While landing epic breaded-ammonitic-elephant: change 458's LLM-Review persistently returned coverage-gap (review-error). Root cause via SSM was the full host disk, not the change.

## What

The central index `docs/README.md` is incomplete (4 living/normative docs unlinked) and mixes living reference docs with historical evidence with no visual/structural distinction. Complete the index and add a taxonomy — **in place, WITHOUT relocating any files.**

Verified state (`origin/main`): exactly four `docs/*.md` are unlinked from the index — `attest-substrate.md` (living developer API ref), `review-policy.md` (normative policy), `session-id-shims.md` (living reference), and `dco-rollout-evidence.md` (historical). The other historical docs (`88ab-feature-branch-evidence.md`, `bash-migration.md`) ARE already linked, just not labeled as historical.

## Decision: label-in-place, NO git-mv (resolves the plan-review E2/T7/E4/G1G2 findings)
The audit floated "and/or move historical files under `docs/archive/`". **We deliberately choose NOT to relocate any file.** Rationale: the inbound-link blast radius of moving these files is large and cross-cutting — `bash-migration.md` alone is referenced by 8-10 `src/rebar/` production docstrings, the root `README.md`, `docs/oss-comparison-and-remediation.md`, and test files; `88ab-feature-branch-evidence.md` is referenced by `infra/gerrit/feature-branch-e2e-scenarios.sh`. A `git-mv` would silently break all of these for near-zero reader benefit. Instead, historical docs stay at their current paths and are grouped under a clearly-labeled **"Historical evidence"** section in the index. No file moves ⇒ no inbound link can break.

## Scope
- Add index entries for the 3 living/normative unlinked docs (`attest-substrate.md`,
  `review-policy.md`, `session-id-shims.md`) under the appropriate living-reference/policy
  buckets.
- Add a clearly-labeled **"Historical evidence"** section to the index and list the
  historical docs there (`dco-rollout-evidence.md` — currently unlinked, add it;
  `88ab-feature-branch-evidence.md` and `bash-migration.md` — move their LISTING into this
  section, files stay put).
- Add a short taxonomy note at the top of the index defining the buckets: **living
  reference / policy / design rationale / historical evidence** — so future docs land in
  the right place.
- Do NOT git-mv or move any file; do NOT edit any inbound links (nothing moves).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The 3 living/normative docs are each linked EXACTLY ONCE from the index
      (verify, prints nothing):
      `for b in attest-substrate.md review-policy.md session-id-shims.md; do [ "$(grep -cF "($b)" docs/README.md)" = 1 ] || echo "BAD $b"; done`
- [ ] The 3 historical docs are each linked EXACTLY ONCE (so the old Contributor
      entries for bash-migration.md / 88ab-feature-branch-evidence.md were MOVED, not
      duplicated) AND appear under the "Historical evidence" heading (verify, prints
      nothing for both loops):
      `for b in dco-rollout-evidence.md 88ab-feature-branch-evidence.md bash-migration.md; do [ "$(grep -cF "($b)" docs/README.md)" = 1 ] || echo "DUP/MISSING $b"; done`
      and
      `for b in dco-rollout-evidence.md 88ab-feature-branch-evidence.md bash-migration.md; do awk '/^## Historical evidence/{h=1;next} /^## /{h=0} h' docs/README.md | grep -qF "($b)" || echo "NOT-IN-SECTION $b"; done`
      (`grep -cF` is a LITERAL count — no regex/dot-escaping issues; `=1` catches both
      a missing link and a duplicate left behind in Contributor, closing the G6 gap.)
- [ ] A "Historical evidence" section heading exists and a brief taxonomy note defines
      the four buckets (verify, prints nothing):
      `grep -qi '^#\+ *Historical evidence' docs/README.md || echo "NO SECTION"; for t in 'living reference' 'policy' 'design rationale' 'historical evidence'; do grep -qi "$t" docs/README.md || echo "NO BUCKET: $t"; done`
- [ ] No file is relocated and no inbound link edited — only `docs/README.md` changes
      (verify): `git status --porcelain -- docs/` shows exactly one ` M docs/README.md`
      line and NO `R`/`D` (rename/delete) entries.

Files: `docs/README.md` (only).
baseline.summary: P2: Complete & de-mix docs index; separate living refs from historical evidence

# Fleet notice primitive: TTL'd shared state for orchestrator-agent coordination

## Problem (observed, 2026-08-11/13 bug-bash session)
A ~30-agent, 3-session, 24-hour bug bash stress-tested rebar as a coordination substrate. Task-scoped communication worked well as-is: ticket comments carried premise corrections/evidence/dispositions durably; links carried provenance; claims were the load-bearing mutex (they arbitrated a two-session epic collision cleanly). But CROSS-CUTTING, fast-changing fleet state had no home:

- The CI-failure playbook (stale-base signatures like `invalid choice: 'select'` and complexity-baseline drift → rebase; cert flakes → recheck; comment-hygiene → real fix) was discovered incrementally and had to be copy-pasted into ~30 agent briefs and re-sent point-to-point as it grew. The coordinator WAS the bulletin board — a single point of failure whose briefs bloated with boilerplate, and late-spawned agents missed anything omitted.
- Transient environment state ("main is RED on the complexity gate, hold pushes", "quiet window in effect, hold tracker transitions", "global install broken mid-update, use the worktree venv") went out point-to-point and aged badly — one agent acted on a stale main-red note.
- The absence of a well-known shared address caused a real anti-pattern: a work ticket (b902) accumulated cross-cutting analysis records as comments until the operator flagged it; records were migrated to session log d0d8-9dfe-f2d8-4364 (see its index).

## Alternatives considered
1. **Bulletin-board ticket by convention** — zero code, but formalizes the observed anti-pattern: unstructured append-only comment stream, no expiry, reads require scanning. Rejected.
2. **Harness-side messaging improvements** — fixes delivery mechanics but is ephemeral (agent/session deaths were constant), unaudited, and invisible to non-Claude harnesses (against AGENTS.md's cross-vendor stance). Rejected as the primary mechanism.
3. **Docs/AGENTS.md via normal Gerrit changes** — correct for STABLE lessons (several from this session should graduate: the playbook signatures, batch-plan-edits-then-review-LAST, the stale-tree grep trap, never-git-stash) but two review gates per update is wrong for state that changes in minutes. Complementary, not sufficient.
4. **First-class notice primitive (PROPOSED)** — see below.

## Proposal
A small keyed notice surface in the tracker store (alongside, not inside, ticket dirs — precedent: bridge_alerts, .rebar/criteria_routing.json, env-scoped attestations are already store-level non-ticket shared state):

- `rebar notice set <key> <text> [--ttl <duration>] [--scope fleet|session]` — upsert, records author env/session + timestamp; TTL default e.g. 24h; expiry is read-side (expired notices are omitted, history stays in the event log).
- `rebar notice list [--all]` / `rebar notice clear <key>`.
- **Surfacing is the key design point**: active notices are shown automatically at `claim` time and at `review-plan`/`verify-completion` start (count + text), so agents cannot miss them without ignoring their own command output. MCP read tool mirrors it.
- Durable + auto-pushed like all tracker writes; write contention bounded by the landed lock-retry work (cc69cc1179).

## Tradeoffs / risks
- New surface to maintain; must not become config-by-another-name (mitigation: TTL mandatory, no code reads notices for behavior — display-only contract).
- Hot-key write contention on busy fleets (mitigated by lock retries; notices are low-frequency writes).
- Scope question: is fleet orchestration in a ticket system's remit? Adjacent prior art: idea ticket aurous-chewable-blackrhino (session-resumption contract). The display-only contract keeps this on the "shared memo" side of the line rather than orchestration logic.

## Half-life rule (the framework this fits into, operator-endorsed direction)
Stable lessons → docs via normal changes. Task-scoped → ticket comments/links. Session records → session logs. Fast-changing fleet state → notices (this proposal).
baseline.summary: Fleet notice primitive: TTL'd shared state surfaced at claim/review time

# Realign rebar reviews to the three-pass (evidence -> binary-verify -> deterministic-gate) structure

## Context
Industry practice and 2025-2026 research converge: an LLM reviewer should surface cited evidence against a locked rubric; a SEPARATE agent should validate each finding via atomic binary sub-questions; and a DETERMINISTIC policy (not the model) should decide severity and blocking. LLMs are unreliable at holistic severity/confidence judgments, so neither is emitted by the model. This epic builds that shared three-pass framework and migrates rebar's existing reviewers onto it.

## Prerequisite foundations — current codebase state (2026-06)

Foundations shipped since this epic was written; the design is UNCHANGED, but the substrate is now CONCRETE for
parts and the reviewer migration is PARTLY done (the closed prerequisite epics are NOT reopened — this realigns
THIS epic to what they delivered):

- **Reviewer PROMPT migration DONE; three-pass STRUCTURE migration still pending (epic `da27`, closed).** The
  existing reviewers (`code_quality`/`security`/`tests`/`spec_alignment`/`ticket_quality`/`completion_verifier`)
  were migrated to the front-matter CONTRACT model — `inputs`/`outputs` schema-name contracts, `execution_mode`,
  `dimension`, `applies_to` globs, a derived index + CI drift gate (`src/rebar/llm/prompts.py`, `reviewers/*.md`).
  That is the PROMPT-STORAGE half of 'migrate existing reviewers'. They still emit the OLD pass-1 shape
  `{findings:[{severity, dimension, detail, citations}], summary}`, NOT this epic's pass-1 EVIDENCE contract
  `{finding, criteria[], evidence[], scenarios[], impact}` — migrating the pass-1 SHAPE + adding Pass-2/Pass-3 is
  THIS epic's remaining work, layered on the already-contracted prompts.
- **Pass-1 data substrate (partial) + single-pass `review_code`.** `src/rebar/llm/findings.py`
  (`normalize_finding`, citation coercion, schema validation) + `src/rebar/llm/aggregate.py` (cluster +
  severity×agreement rank) exist; `review_code` (`src/rebar/llm/code_review.py`) runs reviewers + aggregates today
  as a SINGLE PASS. There is NO Pass-2 verifier agent and NO Pass-3 deterministic gate yet — both are NEW WORK here.
- **Provider-agnostic runner + workflow engine (epic `e6d9`, closed).** `PydanticAIRunner` (`src/rebar/llm/runner.py`)
  is the sole runtime (LangGraph cut over), honoring the `execution_mode` {single_turn|agentic} seam — the substrate
  Pass-1 and the separate-context Pass-2 verifier run on; the declarative workflow engine (`run_workflow`) + the
  Inspect-AI eval seam shipped alongside.
- **Code-grounding for Pass-2 (epic `8f6c`, closed).** `src/rebar/grounding/` (the `refute_absence`/`applies`/`scan`
  facade, exported from `src/rebar/grounding/__init__.py`) is the substrate for Pass-2's RE-GROUNDING in the actual
  code + the cited-code-reference-accuracy VETO. The overlay catalogs' 'Scanner pre-pass (Semgrep/Gitleaks/Trivy)'
  maps to the oracle's EXTENSIBLE detector registry (`detectors/registry.py`; OpenGrep/ast-grep shipped) — but
  security/secrets/CVE detectors are NOT yet shipped (only `smell_generic` + applicability), so those remain new
  work (here or shared with the code-review capability epic `b744`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Pass-1 finding contract: `{finding (free text), criteria[] (each in the prompt's locked rubric set), evidence[] (flexible free text: code citations, prose, OR absence rationale), scenarios[] (free text), impact (free text)}`. Criteria is an array. No model severity/confidence.
- [ ] Pass-2 verifier = a separate agent / independent context that re-grounds in the actual code (via the shipped 8f6c grounding-oracle facade `refute_absence`/`scan` for cited-reference + smell grounding) and emits per finding: (a) severity attributes `{prod_impact, debt_impact, blast_radius, likelihood, reversibility}` (coarse ordinals); (b) typed binary sub-answers `{verdict: yes|no|insufficient, evidence_span/reason}`.
- [ ] Binary sub-question set (typed): the ONLY veto is cited-code-reference-accuracy, applied ONLY when a code citation is present (no-op for absence findings / non-code reviews); all others GRADED: is-verifiable (signal), evidence-entails-finding, path-reachable, impact-follows-necessarily, no-viable-alternative-explanation, no-existing-mitigation, severity-claim-justified.
- [ ] Pass-3 deterministic aggregator: conditional veto gate -> graded confidence (weighted fraction / log-odds) -> severity-from-attributes -> `block | advisory` against per-criteria thresholds (project-overridable; defaults start high -> almost all findings advisory while calibration data is gathered). No interactive escalation path (autonomous).
- [ ] Verifier prompt obeys the research rules: atomicity (one proposition per question); independence (do not show the finding's own conclusion when answering each sub-question); verdict-with-citation, NOT verdict-with-proposed-fix; allow "insufficient".
- [ ] Existing code-review reviewers (review_ticket and the code-quality/security/tests reviewers) migrated to the pass-1 EVIDENCE contract + shared pass-2/pass-3 — these are ALREADY on the da27 front-matter CONTRACT model (inputs/outputs/execution_mode/dimension/applies_to + derived index), so this is the pass-1-SHAPE + Pass-2/Pass-3 migration ON TOP of that, NOT a from-scratch reviewer rewrite; findings schema extended (`src/rebar/llm/findings.py`); aggregation + citation-resolution + schema-pin tests updated. (completion_verifier is OUT OF SCOPE: not migrated, unchanged.)
- [ ] Rubric sourced from Google eng-practices + Anthropic security taxonomy (locked + versioned); Conventional Comments not adopted.
- [ ] Known limitations recorded: veto-brittleness mitigated by the single conditional veto; decomposition controls validity PRECISION not finding-type RECALL; threshold calibration is explicitly out of scope (separate future work).
- [ ] All rebar reviews emit the pass-1 evidence contract; a shared pass-2 verifier agent and pass-3 deterministic aggregator exist and are used.
- [ ] Severity is computed deterministically from structured attributes; validity/confidence from typed binary sub-answers. No model-emitted severity number, confidence number, or high/med/low rating in the decision path.
baseline.summary: Realign rebar reviews to three-pass (evidence -> binary-verify -> deterministic gate); migrate existing reviewers

baseline.description:
## Why

A review pipeline runs N criteria-prompts in budgeted BATCHES (one LLM call per batch), with runtime fallback (split -> one-per-call -> escalate model) on a context-limit. No surveyed engine makes adaptive cost-budgeted batching first-class — it is app code everywhere — and encoding it in the IR would break replay determinism (batch composition depends on a runtime token estimate + which call hit a context limit). So the IR gets a THIN step that delegates the adaptive work to a runner.

## What

Add a `batch` step kind whose IR surface is purely declarative parameters: `group` (the prompt set), `usd_budget`, `model_ladder`. A batch-runner SEAM (protocol) performs the adaptive packing / token-estimation / context-limit fallback / model-escalation / shed-to-INDETERMINATE / fingerprint- checkpoint, and JOURNALS its batch-plan + fallback transitions as OPAQUE events. The interpreter STORES the journaled plan as an output but NEVER branches on its internals (thin-interpreter / Burr- tripwire preserved). Ship a reference/default batch-runner; epic B supplies the production runner (extracted from the gate's sizing.py) behind this seam.

## Scope

- src/rebar/llm/workflow/schema.py + JSON Schema: the `batch` step kind + its params + validation.
- A batch-runner protocol/seam (alongside AgentStepRunner in executor.py) + a reference default runner.
- The journaled batch-plan / fallback event vocabulary (recorded decisions, not recomputed).
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/interpreter.py: invoke the batch-runner, store the opaque plan as the step
  output; the interpreter must not interpret batch internals.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `batch` step parses + schema-validates with `group`/`usd_budget`/`model_ladder`; bad params
      are validation errors.
- [ ] A batch-runner SEAM exists with a reference default runner; the runner journals its batch-plan
      + fallback transitions as opaque recorded events.
- [ ] The interpreter stores the journaled plan as the step output and NEVER branches on its
      internals (a test asserts this); replay reads the recorded plan rather than recomputing it.
- [ ] The Burr-tripwire stays green (no asyncio/threading/concurrent leaks outside the confined
      fan-out path).
- [ ] make lint + the workflow test suite pass.
baseline.summary: Batch step: a thin delegating step kind + batch-runner seam + reference runner (journaled batch-plan)

baseline.description:
## GHA reconcile-bridge: sign inbound writes inline + inject key

CRITICAL: the reconciler's inbound writer (`_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py` `_write_event_file`, ~214-259) calls the `rebar._store` primitives DIRECTLY, bypassing `_seam.append_event`, and stamps only `author` (no `author_email`/`author_id`/`author_sig`). So Jira-sourced events classify `unknown-author`/`unsigned` under `verify-identity`. Config alone is insufficient — this needs a code fix.

### Chosen approach: stamp + sign INLINE (not via `_seam.append_event`)

Enrich the event dict in `_write_event_file` BEFORE it is serialized/written:
1. `event.update(_seam.attribution_fields(repo_root))` — adds `author_email` and (when a
   current identity resolves) `author_id`.
2. `_seam._apply_authorship(event, ticket_id, event_type, data, str(tracker_dir), repo_root)`
   — when `author_id` + `identity.signing_key` are present, signs the canonical event bytes
   and stores the DSSE envelope under `author_sig` (best-effort; a miss writes unsigned).

**Rationale (why inline, NOT `_seam.append_event`):** `append_event` calls `write_and_push()`, which COMMITS + PUSHES per event; `_write_event_file` intentionally writes an uncommitted file so the reconciler's own orchestration can batch-commit the pass. Routing through `append_event` would break that batch-commit model and thread `repo_root`/`tracker` through 12+ call sites. Inline stamping reuses the exact seam helpers, preserves the uncommitted-file model, and is minimal blast radius. The added author fields are additive (older readers ignore unknown keys — no store-format break). `_write_event_file` will need `repo_root` available (derive from `tracker_dir.parent` or `config.repo_root()`).

### Prerequisite (SATISFIED)

Signing resolves `author_id` only if a Rebar Bot identity ticket with `email=joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com` exists — it does (task bffe created identity `594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d`, public key registered). So with `BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL` = that address the git-email resolver maps reconciler writes to the bot identity.

### Workflow wiring

In `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`: write `secrets.REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY` to a job-local file (`mktemp`, `chmod 600`, `::add-mask::` the value), set `identity.signing_key` (or `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY`) to that path, and set `BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL=joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com` (currently `rebar-bridge@users.noreply.github.com`) so git-email resolution maps to the bot.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_write_event_file` stamps `author_email`/`author_id` (via `_seam.attribution_fields`) and signs `author_sig` (via `_seam._apply_authorship`) inline before writing; a reconciler-authored event written with the bot identity + a signing key verifies as `verified` under `rebar verify-authorship` (proven by a unit test that configures a bot identity + signing key, drives `_write_event_file`, and asserts the written event carries `author_id`/`author_email`/`author_sig` and verifies).
- [ ] Additive-fields regression test: a unit test constructs an event WITHOUT the new author fields (older-format) and asserts the reducer / `rebar show` still round-trips it cleanly (unknown/absent keys ignored, no format break). The batch-commit orchestration is unchanged (no eager commit/push added to the inbound path).
- [ ] `reconcile-bridge.yml` writes the key to a `chmod 600` job-local file, `::add-mask::`s it, and sets `identity.signing_key`/`REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY` to that path. For the committer email: the existing "Configure git identity" step reads `BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL: ${{ vars.BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL || 'rebar-bridge@users.noreply.github.com' }}` — CHANGE that fallback default to `joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com` (so resolution maps to the bot identity without depending on a repo variable being set; the `vars.BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL` override still wins if present). The key is never logged or committed.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: GHA reconcile-bridge: route inbound writes through signing seam + inject key

baseline.description:
## Problem

The review-bot's shutdown drain covers only HALF of its review paths.

`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py`'s lifespan does:

    await asyncio.wait_for(queue.join(), timeout=shutdown_drain_seconds())

then cancels every task, bounded by `shutdown_cancel_seconds()` (10s).

`queue.join()` waits for the webhook QUEUE to empty, so a webhook-queued review IS protected (1200s drain, and compose grants `stop_grace_period: 1320s` — both far exceed the ~10 min review).

But `reconcile.reconcile_once` awaits `review_and_vote` INLINE, not through the queue. When the queue is empty, `queue.join()` returns IMMEDIATELY and the `reconcile_loop` task is cancelled within ~10s — abandoning a backfill review that may be minutes in.

Found while implementing [rebar:34cd-1a7c-b9b1-4b05]; verified by reading origin/main d4095763e3.

## Why it matters independently of 34cd

34cd fixes this from the DEPLOY side: autodeploy now defers a container recreation while `/health` reports `in_flight > 0`, so the autodeploy path no longer kills reconciler reviews.

The underlying drain gap is untouched by that. ANY other container stop still kills a reconciler review with effectively no drain:
  - an operator `docker compose restart` / `up -d` run by hand
  - `compose-up.sh` during a manual deploy
  - a host reboot / systemd stop
  - the rollback path inside autodeploy itself (`docker compose up -d` after re-tagging `:prev`)

The reconciler is also the path that RETRIES a review killed by anything else, so the gap sits on the self-heal path. And it is silent for the same reason 34cd was: a cancelled review fails nothing, so no `VOTER_ERROR` is emitted and `restarts` stays 0.

## Suspected fix

Make the drain cover in-flight reconciler work, not just the queue — e.g. have the lifespan wait on the same in-flight review count that 34cd added (`voter.in_flight_reviews()`) under the existing `shutdown_drain_seconds()` budget, before cancelling tasks. The budget and `stop_grace_period` are already sized for a full review, so this likely needs no new tunables.

Note the ordering constraint: the wait must not let a reconcile pass START a NEW review while draining, or shutdown could be extended repeatedly. The reconciler probably needs a stop-accepting-new-work signal alongside the drain.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A reconciler review in flight at shutdown is drained (bounded by the existing
      `shutdown_drain_seconds()`), not cancelled within `shutdown_cancel_seconds()`.
- [x] The drain does not extend indefinitely: no new review may start once shutdown has begun,
      proven by a test.
- [x] The existing webhook-queue drain behaviour is unchanged.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
baseline.summary: Shutdown drain misses the reconciler's in-flight review, so any container stop kills it

## What

**Retire the band-aids** now that the ref-lock (C3) is proven, flip the default backend to `ref`,
and remove the dead file-lock machinery + `merge=ours` entry, with a migration for existing repos.

**Depends on: 2711-21bf-ab71-4136 (C3).** The ref backend must be wired and validated first;
removing the file backend / retry loop before C3 would leave the reconciler with no working lock.

- Flip `[reconciler] lock_backend` default to `ref` and remove the `file` backend path from
  `_advisory_lock.py` once the ref backend has baked.
- **Remove the `b859-8fa1` retry loop** in `acquire_pass_lock` AND its now-dead helpers
  (`_resolve_retry_budget`, `_LOCK_RETRY_BUDGET_DEFAULT`, `_compute_backoff_seconds`, and the
  b859-only backoff constants). Retire the config key `lock_max_retries` (`_config_schema.py`
  `ReconcilerConfig` field + coercion entry) and its env aliases
  (`REBAR_RECONCILER_LOCK_MAX_RETRIES` + deprecated alias `REBAR_RECONCILER_LOCK_RETRY_BUDGET` in
  `config.py`). Delete/adjust the tests that exercise them:
  `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock_retry_jitter.py`, and the retry-budget
  assertions in `tests/.../test_config_file_wiring.py` + `test_ev3c_env_renames.py`.
- **Deprecation path for the retired config key.** `lock_max_retries` removal is operator-visible;
  rather than a hard break, treat a still-present `lock_max_retries` as **deprecated** — emit a
  one-time deprecation warning (config-load path) and ignore it — and note the removal in
  `docs/config.md` + the changelog, so existing operator configs do not error on upgrade.
- **Remove `.reconciler-*` from `_GITATTRIBUTES`** in `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` (leave
  `.bridge_state/* merge=ours` untouched — that is WS-1 binding data, out of scope), and update
  `tests/interfaces/store/test_gitattributes_merge.py` to assert `.reconciler-*` is absent and
  `.bridge_state/*` still present.
- **Migration for already-initialized trackers:** `_commit_gitattributes` is create-if-absent only,
  so editing the constant does not fix existing repos. Add an update-migration arm (mirroring the
  `_commit_gitignore` line-migration) that strips the `.reconciler-* merge=ours` line from an
  already-committed `.gitattributes`. Idempotent; on git failure, log-and-continue (do not abort).
- **One-time cleanup:** remove any pre-existing `.reconciler-pass-lock`/`.reconciler-phase-gate`
  committed on the tickets branch from the old scheme (a single named helper, idempotent, invoked
  from exactly one site — reconciler startup; state the site explicitly).
- Extend the ref-lock ADR to record that the b859 loop is superseded by the C3 self-healing lock.

## Design decisions (resolves plan-review ambiguities; binding on the implementation)

1. **Precise removal set (verified dead by grep, not by line number).** After the file backend is
   gone, delete every symbol left with zero consumers: the file dispatch branches in
   `acquire_pass_lock` / `release_pass_lock` / `check_phase_gate`; `_write_file_to_tickets_branch`,
   `_delete_file_from_tickets_branch`, `_commit_in_detached_tickets_worktree`,
   `_git_show_tickets_file`, the file-based `check_pass_lock`, the `_LOCK_FILE`/`_GATE_FILE`
   constants; the b859 outer-retry loop + `_resolve_retry_budget` / `_LOCK_RETRY_BUDGET_DEFAULT` /
   `_compute_backoff_seconds`; and `_cas_advance_with_retry` / `_cas_backoff_seconds` /
   `_jittered_backoff` / the backoff constants **iff** grep confirms no remaining consumer once the
   file backend is deleted. **KEEP** `_cas_once` and `_is_cas_mismatch` — they are imported by
   `_ref_lock.py` and are the shared CAS discriminator. Every deletion is justified by a
   zero-consumer grep across `src/` and `tests/`.
2. **`lock_backend` post-removal.** Keep the key (default now `ref`); the acquire/release/gate
   dispatch becomes unconditional ref. A still-configured `lock_backend=file` is
   **deprecated-and-ignored**: a one-time warning is logged and the ref backend is used anyway
   (rollback via `file` is intentionally gone — ref is proven). The `{file, ref}` choice validator
   stays so the value still parses.
3. **`lock_max_retries` deprecation mechanics.** Removing the `ReconcilerConfig.lock_max_retries`
   field means a config that still sets it hits `Config.from_mapping`'s existing **unknown-key
   path**, which WARNs-and-ignores under the default non-strict load — exactly the required
   "one-time warning, not a load error". Verify no reconciler config-load site passes `strict=True`
   (which would reject it); if one does, add `lock_max_retries` to an explicit deprecated-and-ignored
   set rather than letting it error. The env aliases are removed from `config.py`'s env map.
4. **Migrations — two distinct, idempotent, single-site helpers.**
   (a) *gitattributes line-strip* lives in `init.py` (an update arm on `_commit_gitattributes`,
   mirroring the `_commit_gitignore` line-migration): if the committed `.gitattributes` contains a
   `.reconciler-*` line, rewrite without it and commit; on any git failure log-and-continue (never
   abort init). (b) *committed-lock-file cleanup* is a single named helper (e.g.
   `_purge_committed_reconciler_locks`) invoked from exactly one site — the reconciler startup in
   `rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:main()`, before the pass acquires — that deletes any
   `.reconciler-pass-lock` / `.reconciler-phase-gate` still committed on the tickets branch (no-op if
   absent → idempotent; git failure log-and-continue).
5. **Regression test.** A test asserts no `.reconciler-*` path is ever committed to the tickets
   branch after a ref-backend pass (and that the cleanup helper removes a pre-seeded one).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `lock_backend` defaults to `ref`; the file-lock backend + the `b859` retry loop are deleted,
      along with `_resolve_retry_budget`, `_LOCK_RETRY_BUDGET_DEFAULT`, `_compute_backoff_seconds`,
      any then-dead backoff/CAS-retry helpers (grep-verified), the `lock_max_retries` config field +
      coercion + env aliases, and their tests. `_cas_once`/`_is_cas_mismatch` are kept (used by
      `_ref_lock`). A configured `lock_backend=file` is deprecated-and-ignored (one-time warning).
- [ ] `.reconciler-*` is removed from `_GITATTRIBUTES`; `.bridge_state/*` is left in place;
      `tests/interfaces/store/test_gitattributes_merge.py` updated accordingly.
- [ ] A `.gitattributes` update-migration (mirroring `_commit_gitignore`) strips
      `.reconciler-* merge=ours` from already-committed trackers; idempotent; git failure logs and
      continues rather than aborting.
- [ ] A single, named, idempotent startup migration (invoked from `__main__.main()` before acquire)
      removes any pre-existing committed `.reconciler-*` files; a regression test asserts no
      `.reconciler-*` path is ever committed to the tickets branch.
- [ ] `lock_max_retries` is handled as deprecated-and-ignored (one-time warning, not a load error)
      and its removal is documented in `docs/config.md` + changelog.
- [ ] Full non-integration suite green.
baseline.summary: Retire merge=ours .gitattributes + b859 lock-retry band-aid; migrate committed locks

baseline.description:
## Problem

Several reconciler test helpers load engine modules by path with this pattern:

    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    mod  = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules.setdefault(name, mod)   # <-- does NOT replace an existing entry
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)        # <-- but execs into the NEW object
    return mod                          # <-- and returns the NEW object

When `sys.modules[name]` is already populated (another test file in the same worker loaded it first), `setdefault` keeps the OLD module object while the helper execs and returns a NEW one. Any engine module that then does `import mutation` resolves the OLD object, so the class the code constructs and the class the test asserts against are DIFFERENT objects with the same name.

Symptom, from CI (macos-latest, py3.13):

    tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ.py::test_new_key_in_local_produces_outbound_create_mutation
    >   assert isinstance(m, mutation_mod.Mutation)
    E   AssertionError: assert False
    E    +  where False = isinstance(Mutation(direction=..., action=..., target='DSO-42'...), <class 'mutation.Mutation'>)

## Why it surfaced now

It is latent and ORDER-DEPENDENT, so it only fires when a particular pair of files lands in the same xdist worker. Change 1043 (story 2932) added tests, which changed sharding: patchset 1 passed CI, patchset 2 failed twice deterministically, with the only delta being added tests in an unrelated subsystem. The reconciler code itself is untouched by that change.

Not reproducible on a py3.14 local venv even running the whole `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/` directory in one process; the failing CI job is py3.13 on macos-latest. Treat CI as the reproducer.

## Fix

Make the helper return the module that is ACTUALLY registered, so exactly one class object exists per name:

    existing = sys.modules.get(name)
    if existing is not None and getattr(existing, '__file__', None) == str(path):
        return existing
    ... module_from_spec ...
    sys.modules[name] = mod        # assign, do not setdefault
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)

The path guard matters: these names (`mutation`, `differ`, `applier`) are generic, so blindly reusing any same-named module could bind to something unrelated.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] no reconciler test helper uses `sys.modules.setdefault` for by-path module loading: `grep -rn 'sys.modules.setdefault' tests/` is empty
- [ ] a test asserts the helper returns the SAME object on a second call for the same name+path (one class object per name)
- [ ] a test asserts a same-name/different-path load does NOT silently reuse the wrong module
- [ ] [operator-attested] CI is green on macos-latest/py3.13 for a change that previously reproduced the failure, evidenced by the Gerrit change id and its Verified +1 recorded in a comment
baseline.summary: Reconciler test _load_module uses sys.modules.setdefault, yielding two class objects and order-dependent isinstance failures

# DC sub-task parent sync: two live cells have never passed — they are WRONG ORACLES, plus one real silent-drop defect

Filed under epic [rebar:e369-a449-4773-48fb]. Operator ruling (2026-08-04): **resolve the failures; do NOT delete, skip, or `xfail` any cell.**

## Evidence — never passed, measured across 12 consecutive harness runs

Per-cell failing sets from every `Live External Integration` job `30834117797` (08-03 16:52) through `30951453979` (08-04 21:14). Both cells appear in the FAILED set of **all 12**:

    test_inbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips     12/12 FAILED
    test_outbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips    12/12 FAILED

**"Never passed", NOT a regression** — no bisect, no revert. The harness demonstrably detects fixes (6 -> 3 failures over the window, with six named cells dropping out at identifiable runs); these two never did.

## Mechanism — RE-MEASURED, with two premises of the original filing corrected

### Platform half — CONFIRMED (ticket 1a9f)

DC 8.17.1 accepts `PUT fields.parent` on a sub-task and **silently ignores it**. Re-confirmed live in run `30951453979`, whose own failure text is the measurement: rebar asked for `RBJREXN-2`, Jira accepted, a fresh REST read still reported `RBJREXN-1`. Capability map req-0056 (HTTP 204) / req-0058 (read-back unchanged) hold. Re-asserting mattered because this epic RETRACTED the map's label-ceiling entry when a live cell contradicted it.

Clearing is separately impossible on a sub-task: `{"fields":{"parent":null}}` -> 400, `{"update":{"parent":[{"set":null}]}}` -> 400, sub-task `editmeta` exposes NO `parent` field (req-0054/0055/0057, [rebar:37e7-d751-0042-4b94]).

### CORRECTION 1 — the apply-side symbol was mis-located, and the "disjoint gates" premise is REFUTED

`set_parent` lives in **`adapters/jira_datacenter/_hierarchy.py:100`**, not `transport.py` (which contains no parent code). And it no longer "accepts only a sub-task child": since 39c1/change 1311 its non-sub-task branch WRITES the discovered Epic Link field (`_hierarchy.py:147-168`). The emit and apply gates therefore **already overlap** for the epic shape, pinned on both sides — unit `test_dc_epic_link_parent_39c1.py:296` and live `test_outbound_epic_parent_reaches_dc_THROUGH_A_RECONCILE_PASS`, **PASSED in run 30951453979**. A reconcile pass demonstrably emits and lands a parent on DC today.

### CORRECTION 2 — the remaining rebar defect is SILENCE, not disjointness

`_resolve_local_parent` (`outbound_field_diff.py:138-139`) returns `(False, None)` for a non-epic parent — **byte-identical to :142's "unbound this pass, retry next pass"** — with no log call of any kind, and the caller at :383-385 does nothing when `not present`. So a user's parent edit against a non-epic parent never enters `fields`, `dispatch_one._update_one_apply_parent:523` never runs, and the entire `record_parent_divergence` / `bridge_alerts` apparatus (`pass_io.py:103-146`) is **structurally unreachable**. The pass exits 0 and reports convergence while the hierarchy diverges.

This violates the project's own contract, cited: `pass_io.py:113-118` — "a log line is not a signal: the pass still exits 0 and **nothing durable says the hierarchy diverged**" — and `dispatch_one.py:561-564` — "Warn-and-continue alone is why 'the parent never reached the tracker' stayed invisible through **five instances of this class**." 39c1 wired that contract into *apply-time* failure and left *emit-time* suppression silent. `record_parent_divergence` has **zero** references in `tests/`. This is an **incomplete implementation of 39c1 AC4** and is pure rebar, fixable with no platform capability.

## THE RE-HOME TARGET, NAMED AND CAPABILITY-CHECKED

AC1's answer is **negative for a genuine sub-task** and **positive for the Epic Link**, and the supported mechanism is therefore named rather than assumed:

> **The Epic Link custom field on a NON-sub-task child.** Both directions and both operations are
> already GREEN on the live instance in run `30951453979`:
> `test_outbound_epic_parent_round_trips_via_the_epic_link` (set AND clear, raw-REST read-back),
> `test_outbound_epic_parent_reaches_dc_THROUGH_A_RECONCILE_PASS` (through a real pass), and
> `test_inbound_clear_parent_round_trips` (Epic Link clear observed inbound via 9bb9's
> `get_parent_map` fallback). Capability map req-0040/0041.

Re-homing changes the CHILD SHAPE from sub-task to standard issue. That is the point, not a loss: an oracle for an operation the platform cannot perform is a wrong oracle. The **subject of each cell is preserved** — see AC4/AC5 below — and the platform impossibility stays pinned by the two cells that already assert it (`test_a_subtask_reparent_is_REFUSED_rather_than_silently_ignored`, and 37e7's sub-task-clear pin at `test_dc_mutations.py:1810-1817`), so a future DC that starts allowing it is caught rather than silently forgotten.

**Why this ticket's ruling supersedes 1a9f's disposition.** 1a9f left the two round-trip cells RED and carried the loudness in a separate refusal cell. That left two permanent reds in a suite whose value is that a red means something, and the epic's goal is DC support **without** standing failures. The operator's 2026-08-04 ruling for this ticket is to resolve them, and re-homing is the already-endorsed instrument for exactly this shape — used by 37e7 (Row 13 inbound), b9b8 (Row 14), and [rebar:4b9e-bcad-456a-4233]. This ticket adopts that framing explicitly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC1 — LIVE measurement of whether ANY supported DC mechanism moves a sub-task's parent.**
      ANSWERED, run `30951453979`: `fields.parent` on a sub-task is accept-and-ignore (req-0056/0058,
      reproduced in the run's own failure text); nulling it is 400 both spellings (req-0055/0057);
      sub-task `editmeta` exposes no `parent` (req-0054). **Negative for a sub-task.** The supported
      mechanism is the **Epic Link on a non-sub-task child**, green in the same run (req-0040/0041).
- [x] **AC2 — the emit side stops failing SILENTLY.** A non-epic parent the tracker cannot represent
      must produce a durable, operator-visible record (a `bridge_alerts` entry), not a bare `return`
      indistinguishable from "retry next pass". 8b25's guard is **preserved** — the field stays
      omitted, so rebar still never issues a write DC would ignore. Scoped to what rebar controls;
      this does not claim the sub-task shape becomes emittable.
- [x] **AC3 — no write DC is measured to accept-and-ignore is ever issued, and the unsupported case
      fails LOUDLY** (raise + bridge alert naming the reason and the supported alternative), never a
      silent no-op reporting success.
- [x] **AC4 — `test_inbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips` PASSES, re-homed, subject preserved.**
      Its subject is **rebar's inbound pass carrying a parent change into `.parent_id`**; the DC-side
      reparent was only SETUP, and that setup is the impossible part (it fails at
      `test_dc_mutations.py:1664`, before the subject is ever reached). Re-homed to an Epic Link
      re-parent (child under epic A, moved DC-side to epic B), the oracle still asserts the
      user-visible outcome end to end: **the child ends up under the intended parent locally.**
- [x] **AC5 — `test_outbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips` PASSES, re-homed, subject preserved.**
      Re-homing it to "epic parent outbound" would duplicate two already-green cells and assert
      nothing new. Its live subject becomes the claim currently unasserted anywhere: **when a user
      sets a parent the tracker cannot represent for this child shape, rebar must tell the operator
      rather than dropping it.** The oracle asserts the user-visible outcome for the unsupported
      case — a bridge alert naming the reason and the supported alternative, AND the remote parent
      unchanged. This is a **rebar** capability, not a platform one, so it is reachable; and it is
      distinct from `test_a_subtask_reparent_is_REFUSED_rather_than_silently_ignored`, which asserts
      the transport-level raise, not what a PASS surfaces.
- [x] **AC6 — no cell is deleted, skipped, or `xfail`ed to reach green** (operator ruling). The
      sub-task platform impossibility remains pinned by the two cells named above.
- [x] **AC7** — `docs/jira-dc-capability-map.md` records the outcome with run id `30951453979`.

## Testing

    pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 4 --dist worksteal -q
    gh workflow run "Live External Integration" --ref main   # the only place these cells run
baseline.summary: DC sub-task parent sync is unimplemented: two live cells have never passed in any harness run
