# Code-review 'new-behavior-without-test' landmine detector

## Context (discovered from grusome-uncheerful-nematode)
Child #7 originally bundled two changes: (a) the docs/llm-prompts nit down-rank (shipped in #7)
and (b) a grounding-assisted detector that fires when a diff adds new public behavior with no
correlated test. Investigation during the epic established that (b) needs a BESPOKE seam that
does not exist yet, so it was split out here to keep #7 landable.

## Why it needs a bespoke seam (not an existing one)
- Code-review DET detectors are **Engine B** grounding rules (gitleaks/opengrep-style YAML
  pattern rules) selected by `exec: DET` routing `detector` selectors and run via
  `run_detectors` -> `engine_b.scan`. A 'new-behavior-without-test' check requires diff-parsing
  the added public definitions AND cross-file correlation to test files — that is NOT the
  pattern-matching model Engine B implements.
- `rebar.grounding.resolve.extract_references_from_diff` extracts **imports only** (Python), not
  added symbol DEFINITIONS, so it cannot supply the added-definition set the detector needs.

## Sketch of the required seam
A Python code-review detector (in `code_review/detectors.py` or a new module) invoked in the DET
phase that: (1) parses the unified diff for newly-added exported/public defs via ast-grep /
universal-ctags (language-aware); (2) correlates against added/updated test files; (3) FIRES
(advisory/permissive first) when a new public def has no correlated test; (4) ABSTAINS
fail-open on: unparseable/garbled diff, no grounding backend available, or docs/config-only
change. Coaching surfaces through the existing `code_review_coach` path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A grounding-assisted `new_behavior_without_test` detector exists and is wired into the
      code-review DET phase, using real ast-grep/ctags grounding (added-definition extraction,
      NOT imports-only), shipped advisory/permissive first.
- [ ] MUST-FIRE (new public def, no test) / MUST-NOT-FIRE (def with a correlated test) /
      ABSTAIN (docs-only, unparseable, no backend) unit tests.
- [ ] Proving command: `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_new_behavior_detector.py -v`.
baseline.summary: Code-review 'new-behavior-without-test' landmine detector (bespoke diff-parse + cross-file test-correlation seam)

## Problem

The `rebar-implement` skill (examples/agent-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md) carries a "Model tiering" section that pins the implementer subagent to strong/standard/cheap model tiers to save tokens. This model-level gradient adds significant complexity (a tier table, per-dispatch tier-naming rules, a dedicated 4e-bis "Tier escalation" ladder, and per-leaf tiering session-log requirements) for savings that only materialize on wide epics. We are removing it.

Separately, Phase 0's preflight hard-stops on any ticket with no children, telling the user to decompose first. That is too strict: a `story`/`task` that has no children but DOES carry a recorded file impact is already an executable code leaf — the file impact is exactly the acceptance the completion-verifier close gate needs. The skill should execute such a ticket as a single leaf instead of refusing it.

## Plan

1. Remove the model-level gradient:
   - Delete the entire "## Model tiering" section.
   - Strip tiering language from every downstream reference (Phase 3 non-code leaf, 4a spec
     derivation, 4d implementer dispatch + constraints note) while PRESERVING the held-out
     discipline (the implementer remains a *separate subagent*, which never depended on tiering).
   - Rewrite 4e-bis from "Tier escalation" to a tier-free "Escalation — when re-dispatch isn't
     enough" (re-dispatch -> take-the-leaf-yourself -> report blocked).
   - Reground the Phase 5 residual-sweep example that referenced tier-based validation.

2. Allow a childless story/task with a recorded file impact to run as a single leaf:
   - Phase 0 now recognizes two executable shapes: (a) has children -> tree; (b) childless
     `story`/`task` with non-empty `rebar get-file-impact` -> single code leaf. Stop only when
     neither holds.
   - Add a Phase 2 callout so the epic ceremony (Phases 3/5/6) collapses to one change for the
     single-leaf run.
   - Update the frontmatter description, the Phase 0 heading, and the Reporting stop line to
     match.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Root cause established for why the upload event does not queue a review — proven, not inferred. Runtime experiment (3 reconcile passes, `since`-honouring events-log double) plus a live events-log probe proving `?t1=` is a server-side inclusive lower bound; see the RCA comment.
- [x] A patch-set upload that the webhook drops is re-driven WITHOUT any manual comment. `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py::test_reconcile_cursor_holds_back_an_abandoned_non_newest_candidate` — two passes, a multi-event window, the abandoned NON-newest candidate re-driven on pass 2. Seen RED first (its own assertion message), held out from the fix author, and returned to RED by a defect-seeded mutation.
- [x] A terminal outcome does NOT pin the cursor. `test_reconcile_cursor_advances_past_a_terminal_outcome` — a `skipped`/`post_vote_closed` candidate lets the cursor advance to the newest event.
- [x] A chronically-failing candidate cannot pin the window forever. `test_reconcile_holdback_is_bounded_so_a_poison_pill_cannot_pin_the_window` — past `RECONCILE_MAX_HOLDBACK_SECONDS` the cursor advances and `RECONCILE_DEGRADED reason=holdback_expired` is emitted.
- [x] Backfill's carried backlog is OBSERVABLE. `test_reconcile_done_reports_the_carried_backlog` asserts `reconcile_done` emits `held_back` and `cursor`.
- [x] `recheck-review` remains available as a manual override, and is no longer the routine path. The retrigger path is untouched by this change and its 31 tests pass (`tests/unit/test_review_bot_retrigger.py`); "no longer routine" is proven transitively by the automatic re-drive above, and by this change's own landing — patch sets 1, 2 and 7 of Gerrit change 1512 each auto-queued a review with no nudge (17m58s, ~6m, ~5m).
- [x] 'not queued' vs 'queued behind N' vs 'running' is visible. `tests/unit/test_review_bot_in_flight.py::test_health_endpoint_reports_the_queue_depth` asserts `/health` returns `queue_depth` (0 with no queue, N with N queued) alongside the unchanged `in_flight`.
- [x] `docs/adr/0009-review-bot-pipe.md:82` no longer claims the webhooks plugin delivers at-least-once — corrected there and in `src/rebar/review_bot/dedup.py` to at-most-once/best-effort, with the reconciler named as the recovery path.

Landed as Gerrit change 1512, MERGED (`2bda965db6`), `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.

# fsck should RESTORE deleted sources, not just refuse

## STACKED ON UNLANDED CHANGE 1557 (bug b636) — read this first
This story is the SECOND change in a stack. Gerrit change 1557 (bug `b636`) is unlanded at the time of writing, and it INTRODUCES the symbols this plan builds on. They do NOT exist on `origin/main` yet:
- `compact_rebuild.snapshot_missing_sources(ticket_dir)` — the cited-but-absent-source
  predicate (1557 also extracts the whole rebuild cluster from `compact.py` into the new
  `_commands/compact_rebuild.py` leaf for the module-size cap).
- `fsck._maybe_repair_snapshot(...)` — 1557 extracts the previously INLINE repair block from
  `fsck._scan` (main's fsck.py:180-190) into this helper.
- the `SNAPSHOT_MISSING_SOURCES` fsck finding.
Do not start this story until 1557 has merged; re-verify these names against the merged tree before implementing.

## Why
1557 makes the rebuild FAIL CLOSED when the prior SNAPSHOT cites source events absent from disk. That stops new corruption but leaves the population permanently un-repairable: a dry run of the fixed fsck reports 505 live tickets in that shape, and `fsck --repair` can then never drive them to fsck-zero.

## Evidence restoration is possible
Deleted event files remain reachable in `origin/tickets` history at the deleting commit's parent. Over the 505 flagged tickets: 504 have deletion records covering every cited-missing uuid, 1 partial, 0 with none. Validated on a COPY of the live store: restoring every deleted event file then rebuilding restored 214/214 already-regressed tickets (486 events).

## Prior art to REUSE, and where it must DIFFER
`attest/authorship.py:build_ticket_position_commit_map` is the ticket-scoped, single-pass `git log --diff-filter=A --name-only` walk, cost-tuned as the batched form of `resolve_event_commit`. Reuse that SHAPE. CRITICAL DIFFERENCE: that helper streams newest->oldest and OVERWRITES, so the OLDEST commit wins — correct for `--diff-filter=A` (the oldest ADD introduced the event). For `--diff-filter=D` the correct fold is the NEWEST deletion (the last time the path was removed), because a path may be added and deleted more than once across successive compactions. Copying the oldest-wins fold direction would read a stale pre-image. Use first-seen-wins over the newest-first stream, and TEST a path deleted twice. Blob reads use the existing `git show <ref>:<path>` idiom (`binding_store.py`, `_store/compat.py`).

## Naming
`_commands/fsck_recover.py` already owns 'recover' here, so the new primitive is `restore_deleted_sources`.

## Why the snapshot's citation list is not enough
Ticket 72d5 recovered its close STATUS but still read in_progress: an EARLIER deleted STATUS that no surviving snapshot cites broke the chain's current_status precondition, so the reducer rejected both it and the close. Restoration must sweep the ticket's FULL deletion history.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `compact_rebuild.restore_deleted_sources(tracker, ticket_id, ticket_dir) -> list[str]`
      restores every event file deleted from that ticket dir, enumerated by ONE ticket-scoped
      `git log --diff-filter=D --name-only -- <tid>/` pass, NEWEST-deletion-wins, each blob
      read at the deleting commit's parent and written back as a folded `.retired` source
      (never resurrected live). Returns restored filenames.
- [ ] `compact_rebuild.rebuild_with_restore(...)` owns restore -> re-check
      `snapshot_missing_sources` -> rebuild, refusing (1557 fail-closed) only when restoration
      cannot complete the log.
- [ ] BOTH live rebuild call sites route through it: `fsck._maybe_repair_snapshot` (post-1557)
      and `fsck_repair.py:268`. Neither may call `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` directly.
- [ ] `--dry-run` reports per ticket how many events WOULD be restored and whether a rebuild
      would follow, writing nothing.
- [ ] Per-ticket scan only (no full-history index build) so it stays usable on a large store.
- [ ] BACK-OUT + blast-radius: the run pre-tags the tracker before any write (as A3 did, but
      the tag MUST be created before the FIRST batch — `pre-a3-remediation` was stamped
      mid-run, after 2 of 4 batches, and is therefore not a valid rollback point). Before any
      live run, the whole sweep is executed against a COPY of the store and the resulting
      status of EVERY ticket is diffed against the pre-run state; only the intended
      restorations may change status.
- [ ] Held-out test: a ticket whose close exists ONLY in history is restored and reads closed
      after `fsck --repair`.
- [ ] Held-out test: a path deleted TWICE restores the newest pre-image, not the oldest.
- [ ] Held-out test: a ticket with genuinely unrecoverable sources still refuses, unchanged
      from 1557.
baseline.summary: fsck: auto-recover deleted SNAPSHOT sources from tickets history, then rebuild

# Drop the unused `inspect-ai` dependency and the `[eval]` extra it is the sole content of

## Context / Problem

Per the OPERATOR DECISION comment on this ticket (2026-08-07): **Option A — drop inspect-ai.** The original scope (smoke-test the inspect-ai eval path) is void because there is no such path.

`inspect-ai>=0.3.221` is declared at `pyproject.toml:150` as the only member of the `[eval]` extra, and rebar never imports it: `grep -rn "inspect_ai" src/` returns exactly one hit, `src/rebar/_optional.py:36`, which is the extras-registry NAME string, not an import. There are zero `import inspect_ai` / `from inspect_ai` statements. `INSPECT_MIN_VERSION` at `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:40` is referenced by nothing else in the tree.

Carrying it costs three separate pieces of live machinery, all of which exist only for it:

1. Both `[tool.uv] conflicts` entries (`pyproject.toml:275-278`, `eval` vs `bedrock` and `eval`
   vs `dev`) — `[eval]` -> inspect-ai -> aioboto3 -> aiobotocore pins `boto3 < 1.40.62` against
   `pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]` needing `boto3 >= 1.42.63`.
2. `override-dependencies = ["click>=8.3.3"]` (`pyproject.toml:285-287`) — inspect-ai caps
   `click < 8.2.2`, which held the whole universal lock on click 8.2.1 and made CI's gating
   pip-audit fail on every in-flight change (PYSEC-2026-2132).
3. This ticket's own premise: a pytest smoke test gated on `[eval]` would run in zero lanes,
   because the eval/dev conflict keeps pytest and inspect-ai out of the same environment.

## Approach

Delete the dependency and everything that exists solely to accommodate it, then let the resolver prove the accommodations were unnecessary rather than asserting it.

The `[eval]` extra is **removed entirely**, not retained empty. inspect-ai is its only member, so once removed the extra installs nothing. It is not redefined as an alias for `[agents]` either: the offline prompt-eval surface (`rebar prompt eval`, spec validation, grader discipline, JUnit conversion) is stdlib-only and needs no extra, and the live run's own solver already documents its real requirement as the `agents` extra (`src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py`, `_live_solver`: "Needs the `agents` extra (pydantic_ai)"). An alias extra would make `extra_installed("eval")` a synonym for `extra_installed("agents")` — a second name for one capability, which is the machinery this change is deleting.

Each removal is checked against the resolver before it is kept: `uv lock` is regenerated and `uv sync --locked` is run for the extra combinations the conflicts previously forked apart. Both conflicts entries name the `eval` extra, so deleting the extra necessarily deletes them — a conflict cannot reference an extra that does not exist. The acceptance criterion that no conflicts entry names `eval` therefore governs absolutely. Should the resolver nonetheless fail without one of them, that is a blocking discovery about a dependency diamond unrelated to inspect-ai: it is recorded on this ticket and escalated, not worked around by keeping a dangling conflict — there is no partial-land path for that branch.

Back-out is a straight `git revert` of the `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` changes, which restores the extra and its accommodations exactly. No deprecation window is offered: `[eval]`'s sole member is never imported, so the extra delivered no functional capability to any consumer and there is nothing for a deprecation period to keep working. `pip` treats an unknown extra as a warning rather than an error, so an existing `nava-rebar[eval]` pin keeps installing the base package instead of failing; `uv sync --extra eval` does fail, and the release notes say so.

Removing a published extra is a deliberate consumer-visible break, so it is documented in both `CHANGELOG.md` (user-facing) and `docs/release-notes.md` (agent-visible contract changes), per the split those two files declare in their own headers.

The stale docstring is fixed in the same change because it is the same falsehood. That docstring makes the claim **twice** — line 6 ("runs through **Inspect AI**") and line 21 ("only the actual *run* (`run_eval`) imports Inspect AI, lazily, behind `guard_import`") — and both are contradicted by the same file: the comment above the live-run section says "NOT routed through Inspect AI ... would add a dependency and an impedance mismatch for no gain", and `_live_solver` imports `rebar.llm.config` / the pydantic-ai runtime, never `inspect_ai`. Both claims are rewritten to describe the native solver loop that actually runs.

## Scope

- `pyproject.toml` — remove the `eval` extra and its comment block; remove both `[tool.uv]
  conflicts` entries; remove `override-dependencies`; update the `botocore`/`boto3` floor
  comment in `[dev]` that explains itself by reference to the conflicts fork; update the
  lean-install comment at line 59 that names `inspect_ai`.
- `uv.lock` — regenerated with `uv lock`.
- `src/rebar/_optional.py` — drop the `"eval"` entry from `EXTRAS` and the `[eval]` bullet
  from the module docstring.
- `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py` — rewrite the module docstring to describe the native
  solver loop it actually runs; delete `INSPECT_MIN_VERSION`.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — drop `"eval_extra"` from `available_backends()`.
- `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py` — four live references to the extra: drop `eval` from
  the extras probed (line 239) and printed (line 283) by `rebar llm setup`, and correct the two
  places that misstate the live prompt-eval requirement as the `eval` extra — the `_prompt_eval`
  docstring (line 22) and the hint it prints (line 93). Both become `agents`, which is what
  `_live_solver` actually needs.
- `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/*.eval.yaml` and `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/README.plan-review.md` —
  the header comments that tell a reader a live run needs the `[eval]` extra; same correction to
  `[agents]`.
- `README.md` — the `[eval]` bullet under optional capabilities (line 179), the
  `pip install 'nava-rebar[eval]'` recipe (line 227), **and** the union recipe on line 229,
  `pip install 'nava-rebar[agents,eval,tracing]'`, which names the extra in combined form and
  would otherwise stay in the README as a documented command naming a removed extra.
- `docs/llm-framework.md` — the `[eval]` extra bullet and the two `[bedrock]`-conflicts-with-
  `[eval]` statements.
- `docs/adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md:171` — the prose lists `inspect_ai` as a member of the
  lean-install ban-list this change edits. The ADR's *decision* is untouched; only that
  sentence's claim about live CI machinery is corrected, so the ADR does not describe a
  ban-list entry that no longer exists.
- `docs/dependency-advisory-runbook.md` — its worked `override-dependencies` example IS this
  inspect-ai/PYSEC-2026-2132 override, with a `REMOVE-WHEN` note this change moots. The example
  and every phrase `tests/unit/test_dependency_advisory_wiring.py` pins stay (they are the
  banked uv knowledge); a short note records that this particular override was retired by
  deleting the capping dependency rather than by waiting for upstream — the cheaper remedy the
  runbook should teach first.
- `.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml` — every mention of the extra, not only the install: the
  `eval-live` job's `uv sync --locked --extra agents --extra eval` (line 72) and the conflict
  comment above it (line 69), the step name on line 68, the workflow-header comment on line 11
  ("needs the `[agents,eval]` extras + credentials"), and the job's display `name:` on line 52.
  After the change the job installs `--extra agents` only, and nothing in the file advertises a
  removed extra.
- `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` — remove `inspect_ai` from the lean-install
  must-not-import probe list.
- `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/release-notes.md` — the breaking-change entries.
- `tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py`, `tests/unit/grounding/test_non_adoption.py` — remove
  `inspect_ai` from their must-not-be-imported module lists.
- `tests/unit/test_new_eval_specs.py`, `tests/unit/test_plan_review_evals.py`,
  `tests/unit/test_code_review_evals.py` — their module docstrings each tell a reader the live
  eval run "needs the `[eval]` extra + credentials", which is the same misstatement being
  corrected in the CLI hints and the spec headers; retarget all three to `agents`.
- `tests/unit/test_optional.py`, `tests/unit/test_llm_setup_cli.py` — retarget the assertions
  that name the `eval` extra onto **`tracing`**, chosen because it is the other net-new extra
  those tests already reference and, like `eval` was, it is absent from the dev venv — so
  `test_require_extra_missing_raises_with_install_hint` keeps exercising the missing-extra
  branch instead of skipping.
- `tests/unit/test_packaging_dependencies.py` (new) — the contract tests below.

## Testing

New tests in `tests/unit/test_packaging_dependencies.py`, parsing `pyproject.toml` with `tomllib` (stdlib, Python >= 3.11 per the project's own floor):

- happy path: `inspect-ai` appears in no dependency list anywhere in `pyproject.toml`, and no
  `eval` key exists in `[project.optional-dependencies]`.
- the two accommodations are gone and stay gone: `[tool.uv]` has no `override-dependencies`
  key, and no `conflicts` entry mentions the `eval` extra.
- edge/regression: every extra name in `rebar._optional.EXTRAS` resolves to a real key in
  `[project.optional-dependencies]` — so a future extras rename cannot leave the registry
  pointing at an extra that does not exist (the exact drift this change is fixing by hand).

Resolver + audit evidence, run in the worktree and recorded on the ticket:

- `uv lock` regenerates cleanly, and `uv sync --locked --extra dev`,
  `--extra dev --extra bedrock`, and `--extra dev --extra agents` all resolve and install —
  the dev+bedrock combination is the one the removed conflicts previously forked.
- `pip-audit` over the resulting `dev` environment passes with no `override-dependencies`
  present, confirming the override was a workaround for inspect-ai's stale click cap and not
  load-bearing on its own.
- the full gate — `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the pytest suite — passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `grep -rn "inspect.ai\|inspect_ai" pyproject.toml src/ tests/ .github/` returns no
      dependency, import, registry, or probe hit (docs/CHANGELOG history may still mention it).
- [x] `[project.optional-dependencies]` has no `eval` key, verified by the new tomllib test.
- [x] `[tool.uv]` has no `override-dependencies` key and no `conflicts` entry naming `eval`,
      verified by the new tomllib test.
- [x] `uv lock` regenerates `uv.lock` and `uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra bedrock`
      installs successfully — the combination the removed conflicts previously forbade.
- [x] `pip-audit` reports no vulnerability on the locked `dev` environment with the click
      override removed; the installed click is >= 8.3.3.
- [x] `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py` has no `INSPECT_MIN_VERSION` and neither docstring claim
      (line 6 and line 21) survives, so the module header no longer contradicts the
      implementation comment above its live-run section.
- [x] `grep -rn "eval\] extra\|nava-rebar\[eval\]" src/ tests/ README.md docs/llm-framework.md`
      returns nothing: no remaining text in code, tests, or user documentation tells a reader
      that a live run needs the removed extra, and no documented install command names it —
      including README.md's `[agents,eval,tracing]` union recipe. The surviving hints name
      `agents`.
- [x] `grep -rn "eval_extra" src/rebar/` returns nothing, so `available_backends()` no longer
      reports a key for the removed extra.
- [x] `docs/adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md` and `docs/dependency-advisory-runbook.md` no
      longer describe `inspect_ai` as a current lean-install ban-list entry or the click
      override as an active workaround: the ADR's ban-list sentence drops `inspect_ai`, and the
      runbook records that this override was retired by deleting the capping dependency (while
      keeping every phrase `tests/unit/test_dependency_advisory_wiring.py` pins, which still
      pass).
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` (Unreleased) and `docs/release-notes.md` each carry an entry stating that
      the `[eval]` extra is removed and what a consumer installing it should do instead.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the full pytest suite pass.
baseline.summary: Drop the unused inspect-ai dependency and the [eval] extra

# J6 — Data Center transport on `pycontribs/jira`, behind an opt-in extra

## Context / Problem

The DC backend needs a transport satisfying rebar's `TicketTransport` role plus `SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`, and `SupportsAbsenceProbe` (`_backend.py:80-282`). The Cloud transport is an ACLI subprocess (`adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py:31` shells out to the `acli` binary), which is Cloud-shaped and must not be disturbed. PR #120 hand-rolled a stdlib `urllib` REST v2 client for DC.

## Approach

Build the DC transport on **`pycontribs/jira`**, the maintained Python client that already handles Server/DC versus Cloud differences, PAT bearer auth, pagination, and payload quirks that a hand-rolled client would rediscover. It is confined to an opt-in `[jira-datacenter]` extra and imported **lazily inside the functions that need it**, so the engine's `dependencies = []` contract holds and `import rebar` stays dependency-free; a missing extra raises a clear install-naming error, mirroring `runner._import_pydantic_ai`.

Auth is a Personal Access Token read env-only from `JIRA_PAT` (DC PATs, Jira 8.14+), passed as `token_auth`; `url` and `project` come from the typed config so a `[tool.rebar.jira]` value is honored. A malformed config **fails loudly** rather than degrading to env-only — PR #120 swallowed `ConfigError`, which is against rebar's fail-loud posture.

The library's object model is unwrapped at this boundary: every method returns the **raw payload shapes** rebar's existing mappers already consume (`{"key": …, "fields": {…}}`), so nothing downstream learns about `jira.Issue`. Retry, timeout, and error typing are mapped onto rebar's existing transport contract — transient connectivity faults retried with the same 2s/5s backoff as `adapters/jira/acli_rest._rest_urlopen_with_retry`, HTTP errors never retried, and assignee failures raised as `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError` (`_backend.py:48`).

This story also supplies the `NameIdentity` resolver's user-search lookup [rebar:0a94-e104-7304-4d85].

**Alternative rejected: a hand-rolled stdlib client (PR #120).** Competent, but it re-owns Jira REST semantics that a widely-used library has already hardened, and confining the dependency to an extra means non-DC users pay nothing for it.

**Alternative rejected: reusing the ACLI transport for DC.** ACLI is the Cloud-validated path; pointing it at DC would risk the one transport we have live confidence in, which this epic explicitly must not do.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` (new).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py` (new) — `JIRA_URL`/`JIRA_PROJECT`
  from typed config, env-only `JIRA_PAT`, fail-loud on `ConfigError`.
- **`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/__init__.py`** — add the DC backend import beside the
  existing `from .jira import backend as _jira_backend` (line 15). That import is not decorative: importing an
  adapter's backend module is the SIDE EFFECT that calls `register()` into `_backend_registry`, which is how
  `select_backend()` finds it. Without the DC equivalent, `select_backend("jira-datacenter")` raises
  `BackendRegistryError` at runtime ("unknown reconciler backend ...; registered keys: [...]",
  `_backend_registry.py:71` — NOT `KeyError`, which an earlier draft of this note claimed) even with the extra
  installed and every other file correct — a failure that no unit test of the
  transport itself would catch.
- **`src/rebar/_config_schema.py`** — the DC connection settings this story's own ACs already claim (the
  TLS/`allow_insecure` validator, `ca_bundle`, and `resolved_statuses`), which the parent epic's Scope assigns
  here. It was named in the ACs but missing from this list.
- `pyproject.toml` — `[jira-datacenter]` extra.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_dc_transport.py` (new).
- **`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_transport.py`** (new) — note the path: J5
  [rebar:c97f-90ae-4976-47c7] landed the harness under `tests/external/`, and an earlier draft of this Scope
  said `tests/live_jira_dc/`, which does not exist. The distinction is not cosmetic: `tests/external/` is the
  only tier fenced off from per-commit CI, so a live test outside it is collected by the default suite AND by
  `_build-and-test.yml`'s dedicated `pytest -m integration` step, on runners with no Docker, no Jira and no
  egress — breaking CI for everyone. Landing under the right path also inherits three mechanisms this story
  must honour: `tests/external/conftest.py` auto-applies the `external` marker (and hard-fails collection if
  it appears elsewhere); the autouse `_require_external_opt_in` fixture skips everything without
  `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1`; and a module-level `_live_jira_ready` sentinel is what enrols the module in the
  all-skip canary, so **`test_transport.py` MUST define one** or a silently-all-skipped run reads as green.
  Absent harness ⇒ SKIP with an actionable message, never a hard failure.

## Testing

Two tiers. A stateful fake for fast unit coverage of shape mapping, and the J5 harness [rebar:c97f-90ae-4976-47c7] as the real oracle — the test-design standard's "stateful verified fake plus a live canary where justified", and DC semantics are exactly where a fake's assumptions are most likely to be wrong.

- unit (fake library client): each `TicketTransport` method returns rebar's raw payload shape, not a
  `jira.Issue`; `JIRA_PAT` is sent as bearer token auth; a missing `[jira-datacenter]` extra raises naming the
  install command; a malformed config raises rather than degrading.
- unit failure paths: an HTTP error is NOT retried (call count is exactly 1) while a connection timeout IS
  retried with the documented backoff; an unknown assignee raises `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError`.
- live (J5 harness): create → read → update → transition-by-name → comment → link → probe a real issue and
  assert each observable postcondition on the server, including that a transition to a name the workflow does
  not offer raises rather than silently no-oping.
- live edge: the absence probe returns the classifier's not-found state for a deleted issue, and a distinct
  state for one that merely lost permission.
- collateral invariant: no Cloud test changes and `adapters/jira/acli*.py` are untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [operator-attested] every `TicketTransport`, `SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`, and `SupportsAbsenceProbe` method has a
      passing live test against the J5 harness, output summarized in a ticket comment
- [ ] a test asserts an HTTP error is attempted exactly once and a timeout is retried per the documented backoff
- [ ] `pip install nava-rebar` then `pip show jira` reports not-installed, and `import rebar` succeeds
- [ ] importing the DC transport without the extra raises an error naming `pip install nava-rebar[jira-datacenter]`
- [ ] a malformed `[tool.rebar.jira]` config raises `ConfigError` rather than falling back to env-only
- [ ] the `NameIdentity` user-search lookup this story supplies [rebar:0a94-e104-7304-4d85] is covered: a test
      asserts the resolver returns an authoritative identity for a user that exists on the DC instance, and
      raises `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError` for one that does not. J4 shipped `NameIdentity` taking its
      resolver as an explicit constructor parameter precisely so this story could supply a REAL lookup; leaving
      it unwired would restore the permanently-non-authoritative assignee (and the diff churn) that J4's
      anti-churn oracle exists to prevent
- [ ] `select_backend("jira-datacenter")` resolves after `import rebar_reconciler.adapters` — a test pins the
      registry lookup, so a missing self-registration import fails here rather than at an operator's first run.
      The negative half of that test expects `BackendRegistryError` (`_backend_registry.py:71`), NOT `KeyError`:
      a `pytest.raises(KeyError)` would never match and the guard would be worthless
- [ ] `git diff --stat` shows no change under `adapters/jira/acli*`
- [ ] the DC backend REJECTS a non-`https` `reconciler.base_url` with a `ConfigError` naming the cleartext
      risk, unless `allow_insecure = true` is set; a unit test covers the reject branch with a non-loopback
      `http://` URL, and a second test asserts the override path emits a warning naming the risk (epic AC13)
- [ ] every live test against the J5 harness sets `allow_insecure = true` explicitly (the harness serves plain
      `http://localhost:2990/jira`), so the loopback path exercises the override rather than bypassing the
      validator
- [ ] the `[jira-datacenter]` extra pins a minimum `jira` version with a compatible-release bound (e.g.
      `jira>=3.8,<4`), and a comment records which DC-vs-Cloud auth behavior that floor guarantees
- [ ] this story owns the `_config_schema.py` DC connection settings: the TLS/`allow_insecure` validator, the
      `ca_bundle` key, and `resolved_statuses` (J7 owns only the `reconciler.backend` choice widening)
- [ ] TLS certificate verification is never disabled — asserted against the parameter form the library
      ACTUALLY reads. `pycontribs/jira` takes TLS config through its **options dict**, not a bare constructor
      kwarg: `verify` is a key of `JIRA.DEFAULT_OPTIONS` (defaulting to `True`) and is consumed as
      `self._options["verify"]` (verified in upstream `jira/client.py`). So the test asserts the effective
      `options["verify"]` the transport passes is never `False` — either left at its default or set to a CA
      bundle path. An earlier draft said "constructed WITHOUT `verify=False`", which would be VACUOUS: no such
      kwarg exists, so the assertion would pass unchanged even with verification disabled through the options
      dict. The test must also assert a verification failure raises an error naming the `ca_bundle` setting
      rather than silently proceeding. `allow_insecure` is asserted to affect the URL scheme check ONLY — a test
      confirms it does not relax certificate verification
- [ ] `reconciler.resolved_statuses` configures the DC absence-probe's resolved-status set, defaulting to
      `{Resolved, Done, Cancelled}` when unset; a test covers both the default and a custom workflow's names
baseline.summary: J6 — Data Center transport on pycontribs/jira, behind an opt-in extra

baseline.description:
## Problem
Nothing validates, before a reconcile pass mutates a live client Jira, that the mapped projects EXIST / are visible to the bridge bot. Two live-only failure modes:
1. A mapped-but-nonexistent (decommissioned / permission-lost) project key is syntactically
   valid, so `_validate_project_key` passes; the failure only surfaces deep in fan-out as an
   ACLI error. This is exactly the `05b8-4efe-8d58-4c27` incident class.
2. `resolve_project` (projects_store.py) returns `mapping.legacy_default` VERBATIM,
   unvalidated. Every unbound/legacy ticket (absent bridge_project) resolves there. The
   cross-project write guard's allowed set = `read_projects().keys()` and EXCLUDES creates
   (applier.py `_cross_project_targets`), so a legacy_default pointing at a real-but-wrong
   (or nonexistent) project drives a mass CREATE storm into the wrong place, unguarded.

## Approach
Add a reconcile-pass PREFLIGHT that runs BEFORE any outbound mutation and validates every project the pass could touch is visible to the configured backend.

Required-key set (single source of truth, mirrors the fetcher fan-out at fetcher.py:540 so it validates exactly what fan-out queries): `read_projects(repo_root).keys()`; when that mapping is EMPTY the fetcher falls back to the single configured backend `query_project` (`[_query_project]`) — the exact green-state incident shape `{legacy_default:'REB', projects:{}}` — so the preflight INCLUDES that fallback `query_project` when `projects` is empty. PLUS `legacy_default` (when non-empty), since `resolve_project` sends every unbound/legacy create there. Empty-and-no-fallback → nothing to check (never probes).

Probe transport: reuse `access_check.py`'s existing `AcliClient` transport. Enumerate bot-visible keys through the client's ALREADY-PRESENT generic REST accessor `AcliClient._direct_rest_get` (acli_rest.py:207 — used by `get_issue_property`, `transition_issue`, `validate_assignee_exists`) against the standard Jira Cloud "Get projects paginated" endpoint `GET /rest/api/3/project/search`. That endpoint returns a PageBean (`values[]` / `startAt` / `maxResults` / `total` / `isLast`), NOT the token-cursor enhanced-search shape; the loop advances `startAt` by the page size and terminates on `isLast`, an empty `values` page, or `startAt >= total`. A hard page cap guards a server that never terminates; if the cap is hit WITHOUT a clean termination the probe FAILS CLOSED (raises `TransportUnavailableError`) rather than treating the partial key set as authoritative (a partial set could yield a FALSE project-not-visible). No new transport class or subprocess.

Retry vs hard fail: `_direct_rest_get` ALREADY retries transient transport faults itself (acli_rest.py `_rest_urlopen_with_retry`: 3 attempts over TimeoutError/ConnectionError) and raises `HTTPError` deterministically on auth/HTTP errors (401/403). The helper adds NO retry loop of its own (it does NOT reuse the unrelated JQL empty-results consistency loop); it catches `urllib.error.HTTPError` / `URLError` / `TimeoutError` / `ConnectionError` / JSON-decode errors from `_direct_rest_get` and maps them to a distinct `TransportUnavailableError` (fail-closed, own message), separate from `ProjectVisibilityError` (a reachable backend that simply does not list a required key).

Reusable single source of truth: an importable `access_check.py` function `check_mapped_project_visibility(repo_root, *, client=..., query_project=..., ...)` returning a structured `ProjectVisibilityResult` (`status` in {`ok`,`missing`,`transport_unavailable`, `skipped`}), plus an `enforce_*` wrapper that raises. Ticket `9702` (bridge fsck live diagnostic) reuses this exact function — NOT inlined into the reconcile pass.

Backend-neutrality: the WIRING GATES ON THE BACKEND — it reads `rebar.config.load_config().reconciler.backend` and only builds the Cloud `AcliClient` and probes when that key is `"jira"`. Any other backend (e.g. `"jira-datacenter"`, whose pycontribs transport has no `_direct_rest_get`) logs an observable "skipped: backend <key> has no visible-projects probe" and returns without a Cloud client. Defence in depth: the helper returns `status="skipped"` if handed a client lacking a callable `_direct_rest_get`.

Wiring + result classification: wired at `__main__.py` `run_pass_result`, STRICTLY BEFORE `reconcile.reconcile_once` (the only outbound-mutation call), only for mutating passes. Read-only passes are skipped by concrete pre-`reconcile_once` signals: `route == "preview"`, and `target_mode.value in {"dry-run","reconcile-check"}` (`reconcile-check` is already short-circuited in `main()`; `no_write` is computed INSIDE `reconcile_once`, after this point, so it is NOT used here). A preflight failure is CONVERTED INTO a classified `PassResult` (`_Disposition.OPERATIONAL_FAILURE`, exit 1) like the existing `reconcile_once` path — never an uncaught raise, so the `run_pass` / `_lib_ops.py` consumers do not crash. The missing-project message names the offending key(s) + the fix; observable via stderr/log.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A pass with a mapped key not visible to the bot aborts at preflight naming the key
      BEFORE any Jira write — `reconcile.reconcile_once` NOT called; `run_pass_result` returns
      an `OPERATIONAL_FAILURE` `PassResult`. Verified by
      `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_preflight_project_visibility.py -q`.
- [x] `legacy_default` (when non-empty) is in the check; an invisible `legacy_default` is
      caught, naming it. Verified by the same test module.
- [x] When `projects` is empty, the configured `query_project` fallback is included, so an
      invisible fallback is caught. Verified by the same test module.
- [x] An all-visible mapping passes and the pass proceeds unchanged (`reconcile.reconcile_once`
      is called; no happy-path change). Verified by the same test module.
- [x] A hard auth/transport error fails closed with a distinct transport-unavailable message
      and is observable via log/stderr. Verified by the same test module.
- [x] A non-Cloud backend (`config.reconciler.backend != "jira"`) and a client lacking
      `_direct_rest_get` are both skipped (observable) and the pass proceeds without a Cloud
      client. Verified by the same test module.

## Testing
- `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_preflight_project_visibility.py -q` —
  fake/injected transport (no live Jira). Helper: fake client `_direct_rest_get` returns
  `project/search` pages listing `{GOOD}` / `BAD` absent → `enforce_*` raises
  `ProjectVisibilityError` naming `BAD`; all-visible → `status="ok"`; `legacy_default=WRONG`
  caught; empty `projects` + `query_project=FALL` (not visible) caught; `_direct_rest_get`
  raising → `TransportUnavailableError`; no `_direct_rest_get` → `status="skipped"`; multi-page
  `values` all collected. Wiring (`run_pass_result` with stubbed `reconcile_once`): missing →
  NOT called + `OPERATIONAL_FAILURE`; transport-unavailable → NOT called + `OPERATIONAL_FAILURE`;
  all-visible → called once; `route=="preview"`, `target_mode.value=="dry-run"`, and a
  non-`"jira"` backend each skip the probe and proceed. RED first: without the preflight the
  pass proceeds to fan-out on an invisible key.
- No unit test hits live Jira; the real envelope/pagination is unit-tested against the
  documented Jira Cloud shape, live verification deferred to the existing
  `rebar bridge access-check` / staging path (same transport/credentials).
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` from the worktree.

## Sequencing
Lives in `access_check.py` (new importable reusable helper) + wiring at `__main__.py` `run_pass_result`. Disjoint from A/B/C/E files. Reads projects_store (no edit).
baseline.summary: Reconciler preflight: verify every mapped project + legacy_default is visible in target Jira before any mutation

baseline.description:
## Problem
The reconciler multi-project fan-out (story 1734) runs every mapped project's base (active + done-recent) JQL queries in a single flat loop with NO per-project error isolation: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` `_build_snapshot` builds `queries` across all projects and iterates `for jql, cap in queries:` — any single project's transport failure (ACLI 400 unknown-project, 401/403 permission, 404, 429 rate-limit, 5xx, timeout) propagates out and ABORTS THE ENTIRE PASS for all projects. The enrichment loop directly below already fails open per-project (`_enrich_project` "each pass failing open independently so a per-project fault degrades only that project"). The base-query loop never inherited that resilience.

This is the PROVEN root cause of the 2026-08-15 production outage (bug 05b8-4efe-8d58-4c27): a single mapped-but-nonexistent project key (`LEG`) — syntactically valid, so `_validate_project_key` passes — made ACLI exit 1 and took down ~12h of scheduled Reconcile Bridge passes across every project.

## Approach
Extract a `_fetch_project(client, proj, pass_id, repo_root, alert_store)` helper (symmetric to `_enrich_project`) that drains BOTH base queries (active + done-recent) for one project into a LOCAL dict and returns it. `_build_snapshot` calls it inside a per-project try/except and merges the returned dict into the shared `snapshot`/`seen_keys` ONLY on success. This makes the no-partial-merge contract true by construction: a transport failure mid-pagination of the active query, or after the active query merged but the done-recent query fails, discards that project's LOCAL dict entirely — no partial keys ever reach the shared snapshot where the differ would read them as deletions.

On a per-project transport error the boundary emits an observable alert via `alert_store.append({"kind": "fetcher-project-fetch-failed", "project": <key>, "pass_id": pass_id, ...})`, discards the local dict, and CONTINUEs to the other projects. Preserve the existing fail-CLOSED behavior for a syntactically-invalid/absent key: `jql_active`/`jql_done_recent` call `_validate_project_key` OUTSIDE the per-project try (bug 626d intent unchanged) so a bad key still aborts the pass. Preserve the re-raise of `BackendPaginationStallError` (a stalled pager is a truncated whole-project read and must still surface), matching the enrichment loop's exception handling exactly. Keep the dedup (`seen_keys`) and the `fetcher-dedup-suppressed` alert behavior intact — dedup now runs at the atomic merge of each project's local dict.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] One mapped project's base-query transport error does not abort the pass; the other projects' issues still land in the snapshot, and NO partial keys from the failed project are merged. Verified by the new unit `test_one_project_base_query_failure_does_not_abort_pass` in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_fetch_multi_project.py`.
- [x] A per-project base-query fetch failure emits an observable `fetcher-project-fetch-failed` alert naming the project and pass_id. Verified: the new unit asserts a matching record in `bridge_state/bridge_alerts/*.jsonl`.
- [x] The single-project (unseeded store) path remains regression-identical. Verified: the existing `test_single_project_fallback_is_regression_identical` still passes.
- [x] A syntactically-invalid/absent key still fails closed (626d preserved) and a `BackendPaginationStallError` still re-raises. Verified: `_validate_project_key` is still called by `jql_active`/`jql_done_recent` outside the per-project try, and the boundary re-raises `BackendPaginationStallError` exactly as `_enrich_project` does.

## Testing
Add an always-on unit (no live Jira) to `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_fetch_multi_project.py` using a `_FakeClient` whose `search_issues` RAISES for project `BAD` (e.g. an `HTTPError`/ACLI error) but returns issues for `OK`; assert `OK`'s issues land in the snapshot, the pass is not aborted, and the `fetcher-project-fetch-failed` alert fired for `BAD`. This is the always-on regression the incident lacked (closes the P0-3 test gap). Mutation check: reverting the per-project try/except returns the test to RED. Run with `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_fetch_multi_project.py -q`, plus `make lint` and `make typecheck`.

## Sequencing
Edits `fetcher.py` `_build_snapshot` base-query region. Ticket C (non-Done status) also edits `fetcher.py` — C is sequenced AFTER this ticket to avoid conflict.
baseline.summary: Reconciler fan-out: per-project resilience in base-query loop (no whole-pass abort on one bad project)

baseline.description:
## Problem
Running `rebar metrics` with NO `--since/--until` (the default invocation) silently breaks every ticket-derived (agent_process) metric. The CLI defaults the flags to empty strings and passes them into the readers; `metrics.event_metrics._bounds("")` calls `datetime.fromisoformat("")` which raises `ValueError: Invalid isoformat string: ''`. The CLI's per-metric fault isolation catches it and renders each metric as `unavailable` with reason="Invalid isoformat string: ''", so the failure is silent.

## Reproduced (in the rebar repo itself)
`rebar metrics --output json` -> attempts_per_ticket / first_pass_rate / revert_recovery / reopen_recovery / rework_within_7_days all report `{unavailable: {reason: "Invalid isoformat string: ''"}}`. With explicit dates (`--since 2026-01-01 --until 2026-12-31`) they compute correctly (e.g. first_pass_rate -> 0.9984). The git readers guard the empty string (churn returns data); the event/sidecar readers do not — an inconsistency.

## Expected
With no `--since/--until`, default the window to the **last 30 days** (until=today, since=today-30d) rather than passing empty strings. Empty/whitespace date values should normalize to this default (or to `None` open bounds) at the CLI boundary so no reader ever receives an unparseable string.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `rebar metrics` with no date flags returns real values for the agent_process metrics over a last-30-days window (no 'Invalid isoformat' unavailable).
- [ ] Default window documented in `rebar metrics --help`, user-guide, and the help text file.
- [ ] Explicit `--since/--until` still override the default; explicit empty-string values are handled gracefully.
- [ ] Unit/interface test covering the no-flags invocation (regression: currently masked as unavailable).
baseline.summary: rebar metrics with no --since/--until fails ticket-derived metrics; default to last 30 days

baseline.description:
## Problem
The `verify-identity (whole-store authorship gate)` job in `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` fetches the full `tickets` branch (`git fetch --filter=blob:none`) and fails closed if the resulting pack exceeds `REBAR_TICKETS_PACK_LIMIT_KIB` (131072 KiB = 128 MiB). As of 2026-08-04 the tickets pack measures **131830 KiB**, ~758 KiB (0.6%) over the limit, so the gate casts **Verified -1**.

This blocks EVERY Gerrit change (repo-wide), not any one change's code. First observed on change 1385 (ad85), whose own pytest/lint/typecheck jobs all pass.

## Why history cannot be truncated
The gate deliberately mounts FULL tickets history for commit-ancestry era scoping (ADR 0051; the append-only event log is authorship-critical). So the pack only grows monotonically; compaction/truncation is not an option.

## Decision (chosen approach)
REMOVE the pack-size gate entirely (not bump the limit). Deliberate choice: the `REBAR_TICKETS_PACK_LIMIT_KIB` ceiling has repeatedly blocked the normal review workflow since the feature was implemented, for reasons unrelated to the change under review, because the tickets branch is append-only full-history (ADR 0051) and its pack only ever grows — a fixed KiB ceiling is guaranteed to keep tripping and, once tripped, casts Verified -1 on EVERY Gerrit change repo-wide. It cost far more than it protected. Change 1392 removes the env var + the fail-closed step and leaves an in-file NOTE recording the rationale. If tickets-pack growth ever needs bounding, use a real mechanism (server-side gc / history compaction).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] The `REBAR_TICKETS_PACK_LIMIT_KIB` env var and the "Fail closed if the filtered tickets pack exceeds its limit" step are removed from `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`, with an in-file NOTE documenting the deliberate removal.
- [x] A Gerrit change passes the `verify-identity` whole-store gate (Verified +1) without the pack-size check.
baseline.summary: Gerrit Verified gate blocks all changes: tickets pack crossed CI size limit (131830 > 131072 KiB)

Independent observation — apply exit-0 != converged; require zero-diff re-read. This is the original e983 defect done properly.

baseline.description:
## Reproduction Steps

Run `rebar bridge-fsck` — the offline binding-drift arm (epic 3006-e198, the convergence parity oracle) reports a non-empty `binding_drift` section.

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** `binding_drift` is empty (every bound pair converged).
- **Actual:** dangling=1
- **Detected at:** 2026-08-01T03:06:52Z
- **Canary run:** https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/30681164965

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each reported drift is triaged (would_terminal → local archive/delete
      to propagate; dangling → confirmed 404 GC; unbound_jira → adopt or
      archive the Jira-native issue; local_gone → investigate).
- [ ] `rebar bridge-fsck` reports an empty `binding_drift` section.

# Convergence rollout tail: Phase-3 consumer swap + live shadow validation + capped live heal

## Summary
High-risk tail of the baseline convergence rollout (carved from soar-quill-flare / 7d23). This AGENT (with
ACLI access) performs the live validation directly, with GUARANTEED cleanup of test artifacts in both live Jira
and the local store. `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` runs `rebar reconcile --mode live` every ~20 min.

## Already landed (7d23, on main)
- Phase-1 baseline dual-write SHADOW (`baseline_shadow.py`) behind `reconciler.baseline_dual_write`, with per-pass
  `baseline_shadow_check` logging + `baseline_shadow_divergence` alert.
- Circuit breaker (`check_blast_radius`, default 0.10) before the first acting mutation.

## Key facts established (code-verified — the plan is built on these)
- **The swap is namespace-COMPATIBLE.** In `_diff_fields`, `field_name` iterates `local_mapped` (output of
  `_map_local_to_jira_fields`), which emits **JIRA** names (`"summary"`, `outbound_fields.py:138,371-378`).
  `prev_snapshot[jira_key]` is JIRA-keyed (`_snapshot_schema.py:135`), and `BindingStore.get_baseline` returns the
  same JIRA-keyed shape (`_BASELINE_FIELDS = ("summary","description","priority","status","assignee")`,
  `binding_store.py:46-54`). So feeding `get_baseline(local_id)` where `prev_jira_fields` is read today is
  shape-for-shape compatible — no field-name translation is required for the swap.
- **`_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS` (`{"title",...}`, LOCAL names) is a pre-existing partial no-op**, NOT part of this
  swap. The guard `if field_name in _INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS` (outbound_fields.py:405) never fires for the
  title/summary field (`"summary" ∉ {"title",...}`); it only fires for the four coinciding names
  (description/priority/status/assignee). This asymmetry is UNCHANGED by the swap. Document it; do NOT silently
  "fix" `"title"→"summary"` as part of the swap (that changes behavior and is out of scope).
- **`get_baseline` cannot signal "corrupt".** It returns `None` for BOTH absent and non-dict baseline
  (binding_store.py:314-318), and `None` is documented-VALID = "no ancestor → local-wins" (ADR 0026 §2). A corrupt
  `bindings.json` (the baseline lives inside it as `entry["baseline"]`) fails **CLOSED at LOAD**: `BindingStore._load`
  raises `ValueError` (binding_store.py:103-124) at pass start, before any `get_baseline`. So the fail-closed
  invariant is preserved by the existing load guard — the consumer swap needs NO new corrupt-detection branch.
- **`classify()` is NOT wired into the field-differ path for active bindings.** `binding_walk` skips active
  bindings (`binding_walk.py:169-170` "handled by the field differ") and only runs `classify()` on OFF-snapshot
  pairs. So there is NO production code path where both `classify()`'s decision and the field-differ's action exist
  for the SAME active binding — comparing them there would require a parallel engine (explicitly forbidden).
- **`decision_census` is documented-but-never-emitted.** Only `binding_walk_census` is logged
  (`run_differs.py:652`); `decision_census` appears only in a docstring (`classify.py:351`) with no `.log()` call.
  So there is no live expand-contract yet — the census task STARTS emitting `decision_census`.

## Remaining CODE
1. **Add the flag.** New `baseline_consumer_swap: bool = False` in `ReconcilerConfig` in the TOP-LEVEL
   `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` (NOT under `rebar_reconciler/` — that path does not exist; it is where
   `baseline_dual_write` already lives, ~line 355). **TWO edits, both required** (mirror `baseline_dual_write`
   exactly): (a) the dataclass field `baseline_consumer_swap: bool = False` after line 355, AND (b) the coercer
   entry `"baseline_consumer_swap": lambda v, k: _as_bool(v, k),` in `_SECTIONS["reconciler"]` (~line 464) — without
   (b) the TOML key is silently dropped at parse. Read it ONCE at the orchestration layer
   (mirror `reconcile.py:936`'s `bool(_load_config().reconciler.baseline_dual_write)`) and thread the bool down,
   not per-field `_load_config()`. Document the flag + flip procedure in `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`.
2. **Phase-3 consumer swap (two call-sites, both in `outbound_fields._diff_fields`).**
   - Site A — direction-suppression: `outbound_fields.py:405-407` (`_local_matches_prev(field_name, local_val,
     prev_jira_fields or {})`).
   - Site B — conflict-sink: `outbound_fields.py:519-526` (`_local_matches_prev(fname, local_mapped.get(fname),
     prev_jira_fields)`).
   Plumbing: thread `local_id` (already in scope at `outbound_differ.py:622`) into the `_diff_fields` call
   (`outbound_differ.py:699-708`) plus the `baseline_consumer_swap` bool. `_diff_fields` already receives
   `binding_store`. When the flag is ON, compute `baseline = binding_store.get_baseline(local_id)` once and pass it
   (JIRA-keyed, same shape) wherever `prev_jira_fields` is used by the two `_local_matches_prev` calls; when OFF,
   behavior is byte-for-byte the current `prev_snapshot` path. `None` baseline → the EXISTING absent branch
   (`_local_matches_prev` returns False → local-wins). Corrupt-store fail-closed is inherited from load time (above);
   no new consumer branch.
3. **RED-first direction-preservation property test.** With the flag ON (swapped consumer), assert that for each of
   the five mirrored fields, when local == baseline the outbound diff SUPPRESSES the field (inbound-wins), and when
   local != baseline it emits the mutation — matching `direction_is_inbound` (`classify.py:258-273`). RED before the
   swap wiring, GREEN after. Include the title/summary asymmetry as an explicit documented case (title is not
   suppressed today — the test pins that unchanged behavior, it is not a regression).
4. **Census expand-contract.** Emit `decision_census` (the documented-but-missing key) from the same `census(...)`
   record currently shipped under `binding_walk_census` (`run_differs.py:652`); migrate any consumer to
   `decision_census`; then DROP `binding_walk_census`. Rollback path for the drop: re-add the `binding_walk_census`
   emit (one line) — documented in the commit.
5. **Divergence signal = the EXISTING `baseline_shadow_check` (no new classifier-vs-legacy alert).** The
   code-verified reality: there is NO production path where a `classify()` decision and a competing "legacy" action
   coexist for the same binding — `binding_walk` runs `classify()` only on OFF-snapshot pairs (no legacy there),
   and the field-differ owns ACTIVE bindings (no `classify()` there). Building a per-binding classifier-vs-legacy
   comparison would require a parallel engine, which this ticket explicitly forbids. Therefore the rollout's
   divergence gate is the ALREADY-LANDED `baseline_shadow_check` / `baseline_shadow_divergence` (baseline_shadow.py:
   91-95), which compares the dual-write baseline against `prev_snapshot` arbitration for active bindings — exactly
   the swap being validated. This item is a DOCUMENTATION step: record in `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` that
   `baseline_shadow_check` is the divergence gate and why a separate classifier-vs-legacy alert is not built (no
   legacy engine). No new alert code.

## Remaining OPERATIONAL (agent-run with ACLI; guaranteed cleanup) — wall-clock-bound
- **≥10 CONSECUTIVE clean shadow passes** (`baseline_shadow_check` divergent==0) BEFORE flipping the flag.
  **Streak source (design gap resolved, NO code):** `bridge_state/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:10`), so the
  `sync-log-*.jsonl` SyncLogger output is EPHEMERAL — torn down with the GHA runner. But the reconcile-bridge run
  already prints `baseline_shadow_check` (and `baseline_shadow_divergence`) to stdout, which GitHub Actions captures
  durably in each run's logs. Derive the streak OPERATIONALLY (no new persistence code, no workflow edit) by
  querying the last N reconcile-bridge runs and reading their emitted divergent counts:
  `gh run list --workflow=reconcile-bridge.yml --limit N --json databaseId,createdAt,conclusion` then
  `gh run view <id> --log | grep baseline_shadow_check`. A run with divergent>0, a failed/absent run, or a gap
  > 2× the schedule interval RESETS the streak. This keeps the streak recomputable by any agent from durable GHA
  history without touching the workflow or the gitignored sync-log. COORDINATION: A3's live remediation pauses the
  reconciler and RESETS this streak — A3's live pass already ran this session, so the streak starts fresh AFTER it;
  do not run another A3 pass during the window.
- **Capped live heal** under bootstrap-strict incl. the GC-after-grace deletion (f8b5-2f30 → REB-530). PRE-HEAL
  BACKUP covers BOTH sides: export affected Jira issue state (JSON via Jira API) AND tag the tickets branch
  (`git tag pre-heal-<date>`); if either backup fails, ABORT the heal. Store artifacts in the workflow run
  artifacts (retention documented).
- **Flip the flag only after BOTH gates.** Rollback rehearsed: (a) revert the flag to false and confirm the
  reconciler reverts to `prev_snapshot` arbitration with no divergence, AND (b) force one `--mode dry-run` pass
  confirming zero mutations; record both workflow run-ids.

## Scope (files EDITED)
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — add `baseline_consumer_swap` (top-level rebar config, beside `baseline_dual_write`)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` — add `baseline_consumer_swap: bool = False` to the `OutboundDiffConfig` dataclass (outbound_differ.py:242-273 — the sole config conduit to `_diff_fields`); thread `local_id` + the flag into `_diff_fields`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_fields.py` — `_diff_fields` reads `get_baseline` behind the flag
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/run_differs.py` — census expand-contract; scoped divergence alert
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py` — read `baseline_consumer_swap` ONCE at the orchestration layer (mirror :936's `baseline_dual_write` read) and thread the bool down
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/baseline_shadow.py` — emit the `RECON: baseline_shadow_check` diagnostic line (Round-5 decision)
- `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` — flag + flip/rollback procedure
- new test file under `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — RED-first direction-preservation property test

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] [CODE] `reconciler.baseline_consumer_swap` flag added (distinct from `baseline_dual_write`) as BOTH the
      dataclass field AND the `_SECTIONS["reconciler"]` coercer entry, + documented in `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`.
      Proof: a config-parse test asserts default False AND that a TOML `baseline_consumer_swap = true` round-trips
      (proving the coercer entry exists, not silently dropped).
- [ ] [CODE] Both `_local_matches_prev` call-sites (outbound_fields.py:405, :519) read `get_baseline(local_id)`
      behind the flag; flag OFF is byte-for-byte the `prev_snapshot` path; `None` baseline → local-wins; corrupt
      `bindings.json` still fails closed at load (existing `_load` guard — a test asserts a corrupt store aborts the
      pass). Proof: named property/unit tests.
- [ ] [CODE] RED-first direction-preservation property test over the five mapped fields: RED (fails) before the
      swap wiring, GREEN after; the title/summary asymmetry is pinned as an explicit case.
- [ ] [CODE] Census emits `decision_census`; consumers migrated; `binding_walk_census` dropped WITH a documented
      one-line rollback. Proof: a test asserts `decision_census` is emitted and `binding_walk_census` is not.
- [ ] [CODE/DOC] No new classifier-vs-legacy alert is built (no production path has both a `classify()` decision
      and a legacy action for the same binding without a parallel engine). `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` documents that
      the EXISTING `baseline_shadow_check` is the rollout divergence gate and why. Proof: a doc-grep AC —
      `grep -q "baseline_shadow_check" docs/jira-sync-setup.md`.
- [ ] [OPERATIONAL] ≥10 consecutive clean shadow passes, with the streak derived from GHA reconcile-bridge run
      logs (`gh run view <id> --log | grep baseline_shadow_check`; reset on divergent>0 / failed run / >2×-cadence
      gap — no new persistence code), not overlapping A3's live pass; evidence (run-ids + divergent counts)
      recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] [OPERATIONAL] Capped live heal with a bilateral pre-heal backup (Jira JSON + tickets-branch tag); heal aborts
      if either backup fails; artifacts stored + linked.
- [ ] [OPERATIONAL] Flip only after both gates (>=10 clean shadow passes + clean flag-ON live pass).

## Round-5 resolved decision (2026-07-09, epic adept-hedge-stain continuation)

**Streak-source gap CLOSED with a small CODE emission (not merely an ops procedure).**
Code-verified: `baseline_shadow_check` is emitted ONLY via `sync_logger.log` (baseline_shadow.py:92),
which writes the gitignored `bridge_state/sync-log-*.jsonl` — it NEVER reaches stdout, so the OPERATIONAL
streak AC's `gh run view <id> --log | grep baseline_shadow_check` would find nothing. Resolution:
`baseline_shadow.py` additionally prints a `RECON: baseline_shadow_check divergent=<N> equal=<M>` line to
**stderr** (`file=sys.stderr`, flush=True) — matching the VERIFIED existing `RECON:` convention (applier.py:488,799
all use `file=sys.stderr`); `gh run view <id> --log` captures stderr too — so the
reconcile-bridge GHA captures the divergent count durably in each run's logs and the >=10-clean-pass streak
is derivable via `gh run view --log`. This adds `baseline_shadow.py` to the edited-files set. It is the ONLY
new persistence-adjacent mechanism (no workflow edit, no store write, no gitignored file relied on).

## Acceptance Criteria (round-5 addition)

- [ ] [CODE] `baseline_shadow.py` prints a `RECON: baseline_shadow_check divergent=<N> equal=<M>` line to
      **stderr** (`file=sys.stderr`, flush=True) whenever the shadow check runs — matching the VERIFIED `RECON:` convention — so the
      operational >=10-clean-pass streak is derivable from GHA reconcile-bridge run logs (making the existing
      `gh run view --log | grep baseline_shadow_check` OPERATIONAL AC achievable). Proof: a unit test captures
      stderr and asserts the `RECON: baseline_shadow_check divergent=` line is printed with the correct count.


## Round-5 clarifications (review round-1 remediation)

- **BLOCK-4 (Site B full guard swap).** At `outbound_fields.py:519` the outer guard is
  `if conflict_sink is not None and prev_jira_fields and jira_key:` — `prev_jira_fields` is used as a

  conflict-sink), which is the correct local-wins behavior (no ancestor → no conflict to record).

`baseline_consumer_swap: bool = False` so the default is off end-to-end.

## Summary
tests/integration/test_store_concurrency.py::test_concurrent_writer_storm_no_loss (integration tier, run under pytest-xdist -n4 on GitHub-hosted runners) intermittently fails when its 8 concurrent subprocess writers race the git object/tree build on the shared store. Two distinct symptoms observed, same root class:
- 'git commit failed while holding lock: error: invalid object 100644 <sha> for "<ticket>/...-COMMENT.json" ... error: Error building trees' (run 29300833741, main f542/560180461, ubuntu py3.12, 2026-07-14)
- 'git commit failed while holding lock: fatal: could not parse HEAD' (run 29296542560, main 5348d2adf, integration tier, 2026-07-13)

## Reproduction Steps
1. Run the integration tier under load: pytest -m integration -n 4 (as CI does) on a loaded runner.
2. Intermittently: all 8 writers in test_concurrent_writer_storm_no_loss fail with a git tree-build/HEAD-parse error while holding the store lock.
Expected: concurrent writers serialize cleanly (the test asserts no writer failures + no lost events). Actual: under contention a writer builds a tree referencing a blob object not yet durable / reads an unborn-or-mid-update HEAD, and git aborts with 'invalid object ... Error building trees' or 'could not parse HEAD'. Passes 5/5 locally on an unloaded machine — load-dependent.

## Notes
Not introduced by recent changes (observed on both 5348d2adf and f542). Distinct from the b228 timing flake and the 85c3 harness/acli flakes. Likely a git object-write vs tree-build ordering race in the store write path under the lock (concurrent processes sharing one git dir).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] test_concurrent_writer_storm_no_loss no longer fails under CI-load parallelism (the git tree-build/HEAD race is closed — e.g. ensure blobs are durably written before tree-build, or serialize the object-write+commit under the lock, or retry on the transient object/ref error).
- [ ] It still asserts no lost events under a concurrent writer storm.
- [ ] Regression coverage runs in the gerrit-verify Verified gate (integration tier).
baseline.summary: Flaky integration test test_concurrent_writer_storm_no_loss — concurrent git tree-build race under CI load

# P1.4 — rebar gc + maintenance doctrine (bounded growth, recovery-safe)

## Context (problem + research)

Every mutation is a committed file, and the write path sets `gc.auto=0` (`_store/event_append.py:64 _ensure_gc_auto_zero`) so a background `git gc` can't prune the reflog commits the reset-recovery net relies on (now in `rebar._store.sync:54-77`, `reset --hard origin/tickets` for unrelated/diverged histories, "recoverable via reflog"). The cost is **unbounded** loose-object/pack growth on long-lived `tickets` branches. git-bug packs ops into fewer objects with a cache; Fossil's SQLite sidesteps small-object blowup. rebar sells "built to scale" but ships no safe reclaim path. Akka's distributed-data pruning teaches the discipline: gate discard on dissemination + a TTL marker, never wall-clock alone.

## Evidence (experiments)

- EXP6: a discarded commit **survives** `git gc --prune=14.days.ago` but is
  **destroyed** by `--prune=now` -> a conservative window is mandatory.
- EXP-R6 (real code): the gc recipe on the **real `.tickets-tracker` orphan-branch
  worktree** packed 26 -> 0 loose objects and `rebar show` still read correctly.

## What / Implementation detail

Operator-only `rebar gc` (**not** over MCP, like `init`), under the write lock (I5) and only when not mid-recovery (reuse `rebar._store.lock.check_no_rebase_in_progress` — no leading underscore):
1. `git -C <tracker> reflog expire --expire=<window> --expire-unreachable=<window> --all`
   (BOTH flags — EXP6: unreachable objects are governed by `--expire-unreachable`/
   `--prune`).
2. `git -C <tracker> gc --prune=<window>.ago` (**never `--prune=now`**); conservative
   default `gc.reflog_window` = 14 days that must exceed the worst-case offline/
   un-pushed interval.
3. Report bytes reclaimed. A `--compact-first` flag runs per-ticket `compact`
   over eligible tickets first (I1/I9-safe: SNAPSHOT folds, `*.retired` renames
   union). Document the "compact then gc" cadence in `docs/concurrency.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] operator-only `rebar gc` (reflog expire --expire+--expire-unreachable, gc --prune=<window>.ago, never now)
- [ ] `--compact-first` runs per-ticket compaction before packing
- [ ] mid-recovery guard via `check_no_rebase_in_progress`; not exposed over MCP
- [ ] gc-then-recover regression test + bytes-reclaimed sanity on a synthetic many-event ticket
- [ ] `docs/concurrency.md` documents the compact-then-gc cadence and window rationale

See `docs/remediation-implementation-plan.md` (P1.4).
- [ ] `rebar gc` reclaims space and reports it; reads work afterward.
- [ ] A `gc`-then-recover regression proves `_store.sync` recovery still works after gc
- [ ] Refuses to run mid-recovery; absent from the MCP surface.
baseline.summary: P1.4 — rebar gc + maintenance doctrine (bounded growth, recovery-safe)

## What

Epic completion-verification (`verify_completion` behind the close gate) is **count-dependent and unreliable for the child-closure check**. Closing an epic with 8 closed+signed children either **exhausts the LLM step budget** (`recursion_limit=120`) or returns a **false negative** that it "cannot confirm" some children exist — because it tries to find children by searching the *codebase for their aliases* instead of enumerating the epic's children deterministically.

The child-closure check should be a **minimal, deterministic, count-independent** operation: list the epic's children via the `parent_id` hierarchy and confirm each is `closed` with a valid completion signature. The number of children should be irrelevant to whether verification can run.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Create an epic with N children; implement + close each child (each gets an
   HMAC completion signature under the close gate).
2. `rebar transition <epic> in_progress closed` (gate on; `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM=1`).

**Expected:** the gate confirms each child has a signed close (a cheap hierarchy + signature lookup), verifies the epic's OWN criteria, and signs — in time roughly independent of child count.

**Actual (epic e59d-0ae4-e3c8-45e8, 8 children):**
- First attempt: `agent exceeded its step budget (recursion_limit=120)` → gate
  could-not-run → fail-closed → blocked.
- With `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=400`: ran, but FAILED "Acceptance Criterion #1" stating it
  "cannot be confirmed via show_ticket that [five] tickets exist as children" — it only
  found the 3 children whose aliases happen to appear in the codebase, and "the ticket
  store directory is hidden from listing." All 8 children DO have `parent_id` = the epic
  and `status=closed` with `signature` present (verified directly), so this is a false
  negative.

## Likely cause

The verifier prompt/toolset has no deterministic "list this epic's children + their close-signature status" capability, so the agent improvises (searches code for aliases, attempts `show_ticket` on guessed ids) — which is both expensive (drives the step-budget blowup) and incomplete (misses children not referenced in code). The intended design ("epic verification = own criteria + child-closure **trust**", commit 7b09ab5f) needs a concrete child-enumeration input/tool to realize the "trust" half.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Epic completion-verification enumerates children via the `parent_id` hierarchy
  (e.g. a `list_tickets(parent=…)` / children query or a precomputed child-closure
  summary injected into the verifier) rather than searching the codebase for aliases.
- [ ] For each child it checks `status == closed` AND a valid completion signature, and
  reports any child lacking one — a deterministic check whose cost does not scale with
  re-reading each child's full body.
- [ ] An epic with many (e.g. ≥8) closed+signed children verifies without exceeding the
  default LLM step budget.
- [ ] A regression test: an epic with all children closed+signed PASSES; an epic with a
  child that is open or closed-without-signature FAILS, citing that child.
</content>
baseline.summary: epic completion-verification is count-dependent: child-closure check should be a minimal deterministic hierarchy+signature lookup

## Why

`src/rebar/_store/push.py` async mode spawns a detached child (`start_new_session=True`, `close_fds=True`, streams to `DEVNULL`, reconstructed `PYTHONPATH`) whose whole purpose is to finish the push AFTER the calling process exits. The current E2E (`tests/interfaces/store/test_push_policy_e2e.py`) writes in-process and polls origin while the parent stays alive — proving "lands in background," not "survives parent exit." Spawn-failure logging and generic `PUSH_PENDING` surfacing are already covered elsewhere, so only the parent-exit survival contract is untested.

## What

- Add a forced-order test proving the detached push completes after the spawning CLI
  process has exited.
- Order the interaction with a controlled `git` wrapper on `PATH` that blocks at
  `git push` behind a release file, so the parent provably exits before the child's
  push completes.

## Scope

- `tests/interfaces/store/` (new parent-exit survival test)
- A test fixture `git` shim (passes non-push commands through; blocks on push).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `git` shim on `PATH` passes non-push commands through and, on `git push`, writes
      an "entered push" marker and blocks on a release file/pipe.
- [ ] Launch `rebar create` with async push in a subprocess; wait for the "entered push"
      marker; assert the CLI parent has EXITED while the push child is still blocked.
- [ ] Release the push; poll the bare origin and assert the exact created event/commit
