The completion-verification close gate's escape hatch `--force-close="<reason>"` is reachable from the CLI but NOT from the Python library API: `rebar.transition(...)` (`src/rebar/__init__.py:125`, the `def` line) exposes only `force`, not `force_close`. A programmatic client that hits the close gate with LLM deps absent therefore has no in-library bypass and must shell out to the CLI — a real client-facing reliability/UX gap.

## Why
Library, CLI, and MCP are meant to be behaviorally at parity over one store (`tests/interfaces/facades/test_parity.py`). The close-gate bypass is an asymmetry that breaks that contract for library consumers.

## What / files (verified against current code)
The command layer ALREADY implements `force_close` end-to-end — `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py` `_parse_flags` extracts `--force-close` (lines 107/131/136), and `transition_compute(..., force_close: str = "")` (lines 185/316) honors it on the close path (lines 214/463-470: a forced close skips BOTH the completion verifier and signing, leaving `signature: null`). The CLI already maps `--force-close` here. So the ONLY missing wiring is the library wrapper:
- `src/rebar/__init__.py` — add a `force_close: str | None = None` parameter to the `transition()` wrapper and thread it into the existing `_commands` call (the same call that already passes `force`). Map `None`→`""` to match the command-layer default. Do NOT duplicate or re-implement any gate logic; just pass the value through to the seam that already honors it. Positive rationale: the command layer is the single source of truth for the bypass; the wrapper's only job is to expose the existing parameter so library consumers reach the same seam as the CLI.

## Parity test
- The shared `Adapter` protocol (`tests/interfaces/adapters.py:76`) declares `transition(self, tid, current, target)` with no `force_close`, and `LibraryAdapter`/`CliAdapter`/`McpAdapter` mirror it. Add a FOCUSED parity test (not a change to the generic protocol's existing call sites) that drives a force-close through BOTH the library (`rebar.transition(id, "in_progress", "closed", force_close="reason")`) and the CLI (`rebar transition id in_progress closed --force-close=reason`) under `require_completion_verification_for_close=true`, and asserts identical outcome: ticket reaches `closed` AND `signature is None` (the closed-without-signature signal) in both. Keep `tests/interfaces/facades/test_parity.py` untouched if extending it is invasive — a new focused test module is acceptable.
- Proving command: `pytest <the new parity test> -q` (named in the verify commands).

## Scope
In: library `transition(force_close=...)` parity + the focused parity test. Out: changing gate semantics, the CLI surface (already correct), the command-layer `transition.py` (already honors `force_close`), and MCP. Non-happy-path input validation is out — mirror the CLI exactly (a non-empty reason string is required by the CLI's `--force-close=`; the library passes the string through unchanged).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar.transition(id, "in_progress", "closed", force_close="reason")` closes a ticket under `require_completion_verification_for_close=true` WITHOUT running the verifier, mirroring the CLI (the command layer already honors it; only the wrapper param is added).
- [ ] The forced close records the same closed-without-signature signal as the CLI path (`signature: null`).
- [ ] A focused parity test asserts CLI and library force-close behave identically (closed + `signature is None`); it is the named proving command (`pytest …`).
- [ ] No change to the non-forced close path; the existing `test_parity.py` parity suite still passes unchanged.
- [ ] `make check` passes.
baseline.summary: Library/CLI parity: add force_close to rebar.transition

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

A plan-review finding, once surfaced, can replay verbatim on every later review of the same ticket even after the plan is edited to fully address it, so the revise-review loop never converges and each round costs a full LLM review. Confirmed on epic `0e68-41eb-5782-4336`, where one G6 finding blocked five consecutive rounds. The root cause is recorded in full on this ticket's first comment; the load-bearing evidence is summarised below.

## Approach

`sidecar.prior_concerns` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py`) selects prior findings for re-surfacing on `decision in {"block","advisory"}` and `priority >= RECALL_MIN_PRIORITY` alone. `pass1.run_pass1` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py`, the "Recall" block after the ISF pass) then injects each one with a hardcoded `"evidence": []` and `"impact": ""`. Because `sidecar.build_payload._slim` persists an explicit allow-list that does not include the `_recall` marker, a re-surfaced finding is re-verified, re-decided `block`, and re-persisted indistinguishably from a fresh one — so it re-qualifies for recall every round. Recall was built as a one-shot backstop for a finder that MISSED a finding on identical material (`sidecar.py`, the recall section comment) and instead behaves as a permanent ratchet.

The designed Pass-2 backstop does not fire because the injected candidate carries no grounding: `review_kernel/verify.finding_listing` renders `evidence:` as an empty string, so `evidence_entails_finding` has nothing to test, and the absence veto in `review_kernel/decide.py` (`claims_absence == "yes"` AND `absence_confirmed_in_context == "no"`) never fires because the verifier confirms the bare restatement instead of searching the current plan for the refuting provision. Verified on the epic's final sidecar: the blocking finding recorded `claims_absence: "yes"`, `absence_confirmed_in_context: "yes"`, `evidence: []`, while `orchestrator.assemble_context(...).plan_text` (7568 chars, in the verifier's context via `prompts.shared_plan_prefix`) contains the refuting provision verbatim.

The fix keeps all three changes inside the recall eligibility/injection path so fresh-finding verification is untouched:

1. `prior_concerns` carries the prior finding's persisted `evidence` (and `impact`) into the
   concern, and `run_pass1` injects them instead of blanking them. v2 sidecars already persist
   `evidence` losslessly (`build_payload._slim`); `prior_concerns` simply never read it. This
   is the re-grounding: Pass-2 now judges the original quotes against the CURRENT plan text
   rather than rubber-stamping an assertion with nothing behind it.
2. A prior finding with no persisted grounding evidence is INELIGIBLE for recall — there is
   nothing to re-ground it with. That set is exactly the previous recall injections, so this
   breaks the ratchet, and it works against already-written sidecars with no migration.
3. Recall is suppressed wholesale when the prior sidecar's `material_fingerprint` differs from
   `attest.current_material_fingerprint(ticket_id, repo_root=...)`. On CHANGED material the
   fresh finder's silence is evidence the edit resolved the finding, not a miss — which is
   recall's own stated contract. Both fingerprints must be present for the comparison to
   apply; a missing one leaves recall enabled (best-effort, as today).

Why this shape rather than a new LLM re-grounding sub-call: the sidecars already record every signal needed (`evidence`, `material_fingerprint`), so the gap closes deterministically at zero additional token cost and stays unit-testable without a model. A genuinely unaddressed gap still blocks, because the fresh Pass-1 finder re-emits it with real evidence on the changed plan (observed on the epic: the finding was found fresh with 3 evidence items while it was genuinely unaddressed, and only went evidence-empty once the plan was fixed).

`build_payload._slim` additionally persists a `recalled` boolean so the ratchet is visible in offline calibration, and `run_pass1` records the suppression reason in `coverage`.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py` — `prior_concerns`: carry `evidence`/`impact`,
  exclude evidence-less priors, add the material-fingerprint suppression; `build_payload._slim`:
  persist `recalled`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` — the recall block: inject the carried
  `evidence`/`impact`; record the suppression/eligibility counts in `coverage`.
- `tests/unit/test_pass1_recall.py` — the regression test for the replay scenario, plus fixture
  updates for the tightened eligibility contract.

No change to `review_kernel/verify.py`, `review_kernel/decide.py`, the verifier prompts, or any fresh-finding path. The completion-verifier work on tickets `1656` and `1700` is on a different path (`completion_subcall.py` / `completion_sidecar.py`) and is not touched.

## Testing

- Happy path: a prior `block` finding WITH evidence, on UNCHANGED material, is still recalled
  and now carries its evidence and impact into the injected candidate.
- The replay regression: a prior `block` finding with `evidence: []` (the signature a previous
  recall injection leaves) is NOT recalled, so a second review cannot replay it.
- Changed material: a fully eligible prior finding is NOT recalled when the sidecar's
  `material_fingerprint` differs from the current one, and IS recalled when they match.
- Edge/degrade: a sidecar missing `material_fingerprint`, and an `attest` lookup that raises,
  both leave recall enabled rather than failing the review (the existing best-effort posture,
  covered by the existing `test_prior_concerns_best_effort_on_reader_error`).
- Unaffected: `test_finder_never_receives_prior_findings` and
  `test_recalled_candidate_dropped_by_pass2_when_resolved` continue to pass unchanged, pinning
  that Pass-1 independence and the Pass-2 validity backstop are not weakened.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The root cause is recorded as a comment on this ticket naming where recall reinjects

# Guard the provider session: wrap run() in `with ProviderSession(...)`

ADR 0056 decision 2. A CORRECTNESS fix, not a refactor — independently valuable, and it should land even if the rest of the decomposition is descoped.

## The defect (RE-MEASURED at c1fc3cee4, after e6bd and 8229 landed)

    runner.py:294   provider_session = ProviderSession(cfg)   # its builders open httpx clients
    runner.py:445   try:                                       # <-- guard starts 151 lines later
    runner.py:495   finally:
    runner.py:501       provider_session.close()

Lines 294–444 sit OUTSIDE the guard, and code in that window raises BY DESIGN: `_check_tool_capability(...)` is called at runner.py:337 and raises `LLMConfigError`. Anything raising there leaks an opened `httpx.AsyncClient` — one per affected call.

`ProviderSession.__enter__` / `__exit__` ALREADY EXIST at **providers.py:323 and :326** and are never used: `grep -c 'with ProviderSession' src/rebar/llm/runner.py` returns 0. Meanwhile providers.py:18–24 documents "`runner.run()` wraps its body in `with ProviderSession(cfg) as session:`" — a caller that does not exist. This ticket makes that docstring true.

NOTE ON COORDINATES: an earlier version of this plan cited 301/474/582 for the three sites and providers.py:295–299 for the dunders. Those were correct when written and are now ALL STALE — e6bd removed the except spine and 8229 removed the settings block, shifting everything. The numbers above are re-measured at c1fc3cee4. **Re-locate by CONTENT, not by these offsets** if the base moves again.

## Approach

Move construction into a `with` covering provider resolution through the call and teardown, and drop the now-redundant `finally: provider_session.close()` — `__exit__` owns it. Preserve the existing best-effort semantics (close logs, never raises).

CONSTRAINT: `assert_gated("agentic filesystem tools")` at **runner.py:261** is a FAIL-CLOSED security check and MUST stay AHEAD of provider construction. Do not reorder it into the guarded region in a way that opens a client before the refusal path runs.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — the `with`, and removal of the redundant `finally`.
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py` — **REQUIRED, and this ticket owns it.**
  See below; omitting it breaks that test at runtime.
- `tests/unit/` — the leak test.

### THIS TICKET OWNS ONE STUB REPAIR — it is not optional and not a "later child" problem

`tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py:111` defines `_NoBuildProviderSession` and installs it at :124 via `monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, "ProviderSession", _NoBuildProviderSession)`. MEASURED: that stub implements `__init__`, `supports`, `is_resolvable` and `close` — and **NOT** `__enter__` / `__exit__`. The moment `run()` says `with ProviderSession(cfg) as ...`, the stub stops satisfying the context-manager protocol and that test fails at runtime.

**Add `__enter__` (returning `self`) and `__exit__` (calling `self.close()`) to that stub IN THE SAME COMMIT as the `with`.** This is a stub gaining the protocol the real object already has (providers.py:323/326) — NOT a weakened assertion, so it is compatible with the "no test ASSERTION changed" criterion.

This is a DIFFERENT failure mode from the six `monkeypatch.setattr` rebind hazards the parent story documents: nothing moved modules here, so re-importing a name fixes nothing. The stub's INTERFACE fell behind the call site. Do not go looking for a module-globals explanation.

## Testing

Unit tier with a stubbed builder recording opens/closes; no network.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a test asserts that when the pre-call window raises (e.g. `_check_tool_capability`), the
      session's client is STILL closed — this test FAILS against today's code, so it cannot pass
      vacuously
- [ ] a test asserts the happy path closes EXACTLY once (a `with` plus a leftover `finally` would
      double-close, which the stub must be able to detect)
- [ ] `grep -c 'with ProviderSession' src/rebar/llm/runner.py` is 1, so providers.py:18–24 no longer
      documents an absent caller
- [ ] a close that raises is still logged and never propagated (best-effort semantics unchanged)
- [ ] `_NoBuildProviderSession` in `tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py` gains
      `__enter__`/`__exit__` in THIS commit, and that test file passes
- [ ] `assert_gated("agentic filesystem tools")` still executes BEFORE any provider client is
      constructed — asserted by a test in which the gate refuses and NO client is opened, so the
      fail-closed ordering is proven rather than assumed
- [ ] the full suite passes with no test ASSERTION weakened, skipped or deleted
baseline.summary: Guard the provider session with a context manager in run()

## Context
115b/8c4f reconciled 13 benign fsck ORPHAN_EVENTs caused by a distributed write race: the Jira reconciler (env_id=reconciler) writes an assignee EDIT, a compaction in a DIFFERENT clone snapshots 3.7s-147s later without having observed that EDIT (so source_event_uuids omits it), then the reconciler re-emits an identical EDIT after the snapshot. fsck flags the pre-snapshot EDIT as orphaned. Live state is always correct (the post-snapshot duplicate drives it), so these are benign — but they recur and require manual retire-to-zero each time.

## Idea
A durable fix so the race stops generating orphans, e.g.: (a) compaction refuses to snapshot within N seconds of an unobserved remote write / syncs+refetches immediately before snapshotting; or (b) the reconciler's idempotent re-emit is suppressed when the value is unchanged; or (c) fsck learns to treat a pre-snapshot EDIT whose effect is superseded by an identical post-snapshot EDIT as non-orphan. Evaluate tradeoffs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root cause reproduced in a test (concurrent compaction + reconciler EDIT).
- [ ] A chosen mitigation implemented so the race no longer produces ORPHAN_EVENTs.
- [ ] Regression test pins that the previously-orphaning sequence now fscks clean.
baseline.summary: Durable fix: compaction-vs-reconciler snapshot write race produces benign fsck ORPHAN_EVENTs

# A stranded local refs/reconciler/lock wedges every local reconcile pass permanently

## Context / Problem

Local `rebar reconcile` repeatedly fails with `reconcile: refs/reconciler/lock held by a live pass — yielding` (exit 3) even when the authoritative remote holds no lock and no holder process exists anywhere. Recovery required a manual `git update-ref -d refs/reconciler/lock`, and the condition kept recurring.

Proven mechanism, reproduced end-to-end in a clean sandbox (real bare remote + working clone, real `_ref_lock` primitives, no mocks):

1. The GitHub Actions bridge acquires the lock on the remote (it holds/heartbeats it near-continuously: `git ls-remote origin refs/reconciler/lock` returns a DIFFERENT oid on successive samples).
2. Any local pass calls `read(..., remote="origin")`. `_fetch_ref` (`_ref_lock.py:288-293`) runs `git fetch origin +<ref>:<ref>`, which PLANTS a local copy of the bridge's lock.
3. The bridge releases. `release` in remote mode (`_ref_lock.py:381-406`) pushes a delete to the REMOTE ONLY and never touches the local ref, so the local copy is STRANDED: remote free, local still held.
4. Every later local `read` reports `HELD holder=GHA-bridge` while the remote is free, because `_ref_oid` (`:301-315`) force-fetches and then falls back to `rev-parse` on the surviving local ref. Git cannot delete a local ref via a refspec whose source is absent, so the fetch failing (`fatal: couldn't find remote ref`, exit 128) leaves the orphan intact — contrary to `_fetch_ref`'s own comment claiming it "becomes absent locally = free".
5. `steal()` cannot break it either: `--force-with-lease` against an absent remote ref is rejected as `stale info`, which `_PUSH_REJECT_MARKERS` (`:619`) classifies as a CAS mismatch, logged misleadingly as "CAS lost to another contender". Measured: `steal(...)` returns None with the orphan intact.

Net effect: the checkout is wedged FOREVER and manual break-glass is the only escape.

## Why this is a defect (authority)

`docs/adr/0031-reconciler-ref-lock.md` §"Distributed operation": "The lock must be authoritative across CI runners, manual invocations, and clones" and with `remote="origin"` "the remote is the truth". A stranded local ref overriding a free remote violates that invariant directly.

Same ADR §"Operator break-glass": "C2's relative-duration lease makes this rarely necessary — a crashed holder's lock becomes steal-able after one lease interval automatically." Here it is NEVER steal-able and break-glass is ALWAYS required. The ADR also names both halves of a clear (`git push origin :refs/reconciler/lock` AND `git update-ref -d refs/reconciler/lock`), showing the design knows the local ref is a separate artifact the release path must handle.

## Acceptance criteria

- After a remote holder acquires, a local pass reads, and the remote holder releases, a later local `read(..., remote="origin")` reports the lock FREE (not HELD).
- `release(..., remote="origin")` leaves no local `refs/reconciler/lock` behind.
- A stranded local ref is reclaimable without manual intervention — either it reads free, or `steal()` breaks it.
- A GENUINELY live remote holder still reads as HELD, so cross-machine mutual exclusion is preserved (the fix must not make every lock look free).
- No local pass source is introduced or required: the Reconciler Bridge runs on GitHub Actions only.

## Ruled out during investigation

- The steal kill-switch: `REBAR_RECONCILER_LOCK_STEAL` defaults ON (`__main__.py:170-184`) and is unset locally; driving `steal_pass_lock` directly DID break a stale lease (fence 2 -> 3). Stealing is not disabled.
- A hidden local scheduler: no git hook, LaunchAgent (only a build updater + worktree GC), crontab, MCP tool, or implicit CLI path runs a reconcile pass. Operator-run local passes plus this bug fully explain recurrence.
- `_advisory_lock.py`'s fail-closed swallow: no exception is raised; `steal()` returns None cleanly.
baseline.summary: Stranded local refs/reconciler/lock wedges every local reconcile pass permanently

## Context / Problem

Ticket e39f-5055-f5af-424a makes the reconciler's inbound link-removal path (G5, apply_inbound_records.py::_inbound_unlink_one) converge by removing exactly the mirrored (target, relation) link. The safety analysis surfaced a PRE-EXISTING blind spot inherited from 2b16's design: managed_refs marks a ref managed the instant it is created LOCALLY (reducer/_managed_refs.py — strictly monotonic), so G3 cannot distinguish a brand-new never-pushed local link from a peer-deleted one. G4 (same-pass outbound-ADD suppression) covers that blind spot ONLY when the outbound differ emits the re-ADD; outbound_links.py::_diff_links dedups ADDs direction-agnostically on (vendor_type, target_key) ('intentionally NOT deduped on relation'), so a local link whose vendor type collides with an existing remote link in the other direction (blocks vs inward Blocks) is never pushed AND not G4-protected — an inbound removal record for it can reach G5 and remove a never-pushed local link. This is order-dependently true TODAY (when the never-pushed link is the pair's most-recent, pair-scoped unlink removes it after G5's relation match passes); e39f makes the outcome order-independent but does not add a discriminator.

## Approach

Design pass: persist enough peer-link history (e.g. record (relation, target) as 'peer-confirmed' only after an outbound link ADD is successfully applied or the link is observed in a fetched snapshot) so _inbound_unlink_one can decline removals of never-peer-confirmed links. Must reconcile with managed_refs monotonicity and compaction (SNAPSHOT restore).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] a removal record for a managed-but-never-peer-confirmed link is declined and logged.
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py -k declines`
- [x] a removal for a peer-confirmed link still converges.
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py -k converges`
- [x] behavior covered by behavioral tests through compute_inbound_mutations/_inbound_update_apply_links.
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py`
- [x] all four children (S1-S4) are closed and their changes are Verified +1 on Gerrit.
      Proof: `rebar list --parent despotic-floriated-leopard` shows every child `closed`

## Testing

Each child carries its own suite and gate commands; the epic is proven by the union of them: `make lint && make typecheck && pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` green on the final child, plus the existing `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_link_removal_2b16.py` regression suite staying green throughout.

## Chosen direction (operator-approved 2026-08-12; research comments above are the evidence base)

Follow the pattern both maintained comparisons converge on (GitHub ghas-jira-integration; contrast softrams/bulwark): **retain durable association/provenance and perform explicit managed mutations; never treat an unqualified missing link as deletion evidence.**

Concretely: persist a **full peer-confirmation record** per managed link (Jira linkId, direction, the confirming snapshot revision, confirmed-at time) — not a minimal boolean — because Jira exposes deletion as an explicit event keyed by stable linkId, and the completeness tracking S2 needs is impossible with a boolean. A partial/paginated/failed read is NON-EVIDENCE. Backfill grandfathers existing managed links as confirmed-at-upgrade (marked as such) so the first post-upgrade run does not decline every legitimate removal.

## Decomposition (children)
- S1: define + persist the peer-confirmation record (written on successful outbound link ADD; survives SNAPSHOT compaction; reconciled with managed_refs monotonicity).
- S2: populate confirmations from fetched authoritative snapshots, recording snapshot completeness; partial reads can never confirm nor deny.
- S3: _inbound_unlink_one declines-and-logs removal of never-peer-confirmed links (behavioral tests through compute_inbound_mutations).
- S4: backfill migration marking existing managed links confirmed-at-upgrade.
baseline.summary: Discriminate never-pushed managed links from peer deletions in the inbound removal path

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Gerrit change 1757 (merged as 065af7c163, ticket small-delicious-loris) taught rebar._store.sync._union_merge to recover ONE merge-abort class: untracked files origin wants to create ("untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge") — quarantine the named paths, retry once. The second proven abort class, variant (b), remains unhandled: tracked files with local working-tree changes — in practice deletions of tracked per-ticket artifacts left by an interrupted compaction fold — make `git merge origin/tickets` abort with "Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge". The abort leaves reconverge unable to advance and strands local ticket commits off origin (live recurrence recorded on e72e-259d-5ee7-4e73: 119 tracked `.archived` deletions wedged the store). Sibling story untrack-runtime-markers removes the marker sub-class at its source, but an interrupted fold can still leave tracked EVENT-file deletions (compact_txn renames sources to `*.retired` — a rename of a tracked file is a tracked deletion + an untracked creation), so reconverge must self-heal this class regardless.

## Approach
Extend the recovery seam 1757 added in src/rebar/_store/sync.py: on merge failure, additionally detect the "Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge" signature and parse the paths git names (same parsing pattern as the merged `_untracked_overwrite_paths`). For each named path, act by its status: a working-tree DELETION of a tracked file (`git status --porcelain` reports ` D`) is restored non-destructively via `git checkout -- <path>` (content already at HEAD — nothing can be lost); a working-tree MODIFICATION is first copied into the same quarantine directory 1757 established (`<git-common-dir>/reconverge-quarantine/<utc-ts>/`) and then restored via `git checkout -- <path>` (the local bytes are preserved in quarantine, the HEAD bytes unblock the merge). Then retry the merge once. Any other failure — including a genuine index/content conflict — keeps today's behavior exactly: `git merge --abort`, keep local, hint `rebar fsck-recover`. Positive rationale: this reuses the exact recovery shape already reviewed and merged for variant (a) (parse-what-git-names, move-never-delete, single retry, fall back to abort), extending one proven seam rather than adding a second recovery mechanism.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_store/sync.py — detect + parse the local-changes abort; restore/quarantine the named paths; single retry.
- tests/unit/test_store_sync_reconverge.py — extend the 1757 test module with RED-first coverage for variant (b): tracked-deletion fixture and tracked-modification fixture.

## Testing
- RED first: fixture tracker where HEAD tracks a file, the worktree deletes it, and origin/tickets modifies it; assert the union merge currently aborts and HEAD is un-merged, for the local-changes reason specifically.
- GREEN: same fixture after the fix — merge completes with both parents, the local-only commit stays reachable, the deleted file is back at its merged content.
- Modification path: worktree-modified tracked file named by the abort — quarantine copy exists with the local bytes, merge completes.
- Guard: a genuine content conflict (both sides commit different content) still aborts and keeps local (unchanged behavior); `.tmp-event-*` and paths git does not name are untouched.
- Mutation check: skipping the restore step returns the RED assertion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A reconverge whose union merge aborts only on local changes to tracked store-artifact paths now completes keeping both parents, with no local commit orphaned; checked by the new RED-to-GREEN tests.
- [x] A worktree modification named by the abort is preserved byte-for-byte in the quarantine directory before restore; checked by test comparing quarantined bytes.
- [x] A genuine merge conflict still aborts, keeps local, and hints fsck-recover; checked by the guard test.
- [x] [operator-attested] `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1) before close.
baseline.summary: Reconverge variant (b): recover the local-changes merge abort on tracked store artifacts (restore deletions, quarantine modifications, retry once)

baseline.description:
## The defect

`CodeHealthConfig.enabled` (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:538`, default `False`) has ZERO read sites in `src/rebar`. Nothing gates on it.

A code trace of the live path confirms it: `_commands/metrics.py:139-148` loads `config.load_config(root).code_health` and carries only `scan_roots` (:144), `size_cap` (:145) and `size_near_fraction` (:146) into the metrics context. `enabled` is never consulted, so the structural metrics (`module_size_distribution`, `oversized_module_count`, `complexity_summary`, `duplication_summary`) evaluate even at the default `enabled=False`.

The field is documented and settable, so an operator can set `enabled = false` and reasonably believe code-health analysis is off. It is not.

## Why it was never caught

The 6754 inert-config gate cannot see this one -- see the sibling bug on that gate. It matches bare attribute NAMES globally, and `.enabled` is read on other configs (`ui.enabled`, `LangfuseConfig`, under `llm/`), so this field passes without ever being read itself. That is also why it carries no `# read-via:` marker while the neighbouring `analyzers` field needed one.

## The decision this needs

Same shape as dce2: either HONOR the flag (gate structural metric evaluation on it) or DELETE it. Honoring it is a behavioral change -- metrics that run today would stop running for anyone on the default -- so this needs an explicit operator ruling, not an agent's judgment.

Note the interaction with dce2's ruling: the operator chose to DELETE the inert `analyzers` field rather than wire it, with intent preserved as idea 94bc-a0b4-bc37-47b2. A consistent ruling here is plausible but must not be assumed, because the two differ -- deleting `analyzers` removes a knob that never did anything, whereas deleting `enabled` removes the only advertised off switch for the whole code-health subsystem.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] An explicit operator decision is recorded: honor `enabled` or remove it.
- [x] If HONORED: structural metric evaluation is gated on it, with a test proving the metrics do
      NOT evaluate at `enabled=False` and DO at `enabled=True`; the default's behavior change is
      called out in the changelog.
- [x] If REMOVED: the field, its coercion row and its config-surface entries go, and the docs no
      longer advertise an off switch that does not exist.
- [x] Either way, a guard prevents it silently regressing to inert again (this depends on the 6754
      gate fix -- a same-named field cannot be policed until that lands). MOOT: nothing left to regress.

## Provenance

Found by a code-trace archaeology pass over the metrics/code-health system while scoping dce2.

## Operator ruling — RECORDED

**Decision: REMOVE `CodeHealthConfig.enabled`.** Ruled by the operator on 2026-08-05 and recorded as the first comment on this ticket ("OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-05: REMOVE the field", author `RebarBotNava`, `author_id` `594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d`) — that comment is the citable attestation this AC closes against.

The counter-argument was surfaced to the operator before the ruling: this differs from dce2 because deleting `analyzers` removed a knob that never did anything, whereas deleting `enabled` removes the only advertised OFF SWITCH for the whole code-health subsystem. The operator considered that tradeoff and chose removal knowingly. This is a one-way door for the advertised switch; the intent it expressed is not being preserved as a follow-up idea (unlike dce2, whose analyzer-dispatch intent survives as idea 94bc-a0b4-bc37-47b2) because there is no surviving design for a code-health off switch — re-adding one later would be a fresh feature decision, not a restoration. Do not re-litigate the ruling.

## Fix plan (REMOVAL, per the recorded operator ruling above)

Pure removal — the field controls nothing today (zero read sites), so deleting it cannot change what runs.

1. `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — delete the `enabled: bool = False` field from
   `CodeHealthConfig`; delete its `"enabled": lambda v, k: _as_bool(v, k)` coercion row from
   the `code_health` entry of `_SECTIONS`; refresh the class docstring, which no longer
   describes an inert-by-default toggle.
2. `src/rebar/_deprecations.py` — add TWO warn-class tombstones to `_TOMBSTONE_REGISTRY` so a
   still-set input WARNs and exits 0 rather than being silently dropped: an `env` tombstone for
   `REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ENABLED` and a `cfg` tombstone for `code_health.enabled`. This is
   mandatory, not optional: `tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py` fails the build when a
   golden-pinned key exists in neither the live schema nor the tombstone registry.
3. `docs/config.md` — drop `enabled` from both TOML examples and from the prose type list in
   the `code_health.*` section (so the docs stop advertising an off switch that does not
   exist), and add both tombstoned inputs to the warn-class list.
4. `tests/unit/test_code_health_config.py` — drop only the plain `value.enabled is False` /
   `value.enabled is True` assertions from the two happy-path tests.
5. `tests/unit/test_code_health_config_heldout.py` — drop the `-c code_health.enabled=true`
   CLI override argument, the `enabled` entries in the composed config/sources assertions, and
   `code_health.enabled` / `REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ENABLED` from the golden-surface expectation
   sets.
6. `tests/scripts/test_metrics_docs.py` — drop `enabled` from the documented-keys tuple.
7. `tests/unit/test_config_backcompat.py` — add a RUNTIME test (the home of the existing
   tombstone/warn tests) asserting the new tombstones actually fire: loading a config with
   `[code_health] enabled = true` set, and separately with `REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ENABLED` set,
   emits the warn-class removed-input message and does NOT raise (warn class, not error
   class). Registry presence alone is not proof — the warn path is verified by execution.

Not touched: `tests/golden/config_surface.json` stays pinned (that is the point of the golden — the tombstones, not a golden edit, account for the removed entries).

`_as_bool` is NOT orphaned by this removal (dozens of other coercion rows in `_SECTIONS` use it), unlike dce2's `_as_str_dict`.

### How the removal is proved

- `grep -rn "code_health.enabled\|REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ENABLED" src/rebar` returns nothing.
- `pytest tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py tests/unit/test_config_backcompat.py
  tests/unit/test_code_health_config.py tests/unit/test_code_health_config_heldout.py` passes.
- `rebar config validate` with the key still set exits 0 and reports it as a removed input.

### Evidence of no behavior change

`rebar metrics` before and after produces the same structural metrics (`module_size_distribution`, `oversized_module_count`, `complexity_summary`, `duplication_summary`). A byte-identical whole-output diff is NOT achievable — two consecutive runs already differ in time- and store-driven ticket metrics (dce2 found the same) — so the evidence is per-metric attribution over the code_health lens.

### On the guard AC

MOOT for a deleted field: there is nothing left to regress to inert. It also depended on bug 2c58-e710-275e-4ff7 regardless — the current inert-config gate could never have caught this field, because `.enabled` is read on other configs (`ui.enabled`, `LangfuseConfig`).
baseline.summary: CodeHealthConfig.enabled is inert: structural metrics run regardless of it

baseline.description:
# The review-bot container resolves NO AWS region — a Bedrock cutover fails at client construction

## MEASURED (from inside `compose-review-bot-1` on i-00880b2c7f13527c5, account 896586841071)

```
env | grep '^AWS_'        -> (nothing: no AWS_REGION, no AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, no keys)
env | grep '^REBAR_LLM_'  -> NO_REBAR_LLM_ENV   (so REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION is unset too)
boto3.session.Session().region_name        -> None
boto3.client('bedrock-runtime')            -> NoRegionError: You must specify a region.
converse(...) with no explicit region      -> NoRegionError: You must specify a region.
```

Every earlier Bedrock probe in this epic passed `region_name="us-east-1"` EXPLICITLY, which is exactly why this went unnoticed — those probes never exercised ambient resolution.

## Why this breaks the cutover

`src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py::build_bedrock_provider` does:

```python
region = cfg.bedrock_region_name or None
return BedrockProvider(region_name=region)
```

`cfg.bedrock_region_name` comes from `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION`, which is UNSET in the container. So `region=None` and `BedrockProvider` falls through to boto3's own resolution — which, as measured, finds nothing and raises `NoRegionError`.

That is a HARD failure at client construction, before any model call, and story eb6e ships the cutover with **NO cross-provider fallback**. So flipping `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` to `bedrock:...` without also setting a region takes the `LLM-Review` gate down for every landing rather than degrading it.

**Notably, IMDS is NOT the region source here.** IMDS is reachable from the container (token PUT returns 200, role resolves — see 9249), yet `session.region_name` is still `None`. So region discovery is ORTHOGONAL to the IMDS/hop-limit contingency: fixing IMDS reachability would not supply a region, and region must be configured explicitly no matter what IMDS does. That distinction matters because it is easy to assume the instance-metadata path covers both.

## Approach (candidate)

Set the region explicitly for the bot service — `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` (rebar's own knob, which `build_bedrock_provider` already threads) or `AWS_REGION` in the container environment. Prefer the rebar knob so the value is visible to rebar's config layer and to `provider_provenance` (343b).

Consider ALSO failing loudly and early: today a missing region surfaces as a boto3 `NoRegionError` from deep inside provider construction. A pre-flight check that names `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` would turn a confusing runtime stack trace into an actionable config error — the same shape as the existing typed `LLMConfigError` for a missing bedrock package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the cutover runbook records the Bedrock region setting and its value
- [ ] [operator-attested] the bot service environment sets an explicit Bedrock region, evidenced by
      container `env` output in a comment
- [ ] a test asserts that building the bedrock provider with NO resolvable region raises a TYPED, actionable rebar error naming the region setting — not a bare boto3 `NoRegionError`
- [ ] [operator-attested] from inside the review-bot container, `boto3.client('bedrock-runtime')` with NO explicit region succeeds after the change, evidenced by command output in a comment
- [ ] the runbook states that IMDS reachability does NOT supply a region, so the hop-limit contingency and region config are independent concerns
baseline.summary: Bedrock cutover hard-fails with NoRegionError: the review-bot container has no region configured

## Context / Problem
A measured bug class: validation implemented in one CLI command while the MCP/library/reconciler paths skip it — the engine-vs-interface placement decision is made silently at plan time and never reviewed.

## Approach
Add project criterion project.engine-layer-enforcement to the plan-review registry (via .rebar/criteria_routing.json overlay + criterion definition): ADVISORY posture; deterministic trigger = plan file_impact/scope touching src/rebar/_commands/ or interface modules while naming validation/guard/check work; the reviewer asks where the invariant is enforced and flags CLI-only placement, suggesting the engine seam. Advisory (not blocking) because placement can be legitimately interface-local; the criterion teaches, the census (skill-side) enumerates.

## Scope
- criteria registry/routing overlay + generated criteria guide regeneration
- criterion detection detail per docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md conventions

## Testing
Behavioral eval per LLM-surface conventions (pinned config, repeated trials): plan placing validation in CLI-only -> advisory finding fires; plan placing it in engine with CLI delegating -> no finding. Registry round-trip: rebar explain project.engine-layer-enforcement renders.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Criterion registered, routed by the deterministic trigger, ADVISORY posture, with detection detail in the generated guide.
- [x] Eval demonstrates fire/no-fire on the two plan shapes above.
- [x] rebar explain <id> serves the criterion.

## Why
Epic 88ab (elfish-chair-lug) S5 — the epic's close gate. The pattern's five requirements (R1–R5) must be proven live under multi-agent parallel conditions, not asserted from config. Scripted alongside `infra/gerrit/reviewbot-e2e.sh`; every scenario's change URLs + votes recorded on the EPIC ticket.

## What
Seven scenarios on the running Gerrit against a throwaway `feature/e2e-<date>` branch:
1. **Parallel siblings** — two agents in separate worktrees push independent story changes; both earn LLM-Review + Verified and submit WITHOUT either rebasing (second submit via MERGE_IF_NECESSARY, no manual rebase). Also live-proves webhook + g2p branch-agnostic dispatch.
2. **Stacking** — a third agent pulls the branch (both stories in history) and pushes on top; reviewed diff covers ONLY its delta (assert via robot comment/diff scope).
3. **Merge-back** — --no-ff merge change to main: bot reviews the auto-merge delta only (assert NOT the whole-feature diff), CI green on the merge tree, both votes present, submit lands atomically, replication advances GitHub main with all commits, branch deleted.
4. **Vote-carry on re-merge** — land an unrelated change on main mid-flight; re-merge (MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE): LLM-Review +1 CARRIES, Verified RE-RUNS; then change the feature tip: BOTH wiped (REWORK).
5. **Textual conflict** — overlapping feature-vs-main edits resolved in the merge commit; bot reviews the non-empty auto-merge delta.
6. **Semantic conflict** — textually clean, semantically broken (rename on main + new call-site on feature): auto-merge diff empty, LLM-Review passes, CI red → Verified=-1 BLOCKS submit (two-vote complementarity).
7. **Races + negatives** — concurrent submits into the branch behave; merge push WITHOUT pushMerge refused; branch creation outside feature-branch-drivers refused; reconciler backfills a dropped webhook for a feature-branch change INCLUDING a merge change (transparent merge detection).

## Scope
E2E script + live evidence only. Depends on S1 (config/ACLs), S2 (bot merge path), S3 (CI coverage). Requirement mapping: R1: 2+3; R2: 3; R3: 1+3+6; R4: 1+4; R5: ADR + apt-otter-urn.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Scenario script committed alongside reviewbot-e2e.sh (reusing its helpers where sensible)
- [ ] All 7 scenarios pass live; change URLs + votes recorded on the epic ticket
- [ ] RED/BLUE/GREEN replay (1–3) shows zero vote wipes, zero manual rebases, zero re-reviews of attested stories, single atomic landing
- [ ] Scenario 6 demonstrates Verified=-1 blocking submit on an empty auto-merge diff
- [ ] Cleanup: e2e feature branch deleted; throwaway changes abandoned
baseline.summary: S5: Live multi-agent E2E validation — 7 feature-branch scenarios on the running Gerrit

## What
Add a deterministic precheck to the completion-verification close gate: when a ticket records `file_impact` (a claimed code change) but no commit references it via a `rebar-ticket:` trailer, fail fast BEFORE the billable LLM verifier runs, with a message describing the reason and remediation.

## Why
A ticket recording file_impact claims a concrete code change. If no commit references it, the implementation has not landed and completion cannot be confirmed — so there is no point spending an LLM call. This mirrors the existing open-children structural guard.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py`: new helper `_referencing_commit_exists()` (scans
  `git log`, resolves each commit's `rebar-ticket:`/`<id>:` refs through the shared resolver);
  the precheck wired into `_completion_precheck` after the bug-reason check, before the LLM call.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py`: coverage for block/pass/skip/force-close.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A ticket with file_impact and no referencing commit is blocked (exit 1) before the LLM call.
- [ ] The same ticket closes once a commit references it via a rebar-ticket trailer.
- [ ] A ticket without file_impact is unaffected (no commit check).
- [ ] `--force-close` bypasses the precheck (withholds signature, still closes).
- [ ] The error message names the reason (file_impact) and remediation (referencing commit).
baseline.summary: Fail completion verification fast when a file_impact ticket has no referencing commit

baseline.description:
## The defect

`Makefile` line 128 (the `worktree` target) provisions the new worktree's venv with:

    python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && $(MAKE) install

It inherits whatever `python3` resolves to on the host. Nothing pins or checks the version, and `requires-python = ">=3.11"` (pyproject.toml:16) accepts anything from 3.11 upward, so `uv sync --locked` succeeds and the mismatch is silent.

## Measured on this host 2026-08-05

    system python3            -> Python 3.14.6   (/opt/homebrew/bin/python3)
    CI matrix                 -> 3.11, 3.12, 3.13   (.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml)
    worktree c6c9-attest-split/.venv      -> Python 3.14.6
    worktree rebar-8a5e/.venv             -> Python 3.14.6
    worktree fix-c5b3-scc-byfile/.venv    -> Python 3.14.6
    main checkout .venv                   -> Python 3.12.13

Every worktree created by `make worktree` runs **3.14.6, which CI never tests**. The main checkout is on a tested version only by accident of WHEN it was created — its venv predates the host's python3 moving to 3.14.

## The cost, which is not hypothetical

This is the canonical local-vs-CI divergence, and it burned real time tonight. Multiple agents working in fresh worktrees hit local test failures that CI did not reproduce, then each spent cycles proving them "pre-existing and environment-specific" -- correctly, but only after the fact. Two failures repeatedly implicated:

    tests/unit/grounding/test_coverage_reconstruction.py::test_full_backend_account_is_present
    tests/unit/metrics/test_jscpd_dup_heldout.py::test_live_clone

Each agent rediscovered this independently. The failure mode is corrosive rather than loud: local red that CI does not show trains agents (and humans) to discount local failures generally, which is exactly backwards -- the next genuine local-only regression gets waved through with the same reasoning.

It also cuts the other way: a change that breaks on 3.11 but passes on the developer's 3.14 looks clean locally and only fails after push, which is the slowest possible place to learn it.

## Note on scope

The version floor is separately declared and enforced for **git** (ticket 980d added `.github/git-version-floor.txt` plus a conftest session-abort). There is no equivalent for Python, even though Python is the far more likely source of behavioral divergence.

## Candidate approaches (weigh; not prescribed)

1. Pin the worktree venv to a CI-tested interpreter, e.g. `uv venv --python 3.12` (uv can fetch
   it), so a fresh worktree matches the matrix by construction.
2. Warn or fail loudly in `make worktree` / `make install` when the resolved interpreter is
   outside the CI matrix, naming the mismatch. Cheapest, and mirrors the git-floor pattern
   980d already established.
3. Add the host's version to the CI matrix -- rejected as stated, since it grows CI cost for
   every contributor to accommodate one machine, and does not stop the next drift.

Option 2 alone leaves the developer to act; option 1 removes the failure mode. They compose.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A venv created by `make worktree` runs a Python version the CI matrix actually tests, or
      the command fails/warns explicitly naming the mismatch and the supported set.
- [x] The supported set is single-sourced from the CI matrix rather than duplicated, so adding
      or dropping a version in CI cannot silently desynchronize the check (the same
      single-sourcing discipline as `.github/module-size-limit.txt` and
      `.github/git-version-floor.txt`).
- [x] A test proves the check fires for an out-of-matrix interpreter and stays silent for an
      in-matrix one.
- [x] `docs/local-dev-env.md` states the supported Python versions and how to provision a
      matching venv when the host default differs.
- [x] The two failures listed above are re-checked on an in-matrix interpreter and either
      confirmed genuinely pre-existing or filed as real bugs -- right now nobody knows which,
      because every observation of them has been on an untested Python.

## Provenance

Surfaced by the a573 agent, which noticed its worktree venv was 3.14.6 while explaining three local-only test failures. Independently verified here: system python3, the Makefile line, three worktree venvs, and the CI matrix all measured directly.
baseline.summary: make worktree builds its venv from ambient python3, so fresh worktrees run a Python CI never tests

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The plan-review `[rebar:<C>]` citation-escape lets a plan cite a symbol a prerequisite ticket will create; the E4/G1G2/E6 finders are instructed to "retrieve C via the `show_ticket(C)` tool" and credit the citation only if C's plan establishes the functionality (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_E4.md:16`, `plan_review_G1G2.md:10`). The agentic finder's `show_ticket` tool is `rebar.llm.pai_tools.rebar_tools`'s inner `show_ticket` (`src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py:204`), which forwards its argument verbatim to `_reads.show_ticket`.

**Defect:** the citation token is literally `[rebar:<id>]`, so the finder passes the token content **`rebar:<id>` — including the `rebar:` scheme** — to the tool. rebar's id resolver does not recognize the `rebar:` prefix, so `rebar show 'rebar:<id>'` exits "Ticket not found," the finder cannot confirm the prerequisite, and the citation-escape **fails closed on a spurious "cited prerequisite does not exist"** BLOCK. Runtime-proven by an instrumented review: the finder called `show_ticket('rebar:8153-…')` and `show_ticket('rebar:fc72-…')` (both → "not found") while the bare-id call `show_ticket('41e2-…')` returned OK. Because the LLM only *sometimes* strips the prefix itself, the failure is intermittent — which is why some citing plans pass and others block. This breaks the documented citation mechanism (`docs/writing-a-passing-plan.md` "Citing a prerequisite's symbol").

## Approach

Normalize the agent-supplied ticket ref at the tool boundary — the single site where a `rebar:`-scheme ref originates. Add `_normalize_ticket_ref()` to `pai_tools.py` that strips a leading `rebar:` (case-insensitive) plus any wrapping `[]`/whitespace, and call it in both `show_ticket` and `comment_ticket` before resolving. Stripping is unambiguous and safe: no ticket id (hex groups `[a-z0-9]{4}-…`) or alias (hyphenated words) contains a colon, so a leading `rebar:` is never part of a real id; the function is idempotent on a bare id.

**Rejected alternative.** Fixing it in the reviewer prompts (tell the LLM to strip the scheme) — probabilistic (LLM may still forget) versus a deterministic tool-boundary normalization. Rejected widening `_reads.show_ticket` / the CLI id-resolver — the `rebar:` scheme only ever arrives from the LLM citation-token path, so normalizing at that boundary keeps CLI/library id semantics untouched.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py` — add `_normalize_ticket_ref`; apply in `show_ticket` and
  `comment_ticket`.
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_scoped_ticket_tool.py` — add a RED-first case pinning that the tool
  resolves a `rebar:<id>`-form ref.

## Testing

- Happy path (the defect): `show_ticket(f"rebar:{tid}")` resolves to the same ticket as the bare
  `tid` — returns the ticket JSON (title + id present), not `Error: … not found`. Fails RED against
  the current tool; passes after the strip.
- Parity: the existing `test_show_ticket_tool_reads` (bare id) and `test_comment_ticket_tool_comments`
  still pass — a bare id is unchanged (idempotent normalization).

Tier: unit (interfaces/store) — builds a real store via the `rebar_repo` fixture, creates a ticket, invokes the actual `rebar_tools` `show_ticket` function; no LLM.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The agentic `show_ticket` tool resolves a `rebar:<id>`-scheme ref to the same ticket as the
      bare id; verified by
      `rtk .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/interfaces/store/test_scoped_ticket_tool.py -k rebar_scheme_prefix`
      (the new case passes).
- [ ] Bare-id reads and comments are unchanged (parity); verified by
      `rtk .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/interfaces/store/test_scoped_ticket_tool.py`
      (the full file passes, including the pre-existing read/comment cases).
baseline.summary: Plan-review show_ticket tool rejects the rebar: citation-scheme prefix, breaking the [rebar:<C>] escape

baseline.description:
The review-bot fails 100% of `code_review` artifact emissions with git's dubious-ownership error, because the container runs as root over a persistent tickets volume owned by uid 1000 and no `safe.directory` is configured.

## Reproduction Steps
1. On the box, observe the recurring bot log marker:
   `journalctl CONTAINER_NAME=compose-review-bot-1 | grep ARTIFACT_EMIT_ERROR`
2. Each entry: `rebar create failed (exit 1): git commit failed while holding lock: fatal:
   detected dubious ownership in repository at '/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets'`.

## Expected vs Actual
- **Expected:** `emit_code_review_artifact` (voter.py, story limestone-unethical-zebrafinch)
  writes a durable `code_review` ticket into the persistent tickets store on every vote.
- **Actual:** every write fails with dubious-ownership; artifact emission is a total no-op
  (non-fatal only because emit is post-vote/best-effort, so votes still land).

## Root cause (proven)
- The review-bot container runs as **root** (uid 0; no `USER` directive in
  `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot`).
- The tickets store is a **persistent named docker volume** (`gerrit_reviewbot_tickets`) whose
  `.git` is owned **uid 1000:1000** (legacy population; it survives container rebuilds).
- `HOME` is **unset** in the container and no `safe.directory` is configured
  (`git config --global --get-all safe.directory` → none).
- Git >=2.35.2 refuses to operate on a repo owned by a different uid → dubious-ownership. This
  aborts BOTH the `reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` convergence (its `git -C <dir> config`) AND
  rebar's runtime `git commit` inside `emit_code_review_artifact`.
- CONFIRMED on the box: `git -c safe.directory=/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets rev-parse
  --is-inside-work-tree` returns `true` — i.e. `safe.directory` resolves the guard.

## Fix
Inject `safe.directory=/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets` into the review-bot container via `GIT_CONFIG_*` env in `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` (`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_0/VALUE_0`). This is equivalent to `git -c safe.directory=...` (the confirmed-working form), is honored for `safe.directory` (which is ignored from repo-local config), is **HOME-independent** (HOME is unset) and **system-config-independent**, and applies to EVERY git process from container start (entrypoint clone, ensure-tickets convergence, and rebar's runtime commit). rebar does not use `GIT_CONFIG_*` itself (grep-verified), so there is no conflict. Chosen over chowning the volume to root each boot (heavy recursive chown of ~1500 entries; fights whatever re-provisions the volume as 1000) and over `git config --global` (HOME is unset, so it writes nowhere git reads).

## Scope
- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`: add the three `GIT_CONFIG_*` env keys to `review-bot`.
- `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py`: assert the compose service declares the safe.directory config.
- Non-goal: changing the container's uid or the volume's ownership (out of scope; safe.directory
  is git's sanctioned remedy for a trusted repo owned by another uid).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` review-bot service injects
      `safe.directory=/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets` via `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1` +
      `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0`/`GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0`.
      Proving command: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -k safe_directory -q`
      passes and is confirmed RED on the pre-fix tree.
- [ ] The compose file still parses and config-check passes.
      Proving command: `make config-check` exits 0.
- [ ] [operator-attested] After redeploy, `ARTIFACT_EMIT_ERROR` no longer appears for new votes
      and a `code_review` artifact ticket is written for a fresh review.
      Proving evidence: a bot-log window post-redeploy showing a vote with NO subsequent
      ARTIFACT_EMIT_ERROR (recorded as a ticket comment).
- [ ] Existing gates stay green.
      Proving command: `make lint && make typecheck && python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -q` all exit 0.
baseline.summary: review-bot: dubious-ownership fails all code_review artifact emissions (safe.directory)

# gitleaks false-positive on a docs example secret blocks docs changes (+ 189 unblock)

## What
gitleaks' generic-api-key rule flags a DOCUMENTED throwaway placeholder in docs
(docs/llm-framework.md:311 `export LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-1234567890`), and because the
secret detector scans the whole CHANGED FILE, any edit to that file (e.g. change 189) is
force-BLOCKed. Fix the false-positive class without weakening detection of genuine secrets.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Add a `.gitleaks.toml` allowlist scoped to documented placeholder patterns (sk-lf-/pk-lf- throwaways; docs example keys) — NOT a blanket **/*.md exclusion (a real doc secret must still block).
- [ ] Fix the misleading docs/llm-framework.md:311 placeholder to an obviously-non-secret form.
- [ ] The secret detector still fail-closes on a genuine secret (a test/fixture proves a real pattern still matches).
- [ ] This sits at/before change 189 in the Gerrit stack so 189's re-review passes gitleaks; make lint green; commit carries a rebar-ticket trailer.
baseline.summary: gitleaks false-positive on docs example secret blocks docs changes

# WU-2 — Write surface: CLI / library / MCP emit TAG_DELTA

Reroute every *local* tag writer to emit `TAG_DELTA`, and add the new editing grammar. After this unit the only remaining whole-field `EDIT.tags` writer is the Jira inbound applier (handled in WU-3). Depends on WU-1 (event type + reducer).

## What / Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/leaf.py`: reroute `tag`/`untag` (:85-92, :107-114) to emit
  `TAG_DELTA{added:[t]}` / `{removed:[t]}`; preserve existing command-time no-op
  suppression (they already read `current_tags` and return without an event).
- `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py` (`edit_core`, `_EDIT_FIELDS` :254) + the CLI
  arg layer: add `--add-tag`, `--remove-tag`, `--set-tags`.
  - `--set-tags=x,y` compiles to a delta vs locally-observed reduced state:
    `removed=observed−{x,y}`, `added={x,y}−observed` (convergent add-wins).
    `--set-tags=""` clears OBSERVED tags only.
  - Mutual exclusion → error: `--set-tags` with `--add-tag`/`--remove-tag`; the
    same tag in both `--add-tag` and `--remove-tag`.
  - Command-time no-op suppression (drop adds present / removes absent; emit
    nothing if delta empty).
  - **DROP `--tags` from CLI `edit`** (remove from `_EDIT_FIELDS`). Keep
    library/MCP `edit(tags=)` as a DEPRECATED alias for `set_tags`, intercepted as
    a **pre-pass in `edit_core` BEFORE the `_EDIT_FIELDS` validation loop**

## What
Continuous alerting for the two post-cutover silent-failure modes of the Gerrit->GitHub mirror:
replication failing (GitHub main stops advancing while Gerrit main moves), and the
gerrit-mirror-lock-main ruleset being mutated/deleted out-of-band (drift to unprotected).

## Design (two independent, secretless watchers)
- A tested Python module (src/rebar/mirror_guard.py) holds the verdict LOGIC + I/O + a CLI, driven
  by a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow (the PRIMARY guardian): native GITHUB_TOKEN authenticates
  the GitHub Rulesets API fetch; the Gerrit main SHA is read ANONYMOUSLY (public REST); no new secret.
- A lightweight bash probe in observability.sh is the SECONDARY, house-style replication watcher:
  it compares the anon Gerrit main SHA vs the anon GitHub main SHA (git ls-remote) and publishes a
  CloudWatch metric (no auth, matching the S5 replication probe) -> a Terraform alarm -> SNS.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] src/rebar/mirror_guard.py exposes replication_verdict(gerrit_sha, github_sha) returning an in-sync/diverged verdict.
- [ ] src/rebar/mirror_guard.py exposes ruleset_verdict(ruleset) enforcing the full lock contract (active, target=branch, refs/heads/main, rules update+deletion+non_fast_forward, bypass = DeployKey only).
- [ ] src/rebar/mirror_guard.py provides thin I/O fetchers for the Gerrit main SHA (anon), the GitHub main SHA, and the GitHub ruleset (GITHUB_TOKEN from env).
- [ ] python -m rebar.mirror_guard runs both checks, prints a JSON result, exits non-zero when unhealthy.
- [ ] Behavioral tests cover in-sync vs diverged for replication_verdict.
- [ ] Behavioral tests cover locked vs each ruleset drift mutation (disabled, missing rule, extra bypass, wrong ref, deleted).
- [ ] Contractual tests pin the verdict output schema.
- [ ] Contractual tests pin the CLI exit codes.
- [ ] .github/workflows/mirror-guard.yml runs the CLI on a cron schedule plus manual dispatch.
- [ ] The workflow grants the job permissions: administration: read so the Actions GITHUB_TOKEN can read the repo ruleset; if org policy disallows that, a fine-grained PAT (administration:read) stored as an Actions secret is the documented fallback.
- [ ] The workflow fails (producing a notification) when either check is unhealthy.
- [ ] infra/scripts/observability.sh publishes the rebar/host:mirror_out_of_sync metric via aws cloudwatch put-metric-data (dimensionless), comparing the anon Gerrit and GitHub main SHAs in bash.
- [ ] infra/terraform/monitoring_ws7.tf defines a CloudWatch alarm on that metric wired to the rebar-gerrit-alerts SNS topic.
- [ ] The guardian is verified LIVE reporting healthy plus locked against production.
- [ ] A simulated ruleset drift is detected by the guardian, then reverted.

## Files
- src/rebar/mirror_guard.py, tests/unit/test_mirror_guard.py, .github/workflows/mirror-guard.yml, infra/scripts/observability.sh, infra/terraform/monitoring_ws7.tf
baseline.summary: Replication-health + ruleset-drift alerting for the Gerrit->GitHub mirror

baseline.description:
## Why

The most-advertised property of the `rebar.llm` framework is: *"`import rebar` stays dependency-free; only **running** an op needs the `[agents]` extra, and the absence of the extra degrades gracefully."* There is a dedicated contract test for the **degradation** half — but it runs in **zero** CI lanes, so a regression that broke the no-extra fallback would ship green. The validator proved this empirically and found it *understated*: the 4 skip decorators expand to **10 always-skipped test instances**.

## What

Execute `tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_optionality.py`'s degradation tests in a CI lane where the `[agents]` extra is **absent**, so `_AGENTS` is False and the `skipif(_AGENTS)` tests actually run.

## Scope

- In scope: `.github/workflows/optionality.yml` (the clean-core-wheel lane is the
  natural home — it already runs with no extras).
- Out of scope: changing the tests themselves, changing `[dev]`'s dependency on
  `[agents]` (that is intentional — it makes the *positive* LLM tests run in the
  main lane).

## Context (citations)

- **The skipped tests:** `tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_optionality.py:87,113,191,250`
  are `@pytest.mark.skipif(_AGENTS, reason="agents extra installed → degradation
  path not exercised")`. `_AGENTS = agents_extra_installed()` at line 52;
  `agents_extra_installed()` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:330`) returns True iff
  langchain **and langgraph** + langchain-anthropic + langchain-mcp-adapters are
  importable (via `find_spec`, no import). (Earlier draft omitted langgraph.)
- **Why they always skip in the main lane:** `pyproject.toml:93` lists
  `"nava-rebar[agents]"` inside `[dev]`; `.github/workflows/test.yml` installs
  `pip install -e '.[dev]'` in both the `lint` job (≈ line 41) and the `test` job
  (≈ line 100) → `_AGENTS == True` → all 4 (10 parametrized instances) skip.
- **Why the existing clean lane doesn't cover them:**
  `.github/workflows/optionality.yml` has two lanes — an import-linter lane that
  runs only `tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py` + `tests/unit/test_optional.py`
  (≈ line 39), and a clean-core-wheel lane (≈ lines 58-73) that runs a **hand-written
  inline Python import snippet**, *not* pytest on `test_llm_optionality.py`.
- **Empirical proof:** in the dev venv, `CI=true pytest
  tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_optionality.py -rs` → **10 skipped** (reasons
  pinned to lines 87/113/191/250); `env -u CI` with a clean (no-agents) venv runs
  them.

## Implementation plan

1. Open `.github/workflows/optionality.yml` and locate the clean-core-wheel lane
   (no `[agents]` installed). Confirm what it installs (likely just the built
   wheel / `pip install .` with no extras).
2. Add a step to that lane (after the wheel install, in the clean venv) that runs:
   `pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_optionality.py -m "not external" -rs`.
   - **PLAN-REVIEW CORRECTION — do NOT blanket-deselect the other tests.** The
     review confirmed the file *collects* without jsonschema/mcp (all heavy imports
     are function-local; `import rebar`/`rebar.llm` are lazy), and the ~7
     non-degradation tests **pass or cleanly skip** in a no-agents env — they do not
     break. So prefer running the **whole file**. One parametrization
     (`test_interface_import_pulls_no_agents_stack[rebar.mcp_server]`) needs `mcp`
     via `importorskip`, so `pip install mcp` (and `jsonschema`) in the clean lane
     to cover it. If anything genuinely needs agents, deselect ONLY by the specific
     `_AGENTS`-skip node ids — not a broad "~7 tests" cut.
3. Ensure the lane does NOT have `[agents]` on the path (verify `agents_extra_installed()`
   would return False there — no langchain). If the clean wheel lane already
   guarantees this, no change needed beyond the pytest step.
4. Confirm the conftest network guard and collection guards don't exclude
   `tests/interfaces/` in that minimal environment (interfaces tier may need the
   `mcp`/`jsonschema` test deps — install the minimal `[dev]`-minus-`[agents]` set
   if required, or `pip install pytest jsonschema mcp`).
5. Run the lane logic locally in a fresh venv to confirm the 4 degradation tests
   now PASS (not skip): create a venv, `pip install .` (no agents), `pip install
   pytest jsonschema mcp`, then the pytest command — assert 0 skipped for those 4.

## Tradeoffs

- **Benefit:** restores the safety net for the framework's headline optionality
  contract at near-zero cost (a few CI minutes on an already-existing clean lane).
- **Cost/risk:** the minimal environment may lack test-only deps the interfaces
  tier expects (jsonschema/mcp); the plan installs them explicitly. Keep the
  degradation tests deselected from the *main* lane (they correctly skip there) —
  do not try to force them to run with agents present.
- **Alternative considered:** invert the skip (run when agents *present* too) —
  rejected; the degradation path is meaningless with the extra installed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A CI lane runs `tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_optionality.py`'s
  `skipif(_AGENTS)` degradation tests with `_AGENTS == False` (agents extra absent).
- [ ] That lane reports those tests as PASSED (not skipped) — verified in the CI log.
- [ ] The main `test.yml` lane still skips them (correctly — agents present there).
- [ ] No new always-skip is introduced; `pytest -rs` in the clean lane shows the
  degradation tests executing.
</content>
