baseline.description:
## Why

E6 measures whether the plan-review gate's **LLM-as-judge is reliable** — the same judgment, re-run, must land the same way. Two documented judge failure modes threaten the shared Pass-2 verify / Pass-3 decide vocabulary that R3 and R5 build on:

- **Self-consistency drift.** An unstable per-finding decision injects noise into the
  Pass-2 sub-answer vocabulary. R5 adds a new Pass-2 sub-answer
  (`asserted_capability_confirmed`) routed over the G6/E4/T3 cohort
  (`docs/research/task-decomposition-sota-2026.md:195-199`); it is only worth adding if
  the judge that emits it is stable across repeats. Our own research substrate records
  that "~3-vote self-consistency captures most of the available gain (+4pp, saturating)"
  and that "judges are systematically overconfident" (`sota:44`; refs at `sota:241` —
  Wang et al., *LLMs are not Fair Evaluators*, ACL 2024, arXiv:2305.17926; Zheng et al.,
  MT-Bench, arXiv:2306.05685; judge overconfidence, arXiv:2508.06225).
- **Order sensitivity.** Section-order permutation of the input plan should not flip the
  gate verdict. `sota:44` records order-swap flipping 82.5% of *pairwise* verdicts (Wang,
  ACL 2024). Our gate already uses the recommended mitigation — absolute rubric scoring,
  never pairwise — so E6 empirically confirms the **residual** order-sensitivity of the
  actual gate is below a floor before R3 lands a new (order-exposed) container criterion.

E6 **re-judges an existing sample and measures agreement (reliability), not accuracy against gold** (`runs/README.md:154-156`: "E6 re-judges these findings for self-consistency; it never needed the TP/FP labels"). This is why E6 survived the E1 descope (ticket comment 2026-07-16): re-running the gate's own judge to measure its *stochastic stability* is the textbook definition of a self-consistency test — it is **not** the circular-adjudication error that invalidated E1's finding-level TP/FP labeling (which mis-used the gate's judge as *gold truth for accuracy*). E6 never treats any judge output as truth; it only compares repeated judge outputs to each other.

E6 gates two downstream stories: R3 (with E2) and R5 (with E5).

## What

Two bounded judge-reliability experiments, each with an explicit metric + pass/fail floor, run over **committed, reproducible samples**. No `src/rebar` behavior changes — E6 is measurement over the *existing* gate (Pass-2 verify → Pass-3 decide → `orchestrator.finalize_verdict`).

### Grounded definitions (verified against the code/corpus, not assumed)

- **"decision"** (self-consistency unit of agreement) = the Pass-3 output field
  `decision ∈ {block, advisory, dropped, indeterminate}` produced by
  `three_pass.pass3_decide(...)` (the deterministic decision path; harness
  `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/three_pass.py`), whose vocabulary matches
  the persisted sidecar `decision` enum. Pass-3 is deterministic given Pass-2, so all
  measured variance is the judge's Pass-2 stochasticity.
- **"verdict"** (order-shuffle unit of agreement) = the gate's overall
  `verdict ∈ {PASS, BLOCK, INDETERMINATE}` on the `plan_review_verdict` dict returned by
  the public entrypoint `rebar.llm.plan_review.review_plan` (`__init__.py:387`), which
  computes it in `orchestrator.finalize_verdict` (`orchestrator.py:467-503`). A
  `PASS↔BLOCK` or `PASS↔INDETERMINATE` flip across permutations is a disagreement.
- **Infra-INDETERMINATE exclusion is defined concretely, not hand-waved.**
  `finalize_verdict` records *why* a verdict is INDETERMINATE on the verdict's `coverage`
  record: an INDETERMINATE carrying `coverage.get("llm_unavailable")` (systemic LLM-tier
  failure) or `coverage.get("verify_failed")` (Pass-2 verifier could not run — e.g. the
  agentic verifier exhausted its step budget, bug 59bc) is an **execution failure, not a
  stable judge outcome** (`orchestrator.py:491-501`). E6 **drops and re-runs** any
  permutation whose verdict is INDETERMINATE **with either flag set**, and **keeps**
  a genuine judge-INDETERMINATE (INDETERMINATE with *neither* flag — e.g. a preserved
  Pass-1 indeterminate on a blocking-enabled criterion) as its own agreement category.
  (A genuine unsupported-stack abstain where the tier ran but a criterion could not ground
  is *not* `llm_unavailable` and surfaces as PASS, `orchestrator.py:488` — so it never
  pollutes the INDETERMINATE category.) The exact fields/values were verified in
  `finalize_verdict`; the exclusion is not a guessed mechanism.

### Experiment A — self-consistency of the Pass-2/Pass-3 judge over the R5 cohort

- **Sample frame (concrete).** `runs/adjudication_corpus.jsonl` rows filtered by
  `criterion ∈ {G6, E4, T3}` — **exactly the R5 sub-answer's own routing cohort**
  (`sota:195-199` routes G6/E4/T3 through the agentic verifier for
  `asserted_capability_confirmed`). Verified in the committed file: **74 rows across 66
  distinct tickets** (advisory 47 / dropped 20 / block 7) — the cohort exists and clears
  the N≥50 floor with 24 rows of headroom. (Chosen over the CLAUDE.md "G1G2+E4" framing
  because E6 gates *R5*, and R5 itself is defined at `sota:195-199` as the G6/E4/T3
  cohort; the corpus has no `asserted_capability` label, so a criterion-set filter is the
  only grounded slice.)
- **N = 50** findings, sampled deterministically (fixed seed) from the 74-member cohort,
  deduped by `(ticket_id, finding_id)` (finding_id alone is non-unique: 388 unique of
  400). The 24-row headroom absorbs any ticket whose plan text cannot be snapshotted.
- **Re-judge inputs are frozen and committed** to defeat the "no plan-text corpus" gap:
  a build step snapshots, once, each sampled finding's ticket plan text via
  `rebar show <ticket_id>` (the replay-derived `description` == the reviewed plan) plus
  the finding record, writing `runs/e6_selfconsistency_inputs.jsonl`
  (`{finding_id, ticket_id, title, plan, criterion, finding, location, suggested_fix}`).
  A ticket whose plan is unretrievable (compacted/archived) is skipped and the sample is
  topped up deterministically from the cohort remainder to hold N=50. The N-vote harness
  reads **only this committed file** — no live-store dependency at judge time.
- **Judge run — the agentic Pass-2 path requires BOTH an explicit `repo_root` AND an
  active gate session (verified execution recipe).** The agentic verifier only activates
  when `agentic=True` **and** `repo_root` is non-empty **and** the finding's criteria are
  code-grounded (`three_pass.pass2_verify`, dispatch at `three_pass.py:185`); the harness's
  `CODEBASE_GROUNDED` set (`three_pass.py:34`) contains **all of `{G6, E4, T3}`**, so every
  cohort finding takes the agentic path. Wire the session with `gate_source` so the
  agentic verifier's read-only repo tools are permitted (`config.assert_gated`):

  ```python
  from rebar.llm import gate_source
  from harnesses import three_pass
  handle = gate_source.resolve_gate_handle(None, "local", REAL_REPO_CHECKOUT)  # gate_source.py:80
  with gate_source.gate_read_root(handle):        # gate_source.py:105 — marks the gate session; local mode reads the in-place checkout
      for inp in frozen_inputs:                    # runs/e6_selfconsistency_inputs.jsonl
          for _ in range(3):                       # 3 votes (sota:44 — 3-vote self-consistency saturates the gain)
              v = three_pass.pass2_verify(inp["title"], inp["plan"], inp,
                                          repo_root=REAL_REPO_CHECKOUT, agentic=True)
              # pass2_verify returns {"verify": <inner dict|None>, "mode":..., "tool_calls":...}
              # (both the single-turn and _verify_agentic paths, three_pass.py); pass3_decide
              # consumes the INNER verification dict, so pass v["verify"], not v:
              d = three_pass.pass3_decide(v["verify"], block_threshold=..., blocking_enabled=...)
  ```

  `repo_root=REAL_REPO_CHECKOUT` is passed **explicitly** to `pass2_verify` **and** the
  `gate_read_root(handle)` context is entered — both are required; in `local` mode the
  handle leaves the code root as the in-place checkout while still marking a deliberate gate
  session (`gate_source.py:105-118`). Record every vote's `decision` and the **existing**
  Pass-2 binary sub-answers in the current `PASS2_TOOL`/`GRADED` schema (`three_pass.py`).
  `asserted_capability_confirmed` is **R5's future addition** and does NOT exist yet — E6
  does not record it; E6 measures the reliability of the *existing* judge, which is the
  prerequisite R5 depends on. The agreement metric (below) is computed over `decision` —
  not over any R5 field.
- **Per-vote infra exclusion (defined concretely).** `pass3_decide` returns
  `{"decision": "indeterminate", "reason": "no-verification"}` **only** when its argument
  is falsy — i.e. when `v["verify"]` is `None` (Pass-2 returned no verdict: an error or
  agentic-no-verdict result; its sole indeterminate path, verified in
  `three_pass.pass3_decide`). That is an execution failure, not a stable judge decision, so
  E6 **drops and re-runs** any vote with `decision == "indeterminate"` until 3 substantive
  votes (`block`/`advisory`/`dropped`) are collected per finding, capping retries and
  recording any finding that cannot reach 3 votes as an excluded, reported row (never
  silently padded).
- **Metric + floor.** Over the N findings × 3 votes, compute **Fleiss' κ** (raters = the
  3 interchangeable votes; subjects = findings; categories = the 4-value `decision`
  space) **and raw exact-agreement** (fraction of findings where all 3 votes are
  identical). **PASS iff κ ≥ 0.6 (Landis–Koch "substantial") AND raw agreement ≥ 0.8;**
  below **either** → FAIL, recorded as an **R5 blocker**. Both floors are reported
  because κ deflates under skewed base rates (the cohort is advisory-heavy), so raw
  agreement is the prevalence-robust co-floor.

### Experiment B — order-shuffle stability of the gate verdict

- **Sample frame (concrete).** `runs/corpus_sample.json` — 19 committed plan-review
  inputs that **carry full plan text** (the only committed plan-text corpus; the outcome
  and adjudication corpora store no plan text). The order-shuffle inclusion criterion is
  **≥3 top-level `##` sections**, because a plan needs 3 *distinct* permutations and a
  2-section plan has only `2! = 2` orderings — so ≥3 sections (`3! = 6` orderings)
  guarantees 3 distinct permutations are available. Verified in the committed file: of the
  19 inputs, **14 have ≥3 top-level `##` sections** (the permutable set); the 5 plans with
  <3 sections (one =2, four =1) are excluded from the shuffle denominator. **N = 14 plans**
  (each judged over exactly 3 distinct permutations, below).
- **The "≥20 container plans" contradiction is resolved by DROPPING the
  container-specific requirement.** Only 5 of the 19 inputs are containers
  (`has_children=true`: 3 epics + 2 stories) and the run corpora hold exactly one
  container-type ticket — a container-only shuffle is under-powered and irreproducible.
  Order-sensitivity is a **general** judge property: if the gate verdict is unstable under
  section shuffle at large, any new criterion (including R3's container criterion)
  inherits that instability, so a stable general-plan result is a **prerequisite** for
  trusting R3. The 5-plan container subset is reported **descriptively only** (not a
  gate).
- **Mechanism (verified execution recipe — the PUBLIC entrypoint, not raw
  `finalize_verdict`).** For each plan, a pure helper `permute_sections` generates **exactly
  3 distinct section-order permutations** by reordering the plan's top-level `##` section
  blocks (content preserved verbatim — only the block order changes). **Deterministic
  selection rule:** permutation 0 is the **identity** (the plan's original section order);
  permutations 1 and 2 are drawn by repeatedly `random.Random(SEED).shuffle`-ing the list
  of section indices — with a **pinned per-plan seed** `SEED = int(plan_id.split("-")[0], 16)`
  — and taking the next ordering that is **not already selected** (dedup against permutations
  0..k-1), so all 3 are distinct. Since every qualifying plan has ≥3 sections (≥6 orderings),
  3 distinct permutations always exist; the identical seed makes the selection reproducible.
  The concrete `section_order` (an index list) of each of the 3 is committed (below), so the
  experiment is re-runnable without re-deriving the shuffle. `finalize_verdict` cannot be
  called standalone (it requires
  an assembled `PlanContext` + Pass parts), so E6 drives the whole gate through the public
  entrypoint `rebar.llm.plan_review.review_plan` (`__init__.py:387`). Because `review_plan`
  reads the plan **from the ticket store**, section order is varied by pointing the ticket
  reads at a **throwaway store clone** — the store root and the code-grounding root are
  separable (`config.py:119-136` — `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` wins for ticket reads;
  `gate_dispatch.py:141-147` — store-root vs code-root are independent). Per permutation:

  ```
  1. set REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=<tmp clone of the tickets store>            # ticket reads only; real store untouched
  2. write the permuted plan as the ticket's description:  rebar edit <ticket_id> --description=<permuted>
  3. verdict = review_plan(ticket_id, source="local", repo_root=REAL_REPO_CHECKOUT,
                           sign=False, emit_sidecar=False, force=True)  # __init__.py:387
  ```

  `source="local"` + `repo_root=REAL_REPO_CHECKOUT` make code-grounding read the **real
  repo**; `sign=False` / `emit_sidecar=False` keep the run **non-mutating** (no attestation,
  no `REVIEW_RESULT` event) and `force=True` defeats idempotent review-reuse so every
  permutation is judged fresh (`__init__.py:508-518, 570-587`). Only the throwaway
  `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` clone is edited — the real tickets store is never written. Record the
  resulting `verdict`, applying the infra-INDETERMINATE exclusion defined above (re-run a
  permutation whose INDETERMINATE carries `coverage.llm_unavailable`/`verify_failed`).
  The frozen `{plan_id, permutation_index, section_order}` specs are committed to
  `runs/e6_ordershuffle_inputs.jsonl` for reproducibility.
- **Metric + floor.** Over 14 plans × 3 permutations, compute **Fleiss' κ** and **raw
  exact-agreement** on the `verdict` categories. **PASS iff κ ≥ 0.6 AND raw agreement ≥
  0.8;** below → FAIL, recorded as an **R3 prerequisite failure**. Secondary descriptive
  metric: mean per-plan Jaccard of the fired-criteria set across permutations (not gated).

### LLM-spend honesty

E6 **does** make repeated live, billable LLM calls — self-consistency and order-shuffle inherently require re-runs; there is no persisted-sidecar shortcut for a *stability* measurement. Spend is bounded and stated: **A = 50 findings × 3 votes = 150 agentic Pass-2 calls** (Pass-3 is deterministic/free); **B = 14 plans × 3 permutations = 42 full-gate runs**. This is deliberately a bounded sub-sample — not the 400-finding adjudication corpus nor the 628-row outcome corpus.

## Scope

- **`docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/e6_judge_reliability.py`** — the driver:
  builds frozen inputs (Exp A snapshot + Exp B permutations), runs the votes/permutations,
  and writes the agreement tables + summary. Exp A reuses `three_pass.pass2_verify` /
  `pass3_decide` inside a `gate_source.gate_read_root` session with an explicit
  `repo_root`; Exp B drives the public `rebar.llm.plan_review.review_plan` entrypoint
  against a throwaway `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` store clone (real store untouched). It does not
  modify any `src/rebar` code.
- **`docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/`** — committed inputs + outputs (all paths
  in the ACs below).
- **`tests/unit/test_e6_agreement.py`** — CI-collectable golden test for the pure helpers
  (`fleiss_kappa`, `raw_agreement`, `permute_sections`) on fixed fixtures; **no LLM**.
- **README writeup** — a new "E6 — judge reliability" section in
  `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/README.md`.
- **No `src/rebar` changes.** E6 measures the existing gate; R3/R5 later consume E6's
  recorded verdicts. Consumes `runs/adjudication_corpus.jsonl` (Exp A cohort) and
  `runs/corpus_sample.json` (Exp B plans), both already committed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Exp A run recorded.** `runs/e6_selfconsistency_inputs.jsonl` (N≥50 frozen
  cohort inputs, each `criterion ∈ {G6,E4,T3}` with non-empty `plan`) and
  `runs/e6_selfconsistency.jsonl` (3 votes/finding, each with `decision` and Pass-2
  binary sub-answers) both exist and are consistent.
  Proving:
  `python3 -c "import json; ins=[json.loads(l) for l in open('docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/e6_selfconsistency_inputs.jsonl')]; assert len(ins)>=50 and all(r['criterion'] in {'G6','E4','T3'} and r['plan'] for r in ins); v=[json.loads(l) for l in open('docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/e6_selfconsistency.jsonl')]; ids={r['finding_id'] for r in ins}; per={i:0 for i in ids}; [per.__setitem__(r['finding_id'], per[r['finding_id']]+1) for r in v]; assert all(c==3 for c in per.values()), per; print('OK', len(ins), 'findings x3 votes')"`

- [ ] **Exp A passes its floor (self-consistency).**
  `runs/e6_selfconsistency_agreement.csv` (one row per finding:
  `finding_id,criterion,decision_1,decision_2,decision_3,all_agree,modal_decision`) and
  `runs/e6_summary.json` record **Fleiss' κ AND raw agreement**; the summary states
  `self_consistency.pass == (kappa>=0.6 and raw_agreement>=0.8)`. A sub-floor result is
  recorded verbatim as an **R5 blocker** (not silently passed).
  Proving:
  `python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/e6_summary.json'))['self_consistency']; assert d['n_findings']>=50 and set(('fleiss_kappa','raw_agreement','pass'))<=set(d) and d['pass']==(d['fleiss_kappa']>=0.6 and d['raw_agreement']>=0.8); print('self-consistency', d)"`

- [ ] **Exp B run recorded (order-shuffle over the committed plan-text corpus).**
  `runs/e6_ordershuffle_inputs.jsonl` (the 14 plans from `corpus_sample.json` with ≥3
  top-level sections, each with exactly 3 **distinct** section-order permutations —
  identity + 2 seeded, deduped) and `runs/e6_ordershuffle.jsonl` (one
  `verdict ∈ {PASS,BLOCK,INDETERMINATE}` per plan×permutation, produced via `review_plan`,
  with infra-INDETERMINATE — `coverage` `llm_unavailable`/`verify_failed` —
  excluded-and-re-run per the mechanism above) exist and are complete.
  Proving:
  `python3 -c "import json,collections; ins=[json.loads(l) for l in open('docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/e6_ordershuffle_inputs.jsonl')]; byp=collections.defaultdict(set); [byp[r['plan_id']].add(tuple(r['section_order'])) for r in ins]; assert len(byp)>=14 and all(len(s)==3 for s in byp.values()), {k:len(v) for k,v in byp.items()}; o=[json.loads(l) for l in open('docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/e6_ordershuffle.jsonl')]; assert all(r['verdict'] in {'PASS','BLOCK','INDETERMINATE'} for r in o); print('OK', len(byp), 'plans x3 distinct permutations')"`

- [ ] **Exp B passes its floor (order-shuffle stability), with an explicit pass/fail … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: E6: judge reliability - self-consistency + order-shuffle for new sub-answer/criterion

# S3 — Gerrit project + LLM-Review label + submit requirement + submitWholeTopic

## Why
This is the gate's integrity rule: a change is submittable ONLY when the deterministic
`LLM-Review` vote is MAX and there are no unresolved comments. `copyCondition` avoids re-paying
for an expensive LLM review on a no-code-change re-upload; `submitWholeTopic` lands whole
reviewed features atomically. The integrity property is not just "the label gates submit" but
"ONLY the bot can set the label" — so a human cannot cast `LLM-Review` and bypass the gate.
Gerrit is pinned to **3.14.1** (d251 docker-compose), so every predicate/feature used here
(`-has:unresolved`, `copyCondition`, submit requirements) is above its minimum and was
validated to parse against live 3.14.1.

## What
- Create the `rebar` project in Gerrit (NoteDb).
- `LLM-Review` label in `refs/meta/config` (project.config): `function=NoBlock`; values `-1..+1`;
  **`copyCondition = changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE`** (peer-pattern correction). We deliberately do
  NOT include `changekind:TRIVIAL_REBASE`: a TRIVIAL_REBASE copies the vote even when the change
  was rebased onto a **different base** (diff is byte-identical but the base moved), which would
  certify a tree the LLM never reviewed against the new base — the "copyCondition certifies an
  unreviewed tree" risk the Opus red-team flagged. `NO_CODE_CHANGE` pins the parent tree, so it
  only carries the vote across a true no-op re-upload (e.g. commit-message-only edit). A real
  rebase therefore drops the vote and forces a fresh review (the safe default for a correctness
  gate). `function=NoBlock` is **required, not a free choice**: on 3.14.1 a blocking label
  function is rejected, so blocking comes from the submit requirement.
- Submit requirement (project.config): `submittableIf = label:LLM-Review=MAX AND -has:unresolved`.
  This is what blocks submit; the label is advisory on its own. Both predicates validated to
  parse (HTTP 200) on live Gerrit 3.14.1.
- `change.submitWholeTopic=true` — set in the **server-level** `gerrit.config` `[change]`
  section, NOT in project.config (it is a server-global key, silently ignored in project.config).
  GOTCHA (peer research): topics are **global + un-namespaced**, so a topic name reused in a repo
  the submitter can't see could silently block submit; for this single-repo PoC that risk is
  minimal, but adopt a topic naming convention (e.g. `rebar-<feature>`) and document it.
- Access controls: grant the auto-generated `label-LLM-Review` vote permission to the **Service
  Users** group; humans may push changes for review but cannot submit without the label and
  cannot themselves cast `LLM-Review`. The Service Users group is created/wired in **S4**; S3
  lands config that references it and is testable in S3 by an **admin** casting the vote.

## Scope
In: project + `LLM-Review` label (NO_CODE_CHANGE copyCondition) + submit requirement +
server-level topic config + the label ACL grant. The "only the bot votes" end-to-end proof is
completed in S4 (the bot account does not exist in S3); in S3 the vote is exercised by an admin.
Out: the bot account + event/vote wiring (S4); replication (S5); GitHub lockdown (S6). Gerrit
version is fixed upstream by d251 (3.14.1).

## Files
- `infra/gerrit/project.config` (pushed to `refs/meta/config`): label, submit requirement,
  `copyCondition=changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE`, ACL grant.
- `infra/gerrit/gerrit.config` (server-level): `[change]\n  submitWholeTopic = true`. (Impl
  note: same gerrit.config d251 mounts; S3 owns/patches the `[change]` section.)
- `infra/gerrit/setup-project.sh`: provisions the project + pushes `refs/meta/config`. Impl
  notes (not separate ACs): (a) **idempotent** — push a fully-declarative project.config via
  `git push HEAD:refs/meta/config`, guard project creation with check-before-create; (b)
  **auth** — needs Gerrit admin creds (HTTP password / SSH key), source documented (env/SSM),
  fail-fast if absent; (c) **dry-run/diff** mode before mutating the live instance.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A change can be pushed for review to the `rebar` project; submit is BLOCKED until
      `LLM-Review=+1` (MAX) AND no unresolved comments — verified by an admin casting the vote
      (the bot-only path is proven in S4). Both predicates parse + enforce on 3.14.1.
- [ ] The `label-LLM-Review` vote permission is granted **exclusively** to the Service Users
      group: a regular developer cannot cast `LLM-Review` (push `%l=LLM-Review+1` is rejected /
      not applied) while a Service-Users member can.
- [ ] `copyCondition=changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE` carries the vote across a no-code-change
      re-upload (e.g. commit-message-only amend) BUT a genuine rebase onto a moved base
      (TRIVIAL_REBASE) does NOT carry it — the vote is dropped and re-review is required.
      Verified on 3.14.1 by (a) a message-only amend keeping the vote and (b) a real rebase
      dropping it.
- [ ] `change.submitWholeTopic=true` is set in server-level `gerrit.config` `[change]` (NOT
      project.config), and demonstrated: two changes under one topic submit atomically and
      neither submits independently while its topic partner is open.
- [ ] The submit requirement is the SINGLE code-review vote in v1 (no human Code-Review / CI
      Verified yet — follow-on epic 1fa8). Record this deliberate single-gate stance + planned
      evolution in a brief ADR/note.
baseline.summary: infra: S3 — Gerrit project + LLM-Review label + submit requirement + submitWholeTopic

## Context

Langflow is NOT adopted (engine/editor); Langfuse is optional (OTLP trace sink only). Direction (A) approved; the plan reached an Opus-APPROVED v3 after a 3-round review loop.

The deterministic gate's SECURITY (signing/attestation/protected-tags/trust-boundary) is OUT OF SCOPE and tracked in epic 8a1c-fdaf-f57a-4104. Here the gate is an ordinary, unsecured example step.

## Context / Proven Defect

The 8322 close incident was rebar-debugged to a strict-tag ordering issue, not a recovery failure. The second verifier FAIL occurred at event timestamp 1786063291486790001 while the Gerrit criterion was still untagged; the exact `[operator-attested]` edit followed 37.30 seconds later at 1786063328784010001. ADR 0043 and `completion_verifier.md:81-86` intentionally treat every untagged criterion as codebase-verifiable, so rejecting ticket-only external evidence was correct.

The actionable defect is `COMPLETION_REMEDIATION_GUIDANCE` in `src/rebar/llm/completion.py:48-65`. It tells every FAIL caller that adding concrete evidence to a ticket comment will be considered on retry, but omits the exact `[operator-attested]` tag prerequisite for evidence that inherently lives outside the repository. The operator followed that incomplete guidance and incurred a second 240-request verifier run that could not pass by contract.

## Approach

- Preserve the generic guidance and existing no-force posture.
- State the two evidence channels affirmatively: repository-verifiable criteria require repository evidence (a comment may point the verifier to it); external evidence is admissible from a concrete ticket attestation only when the criterion begins with the exact `[operator-attested]` tag.
- Keep malformed or untagged criteria on the existing codebase-verifiable default; do not weaken ADR 0043 injection boundaries or completion judgment.
- Strengthen the existing interface test for FAIL remediation so it requires the exact tag prerequisite and the untagged-external fallback.

## Testing

- RED: the existing remediation interface test, strengthened to require `operator-attested`, the exact tag, and the untagged external-evidence limitation, fails against current guidance.
- GREEN: focused interface test passes after the guidance-only change.
- Run focused completion-verifier interface tests, lint, typecheck, and the default test suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every FAIL remediation distinguishes repository-verifiable evidence from external operator-attested evidence.
- [x] The remediation names the exact `[operator-attested]` tag prerequisite and says an untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone.
- [x] The guidance remains generic, does not advertise force/bypass, and does not change completion-verdict semantics.
- [x] [operator-attested] The strengthened remediation interface test is observed RED before the fix and GREEN after it.
- [x] [operator-attested] Lint, typecheck, and the default test suite pass.
baseline.summary: Completion FAIL remediation omits operator-attested tag prerequisite

## Context
Cloud summary writes currently cross ACLI subprocess behavior and a shared REST helper that retries three times with 2s/5s waits. The selected route must consume only the shared logical budget without weakening unrelated callers.

## Outcome
Implement one Cloud summary write invocation and primary-store observation under the S1 contract. Each write launches one ACLI process; summary recovery performs one REST request with no inner sleep.

## Plan
1. Add sanitized historical exit/stdout/stderr fixtures, including the real exit-1 unauthorized shape, and fail loud on unknown shapes.
2. Execute one `acli jira workitem edit` process per physical write invocation. Preserve POSIX process-group and non-POSIX child cleanup.
3. Add a per-call retry policy to `_rest_urlopen_with_retry`. `get_issue_by_rest` summary recovery alone selects one attempt/no sleep; every existing caller retains three attempts and 2s/5s waits.
4. Classify auth/TLS/permission/invalid requests as permanent; eligible network, 429, and retryable 5xx outcomes return metadata to the shared budget rather than replaying locally.
5. Observe the primary REST issue resource, never indexed ACLI JQL, before any ambiguous replay.
6. Emit exactly one redacted completion log for every terminal/exhausted outcome or cleanup failure. Include only logical id, disposition, invocation count, request count, cleanup status, `retry_not_before`, and one redacted message capped at 512 Unicode code points; cap the whole serialized log at 1,024 Unicode code points.

## Testing
Stateful fakes and real child-process tests assert process/request counts, cleanup, classification, redaction, exact completion-log fields and bounds, one-log emission cardinality, and neighbor retry behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] One Cloud write invocation launches exactly one ACLI process.
- [ ] Summary recovery performs one primary-store REST request with no inner sleep or JQL.
- [ ] All unrelated REST callers retain three attempts with 2s/5s waits.
- [ ] Permanent and transient outcome classes map to the shared contract without adapter replay.
- [ ] Historical triples decode deterministically and unknown triples do not retry.
- [ ] Timeout cleanup passes for POSIX process groups and non-POSIX child processes.
- [ ] Operation diagnostics hold at most eight entries and every message is redacted before its 512-Unicode-code-point cap.
- [ ] Every terminal/exhausted outcome or cleanup failure emits exactly one completion log with only logical id, disposition, invocation/request counts, cleanup status, `retry_not_before`, and one redacted message capped at 512 Unicode code points; the whole log is at most 1,024 Unicode code points.

## Out of scope
Core dispatch cutover and Jira DC execution.
baseline.summary: RP-03 S1 T2 — Execute and observe one Cloud summary postcondition

## Context / Problem
Advanced bridge/reconciler, audit, LLM/review, workflow, identity, and gate commands mix inline argparse construction with manual dispatch. Their current `--help` behavior is also the source of the 21 unsafe/incomplete top-level help forms. The grammar must become reusable without importing optional runtimes.

## Approach
Inventory every registered advanced grammar in `src/rebar/_cli/`, standalone verification/auth command modules, and the reconciler request CLI. For each family:

1. Extract existing argparse construction into the S2a side-effect-free factory contract; migrate manual nested dispatch where required.
2. Switch the selected runtime handler to the same factory in the same change.
3. Keep parser factories in lean modules: no Pydantic AI/provider, FastAPI/UI, Jira transport, workflow executor, metrics, tracing, or other optional runtime imports.
4. Reuse argument-definition helpers between canonical nested bridge forms and `bridge-fsck`, `bridge-probe`, `jira-onboard`, and hidden `bridge-status`; only `prog`, visibility, and replacement epilog differ.
5. Preserve handler-owned nested command selection, lean modes, backend/mode selection timing, diagnostics, streams, and exit codes. Optional capability enforcement remains S4 and never occurs during parser construction.
6. Register all parser references and make every visible advanced route generation-ready, without changing top-level help routing yet.

Families include bridge and reconcile, audit, prompt/criteria/LLM setup, review/scan/explain/sign operations, workflow, config/identity verification/trusted-environment/remote-certificate commands, and enrichment.

## Compatibility and Rollback
No top-level help cutover occurs here. Current execution behavior remains invariant. The later help normalization is approved, but generated bytes do not become authoritative until S2d. Each family reverts with its handler switch; no stored data changes.

## Testing
Use parser unit matrices plus real subprocess/interface tests for nested selection, help-safe parser construction, aliases, lean modes, failures, streams, and exit codes. Install import blockers for every heavy optional module and use negative controls that prove selected execution still imports what its mode actually requires.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every registered advanced command and nested subcommand runtime uses one S2a parser factory; no inline/manual duplicate grammar remains.
- [ ] Canonical and compatibility bridge spellings share argument-definition helpers while retaining approved `prog`, replacement, visibility, and historical usage behavior.
- [ ] Parser construction succeeds in the no-extras environment and imports no handler executor, provider, UI, Jira transport, or other optional runtime.
- [ ] Production-path tests show no unapproved delta in nested selection, accepted/rejected argv, diagnostics, streams, exit codes, or lean-mode availability.
- [ ] Every advanced route has a valid factory reference and is ready for deterministic S2d generation.
baseline.summary: RP-05 S2c — Migrate advanced command grammars to lean argparse factories

# Discovered while closing the map-staleness gap on [rebar:259b-b7da-a346-4785] (Gerrit 1394)

259b now makes the capability map's **provenance** checkable: `run_metadata.json` derives the harness digest from the Dockerfile's `FROM` line instead of a hand-copied constant, and `docs/jira-dc-capability-map.md` records the digest it was measured against, asserted against that pin by `tests/unit/test_jira_dc_capability_map_workflow.py`. A re-pin now lands red until the map is regenerated.

## What that does NOT cover

The staleness gate keys on the **digest**. It detects "these answers describe a different image". It cannot detect **"these answers are wrong about THIS image"** — and that is the failure mode this epic has actually hit:

* `docs/jira-dc-capability-map.md` recorded that DC rejected a 255-char label. A dedicated live
  cell later posted 254- and 255-char labels to the SAME pinned image and both were accepted.
  The entry was retracted. The digest never changed, so no digest-based check could have caught
  it.

The mechanism is that the map's answers are produced by an **agentic LLM run** summarising raw REST evidence. The evidence in `evidence.json` was correct; the *reading* of it was wrong. So the map has a trust boundary at exactly the point the ticket wanted removed — 259b's own words: "otherwise we have swapped 'discovering from the instance' for 'trusting a model', which is worse."

## The shape of a fix (not prescribing it)

A **deterministic, non-LLM re-measurement** pass: a script that reads the committed contract and re-asserts each claim with a fixed REST call and an exact comparison, exiting non-zero on divergence — no model in the measurement path. `scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py` (bug 1019) is the existing precedent for a deterministic probe alongside the agentic map, and `_assert_project_capabilities` in `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py` is the precedent for "declared contract, fail loudly on divergence". The agentic run stays useful for DISCOVERY (open questions, new checklist items); it just should not be the last word on a value the harness then depends on.

## Also recorded: one measurement gap left open by 259b

`docs/jira-dc-capability-map.md` notes the description/comment 32767 boundary is a **coverage gap** — `jira.text.field.character.limit=32767` was read from the instance, but a literal 32K+ payload was never written, so the limit is confirmed as *configured*, not as *observed*. That needs an amd64 live run; it cannot be settled from a dev worktree.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] every claim the harness DEPENDS on is re-assertable by a deterministic (no-LLM) pass whose
      comparison is exact, and which exits non-zero on divergence
- [ ] the pass is runnable against the pinned image on demand, and its failure message names the
      committed claim that diverged
- [ ] the description/comment ceiling is measured with a real over-limit payload and read-back,
      closing the recorded coverage gap
- [ ] the agentic map's role is documented as DISCOVERY, with the deterministic pass as the
      authority for anything the harness relies on
baseline.summary: The capability map's answers are LLM-summarised, so a wrong answer at an unchanged digest is still undetectable

## Why

GitHub CodeQL flags 28 remaining open code-scanning alerts on `main`: 27 `py/path-injection` and 1 `py/stack-trace-exposure`. All are genuine (the false positives were already dismissed under 5b57). They collapse to a small number of root causes:

1. **Unvalidated ticket-id → filesystem path.** `rebar._ids.resolve_ticket_id()` has a fast
   path that returns the caller's raw string verbatim when it happens to name an existing
   directory (`_ids.py:152`), *before* any regex/allowlist check. A traversing/absolute id
   (`../sibling`, `/etc/x`) is handed back as if canonical, then callers join it to the
   tracker dir. This is the source for ~18 sinks (the reducer read path + `reads.py`).
2. **Sidecar `resolve_ticket_id(id) or id` fallback.** The audit readers in
   `completion_sidecar.py` and `plan_review/sidecar.py` fall back to the *raw* id when
   resolution returns `None`, so even a hardened resolver is bypassed — the raw string builds
   a `os.path.join(tracker, id)` → `os.listdir`/`open` (sinks 112/119/156/163, 184/192).
3. **Editor prompt-id traversal.** The workflow editor server's `/prompt?id=` handler builds
   `<repo>/.rebar/prompts/{pid}.md` from an unvalidated query param (`editor_server.py`
   158/159); the packaged branch is allowlist-guarded but the project-override branch is not.
4. **Stack-trace exposure.** The review-bot `/rerun` 502 returns the Gerrit exception string
   in the response body (`review_bot/app.py:266`).

Trust model: rebar is a single-tenant local tool; the realistic vector is the MCP/CLI confused-deputy (an agent driven by untrusted ticket content passing a crafted id). Severity is Low–Medium, but the fixes are low-risk (no legitimate ticket id / prompt id contains a path separator, `..`, or is absolute) and retire the whole alert class.

## What

Four containment barriers, mirroring the taint map:

- **`_ids.py`** — add `_is_safe_segment(name)` and reject non-segment ids at the top of
  `resolve_ticket_id`; rewrite the fast path to normalize + containment-check the candidate
  against `tracker_dir` and return the directory's `basename` (separator-free by
  construction). Sanitizes the 18 downstream sinks that build paths from the return value.
- **`completion_sidecar.py` / `plan_review/sidecar.py`** — drop the `... or ticket_id`
  fallback in the filesystem-path readers; on `None` return the function's existing empty
  result (`None`/`[]`/`0`). The hardened resolver's fast path already subsumes the fallback's
  only legitimate purpose (an id that already names a real dir), so this is behavior-preserving
  for valid input.
- **`editor_server.py`** — contain the prompt-id path in `_raw_prompt_text` (resolve +
  `is_relative_to` the prompts dir) and reject separator-bearing ids at the handler entry.
- **`review_bot/app.py`** — log the Gerrit exception server-side; return a generic 502 body.

Default CodeQL query suite unchanged; this is a `src/rebar` change plus new unit tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `resolve_ticket_id` returns `None` for any id that is not a safe single path segment
      (rejects `../x`, absolute paths, `..`/`.`, `/`/`\` separators, and leading-dot names),
      and its fast path returns a separator-free canonical directory name — so no untrusted id
      escapes the tracker directory. Valid full/short/alias/Jira-key/prefix ids still resolve.
- [ ] The audit sidecar readers in `completion_sidecar.py` and `plan_review/sidecar.py` no
      longer fall back to the raw unresolved id; when resolution fails they return their empty
      result instead of building a filesystem path from unvalidated input.
- [ ] The workflow editor `/prompt` read (`_raw_prompt_text`) cannot read a file outside
      `<repo>/.rebar/prompts/`; a traversing prompt id yields no file (returns `None`/404).
- [ ] The review-bot `/rerun` 502 response body contains no exception/stack-trace text; the
      detail is logged server-side.
- [ ] New unit tests assert traversal rejection for the resolver, one sidecar reader, and the
      editor prompt read, and assert the review-bot 502 body carries no exception detail.
      `make lint` and the affected test suites pass.
baseline.summary: Harden ticket-id/prompt-id path handling + review-bot error body (retire remaining CodeQL path-injection & stack-trace alerts)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The completion verifier receives only the fenced ticket_context (description + comments, gate_ops.py assemble step) — zero file contents. Every file is discovered agentically: measured across five live verifier runs, 84-158 requests x ~4-6s each, dominated by read_file/search_files round-trips, and all four captured runaway loops were search_files repeat signatures — the model hunting for text it expects to exist. Wall-clock cost is round-trips, not tokens: runs already cache-read 8.7M of 8.8M input tokens, but that history was assembled one tool round-trip at a time. Overlap analysis of the four live gate traces against the closing subtree's file_impact union shows 67-82% of distinct file reads are covered by declared file_impact — the verifier spends its opening requests re-fetching files the tickets already name. NOTE: all four captured traces are CLOSE-path (graph=False) runaway loops; none exercise the graph=True deep-review path.

## Approach

PRE-FETCH, do not restrict (operator-ratified direction): append a bounded, clearly-labelled prefetched-content section to the byte-stable leading part of the fenced verifier context — the ticket's declared file_impact contents plus the referencing commits' diffs — while keeping the full tool surface untouched so the agent still explores beyond the prefetch. Assistance, not a ceiling.

### Which file_impact set each entrypoint prefetches (close gate is graph=False)

The completion CLOSE gate (`_commands.transition`) passes `graph=False` (gate_ops.py:133-143): an epic close verifies its OWN completion criteria, not its whole descendant subtree — re-deriving graph here was the removed runaway bug that blew the step budget (gate_ops.py:138-140). The prefetch MUST honour that same boundary, keyed off the `graph` flag `assemble_context` already receives (operations.py:78):

- **Close path (graph=False, the dominant runaway case):** prefetch ONLY the closing ticket's OWN declared file_impact contents + its referencing-commit diffs. No subtree union, no descendant walk.
- **Standalone deep-review path (`verify-completion --graph`, graph=True):** prefetch the subtree file_impact union, ranked (below). This is the only entrypoint that legitimately sees descendants.

### assemble_context is SHARED — prefetch is opt-in, default off

`operations.assemble_context` (operations.py:78) is also called by the generic dimension-review op `_review_ticket_impl` (operations.py:161) and its workflow wrapper (review_workflows.py:53), NOT only the completion gate (gate_ops.py:144). Keying the prefetch purely off the existing `graph` flag would inject the prefetched-file-contents section into a plain `review_ticket --graph` dimension review, where the completion-verifier trust paragraph does not apply. Therefore add an explicit opt-in parameter `prefetch: PrefetchSpec | None = None` to `assemble_context`, default `None`. Only gate_ops.py (the completion gate) passes a spec; `_review_ticket_impl` / `review_workflows` keep passing nothing, so their assembled output stays BYTE-IDENTICAL. The `graph` flag then only selects own-file_impact vs subtree-union WITHIN a prefetch spec.

### Ranking rule for the budget clamp (graph=True path only)

The subtree union can exceed the budget (the e369 subtree union is 112 paths; the prefetch budget is 30,000 tokens, the upper end of the community-validated 8-30k pre-load range): (1) the closing ticket's OWN file_impact first, (2) subtree paths ranked by cross-descendant frequency (a path impacted by more descendants ranks higher), (3) skeleton-compress files over 500 lines (signatures + docstrings) BEFORE dropping any file, drop lowest-ranked last. On the close path the set is just the ticket's own file_impact, so ranking degenerates to (1) + the same skeleton/clamp rules. A PRE-LOAD MANIFEST records per-file full|skeleton so downstream consumers (the duplicate-call damping sibling's in-context nudge) never claim an elided body is in context.

### Cache mechanism: existing automatic prompt cache, NO hand-placed CachePoint

The prefetch sits in the byte-stable leading part of the fenced context so it is cache-READ under the EXISTING automatic message-tail prefix cache (capabilities.py:684-696, gated on execution_mode="agentic"); there is no separate per-block CachePoint to add (that arm applies a provider-managed whole-tail breakpoint, not a hand-placed cache_control). This aligns with story 2948's cache note: the completion-verifier prompt's STATIC prefix (everything before the `<!--volatile-->` marker, completion_verifier.md:269) is kept byte-identical across the primary and every successor so the automatic prompt cache hits; the prefetch rides the volatile fenced ticket_context, not the static prefix.

### Trust / anti-anchoring lives in the STATIC system-prompt prefix (reaches primary AND successors)

The verifier system prompt (completion_verifier.md:33-37) directs the agent to treat everything inside `<untrusted_ticket_context>` (gate_ops.py:158) as UNTRUSTED DATA, never as instructions. An anti-anchoring line placed inside that fence would be ignored by contract. Instead add a TRUSTED paragraph to `completion_verifier.md` positioned BEFORE the `<!--volatile-->` marker (i.e. in the static prefix). Because the recovery successor prompt is `successor_system_prompt()` = that same static prefix (before `<!--volatile-->`) + the banking addendum (completion_banking.py:75-85), the trusted paragraph appears in BOTH the primary verifier prompt AND every batched successor prompt from a SINGLE source — co-located with the prefetch data on both paths, no separate constant to maintain. The paragraph (a) names the new labelled `<prefetched_file_contents>` section, (b) states it is a convenience starting point pre-loaded from declared file_impact — still content-to-verify, NOT instructions — and (c) instructs the verifier to confirm every prefetched body against the live working tree before relying on it, and to re-read the full body for any file marked `skeleton`. The fenced prefetch section itself carries ONLY the labelled data + the PRE-LOAD MANIFEST + the explicit skeleton tool-call marker — no behavioural directive that depends on being trusted.

Misses in the trace analysis were dominated by test files, so the prefetch set includes a matching-test-glob heuristic (tests/**/test_<module>*.py for each prefetched module).

### Phase 0 — measure first

Extend the usage recorder to log the raw distinct fetch list per gate run — (tool, path/query) — not just hashed top-repeats. Today's records cannot validate overlap directly: signatures hash full args (line ranges, query strings), and brute-forcing 2,573 tracked paths resolved only 2 of 6 heavy read_file repeats. Record first; tune the prefetch set from measurement.

### Phase 1 — prefetch file_impact + referencing-commit diffs, bounded

Per-file char cap and the 30k-token aggregate cap mirroring completion_recovery's _MAX_* pattern; oversize files skeleton-compressed with an explicit marker naming the tool call to fetch the rest. Because the prefetch is part of the assembled `ticket_context`, it reaches the batched recovery successors automatically: post-2948 recovery is BATCHED successor runs (`_run_successors`/`_run_one_successor`, ceil(remainder/batch_cap), ≤8 criteria/batch — the per-criterion fan-out was deleted by story 2948), and `successor_instructions` (completion_banking.py:118) embeds the same `ticket_context` verbatim. The prefetch is therefore sent once per batch (a handful of batches, not per criterion) and cache-read after the first via the byte-stable static prefix. `physical_context_ceiling` (completion_recovery.py:108) already bounds `len(context)` for every primary/successor run; the 30k aggregate prefetch cap keeps the assembled context under that ceiling, and the prefetch bytes are included when the recovery inputs are validated against it so an oversize prefetch is trimmed (not overflowed into the hard "context bound exceeded" refusal).

## Scope

- src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py — Phase 0: record raw distinct fetch list per gate run.
- src/rebar/llm/operations.py — add opt-in `prefetch: PrefetchSpec | None = None` to `assemble_context` (default None → `_review_ticket_impl`/review_ticket callers byte-unchanged); build the prefetched-content section + manifest when a spec is passed, selecting own-file_impact vs subtree-union by the graph flag; include referencing-commit diffs.
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py — Phase 1: pass a PrefetchSpec into assemble_context for the completion gate only; the fenced context now carries the labelled prefetch section.
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py — include the prefetch bytes in the physical_context_ceiling input validation so an oversize prefetch is trimmed; no separate cache_prefix (the prefetch rides ticket_context and the static system prefix already cache-hits across batches).
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md — TRUSTED paragraph BEFORE the `<!--volatile-->` marker describing the prefetched-file-contents section and the confirm-against-working-tree / re-read-skeleton rule (automatically inherited by successor_system_prompt).
- tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_prefetch.py — new: ranking, clamp, manifest, skeleton marker, toolset pin, graph=False-vs-True set selection, assemble_context prefetch=None no-op for the generic review callers, successor context carries the prefetch, ceiling accounting, and a static-prefix system-prompt test asserting the trusted paragraph precedes `<!--volatile-->` (so it is in both primary and successor prompts).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Phase 0: every agentic gate run records its distinct fetch list (tool name + primary path/query arg) in the usage log by default; checked by a unit test asserting the recorded shape for a run with known tool calls.
- [x] Overlap measurement exists: an analysis entry point reports the fraction of recorded fetches covered by a ticket's file_impact; checked by running it on recorded data.
- [x] Phase 1: the completion verifier's context includes a labelled prefetch section with ranked file_impact contents and referencing-commit diffs, bounded per-file and by the 30k-token aggregate cap; unit test pins the assembly (ranking order, bounds, skeleton marker, label).
- [x] Entrypoint boundary honoured: on the close path (graph=False) the prefetch set is the closing ticket's OWN file_impact only (no subtree walk); the subtree union + frequency ranking applies only on the graph=True deep-review path; unit test pins both selections.
- [x] Opt-in / no-op for shared callers: `assemble_context` prefetch defaults to None, and `_review_ticket_impl` / review_workflows call sites produce byte-identical context to today (no prefetch section); unit test pins the no-op for a graph=True generic review call.
- [x] The pre-load manifest records per-file full|skeleton and is exposed to the tool-wrapping seam; unit test pins its shape.
- [x] The tool surface is unchanged: the verifier retains read_file/search_files/list_directory; unit test pins the toolset with prefetch enabled.
- [x] Trusted anti-anchoring: the confirm-against-working-tree / re-read-skeleton guidance lives in the completion_verifier.md static prefix BEFORE `<!--volatile-->` (not inside the untrusted fence), and names the prefetched-contents section; a unit test asserts the paragraph precedes `<!--volatile-->` (so `successor_system_prompt` inherits it) and that the fenced section carries no behavioural directive.
- [x] Recovery successors receive the prefetch via the shared assembled ticket_context (batched successor runs, not per-criterion), and the prefetch bytes are included in the physical_context_ceiling input validation so an oversize prefetch is trimmed rather than raising; unit test pins that a successor's assembled context carries the prefetch and the ceiling accounting.
- [x] Post-clamp coverage recorded PER ENTRYPOINT: (a) the clamped CLOSE-path (own file_impact) set's coverage is computed against the four recorded live (graph=False) traces' distinct reads and recorded on this ticket; (b) the clamped graph=True (subtree-union) set's coverage is computed against a NAMED synthetic subtree fixture (the e369 112-path union), NOT the close-path traces, and recorded. The unclamped 67-82% figure does not carry over to either.
- [x] Live Bedrock A/B before ship (session experiment, not in unit suite): BASELINE is defined as a verifier-scale run on the same real closed ticket's material with prefetch DISABLED, captured immediately before the prefetch run (same tool surface, same ticket, same config otherwise); its request count and verdict class are recorded first. The prefetch run then reduces total request count by at least 20% versus that baseline and produces an equal verdict class; both request counts and verdicts recorded on this ticket.
- [x] make lint and make typecheck clean; full CI marker suite matches the pre-existing baseline.

## Testing

Held-out unit oracle for context assembly + toolset pins (python -m pytest tests/unit/workflow/ -q): ranking order over a synthetic subtree, close-path (graph=False) own-file_impact selection vs graph=True subtree-union selection, assemble_context prefetch=None no-op for the generic review callers, aggregate clamp with skeleton-before-drop, manifest shape, truncation marker text, successor context carries the prefetch, physical_context_ceiling accounting for prefetch bytes, and a static-prefix system-prompt test asserting the trusted anti-anchoring paragraph precedes `<!--volatile-->` and names the prefetch section. Phase-0 recorder shape test alongside existing usage_log tests. Live A/B on Bedrock recorded as ticket comments with usage-log figures: baseline (prefetch off) then prefetch run.
baseline.summary: Prefetch file_impact contents into the completion verifier's context

## Context / Problem
S1-S6 provide the new composition paths, but RP-04 is not complete while legacy ambient reads can return or future code can bypass the central seam. The recovered design explicitly requires an AST ownership guard, generated operator documentation, hosted parity/delta canaries, and contract-phase removal. The existing `scripts/check_config_reads.py` proves each schema field is consumed; it does not prove only approved owners consume configuration.

## Outcome
Enforce centralized ownership with a separate deterministic AST gate, wire it into the portable local gate and CI, generate configuration/security lifecycle documentation from the authoritative registry, run final canaries, and remove legacy facades only after all proof passes.

## Plan
1. Add `scripts/check_config_ownership.py` and an explicit registry of approved composition roots/provider boundaries. Derive configurable environment spellings and provider credential names from the authoritative config/adapter registries, and fail when a newly declared name lacks one owner. Reject direct/aliased `load_config`, `os.getenv`, `os.environ.get`, `os.environ[...]`, literal-`getattr` equivalents, backend property reload, credential reads, and configurable adapter defaults below those seams. Test-only controls and protocol constants require exact path+symbol+rationale entries, not broad path globs.
2. Add synthetic red-proof fixtures for direct and import/local-alias call forms, every prohibited environment access form, and self-tests that deliberately insert a new bypass or registry name without an owner. The gate reports path, symbol, access kind, and owning seam. Legacy migration exceptions are exact, shrink-only, and empty before close. Document that this deterministic change detector covers conventional static forms rather than claiming to be a security sandbox; S1-S6 behavioral oracles remain authoritative.
3. Wire the guard through `make lint` (portable/no-CI path) and the build workflow; extend CI parity tests so the workflow cannot silently omit it. Keep `check_config_reads.py` as the opposite-direction field-consumption gate.
4. Generate the config precedence/source/lifecycle reference in `docs/config.md` and a new indexed `docs/security.md` from schema plus ownership/secret-name registries; update `docs/README.md` and `docs/architecture.md` navigation. Drift checks cover MCP/CLI exposure, restart/redeploy rotation, native refresh, observability exception, subprocess limitations, and explicit behavior deltas.
5. Run focused suites and bounded Anthropic/Bedrock, AWS review-bot/op-cert, reconciler check/dry-run/bounded-live canaries. Compare redacted snapshot fingerprints and provider-neutral outcomes; record each approved delta. Then delete legacy ambient/per-job facades, migration switches, and exception entries.

## Testing (RED -> GREEN)
- Structural change-detector tests feed synthetic modules for direct/import/local aliases, attribute/subscript/literal-`getattr` environment access, backend property reload, newly registered credential/config names, configurable duplicate defaults, broad/glob exceptions, missing rationales, and expired migration exceptions; each must fail with the expected diagnostic.
- Real-tree held-out tests assert the ownership registry maps each approved read to one seam, the legacy exception set is empty, generated docs are current, and local/CI invocation exists.
- Behavioral regression suites from S1-S6 remain the correctness oracle; the AST gate supplements rather than substitutes for them.
- [operator-attested] Live evidence includes run/change ids, timestamps, selected provider/auth-source kind, retry/cache counters where applicable, redacted fingerprint/outcome, and rollback decision. No credential value/path is recorded.

## Compatibility / rollback
Do not remove a legacy facade until its focused suite and bounded live path pass. Before removal, rollback selects the facade. At contract phase, retain only the S1 snapshot-envelope compatibility floor; rollback below it is unsupported and documented. Stored ticket/event/bridge/binding formats remain unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every synthetic prohibited access/alias/default/exception and unowned-new-registry-name fixture fails the ownership gate with path, symbol, access kind, and expected owning seam; clean approved fixtures pass.
- [ ] `make lint` and CI execute both ownership-direction and existing field-consumption gates, and parity tests fail if either invocation disappears.
- [ ] The real tree has no direct ambient config/credential read, backend reload, or configurable adapter default below approved seams; every declared config/credential name has one owner, the legacy exception set is empty, and no exception uses a path glob.
- [ ] Generated config/security/operator docs are byte-current with schema/ownership registries and cover every lifecycle, precedence, restart, observability, subprocess, and behavior-delta topic named in the epic.
- [ ] All S1-S6 behavioral suites pass after legacy removal; structural gates remain change detectors, not substitutes for those observable oracles.
- [ ] [operator-attested] Bounded provider, AWS review-bot/op-cert, and reconciler check/dry-run/live canaries pass with required redacted evidence and no unauthorized fallback/leakage.
- [ ] Legacy facades, switches, per-job SSM path, ambient reloads, and migration exceptions are removed only after their proof passes; documented rollback retains the snapshot-envelope compatibility floor.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
`.rebar/enrich-drain.lock` is an `O_EXCL` existence lock with no owner stamp and no staleness path. `enrich_drain._acquire_advisory_lock` creates it and never writes to the fd; `_release_advisory_lock` unlinks it. A drainer dying between those calls leaks a 0-byte file PERMANENTLY: every later drain sees `FileExistsError`, returns `None`, and `drain()` logs at INFO and returns `{"skipped": "lock-held"}` — enrichment stops with no error and no visible signal. `rebar doctor`'s new lock-health report (513e-35e1-2c80-4428) found exactly this on this host's live tracker: a 0-byte drain lock held ~26 days with no drain process alive, silently skipping enrichment for a month.

## Approach
Give the drain lock the ownership discipline the store's mkdir write lock already has, by REUSING that machinery rather than writing a third locking dialect.

1. **Stamp on acquire.** After the `O_EXCL` create succeeds, write
   `lock_owner._owner_stamp()` (the existing v2 `host=/ns=/pid=/start=` line) into the
   file — best-effort like `lock.py`'s mkdir stamp write, since a failed stamp leaves an
   unstamped lock the ceiling still bounds.
2. **Adjudicate on collision.** Extract the decision table already inside
   `lock_owner._mkdir_lock_is_stale` into a shared core

       _stamp_is_stale(stamp, artifact_path, *, fcntl_held, unrecognised_via_ceiling)

   taking an already-read stamp plus the path whose mtime measures the hold age.
   `_mkdir_lock_is_stale` becomes a thin reader that delegates; a new sibling
   `stamped_file_is_stale(path)` reads the stamp from the FILE and delegates to the same
   core with `fcntl_held=False`. No new threshold, no new pid probe: the pid-recycle
   qualification, the refuse-without-proof branches and the 1h
   `_MKDIR_LOCK_STALE_CEILING_S` backstop are inherited as-is.

   `unrecognised_via_ceiling` is the ONLY behavioural knob; it selects what happens to a
   stamp that is not v2 (empty or any other unrecognised text), and nothing else in the
   core branches on it — `fcntl_held` does not and cannot select it.

   - `_mkdir_lock_is_stale` passes `False`, preserving TODAY's routing exactly: non-v2 →
     `_legacy_stamp_is_stale`. Worked example: an owner file containing `""` parses
     non-v2, reaches `_legacy_stamp_is_stale("")`, finds no `:`, returns False — the same
     answer as today, so the mkdir leg is unchanged.
   - `stamped_file_is_stale` passes `True`: non-v2 is NO PROOF OF OWNERSHIP and falls to
     the ceiling. Worked example: the leaked 0-byte `enrich-drain.lock`, 26 days old,
     parses non-v2, takes the ceiling branch, exceeds 3600s, returns True — reclaimable.
     The same file 5s old is under the ceiling and returns False — respected.

   The asymmetry is load-bearing: the mkdir lock has a real legacy `<host>:<pid>` dialect
   to honour; the drain lock never had one, so "unrecognised" there can only mean
   "unstamped orphan" — the exact pre-fix shape this bug must make reclaimable.
3. **Bounded, loud reclaim.** On `FileExistsError`, ask `stamped_file_is_stale`. If it
   refuses, skip as today. If it says stale, log at WARNING naming the holder stamp and
   the age (mirroring `_reclaim_mkdir_lock`), unlink, and retry the create EXACTLY ONCE;
   a second `FileExistsError` means another drainer won the race, so we skip. No loop. A
   live, corroborated holder is never broken because the shared core refuses it.
4. **Attributable skip.** `drain()`'s skip log moves from INFO to WARNING and names the
   holder decoded from the stamp, so a wedge is visible without running doctor.

The drain lock is advisory only (it stops two drain PROCESSES from redundant work; the queue claim is separately optimistic), so a lost reclaim race costs one redundant drain, never correctness — which is why one bounded retry needs no arbitration.

**Prerequisite.** `rebar doctor`'s drain leg reports `not-assessable` from `_commands/doctor_locks.py`, a NEW module created by task 513e-35e1-2c80-4428 (Gerrit 1701, `LLM-Review +1`, awaiting `Verified`), absent from today's tree. This change is COMMITTED to landing as 1701's stacked child — authored on top of 1701's commit, so `doctor_locks.py` is a guaranteed edit target and 1701 submits first; if 1701 merges first the stack collapses to a plain rebase. The edge is `relates_to`, not `depends_on`: a blocking edge to a still-open prerequisite makes `review-plan` fast-fail without running, and 513e is in flight, not waiting.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_store/lock_owner.py` — extract `_stamp_is_stale` core; add
  `stamped_file_is_stale`; `_mkdir_lock_is_stale` delegates (behaviour preserved).
- `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` — stamp on acquire; stale-reclaim with one bounded
  retry; holder description helper; WARNING skip log.
- `src/rebar/_commands/doctor_locks.py` — the drain leg decodes the stamp and reports a
  real staleness verdict instead of `not-assessable`; `schemas/doctor.schema.json`,
  `_cli/help/doctor.txt` and `docs/cli-reference.md` follow if its vocabulary changes.
- `tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py`, `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor_locks.py`.

## Testing
Unit tests in `tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py` drive `_acquire_advisory_lock`/`drain` against a lock file planted in each state: stamped-for-a-dead-pid (reclaimed), 0-byte and back-dated past the ceiling (reclaimed), 0-byte and fresh (refused — the create/stamp window), stamped-for-a-live-pid (refused, bytes unchanged, WARNING names the holder), and foreign-host (refused while young). One forces every `os.open` to raise `FileExistsError` and asserts two attempts; one asserts release still removes the file; one asserts an acquired lock's bytes parse as a v2 stamp naming us. The existing lock-owner suites (`test_lock_age_ceiling.py`, `test_lock_stale_reclaim.py`, `test_lock_container_recreate.py`) guard the extraction's unchanged behaviour. `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor_locks.py` covers the doctor drain leg: dead-pid stamp → `stale-lock` finding + exit 1, live-pid stamp → no finding + exit 0, read-only preserved.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A dead holder no longer wedges enrichment: with a drain lock stamped for a
      provably-dead pid, a test asserts `drain()` returns a non-skipped result.
- [x] A pre-fix unstamped orphan is reclaimed: with a 0-byte lock back-dated past the
      ceiling, a test asserts acquisition succeeds.
- [x] The create/stamp window is respected: with a 0-byte lock created just now, a test
      asserts acquisition is refused.
- [x] A live holder is honoured: with a lock stamped for a live pid, a test asserts
      `drain()` returns `{"skipped": "lock-held"}`.
- [x] That refused attempt leaves the lock file byte-identical, asserted by comparing
      its bytes before and after.
- [x] An acquired lock carries the existing v2 stamp: a test asserts its contents parse
      with `lock_owner._parse_v2_stamp` into our own host and pid.
- [x] No second staleness heuristic exists: a grep of the diff shows no new age constant,
      no pid probe deciding staleness outside `lock_owner`.
- [x] The reclaim is bounded: with every create raising `FileExistsError`, a test asserts
      `os.open` was called exactly twice.
- [x] The reclaim is loud: `caplog` shows a WARNING naming the stamp and age.
- [x] A skipped drain is attributable: `caplog` shows a WARNING naming the holder.
- [x] `rebar doctor`'s drain leg reports a real staleness verdict rather than
      `not-assessable`, asserted on its `--output json` row.
- [x] A dead-holder drain lock becomes a `stale-lock` finding at exit 1, asserted in
      `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor_locks.py`.
- [x] Doctor still reclaims nothing: its read-only test passes with the drain lock file
      unchanged after a run.
- [x] Every touched `src/rebar` file stays under the 800-LOC cap (module-size gate).
- [x] The full local gate set is green: `check_*` gates, generators re-run with no diff,
      `make lint`, `make typecheck`, CI's pytest run.

## Report

Two agents measured the store write lock held ~12 minutes by a process that had ALREADY EXITED. Investigated under royal-weariless-zebrafish, which REFUTED both an fd leak and `start=-` defeating liveness.

## Premise verified in current `origin/main` (cc69cc1179)

`src/rebar/_store/lock.py`, `_mkdir_lock_is_stale` (**507**), same-host/same-namespace branch, lines **565-572**:

```python
if not _pid_alive(pid): return True                                               # 565-566
stamped_start = None if fields["start"] == _STAMP_UNKNOWN else fields["start"]    # 567
current_start = _process_start_time(pid)                                          # 568
if stamped_start is not None and current_start is not None and stamped_start != current_start:
    return True                                     # 569-571  -- recycled-pid discriminator
return False                                        # 572
```

`_process_start_time` (line **265**) reads **only** `/proc/<pid>/stat` (line 273), returning `None` on every `OSError` (275-276). macOS has no `/proc`, so it ALWAYS returns `None`; `current_start` at 568 is therefore always `None` there, the line-569 condition is **unsatisfiable by construction**, and the branch falls to `return False`.

So when the holder is dead but its pid NUMBER was recycled by an unrelated live process, `_pid_alive` reports "live" and the lock is judged fresh. That branch is deliberately exempt from the 1h `_MKDIR_LOCK_STALE_CEILING_S` backstop (constant at **107**; exemption documented in the decision table at **525-531**, "never on a timer alone") because a live pid is treated as positive proof of liveness. With no start time it is not proof — it is a bare pid-number collision. Net effect on any platform without `/proc`: an **unbounded** wedge. Recycling is live on this host (`kern.maxproc: 16000`, already wrapped past the observed stamp pid).

Secondary, already-bounded wedge: `_reclaim_mkdir_lock` removes the owner file then rmdirs, both best-effort; a failed rmdir leaves an owner-less dir, cleared at the ceiling by the owner-unreadable branch. Asserted by a test here, not changed.

## Direction (conservative, as recorded)

Apply `_mkdir_lock_age_exceeds_ceiling` on the live-pid branch **only when `current_start` is unavailable** — only when the "live pid" verdict is unqualified and so not a liveness proof:

* `current_start` known and DIFFERENT from a known `stamped_start` -> reclaim now (unchanged).
* `current_start` known and matching -> `False`, never reclaimed on a timer (unchanged;
  preserves "never break a live owner on a timer alone" wherever `/proc` exists).
* `current_start` is `None` -> unqualified verdict, so fall back to the same 1h ceiling that
  backstops every other unprovable case here. This is the ONLY behaviour change.
* `stamped_start` `None` with `current_start` known -> unchanged `False` (not widened).

**Why the ceiling cannot break a genuinely-live, non-recycled owner.** The worry is a real owner, alive and holding on a no-`/proc` platform, losing its lock at 1h. The dual-leg invariant rules it out: `_mkdir_lock_is_stale` is only reached from `_acquire_mkdir` (**602**), which by its stated precondition runs only AFTER this acquirer took the exclusive `fcntl.flock` leg, held for the ENTIRE lifetime of the mkdir leg (release order: mkdir, then fcntl). A live owner inside its hold still holds that fcntl leg, so a reclaimer could not have acquired it and cannot be at this line at all. Reaching the ceiling check is itself evidence the stamped owner let go — the orphan case. Blast radius: orphans only.

**Considered and NOT done:** also reclaiming on `fcntl_held` here. The same invariant would justify reclaiming an orphan at once rather than after an hour, but it widens *when a lock may be broken* beyond the recorded direction, so it is left for a follow-up decision.

## Module-size seam (required)

`src/rebar/_store/lock.py` is **798** lines against the hard cap of **800** (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`, CI-enforced), so the fix cannot land without a split. Split on the existing call-graph seam: extract the owner-identity / stamp / staleness / reclaim cluster into a new sibling `src/rebar/_store/lock_owner.py` —

`_STAMP_UNKNOWN`, `_STAMP_V2_PREFIX`, `_BOOT_ID_PATH`, `_PID_NS_PATH`, `_MKDIR_OWNER_FILE`, `_MKDIR_LOCK_STALE_CEILING_S`, `_read_boot_id`, `_read_pid_namespace_id`, `_process_start_time`, `_host_identity`, `_owner_stamp`, `_parse_v2_stamp`, `_describe_stamped_pid`, `_mkdir_lock_age_s`, `_mkdir_lock_age_exceeds_ceiling`, `_pid_alive`, `_legacy_stamp_is_stale`, `_mkdir_lock_is_stale`, `_reclaim_mkdir_lock`

— leaving `lock.py` with the fcntl leg, `_acquire_mkdir`, `LockHandle`, and the `acquire`/`write_lock` API. The cluster is 270 LOC, so `lock_owner.py` lands near 290 (with header and imports) and `lock.py` near 548: both inside the 200-800 band, no file under 100.

The dependency runs **one way, `lock.py` -> `lock_owner.py`**, no cycle. It is NOT the case that nothing left behind references the cluster: `_acquire_mkdir` calls `_owner_stamp`, `_mkdir_lock_is_stale`, `_reclaim_mkdir_lock`, and the two public reporters that stay — `write_lock_is_busy` (**333**) and `describe_lock_holder` (**383**) — reach `_parse_v2_stamp`, `_describe_stamped_pid`, `_mkdir_lock_age_s`, `_MKDIR_OWNER_FILE`. All become imports from `lock_owner`; nothing in `lock_owner` imports `lock`.

**Migration detail — BOTH reference forms, not just patches.** A sweep of the 4 affected test modules found:

* **12 string-form `monkeypatch.setattr` sites** over `_read_boot_id`,
  `_read_pid_namespace_id`, `_process_start_time`, `_pid_alive`, `_parse_v2_stamp`, plus 2
  patching `_lock.socket.gethostname` (read by `_host_identity`).
* **42 plain attribute-access sites** on the `from rebar._store import lock as _lock` binding
  — the larger half, breaking identically: `_mkdir_lock_is_stale` (17), `_owner_stamp` (13),
  `_MKDIR_OWNER_FILE` (5), `_reclaim_mkdir_lock`, `_host_identity`,
  `_MKDIR_LOCK_STALE_CEILING_S` (1 each) — over `test_lock_age_ceiling.py` (14),
  `test_lock_container_recreate.py` (15), `test_lock_stale_reclaim.py` (9),
  `test_lock_timeout_names_holder_7084.py` (4).

A re-export shim would keep the attribute half green while **silently breaking the patch half**: the moved `_mkdir_lock_is_stale` resolves patched names through its OWN module globals, so a shim would leave those tests asserting nothing. No shim — every site of either form is repointed at `lock_owner`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A dead holder whose pid was recycled by an unrelated live process is reclaimed once past
      the ceiling where `_process_start_time` returns `None` — test stamps a lock with a
      live-but-unrelated pid, forces no start time, asserts stale past the ceiling and NOT
      before it
- [x] A live holder whose stamped and current start times both exist and MATCH is never
      reclaimed however old the lock — test asserts refusal well past the ceiling
- [x] A live pid whose known start time DIFFERS from the stamp is still reclaimed at once,
      independent of age — test (regression guard on the existing branch)
- [x] The owner-less-dir path is bounded by the ceiling — test removes the owner file and
      asserts stale only past it
- [x] `lock.py` and `lock_owner.py` are each within `.github/module-size-limit.txt` and no new
      file is under 100 LOC — verified against `git archive HEAD`
- [x] The split is behaviour-preserving: every pre-existing lock test passes with BOTH
      reference forms repointed to `lock_owner` (12 patch-string, 42 attribute-access), and
      `rebar._store.lock` carries no re-export shim for any moved name — test asserts the
      moved names are absent from `lock`'s namespace [operator-attested]
- [x] The reported defect no longer reproduces: a recycled pid on a platform without `/proc`
      is reclaimed rather than wedging the store unboundedly [operator-attested]
baseline.summary: Stale mkdir lock is UNBOUNDED on platforms without /proc: recycled pid defeats reclamation
