# Mutation gate has no "change predates the gate" guard, so it hard-fails older changes

The bounded mutation gate runs its reusable workflow from `refs/heads/main` but executes it against the CHECKED-OUT PATCHSET tree. When a change is based on a commit older than the one that introduced `scripts/mutation_gate.py`, the script is absent from that tree and the step dies:

    /home/runner/work/rebar/rebar/.venv/bin/python3: can't open file
    '/home/runner/work/rebar/rebar/scripts/mutation_gate.py': [Errno 2] No such file or directory
    ##[error]Process completed with exit code 2.

The result is a `Verified -1` that says nothing about the change's own quality.

## Evidence

Two consecutive runs, both failing pre-analysis, on changes based on `c0bb6dcc` (which predates the walking-skeleton commit `57d19254` that added the script):

- change 1621 patchset 1 — run 31561319537, job 94004044... exit code 2
- change 1624 patchset 1 — run 31561579063, job 94005317237, exit code 2

On 1624 the checkout step itself SUCCEEDED ("Checkout the Gerrit patchset ✓"); the failure is in "Run changed mutation shards", so this is not a fetch race. It is deterministic for any change whose base predates the script.

## Why this is the gate's bug, not the author's

Every sibling gate in the same workflow already guards for exactly this, and skips with an explanatory message rather than failing. For example the env-var registry gate:

    if [ ! -f scripts/gen_env_registry.py ]; then
      echo "scripts/gen_env_registry.py not in checked-out tree (change predates the gate) \
    — skipping; the gate re-enforces on rebase and on every post-merge change"
      exit 0
    fi

`scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py` carries the same guard. The mutation gate is the only one missing it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The mutation gate skips cleanly (exit 0, explanatory message) when
      `scripts/mutation_gate.py` is absent from the checked-out tree, matching the wording
      and behaviour of the sibling gates.
- [x] A change based before the walking-skeleton commit gets no `Verified -1` from this
      gate.
- [x] A change based at or after it still runs the gate for real — the skip must not
      become a silent bypass on current changes.

## Workaround

Rebase the change onto current `origin/main`; the script then exists and the gate runs (and correctly reports "no protected shard selected" for changes touching no shard).

## Provenance

Hit twice while landing the build-drift warning (`tasty-unappeased-leopard`, b273-e0ba-f719-4f1c). Filed at operator direction so the mutation-testing work has the signal.
baseline.summary: Mutation gate hard-fails changes that predate its own script

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`rebar link <a> <b> depends_on` can silently record a different edge than the one requested, and can produce an edge in which a ticket blocks its own subtree. Bug 1803-df54-18bb-4881 hit this while wiring epic 8fc2-0306-a9a0-4864's dependency graph: an epic ended up `depends_on` its own child, the requested child-level dependency was never recorded at all, and the operator had to retype children and hand-unlink the bad edge. Self-blocking edges distort `ready`, `next-batch` and the parent-first claim cascade, so parallel agents are handed a wrong work order.

The cause is a policy defect rather than a coding slip. `resolve_hierarchy_link` (`src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:98`) decides "comparable level" for blocking links from the ticket's TYPE TIER (`_TYPE_TIER`, `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:26`) instead of from its position in the parent hierarchy. Bug jira-reb-1582 names the correct rule directly: comparability is structural, and any two tickets sharing a parent may hold a dependency. This story supersedes both bugs and replaces the policy.

## Approach

Replace type-tier comparability with structural (nearest-common-ancestor) comparability; add a resolved-pair invariant that makes ancestor-blocking edges unrepresentable regardless of how the edge was produced; then detect and repair the edges already written under the old rule.

Rejected alternative — keep the type tiers and special-case the failing shape by clamping promotion below the nearest common ancestor. That removes 1803's specific symptom but leaves comparability keyed on a ticket's *type*, so a task and a story that are genuine siblings still could not hold a direct dependency, and re-typing a ticket would silently rewrite the meaning of the dependency graph. jira-reb-1582 asks for the rule itself to change; patching the fallback at `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:93` would leave the store's semantics wrong in the same way.

Rejected alternative — reject cross-subtree blocking links with an error instead of escalating them. Honest, but it breaks every caller relying on auto-escalation today, including the `link` MCP tool and the reconciler's inbound apply path (`rebar.link` at `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py:502`). Escalation is retained, and its existing machine-readable redirect record (`src/rebar/graph/_links.py:207`) is kept unchanged. Note it is NOT uniformly visible: `add_dependency` prints it to stdout, which the CLI surfaces, but the library facade `rebar.link()` calls `composer.link_core(..., quiet=True)` (`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:615`), and `quiet` redirects stdout/stderr into a `StringIO` sink (`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:628`) — so library and MCP callers have the record DISCARDED and see a silent substitution. That predates this story and is not changed by it, but it is the same silence bug 1803-df54-18bb-4881 complained about, still present on the MCP path; recorded as follow-up on the doctor epics rather than fixed here.

## Success Criteria

- The blocking-link resolver decides comparability from the parent hierarchy alone; `_TYPE_TIER` no longer participates in that decision.
- No blocking edge can exist between a ticket and its own ancestor or descendant, by any path into the resolver.
- Blocking edges already written under the type-tier rule are detectable store-wide and repairable in a single pass.
- The escalation contract callers depend on — auto-escalate a cross-subtree link, emit the redirect record — is unchanged.

## Decomposition

Two children, in dependency order:

1. **Structural comparability and the ancestor invariant** (leaf) — rewrites the resolver in `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py` and moves the redundancy guard in `src/rebar/graph/_links.py` onto the resolved pair. This is the fix for both superseded bugs.
2. **`doctor` detection and repair** (leaf, shipped as the first check of `rebar doctor`) — a store-wide scan plus one-shot repair for edges written under the old rule. It declares `depends_on` child 1, because the repair re-resolves each existing edge through the new resolver and cannot be written before those semantics are final.

The split follows the deliverable seam: child 1 changes what a new link means, child 2 fixes data already on disk. Each lands as one reviewable change. Neither is large enough to split further, and combining them would put a store-wide data rewrite in the same change as the semantics that rewrite depends on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The repro from bug 1803-df54-18bb-4881 (a task and a story that are both direct children of one epic) records the requested task-to-story edge unchanged and produces no epic-to-child edge; verified by the regression test added in child 1, run against the store fixture.
- [ ] The worked example from bug jira-reb-1582 resolves as that ticket specifies — Task D under Story C escalates to Story C when linked to Task B, while Task B to Story C records directly; verified by the regression test added in child 1.
- [ ] [operator-attested] `rebar doctor` against this repository's own tracker reports zero findings that can affect scheduling; verified by listing each remaining finding's BLOCKED side (the source for `depends_on`, the target for `blocks`) and attesting on this ticket that every one is `closed`, since a closed blocked-side can never appear in `ready` or `next-batch`. Attested rather than asserted in-repo because it is a statement about live tracker state at a point in time, and the pre-repair count cannot be reconstructed from the post-repair store.
- [ ] Both children are closed, each with its Gerrit change at `Verified +1` and `LLM-Review +1`; verified by the change status in Gerrit before each close.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `pytest tests/scripts/graph/` all pass; verified by running them in the worktree.
baseline.summary: Resolve blocking-link comparability structurally, forbid ancestor self-blocks, and repair existing edges

# `_llm_float` is invisible to the env-var registry scanner: 4 undocumented env vars

## Context / Problem
`scripts/gen_env_registry.py` generates `docs/env-vars.md` from env-var reads under `src/rebar`, and a CI drift gate fails the build when the committed doc disagrees (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:314`). The generator recognises a read only when the callee is a KNOWN helper AND the name argument is a STRING LITERAL (`gen_env_registry.py:117-124`); `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` at `:37-47` registers `"_llm_str": (2, "")` and `"_llm_int": (2, "")`.

**`_llm_float` is NOT registered.** So every env var read through it is silently absent from the generated registry. MEASURED by running the generator: `REBAR_LLM_TEMPERATURE` (`llm/config.py:651`), `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_MAX_DOC_FREQ` (`:692`), `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_MIN_SHOULD_MATCH` (`:699`) and `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_CONF_THRESHOLD` (`:720`) are all real, settable, operator-facing knobs and NONE appears in `docs/env-vars.md`.

This is exactly the bug class the registry exists to prevent, and the gate is currently GREEN while incomplete — a clean `--check` is therefore not evidence of completeness. `_llm_float` is defined at `llm/config.py:459-476` alongside `_llm_str` (`:426-436`) and `_llm_int` (`:439-456`); the omission is an oversight, not a decision.

## Approach
Add `"_llm_float": (2, "")` to `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` and regenerate `docs/env-vars.md`.

Land this BEFORE any structural change to `config.py`, so the derived-doc diff caused by fixing the scanner is not tangled with the diff caused by moving code. That keeps both changes reviewable.

**Also close the hole that let this hide:** the existing test `tests/unit/test_llm_config_pointer.py:259-267` asserts one specific var is statically visible to the generator. Generalize the idea — assert that the helper registry covers every `_llm_*` resolver defined in `llm/config.py`, so adding a fifth resolver without registering it fails a test rather than silently dropping knobs from the docs.

## Scope
- `scripts/gen_env_registry.py` — one entry in `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS`.
- `docs/env-vars.md` — regenerated, not hand-edited.
- `tests/unit/` — the completeness assertion.

## Testing
- a test asserts each of the four named vars appears in the generated registry (fails today).
- a test asserts every `_llm_*` helper defined in `llm/config.py` is present in `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS`,
  so the next resolver cannot be added unregistered.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] a test asserts `REBAR_LLM_TEMPERATURE`, `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_MAX_DOC_FREQ`,
      `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_MIN_SHOULD_MATCH` and `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_CONF_THRESHOLD` are all present in
      the generated env registry. This criterion FAILS against the current implementation
- [ ] a test asserts every `_llm_*` resolver defined in `src/rebar/llm/config.py` is registered in
      `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS`, so an unregistered future resolver is caught
- [ ] `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py` leaves the tree clean and `docs/env-vars.md` is committed
      as generated output
baseline.summary: _llm_float is invisible to the env-var registry scanner: 4 undocumented env vars

## Context / Problem

The S3 ticket-store backend (parent epic) is only usable if operators can discover the optional dependency and configure S3 from the docs alone — today `docs/config.md` documents `sync.remote` (line ~128) and `tracker.branch` (line ~154) only for the GitHub/git case, and nothing names the `git-remote-s3` dependency, the SSE-KMS bucket setup, or the auto-doctor behavior. This story documents the feature and records the architecture decision. It is documentation-only; the code lands in the sibling stories.

## Approach

1. **`docs/config.md`** — under the `sync` section, document that `sync.remote` may point at a
   git remote whose URL is `s3://bucket/prefix` (or `s3+zip://`), served by the optional
   `git-remote-s3` helper, and that this keeps ticket history entirely out of GitHub. Cross-
   link the new backend page.
2. **New `docs/s3-backend.md`** — the operator guide: (a) install the optional dependency
   (`pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]'`, minimum `git-remote-s3>=0.3.2`); (b) create the SSE-KMS bucket
   (default encryption with a customer CMK, versioning on, public-access-block on) and the
   IAM policy scoped to the bucket + CMK; (c) add the git remote (`git remote add <name>
   s3://bucket/prefix`) and set `sync.remote` to it; (d) the **trust boundary**: AWS
   credentials come from the standard boto3 chain (never stored in rebar config or events),
   data at rest is SSE-KMS in the customer bucket, S3 access is IAM/SigV4 (no anonymous
   access); (e) operational behavior: the non-interactive auto-doctor self-heals a
   multiple-bundles state by merge (no data loss), and a stale lock self-heals during the next
   push's lock acquisition (git-remote-s3 v0.3.2 `remote.py` `acquire_lock` deletes a lock older
   than the TTL and re-acquires in the same call; a manual `git-remote-s3 doctor --lock-ttl`
   path also exists per `remote.py:236-237`). The TTL is `DEFAULT_LOCK_TTL_SECONDS`
   = 60s (`remote.py:45`), overridable via the `GIT_REMOTE_S3_LOCK_TTL_SECONDS` env var — a
   rare, bounded delay we intentionally do not lower. Primary-source verified against the v0.3.2
   release tarball (tag `v0.3.2` = commit `9f3290e1f19090a9c11ae5b8c01ec8abe6184ab9`):
   `git_remote_s3/remote.py:95` reads `os.environ.get("GIT_REMOTE_S3_LOCK_TTL_SECONDS",
   DEFAULT_LOCK_TTL_SECONDS)`, and the string `GIT_REMOTE_S3_LOCK_TTL` (no `_SECONDS`) appears
   ONLY in upstream's README, in NO `.py` file of the release — so the code does not honor it.
   The docs use — and flag — the `_SECONDS` form the code actually reads, with a "verify against
   your installed version" note to remove any mislead hazard.
3. **New `docs/adr/0093-s3-ticket-store-backend.md`** — record the decision: use
   `awslabs/git-remote-s3` (Apache-2.0, maintained) below rebar's shell-out git layer so the
   event/data format is unchanged; SSE-KMS (not client-side) is acceptable per requirements;
   the multi-bundle risk is handled by a rebar merge-based auto-doctor because upstream's
   `git-s3 doctor` is interactive and discards a head; lowering the lock TTL was rejected.
   Follow the format of an existing ADR (e.g. `docs/adr/0091-*`); 0093 is the next free number
   (highest existing is 0091). **An ADR is not a standalone file:** after writing the prose file
   run `python scripts/gen_adr_index.py`, which (a) creates the per-number marker
   `docs/adr/.numbers/0093` (content = the ADR filename — the add/add-conflict uniqueness
   mechanism) and (b) regenerates the GENERATED, do-not-hand-edit index `docs/adr/README.md`
   (the new ADR sorts into the "Other decisions" fallback group, since its slug matches no
   workstream keyword). CI enforces both: `scripts/check_adr_numbers.py` asserts the
   number↔file bijection and that no ADR cross-reference dangles, and `gen_adr_index.py --check`
   fails if the committed marker/index drift from a regeneration. Commit the ADR file, its
   `.numbers/0093` marker, and the regenerated `README.md` together, and ensure every link in
   the ADR resolves (no dangling target).
4. **`docs/README.md`** (docs index) and, if it lists extras, a one-line pointer — link the
   new backend page and ADR so they are discoverable.

Rationale: a dedicated backend page plus an ADR matches how rebar already documents optional capabilities and architecture decisions (the `docs/adr/` series), giving operators a single configuration entry point and preserving the decision record the maintainability criterion expects; keeping it docs-only avoids coupling the write-up to any one code story's landing.

## Scope

- `docs/config.md` — extend the `sync.remote` documentation for the `s3://` case.
- `docs/s3-backend.md` — new operator guide (install, bucket/KMS/IAM, config, trust
  boundary, self-heal behavior).
- `docs/adr/0093-s3-ticket-store-backend.md` — new ADR (prose file).
- `docs/adr/.numbers/0093` — new per-number marker (generated by `scripts/gen_adr_index.py`).
- `docs/adr/README.md` — regenerated ADR index (generated; not hand-edited).
- `docs/README.md` — add index links to the two new pages.

No source, schema, or test changes. Running `scripts/gen_adr_index.py` (a repo-provided generator) to produce the two derived ADR artifacts above is part of the mechanical ADR-add procedure, not a code change to the generator itself.

## Testing

Documentation-only; no automated test tier applies (mechanical prose changes, consistent with how other `docs/` and ADR changes land). Validation is by review against the acceptance checks below.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `docs/config.md` documents that `sync.remote` accepts an `s3://bucket/prefix` remote
      served by the optional `git-remote-s3` helper and links `docs/s3-backend.md`. Verified
      by the section being present and cross-linked.
- [x] `docs/s3-backend.md` exists and contains all five subsections: install (naming
      `pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]'` and the `git-remote-s3>=0.3.2` minimum), SSE-KMS bucket + IAM/CMK
      setup, remote + `sync.remote` configuration, the credentials/encryption trust boundary,
      and the auto-doctor + 60s stale-lock self-heal behavior. Verified by the named
      subsections being present.
- [x] `docs/adr/0093-s3-ticket-store-backend.md` exists, follows the existing ADR format, and
      records the git-remote-s3 choice, SSE-KMS decision, the merge-based auto-doctor
      rationale (vs upstream's interactive/discarding doctor), and the rejected TTL-lowering.
      Its per-number marker `docs/adr/.numbers/0093` and the regenerated `docs/adr/README.md`
      are committed, and `python scripts/gen_adr_index.py --check` + `scripts/check_adr_numbers.py`
      both pass (bijection holds, no dangling ADR cross-reference). Verified by the ADR sections
      being present and both ADR gates green in CI.
- [x] Both new pages are discoverable from the docs index (`docs/README.md`): the operator
      guide `docs/s3-backend.md` is linked directly, and ADR 0093 is discoverable via the
      project's standard ADR path — `docs/README.md` links the `adr/` directory, whose
      generated index `docs/adr/README.md` lists `0093-s3-ticket-store-backend.md`. Per repo
      convention individual ADRs are indexed through the generated ADR index, not linked
      one-by-one from `docs/README.md`. Verified by the links being present.

--- **Delivery note (landing-time deviation):** ADR number bumped from the planned 0092 to **0093** because ADR 0092 was claimed on `main` at landing time by `0092-bridge-primary-vocabulary-compatibility-adapters.md`. The plan's intent ("next free ADR number") is preserved; only the concrete number changed. Delivered as `docs/adr/0093-s3-ticket-store-backend.md` + `.numbers/0093`, regenerated `docs/adr/README.md`. Merged as Gerrit change 1552 (LLM-Review+1, Verified+1), commit b7d29e58c7.
baseline.summary: Document the optional S3 dependency, S3/SSE-KMS configuration, and the backend ADR

## Context / Problem
Source comments carry commit SHAs, run/thread IDs, and dated incident narratives that rot: 8 of 18 cited SHAs in the tree are ALREADY unresolvable (Gerrit rebase-on-submit guarantees pre-land SHA death), and run IDs die with retention windows. Policy: source is for current state + concise rationale; the ticket system owns historical detail. The detector is NET-NEW code (the prototype that produced the corpus numbers ran in the planning session and was not committed; its measured results — 0 FPs, 15 violating sites, 47 compliant blocks on the then-current tree — are recorded here as design evidence, and the corpus is re-derived by running the new detector at the implementation worktree's HEAD, which is authoritative; the ticket comment records census drift to 16 sites already).

## Approach
(1) Remediate every detector hit at HEAD (17 pinned above as-of-plan: the original 15 census sites, of which 2 were later found under src/ in the PR-375 bucket, plus 3 post-plan RUN-id sites minus overlap) — each maps to a specific replacement already adjudicated: delete.py:188 drop dead-SHA mechanism sentence; classify.py:310 + test_frozen_census.py:79 cite epic 3006-e198; reconcile.py:588 + tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_commit_binding_store_failure.py:10 (module docstring's 'cf93b2b7ad failure class') describe the failure class in behavioral terms (story findable via git log -S); test_ci_actionlint_install.py cite bug 4e99-b2ae; test_plan_review_explain.py:308 (docstring narrates 'the class of bug `62933ff62` fixed for plan-review deep-links' — a raw dead SHA) drop the SHA and cite bug c7e3-dd16; test_execution_mode_dispatch.py cite 454a-9266; test_inbound_differ_field_contract.py point at the live CONTRACT block + story a130-2b7c; 7 PR-#375 sites keep 'PR #375 review' and drop raw thread ids (tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_inbound_leaf_bodies.py:63/69/210/310/451 + src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/typed_dispatch.py:128 + src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound.py:233); test_at_most_one_invariant.py:199 drop e04e0b289c; 3 RUN-id sites from the post-plan J11/5200 work (tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py:163/1638-context + tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_inbound_assignee_oracle_discriminates_5200.py:20-context, runs 30721408463/30763838558) get the same treatment — narrative to a ticket, cite the ticket. Line numbers are as-of-plan pins; the re-run detector census at HEAD is the authoritative remediation list and may add/retire sites (same adjudicated replacement rules apply). (2) CI guard (detector is NET-NEW per Context; prior art/reuse: it follows the repo's scripts/check_*.py guard convention — check()/main() shape, wired as a named step in .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml like check_verify_gate_parity.py — landing as scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py): block-level scan (comment blocks + AST docstrings); rot-prone = SHA-like hex >=7 with digits+letters (denylist ed25519/sha256 etc), run/job/thread id >=8 digits after keyword, date+evidence-verb — defined as: a date token (YYYY-MM-DD or 'Month DD, YYYY') in the same block as a past-tense incident verb from the ENUMERATED set {failed, broke, regressed, fixed, caught, observed, hit, crashed, flaked} (the block narrates a dated incident); 'surfaced' is deliberately EXCLUDED from the verb set — the prototype's 'bug surfaced' FP introduces current-state explanation, not an incident date, and must not trigger. Acceptor interaction: triggers are evaluated first, then a triggered block is ACCEPTED iff it cites a qualifying id — the gotcha cases must not trigger at all (they never reach the acceptor); ACCEPTED when the block cites a ticket/epic/story/bug/rec/ADR id — hex-grouped (4x4 like 3006-e198-…) or word-triple alias (three lowercase hyphen-joined dictionary words, e.g. robe-creek-zealot, the store's human alias form) — pointing history at the ticket system is the sanctioned pattern; escape hatch 'context: external' for vendor-pinned refs (changelogs, upstream issue SHAs). Self-exclusion (sibling-guard convention): the detector's own unit-test module (tests/unit/test_comment_hygiene_guard.py, whose fixtures MUST contain live rot-prone tokens as RED/gotcha cases) is excluded from the tree scan by an EXCLUDED_FILES tuple in the script — the same mechanism check_criteria_vocabulary.py uses (scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py:38); fixtures live only in that one excluded module, so 'zero suppressions' means zero IN-TREE escape-hatch uses, with the single structural exclusion visible at the top of the script.

## Scope
- the detector-hit sites listed above (src/ + tests/; authoritative list = detector re-run at HEAD)
- scripts/ or CI lint module implementing the detector + workflow wiring
- short policy note in CONTRIBUTING.md or docs (source=current state, tickets=history)

## Testing
Detector unit tests re-derived at HEAD (prototype-measured shape: ~15-17 pre-fix sites RED, ~47 compliant blocks green — exact counts pinned when the detector lands), the acceptor-arm gotchas ('bug surfaced', 'ticket dirs' must NOT accept; grouped 4x4 ids and word-triple aliases MUST accept), escape hatch honored. Post-remediation tree scans clean.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] All detector-hit sites at HEAD remediated, each in one of three sanctioned forms: (a) cites a ticket/epic/story/bug id that RESOLVES in the ticket system (spot-check via rebar show), (b) drops the rot-prone token leaving durable current-state prose (PR-#375 bucket keeps 'PR #375 review', drops raw thread ids), or (c) replaces a SHA narrative with a behavioral description findable via git log -S (the test_commit_binding_store_failure.py form).
- [x] CI guard fails on reintroduced rot-prone refs, passes the current remediated tree with zero suppressions.
- [x] Escape hatch documented; policy note landed.
- [x] Detector unit tests cover the FP gotchas measured in the planning prototype ('bug surfaced'/'ticket dirs' NOT accepted; grouped 4x4 ids and word-triple aliases accepted; escape hatch honored).
baseline.summary: Comment hygiene: remediate rot-prone historical refs in code + CI guard

## Why

Two work tickets (115b, 8c4f) burned close-gate cycles: their acceptance criteria had "done" evidence that lives OUTSIDE the codebase (live-store fsck surgery, phantom-dir deletion, changes landed through Gerrit) but were NOT tagged `[operator-attested]` (ADR-0043), so the completion verifier failed looking for code proof until the tag was added retroactively. A cheap DETERMINISTIC pass-1 lint that surfaces this at PLAN time — before claim — removes the whole round-trip. Rule-based lexicon checks are the proven high-recall/cheap tier for requirement-defect shape (AQUSA-grade prior art); this project already ships two such lexicon lints in the same P6/P7 family (`p6_ac_quality`'s vague-term + verify-command lint at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:686`, and `p7_destructive` at `:762`), so this is a well-precedented extension, not a new mechanism.

## What

Add an ADVISORY, prompt-less DETERMINISTIC lint (ADR-0016 `exec: DET`, the P6/AC family) that flags AC checklist items whose text carries operational-evidence markers (deploy / prod / live-run / IaC-apply / cloud-state / merge-gate / human-action / drill / store-surgery / recorded-attestation) but which are NOT tagged `[operator-attested]`. It NEVER blocks (advisory coaching only).

### Design decisions (grounded against the code)

- **It EXTENDS `p6_ac_quality`; it does NOT add a `P10` and does NOT touch
  `criteria_routing.json`.** The static DET floor (`DET_CHECKS`,
  `det_floor.py:880`) is hardcoded P1–P9 and enumerated in
  `registry.py:78 CANONICAL_DET`; DET checks are NOT routed through
  `criteria_routing.json`. `registry.validate_packaged_routing()`
  (`registry.py:445-446`) flags any routing key not in `CANONICAL_LLM` as an
  ORPHAN and fails CI, so a packaged DET routing entry is impossible without a
  larger, out-of-scope change. And `.rebar/`-overlay `exec:DET` criteria run
  through `det_invariants.run_project_det_checks` (`det_invariants.py:207`),
  which scans CODE with a grounding detector (`engine_b`) — structurally wrong
  for an AC-TEXT lexicon. The existing regression test
  `tests/unit/test_det_invariants.py:327` already pins "the lint EXTENDS p6 …
  DET_CHECKS stays exactly P1-P9", exactly matching how the verify-command lint
  (G-3a) was folded into p6. So the correct home is `p6_ac_quality`, keeping
  `DET_CHECKS` at 9 and `CANONICAL_DET` unchanged. The task's suggestion of a
  `criteria_routing.json` entry is refuted by the code and is deliberately NOT
  done; `p6_ac_quality` already ships in the packaged registry (no config flag),
  satisfying "advisory in packaged registry".

- **Single-source the tag matcher.** The canonical `[operator-attested]` matcher
  is `workflow_ops._OPERATOR_ATTESTED_AC_RE` (`workflow_ops.py:61`), consumed by
  the completion-verifier enrichment path (`workflow_ops.py:80
  enrich_operator_attested`, `passes.py:769`). `det_floor` imports nothing from
  `workflow_ops`, and `workflow_ops` imports `det_floor` lazily
  (`workflow_ops.py:135`), so `det_floor` will OWN the regex as
  `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` and `workflow_ops` will import it — no import cycle,
  one source of truth, so the lint and the verifier agree on "tagged" by
  construction (guarded by a unit test).

- **Precision-first (advisory posture).** An advisory lint must not nag, so the
  lexicon is tuned for precision with a codebase-verifiable SUPPRESSION co-signal
  (drop items that name an in-repo proving command / test / doc / config-file
  deliverable, or carry a "… — landed on main" trailer) and a NEGATION guard
  ("no live", "read-only provisioning"). Recall is a reported figure, not a gate.

### Self-gate (DETERMINISTIC — no LLM anywhere)

Run the locked lexicon over the frozen historical AC corpus committed under `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/`. The corpus is the AC checklist items of the 556 E1 outcome-corpus tickets that resolve in the store (`docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/outcome_corpus.jsonl` → 3091 AC items, 31 already tagged `[operator-attested]`). Ground-truth for precision is a frozen per-item TP/FP adjudication of the full flagged set (a census ≥ the required 50-item sample); recall is measured against the 31 tagged items with their tag stripped. Measured on this corpus: flag rate 2.07% (≤5%), recall 61% (19/31), precision ~92% (census of 64 flagged items, 6 adjudicated false-positive), and both known cases (115b, 8c4f) fire. NO LLM call runs in the eval or the lint.

### Landing order (pre-registration, git-ancestry)

Landed as a 2-commit Gerrit stack so the eval is committed BEFORE the lint is active: commit 1 adds the frozen corpus + the harness + the committed `eval.json` result and the detector helper `_operator_evidence_ac_gaps()` in `det_floor.py` in DORMANT form (defined, used only by the harness, not yet called by `p6_ac_quality`); commit 2 wires the helper into `p6_ac_quality` (activation), adds the unit tests + the `workflow_ops` single-source import, and documents the lint in `docs/plan-review-gate.md`.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` — the `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE`,
  the operational-evidence lexicon (marker families + suppression + negation),
  the pure helper `_operator_evidence_ac_gaps(text) -> list[(ac_line, markers)]`,
  and its wiring into `p6_ac_quality` (append one advisory coaching issue per
  gap; never changes P6's non-blocking status).
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py` — import
  `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` from `det_floor` (drop the local duplicate).
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/operator_attested_eval.py` — the
  deterministic eval harness (imports the shipped helper; runs over the frozen
  corpus; computes flag rate / recall / known-case firing; loads frozen precision
  adjudications; asserts the gate).
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/operator_attested_ac_corpus.jsonl` —
  the frozen AC corpus.
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/operator_attested_eval.json` — the
  committed eval result (precision/recall/flag-rate/known-cases + adjudications +
  PASS verdict).
- `tests/unit/test_det_floor_operator_attested.py` — table-driven unit tests over
  labeled AC strings (115b/8c4f fixtures fire; negative controls do not;
  already-tagged items do not; agreement with `workflow_ops`).
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — document the lint (advisory P6-family DET,
  ADR-0016/0043).

## Out of scope

- Any `criteria_routing.json` change (refuted by the code, see above).
- A new `P10` DET check or any change to `CANONICAL_DET` / `DET_CHECKS`
  cardinality.
- Blocking posture, LLM rubric, or an `.rebar/` overlay entry.
- Any human-adjudicated gold set (parked as idea e59d).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The deterministic lexicon eval is committed under
  `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/operator_attested_eval.json` BEFORE the
  lint is activated (its commit is a git ancestor of the p6 activation commit),
  recording sampled precision ≥ 70% over a ≥ 50-item flagged sample AND overall
  flag rate ≤ 5% over the frozen corpus, plus the recall figure. Proof:
  `python -c "import json; d=json.load(open('docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/operator_attested_eval.json')); assert d['precision']['precision_pct']>=70 and d['precision']['sample_size']>=50 and d['flag_rate_pct']<=5.0 and d['gate']['verdict']=='PASS', d"`
  and `git merge-base --is-ancestor <eval-commit> <activation-commit>` exits 0.
  (If the eval had failed the thresholds, the story closes deferred with the
  failing result recorded instead.)
- [ ] Both known cases fire on their historical (tag-stripped) AC text, pinned as
  unit-test fixtures, and an already-tagged item does NOT fire. Proof:
  `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_det_floor_operator_attested.py -q` passes,
  including `test_known_case_115b_fires`, `test_known_case_8c4f_fires`, and
  `test_tagged_item_not_flagged`.
- [ ] The lint ships ADVISORY and prompt-less in the packaged floor: it extends
  `p6_ac_quality` (which never blocks), `DET_CHECKS` stays exactly 9 and
  `CANONICAL_DET` is unchanged, and no `criteria_routing.json` entry is added.
  Proof: `python -c "from rebar.llm.plan_review.det_floor import DET_CHECKS; assert len(DET_CHECKS)==9"`;
  `python -c "from rebar.llm.plan_review import registry,det_floor; assert list(registry.CANONICAL_DET)==['P1','P2','P3','P4','P5','P6','P7','P8','P9']; assert registry.validate_packaged_routing()==[]"`;
  and a unit test asserting a `p6_ac_quality` result on an untagged operational
  AC has `status=='fail'` with `blocking is False`.
- [ ] The lint and the completion-verifier agree on "tagged": `det_floor` owns
  `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` and `workflow_ops` imports it. Proof:
  `python -c "from rebar.llm.plan_review.det_floor import _OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE as a; from rebar.llm.plan_review.workflow_ops import _OPERATOR_ATTESTED_AC_RE as b; assert a is b"`
  and a unit test asserting `_operator_evidence_ac_gaps` never flags a line that
  `workflow_ops.operator_attested_ac_texts` recognizes as tagged.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` documents the new advisory P6-family DET lint
  (what it flags, that it is advisory/prompt-less, its self-gate result). Proof:
  `grep -qi "operator-attested" docs/plan-review-gate.md`.
- [ ] The whole suite stays green: `make lint && make typecheck && make test`
  pass (or the targeted `det_floor` / `plan_review` / `criteria_overlay` subsets
  plus the module-size gate).
- [ ] [operator-attested] The change is landed on `main` through Gerrit
  (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1, no unresolved comments), attested on this
  ticket with the Gerrit change number(s) and the merge commit sha.
baseline.summary: R2: operator-attested evidence-kind DET lint (P6 family, advisory)

## Context
The rebar-debug construct sweep for `fibrous-fabulous-dungbeetle` found a third live instance of the same centralization regression. `applier._load_concurrency()` executes `_concurrency.py` by file path under the non-package key `_concurrency`, but `snapshot_head()` unconditionally executes `from rebar_reconciler import git_adapter`. In a supported installed in-process environment, the top-level package is intentionally absent.

## Runtime Evidence
A fresh process with `find_spec("rebar_reconciler") is None` loaded `_concurrency.py` by file path, initialized a real temporary git repository, and called `snapshot_head(repo)`. It deterministically raised `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named rebar_reconciler` at `_concurrency.py:55`. `applier.py:268-278` is the production by-path loader.

## Plan
- Run rebar-debug independently to confirm legitimacy, loader identity requirements, and affected callers.
- Add a RED oracle through the real `applier._load_concurrency()` path.
- Restore standalone-safe git_adapter loading with the canonical dotted cache key, preserving package identity and snapshot semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A by-path-loaded concurrency module resolves the current snapshot from a real temporary git repository without package-path seeding.
- [ ] Package-context and standalone execution share one canonical git_adapter module object.
- [ ] Existing concurrency and applier suites pass.
baseline.summary: Standalone concurrency loader cannot import git adapter

baseline.description:
## Context

Accepted `/rerun` and `recheck-review` requests are currently represented only by a forced event in the process-local asyncio queue. If the receiver exits before that event is processed, the request disappears. Local dedup and the existing Gerrit `LLM-Review` vote then cause reconciliation to skip the revision.

The approved contract uses Gerrit as the durable source of truth: an accepted request first changes the exact revision to no nonzero `LLM-Review` vote. That label write also emits a fresh Gerrit `comment-added` event carrying the revision and ref, re-admitting even an old change to the reconciler’s events-log window. No `forced_pending` table is introduced.

## Proven root cause and capability evidence

Both acceptance paths currently reset the attempt budget and enqueue/return a forced event without first creating durable state. Reconciliation checks local `voted` state before Gerrit and therefore skips a revision whose stale local row survives after its Gerrit vote is reset. `review_and_vote` has the same local-first guard.

A read-only probe of the production Gerrit events-log on 2026-08-09 found 551 `LLM-Review` approval events. Every one was a `comment-added` event with both `patchSet.revision` and `patchSet.ref`; observed values included `0`, `-1`, and `1`. This verifies that a review-label write produces the fresh patchset-bearing event the reconciler consumes, independently of the original patchset-created event’s age.

## Security invariant update

The existing recheck documentation says the path never writes any label because its reply uses label-free `post_comment`. The approved vote-reset-first design intentionally narrows that invariant: an untrusted contributor comment can never choose a label value or mint a PASS/BLOCK. Only after privileged-side eligibility succeeds may the bot invoke a distinct reset operation whose fixed value is exactly neutral `0`. The affirmative/refusal reply still uses `post_comment` and remains provably label-free. Ineligible comments, malformed events, and failed eligibility checks write no label. Update the retrigger module documentation and tests to state this fixed-neutral-reset invariant; retain the existing `post_comment` body assertion unchanged.

## Plan

1. Add `GerritClient.reset_llm_review_vote(change_id, revision)`, which writes exactly `LLM-Review: 0` plus a rerun-request message on the exact revision.
2. After reset succeeds, call the existing all-accounts vote reader and require no nonzero `LLM-Review` vote. A surviving concurrent/admin vote is intentionally fail-closed: reject because the bot can reset only its own account’s vote and therefore cannot establish the durable marker.
3. On reset/write/read rejection, emit a warning keyed by change and revision. Return a non-success response for `/rerun`; for recheck, emit `RETRIGGER_REFUSED` and do not post the affirmative accepted reply.
4. For accepted `/rerun` and recheck, perform reset, verify, reset the retry-attempt budget, then enqueue/return the forced event.
5. Add `DedupStore.clear_voted(change_id, revision)`, implemented as an exact-key `DELETE FROM voted WHERE change_id=? AND revision=?`; it is distinct from `reset_attempts`, which deletes from `review_attempts`.
6. Reconcile only the bounded candidate set in the existing events-log window. Query Gerrit before trusting local dedup. A successful no-nonzero-vote result calls `clear_voted` and invokes the ordinary voter. The existing Gerrit-error branch preserves dedup, emits `reconcile_check_error`, and holds the cursor back for retry.
7. Preserve the normal skip when Gerrit has any nonzero vote. Preserve the forced live path for the accepted request already in memory.
8. Prove the complete restart path with a stateful Gerrit fake: reset appends a production-shaped `comment-added` event after an advanced cursor; a replacement queue starts empty; reconciliation consumes the event, clears matching stale dedup, and reviews the exact revision.
9. Run focused review-bot tests and repository gates.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Unit/API test proves `/rerun` resets the exact revision before resetting attempts.
- [x] Unit/API test proves `/rerun` returns HTTP 202 only after reset succeeds.
- [x] Unit/API test proves `/rerun` returns HTTP 202 only after the verification read finds no nonzero vote.
- [x] Unit/API failure test proves reset failure returns non-success and enqueues nothing.
- [x] Unit/API failure test proves verification-read failure returns non-success and leaves attempts unchanged.
- [x] Unit/API failure test proves a surviving nonzero vote returns non-success and emits a warning keyed by change/revision.
- [x] Unit/retrigger test proves eligibility is decided before the fixed-neutral reset.
- [x] Unit/retrigger test proves accepted recheck resets and verifies before resetting attempts.
- [x] Unit/retrigger test proves the reset body fixes the label value at exactly `0`; contributor text cannot influence it.
- [x] Unit/retrigger failure test proves an ineligible request writes no label.
- [x] Unit/retrigger failure test proves reset/read/nonzero rejection produces no forced event and emits `RETRIGGER_REFUSED`.
- [x] Existing unit test continues proving `post_comment` replies contain no `labels` member.
- [x] Stateful reconciliation test proves reset appends a patchset-bearing `comment-added` event newer than an advanced cursor.
- [x] Stateful restart test proves an empty replacement queue plus retained stale dedup is recovered from that event.
- [x] Stateful invariant test proves `clear_voted` deletes only the matching row.
- [x] Contrast test proves reconciliation skips a revision with any nonzero Gerrit vote.
- [x] Error-path test proves a Gerrit vote-read failure preserves dedup and emits `reconcile_check_error`.
- [x] Mutation proof restores local-dedup-first ordering and makes the held-out restart regression fail.
- [x] Focused review-bot tests pass.
- [x] `make lint` passes.
- [x] `make typecheck` passes.
- [x] `make test` passes.
baseline.summary: /rerun and recheck-review are fire-and-forget into a volatile queue, and the reconciler cannot back them up because the change already has a vote

## Why
4b5b (change 581) documented the DELIVERED (diverged) design — raw-bytes authorship, HLC-epoch validity, the `{author_id, author_sig, epoch}` ledger, and a 4-way verdict without `key_not_valid_at_era`. Once TS1/TS2/TS3 transition the implementation to the APPROVED design, the docs + ADR must be rewritten to match. Depends on TS1, TS2, TS3. (User rejected the delivered design; see session_log d7c0.)

## What
Rewrite `docs/identity.md` and `docs/adr/0045-authenticated-identity.md` to the approved design:
- Authorship = in-toto Statement (subject binds `{event_uuid, content_hash}`), DSSE
  payloadType `application/vnd.rebar.authorship.v1+json` (TS1).
- Key validity = git-commit-ancestry (TS2). The reducer keyring binds
  `{public_key, added_at, revoked_at}` where `added_at`/`revoked_at` are the KEY event
  POSITIONS; a resolver maps each to the introducing tickets-branch commit
  (`added_at_commit`/`revoked_at_commit`), and an event is valid iff its introducing
  commit descends `added_at_commit` and NOT `revoked_at_commit` — plus WHY the DAG
  (immutable) beats wall-clock/HLC ordering (backdating).
- Snapshot ledger schema `{event_uuid, content_hash, signature, signer_pubkey,
  position}` where `position` is nested `{commit_sha, position}` (the introducing
  commit + intra-commit order); a compacted event re-verifies from the ledger alone (TS3).
- Verdict vocabulary: the `verify-authorship` gate's own verdicts —
  `verified` / `unsigned` / `unknown-author` / `bad-signature` / the new
  `key_not_valid_at_era` — with the verified / unverified(bad-signature|key_not_valid_at_era|
  unknown-author) / unsigned display grouping (TS3). Note this is DISTINCT from the
  separate `verify-signature` (HMAC attestation) verdict schema, which is unchanged.
- Keep the docs-index linkage green.

## Scope
In: docs/identity.md + ADR 0045 rewritten to the approved design; docs-index stays green. Out: the implementation (TS1/TS2/TS3).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/identity.md` describes the in-toto Statement authorship, git-commit-ancestry
  key validity, the approved ledger schema, and the verdict enum + grouping — matching
  the delivered TS1/TS2/TS3 code (no HLC-epoch / raw-bytes / old-ledger language remains).
- [ ] `docs/adr/0045-authenticated-identity.md` records the approved decisions
  (in-toto Statement, opaque-id keying, git-commit-ancestry validity) with the DAG-vs-
  wall-clock security rationale and rejected alternatives, and NO HLC-epoch /
  merged-log-epoch / raw-bytes / old-`{author_id,author_sig,epoch}`-ledger language
  remains in the ADR body.
- [ ] The docs-index completeness gate passes (`python scripts/check_docs_index.py
  --check` exits 0).

## file_impact
- `docs/identity.md`
- `docs/adr/0045-authenticated-identity.md`
baseline.summary: transition: docs + ADR rewrite to approved design (in-toto, commit-ancestry, ledger, verdict)

## Context
`src/rebar/_store/event_append.py` is **794 LOC** on `origin/main` @5f4a5c1d40 — 6 under the 800 hard cap the CI module-size gate enforces, one feature from breaking the build. Re-measured after the `staging.py` extraction (267 LOC, owner of the `.tmp-newticket` convention) and the compaction change landed; neither relieved the pressure. Flagged by audit ae1b.

It mixes four independent concerns (full call-graph map in a comment):
- **A. pre-lock event preparation** — validate the event dict, serialise CANONICAL bytes, hand to `staging.stage_event`. No lock, no git.
- **B. bounded/retry-composed git verbs** — every lock-held git child, wall-clock-bounded, composing gitutil's index.lock + HEAD-parse retries with a local object-DB retry.
- **C. commit-failure self-heal** — recover a commit git refused for an unmerged (UU) or poisoned (missing-object) index.
- **D. locked write orchestration** — three `lock.write_lock(…, retries=…)` transactions, batch rollback, push/enrich hand-off.

## Approach — extract A and B as leaves, keep C with D
Behavior-preserving: moved regions stay byte-identical apart from import rebinding, and every relocated name is re-exported from `event_append`, so no consumer, monkeypatch target, or import path changes.

1. **NEW `src/rebar/_store/event_prepare.py`** (A, ~140 LOC) — `EVENT_TYPES`, `StoreError`, `event_filename`, `_ensure_initialized`, `_validate_event`, `_prepare_event`, plus the `canonical_bytes` and `reducer._version` (`KEY_ADD`/`KEY_REVOKE`/`TAG_DELTA`) imports. Composes with `staging.py` rather than duplicating it: `_prepare_event` keeps delegating the `.tmp-newticket` atomic-publish convention to `staging.stage_event`, its docstring pointing at `staging.py` instead of restating it. Leaf: imports `staging`+`canonical` only.
2. **NEW `src/rebar/_store/event_commit_git.py`** (B, ~220 LOC) — `_GIT_TIMEOUT`, `_run_git`, `_TRANSIENT_ADD_MARKERS`, `_GIT_ADD_ATTEMPTS`, `_GIT_ADD_BACKOFF_S`, `_is_transient_add_error`, `_with_transient_add_retry`, and the verbs `_git_add`/`_git_commit`/`_git_rm`/`_git_commit_paths`/`_restore_paths`/`_unstage`. Owns `import subprocess`/`import time` and the `# raw-git-ok:` markers, which travel with their functions. Leaf: it **imports** gitutil's shared retries and does **not** edit `gitutil.py` (concurrent work).
3. **`event_append.py` retains C+D** (~500 LOC, ~300 of cap headroom) — `delete_events`, `stage_and_commit`, `batch_stage_and_commit`, `write_and_push`, `batch_write_and_push`, `_rollback_batch`, `_maybe_enrich_drain`, `_silent_unlink`, and the self-heal set (`_recover_from_unmerged`, `_recover_from_invalid_object`, `_is_invalid_object_error`, `_staged_index_paths`, `_REGENERABLE_PREFIX`, `_INVALID_OBJECT_MARKERS`). Docstring retitled to that concern, pointing at the leaves.

### Why C is NOT split out — a deliberate seam choice
`_recover_from_invalid_object` and `_recover_from_unmerged` each re-issue `_git_add`, and `test_event_append_transient_retry.py::test_own_vanished_object_is_regenerated` does a SINGLE `monkeypatch.setattr(event_append, "_git_add", …)` that today reaches BOTH `stage_and_commit`'s add and the recovery re-add through one module global. Moving C out would put those callers in different namespaces and silently decouple that seam. C is also intrinsic to the commit step it heals, so keeping it with D leaves a coherent concern, not a residue. A and B have no such coupling.

## Re-export shim (zero test/consumer edits)
Every consumer and test reaches these symbols through the `event_append` module object. The inventory is derived over all three access forms — dotted `event_append.NAME`, string-literal `setattr`/`getattr(event_append, "NAME")`, **and ALIASED `<alias>.NAME`**, since three consumers import under an alias: `_seam.py` (`_store_append`), `inbound_translate.py` (`_store_event_append`), `tests/scripts/graph/conftest.py` (`_ea`). Aliases are resolved by grepping `from rebar._store import event_append as <alias>` then each `<alias>.NAME`, cross-checked with Serena `find_referencing_symbols`. That found one **alias-only** binding a literal-name grep misses — `conftest.py` calls `_ea.canonical_bytes` — so `canonical_bytes` MUST stay on the namespace. `event_append.py` re-exports, under `# noqa: F401`:

- from `event_prepare`: `EVENT_TYPES`, `StoreError`, `event_filename`, `canonical_bytes`, `_ensure_initialized`, `_validate_event`, `_prepare_event`
- from `event_commit_git`: `_run_git`, `_git_add`, `_git_commit`, `_git_rm`, `_git_commit_paths`, `_restore_paths`, `_unstage`, `_is_transient_add_error`, `_with_transient_add_retry`, `_GIT_TIMEOUT`, `_GIT_ADD_ATTEMPTS`
- RETAINED, not moved — concern C calls these directly, so `event_append.py` keeps its own gitutil imports `_with_transient_head_retry`, `discard_unmerged_paths`, `path_is_foreign_to_branch` and the `_INDEX_LOCK_STALE_S` re-export, plus `_lock`, `LockTimeout`, `RebaseGuard` and `import subprocess` under `# noqa: F401` (tests patch `event_append.subprocess.run`; it is the SAME cached module object `event_commit_git` calls, so that seam still reaches the relocated verbs).

`event_append` calls the relocated verbs by **bare name** (never `event_commit_git._git_add`) so the module-global lookup stays monkeypatch-visible — that preserves the single-`setattr`-reaches-both-callers property above.

## Structural gates checked
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` has no `event_append` keys → no path-key churn. `check_raw_git_writes.py` sanctions by inline `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` marker, no allowlist → markers travel with their functions.
- `test_lock_retry_zebrafish.py::test_opted_in_sites_are_exactly_the_declared_set` pins `{"event_append.py": 3, …}`; all three `write_lock(retries=…)` sites are in D and stay put, so the count holds.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py` — MODIFY: remove concerns A and B, add the re-export shim, retitle the docstring.
- `src/rebar/_store/event_prepare.py` — NEW (concern A).
- `src/rebar/_store/event_commit_git.py` — NEW (concern B).
No test, consumer, or `gitutil.py` change.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `wc -l src/rebar/_store/event_append.py` ≤ 560 (from 794; ≥ 240 LOC of cap headroom); every `src/rebar/_store/` file ≤ 800.
- [x] `event_prepare.py` and `event_commit_git.py` are each ≥ 100 and ≤ 500 LOC and each a LEAF — neither imports `event_append` nor the other (asserted by both module names being absent from their source), with `import rebar._store.event_append` succeeding.
- [x] Every prior binding resolves unchanged through the `event_append` namespace: `getattr` succeeds on the imported module for each of `stage_and_commit`, `batch_stage_and_commit`, `write_and_push`, `batch_write_and_push`, `delete_events`, `StoreError`, `EVENT_TYPES`, `event_filename`, `subprocess`, `_run_git`, `_git_add`, `_git_commit`, `_git_rm`, `_git_commit_paths`, `_unstage`, `canonical_bytes`, `_GIT_TIMEOUT`, `_is_transient_add_error`, `_INDEX_LOCK_STALE_S`, `_maybe_enrich_drain`, `_recover_from_invalid_object`, `_prepare_event`, `_lock`, `LockTimeout`, `RebaseGuard`.
- [x] Re-export completeness is a CHECKED, ALIAS-AWARE invariant: build the reference set over `tests/`+`src/` as the union of (a) `event_append.NAME`, (b) `(set|get)attr(…event_append, "NAME")`, (c) `<alias>.NAME` for EVERY alias found by grepping `from rebar._store import event_append as (\w+)` — today `_store_append`, `_store_event_append`, `_ea` — then assert `getattr` succeeds on the imported module for every name in it. baseline.description:
## Why
Every gate row and all post-ship dogfooding in this epic needs standing outcome instrumentation: today nothing routinely ties plan-review verdicts to downstream outcomes (post-claim edits, reopens, force-closes, verifier FAILs), so false-positive drift stays invisible until it burns author trust (the Tricorder <10% blocking-FP cliff). E1 froze the per-ticket **outcome corpus** (`runs/outcome_corpus.jsonl`, 628 rows) and the miner that produces it; this ticket turns that one-shot artifact into a **re-runnable gate-eval job** that classifies each reviewed ticket, emits trailing per-criterion FP-proxy metrics, and documents the alarm/demotion playbook.

## What
Commit a re-runnable **gate-eval instrumentation job** at `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/gate_eval_instrumentation.py`.

**Corpus acquisition (subprocess, not import).** The job refreshes the outcome corpus by invoking `mine_outcome_corpus.py` **as a subprocess** (`python <harnesses>/mine_outcome_corpus.py`, which atomically writes `runs/outcome_corpus.jsonl`), then reads that JSONL. It does NOT `import` and call `build_corpus()`, because that entry calls `sys.exit()` on floor-check failure (`mine_outcome_corpus.py:381`), which would terminate the caller; and the miner lives in a non-package `harnesses/` dir, so subprocess-by-path is also the clean invocation. A `--no-refresh` flag skips regeneration and reads the committed corpus (offline / CI use). It then reads each reviewed ticket's persisted `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecars via `rebar.llm.plan_review.sidecar.all_review_results`.

**Outcome classifier (deterministic; the honest finding is that the sidecar findings do NOT carry the separating signal).** Investigation against the 8 §5.2 cases proved a classifier over the sidecar findings *alone* reaches only **4/8** — the CAUGHT-BUT-IGNORED cases (c8cc, f5df) have finding profiles at or *below* the MISSED cases, because "caught-but-ignored" is a fact about the author's **post-claim edit**, not about what the gate saw. The separating signal lives in two outcome-corpus fields plus one sidecar-derived strength predicate. The classifier is a first-match cascade, applied ONLY to tickets with `had_persisted_review` AND a post-claim signal (`post_claim_edit_class != "none"` OR `review_round_count >= 2`); all others are **N/A**:

```
C1  post_claim_edit_class == "operator-attested-retag"  → CAUGHT-BUT-IGNORED
C2  review_round_count >= 2                              → CAUGHT-BUT-IGNORED
C3  has_strong_finding                                   → UNKNOWABLE
C4  else                                                 → MISSED
```
- `review_round_count` is the **git-walk outcome-corpus** count (true count), not the pruned
  on-disk sidecar count.
- **`has_strong_finding`** (the exact "substantive advisory" predicate, evaluated over the
  ticket's deduplicated round union — see Multi-round handling): ∃ a finding with
  `decision ∈ {"block","advisory"}` AND `priority >= 0.5` AND `severity ∈ {"critical","major"}`.
  The 0.5 floor is the codebase's own `RECALL_MIN_PRIORITY`
  (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py:299`); the severity conjunct excludes
  high-priority-but-procedural (P6/P9) findings.

This **core** cascade reproduces the 8 frozen labels at **7/8** (only c8cc, a lone `substantive-unclassified` case, misclassifies as MISSED). A `substantive-unclassified → CAUGHT` rule would reach 8/8 but rests on that single case, so it is **deliberately excluded** as overfitting and documented as such. The README states plainly that the classifier separates via outcome-corpus fields + a sidecar strength predicate, NOT via sidecar findings alone (which achieve only 4/8) — the load-bearing methodological finding.

**adverse post-claim edit** (used by both the classifier gate and the metrics below) is defined once: `post_claim_edit_class ∈ {"plan-authored-post-claim", "ac-strengthened", "substantive-unclassified"}` (the substantive classes; `operator-attested-retag` is handled by C1; `cosmetic`/`none` are not adverse).

**Multi-round handling (load-bearing — `all_review_results` returns every retained round).** `sidecar.all_review_results(ticket_id)` returns ALL retained review payloads (newest→oldest, up to the 50/ticket cap), not just the latest. For each ticket the harness forms the **deduplicated union** of findings across all retained rounds, keyed by `(tuple(sorted(finding["criteria"])), finding["finding"])` — so a finding that persists across rounds counts exactly **once** (no denominator inflation for high-round tickets) and a finding cleared in a later round is still counted (no omission of earlier blocks). `has_strong_finding` is `∃ a strong finding in this union` (consistent with the §5.2 investigation — 8c4f's strong finding lived in its earlier BLOCK round, cleared by round 2), and every per-criterion metric denominator below counts C's findings in this union.

**Per-criterion trailing metrics (FINDING-level, matching the parent epic's definition).** Over the trailing window (see `--window`), joining each ticket's deduplicated finding union to its outcome row by `ticket_id`, for each criterion C:
- **blocking_fp_proxy(C)** = (# of C's **blocking** findings whose ticket was subsequently
  adjudicated not-block-worthy) / (total # of C's blocking findings). The automatic proxy for
  "adjudicated not-block-worthy" is **`force_close OR reopen_count > 0`** (an explicit gate
  bypass, or a post-close reopen). The earlier `(no adverse post-claim edit)` disjunct is
  **removed**: blocking findings are remediated *pre-claim* in the review loop, so ~95% of
  tickets legitimately have `post_claim_edit_class == "none"`, and that disjunct would fire on
  nearly every honored block and mislabel it FP. This proxy is therefore a deliberately
  conservative **lower bound** (force-close can also happen for orthogonal operator-attestation
  reasons, ADR 0043), so the >10% alarm **triggers human review** of that criterion's recent
  blocks rather than an automatic demotion. Per-FINDING, matching the parent's "fraction of that
  criterion's blocking findings … subsequently adjudicated not-block-worthy."
- **advisory_application_rate(C)** = (# of C's **advisory** findings whose ticket later shows an
  adverse post-claim edit) / (total # of C's advisory findings).
- **rounds_per_ticket** = the `review_round_count` distribution over the window.
- **sample_counts(C)** = `{"blocking_findings": int, "advisory_findings": int, "tickets": int}` —
  the denominators (count of C's blocking findings, C's advisory findings, and distinct tickets
  touching C, over the deduplicated union in the window). Emitted with each criterion so a rate
  computed from a tiny sample is visible rather than hidden behind a bare fraction.

**Empty / degenerate input.** On the live store (628 reviewed tickets) the corpus is always non-empty; defensively, if the window resolves to zero tickets `--emit` exits non-zero with a message (rather than writing a trivial `{}`), a criterion with zero findings is omitted, and `--verify-repro` fails loudly if any of the 8 frozen case ids cannot be resolved.

**`--window N`** bounds the corpus to the last `N` rows in the miner's deterministic emission order (the corpus has no timestamp field; emission order is the stable proxy, documented as such — a strictly chronological window is future work needing a timestamp). Default N=200.

**Alarm / demotion rule (documented playbook).** When a criterion's trailing **blocking_fp_proxy exceeds 10%**, demote it from blocking to advisory via an ordinary `criteria_routing.json` edit (`default_posture: "advisory"`). Precedent for demotion on FP evidence: **T5e**, demoted to advisory in calibration-3 (task relishable-ammonitic-hoverfly). (T3/T10 are a *different* precedent — criteria kept non-blocking from the start; never demoted — so they are NOT cited as demotion precedent.) Dogfood monitoring, not a config flag; no gate/source behaviour change.

## Scope
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/gate_eval_instrumentation.py` — the job: a pure
  top-level `classify(post_claim_edit_class, review_round_count, has_strong_finding) -> str`
  (unit-testable), the `has_strong_finding` sidecar extractor, the finding-level metrics
  computation, and CLI flags `--verify-repro`, `--emit`, `--window N`, `--no-refresh`.
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/README.md` — classifier rules, the 4/8-vs-7/8 finding, the
  metric definitions + join key, cadence, and the metrics output path.
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — the alarm/demotion playbook (>10% blocking-FP rule, T5e
  precedent, operator response). The ONLY change outside `docs/experiments/`; documentation only.
- `tests/unit/test_gate_eval_classifier.py` — a golden test importing the pure `classify` and
  asserting the 8 frozen `(cls, rounds, strong) → label` tuples reproduce ≥6/8, plus a
  non-triviality assertion on a metrics fixture and a `--window` subset check.
- No change to `src/rebar/` behaviour — no gate or source behaviour change.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `--verify-repro` recomputes the classifier over the 8 frozen cases (MISSED: dc58-af7b,
      db7b-c8fd, 5886-d028; CAUGHT-BUT-IGNORED: c8cc-68b8, f5df-0069, 115b-ceea, 8c4f-b81c;
      UNKNOWABLE: 3006-e198), prints the confusion table, and asserts **≥6/8 agreement** (exits
      non-zero below 6/8). Proving command:
      `python docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/gate_eval_instrumentation.py --verify-repro`.
- [ ] `--emit` writes per-criterion metrics to
      `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/gate_eval_metrics.json` — a non-trivial object with
      ≥1 criterion whose `blocking_fp_proxy` and `advisory_application_rate` are **numeric**
      (a float in [0,1], not null) and whose `sample_counts` is a non-empty dict with a
      **positive total** (so the AC is NOT satisfiable by `{}`, all-null values, or all-zero
      sample counts). Proving command:
      `python docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/gate_eval_instrumentation.py --emit && python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/gate_eval_metrics.json'));assert d and any(isinstance(v.get('blocking_fp_proxy'),(int,float)) and isinstance(v.get('advisory_application_rate'),(int,float)) and isinstance(v.get('sample_counts'),dict) and sum(v['sample_counts'].values())>0 for v in d.values())"`.
- [ ] The pure `classify` reproduces ≥6/8 on the 8 frozen input tuples in a CI-collected test,
      and `--window N` yields a subset for smaller N. Proving command:
      `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_gate_eval_classifier.py -q`.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` gains a new **"Blocking-FP-proxy demotion"** section
      documenting the >10% `blocking_fp_proxy` alarm rule, the operator demotion response, and the
      correct T5e precedent (not T3/T10, cited inside that section); the harnesses README
      documents the `sidecar-findings-alone` 4/8-vs-7/8 finding. Proving command (both sentinels
      are new content — neither pre-exists in its file, verified by `grep -c`):
      `grep -q "Blocking-FP-proxy demotion" docs/plan-review-gate.md && grep -q "sidecar-findings-alone" docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/README.md`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green; landed through Gerrit (evidence: the Gerrit change id, merge commit, and CI Verified vote recorded in a ticket comment).
baseline.summary: R7: standing gate-eval outcome instrumentation + dogfood FP monitoring

## Why
Three sources disagree on the write-lock lifecycle:
- `docs/concurrency.md` I5 (lines ~107-117) still documents the retired **bash**
  `_flock_stage_commit` (`ticket-lib.sh:270`, FD 200) as the ACTIVE write path.
- `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` (docstring lines 7-23) frames the fcntl+mkdir dual acquisition as
  a **migration window** that "flips `dual_window` to `False` permanently after the bash core
  is retired" — yet still defaults `dual_window=True` (`lock.py:281`).
- `tests/integration/test_store_concurrency.py` states the bash core is ALREADY retired and
  that the durable single-impl mechanism is the unified dual-leg lock where "the mkdir leg is
  always taken, which is exactly what closed the gap."

So the lock module says the mkdir leg is going away, while the test says it is the permanent mechanism it relies on. A test cannot reliably enforce a contract the docs contradict. VALIDATED.

## Decision: dual_window is a PERMANENT, intentional contract (not migration residue)
Chosen because it is the zero-behavioral-risk reconciliation AND it is what the surviving code already assumes:
- The integration writer-storm gate explicitly depends on "the mkdir leg is always taken";
  the fcntl+mkdir pair is the durable descendant of the stiff-mop-lane gate, not scaffolding.
- The mkdir leg is the portable second window — atomic on POSIX where util-linux `flock` is
  absent (default macOS) — and underpins the foreign-host/shared-filesystem handling already
  coded in `_mkdir_lock_is_stale`. Removing it would weaken portable exclusion.
- Keeping `dual_window=True` changes NO production behavior; only the stale
  "migration-window / flips-to-False" narrative and the bash-era doc are corrected.

## What
1. `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` docstring: replace the "Tier D migration window / after bash
   retired `dual_window` flips to `False`" language with an intentional-permanent-contract
   note — fcntl (fast local) + mkdir (portable second window, atomic on POSIX / no-flock
   hosts) is the standing write-lock contract; `dual_window=True` is the permanent default,
   `dual_window=False` remains an fcntl-only escape hatch. No code/default change.
2. `docs/concurrency.md` I5: stop describing the retired bash `_flock_stage_commit`/FD 200 as
   the active path; describe the current Python unified fcntl+mkdir dual-window lock
   (`rebar._store.lock.write_lock` / `event_append`) as the permanent contract, mkdir as the
   portable leg on no-flock platforms.
3. Add an enforcing test (in `tests/unit/test_lock_stale_reclaim.py`, fast + deterministic)
   that pins the permanent contract behaviorally: holding the DEFAULT write lock creates BOTH
   the `.ticket-write.lock` fcntl file AND the `.ticket-write.lock.d` mkdir dir; with
   `dual_window=False` only the fcntl file is taken (no mkdir dir). Align the
   `test_store_concurrency.py` module docstring to the permanent framing (drop any
   migration-window wording).

## Scope
- `docs/concurrency.md`, `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` (docstring only), `tests/unit/
  test_lock_stale_reclaim.py` (new enforcing test), `tests/integration/
  test_store_concurrency.py` (docstring wording).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A single, consistent lifecycle statement across the doc, the lock module, and the
      integration test: the fcntl+mkdir dual-window lock is the permanent write-lock contract.
- [ ] `docs/concurrency.md` no longer describes the retired bash `_flock_stage_commit` path as
      the active write mechanism.
- [ ] The lock module's "migration window / flips to False" language is replaced with an
      intentional-permanent-contract note (default `dual_window=True` unchanged).
- [ ] A test enforces the contract: the default lock takes BOTH legs; `dual_window=False`
      takes only the fcntl leg.
- [ ] `make lint && make test` green.
baseline.summary: Settle the dual_window lock-portability lifecycle across docs, lock module, and tests

# A gate run does not notice its own binary is older than the base ref it pins

`review-plan` (and every other code-reading gate) snapshots the base ref's tree into `/tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots/<sha>/` and reviews against it, but nothing compares the RUNNING BUILD to that sha. A checkout that has drifted behind `origin/main` silently reviews new material with old code.

## Observed

Three consecutive `review-plan` runs were executed from `~/rebar/.venv` — a legitimate repo checkout venv, which is what AGENTS.md asks for — while that checkout sat 24 commits behind `origin/main`. The only symptom was one easily-missed line:

    WARNING rebar.config: rebar config (/tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots/2bce1407.../rebar.toml):
    unknown key 'verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets' ignored (typo? see docs/config.md)

That key is not a typo. Commit 74a7332606 ("9416: rename overlap_enabled for what it does") renamed `verify.overlap_enabled` -> `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets`. The stale build predates the rename, so it read the CURRENT base ref's config, did not recognise the current key name, and silently ignored the operator's setting.

## Scope

Operator decision (2026-08-12): this ticket covers the build-drift warning only. The fourth criterion of the original report — surfacing repeated non-fatal LLM step failures in run summaries — is split out to `eclectic-industrial-argali` (61a1-ee49-3c42-4b09), linked `discovered_from`.

## Design

All code-reading gates converge on `rebar.llm.gate_source.resolve_gate_handle`, which resolves the base ref to a pinned sha and acquires the snapshot handle. That is the one seam where a drift check belongs.

The running build's commit is already resolvable: `rebar.signing._gate_commit_sha()` returns the live rebar source checkout's short sha, falling back to the build-baked `rebar._build_info.COMMIT` (written by `hatch_build.py`) for wheel installs, and `None` when neither exists.

Drift = the running build's commit is a strict ancestor of the pinned sha, measured in the target repo. When the gate code and the target repo are different repositories the build sha simply is not present in the target repo, so the check finds nothing and stays silent — which is the correct behaviour, since drift is only meaningful when rebar is reviewing rebar.

The warning is advisory: reviewing from a slightly-behind checkout is legitimate, so this must never fail a run, never alter a verdict, and never change signing or provenance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1 — When the running build's commit is a strict ancestor of the sha a gate pins,
      the gate emits ONE warning naming the build sha, the build commit's date, the pinned
      sha, and the drift count in commits. It does NOT fail and does NOT alter the verdict,
      exit code, signature, or provenance stamp.
- [x] AC2 — The warning is emitted at most once per (build sha, pinned sha) pair per
      process, so a run that resolves the handle more than once does not produce a warning
      storm.
- [x] AC3 — When build provenance is unavailable or drift cannot be established, the gate
      is SILENT: no warning when `_gate_commit_sha()` returns `None`, when the build sha is
      not present in the target repo (gate code and target are different repos), when the
      pinned sha is unknown, when git is unavailable, or when the build is at or ahead of
      the pinned sha.
- [x] AC4 — An unknown key in a config snapshot is reported differently when the running
      build is known to be behind the pinned ref: 'unknown key X (this build may predate
      it; see docs/config.md)' instead of the 'typo?' wording, which actively misdirects.
      The default wording is unchanged when no drift was detected.
- [x] AC5 — Held-out unit tests cover: behind -> warns once; at/ahead -> silent; provenance
      unavailable -> silent; build sha absent from the target repo -> silent; and the
      config unknown-key wording in both the drifted and undrifted states.
- [x] AC6 — `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the unit + interfaces suites pass; every
      touched file stays under the 800-LOC module cap.

## Provenance

Found while re-running plan review for task b2bb during the store/signing remediation. Re-running from a worktree venv at origin/main is the workaround.
baseline.summary: Gate runs do not warn when the running build is behind the base ref

## Summary

The environment-aware `resolve_symbol` grounding tool (`pai_tools.grounding_tools`, bug 406f) classifies a resolved symbol as `repo-local` vs `third-party/stdlib` by root-containment alone (`_within_root(origin, root)` at `src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py`). When the virtualenv lives INSIDE the repo (`<repo>/.venv/.../site-packages/<pkg>`), a third-party dependency's origin path is under the repo root, so it is wrongly labelled `repo-local` — defeating the tool's whole purpose of separating first-party symbols from installed dependencies.

The discovery tools already avoid this (their `skip_dir` prunes `.venv`/`venv` via `_NOISE_DIRS`), but the `resolve_symbol` locality check had no equivalent exclusion.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Have a repo-nested virtualenv (`<repo>/.venv`) with a third-party dep installed
   (e.g. PyYAML).
2. Call `grounding_tools(".")`'s `resolve_symbol("yaml")`.

- Expected: `EXISTS: … [third-party/stdlib (site-packages), origin=…]`.
- Actual: `EXISTS: … [repo-local, origin=…]` — the in-tree `.venv` origin is under
  the root, so it is misclassified as first-party source.

## Root Cause

`resolve_symbol` computes locality as `_within_root(realpath(origin), root)` only. A repo-nested `.venv`/site-packages path satisfies `_within_root`, so third-party deps installed in-tree read as `repo-local`.

## Fix

- Add `_is_dependency_path()` (+ `_DEPENDENCY_PATH_PARTS`) to `src/rebar/llm/fs_tools.py`
  detecting `site-packages`/`dist-packages`/`.venv`/`venv` path components.
- Gate the classification in `src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py`: `repo-local` requires
  under-root AND not a dependency path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `resolve_symbol` classifies a dependency installed in a repo-nested `.venv`
      (origin under `<repo>/.venv/.../site-packages/…`) as `third-party/stdlib`, not
      `repo-local`.
- [ ] Genuine first-party source under the root (e.g. `src/rebar/…`, not in a
      dependency root) still classifies as `repo-local` (no over-exclusion).
- [ ] `_is_dependency_path` in `src/rebar/llm/fs_tools.py` flags
      `site-packages`/`dist-packages`/`.venv`/`venv` path components.
- [ ] Regression tests cover the in-tree-`.venv` case and the first-party `src/` case.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the affected unit tests pass.
baseline.summary: resolve_symbol misclassifies repo-nested .venv deps as repo-local

baseline.description:
The agent step-budget default is too low for the agentic plan-review VERIFIER, causing routine INDETERMINATE plan reviews on code-grounded tickets.

## Why
`DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS = 25` (env `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS`, src/rebar/llm/config.py:237) is too low for the agentic verifier (`plan-review-verifier-agentic`), which re-grounds findings against real code with tools. On code-grounded tickets it routinely exceeds 25 steps mid-verify → the `verify` step fails → the gate degrades to INDETERMINATE (`llm_unavailable`) → no signed review → the claim is blocked. Observed this cycle on `tarry-creep-range` (c38b): default 25 → INDETERMINATE; `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=50` → PASS + signed. Doubling the default to 50 removes the routine flake while staying well under the review-op floors that still apply.

## What / files
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — `DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS` 25 → 50, and refresh the env-doc comment ("25 ~= 12 tool calls" → "50 ~= 25 tool calls").
- `src/rebar/llm/completion.py`, `src/rebar/llm/code_review.py`, `src/rebar/llm/operations.py` — refresh the stale "REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=25 ≈ 12 tool calls" comments to the new default (the flooring to `_REVIEW_MIN_STEPS=120` / `_VERIFY_MIN_STEPS=240` is unchanged; the "far too low for review" sentiment still holds since 50 < 120).
- `tests/unit/test_config_llm.py` — the default assertion `(16000, 25, 600)` → `(16000, 50, 600)`.
- `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_review_budget.py` — the `cfg.max_iterations == 25` preconditions → `== 50` (the `>= _FLOOR` assertions stay valid since 50 < 120).

## Scope
In: the default value + the stale doc/comment refresh + the two test updates. Out: the per-op floors (`_REVIEW_MIN_STEPS`/`_VERIFY_MIN_STEPS`), `max_tokens`, `timeout`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS` is 50; `LLMConfig.from_env()` with no override yields `max_iterations == 50`.
- [ ] The `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS` env override and the `REBAR_LLM_MAX_ITERS` legacy alias still take precedence over the default (unchanged).
- [ ] No doc/comment still claims the framework default is 25 (the stale "=25 ≈ 12 tool calls" notes are refreshed).
- [ ] The review/verify op floors (`_REVIEW_MIN_STEPS=120`, `_VERIFY_MIN_STEPS=240`) are unchanged and still applied above the new default.
