## Context / Problem
`src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` is 798 LOC (2 under the 800 cap) and a "god command": it bundles the compaction **transaction** (`_compact_locked`, CCN 24), **snapshot reconstruction** (`rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log`, CCN 21), and the **CLI** surface in one file. Zero in-progress contention. Flagged by audit ae1b for both size and complexity. It also blocks bug `aea0`, whose one-line fix plus its rationale comment does not fit.

## Approach
Turn `compact.py` into a thin CLI facade over two extracted engines, decomposed by responsibility (the recurrence-preventing fix — future mechanism/format changes land in the engine module, not the command file). The public CLI entry points **stay in `compact.py`** so the contended `_cli/__init__.py` dispatcher is NOT touched.

1. **`compact_txn.py`** (NEW) — the compaction TRANSACTION: `_compact_locked`,
   `_sync_before_compact`, `_maybe_pause_at_rename_barrier`, `_git`, **and the snapshot
   primitives BOTH engines share**: `_git_author`, `_snapshot_strip_keys`,
   `_build_authorship_ledger`.
2. **`compact_rebuild.py`** (NEW) — snapshot reconstruction: `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log`,
   `_read_event_uuid`, and the rebuild counter. **Move the counter with its incrementer:**
   `_REBUILD_COUNT` and `get_rebuild_count` MUST live here, because
   `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` does `global _REBUILD_COUNT` — leaving `get_rebuild_count`
   in `compact.py` would read a different module global and silently report zero.
   `get_rebuild_count` is re-exported from `compact.py` to preserve its path.
3. `compact.py` retains the CLI facade: `compact_cli`, `compact_all_cli`,
   `_scan_snapshot_state`, `_usage`, plus the re-exports.

### Why the shared helpers live in `compact_txn`, not `compact_rebuild`
The dependency MUST run one way. `_compact_locked` needs `_build_authorship_ledger`, `_snapshot_strip_keys` and `_git_author`; `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` needs those SAME three plus `_git`. Splitting them — helpers in `compact_rebuild`, `_git` in `compact_txn` — makes each module import the other, i.e. a circular import. Hosting all four in `compact_txn` gives `compact -> {txn, rebuild}` and `rebuild -> txn`, which is acyclic, and puts the repair path in the natural position of depending on the normal path.

Complexity reduction rides on the move: `_compact_locked` gives up its candidate-parse, snapshot-envelope, retire/rollback and commit clusters to named helpers, and the rebuild gives up its source-partition and commit clusters. Update `.github/complexity-baseline.json` **downward only** (shrink-only ratchet).

Rationale (G6): the three responsibilities have different change-drivers (transaction safety, snapshot format, CLI ergonomics); separating them gives each a stable home.

## Preserve public + test import paths via re-export (G1G2)
Every consumer outside this module reaches the moved symbols through `rebar._commands.compact`, so `compact.py` must re-export them. The VERIFIED consumer set (semantic search + string grep, per AGENTS.md — the string grep matters because two sites name the symbol as a monkeypatch STRING):

- `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` — `_commands/fsck_repair.py:269` and
  `_commands/fsck_restore.py:202`, both importing INSIDE the function body (so the attribute
  is re-read per call and the string monkeypatch below still lands). Tests:
  `tests/integration/test_b636_rebuild_history_loss.py:78,138`,
  `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py:946`,
  `tests/unit/test_identity_4e9d_heldout.py:123` (via `_compact.`), and monkeypatched BY
  STRING at `tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_stale_channel_repair.py:46` and
  `test_fsck_stale_channel_repair_heldout.py:97,131,189,229`.
  **NOT** imported by `_commands/fsck.py` — fsck.py:281 only MENTIONS the name in a comment.
- `_snapshot_strip_keys` — `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:9`,
  `tests/unit/test_legacy_signature_mirror_drop.py:14`, and
  `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_creation_channel_compaction.py:138` (via `_compact.`).
- `_build_authorship_ledger` — `tests/unit/test_identity_gate_scope_and_ledger.py:362,401`
  and `tests/unit/test_authorship_batched_ticket_map_7084.py:176,215,238,244`.
- `get_rebuild_count` — no consumer outside `compact.py` was found; re-exported anyway to
  keep the documented path stable.

  Also `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_creation_channel_compaction.py:170` calls
  `_compact.rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` — re-export-covered, no edit needed.

These are plain `from ... import` / attribute consumers, so the re-exports keep them passing with NO edit.

## `compact.py` also needs these symbols for ITSELF — not only as re-exports
Distinct from the public re-export list above: the functions that STAY in `compact.py` consume three symbols this split moves out, so the facade must bind them back or it will not even import.

- `compact_cli` calls `_sync_before_compact` and `_compact_locked`.
- `compact_all_cli`'s batch-commit block (`compact.py:778-782` pre-split) calls `_git`.

So `compact.py` does `from .compact_txn import _compact_locked, _git, _sync_before_compact` in addition to the re-exported names. `_git` is therefore bound for BOTH reasons — the facade's own use and the module-attribute seam a test patches — which is why it is listed twice and must not be pruned as "unused" by a lint pass.

## Two test seams MUST be repointed — the monkeypatch hazard
`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_negative.py` patches implementation internals ON THE `compact` MODULE OBJECT, and those internals move:

- `monkeypatch.setattr(_compact, "_git", ...)` — `_compact_locked` reads `compact_txn`'s
  module global, so a patch on the facade does not take. This does not merely fail loudly:
  the compaction SUCCEEDS, the test's `assert rc == 1` fails, and had the assertion been
  weaker the test would have passed while exercising nothing.
- `monkeypatch.setattr(_compact.lock, "acquire", ...)` — `compact.py` no longer imports
  `lock`, so the attribute does not exist (AttributeError).

Both are repointed at the symbol's new home (`compact_txn._git`; `_lock`, which the file already imports). This is the ONLY test change, it is mechanical, and it is REQUIRED — the earlier "no test edits" claim was wrong and is corrected here. Both failures were confirmed empirically by running the suite against the split before touching the tests.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` — CLI facade + re-exports.
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py` — NEW (transaction + shared snapshot primitives).
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact_rebuild.py` — NEW (snapshot reconstruction).
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` — shrink-only.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_negative.py` — repoint the two seams above.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_rebuild_counter_b2bb.py` — NEW: the
  counter-increment proof (it needs the `rebar_repo` fixture, which is scoped to
  `tests/interfaces/`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `wc -l src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` <= 500; both new modules >= 100 LOC; the
      module-size gate is green. MEASURED on the merged change: compact.py 275,
      compact_txn.py 448, compact_rebuild.py 238; `test_module_size_contract.py` passes.
- [x] `.github/complexity-baseline.json` entries for `_compact_locked` and
      `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` are <= their current values (24 / 21) or removed
      entirely, and `check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports `new=0 increased=0`.
      ALL THREE compact.py entries were REMOVED (decomposition put every function under the
      reporting threshold) — a pure shrink, which the locked ratchet accepts. `--check` now
      reports `active=65 new=0 increased=0 stale=0` and zero `compact.py::` entries remain.
- [x] `_cli/__init__.py` is unchanged (`git diff --name-only <commit>~1 <commit> --
      src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` returns nothing), and
      `python -c "import rebar._commands.compact as c; c.rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log;
      c.compact_cli; c.compact_all_cli; c._snapshot_strip_keys; c._build_authorship_ledger;
      c.get_rebuild_count"` resolves all six names.
- [x] The counter co-location is PROVEN, not merely re-exported: a test calls
      `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` on a real ticket and asserts
      `compact.get_rebuild_count()` strictly increased across the call. Without this the
      suite could stay green while `get_rebuild_count` read a different module global and
      silently reported zero — the exact failure the co-location exists to prevent. (No
      consumer outside `compact.py` exercises the counter today, so nothing else covers it.)
- [x] Full default suite green — 11820 passed, 155 skipped. The only EDIT to an existing test
      is repointing the two monkeypatch seams in `test_compact_negative.py` (no assertion
      weakened); the other test file touched is the NEW counter proof, an addition.
baseline.summary: Split near-cap module _commands/compact.py (793 LOC) and reduce its local complexity

baseline.description:
## Summary
`rebar show` (and its JSON output) surfaces the internal `managed_refs` provenance
projection in a way that reads as a **live `relates_to` link**, even after that link
has been removed with `unlink`. This makes a correctly-removed link look like it is
still present, and makes `unlink` look broken when it is working correctly.

## Context / root cause
`managed_refs` (`src/rebar/reducer/_managed_refs.py`) is a **strictly-monotonic**
projection of every logical reference a ticket has *ever* managed. Per its own module
docstring (lines 32-38) and `add_managed_ref` ("Never removes", lines 92-103) it is
**deliberately never pruned by UNLINK/detach** — it exists so a local link/parent
removal can be propagated to a peer system (Jira) without being resurrected by the
next inbound sync. That behavior is correct and intentional for reconciliation.

The problem is purely **presentation**: `show` renders `managed_refs` alongside the
live link data with a `relates_to <target>` shape indistinguishable from an active
relation, with nothing marking it as "removed / provenance-only." The live link set
(`deps`) is the source of truth for what links actually exist.

## Reproduction Steps
1. `rebar link A B relates_to`  (creates the link).
2. `rebar unlink A B`  (removes it; reciprocal side removed too for relates_to).
3. `rebar deps A`  → shows `deps: []` (link is genuinely gone).
4. `rebar show A`  → still shows `managed_refs: [["relates_to", "B"]]`.
5. `rebar unlink A B` again → `Error: no LINK event found …` (confirms nothing to remove).

- **Expected:** after unlink, `show` does not present B as a current `relates_to`
  relation of A. Any provenance/ever-managed info is either hidden from the default
  human view or clearly labeled as removed/provenance-only, distinct from live links.
- **Actual:** `show` presents `managed_refs` such that B looks like a current
  `relates_to` link of A, contradicting `deps: []` and misleading the reader into
  thinking `unlink` failed.

## Impact
- Users (and agents) reading `show` conclude an unlinked relation is still present,
  and that `unlink` is broken — wasted debugging (this bug was filed after exactly
  that confusion). It undermines trust in the unlink/link surface.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] After a successful `unlink`, the default human `rebar show` output does not
      present the removed relation as a current/live link.
- [ ] If provenance (`managed_refs`) is shown at all in user-facing output, it is
      clearly labeled as provenance/ever-managed (removed links distinguishable from
      active ones) — not rendered identically to live `deps` relations.
- [ ] The live link source of truth (`deps`) and the monotonic `managed_refs`
      projection are visually/structurally distinct in `show`/JSON so they can't be
      conflated.
- [ ] `managed_refs` remains monotonic (this bug must NOT be "fixed" by pruning it on
      UNLINK — that would reopen the Jira removal-resurrection window the field guards).
- [ ] A regression test asserts that `show` for a ticket with a removed relates_to
      link does not present it as an active relation.
baseline.summary: rebar show surfaces monotonic managed_refs as a live link, making removed (unlinked) relations look present

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
S2 needs a lean contract that can describe routes and locate one execution/help parser without importing handlers or optional dependencies. Existing command sets and parser styles cannot be migrated safely until factory, formatting, validation, and compatibility rules are fixed.

## Approach
Add a stdlib-only CLI parser foundation and immutable route registry.

- Define a narrow factory protocol equivalent to `build_parser(*, prog: str) -> argparse.ArgumentParser`.
- Provide one Rebar ArgumentParser/formatter customization for deterministic width/order/newlines and compatibility-preserving parse errors/return control. It extends argparse; it does not define another grammar.
- Let route records hold lazy handler and parser-factory references plus identity/alias/visibility/help, mount/init, confirmation/output, and possible-capability metadata.
- Validate duplicate spellings, illegal alias/retired collisions, contradictory policies, unknown capability ids, malformed references, and resource/parser census state without resolving command handlers.
- Derive the legacy policy-set exports from routes and run a shadow comparison against all current sets/arms. Do not cut help or execution over in this task.
- Define reusable argument-definition composition for canonical/nested/compatibility spellings so aliases can vary `prog`/epilog without copying options.

The formatter policy is an explicit byte contract: fixed width independent of terminal, deterministic command/option ordering, UTF-8 LF output, and one trailing newline.

## Compatibility and Rollback
No public behavior changes. Existing help files and execution ladder remain authoritative. Reverting this task removes only unused expansion scaffolding.

## Testing
Use in-process unit tests with synthetic factories/routes. Observable oracles are exact formatted bytes, parse success/failure without process termination, deterministic validation findings, derived-set parity, and blocked imports proving registry construction resolves no handlers or optional packages.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The factory protocol and shared argparse customization produce deterministic help and compatibility-shaped parse errors from one parser object.
- [ ] Frozen route records represent every current spelling and derive compatibility policy exports with zero shadow-census delta.
- [ ] Registry validation rejects each synthetic duplicate, contradiction, unknown capability, malformed reference, and alias/retired collision deterministically.
- [ ] Import blockers prove registry construction and route lookup import neither handlers nor optional dependencies.
- [ ] No runtime help or execution path has cut over, and rollback is removal-only.
baseline.summary: RP-05 S2a — Define the lean parser and route registry contract

# Extract the gate read-root/session domain out of llm/config.py

## Context / Problem
`src/rebar/llm/config.py` is at 793 LOC against the absolute 800 cap, so SEVEN lines of headroom, and it is the most CENTRAL near-cap file in the repo (fan-in 93). Ticket d23e's entire scope is this file — a `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` deprecation alias, which must keep honouring the old name, warn, and prefer the new. MEASURED comparable: the `REBAR_LLM_MAX_ITERS` tombstone (`3eb3e71337`) cost +8 lines, and an alias is strictly bigger than a tombstone, so realistically 10-16 lines. Per-knob cost in this file is MEASURED at 10-13 lines. d23e is genuinely blocked.

## Approach
**ADR 0056 §Decision 5 pre-diagnosed this file and its prescription does NOT hold. Do not follow it.** It said config.py's problem is "178 lines of FLAT independent env reads" wanting "a declarative field table". Verified against the tree:
 * The SPAN claim holds (`from_env` is `config.py:575-753` = 179 lines) but the characterisation does
   not. Only 125 of those lines are the flat `return cls(...)`; the other 53 are an ORDERING-COUPLED
   preamble (the tombstone raise at `:581-584` must precede everything; `table`/`cli` must precede
   every read; `current_code_root()` must beat the env var, `:617-625`). Of 29 kwargs, 22 are regular
   and SEVEN are irregular (a derived non-knob `runner`; `api_key` env-only by secret policy; a 3-way
   `repo_path` cascade rooted in a ContextVar; `tickets_path` with no env var at all; 20 lines of
   custom `mcp_servers` JSON parsing; a nested `LangfuseConfig`; an enum-validating `overlap_drain`),
   plus two field/env/file name mismatches a convention-driven table cannot derive.
 * **A TABLE WOULD BREAK THE ENV-VAR DRIFT GATE — this is the crux.** `scripts/gen_env_registry.py`
   is a pure AST walk with no name resolution: it recognises a read only when the name argument is a
   STRING LITERAL (`:117-124`) and files anything else under "dynamically-constructed reads", where
   the variable DISAPPEARS from the table. A loop over spec rows makes that argument an
   `ast.Attribute`, so all 19 currently-resolved rows vanish from `docs/env-vars.md` and CI fails.
   `tests/unit/test_llm_config_pointer.py:259-267` exists to catch this class and names the precedent
   ("exactly what happened on sibling task f844"); `llm/model_classes.py:112-130` spells out nine
   literal `os.environ.get` calls rather than one indirection for the same reason. **The repo has
   already tried the table shape here and rejected it.**
 * In-file, a table nets roughly ZERO lines anyway (~66 lines of rows replacing ~110, plus ~20 of
   dispatch). It relieves nothing.

**What the ADR missed, and what this ticket does instead: 219 of the 793 lines are not configuration at all.** `config.py:51-152` and `:190-269` are the gate read-root / snapshot-session domain — four ContextVars and eleven functions (`current_code_root`, `resolve_code_root`, `current_tickets_root`, `current_code_sha`, `in_gate_session`, `gate_session`, `assert_gated`, `use_code_root`, `use_tickets_root`). `assert_gated` (`:216-240`) raises about `rebar.llm.gate_source` — it is a RUNTIME FAIL-CLOSED SECURITY GUARD, not a config knob.

Three properties make this the right cut rather than a mechanical carve:
 1. **The seam already has a consumer proving it real.** `llm/gate_source.py:35` imports exactly
    `gate_session, use_code_root, use_tickets_root`, and its module docstring (`:1-18`) already
    documents the block being moved.
 2. **The domain is INERT.** All 154 lines of gate-context growth landed in five commits on or before
    2026-07-09; ZERO since. Every commit after that date landed in the knob region. So this moves
    cold mass out of the way of the hot region.
 3. **One-way dependency, no cycle.** `gate_context` needs only stdlib + `rebar.config` + a lazy
    `rebar.llm.errors`; it imports NOTHING from `llm.config`. `llm.config` imports it at module scope
    for `from_env`. This respects `model_classes.py:16-20`'s rule that config must never import back.

LEAVE `config.py:155-187` (`_active_gate_config`, `gate_config`, `resolve_gate_config`) IN PLACE — it is genuinely about `LLMConfig` and moving it buys a lazy import for no benefit.

**HONEST LIMIT, state it in the change and the ADR: this RELOCATES MASS, it does NOT REMOVE THE ABSORBER.** The absorber is the ~10-13 line per-knob cost in `from_env`, and the only structural fix for that is blocked by the scanner. This buys about 15 knobs of runway, not permanence. The durable follow-ups are (a) teach `gen_env_registry.py` to consume an exported spec list — precedent exists at `:150-160` where it already imports and unions `rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY` — and only THEN table-ify, or (b) domain-split the knobs per feature cluster (the 12 `overlap_*` fields are ~115 lines but change `cfg.overlap_k` to `cfg.overlap.k` at ~31 sites). Both are separate epics.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — remove `:51-152` and `:190-269`; add a re-export block.
- `src/rebar/llm/gate_context.py` — NEW, ~202 LOC (clears the 100-LOC floor).
- `docs/env-vars.md` — one regenerated cell: `REBAR_GATE_ALLOW_UNGATED` moves file (`config.py:227`).
- `tests/unit/` — the headroom guard.

## Testing
**The relocation must require ZERO test edits. A required edit means the cut is wrong.** THE RULE THAT MAKES THAT TRUE: re-export the moved names from `llm.config` and repoint NO consumer in `src/`. 13 monkeypatch targets name a moved symbol, and every consumer of `current_code_sha` / `assert_gated` uses a FUNCTION-LEVEL `from rebar.llm.config import ...` (verified at `attest.py:123`, `:251`, `:429`, `sidecar.py:404`, `runner.py:259`), so the name is resolved in `config`'s globals at call time — exactly what `monkeypatch.setattr` rebinds. Repointing a consumer while a test patches `rebar.llm.config.<name>` is the silent-break mode ADR 0056 warns about.

Loud canaries, which fail at COLLECTION if the re-export is wrong: `tests/interfaces/store/test_pass1_fanout_gate_session.py:19` and `tests/unit/test_code_review_gate_session.py:27` both do a module-scope `from rebar.llm.config import <moved name>`. `tests/unit/test_provider_session_guard.py:173` patches `llm_config.assert_gated` and fails loudly if the rebind stops taking effect.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/config.py` is at or below 640 LOC and `src/rebar/llm/gate_context.py` is at least
      100 and under 800
- [ ] the seam guard for `llm/config.py` is TIGHTENED from the staged `<= 800` that sibling d8ef
      introduces to the `< 700` policy target, in this same change — the change that creates the
      headroom is the one that may assert it. (d8ef ships the staged bound because config.py is 793
      today; do not re-add a guard, tighten the existing one in
      `tests/unit/test_plan_review_workflow_ops_seam.py`.)
- [ ] the full suite passes with ZERO edits to any existing test file
- [ ] no module under `src/` imports the moved names from `gate_context` — every consumer still reaches
      them through `rebar.llm.config`, so the monkeypatch targets keep working
- [ ] `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py` leaves the tree clean, with the moved
      `REBAR_GATE_ALLOW_UNGATED` row regenerated rather than hand-edited
- [ ] the NEW module's docstring states, IN-REPO, that this relocates inert mass and does NOT remove
      the per-knob absorber in `from_env` — so the next reader sizing up config.py's growth curve
      meets that caveat in the code rather than in a ticket they will not read
- [ ] `assert_gated`'s hardcoded `logging.getLogger("rebar.llm.config")` (`config.py:230`) is
      re-pointed to the module that actually contains it after the move, and a test asserts the
      REBAR_GATE_ALLOW_UNGATED override warning is emitted on the `gate_context` logger rather than
      the `config` one. This is an AUDITED security-relevant warning — the message itself says the
      override is "audited" — so attributing it to a module that no longer holds the code sends
      whoever greps the logs to the wrong file. VERIFIED SAFE to change: `grep -rn '"rebar.llm.config"'
      src/ tests/` returns ONLY that one line, so no test filters on the name and no consumer keys
      off it. Swept the rest of the moved block for the same class: the only other identity literals
      are the three `ContextVar` debug names, which remain accurate under `rebar.llm` and need no
      change

- [ ] [operator-attested] the same caveat appears in the Gerrit commit message. Tagged because the
      completion verifier reads repository files ONLY and cannot read git history, so a criterion
      about a commit message is unconfirmable from the codebase and would burn a close cycle
baseline.summary: Extract the gate read-root/session domain out of llm/config.py

# Compaction: rename folded events to `*.retired` (invariant I1)

## Why
Compaction hard-deletes the event files it folds (`compact.py:140-144` `os.remove`). A delete/add reconciliation (a rebase — the RC1 class) can resurrect a folded source event -> `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT`. `docs/concurrency.md` I1 already SAYS compaction must rename folded files to `*.retired`; the code does not. Prerequisite for A2 (glandulous-potent-waxwing) rebuild backstop and A3 (entitled-unsweet-nutria) remediation.

## What
- Add ONE shared contract: `RETIRED_SUFFIX = ".retired"` + `is_active_event(name)` helper (in
  `reducer/_cache.py` or a small util), imported by compaction, the reducer, and fsck — single source of truth.
- `compact.py:140-144` — replace `os.remove(fp)` with `os.rename(fp, fp + RETIRED_SUFFIX)`.
- ORDERING/IDEMPOTENCY: write the SNAPSHOT atomically FIRST, then rename; a re-run after a mid-loop crash
  skips files already `*.retired` (the SNAPSHOT-present short-circuit at compact.py:227-231 / _scan_snapshot_state
  :266-268 makes a re-compact a no-op). Race guard: `if os.path.exists(fp + RETIRED_SUFFIX): continue`.
- ERROR HANDLING: do NOT silently swallow `OSError` — log WARNING per failure / INFO per success so a partial
  rename is observable; on failure, reverse already-completed renames before re-raising (atomic).
- `reducer/_cache.py` — exclude `*.retired` in BOTH listing paths: the `event_filenames` list (~line 97) AND
  the `*.json` glob (~line 102), via `is_active_event`.
- `fsck.py` — explicit `is_active_event` guard in the `_check_snapshot` loop; `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT` must NOT
  fire on a retired source file.
- `docs/concurrency.md` (I1) — align doc with code; ADD a `.retired` lifecycle note: retention permanent for
  now (accepted storage tradeoff); branch-wide `.retired` GC is a documented FOLLOW-UP (new linked ticket),
  safe only past causal stability. State that `.retired` files are benign under a code rollback (old `*.json`
  glob ignores them).

## Scope
Compaction + reducer/fsck `.retired` exclusion + the shared constant/helper + the I1 doc. Does NOT change replay ordering (A2) or remediate the live store (A3).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Step 0 (RED): write the two-clone merge+rebase resurrection test; record it FAILING on unpatched code.
- [ ] `RETIRED_SUFFIX` + `is_active_event` defined once and used by compaction, reducer (both listing paths), fsck. Proof: `grep -rn "\.retired" src/rebar | grep -v RETIRED_SUFFIX` shows only the constant def.
- [ ] `os.remove` gone from the fold loop. Proof: `grep -n "os.remove" src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` — no fold-loop match.
- [ ] SNAPSHOT written before renames; simulated mid-loop-crash re-run is a no-op (idempotent); rename failures logged (not swallowed) and reversed (atomic).

baseline.description:
## Symptom
Every `rebar transition ... closed` now detaches a compaction sweep (`rebar._commands.compact_trigger.run_sweep`, landed in `e0a55d5fac` / `d2dea317ec`). Observed today: a sweep held `.tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock` for **24+ minutes**, during which every rebar write host-wide failed:

```
flock: could not acquire lock after 181s (holder: pid=57999 held=47s pid_state=live)
WARNING rebar._store.lock: write lock still held after 60s (pass 1/3) — retrying
```

It blocked a `set-file-impact`, then a `transition ... closed` (which aborted with `could not acquire lock` after its completion verification had already run). A second sweep — spawned by a DIFFERENT worktree's close (`ci-config-schema-gate`) — did the same a few minutes later, so this is host-wide and recurring, not one bad run.

## The sweep is not hung; it is quadratic-ish
The process sits at **0.0% CPU** because it is I/O-bound on git. It spawns one child at a time:

```
git -c log.showSignature=false -C <tracker> log --diff-filter=A --full-history --no-renames \
    --format=%H -- '*<event-id>*.json'
```

That is a `--full-history` pathspec walk of the ENTIRE tracker history, with a LEADING-WILDCARD glob (so no pathspec fast path), run once PER EVENT. Cost scales as (events to fold) x (history length), and both grow with the store.

## Why this contradicts the feature's own design
`run_sweep`'s docstring is explicit that compaction "is optional housekeeping and must yield to work someone is waiting on, never compete with it", and that "a skipped sweep is a no-op for correctness (the events stay live and the next trigger folds them)".

The stand-aside probe (`_lock.write_lock_is_busy`) implements that — but it runs **ONCE, before** taking the store lock. After that the sweep holds the lock for its whole multi-minute run, so a writer arriving one second later waits the full duration. The guard prevents the sweep from STARTING during contention; nothing makes it yield to contention that arrives afterwards.

The design's own correctness argument is what makes the fix cheap: because an abandoned sweep is a no-op, the sweep is free to bail at any point.

## Suggested directions (not prescriptive)
- **Re-probe and yield mid-sweep**: check `write_lock_is_busy` between units and abort when a writer is waiting. Aligns with the stated contract and is correctness-free.
- **Do not hold the store lock across the whole sweep**: take it per fold, or fold into a scratch area and take it only to commit.
- **Fix the per-event git walk**: one `git log --diff-filter=A --format='%H' --name-only` pass building an id->commit index costs one history walk total instead of one per event.
- **Bound the work per trigger** so a large backlog drains over several sweeps rather than one long hold.

## Impact
Closes, `set-file-impact`, comments and reviews all block behind it, and the failure mode reads as a mysterious multi-minute hang rather than 'housekeeping is running'. In this session it required manually SIGTERMing sweeps twice to make progress — safe per the design's own no-op guarantee, but not something every operator will know.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A foreground store write arriving while a sweep is running acquires the lock within seconds rather than waiting for the sweep to finish; verified by a test that starts a sweep over a store with pending folds and asserts a concurrent write completes promptly.
- [ ] The sweep detects a waiting writer mid-run and stands down, leaving the store consistent and the unfolded events live (the documented no-op outcome).
- [ ] Event->commit resolution does not run one `git log --full-history` per event; verified by asserting the number of git invocations does not scale with the event count.
- [ ] A sweep interrupted at any point leaves no partial state that a later sweep cannot fold.
baseline.summary: Out-of-band compaction sweep holds the shared store write lock for many minutes

## Summary
`rebar review-plan <id>` unconditionally re-runs the full (billable, multi-turn LLM) plan review every time it is invoked, even when **nothing about the ticket has changed since the last successful review**. When several agents act on stale ticket state — or a single agent re-invokes after an unrelated `HEAD` advance — this burns tokens and wall-clock re-deriving an identical verdict. Plan review should be **idempotent against an unchanged ticket**: if the material the last review was computed over is unchanged, short-circuit and reuse the existing attestation, emitting a clear feedback message that explains why it did not re-run. A `--force` flag must let a client override and re-run unconditionally.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Run `rebar review-plan <id>` on a ticket and let it produce a passing attestation.
2. Without editing the ticket's description/acceptance criteria/type (i.e. the reviewed
   material is byte-identical), run `rebar review-plan <id>` again.
3. Observe a second full LLM review is performed (new billable call, ~minutes of wall-clock),
   producing a verdict equivalent to the first.

**Expected:** the second invocation detects the material is unchanged since the last review, **skips** the LLM call, and prints a feedback message (e.g. "plan review skipped: ticket unchanged since last review at <sha>/<ts>; pass --force to re-run"). The existing attestation is reused. `--force` bypasses the check and re-runs. **Actual:** a full re-review runs unconditionally regardless of whether anything changed.

## Notes / design pointers
- The plan-review attestation already records a `material` fingerprint (see the signed
  manifest, e.g. `material: c2b48241ad85a805`) and a `verified-at-sha`. The idempotence
  check should key on the **reviewed material fingerprint** (ticket content), NOT bare `HEAD`
  — a `HEAD` advance that does not touch the ticket's material must not force a re-run. Note
  the current claim gate treats an attestation whose `head_sha != HEAD` as "stale" and demands
  a re-run; that staleness definition is over-broad and is the root of the wasted work here.
- Decide the precise change-detection basis (material fingerprint vs. cited-code drift) and
  document it, so "unchanged" has one authoritative definition shared with the claim gate.
- `--force` must be plumbed through the CLI (`_review_plan`) and any MCP `review_plan` surface.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar review-plan <id>` short-circuits (no LLM call) when the ticket's reviewed
      material is unchanged since the last successful review, reusing the prior attestation.
- [ ] The short-circuit prints a clear feedback message explaining the behavior and how to
      override (`--force`).
- [ ] `rebar review-plan <id> --force` re-runs the review unconditionally.
- [ ] A `HEAD` advance that does not change the ticket's reviewed material does NOT by itself
      trigger a re-run (idempotence is keyed on material, not bare HEAD).
- [ ] The MCP `review_plan` surface exposes the same `force` override.
- [ ] Regression test: two back-to-back reviews with no ticket change ⇒ exactly one LLM call;
      with `--force` ⇒ two calls.
- [ ] Docs (plan-review-gate.md) document the idempotence behavior and the `--force` escape hatch.
baseline.summary: plan review re-runs on unchanged ticket; add idempotence short-circuit + --force override

## Context

Establish the nested `rebar bridge` CLI through a shippable vertical slice. The parent story originally proposed advertising all eight final verbs before their owning stories implemented them. That would expose broken placeholders on `main`. This task therefore registers only the two verbs it owns now: `preview` and `sync`. Later dependency-ordered stories extend the group only when each handler is functional.

`preview` is the read-only path over the existing reconciler dry-run mode. `sync` is the mutating path over the existing live mode. The legacy top-level `reconcile`, `jira-onboard`, `bridge-probe`, and `bridge-fsck` spellings remain unchanged at this boundary.

## Approach

- Add `src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py` as the nested-group parser and shared reconciler subprocess launcher.
- Keep `_cli._reconcile` as a compatibility wrapper around that launcher until story `4a44-4abb-ae91-4e51` retires the top-level verb.
- Route the help-backed `bridge` noun from `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`.
- Register only `preview` and `sync`: preview forces `dry-run`; sync forces `live`.
- Reject `--mode`, `--filter-local-ids`, and arbitrary trailing arguments so callers cannot override the read/write distinction. The public `--max-changes`, `--only`, `--except`, and `--max-age` flags do not exist yet; story `4a44-4abb-ae91-4e51` will add them together with their behavior and migration.
- Define exact discovery contracts: no nested verb prints group usage; `--help` prints usage; an unknown nested verb fails with the valid choices and never falls through to a same-named top-level command.
- Update `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` and regenerate `docs/cli-reference.md` for the nested group; add the new dispatcher arms and exit contracts to `docs/exit-codes.md`; update `docs/user-guide.md` with preview-versus-sync guidance; and update `docs/release-notes.md` to announce only the staged surface that actually ships.
- Keep public help free of the parent story's exact internal-vocabulary denylist: `mode`, `rank`, `gate`, `lock`, `cap`, `pass`, `binding store`, and numeric exit-code values.
- Preserve `Mode`, `MODE_CAPS`, the `gated_mode: "reconcile-check"` round trip, top-level `doctor`, and all legacy bridge spellings.

## Surface parity

- CLI: in scope and exercised through the real `rebar` entrypoint.
- Library and MCP: out of scope; story `f789-3f9d-8b35-4e0d` owns those surfaces.
- Automated workflows and scripts: out of scope; story `4a44-4abb-ae91-4e51` owns their migration.
- Dual direction: both preview/read and sync/write are proven here.

## Testing

Use a real CLI subprocess against a temporary git-backed tracker plus a stateful fake Jira transport built from production-shaped fixtures. A unit-only dispatch test is insufficient because parsing, subprocess wiring, mode selection, and persisted state are contractual.

RED-first oracle:
- happy path: `rebar bridge preview` returns the real reconciler JSON plan;
- held out: exact before/after snapshots prove preview performs zero Jira writes and zero ticket or bridge-state writes;
- held out: sync starts from an unbound remote-only issue, creates the real local/binding mutation, and preserves unrelated event bytes;
- held out: no-verb, help, unknown verb, top-level-name collision, forbidden flag, phase-gate, doctor, legacy-command, generated-reference, and exit-code-table contracts; the help oracle lowercases captured output and rejects every literal denylisted term and any numeric exit-code value;
- mutation: routing preview to live must fail the no-write oracle; routing sync to dry-run must fail the persisted-mutation oracle.

This wrapper adds no new composed store operation, retry loop, or cache, so the shared contention suites remain the responsibility of the reconciler core.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `rebar bridge`, `rebar bridge --help`, `rebar bridge preview --help`, and `rebar bridge sync --help` expose only functional `preview` and `sync` verbs with pinned exit/stream contracts.
- [x] An unknown nested verb fails with valid choices and never dispatches a same-named top-level command.
- [x] `bridge preview` performs zero Jira writes and zero ticket or bridge-state writes, proven by exact snapshots and the fake transport log.
- [x] `bridge sync` performs a persisted mutation from a production-shaped fake Jira fixture while preserving unrelated state.
- [x] `--mode`, `--filter-local-ids`, and unknown arguments are rejected on both verbs.
- [x] Captured `bridge`, `preview`, and `sync` help contains none of `mode`, `rank`, `gate`, `lock`, `cap`, `pass`, `binding store`, or numeric exit-code values.
- [x] `Mode`, `MODE_CAPS`, and `gated_mode: "reconcile-check"` remain intact and exercised by `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_mode.py` and `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock.py`.
- [x] Top-level `doctor`, `reconcile`, `jira-onboard`, `bridge-probe`, and `bridge-fsck` behavior remains unchanged; continuity is exercised by `tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_cli_heldout.py::test_legacy_reconcile_keeps_dry_run_default` plus the existing `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py`, `tests/unit/test_jira_onboard.py`, and `tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_fsck.py` suites.
- [x] `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` generates the nested group, proven by `tests/unit/test_gen_cli_reference.py::test_render_expands_the_staged_bridge_group`; `docs/cli-reference.md`, `docs/exit-codes.md`, `docs/user-guide.md`, and `docs/release-notes.md` describe only the staged surface that ships.
- [x] [operator-attested] Focused pytest nodes, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `make test` pass.

## Rollback

This is additive and changes no persisted schema. Revert the single Gerrit change to remove the nested group while leaving every legacy spelling intact.
baseline.summary: Add safe bridge noun with functional preview and sync

# Move fsck's shared filesystem primitives out of `fsck_repair.py`

## Context / Problem

Surfaced by the architectural analysis on `defaceable-icy-antelope` (which split `_commands/fsck.py` into a command driver, `fsck_scan.py` and `fsck_tracker_health.py`).

Two pure filesystem primitives — `_ticket_dirs` (list the tracker's ticket directories) and `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` (resolve the tracker's git dir) — live in `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py`. They are there for a historical reason, not a structural one: `fsck_repair` was the first module extracted out of `fsck.py`, and the helpers went along with the cluster that happened to move first.

The result is an inverted dependency. Neither primitive has anything to do with repair, yet four consumers now reach into the **repair** module to get them:

- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_scan.py` — the read-only diagnostic walk;
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py` — re-exports both for module-attribute callers;
- `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` — imports `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` (twice, function-local);
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_recover.py` — imports `_resolve_tracker_git_dir`.

So a store-layer module (`gitutil`) depends on a command-layer *repair* module to answer 'where is the tracker's git dir', and the diagnostic path cannot be read without loading the mutating one. Both primitives are also the sort of thing a future non-fsck caller would want, and would have no reason to look for under 'repair'.

## Approach

Move `_ticket_dirs` and `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` to a neutral home and repoint the consumers. Prefer an existing store-layer module over a new one — `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` is a git-dir resolution question, so `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` is the natural owner and already imports it; if the two primitives do not sit comfortably together there, put both in a small store-layer module rather than leaving either in `fsck_repair`. Assume the `gitutil` home unless the import graph makes it circular, in which case use a new `_store` leaf.

Keep `fsck.py`'s existing re-exports so `fsck.<symbol>` attribute access keeps resolving for the callers and tests that bind to it — that compatibility surface is documented in the architectural-analysis comment on `defaceable-icy-antelope`.

Behaviour-preserving: no logic change, imports repointed only.

## Testing

No new behaviour; the existing suite is the oracle and is run unmodified. The bindings at risk are exercised by `tests/interfaces/store/test_event_append_transient_retry.py` and `tests/interfaces/store/test_stale_lock_reclaim_write.py` (both import `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` from `fsck`), plus the fsck suites under `tests/interfaces/store/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: `_ticket_dirs` and `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` are no longer defined in
      `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py` — verified by
      `! grep -qE '^def (_ticket_dirs|_resolve_tracker_git_dir)' src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py`
      exiting 0.
- [ ] AC2: `_store/gitutil.py` and `_commands/fsck_recover.py` no longer import either symbol
      from `fsck_repair` or `fsck` — verified by
      `! grep -rq 'from rebar._commands.fsck.* import _resolve_tracker_git_dir' src/rebar/_store/ src/rebar/_commands/fsck_recover.py`
      exiting 0.
- [ ] AC3: `from rebar._commands import fsck; fsck._resolve_tracker_git_dir` and
      `fsck._ticket_dirs` still resolve — verified by a `python -c` import exiting 0.
- [ ] AC4: no test file is edited — verified by `git diff --stat origin/main -- tests/`
      producing no output.
- [ ] AC5: `make lint`, `make typecheck`,
      `scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` and
      `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` each exit 0.
baseline.summary: fsck's shared filesystem primitives live in the repair module

## Why
The engine needs a lean DECLARATIVE IR expressing steps + conditionals + loops + map as DATA — the git source of truth, agent-editable, and projectable to a visual editor. v1 is a strict acyclic DAG whose only control flow is an `if:` skip-guard, which cannot express branching, loops, or fan-out.

## What
Define a v2 schema extending the v1 GitHub-Actions-style YAML: route/conditional edges, loop frames (mandatory max_iterations), and map/fan-out over a collection; stable step ids. Add a v1->v2 migration shim and update the linter so cycles are legal ONLY via declared loop frames (raw `needs` cycles still rejected), with frame-scoped reference integrity and map `as` binding checks.

- src/rebar/schemas/workflow.v2.schema.json (additionalProperties:false retained)
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/schema.py, lint.py, migrate.py
Out: the interpreter (separate story).

- [ ] v1->v2 migrate shim registered in migrate.py with a golden round-trip test.
- [ ] Linter: raw `needs` cycles rejected; declared loop frames legal; frame-scoped reference checks; map `as` binding validated.

# Plan-review threshold + posture recalibration (approved pre-redesign changes)

## Why
Adjudication of would-block/near-block plan-review findings showed the gate UNDER-blocks: 15/20 findings in the 0.60-0.69 band on blocking criteria were block-worthy with ZERO false-positives, and four currently-advisory criteria (G1G2, T1, T8, E4) scored 75-100% block-worthy at their would-block slice. The 0.70 bar strands real blocks and the blocking set omits load-bearing criteria. (E1 and T3 also scored ~75% but are NOT promoted here — no threshold cleanly separates their borderline findings; deferred.)

## What
Apply the approved per-criterion thresholds/postures in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json`:
- Lower `block_threshold` 0.70 -> 0.60 for exactly: COH, E2, F1, G5, G6, T5e.
- Keep T4 @ 0.70 (its band findings were fail-safe migrations).
- Promote to `default_posture: blocking`: G1G2 @0.70, T1 @0.70, T8 @0.70, and E4 @0.75.
- E1, T3, A1 remain advisory. No other criterion changes.

## Scope
- Edit only the routing JSON + the plan-review unit tests asserting per-criterion `block_threshold` /
  `default_posture`. No engine or aggregation changes here (the impact redesign is a separate child).
- This is a deliberate BREAKING behavioral change: plans that passed before may now BLOCK. Rollout is
  coupled to the permissive-rollout child (ship the wider set first, tune via the calibration harness);
  rollback is reverting the JSON (single-commit, trivially reversible).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `criteria_routing.json` matches the table above EXACTLY (per-criterion `block_threshold` +
      `default_posture`); a test asserts each of the SIX lowered (COH/E2/F1/G5/G6/T5e @ 0.60) + the FOUR
      promoted (G1G2/T1/T8 blocking @ 0.70, E4 blocking @ 0.75) + T4 UNCHANGED (@ 0.70, blocking).
- [ ] Plan-review unit tests updated and green; `make lint` passes. Proving command:
      `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_threshold_recalibration.py -v`.
- [ ] DETERMINISTIC simulation (no live corpus): using the packaged routing + the shared
      `threshold_for` / `pass3_decide`, a test asserts that for EACH of the six lowered criteria a synthetic
      finding at priority 0.65 now BLOCKS (>= 0.60) whereas at the OLD 0.70 it would NOT have; and that for
      EACH of the four promoted criteria the posture is now `blocking` and a finding blocks only at/above its
      NEW threshold (0.70 or 0.75). (Live-corpus block-rate delta on the accumulated sidecar corpus is
      measured by the calibration child raptorial-galloping-dragon, NOT gated here.)
- [ ] No criterion OUTSIDE the approved set {COH,E2,F1,G5,G6,T5e,T4,G1G2,T1,T8,E4} changes posture or
      threshold. A test pins the COMPLETE expected routing as an INLINE fixture inside
      `tests/unit/test_threshold_recalibration.py` — a dict mapping EVERY criterion id to its expected
      `(block_threshold, default_posture)` — and asserts the packaged `criteria_routing.json` matches it
      exactly. Any unintended change to ANY criterion (approved or not) fails the assertion; the expectation
      lives in the test (versioned with it), so there is NO separate baseline snapshot file to drift.
baseline.summary: Plan-review threshold + posture recalibration (approved pre-redesign changes)

# WS-EVAL-EXISTING — make the migrated reviewers regression-gated

## Why

`verify_completion`, `review_ticket`, and `scan_spec` migrated onto the engine but
have NO standing eval coverage, so a prompt edit or migration is a blind cutover.
Worse, the eval LIVE tier is currently an unwired stub (`run_eval()` raises
NotImplementedError; deterministic scorer NAMES are inert strings with no registry
that executes them; the `eval-live` promptfoo step is a placeholder echo). So even the
4 existing plan-review/code-quality specs are validated for shape but never SCORED.

## What

Deliver eval coverage that actually gates, for the 3 uncovered reviewers, by also
finishing the shared eval-execution machinery (which benefits all 7 specs). Design
aligns with 2025-26 community consensus: a cheap DETERMINISTIC gate on every PR
(eval-discipline, zero-cost) and an expensive LLM-JUDGE tier OFF the PR critical path
(eval-live: manual + weekly schedule, non-blocking, cached, concurrency-capped).

## Scope (delivered via task children)

- Phase 1: author 3 eval specs (completion-verifier, ticket-quality, spec-alignment) + offline discipline tests.
- Phase 2: 2.1 deterministic-scorer registry + impls; 2.2 live solver w/ context-injection + repo-tool stubbing
  (the 3 reviewers read the store + repo via tools, so they are NOT inline-feedable); 2.3 per-reviewer dataset
  schema + validation (incl. scan_spec BATCH unit); 2.4 fixture corpus + label adjudication
  (completion-verifier FAIL findings need source-citation fixtures); 2.5 Inspect Task glue + eval-live CI wiring.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] 3 packaged eval specs exist and are validate_eval_spec-clean with disciplined cross-family judges (gates:false), at_least(k)/epochs, coverage threshold, non-empty gold_set.
- [ ] A deterministic-scorer registry exists; every scorer name used by all 7 specs maps to an implemented pure function; validate_scorer rejects unregistered names.
- [ ] `run_eval()` runs live for all dataset-bearing specs (no longer NotImplementedError) via a native loop over the eval solver (Inspect AI intentionally not used — rationale in eval.py); the 3 agentic reviewers run against a disposable fixture store via the solver.
- [ ] `eval-discipline` CI gates all 7 specs on every PR at zero API cost; offline tests assert dataset balance + non-empty gold_set (validate_eval_spec does not).
- [ ] `eval-live` runs on workflow_dispatch + weekly schedule, non-blocking, response-cached, concurrency-capped, fork-safe; provider spend-cap guidance documented.
baseline.summary: WS-EVAL-EXISTING: regression-gate completion-verifier/ticket-quality/spec-alignment (Phase 1+2)

## Operator-stated north star (2026-08-14)
The completion verifier began as a SIMPLE harness-native subagent/background agent: an independent agent with read-only tool access verifying a ticket's ACs before close. It was reliable. Runaway tool calls and context-window overruns — the failure modes ALL the banking/budget/recovery machinery exists to contain — only appeared after the transition from harness-native (DSO) to harness-independent (rebar). The only intended conceptual addition since is [operator-attested], a minor qualifier. Constraint: the verifier MUST stay harness-independent, on the same machinery as the rest of rebar. Goal: step back from the emergent complexity and refocus on a relatively simple, reliable validation that the ACs described in a ticket have actually been completed.

## Investigation directions
1. Root-cause the gap: why does rebar's structured_run loop wander where harness-native agents did not? Hypotheses: harness loops provided context compaction, higher-level search, and model-tuned stopping; rebar hands the model low-level read tools with no evidence pre-assembly, so every verdict is an open-ended search under a budget.
2. Invert the architecture — deterministic evidence PREPACK: assemble the obvious evidence up front (ticket + ACs + evidence comments; file_impact diffs/blobs at HEAD; commits carrying the ticket trailer; referenced test files; direct-child ticket summaries + their manifests) into the verifier's context, then ask for a single-pass verdict with a small bounded follow-up read allowance. A human reviewer works this way; searching should be the exception, not the mechanism.
3. Validate against data: the 7-day failure mining (session artifact verifier-failure-mining.md) shows exhaustion-before-evidence dominates. Re-run the mined corpus through a prepack prototype; measure false-unmet rate and tool-call counts.
4. Success criteria: typical story/bug close verdicts in ONE model call + few follow-up reads; false-unmet ~0 on the mined corpus; banking/recovery demoted to rarely-exercised fallback and enumerated as deletion candidates; budget machinery becomes a dumb runaway backstop only.
5. Relationship to in-flight work: 8d74 (generous budgets + child term + PASS-verdict cache) is interim symptom relief and stays; this ticket aims to make that machinery mostly unnecessary. New verifier complexity must henceforth justify itself against the simple-core goal.
baseline.summary: Simplify completion verification: evidence-prepacked single-pass verifier (harness-independent)

## Why

Cross-system sync (Jira today; Linear / GitHub Issues planned) must propagate a LOCAL removal of a reference (detach a parent, unlink a dependency) WITHOUT it being resurrected by the next inbound pass. The naive approach — gate outbound DELETE on an 'ever-seen' set projected from raw event history (as `local_label_intent` does for labels) — fails CLOSED across `compact_ticket`: compaction collapses the event log to a SNAPSHOT whose `compiled_state` holds only CURRENT refs, so a removal performed at/after the compaction boundary is re-resurrected (the exact churn). We also found the shipped parent CLEAR (drum-ruler-suit / PR #54) is un-gated and clobbers a human-set-in-Jira parent on a locally-parentless ticket.

The field (Unito/Exalate/FolderSync/Syncthing/ghas-jira-integration) validates the intent-gate concept; the load-bearing risks are state DURABILITY and unbounded growth. This story builds the durable, reusable primitive ONCE so parent + links (and future peers) share one provider-agnostic pattern.

## What

A monotonic, compaction-surviving `managed_refs` provenance set maintained by the reducer in `compiled_state` (so `process_snapshot` restores it for free across compaction), plus a shared, provider-agnostic gate the outbound differ uses to decide REMOVE-vs-ADOPT for any reference kind.

- `managed_refs`: the union of every logical reference this ticket has ever managed — normalized `(kind, target_local_id)` where kind in {parent, blocks, depends_on, relates_to}. Folded in process_create (initial parent + deps), process_link, and parent EDIT (incl. inbound-adopted refs); STRICTLY MONOTONIC — never reduced by UNLINK/detach. Deterministically serialized (sorted list) for SNAPSHOT byte-parity.
- Shared gate `should_propagate_removal(ref, managed_refs) -> bool`: a peer ref present + locally absent => propagate DELETE iff ref in managed_refs; else ADOPT inbound. Provider-agnostic (operates on local logical refs; each provider maps to its entity). Missing/absent managed_refs defaults to EMPTY => the gate returns False (degrade to additive-only: no remove, no clobber, no churn-delete). This is also the back-out posture — disabling the fold leaves the gate a safe no-op.

## Migration (existing + pre-feature tickets)

On the FIRST reduce/restore where `managed_refs` is absent (old SNAPSHOT, pre-feature ticket), the reducer SEEDS it from the ticket's CURRENT deps + parent_id. Seeding is safe in both directions: a ref already in local deps was either created locally or inbound-ADOPTED (rebar owns it -> removable); a Jira-only ref never in local deps is not seeded -> still adopted, never clobbered. A new event type / field is preserved-and-ignored by older clones (forward-compatible rollout; fsck WARNs on newer-than-binary state).

## Reclamation (bounded growth)

managed_refs is strictly monotonic in the reducer (no prune there — pruning in the UNLINK path would contradict monotonicity and re-open the resurrection window). Per-ticket ref cardinality is small (tens), so unbounded growth is not a practical concern at this scale. A safe reclamation requires the PEER snapshot (a ref converged = absent locally AND absent on the peer) and therefore must be a reconcile-time step emitting an explicit prune event — that is documented as a FUTURE hook and is OUT OF SCOPE for v1 (deferring it avoids the prune-vs-fold concurrency hazard entirely).

## Scope

In scope: the reducer `managed_refs` field + compaction preservation + byte-parity + migration-seeding; the shared provider-agnostic gate helper (with its own unit tests); docs establishing the reusable pattern. The parent + link CONSUMER integrations are delivered by the child tickets (tan-elbow-mica, wake-inn-parse) which import this gate; THIS story verifies the gate's API + decision via unit tests, not cross-ticket call-sites. Out of scope: active reclamation/GC (future reconcile-time prune); actual Linear/GitHub providers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Reducer maintains `compiled_state.managed_refs` as a strictly-monotonic, deterministically-sorted union of normalized (kind, target) refs, folded from CREATE/LINK/parent-EDIT (including inbound-adopted), never reduced by UNLINK/detach.
- [ ] When `managed_refs` is absent on reduce/restore (pre-feature / old SNAPSHOT), the reducer seeds it from current deps + parent_id; a test proves a pre-feature compacted ticket's existing refs become managed (its later unlink propagates).
- [ ] `managed_refs` survives `compact_ticket` (restored by process_snapshot): a removal performed before OR after a compaction boundary still propagates and does NOT resurrect — covered by a compact-then-reconcile test.
- [ ] SNAPSHOT byte-parity is preserved (deterministic serialization; the existing byte-parity guard passes).
- [ ] A shared `should_propagate_removal(ref, managed_refs)` gate exists, is provider-agnostic (no Jira-specific logic), defaults missing managed_refs to empty (returns False = no removal), and is unit-tested for the REMOVE-vs-ADOPT decision: a managed ref absent locally => propagate; a never-managed peer ref => adopt.
- [ ] An operator-facing regression proves the churn is observably fixed: unlink a managed ref locally, run two reconcile passes, the ref stays removed (not resurrected).
- [ ] docs/ documents the pattern (the gate contract + the managed_refs field + the future reconcile-time reclamation hook) as the template for future peer-sync providers.
- [ ] A reusable, provider-agnostic managed-ref provenance primitive both parent and link removal sync consume, with no Jira-specific logic in the shared gate.
baseline.summary: Managed-reference provenance: a compaction-surviving, provider-agnostic removal-sync gate

# J7 — Assemble `JiraDataCenterBackend` and hold it to the backend contract suite

## Context / Problem

With the shared Jira-family layer, the two codecs, the two identity models, and the DC transport in place, the DC backend itself is an assembly — but it must actually be *proven*. ADR 0035's "Proof-of-seam" makes the backend-agnostic contract suite the artifact that certifies a backend, and `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_contract.py` parametrizes its `backend` fixture over `["fake", "jira"]`. PR #120 added registry and transport tests but never touched that fixture, so its new backend was never held to the port contract at all.

## What J6 already landed (scope correction, measured against `origin/main` fdc2695a1)

This story's Scope was written before J6 [rebar:9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56] executed, and J6's change 1049 delivered more than this plan anticipated. Verified against the merged tree, NOT assumed:

* `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` **already exists** (273 LOC) with `JiraDataCenterBackend`, the
  `@register("jira-datacenter")` factory, and `_search_users_by_username`;
* `adapters/__init__.py` **already imports** the DC backend (line 16), so `select_backend("jira-datacenter")`
  resolves — J6 pins that with its own registry test.

So this story is NOT "write the backend". It is the part J6 could not do: **make the backend reachable through config, make it actually satisfy the `Backend` port, and hold it to the contract suite.**

## The port-conformance defect this story must fix (measured, not inferred)

`isinstance(JiraDataCenterBackend(transport=...), Backend)` is **`False` on merged `main` today.** The `Backend` `@runtime_checkable` Protocol (`_backend.py`) requires nine members; the DC backend defines seven and is missing **`query_project`** and **`assert_env_ready`**, both of which Cloud's `JiraBackend` implements (`adapters/jira/backend.py:162` and `:169`). Probed directly:

```
vendor True | project True | query_project False | assert_env_ready False
```

This is a production defect, not test bookkeeping, and it is precisely what the contract suite exists to catch — J6's registry test passed while the backend does not satisfy the port:

* **`query_project`** is the backend's configured READ/query scope, with NO create-time default applied. The
  inbound fetcher scopes its search to it and **fails closed on an empty/invalid value rather than querying
  every project** (bug 626d). Absent, the fetcher raises `AttributeError` on any DC inbound pass.
* **`assert_env_ready`** is the fail-fast that raises the neutral `BackendEnvError` naming the missing
  connection essential BEFORE the transport is used in bootstrap-band execution, instead of a cryptic
  downstream failure (ticket 97f2).

Adding `jira-datacenter` to the contract fixture makes `test_isinstance_backend_facade` go RED until both are implemented. The suite is the oracle: **the fix belongs in `backend.py`, and no assertion may be weakened to accommodate the backend.**

## Approach

Widen `reconciler.backend`'s `_as_choice` set to `{"jira", "jira-datacenter"}` and update the field comment, closing the registered-but-unreachable gap. Implement the two missing `Backend` members on `JiraDataCenterBackend`, mirroring Cloud's semantics but resolving through DC's own `resolve_jira_datacenter_settings()` (`adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py`) rather than Cloud's `acli_subprocess.resolve_jira_settings`:

* `query_project` returns `resolve_jira_datacenter_settings().project` with **no default substituted** — empty
  when unset, so the fetcher fails closed exactly as Cloud does;
* `assert_env_ready` raises `BackendEnvError` naming whichever of the DC connection essentials is missing —
  the base URL (`[tool.rebar.reconciler].base_url`) and the env-only `JIRA_PAT` — matching Cloud's message
  shape ("missing … configuration: …").

`JiraDataCenterBackend` already composes the shared layer [rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743] with `WikiTextCodec` [rebar:aac8-b283-22c1-4e66], `NameIdentity` [rebar:0a94-e104-7304-4d85], and the DC transport [rebar:9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56]; it advertises `SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`, and `SupportsAbsenceProbe`, and deliberately **not** `SupportsIncremental` — DC gets a full inbound scan in v1, since incremental fetch is an optimization with its own correctness surface and no client need yet. This story asserts that omission so it cannot be added by accident.

Provenance follows the epic's decision: DC-created tickets carry the shared `jira` creation channel and `jira-` local-id prefix, with the deployment distinguished by `RemoteRef.instance`. Nothing in the store vocabulary changes, so no migration and no compatibility gate are involved.

**Then extend `test_backend_contract.py`'s fixture params to include the DC backend** (constructed with an injected fake transport, exactly as `JiraBackend` already is at that fixture), so every generic port assertion runs against it.

**Alternative rejected:** adapter-local tests only (PR #120). They prove the adapter does what its author expected, not that it satisfies the port the core drives.

## Scope

- **`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py`** — implement the two missing
  `Backend` members, `query_project` and `assert_env_ready` (see the port-conformance section above). This is
  the file the contract suite's RED test drives; it was absent from an earlier draft of this Scope.
- **`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py`** — the inbound identity path derives
  BOTH the identity provider and its creation channel from the backend's vendor string
  (`vendor = select_backend(load_config()).vendor`, then
  `ensure_identity_for(vendor, …, creation_channel=vendor)`). For DC that vendor is
  `"jira-datacenter"`, which is NOT in the store vocabulary
  (`CREATION_CHANNELS = {cli, mcp, python, jira, import, unknown}`), so the mint raises `ValueError`.
  Measured on a scratch repo:

      creation_channel='jira'            ext=acct-cloud -> returned '4802-2404-6de4-4167'
      creation_channel='jira-datacenter' ext=acct-dc    -> ValueError: invalid creation_channel

  **TWO defects here, and they compound — the second is a trap set by the obvious fix to the first.**

  *(a) The active gap.* `_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity` (`:50`) returns early unless the assignee
  object carries a non-empty `accountId`, and `adapters/jira_family/identity_model.py:26` states that
  **DC has no accountId at all** — DC users carry `name`/`key` (REST v2). It is called with the RAW
  Jira user object (`:155`, `:321`), so on a DC deployment it exits at the guard. Result: Cloud mints
  ghost identities on inbound; **DC silently mints none**. Nothing raises — the mint is never
  attempted.

  *(b) The latent landmine behind it.* The channel rejection above is real but currently UNREACHABLE,
  because the `accountId` guard short-circuits first. It fires the moment anyone teaches the guard
  DC's `name` — i.e. the moment someone fixes (a) alone. And because the call sits inside
  `except Exception:  # best-effort ghost mint; never fail the inbound apply`, logged at DEBUG, that
  one-line "fix" converts a silent no-op into a SWALLOWED EXCEPTION, which is strictly harder to
  diagnose. This is epic AC6's premise exactly: the pass still converges either way.

  So the fix is BOTH halves together, and neither alone is sufficient: accept DC's `name` as the
  external id when `accountId` is absent, AND map the backend vendor to its FAMILY channel so the
  resulting mint validates. The ticket-creation path a few lines below ALREADY hard-codes
  `create_data["creation_channel"] = validate_creation_channel("jira")`, so the identity path is the
  inconsistent one. **Do NOT widen `CREATION_CHANNELS`**: that forks the store vocabulary per
  deployment, contradicting the epic's shared-identity decision, fragmenting one human's identity
  across deployments, and dragging in a migration + compatibility gate the epic explicitly avoids.
  **This story is the right home** because its `reconciler.backend` widening is what first makes a DC
  deployment configurable at all. (Folded in from bug [rebar:5f48-244c-7063-42d0], whose original
  mechanism description was corrected on that ticket.)
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — widen the `reconciler.backend` `_as_choice` set (currently `{"jira"}`) and
  update the field comment. **Use a symbol search, not the line number** that an earlier draft of this Scope
  carried (`:697`): the file has changed since, and the validator now sits near `:604`. J6 already owns the DC
  *connection* settings in this file (TLS/`allow_insecure`, `ca_bundle`, `resolved_statuses`); this story owns
  ONLY the backend-choice widening.
- **`tests/unit/test_config_reconciler_backend.py`** — the dedicated config-validator module (it already
  exists, 2.5K, and already covers default/explicit-jira/unknown-key/env-override). The new
  `jira-datacenter` load case, the env-override case, and the `"jira-server"` rejection case all belong HERE,
  alongside their siblings — not in a new module. Note its existing
  `test_unknown_backend_rejected_at_config_load` asserts `"jira" in str(exc.value)`, which still holds after
  the widening, so it needs no edit.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_contract.py` — fixture params.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/backend_support.py` — **decided, not deferred:** the existing `FakeTransport`
  is what the DC fixture uses. It already satisfies every `TicketTransport` member the contract assertions
  reach. It lacks `probe_remote`, which the backend delegates, but NO contract assertion calls it, and
  `SupportsAbsenceProbe` conformance is satisfied by the *backend's* own `probe_remote`, not the transport's.
  So: **add a one-line `probe_remote` to `FakeTransport`** (so the delegation is exercisable and the fake
  matches the surface the DC backend delegates to) and do **not** introduce a rival DC-specific fake.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py` — the reciprocal import rule. The J2
  checker already rejects `adapters/jira/` importing `adapters/jira_datacenter/` (the `_is_within(package,
  _JIRA)` branch in `_violations`), but there is **no rule for the other direction**: a DC module importing
  `adapters/jira/` passes today. That is the half this story adds.
- `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` — add `jira` to the clean-core-wheel absent-module list at line 86
  (today `langchain`, `langgraph`, `anthropic`, `inspect_ai`, `opentelemetry`). Verified safe: `jira` is
  declared ONLY in the `jira-datacenter` extra (`pyproject.toml:168`); the base `dependencies` are just
  `pyyaml`, `jsonschema`, `referencing`, and the `"jira"` at `pyproject.toml:24` is a *keyword*, not a dep.
- **`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py`** (new) — note the path. An earlier draft said
  `tests/live_jira_dc/`, which does not exist; J5 [rebar:c97f-90ae-4976-47c7] landed the harness under
  `tests/external/`, the only tier fenced off from per-commit CI. A live test outside it is collected by the
  default suite on runners with no Docker, no Jira and no egress, breaking CI for everyone. Landing under the
  right path also inherits the tier's three mechanisms: the auto-applied `external` marker, the
  `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1` opt-in, and the module-level `_live_jira_ready` sentinel that enrols the module in the
  all-skip canary — so this file MUST define one. J6 additionally established that a live module must FAIL
  LOUDLY (not skip) when the harness is reachable but the `[jira-datacenter]` extra is absent, because the
  canary counts collected-vs-executed globally and a sibling module's executing tests will otherwise mask an
  all-skip; **reuse the exact guard already written in `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_transport.py`**
  (`_live_jira_ready` / `_jira_extra_installed` / `_extra_missing_but_harness_up` /
  `_fail_if_extra_missing_while_harness_is_up`) rather than reinventing it.
  **Local-side provisioning is settled, not left to the executor:** a reconcile pass needs a local ticket
  store, a git repo and a rebar config, which the DC harness conftest does not provision (it owns only the
  Jira side — project, PAT, issue teardown). The `rebar_repo` fixture that
  `tests/external/test_reconcile_live.py` uses is defined in **`tests/external/conftest.py:159`**, the PARENT
  conftest, so `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` **inherits it by ordinary pytest conftest inheritance**. Use it
  directly together with the DC harness's `jira_dc_project` / `jira_dc_pat` fixtures. No new
  `rebar_repo`-equivalent is to be written.
  **But `rebar_repo` alone is NOT sufficient, and the wiring is specified here rather than left to the
  executor.** That fixture calls `rebar.init_repo()` and writes NO `[tool.rebar.reconciler]` config, so the
  reconcile subprocess would have no backend, no base URL and no credential — it would fail at config-load or
  silently drive the Cloud backend. The test MUST therefore, before reconciling:
  1. write a `rebar.toml` into the `rebar_repo` root containing `[reconciler]` with
     `backend = "jira-datacenter"`, `base_url = <the harness base URL>`, and **`allow_insecure = true`** —
     the latter is REQUIRED, not optional: the harness is `http://localhost:2990/jira`
     (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py:56`, overridable via `JIRA_DC_BASE_URL`), and J6's TLS
     validator in `_config_schema.py` REJECTS a non-`https` base URL at config-load time unless
     `allow_insecure` is set. Also write `[jira]` with `project = <jira_dc_project>`, which is where
     `resolve_jira_datacenter_settings()` reads the project from;
  2. `monkeypatch.setenv("JIRA_PAT", jira_dc_pat)` — `jira_dc_pat` returns a raw token STRING and sets no
     environment variable itself. This does reach the child process: `rebar._engine.engine_env` builds the
     subprocess environment as `dict(os.environ)` (`_engine.py:93`), so the PAT propagates.

## Testing

Contract tier for the port, plus a live end-to-end pass on the J5 harness [rebar:c97f-90ae-4976-47c7] because this story is the point at which the whole assembly first drives a real instance.

- contract: every existing assertion in `test_backend_contract.py` passes with the DC backend in the fixture
  params, unmodified — the suite is the oracle and must not be weakened to accommodate the new backend.
- port conformance (RED-first): `test_isinstance_backend_facade` is asserted to FAIL before `query_project` /
  `assert_env_ready` exist and PASS after — the defect is demonstrated, not merely fixed.
- `query_project` / `assert_env_ready` behaviour, in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/`: `query_project` returns
  the configured project and returns **empty** (not a default) when unset, so the fetcher's fail-closed
  contract holds; `assert_env_ready` raises `BackendEnvError` naming each missing essential and returns
  cleanly when all are present.
- capability: `isinstance` checks confirm `Backend`, `SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`,
  `SupportsAbsenceProbe`, and confirm it is NOT `SupportsIncremental` (the deliberate omission, asserted so it
  cannot be added by accident).
- config, in `tests/unit/test_config_reconciler_backend.py`: `reconciler.backend = "jira-datacenter"` loads;
  the `REBAR_RECONCILER_BACKEND=jira-datacenter` env override resolves; an unknown key still raises
  `ConfigError` naming the valid choices.
- import contract: the new reciprocal rule has TEETH — a synthetic DC-imports-Cloud source is asserted to be
  flagged, mirroring how J2's `test_checker_flags_a_synthetic_violation` proves its own direction, with the
  permitted `jira_datacenter -> jira_family` direction retained as a negative control.
- live end-to-end: a full reconcile pass against the harness creates a remote issue from a local ticket,
  round-trips a status change and a comment inbound, and a second pass is a **no-op** — idempotence is the
  postcondition that proves convergence rather than mere writing.
- provenance oracle: asserted in the **live** module (`test_reconcile_pass.py`), since only a real pass
  produces a genuinely DC-created local ticket — a DC-created local ticket has `creation_channel == "jira"`
  and a `jira-`-prefixed id, and its `RemoteRef.instance` names the DC deployment, pinning the epic's
  shared-identity decision.
- error path: a transport failure PROPAGATES — asserted at the unit tier with `pytest.raises`, driving a fake
  transport that raises on a write. **One behaviour, one assertion style:** the criterion is satisfied by
  propagation only; a caught-and-logged variant does NOT satisfy it, so there is no "or" for an executor to
  resolve.
- zero-unhandled-exceptions mechanism (live): **not `caplog`.** `rebar.reconcile()` runs the reconciler in a
  SUBPROCESS (`subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True)`, `src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:114`), and `caplog` hooks
  only the *test* process's `logging`, so it can never see those records — and on the success path
  `reconcile()` returns parsed stdout JSON and discards stderr entirely. The live test therefore invokes the
  reconciler subprocess DIRECTLY — the same argv `_lib_ops.reconcile` builds
  (`[sys.executable, "-m", "rebar_reconciler", "--mode", <mode>, "--repo-root", <root>]`, with
  `env=rebar._engine.engine_env(root)`) — with `capture_output=True`, then asserts on the captured streams.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `JiraDataCenterBackend` implements `query_project`, and `isinstance(backend, Backend)` is asserted
      `True`
- [ ] `query_project` returns the EMPTY string when the project is unset — no create-time default
      substituted — preserving the inbound fetcher's fail-closed contract (bug 626d)
- [ ] `JiraDataCenterBackend` implements `assert_env_ready`, which raises `BackendEnvError` naming each
      missing DC connection essential and returns cleanly when all are present
- [ ] `test_backend_contract.py`'s fixture includes `jira-datacenter` and the suite passes with no assertion
      weakened (`git diff` shows params-only change to that file)
- [ ] a test asserts the backend is NOT an instance of `SupportsIncremental`
- [ ] `FakeTransport` in `backend_support.py` exposes `probe_remote`, and a test asserts the DC backend's
      `probe_remote` DELEGATES to it (observed via the fake's recorded `calls`)
- [ ] the live end-to-end module exists at `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py`, is
      collected by the `jira-dc-harness` CI job, and its harness guards behave correctly — it SKIPS
      when the harness is absent and FAILS LOUDLY when the harness is up with the
      `[jira-datacenter]` extra missing
- [ ] [operator-attested] a DRY-RUN reconcile pass against the J5 harness completes with no unhandled
      exception — **evidenced**: CI run 30604756524,
      `test_dc_reconcile_pass_raises_no_unhandled_exception` PASSED against a real Jira DC instance
- [ ] **RELOCATED to [rebar:bda8-370d-23ad-4e36] (J9), not dropped:** the WRITING-mode criteria —
      a full `bootstrap-strict` pass converging, an immediately repeated pass writing nothing
      (idempotence), and the DC-created-ticket provenance assertion. This story CANNOT satisfy them:
      CI run 30604756524 proved a writing pass crashes with
      `'JiraDataCenterTransport' object has no attribute 'set_entity_property'`
      [rebar:a357-b747-ece9-4cf5] — a method the core calls from three sites and the
      `TicketTransport` Protocol never declared. That is a port defect outside this story's landed
      scope, and J9 is the story whose fix makes those assertions passable. The tests themselves are
      already written HERE and must pass there UNMODIFIED. Epic e369 still requires a proven live
      writing pass before it closes.
- [ ] the DC-created-ticket provenance assertion is WRITTEN in … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: J7 — assemble JiraDataCenterBackend and hold it to the backend contract suite
