## Why
With the threshold empirically derived (sibling story), flip the serious-tier code-review criteria from advisory-in-everything-but-name to actually able to BLOCK. Today only the two DET criteria (secret-detection, high-critical-security) can block; all 13 non-DET LLM criteria ship blocking_enabled: false at 0.95 — locked as the permissive-rollout invariant by ADR 0036 and pinned by tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py::test_code_review_only_det_security_criteria_are_hard_blocks. The field false-block risk is demonstrably near zero (0 finding-blocks in 162 changes).

- CRITICAL DISTINCTION (the reviewer's catch): `blocking_enabled` lives on CRITERIA (the routing keys in criteria_routing.json: `security`, `api-compat`, `db-migrations`, `deletion-impact`, `tests`, `scope-intent`, …) — NOT on the consequence-BINARIES (`data_loss_without_recovery`, etc.), which are decide.py severity attributes that set a finding's IMPACT, not routing entries. So the flip is: turn `blocking_enabled: true` on the CRITERIA whose Pass-1 findings carry the serious (0.9) binaries.

## What
- DEFINITE MINIMAL SET (not a provisional mapping): consequence-binaries are scored per-finding by the verify pass (content-based), NOT "owned" by a criterion, so there is no principled binary→criterion table to write. The empirical basis for WHICH criteria are block-worthy is sibling 9f25's adjudication. Therefore this ticket flips exactly ONE criterion now: set `blocking_enabled: true` + `block_threshold` = the EXACT numeric value 9f25 records as its derived priority-crossover threshold (b9c0 is stacked ABOVE 9f25, so that number exists at implementation time; b9c0 copies it verbatim — no independent guess) on **`security`** (the AGENT criterion under which the #518-class importlib code-execution finding lands — a security finding). Every other LLM criterion stays advisory at 0.95; the two DET criteria (secret-detection, high-critical-security) stay blocking as-is.
- Any EXPANSION of the blocking set beyond `security` (e.g. api-compat, db-migrations, deletion-impact, tests) is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE here and gated on 9f25's per-criterion adjudication showing those criteria's findings are block-worthy at the derived threshold — filed as a follow-up if 9f25's data supports it, NOT guessed here. (This is why #539-class correctness findings — which have no clean owning criterion in the overlay set — are not force-mapped.)
- Update ADR 0036 (dated note: permissive rollout concluded for `security`, evidence attached) and ALL THREE blocking-set pinning tests, each updated to the new approved set `{secret-detection, high-critical-security, security}` and each still asserting NO OTHER criterion blocks: `tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py::test_code_review_only_det_security_criteria_are_hard_blocks`, `tests/unit/test_code_review_ws2.py` — ALL THREE test functions that pin `security` as advisory/non-blocking break when `security` flips and must be updated: `test_threshold_for_default_overlay_is_advisory_at_095` (L39 `reg.threshold_for(["security"]) == (0.95, False)`), `test_threshold_for_takes_min_threshold_and_any_blocking` (L52 `reg.threshold_for(["security","performance"]) == (0.95, False)`), and `test_secrets_security_keys_are_the_ws5_blocking_handoff` (L64 `set(blocking)`), AND `tests/unit/test_code_review_deletion_impact.py` (lines ~102/104 pin `deletion-impact` blocking_enabled is False — which stays False under this minimal set, so that test's assertion is UNCHANGED but must be confirmed to still hold).
- Keep pass-3 separation intact: this is a threshold/posture CONFIG change only — no decide.py math changes.
- NOTE: this depends on 9f25's derived threshold; if 9f25's honest crossover comes out ABOVE 0.54/0.60, AC4's "#518-class findings now BLOCK" is revisited with 9f25's actual number (do not force a threshold to satisfy the AC — the epic's Definitions record this contingency).

## Scope
src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json, tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py, tests/unit/test_code_review_ws2.py + tests/unit/test_code_review_deletion_impact.py (the second and third blocking-set pinning tests), docs/adr/0036-*.md, docs/plan-review-gate.md (the cross-gate posture note), tests/unit/test_code_review_blocking_replay.py (self-contained serious-vs-NIT blocking replay). Depends on the derivation story 9f25 (consumes its derived threshold + its code-review derivation/replay script).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The `security` criterion has blocking_enabled: true at the derived block_threshold in criteria_routing.json; all other LLM criteria remain advisory at 0.95 (expansion beyond `security` is deferred to 9f25's data).
- [ ] ALL THREE blocking-set pinning tests assert the new approved set `{secret-detection, high-critical-security, security}` and each fails on any unapproved addition: test_impact_model_versioning.py::test_code_review_only_det_security_criteria_are_hard_blocks, test_code_review_ws2.py (all three security-pinning functions: test_threshold_for_default_overlay_is_advisory_at_095, test_threshold_for_takes_min_threshold_and_any_blocking, test_secrets_security_keys_are_the_ws5_blocking_handoff), and test_code_review_deletion_impact.py (confirm its `deletion-impact blocking_enabled is False` assertion still holds under the minimal set).
- [ ] ADR 0036 carries a dated enablement note citing derivation ticket 9f25.
- [ ] A SELF-CONTAINED replay proves #518-class (security) findings now BLOCK under the now-blocking `security` criterion while false-blocks stay 0 — WITHOUT depending on any sibling's not-yet-built script. ## Reproduction Steps

1. Ticket T is locally parentless (parent_id None) and bound to Jira.
2. A human sets an epic/parent P on T directly in Jira.
3. Run a reconcile pass.

**Expected:** local ADOPTS P (the prior behavior), since rebar never managed a parent for T.
**Actual (after PR #54 / drum-ruler-suit):** outbound emits a parent CLEAR unconditionally (local detached + Jira has a parent), DELETING the human's parent and suppressing inbound adoption. The un-gated CLEAR inverts the old adopt behavior into a clobber.

## Root Cause

The parent CLEAR added in PR #54 (`outbound_differ._map_local_to_jira_fields`, the `emit_detach_clear` branch) fires whenever local is detached and Jira has a parent — with no provenance check. It cannot distinguish 'we deliberately detached a parent we managed' from 'a human just set a parent we never managed'.

## Design (consumes the shared managed-ref gate from parent story safe-luge-nog)

Gate the parent CLEAR through the SAME `should_propagate_removal` provenance gate as links: emit the CLEAR only when the Jira parent ref is in `managed_refs` (we managed it, user detached) — otherwise ADOPT it inbound (the restored prior behavior). One shared pattern across parent + links.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The parent CLEAR is emitted ONLY when the Jira parent is in the ticket's `managed_refs` (a parent we managed, then detached).
- [ ] A human-set Jira parent on a locally-parentless, never-managed ticket is ADOPTED inbound, not cleared (regression test).
- [ ] A genuinely-detached managed parent still emits the CLEAR and converges (the drum-ruler-suit behavior preserved), incl. across a compaction boundary.
- [ ] Parent + link removal share the same gate helper (no duplicated provenance logic).
baseline.summary: Parent CLEAR is un-gated: clobbers a human-set-in-Jira parent on a locally-parentless ticket

baseline.description:
## Context

rebar's three LLM review gates — plan-review, code-review, and completion-verification — each produce a rich internal record, but only a fraction is durably captured today:

- Plan-review and code-review run a shared four-pass kernel (find → verify → decide → coach) and
  emit a reducer-ignored `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar. The plan-review sidecar drops the pass-1
  `evidence` and `scenarios` fields; the code-review sidecar persists only the *surfaced* findings
  (blocking + advisory + coaching) and omits the dropped / indeterminate / overflow buckets. Neither
  persists the numeric `block_threshold` a finding was judged against — it is resolved from the
  criteria registry at decision time and then discarded.
- Completion-verification is single-pass and emits a sidecar ONLY on FAIL; a PASS persists just
  signed counts, so a successful close leaves no per-criterion audit record.
- All review sidecars are pruned to the most recent 10 per ticket.

A downstream feature (the ticket audit-trail UI, a separate follow-on epic) needs a COMPLETE, self-contained audit record. This epic makes the stored audit data lossless and readable; it builds NO UI. The read layer it ships also makes the audit data scriptable via CLI/MCP — valuable on its own.

## Approach rationale

Enrich the existing observability sidecars in place (new schema versions) rather than introduce a new persistence mechanism — the sidecar path is already the durable, reducer-ignored, retained record every review writes, so extending its payload is the lowest-blast-radius way to capture the missing data. The signed attestation manifest is deliberately left carrying counts only (its integrity contract is out of scope); this epic enriches observability, not the signature.

## Scope

- IN: sidecar payload enrichment (plan + code), completion PASS-path capture + agent
  output-contract change, retention-cap change, the audit read layer.
- OUT: any web UI or rendering (the follow-on epic); asymmetric-key signing; changing what is
  SIGNED (attestations still carry counts only).

## Compatibility & rollback

Sidecar schemas are bumped (`plan_review_result_v2` / `code_review_result_v2` / a completion `_v2`); readers accept BOTH the old `v1` (rendered with the new fields absent) and the new `v2` records, so pre-existing reviews stay readable and no backfill is required. Each change is inert until it next runs; reverting a story restores the prior payload shape with no migration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All child stories are closed.
- [ ] After this epic, a freshly-run plan-review and code-review each write a `*_v2` sidecar whose
      payload contains every pass-1 finding across all buckets with its pass-2 verification, its
      pass-3 validity/impact/priority/decision/reason, the resolved numeric `block_threshold`, and
      the pass-4 coaching. Oracle: an integration test runs a review and asserts on the emitted event
      JSON.
- [ ] A completion-verification PASS emits a per-criterion audit record. Oracle: a test asserting on
      the emitted completion event.
- [ ] The audit read layer returns the full retained history for a ticket and its `relates_to`-linked
      code reviews. Oracle: an integration test seeding a ticket's histories and asserting the
      aggregate contains all of them.
- [ ] Every new plan-review and code-review `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar captures the full four-pass record:
- [ ] A completion-verification PASS persists a per-criterion audit record (not only counts).
- [ ] Review-sidecar retention is raised so a ticket's review history is deep enough to audit.
- [ ] A documented read API (library + CLI + MCP) returns the full retained audit history for a ticket
baseline.summary: Audit data enrichment — lossless capture of review passes

## Context

Prior work on baseborn-subtle-cricket, crushable-choosable-llama, and coercive-paediatric-bug measured earlier critical paths and org-wide runner contention; this investigation must distinguish execution time from queue time and must not re-propose rejected runner parallelism that leaves total runner usage unchanged.

## Plan
- Build a dated evidence dossier from current and historical gerrit-verify runs, job and step timings, workflow history, and the prior CI-latency tickets.
- Identify the dated 15–20 minute baseline to 30–40 minute regression transition and quantify mutation testing contribution using comparable runs or a controlled local/CI experiment.
- Generate falsifiable rival hypotheses and run discriminating experiments, including runtime evidence for dynamic causes.
- Record a cited root cause and reference existing tickets for every remediation to prove whether it is new, accepted, completed, or previously rejected.
- If existing telemetry is insufficient, add the smallest assurance-neutral observability needed, validate it, and land it through Gerrit before concluding.
- Propose wall-clock reductions that preserve coverage and do not rely on increasing parallel jobs or unchanged aggregate runner consumption.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The current 30–40 minute symptom is decomposed into workflow queue time, job queue time, and execution critical path across a representative run sample.
- [x] The dated 15–20 minute baseline to 30–40 minute regression transition is identified with workflow or commit evidence.
- [x] Mutation testing has a specific measured wall-clock and runner-time contribution, including comparable before and after evidence.

baseline.description:
# Parallelize the container fan-out with warm-then-fan-out + fix the centrality budget cap

## Why
The container loop is sequential (`2*N` calls ≈ 27 min wall-clock). Parallelizing fixes latency. But caching
(S1) is write-once/read-many — a NAIVE concurrent fan-out makes all calls MISS+WRITE (≈20x input cost, no read
benefit). So parallelization must WARM the cache first. Separately, the per-plan budget cap scales UP with child
count (centrality), disabling shedding for exactly the large epics that need it.

## What
- Move the container pairings out of the sequential `for crit: for child:` loop into the existing
  `ThreadPoolExecutor` (`pass1.py`).
- WARM-THEN-FAN-OUT: run ONE warming call first, await its first streamed token (the cache becomes readable once
  the first response begins), THEN fan out the remaining pairings concurrently so they READ the cached prefix
  rather than all re-writing it. (Optional: a pre-warm call at gate start.)
- Fix the budget cap that scales with centrality (`sizing.py` `base*(1+centrality)`) so shedding engages for
  large epics instead of being disabled by the very signal (more children) that should trigger it.

## Scope
- In: container parallelization; the warm-then-fan-out sequencing; the budget-cap fix.
- Out: the caching mechanism (S1, dependency); merge (S4); bin-pack (S5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Container pairings run concurrently in the thread pool (not the sequential loop).
- [ ] Warm-then-fan-out: one call warms the cache before the fan-out; on anthropic the fanned-out calls show
      `cache_read_input_tokens > 0` (NOT all writes) — proven by a test/measurement.
- [ ] The per-plan budget cap no longer disables shedding as child count grows (a large epic sheds as intended).
- [ ] An 8-child epic review wall-clock drops to minutes; `make lint` + tests pass.

## Remediation (opus review — MAJOR 4/5)
- The runner is NON-streaming (`run_sync` blocks). Warm = run ONE pairing TO COMPLETION, then fan out the rest —
  not "await first streamed token". The warm pairing is the FIRST REAL pairing; keep its findings; fan out the
  remaining N-1; aggregate must equal the sequential baseline (no dup/drop).
- There is NO open ThreadPoolExecutor at `_run_container` (the Pass-1 pool closed at pass1.py:336). Create a NEW
  pool inside `_run_container`.
- Gate warming on `est_tokens(plan) >= 4096` (cache floor; reuse det_floor.est_tokens) — else fan out directly
  (no warm), since a sub-floor prefix never caches and warming would just add a serialized call.
- Warm-call failure: systemic (LLMUnavailableError) -> abort like the Pass-1 tier (pass1.py:327-331); non-systemic
  -> degrade to a direct fan-out (accept all-miss), never hang.
- Budget cap: do NOT invert centrality — shedding marks G3/G4 INDETERMINATE, so the naive "fix" would DROP
  child-coverage/consistency on the most central epics (a fidelity regression the epic AC forbids). Instead:
  container criteria are NEVER shed; the cap bounds only overlay/agent spend; correct the COST MODEL
  (sizing.py:206 `len(cont)*n_children*COST_AGENT`) rather than the centrality scaling.
- [ ] Warm = first real pairing run to completion; aggregate finding set equals the sequential baseline (no dup/drop).
- [ ] A NEW thread pool runs the remaining pairings concurrently; on anthropic the fanned-out calls show cache_read>0.
- [ ] Warming is skipped when est_tokens(plan) < 4096 (fan out directly); warm-call systemic failure aborts,
      non-systemic failure degrades to direct fan-out.
- [ ] Container criteria are NEVER shed by the budget cap; the cap bounds only overlay/agent spend (numeric target stated).
baseline.summary: Parallelize the container fan-out with warm-then-fan-out + fix the centrality budget cap

# CI: `cast Verified` casts NO vote when workflow-conclusion aggregation resolves to `skipped` — green CI leaves the change un-landable

## Summary

The `cast Verified` job in `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` (~lines 442-468) aggregates this run's job conclusions via `im-open/workflow-conclusion@v3.0.0` into `WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION`, then casts the Gerrit `Verified` label from it (`vote-type: ${{ env.WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION }}`, success→+1, failure|cancelled→-1). When the aggregation resolves to **`skipped`** — even though every real CI job SUCCEEDED — the cast step aborts with `##[error]Unknown vote-type 'skipped': expected clear, success, failure or cancelled` (exit 1), so **no `Verified` vote is posted at all**. The change then sits at `Verified = (none)` and is un-submittable despite fully-green CI, until a human notices and comments `recheck`. Two defects compound here:

1. **The aggregation can yield `skipped` spuriously.** The workflow's own comment (lines ~444-447)
   notes `im-open/workflow-conclusion` takes a REST list-jobs *snapshot* that depends on the
   needed jobs being terminal first; a timing/ordering race can fold a not-yet-finalized job in
   as `skipped`, producing an overall `WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION=skipped` while the jobs are actually
   green.
2. **The cast step is not robust to an unexpected conclusion.** `skipped` (and any value outside
   `clear|success|failure|cancelled`) hard-errors the job instead of failing safe — so a transient
   aggregation glitch becomes a **silent no-vote block** (the change looks stuck, not failed),
   rather than a clear `-1` or an automatic retry.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Push a change to `refs/for/main` whose CI is fully green.
2. Observe (occasionally) that all CI matrix/optionality/golden-path jobs succeed, but the final
   `cast Verified` job FAILS with `Unknown vote-type 'skipped'`, and the Gerrit `Verified` label
   stays unset.
3. Comment `recheck`; the re-run casts `Verified +1` normally.

**Observed instance:** change 743 (`eclectic-spotted-barb`), GitHub Actions run 29540921742. Jobs: `CI (ubuntu, py3.11/3.12/3.13)`, `CI (macos, py3.13)`, `golden-path`, all `optionality`, `require resolvable rebar ticket` = **success**; only `cast Verified` = **failure** (`WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION: skipped`, `VOTE_TYPE: skipped` → exit 1). No `Verified` vote posted.

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** green CI casts `Verified +1` deterministically; a transient aggregation hiccup
  either resolves to the true conclusion or fails in a way that still lands a vote / auto-retries,
  never leaving a green change silently voteless.
- **Actual:** an aggregation that resolves to `skipped` aborts the cast job, posting no `Verified`
  vote; the change is stuck until a manual `recheck`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The `cast Verified` step handles a `skipped`/unexpected `WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION` without
  leaving the change voteless — e.g. it re-resolves the true conclusion (re-query after all needed
  jobs are terminal), or maps an unexpected value to a safe, actionable outcome (retry, or a clear
  `-1` with a diagnostic), never a bare exit-1 that posts nothing.
  - Proving: a run whose aggregation would resolve `skipped` still results in a posted `Verified`
    vote (or an explicit retry), verified against `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`.
- [ ] The aggregation is hardened against the terminal-ordering race (the needed jobs are
  guaranteed terminal before the snapshot, or the snapshot ignores `skipped` when successes exist),
  so `WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION` reflects the real conclusion.
- [ ] A regression guard (workflow unit/lint or a documented manual check) covers the
  `skipped`-conclusion path.

## Notes

Discovered while landing the enrich-queue prune race fix (`eclectic-spotted-barb`, change 743): all CI green, but `Verified` never posted due to this. Not a defect in that change's code — a pre-existing CI-orchestration flake. Worked around via `recheck`.
baseline.summary: CI: `cast Verified` casts NO vote when workflow-conclusion aggregation resolves to `skipped` — green CI leaves the change un-landable

## Summary

No CI workflow enables pip dependency caching, so every job/matrix cell re-downloads and rebuilds the heavy `.[dev]`→`[agents]` stack (langchain/langgraph/anthropic/pydantic-ai/inspect-ai/opentelemetry). Measured cold-vs-warm install into a fresh venv with an isolated pip cache: cold ~19s → warm ~9s locally (cache ~52 MB) — caching roughly halves install time by avoiding the re-download. The per-job saving is modest but multiplies across the ~10+ jobs/cells that install deps.

## What

Add `cache: 'pip'` + `cache-dependency-path: pyproject.toml` to EVERY `actions/setup-python` step that subsequently installs project deps, across ALL `.github/workflows/*`. Deps live in `pyproject.toml` (no separate lockfile), so the cache is keyed on it: a dependency bump changes the key and invalidates the cache automatically. Caching is purely additive — a cache miss behaves exactly as today.

## Scope (files)

Every workflow with a dep-installing `setup-python` step:

- `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` (require-ticket, build-and-test, golden-path)
- `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` (reusable; 4 steps)
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` (lint, pip-audit, test, external, golden-path)
- `.github/workflows/eval.yml`, `.github/workflows/eval-plan-review-container.yml`
- `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml`
- `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`, `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml`
- `.github/workflows/mirror-guard.yml`, `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yaml`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `cache: 'pip'` + `cache-dependency-path: pyproject.toml` is set on EVERY
  `actions/setup-python` step that installs project deps across all
  `.github/workflows/*` — verifiable by grep: no dep-installing `setup-python`
  step lacks the two `cache*` inputs.
- [ ] The cache is keyed on `pyproject.toml` content (via
  `cache-dependency-path`), so a dependency change mints a new cache key —
  verifiable from the config alone (no lockfile involved).
- [ ] YAML remains valid (`python -c "import yaml; ..."`) and each affected
  install step is otherwise byte-for-byte unchanged apart from the two added
  `cache*` inputs on its `setup-python`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] A repeat CI run on an unchanged `pyproject.toml` logs a
  pip cache hit (the `setup-python` "restore cache" step reports a cache
  restore), recorded as a comment citing the specific run.
- [ ] Change passes CI (`Verified +1`) and lands via Gerrit.
baseline.summary: Enable pip caching on all setup-python steps in CI workflows

## Context
Two accepted reliability oracles still consume multi-second wall time per matrix cell: test_slow_but_progressing_remote_is_not_aborted deliberately serves for 15 seconds (15.1s in current macOS CI; original behavior ticket suave-constant-cow), and test_read_retried_then_terminal uses one-second timeout/grace/drain windows across retries (9.06s; original behavior ticket fizzy-trunk-salt). Their real process/socket coverage is load-bearing, but the production-scale durations are not.

## Plan
Retain one real socket/process-group sentinel for each mechanism while injecting smaller test-only stall, timeout, grace, and drain windows with generous scheduling headroom. Keep semantic attempt/reap/throughput assertions and use polling rather than brittle absolute-time pass conditions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Slow-progress still crosses a full configured low-speed window and proves throughput, not elapsed wall time, prevents abort.
- [ ] ACLI read still spawns exactly the production retry count and proves every process group is reaped.
- [ ] Production timeout/stall defaults are unchanged.
- [ ] The focused tests retain real subprocess/socket execution but complete in low single-digit seconds on macOS CI.
- [ ] No absolute upper-bound assertion is tightened into a loaded-runner flake.

## Summary
Build the FOUNDATION of epic 3006-e198: the pure classifier, the per-binding baseline, the decision-census telemetry, the circuit breaker, and the test harness. This ticket wires NOTHING into the live pass (the four drift-class bugs and the rollout task consume it). All invariants are specified by ADRs 0026-0029 (docs/adr/) — read them FIRST.

## New module: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/classify.py (pure leaf; no I/O, no imports from differ/outbound_differ/inbound_differ)
- `class ObservedJira(Enum): PRESENT | CONFIRMED_404 | ABSENT_IN_WINDOW | TRANSPORT_ERROR` — the four-way observation state of ADR 0028 (NEVER a boolean; ABSENT_IN_WINDOW must never be treated as deleted).
- `class LocalState(Enum): ACTIVE | TERMINAL | ABSENT` — TERMINAL = local status in {archived, deleted} or archived flag.
- `@dataclass(frozen=True) class Decision: kind: DecisionKind; reason: str; payload: dict` — kind is a CLOSED enum: `SYNC_FIELDS | ADOPT | TERMINAL_TRANSITION | PROBE_GET | RETIRE_AFTER_GRACE | SKIP_RETIRED | ALERT | NOOP`.
- `def classify(local: dict|None, jira: ObservedJira-tagged snapshot value, binding: dict|None, baseline: dict|None) -> Decision` — the FULL (LocalState x ObservedJira x binding-present) matrix, every cell explicitly enumerated (no default-else fallthrough: unmatched cell raises).
- Matrix anchor cells (must match the 2026-07-03 spike + the child bugs): bound+ACTIVE+PRESENT -> SYNC_FIELDS; bound+TERMINAL+PRESENT(not Done) -> TERMINAL_TRANSITION; bound+*+ABSENT_IN_WINDOW -> PROBE_GET; bound+*+CONFIRMED_404 (grace met) -> RETIRE_AFTER_GRACE; bound+*+TRANSPORT_ERROR -> NOOP(defer); unbound+PRESENT+retired -> SKIP_RETIRED; unbound+PRESENT -> ADOPT; bound+ABSENT-local -> ALERT.

## Per-binding baseline (ADR 0026 — read its 4 decision points verbatim)
- Extend the bindings.json entry (binding_store.py, `BindingStore`): add `baseline: {summary, description, priority, status, assignee}` + `baseline_advanced_at`; bump the file `version` field; older entries without baseline are VALID (absent baseline degrades to local-wins per ADR 0026 #2).
- New methods `get_baseline(local_id) -> dict|None`, `set_baseline(local_id, fields: dict)`; persisted by the existing `save()` + committed by the existing `_commit_binding_store_snapshot` (reconcile.py) — no new commit path.
- One-shot seed helper `seed_baselines_from_snapshot(prev_snapshot: dict)` — sets a baseline for every bound key present in the snapshot (derisk X4 proved all 613 bound+present keys carry all 5 fields). Do NOT delete prev_snapshot or change its consumers in this ticket.
- Corrupt bindings.json stays FAIL-CLOSED (existing behavior); do not weaken it.

## Circuit breaker (pure function here; live wiring is the rollout task)
- `def check_blast_radius(decisions: Iterable[Decision], total_bindings: int, max_acting_fraction: float) -> BreakerVerdict` in classify.py or a sibling `breaker.py`; acting kinds = {TERMINAL_TRANSITION, RETIRE_AFTER_GRACE, ADOPT}; config key `reconciler.max_acting_fraction` default 0.10 (2026-07-03 census measured 1.14% acting — 8.8x headroom).

## Decision-census telemetry (approved remediation 1)
- `def census(decisions) -> dict` returning {counts-by-kind, acting_count, acting_pct, breaker_verdict}; emitted via the existing `SyncLogger.log("decision_census", **census)` (sync_logger.py) — the emit call itself lands with the first consumer, but the record shape + unit test land HERE.

## Tests (approved remediation 3 included)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/classify/test_matrix.py — table test: EVERY matrix cell, incl. the ADR 0028 regression cells (Done-beyond-cap -> PROBE_GET not RETIRE; transport-error -> NOOP).
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/classify/test_properties.py — hypothesis: (a) convergence: apply decisions to a model world, re-classify -> zero acting; (b) no-orphan; (c) conservation (no double-bind); (d) direction-preservation: a Jira-side edit with local==baseline is never pushed outbound (ADR 0026 consequence).
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/classify/test_frozen_census.py — replay sanitized frozen fixtures (tests/fixtures/bridge_convergence/frozen-2026-07-03/: bindings.json + snapshot skeleton, PII/body-stripped) asserting EXACTLY 7 acting decisions (5x TERMINAL_TRANSITION REB-464/456/465/466/457, 1x PROBE_GET REB-530, 1x ADOPT REB-532) then fixed-point after simulated heal.
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_baseline.py — get/set/seed/version-compat/corrupt-fail-closed.
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/classify/test_multipass_stateful.py — the epic's multi-pass stateful + fault-injection cell: a model world driven through N passes where the baseline is PERSISTED to a real temp bindings.json between passes (the faithful-persistence gap that hid drift class B); inject partial-apply failure (a Decision's apply raises mid-pass) and assert the NEXT pass re-derives the same Decision and self-heals to the fixed point.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] classify.py exists as a pure leaf module (no reconciler imports) with the closed Decision enum and the fully-enumerated matrix; unmatched cells raise.
- [ ] Baseline field + get/set/seed on BindingStore; absent baseline degrades local-wins; corrupt store still fails closed; version bumped with back-compat read.
- [ ] check_blast_radius + census implemented with unit tests; config key `reconciler.max_acting_fraction` (default 0.10) registered in the typed config schema (_config_schema.py).
- [ ] All five test files above pass; frozen-census fixture checked in (sanitized); hypothesis suite includes the four named properties; the multi-pass test persists the baseline through a real file between passes and asserts self-heal after injected partial failure.
- [ ] `make lint` + `make test` green; no file exceeds the 800 LOC soft cap.

## Implementation contract — resolved specifics (remediates plan-review 2026-07-03)

These pin the concrete decisions an executor needs (each was flagged as ambiguous
in the ticket text; all are now decided):

- **`jira` parameter type** — a frozen dataclass, NOT a loose "tagged value":
  `@dataclass(frozen=True) class JiraObservation: state: ObservedJira; key: str = "";
  fields: Mapping|None = None; retired: bool = False`. Matrix cells read
  `jira.state is ObservedJira.PRESENT`; `fields` is the snapshot value (present only
  when PRESENT); `retired` gates ADOPT vs SKIP_RETIRED for an unbound key.
- **Grace-met for `RETIRE_AFTER_GRACE`** — `classify(local, jira, binding, baseline,
  *, grace: int = 3)`: the grace threshold is a keyword-only arg (keeps the documented
  4-positional signature) so the function stays pure. On `CONFIRMED_404`, classify
  PREDICTS whether this miss crosses grace using `binding["absent_404_count"] + 1 >=
  grace`; below grace it returns `PROBE_GET` (keep counting), at/over grace
  `RETIRE_AFTER_GRACE`. `binding_store.note_absent` remains the sole ENACTOR of the
  increment+retire (classify predicts, note_absent enacts — no double count). Raw
  GET outcomes are mapped to `ObservedJira` by the caller (the live probe path;
  `inbound_probe`/`_safe_get_issue` sentinels → `CONFIRMED_404`/`TRANSPORT_ERROR`),
  never inside the pure classifier.
- **Acting kinds vs the "7 drift" frozen census** — the circuit breaker's ACTING set
  is `{TERMINAL_TRANSITION, RETIRE_AFTER_GRACE, ADOPT}` (PROBE_GET is a bounded READ,
  not acting). The frozen-census AC's "7" is the DRIFT/actionable set (5 TERMINAL +
  1 PROBE_GET REB-530 + 1 ADOPT); the test asserts those 7 decisions by key AND
  asserts `census(...).acting_count == 6` (breaker semantics). Both are consistent.
- **`BreakerVerdict`** — a frozen dataclass:
  `BreakerVerdict(allowed: bool, acting_count: int, total_bindings: int,
  acting_fraction: float, max_acting_fraction: float, reason: str)`.
  `total_bindings == 0` ⇒ allowed (nothing to gate; no divide-by-zero).
- **`reconciler.max_acting_fraction`** — registered in `_config_schema.py`
  `ReconcilerConfig` as `float = 0.10`, coercer `_as_float(v, k, minimum=0.0,
  maximum=1.0)`. A `reconciler.baseline_dual_write: bool = False` key is added
  alongside for the rollout's shadow phase.
- **Property tests use stdlib `random` (seeded), NOT `hypothesis`** — the repo
  declares no `hypothesis` dep and no test uses it; adding one would drift CI. The
  four named properties (convergence, no-orphan, conservation, direction-preservation)
  run as deterministic seeded-random model worlds.
- **Frozen fixture provenance** — `tests/fixtures/bridge_convergence/frozen-2026-07-03/`
  holds `bindings.json` + `snapshot.json` + `locals.json`, generated to reproduce the
  2026-07-03 census SHAPE (608 active + 5 archived-live + 1 dangling + 1 unbound =
  614 bindings / 614 issues / 615 cells); summaries/bodies are `[sanitized]` placeholders,
  assignees emptied — no PII.
- **`baseline` lifecycle** — the baseline lives ON the binding entry, so retirement
  (which removes the whole entry) removes it with the binding; no separate cleanup.
- **`seed_baselines_from_snapshot` re-run policy** — idempotent by construction: it
  re-derives each bound key's baseline from the passed snapshot (overwrite-with-same is
  a no-op for a stable snapshot); it never deletes.
- **decision_census record shape** — `{counts: {kind->int}, acting_count: int,
  acting_pct: float, total: int, breaker: {allowed, acting_fraction, max_acting_fraction,
  reason}}`; documented as a contract in the `census()` docstring.
- **800 LOC cap** — classify.py is ~380 LOC; the CI module-size gate
  (`.github/workflows/test.yml`) is the proving check.
- **ADRs 0026–0029** are committed under `docs/adr/` on this branch (the governing spec).
baseline.summary: Convergence foundation: pure classify() + Decision matrix, per-binding baseline, census telemetry, circuit breaker, property/replay tests

## Loosely Coupled Architecture

System architecture directly impacts team velocity. Transitioning from monolithic architectures to loosely coupled designs (like microservices) allows different parts of an application to operate independently.

**The Impact:** Teams can develop, test, and deploy their specific services without waiting on or breaking other teams' work, massively scaling productivity.

Loosely coupled architecture should be treated as a first-class architectural principle enforced through the planning and onboarding workflows — not merely suggested as a best practice.

## Context / Problem
Store-wide maintenance walks visit every ticket directory on every run: the fsck scan loops (`_ticket_dirs` iterations in src/rebar/_commands/fsck_scan.py) and the compact-all sweep (src/rebar/_commands/compact.py, whose per-ticket selection is `_scan_snapshot_state`'s own `os.scandir(tracker)` walk invoked by `compact_all_cli`) are O(all tickets ever created). As the store grows, archived tickets — cold, excluded from default `list` — dominate that walk and make routine health checks and sweeps slower for no operational value. `ticket list` already has the pattern to copy: default excludes archived (marker fast-path at reducer/_api.py with compiled-state confirmation) with an explicit `--include-archived` override.

## Approach
Two coupled changes, ordered so the default flip is safe:
1. **Operation-linked terminal fold.** Today `leaf.archive` (src/rebar/_commands/leaf.py) writes only the ARCHIVED event + `.archived` marker — it does NOT fold, so an archived ticket can carry unfolded tail events and the only thing that folds them is a later compact-all walk reaching it. Before scoping that walk to active tickets, make the fold part of the archive operation itself: `rebar archive` performs the ticket's final fold inline right before writing the ARCHIVED event, reusing the existing single-ticket fold path compact_txn already exposes BUT as a TERMINAL fold that bypasses the incremental gates: it passes threshold=0 (fold even a small ticket) and a fold horizon of now (fold the within-horizon tail too), so a just-archived hot ticket — all of whose events are younger than the normal compaction horizon — still gets a complete SNAPSHOT covering every event. If the shared path cannot express that (horizon/threshold baked in), add an explicit terminal/force parameter to it rather than a parallel fold implementation; a ticket with nothing unfolded is a no-op (no empty SNAPSHOT write). This is operation-linked, so it is portable across environments with diverse or NO CI provider — no scheduled sweep is load-bearing. Any later `--include-archived` sweep becomes redundant belt-and-suspenders for tickets archived by pre-change builds, not the sole fold path.
2. **Active-only default scoping.** Introduce one shared helper (in the module fsck_scan already imports `_ticket_dirs` from) that yields ACTIVE ticket dirs by default — skipping dirs whose net archival state is archived, using the `.archived` marker as the fast-path and the existing `_is_net_archived`-style event-name confirmation, the exact semantics `list` uses — with an `include_archived` flag to yield everything. Switch the fsck scan loops to it, and in compact.py replace `_scan_snapshot_state`'s `os.scandir(tracker)` walk with the shared iterator (matching its existing return contract so `_foldable_event_count` consumers are unchanged), with `compact_all_cli` threading `--include-archived` through to it. Add `--include-archived` to `rebar fsck` and `rebar compact-all` (flag parsing + JSON passthrough; the usage lines live in src/rebar/_cli/help/fsck.txt and compact-all.txt, not in fsck.py). Default = active-only for both: with change 1 in place, an archived ticket really IS folded on its way out, and any deep audit reaches it with the flag.
Back-out path: the default flip is a one-line revert per command (restore the full walk); change 1 is independently safe to keep since folding at archive time is strictly more converged than folding later. Positive rationale: this reuses the archive marker + net-archival semantics that default `list` has proven, rather than inventing a second notion of active.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_commands/leaf.py — archive performs the ticket's terminal fold inline before the ARCHIVED event.
- src/rebar/_commands/fsck_scan.py — scan loops take the shared active-only iterator; `include_archived` threading.
- src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py — CLI flag + JSON passthrough.
- src/rebar/_cli/help/fsck.txt and src/rebar/_cli/help/compact-all.txt — the usage/help text for both commands lives in these files (fsck.py has no usage string); add `--include-archived` there.
- src/rebar/_commands/compact.py — `_scan_snapshot_state` replaces its `os.scandir` walk with the shared iterator; `compact_all_cli` threads `--include-archived` through; default active-only.
- tests/unit/test_scan_scoping.py (new) — visited-set coverage both ways + archive-fold sequence test.
- docs/user-guide.md — document the default, the override, and the archive-time fold.

## Testing
- Happy path: fixture store with N archived (marker + ARCHIVED event) and M active tickets; default `rebar fsck` and `rebar compact-all --dry-run` visit exactly the M active dirs (assert on the visited set / reported counts); with `--include-archived` they visit N+M.
- Archive-fold sequence: archive a ticket that has unfolded events, then run DEFAULT `rebar compact-all`; assert the archived ticket's SNAPSHOT covers those events (nothing stranded) even though the default sweep never visited it — the fold happened at archive time.
- Edge: a ticket dir with a stale marker but NO net-archived state (reverted archive) is still visited by default (the confirmation step, not the marker alone, decides); an archived ticket with a corrupt event file IS reported when `--include-archived` is passed (deep audit still works); a ticket archived by a PRE-change build (unfolded, no inline fold) is folded by a `compact-all --include-archived` run (the belt-and-suspenders path works).
- Empty store: both commands succeed with zero visits.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `rebar archive` folds the ticket inline (SNAPSHOT covers all its events) before writing ARCHIVED; a just-archived ticket followed by default `compact-all` carries no unfolded events; checked by the sequence test.
- [x] Default `rebar fsck` and `rebar compact-all` visit only non-archived tickets, and `--include-archived` restores the full walk (including folding legacy archived-but-unfolded tickets); checked by the visited-set and legacy-fold tests.
- [x] A reverted-archive ticket (stale marker) is never skipped by default; checked by the edge test.
- [x] Usage lines and docs/user-guide.md name the new flag on both commands and the archive-time fold; checked by --help output in the test and the doc diff.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1) before close. [operator-attested]
baseline.summary: Active-only scan scoping: fsck and compact-all default to non-archived tickets with --include-archived override

## Why
Bug c8ed (outbound depends_on link direction) shipped because the link-sync tests exercised the relation vocabulary with a single representative (`blocks`, ~19×; `depends_on` 0×), used mechanical stub assertions, and the only semantic round-trip oracle (`tests/external/test_link_sync_roundtrip_live.py`) is gated behind live Jira. An audit found three OTHER gaps of the same shape, all in the link-sync seam.

## What
Close the sibling gaps by PARAMETRIZING the link tests over the FULL relation vocabulary, so every current AND future relation is covered (no more single-representative blind spots). Test-only change; no production behavior changes.

## Scope
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_link_dedup.py`: parametrize outbound `_diff_links`
  emission over ALL relations — assert `(jira_type, swap)` for each MAPPED relation
  (blocks→Blocks/False, depends_on→Blocks/True, relates_to→Relates/False) and assert `[]` for
  each UNMAPPED/skip relation (duplicates, supersedes, discovered_from). [Findings 1 + 3]
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_link_removal_sync.py`: add a REMOVE case where a
  Jira issue carries an OUTWARD `Blocks` link whose local `depends_on` dep was removed; assert
  the emitted mutation is `{action: remove, relation: depends_on}` (the untested branch of the
  REMOVE path's own inward/outward direction logic at outbound_links.py:193-202). [Finding 2]

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] An outbound emission test is parametrized over all 6 relations: the 3 mapped ones assert
  the exact `(type, swap)` tuple; the 3 unmapped ones assert an empty mutation list.
  Proof: `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_link_dedup.py -q`.
- [ ] A REMOVE test covers outward-`Blocks`→`depends_on`. Proof:
  `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_link_removal_sync.py -q`.
- [ ] The new cases assert per-relation ORIENTATION, not mere presence: the `depends_on` emission
  case asserts `swap is True`, and the applier case asserts the SWAPPED endpoint tuple — so a
  re-drop of the c8ed swap fix would fail them (a real guard, not a tautology). Proof:
  `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_link_dedup.py tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_link_sync.py -q` is green.
- [ ] `make lint`/`make typecheck` pass; no production source files change.
baseline.summary: Harden link-sync tests: parametrize over the full relation vocabulary (close the c8ed test-gap class)

# J10 — Give the Backend port an exception contract

## Problem (verified in source)

The DC transport raises `jira.exceptions.JIRAError` (pycontribs). Two CORE reconciler modules catch only `urllib.error.HTTPError`, which is what Cloud's urllib-based transport raises:

* `dispatch_apply_phases.py:119` — `except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:` around
  `client.set_reporter(...)`. Its own comment calls a 4xx "the common case" (Modify-Reporter not
  granted) and the handler exists to DEGRADE SOFTLY. A DC `JIRAError` does not match, so it escapes
  and fails the whole update instead of degrading.
* `outbound_differ.py:138-141` — `_safe_get_issue` maps `HTTPError.code == 404` to `_DELETED` and
  `URLError/TimeoutError/OSError` to `_TRANSPORT_ERROR`. A DC `JIRAError` matches NEITHER, so a
  remotely-deleted issue is not classified as deleted AND the exception escapes. **Deletion detection
  silently breaks on DC.**

This is the same root as the missing-members defect [rebar:a357-b747-ece9-4cf5]: **the port declares no exception contract**, so the core reaches for a transport-SPECIFIC type. `urllib.error.HTTPError` sitting in a vendor-neutral core module is a Cloud leak.

## Why this is its own story

It was folded into J9 [rebar:bda8-370d-23ad-4e36] and repeatedly produced self-contradictions there (the Approach said "translate into types the core already handles" — implying no core edits — while the Scope listed two core files). Two review rounds returned double-digit findings largely from that tension. Separating the exception CONTRACT from the member IMPLEMENTATION lets each be stated without contradicting the other.

## Decision — ONE strategy, stated once

Declare `BackendHTTPError` on the port (`_backend.py`), **subclassing `urllib.error.HTTPError`** so it carries `.code`. The DC transport translates `JIRAError` into it, preserving the HTTP status.

Consequences, which are the reason for this shape:

* **Cloud is NOT touched.** It keeps raising `urllib.error.HTTPError`. The brainstorm's decision 7 is
  explicit that the live-validated Cloud/ACLI path must not be altered, so changing Cloud's exception
  type is out of bounds.
* **No CORE catch clause changes.** `BackendHTTPError` IS-A `urllib.error.HTTPError`, so the existing
  `except urllib.error.HTTPError` at both sites catches it and `.code` access keeps working — the 404
  → `_DELETED` classification is preserved by construction rather than by a parallel code path.
* The port gains a stated contract, which is the durable asset: the next backend translates to
  `BackendHTTPError` instead of discovering this by a production crash.

**Alternative rejected:** a plain neutral `Exception` with a `.code` attribute plus edits to both core catch sites. Architecturally tidier, but it churns core modules on the live-validated Cloud path for no behavioural gain, and every additional core edit is a chance to regress Cloud.

**Alternative rejected:** teaching each core site `except (urllib.error.HTTPError, JIRAError)`. That puts a second vendor's exception type into vendor-neutral modules — the very leak this story exists to close — and does not scale to a third backend.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py` — declare `BackendHTTPError` and document it as the
  transport error contract every backend must raise.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` — translate `JIRAError`
  to `BackendHTTPError` at the adapter boundary, preserving the status code.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — new tests (below).

**Explicitly NOT in scope:** `dispatch_apply_phases.py` and `outbound_differ.py`. The subclass choice is what makes that true; if a reviewer believes they need editing, the subclass relationship is the thing to check first.

## Testing

- `BackendHTTPError` is an `isinstance` of `urllib.error.HTTPError` and carries `.code`.
- a DC transport call raising `JIRAError(status_code=404)` surfaces as `BackendHTTPError` with
  `.code == 404`.
- `outbound_differ._safe_get_issue` classifies that as `_DELETED` — the SAME verdict Cloud produces —
  driven through the real function, not a re-implementation of its logic.
- `dispatch_apply_phases._update_one_apply_reporter` catches a DC 4xx and records
  `outbound-reporter-not-permitted` rather than letting it escape.
- Cloud regression: a Cloud `urllib.error.HTTPError` still classifies identically (the negative
  control that proves Cloud was not altered).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `BackendHTTPError` is declared in `_backend.py`, subclasses `urllib.error.HTTPError`, and is
      documented as the transport error contract for all backends
- [ ] the DC transport translates `jira.exceptions.JIRAError` into it, preserving the HTTP status code
- [ ] a test asserts a DC 404 reaches `outbound_differ._safe_get_issue` as `_DELETED` — driven through
      the REAL function, since misclassifying a delete is silent divergence rather than a crash
- [ ] a test asserts a DC `set_reporter` 4xx is caught by the EXISTING handler at
      `dispatch_apply_phases.py:119` and recorded as `outbound-reporter-not-permitted`
- [ ] neither `dispatch_apply_phases.py` nor `outbound_differ.py` is modified (`git diff` shows them
      untouched) — the subclass relationship is what makes the fix work, and editing them would mean
      the chosen strategy failed
- [ ] Cloud is unmodified and a Cloud `urllib.error.HTTPError` still classifies identically, asserted
      as a negative control
baseline.summary: J10 — a neutral transport exception contract on the Backend port

# Contributor-triggerable re-review: a `recheck-review` comment re-runs any LLM-Review that is not a real finding

## Problem

An `LLM-Review -1` has two different meanings and only one contributor response: a **real finding** (`[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]`) is fixed by amending; every OTHER `-1` — the coverage-gap family (`gate-disabled`, `llm-unavailable`, `scanner`, `review-error`, `indeterminate`, `merge-review`), including a retry-budget escalation from ticket 0347-b2cc-e6e9-4f6b — is an infrastructure veto the contributor can do nothing about. Today the only remedies are an operator-run `/rerun` (SSM-token-gated; see `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md`) or amending to spin a new patchset. CI already gives contributors `recheck` for a `Verified -1` flake; the LLM lane has no equivalent. This mirrors the OSS norm (Zuul/OpenStack `recheck`, Prow `/retest`) with one deliberate restriction: LLM reviewers are stochastic, so retrying a REAL finding would be dice-rolled self-approval — the retry surface must exclude findings.

## Approach

**Trigger surface: a Gerrit comment containing `recheck-review`** (its own token — `recheck` stays CI's). Wire it end to end:

1. **Event plumbing** — `infra/gerrit/webhooks.config` gains `event = comment-added`
   alongside `patchset-created` (the plugin sends only listed types). Note in the file +
   ticket comment: an operator must re-run `infra/gerrit/service-user.sh` to push the
   rendered config to `refs/meta/config` before the trigger goes live; until then the
   code path is inert (no events arrive).
2. **Routing** — the receiver's `/webhook` already enqueues every payload; the worker
   (`app.py::_worker`) routes `type == "comment-added"` to a NEW module
   `src/rebar/review_bot/retrigger.py` (voter.py is at ~670/800 LOC post-0347; this is a
   separate concern and its own seam) instead of `review_and_vote`. All other types keep
   the existing path.
3. **`retrigger.handle_comment_added(event, config, gerrit, dedup)`** does, in order:
   - **Loop guard**: ignore comments authored by the bot itself (`cfg.bot_user`), else the
     bot's own replies re-trigger events forever.
   - **Token match**: the comment text must contain `recheck-review` (word match, not
     substring of another word); anything else is a silent skip.
   - **Eligibility — decided privileged-side from durable Gerrit state, never from the
     requesting comment**: fetch the bot's change messages via
     `GET /a/changes/{id}/messages` (ChangeMessageInfo), select the latest entry whose
     `_revision_number` equals the current patchset AND whose author is the bot account,
     strip Gerrit's prepended `Patch Set N:` header block (the tag line is the first
     non-empty line AFTER that header — verify the exact preamble shape against a live
     capture during implementation and pin it in a fixture), then parse the tag line.
     The tag grammar is WIDER than `_TAG_SUFFIXES` and the parser must cover all three
     production sites, test-asserted per case: (a) the `_TAG_SUFFIXES` vocabulary
     (adapter.py:44), (b) the hardcoded `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap
     (merge-review)]` literal emitted by `voter.py::_merge_coverage_gap_decision`
     (voter.py:222) which is NOT a `_TAG_SUFFIXES` member, and (c) the merge-change
     variant that appends ` (merge-change, N integrated commit(s))` INSIDE the tag
     brackets (adapter.py:81-83) to any of the above. Parse by STEM: strip a trailing
     `(merge-change, …)` suffix first, then classify the remainder. The ONLY ineligible
     state is a current-revision finding-BLOCK — a tag whose stem is
     `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]`, INCLUDING its merge form
     `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding (merge-change, N integrated commit(s))]` (a dedicated
     test asserts the merge-form finding is refused): a real finding is refused — fix and
     re-push. Everything else is eligible: every coverage-gap sub-reason (including
     `merge-review` and a 0347 retries-exhausted escalation), a PASS (a fresh review can
     only produce a fresh verdict — it can flip PASS to BLOCK, which is
     fail-closed-safe, and never mints an unearned PASS), a vote-less change (harmless:
     equivalent to a reconciler re-drive), and an UNPARSEABLE or absent tag (fail-open
     to a fresh fail-closed review — re-reviewing is always safe; refusing must be
     reserved for the one proven-finding state).
   - **On refusal**: post a short reply comment (a message, never a vote) telling the
     contributor the `-1` is a real finding and the path is amend + re-push; emit a
     greppable `RETRIGGER_REFUSED` log marker.
   - **On acceptance**: `dedup.reset_attempts(change_id, current_revision)` (the 0347
     budget DELETE — the shared-budget harmonization: the human trigger re-arms the
     bounded automatic retries), enqueue the change's current revision with the existing
     `_rebar_force` marker (the `/rerun` force path — bypasses dedup + existing-vote
     short-circuits, still fail-closed), post a short "re-review queued" reply, and emit
     `RETRIGGER_ACCEPTED`.
4. **Harmonize `/rerun`** — the operator endpoint also resets the attempts budget before
   enqueueing (today it would force a review that could immediately re-escalate on a
   stale budget). `/rerun` keeps its unrestricted semantics (an operator may force even a
   finding re-review); the finding-refusal applies only to the contributor comment path.
5. **Gerrit client** — add the two small REST calls `retrigger` needs if absent:
   `get_change_messages(change_id)` (`GET /a/changes/{id}/messages`), and
   `post_comment(change_id, revision, message)` = `POST
   /a/changes/{id}/revisions/{rev}/review` with a JSON body containing ONLY `message` —
   **no `labels` key at all**. Never use a `labels: {LLM-Review: 0}` form: value 0 is
   still a label write and can displace/copy label state. A unit test asserts the
   serialized request body for the reply path has no `labels` member.

### Security property (must be tested, not just implemented)

A `recheck-review` comment on a change whose current revision carries a findings-BLOCK does NOT enqueue a review, does NOT reset the budget, and does NOT touch the vote — asserted by a dedicated test. Also asserted: the bot's own comments never trigger, and a non-matching comment is a no-op. The trigger can only ever request a FRESH review through the same fail-closed pipeline; nothing in this path writes a vote directly.

## Scope

- `infra/gerrit/webhooks.config` — `event = comment-added`.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/retrigger.py` (new) — routing target, eligibility, replies.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py` — worker routes `comment-added` to `retrigger`; `/rerun`
  gains the budget reset.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py` — message-fetch / comment-post helpers if absent.
- `docs/review-policy.md` — the coverage-gap rows' "Your productive response" becomes
  "comment `recheck-review`"; document the finding refusal.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` §2c — mention `recheck-review` beside `recheck`.
- `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` — note the contributor path; `/rerun` stays the
  operator escape hatch.
- Tests in `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py` (worker routing) and a new
  `tests/unit/test_review_bot_retrigger.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: a `recheck-review` comment on a change whose current-revision tag is any
      coverage-gap sub-reason resets the attempts budget, enqueues a forced re-review,
      and posts the "queued" reply — asserted by tests (at least gate-disabled and a
      retries-exhausted escalation case).
- [ ] AC2 (security property): the same comment on a findings-BLOCK revision — BOTH the
      bare `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]` tag AND the merge form
      `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding (merge-change, N integrated commit(s))]` — is
      refused: no enqueue, no budget reset, no vote change, refusal reply posted,
      `RETRIGGER_REFUSED` emitted — asserted by dedicated tests for both tag forms.
- [ ] AC2b: the tag parser classifies all three production tag shapes — `_TAG_SUFFIXES`
      members, the hardcoded `merge-review` literal (voter.py:222), and any tag carrying
      the in-tag `(merge-change, …)` suffix — and an unparseable/absent tag is treated
      as ELIGIBLE (fail-open to a fresh fail-closed review) — asserted by a parametrized
      test.
- [ ] AC2c: the refusal/queued reply path posts a message with NO `labels` key in the
      Gerrit REST body (never a value-0 label write) — asserted by a test on the
      serialized request.
- [ ] AC3: comments by the bot itself and comments without the token are no-ops (no
      reply, no enqueue) — asserted by tests.
- [ ] AC4: `/rerun` resets the attempts budget before enqueueing — asserted by a test.
- [ ] AC5: `webhooks.config` lists `comment-added`; the file's comment and the runbook
      state that `service-user.sh` must be re-run to activate it.
- [ ] AC6: `docs/review-policy.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` §2c document `recheck-review`
      (incl. the finding refusal).
- [ ] AC7: `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the review-bot test modules pass; every
      touched/new `src/rebar` module stays within the 800-LOC cap (new module ≥100 LOC).

## Testing / Verification

From the worktree venv:
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py tests/unit/test_review_bot_retrigger.py -q`
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint && env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`

## Relationship to 0347

Lands AFTER 0347-b2cc-e6e9-4f6b (this ticket consumes its `review_attempts` ledger and `reset_attempts` DELETE semantics). 0347 handles the automatic recovery (vote-less defer + bounded escalation); this ticket is the human escape hatch that re-arms it once the underlying failure is corrected.
baseline.summary: Contributor recheck-review comment re-runs any LLM-Review that is not a real finding

baseline.description:
Wire **secrets (gitleaks) + High-Critical security (semgrep)** scanners as deterministic ground truth feeding the hard auto-block (the LLM triages/prioritizes, never invents). The integration shape below is settled by a derisk experiment (session_log a7e2-381c-6dc6-4d0c, EXPERIMENT 1; tools: gitleaks 8.30.1, semgrep 1.168.0 against Engine B at `src/rebar/grounding/`).

## Detector integration — what actually fits Engine B (experiment-grounded)

Engine B has three backends (`registry.py`: `opengrep`, `ast-grep`, `metric`); a detector is a native matcher YAML rule + `metadata.rebar_envelope`, parsed via `yaml.safe_load`.

- **semgrep = NATIVE fit.** semgrep is the opengrep rule format; PROVEN it passes
  `metadata.rebar_envelope` through verbatim + emits SARIF 2.1.0. High-Critical security
  detectors ship as **detector YAML under `src/rebar/grounding/detectors/builtin/security_*.yaml`
  consumed by the existing `opengrep` backend** — no new backend. **Named rulesets:** a curated,
  vendored, pinned subset of `p/owasp-top-ten` + `p/cwe-top-25` (NOT a live registry pull —
  reproducible/offline). Diff-scoped (changed files only); full-repo is out of scope for v1.
- **gitleaks ≠ native fit.** PROVEN: gitleaks uses TOML config with rules compiled into the
  binary (no per-rule YAML), so it cannot be a per-rule Engine B detector. It emits SARIF 2.1.0.
  gitleaks is integrated via a generic SARIF-ingest backend (`BACKEND_SARIF`): a `_run_sarif()`
  runner that subprocess-invokes the tool (`gitleaks detect --report-format sarif`), then
  normalizes via `sarif.from_sarif(..., trust_rebar_bag=False)`. Chosen over a gitleaks-only 4th
  backend because semgrep ALSO emits SARIF — one seam serves both.

## SARIF-backend dispatch (resolves the G6 empty-registry BLOCK)
Engine B's `scan()` only invokes a backend when `applicable_by_backend[backend]` is non-empty — which requires a registered `Detector`. gitleaks has no per-rule YAML, so WITHOUT a fix the `sarif` backend would never dispatch. **Committed mechanism (one, not a fork):** ship a SENTINEL detector descriptor `detectors/builtin/gitleaks.yaml` — a single `Detector` with `backend: sarif`, `metadata.rebar_envelope`, and a tool reference (the command + report format) INSTEAD of matcher rules (gitleaks carries its own compiled rules). Its presence puts one `Detector` in `applicable_by_backend["sarif"]`, so the existing dispatch loop routes to `_run_sarif`, which runs the tool once and ingests its SARIF (the sentinel's per-rule body is empty — the tool, not the YAML, supplies the rules). No bypass code path in `scan()`; the registry-driven dispatch is preserved. `_run_sarif`/`BACKEND_SARIF` is NEW engine code (a 4th backend runner in `_BACKEND_RUNNERS`) + its own test.

## Fail-CLOSED lives in the CONSUMER, not the oracle (experiment-grounded)
PROVEN: Engine B is **fail-OPEN** — a missing/errored/timed-out binary returns `abstain('no_tool'|'timeout'|'other')`, never blocks (`engine_b.py`; `docs/grounding.md`). Forcing the oracle fail-closed would break every other consumer. So the **fail-closed decision is made by THIS gate's verdict assembly** (the deterministic consumer step), NOT the oracle.

**Abstain→BLOCK bridge — ONE committed design (resolves the G6 fork BLOCK):** the bridge is a deterministic VERDICT-ASSEMBLY forced-BLOCK short-circuit, NOT a synthetic Pass-1 finding. (The synthetic-finding path is rejected: a finding with no real Pass-2 verification hits `pass3_decide(None) → INDETERMINATE`, which can NOT block.) Concretely: `produce_code_review_verdict` (WS4) reads the oracle evidence for the secrets/High-Critical-security detectors; if any returns `abstain` (tool unavailable/errored/timed out) OR a real positive finding, the verdict is forced to `BLOCK` with a `coverage-gap` annotation on the vote (distinguishing a fail-closed abstain from a real-finding block), AFTER and INDEPENDENT of the normal Pass-3 decision over the LLM findings. This is deterministic and never fights `pass3_decide`. WS5 owns this forced-BLOCK consumer step + sets `blocking_enabled=True` for exactly the two detector criteria via WS2's `threshold_for` resolver (the WS2→WS5 handoff).

## Vendored-rule maintenance (resolves the T5e staleness BLOCK)
The vendored `security_*.yaml` rules are pinned for reproducibility but must not silently rot. Mechanism: a `make vendor-security-rules` target re-pulls + re-pins the curated subset from the upstream registry at a recorded version, and a CI freshness check warns when the vendored pinned version is older than a stated cadence (e.g. quarterly). The cadence + the refresh command are documented in the WS5 ADR + an ops note. (v1 ships the pinned snapshot; the refresh is a documented periodic PR, not an automated live pull.)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] semgrep High-Critical security detectors ship as vendored, pinned detector YAML under `src/rebar/grounding/detectors/builtin/security_*.yaml` (named subset of p/owasp-top-ten + p/cwe-top-25 documented), consumed by the existing `opengrep` backend; diff-scoped.
- [ ] gitleaks integrated via the `BACKEND_SARIF` runner (`_run_sarif` → `sarif.from_sarif(trust_rebar_bag=False)`), routed by a SENTINEL `detectors/builtin/gitleaks.yaml` descriptor (backend: sarif, no per-rule body) so the registry dispatch reaches it WITHOUT bypassing `scan()`; a test asserts a planted secret surfaces as a normalized evidence finding.
- [ ] Secrets / High-Critical criteria map to a hard BLOCK; everything else stays advisory at the high starting thresholds (`blocking_enabled=True` set for exactly those two criteria via WS2's resolver — explicit WS2→WS5 handoff).
- [ ] FAIL-CLOSED in the CONSUMER (verdict assembly): RED-fixture test asserts an unavailable/errored secrets/security detector → the verdict is forced to BLOCK + a coverage-gap annotation (distinct from a real-finding block), NEVER a silent pass; the oracle itself stays fail-OPEN (a separate test pins the oracle still returns abstain, not block).
- [ ] The abstain→BLOCK bridge is the deterministic verdict-assembly forced-BLOCK short-circuit (NOT a synthetic Pass-1 finding — `pass3_decide(None)→INDETERMINATE` cannot block); a test pins the exact interface (oracle abstain on a detector criterion → verdict=BLOCK).
- [ ] HAPPY-PATH test: a detector returning real findings surfaces them as ground-truth blocking findings.
- [ ] "Diff-scoped" is a POST-FILTER of Engine B findings to the assembled `changed_files` set (Engine B `scan()` takes only `repo_root`); a test asserts an unchanged-file finding is filtered out.
- [ ] `_run_sarif`/`BACKEND_SARIF` is NEW engine code (a 4th backend runner in `_BACKEND_RUNNERS`) with its own test.
- [ ] An ADR records: the SARIF-ingest-backend choice (vs a gitleaks-only 4th backend), the SENTINEL-detector dispatch mechanism, the consumer-side (verdict-assembly) fail-closed boundary, and the vendored-rule refresh cadence/command.
- [ ] A `make vendor-security-rules` target + a CI freshness check exist; the refresh cadence is documented.

## Plan-review remediation (Round-12, 2026-06-30)
- BLOCK (G6 dispatch): committed to the SENTINEL gitleaks detector descriptor so the registry-driven `scan()` dispatch reaches `_run_sarif` with zero per-rule YAML — no `scan()` bypass.
- BLOCK (G6 abstain→BLOCK fork): committed to the deterministic verdict-assembly forced-BLOCK bridge; removed the synthetic-Pass-1-finding alternative (defeated by `pass3_decide(None)→INDETERMINATE`).
- BLOCK (T5e staleness): added the `make vendor-security-rules` refresh + CI freshness check + documented cadence.
baseline.summary: WS5: Secrets/security detectors (gitleaks/semgrep) behind the grounding-oracle envelope — fail-closed + RED-fixture test

## Context / Problem
RP-01 is now landed on `origin/main`. It made `PydanticAIRunner.run()` -> one per-run `ProviderSession` -> one `_pai_structured`/Pydantic `Agent` operation authoritative and pinned request-budget, output repair, cache, exhaustion, artifact, tracing, usage, and failure behavior. RP-04 must add provider-native auth injection without forking that path.

## Outcome
Add an `LLMRuntime` capability assembled at the trusted operation boundary and consumed only by existing `ProviderSession` builders. Accept provider-native pre-client auth/session capabilities (for example boto3 Session, Anthropic access-token provider, OpenAI callable/workload identity, or provider-specific static input); Rebar still constructs/owns/closes the official client and retains RP-01 policy. Arbitrary constructed clients/runners and a second Agent/retry scheduler remain out of scope.

## Plan
1. Add `src/rebar/llm/auth.py` with typed provider-specific `LLMRuntime` auth/session capabilities. Keep them non-serializable and outside `LLMConfig`, `RunRequest`, snapshots, fingerprints, caches, CLI/MCP schemas, and public output.
2. Extend `PydanticAIRunner`/`get_runner` to receive `LLMRuntime`, then pass it into the one per-run `ProviderSession`. Enrich only the existing Anthropic/Bedrock/OpenAI builder inputs; preserve fallback candidate construction and close ownership.
3. Let each official SDK retain native precedence, refresh, expiry, invalidation, and workload identity. If explicit provider/auth composition is missing or conflicting, fail before a provider model request and never try another ambient principal/provider. Optional observability remains separate.
4. Do not alter `_pai_structured`, output policy, request allowance, complete-or-omit failed-response history, cache breakpoint/settings/accounting, typed exhaustion, final artifacts, candidate tracing, usage normalization, failure translation, or documented limit-raise guidance.

## Testing (RED -> GREEN)
- Extend provider construction unit tests with native capability doubles for Anthropic, Bedrock, and OpenAI; assert the exact existing builder receives the capability, one official client is constructed/closed, and no raw token extraction occurs outside its adapter.
- Run RP-01's S2/S3/S5 authoritative offline oracles and candidate-tracing oracle unchanged. Add an AST/runtime guard that auth injection still has one `ProviderSession`, one runner dispatch, and one Agent operation.
- Failure tests cover absent/conflicting explicit auth, revoked static auth, native refresh success, refresh failure, fallback candidates, transport retry, output retry/exhaustion, and secret canary leakage.
- [operator-attested] Run bounded live Anthropic and Bedrock auth/cache canaries after cutover. Record provider/auth-source kind, cache read/write counters, request/retry counts, trace/run id, timestamp, and redacted outcome; never record credential material.

## Compatibility / rollback
Runtime input is optional during expansion; absence delegates to the exact RP-01 construction behavior. Before callers require the binding, rollback removes the new argument. After cutover, rollback must retain an adapter accepting the binding but may ignore it in favor of the old native environment chain. No LLM result schema changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Anthropic, Bedrock, and OpenAI construction tests prove provider-native capability reaches only the existing `ProviderSession` builder and exactly one Rebar-owned official client lifecycle.
- [x] The unchanged RP-01 authoritative S2/S3/S5 and candidate-tracing suites pass, including one-Agent budget, complete-or-omit retry history, cache/accounting, typed exhaustion, artifacts, tracing, usage, and failure contracts.
- [x] Structural/runtime tests reject a second runner/client owner, Agent construction route, `_pai_structured` caller, or bespoke retry scheduler.
- [x] Missing/conflicting explicit auth fails before a provider model request without anonymous, alternate-principal, or cross-provider fallback; native refresh remains SDK-owned.
- [x] Secret sentinels are absent from config/request/snapshot/fingerprint/cache/schema/output/log/exception/tracing boundaries and unwrap only inside the selected provider builder.
- [x] [operator-attested] Bounded live Anthropic and Bedrock auth/cache canaries pass with the required redacted evidence recorded on this ticket.
  provenance: environment=AWS-hosted rebar review bot (Bedrock) plus GitHub Actions CI reconciler; principal=the review bot native Bedrock workload-identity principal; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — Gerrit change 1844 PS4 (commit 7ed69cba73): LLM-Review +1 from the rebar review bot required a live authenticated Bedrock code review over the S4 auth-injection path (get_runner/LLMRuntime into the single per-run ProviderSession into the official client lifecycle), and Verified +1 from the rebar CI bot ran the S4 oracle green; redacted outcome PASS, no credential material recorded, no anonymous, alternate-principal, or cross-provider fallback occurred.
baseline.summary: RP-04 S4 — Inject LLM auth through the landed ProviderSession

## Context / Problem

Phase 2 of the reconciler vendor-adapter seam (follow-up to 44be / ADR 0035). Phase 1 authored ADR 0035, established `adapters/jira/`, and moved `jira_fields.py`. Phase 2 turns the structural seam into an enforced-by-interface one: pin the backend interface (ADR 0035 §(d), `docs/adr/0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md`), route the core through it, and complete the physical migration of the remaining Jira modules — so a second backend (GitHub Issues, Linear, …) can be added by implementing `adapters/<x>/` with no core rewrite. The first real second backend is out of scope, tracked by epic `be74-7832-03a8-48ac` (this epic `blocks` it).

## Design resolution (the canonical-comparison principle)

The first attempt to finish core neutrality (ticket 97f2's original plan / Gerrit change
920) extended the Backend port with the outbound differ's vendor-shaped comparison helpers
(`_diff_fields` etc., parameterized on Jira snapshot dicts). Plan review blocked it, correctly: ADR 0035 §(d) says the core owns diff/apply and the port only translates, so vendor-shaped helpers belong neither on the port nor in core. The resolution, pinned by this epic and to be recorded in ADR 0035 §(d):

**Core compares only canonical (local-vocabulary) shapes. Vendor shapes cross core solely as opaque payloads, produced by port calls at emission boundaries (`OutboundMapper.map_local_to_remote`, link-payload translation) and consumed by port calls at ingestion boundaries (`InboundMapper.map_remote_to_local`, remote-link reading).** The inbound differ already works this way (`inbound_differ.py:159`); the remaining children bring the outbound differ, link differ, absence probe, and rich-text/comment-limit paths to parity, plus the scalar port surface (project scope, env-readiness, neutral exceptions). Gerrit change 920 is abandoned; its scalar subset is salvageable by cherry-pick from worktree `impl-4af8-differ-di` (see re-scoped child 97f2).

## Child decomposition

Landed and closed:

- S1 `ef33-eaf6-a545-4bfb` — ADR 0035 §(d) pins the interface (change 900).
- S2 `ce4d-c3ca-5412-4798` — Backend port + role/capability Protocols + `RemoteRef` + thin
  `JiraBackend` + contract suite (901).
- S3 `94f9-a9a0-7475-4e75` — `reconciler.backend` config + in-tree registry +
  `select_backend()` (902).
- S4 `6673-7636-a116-4f90` — 4 transport-construction sites routed through
  `select_backend().transport`; provider literals → `backend.vendor`; ~34 test doubles
  migrated (903).
- S5 `dfb9-d2d1-455d-48d9` — 8 vendor modules physically relocated into `adapters/jira/`
  (acli*, adf, outbound_fields, comment_limits) + loader/import updates (905).
- `4af8-2d88-719e-4478` — vendor mapper entrypoints injected into
  outbound_differ/inbound_differ/apply_inbound via the port (914).

Open (the remaining neutrality work, disjoint edit-sets, independently reviewable, parallel-safe):

- `97f2-2d98-2eff-41c1` (re-scoped) — scalar port surface: `project`/`query_project`,
  `assert_env_ready()`, neutral `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError`; rewires fetcher, applier,
  apply_handlers, _attestation.
- Canonical-shape outbound field diff — the differ canonicalizes the snapshot via
  `InboundMapper` and diffs local-vs-local; vendor payload built only via the injected
  `OutboundMapper` at emission; vendor comparison helpers become adapter-internal; ADR §(d)
  amendment.
- Canonical link diff — `SupportsLinks` gains `map_remote_links` +
  `link_payload_for_relation`; `outbound_links.py` compares canonical relations only.
- Vendor absence probe behind `SupportsAbsenceProbe` — Jira REST probe mechanics move to
  `adapters/jira/probe.py`; neutral `ProbeBranch`/`ProbeResult` vocabulary stays in core.
- Canonicalize `reconcile_check.py` (`ad44-9f46-07aa-480c`, depends_on the canonical field
  diff) — the checker's local-vs-snapshot comparison reuses the canonical differ machinery
  (`InboundMapper` canonicalization, `assignee_identity` membership, sanitizer description
  parity); its by-path loads of `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py`/`adf.py` are deleted and
  the gate's documented reconcile_check carve-out is removed.
- Rich-text codec + comment limits behind the port — `outbound_comments.py` and
  `inbound_translate.py` route through `FieldSanitizer`/`InboundMapper`; the
  `"rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira"` lazy-key literals are deleted; a sweep gate bans the
  literal in package-root core (single recorded exemption: `inbound_fields.py`, the Jira
  InboundMapper implementation pending physical relocation — tracked by follow-up ticket
  `556a-5a1f-adb3-4139`, linked `discovered_from` this epic, out of scope here).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] ADR 0035 §(d) pins the interface (S1); Backend Protocols, `RemoteRef`, contract suite
      passing both `JiraBackend` and test-only `FakeBackend` exist (S2) — landed, changes
      900/901.
- [ ] Backend chosen via `config.reconciler.backend` through the registry; default `"jira"`
      reproduces prior behavior end-to-end (S3) — landed, change 902.
- [ ] All transport construction and provider literals route through the port (S4); the 8
      vendor modules physically reside under `adapters/jira/` with loaders repointed and no
      re-export shims (S5) — landed, changes 903/905.
- [ ] **Zero vendor reach-through in core:** every package-root
      `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/*.py` module has NO `adapters.jira`/
      `acli_subprocess` import (module-level or function-nested), NO
      `"rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira"` lazy-key literal, and NO by-path load of a vendor
      sibling (an `adapters/jira/...` path literal, the `reconcile_check.py:61-75` pattern)
      — single recorded exemption: `inbound_fields.py`, the Jira InboundMapper
      implementation — verified by the union of AST/sweep cases in
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py` added by the open children
      (incl. the removal of that gate's documented reconcile_check carve-out), green on
      main.
- [ ] **Canonical comparison:** the outbound field and link differs compare only canonical
      shapes; vendor payloads are built/consumed exclusively via port calls; ADR 0035 §(d)
      records the principle — verified by the canonical-diff children's characterization and
      neutrality tests, green on main.
- [ ] All `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/*.py` modules respect the 800-LOC module-size
      gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`); the full suite is behavior-preserving (all
      children's `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green; each landed with
      LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1).
baseline.summary: Reconciler vendor-adapter seam Phase 2: pin backend interface, route core through it, relocate Jira modules into adapters/jira/
