## Context
Current recovery handles interrupted creates but not the retired-first/live-replace crash state where one exact identity remains both live and tombstoned. Recovery must never guess across mismatched identities.

## Outcome
Extract create recovery and add a pure interrupted-retirement classifier plus repository-backed completion operation behind the `BindingStore` facade. Do not invoke it automatically yet.

## Plan
1. Move keyed/keyless create recovery into `binding_recovery.py` without changing labels, immutable known-key behavior, three-miss plus 3600-second grace, failure tally, or continue behavior.
2. Build real fault-cut fixtures for a tombstone persisted before live replacement fails.
3. Classify retirement completion only when tombstone, forward entry, and reverse entry agree on exact local id and Jira key.
4. Complete by removing the redundant live forward/reverse pair while retaining the tombstone; repeat is a no-op. Mismatch, corruption, or replace failure safety-aborts and retains evidence.

## Testing
Use fresh store reloads, identity-mismatch tables, replacement cuts, and keyed/keyless create-recovery regressions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Exact tombstone/forward/reverse overlap completes to coherent retired-only bytes while retaining the tombstone.
- [ ] Repeating completion performs no write.
- [ ] Any identity mismatch, corrupt live file, or replace failure retains evidence and returns a typed safety abort.
- [ ] Keyed pending recovery performs no search.
- [ ] Keyless pending recovery still requires both three misses and 3600 seconds, and one entry failure does not stop others.

## Out of scope
Automatic invocation boundary, rich-emission caller cutover, and ADR finalization.
baseline.summary: RP-02 S3 T1 — Classify and complete interrupted binding operations

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Closing a **bug** ticket sprays `Error: Ambiguous prefix '<4hex>' matches multiple tickets` lines at the terminal and then leaves the CLI running for minutes after the close has already committed durably. Reproduced twice (2026-08-08, 2026-08-10) with fragments `b2bb`, `28f9`, `a9dd`, `dbb2`, `3e8b`, `03ef`, `94a3`, `c5b3`, `18ae`, `4527`; each time the operator had to interrupt the process after confirming the status change had landed.

This ticket originally attributed the noise to the enrichment drain. That is **wrong**, and the correction is recorded in a triage comment: the drain subtree (`_store/event_append.py:606` -> `llm/enrich_drain.py:216` -> `drain` -> `llm/enrich.py`) resolves only ticket ids that came from `os.listdir(tracker)`, i.e. already-canonical directory names that short-circuit on the fast path at `_ids.py:239-241` and never reach the prefix branch that prints. It has no prose scanner at all, and in async mode its stderr goes to `.rebar/logs/enrich-drain.log`.

## Approach

Both symptoms are ONE defect in `src/rebar/metrics/blame.py`, the optional `caused_by` derivation invoked from `_commands/transition_close.py:246-248` **after** a bug close commits. `_find_fixing_commit` walks the entire branch history and calls `_resolves_to` per commit; `_resolves_to` re-resolves `bug_id` on **every** commit, and every candidate from `verify_commit.extract_ticket_refs` (whose second source is the leading `<token>:` of the commit subject) is resolved with no `quiet=`, no cache, and no shape filter. Any candidate that is not a full/short/Jira id falls through to `_scan_alias`, which opens up to two JSON files for each ticket directory.

Measured on this checkout: 3823 ticket directories, 2137 commits, 620 of them carrying a bare `<4hex>:` subject (487 distinct), and ~0.26s per unresolvable candidate. The per-commit `bug_id` re-resolution alone is ~2137 x 0.26s ~= 9 minutes of pure alias scanning. That is the "hang": an unbounded O(commits x tickets) scan, not a deadlock.

Four changes, none of which alter WHICH id forms resolve:

1. Pass `quiet=True` at EVERY scanner call site in the module — `_resolves_to` (`blame.py:53`
   and `:55`), `_commit_ticket` (`:100`, the culprit commit's own subject), and the final
   self-comparison in `derive_caused_by` (`:135`) — using the seam `_ids.py:221-230` already
   documents for "scanners resolving candidates the user never supplied", the same treatment
   `_commands/close_precheck.py:119` already applies. Kills the terminal noise. All four are
   required: `_commit_ticket` is a SECOND scanner over commit-message candidates, so leaving it
   loud would keep a residual path that violates AC 1.
2. Hoist the `bug_id` resolution out of the per-commit loop (it is loop-invariant).
3. Memoize ref -> resolution for the duration of one derivation, as `close_precheck` does.
4. Short-circuit on a **necessary condition** before touching the store: a ref of hex-quad
   shape can only resolve to the target if the target's canonical id starts with it. This is
   provably semantics-preserving and is restricted to 1-, 2-, and 4-quad hex forms, which
   cannot collide with an alias (aliases are `adj-noun` or `adj-noun-noun` from the wordlist,
   or an 8-hex no-dash fallback) — 3-quad forms are deliberately excluded and still take the
   real resolver. Because that is a cross-module invariant owned by `_ids`/`_alias`, the guard
   carries a comment naming its source and a test asserts no generatable alias can take the
   hex-quad shape the short-circuit rejects, so the optimization cannot silently drift.

Separately, sweep the docs to stop advertising bare 4-digit (single-quad) references, per the operator decision: name alias (preferred), 8-digit two-quad prefix, full canonical id, and Jira/bridge ids as the reference forms. Compatibility resolution is unchanged and stays documented as compatibility.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/metrics/blame.py` — the four changes above.
- `tests/unit/` — new regression tests.
- `src/rebar/_ids.py` — **module docstring only** (no code change): it is the one place that
  literally advertises "unique prefix >= 4 chars" as a supported form.
- `AGENTS.md` — the ticket-identifier authoring paragraph (:66-73). It does NOT advertise a
  bare 4-digit form today (it already discourages copying a short hex prefix and already frames
  short forms as compatibility), so this is an ADDITION: positively name the preferred forms,
  including the 8-digit two-quad prefix, which the file never mentions.

A repo-wide survey found the advertising surface is small: those two places. The ~420 bare 4-hex mentions elsewhere in `docs/` are incidental HISTORICAL citations of specific tickets ("epic 716f", "bug 84aa"), not guidance telling a reader to use that form, so they are out of scope — rewriting them would be a large no-value diff. `docs/cli-reference.md:387` (`rebar resolve <id_or_alias_or_prefix>`) is generated from `src/rebar/_cli/help/resolve.txt` and says "prefix" generically, which correctly includes the PREFERRED 8-digit two-quad prefix, so it is left alone.

Explicitly NOT changed: `_ids.py` resolution semantics, `verify_commit.extract_ticket_refs` (commit-subject candidates keep resolving exactly as today), the close gate, and the `Verified` trailer check. No id form gains or loses the ability to resolve.

## Testing

- A commit message whose subject is a bare `<4hex>:` prefix that matches multiple tickets
  produces **no** `Ambiguous prefix` text on stderr during `derive_caused_by`.
- A bounded-work test: over a synthetic history of many commits carrying distinct 4-hex
  subjects, the number of underlying `resolve_ticket_id` calls stays small and constant rather
  than growing with the commit count (asserted by counting calls through a patched resolver).
- Behavior preservation: `derive_caused_by` still finds the fixing commit and the culprit
  ticket when the commit cites the bug by full canonical id, by 8-hex two-quad prefix, by
  alias, and by an unambiguous bare 4-hex prefix.
- A ref that is a hex-quad shape but NOT a prefix of the target still returns "no match", and a
  3-quad hex form still reaches the real resolver.
- A culprit commit whose OWN subject is an ambiguous bare 4-hex prefix also produces no
  `Ambiguous prefix` text (the `_commit_ticket` path).
- An alias-shape guard test: no alias generatable from the wordlist can take the 1-, 2-, or
  4-quad hex shape the short-circuit rejects.
- Docs: an assertion-style check that the swept files no longer present bare 4-digit ids as a
  recommended reference form.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Closing a bug emits no `Ambiguous prefix` diagnostics for commit-subject candidates the
      user never supplied.
- [x] `derive_caused_by` performs work bounded by the number of DISTINCT candidate refs rather
      than re-resolving per commit, proven by a call-count regression test.
- [x] Every id form that resolves today still resolves: full canonical id, 8-hex two-quad
      prefix, alias, Jira key, and unambiguous bare 4-hex.
- [x] The original post-close reproduction, replayed as a regression test over a synthetic
      multi-commit history, emits no `Ambiguous prefix` text and resolves each DISTINCT ref at
      most once (no per-commit re-resolution of the bug id).
- [x] A regression test asserts that no alias generatable from the wordlist (`adj-noun`,
      `adj-noun-noun`, or the 8-hex no-dash fallback) can take the 1-, 2-, or 4-quad hex shape
      rejected by the short-circuit, so the optimization cannot silently drift.
- [x] `src/rebar/_ids.py`'s module docstring no longer presents "unique prefix >= 4 chars" as
      a plain supported form, and `AGENTS.md`'s ticket-identifier paragraph positively names the
      preferred forms (alias / 8-digit two-quad prefix / full canonical id / Jira ids) while
      retaining its existing compatibility framing.
baseline.summary: Enrichment drain treats unrelated short hex fragments as ticket prefixes and hangs post-write commands

baseline.description:
## Why
The record/fold path (S2) and read surface (S3) handle a single opaque session id, but a bare session id collides across tools (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Cursor). To make the feature genuinely multi-harness, claims must also record WHICH harness produced the id, and the resolver must recognise the other OSS harness session vars.

## What
- **Resolver var-list extension (`src/rebar/_commands/session_id.py`).** Extend
  `_SESSION_ID_VARS` with the OSS harness var OpenCode ships, in popularity order between the
  Claude and ambient vars:
  `REBAR_SESSION_ID -> CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID -> OPENCODE_SESSION_ID -> SESSION_ID`.
  **Codex is deliberately NOT added as a native var:** story 7656 establishes that Codex
  exposes no supported readable session env var, so it is covered by its SessionStart shim
  exporting `REBAR_SESSION_ID` (not a `CODEX_THREAD_ID`). SAFETY: an absent or unrecognised var
  simply falls through (the resolver skips unset vars), so it degrades to a lower-precedence
  var or `None` — never an error.
- **Harness provenance tag.** Add `resolve_harness()` returning the opaque, rebar-owned
  `AI_AGENT` env var (verbatim, never interpolated) or `None`. `AI_AGENT` is rebar's
  harness-provenance convention, holding e.g. `claude-code_<ver>` / `opencode` / `codex` /
  `cursor`. **Population contract (closes the DOA gap):** the capture shims in stories S4
  (ec5c) and S6 (7656) are extended by THIS epic to export `AI_AGENT` alongside
  `REBAR_SESSION_ID`; until then `AI_AGENT` may also be set directly by an operator/hook. When
  unset, `claim_harness` folds to `None` (no error) — the feature degrades gracefully.
  On an `open -> in_progress` STATUS, stamp `data["harness"]` when present; fold to
  `state["claim_harness"]`. Each provenance field folds `data.get(<its key>)` INDEPENDENTLY on
  the edge (same fork-winner gating as `claimed_session`), so a re-claim clears `claim_harness`
  to `None` iff `AI_AGENT` is absent for THAT claim — independent of whether a session id is
  present.
- **Secondary remote session.** Add `resolve_remote_session()` returning
  `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID` or `None`; stamp `data["remote_session"]` and fold to
  `state["claim_remote_session"]` (same gating). This is a secondary field, independent of the
  primary `claimed_session`.
- **State + schema + read surface.** Default `claim_harness` and `claim_remote_session` to
  `None` in `make_initial_state`; enumerate both in `ticket_state.schema.json` and (as compact
  keys `chn` / `rsn`) in `ticket_state_llm.schema.json` + `KEY_MAP` (+ docstring); add both to
  the MCP `TicketStateOut` model; regenerate `types.py`. `rebar show` JSON includes them
  automatically (state keys).
- **Existing-test updates.** Update `tests/unit/test_session_id.py` for the extended list:
  broaden its hardcoded `_ALL_VARS` tuple + autouse clear fixture to the 4 vars, and update
  `test_docs_document_unified_contract`'s exact-string assertion to the extended ordered
  contract (normalising whitespace so doc line-wrapping is irrelevant). Add an
  `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` precedence case, and a case asserting `CODEX_THREAD_ID` is NOT
  recognised (Codex has no native var).
- **Docs.** Extend `docs/config.md` (the ordered var list + `AI_AGENT` +
  `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID`) and `docs/event-schema.md` (the `harness` / `remote_session`
  data keys -> `claim_harness` / `claim_remote_session` state). Env-var name provenance:
  `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` (OpenCode-shipped) and `CODEX_THREAD_ID` (Codex convention) come from
  the epic OSS survey (Codex has no readable var, hence no `CODEX_THREAD_ID`); because an
  unrecognised name simply falls through, a wrong guess degrades to a lower-precedence var or
  `None` with no runtime error.

## Scope
- IN: resolver var-list extension + `resolve_harness` / `resolve_remote_session`; the write
  stamps + reducer folds for `claim_harness` / `claim_remote_session`; state defaults; both
  JSON schemas + `types.py` regen + `to_llm` keys + MCP model; docs; the existing
  `test_session_id.py` updates AND a NEW `tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py` module.
- OUT: the per-harness CAPTURE shims that POPULATE `REBAR_SESSION_ID` / `AI_AGENT` — Claude
  Code (S4 / ec5c) and Codex + Cursor (S6 / 7656), both extended by this epic to also export
  `AI_AGENT`. This story is the store/record side only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `resolve_session_id()` recognises `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` at its precedence, and does NOT
      recognise `CODEX_THREAD_ID` (Codex has no native var). Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_session_id.py -k "opencode or codex" -q`.
- [ ] A claim records `claim_harness` (from `AI_AGENT`) in compiled state, distinguishing the
      source tool; absent `AI_AGENT` -> `None`. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py -k harness -q`.
- [ ] `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID`, when set, is captured as `claim_remote_session`. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py -k remote -q`.
- [ ] Both fields default to `None` in `make_initial_state`, are enumerated in
      `ticket_state.schema.json` + `ticket_state_llm.schema.json` (`chn` / `rsn`), and appear
      in `TicketStateOut`; `types.py` is not stale. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py -k "schema or read" -q` and
      `pytest tests/interfaces/contracts/test_public_types.py -q`.
- [ ] Fork-winner + session-less-clear semantics apply to both new fields (never the loser's;
      cleared to `None` on a provenance-less re-claim). Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py -k fork -q`.
- [ ] `docs/config.md` and `docs/event-schema.md` document the extended var list, `AI_AGENT`,
      and the two new fields. Proof: `pytest tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py -k docs -q`
      asserts `docs/config.md` contains `AI_AGENT` and `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` (Codex has no
      readable var, so there is intentionally no `CODEX_THREAD_ID`), AND `docs/event-schema.md`
      contains `claim_harness` and `claim_remote_session`.
- [ ] The existing `test_session_id.py` is updated for the extended list and stays green
      (4-var `_ALL_VARS` + clear fixture; unified-contract doc assertion updated). Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_session_id.py -q`.
- [ ] A NEW `tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py` module is created covering the resolvers,
      write-stamp/fold, fork-winner + provenance-less-clear, schemas + read surface, and docs.

## Depends on
- S2 (68ef) record/fold path + S3 (199b) read surface — landed in this stack.
baseline.summary: Multi-harness session capture: extend resolver var-list + record harness provenance tag

## Acceptance Criteria

      (or its inputs) change between deployed..target — e.g. add it to a host-materialize trigger.

## The defect

`src/rebar/metrics/analyzers/scc_loc.py:41` builds the command:

    command = ["scc", "--format", "json", str(scan_root)]

It omits `--by-file`. Without that flag scc emits per-language SUMMARIES whose `Files` key is present but EMPTY (`"Files":[]`). `_parse_files` (:76) therefore raises nothing -- the key is a list, it is simply empty -- and iterates zero entries.

The adapter then returns `AnalyzerResult(loc={"files": {}, "max_loc": 0})` at :59.

## Why this is worse than a crash

It fabricates a CONFIDENT ZERO. `rebar metrics` reports:

    module_size_distribution: {"count": 0, "near_cap_count": 0, "over_cap_count": 0, "max_loc": 0}
    oversized_module_count: 0

A reader concludes this repository has no oversized modules. It has 729 analyzable files, the largest at 7011 lines. The metric is not merely wrong, it is wrong in the reassuring direction, and it carries `confidence: high` and `source: structural`.

This is precisely the failure epic 839b-f6d2-7e1a-4051 was created to ELIMINATE. Its motivating audit finding was that the old code_health readers "fabricated authoritative zeros for non-Python clients". The replacement stack fabricates authoritative zeros too, by a different mechanism.

## Verified, not inferred

With scc 3.7.0 on this machine, run from the repo root:

    scc --format json src/rebar          -> 9 language groups, every "Files" is []
    scc --by-file --format json src/rebar -> 729 file entries, max Code = 7011

Direct adapter call `scc_loc.analyze(Path('.'), ['src/rebar'])` returns AnalyzerResult with `files: 0, max_loc: 0`.

Note this was invisible until now because scc was not installed anywhere -- the metric reported `unavailable: scc executable is unavailable`, which is honest. Installing scc is what exposed the bug: an honest Unavailable became a dishonest zero.

## A second defect the fix will expose

With `--by-file` the largest entries are NOT source modules:

    7011  src/rebar/_engine/resources/ticket-wordlist-v2.txt
    2341  src/rebar/_engine/resources/ticket-wordlist.txt
    1932  src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor_assets/dist/editor.js
    1528  src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor_assets/src/rebarProvider.jsx

So simply adding the flag makes `module_size_distribution` report max_loc 7011 from a word list. That does not match the module-size POLICY, which is about Python modules -- the CI gate counts only `src/rebar/**/*.py` against `.github/module-size-limit.txt`. The two would report irreconcilable numbers for the same concept.

## OPERATOR RULING on AC3 -- match the CI gate via PER-PROJECT CONFIG, not a hardcoded filter

Recorded verbatim, because it decides the shape of the fix:

  "matching CI gate. the point of adoption was that it could be polyglot to support diverse
   clients. configuration for this project can be specific to this project's tech stack."

So the adapter does NOT get a Python-only filter baked into it. Epic 839b-f6d2-7e1a-4051's motivating finding was that the old readers hardcoded `src/rebar/**/*.py` and therefore fabricated zeros for non-Python clients; re-hardcoding a language in the replacement stack would recommit that exact defect one layer down. scc was adopted BECAUSE it is polyglot, and it stays polyglot. The file set is PER-PROJECT CONFIGURATION, and this project is configured to its own stack so its metric agrees with its own gate.

BINDING CONSTRAINT on any new knob: it MUST have a live read site and MUST be dogfooded in the same change. Ticket dce2-b93d-4112-451c was closed for the opposite -- `CodeHealthConfig. analyzers` shipped as config with no reader and rotted inert for six weeks. Idea 94bc-a0b4-bc37-47b2 records the operator's standing condition that selection must never ship as configuration alone. A new inert knob here would be the same mistake under a new name.

### Why the narrowing cannot live in `scan_roots` (checked first, as instructed)

`scan_roots` is a DIRECTORY axis: `_scan_roots` resolves each entry to a path and hands it to scc as the positional argument. The files that must be excluded are INTERLEAVED inside the directory that must be kept -- `src/rebar/_engine/resources/*.txt`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor_assets/dist/*.js` and `.../src/*.jsx` all live under `src/rebar`. No set of directories can express "only Python files under src/rebar". The missing axis is file TYPE, orthogonal to the directory axis, so it needs its own expression.

## Plan

1. AC1 -- add `--by-file` to the scc argv.
2. AC2 (load-bearing) -- an empty aggregated file map returns `Unavailable` via the module's
   existing `_unavailable` helper, never a zero-valued `AnalyzerResult`. A zero must mean
   "measured zero", not "measured nothing". Every pre-existing unavailable path is unchanged.
3. AC3 -- add `code_health.include_extensions` (`list[str]`, default `[]` = polyglot, so
   behaviour is unchanged for every other client), read LIVE in `scc_loc.analyze` where it
   becomes scc's `--include-ext` argument, threaded `_commands/metrics.py` -> ctx ->
   `git_metrics._scc_analysis` and folded into that function's analysis cache key so two
   differently-narrowed runs cannot collide. Dogfooded in the SAME change via this repo's
   `rebar.toml` `[code_health]` table (`scan_roots = ["src/rebar"]`,
   `include_extensions = ["py"]`, `size_cap = 800`).
4. AC4 -- read scc's `Lines` (raw line count) rather than `Code` (which excludes blanks and
   comments). The CI gate measures `find src/rebar -name '*.py' | xargs wc -l` against
   `.github/module-size-limit.txt`; scc's `Lines` equals `wc -l` exactly, measured at 0
   mismatches over all 435 files, so the metric reconciles with the gate BY CONSTRUCTION
   rather than leaving a documented gap. `size_cap = 800` is the same integer as the limit
   file, so `near_cap_count`/`over_cap_count` stop being null.
5. AC5 -- a regression, run against real scc, asserts a scan root that demonstrably contains
   files never produces a zero-valued result.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The scc invocation includes `--by-file` (or whatever the installed scc requires) so file
      entries are actually returned; proven RED-first with a test that fails on the current argv.
- [x] An EMPTY file list is reported as `Unavailable`, never as a zero-valued AnalyzerResult --
      a zero must mean "measured zero", not "measured nothing". This is the load-bearing AC.
- [x] The file set is filtered so `module_size_distribution` measures what the module-size
      policy measures; a test asserts a bundled asset and a resource .txt are excluded.
- [x] The metric's numbers are reconciled with the CI module-size gate on this repository -- if
      they still differ, the difference is documented and justified rather than left silent.
- [x] A regression asserts the adapter does not return a confident zero for a scan root that
      demonstrably contains files.

## Provenance

Found immediately after installing scc/lizard/jscpd on the operator's machine to enable code-health metrics for this project. Complexity (lizard) and duplication (jscpd) began producing real values; the scc-backed size metrics did not, which surfaced this.
baseline.summary: scc adapter omits --by-file, so module-size metrics report a confident ZERO instead of Unavailable

## Context

Two consecutive successful macOS Gerrit Verify jobs after change 1730 still report tests/interfaces/io/test_import_batch_resume.py::test_benchmark_commit_count_is_ceil_per_pass at 21.05s and 29.38s. Closed ticket curricular-mean-cuckoo already removed the dominant redundant work and explicitly locks this contract at 3,000 tickets, 3,000 comments, 24 crash-safe import commits, and >=10x commit reduction. This follow-up must preserve that exact behavioral/performance-scale contract and remove only proven redundant work.

## Plan

1. Reproduce the exact N=3000 node on current origin/main with repeated wall-time samples and a full call-count/cumulative-time profile. Separate test construction, importer composition, validation, filesystem writes, Git index/commit subprocesses, materialization, and cleanup.
2. Form competing hypotheses from the profile and run one controlled experiment per hypothesis. Compare against the already-landed author-cache and stale-sweep optimization; do not infer from aggregate suite time.
3. Cross-check the ticket store for prior decisions and compare the proven mechanism with popular maintained OSS bulk-import/test patterns before proposing a change. The curricular-mean-cuckoo workload and durability constraints remain controlling.
4. If the remaining cost is redundant setup or production-path work, add a deterministic held-out oracle for the exact call/effect count, prove RED, implement the narrow optimization, and prove GREEN plus exact-defect mutation RED. If the remaining time is irreducible work needed for the locked scale contract, report that result and evaluate scheduling/tier placement without removing the test from macOS unless equivalent platform assurance is proven.
5. Verify the unchanged N=3000/6000-event/24-commit assertions, import idempotency, rollback, crash-resume, clean-index, author and stale-sweep lifecycle, focused unit/interface suites, lint, typecheck, and the full Gerrit Verify matrix. Report before/after macOS runner-seconds and overall critical-path effect.

## Test contract card

authoritative_contract: curricular-mean-cuckoo and tests/interfaces/io/test_import_batch_resume.py preserve N=3000, 6,000 events, exactly 24 crash-safe import commits, >=10x commit reduction, complete state, rollback, and resume. trigger_preconditions: fresh real Git-backed store importing the fixed synthetic corpus through public rebar.import_tickets. production_path: rebar.import_tickets through import composition, batch staging/commit, and materialization. test_tier: real-Git integration on every supported CI platform currently executing this node. observable_postcondition: identical ticket/comment state, event attribution, commit graph/count, clean index, and deterministic collaborator/effect counts with lower measured wall time. negative_control: independent interactive writes, failure rollback, later-chunk resume, and existing-ticket imports retain current semantics. collateral_invariants: no test, platform cell, mutation shard, coverage measurement, event validation, durability boundary, or contractual assertion is removed or weakened. ci_gate: focused repeated benchmark evidence plus full Gerrit Verified gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Current macOS time over 20s is reproduced and individually attributed to concrete operations with call counts and cumulative time.
- [ ] The exact N=3000, 6,000-event, 24-commit, >=10x, complete-state, rollback, and crash-resume contracts remain unchanged and green.
- [ ] Any implementation is guarded by a held-out deterministic oracle, exact-defect mutation evidence, and negative controls for interactive/failure behavior.
- [ ] Ticket-store prior decisions and relevant maintained OSS practice are documented before remediation.
- [ ] Repeated same-host before/after results quantify test and runner-time savings; time remains evidence, not a flaky threshold.
- [ ] Focused suites, lint, typecheck, full Gerrit Verify, LLM-Review, and merge are green before closure.
baseline.summary: Eliminate remaining macOS N=3000 import benchmark long pole

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Operator directive (2026-08-13): "The tickets branch should never trigger CI. The branch is noisy and doesn't contain code." rebar auto-pushes the `tickets` branch to `origin` on EVERY write (comment/edit/claim/close), so each ticket event fires the four workflows that push- trigger on all-branches-but-two. During the 2026-08-12/13 bug bash this starved the org-wide GitHub Actions runner pool (navapbc is on GitHub Free: 20 concurrent jobs, 5 macOS, shared across the org), queueing a Gerrit `Verified` pytest matrix ~2 hours behind tickets-push runs.

## Approach
Audit every file in `.github/workflows/` for an `on.push` trigger. Measured today, exactly four have one — `test.yml`, `optionality.yml`, `prompt-eval.yml`, `verify-identity.yml` — and all four already use the SAME idiom: `branches-ignore: ["feature/**", "main"]`. The ticket's original finding that `reconcile-bridge.yml` push-triggers is STALE: it is schedule + `workflow_dispatch` only today. Every other workflow is `workflow_call`, `workflow_dispatch`, `schedule`, `pull_request`, or `pull_request_target`.

So the change is minimal and idiom-preserving: append `"tickets"` to those four `branches-ignore` lists (keeping `branches-ignore` as the ONE consistent idiom rather than converting anything to explicit allow-lists), each with a one-line comment citing `refractive-conceptual-sunbear`. No `schedule:` block is touched, so the replacement cadences the directive relies on are unchanged by construction: reconcile-bridge `*/20 * * * *`, verify-identity `53 */6 * * *`, test `41 */6 * * *`, optionality `47 */6 * * *`, prompt-eval weekly `0 7 * * 1`.

Enforcement: the sibling policy module `tests/unit/test_ci_main_push_policy.py` already models GitHub's branch filtering in its `_push_matches_branch` helper but only pins the four known workflow NAMES. A future workflow added with a bare `push:` would silently regress this invariant, so the new test module ENUMERATES every `*.yml`/`*.yaml` under `.github/workflows/` from disk and asserts none of them push-matches `tickets`, plus that non-tickets topic-branch push CI still fires (the scratch-branch push lane is the only pre-merge validation path for a workflow change — the Gerrit Verified lane resolves `uses: ./.github/workflows/...` from the default branch and therefore cannot exercise a workflow edit).

Out of scope, stated as a deliberate default: `pull_request:` filters on the BASE branch, not the head, so a tickets-headed PR cannot be excluded by branch filter — and `lockdown.yml` auto-closes PRs on this mirror anyway. Leave `pull_request` triggers alone.

Not changed, by operator instruction: `gerrit-verify.yaml` stays `workflow_dispatch`-only (it is the sole `Verified` source, dispatched by Gerrit per patchset).

**Adopter documentation (operator scope addition).** This hazard is not specific to this repo: ANY rebar adopter whose CI watches all branches turns every comment into a workflow run, because the store auto-pushes on every write. Document it once where an adopter configures the store's remote, and cross-link rather than triplicate. The canonical warning goes in `docs/concurrency.md` under "Outbound — push (on every write)" (the mechanism section that already states every write auto-pushes); `docs/user-guide.md` gets a short pointer at the "The store **auto-pushes**" paragraph; `docs/config.md` gets a one-line pointer in the `sync.remote` annotation. Wording is adopter guidance — "configure your CI so the tickets branch never triggers workflows; use a schedule for anything that must read the store" — not a retelling of this repo's incident.

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` — add `"tickets"` to `on.push.branches-ignore` + citation comment.
- `.github/workflows/optionality.yml` — same.
- `.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml` — same.
- `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yml` — same.
- `tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_push_policy.py` — NEW: the enumerate-all-workflows invariant.
- `docs/concurrency.md` — canonical adopter warning in the outbound-push section.
- `docs/user-guide.md` — short pointer at the auto-push/comment paragraph.
- `docs/config.md` — one-line pointer in the `sync.remote` annotation.

## Testing
- Happy path: for each workflow file discovered on disk, a push to `tickets` does not match its
  `on.push` filter (a workflow with no `push` key trivially passes).
- Regression/edge: a hypothetical `on: push:` with NO branch filter, and one with
  `branches: [tickets]`, are both classified as matching by the shared filter model, so the
  enumerating test would fail if such a workflow were added later.
- Preserved-behaviour path: the four edited workflows still push-match an ordinary topic branch
  (`wip-some-topic`) and still skip `feature/**` and `main`.
- Schedule path: each edited workflow's cron list is asserted unchanged against its literal.
- Live end-to-end (post-merge, AC2): make a trivial rebar write (a comment on this ticket),
  capture the resulting `tickets` head SHA, then query
  `/repos/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs?branch=tickets` and confirm zero runs exist for that SHA.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] No file in `.github/workflows/` triggers on a push to `tickets` — checked by the new
      enumerating test, which reads the directory rather than a hard-coded name list, so an
      added workflow cannot regress it silently.
- [x] A tickets-branch push made AFTER the change merges produces zero new workflow runs —
      checked by the GitHub Actions API for that push's head SHA, evidence recorded as a
      comment on this ticket.
- [x] Every `schedule:` cron in the repo is byte-identical to its pre-change value — checked by
      `git diff` showing no change inside any `schedule:` block, and by the cron literals
      asserted in the new test (reconcile-bridge `*/20 * * * *` and verify-identity
      `53 */6 * * *` explicitly).
- [x] `gerrit-verify.yaml` remains `workflow_dispatch`-only — checked by the existing
      `test_gerrit_verify_stays_a_dispatch_only_patchset_gate` in
      `tests/unit/test_ci_main_push_policy.py` still passing.
- [x] Push CI for ordinary topic branches is preserved — checked by the new test asserting
      `wip-some-topic` still matches all four edited workflows.
- [x] Client-facing docs warn adopters against CI triggered by tickets-branch pushes — checked
      by `grep` finding the warning in `docs/concurrency.md` (canonical, naming the schedule
      alternative) and a cross-link to it in both `docs/user-guide.md` and `docs/config.md`,
      with the guidance phrased for any adopter rather than as this repo's incident report.
- [x] Full local gate set green (ten `check_*` gates, generators no-diff, `make lint`,
      `make typecheck`, CI-equivalent pytest tier) and the change lands with `LLM-Review +1`
      and `Verified +1`.
baseline.summary: Tickets-branch pushes must trigger no CI (operator directive)

## Context and final-epic intent

Gerrit change 1517 retired two dead implementations: the file-backed top-level `bridge-status` handler, which read an unproduced `.bridge-status.json`, and `purge-bridge`, which had no supported caller and exposed an inverted `--keep` contract. That removal merged as commit `318903aa37` after LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, and zero unresolved comments.

A later dependent story deliberately reintroduced the spelling `rebar bridge-status` as a hidden compatibility alias for the new durable `rebar bridge status` operation. This does not resurrect the removed implementation. At the final epic tip, the old file-backed module remains absent, while the alias routes through the same parser/core/schema as canonical status so workflows and environments using old vocabulary continue to function. `purge-bridge` remains fully retired.

## Completed implementation and continuity

The legacy artifacts removed by change 1517 remain absent:

- `src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge.py`, including its dangling epic citation and unproduced file reader.
- `src/rebar/_commands/purge_bridge.py` and its concurrency-only worker/tests.
- top-level help pages `help/bridge-status.txt` and `help/purge-bridge.txt`.
- the old bridge-status-only tests and schema exemption.
- purge-bridge dispatch, help, docs surface, and schema references.

The final code intentionally retains or recreates these successor surfaces:

- `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` contains hidden `bridge-status` compatibility routing to the canonical nested bridge parser; `purge-bridge` remains absent.
- `src/rebar/schemas/bridge_status.schema.json`, `schemas.BRIDGE_STATUS`, and `OUTPUT_SCHEMAS["bridge_status"]` now describe the surviving durable status snapshot, not the deleted file-backed report.
- `rebar.bridge_status`, `types.BridgeStatus`, MCP `bridge_status` / `BridgeStatusOut`, `schemas/check_mcp_models.py`, and `schemas/gen_types.py` are retained consumers of that durable schema.
- canonical and hidden status entrypoints share output, errors, and exits across CLI, Python library, and MCP; the alias stays absent from top-level help.
- `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py` lists only purge-bridge as retired. Bridge-status continuity is proved by the bridge facade/contract suites.
- current user guide, release notes, ADR 0094, CLI reference, and output-schema docs distinguish the historical dead-handler removal from the later durable compatibility alias.

Surviving bridge alert reads use neutral guidance. Top-level `rebar doctor`, `bridge-fsck`, bridge preview/sync/pause/resume, legacy reconcile adapters, and persisted ticket formats are unchanged.

## Verification

Historical change-1517 evidence: held-out retirement oracle 7/7; focused help/schema/alert contracts 41 passed; lint and typecheck passed; full suite 11,149 passed with 40 skipped and 228 deselected; CI run 31218769114 passed all required matrices.

Final-epic continuity evidence is codebase-verifiable at `694cf894def36241724e7049e3308d782037ef6d`: help coverage proves purge remains retired; bridge CLI/library/MCP contract suites prove the hidden alias and durable schema consumers remain functional; schema/type/MCP drift generators remain current; generated CLI/output docs and ADR index checks pass. Gerrit change 1595 merged after LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.

## Rollback and safety

No persisted data, migration, external integration, authentication boundary, or shared-state format was removed by change 1517. Reverting only the old removal is no longer a valid rollback because it would restore the obsolete file-backed handler beside the durable successor. Any rollback must preserve the current compatibility alias and durable schema while addressing a concrete successor defect.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The obsolete file-backed bridge-status implementation and its dangling citation remain absent.

## Context
Codex currently has no Serena MCP entry, while this project relies on Serena/Pyright for semantic navigation. The tracked `.claude/settings.json` does not configure MCP servers. Separately, this operator machine's untracked Claude project config (`~/.claude.json`) launches Serena via `uvx --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena`; that machine-local fact was inspected only to identify the existing server. The delivery design is independently grounded: the current Codex manual supports project-scoped MCP servers in trusted `.codex/config.toml`, and Serena 1.6.2.dev0 exposes a `codex` context plus `--project-from-cwd` specifically for CLI agents/worktrees.

## Verified inputs
- `uvx --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena serena -V` returned `Serena 1.6.2.dev0`.
- `git ls-remote https://github.com/oraios/serena.git HEAD` returned `c7dbe3bd1198cf451bf7aa8fdeeab88571fa3a6e`.
- `uvx --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena@c7dbe3bd1198cf451bf7aa8fdeeab88571fa3a6e serena start-mcp-server --help` succeeded and documented `--context` plus `--project-from-cwd`.
- `codex mcp list` in the current worktree confirms no `serena` entry exists before the change.

## Plan
- Add a project-scoped `mcp_servers.serena` STDIO entry to `.codex/config.toml`; project scope is intentional so every contributor/worktree gets the repo-required semantic navigation server after trusting the repo, without mutating each operator's global config.
- Launch the same Serena distribution currently used on this machine, but pin the verified upstream commit: `uvx --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena@c7dbe3bd1198cf451bf7aa8fdeeab88571fa3a6e`.
- Pass `serena start-mcp-server --context codex --project-from-cwd` so each checkout/worktree activates itself; commit no user-specific project path.
- Set `startup_timeout_sec = 120` to bound and accommodate a cold uvx resolution. Keep `required` unset/false so a Serena startup failure is reported by Codex without preventing all Codex work.
- Validate TOML with Python 3.11+ `tomllib`; run `codex mcp list` from the isolated worktree and require an enabled `serena` row containing the pinned command/args; run the pinned `serena start-mcp-server --help` command and an MCP initialize/list-tools smoke test from the worktree, bounded by a test harness timeout.
- Negative control: run `codex mcp list` from a temporary untrusted/non-rebar directory and confirm the project-scoped server is not injected there.
- Land the single-file config change through Gerrit with DCO and the ticket trailer.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `codex mcp list` from a trusted rebar worktree discovers an enabled `serena` STDIO server from `.codex/config.toml`, using the pinned upstream commit.
- [ ] The server argv uses Serena's `codex` context and `--project-from-cwd`; no user-specific rebar path is committed.
- [ ] `python -c "import tomllib; tomllib.load(open('.codex/config.toml', 'rb'))"`, the pinned Serena CLI smoke command, and an MCP initialize/list-tools smoke test all succeed.
- [ ] `codex mcp list` outside the trusted rebar project does not expose the project-scoped `serena` entry; Serena startup remains non-required so failure does not block Codex itself.
- [ ] The config diff contains no secrets, and `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default suite remain green; a same-base full-gate result may be reused because this task changes only static Codex configuration.

## References
Current Codex manual: trusted projects may scope MCP servers in `.codex/config.toml`; STDIO entries accept `command`, `args`, `cwd`, `startup_timeout_sec`, and optional `required`. Serena CLI help at the pinned commit documents `--context codex` and `--project-from-cwd`.

## Why
Code review reviews a DIFF fresh with NO memory across runs. The durable `code_review` artifact (per Gerrit change/revision) today persists SURFACED findings write-only (a calibration corpus). This story adds the READER + the content-addressed STATE the region-gated novelty floor (blameless-grindable-noctule) needs, and extends the `code_review_result_v1` payload with the two new fields that state.

## What
- **Payload extension (`code_review_result_v1`, `build_payload`).** Add two fields, both read
  off the verdict dict so they are populated once and flow to EVERY emit path unchanged:
  - `session_id`: TOP-LEVEL, nullable. `build_payload` reads `verdict.get("session_id")`
    (None for Gerrit reviews; set for local session-keyed reviews by the persistence story
    paradoxal-balsamic-bubblefish). Makes local memory queryable by session.
  - `deps`: a `{reviewed-file path: sha256}` content-hash map. `build_payload` reads
    `verdict.get("deps")` (defaulting to `{}`).
- **deps collector + computation seam (`produce_code_review_verdict`).** A thin collector hashes
  each reviewed-file path once and stashes the map on the verdict (`verdict["deps"]`) in
  `_run_code_review_gate`, computed UNCONDITIONALLY after the verdict is produced and BEFORE the
  sidecar emit. This requires importing `code_review.sidecar` (for the collector +
  `_cited_paths_code_review`) EARLIER in `_run_code_review_gate` — at the top of the finalize block
  rather than only inside the existing `if request.target_ticket:` block (an explicit new import in
  `gate_dispatch.py`, enumerated here). Because it lives on the verdict dict, BOTH
  emit callers pick it up via `build_payload` with NO change to either call site:
  - the produce-path emit (`_run_code_review_gate` → `sidecar.emit`), and
  - the Gerrit voter emit (`voter.py::emit_code_review_artifact` → `sidecar.emit`), which passes
    the SAME verdict object it received — so it inherits `deps`/`session_id` for free (voter.py
    stays OUT of scope; it needs no edit).
  - **Reuse boundary:** the collector REUSES the private `attest._hash_file(path, base=…)`
    primitive (raw file-bytes sha256; a missing/unreadable path → the `absent` sentinel, so a
    create/delete is itself detectable) and `attest._hash_basis(repo_root)` for the base. This
    reuse of a private symbol is EXPLICITLY sanctioned by the epic design ("private `_hash_file`
    primitive reused; NOT `dependency_hashes`, which is plan/ticket-coupled"). It does NOT reuse
    `dependency_hashes()` (that pulls ticket file_impact + plan-verdict citation buckets).
  - **Scope of `deps`** = the review's `changed_files` UNION its cited-file paths. NOTE:
    `attest._cited_paths(verdict)` is NOT reusable here — it reads a `citations` list with
    `kind == "file"`, but code-review findings carry no such list (they only have a `location`
    string, e.g. `path` or `path:line`). So define a small `_cited_paths_code_review(verdict)`
    in `code_review/sidecar.py` that extracts the FILE path (strip any `:line` suffix) from each
    finding's `location` across the `blocking` + `advisory` buckets, ignoring empty/non-file
    locations. `deps` = `sorted(set(changed_files) | _cited_paths_code_review(verdict))`.
  - **Basis:** hashed via `attest._hash_basis(repo_root)` at the emit point. Because deps are
    computed AFTER the workflow's `gate_read_root` context has exited, `current_code_root()` is
    already `None`, so `_hash_basis` resolves to the in-place WORKING TREE (`_config.repo_root`) —
    NOT the attested snapshot. This is correct for both keyspaces: a LOCAL `review-code` reviews the
    working tree (so the working tree IS the reviewed basis), and the Gerrit voter bot checks out
    the patchset revision (so its working tree IS the reviewed revision). The content-addressed
    region gate only ever compares hashes WITHIN one keyspace, and each keyspace hashes its own
    working-tree basis consistently across runs, which is all it needs.
  - **Failure posture:** the collector is best-effort — a per-file hash failure yields the
    `absent` sentinel (never raises); a total failure leaves `deps` empty and is logged. It must
    NEVER fail the gate (mirrors the sidecar's best-effort posture).
- **Artifact addressing (title schemes, TYPED keyspaces).** Local artifacts use title
  `code-review: session:{session_id}`; Gerrit artifacts keep `code-review: {change_id} @ {revision}`
  (unchanged). These are two disjoint keyspaces so a prior LOCAL review can never seed a change's
  FIRST Gerrit review.
- **Reader `latest_code_review_result(key, *, repo_root=None)`.** `key` is a TYPED string:
  `session:<id>` or `change:<id>`. Resolution by artifact title:
  - `session:<id>` → the artifact whose title == `code-review: session:{id}` (exact; one artifact).
  - `change:<id>` → STRIP the `change:` tag to get the bare `change_id`, then match artifacts whose
    title starts with `code-review: {change_id} @ ` (spans revisions of the same change; the change
    is the memory key, the revision only makes each artifact idempotent). An unknown key kind → None.
  Artifacts are enumerated via `rebar.list_tickets(ticket_type="code_review")` and matched by title
  in-process (no new list-filter API). Across the matched artifact(s), the reader returns the
  most-recent usable `code_review_result_v1` sidecar payload's SURFACED findings + its `deps` map.
  - **SURFACED-only (mandatory; see old-frilly-plankton).** `code_review_result_v1` stores findings
    in SEPARATE top-level buckets (`blocking`, `advisory`, `coaching`) with NO per-finding
    `decision` field (unlike `plan_review_result_v1`). Therefore "surfaced" is DEFINED as the union
    of the `blocking` and `advisory` buckets; the reader returns ONLY those two buckets (never
    `coaching`, never any future dropped bucket). Dropped findings are never persisted into
    blocking/advisory, so they can never re-enter the novelty prior set.
  - **Posture:** mirrors `plan_review.sidecar.latest_review_result` — best-effort, NEVER raises,
    schema-guarded (only `code_review_result_v1` payloads), walks newest→oldest over each artifact's
    sidecar events tolerating a malformed/foreign newest file, returns None when nothing usable.
    A reader/hash/compare error degrades to None (⇒ the floor runs un-narrowed = no drops).

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py` — payload extension (`build_payload`), the thin deps
  collector, and the `latest_code_review_result` reader.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` — the `deps` computation seam in
  `produce_code_review_verdict` / `_run_code_review_gate` (stash on the verdict before emit).
- OUT of scope: local persistence wiring / setting `session_id` (paradoxal-balsamic-bubblefish);
  the region_gated_floor consumer (blameless-grindable-noctule); `voter.py` (inherits via the
  verdict — no edit).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `build_payload` adds a nullable top-level `session_id` (read from `verdict.get("session_id")`)
      and a `deps` `{path: sha256}` map (read from `verdict.get("deps")`, default `{}`).
- [ ] A thin deps collector reuses `attest._hash_file` (NOT `dependency_hashes`) and the `absent`
      sentinel; scope = `changed_files` ∪ `_cited_paths_code_review(verdict)` (paths parsed from
      each finding's `location`, since code-review findings have no `citations[kind==file]` list).
- [ ] The deps map is computed ONCE in `produce_code_review_verdict`, UNCONDITIONALLY (regardless of
      `target_ticket`), and stashed on the verdict — importing `code_review.sidecar` earlier in
      `_run_code_review_gate` — so both the produce emit and the Gerrit voter emit carry it via
      `build_payload` (voter unchanged).
- [ ] `latest_code_review_result(key)` resolves `session:<id>` (exact title `code-review: session:{id}`)
      and `change:<id>` (strip `change:`, title prefix `code-review: {id} @`); unknown kind → None.
- [ ] The reader returns SURFACED findings = union of the payload's `blocking` + `advisory` buckets
      (never `coaching`/dropped) plus the `deps` map; schema-guarded to `code_review_result_v1`.
- [ ] The reader is best-effort and NEVER raises; malformed/absent/foreign-schema → None (⇒ no drops).
- [ ] Tests: payload carries `session_id` + `deps`; deps collector hashes changed+cited paths with
      the `absent` sentinel for a missing file; reader resolves both typed keyspaces, returns
      surfaced-only, and degrades to None on a malformed/absent artifact.
baseline.summary: Code-review finding-memory reader + artifact payload (session_id + reviewed-file content-hash map)

## Summary
The reconciler preflight (`preflight_status_mapping`, `reconcile.py`) raises `StatusMappingError("local status {status!r} not in local_to_jira_status mapping ...")`. But the same function's Bug-85a1 logic deliberately accepts a value that is EITHER a local-status KEY or a Jira-status VALUE, failing only when it is in neither. So the offending value is frequently a **Jira** workflow status (e.g. `IDEA`, added Jira-side), not a local status. Labeling it "local status 'IDEA'" is misleading and misdirects debugging toward a non-existent local `idea` ticket. The `StatusMappingError` docstring (reconcile.py) makes the same wrong "references a local status" assumption.

## Reproduction Steps
1. A Jira issue is in a workflow status with no reconciler mapping (e.g. `IDEA`).
2. Reconcile → `ERROR: ... local status 'IDEA' not in local_to_jira_status mapping (target=REB-716)`.

Expected: message accurately states the status is unmapped in `local_to_jira_status` in EITHER direction (could be a local-status key or a Jira-status value) — not that it is a "local status". Actual: message asserts it is a "local status", which is false for a Jira-origin status.

## Scope
LOGGING/ERROR-MESSAGE FIX ONLY. Does NOT add the `idea`->`IDEA` mapping (that is story 6173 / tawny-herb-bug, out of scope here).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py` — the `StatusMappingError` message +
  the `StatusMappingError` / `preflight_status_mapping` docstrings.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/conflict/test_status_preflight.py` — assert the message.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The `StatusMappingError` message no longer calls the value a "local status"; it
      states the status is not mapped in `local_to_jira_status` (neither a local-status
      key nor a Jira-status value), and still includes the status value + target.
- [ ] The `StatusMappingError` and `preflight_status_mapping` docstrings no longer assert
      the value is a "local status".
- [ ] A test asserts an unmapped Jira status (e.g. `IDEA`) is not reported as a "local
      status" and the message acknowledges the Jira-status possibility.
- [ ] No mapping/behavior change (the raise condition is unchanged); existing preflight
      tests still pass.
- [ ] make lint passes for the changed files.
baseline.summary: reconciler preflight mislabels an unmapped Jira status as a 'local status'

- Out: changes to the live `~/.claude/skills` copy (personal, not version-controlled); changes to

# `plan_review/attest.py` is at the hard cap with ZERO headroom

## Context

Landing bug c083 (untracked-tolerance on four plan-review snapshot reads) hit this immediately: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` was **799** lines on `origin/main` against the **800** hard cap enforced by `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py::test_no_src_module_over_the_hard_cap` (limit single-sourced in `.github/module-size-limit.txt`).

A two-call-site change — adding `ignore_untracked=True` to two existing calls — could not be landed in the natural form:

- appending the kwarg inline made the line 114 chars, over the ruff E501 limit of 100;
- wrapping the call to satisfy E501 cost +2 lines -> 801, over the cap;
- adding the explanatory comments the change deserved cost more -> 803.

It only fit by importing `collect_plan_relation_snapshot` directly (+1 line for the import, which let the call fit on one line at 95 chars), landing the file at **exactly 800** — passing only because the gate is `> limit`, with **zero** remaining headroom. The file currently sits at **794** on `origin/main`; the headroom problem is unchanged.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

The next change to this file — any change, including a one-line bug fix — cannot land without first splitting it. The cost is not paid by whoever grew the file; it is paid by whoever next needs to fix a bug in it, under time pressure, as an unrelated blocker. That is exactly the situation task `2682` was raised for when `runner.py` hit 800 in the LLM-provider-seam epic, and it was resolved there by a real call-graph split (`runner.py` 800 -> 655 + `structured_run.py`).

It also actively degrades the code: in c083 the comments explaining WHY untracked files must be tolerated had to be cut from `attest.py` and replaced with a pointer to `resign.py`, purely to save lines. The cap is now shaping documentation quality, not just structure.

## Approach — the DECIDED seam (analysis complete)

**This is a pure refactor: zero behavioral change.** No function body is rewritten; a contiguous call-graph cluster moves to a new sibling module and is re-exported so every existing call site and monkeypatch target keeps resolving.

**Seam chosen: the remediation-mode eligibility cluster.** Extract `remediation_mode_candidate` and its single private helper `_sidecar_branch_decision` from `attest.py` into a new sibling `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/remediation_mode.py`.

Why this seam and not the others considered:

- It is a **pre-existing, isolated call-graph cluster**: `_sidecar_branch_decision` has exactly
  ONE caller in the entire repository — `remediation_mode_candidate`, directly above it — and
  `remediation_mode_candidate` is a call-graph LEAF within `attest.py` (nothing else in the file
  calls it). Verified with both Serena `find_referencing_symbols` and a repo-wide string `grep`.
- It is a **distinct concern**: "is this re-review eligible for the remediation floor?" — a
  Pass-3 floor input — as opposed to `attest.py`'s core job of signing attestations and computing
  claim-gate validity.
- The **drift-refresh cluster was evaluated and rejected**: `drift_refresh_candidate` calls
  `compute_validity` and `_authoritative_manifest` (which must stay in `attest.py`), and
  `tests/unit/test_plan_review_resign.py` monkeypatches `attest._rehash` and then calls
  `attest.refresh_attestation`, so moving that cluster would silently break the patch seam.
  This seam has no such inward dependency.

Dynamic-reference safety (the failure mode that broke epic `061c` S1):

- `remediation_mode_candidate` is reached ONLY through the module attribute
  `attest.remediation_mode_candidate` (`plan_review/__init__.py` and four test modules), including
  a `monkeypatch.setattr(attest, "remediation_mode_candidate", ...)`. Re-exporting the moved name
  from `attest.py` keeps every one of those sites resolving unchanged.
- The moved code calls `current_material_fingerprint` and `registry_version`, both of which the
  tests monkeypatch **on the `attest` module object**
  (`monkeypatch.setattr(attest, "current_material_fingerprint", ...)`,
  `monkeypatch.setattr(attest, "registry_version", ...)`). The new module must therefore resolve
  both **through the `attest` module at call time** (`from . import attest` inside the function
  body, then `attest.<name>(...)`) — a `from .attest import <name>` would bind the original and
  silently ignore the patch. The deferred import also keeps the new module import-cycle safe
  against `attest.py`'s re-export.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` is under 700 LOC (real headroom, not 799) — landed at **656** on main (094c4c4525)
- [x] any extracted module is at least 100 LOC (no sub-100-LOC fragmentation) — `remediation_mode.py` is **182**
- [x] `attest.remediation_mode_candidate` still resolves (re-exported), so no call site or
      monkeypatch target in `src/` or `tests/` changes — verified at runtime
      (`attest.remediation_mode_candidate is remediation_mode.remediation_mode_candidate` -> True)
      and by repo-wide grep: every residual reference is either prose or a live
      `attest.remediation_mode_candidate(...)` call
- [x] zero test edits are required by the move, or each required edit is justified in the commit message — **zero** test files touched; the change is 3 files, all under `src/`
- [ ] [operator-attested] the full suite passes with a test count equal to the pre-split count plus any new
      seam tests, evidenced by the two pytest summary lines quoted in a comment
baseline.summary: attest.py sits at exactly 800/800 LOC — zero headroom blocks the next edit

# Engine-wide caching: extend the runner cache to RunnerAgentStep (all workflow agent steps)

## Why
S1 caches plan-review's Pass-1 calls. The same stable-prefix waste exists in every workflow agent step
(verify/decide/coach/grounding) and other workflows (completion-verification, code-review) — they re-send a
stable system prompt + tool surface across runs. Extending caching there is the engine-wide win pulled into scope.

## What
- In the engine `RunnerAgentStep` (`workflow/runs.py:207`, builds RunRequest), populate S1's cacheable-prefix
  boundary: the static system prompt (+ stable inputs) is the cached prefix; per-run ticket data is the
  volatile suffix.
- Add a prompt-model convention to mark which part of an assembled workflow prompt is the byte-stable prefix vs
  per-run volatile inputs, so the boundary is set generically (not per call site).
- Apply `anthropic_cache_instructions` for the system prompt across steps; keep dynamic per-run content OUT of
  the cached prefix (after the CachePoint / a separate message part).

## Scope
- In: RunnerAgentStep prefix wiring; the prompt-model stable-vs-volatile convention; applying to all workflows.
- Out: the runner mechanism itself (S1, dependency); container parallelization (S3).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] RunnerAgentStep populates the cacheable prefix; verify/decide/coach cache their stable system-prompt/tool
      prefix on anthropic (`cache_read > 0` on repeats), unchanged on other providers.
- [ ] completion-verification and code-review workflows benefit (cache reads non-zero on repeats).
- [ ] Per-run volatile inputs are excluded from the cached prefix (stability test).
- [ ] `make lint` + tests pass; no finding change.

## Remediation (opus review — MAJOR 6)
- The workflow system prompt interpolates PER-RUN ticket data (`workflow/runs.py:146 resolve_prompt`), so it is
  NOT byte-stable — `anthropic_cache_instructions` over it would miss every run. Caching requires moving volatile
  ticket data OUT of the system prompt into the USER message across workflow prompts (verify/decide/coach/
  grounding/completion-verification/code-review) and marking the stable vs volatile split in the prompt model.
- file_impact extended to the prompt model/front-matter.
- [ ] The rendered workflow system PREFIX is byte-stable across runs (a stability test); per-run ticket data is
      relocated to the user message.
- [ ] verify/decide/coach + completion-verification + code-review show `cache_read > 0` on repeats (anthropic).

## Remediation (single-pass G3/G4 review — G3-1/G4-A)
- 'No finding change' for the 11 relocated prompts is currently ASSERTED, not measured — and one is the
  completion-verifier that backs this project's mandatory close gate. Add a fidelity check.
- [ ] The relocated gate prompts (esp. completion-verifier + code-review) are FIDELITY-VERIFIED: they produce
      equivalent findings post-relocation (reuse parity.py recall/false-accept, or a targeted spot eval) — not asserted.
baseline.summary: Engine-wide caching: extend the runner cache to RunnerAgentStep (all workflow agent steps)

## Context
Jira DC summary updates can retry in both pycontribs/Jira and `_with_connection_retry`. The selected route needs a dedicated no-SDK-retry client and per-call wrapper policy without changing legacy callers.

## Outcome
Implement the DC summary executor with a guarded `max_retries=0` client and fixed GET -> PUT -> GET invocation. Ambiguous PUT recovery uses a separate single-attempt GET under the shared budget.

## Plan
1. Construct a dedicated executor client through the pinned public `jira.JIRA(..., max_retries=0)` argument; fail fast unless `_session.max_retries == 0`. Preserve legacy client construction.
2. Add an injected one-attempt/no-sleep policy to `_with_connection_retry` for selected executor calls; preserve legacy wrapper defaults.
3. Make one write invocation issue exactly GET/PUT/GET. Failure ends the invocation; successful read-back is authoritative.
4. After ambiguous PUT, consume another physical invocation for one GET observation. Desired state recovers, conclusive old state may replay within budget, and failed/inconclusive observation returns `commit_unknown`.
5. Return classification/delay metadata to the shared owner; do not sleep or replay in SDK/adapter layers.
6. Emit exactly one redacted completion log for every DC terminal/exhausted outcome or cleanup failure. Include only logical id, disposition, invocation count, request count, cleanup status, `retry_not_before`, and one redacted message capped at 512 Unicode code points; cap the whole serialized log at 1,024 Unicode code points.

## Testing
Use fake sessions with raw request counters and poison sleepers/retry adapters. Include the proven Jira 3.10.5 constructor/session guard plus completion-log field, cardinality, redaction, and size assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The dedicated executor client passes `max_retries=0` and rejects a nonzero session value.
- [ ] Legacy DC client SDK retry remains unchanged.
- [ ] Each selected write invocation is exactly GET/PUT/GET without hidden repeats.
- [ ] Selected wrapper calls perform one attempt and no sleep, while legacy wrapper behavior remains unchanged.
- [ ] Desired observation recovers without another write.

- [ ] Every DC terminal/exhausted outcome or cleanup failure emits exactly one completion log with only logical id, disposition, invocation/request counts, cleanup status, `retry_not_before`, and one redacted message capped at 512 Unicode code points; the whole log is at most 1,024 Unicode code points.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The `PreToolUse:Bash` hook fails intermittently with

    PreToolUse:Bash hook error
    Failed with non-blocking status code: /bin/sh: scripts/hooks/serena_grep_reminder.py: No such file or directory

The failure is non-blocking, so tool calls still run — but the Serena-vs-grep navigation guidance the hook exists to inject is SILENTLY ABSENT for those calls, which is the whole point of the hook.

## Root cause — established by construction, not inferred

`.claude/settings.json` configures the hook with a RELATIVE command path:

    "matcher": "Bash",
    "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "scripts/hooks/serena_grep_reminder.py" }]

A relative command is resolved against the SHELL'S CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY at hook time, not against the project root. So the hook works or fails depending purely on where the preceding tool call left the shell.

MEASURED on this host:

    MISSING  /Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker
    PRESENT  /Users/joeoakhart/feat-c403-overlap-batch
    PRESENT  /Users/joeoakhart/fix/1157-ladder-windows
    PRESENT  /Users/joeoakhart/feat/0d76-bedrock-parity

`.tickets-tracker` is the ticket store — a separate git worktree with no `scripts/` directory. Any Bash call issued while the shell sits there fails the hook. That matches the observed occurrences exactly: the errors appeared in a run immediately after ticket-store commands, which leave the shell cwd in `.tickets-tracker`.

This is not a missing file. The script is present and executable in the main checkout and in every code worktree checked; only the resolution path is wrong.

## Why it matters more than a cosmetic warning

* It fails OPEN and QUIET. The guidance simply does not appear, and nothing in the transcript says
  "you are now operating without the navigation reminder" — an agent cannot tell a call that got the
  hint from one that did not.
* It is CWD-dependent, so it is intermittent and looks flaky. That invites the wrong diagnosis
  ("transient hook error") instead of the real one.
* It affects any repo-adjacent working directory, not just `.tickets-tracker` — any tool call run
  from `/tmp`, a scratch dir, or a non-repo path hits the same thing.

## Approach

Make the command path independent of the caller's cwd. Claude Code exposes `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` for exactly this, so the command should be `"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/scripts/hooks/serena_grep_reminder.py"` (quoted). An absolute path would also work but is not portable across checkouts, and this repo is routinely used from multiple worktrees, so the project-dir form is preferable.

Worth checking in the same pass whether any OTHER hook in `.claude/settings.json` uses a relative command and has the same latent defect.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The hook resolves and runs from ANY working directory, including `.tickets-tracker` and a
      directory outside the repository entirely.
- [x] A check or test asserts no hook in `.claude/settings.json` is configured with a relative command
      path, so the defect cannot silently return.
- [x] Every other hook entry in the file is audited for the same relative-path issue and fixed or
      explicitly confirmed safe.
- [x] Verified by running a Bash tool call with the shell cwd in `.tickets-tracker` and observing the
      hook's guidance appear rather than an error.
baseline.summary: PreToolUse Bash hook uses a relative command path, so it silently fails from any cwd without scripts/

## Why
Catch wiring bugs without a (near-undecidable, no-good-library) subsumption engine. Validated by spike E2.

## What
- Extend `src/rebar/llm/workflow/lint_refs.py` with a 3-state SHALLOW structural check: top-level
  required-field presence + primitive kind compatibility -> OK / UNKNOWN / ERROR; ABSTAIN (UNKNOWN)
  on `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf`/`not`/`$ref` (no subsumption).
- Add RUNTIME validation in `src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py`: a produced value is validated
  against the downstream CONSUMER's input contract via the registry validator (the real safety net).
- VALIDATOR-FAILURE handling (parity with S7's endpoint-failure fix): if the runtime validator itself
  errors (unresolvable `$ref`, registry miss, validator exception) — as opposed to producing a
  validation finding — the step run surfaces a distinct, visible "validation unavailable / errored"
  signal and does NOT silently treat the value as valid (fail-loud, never false-pass).
- Editor: render an "unchecked" badge for UNKNOWN/opaque sources (`editor.py`).

## Scope
In: shallow static + runtime validation + validator-failure handling + badge. Out: MCP opaque handling (follow-on epic).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Shallow check returns ERROR on missing-required / kind-mismatch, UNKNOWN on `oneOf`, OK on a matching shape (port spike E2).
- [ ] Runtime validation checks a produced value against the CONSUMER's input contract; a mismatch surfaces.
- [ ] A runtime VALIDATOR failure (unresolvable `$ref` / registry miss / validator exception) surfaces a distinct "validation errored" signal and never silently passes the value (fail-loud), tested.
- [ ] The inspector shows an "unchecked" badge for UNKNOWN/opaque-typed sources.
baseline.summary: Validation depth: 3-state shallow static + runtime-against-consumer

baseline.description:
LLM completion-verification close gate: an optional, signed agentic gate that verifies a ticket's completion criteria are met before closure.

## Context
rebar ships an optional LLM agent-operations framework (`rebar.llm`: review_ticket / review_code / scan_epics_for_spec) over library/CLI/MCP, plus an environment-bound HMAC signing module (`rebar.signing`: sign_manifest / verify_signature, with key-fingerprint attribution and HEAD binding) and an opt-in story/epic close `_signature_gate`. This epic adds a **completion-verifier** agent (adapted from the DSO `completion-verifier`) that, on a close attempt, verifies every acceptance/success/close/completion criterion (and, for bugs, that the bug is resolved) is demonstrably met, then — on PASS — produces a **signed** completion attestation that the close gate certifies.

Trust model (per design): security is only meaningful when rebar runs as the MCP server, whose environment signing key is canonical; CLI/library installs sign with a local key that CI reads as `foreign_key` (accepted-as-insecure by design). CI verifies the attestation under the MCP server's key. `--force-close` closes the ticket but withholds the signature, so a closed-without-signature ticket is the durable signal that validation did not pass.

This is distinct from (but composes with) epic 8a1c (cryptographic gate hardening / protected tags).

## What changes
- A pluggable per-operation structured-output **contract** (the runner stops hardcoding the findings model; each op/workflow selects its contract via `output_schema`).
- A `completion_verdict` schema + contract: `{verdict: PASS|FAIL, findings[], summary}` where each FAIL finding cites the failing criterion, an explanation, and (if applicable) a source-code citation.
- A `completion-verifier` reviewer prompt covering epics/stories/tasks/bugs (read-only fs + read-only rebar ticket access).
- `verify_completion` operation over library/CLI/MCP (MCP gated by `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM`).
- A close-time gate (`verify.require_completion_verification_for_close`, default off) that runs the verifier OUTSIDE the write lock, blocks on FAIL/missing-LLM (fail-closed, `--force-close` bypass), and signs the verdict on PASS.
- Enable the gate + LLM module in THIS project's rebar config.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Pluggable output contract: runner builds the structured-output model from `RunRequest`/step `output_schema` (default = findings), registry-based and tested.
- [ ] `completion_verdict.schema.json` added + registered in the schemas registry; Pydantic mirror pinned by a test.
- [ ] `completion-verifier` reviewer prompt added (catalog + packaged `*.md`); handles epic/story/task/bug; bug → "resolved" check.
- [ ] `verify_completion` exposed on library (`rebar.llm.verify_completion`), CLI (`rebar verify-completion`), and gated MCP (`verify_completion`).
- [ ] Close gate wired into `transition_compute` (outside lock, lazy import): FAIL or missing-LLM blocks (fail-closed) with `--force-close` bypass; PASS signs via `sign_manifest` then closes; force-close skips verify+sign.
- [ ] `verify.require_completion_verification_for_close` typed config flag (default off) with coercion + tests.
- [ ] This project's tracked `rebar.toml` enables the gate (`[verify] require_completion_verification_for_close`) + `[mcp] allow_llm` (`.rebar/config.conf` is git-ignored, so a tracked config is used).
- [ ] Docs updated (docs/llm-framework.md + CLAUDE.md tool set); optionality + schema-pin + gate-behavior + fake-runner tests pass.
- [ ] Closing a task/story/epic/bug with the gate on runs the verifier; PASS attaches a certified signature and the close proceeds; FAIL blocks with findings.
- [ ] `--force-close="reason"` closes without running the verifier and without a signature (no signed confirmation of passing validation).
- [ ] The optionality contract still holds: `import rebar` / `import rebar.llm` pull no heavy deps; a missing `[agents]` extra degrades cleanly on every interface.
- [ ] Each operation/workflow can declare its own output contract; findings remains the default; `completion_verdict` is the first alternate.
- [ ] This project's config enables the gate and the LLM module.
baseline.summary: LLM completion-verification close gate (signed, optional)

## What

Three follow-ups spun out of dc3f (puzzling-obsidian-bunny) after its core gap — 3 undeployed CloudWatch alarms — was fixed by a terraform apply: (1) confirm the alert SNS subscription actually delivers, (2) add terraform drift-detection CI so committed-but-unapplied HCL cannot sit unnoticed (the root cause of dc3f), and (3) bring a live-but-unmanaged alarm under IaC.

These are bundled deliberately: all three harden the SAME alerting/IaC chain for the rebar-gerrit host and are small. Each AC below names a single unambiguous disposition (no open design choice left to the executor).

## Scope

- rebar-gerrit-alerts SNS email subscription (the alert sink).
- No terraform CI exists (apply is manual per infra/runbooks/provision-restore.md), so committed
  HCL can silently sit unapplied — the dc3f root cause.
- One live alarm (rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high) exists in AWS but is absent from HCL/state and has
  an EMPTY alarm_actions list (never notifies).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [operator-attested] AC1 — SNS subscription delivers. The rebar-gerrit-alerts email
  subscription to joeoakhart@navapbc.com is CONFIRMED (not PendingConfirmation) so alarms
  actually deliver. Evidence: a ticket comment recording the get-subscription-attributes result
  (PendingConfirmation=false) with the SubscriptionArn and date. NOTE: verified 2026-07-11 —
  PendingConfirmation=false; this AC is already met and needs NO destructive replacement sink.
- [ ] AC2a — OIDC role (least-privilege, plan-only). The GitHub OIDC provider
  (token.actions.githubusercontent.com) ALREADY EXISTS in account 896586841071 (verified); this
  ticket adds a NEW IAM role `rebar-terraform-plan` in infra/terraform/iam.tf whose trust policy
  is scoped to `repo:navapbc/rebar:*` (sub condition) with aud=sts.amazonaws.com, and whose
  permissions are AWS-managed ReadOnlyAccess + one inline statement granting kms:Decrypt
  constrained by kms:ViaService=ssm (for the alert-endpoint SecureString data source). No apply
  or write permissions — plan-only, least privilege.
- [ ] AC2b — drift-detection CI. `.github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml` runs
  `terraform plan -input=false -lock=false -detailed-exitcode` in infra/terraform, authenticating
  via GitHub OIDC to `rebar-terraform-plan`. `-detailed-exitcode` makes a non-empty plan (exit 2)
  FAIL the check. Triggers: pull_request touching infra/terraform/**, push to main touching
  infra/terraform/** (catches already-committed-but-unapplied drift, not just PR diffs), a daily
  schedule, and workflow_dispatch.
- [ ] AC3 — codify + import the orphan alarm (keep coverage; non-destructive). Add
  `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.gerrit_data_disk_high` (name rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high;
  namespace rebar/host, metric disk_used_percent published by observability.sh, dims
  InstanceId=data.aws_instance.gerrit.id + mount=/var/gerrit, threshold 85, GTE) to
  infra/terraform/monitoring.tf WITH alarm_actions/ok_actions = the SNS topic (closing the
  silent-alarm gap), then `terraform import` it into state so HCL/state/reality agree. The alarm
  is KEPT (data-volume disk pressure is real coverage), not deleted.

## Verification

- AC1: `aws sns get-subscription-attributes` shows PendingConfirmation=false (recorded as a
  comment).
- AC2/AC3: `terraform validate` passes and `terraform plan` (ReadOnlyAccess creds) shows the new
  role/policies/alarm apply cleanly with no errors — run pre-merge in the worktree.
- Post-merge operator step (needs live creds): `terraform import
  aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.gerrit_data_disk_high rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high` then
  `terraform apply` to wire the alarm actions and create the role; the terraform-drift CI then
  reports green (no drift) on the next run.

## Notes / decisions (resolve prior plan-review BLOCKs)

- Shared S3 state backend (rebar-tfstate-896586841071) means terraform writes (import/apply) MUST
  follow the HCL merge — importing to shared state before merge would make an un-branched plan
  read the alarm as "to destroy". So this ticket lands the reviewed HCL/CI via Gerrit; the
  import/apply is the documented post-merge operator step above.
- AC1's original "OR replace with a confirmation-free sink" option is dropped: the subscription is
  already confirmed, so no destructive substitution (which risked dark alerting) is needed.
baseline.summary: rebar-gerrit alerting hardening: confirm/replace SNS subscription + add terraform drift CI
