## Context
The exhaustive current-main macOS census found remaining multi-second costs caused by test-scale wall-clock windows rather than useful production work: review-bot ticket bootstrap is about 10.15 worker-phase seconds per cell, lock-retry coverage totals about 15.56s per cell, review-bot shutdown cases are about 9s per cell, and autodeploy coverage includes an explicit 3s sleep plus an 8.25s unreachable-health case. Production timeout, retry, drain, and health budgets are contractual and must remain unchanged.

Closed classless-dainty-lamprey already proved and landed the same pattern for snapshot low-speed and retry tests. Maintained OSS consensus supports the direction: CPython uses 0.05-0.1s trigger windows with generous cleanup deadlines, and urllib3 injects or scales backoff while retaining real sockets. Ticket history requires retaining real subprocess, lock, process-group, and health behavior: royal-weariless-zebrafish, odorful-epidemic-shelduck, balsamy-eloquent-iggypops, equestrian-clueless-cowbird, and unskillful-supportive-lion.

## Plan
- Reprofile each named family alone on current main and record wall and worker-phase baselines.
- Freeze behavioral contract cards for attempt counts, logical backoff schedules, real lock/process/socket behavior, terminal states, cleanup, and exact error/observability output.
- Inject or scale only test-owned clocks/windows; retain real boundary execution and generous teardown polling.
- Prove each final oracle RED against an exact-defect mutation before implementation, then GREEN.
- Run focused suites, lint, typecheck, and full Gerrit Verify; report per-cell and aggregate runner savings and the first post-merge organic observation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Production timeout, retry, drain, health, and backoff defaults are byte-for-byte unchanged.
- [x] Real subprocess, lock, process-group, and health boundary coverage remains enabled.
- [x] Each shortened case preserves attempt counts, logical schedule, terminal state, cleanup, and observability assertions.
- [x] Each case has legitimate RED-to-GREEN and exact-defect mutation evidence.
- [x] Same-host before/after timings report macOS wall and total runner savings.
- [x] Focused tests, lint, typecheck, LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, and merge are recorded before closure.
baseline.summary: Shorten remaining test-only real-time windows without changing production budgets

# plan-review fan-out optimization: caching, parallelize, merge, bin-pack (token + wall-clock, fidelity-preserving)

## Context

plan-review's container criteria G3/G4 run as `2*N_children` SEQUENTIAL agentic LLM calls
(`pass1.py:_run_container`), OUTSIDE the thread pool — N=8 ⇒ 16 calls ≈ 27 min, each re-sending the whole
parent plan. Proven bounded-but-slow (faulthandler stacks + per-pairing instrumentation), not a loop.
Provenance: authored in the BESPOKE harness (story ca03 / dry-frost-zenith, commit 832b3af0) for
CONTEXT-WINDOW FITTING while keeping content whole ("never chunk content"); the workflow migration extracted
it verbatim; it is NOT a partial-re-review mechanism. G3/G4 are inherently CROSS-CHILD criteria, so the
per-child slice was a window concession that batching can partly reverse for both cost AND fidelity.

Engine impact: most work is inside the ProductionBatchRunner (`run_pass1`/`pass1.py`/`passes.py`/`sizing.py`),
invoked as ONE opaque `batch` step — the interpreter/YAML need no change. The shared seam is the runner
(`RunRequest` + `runner.py`), used by both `passes.py` and the engine `RunnerAgentStep`; caching is applied
there and extended engine-wide. Caching approach + gotchas confirmed against OSS pydantic-ai users
(Arize/phoenix, code-graph-rag, shotgun, varro).

## Children (de-risk order)

1. **S1** caching substrate at the shared runner seam (fidelity-neutral) — foundational.
2. **S3** parallelize the container fan-out + warm-then-fan-out + budget-cap fix (depends S1).
3. **S2** engine-wide caching via RunnerAgentStep (depends S1).
4. **S4** merge G3+G4 into one call per bin (depends S3; eval-gated).
5. **S5** child bin-packing (depends S4; eval-gated).
6. **S6** fidelity-eval harness `da34` (reuse eval_specs + parity.py; gates S4/S5).

Fidelity-neutral pieces (S1, S3, S2) ship ahead of the eval-gated ones (S4, S5).

## Out of scope

Reverting to the pre-ca03 "2 parallel whole-plan calls" design (trades back per-child fidelity); content
chunking/truncation (forbidden by ca03); the grace-thud-feint delta-re-review path (separate).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All six child stories (S1-S6) closed.
- [ ] An 8-child epic review completes in minutes (was ~27 min) with materially lower token cost (cache reads non-zero).
- [ ] Caching is provider-safe: openai/gemini calls succeed unchanged.
- [ ] Findings remain within offline-eval tolerance of the current per-child behavior (no fidelity regression).
- [ ] `make lint` + full suite pass.


## Remediation (opus review)
- S1 RESCOPED: cache the SYSTEM PROMPT (anthropic_cache_instructions/tool_definitions, anthropic-gated) — the stable
  parent plan lives there, not the user message; no RunRequest content-list change (avoids breaking the
  structured-output retry path).
- NEW S6 (`da34-ac98-e375-4af0`) fidelity-eval HARNESS: a SEMANTIC eval (real findings, new-vs-baseline) — the existing parity
  harness is structural (FakeRunner, zero model calls). S4 and S5 now DEPEND ON S6.
- S3: non-streaming warm-then-fan-out (warm = first real pairing to completion); a NEW pool inside _run_container;
  budget cap must NOT shed G3/G4 (fidelity) — fix the cost model, not centrality scaling.
- S2: caching workflow steps requires relocating per-run ticket data out of the (interpolated) system prompt.
- Updated DAG: S1->{S2,S3}; S3->S4; S6->{S4,S5}; S4->S5.

## Sequencing note (single-pass G3/G4 review)
- Land S3 -> S4 -> S5 STRICTLY in DAG order: S4/S5's sizing.py container-cost projections are only correct AFTER S3's 'container never shed' + cost-model fix lands.
baseline.summary: plan-review container fan-out (G3/G4) is sequential — epic review wall-time ~2*N_children agentic calls, looks like a hang

baseline.description:
# The completion verifier cannot bound a runaway: repetition is detected but nothing acts on it

## The defect

The completion-verify agent step has **no bound on a runaway**. When the agent falls into a repeating tool-call cycle it burns its entire step budget on redundant calls and is then **killed with no verdict at all** — leaving `--force-close`, the unattested close this project forbids, as the only exit. **20 of 205 epics in this store already carry a `FORCE_CLOSE` audit comment**, including `1d96` (21 descendants) and `bf50` (19), so this is the established escape hatch, not a hypothetical.

The step budget exists to bound exactly this failure. It does not: it is a flat ceiling that stops the run *after* the waste, rather than a guard that detects the runaway and makes the agent land.

### Measured: three of four real runs of this gate LOOP

Four instrumented live runs, same codebase state except bf31's which predates its own fix:

| run | criteria | calls | **distinct** | redundant | distinct ratio | outcome | `w24 distinct<=0.5` fires |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FULL | 14 | 258 | **238** | 20 | **0.922** | died empty | **never** |
| SPLIT-A | 7 | 257 | **76** | **181** | 0.296 | died empty | **call 88** |
| SPLIT-B | 7 | 270 | 167 | 103 | 0.619 | died empty | **call 196** |
| bf31 pre-fix | 14 | 264 | 135 | 129 | 0.511 | died empty | **call 151** |

Repetition wasted **40-70% of every pathological run**. SPLIT-A is textbook: the IDENTICAL call `search_files("_loader", "src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler")` repeated **144 times**, returning the identical 12,554-char result each time, from call #81 to the end. SPLIT-B looped 62x on `search_files("deleted", tests/.../test_backend_characterization.py)` -> an **honest** `(no matches)` the agent simply would not accept. Only the clean FULL run was genuine breadth.

### The mechanism that turns a runaway into "no verdict"

1. `build_agent_request` (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py:327-339`) builds the `RunRequest` for every
   workflow agent step and never sets `tool_step_limit`; the v3 step schema is closed, so
   `completion-verification.yaml`'s `decide@then/verify` step has no way to supply one.
2. The shipped forced-landing primitive is therefore dormant for the one step that needs it:
   `src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py:64-73` rewrites the toolsets to
   `.filtered(lambda ctx, _: ctx.run_step <= limit)`. Its only production setter is the bounded
   recovery sub-call (`completion_recovery.py:471`, `_EVIDENCE_TOOL_STEPS=16`).
3. Exhaustion raises pydantic-ai `UsageLimitExceeded` -> `interpret_failure`
   (`structured_run.py:75-101`) raises `LLMRunnerError` -> `CompletionAgentStep.run`
   (`completion_recovery.py:429-432`) catches only `UnretryableOutputError`, of which
   `LLMRunnerError` is a strict **ancestor** (`errors.py:29-46`) -> `failure_diagnostic` stays
   `None` -> `raise_completion_workflow_failure` raises a bare `LLMError` at
   `completion_recovery.py:400`. No verdict, no `gate_error_v1` sidecar, computed diagnostic
   discarded one frame from the surface.

---

## WITHDRAWN PLAN (kept visible deliberately — the wrong version is the instructive artifact)

> **An earlier revision of this ticket proposed a FLAT FORCED LANDING: set
> `tool_step_limit = max(0, request_limit - 1)` (= 239 at the default budget) unconditionally on the
> primary verify step, so tools are withdrawn near the end of the budget and the agent must emit a
> verdict.**
>
> **WHY IT WAS WITHDRAWN.** The design intent of the step budget is to bound **FAILURES** — runaway
> tool calls under error conditions — and **NOT to cap capacity**; it was explicitly never meant to
> restrict tool calls for large epics. A flat landing inverts that: it caps capacity for every run,
> including healthy ones.
>
> The data refutes its necessity as well as its intent. The only run that was genuinely budget-bound
> by *breadth* is the clean FULL run — 92% distinct signatures, 93.8-100% novelty in its final block.
> Truncating that at 239 requests would land a verdict on deliberately-truncated evidence for
> legitimate work: **a worse verdict, not a safer one**, and on a gate that SIGNS its output.
>
> The withdrawn plan was not wrong about the mechanism — links 1-3 above still hold, and the
> ACTUATOR it named (withdraw tools so the agent lands) is retained. It was wrong about the
> **trigger**: budget-proximity instead of runaway-detection.

---

## THE FIX: trigger the existing actuator on repetition, not on budget proximity

Withdraw tools **when a runaway is detected**, so the agent lands a verdict on the evidence it has. Healthy breadth is never touched.

### Blocker: the existing detector's headline metric is INVERTED on real data

`max_consecutive_repeat` (`src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:213-235`) counts only *adjacent identical* signatures, so it is blind to any cycle of length >= 2:

| trace | what it is | **`max_consecutive_repeat`** |
|---|---|---|
| bf31 pre-fix | a genuine **4-call cycle** repeated 31-37x | **1** |
| FULL | **healthy** breadth | **5** |

**The pathological run scores 1; the healthy run scores 5.** An actuator wired to this metric would fire on healthy work and miss real cycles — the exact inversion of what is wanted. It catches SPLIT-A's 144x 1-cycle (137) only because the degenerate 1-cycle is the single shape it can see. This is also why ticket a89d-4dd2-f421-417a measured `max_consecutive_repeat=1` and concluded *"It is NOT a runaway loop."*

**This ticket therefore `depends_on` [rebar:70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0]**, which fixes the metric. Building the actuator against today's signal is the one thing this evidence forbids. Sequencing is not optional here.

### The discriminator that works: a windowed distinct-ratio

Lowest distinct-ratio over any trailing window, all four runs:

| window | bf31 | SPLIT-A | SPLIT-B | **FULL (healthy)** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | 0.250 | **0.062** | 0.062 | **0.750** |
| 24 | 0.167 | **0.042** | — | **0.833** |
| 32 | 0.125 | **0.031** | — | **0.875** |

`distinct(last 24 tool calls) <= 0.50` fires on **all three** pathological runs (calls 151, 88, 196) and **never** on the healthy one — a ~5x margin. It is a set cardinality over a window, therefore **order-insensitive**, so unlike adjacency its value does not change when tool calls complete out of emission order (which these traces do).

### Feasibility — MEASURED, not assumed (each claim has an experiment)

* **A tools-withdrawn turn DOES emit a schema-valid verdict.** Experiment E1, `FunctionModel`
  looping unconditionally, `mode="structured"` / `output_schema="completion_verdict"`, the real
  runner: with `tool_step_limit=6` the tool surface offered per request went
  `[6, 6, 6, 6, 6, 6, 0]` and the run **returned a valid `completion_verdict`** (verdict=FAIL, one
  finding) in 7 requests. The control arm (`tool_step_limit=None`) raised `LLMRunnerError` with no
  verdict. This retires the objection recorded on ticket 9a08-614d-a9d4-4a81, whose prototype
  withdrew tools and found "the exhausted agent emitted unparseable prose": under `mode="structured"`
  the Agent is constructed with `output_type` (`structured_run.py:191-196`), so the landing turn is
  schema-constrained.
* **A runaway CAN be aborted mid-run, so it can be ROUTED rather than merely capped.** Experiment E5:
  an exception raised from inside the toolset filter predicate propagates cleanly out of
  `agent.run_sync` and survives in the `__cause__` chain (control arm, returning `False`, returns a
  verdict as in E1). **Caveat that this plan must handle:** it currently arrives at the surface as
  `LLMUnavailableError: the LLM provider call failed`, because `interpret_failure`'s third branch
  (`structured_run.py:110-155`) sweeps any unrecognised exception into the provider-outage bucket. A
  runaway misreported as a provider outage would be a NEW defect of exactly the kind this ticket
  exists to remove, so `interpret_failure` must gain a typed branch AHEAD of that fallback.
* `run_ctx.messages` and `run_ctx.usage.tool_calls` are both available inside the predicate (verified
  against `pydantic_ai.tools.RunContext` fields).
* `usage_log.failure_usage` duck-types on a plain message list (`type(m).__name__ == "ModelResponse"`
  / `"ToolCallPart"`), so the existing signature logic runs **verbatim** on the live history.

### Cost: the predicate runs ONCE PER TOOL PER STEP — the detector must not re-walk history

Measured in E5: with 6 tools registered the predicate was invoked **6 times per run step** (30 calls across 5 steps), and the history it sees grows by 2 messages per step. Recomputing signatures over the whole message list on every invocation is therefore O(tools x steps x history) — on a 250-request run that is a self-inflicted cost on the healthy path this ticket promises not to disturb. The discriminator must be computed **at most once per `run_step`** (memoised on the step number) and read only the trailing window, never the full history.

### On runaway detection, ROUTE TO THE TOOL-FREE FINALIZER — do not land on the poisoned history

The earlier revision of this section said "withdraw tools so the agent lands a verdict on the evidence it has". **That is superseded.** The objection that killed the flat forced landing — *a worse verdict on degraded evidence, on a gate that SIGNS its output* — applies with equal force to landing on a history that has just repeated one identical call 144 times (SPLIT-A). Applying that standard consistently means the runaway's own context must not be the basis of a signed verdict.

Instead, a detected runaway routes into the **already-shipped bounded recovery + tool-free finalizer** (`completion_recovery.py:453-521`): each explicit criterion is re-evaluated in a **fresh history** (so the loop cannot persist), the evidence run converges after `_EVIDENCE_TOOL_STEPS=16` (post-[rebar:e1b1-859e-a7b4-48f2] that boundary steers with synthetic tool results rather than withdrawing tool definitions, which 400s on Bedrock/Anthropic mid-history), and a `single_turn`, tool-free structured finalizer emits the `completion_verdict` from that clean evidence. This is the design ticket 9a08-614d-a9d4-4a81 shipped and gated on token exhaustion alone; this ticket adds the runaway trigger it was never wired to.

Concretely the actuator becomes: detect -> raise a typed runaway error -> `interpret_failure` classifies it (see the caveat above) -> `CompletionAgentStep.run` (`completion_recovery.py:425-431`, which today catches only `UnretryableOutputError` under `_is_token_exhaustion`) also catches the runaway error and calls the existing `_recover(...)`.

**Fallback if the finalizer still yields nothing.** Recovery is not assumed to succeed: it can fail its own preconditions (`_validate_recovery_inputs`), exceed `_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS`/evidence bounds, or the finalizer can fail validation. Every such path already raises `CompletionRecoveryError` carrying a bounded diagnostic, and `raise_completion_workflow_failure` (`completion_recovery.py:373-402`) then emits the `gate_error_v1` sidecar. So the terminal state is "no verdict, WITH a recorded diagnostic naming the runaway" — strictly better than today's bare `LLMError` with `diagnostic = null`, and an AC below pins it.

### The shared discriminator contract — THREE consumers, one definition

The signal must be pinned here, not left to "e.g. a windowed distinct-ratio", or two tickets ship incompatible halves. The contract:

| item | value |
|---|---|
| summary field name | `distinct_ratio_window` |
| window (trailing tool calls) | `24` |
| trip condition | `distinct_ratio_window is not None and distinct_ratio_window <= 0.50` |
| semantics | set cardinality of tool-call signatures over the trailing window, divided by the window size; order-insensitive; `None` when fewer than 24 signatures exist (insufficient sample — consumers never trip on short runs) |
| producer | `usage_log._repetition_summary` (ticket 70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0) |

Consumers, all three of which must agree on that one field:
1. **this ticket's actuator**, which trips on it;
2. **[rebar:70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0]**, which produces it (its AC currently says only "*e.g.* a windowed
   distinct-ratio" and must be tightened to this exact field name, window and semantics);
3. **ticket aec1-76e7-bb95-4c86** (usage instrumentation, already claimed and in progress), which must
   record this field alongside `tool_calls` (its `_SHAPE_FIELDS` allowlist includes
   `distinct_ratio_window`) so a run's repetition profile is recoverable after the fact. (Ticket d166-036c-238c-4b39 recorded the same mechanism — the `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` no-op and the
   missing `tool_calls` field — and `aec1-76e7-bb95-4c86` is the live work ticket for it.)

The window and threshold are named constants single-sourced beside the producer, not literals buried in the predicate.


### Both kill paths must be bound — as FAILURE conditions, not workload ceilings

`build_usage_limits` (`structured_run.py:399-412`) installs two independent ceilings:

    request_limit    = max(1, ceil(eff_max_iter / 2))   # 240 at the default max_iterations=480
    tool_calls_limit = max(8, eff_max_iter)              # 480

`run_step` increments once per **model request** (`pydantic_ai/_agent_graph.py:856`) and therefore bounds only the first. Measured sweep: at 3 tool calls/request a `tool_step_limit` of 239, 216 **and** 180 all still die. The clean FULL run sat at 258/240 = **1.075**; ticket a89d-4dd2-f421-417a measured a real run at 475/240 = **1.979**, clearing the 480 ceiling by **2 calls**. A guard keyed on `run_step` alone passes a 1-call-per-request test and still dies in production.

Because the discriminator is computed over **tool calls**, a runaway that burns calls without burning requests trips the same signal — so both paths are bound without introducing any workload ceiling.

**Enforcement point (pinned from the vendored source):** `UsageLimits.check_before_tool_call` (`pydantic_ai/usage.py:412-419`) is called from `_agent_graph.py:1703-1706` with **projected** usage (`usage.tool_calls + len(calls_to_run)`) and raises **before** executing, so `usage.tool_calls` never overshoots — the run dies instead. The guard must therefore act while headroom still remains.

---

## HONEST LIMITS OF THIS FIX — do not soften these

**1. This does NOT make e369's full-criteria close reach a verdict.** The clean FULL run never trips the discriminator, so it would still die budget-exhausted on genuine breadth. **Per the stated design intent that is CORRECT behaviour, not a bug to route around** — the budget bounds failures, and that run contains no failure to bound.

**2. The path to e369 reaching a verdict is AC-split PLUS this actuator, is two tickets, and promises no PASS.** Each half's genuine work (76 and 167 distinct calls) sits inside the budget once its loop is cut — but "reaches a verdict" is not "passes". Criterion #1's Gerrit half remains unreachable by any repository tool (ticket 6ec8-24c7-182b-40d0), and the flat budget still does not scale with claim volume (ticket a89d-4dd2-f421-417a, ticket d59e-e042-2b94-4b70).

## The AC-split fallback: tested live — both halves still died; belongs in its own ticket

Split by explicit AC index (never inferred), each half carrying the full context: 14 criteria -> 7 + 7, context 99,347 -> 96,631 (A) / 96,086 (B) chars. The criteria partition cleanly (each is an independent `- [x]` item), but **both halves still died empty**, and the per-criterion cost did not fall:

| run | criteria | distinct calls | **distinct per criterion** |
|---|---|---|---|
| FULL | 14 | 238 | 17.0 |
| SPLIT-A | 7 | 76 | 10.9 |
| SPLIT-B | 7 | 167 | **23.9** |

SPLIT-B spent **more** evidence per criterion than the full run; run-to-run variance (10.9-23.9) dominates any halving effect. Two signatures over two disjoint criteria subsets is also a **material change to what the attestation means** and needs its own design. It is a capability, not this bug's fix — and only viable at all *with* this actuator, since both halves were killed by loops, not breadth.

## Measurement gap found along the way

The control-group question ("how many requests did the epics that PASSED consume?") **could not be answered honestly**: `usage_log.record()` no-ops unless `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` is set (unset by default), and even then `_FIELDS` (`usage_log.py:32`) omits `tool_calls`. Filed as ticket d166-036c-238c-4b39 — a gate whose spend cannot be measured after the fact cannot be tuned, the same "computed then discarded" shape as ticket 8b97-a0ca-82a4-4d4e.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] a runaway (a repeating tool-call cycle) is detected DURING the run and the run is aborted at
      that point, rather than continuing until the step budget is exhausted
- [x] the detected runaway is routed into the shipped bounded recovery + tool-free finalizer
      (`completion_recovery.py:453-521`), so the emitted `completion_verdict` is built from freshly
      gathered per-criterion evidence and NOT from the history in which the agent looped
- [x] the runaway error is classified by `interpret_failure` with its OWN typed branch placed ahead
      of the generic `LLMUnavailableError` fallback (`structured_run.py:110-155`); a test asserts a
      runaway is NOT reported as "the LLM provider call failed"
- [x] the trigger is runaway detection, not budget proximity: a run whose trailing-window
      distinct-ratio stays above the threshold is never aborted. Pinned by a test built from the FULL
      run's profile (0.922 overall distinct ratio, minimum 24-window ratio 0.833) asserting the guard
      does not fire
- [x] the guard fires on a k-cycle with k >= 2: a test replays a 4-cycle (which scores
      `max_consecutive_repeat == 1`) and asserts the guard fires, so the metric blind spot cannot
      return
- [x] both kill paths are bound as failure conditions. The RED test varies the calls-per-request
      ratio across 1, 2 and 3 calls per request and includes a case that a `run_step`-keyed guard
      fails to bound; a fixture pinned at 1 call/request does not satisfy this criterion
- [x] the discriminator is computed at most ONCE per `run_step` (memoised on the step number) and
      reads only the trailing window; a test asserts the number of signature computations is <= the
      number of run steps, given a tool surface of 6 tools (measured: the predicate is invoked once
      per tool per step)
- [x] the actuator reads the field named `distinct_ratio_window` with window 24 and trip condition
      `<= 0.50`, and window/threshold are named constants single-sourced beside the producer in
      `usage_log`; the same field name and semantics are pinned in [rebar:70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0]
- [x] if recovery or the finalizer also fails to produce a verdict, the run terminates with a
      `gate_error_v1` sidecar whose diagnostic names the runaway (`distinct_ratio_window` and the
      top repeated signatures) — a test asserts the sidecar is emitted, so the terminal state is
      never today's bare `LLMError` with `diagnostic = null`
- [x] no new workload ceiling is introduced: no run is aborted merely for being large, and a test
      drives a high-novelty run past the previous flat-landing threshold without an abort
- [x] `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_token_recovery.py:132`
      (`assert runner.requests[-1].tool_step_limit is None`) still passes UNEDITED — it pins the
      tool-free finalizer, which this change must not alter
- [x] the full CI selection (`pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 4 --dist worksteal`) is
      green apart from the known pre-existing failure recorded on ticket 354d-c85d-6689-4302

## Testing
 … [truncated by reconciler]

## Why

CI keeps two ratchets advisory/non-gating (test.yml): full-tree mypy and the full-set ruff. The clean core (reducer/graph/_store) is mypy-gated, but the rest of src/rebar carries 158 mypy errors so gating it would red every build; and BLE001 (blind-except) is relaxed for tests/**. This let a type error reach CI on #56 (the local hook only runs ruff). Goal: drive the debt to zero and make both fully gating, so type/blind-except regressions fail at commit + CI, not after merge.

## What

- Drive `mypy src/rebar` to ZERO (158 errors / 37 files): llm (56), _engine_support (47), _engine (46), _io (6), _commands (3). Fix properly — real annotations / guards / TypeGuards; a justified `# type: ignore[code]` ONLY for genuine external-untyped / false-positive cases, never blanket silencing.
- Tighten BLE001: remove `BLE001` from the `tests/**` per-file-ignore and resolve the 20 blind-excepts (specific exception types or inline-justified `# noqa: BLE001`). KEEP the T201 CLI-print ignores (intentional operator output — out of scope).
- Flip CI to gating: expand `make typecheck` to the full `src/rebar`; make the test.yml mypy step gating (drop the advisory `|| true`); remove the now-redundant advisory full-set ruff step (the gating `make lint` already covers E,F,W,I,UP,B). Add a `typecheck` pre-commit hook so type errors fail at commit time.

## Scope

In scope: the mypy + BLE001 remediation + the CI/Makefile/hook gating flip. Out of scope (separate efforts, flagged): the module-size allowlist (file-splitting refactor), coverage fail_under=50 (needs new tests), the intentional T201 CLI-print ignores.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `mypy src/rebar` reports zero errors (was 158); fixes are real type corrections, with any `# type: ignore` carrying a code + one-line justification.
- [ ] `ruff check src tests` passes with BLE001 removed from the tests/** ignore (the 20 blind-excepts resolved); the T201 ignores are retained.
- [ ] `make typecheck` covers the full `src/rebar`; the CI mypy step is gating (no `|| true`); the redundant advisory ruff step is removed.
- [ ] A `typecheck` pre-commit hook runs `make typecheck` (check-only, never mutates), consistent with the existing lint hook.
- [ ] The full non-integration test suite stays green; no behavior change (type/lint-only edits).
baseline.summary: Enable full mypy + ruff(BLE001) gating in CI — remove the advisory ratchets

## Context

`tests/unit/test_opcert_service_app.py::test_matching_guard_is_accepted` intermittently CRASHES its xdist worker on CI (ubuntu py3.11, `-n 4 --dist worksteal`) instead of failing an assertion:

    [gw3] node down: Not properly terminated
    worker 'gw3' crashed while running '...::test_matching_guard_is_accepted'

Seen across many runs and several worker slots (gw0/gw1/gw3), so it follows the TEST, not a slot. No traceback, no `Fatal Python error`, no `Segmentation fault`, no `INTERNALERROR` in any log.

## Root cause (investigated; full evidence in the ticket comments)

**1. How the worker dies — deliberate process exit.** CI runs the suite with `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread` (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`). On expiry pytest-timeout's thread watchdog writes a stack dump to the worker's CAPTURED stderr and then calls `os._exit(1)` — no flush, no unwind, no exception. The execnet channel dies mid-test and the dump is discarded. Reproduced byte-for-byte locally with a throwaway `sleep(60)` test under `--timeout=5 --timeout-method=thread -n 2`, including the absence of a traceback and of any `Timeout >` line. This is NOT an OOM kill, native abort, or xdist protocol failure.

**2. What burns the 300s — an unbounded shutdown wait.** `test_matching_guard_is_accepted` is the ONLY test in the file that returns while a job is still IN FLIGHT (every other test either polls to a terminal status or enqueues nothing), so it is the only one whose `client` fixture teardown races a live job. `opcert_service/app.py` `_worker` offloads with `asyncio.to_thread`, i.e. onto the event loop's DEFAULT executor. `lifespan` cancels the worker — which returns immediately — but the orphaned OS thread stays registered with the default executor, and the loop's teardown then calls `loop.shutdown_default_executor()`, which joins it with NO timeout. Measured with a probe that enqueues a job and immediately exits the `TestClient` context:

- 12s job, `job_timeout_seconds=30` -> teardown returned at 12.01s
- 30s job, `job_timeout_seconds=30` -> teardown returned at 30.02s

Teardown tracks the JOB duration, not the configured timeout, pinning the wait on the executor join rather than on `asyncio.timeout`. Same on 3.11.13 and 3.12.13. `lifespan` also awaits its tasks UNBOUNDED (`await task`), which the sibling `review_bot/app.py` explicitly bounds under `shutdown_cancel_seconds()`; `opcert_service` copied that app's ACK-fast queue+worker shape without the bound. `review_bot`'s own comment asserts a `to_thread` offload "returns immediately without waiting for the orphaned OS thread" — true of the `await`, but blind to the executor join.

This is also a live production defect, independent of CI: `DEFAULT_JOB_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` is 900, so a deploy-time SIGTERM during a gate job blocks shutdown for up to 15 minutes rather than a bounded grace window.

**Not proven, stated plainly.** In this test `jobs.run_job` is faked to a pure, instant function, so what makes the in-flight job slow enough to reach 300s on a loaded runner is INFERRED, not demonstrated. Naive repeats do not reproduce (12 module loops and a generated 400-copy stress file under `-n 4 --dist worksteal` all passed clean). The remediation therefore targets what IS proven: remove the only unbounded wait reachable from this test, so no in-flight job can ever consume the per-test budget regardless of why it is slow. This is a mechanism fix, not a retry, skip, or quarantine — the test keeps asserting exactly what it asserts today.

## Approach

1. `src/rebar/opcert_service/config.py` — add `shutdown_cancel_seconds` (env
   `REBAR_OPCERT_SHUTDOWN_CANCEL_SECONDS`, positive-or-default fallback, mirroring `_timeout_env`).
2. `src/rebar/opcert_service/app.py` — give the app its OWN `ThreadPoolExecutor`, created in
   `lifespan` startup and used by the worker via `loop.run_in_executor` behind a module-level
   `_offload` seam instead of `asyncio.to_thread`. Keeping the job OFF the loop's default executor
   is the load-bearing part: bounding the task await alone does NOT help, because the block lives in
   `shutdown_default_executor()`. On shutdown: cancel tasks, join them under
   `shutdown_cancel_seconds`, then `executor.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)` to ABANDON
   whatever is still running (the review_bot abandon semantics).
3. `tests/unit/test_opcert_service_app.py` — repoint the two worker tests that currently patch
   `app_module.asyncio.to_thread` at the new `_offload` seam, and add a regression test asserting
   lifespan shutdown returns promptly with a deliberately blocking job in flight.

Prototype measured: dedicated executor + `shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)` returns the shutdown path in 0.00s where the current code blocks for the job's full duration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The worker's cause of death is captured and recorded on this ticket: pytest-timeout
      `--timeout-method=thread` -> `os._exit(1)`, with the CI signature reproduced locally.
- [x] The mechanism is classified on this ticket as DELIBERATE PROCESS EXIT (not OOM kill, native
      abort, or xdist protocol failure), with the evidence that rules out each alternative.
- [x] `rebar.opcert_service.config.OpcertServiceConfig` exposes `shutdown_cancel_seconds`, sourced
      from `REBAR_OPCERT_SHUTDOWN_CANCEL_SECONDS`, falling back to the default when missing,
      unparseable, or non-positive.
- [x] The op-cert worker runs jobs on an app-owned executor, NOT the event loop's default executor,
      and `lifespan` shutdown bounds the task join and abandons the executor without waiting.
- [x] A regression test in `tests/unit/test_opcert_service_app.py` enqueues a deliberately blocking
      job and asserts lifespan shutdown returns in well under that job's duration. It FAILS against
      the pre-fix code (teardown tracks the job) and PASSES after.
- [x] `test_matching_guard_is_accepted` still asserts the 202 it asserts today — unchanged
      assertions, not skipped, not quarantined, not retried.
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_opcert_service_app.py -n 4 --dist worksteal --timeout=60
      --timeout-method=thread` passes repeatedly on py3.11, and `make lint` + `make typecheck` pass.
baseline.summary: Flaky CI: test_matching_guard_is_accepted kills its xdist worker with no traceback

## Context

rebar forked from navapbc/digital-service-orchestra (DSO) and inherits DSO's Jira-reconciler design, but rebar currently has **no CI that runs the reconciler** — Jira sync only happens when a human runs `rebar reconcile` locally. We want the Jira <-> rebar sync to run automatically and observably, modeled on DSO's two GitHub Actions workflows (`reconcile-bridge.yml` + `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml`), translated to rebar's diverged surface, and documented so client projects can adopt it from templates we ship.

### Confirmed divergences from DSO (drive the translation)
- Invocation: `rebar reconcile --mode live` (== `python -m rebar_reconciler`).
  Exit 75 = reschedule (re-run, NOT failure); exit 3 = another pass in flight.
- **Reconciler does NOT push its event writes.** It writes inbound events as
  uncommitted files into the `.tickets-tracker` worktree and bypasses the CLI
  auto-push path, so a CI **commit-back + push to `origin/tickets`** step is
  REQUIRED (DSO's loop is necessary, not redundant). `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH` does not
  cover this.
- No `BRIDGE_ENV_ID`; optional `REBAR_ENV_ID` (default author stamp "reconciler").
- Env names are the new `REBAR_*` set; Jira creds stay `JIRA_URL/JIRA_USER/
  JIRA_PROJECT` (vars) + `JIRA_API_TOKEN` (secret, env-only).
- Canary ticket ops -> `rebar list --has-tag --output json`, `rebar create bug
  ... --priority --tags --description`, `rebar comment`, `rebar transition <id>
  open closed --reason "Fixed: ..."` (bug-close reason prefix enforced).
- Do NOT wire `scripts/jira-pressure-test/` e2e probes into CI (explicitly manual,
  live-mutating). Prefer `rebar bridge-probe` / `--mode reconcile-check`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`: schedule (~*/20) + workflow_dispatch
      (mode choice incl. dry-run/reconcile-check/live); mounts the `tickets` orphan
      branch as `.tickets-tracker` worktree; installs rebar + pinned acli (checksum
      verified) and authenticates; runs `rebar reconcile --mode <mode>`; treats exit
      75 as reschedule and 3 as benign "pass in flight"; commits reconciler events
      back and pushes to `origin/tickets` via a fetch-rebase-push retry loop; single-
      flight `concurrency`; failure surfaced to the run summary.
- [ ] `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml`: hourly schedule; checks the
      last successful `reconcile-bridge.yml` run via the Actions API; when stale
      beyond the window, opens (or comments on) a `heartbeat-alert`-tagged bug via
      the `rebar` CLI and auto-closes it on recovery; treats API errors as transient
      (no false alarms); commits ticket changes back to `origin/tickets`.
- [ ] Necessary+sufficient validation written up: each workflow step justified
      against rebar's actual reconciler surface (commit-back required, exit codes,
      lock semantics, creds), with anything intentionally omitted called out.
- [ ] `rebar.toml` carries the `[jira]` sync target (url/user/project=REB); the
      `JIRA_API_TOKEN` secret stays env-only.
- [ ] A setup doc (e.g. `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`) documents, for a CLIENT project,
      exactly which repo **variables** (JIRA_URL/JIRA_USER/JIRA_PROJECT, ACLI_VERSION/
      ACLI_SHA256, bridge-bot identity) and **secrets** (JIRA_API_TOKEN) to set, how
      to mount the tickets branch, and how to copy the workflow templates; the two
      workflow files double as the copy-paste templates.
- [ ] Workflows lint/parse (actionlint or equivalent) and a dry-run/`reconcile-check`
      dispatch path is described for safe first validation before enabling `live`.
- [ ] A scheduled GitHub Actions workflow keeps the REB Jira project and the rebar
- [ ] A heartbeat canary detects when the reconciler goes stale and files/auto-closes a
- [ ] The set of workflows + repo vars/secrets is validated as NECESSARY and SUFFICIENT
- [ ] Client projects can stand up the same sync by copying templates and following a

## Plan-review remediations (advisory findings triaged — all valid)

- **Canary staleness threshold (fd3a, E2).** Pin the window: alert when no
  successful `reconcile-bridge.yml` run completed in the **last 60 minutes**
  (3x the 20-min cadence); exposed as a `workflow_dispatch` override
  (`alert_window_hours`, default 2 to match DSO) and validated as a positive int.
- **Necessary+sufficient write-up location (f67d/T7, F1).** It lives as a
  **`## Necessary & sufficient` section inside `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`** — ONE
  doc, not a separate design doc (resolves the navigation-ambiguity finding). The
  section maps each workflow step to the rebar reconciler fact that requires it.
- **Rollback / disable path (f8f1, T4).** Document: disable via Actions UI (toggle
  the workflow) or remove the `schedule:` trigger; an erroneous `origin/tickets`
  push is revertable via normal git history on the orphan branch; the
  `dry-run` / `reconcile-check` dispatch mode is the mandatory safe-first-validation
  gate before enabling `live`.
- **Least-privilege token + identity (f638, T10).** Each workflow pins an explicit
  minimal `permissions:` block — reconcile-bridge: `contents: write`; canary:
  `contents: write` + `actions: read`. The default `GITHUB_TOKEN` is sufficient for
  both the `origin/tickets` push and the Actions API read (no PAT needed); the
  commit identity is a configurable bridge-bot (`BRIDGE_BOT_NAME`/`_EMAIL` repo vars).
- **AC-quality / observable outcomes (f607, P6).** "Sufficient" is operationalized:
  the necessary+sufficient claim is checkable as the `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`
  section that justifies every step against a cited reconciler fact (commit-back
  required, exit 75/3 handling, lock semantics, env/creds), with omissions listed.
baseline.summary: Automated Jira<->rebar sync via GitHub Actions (reconcile-bridge + heartbeat canary) + client setup docs

## Summary
Outbound Jira link sync writes `depends_on` dependencies with **inverted endpoints**, because the apply seam drops the `swap_endpoints` flag. This produces backwards "Blocks" links in Jira and perpetual, non-fatal `rebar.link … "would create a cycle"` WARNINGs on every inbound pass.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Create rebar tickets A, B with `A depends_on B` (B blocks A).
2. Reconcile outbound to Jira; observe Jira records **"A Blocks B"** (WRONG — should be "B Blocks A").
3. Reconcile inbound; the reconciler reads the inverted link and tries `add_dependency(A, B, blocks)`,
   which collides with the existing `A depends_on B` edge → `check_would_create_cycle` rejects it.
   Observed live for the 6 closed sibling stories under epic `jira-reb-687` (30ff/a879/95a5/978d/9a82/fd1d).

**Expected:** `A depends_on B` → Jira "B Blocks A"; inbound re-read is idempotent (no cycle). **Actual:** Jira "A Blocks B" (inverted); inbound re-read cycle-rejects on every pass forever.

## Root Cause (verified, runtime-reproduced)
`depends_on` maps to `("Blocks", swap=True)` — "A depends_on B" must be written as "B Blocks A".
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_links.py:121`: `jira_type, _swap = mapped` — **`_swap`
  is discarded**; the emitted mutation carries `type`/`to_key`/`relation` but no direction correction.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py:831`: applies `set_relationship(issue_key,
  to_key, link_type)` — always making `issue_key` the outward/blocker side; **`relation` is never read,
  no swap anywhere in the apply path.** This violates the module's own documented contract
  (`outbound_links.py:105`: "swap_endpoints is handled by the applier when issuing the directional
  Jira call") and the intent of bug 3f04 (`f57cdcd2d`, "sync issue-link relationships in both directions").
- Pre-existing since 3f04 (2026-06-26); unrelated to the reconcile-bridge outage fix.

## Impact
- **rebar store:** no divergence/data loss — the acyclic DAG is correct; the rejected inbound links are
  the inverse edges that *should not* exist. The WARNINGs are cosmetic noise to rebar.
- **Jira:** real, persistent, SILENT data-fidelity divergence — every `depends_on`-derived link points the
  wrong way and never self-heals (outbound + inbound are both ADD-only and dedup "either direction").

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Outbound apply honors `swap_endpoints`: a `depends_on` dep emits Jira "B Blocks A" (swap `--out`/`--in`),
  while `blocks` is unchanged. Proof: unit test on the applier for both relations.
- [ ] `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_link_sync.py` gains a `depends_on` (swap=True) case (currently
  only the `blocks`/swap=False path is tested — the gap that let this ship).
- [ ] After the fix, an inbound pass over an A depends_on B pair applies idempotently (no cycle WARNING).
- [ ] [operator-attested] one-time repair of the already-inverted Jira links (neither diff self-corrects them).
baseline.summary: Outbound Jira link sync inverts depends_on direction (drops swap_endpoints) — backwards Jira links + perpetual cycle-warning noise

# The close gate never names the one remedy that works for a duplicate close

## Context / Problem

`close_precheck` exempts a bug closed as `duplicate` / `not_a_bug` / `escalated` from the billable completion verifier when it names a live replacement: `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:232` calls `_has_live_replacement_link` (`:49-91`), and on True routes to `close_disposition.verdict()` (`:236-238`).

When that predicate returns **False** the branch simply falls through to the ordinary completion path (`:241` onwards) and the LLM verifier synthesizes "Bug <title> is actually resolved", which correctly FAILS — a duplicate's defect is not resolved by the duplicate. But the remediation text then offers only two impossible paths: complete the unfinished work (it belongs to the canonical ticket), or mark the criterion `[operator-attested]` (a false attestation). The single action that works — recording the `duplicates` link — is never mentioned. Observed on bug 9b70: repeated close failures, nearly escalated for a gate change or a `--force`; the actual fix was `rebar link 9b70 6a81 duplicates`.

## Approach

Add a deterministic, pre-LLM hard fail at the existing fallthrough. When the ticket is a `bug` and `close_class == "duplicate"` and `_has_live_replacement_link` returned False, raise `CommandError` naming the missing link and the exact `rebar link <id> <canonical> duplicates` command, instead of falling through.

Three decisions, each taken deliberately:

1. **Scope the hard fail to `duplicate` only**, not all of
   `_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES` (`close_precheck.py:26`). This follows the operator
   decision recorded on this ticket ("APPROVED to hard-fail a `--class duplicate` close").
   It is also the only class with a canonical counterpart: `not_a_bug` asserts there is no
   defect and `escalated` may point outside the tracker, so demanding a `duplicates` link
   from either would be wrong. Those two keep today's fallthrough behaviour exactly.
2. **Require the link's EXISTENCE, not an open target** — the operator's confirmed
   refinement, since closing a duplicate of an already-closed canonical is the common case.
   No code change is needed to honour this: `_is_live_ticket` (`close_precheck.py:29-46`)
   already accepts any resolvable, non-archived, non-deleted ticket and only rejects
   `status in {"archived","deleted"}` — a `closed` canonical already passes. A regression
   test pins that so a future tightening of `_is_live_ticket` cannot silently reintroduce
   an open-target requirement.
3. **Distinguish a dead target from a missing one.** A new helper reads the same reduced
   state and reports whether a `duplicates` dep (or inbound `supersedes` link) was recorded
   at all. Named-but-unresolvable gets "the ticket you named is archived/deleted/unknown —
   re-link to a live canonical"; nothing recorded gets "you named none — run `rebar link
   …`". This is pure reduced-state reading, so it costs no LLM request.

The new helper is added rather than folded into `_has_live_replacement_link` because two existing tests monkeypatch that predicate by name (`tests/unit/test_close_disposition_attestation_738a.py:66,101`); keeping its bool signature intact keeps the disposition attestation (bug 738a) wiring tests meaningful.

The check sits after the `force_close` early return (`:211`) and after the `bug_close_class_ok` guard (`:218`), so `--force` still bypasses it and an invalid `--class` still reports its own error first.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py` — new `_recorded_replacement_target()` helper and
  the hard-fail branch at the `_has_live_replacement_link` fallthrough. File is 394 LOC;
  the change keeps it well under the 800-LOC cap.
- `tests/unit/test_close_precheck_duplicate_link_c8fd.py` — new unit test module for the
  four cases below.

## Testing

- Happy path: `--class duplicate` on a bug whose `duplicates` link targets an **open**
  ticket still routes to the disposition verdict (no error, no LLM call).
- Operator-confirmed path: same, but the target is **closed** — must also proceed, proving
  the gate requires link existence and not target openness.
- Failure path: `--class duplicate` with **no** link raises `CommandError` whose message
  contains the literal `duplicates` link command and the ticket id, and the completion
  verifier (`rebar.llm.verify_completion`) is **never** called.
- Edge path: `--class duplicate` naming an **archived/unresolvable** target produces the
  distinct dead-target message, not the "you named none" one.
- Unaffected path: `--class not_a_bug`, `--class escalated`, and a non-disposition class
  such as `plan_defect` with no link all fall through to the completion path unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `_completion_precheck` raises `CommandError` (returncode 1) for a `bug` closed
      `--class duplicate` with no recorded replacement link, and the message contains
      `rebar link`, the word `duplicates`, and the ticket id.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_close_precheck_duplicate_link_c8fd.py -q`
- [x] The hard fail runs BEFORE any billable LLM call: the test asserts a monkeypatched
      `llm.verify_completion` recorded zero calls on that path.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_close_precheck_duplicate_link_c8fd.py -q -k llm`
- [x] A `duplicates` link whose target is **closed** still takes the disposition path (link
      existence only; target need not be open).
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_close_precheck_duplicate_link_c8fd.py -q -k closed`
- [x] A `duplicates` link naming an archived/unresolvable target yields a message that
      names the dead target and differs from the no-link message.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_close_precheck_duplicate_link_c8fd.py -q -k dead`
- [x] `not_a_bug`, `escalated`, and non-disposition classes are unchanged — no new error on
      the no-link path.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_close_precheck_duplicate_link_c8fd.py -q -k unaffected`
- [x] The existing disposition-attestation suite still passes unchanged.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_close_disposition_attestation_738a.py -q`
- [x] Repository gates pass.
      Verify: `make lint && make typecheck && python -m pytest tests/unit -q -k close`

## Provenance

Found closing 9b70 (itself a duplicate of 6a81). Cross-referenced there.
baseline.summary: Close gate does not tell a duplicate close it needs a replacement link

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
When the store wedges (dirty tracker tree, stale locks, stranded merge state), today's tooling is partial: `rebar fsck` checks event integrity but does not report the dirty-tree class that caused the recent P0 wedges (tracked working-tree deletions of store artifacts, untracked regenerable compaction leftovers, orphaned lock files, orphaned `.tmp-event-*`); `rebar tracker-maintenance --clean` handles only a stranded index and foreign worktree paths (verified: its `_stranded_paths`/`_foreign_worktree_paths` scans reported 0 findings while the store sat wedged with 119 tracked `.archived` deletions); the documented recovery for the live wedges was ad-hoc raw git under the write lock, recorded by hand on tickets 6ccc-0577-198c-44fa / e72e-259d-5ee7-4e73. Operators (and agents) need one sanctioned, non-destructive door: fsck DETECTS the class, doctor --repair HEALS it.

## Approach
Detection: add a tracker-dirty check to the fsck surface (src/rebar/_commands/fsck_tracker_health.py, which already owns tracker-level health lines) that classifies `git status --porcelain` output into: (1) tracked deletions of store artifacts restorable from HEAD, (2) untracked regenerable compaction leftovers (`*-SNAPSHOT.json`, `*.retired` whose retired-source is already folded), (3) orphaned `.tmp-event-*` (never auto-touched — named for manual triage), plus lock-artifact staleness reported via the existing doctor_locks scan. Each class gets a distinct finding line, and the JSON contract is wired end-to-end: fsck's JSON is produced by `_transform_json` in src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py over a fixed `_STRUCTURED_KINDS` set, so the three new tracker-dirty kinds are registered there (each emitting a `KIND: detail` line whose detail carries count + paths) — fsck.py is an explicit edit target, not an implied one. Repair: extend `rebar doctor --repair` (src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py's existing scan/repair_finding registry pattern) with repair actions using TWO lock windows, because the store write lock (rebar._store.lock.write_lock) is non-reentrant — doctor's own `run_repair` deliberately holds NO outer lock (its regression test pins that an outer hold starves inner per-write acquisitions), and `sync.reconverge` acquires the write lock internally. So: (window 1) the raw file-mutating steps — restore class-1 paths via `git checkout --` (non-destructive; bytes exist at HEAD) and move class-2 paths into the quarantine directory established by change 1757 (`<git-common-dir>/reconverge-quarantine/<utc-ts>/` — move, never delete) — run under one short-lived scoped write_lock acquisition, through the store seam (gitutil.run_git), and that lock is RELEASED before convergence; (window 2) the existing reconverge entry (rebar._store.sync.reconverge) is then invoked and takes the write lock itself, converging the previously wedged store in the same command. Class-3 paths are left untouched and printed. Safety envelope: before the first mutating repair, record a backup ref (`refs/rebar-doctor/<utc-ts>` pointing at the tickets HEAD) mirroring the backup-ref + durable-audit envelope `tracker-maintenance` actually provides (tracker-maintenance holds no write lock; its envelope is the backup ref plus audited raw `_git` calls — that, not a lock, is the precedent adopted here), and every action is recorded in the doctor output. Positive rationale: doctor already owns scan-classify-repair with typed findings; extending its registry avoids inventing a second repair CLI.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_commands/fsck_tracker_health.py — tracker-dirty classification (text lines).
- src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py — register the three tracker-dirty kinds in `_STRUCTURED_KINDS` / extend `_transform_json` so fsck --output json carries per-class counts and paths.
- src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py — new finding types + repair actions (scoped write_lock window for file mutations; backup ref; post-release reconverge call).
- tests/unit/test_doctor_dirty_tree.py (new) — seeded-wedge end-to-end coverage.
- docs/user-guide.md — document the new fsck findings and doctor repairs.

## Testing
- Happy path: fixture tracker seeded with all three classes plus a diverged origin; `rebar fsck` names each class; `rebar doctor --repair` restores class 1, quarantines class 2 (bytes preserved), leaves class 3 in place, and the store converges (ahead/behind 0/0, `git status` clean except class 3).
- Failure/edge: doctor --repair on a CLEAN store makes zero changes and zero commits (idempotent); the file-mutating window respects existing lock semantics (a held write lock makes it wait/fail per the lock contract rather than mutate unlocked); class-3 files are byte-identical after the run; the backup ref exists after a mutating repair and is absent after a no-op run.
- Lock discipline: a test asserts the write lock is NOT held when reconverge is entered (mirroring doctor's existing test_run_repair_does_not_hold_a_lock_that_blocks_event_writes pattern), and IS held during the checkout/move steps.
- JSON contract: fsck --output json carries the per-class counts and paths (via the registered kinds).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `rebar fsck` on a seeded dirty tracker reports each class with a distinct finding id in text AND in `--output json` (counts + paths); clean stores report none; checked by the new test.
- [x] `rebar doctor --repair` heals a seeded wedge end-to-end (tree clean apart from `.tmp-event-*`, merge converged, no event bytes lost — quarantine holds moved files, backup ref recorded); checked by the end-to-end test.
- [x] Each file-mutating repair step runs under its own scoped write-lock acquisition, the lock is released before reconverge (which self-locks), and no repair path deletes a file (moves or restores only); checked by lock-state assertions and quarantine contents in the test.
- [x] [operator-attested] `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1) before close.
baseline.summary: fsck detects the dirty-tree/stale-lock wedge class; doctor --repair heals it under the write lock
