## Context / Problem
After S2b/S2c, runtime and factories agree, but users still see hand-maintained package help and the old two-family intercept behavior. Canonical generated artifacts may become authoritative only after the complete parser/route census is proven.

## Approach
Add `scripts/gen_cli_help.py` with write and `--check` modes.

- Enumerate canonical/compatibility/hidden routes from the immutable registry; resolve parser factories only in generation/check execution.
- Render with S2a's fixed `prog`, width, formatter, ordering, UTF-8 LF, and trailing-newline policy.
- Write one artifact per canonical help key; exact aliases reuse canonical bytes. Compatibility/hidden spellings render the same argument-definition helpers with approved alias `prog` and replacement epilog.
- Generate the grouped overview from route group/order/visibility plus parser summaries. Canonical visible commands appear once; aliases are annotated rather than duplicated; hidden routes are omitted.
- Fail `--check` on any missing/stale/stray artifact, unresolved factory, non-deterministic second render, registry/parser census mismatch, or generated package-data diff.
- Keep curated explanations/examples inside parser descriptions/epilogs or later editorial reference sections; no hand-authored usage line or option table may be concatenated after generation.

Cut top-level overview/help/unknown routing to the registry and committed artifacts. The lexical pre-scan handles global config-prefix token shape, command identity, `rebar help <command>`, and a first `--help`/`-h` token after the spelling. It must complete before RP-04 snapshot, config parsing/materialization, mount, handler/factory resolution, or optional imports. Free-text `--help` later in argv remains data/handler input as today.

Approved behavior changes: the 21 formerly intercept-only help forms now succeed safely; overview grouping changes; help output becomes deterministic parser-rendered text. Unknown/help streams and exit codes, historical `jira-onboard`, hidden `bridge-status`, and unknown `purge-bridge` remain as specified.

## Compatibility and Rollback
The existing execution ladder remains active. Commit generator, artifacts, route-help lookup, and subprocess tests together. Reverting this task restores the old help family without changing runtime grammar or stored data.

## Testing
Use generator unit tests and real CLI subprocess tests in a fresh attachable checkout. Sentinels raise if help/unknown paths compose an operation snapshot, read config, mount/create a store, resolve a parser/handler, or import heavy optional modules. Assert exact artifact bytes, streams, exit codes, overview uniqueness/grouping, every alias class, malformed global syntax, free-text negative control, and a normal execution control that still crosses operation/mount boundaries.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `scripts/gen_cli_help.py --check` proves every registered help artifact and overview are deterministic, parser-derived, complete, and free of stale/stray resources.
- [ ] Every visible canonical command appears once in the grouped overview; exact aliases reuse bytes and compatibility/hidden/retired spellings follow the approved rules.
- [ ] Both top-level help forms return exact committed generated bytes before operation/config/store/parser/handler/optional-import boundaries.
- [ ] Free-text later `--help`, malformed global syntax, unknown commands, streams, and exit codes match the explicit compatibility contract.
- [ ] A normal execution negative control still reaches RP-04 operation composition and established mount/init behavior through the old execution ladder.
- [ ] No hand-maintained usage or option table remains in package help.
baseline.summary: RP-05 S2d — Generate and serve canonical help from runtime parser factories

## Client report
`AGENTS.md` and the setup/onboarding documentation do not tell a new contributor to run `rebar identity create --self` before using gates that sign attestations. A correctly installed checkout can therefore reach a signing gate without the local identity prerequisite and fail only at gate time.

The documentation gap is reported by a client project. Investigation must first confirm which supported bootstrap flows create an identity automatically, which gates require one, and whether `identity create --self` is universally correct or conditional on repository policy.

## Plan
- Reproduce onboarding from a clean temporary home/config using the documented setup path and the first signing gate.
- Trace the identity lookup/error path and inventory every authoritative setup surface (`AGENTS.md`, local-dev/setup guides, contributor guide, packaged explanations).
- Confirm the intended prerequisite and placement before editing docs.
- Add a documentation/CLI contract test or rendered-help assertion at the smallest tier that fails when all setup paths omit the prerequisite.
- Update each authoritative onboarding surface without duplicating contradictory guidance.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A clean-environment reproduction identifies the first signing operation that fails and the exact missing identity state.
- [ ] The intended use and scope of `rebar identity create --self` are cited from implementation/help or an approved identity contract.
- [ ] Every authoritative setup/onboarding path either creates the identity or instructs the user when and how to run `rebar identity create --self`.
- [ ] The guidance explains how to verify the identity and distinguishes repository-local versus user-global state as applicable.
- [ ] A gating test detects regression of the prerequisite guidance without asserting incidental prose formatting.
- [ ] Existing install/bootstrap flows that already provision identity remain accurate and are not duplicated or contradicted.
baseline.summary: Setup docs omit rebar identity create --self before signing gates

baseline.description:
## The documented guarantee is false

`docs/user-guide.md` states, as a SECURITY property of the DC backend:

> `JIRA_PAT` is read from the environment and is **not** accepted from a committed config file, so
> the credential cannot be checked into a repo by accident; the transport never logs it, and **a
> missing `JIRA_PAT` fails with an error naming the variable rather than falling back to anonymous
> access.**

The first two clauses hold. The third does not.

## Mechanism, read from the code

* `adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py:76` — `pat=os.environ.get("JIRA_PAT", "")`. Absent variable
  yields the EMPTY STRING. There is no validation anywhere that the PAT is non-empty.
* `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py:95` — `jira_cls(server=settings.url,
  token_auth=settings.pat, options=...)`. The empty string is passed as the bearer token. The client
  constructs successfully, and requests go out with no usable credential, so Jira treats the caller as
  ANONYMOUS.

## Observed live — GitHub Actions run 30652534806, job "jira DC harness smoke"

`test_the_documented_setup_refuses_to_read_the_pat_from_config` removes `JIRA_PAT` from the environment (leaving it only in the config file, which must NOT be honoured) and runs the documented `rebar reconcile --dry-run`. Expected: a failure naming `JIRA_PAT`. Actual:

    ERROR: reconcile_once raised: HTTP Error 400: JiraError HTTP 400
      url: .../rest/api/2/search?jql=project+%3D+RBJUXFD+AND+...
      response text = {"errorMessages":["The value 'RBJUXFD' does not exist for the field 'project'."]}

Jira returns exactly "does not exist for the field 'project'" when the caller lacks Browse permission — it deliberately does not distinguish absent-from-forbidden, to avoid leaking project existence. So an anonymous request against a real project produces precisely this message.

Corroborating evidence from the SAME run: `test_the_documented_config_and_dry_run_work_against_a_real_dc_instance` PASSED against the same harness, same fixture, same scratch-project machinery, with `JIRA_PAT` SET. The only difference between the passing and failing case is the credential.

## Why this matters beyond tidiness

1. **The failure MISATTRIBUTES, in the most expensive possible direction.** An operator who forgets to
   export `JIRA_PAT` is told their PROJECT does not exist. They will go and check project keys,
   permissions and JQL — everything except the credential. This is the same misattribution class that
   cost this epic a debugging session on the PAT-cap bug, where the error surfaced in an untouched
   module.
2. **It is a documented SECURITY guarantee that nothing enforces.** The guide is telling operators
   that rebar fails closed on a missing credential. It fails OPEN, to anonymous.
3. **An anonymous pass can look benign.** On an instance where anonymous CAN browse the project, a
   credential-less run would not error at all — it would read a partial or empty view and report a
   converged pass. That is the "green but broken" shape this epic keeps finding.

## Approach

Validate the PAT at CLIENT-CONSTRUCTION time (`build_client_from_settings`) and fail with an actionable error naming the variable — the behaviour the guide already promises.

**REVISED after CI falsified the first placement.** An earlier draft put the check in `resolve_jira_datacenter_settings` and rejected client-construction on the reasoning that "the invariant belongs where the value is resolved". That reasoning was wrong, and the evidence is concrete: resolution is reached from PROPERTIES (`JiraDataCenterBackend.query_project`), and on Python <= 3.11 `isinstance(x, SomeRuntimeCheckableProtocol)` evaluates properties via `hasattr`. A raise there breaks every Protocol conformance check. Python 3.12+ switched to `inspect.getattr_static`, which does NOT execute properties — so the breakage is INVISIBLE on a modern local interpreter and appears only on the CI matrix's 3.11 leg. Measured: two backend-facade tests (`test_isinstance_backend_facade[jira-datacenter]`, `test_dc_backend_satisfies_the_backend_facade`) passed on 3.14 locally and failed on 3.11 in CI run 30653881576, earning a Verified -1.

Client construction is strictly better anyway: it is the LAST point before the network, it is the one place an anonymous client can come into existence, and it cannot be reached by an attribute probe. Settings resolution therefore stays TOTAL — it must not raise merely because a credential is absent — and a regression test asserts that via `hasattr` on the property, so the guarantee holds regardless of which interpreter runs the suite.

Note `Backend.assert_env_ready` ALREADY makes this check and names JIRA_PAT, but it is only reached from the bootstrap-band path (`_attestation.py:68`), which is why dry-run and ordinary reconcile passes still went anonymous.

The error must name `JIRA_PAT` explicitly and say it is environment-only, because the most likely mistake is putting it in the config file — which is exactly what the guide forbids and what this test simulates.

**Rejected: validating at settings resolution.** It is the more obvious home and was the first attempt; it breaks Protocol conformance checks on Python <= 3.11 for the reason above. Any future move back must first explain how `query_project` stays probe-safe.

**Rejected: allowing an empty PAT for read-only/anonymous instances.** Anonymous access is not a supported deployment for this backend (the guide's least-privilege section mandates a dedicated service account), and the failure mode above shows an anonymous run is indistinguishable from a working one on a permissive instance.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` — reject an
  empty/missing PAT in `build_client_from_settings`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py` — keep resolution TOTAL
  (a comment records why the guard is not here).
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — unit coverage for the new guard.

## Testing

* **unit** — `build_client_from_settings` with an empty / whitespace / blank PAT raises an error whose
  message contains `JIRA_PAT` and names the anonymous-fallback consequence; with a real value it
  builds a client and passes the token through as `token_auth`.
* **unit** — the error is raised BEFORE any client is constructed or any network call is attempted,
  asserted by a client factory that fails the test if it is invoked.
* **unit, the py3.11 regression guard** — `resolve_jira_datacenter_settings` stays TOTAL with
  `JIRA_PAT` unset, asserted the way Python 3.11's Protocol check exercises it
  (`hasattr(backend, "query_project")` must be True and must not raise). Written as a direct `hasattr`
  assertion rather than an `isinstance` so it holds on ANY interpreter — a 3.12+ runner would not
  reproduce the failure through `isinstance` at all, which is precisely how this shipped a Verified -1.
* **live** — `test_the_documented_setup_refuses_to_read_the_pat_from_config`, already written and
  currently FAILING in the harness job, passes. That test is the regression oracle and it was authored
  before this defect was known, so it is not fitted to the fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] with `JIRA_PAT` absent, BUILDING THE DC CLIENT fails with an error whose text contains
      `JIRA_PAT` and names the anonymous-fallback consequence, asserted by unit test
- [ ] a whitespace-only `JIRA_PAT` is rejected the same way, since an accidental empty export is the
      same failure with a different shape
- [ ] the failure happens BEFORE any network call, asserted by a client factory that fails the test
      if it is invoked
- [ ] settings resolution stays TOTAL — it does not raise on a missing credential — asserted the way
      Python 3.11 exercises it (`hasattr` on `query_project`), so `isinstance(backend, Backend)` keeps
      working on the 3.11 CI leg. This is the specific regression that earned a Verified -1
- [ ] a PAT present ONLY in the config file does not satisfy the check — the env-only contract the
      guide promises is preserved
- [ ] the live `test_the_documented_setup_refuses_to_read_the_pat_from_config` passes in the
      `jira DC harness smoke` job, read from the JOB log
- [ ] the guide's wording and the code now agree; no doc change should be needed, so if one IS made
      it must be because the code cannot deliver the promise, and that must be stated explicitly
baseline.summary: Missing JIRA_PAT falls back to ANONYMOUS access instead of failing with a named error

baseline.description:
## Status

**Parked as an idea mid-brainstorm (2026-07-18).** The design is NOT final. We paused at
Decision 2 (freshness). "Open decisions" at the end records exactly where to resume. This
ticket is the durable, self-contained capture of the research, discussion, and decisions so
far, per the user's request to "park this as an idea with full details."

## Purpose

Standardize a **mandatory, compact handoff structure** for interrupted or reassigned agent
work. Rebar already has durable tickets, comments, scratch, git state, and claims; what is
missing is a fixed, small contract that lets a fresh context (the same agent after its window
dies, a different agent, or an orchestrator) **reproduce a known-good baseline and understand
the in-flight state** instead of reconstructing assumptions from scratch.

## Two failure modes it kills

1. Treating partially-completed work as a sound foundation **without validating it**.
2. Spending a new context window **reconstructing assumptions that should have been
   externalized**.

It also gives the orchestrator a structured way to distinguish **ordinary continuation** from
a **plan-invalidating event** (baseline no longer reproduces).

The originally-proposed 10 fields: (1) Known-good commit, (2) Baseline verification command,
(3) Baseline result, (4) Current change objective, (5) Files/contracts changed, (6) Unresolved
observations/hypotheses, (7) Currently failing checks, (8) Next bounded action,
(9) Stop/escalation condition, (10) Rollback point.

---

## Research — existing rebar building blocks (reuse vs off-limits)

Verified against source by three exploration passes. Key file:line anchors preserved so a
resumer can go straight to them.

- **`verify_commands`** event/state + `set_verify_commands`/`get_verify_commands` lib API —
  already stores per-ticket verification commands, synced, first-class. This IS field #2
  (baseline verification command). Shape: `{dd_id?, dd_text?, command}`.
- **`commits`** / `attach_commits` (lib) — commit provenance on a ticket. Home for field #1
  (known-good commit / rollback point).
- **`file_impact`** event/state (`{path, reason}`) + `get/set_file_impact` — home for field #5
  (files/contracts changed). Note: it records *intended impact*; the resumer wants the *delta
  since baseline*.
- **`session_log`** ticket type (`docs/event-schema.md:69-100`) — the existing append-only
  **handoff trail** (narrative history). Gate/lifecycle-exempt; cannot be claimed/transitioned;
  searchable but hidden from `list`; non-blocking links only; never synced to Jira. Content
  lives in COMMENTs. Local git-ignored pointer `.rebar/current_session_log` **auto-rotates per
  session fingerprint** (`REBAR_SESSION_ID → CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID → SESSION_ID`); degrade-safe
  when no fingerprint. This is the *history/trail*; the resumption contract is the *current
  distilled state* — complementary (tiered-memory pattern).
- **`scratch`** (`src/rebar/_commands/scratch.py`) — per-ticket key/value string store, BUT
  **filesystem-only, never synced, no lock, purged on ticket close/delete**, 96 KiB/value.
  **OFF-LIMITS as the substrate** — a resumer on another machine would never see it. The
  handoff MUST live in the synced store (events on the `tickets` branch, auto-committed +
  auto-pushed to `sync.remote`).
- **Comments** — freeform `body` string + fixed metadata (`author`, `timestamp`); non-string
  bodies are JSON-coerced to a string. No first-class structured payload — structure must be
  serialized into the body.
- **Claim** — one-shot `open → in_progress`; stamps only scalar session-provenance keys
  (`claimed_session`, `claim_harness`, `claim_remote_session`). **There is NO pause / release /
  yield / un-claim operation, and no `resumed_by`/`resumed_at`.** Transition *into* `in_progress`
  (from `open`, `blocked`, or reactivating `closed`) is gated identically to claim.
- **Gates** — inline, **opt-in, default-OFF**, funneled through one seam
  (`src/rebar/_commands/gates.py`, keyed `verify.<flag>`, fail-open on unreadable config). Two
  today: the **plan-review claim gate** (on claim + transition-to-in_progress) and the
  **completion-verifier close gate** (on `→ closed`, fail-closed). This seam is the natural
  wiring point if "reproduce baseline before continuing" becomes an enforced gate. NB: default-off
  cuts against calling anything "mandatory by default."
- **Description "templates"** — NOT a stored scaffold; enforced as a **clarity-gate scoring
  heuristic** (`_clarity_score`, `gates.py:110-167`) that rewards per-type `##` headings.
- **Naming collision:** "checkpoint" and "baseline" are already taken — by the plan-review LLM
  engine and the reconciler three-way-merge respectively. Pick a distinct name (e.g.
  "resumption", "handoff").

## Research — prior-art synthesis (what to keep, add, avoid)

**The reproducibility trio (#1 commit, #2 command, #3 result) is the design's genuine
differentiator.** Most human and AI handoff formats only *soft drift-check* and assume the
workspace is intact; re-deriving a verified baseline is the strongest, best-established idea in
the body of prior art and this design has it front-and-center. Backing: git bisect
known-good/known-bad + adjudicating test; CI "last-known-good / green trunk"; TDD RED→GREEN
("one small step from green"); SLSA provenance + in-toto ("verify before trust"); reproducible
-builds ("same source + env + instructions"); "Reflections on Trusting Trust" / diverse
double-compiling (don't trust inherited state; independently reproduce).

**Additions prior art demanded (ranked), and our disposition:**

- **Receiver read-back / re-verification step** (I-PASS "Synthesis"; SBARR/ISBARR read-back;
  aviation challenge-response; ICS face-to-face transfer; SLSA VSA digest-match). The single
  biggest structural pattern: the contract as proposed is **write-only**; every mature protocol
  added a receiver step. The user's spec ALREADY includes this ("the resumer first reproduces
  the baseline") — it is the strongest part, so enforcement should bite HERE. → **Decision 4
  (open).**
- **Decisions / dead-ends layer** (Cognition "Don't Build Multi-Agents": compress history into
  *decisions*; Anthropic context-engineering: preserve architectural decisions;
  `claude-handoff` format calls "Failed Approaches" its "most valuable part"; blameless
  postmortem "who decided X and why"). → **Folded into field #6 (open + closed), with a pointer
  to the comment trail** (my recommendation; standing unless vetoed).
- **Freshness stamp** (SHA + timestamp + branch on the record; SLSA identity; SRE
  "last-updated by jennifer"; docs-rot). Kills the "note written at step 3, read at step 30,
  silently lies" mode. → **APPROVED.**
- **Environment / toolchain fingerprint** (reproducible-builds "same commit ≠ same baseline";
  hermetic builds; MCVE env). → **DROPPED** (project builds not env-sensitive enough to earn a
  usually-noise field).
- **Owner / next-owner / escalation target** (ICS, SRE, PagerDuty, OPORD). Partially covered by
  field #9. → **not yet decided.**
- **Definition-of-done / desired end-state / commander's intent — the "why"** (SRE Exit
  Criteria; Agile DoD; OPORD end-state). The fallback when field #8's next-action turns out
  wrong. → **not yet decided (tie to field #4).**
- **Severity / blast-radius**, **in-flight/pending work** (running CI, spawned sub-agents,
  awaited reviews — field #7 captures failing, not pending). → severity not adopted; pending-work
  noted as a #7 refinement.

**Field refinements prior art suggests (not yet locked):** #3 baseline result should be
*evidence* (exit code / digest), state what "green" covers, and have a **third "unverifiable"**
state (git bisect exit 125), not a boolean. #4 should separate *what* (objective) from *why*
(intent/end-state). #7 should carry expected-vs-actual and a deterministic-vs-flaky qualifier.
#8 should be specific, measurable, idempotent/safe-to-replay. #9 should be plural if-then +
named escalation target.

## Research — failure modes to design around

- **Mandatory write-side template = documented failure.** Ontario mandated the WHO surgical
  checklist: 92–100% compliance, **zero** measurable benefit (NEJM 2014) — pure box-ticking.
  Goodhart's / Campbell's law, normalization-of-deviance, and cargo-cult process all predict a
  "template completed" target becomes a plausible fill, not truth. A 20k-session study found
  agents "prematurely claim success" 27.6% of the time; agents emit "all tests pass" even when
  hidden tests fail. → **Put the mandate on the machine-verifiable resume action (re-run the
  baseline), keep the self-authored fields lean and evidence-bearing, grade *resumption
  success*, not fields-filled.**
- **Handoff is written at the worst moment** — interruption coincides with a full window /
  context rot (least-reliable model) and human-factors omission-under-load. → maintain the
  record continuously; derive machine fields from git/test output, not degraded recall.
- **Staleness / docs-rot** — a note read late actively misleads. → freshness stamp; resumer
  diffs stamp vs reality first.
- **Checklist bloat / "lost in the middle"** — 10 fields is at Gawande's 5–9 ceiling; long
  handoffs are partially ignored (U-shaped attention, arXiv 2307.03172). → killer items only;
  front-load the resume point; cut re-derivable/usually-empty fields.
- **Trusting-trust circularity** — never trust inherited "result: green"; the resumer
  independently re-derives.

**Two structural patterns the research repeatedly points to:** (a) **split by direction** —
*writing* = DO-CONFIRM (short verification pause on killer items); *resuming* = READ-DO (an
ordered recipe of commands the resumer executes to re-establish + confirm the baseline before
continuing). (b) **tier memory** — compact contract PLUS a pointer to the full searchable trace
(session_log / comments).

---

## Decision log (locked so far)

1. **Freshness stamp — ADDED.** Record carries its own commit SHA + timestamp + branch.
2. **Rollback point merged into known-good commit** — one field (CI treats last-known-good as
   both baseline and revert target).
3. **Environment fingerprint — DROPPED.**
4. **Decisions/dead-ends — folded into field #6** (reframe as open + closed items, with a
   pointer to the comment trail), not a new 11th field. *My recommendation; standing unless the
   user vetoes.*

## Current field list (evolving)

1. **Known-good commit** (also the rollback point) — reuse `commits`/`attach_commits`.
2. **Baseline verification command** — reuse `verify_commands`.
3. **Baseline result** — evidence (exit code/digest); three states incl. "unverifiable" *(refine)*.
4. **Current change objective** — possibly split what vs why/end-state *(open)*.
5. **Files/contracts changed** — reuse `file_impact`; foreground delta-since-baseline.
6. **Open + closed items** — unresolved observations/hypotheses AND ruled-out approaches /
   settled decisions, with a pointer to the comment trail *(folded, per Decision 4 above)*.
7. **Currently failing checks** — + expected-vs-actual, deterministic-vs-flaky, pending/in-flight *(refine)*.
8. **Next bounded action** — specific, measurable, idempotent/safe-to-replay *(refine)*.
9. **Stop / escalation condition** — plural if-then + named escalation target *(refine)*.
10. **Freshness stamp** — NEW, approved.

## Open decisions (RESUME HERE)

- **Decision 2 — freshness (PAUSED HERE).** Continuous-at-checkpoints *(my lean: robust to
  ungraceful interruption; stamp makes lag visible)* vs write-at-interruption *(simpler, but the
  interruptions you most need to survive are the ungraceful ones)*.
- **Decision 3 — who fills it in.** Hand-typed vs auto-derive the mechanical fields
  (commit / failing checks / changed files) from git/test output, agent adds only judgment
  fields. (Determines whether "continuous" is realistic or ceremony.)
- **Decision 4 — what the resumer MUST do.** Read only vs must re-run the baseline before it is
  allowed to continue (the receiver read-back the prior art most strongly endorses).
- **Decision 5 — what "go into diagnosis" is.** A real recorded task state the orchestrator can
  see, vs behavioral guidance only.
- **Decision 6 — how mandatory, enforced by what.** Rebar code gate (via the `gates.py` seam)
  vs skill/convention. This also decides whether rebar core changes at all, or it's a protocol
  layered on existing primitives (session_log + verify_commands + a description convention).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Brainstorm resumed and Decisions 2–6 settled before any implementation.
- [ ] Final design records purpose, edge-case behavior, and a high-confidence implementation
      plan for the chosen substrate/enforcement.
- [ ] (When built) implementation tickets authored to pass the plan-review gate.
baseline.summary: Session-resumption contract — standardize a compact handoff for interrupted/reassigned work (DESIGN IN PROGRESS)

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` measures **777 lines** against the hard 800-line module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), which CI enforces with no allowlist. The sibling story that projects two new ticket state fields needs more than the 23 remaining lines.

## Approach

Extract the STATUS-processing cluster into a new `_processors_status.py`: `_fold_plan_review_phase` (`:32-38`), `_fold_claimed_session` (`:187-208`), `_fold_close_class` (`:211-225`) and `process_status` (`:228-328`).

The seam already exists and is closed: `process_status` is the **sole caller** of all three folds, at `:279,281,282` in the fork-winner branch and `:307,308,309` in the normal branch. The one function that might have made the cluster leaky does not — `process_snapshot` sets `plan_review_phase` inline at `:705-710` rather than calling `_fold_plan_review_phase`.

The sibling `_processors_identity.py` (179 lines) is the exact precedent, and its own header states the contract this follows: it imports nothing from `_processors`, so the split stays one-way, and `_processors` re-exports every symbol for back-compat. The re-export block at `_processors.py:15-22` is the pattern to mirror.

The alternative cut — the CREATE/genesis cluster (`process_create` `:40-152` plus `_project_legacy_creation_channel` `:155-184`, 143 lines) — is also valid but strictly weaker: `_project_legacy_creation_channel` has a second caller in `process_snapshot` (`:777`), so the extracted symbol would have to be imported back. The STATUS cluster has no such back-edge.

This is a behaviour-preserving move: no logic is rewritten.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors_status.py` (new) — the moved cluster, ~171 lines
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` — drops to ~632 lines, plus a re-export line

## Testing

No new behaviour, so the oracle is the existing suite passing unchanged. This extraction is the cheapest of the set — the new module's only import is `logging`, and it touches no other module-level name — so the risk concentrates entirely on the re-export:

- Re-export assertion: `from rebar.reducer._processors import process_status` still resolves. The
  complete consumer set is **seven** importers, all of which must stay green with **zero** edits:
  two in production — `src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py` (multi-line import at `:19,32`, used in the
  dispatch table at `:97`) and `src/rebar/reducer/__init__.py` (`:39`, re-exported in `__all__` at
  `:76`) — and five test modules: `tests/unit/test_attestations_reducer.py:13,17`,
  `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:10`, `tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py:20`,
  `tests/unit/test_claimed_session.py:20`, `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_happy.py:6`.
  Two of these use multi-line `from ._processors import (...)` blocks and are invisible to a
  single-line grep for `import process_status`, so the inventory must be derived with a
  multi-line-aware search rather than a one-line pattern.
- Replay equivalence: replaying a fixture ticket through the reducer yields byte-identical state
  before and after the move. This is the assertion that actually proves behaviour preservation for a
  reducer, since a status fold silently dropping would still leave a passing import.
- One-way import: `_processors_status` must not import `_processors`, asserted directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `_processors.py` and `_processors_status.py` are each at or below 650 lines; checked by the
      module-size gate with both counts recorded.
- [x] `process_status` still resolves from `rebar.reducer._processors` and from `rebar.reducer`;
      checked by importing it by both paths and running all five named test modules unedited.
- [x] Replaying a fixture ticket yields byte-identical compiled state before and after; checked by
      comparing the serialized state against a pre-move capture.
- [x] `_processors_status.py` imports nothing from `_processors`; checked by an explicit assertion on
      the module's imports.
- [x] The full existing test suite passes with no test-file edits; checked by the gating test command.
baseline.summary: Size relief: extract the STATUS cluster from reducer/_processors.py into _processors_status.py

## Context

`gerrit-verify.yaml` (the Gerrit `Verified` gate) has a critical path of `clear-vote → require-ticket → build-and-test → vote` with a measured wall clock of ~32–42 min, dominated by the `build-and-test` matrix. Measured evidence (default suite, 5,701 tests, `-m "not integration and not external"`) recorded on ticket crushable-choosable-llama (7654):

- serial + branch-coverage (the EXACT current CI command): 1361s pytest / ~1700s incl. report.
- `pytest -n4 --dist worksteal`: 331s (no cov) / 351s (+cov) → **~5× faster**, with
  **byte-identical outcomes** to serial (5877 pass / 14 skip / same 1 known-Py3.14 fail).
- Coverage overhead is only ~6% at -n4 → KEEP coverage on the gate.
- No pip caching exists in any workflow; the heavy `.[dev]`→`[agents]` stack is rebuilt
  every job. Measured cold vs warm install: 19s → 9s locally (halves install).

This epic delivers three assurance-neutral, proven changes: (#1) parallelize the test run with pytest-xdist, (#2) add pip caching, (#6) bake per-test performance logging into the gate. All three are validated by local experiments (see child tickets); none changes what is tested, the coverage measured, or the matrix breadth.

## Scope (this epic)

- IN: pytest-xdist parallelization of the default tier + non-live integration; pip
  caching on all `setup-python` steps; `--durations` per-test logging + optional
  `.test_durations` store. Applied to `gerrit-verify.yaml` (and `test.yml` for parity).
- OUT (separate follow-up epic): factoring platform-independent gates out of the matrix,
  de-duplicating mypy/ruff, taking require-ticket off the critical path, tiered matrix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All three child stories/tasks are closed.
- [ ] The changes are landed on `main` through Gerrit.
- [ ] `docs/coverage.md` (and any CI docs) updated to note the xdist + `parallel=true`
      coverage-combine requirement.
- [ ] `gerrit-verify` build-and-test test step runs under pytest-xdist pinned to the
- [ ] Reported coverage under xdist equals the serial value (≥ `fail_under = 70`); no
- [ ] Test OUTCOMES under xdist are identical to serial (no new failures, no
- [ ] pip cache hit reduces per-job install time on repeat runs.
- [ ] Every gate run logs its slowest tests (`--durations`).
baseline.summary: Speed up gerrit-verify: xdist test parallelization + pip cache + per-test perf logging

baseline.description:
## Problem
`origin/main` is currently RED on the CI **Module-size gate**: `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` is **803 LOC**, exceeding the absolute 800-LOC hard cap (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`). The gate (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`, step "Module-size gate") runs `find src/rebar -name '*.py' | xargs wc -l` over the WHOLE tree with no allowlist, so this reddens EVERY open Gerrit change with `Verified -1` — no change (1377/e34a, 1379/bdb8, and any future) can reach `Verified +1` until the file is back under the cap.

Evidence:
- `git show origin/main:src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py | wc -l` -> 803 (cap 800; only file over cap on origin/main).
- Change 1377 (story e34a) got `Verified -1` solely on this gate; the file is unmodified by that change.
- The file crossed the cap around commit 339262b990 ("af11: silence unrelated ambiguity in close scan").

## Approach — split along the existing completion-precheck call-graph seam
Extract the self-contained **completion-verification precheck** cluster out of `transition_close.py` into a new sibling module `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close_precheck.py`. These four functions form a closed sub-graph — only `_completion_precheck` is called by `close_ticket`; the other three are private helpers reachable ONLY through it:
- `_completion_precheck` (the pre-close, outside-the-lock verification half; called by `close_ticket`)
- `_has_live_replacement_link` (called only by `_completion_precheck`)
- `_is_live_ticket` (called only by `_has_live_replacement_link`)
- `_referencing_commit_exists` (called only by `_completion_precheck`)

The module-level constant `_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES` (used ONLY by `_has_live_replacement_link`) moves with the cluster. `_PLAN_REVIEW_CLOSE_TYPES`, `_raise_plan_review_close_gate_error`, and `_compact_on_close` STAY in `transition_close.py` (they are called by `close_ticket`, not by the precheck). This is a genuine call-graph seam (not a mechanical trim): the cluster is the "verify" phase of the load-bearing verify->close->sign order documented in the module docstring.

Post-split sizes: `transition_close.py` ~= 480 LOC (in the 200-500 target band); new `transition_close_precheck.py` ~= 340 LOC (in band, > 100-LOC floor). No file left over 800; no file created under 100.

### Binding design — how "behavior unchanged" is GUARANTEED (the load-bearing decision)
`transition_close.py` will `from rebar._commands.transition_close_precheck import _completion_precheck, _referencing_commit_exists` at module top. This BINDS both names as attributes of the `transition_close` module object, so:
1. `close_ticket` keeps calling the bare name `_completion_precheck(...)`. Python resolves that against `transition_close`'s module globals AT CALL TIME (dynamic lookup), so it picks up the imported binding — and, crucially, ALSO picks up any monkeypatch that rebinds `transition_close._completion_precheck` (the patch replaces the module global the function body reads). The interception behavior of the three monkeypatching tests is therefore preserved without any change to how `close_ticket` references the symbol.
2. `transition_close._completion_precheck` and `transition_close._referencing_commit_exists` remain valid module attributes, so tests that call them as `_tc._completion_precheck(...)` / import `_referencing_commit_exists from transition_close` still resolve.
Because `_completion_precheck` is genuinely used by `close_ticket`, its import is not dead (no F401). `_referencing_commit_exists` is NOT used elsewhere in `transition_close.py` after the move; rather than a re-export that ruff would flag as unused, the single test that imports it (`test_transition_close.py`) is repointed to the new module (see below). `_is_live_ticket` / `_has_live_replacement_link` / `_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES` are private to the cluster with ZERO external references (verified via grep, incl. as monkeypatch string targets), so they move cleanly with no rewiring.

### Consumers of the moved symbols (COMPLETE enumeration — grep-verified across all of `src/` and `tests/`, including string/monkeypatch targets)
`_completion_precheck`:
- `close_ticket` (same file, ~line 638) — direct call; satisfied by the module-top import (binding design above).
- Direct module-attribute calls `_tc._completion_precheck(...)` in `tests/unit/test_llm_failure_matrix.py` (2 calls), `tests/unit/test_close_gate_step_budget_message_d59e.py`, `tests/unit/test_close_gate_bound_remedy_db1c.py`, `tests/unit/test_close_gate_bound_message_d59e.py` — satisfied by the import binding (attribute still present on `transition_close`); NO edit needed.
- Monkeypatch `transition_close._completion_precheck` in `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_close_gate_lifecycle.py:59`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_attested_signing.py:302` (spy wrapping `tc._completion_precheck`), `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_idea_close_bypass.py:140` — satisfied by dynamic global lookup in `close_ticket` (binding design); NO edit needed.
- Docstring-only mentions in `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py`, `test_close_gate_subtree.py`, `test_attested_signing.py`, `test_close_ref_target_80af.py`, `test_idea_close_bypass.py` — no code change; NO edit needed.

`_referencing_commit_exists`:
- `tests/unit/test_transition_close.py` imports it (line 24) and calls it directly (no monkeypatch of the transition_close copy) — REPOINT the import + the docstring path (line 4) to `transition_close_precheck`. Import-path-only change; assertions unchanged.

`_is_live_ticket`, `_has_live_replacement_link`, `_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES`: no references anywhere outside the cluster (grep-verified) — move with zero rewiring.

No other `src/` module imports any of the four moved symbols (grep-verified: cross-module imports from `transition_close` are only `close_ticket`, `sign_completion_verdict`, `_verdict_manifest`, `_material_drifted` — none of which move).

## Test strategy (held-out, behavior-preserving)
This is a pure move (no logic change); the guard is the existing suite plus a new seam test:
1. Add a new test `tests/unit/test_transition_close_precheck_seam.py` (held-out; write FIRST, expect RED = ImportError before the module exists): asserts `transition_close_precheck` exposes `_completion_precheck` and `_referencing_commit_exists`; asserts `transition_close._completion_precheck is transition_close_precheck._completion_precheck` (the binding); and asserts that monkeypatching `transition_close._completion_precheck` is observed by `close_ticket` (drive a minimal close and confirm the patched sentinel ran) — locking in the binding contract that makes the move safe.
2. Repoint `tests/unit/test_transition_close.py`'s import of `_referencing_commit_exists` to the new module; its existing assertions must stay green unchanged.
3. Run the full close/completion suites with NO assertion edits and confirm green: `tests/unit/test_llm_failure_matrix.py`, `tests/unit/test_close_gate_step_budget_message_d59e.py`, `tests/unit/test_close_gate_bound_remedy_db1c.py`, `tests/unit/test_close_gate_bound_message_d59e.py`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_close_gate_lifecycle.py`, `test_attested_signing.py`, `test_idea_close_bypass.py`, `test_completion_gate.py`, `test_close_gate_subtree.py`, `tests/unit/test_attestation_signing.py`, `tests/unit/test_llm_disposition_plumbing.py` — proving the monkeypatch/direct-call consumers still work.
4. `make lint` + `make typecheck` clean; module-size contract test (`tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`) green.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` is <= 800 LOC (target 200-500), split ONLY along the completion-precheck call-graph seam above — not a mechanical trim, and no new file < 100 LOC.
- [ ] New module `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close_precheck.py` holds the four precheck functions + `_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES`, within the 100-800 LOC policy band.
- [ ] `transition_close.py` imports `_completion_precheck` (and re-binds it as a module attribute) so both direct module-attribute calls AND `transition_close._completion_precheck` monkeypatches in the existing tests keep steering `close_ticket` — verified by a new seam test.
- [ ] The CI Module-size gate passes (no `src/rebar/**/*.py` over 800), restoring reachable `Verified +1` on Gerrit changes.
- [ ] All listed close/completion tests pass with NO assertion changes (behavior unchanged); only `test_transition_close.py`'s import path is repointed.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean.
baseline.summary: transition_close.py (803 LOC) exceeds 800-LOC module-size cap — main CI red, blocks all Gerrit changes

baseline.description:
## Context
rebar's LOCAL ticket-store write path commits one git object graph per event (~3.3 commits/event on the `tickets` branch). This is the git-issue-style high-bloat pattern; the durable way to bound growth is to create fewer objects at the source — the git-bug `operationPack` pattern (multiple ops serialized -> one commit). Supersedes orphan e3d0 (sleek-bur-train) and folds duplicate 39c5 (grungy-grain-drawl). Discovered from the closed bounded-git-growth epic 97e7, which addressed *reclaim* (stock gc) but left the *growth rate* at write time out of scope.

**SCOPE (corrected — the original text was stale).** This epic is about the LOCAL ticket store write path ONLY (`src/rebar/_store`). The Jira **reconciler** (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`) is OUT OF SCOPE — the original "WS-B3: reconciler batch-apply" line was a mis-scoped artifact and is DROPPED. The reconciler's inbound path is a REFERENCE only (proof the batch pattern is safe in this codebase — same store, same lock, same canonical bytes): `inbound_translate._write_event_file` writes an event file under the write lock WITHOUT committing per-event, and the run commits the accumulated files in a batch. We do NOT modify the reconciler; the new primitive lives in `_store` and is index-based (atomic-rename + `git add` + one `git commit`), mirroring the existing single-event `stage_and_commit`. (We deliberately keep the porcelain add+commit-against- the-shared-index mechanism rather than a detached-GIT_INDEX_FILE plumbing variant, so the batch path reuses `stage_and_commit`'s exact lock/rebase-guard/unmerged-recovery code and stays byte-identical; no second write mechanism to maintain.)

**Why batching is invariant-safe (verified).** Replay, dedup, union-merge convergence, and SNAPSHOT compaction all key off each event's per-event UUID, NOT commit boundaries (`reducer/_replay.py`, `_cache.py`, `_commands/compact.py`). So collapsing N commits into 1 is invisible to readers as long as each event stays its own uuid-named file (invariant I2) and the single locked writer (I5) is preserved.

**Already shipped (do NOT rebuild).** The importer (`src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py`) already has idempotency-by-`source_id` (`_scan_existing_source_ids`) and deferred-push (it sets `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off` and does one final push). What remains is that it still commits one-per-event: its passes call `rebar.create_ticket`/`edit_ticket`/`link`/`comment`, each of which flows `composer.create_core`/`_commands/_seam.py::append_event` -> `event_append.write_and_push` (one lock + one commit per call). Those two seam functions are the real per-event-commit bottleneck, NOT `import_ndjson.py` alone.

## Workstreams
- **B1** — `_store.batch_stage_and_commit(items)` where `items` is a sequence of
  `(ticket_id, event_dict)`. Acquire the write lock ONCE (it is NOT re-entrant, so B1 must
  NOT loop `stage_and_commit`); validate + canonical-stage every event BEFORE the lock;
  then holding the lock, atomic-rename each temp into its I2 path, one `git add`, ONE
  `git commit`. All-or-nothing: any failure (validation, rename, add, non-recoverable
  commit) unstages AND unlinks ALL already-placed paths (not just the failing one) — the
  single-path `_unstage`/`_silent_unlink` helpers are looped over every path. The
  `_recover_from_unmerged` helper is generalized to re-add the FULL list of batch paths on
  retry (re-adding one would drop the other N-1). Add a batched `write_and_push` variant
  (one push after). Single-event path unchanged (the reversibility guarantee: the importer
  can fall back to per-event writes by not calling B1).
- **B2** — adopt B1 on the importer's INDEPENDENT passes (Pass 1 CREATE, Passes 2a–2d
  parents/links/file-impact/comments). Bridge the interface gap explicitly: add a
  compose-ONLY seam (a variant of `create_core`/`append_event` that RETURNS the composed
  `(ticket_id, event_dict)` without committing), buffer the composed events per pass, and
  flush each buffer through `batch_stage_and_commit` in chunks. Chunk size default = 256,
  hard-coded (NO new config key — single consumer, no second call-site). Pass 2e
  (statuses) is STATEFUL (children-before-parents, `cascade=False`) → left per-event.
- **B4** — benchmark + crash-resume. A synthetic N-event import asserts commit count drops
  from ~N to `ceil(N/256)`. A malformed event mid-chunk must trigger whole-chunk rollback
  (no partial commit). A simulated crash mid-batch (kill before commit) must leave either
  the whole batch's commit or none; the next run's `source_id` re-scan skips already-
  committed events and re-emits the rest — proving partial-batch recovery. Named regression
  suites that must stay green: `tests/unit/test_store_batch_write.py`, the replay/dedup/
  union-merge tests under `tests/unit` + `tests/interfaces/store`, and the SNAPSHOT
  compaction tests.
- **(optional stretch)** — cascade transition/claim batching (parent-first cascade emits
  one commit per ancestor; stateful, medium risk). Note only; build only if B1/B2 land
  easily.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_store.batch_stage_and_commit(items)`: one lock acquire, N uuid-named event files (I2), one commit; single-event write path unchanged
- [ ] All-or-nothing rollback: on any failure ALL already-renamed paths are unstaged from the index AND unlinked from the worktree; `_recover_from_unmerged` re-adds the full batch path list on unmerged-recovery retry
- [ ] Batched `write_and_push` variant (one push after the batch commit)
- [ ] Importer adopts B1 via a compose-only seam: independent passes (1, 2a–2d) buffer composed events and flush through B1 in 256-event chunks; Pass 2e (statuses) stays per-event
- [ ] Commit-count reduced to `ceil(events / 256)` on a synthetic many-event import (before/after benchmark asserts a >=10x reduction), exercised via a real import run producing a real tickets branch
- [ ] No regression: `tests/unit/test_store_batch_write.py`, replay/dedup/union-merge convergence, and SNAPSHOT compaction tests green
- [ ] Crash-resume test: partial-batch recovery leaves whole-commit-or-none and the source_id re-scan resumes cleanly; a malformed-event-mid-chunk test proves whole-chunk rollback
- [ ] Docs updated: the `docs/scale-envelope.md` "no batched-commit fast path" assertion is corrected, and an ADR captures the batch-commit decision, the I2/I5 invariants it preserves, and the deliberate reconciler-path exclusion
- [ ] A batch-commit write primitive exists in `_store` and is adopted on the importer's
baseline.summary: Write-time op batching — a batched-commit primitive for the LOCAL ticket store + bulk-path adoption

## Context / Problem

Today the reconciler core reaches into the Jira adapter directly (ADR 0035 §(a)/§(b)
inventory). There is no named interface a second backend could implement. This story introduces
that interface — the `Backend` facade, its role Protocols, and the `RemoteRef` identity type
pinned in ADR 0035 §(d) [rebar:ef33-eaf6-a545-4bfb] — plus a backend-agnostic **contract test
suite** and a thin `JiraBackend` that wraps today's Jira modules with **zero behavior change**.
No core call sites are rewired here (that is S4 [rebar:6673-7636-a116-4f90]); this story only
lands the port and its first implementation.

Edit-set:
- New `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py` — the `Backend` facade, the five role
  Protocols (`TicketTransport`, `OutboundMapper`, `InboundMapper`, `FieldSanitizer`,
  `IdentityConvention`), the three opt-in capability Protocols (`SupportsLinks`,
  `SupportsComments`, `SupportsIncremental`), and the `RemoteRef{vendor, instance, remote_id}`
  dataclass. **Capability-detection mechanism (pinned here):** callers (and the contract suite)
  detect an opt-in capability with `isinstance(backend, SupportsLinks)` /
  `isinstance(backend, SupportsComments)` / `isinstance(backend, SupportsIncremental)` — the
  three capability Protocols are declared `@runtime_checkable`, which is already the reconciler's
  established pattern (`outbound_differ.py:228`, `inbound_differ.py`). There is **no**
  `capabilities()` method. `FakeBackend` (test-only) exercises the guarded path by *inheriting*
  the opt-in Protocol and the skip path by *omitting* it — so "observed via behavior" means
  `isinstance`-guarded dispatch, not structural attribute introspection.
- New `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/backend.py` — `JiraBackend`, a thin
  wrapper delegating to the existing Jira modules (`acli.AcliClient`, `outbound_fields`,
  `inbound_fields`/`inbound_translate`, `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py`, `comment_limits`).
- New `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/identity.py` — the `IdentityConvention`
  pure convention object (see Approach). This is a **new file** (not a delegation shim), so it is
  part of this story's produced file-set and appears in AC4's whitelist below.
- New tests: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_contract.py` (the parameterized contract
  suite), a `FakeBackend`, and characterization tests over the pure Jira mappers.

## Approach

Derive each Protocol's method signatures from the **de-facto surface the core already calls**,
so `JiraBackend` is a pure delegation shim and no logic moves yet:
- `TicketTransport` ← the create/read/update/transition/comment methods on `acli.AcliClient`.
- `OutboundMapper` ← `outbound_fields._map_local_to_jira_fields` (+ `adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit`).
- `InboundMapper` ← the `inbound_fields`/`inbound_translate` payload→local extraction.
- `FieldSanitizer` ← `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py` sanitizers + `comment_limits` size-fit.
- `IdentityConvention` ← the `rebar-id:<local_id>` label read/write convention. Unlike the
  other four Protocols, this one has **no single existing function to delegate to** — the
  convention is currently *inlined* at four core call sites: the write is
  `client.add_label(…, f"rebar-id:{local_id}")` at `dispatch_one.py:320`,
  `binding_store.py:516`, and `apply_inbound_records.py:223`, and the read is the
  `"rebar-id:"`/`"rebar-id-"` prefix scan at `binding_walk.py:341`. So S2 introduces
  `IdentityConvention` as a **new, self-contained pure convention object under
  `adapters/jira/` (new file `adapters/jira/identity.py`)** that formats a `RemoteRef` → the `rebar-id:{remote_id}` label string and
  parses that label back to a `RemoteRef` (the single source of the format those four sites
  currently hand-inline). It is **not** a delegation shim over existing core code, and the four
  core call sites are **not** rewired to it here — routing them through
  `IdentityConvention` is S4 [rebar:6673-7636-a116-4f90]. The S2 contract test exercises the
  convention object directly (stamp a `RemoteRef` → label string; parse label string →
  `RemoteRef`; round-trip), needing no transport and touching no core module.

**Driving the contract suite without a live Jira** uses the pattern already established in the
apply tests: inject a fake transport
(`types.SimpleNamespace(AcliClient=lambda **_: mock_client)`, as in
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_applier_mapping.py:157`). The contract suite is
parameterized over a `backend_factory` fixture and run against both `JiraBackend` (transport =
that injected mock) and an in-memory `FakeBackend` (test-only; lives under `tests/`, never
shipped). The **mapping** contracts assert against the pure mapper functions
(`_map_local_to_jira_fields`, `adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit`, inbound extraction), which need no
transport at all. TDD-held-out: the contract + characterization tests are authored and seen RED
first, then `JiraBackend` is implemented to green.

## Scope

- The `_backend.py` port module (five role Protocols + three capability Protocols + `RemoteRef`).
- `JiraBackend` thin wrapper (delegation only — no field-mapping logic relocated; that is S4).
- The contract suite (driven by an injected mock transport + `FakeBackend`) + characterization
  tests over the pure mappers.
- **Out of scope:** rewiring any core call site or construction site (S4); the registry / config
  selection (S3 [rebar:94f9-a9a0-7475-4e75]); physically moving the vendor modules (S5
  [rebar:dfb9-d2d1-455d-48d9]); any real second backend (epic `be74`).

## Testing

- **Tier:** unit + contract, RED-first (held-out oracle per rebar-implement).
- **Contract suite** (backend-agnostic, run against `JiraBackend` with an injected mock
  transport and against `FakeBackend`): outbound map→inbound unmap round-trips to the same local
  fields the reconciler syncs; the sanitizer enforces label/comment limits and is idempotent;
  `IdentityConvention` stamps and finds a `RemoteRef`; a capability Protocol's methods are
  exercised only when the backend advertises it (observed via behavior — a backend that does not
  implement `SupportsLinks` is never asked to sync links), not via structural introspection.
- **Characterization tests** pin the **exact current** outputs of the pure Jira mappers
  (`_map_local_to_jira_fields`, `adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit`, inbound extraction) for
  representative tickets, proving `JiraBackend` delegation is behavior-preserving.
- **Teeth:** perturb a `JiraBackend` delegation (e.g. drop the priority map) and confirm a
  contract/characterization test goes RED, then restore.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_backend.py` defines `Backend`, the five role Protocols, the three capability Protocols
  (`SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`, `SupportsIncremental`), and `RemoteRef` — importable via
  `from rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler._backend import Backend, RemoteRef` (verified by an
  import test that asserts each name resolves and `RemoteRef(vendor=…, instance=…, remote_id=…)`
  constructs).
- [ ] `JiraBackend` implements `Backend`; the contract suite passes when parameterized over
  **both** `JiraBackend` (injected mock transport) and `FakeBackend` — verified by `make test`
  running the suite twice via the `backend_factory` fixture.
- [ ] Characterization tests assert the pure Jira mapper outputs are byte-for-byte identical to
  pre-story `main` for the representative fixtures — verified by literal expected values captured
  from current behavior (a diff of the captured vs. produced dict is empty).
- [ ] No core differ/apply module is modified by this story — verified by `git diff --name-only`
  touching only `_backend.py`, `adapters/jira/backend.py`, `adapters/jira/identity.py` (the new
  `IdentityConvention` object — or whatever single filename it is given under `adapters/jira/`),
  and files under `tests/`.
- [ ] **Teeth:** perturbing a `JiraBackend` delegation (drop the priority map from the
  `OutboundMapper` delegate) makes a contract/characterization test go **RED**, and restoring it
  returns to green — proving the suite catches a real delegation regression, not a tautology.
  Verified by running the mutated tree (`pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_contract.py`
  fails with a non-zero exit on the perturbation) then confirming exit 0 after restore.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` all green.
baseline.summary: Define Backend role Protocols + RemoteRef + adapter contract suite; adapters/jira thin-wrapper impl

# S2 — Broaden Gerrit replication to change refs (ADR-0010 reversal)

Part of epic 1fa8 (CI as a second Gerrit gate vote via gerrit-to-platform → GitHub Actions).

## Why
The GitHub Actions runner must fetch the exact patchset under test. The g2p production pattern
(ONAP/O-RAN-SC) relies on Gerrit replicating change refs to the GitHub mirror; today
`infra/gerrit/replication.config` mirrors only `refs/heads/main` + `refs/tags/*` (ADR-0010).

## What
Broaden replication with a **scoped** change-ref refspec — deliberately NOT a wildcard `refs/*`,
which would replicate `refs/meta/config` (it embeds the webhook token; ADR-0010/0014 keep it off
GitHub). Record the reversal as an ADR superseding/amending ADR-0010.

## Scope
- `infra/gerrit/replication.config` (add one scoped refspec line).
- New ADR superseding/amending ADR-0010; update the refspec table in `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md`.
- Out of scope: g2p install, credentials, the workflow, the gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Add a scoped `refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*` refspec to `infra/gerrit/replication.config`
      alongside the existing `refs/heads/main` + `refs/tags/*` lines (NOT wildcard `refs/*`).
- [ ] Retain `replicatePermissions = false` and ensure `refs/meta/*` is NOT replicated (protects the
      webhook token per ADR-0014); `checkout-gerrit-change-action`'s `gerrit-url` fallback covers
      replication lag.
- [ ] Confirm the GitHub mirror-lock ruleset still bars all non-replication writes to `main`.
- [ ] Write an ADR superseding/amending **ADR-0010** (replication now includes change refs).
- [ ] Update the refspec table in `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md`.
baseline.summary: S2 — Broaden Gerrit replication to change refs (ADR-0010 reversal)

# Go uv-canonical: matched pydantic-ai-slim + anthropic floors, [tool.uv] extras conflicts, committed uv.lock, and uv-locked install paths

## Problem

The direct Anthropic provider cannot import in uv-provisioned envs: `pydantic_ai.models.anthropic` (in pydantic-ai-slim 1.38.0) does `from anthropic.types.beta.beta_web_search_tool_20250305_param import UserLocation`, which does not exist in anthropic 0.120.2. rebar's default config resolves `claude*` -> `_build_anthropic` -> `AnthropicModel`, so local dev and the plan-review / code-review LLM gates break at import time. The production review-bot is unaffected only because Bedrock does not import that module.

**Root cause (investigated, reproducible from scratch — NOT a stale lock):** uv's universal resolution locks ALL extras jointly. `[eval]` -> inspect-ai -> aioboto3 -> aiobotocore (latest 2.25.1) pins `boto3>=1.40.46,<1.40.62`, while `pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]>=1.107` (pulled by the `[bedrock]` and `[dev]` extras) requires `boto3>=1.42.63`. Disjoint -> uv caps pydantic-ai-slim below 1.107 -> 1.38.0. A bare floor bump to `>=1.107` makes the project UNRESOLVABLE under uv. pip is unaffected (installs one extra set at a time; `[dev]`/`[agents]` never co-resolve with `[eval]`'s boto3 caps), which is why `make install` envs get the healthy 1.107.1 + 0.120.2 pair.

**Verified fix for the resolution:** declare the extras conflict to uv — `[tool.uv] conflicts = [[{extra="eval"},{extra="bedrock"}], [{extra="eval"},{extra="dev"}]]` — plus floor `pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,retries]>=1.107,<2`. Tested against the real pyproject in isolation: resolves cleanly to pydantic-ai-slim 1.107.1 + anthropic 0.120.2. The minimal conflict set keeps `eval`+`agents` co-installable, matching the only real co-install (`.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml` installs `.[agents,eval]`). Nothing installs dev+eval together.

## Decision (operator-approved 2026-08-02)

Adopt the pattern actively maintained OSS projects have converged on (pydantic, pydantic-ai itself, Flask, MCP python-sdk, Ruff, openai-python all commit `uv.lock` and install from it in CI): **go uv-canonical**. A committed lock is only a reproducibility guarantee if the install paths honor it, so this ticket changes both together. Published metadata keeps loose floors (nava-rebar is consumed externally from PyPI — no speculative upper caps, per mainstream practice); the committed lock pins the repo's own envs.

## Scope

1. **`pyproject.toml`**
   - `[agents]`: raise floor to `pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,retries]>=1.107,<2` (floors only —
     drop the previously proposed `<1.108` / `anthropic<0.121` caps; pydantic-ai-slim 1.107's own
     `[anthropic]` extra already floors the SDK correctly, verified: fresh resolve picks 0.120.2).
   - Add `[tool.uv] conflicts` for `eval`⊥`bedrock` and `eval`⊥`dev` (the verified minimal set).
2. **Commit the lock**: remove `uv.lock` from `.gitignore` (rewrite the comment block at
   .gitignore:59-63), generate a fresh `uv.lock`, and verify it locks
   pydantic-ai-slim>=1.107 + a compatible anthropic.
3. **Install paths honor the lock**:
   - `Makefile` `install` -> uv-based locked install (`uv sync --locked` with the dev extra;
     keep the pre-commit hook wiring intact).
   - CI workflows -> `astral-sh/setup-uv` + `uv sync --locked` (respect the existing
     per-workflow extras, e.g. prompt-eval's `[agents,eval]`), plus a `uv lock --check` gate so
     a drifted lock fails CI.
   - `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot` / `.opcert` -> locked uv install of
     `[agents,reviewbot]`.
   - (`Dockerfile.gerrit`'s unrelated pinned tool venv may stay pip.)
4. **`.github/dependabot.yml`**: add the `uv` block (the file's own comment anticipates exactly
   this: "Add a `uv` block only if a uv.lock is ever committed").
5. **Regression guard**: a CI-run import smoke test asserting
   `from pydantic_ai.models.anthropic import AnthropicModel` succeeds in the locked env with the
   agents extra.
6. **Docs**: `docs/local-dev-env.md` (uv becomes canonical, pip the alternative) and any
   bootstrap references in AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING.md that name `pip install -e '.[dev]'`.

Out of scope: provider selection, Bedrock/multi-provider changes, and any change to published dependency metadata beyond the floors above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: `pyproject.toml` `[agents]` floors `pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,retries]>=1.107,<2`
      (no one-minor upper caps anywhere in the change) and declares the `[tool.uv]` conflicts
      (`eval`⊥`bedrock`, `eval`⊥`dev`). No provider-selection changes.
- [ ] AC2: `uv.lock` is committed (removed from `.gitignore`), and a from-scratch
      `uv lock` reproduces it (`uv lock --check` passes); it locks pydantic-ai-slim>=1.107 with a
      compatible anthropic.
- [ ] AC3: `from pydantic_ai.models.anthropic import AnthropicModel` succeeds in a
      lock-synced venv, asserted by a CI-run smoke test.
- [ ] AC4: `make install`, CI test/lint/typecheck workflows, and the reviewbot/opcert images all
      install through the committed lock (`uv sync --locked` or equivalent `--frozen` uv install);
      CI fails when the lock drifts from pyproject.
- [ ] AC5: `.github/dependabot.yml` gains the `uv` block keeping the lock fresh.
- [ ] AC6: `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the full test suite passes in the uv-locked CI.
- [ ] AC7: docs (`docs/local-dev-env.md`, bootstrap references) describe uv as canonical with pip
      as the equivalent alternative.

## Testing / Verification

From a fresh worktree venv provisioned via the new path:
- `uv sync --locked --extra dev && uv lock --check`
- `python -c "from pydantic_ai.models.anthropic import AnthropicModel; print('ok')"`
- `python -c "import anthropic, pydantic_ai; print(anthropic.__version__)"`
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`, targeted reviewbot/container build if feasible locally.

## Risks / Notes

- The `eval`⊥`dev` conflict means `uv sync` cannot co-install those extras; verified no current
  consumer does (prompt-eval uses `[agents,eval]`; Makefile uses `[dev]`).
- The boto3 diamond heals itself when aiobotocore catches up to boto3>=1.42.63 upstream; the
  conflicts block can be revisited then but is harmless to keep.
- This may be large for one Gerrit change; if review friction demands, split along the seams
  (1+2 pyproject/lock, 3+4 install paths, 5+6 guard/docs) — each lands green independently with
  1+2 first.
baseline.summary: Go uv-canonical: matched pydantic-ai-slim + anthropic floors, extras conflicts for uv resolution, committed uv.lock, locked install paths

## Context / Problem
Operator directive (verbatim, 2026-08-13): 'add that alongside our existing portability invariant as an agent guidance rule for this project: keeping rebar portable means it working across environments with diverse CI providers or no CI provider.'

Discovered via the compaction redesign: story A dropped the operation-linked compaction trigger and story B replaced it with a GitHub-Actions-only schedule — silently breaking any adopter with no CI. rebar already has a portability invariant with teeth: the blocking plan-review criterion `project.portability`, activated by `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` and detected by `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md`. Its `Platform and venue` matrix cell reads "macOS, Windows, Linux, BSD, CI, servers, developer workstations" — one undifferentiated `CI` cell. Under it, a plan triggered only by GitHub Actions names a supported cell and draws no finding, because neither "a different CI provider" nor "no CI provider at all" is a nameable alternate shape. That is the gap.

## Approach
One authoritative wording, in the criterion's detection text; everything else points at it.

1. **Extend the criterion's detection text** — `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md`:
   - split the `Platform and venue` matrix cell so both alternate shapes are nameable: "macOS, Windows, Linux, BSD, CI under any provider (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, and others), projects with NO CI provider at all, servers, developer workstations."
   - add one rule under the matrix, in the rubric's cause-and-effect style: a capability whose ONLY trigger is a specific CI system is not portable; a plan scheduling recurring or automatic work must state an operation-linked or in-process fallback, and one that does not is a finding whose alternate shape is "a project with no CI provider" and whose observable breakage is "the capability never runs at all."
   The four-element finding threshold and the Non-findings guard are untouched, so silence about CI stays a non-finding and configured, opt-in CI behavior stays allowed — only a hard dependency fires.
2. **Pin the new detection text** — `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py::test_client_shape_matrix` asserts the `Platform and venue` value as an exact string, so it carries the new value; add a sibling assertion for the no-CI-provider rule so it cannot be silently dropped.
3. **Update the one hand-authored mirror** — `docs/plan-review-gate.md` §"Dogfooding a project portability guard" reproduces the matrix verbatim (line 397), and `tests/unit/test_project_portability_docs.py::test_client_shape_matrix` (line 94) pins that copy as an exact string. The doc mirror must carry the same new cell and the same rule, and that test must be re-pinned, or it fails. The rubric stays the authority; the doc is a mirror, not a second wording.
4. **Surface it where agents read** — `AGENTS.md` gains ONE bullet in the existing "Where to read (one-line pointers into `docs/`)" list, in that section's pointer style: the rule named in a clause, pointing at `docs/plan-review-gate.md` (already the AGENTS.md pointer target for gate protocols) and at `rebar explain project.portability`. `explain` prints the rubric body including the matrix — verified in-session: `rebar explain project.portability | grep -n 'Platform and venue'` returns the matrix line, so the new cell and rule reach that surface. No restatement of the rubric text; AGENTS.md's keep-it-lean rule forbids it.

**Deliberately out of scope, with reasons.**
- `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is generated by `regenerate_criteria_guide`, which calls `load_criteria(repo_root="")` — the built-in registry, overlays excluded — and builds sections from registry `scenario`/`checklist`, not from `.rebar/prompts/*.md`. `project.portability` is an overlay with no section there, so regenerating produces NO diff. Not a deliverable; the generator runs only as a no-diff check.
- `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml` is pinned by `tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py` at exactly 8 cases (`PORT-F1..F4`, `PORT-N1..N4`) with `coverage_threshold: 1.0`; a ninth CI case changes the corpus contract and needs its own live `rebar criteria eval` attestation run.
- `docs/ci-provider-matrix.md` covers the external LLM suite's provider matrix, not CI systems.

## Scope
- `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md` — matrix cell + the no-CI-provider rule (the authoritative wording).
- `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py` — pin the new matrix value and the new rule.
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — the hand-authored matrix mirror + the rule.
- `tests/unit/test_project_portability_docs.py` — re-pin the mirrored matrix value and the rule.
- `AGENTS.md` — one pointer bullet.

## Testing
String-pinning alone would only prove the wording shipped, not that the reviewer acts on it, so detection efficacy is verified live as well.
- **Happy path:** `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py` passes with the new `Platform and venue` value, and the new assertion finds the no-CI-provider rule in the rubric body.
- **Failure path:** the new assertion targets the rule's load-bearing phrase, so deleting the rule fails the test — verified by removing the phrase locally and watching it fail before restoring it.
- **Live detection check (the efficacy test):** create a scratch ticket whose plan schedules recurring work behind a GitHub-Actions-only trigger with no fallback, run `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION=us-east-1 rebar review-plan <scratch>`, and confirm a `project.portability` finding naming the no-CI-provider shape is emitted; re-run against the pre-change rubric to confirm it did NOT fire before. That A/B distinguishes a working rule from present text. Both verdicts are recorded as a comment here and the scratch ticket closed.
- **Mirror parity:** `tests/unit/test_project_portability_docs.py` passes against the updated `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, so the doc mirror cannot drift from the rubric.
- **Unchanged contracts:** `tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py` and `tests/unit/test_project_portability_coaching.py` must pass untouched, proving the eval corpus contract and the `project-portability` coaching move are not disturbed.
- **Generator no-diff:** re-running the criteria-guide generator leaves the tree clean, confirming the overlay-exclusion reasoning above rather than assuming it.
- **Gates:** `make lint`, `make typecheck`, the `check_*` gates (notably `check_criteria_vocabulary.py`, which lints criterion wording), and the CI unit selection.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The rubric names both "CI under any provider" and "projects with NO CI provider at all" in its `Platform and venue` cell, and carries a rule stating that a capability whose only trigger is a specific CI system is not portable and needs an operation-linked or in-process fallback.

# BUG: MCP run_workflow bypasses REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM for v3 branch/loop/map LLM steps

## Reproduction Steps
1. On a write-enabled MCP server with `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` unset, call `run_workflow("plan-review", <ticket>)`.
2. Observe the ALLOW_LLM fence (`mcp_server.py:946`) is skipped and billable single-turn finder calls fire.

Root cause: `has_llm_steps._scan` (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py:285-308`) flattens a v3 branch
step's `{when, then:[...], else:[...]}` dict via `list(values())`, so the bare-array arms become
list items that are skipped by `if not isinstance(s, dict): continue`. Empirically `has_llm_steps`
returns **False** for both `gates/plan-review.yaml` and `gates/completion-verification.yaml` (their
LLM steps live only inside branch arms), while `code-review.yaml` (top-level LLM steps) returns True.

Expected: `has_llm_steps` returns True for any workflow with an LLM step nested in a v3 branch/loop/map arm.
Actual: returns False -> the documented billing/policy gate is bypassed on default-shipped gates.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_scan` descends into bare-array arms (v3 `then`/`else`/`body`) after flattening.
- [ ] Regression test asserts True for a minimal v3 branch-with-LLM-arm AND for the shipped
      `plan-review.yaml` + `completion-verification.yaml` gates.
- [ ] `make lint` + the workflow test suite pass; commit carries a `rebar-ticket:` trailer.
baseline.summary: BUG: run_workflow bypasses REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM for v3 branch/loop/map LLM steps

# WU-3 — Jira reconciler: inbound TAG_DELTA + intent set

Reroute the Jira **inbound** label applier to emit `TAG_DELTA`, removing the last live whole-field `EDIT.tags` writer, and update the user-intent extractor so delta-added tags still drive outbound sync. Depends on WU-1 (event type + reducer). Outbound (`_diff_labels`) is intentionally unchanged — it diffs reduced state and is event-type-agnostic.

## What / Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound.py` (:359-432): replace the
  read-reduce-mutate-write whole-list `EDIT{fields.tags=new_tags,source:inbound}`
  (:426-431) with a `TAG_DELTA` built from the add/remove ops it already computes
  (:404-416). Carry `source="inbound"` at the `data.source` level (matching the
  EDIT today). **Dedup `added∩removed`** before emitting (Jira may surface both in
  one pass; there is no command-layer mutual-exclusion guard on this path — the
  reducer add-wins contract is the hard fallback, but dedup keeps the event
  clean).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/local_label_intent.py`
  (`_extract_tags_from_event` :26-67): handle `TAG_DELTA` — check
  `data.source=="inbound"` FIRST and return `None` if so (same order as the EDIT
  branch :50), else fold ONLY `data.added` into the ever-seen set. Do **NOT** fold
  `data.removed`: `compute_label_intent_set` is an ever-seen UNION (:107); 
  subtracting removals would resurrect the a06c spurious-REMOVE bug.

## Delivery / green state

No live whole-field `EDIT.tags` writer remains anywhere. Jira round-trips through deltas: a user-added (delta) tag is pushed outbound; inbound-applied labels do not count as local user intent. Existing reconciler tests stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Inbound applier emits `TAG_DELTA` (built from computed add/remove ops) with
      `source="inbound"` at `data.source`; `added∩removed` deduped
- [ ] `_extract_tags_from_event` handles `TAG_DELTA`: inbound-source check first
      (returns None), else folds ONLY `added`; `removed` never subtracted
- [ ] Test: a delta-added user tag is pushed outbound to Jira (not suppressed)
- [ ] Test: inbound-sourced `TAG_DELTA` excluded from local user-intent
- [ ] Test: inbound `added∩removed` collision handled (dedup + reducer add-wins)
- [ ] Existing Jira reconciler tests stay green; full suite green
baseline.summary: WU-3 — Jira reconciler: inbound TAG_DELTA + intent set

# Sweep: MCP surface (mcp_server.py) + llm/workflow/ + llm top-level — raise/ToolError, fix masking swallow

The MCP surface adopts the framework-native convention: tool handlers `raise` (the framework converts to an `isError` result); use `ToolError` for intentional client-facing messages. Includes a specific fix: the nested `except Exception: pass` at `mcp_server.py:892` masks the real error WHILE reporting a failure.

## What
- `src/rebar/mcp_server.py`: ensure tool handlers surface errors by raising (map domain errors like
  `ConcurrencyError`/validation to `ToolError` for clean client messages); do NOT catch-and-return error
  dicts as normal results. Keep the server off stdout (no `print`).
- Fix the masking swallow at `src/rebar/mcp_server.py:892` so the error-reporting path cannot hide the
  original failure.
- Bring broad-excepts in `src/rebar/llm/workflow/` and `src/rebar/llm/` (top-level) to the observability
  floor; migrate stderr diagnostics to the named logger.
- Remove these packages from the BLE001/T201 allowlist as they become conformant.

      `print` reaches stdout from the MCP path.
- [ ] `mcp_server.py:892` no longer masks the original error.
- [ ] Broad-excepts in `llm/workflow/` and `llm/` (top-level) meet the observability floor.
