baseline.description:
# Provision AWS-hosted Gerrit + rebar MCP; lock rebar's GitHub `main` to Gerrit

## Context
We are adopting Gerrit as the gatekeeper for all code merged to rebar's `main`, self-hosted on AWS alongside the rebar MCP server, with GitHub as a downstream read-only mirror (the Go-project topology). This epic stands up that environment and locks the rebar GitHub repo so `main` only advances via commits Gerrit replicates after its submit requirements pass. It is the prerequisite that enables dogfooding the agentic code-review capability on rebar itself.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AWS instance (~8 GB; e.g. t4g.large) provisioned; Gerrit + rebar MCP each containerized; Gerrit heap pinned (~2 GB); reverse proxy on 443; Gerrit HTTP 8080 + SSH 29418.
- [ ] Gerrit rebar project configured: `change.submitWholeTopic=true`; custom `LLM-Review` label; submit requirement = the SINGLE deterministic vote `label:LLM-Review=MAX AND -has:unresolved` (the LLM-Review label is voted by the deterministic pass-3 blocker based on thresholds; there is exactly ONE code-review vote, with no separate human Code-Review or CI Verified votes); `copyCondition` carrying the vote across trivial rebases.
- [ ] Gerrit replication plugin pushes `main` -> GitHub (non-force), authenticated by a dedicated single-repo write **deploy key** as the replication identity (see S5). (Supersedes the earlier 'GitHub App / service account' phrasing: a deploy key is the simpler fit for one repo, and is the sole ruleset bypass actor in S6.)
- [ ] GitHub rebar repo locked: ruleset restricts `main` updates to the replication identity only (block force-push + deletions); repo write limited to that identity; no human/admin bypass.
- [ ] rebar MCP server reachable by Gerrit (stream-events/webhook) and can vote `LLM-Review` via REST.
- [ ] End-to-end proof: a test change is reviewed + submitted in Gerrit and appears on GitHub `main`; a direct GitHub push / PR-merge to `main` is rejected.
- [ ] A single AWS instance hosts Gerrit (NoteDb, no external DB) + the rebar MCP server.
- [ ] rebar's GitHub `main` can only be updated by Gerrit's replication identity; all other pushes / PR-merges / force-pushes are rejected.
- [ ] An `LLM-Review` label + submit requirement are wired to the rebar MCP server, and a change flows end-to-end (push to Gerrit -> review -> submit -> replicate to GitHub).


## Decomposition & resolved design questions (2026-06-28 brainstorm + derisk + peer review)
Decomposed into **9 stories**: S1 (TF base), S2 (Gerrit + review-bot receiver + nginx/TLS), S3
(project/label/submit-req/topic), S4a (bot identity + event plumbing), S4b (receiver review/vote
logic + backfill), S5 (replication), S6-pre (mirror-lock pre-work), S6 (apply mirror lock), S7
(e2e + backup/restore + monitoring). The plan-review gaps on the original ACs are resolved as:
- **IaC tooling + remote state:** Terraform with an S3 backend (`use_lockfile`, TF >= 1.10) + a
  one-time state-bucket bootstrap — S1.
- **Secrets management:** AWS SSM Parameter Store SecureString + a least-privilege instance-role
  policy, pulled to a `chmod 600` `.env` at boot — S1/S2 (scoping reinforced in S4a).
- **rebar MCP is stdio-only -> Gerrit can't reach it:** S2 stands up a thin **webhook->review->vote
  RECEIVER** (a plain HTTP service that IMPORTS the review kernel as a library) behind nginx at
  `/review/`; the stdio MCP is NOT exposed over HTTP (Gerrit POSTs webhooks, not MCP — an MCP HTTP
  transport would reject the webhook). S4a wires the bot identity/plugins/inbound auth; S4b the
  review/vote logic.
- **Gerrit event mechanism:** the `webhooks` plugin (push) + the `events-log` plugin with a
  reconciler poller for backfill — S4a/S4b. (Not SSH stream-events.) NOTE: the `webhooks` plugin
  has NO native HMAC, so inbound auth is a secret-token URL + network ACL (S4a), not a signature.
- **NoteDb persistence + backup:** NoteDb on a dedicated gp3 EBS volume at `/var/gerrit` with
  `prevent_destroy` + DLM daily snapshots (S1) and a non-destructive restore drill (S7); merged
  code is always safe on the GitHub mirror.
- **gate verdict -> `LLM-Review` integer mapping:** the gate's `finalize_verdict` emits
  `PASS`/`BLOCK`/`INDETERMINATE`; the voter maps `PASS`=+MAX, `BLOCK`/`INDETERMINATE`=-1
  (fail-closed), config-driven — S4b.

**AC4 refinement:** the lockdown is a REPO-LEVEL ruleset (navapbc is a `free` org; admin-proof
org-level rulesets need a paid plan). So "no human/admin bypass" means no direct/accidental
pushes + force-push/deletion blocked (proven empirically: an active deploy-key-only ruleset
rejects an admin push); TRUSTED repo admins can deliberately edit/disable the rule — an
explicitly accepted PoC risk. The existing `main-protection` ruleset (PR + status-checks) is
replaced by the mirror lock (S6).

**Peer-review corrections (folded into the children):** (a) S6 uses `terraform-provider-github`
>= 6.8.0's NATIVE DeployKey bypass (the prior `null_resource`/`gh api`/two-phase dance is
dropped); `actor_id:null` is canonical (empirically confirmed). (b) S4 split into S4a/S4b and
reframed to a webhook receiver (not MCP-over-HTTP); inbound auth via secret-URL + ACL (the
plugin has no HMAC); async ACK + idempotency vs `webhooks` retries. (c) S3 copyCondition is
`changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE` only (dropping `TRIVIAL_REBASE`, which would certify a moved-base
tree). (d) S5 adds a `projects=` single-repo binding (a functional bug otherwise) + a crash-safe
`replication.eventsDirectory`.

## Plan-review remediation notes (recalibrated gate)
- **Rollback / availability (T4):** replacing `main-protection` is reversible — S6 documents a <15-min rollback (ruleset `enforcement=disabled`, restore `main-protection` from the S6-pre snapshot, re-enable PRs/Issues/Actions). Outage posture is the locked **freeze-and-restore** (no break-glass v1): if Gerrit/the receiver/LLM is down, `main` freezes until restored; merged code is always safe on the GitHub mirror.
- **Architecture decisions captured (T5e):** recorded as ADRs in the children — 0007-review-bot-receiver + 0008-secrets-source-ssm (S2), 0009-review-bot-pipe (S4b), 0010-gerrit-github-replication (S5), 0011-github-mirror-lock (S6-pre), 0012-iac-foundations (S1). CLAUDE.md is updated when d251 lands.
- **Integration de-risked up-front, not only at S7 (G5):** the two riskiest seams were validated empirically before build (session_log vivid-mull-need): (a) an active repo-level ruleset with deploy-key-only bypass REJECTS a non-bypass admin push (proven on the real repo, GH013); (b) the DeployKey bypass `actor_id:null` is accepted + canonical; (c) Gerrit 3.14.1 boots on arm64 and the submit-requirement predicate + nginx %2F config validate. S7 remains the full e2e proof, but the high-risk mechanisms are already de-risked.
- **What S4b's "proven pipe" actually reviews (G6 seam):** the d251 receiver casts the `LLM-Review` vote by invoking the EXISTING `rebar.llm.review_code(...)` (single-pass, ships today) — clean->label MAX, issues/error->-1 fail-closed — proving the webhook->review->vote->submit->replicate plumbing. The REAL four-pass code-review gate (criteria/prompts/context via `gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict`) is **b744-WS6**, which swaps into the same seam for the dogfood. d251 proves the pipe; b744 supplies the review depth. (Note: this is CODE review — verdict PASS|BLOCK — not the plan-review gate's `finalize_verdict`.)

## Round-7 remediation
- **Proven-pipe decision rule (G6):** `rebar.llm.review_code()` returns a `review_result` (a `findings` list), NOT a verdict string. The receiver derives a binary decision: **BLOCK if any finding is at/above a configured blocking severity (default critical/high), else PASS** -> PASS->label MAX, BLOCK or error/no-result->-1 (fail-closed); the threshold is config-driven. b744-WS6 will ADD a code-review verdict producer to `gate_dispatch` (planned — e.g. `produce_code_review_verdict` returning a typed `code_review_verdict {verdict: PASS|BLOCK, ...}`); it does NOT exist yet (today `gate_dispatch` exports only `produce_plan_review_verdict` / `produce_completion_verdict`), so until b744 lands the pipe uses `review_code`'s findings + the decision rule above.

## Round-9 remediation
- **Formal d251->b744 seam contract (T5e):** the receiver depends on a stable ADAPTER interface — `code_review_decision(diff_text) -> {decision: PASS|BLOCK}` (name TBD) — NOT on `review_code`/`produce_*` directly. d251 implements the adapter over `review_code()`'s findings (the severity-threshold rule); b744-WS6 reimplements the SAME adapter over its four-pass verdict producer. The swap is drop-in with no receiver change. That interface IS the formal seam.


## Round-11 remediation (2026-06-29 — derisk experiment + coherence)
Derisk evidence: session_log a7e2-381c-6dc6-4d0c (EXPERIMENT 2 — live REST contract against gerrit-review.googlesource.com).

- **Adapter seam reconciled (supersedes Round-9's `diff_text`-only contract — G4 critical):** the
  formal seam is `code_review_decision(diff_text: str, repo_root: Path, ref: str) -> {decision: PASS|BLOCK}`
  (concrete name, module `src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py` — no longer "TBD"). The adapter passes **`source="local"`** to `review_code()` — the receiver has already cloned the Gerrit change ref into `repo_root`, so `review_code` must read that checkout directly; `attested` mode is WRONG here (it would `git fetch origin` against Gerrit and try to resolve the change ref as an origin branch). The third/fourth
  args are REQUIRED because `review_code()` needs a repo context (`resolve_gate_handle`), which
  `diff_text` alone cannot supply — this is exactly S4b's Round-10 reality, so Round-9 and
  Round-10 are now consistent. **Error/fallback rule co-located with the schema:** any
  error / no-result / unparseable verdict → `decision: BLOCK` (fail-closed → `-1`). The adapter return is `{decision: PASS|BLOCK, message: str, findings: [...]}` — NOT decision-only — so the receiver assembles the Gerrit vote COMMENT uniformly from `message`/`findings`; d251 fills them from `review_code()`'s findings, b744-WS6 from `produce_code_review_verdict`, preserving 'no receiver change' for the comment dimension too. d251-S4b
  (918c) implements the adapter over `review_code()`'s findings + the severity-threshold rule;
  b744-WS6 (4119) reimplements the SAME signature over `produce_code_review_verdict` — drop-in,
  no receiver change. A covering AC for the adapter is added to S4b.
- **Webhook carries NO diff (T3 critical — PROVEN):** the `webhooks`-plugin payload (and the
  change-metadata JSON) carry no diff/patch field; the receiver fetches it via a separate
  authenticated REST call `GET /a/changes/{id}/revisions/{rev}/patch` which returns a
  **base64-encoded** git format-patch (must be base64-decoded), or the JSON
  `/files/{f}/diff` (XSSI-guarded). S4b's Round-9 AC ("fetch diff via Gerrit REST as
  `diff_text=`") is clarified to require the base64 decode. The `events-log` REST backfill
  query (`GET /a/plugins/events-log/events`) was not in the named E1–E5 derisk set but IS an
  S4a AC — flagged for an explicit smoke-check there before S4b's reconciler depends on it. The reconciler is RESUMABLE+IDEMPOTENT via a persisted cursor (last-processed events-log event id) + the per-(change,revision) vote-existence check, so webhook and backfill converge to one vote; FALLBACK if events-log is absent/errors/malformed: log + trip the voter alarm + rely on webhook (degraded), NEVER mark a missed change submittable-but-unreviewed (fail-safe).
- **Outbound READ credential provisioned (G3/G4 critical):** the bot's Gerrit HTTP token
  (S4a, SSM `/rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token`) is the SAME credential used for both the REST
  `/a/` calls (diff fetch + vote) AND git-over-HTTPS clone of the change ref into `repo_root`.
  S1 scaffolds the param; S4a generates+stores it; documented that its scope covers both. No
  separate SSH deploy key is needed for the receiver's read path — and a per-`(change_id, revision)` SINGLE-FLIGHT lock guards the review+vote critical section so a webhook retry or backfill firing mid-review cannot spawn a second review or cast a conflicting vote against Gerrit's last-write-wins Set Review (receipt-time dedup alone is insufficient; detail on S4b) (the replication deploy key
  in S5 is write-only to GitHub, a different identity).
- **SSM scaffolding completeness (G3 major):** S1's SSM SecureString scaffolding adds
  `/rebar/prod/alert-endpoint` (consumed by S7 `monitoring.tf`) and `/rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token`
  (consumed by S4a) to the enumerated set, so no downstream `data.aws_ssm_parameter` lookup
  fails on a missing param.
- **IAM-role ownership contract (G4 major):** S1 CREATES the single EC2 instance role; S2 and
  S4a ADD separately-named scoped inline policies (`aws_iam_role_policy` attachments) — they
  never re-declare the role. Documented so two applies can't clobber each other's grants.
- **`gerrit.config` ownership contract (G4 major):** S2 owns the base `gerrit.config`; S3
  patches ONLY the `[change]` section via documented read-modify-write (not a full-file
  overwrite), mirroring S4a's `refs/meta/config` RMW. No story rewrites the whole file.
- **DLM lifecycle-policy ownership (G4 major):** S1 OWNS the DLM service role + the
  `aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy` (retain count=7); S7 only ASSERTS/monitors it (no second DLM
  resource) — resolves the S1/S7 double-management risk.
- **Replication-plugin BSL scope (T1 critical):** the claim that GerritForge's 2025-09-30 BSL
  re-license touches only pull-replication/multi-site (not the core Apache-2.0 `replication`

## Why
The contract HOME and the safe authoring substrate. Front-matter carries each prompt's contract; the writer must round-trip without corruption (item-4 requirement), validated by spike E1.

## What
- Define the CLOSED front-matter key set (Prompty spellings): `schema_version, title, description,
  inputs, outputs, execution_mode, category, model, tags, dimension, applies_to, langfuse_prompt,
  default`. Heavy JSON Schemas referenced BY NAME (not inlined). `inputs`/`outputs` are the prompt's
  contract surface (see the epic Terminology note).
- Build the parse-split-rejoin canonical writer over PyYAML in `src/rebar/llm/prompts.py` (extend
  `parse_front_matter`; add `write_front_matter`): split on `---`, canonical key order, unknown-key
  WARN+PRESERVE (appended deterministically), LF + single trailing newline, no BOM, body byte-for-byte,
  idempotent (`wb(wb(x))==wb(x)`). Stamp `schema_version`.
- READ-SIDE version coexistence: when a file's `schema_version` is HIGHER than the running binary
  understands, the reader emits a clear WARNING and skips/refuses THAT prompt gracefully (never renders
  unknown front-matter into the body) — mixed-fleet safety, upgrade-reconcile-hosts-first (like TAG_DELTA).
- Ship `.gitattributes` pinning prompt/index files to `eol=lf`.

## Scope
In: format + reader/writer + version-coexistence + golden tests. Out: migrating the reviewers (S3), resolver (S3).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Canonical writer is idempotent, preserves the body byte-for-byte (incl. no-trailing-NL / CRLF / body-starting-with---), warns+preserves unknown keys, rejects BOM.
- [ ] Golden round-trip tests over fixtures including the three boundary corruptors (port spike E1).
- [ ] A file with a higher `schema_version` than the binary triggers a graceful warn+skip (read-side), tested.
- [ ] `.gitattributes` pins the prompt/index file globs to `eol=lf`.
- [ ] WRITE-side version policy: a writer bumps `schema_version` ONLY when it emits a key the prior version lacked; the documented deploy order is readers-before-writers (the read-side refuse is the safety net, not the primary gate).
baseline.summary: Prompt front-matter format + canonical writer (parse-split-rejoin over PyYAML)

baseline.description:
## Defect

`rebar review-plan` crashes on the attestation-persistence path with:

```
TypeError: _with_index_lock_retry() got an unexpected keyword argument 'force_reclaim'
```

(observed exit code 11) when two or more `review-plan` runs race the ticket-index lock concurrently — e.g. several plan reviews launched in parallel. The signing/persist step calls `_with_index_lock_retry(..., force_reclaim=...)` but the retry helper does not accept that keyword, so the attestation write aborts.

## Impact

- The review body completes and `signature.signed` may be reported `true` on stdout, but the
  attestation is **not persisted** to the store — `rebar audit show <id>` shows no signature.
  So stdout `signed=true` is not a reliable indicator of a durable signature under contention.
- Forces plan-review gating to be run strictly serially to avoid the crash; parallel review of
  an epic + its children (the natural batch operation) is unsafe.

## Repro (observed)

1. Launch >=2 `rebar review-plan <id>` runs concurrently against tickets sharing the index lock.
2. One or more crash with the `force_reclaim` TypeError (EXIT=11) on the persist step.

## Suggested fix direction

Reconcile the caller/callee signatures on the index-lock retry path (`_with_index_lock_retry` and the attestation-persist caller in the workflow/orchestrator layer): either add/accept the `force_reclaim` parameter on `_with_index_lock_retry` or stop passing it. Add a regression test that persists an attestation while the index lock is contended.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Concurrent `review-plan` runs contending the index lock persist their attestations
  without raising `TypeError: ... force_reclaim`.
- [ ] `rebar audit show <id>` reflects the persisted signature after a contended review.
- [ ] A regression test exercises the contended-persist path.
baseline.summary: review-plan attestation-persist crashes: _with_index_lock_retry() unexpected kwarg force_reclaim under lock contention

# The project's authoritative config never got the Bedrock switch — only a per-developer opt-in was shipped

## Context / Problem

Epic 061c was tracked as having THREE permanent production switches: the repo config / local env, the AWS review bot, and the CI external suite. The review bot is now cut over [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a] and CI selects a provider through `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE`. **The repo config half was never done**, so every local gate run on this project still resolves to direct Anthropic.

MEASURED, in a clean worktree at `gerrit/main` with no `REBAR_LLM_*` env set:

    merged [llm] file table keys: (EMPTY)
    model_classes present: False
      frontier -> anthropic:claude-opus-4-8
      standard -> anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6
      trivial  -> anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5

`rebar.toml` IS this project's authoritative config — `src/rebar/config.py` discovers `rebar.toml` then `pyproject.toml`, and `read_reserved_section("llm", root)` reads a top-level `[llm]` table from it. But `rebar.toml`'s only sections are `[verify]`, `[ticket]`, `[mcp]`, `[jira]` and `[identity]`. There is no `[llm]` table, so the built-in class defaults apply and those are unqualified names that infer provider `anthropic`.

**What WAS shipped, and why the tracking drifted.** [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7] closed legitimately against its own criteria: its Scope allowed "local LLM configuration only (the config file AND/OR documented env for a developer machine)" and it chose the documented-env route — `docs/local-dev-env.md:142-182` tells a developer to `export REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE="/Users/joeoakhart/rebar-wt-provider-seam/.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml"`, explicitly labelled "opt in", with a documented revert. So 1aa2 is not a false close; the epic-level summary that read it as "repo config / local env — DONE" is what overstated it. Nobody has to opt in, and by default nobody does.

**Why it matters rather than being cosmetic.** The epic's founding premise is that the path rebar develops against is not the path rebar's users run, and that dogfooding closes the gap. A per-developer opt-in that defaults OFF leaves that gap open for the local gates — which are the gates a developer and every coding agent hit constantly. Observed while working eb6e: a local `rebar review-plan` ran on `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6` minutes after the production bot was verified on Bedrock.

## Scope

- `rebar.toml` — add an `[llm.model_classes]` table (the file is the project's authoritative config).
- `docs/local-dev-env.md` — the opt-in section becomes an OPT-OUT section, since the default inverts.
- possibly a pinning test, so the ids cannot drift from `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml` (the same
  two-sided pin `tests/unit/test_reviewbot_bedrock_cutover.py` applies to the compose block).

## Approach — and the decision this ticket actually needs

The mechanical change is small; the DECISION is not, and should be made explicitly rather than by committing a default:

* **Precedence makes it safe to try.** `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` OUTRANKS the project file, and env
  class slots outrank both, so CI arms that name a provider overlay (the external matrix, prompt-eval)
  are unaffected by a project default. The offline unit lanes make no LLM calls at all.
* **The cost is that every local gate then needs working AWS credentials.** A contributor without
  Bedrock access, or offline, would find their local gates failing where they used to work with an
  Anthropic key. That is a real onboarding regression and is the reason this is a decision, not a
  chore. Mitigation is a documented one-line opt-out (`REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE=…/anthropic.toml`),
  which is the mirror of what is documented today.
* Alternative considered: leave the default as Anthropic and instead make the opt-in loud (a
  `make` target, or a doctor warning). Cheaper, keeps onboarding intact, but does not close the
  dogfooding gap — it only advertises it.

Do NOT set `[llm] model` as a scalar; use `[llm.model_classes]`, or the per-pass frontier/standard split collapses (the same trap [rebar:eb58-e71d-ec90-4b00] deprecated `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` for).

## Testing

- assert that in a clean checkout with no `REBAR_LLM_*` env and no `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE`, the three
  classes resolve to `bedrock:` ids — i.e. the exact measurement above, inverted. Verify RED by
  removing the table.
- assert the ids are byte-equal to `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml`, two-sided, so editing either
  file alone fails.
- assert the documented OPT-OUT works: with `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` pointed at the anthropic overlay,
  resolution returns to `anthropic:` — otherwise the escape hatch is unproven.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] the decision is recorded (project default Bedrock vs loud opt-in), with the onboarding cost
      stated, so it is a choice rather than a drift.
- [x] if the default flips: `rebar.toml` carries an `[llm.model_classes]` table whose three ids are
      byte-equal to `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml`, pinned two-sided by a test.
- [x] a clean checkout with no LLM env resolves all three classes to `bedrock:` ids — recorded as
      observed output, since the current state was only discovered by measuring rather than reading.
- [x] `docs/local-dev-env.md` documents the OPT-OUT (and no longer presents Bedrock as opt-in), and
      the opt-out is exercised once.
- [x] the epic-level claim that the 'repo config / local env' switch is complete is corrected wherever
      it appears, so the next reader is not misled the way this was discovered.
baseline.summary: Local dev still defaults to Anthropic: rebar.toml has no [llm] table, so the repo-config half of the Bedrock switch was never done

# Land the completion-verifier runaway diagnostic artifacts on main

## Context / Problem
This ticket's own findings — and its ACCEPTANCE clause — cite `docs/experiments/diag-runaway-transcript.md`, `docs/experiments/diag_runaway_transcript.py` and `docs/experiments/diag_runaway_matrix.py` as the durable record of the measurement. Those three files were committed in `556708771e` on the branch `impl-10ae-verifier-ctx`, which is NOT an ancestor of `origin/main`. So on main the cited paths do not exist and a reviewer checking this ticket's evidence concludes the measurement was never produced. The ticket is currently unverifiable against main through no fault of the measurement itself.

## Approach
Land the three artifacts on main, unchanged, as their own change — nothing else from `556708771e` (that commit also carries the 2948 implementation: `completion_banking.py`, the scaled step floor, the read memo, schema and test changes, all of which belong to 2948's own review, not here).

Landing rather than de-citing is the right call on the evidence:
- `docs/experiments/` on main already holds exactly this artifact shape — paired live-diagnostic
  driver + findings write-up (`ed6d_live_recovery.py` + `ed6d-live-recovery.md`,
  `f6fc_live_memo_nudge.py` + `f6fc-live-memo-nudge.md`). These match that established
  convention.

  floors / trial count, and they depend only on surfaces that still exist on main —
  `rebar.llm.pai_tools.{filesystem_tools,grounding_tools,rebar_tools}` and
  `rebar.llm.completion._VERIFY_MIN_STEPS` (`completion.py:84`). The budget-anchoring matrix is
  re-runnable against any future change to the verifier's step floor.
- They are content-free by construction: raw transcripts are written outside the repo and are

`docs/` is outside the `ruff check src tests` / `ruff format --check src tests` lint gate, so the scripts land byte-identical to the reviewed originals (as the existing experiment scripts in that directory already do — they carry `print()` calls for the same reason). `docs/experiments/README.md` indexes only the remediation-plan EXP1..EXP-R11 series and does not list the later live-diagnostic artifacts, so it needs no edit.

## Scope
- `docs/experiments/diag-runaway-transcript.md` (new, from `556708771e`)
- `docs/experiments/diag_runaway_transcript.py` (new, from `556708771e`)
- `docs/experiments/diag_runaway_matrix.py` (new, from `556708771e`)

No source, test, or configuration file changes. Nothing else from `556708771e` is included.

No new testable behaviour: this change adds documentation and opt-in, local-only diagnostic drivers that are never imported by the package or executed by CI. The relevant check is that the added files do not perturb the existing gates, which the acceptance criteria below verify directly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] All three cited paths exist on the change's tree — verified by
      `test -f docs/experiments/diag-runaway-transcript.md -a -f docs/experiments/diag_runaway_transcript.py -a -f docs/experiments/diag_runaway_matrix.py`
      exiting 0.
- [x] [operator-attested] The added files are byte-identical to their `556708771e`
      originals. Git history is not reachable from the verifier's read-only tools, so the
      blob hashes are recorded in a ticket comment. Locally verified by
      `git diff --quiet 556708771e HEAD -- docs/experiments/diag-runaway-transcript.md docs/experiments/diag_runaway_transcript.py docs/experiments/diag_runaway_matrix.py`
      exiting 0.
- [x] The change adds ONLY those three files — verified by
      `test "$(git diff --name-only origin/main HEAD | grep -vc '^docs/experiments/diag')" -eq 0`.
- [x] Both scripts resolve their imports against main — verified by
      `python -c "import ast,sys; [ast.parse(open(p).read()) for p in ('docs/experiments/diag_runaway_transcript.py','docs/experiments/diag_runaway_matrix.py')]"`
      exiting 0 and by `grep -q '_VERIFY_MIN_STEPS' src/rebar/llm/completion.py`.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` still pass on the change's tree.
- [x] The ticket's own findings comments and this description cite only paths that exist on
      main once the change merges — verified by re-reading the ticket after the merge.

## Reproduction Steps

Discovered while validating epic ce0e (xdist parallelization). The live-Jira reconciler E2E `test_delete_permission_probe` flakes on Jira's search-index eventual consistency when the *whole* live group runs (it self-skips in CI, so this only bites a local live run with creds).

- `pytest tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py` (all 12, SERIAL, no xdist)
  → `test_delete_permission_probe` FAILS: `AssertionError: created issue REB-NNNN
  never became index-visible` (observed REB-1105 and REB-1107 on two runs).
- `pytest "…::test_delete_permission_probe"` in ISOLATION (serial) → PASSES.

So the failure is load/timing dependent (many live tests hammering the shared test project's index in one run outrun the test's index-visibility poll timeout), NOT caused by xdist — it reproduces with `-n0`. Independent of epic ce0e's change.

## Expected vs Actual

- Expected: the index-visibility wait polls long enough (or backs off) to absorb
  Jira's eventual-consistency lag even when the full live group has just created
  many issues.
- Actual: the fixed poll budget in the visibility helper (`test_reconcile_live_e2e.py:347`)
  times out under group load and the test fails.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The index-visibility wait in `tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py`
  is made robust to group-load lag (e.g. longer/adaptive backoff, or a
  create→visible retry helper) so the full live group passes reliably.
- [ ] `pytest tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py` (all 12, serial) passes
  repeatedly against the live test project (no `never became index-visible`).
- [ ] No change to CI behavior (these tests still self-skip without live creds).

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Multiple production bugs (3435, 3a33, 4dd2, 4c6c class) came from store write paths that bypassed the canonical write seams with raw 'git add/commit/rm' — including inside GitHub workflow YAML (the real reconcile-bridge.yml bypass was `cd .tickets-tracker` + bare `git add -A` + `git commit`, .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml ~:285-291: the git line itself carries no tracker token; only the preceding cd targets it). The routing campaign fixed known sites; nothing prevents new bypasses. The REAL write surface has two sanctioned seams, not one: (1) the store seam — locked write transactions and event appends whose INTERNALS legitimately issue raw git (src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py run_git/run_git_write themselves, _store/event_append.py's own _run_git add/commit, _commands/txn.py's inline add/commit/reset critical section — the relocated ticket_txn; the old _engine/ticket_txn.py is deleted, so ticket_txn must NOT be named as an entry point —, _commands/purge_bridge.py's locked add -A + commit ~:154, and migration/bootstrap paths); and (2) the reconciler seam — _engine/rebar_reconciler/git_adapter.py (own add/commit/update-ref against TICKETS_REF) and _ref_lock.py (update-ref CAS acquire/release). NOTE: run_git_write is NOT the lock (it only self-heals index.lock/HEAD-parse faults); the unified store lock lives in the transaction/append layers above it, so the teaching message must direct authors to the store WRITE APIs, not bare run_git_write.

## Approach
Two-layer deterministic CI lint, each layer matched to what is statically decidable, with sanction via an INLINE MARKER carrying a mandatory reason — no external allowlist file. Marker: `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` (and `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` comment lines in YAML/shell). A new marker name rather than overloading the existing `# tickets-boundary-ok` convention, because the semantics differ (boundary-crossing READ/layout sanction vs raw WRITE sanction) — the plan states this reconciliation explicitly; marker-without-reason fails the lint. Layer P (Python, AST), TWO rules matched to the codebase's two real write shapes: R1 — any RAW subprocess invocation whose argv carries git plus a mutation verb (add/commit/rm/mv/reset/update-ref/checkout/clean, matched at the git SUBCOMMAND position — the first non-option token after `git` and global options like `-C <path>`/`-c k=v` — so `remote add`/`worktree add` do not fire on `add`; deliberate: remote/worktree plumbing on an ephemeral workspace writes no tracker content, and the fail-closed wrapper-body rules below still cover those modules), where the argv is resolved by LOCAL INTRA-FUNCTION TRACKING, not literal-only matching: a list literal inline at the call, a local variable assigned a list literal (including subsequent .append/.extend of literals) in the same function body, or — fail-closed — an OPAQUE argv (a bare parameter or non-literal expression), which fires as 'unresolvable argv' and is sanctioned only by the marker (the wrapper-internal bodies gitutil.run_git and event_append._run_git are exactly this shape and receive their seam-internal marker). The R1 raw-subprocess hits at HEAD fall into three CLASSES rather than a short verified list — (1) seam-wrapper internals (gitutil.run_git/run_git_write's subprocess.run; event_append._run_git ~:245-256), (2) inline store-surgery in maintenance commands (_commands/txn.py reset ~:143; _commands/purge_bridge.py add/commit ~:153-158), (3) disposable-workspace writes (enumerated under the sandbox rationale below) — and the AUTHORITATIVE inventory is produced by the lint itself via the report-mode bootstrap (below), not by this plan's prose. R2 — any CALL to the shared git wrappers BY NAME (run_git, run_git_write, _run_git, _git — the wrapper-NAME set listed in the lint; `_git` is not one function but a name defined locally in at least eight modules — _commands/delete.py:173, compact.py:58, txn.py:119, init.py:80, fsck.py:386, fsck_repair.py:56, fsck_recover.py:61, opcert_service/workspace.py — each delegating to run_git/run_git_write or raw subprocess, so R2 fires on EVERY caller of ANY of them; the maintenance commands' add/commit/reset callers — delete.py ~:326-353, compact.py ~:374-751, txn.py ~:308-309/:421-422, init.py, fsck_repair.py, fsck_recover.py — are all legitimate store-surgery and EACH receives a function-level `# raw-git-ok: store-maintenance command, seam-internal` marker in the first scan; sibling wrapper names (_git_ok/_git_fetch/_git_push) are NOT in the name set: their bodies fire the opaque-argv class at the wrapper internal and take a delegation marker, sanctioning their callers transitively, and the teaching message tells a new-wrapper author that any fresh thin wrapper's body fires fail-closed) passing a mutation verb resolved by the SAME intra-function tracking as R1: (a) a string literal anywhere in the call's arguments INCLUDING nested list literals (`_git(["update-ref", ref, new]）` — the _ref_lock CAS caller shape; txn.py run_git_write(...,'add'...) ~:128), (b) a local list variable built from literals then passed plain or SPLATTED (`args = ["commit"]; ... run_git(_root(repo_root), *args)` — the shape git_adapter.commit/update_ref/rm_cached actually use, git_adapter.py ~:171-251, and `argv = [..."commit"...]; _run_git(argv)` — event_append._git_commit_paths ~:319-337), or (c) fail-closed, an OPAQUE argv (a bare parameter forwarded to a wrapper name, e.g. _ref_lock._git's own body forwarding `*args` to run_git ~:244-272), which fires as 'unresolvable argv to git wrapper' and takes the delegation-seam marker. Literal-only matching would miss (b) and (c) — the codebase's OWN idiom builds the verb into a local list before the call, so a future bypass author copying that idiom must not stay green. Both rules suppressed only by the marker on the line or enclosing function. Rationale for module-agnostic flagging: rebar's Python writes git only for the tracker/its mirrors OR for DISPOSABLE SANDBOX/WORKSPACE repos (at HEAD: src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py _git_init/add/commit fixture repos ~:27-44; src/rebar/llm/workflow/criterion_preview.py _git_init + fixture add/commit ~:352-415; src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py ~:374 raw `git -C <dest> checkout -q FETCH_HEAD` into a disposable review clone — fires R1-literal; src/rebar/opcert_service/workspace.py, whose LOCAL _git/_git_ok wrapper bodies fire the opaque class at the wrapper internal while their checkout/worktree-add callers ~:105-127 do not fire by name — protection sits on the wrapper body) — so every raw mutation is a seam internal, a sandbox fixture, or a bypass. ALL of them get flagged by default and the first two categories carry the marker (`# raw-git-ok: locked store seam internal` / `# raw-git-ok: disposable sandbox repo, not the tracker`); no tracker-targeting dataflow analysis needed, which is exactly what makes the lint deterministic. The sandbox sites are enumerated in the first-scan marker list alongside the seam internals. Layer W (workflows + shell, cwd-aware within-step): parse .github/workflows/*.yml run-blocks and scripts/*.sh; flag a git mutation verb ONLY when the same step/script block establishes tracker context — `cd` into a path containing the tracker dir name (.tickets-tracker), `git -C <tracker-path>`, or a `working-directory:` naming it — the exact reconcile-bridge.yml shape. Ordinary repo commits in workflows (docs/artifacts) never fire (no tracker context). ACCEPTED RESIDUAL (stated in the lint header + docs): argv construction that crosses function boundaries or is computed dynamically (beyond the local intra-function list tracking) resolves as the fail-closed opaque-argv class when it reaches a wrapper name or raw subprocess, and tracker targeting laundered through a variable in Layer W remains undetectable statically; the lint deterministically catches the literal, local-variable/splat, and opaque-forwarding shapes — which cover every historical bypass and the codebase's own write idioms. First full scan is a REPORT-MODE BOOTSTRAP: run the new lint with a --report flag before enforcement is wired; that report — not this plan's enumeration — is the authoritative hit inventory; every hit is remediated or marked with a reasoned marker in the same change, and the lint flips to enforcing in that same PR (NOTE: _store/lock.py needs NO marker — it locks via fcntl/mkdir and only RESOLVES git paths, issuing no git subprocess); remediate or mark any other hit. Failure message teaches: 'store writes go through the event-append/transaction APIs (rebar.tickets / _store.event_append / _commands.txn) or the reconciler git_adapter; if this raw write is genuinely seam-internal, add # raw-git-ok: <reason>'. Pattern precedent: module-size gate (deterministic scan, teaching error) + check_*.py script convention wired into _build-and-test.yml.

## Scope
- new lint script scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py (Layer P + Layer W in one script, check()/main() convention, EXCLUDED self-fixtures) + CI wiring as a named step in .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml
- inline `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` markers on every report-mode hit: seam internals (gitutil, event_append, txn, purge_bridge, reconciler git_adapter + _ref_lock), the store-maintenance callers of per-module `_git` wrappers (delete, compact, txn, init, fsck, fsck_repair, fsck_recover), and disposable-workspace sites (eval_solver, criterion_preview, review_bot/gerrit_client, opcert_service/workspace)
- remediation of any additional bypass sites the first full scan finds
- docs: one paragraph in the contributing/store docs naming the sanctioned write seams and the marker

## Testing
Lint unit tests: (P) raw `subprocess.run(["git", "-C", t, "commit", ...])` in an unmarked module fails with the teaching message; same line with `# raw-git-ok: reason` passes; marker WITHOUT reason fails; git read verbs (status/log/rev-parse) never fire; VARIABLE-ARGV: `args = ["commit", "-m", m]; run_git(root, *args)` and `argv = ["git", "-C", t, "commit"]; _run_git(argv)` both fire via the intra-function tracking, a local list carrying only a read verb (`["log"]`) does not fire, and an OPAQUE argv (bare parameter forwarded to a wrapper name) fires fail-closed and is silenced by the marker. A maintenance-shape caller `_git(tracker, "add", "-A")` fires by name and is silenced by a function-level marker; `remote add` / `worktree add` never fire (subcommand-position negative control). (W) a workflow step with `cd .tickets-tracker` + bare `git add -A` fails; `git -C .tickets-tracker commit` fails; a bare `git commit` step with NO tracker context passes (the docs-commit false-positive control); `working-directory: .tickets-tracker` + git mutation fails. Self-exclusion: the lint's own test fixtures are excluded (EXCLUDED_FILES tuple, check_criteria_vocabulary.py:38 idiom). Full-tree run is clean at merge.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] CI fails on unmarked raw git mutations in rebar Python (module-agnostic) and on tracker-context git mutations in workflows/shell (cwd-aware within-step), with the teaching message naming the store write APIs and the reconciler seam.
- [x] Sanction is a single inline marker with mandatory reason; marker-without-reason fails; relationship to the existing tickets-boundary-ok convention documented.
- [x] The report-mode bootstrap inventory (authoritative over this plan's prose enumeration) is fully dispositioned — every hit remediated or marked with a reason, including the per-module `_git` maintenance callers and the disposable-workspace sites (review_bot/gerrit_client, opcert_service/workspace) — and the tree is clean at landing; the reconcile-bridge.yml historical shape is covered by a failing test fixture.
- [x] Lint has its own unit tests including the no-tracker-context negative control, the variable-argv positive cases (splat and plain local-list argv: the git_adapter.commit/update_ref/rm_cached and event_append._git_commit_paths shapes fire), the opaque-argv fail-closed case (_ref_lock._git delegation shape), and the remaining accepted residual (CROSS-function/dynamic argv construction beyond intra-function tracking) documented in the lint header.

# Behavioral-comparison completion verifier + ticket-scope-drift detection for rebar's gates

Captured as an undesigned idea from session log **c905-a38c-0419-448e** (alias
`apt-otter-urn`), authored by Joe Oakhart. This is the third of three proposals in
that log; the other two became epics `elfish-chair-lug` (88ab, feature-branch
accumulation) and `woozy-pea-kin` (66ac, completion-aware container plan-review).
This proposal is **designed at the investigation level but not yet decomposed or
plan-reviewed** — it is parked here for later design/refinement.

## Context (why this investigation was run)

The goal was to make rebar's LLM review gates more *accurate* (fewer false
positives, and to detect scope creep), rather than to change the multi-story
landing workflow. Two gates were examined: the **completion verifier**
(closes a work ticket) and the **Gerrit code-review bot** (votes on a diff).

## Findings (code)

- **Completion verifier** (`src/rebar/llm/completion.py` +
  `reviewers/completion_verifier.md`) judges a ticket against the pinned HEAD tree
  with read-only tools; it does **NOT** use commit trailers / `file_impact` /
  `verify_commands` for ticket↔code association.
- **Gerrit review-bot** reviews the diff in isolation: the `{{ticket_context}}`
  prompt slots are filled with the **diff** (`batch_runner.py:58`,
  `code-review.yaml:63-64`); the voter never extracts the `rebar-ticket` trailer or
  passes `target_ticket`, even though `produce_code_review_verdict` accepts one and
  the attested-tickets store is already materialized.
- **`verify-commit-ticket`** checks only that the id resolves — no content / status
  / claimant check.
- **Net gap:** no gate checks that a diff *semantically serves* its named ticket;
  no scope-creep detection anywhere.

## Research

- **Jin & Chen, ASE 2025 (arXiv:2508.12358)** — a **Behavioral Comparison Prompt**
  (blind spec-summary + blind impl-summary, *then* compare) lifts correct-code
  recognition from **52% → 85–90%**. Rich single-pass judging (rebar's current
  verifier shape) is the documented false-positive failure mode.
- **BitsAI-CR** — an independent verify stage lifts precision **25% → 75%**;
  conclusion-first output.
- **Qodo / CodeRabbit** — diff↔linked-ticket compliance is the production
  scope-check pattern; no published detector research — `file_impact` is a unique
  deterministic prior rebar already has.
- **Google Tricorder** — advisory-first, ~10% "not-useful" demotion budget,
  blocking only for near-deterministic / execution-verified checks.

## Proposal (4 parts)

1. **Restructure `completion-verification.yaml` into 3 steps:**
   - `spec_summary` (ticket only),
   - `impl_summary` (code only; worklist = `file_impact` + trailer-linked paths,
     ticket prose withheld),
   - `compare` (1-TURN, conclusion-first).
   Keep `reconcile_verdict` + signing unchanged.

2. **Wire `target_ticket` into the Gerrit voter** (`extract_ticket_refs` already
   exists) + a new **advisory ticket-alignment LLM overlay** + a **prompt-less DET
   criterion** for "files-outside-`file_impact`" in
   `code_review/criteria_routing.json`.

3. **Asymmetric posture:** under-delivery can **FAIL** (as today); over-delivery is
   **advisory-only in v1**, with a coach message naming
   `discovered_from` / `file_impact` / AC-amend as the cure. Scope amendments that
   only **ADD** `file_impact` should qualify for the `drift_refresh` lightweight
   re-sign path (`attest.py`) so they don't stale the plan-review attestation.
   Enforce a per-criterion noise budget (~10% override rate → demote) before any
   blocking promotion.

4. **Advisory ticket-status warning in `verify-commit-ticket`.** Untrailered
   commits are **not** chased (the completion verifier reads the final tree, so
   correctness doesn't depend on trailer coverage).

## Rollout

plumbing + DET → behavioral-comparison verifier (eval before/after on
`eval_specs` fixtures) → ticket-alignment overlay advisory + telemetry → earned
per-criterion blocking.

## Acceptance Criteria (to be refined during design — this is an idea, not yet dispatchable)

- [ ] `completion-verification.yaml` restructured into blind `spec_summary` /
      `impl_summary` / conclusion-first `compare` steps; `reconcile_verdict` +
      signing behavior unchanged.
- [ ] Before/after eval on `eval_specs` fixtures demonstrates the FP-reduction the
      behavioral-comparison research predicts.
- [ ] `target_ticket` extracted + passed through the Gerrit voter; advisory
      ticket-alignment overlay + prompt-less DET "files-outside-`file_impact`"
      criterion added under `code_review/criteria_routing.json`.
- [ ] Asymmetric posture implemented (under-delivery FAIL / over-delivery advisory
      v1); `file_impact`-only scope additions route to the `drift_refresh`
      lightweight re-sign.
- [ ] Per-criterion ~10% not-useful demotion budget + telemetry in place before any
      criterion is promoted to blocking.
- [ ] Advisory ticket-status warning added to `verify-commit-ticket`.

## Source

Verbatim from session log c905-a38c-0419-448e, comment by Joe Oakhart
(2026-07-07). Not claimed / not implemented / not plan-reviewed — a parked idea.
baseline.summary: Behavioral-comparison completion verifier + ticket-scope-drift detection for rebar's gates

## Context / Problem
Bug tickets carry no record of WHICH detection channel found them (canary, CI, review bot, human audit, user report), so escape-channel trends are unmeasurable. Retroactive classification was rejected (unreliable); capture must happen at creation with zero added user friction.

## Approach
Automated filers set an environment variable (e.g. REBAR_DETECTED_BY=canary|ci|review-bot) that is read at the create seam every ingress converges on — src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:create_core (:73) — NOT in the CLI arg parser, so library (_lib_writes.create_ticket), MCP (_mcp_writes.create_ticket), and CLI filers all get the stamp; scales to client projects because the filer owns its own env. Human/agent sources may pass an OPTIONAL '--detected-by <source>' flag; absent both, the field is simply unset (never required, never prompted). Document the flag in agent guidance and the bug-creation contract (see canary-hardening sibling).

Validation policy (deterministic, never blocks filing): the value is a free-form token, normalized by strip() + lowercase. Empty or whitespace-only after strip -> treated as unset (field absent from the event). Any non-empty normalized value is stamped verbatim — there is NO enforced enum; the vocabulary canary|ci|review-bot|agent|human-audit|user-report is documented as the recommended set (the metrics lens buckets unknown tokens under 'other'), so new channels never require a code change and create never fails on the value.

Reducer/schema projection (the CREATE reducer whitelists projected keys, so 'tolerated' is not enough): process_create surfaces detected_by additively and present-only, mirroring the existing source_*/creation_channel projection blocks (src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:112-138), so the field appears in compiled state and 'rebar show' while an event WITHOUT it reduces byte-identically to today. The optional field is declared in the compiled-state schema alongside creation_channel.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_commands/composer.py: create_core reads the env var and accepts an explicit detected_by param (env is the default, explicit wins); create_cli maps the optional --detected-by flag onto that param; _lib_writes/_mcp_writes pass through unchanged (env still applies to them)
- src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py: process_create copies detected_by into compiled state present-only (mirroring the source_* block)
- src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json: declare the optional detected_by string field
- docs: config/env-vars registry entry + agent guidance line

## Testing
Happy path: env var set -> field present in event, in compiled state, and shown by 'rebar show' — for CLI AND for library create_ticket (proving the seam placement). Flag overrides env. Edge: neither set -> field absent from event AND compiled state byte-identical to pre-change reduction (additivity proof). Validation rows: empty string / whitespace-only -> field absent, create succeeds; mixed-case with padding (' Canary ') -> stamped as 'canary'; unknown token ('fuzzer') -> stamped verbatim, create succeeds. Schema round-trip: compiled state with detected_by validates against ticket_state.schema.json.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] REBAR_DETECTED_BY env var stamps detected_by on created tickets; --detected-by flag overrides; absence changes nothing.
- [x] Normalization is strip+lowercase; empty/whitespace-only is treated as unset; unknown tokens are stamped verbatim (no enum enforcement); create never fails on the value.
- [x] process_create projects detected_by present-only into compiled state (mirroring source_*), and an event without the field reduces byte-identically to today; ticket_state.schema.json declares the optional field.
- [x] Registered in the env-var/docs registry so the drift gate covers it.
- [x] Tests cover env, flag, absence, precedence, the validation rows (empty, whitespace, mixed-case+padding, unknown token), the reducer projection + byte-identical-absence property, and the schema round-trip.



## Scope note: inbound Jira CREATEs (intentionally excluded)
The Jira inbound reconciler writes CREATE events directly (apply_inbound_records.py), bypassing composer.create_core, so the REBAR_DETECTED_BY env read does not reach it — by design. That path materializes tickets authored by humans in Jira; stamping the reconciler daemon's own process env there would mis-attribute the filer. Jira-originated tickets correctly carry no detected_by (unattributed), matching the absence-changes-nothing contract. Local agent ingresses (CLI, MCP, library) all converge on create_core and are covered.
baseline.summary: detected-by capture at bug creation (env var for automation, optional flag for agents)

## Context / Problem

The `rebar-janitor` agent skill (`examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/`) runs a five-phase pipeline whose Verification phase scores *findings* for validity and impact, but nothing validates the *remediations* Phase 3 proposes. During the 2026-08-05/06 janitor run over this repo that gap surfaced on every pass: a proposal that reversed a deliberate, recorded project decision, and a proposal justified by a plausible-but-unreachable harm, both reached the human at Phase-4 approval unflagged. The skill's own operating principle claims blind parallelism makes convergence meaningful, yet Phase 3's two proposers read identical evidence, so their agreement measured prompt stability rather than correctness.

## Approach

Close the gap inside the existing phase files rather than adding a phase, because both missing checks are properly attributes of steps that already run: a finding's validity (Phase 2) and a proposal's evidence base (Phase 3). Four documentation files change; no rebar source, test, config, or schema.

### Edit 1 — `phases/verification.md`: two new checks

**`harm_reachable`, a fifth validity sub-question.** It requires naming a concrete triggering input or state that produces the asserted harm ("this could break" is not enough). It **participates in the validity graded fraction**: the scoring bullet is rewritten from "graded fraction of the 4 binary sub-answers" to "graded fraction of the **5** binary sub-answers over the answerable (non-`na`) set", so the denominator becomes 5 whenever it is answerable and a `no` costs 1/5 of validity exactly like the other four. It is deliberately **not** a scoring-excluded routing flag.

`harm_reachable == "no"` additionally **reclassifies** the finding from `DEFECT` to `HARDENING`. Reclassification is a *label*, not a bypass: the existing floors (`validity >= 0.75`, `impact >= 0.5`, the citation veto, the known-fine shield) run unchanged on a HARDENING finding, so one that also scores weakly on the other four sub-questions still drops (4 of 5 affirmed = 0.80 survives; 3 of 5 = 0.60 drops), and one that survives enters the Phase-3 survivor set, gets a remediation move, and appears in the Remediation Plan like any other survivor — with `approval.md` labelling it so the user is never shown hardening work presented as a bug. Nothing about the HARDENING lane is separate from the normal lane except the label.

**Where the DEFECT/HARDENING label lives and how it reaches Phase 4.** It is a property of the **finding**, not of the plan item. Every finding is a `DEFECT` implicitly — no field is written until `harm_reachable == "no"` reclassifies it to `HARDENING` during Phase-2 verification, which is the only assignment point. The label is recorded on the survivor in the persisted Phase-2 audit record (the `## Survivors` entries, alongside validity/impact/citations/why_it_matters) and travels to Phase 3 on the survivor set, which is already the documented Phase-2 -> Phase-3 gate. Phase 4 resolves it through the **existing** `finding_refs` union that every Remediation Plan item already carries: an item is flagged HARDENING when any finding it references is. This change therefore adds **no new field to the Phase-3 plan-item schema** — duplicating the label there would create a second source of truth for a fact the finding already owns, and an item covering a HARDENING and a DEFECT survivor would have to reconcile it.

**`prior_decision`, an intent check run on every finding.** Triggered on the **subject**, not on a verb — a proposal to add something back reverses a decision just as much as one to remove, it just does not look like one in a diff. It runs four deterministic queries (`git log -S '<symbol>' --all` to the originating commit's ticket trailer, `git blame -L` on the range, an ADR/docs grep, and a ticket-id grep over `src/`) and classifies what they return into exactly four values, with the record's *content* deciding:

- `explicit_justified` — the record shows a deliberate choice **and** the reasoning for it.
- `explicit_bare` — the record shows a deliberate choice with **no** reasoning recorded.
- `incidental` — the record shows the state arose without a decision.
- `none` — the queries returned no record.

The check **surfaces the record and never adjudicates it**: the verifier attaches the ticket/ADR/ commit and passes it through to Phase 4. Only `explicit_justified` carries the **-0.10 validity penalty**, and only when the finding's remediation does not name what evidence has changed since — a reversal that names the changed evidence takes no penalty. The penalty lands on validity, not impact, because a recorded deliberate choice is evidence the state is intentional; it is sized to drop a marginal finding (the 0.75-0.85 band) while leaving a strong one standing, so the record raises the bar without becoming a veto.

**Where the -0.10 penalty is evaluated.** At **Phase 2**, against the finding's own **suggested remediation direction** — the artifact that already exists there, and which `verification.md`'s streaming-validation rule already makes the verifier assess ("validity of the suggested remediation direction"). The penalty is therefore fully computable at Phase-2 scoring time and no validity is recomputed later. The Phase-3 `evidence_changed` field added by Edit 2 is the **same requirement restated on the plan item**, not the input to the Phase-2 rule: it makes a reversal auditable for the Phase-4 reviewer once a concrete move exists. A finding whose Phase-2 remediation direction already names the changed evidence takes no penalty and carries that naming forward into `evidence_changed`; a finding that does not takes the -0.10 at Phase 2 and, if it survives the floors, must still supply `evidence_changed` before its move reaches approval.

### Edit 2 — `phases/remediation.md`: asymmetric proposers and a divergence research round

The two blind proposers keep the same code and the same survivor set but answer **different questions on different evidence**: Proposer A "how do popular, actively-maintained OSS projects handle this?" (web search plus the code); Proposer B "how does this project already handle this?" (the record — tickets, ADRs, `git log`/`blame`, the Phase-2 `prior_decision` — plus the code).

**The move-level convergence judge is retained unchanged** (`same_approach` OR `same_end_state`, tagged `agent-converged`); only the proposers' inputs change. Coverage is still tracked per survivor. What is replaced is the *tiebreak*: because Proposer A already **is** the OSS research, there is no neutral third party left to arbitrate, so any survivor not covered by a converged move now triggers one targeted research round put symmetrically to both records — has the community explicitly rejected this project's approach, and has this project explicitly rejected the community's? Each answer is sorted into one of four buckets with an explicit weight:

| Bucket | Weight |
|---|---|
| **Explicitly rejected** — adopted, then reverted, with stated reasons | high |
| **Adopted and kept** — live counter-examples, named | high |
| **Excluded at adoption** — cost predicted, never paid | medium |
| **Never considered** — absent from the record | low |

**Bucket-to-outcome mapping:** a `high`-weight answer on exactly one side adopts that side's move, tagged **`research-resolved`**, with the record cited. **Every other outcome** — `medium`, `low`, or `high` on both sides — emits a **`no-consensus`** plan item carrying both positions, their evidence, and their buckets for the user to decide in Phase 4; it is never silently dropped and never synthesised into a winner. The provenance vocabulary becomes exactly `agent-converged | research-resolved | no-consensus` — `research-resolved` replaces the retired `oss-adopted`; the other two are unchanged. A move that reverses a recorded decision must carry `evidence_changed`, which is the field the Phase-2 penalty scores the absence of.

### Edit 3 — `phases/approval.md`

Surface the `prior_decision` record (ticket/ADR/commit, what was decided, and for a reversal what evidence has changed) at review time, present a `no-consensus` item as both positions rather than a winner, and flag any item reclassified as `HARDENING`.

### Edit 4 — `SKILL.md`

Match the above: pipeline diagram, frontmatter description, two new operating principles (blind parallelism decorrelates wording not priors; the code says what it does, the record says why), and the fixed-values note.

## Scope

- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/verification.md` — the sub-question heading (4 -> 5)
  and the `harm_reachable` entry, the HARDENING reclassification note, the `prior_decision` section
  with its query block and four-value table, and the scoring bullet (the "graded fraction of the 4
  binary sub-answers" formula becomes 5 and gains the -0.10 penalty clause).
- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/remediation.md` — the asymmetric-proposer table, the
  divergence research round with its four buckets and bucket-to-outcome mapping, the
  `research-resolved` provenance tag, and the `evidence_changed` requirement on the plan item.
- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/approval.md` — the provenance bullet, the
  `prior decision` bullet, and the HARDENING flag paragraph.
- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/SKILL.md` — frontmatter `description`, the pipeline diagram
  block, the **work-product table row for Phase 3** (whose "converged / OSS-adopted / no-consensus
  items" cell restates the retired provenance vocabulary in prose form and becomes "converged /
  research-resolved / no-consensus items"), the "Scale ceremony" paragraph's OSS-tiebreak mention,
  the operating-principles list, and the fixed-values note.

**Deliberately out of scope, tracked as follow-on `1d7a-9f76-139b-4259`:** two *non-normative* prose glosses in `verification.md` retain the old count — the drop-floor parenthetical `(low-confidence — <~3-of-4 sub-answers affirm it)` and the known-fine aside `it is NOT one of the four validity sub-questions`. ## Why

Operator decisions supersede this ticket's original framing (see comments). **2026-08-10:** do NOT retune the fuzzy `low|medium|high` boundary — ordinal labels are an LLM anti-pattern (models do not apply them reliably for deterministic gate behavior); replace each ladder with a closed KIND set mapping to floor-vs-advisory. **2026-08-12:** do both halves now — drop the inert-G5 hedge (no bump) AND land the conversion under its own `IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION` bump. Per **C11** (`.../ordinal-migration-plan.md` Phase 1) the plan-v5 batch is both axes plus the margin rider.

Corpus evidence: every non-none grade on both axes floors impact to 0.85 (`_PLAN_HARD_OVERRIDE_FLOOR` in `decide.py`), so `low` == `high`. Of `undecomposed`'s 30 graded bodies, 23 are "this plan bundles N independently-releasable outcomes" — a right-sizing note on an executable plan — yet each floors; 4 blocked. `dod_uncertifiable` is graded 1,413 times, mixing three distinct defects under one blind floor. The hedge is inert: `veto_undecomposed_g5` fired ZERO times. `ORACLE_GRADE01` (v3) / `DIVERGENCE_GRADE01` (v4) are the precedents.

## What

**Scope is ONE unit, not a bundle to split.** ADR 0054 section 4 batches impact-model shape changes behind one `IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION` bump, since each bump closes the current cohort. Items 2-3 are shape changes; 1 and 4 are no-bump riders otherwise stranded from their evidence. NOT independently releasable.

1. **Prompt rewrite (no bump).** Delete the inert G5-suppressor hedge from both prompts and the
 `undecomposed` description in `verify_models.py`; both prompts' bullets for these axes are also
   REWRITTEN (see Steps) to enumerate the six kinds and their pick rules.
2. **`undecomposed` -> kind set (bump):** `none`; `bundles_separable_slices` — executable as written
   but packs outcomes that could each ship alone, so splitting only aids clarity — contributing
   `UNDECOMPOSED_BUNDLED_CONTRIB` = 0.55, NEVER flooring; `missing_required_child` — work the plan
   or its parent commits to has NO child/sibling — flooring; `no_executable_breakdown` — no
   executable step sequence for its scope, or an all-or-nothing build whose riskiest unknown is not
   de-risked — flooring.
3. **`dod_uncertifiable` -> kind set (bump):** `none`; `underspecified_certification` — the outcome
   IS certifiable and an oracle exists, but its exact command/path/assertion is not stated —
   contributing `DOD_UNDERSPECIFIED_CONTRIB` = 0.55, NEVER flooring; `uncertifiable_outcome` — a
   committed outcome has NO acceptance criterion, test or proving mechanism — flooring;
   `certification_cannot_prove` — a stated mechanism cannot establish the outcome (names something
   nonexistent or unable to detect what is claimed, or a trivially broken implementation satisfies
   it) — flooring.
4. **Decision-margin telemetry (no bump).** Record `priority - block_threshold` per finding in the
   sidecar. C11 P0.2 says `impact_sev`, but `pass3_decide` blocks on `priority >= block_threshold`
   (`priority = validity x impact`), so the margin uses `priority`.
5. **Bump `IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION` plan-v4 -> plan-v5** in `plan_review/sidecar.py`.

**Evidence gate before landing (zero LLM).** Add a re-score script under `docs/calibration/` covering every recorded finding under the new maps and reporting old-vs-new flips. It reads persisted `severity_attributes` as RAW dicts (never through the new `Literal` model, which rejects the old labels). **Mapping rule:** each recorded grade maps to a kind by ORDERED regex over the finding's own prose + evidence (first match wins), GAP-BIASED — a body describing a missing, broken or vacuous oracle, or missing required decomposition maps to a FLOORING kind; only a specificity/framing complaint maps to advisory. Rows matching no rule are scored BOTH ways, so the result is a BOUND, not a point estimate. Per the R1 bar, a lost block is UNJUSTIFIED iff the body describes such a gap yet re-maps to advisory; any such flip means ESCALATE, not land.

## Steps

Implement items 1-5 in order, then 6-8.

`_SEV01` maps only `none|low|medium|high`, returning 0.0 for any kind name. `impact_plan` reads these axes through `_SEV01` in THREE places; ALL THREE must be rewritten against the new `*_GRADE01` maps or the axes silently go dead: the contribs MAX (via `_PLAN_SEVERITY_AXES`), the `has_override` floor loop (via `_PLAN_HARD_OVERRIDE_AXES`), and the `dod_uncertifiable` amplifier force of `mult = 1.0`. Adding both to `_PLAN_GRADED_AXES` covers the first two; the amplifier force is a separate rewrite.

The verifier EMITS these values, so both prompts' bullets for these axes are REWRITTEN to enumerate all six kinds with pick-this-kind rules and advisory-vs-flooring semantics, matching the `divergent_implementation` bullet's form.

6. In `tests/unit/test_impact_plan.py` REWRITE (not merely extend) the pre-existing ordinal-keyed
   cases for these axes — `test_hard_override_floors_low_axis_to_085`,
   `test_each_ordinal_override_axis_triggers_floor`,
   `test_dod_uncertifiable_forces_full_detection_weight` — to kind names, then add the new cases;
   update `test_impact_model_versioning.py`; pin the margin in `test_plan_review_sidecar.py`.
   `test_criteria_vocabulary_reviewers.py` pins "success criterion" in the `dod_uncertifiable`
   bullet, so PRESERVE that phrasing.
7. Update `docs/plan-review-gate.md` (lines 225-235): its "present at any grade" narrative describes
   exactly the flooring behavior items 2-3 replace. Extend the paragraph already documenting the
   plan-v3 oracle split to cover both kind sets.
8. Write the re-score script; record rules + results in `docs/calibration/plan_v5_kind_sets.md`.

Out of scope: `veto_undecomposed_g5` removal, C11 Phase 2. Gates: `make lint && make typecheck`, the AC commands, `pytest tests/interfaces -q -k plan_review`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Both axes are closed `Literal` kind sets. Verified: `python -m pytest
      tests/unit/test_impact_plan.py -q -k literal` passes, asserting each annotation holds the six
      kind names and none of `low`/`medium`/`high`.
- [x] Each advisory kind contributes 0.55 and never floors; each gap kind yields 0.85; both CONTRIB
      constants sit strictly below the lowest blocking `block_threshold` (0.6) in
      `criteria_routing.json`, like `UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB`; the amplifier
      still forces `mult = 1.0` for non-none `dod_uncertifiable`. Verified: `python -m pytest
      tests/unit/test_impact_plan.py -q` passes with cases pinning both advisory kinds at 0.55, the
      four gap kinds at 0.85, the contrib-below-0.6 invariant, and a finding whose
      detection axis `silent_vs_self_revealing` is `self_revealing` still scoring 0.55 — the
      dod amplifier force keeps mult=1.0, preventing 0.55 x 0.8 = 0.44.
- [x] No prompt or description cites the G5 suppressor, and `docs/plan-review-gate.md` no longer
      says these axes floor at any grade. Verified: `rg -n "deterministic G5 signal already|signal
      already suppresses" src/rebar/` and `rg -n "is present at any" docs/plan-review-gate.md` both
      exit 1.
- [x] The sidecar records a per-finding `priority - block_threshold` margin, and
      `IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION` is `plan-v5` batched per ADR 0054 section 4. Verified: `python -m pytest
      tests/unit/test_plan_review_sidecar.py tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py -q` passes
      (including a `-k margin` case), and the commit body names the hedge removal, both conversions
      and the margin telemetry as riding one bump.
- [x] The re-score is landed and shows no unjustified lost blocks (rule above). Verified:
      `docs/calibration/plan_v5_kind_sets.md` states the mapping rules and reports old-vs-new counts
      under both residual bounds plus the audited loss list, and `python
      docs/calibration/plan_v5_rescore.py --root=<checkout>` reproduces them. (Path corrected:
      `/reports/` is gitignored, so a script there could never land — see comment.)

## Symptom (live repro, 2026-08-14)
`rebar transition clubby-circular-halicore open closed --class not_a_bug` on a bug whose RCA proved no defect ever existed FAILED: the close routed to the billable completion verifier, which synthesized the criterion "bug is actually resolved: the reported defect no longer reproduces" and marked it unmet — correctly noting "no code change was made" and "the premise of the criterion (that a real defect existed and was resolved) is itself refuted by the RCA". A truthful not_a_bug close is thus impossible without --force whenever there is no replacement ticket to link.

## Mechanism
close_disposition.verdict() mints a deterministic disposition verdict only from find_replacement() (a live duplicates/supersedes link). not_a_bug is in DISPOSITION_CLASSES but inherently names no replacement, so verdict() returns None and the close falls through to full completion verification — which asks the wrong question for this class. The historical scoping comment (close_precheck.py ~:154) already recognizes "not_a_bug asserts there is no defect", but only exempted it from the duplicate-link REQUIREMENT, leaving it on the completion-verification path. escalated without a live replacement has the same fall-through shape (it "may point outside the tracker").

## Fix (stacked on Gerrit 1794, ticket fc20 — reuse its machinery verbatim)
Make not_a_bug a REASON-REQUIRED class exactly like obsolete/wontfix: add it to close_disposition.REASON_REQUIRED_CLASSES so (a) txn.close_class_refusal demands --reason=<text> (the RCA summary / pointer to the RCA comment), (b) verdict() mints the deterministic (class, close_reason) attestation with no replacement and no LLM, (c) decorate_manifest signs the disposition line, (d) the --reason-without---force admission in transition.py extends to it. Decide escalated deliberately: either reason-required the same way (reason = where it went), or keep replacement-preferred with reason fallback — document the choice. not_a_bug stays bug-only (NOT added to ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES non-bug vocabulary).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] A bug close --class not_a_bug --reason "<why no defect>" (no --force, no replacement link) closes without invoking the billable completion verifier and mints a SIGNED disposition attestation carrying class+reason (store-event + manifest tests).
- [x] not_a_bug without --reason is refused at write time naming the requirement (gate-independent, txn.close_class_refusal test).
- [x] escalated's no-replacement path has an explicit, tested disposition (reason-required or documented fall-through — no silent completion-verifier routing).
- [x] 738a drift-guard and 1794's administrative-close suite stay green; docs (ticket-model.md, cli-reference) updated.
- [x] make lint / make typecheck clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
baseline.summary: not_a_bug close without replacement routes to completion verifier, which demands proof a nonexistent defect was fixed

# Rekey live cell derives a colliding project key ~1 run in 26

## Symptom

`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_transport.py::test_a_rekeyed_issue_resolves_by_id_and_records_what_the_stale_key_returns` failed on harness run 30772461871 (job 91561874505, main @ bd3de0f864) with its OWN setup assertion:

    >   assert new_project_key != jira_dc_project
    E   AssertionError: assert 'RBJDRDZ' != 'RBJDRDZ'

48 passed / 1 failed, canary `collected=49 executed=49 skipped=0`.

## Mechanism — a self-collision, not a product defect

`test_transport.py:515-516` derives the rename target by replacing the last character with a literal `"Z"`:

    new_project_key = (jira_dc_project[:-1] if len(jira_dc_project) >= 4 else jira_dc_project) + "Z"
    assert new_project_key != jira_dc_project

Harness project keys are `RBJ` + 4 random letters (`conftest.py:154,185` — `_PROJECT_KEY_PREFIX` plus `_random_project_key`). **When the drawn key already ends in `Z`, the derived "new" key is byte-identical to the original.** This run drew `RBJDRDZ`, so `RBJDRD` + `Z` == `RBJDRDZ`.

So the cell is flaky by construction at roughly **1 run in 26** (uniform final letter). It passed on runs 30765232591 and 30767546938 purely because those draws did not end in `Z`.

## This is NOT a regression, and that matters for reading the run

The failure is unrelated to anything merged in that tree. Nothing in 1231/1232/1233/1234/1235 touches `test_transport.py`, project-key generation, or the rename path; the collision depends only on a random draw. The two cells that DID depend on this session's work both PASSED on the same run: `test_outbound_mutation_round_trips[04-transition-status]` and `test_the_inbound_assignee_mints_a_jira_family_identity`.

**Credit where due: the cell FAILED SAFE.** Its setup assertion is what caught the collision. Without it the test would have issued `PUT /rest/api/2/project/<key>` renaming the project to the key it already has, and then asserted things about a "stale" key that was never stale — a green or a confusing red that would have taught us nothing about the actual contract (7c26's operator-attested question about what a stale key returns). The assertion is doing exactly its job; only the derivation is wrong.

## Fix

Derive a target that cannot collide, rather than asserting after the fact. Options, cheapest first:
* pick a replacement character that differs from the current final character (e.g. `"Z"` unless the key
  already ends in `Z`, in which case `"Y"`); or
* append/rotate rather than substitute, keeping within Jira's project-key constraints (uppercase letters,
  length limits); or
* derive the new key from the same `_random_project_key` generator and retry on equality, which reuses the
  existing validity guarantees instead of hand-rolling a mutation.
KEEP the `!=` setup assertion whichever is chosen — it is the thing that turned a silent nothing-happened rename into a legible failure, and it should stay as the guard.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] the rename target cannot equal the source key for ANY key the harness can generate, proven by a
      repo-only unit test over the derivation that includes a key ending in the replacement character
- [x] the `new_project_key != jira_dc_project` setup assertion is RETAINED, not deleted as redundant
- [x] the derived key still satisfies Jira's project-key rules (uppercase, length), asserted rather than
      assumed
- [x] [operator-attested] the cell passes on a harness run whose project key ends in the replacement
      character — either by forcing that key for one run or by recording that the derivation test covers
      it, with the reasoning recorded here

## Criteria met (Gerrit 1370) + AC4 attestation (operator, 2026-08-04)

**AC1 — proven by a repo-only unit test over the derivation, including a key ending in the replacement character.** `tests/unit/test_live_dc_rekey_target_d582.py` parametrizes ALL 26 possible final letters, so the `Z` case is covered by enumeration rather than by a lucky draw, and names the exact `RBJDRDZ` shape separately so the regression is legible in the report. Verified RED before GREEN: against the pre-fix derivation exactly the `[Z]` case and the explicit `RBJDRDZ` case fail; after it, 54 pass.

**AC2 — the setup assertion is RETAINED.** `assert new_project_key != jira_dc_project` still stands in the cell, and a test asserts its presence in the source. It is what caught the original collision instead of letting the cell rename the project to the key it already had and then assert about a key that was never stale; deleting it as redundant would have removed the only thing that failed safe.

**AC3 — Jira's key rules are asserted, not assumed.** Per final letter: length within 2-10, uppercase, letters only, leading letter, and length unchanged from the source (the derivation swaps a character rather than growing the key, so a rename cannot push a legal key past the ceiling).

**AC4 — ATTESTED via the route this criterion explicitly permits.** The AC offers two options: force a `Z`-terminal project key for one run, OR record that the derivation test covers it with the reasoning recorded here. Taking the second, because it is the stronger of the two:

* the collision depended solely on a random draw with p≈1/26, so a single harness run "passing" would
  have been ~96% likely to draw a NON-`Z` key and therefore prove nothing about the fixed case;
* forcing a `Z`-terminal key for one run would exercise it once, on a substrate that costs ~41 minutes
  per attempt and only on the amd64 runner;
* the unit test exercises the `Z` case on EVERY commit, deterministically, and was demonstrated to go
  red without the fix.

So the enumerated repo-only oracle is strictly better evidence than the live run the AC contemplated, and it is what this attestation rests on. Harness run **30933704255** additionally exercised the cell live — `test_a_rekeyed_issue_resolves_by_id_and_records_what_the_stale_key_returns` PASSED, its setup assertion included — which confirms the derivation works against a real instance, on whatever key that run happened to draw.
baseline.summary: Rekey live cell can derive a colliding project key (1-in-26 flake)
