# Remove the dead per-language analyzer dispatch and its inert config field

## Scope WIDENED 2026-08-05 by operator decision, after an archaeology pass

Originally scoped to `CodeHealthConfig.analyzers` alone. Widened to the whole dead dispatch, because story `c23c-c32b-982c-4196` already sanctioned exactly this and the clause was never executed.

## What the record shows

Epic `839b-f6d2-7e1a-4051` designed per-language analyzer dispatch selected by per-project config. Story `3b30-2168-ba16-41fc` built the seam and shipped the registry INTENTIONALLY EMPTY -- its AC says "import registers nothing into REGISTRY as a side effect (opt-in wiring lands in 0734)". That wiring never happened.

`0734-ceae-be55-4fa7` then bypassed it for size, with a stated reason: "module size is POLYGLOT aggregate LOC, so it uses the single language-agnostic LOC analyzer directly -- NOT resolve_analyzer(lang)".

`c23c-c32b-982c-4196` retired the design outright: "implement direct adapter composition, not the unused language-dispatch table... If ANALYZERS/resolve_analyzer/analyze_or_unavailable remain unused after this direct composition, REMOVE THAT DEAD DISPATCH while retaining AnalyzerResult/Analyzer protocol compatibility." c23c implemented the composition but never executed the removal clause -- it was conditional and was not an acceptance criterion, so no gate held it. This ticket executes it.

The seam was also never viable as designed: `analyze_or_unavailable` calls `analyzer.analyze(repo_root, languages=languages)` BY KEYWORD, but `scc_loc.analyze`'s second parameter is named `scan_roots`. Verified at runtime: TypeError, unexpected keyword argument 'languages'. mypy --strict does not catch it because module-as-protocol checking is lenient about parameter names. So populating the registry would have crashed on the scc adapter.

## DELETE

- `ANALYZERS` (src/rebar/metrics/analyzer.py:32) -- never populated in src/, only monkeypatched by tests
- `resolve_analyzer` (:44) -- dead in production
- `analyze_or_unavailable` (:50) -- ZERO production callers
- `load_lizard` (:35) -- dead, and duplicates the guard `lizard_complexity.analyze` already does at :27-30
- `CodeHealthConfig.analyzers` (src/rebar/_config_schema.py:541) and its coercion row (:716)
- the self-referential escape marker `# read-via: inert pending bug dce2-b93d-4112-451c` (:540)
- the now-dead tests that exercise only the removed symbols (tests/unit/metrics/test_analyzer.py,
  test_analyzer_heldout.py) -- keep any that cover retained symbols

## KEEP -- do NOT remove

- `AnalyzerResult` -- LIVE, imported by git_metrics.py:14 and all three adapters
- the `Analyzer` Protocol -- c23c explicitly said "retaining AnalyzerResult/Analyzer protocol
  compatibility". It becomes documentation-only once its callers go; that is intended.
- the whole live path in git_metrics.py (`_scc_analysis`, `_lizard_analysis`, `_jscpd_analysis`,
  `_cached_analysis`, `_structural_spec`) -- this is the working composition and must not change
- `code_health.enabled` -- separately inert, tracked by its own bug; NOT in scope here

## NOT in scope

Reviving selection is idea `94bc-a0b4-bc37-47b2`, which carries the operator's condition that it must ship with a dogfooded project-specific analyzer rather than as config alone. The inert `code_health.enabled` field is bug `a573-00ea-2bf6-4eb1`. The 6754 gate's global-name-matching weakness is bug `2c58-e710-275e-4ff7`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] All six deletion targets above are removed; `grep -rn "ANALYZERS\|resolve_analyzer\|analyze_or_unavailable\|load_lizard" src/` returns nothing.
- [x] `AnalyzerResult` and the `Analyzer` Protocol still exist and `git_metrics.py` still imports `AnalyzerResult`.
- [x] `rebar metrics` produces byte-identical output before and after on this repo (all four structural metrics remain Unavailable for the same reasons -- the tools are not installed here -- proving a pure removal with no behavior change).
- [x] The `# read-via:` marker is gone AND `scripts/check_config_reads.py` passes without it, because the field it exempted no longer exists.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the full suite pass; test count changes ONLY by the removal of tests that covered deleted symbols, and that delta is stated explicitly in the commit message.
- [x] Reference sets confirmed with BOTH a semantic search and a plain string grep, per AGENTS.md -- the removed symbols are reached via `monkeypatch.setattr`/`setitem` in tests, which the LSP does not see.
baseline.summary: CodeHealthConfig.analyzers is inert: zero read sites outside config plumbing

# S6-pre — GitHub mirror-lock pre-work (snapshot, ADR, backend/token scope)

## Why
The GitHub mirror lock (S6) is a one-way-door change to a PUBLIC repo. De-risk it by doing
the no-live-repo-change pre-work FIRST: capture a restorable snapshot of the current
protection, record the decision + accepted risk in an ADR, and confirm the IaC backend +
token scope — so S6's live apply is fast, ordered, and reversible. This story makes NO change
to the live repo.

## What
- Snapshot the existing `main-protection` ruleset (DERISK E5: id 18048287 — `pull_request` +
  `required_status_checks` + `deletion` + `non_fast_forward`, admins bypass-via-PR) to a
  committed `infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json`
  (`gh api /repos/navapbc/rebar/rulesets/18048287`), so the prior PR-based protection can be
  restored on rollback. Snapshot ONLY — the live ruleset is not modified here.
- Write `docs/adr/0011-github-mirror-lock.md`: the repo-level-vs-org-level trade-off (free org
  -> no admin-proof org-level rule; trusted-admin editability accepted), the DeployKey-bypass
  `gh api` workaround (UI omits DeployKey; terraform-provider-github historically rejects it) +
  its retirement path, and the one-way-door nature (replaces the human-PR model; disables
  PRs/Issues/Actions).
- Confirm the `Administration: write` token scope (fine-grained PAT scoped to navapbc/rebar,
  injected as a `sensitive` Terraform var from a CI secret, never in `.tfvars`) and the shared
  remote backend + state locking that S6 will use.

## Scope
In: snapshot + ADR + token-scope/backend confirmation (NO live-repo changes). Out: creating /
enforcing the rulesets + mirror hygiene (S6); the Gerrit-side replication (S5).

## Files
- `infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json` (committed snapshot, for rollback)
- `docs/adr/0011-github-mirror-lock.md`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json` contains the full current definition of
      ruleset 18048287 (captured via `gh api`), sufficient to recreate it on rollback.
- [ ] `docs/adr/0011-github-mirror-lock.md` records the repo-level-vs-org-level trade-off, the
      accepted trusted-admin-editability risk, the DeployKey `gh api` bypass workaround +
      retirement path, and the one-way-door nature.
- [ ] The required token scope (`Administration: write`, fine-grained PAT scoped to this repo,
      injected as a `sensitive` var from a CI secret, never committed) is documented.
- [ ] The shared remote backend + state locking that S6 will use is confirmed available; this
      story makes NO change to the live repo (snapshot/docs only).
baseline.summary: infra: S6-pre — GitHub mirror-lock pre-work (snapshot main-protection, ADR, backend/token scope)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

On the AGENTIC path the growing tool-result history is re-sent UNCACHED every turn, so input cost grows O(N^2) in turns — and rebar's own telemetry cannot see it.

`capabilities.py:333-355` `cache_settings_for` sets exactly two of the four available breakpoints:

    anthropic_cache_instructions=True
    anthropic_cache_tool_definitions=True

and its docstring says so outright: "neither `*_cache_messages` nor `anthropic_cache` is touched." Applied once at `runner.py:394`.

BOTH UNUSED KNOBS ALREADY EXIST in the pinned dependency — verified by introspection against the repo's own `.venv` at pydantic-ai 1.107.1, not from docs:

    AnthropicModelSettings: anthropic_cache, anthropic_cache_instructions,
                            anthropic_cache_messages, anthropic_cache_tool_definitions
    BedrockModelSettings:   bedrock_cache_instructions, bedrock_cache_messages,
                            bedrock_cache_tool_definitions

## The failure, concretely

`DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS = 250` (`config.py:127`) yields `request_limit = 125` (`structured_run.py:331`). The agentic Pass-1 criteria and container calls (`plan_review/passes.py:330, 434`) run a tool loop in which EVERY turn re-sends the full accumulated message history. With only a system breakpoint that history is never written to cache and never read. On a 40-turn review whose file-read tool results average 2k tokens, turn 40 re-sends ~80k uncached tokens that turn 39 also sent.

IT IS INVISIBLE TO OUR TELEMETRY. `warn_if_cache_ineffective` (`structured_run.py:417-422`) requires `cache_read_tokens == 0`, but the SYSTEM block IS hitting cache, so the counter is nonzero and the predicate never fires. We would never learn this from a usage log.

## Consensus — this is the documented multi-turn shape, not an exotic optimisation

* Anthropic's prompt-caching doc recommends TWO breakpoints for multi-turn: system AND "the final
  block of the final message... so the conversation can be incrementally cached", and names automatic
  caching the "recommended starting point" for multi-turn.
* LangChain's `AnthropicPromptCachingMiddleware`
  (`libs/partners/anthropic/langchain_anthropic/middleware/prompt_caching.py`) tags system + last tool
  and delegates the tail to `model_settings["cache_control"]`.
* pydantic-ai's own Anthropic docs recommend the same triple.
System-only is the documented minimum for a STATIC-PROMPT workload; it is not the shape for an agent.

Corroborating that this was once in scope and got dropped: story REB-458 is titled "Prompt caching at the shared runner seam (CachePoint + anthropic_cache_*, provider-safe)" and is marked Done, but the shipped `cache_settings_for` sets two of four knobs and no CachePoint.

## Approach

Thread the execution mode into `cache_settings_for` and, for `agentic` ONLY, add `anthropic_cache=True` on the Anthropic arm and `bedrock_cache_messages=True` on the Bedrock arm.

MIND THE PROVIDER ASYMMETRY — this is the trap: Bedrock has NO `bedrock_cache` automatic key. LangChain hit exactly this (langchain#37042): `AnthropicPromptCachingMiddleware` regressed on Bedrock in 1.4.1 because it switched to top-level automatic caching, which Bedrock rejects with `cache_control: Extra inputs are not permitted`. So the two arms need different keys, not one shared setting.

Breakpoint budget is safe: pydantic-ai's `_limit_cache_points()` sets `MAX_CACHE_POINTS = 3 if automatic_caching else 4`, and this change puts rebar at 3.

Single-turn paths must stay BYTE-IDENTICAL — that is the regression risk and the thing to pin.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] On the AGENTIC path the message tail is cached: a captured multi-turn request shows a breakpoint
      after the accumulated history, and a live run records nonzero `cache_read_tokens` attributable to
      the message tail rather than only to the system block.
- [x] The Anthropic and Bedrock arms use their OWN keys (`anthropic_cache` vs
      `bedrock_cache_messages`); a test pins that the Bedrock arm never receives a top-level

      and after — this is the regression this change could plausibly cause.
- [x] The cost effect is MEASURED on a real multi-turn agentic run, before and after, and recorded.
      A narrowly-scoped live run is sufficient and is preferred over any eval sweep.

# Tier-2: native cross-platform scheduler registration for the enrichment drain

## Context
Follow-on to the cross-ticket overlap epic (only-crave-art). v1 ships Tier 1 only (opportunistic detached drain). Tier 2 adds a `rebar maintenance start`-style command that registers a recurring drain with the native platform scheduler, for repos that are not actively touched (Tier 1 goes stale when nobody runs rebar).

Prior art: `git maintenance start` abstracts over four schedulers behind `--scheduler=auto|crontab|systemd-timer|launchctl|schtasks` — launchd on macOS (so credentials/API keys resolve — the documented reason to avoid cron there), schtasks on Windows, systemd-timer-else-cron on Linux. Register hourly/daily/weekly timers, random minute per client (avoid fleet stampede on the shared remote), full binary path baked in, and split `register` (config-only) from `start` (installs timers).

## Why deferred
Prove the daemon-free Tier-1 model works first. Tier 2 is the most code (four-backend abstraction) for the narrowest case (dormant repos).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar maintenance start` registers a recurring enrichment drain via the platform-appropriate scheduler (launchd/schtasks/systemd-timer/cron, `auto`-selected).
- [ ] hourly/daily/weekly timers, random minute per client, absolute binary path baked in.
- [ ] `register` (config-only) vs `start` (installs timers) are separate; a `stop`/`unregister` cleanly removes them.
- [ ] macOS uses launchd (not cron) so the drain can resolve the API key.
baseline.summary: Tier-2: native cross-platform scheduler registration for the enrichment drain

baseline.description:
## Problem

A completion criterion backed by a file that genuinely exists can be banked met=false because the verifier never obtains that file.

`src/rebar/llm/completion_tool_policy.py` (origin/main) enforces **one governed action per model response**: line 124 holds `acted_steps: set[int]`, and lines 152-156 claim the step before dispatch — the first governed call in a response wins, and every other governed call in the same response returns `COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE` (line 154) **without being executed**. Nothing re-executes the loser and nothing carries its result forward.

The cost is not one round trip, it is the criterion's evidence: the finite boundary at lines 166-172 counts **responses** (`current_evidence_steps`, line 162), so a response whose only useful call was suppressed still burns one of the three. Three such responses bank `met=false` via `BOUNDED_FALLBACK_EVIDENCE` against a file that is present and correct.

## Evidence this is real (99d3 disproof rig, artifacts on 99d3)

Oracle 2 ran the **unmodified shipped policy** — no injection — over a six-criterion manifest against a disposable fixture in which every criterion is genuinely TRUE. In **4/4 trials** the model batched at run_step 1, a `read_file` for the c1 target lost the batch, and c1 was banked `met=false` carrying the bounded-fallback evidence string. Oracle 4 showed the benign contrast: when alternative tools still work the model recovers unaided (3/3 met=true), which is why the defect is intermittent in production rather than constant.

## Constraint on the fix (measured counter-evidence)

Rewording the notice to instruct a retry was tested and **regressed**: suppressed-call counts rose 6 -> 12 -> 49 across matched trials and one trial died `UsageLimitExceeded` with no verdict recorded at all. Any remedy that depends on the model *choosing* to re-issue inherits that risk. The remedy must be mechanical.

## Approach

Make the mutual exclusion **per kind, not per response**. The invariant that actually protects the design is that a verdict record must not share a response with evidence gathering (COMMIT discipline) — not that two read-only file reads must not share one. Concretely, replace the `acted_steps: set[int]` claim with a per-step *kind* claim:

- A response's first governed call claims the step as `evidence` or `record`.
- Further **evidence** calls in a step already claimed as `evidence` **execute normally** and
  return real repository content.
- A **record** in a step claimed by anything, and **evidence** in a step claimed by a
  `record`, keep returning `COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE` exactly as today.

This is the limiting case of "re-execute the suppressed call": the call is never suppressed, so recovery costs **zero** extra round trips rather than one. The finite boundary is untouched — `current_evidence_steps` is a set of steps, so N evidence calls in one response still consume exactly one evidence response. No prompt text, tool schema, notice constant, workflow key, or public surface changes; `COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE` keeps its current wording so the measured retry-storm lever is not pulled.

## Experimental protocol (results recorded as a ticket comment before landing)

Two arms on the identical Oracle-2 rig (real policy, real `pai_tools.filesystem_tools`, real `completion_verifier.md`, bedrock sonnet-4-6, temperature 0.0), differing only in which `src` tree is imported:

- Arm A = origin/main policy (baseline). Arm B = patched policy.
- N=4 trials per arm. Per trial record: governed call count, suppressed count, run steps,
  verdicts, and any criterion banked `met=false`.
- The fix is proven only if Arm B eliminates the false `met=false` on c1 while its governed
  call count and step count do not exceed Arm A's, and no trial exhausts its budget.

If the experiment does not show that, the change is not landed and the outcome is recorded here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A held-out live oracle running the **unmodified** shipped policy reproduces a criterion
      banked `met=false` whose backing file exists and satisfies it, caused solely by a
      governed evidence call that lost its response batch (baseline arm, >=4/4 trials).
- [x] With the change, the same oracle on the same fixture banks that criterion `met=true` in
      every trial (>=4/4), citing real file content.
- [x] Arm B's mean governed-call count and mean run-step count are **not greater** than Arm A's,
      and no Arm B trial raises `UsageLimitExceeded`.
- [x] A deterministic unit test (no LLM) asserts that two `read_file` calls in one `run_step`
      both return real content, that `record_criterion_verdict` sharing a step with evidence
      still receives `COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE`, that evidence sharing a step with a record still
      receives it, and that N evidence calls in one step consume exactly one of the three
      evidence responses.
- [x] `COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE`, `BOUNDED_FALLBACK_EVIDENCE`, `BOUNDED_FALLBACK_NOTICE`,
      `ALL_CRITERIA_BANKED_NOTICE`, the tool schemas, the reviewer prompt, and the CLI/MCP/
      library surfaces are unchanged.
- [x] Existing completion tests, lint, typecheck, and full CI pass.
baseline.summary: Completion verifier false unmet: suppressed governed read is never recovered

## Context
RP-01 proposes replacing Rebar’s bespoke structured-output orchestration with authoritative Pydantic AI seams. The replacement is not behavior-preserving by default: historical bugs encode hard-won behavior around deterministic repair and extraction, refusal/truncation handling, retry and tool/request limits, per-operation output budgets, provider fallback, usage accounting, telemetry, and failure taxonomy. Before RP-01 can be approved or ticketized, reconstruct the behavioral contract from both ticket history and the existing test suite and exercise the worktree virtualenv’s resolved Pydantic AI distribution. A behavior may be preserved or intentionally changed, but no observed delta may be accidental or left to the implementer.

The checkout-local probe path is `.joe-janitor/rp01-pydantic-native-probe.py`. The entire `.joe-janitor/` archive is intentionally excluded from repository snapshots, so an attested-source reviewer cannot see this path; use the existing local file when present and create it at that exact path if absent. The worktree virtualenv resolves `pydantic-ai-slim` to exactly 1.107.2, verified with `python -c "import importlib.metadata; print(importlib.metadata.version('pydantic-ai-slim'))"`; the probe must print and record that resolved version rather than infer it from the repository’s `>=1.107,<2` range.

## Plan
- Deduplicate ticket-derived scenarios with behavioral cases from the structured runner, failure-matrix, budget, timeout, and agent-call seam test suites.
- Record each scenario’s current observable behavior and its authoritative ticket/test evidence.
- Continue or create the checkout-local `.joe-janitor/rp01-pydantic-native-probe.py` to exercise Pydantic AI 1.107.2 native output, prompted output, output retry, usage limits, FallbackModel predicates, provider errors, truncation/refusal, telemetry, and artifact-capture feasibility without live model calls.
- Classify each scenario as preserve, intentionally change, or requiring an explicit maintainer decision; do not infer an invariant from the current implementation alone.
- Record the resulting evidence and experiment outputs in the local `.joe-janitor/` recovery archive and summarize the decision matrix on this ticket.

## Verification
This is an investigation task. The behavior-crossing tier is an in-process integration probe using the real Pydantic AI 1.107.2 Agent/FunctionModel/output/limits/hooks seams while mocking only provider transport. The oracle is the exact call count, request mode, accepted semantic output, exception class, usage/accounting fields, and captured telemetry for each predeclared scenario. Existing unit tests provide the current-Rebar side of the comparison. Run the probe with `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python .joe-janitor/rp01-pydantic-native-probe.py`; it must report the resolved `pydantic-ai-slim` version as 1.107.2 before its scenario results.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] [operator-attested] The matrix maps every material ticket-derived scenario to exact ticket aliases.
- [x] [operator-attested] The matrix maps every material test-derived scenario to exact test nodes or source locations.
- [x] [operator-attested] The matrix states current Rebar behavior for every scenario.
- [x] [operator-attested] The matrix states observed Pydantic AI 1.107.2 behavior for every exercised scenario.
- [x] [operator-attested] Every outcome difference is labeled preserve, intentionally change, or explicit decision required; no difference is silently inherited from either implementation.
- [x] [operator-attested] The offline probe executes the real Pydantic AI output/retry/fallback/limits/hook seams and records exact observable oracles without a live model call.
- [x] [operator-attested] The RP-01 research note is stored under `.joe-janitor/` beside the recovered janitor report.

  provenance: environment=local-checkout-b0aac2314; principal=joeoakhart@navapbc.com; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — Read back the ticket comment and compare each recorded artifact path, command result, coverage total, and decision against the local research note.

## Context
The rolling 5-of-10 breaker counts low-level noise and cannot distinguish an exhausted logical operation from its physical attempts. The approved replacement must stop only demonstrably unhealthy scopes without terminating work that historical jobs completed.

## Outcome
Implement an endpoint/provider finite-pass fuse over normalized coordinator outcomes. Endpoint opens after three consecutive eligible exhausted logical outcomes across at least two tickets; provider additionally requires two endpoint families. Matching success resets consecutive state.

## Plan
1. Count only exhausted logical outcomes eligible under the failure policy. Never count physical attempts, recovered warnings, permanent failures, ticket-local 404s, or opaque diagnostic text.
2. Track endpoint consecutive outcomes and distinct tickets. Track provider scope only when failures span two endpoint families.
3. Reset matching consecutive state on success; independent scopes retain their own state and continue.
4. Preserve direct authoritative credential, configuration, quota, rate, issue, endpoint, tenant, provider, and global stop/defer behavior without inferring scope from text.
5. When open, return explicit scope/reason/`retry_not_before` metadata; do not execute matching remaining plans.

## Testing
Sequence tables pin threshold boundaries, exclusions, reset, two-ticket/two-family requirements, and independent scopes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Endpoint fuse opens only after three consecutive eligible exhausted outcomes across at least two tickets.
- [ ] Provider fuse additionally requires two endpoint families.
- [ ] A matching success resets the consecutive state.
- [ ] Physical attempts, recovered warnings, permanent failures, ticket-local 404s, and opaque diagnostics never increment inferred counters.
- [ ] Independent scopes continue when another scope opens.
- [ ] Open-fuse outcomes include exact scope, reason, and `retry_not_before`.

## Out of scope
Production routing, batch tallies, and historical replay integration.
baseline.summary: RP-03 S3 T2 — Implement the scoped finite-pass fuse

baseline.description:
## Context
A first-class `identity` entity on rebar's event machinery, modeled on the `session_log` / `code_review` exemption pattern: gate / lifecycle / graph / Jira-sync exempt. It holds a display name, an email, a list of provider mappings, and a list of public keys, keyed by an opaque rebar ticket id. This is the foundational data structure the rest of the epic builds on (event `author_id`, authorship attestations, key-rotation eras, Jira accountId mapping).

## Why
Authorship certification and provider-neutral user mapping both need one durable home for "who a contributor is" that is not itself dispatchable work. Reusing the ticket substrate (like `session_log`) gives event-sourcing, replication, and `show`/`search` for free without polluting the dependency graph or Jira sync.

## What
Introduce `identity` as a new exempt ticket-type, a create path, and a self-identity config pointer.

### 1. Register `identity` as an exempt ticket-type (mirror session_log/code_review)
Add the type at EVERY site the existing exempt types appear (grounded, verified file:line list — omitting any one leaves a seam silently un-patched):
- `src/rebar/schemas/common.schema.json` `$defs/ticket_type` enum — SOURCE OF TRUTH.
- `src/rebar/types.py` is GENERATED — regenerate via `python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types`
  (never hand-edit); confirm `TicketType` now includes `identity`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:34` `_TYPES` tuple (accepts `create`), AND
  `:41` `_FILE_IMPACT_EXEMPT_TYPES` (so create emits no spurious no-file_impact nudge).
- `src/rebar/reducer/_api.py:23` `_NON_GRAPH_ARTIFACT_TYPES` (drop from graph/health).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/config.py:13` `EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES`.
- `src/rebar/_engine_support/gates.py:26` `_GATE_EXEMPT_TYPES` (the shared constant
  the three per-ticket gates check_ac/clarity_check/quality_check consult).
- `src/rebar/_commands/gates.py:118` inline `("bug","session_log","code_review")`
  tuple in `claim_gate_check()` (the plan-review START-WORK gate on claim/transition).
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:99` inline `("session_log","code_review")`
  tuple in the completion-verification close-gate pre-check.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:563` inline drift_refresh guard AND the
  `workflow_ops.py:79` exempt tuple.
None of these inline tuples delegate to `_NON_GRAPH_ARTIFACT_TYPES`, so each is a discrete edit. Excluded from `ready`/`next_batch`/default `list` follows structurally from the graph exemption (same mechanism as `session_log`). Recommended: where practical, route the new inline tuples through one shared constant to prevent future drift (implementer's discretion; not required by AC).

### 2. Create path (`rebar identity create` + library + MCP)
A single CREATE event mints an identity carrying:
- `name`: str (display name)   - `email`: str
- `mappings`: list of `{"provider": str, "external_id": str}`. `provider` is an
  OPEN lowercase-string vocabulary (well-known `jira`/`github`/`gitea`; not a
  closed enum). `external_id` is the provider's opaque stable id (NEVER an email).
  CLI: repeatable `--mapping <provider>:<external_id>` (first colon splits;
  `external_id` may contain colons).
- `keys`: list of OpenSSH authorized-keys public-key line strings
  (`"ssh-ed25519 AAAA..."`). The key-type is embedded in the line itself; NO
  separate `algorithm` field (avoids duplicating/desyncing it). The foundation
  attest scheme name is `sshsig`; the key-type token is parsed from the line by
  downstream verify (bde5).
`show` renders name/email/mappings/keys. (The provider vocabulary and authorized-keys key format are recorded as an ADR in sibling task 4b5b; this ticket adopts the above defaults.)

### 3. Self-identity config pointer (`.rebar/current_identity`)
- **Path**: `.rebar/current_identity` (`.rebar/` is already git-ignored via
  `.gitignore:11`; mirrors `.rebar/current_session_log`, see
  `src/rebar/_commands/session_log.py`). No gitignore edit needed.
- **Format**: JSON `{"identity_id": "<ticket_id>"}` (extra keys tolerated).
- **Write path**: `rebar identity use <id>` writes the pointer; `rebar identity
  create --self` writes it to the just-created identity in the same invocation.
- **Resolution — `resolve_current_identity() -> Optional[str]`**:
  1. Pointer file present AND names an existing `identity` ticket -> that id.
  2. Else match `git config user.email` (exact, case-insensitive) vs identity
     `email` fields.
- **Fallbacks (all return `None`; identity is opt-in so unauthenticated is a
  valid state, never an error)**: git email unset/unconfigured -> `None`;
  the `git config` subprocess errors (git missing, OSError, non-zero exit,
  timeout) -> `None` (caught, not propagated); zero identities match -> `None`;
  >=2 match -> `None` + a WARNING naming the ambiguity; pointer names a
  deleted/absent identity -> fall through to git-email match, else `None`.
- **Export side-effect (accepted)**: adding `identity` to
  `_NON_GRAPH_ARTIFACT_TYPES` hides identity tickets from default NDJSON export,
  opt-in via the existing `--include-session-logs` flag — same posture as
  `session_log`; acceptable for this ticket (no new flag).

## Scope
In: type registration at all listed sites, the create path (CLI/lib/MCP), `show` rendering, the pointer write + resolver + fallbacks. Out: event `author_id` (4e9d), authorship signing (bde5), key rotation (e165), Jira mapping (264f/2f13), enforcement (3183).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `identity` is registered at all listed sites and is exempt from
  lifecycle/gates/graph/Jira-sync (mirrors session_log); a test asserts an
  `identity` ticket is absent from `ready`/`next_batch`/default `list` and that
  `check_ac`/`clarity_check`/`quality_check` return pass for it.
- [ ] A create path (`rebar identity create` + `rebar.create_identity` + MCP)
  mints an identity in one CREATE carrying name, email, mappings, keys; a test
  round-trips create then asserts `rebar show <id> --output llm` (structured
  JSON) contains all four fields with the created values.
- [ ] `resolve_current_identity(*, repo_root=None) -> str | None` (keyword-only `repo_root`) reads `.rebar/current_identity`
  (`{"identity_id": ...}`) when present, else matches `git config user.email`
  case-insensitively; a test asserts (a) pointer hit, (b) git-email default hit,
  (c) each fallback (no email / subprocess error / zero match / multiple match /
  dangling pointer) returns `None` without raising.

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/schemas/common.schema.json`, `src/rebar/types.py` (regenerated)
- `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py` (_TYPES + _FILE_IMPACT_EXEMPT_TYPES + create)
- `src/rebar/reducer/_api.py`, `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/config.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine_support/gates.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/gates.py`,
  `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py`
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py` + `workflow_ops.py`
- new identity module (create path + resolver) + CLI/lib/MCP wiring
baseline.summary: identity: `identity` entity + ticket-type (attributes, exemptions, creation)

# Adopt the DCO: declarative Gerrit enforcement, contributor docs, agent sign-off policy

## Why

rebar has no inbound-IP mechanism (no DCO, no CLA). Both external reports and peer convergence recommend DCO over CLA: Qt's CLA is the stated reason it cannot accept PRs, and OpenStack replaced its CLA with the DCO for all contributions (TC resolution 2025-05-20, https://governance.openstack.org/tc/resolutions/20250520-replace-the-cla-with-dco-for-all-contributions.html) explicitly to lower the barrier, directing enforcement into Gerrit itself — the server rejects an unsigned push at `refs/for/*` time, zero new infrastructure. Gerrit documents `receive.requireSignedOffBy` as a per-project `project.config` key (https://gerrit-review.googlesource.com/Documentation/config-project-config.html#receive.requireSignedOffBy — inheritable, NOT site-only); live verification below guards against placement surprises anyway.

Sequencing note (resolves the file-existence review findings): `docs/your-first-change.md` does not exist at plan time — it is created by story **fat-leaflike-canary**, which this story `depends_on` (edge recorded in the store). Every edit this story makes to that file executes only after that story lands; in dependency order the target exists.

## What

- **Declarative config path (never a manual push):** add `requireSignedOffBy = true` to the `[receive]` section of `infra/gerrit/project.config` and roll out via the existing `setup-project.sh` flow to `refs/meta/config` (JoeOakhartNava admin identity). Rationale: `setup-project.sh` overwrites `project.config` on every run; a one-off manual push would be silently reverted. **Rollback:** revert the line, re-run `setup-project.sh` — documented in a comment beside the key.
- **Two distinct sign-off rules (resolves the identity-mismatch finding):**
  1. **Agent commits (RebarBotNava / `joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com` committer):** trailer is exactly `Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart <joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com>` — the responsible human's real name with his registered plus-addressed mailbox (routes to the human; kernel practice accepts plus-addresses; the certifier is the human, satisfying DCO 1.1). Documented in CLAUDE.md's commit guidance verbatim.
  2. **e2e test scripts** (`infra/gerrit/reviewbot-e2e.sh`, `infra/gerrit/feature-branch-e2e.sh`, `infra/gerrit/feature-branch-e2e-scenarios.sh` — all push to `refs/for/*` and would be rejected post-flip): each script adds `-s` to its `git commit` invocations so the sign-off is the script's OWN configured test identity (a hardcoded human trailer would mismatch the test committer). No other trailer engineering.
- **Automation inventory (decision rule):** enumerate commit-creating automation with `rg -l "git commit" infra/ scripts/ .github/ Makefile` at execution; the three e2e scripts above are the known set; anything newly found is updated the same way (add `-s`) or ticketed via discovered_from.
- CONTRIBUTING.md "Sign your work (DCO)" section, moby/Docker template (https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md "Sign your work"): link developercertificate.org, show the trailer, `git commit -s`, real-name requirement, push-time rejection note, Envoy-style "fixing DCO" note (amend/rebase re-signing), the shepherded-patch two-trailer rule (contributor's own sign-off required in the patch; shepherd adds theirs on amend — coordinated with the PR-posture story), **and a one-line CLA decision record: "rebar uses the DCO, not a CLA; a CLA would be adopted only if Nava counsel requires rights beyond Apache-2.0 §5 + DCO"** (the durable in-repo record of that decision).
- Cross-link retarget INTO `docs/your-first-change.md` (after fat-leaflike-canary lands — see sequencing note): point the tutorial's interim developercertificate.org link at the new CONTRIBUTING DCO section.
- **Migration order (strict, and provable from git history, not tracker artifacts):** commits land in this order — (1) docs (CONTRIBUTING/CLAUDE.md/tutorial retarget); (2) e2e-script `-s` fixes; (3) the `infra/gerrit/project.config` flag + `setup-project.sh` rollout. Because all three are commits in this repo, the order is verifiable post-hoc: the commit touching `infra/gerrit/project.config` must be a descendant of the commits touching the e2e scripts and docs (`git log --oneline -- <path>` comparison). No window where agent/bot pushes fail.
- **Post-flip failure runbook** (one paragraph in the CONTRIBUTING DCO section): rejected push → `git commit --amend -s --no-edit`, re-push; agent-tooling regression → roll back the flag while fixing.
- Flip GitHub's "require sign-off on web-based commits" on the mirror (one settings toggle; belt-and-braces).
- Peer-norm citation for the human-signs policy: Kubernetes AI-review governance (https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/github-management/ai-code-review-tools.md) — cited as supporting practice, not load-bearing authority (the policy stands on DCO 1.1's own terms).

## Scope

IN: `infra/gerrit/project.config` + setup-project.sh rollout, rollback note, CONTRIBUTING.md DCO section (incl. CLA record + failure runbook), CLAUDE.md agent-trailer guidance, e2e-script `-s` fixes, tutorial cross-link retarget (post-dependency), GitHub web-signoff toggle, live verification. OUT: CLA machinery; the probot/dco GitHub app (acts on PR checks; PRs here are answered/closed by the lockdown workflow the PR-posture story lands); retrofitting existing history (DCO applies to new commits only — kernel/OpenStack precedent); CLAUDE.local.md (gitignored, not a reviewable artifact).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Config flag present and rolled out — prove: `grep -A5 "\[receive\]" infra/gerrit/project.config | grep -q "requireSignedOffBy = true"`; the rollback note exists — prove: `grep -qi "rollback" infra/gerrit/project.config`.
- [ ] Live verification: an unsigned push to `refs/for/main` is rejected (server message captured in the commit message or a `docs/` note) and the same commit re-pushed after `git commit --amend -s` is accepted.
- [ ] e2e scripts sign their commits — prove, per file: `grep -q "commit .*-s\b\|commit -s" infra/gerrit/reviewbot-e2e.sh`; same grep for `infra/gerrit/feature-branch-e2e.sh` and `infra/gerrit/feature-branch-e2e-scenarios.sh` (three separate checks); one e2e suite run passes post-flip.
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md DCO section — prove: `grep -q "developercertificate.org" CONTRIBUTING.md`; `grep -q "commit -s" CONTRIBUTING.md`; `grep -qi "not a CLA" CONTRIBUTING.md` (the CLA decision record); `grep -qi "amend" CONTRIBUTING.md` (fix-up/runbook).
- [ ] CLAUDE.md names the exact agent trailer — prove: `grep -q "Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart <joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com>" CLAUDE.md`.
- [ ] Migration order provable from history — prove: the commit touching `infra/gerrit/project.config` is a descendant of the latest commits touching the three e2e scripts and the CONTRIBUTING DCO section (compare `git log` for the paths).
- [ ] Tutorial retarget done after dependency — prove: `grep -q "Sign your work\|DCO" docs/your-first-change.md` links the CONTRIBUTING section (executes post fat-leaflike-canary).
- [ ] GitHub web-signoff on — prove: `gh api repos/navapbc/rebar --jq .web_commit_signoff_required` = true.
baseline.summary: Adopt the DCO: Gerrit server-side enforcement, contributor docs, agent sign-off policy

## Why
rebar records cross-cutting review-gate design in ADRs (plan-review's novelty rising floor is ADR 0008). The code-review novelty convergence mechanism — its divergence from plan-review (per-citation region gate; typed local/Gerrit keyspaces; content-addressed resilient region detection), the reuse boundary (shared kernel primitives vs gate-specific orchestration), and the deliberate NON-additions — needs a durable ADR + docs so future work does not re-litigate or accidentally fork the novelty definition.

## What
Write **`docs/adr/0037-code-review-novelty-convergence.md`** (status Accepted — it documents DECISIONS that are IMPLEMENTED on this epic's stack) and cross-link the docs. The ADR documents, each citing its backing implementation module so a reader can verify it:

- **Reuse the novelty sub-call + `rising_floor_drop`** — the shared kernel primitives
  (`review_kernel.verify.novelty_model` / `NOVELTY_SUBANSWERS` / `reshape_novelties`,
  `review_kernel.decide.novelty` / `rising_floor_drop`) reused UNCHANGED. Code-review-specific
  orchestration: `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py::score_code_novelty` +
  `apply_region_gated_floor`, the `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code_review_novelty.md` prompt + the
  `code-novelty` reviewer id, and the `code_review_novelty` contract registered in
  `src/rebar/llm/code_review/contracts.py`.
- **The new `region_gated_floor` conjunct + its tri-state fail-safe (UNKNOWN == raise)** —
  `src/rebar/llm/code_review/region_gate.py` (constants `REGION_UNCHANGED` / `REGION_CHANGED` /
  `REGION_UNKNOWN` + the detector); the floor drops iff `rising_floor_drop(...)` AND region is
  `REGION_UNCHANGED`, and CHANGED/UNKNOWN always raise (fail-safe direction).
- **Surfaced-only prior set** — the reader `latest_code_review_result`
  (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py`) returns only the persisted `blocking` + `advisory`
  buckets, so a dropped finding never re-enters the novelty prior set (the code-review counterpart
  of child c3e4 / bug old-frilly-plankton).
- **Permanent low-impact drop = the intended compromise; the priority floor is the escape hatch.**
  Define "permanent" PRECISELY: the drop persists across RE-REVIEWS FOR THE SAME KEY (session or
  change) — it does NOT reset per review the way plan-review's floor re-scores each run — because
  the surfaced-only reader excludes a dropped finding from the prior set, so on recurrence it scores
  as NOVEL and is dropped again (as long as it stays low-priority + region-unchanged). Permanence is
  WITHIN one keyspace, not cross-key. The priority floor (`verify.novelty_priority_floor`) is the
  escape hatch: a higher-impact finding is never eligible, so it keeps surfacing. Trust the priority
  score — no categorical criterion exemption.
- **Typed session/change keyspaces, and why local must NOT seed a change's first Gerrit review** —
  `session:<id>` (local, `code-review: session:{id}`) vs `change:<id>` (Gerrit,
  `code-review: {change_id} @ {revision}`); the reader (`latest_code_review_result`) matches only
  its own title scheme, so the keyspaces are disjoint and a prior LOCAL review can never seed a
  change's FIRST Gerrit review.
- **Content-addressed region detection and its resilience to rebase/force-push** — the artifact
  stores `{path: sha256}` (reusing `plan_review.attest._hash_file`, computed in
  `code_review/sidecar.py::reviewed_file_hashes`); comparison keys on CONTENT, not a reachable
  commit, so it survives a rebase/force-push. File-level in v1; line-level deferred.
- **Explicit NON-additions (AC2).** Record the decision to add NO "dso-style
  arbiter/relation-taxonomy/oscillation-loop", DEFINING those terms inline so the rejection is
  evaluable: a **DSO-style arbiter** = a standalone decision/signal orchestrator that ADJUDICATES
  between competing findings/signals; a **relation-taxonomy** = a typed model of relationships
  BETWEEN findings (duplicates/supersedes/refines/…); an **oscillation-loop** = a detector that
  tracks a finding surfacing→dropping→resurfacing across runs to break cycles. The ADR records WHY
  the lightweight novelty floor suffices instead: a permanent, priority-gated drop of novel
  low-impact findings on unchanged regions monotonically narrows the surfaced set across
  patchsets without modeling oscillation or inter-finding relationships — so the heavier machinery
  buys no demonstrated benefit for added failure modes. This positively discharges the epic's
  original oscillation/convergence-signal criterion as a DESIGN decision, not a deferral.

Also update the docs to cross-link: **`docs/review-kernel.md`** (its "Code-review consumer" section — documenting the novelty convergence behavior: carryover labeling, region-gated drop, keying, resilience) and **`docs/reuse-surface.md`** (pointing the shared kernel primitives at the code-review-specific region-gate seam).

## Scope
- `docs/adr/0037-code-review-novelty-convergence.md` (NEW), `docs/review-kernel.md` (the
  "Code-review consumer" section — the code-review gate doc), and `docs/reuse-surface.md`.
- Documents the IMPLEMENTED behavior landed by c639 / 3bff / e51b + the c3e4 surfaced-only fix.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] ADR 0037 captures the design decisions above, INCLUDING the deliberate divergence from
      plan-review's whole-artifact floor (the per-citation region gate), each element citing its
      backing implementation module.
- [ ] ADR 0037 records the explicit decision to add NO dso-style arbiter / relation-taxonomy /
      oscillation-loop (terms DEFINED inline) and why the lightweight novelty floor suffices.
- [ ] ADR 0037 defines "permanent" drop precisely (within-key, via the surfaced-only prior set) and
      how it diverges from plan-review's per-review re-scoring.
- [ ] `docs/review-kernel.md` (Code-review consumer section) documents the novelty convergence
      behavior (carryover labeling, region-gated drop, keying, resilience).
- [ ] The docs cross-link the shared kernel primitives vs the code-review-specific region gate
      (`docs/reuse-surface.md`).
baseline.summary: ADR + docs: code-review novelty convergence (mirror plan-review ADR 0008)

## Evidence — reproduced, not inferred

`fetcher._iter_pages` (the pager behind `fetcher.collect`, which builds the INBOUND SNAPSHOT the entire inbound differ runs on) terminates on a SHORT page and advances by the REQUESTED page size:

    src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py:324-326
        if len(page) < page_size:
            return
        start_at += page_size

Jira Data Center silently truncates `maxResults` when it exceeds `jira.search.views.default.max` — a common hardening, and the same server behaviour already established for this codebase when the identical defect was fixed in `get_parent_map` (change 1105). A truncated FIRST page therefore reads as "that is all there is".

Measured against a client that serves 250 issues but caps every page at 20 (default `page_size=100`):

    issues recovered: 20 of 250
    CONFIRMED DEFECT: 230 issues (92%) silently lost from the inbound snapshot

## Why this is more serious than its two siblings

This is the THIRD instance of one defect class. The first was `get_parent_map` (fixed, change 1105). The second is [rebar:9263-b404-cb6c-463f] — `get_issuelinks_map` / `get_comment_map`, which lose links and comments. This one loses THE ISSUES THEMSELVES.

`collect()` feeds `_build_snapshot`, so a truncated read is not a missing attribute on a present issue — it is an issue the pass never sees at all. Every unseen bound issue is a candidate for the absence/deletion path, and every unseen unbound issue simply fails to reconcile. A run in that state reports success: it raises nothing, and "converged" is true of the 8% it looked at.

## Blast radius — wider than the DC adapter, which is why this is NOT folded into 9263

9263 is confined to `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py`. This is CORE `fetcher.py`, on the shared inbound path, so a change here reaches the live Cloud bridge as well as DC. That is a different risk profile and deserves its own review and its own live verification rather than riding along on an adapter-local fix.

Cloud reaches the same lines but is not known to be affected in practice: its ceiling and `same-token-twice` cursor-stall guards target a different truncation mode, and no short-page truncation has been observed there. The fix must therefore be verified as SAFE FOR CLOUD, not merely correct for DC.

## Approach

Advance by `len(page)` and terminate only on an EMPTY page — the same correction already applied to `get_parent_map`, whose docstring records the reasoning.

One thing the `get_parent_map` fix did not have to handle and this one does: `_iter_pages` must not spin forever if a server ignores `startAt` and returns the same non-empty page indefinitely. The existing `same-token-twice` guard covers the Cloud CURSOR stall, not an OFFSET stall. Add an offset-stall guard that raises `SilentTruncationError` (the type this function already raises for truncation it refuses to hide) rather than looping.

`cap` and ceiling semantics are unchanged.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` — the pager's advance/terminate conditions, plus the
  offset-stall guard.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — held-out regression tests.

## Testing

- a client serving N issues while capping every page below the requested size yields ALL N (the
  reproduction above, which currently returns 20 of 250)
- an exactly-full final page followed by an empty page terminates without an extra spurious request
- a server that ignores `startAt` raises `SilentTruncationError` rather than looping forever
- `cap` still clips, and the ACLI ceiling still raises — asserted so the Cloud contract is pinned
  unchanged by this fix

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the 250-issue/20-cap reproduction recovers 250, asserted by a held-out unit test that FAILS on
      the current code
- [ ] termination is on an EMPTY page only, and the advance is by `len(page)` — read from the source
- [ ] a `startAt`-ignoring server raises `SilentTruncationError` instead of looping, asserted by test
      with a bounded-time guarantee
- [ ] the existing `cap`, ACLI-ceiling and `same-token-twice` behaviours are unchanged, each asserted
      by a test that exercises them — this touches the shared Cloud path, so "DC is fixed" is not
      sufficient evidence
- [ ] the full unit suite passes, and the live DC harness job stays green
baseline.summary: fetcher._iter_pages truncates the inbound snapshot on a short page: 92% of issues silently lost

## Summary
_has_rebar_id_label (binding_walk.py) matches ANY label with the rebar-id:/rebar-id- PREFIX, including a malformed empty 'rebar-id:' (no local id). The L10 adopt guard then stands down (treats it as identity-bound) and defers to binding-recovery — but with an empty id there is nothing to re-link, so the key is never adopted AND never bound, and bridge-fsck reports it as unbound_jira on every run. Surfaced by REB-659 (a manual 'assignee clobber' experiment carrying label 'rebar-id:'), which produced a perpetual bare-forge-tapir drift alert.

## Reproduction Steps
1. A Jira issue has label 'rebar-id:' (empty value) and no binding-store entry.
2. Run the binding walk / bridge-fsck.
3. The issue is neither adopted (L10 stands down) nor bound → perpetual unbound_jira drift.

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: an empty/malformed rebar-id: marker is treated as UNMARKED (adoptable), so the key adopts (create+bind) normally.
- Actual: the empty marker counts as a binding marker → adoption stands down → the key is stranded.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] _has_rebar_id_label returns True only for a WELL-FORMED marker (non-empty id after the prefix).
- [ ] A key with an empty 'rebar-id:' label is adopted (inbound create); a well-formed 'rebar-id:<id>' still stands down (no double-bind).
- [ ] Regression test in tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_binding_walk.py; reconciler suite green.
baseline.summary: reconciler: malformed empty rebar-id: marker traps a Jira issue in unbound-drift limbo

## What

`ruff check src tests` (the project's documented lint gate over the `E,F,W,I,UP,B` families, per `pyproject.toml [tool.ruff.lint]`) currently reports **29 errors** — the gate is RED. These are **pre-existing**, introduced by recent completion-verifier and sync-union work, NOT by the 2026-06-18 maintenance epic (every file the epic touched is ruff-clean). Discovered while verifying that epic.

## Reproduction Steps

```
ruff check src tests   # ruff 0.15.x
```

**Expected:** no errors (the docs describe the tree as clean for its own ruff gate). **Actual:** 29 errors — 24 `E501` (line-too-long), 2 `E731` (lambda-assignment), 2 `I001` (unsorted-imports), 1 `E402` (module-import-not-at-top).

## Affected files

- `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` (1 — E501)
- `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py` (1 — E402: the mid-file `import re as _re`)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound.py` (1 — E501 in the labels block)

- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py` (7)

- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_verify_completion_facades.py` (2)

  the E731 lambdas to defs).
- [ ] CI runs a ruff version consistent with what fixes were validated against (pin or

- [ ] No behavior change — lint-only.
</content>

## Context
ADR 0043 defines exactly two completion-evidence kinds: untagged acceptance criteria are codebase-verifiable, while criteria whose evidence inherently lives outside the repository must use the exact `[operator-attested]` tag. The current P6 deterministic lexicon only coaches on a subset of untagged operational phrases and cannot semantically inspect every criterion or detect an incorrectly applied tag. A1 `f7ee-572b-1eb0-4af8` demonstrated the gap: plan review passed a repo-level benchmark criterion without the required tag, then completion verification failed after the work was already merged.

## Approach
- Add an explicit plan-review criterion that evaluates every acceptance-criterion checkbox independently and classifies where its completion evidence can truthfully be verified.
- Preserve ADR 0043 fail-safe semantics: untagged and malformed tags remain codebase-verifiable; only the exact case-insensitive `[operator-attested]` token selects ticket-attestation evidence.
- Find both error directions: externally verifiable criteria missing the exact tag, and codebase-verifiable criteria incorrectly tagged operator-attested (which would weaken completion proof to a comment).
- Require evidence specific to the criterion, not keyword-only classification. Reuse the existing deterministic detector as candidate/coverage input where useful, but keep semantic judgment in the new criterion and leave the P6 lexicon fail-open/advisory.
- Route and document the criterion through the canonical registry, reviewer prompt/contract, criteria routing, generated criteria guide, and frozen evaluation corpus.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The new plan-review criterion visits every `- [ ]` / `- [x]` acceptance item and returns one of two evidence kinds, `codebase-verifiable` or `operator-attested`, with criterion-specific evidence for the classification. Tier: reviewer contract/unit test plus behavioral eval.
- [x] An inherently external criterion with no tag or a malformed near-miss produces a finding whose remediation names the exact `- [ ] [operator-attested] …` syntax; an exact tag on an external criterion is accepted. Tier: prompt-contract fixtures and behavioral eval.
- [x] A codebase-verifiable criterion carrying `[operator-attested]` produces a finding explaining that ticket comments cannot substitute for repository proof; the same criterion untagged is accepted. Tier: prompt-contract fixtures and behavioral eval.
- [x] A criterion that bundles repository proof and outside-world proof is not silently assigned one evidence kind: review tells the author to split it into independently certifiable criteria. Tier: behavioral eval with a mixed-evidence fixture.
- [x] High-confidence misclassification findings participate in the normal validity × impact blocking policy, while deterministic keyword detection remains advisory/fail-open and records abstentions. Tier: policy/registry unit tests.
- [x] Registry completeness, criteria routing, reviewer resources, generated `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md`, and author guidance describe the new check and ADR 0043 exact-tag semantics without drift. Verify with the repository generation/drift gates.
- [x] [operator-attested] A pinned multi-sample before/after evaluation over a frozen corpus that includes A1, the historical 115b/8c4f cases, codebase negatives, malformed tags, over-tagged code criteria, and mixed-evidence items meets these predeclared thresholds: 100% precision (zero false positives) on the genuine-external negative set; 100% recall on the named A1, 115b/8c4f, malformed-tag, and over-tagged-code fixtures; macro precision and recall ≥ 0.90 across the full frozen corpus; and no previously passing fixture regresses; record model/config, sample counts, per-class results, and the run artifact on this ticket.
      provenance: environment=rebar plan-review production-equivalent workflow at the ticket verified_at_sha; principal=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the frozen corpus runs through the same signed plan-review workflow and model/runtime configuration used by this repository gate
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `make test` pass, including focused tests proving the completion verifier still treats untagged criteria as codebase-verifiable and exact-tag criteria as operator-attested.

## Scope
Plan-review criterion and its tests/eval/documentation only. Do not broaden the completion verifier’s trust boundary or add external-service access.
baseline.summary: Validate acceptance-criteria evidence classification in plan review

## Context
The canonical audit run produced 11,480 passes but exposed two reproducible test-environment assumptions. tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py::test_shipped_surfaces_name_no_retired_bridge_command recursively UTF-8-decodes every file under src/rebar, including ignored editor_assets/node_modules binaries such as the Mach-O esbuild executable. tests/unit/test_attestation_signing.py::test_hook_falls_back_to_git_when_env_unset clones the current checkout and fails when it is a shallow promisor clone with unavailable historical objects. - Keep both tests behavioral: stale shipped command tokens and Git-fallback build provenance must still fail when broken.

- [x] The provenance fallback test does not depend on the audit checkout having a complete object database.

## Status — RESCOPED + CLOSED (operator-approved 2026-07-18)

This story is closed against a **rescoped** acceptance set. It had two separable halves:

1. **A DETERMINISTIC half — DESIGNED AND BUILT.** The stratified **sample**, the frozen
   **baseline**, the **FP-control pool**, the **replay driver** (clone + REVIEW_RESULT-strip +
   manifest seams), the **pure LLM-free metrics library**, and its **golden tests**. This lives as
   WIP in the `cal-e3` worktree on branch `calib/6982-e3` (`replay_candidate.py`, `e3_metrics.py`,
   `runs/e3/sample.jsonl`, `runs/e3/baseline.jsonl`, `runs/e3/fp_control_pool.jsonl`,
   `tests/unit/test_e3_metrics.py`). It is **not landed on main** — the driver's only runtime
   purpose is to drive the rejected batch (below), so landing it would ship a moot LLM-spend entry
   point. It is recorded here as documented WIP.

2. **An EXPENSIVE LLM BATCH REPLAY — PERMANENTLY REJECTED on cost, and SUPERSEDED.** The
   ~450-run live gate replay (the coarse ~200-ticket single sweep PLUS the precise ~50-ticket ×3
   candidate + ×3 current fresh runs, and the `raw_verdicts.jsonl` / `transition_matrix.json` /
   `criterion_deltas.jsonl` / `fp_control.json` they would emit) is **dropped**. It is superseded
   by story **d8a5** (change **#798, MERGED**): the standing per-criterion effectiveness recorder
   (`criterion_effectiveness.py`, on main), which accumulates the SAME detection / blocking-FP
   perturbation signal from real production reviews at **$0 marginal LLM cost**. Baseline **mining**
   is also dead: only ~4 `plan-v3` sidecar baselines exist against the ~200 needed — the
   `impact_model_version` bump stranded the history (which is exactly why a live replay, not a
   sidecar re-score, would have been required, and why the cost was unjustifiable).

The design record below (Why / definitions / mechanism) is retained as the account of what was
built; the Acceptance Criteria are rescoped to the delivered deterministic WIP only.

## Why

R1 (asserted-capability grounding probe) edits the Pass-1 finder rubric, so it changes what EVERY
plan review surfaces. Before any gate candidate is exposed to production, we must measure how much
it perturbs the verdicts of plans that already passed and closed cleanly. E3 was the counterfactual
replay that would produce that measurement; with E2 it was the evidence R1 is gated on.

The gate has a hard false-positive bar (`docs/research/task-decomposition-sota-2026.md` §5 / R1):
R1 FAILs if, on 30 sampled historical plans that PASSed and closed with zero post-claim edits,
>3/30 gain a new blocking finding, or the median new-advisory count rises by >1 per review; the
epic also reports a PASS→BLOCK flip rate ≤2% on the wider cleanly-closed sample.

**The design removes two confounds** (both verified in code): recall contamination (`review_plan`
re-surfaces a ticket's own prior findings via `prior_concerns`, which `emit_sidecar=False` does
not disable) and baseline drift + LLM nondeterminism. It does so with a **recall-stripped clone**
(copy the store, delete every `*-REVIEW_RESULT.json` under sampled tickets, run over the clone),
a **material-fingerprint drift guard**, and a **two-tier** structure: a coarse descriptive ~200
sweep, plus a precise 30-plan FP-control that replays BOTH the candidate and the current gate fresh
(N=3, two-level median, current-vs-current null floor) to isolate the candidate's true effect.

The deterministic pieces — the reproducible stratified sample, the frozen `plan-v3` baseline, the
over-sampled 50-ticket FP-control pool, the clone/strip/manifest driver seams, and the entire pure
`e3_metrics` library (`build_matrix`, `criterion_deltas`, `tkey`, `pass_to_block_flip_rate`,
`fp_control_eval`, `fp_control_valid`) — were completed and golden-tested offline.

**Why the batch was never worth its cost.** The only thing the ~450 live gate runs add is a
one-shot snapshot of one candidate's verdict perturbation — a signal d8a5's standing recorder now
produces continuously from real reviews for free, and which mining cannot reconstruct (the
`plan-v3` bump stranded the sidecar history to ~4 rows). The operator therefore rejected the batch
replay permanently and accepted the deterministic build as the deliverable.

## Scope (delivered as WIP on `calib/6982-e3`; NOT landed on main)

- `harnesses/replay_candidate.py` — driver (`sample` / `run` / `analyze` / `--verify`), incl. the
  clone + REVIEW_RESULT-strip + manifest seams. Its `sample`/`analyze`/metrics paths are offline;
  its live `run` gate replay is the rejected batch and is NOT to be executed.
- `harnesses/e3_metrics.py` — pure, LLM-free metrics library (golden-tested).
- `runs/e3/{sample.jsonl, baseline.jsonl, fp_control_pool.jsonl}` — deterministic sample + frozen
  baseline + over-sampled FP-control pool.
- `tests/unit/test_e3_metrics.py` — CI-collectable golden tests over synthetic fixtures (no LLM).
- README (E3 section) documenting the design as WIP + the batch deferral.
- NO `src/rebar` behavior change (E3 was measurement).

## Acceptance Criteria (rescoped — delivered deterministic WIP only)

- [ ] **Sample + frozen baseline BUILT and reproducible.** `runs/e3/sample.jsonl` (stratified,
  deterministic `random.Random(1729)`) satisfies the cleanly-closed filter on every row
  (`post_claim_edit_class=="none"` AND `reopen_count==0` AND `force_close==false`);
  `runs/e3/baseline.jsonl` carries a `plan-v3` `baseline_verdict ∈ {PASS,BLOCK}` +
  `material_fingerprint` per ticket; `runs/e3/fp_control_pool.jsonl` is the 50-ticket over-sampled
  FP-control pool. Built and verifiable in the `calib/6982-e3` worktree; deterministic (no LLM).
- [ ] **Pure metrics library BUILT + golden-tested.** `e3_metrics.py`'s `criterion_deltas`
  (COMPUTED `sidecar.norm_id` join), `tkey` (criteria-independent text key), `build_matrix`,
  `pass_to_block_flip_rate`, `fp_control_eval` (two-level-median candidate↔current pairing;
  `null_floor` current-vs-current; `r1_pass = new_blocking_median <= max(3, null_floor) AND
  new_advisory_median_delta <= 1`), and `fp_control_valid` (usable≥30 boundary) pass
  `pytest tests/unit/test_e3_metrics.py` offline (no LLM). Built as WIP on `calib/6982-e3`.
- [ ] **Replay driver seams BUILT.** `replay_candidate.py` implements the recall-stripped clone
  (copy store + delete `*-REVIEW_RESULT.json`), the material-fingerprint drift guard, the
  over-sampling ticket-drop rule, and the manifest/candidate-build-verification write. These seams
  are present and offline-exercisable (`sample`, `analyze --verify`); the live `run` gate replay is
  the deferred batch and is NOT executed. Verified by code inspection.
- [ ] **[operator-attested] Batch replay DEFERRED — permanently rejected on cost, superseded by
  d8a5.** The live ~450-run gate replay (coarse ~200 sweep + precise ~50×3 candidate + ~50×3
  current) and its `raw_verdicts.jsonl` / `transition_matrix.json` / `criterion_deltas.jsonl` /
  `fp_control.json` outputs are intentionally NOT produced. The verdict-perturbation signal they
  would have measured is now accumulated at $0 marginal LLM cost by d8a5's standing
  `criterion_effectiveness.py` recorder (change #798, MERGED, on main), and history-mining is dead
  (~4 `plan-v3` baselines vs ~200 needed). Evidence lives outside this codebase: operator decision
  2026-07-18 + d8a5 / change #798. This AC is closed by operator attestation, not machine check.
- [ ] **Design documented as WIP.** The README E3 section records the baseline source + chosen
  round, the cleanly-closed filter, the recall-strip + fresh-both-gates design, the
  material-fingerprint drift control, the two-tier nondeterminism/cost story, and the batch
  deferral + d8a5-supersession, so the WIP status and drop rationale are auditable.
baseline.summary: E3: counterfactual replay of gate candidates over ~200 historical reviews

## Context / Problem

The graph loader/BFS centralization (985c-32d2-e828-4e6a, Gerrit 1708, merged 1c3e945cb8) named two behaviours as explicit helpers that had previously been inline, and the rebar code-review bot flagged both as untested. The gaps are PRE-EXISTING — the same logic was uncovered while inline — but naming them made them visible. Nothing regresses today; the risk is that a future traversal or loader refactor silently drops either behaviour with the suite still green.

## Approach

Characterization tests ONLY — no `src/rebar` change. Follow the pattern of `test_get_all_blocked_by_accumulates_targets_without_a_ticket_dir` (added by 985c in `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_cycles.py`): assert the behaviour that exists today so the tests pin the contract rather than propose a new one. Each new test was validated by mutating the production branch locally, observing the test go red, and reverting — the mutation results are recorded per criterion below.

### Gap 1 — the cross-level traversal refusal (`rebar.graph._graph`)

`_same_level_neighbors` confines the walk with two separate guards. The CURRENT-side guard is an inline `state.get("ticket_type", "").lower() != level` early-return on the node being expanded (`_graph.py` L251). The TARGET-side guard is the single call to `_is_at_level`, on each candidate dep (`if target and target not in visited and _is_at_level(...)`, L257). Every existing `check_cycle_at_level` test in `test_graph_cycles.py` uses a single uniform level, so the target-side guard is never exercised.

The two guards are not interchangeable, and this dictates the test shape: for an `epic → task → epic` chain the inline CURRENT-side guard alone already stops the walk, so deleting the `_is_at_level` call leaves that case still returning False. The only mutation-sensitive probe is a DIRECT cross-level edge whose far end IS the queried `source_id`: `check_cycle_at_level("task-M", "epic-B", level="epic")` where `epic-B depends_on task-M`. Today `bfs` (in `rebar.graph._relations`) accumulates nothing, so the answer is False; with the target-side `_is_at_level` deleted, `task-M` is yielded and accumulated and the answer flips to True. Both shapes get a test: the direct one pins the guard, the `epic → task → epic` hop one pins the end-to-end "a lower-level hop cannot reconnect two same-level nodes" contract.

### Gap 2 — the three tombstone-loader branches (`rebar.graph._unblock`)

All three are driven through the public `detect_newly_unblocked`, not the private `_load_states_with_tombstones`. One shared fixture shape makes each branch observable: a target ticket carrying two `depends_on` LINK events (so the blocking edges live in the TARGET's dir and survive an unreducible blocker dir), one blocker closed by the batch and one blocker tombstoned. `_was_already_unblocked` then cannot short-circuit, so the verdict turns entirely on how the tombstoned blocker's status is loaded.

- (a) reduce-returns-None + tombstone present yields a status-only stub. Observable only when
  the recorded status is NON-terminal: with the stub the blocker reads `open` and the target
  is NOT newly unblocked; without it the blocker is absent and
  `_is_closed_after_batch`'s "missing dir → tombstoned, treat as closed" fallback unblocks
  the target. The test therefore uses a tombstone recording `open` — `_read_tombstone_status`
  takes `.get("status", "deleted")` verbatim with no validation, and that verbatim
  propagation is exactly what the test pins.
- (b) a present tombstone's status OVERRIDES the reduced status: an `open` blocker dir with a
  `{"status": "deleted"}` tombstone (the payload `rebar._commands.delete` writes) counts as
  closed and unblocks the target.
- (c) a malformed tombstone degrades to `deleted` rather than to "no tombstone": the same
  `open` blocker dir with unparseable tombstone bytes still counts as closed.

## Scope

- `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_cycles.py` — two tests for the level-confined traversal,
  reusing the existing `_helpers._make_ticket` / `_write_link_event` / `_get_check_cycle_at_level`.
- `tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py` — three tests, reusing the file's existing
  `_write_ticket` and `_write_depends_on_link` helpers. No new helper: `_write_ticket(deps=...)`
  is unusable here because it writes `blocks` links into the BLOCKER's dir, which an
  unreducible blocker dir cannot carry, but `_write_depends_on_link` already writes the LINK
  into the DEPENDENT's dir — exactly the shape these fixtures need.

No file under `src/rebar` is modified. If a test reveals a real defect, it is recorded and filed as a `discovered_from` bug rather than fixed here.

## Testing

The new tests ARE the deliverable; each is validated by mutation rather than by assertion of a guess:

- delete the `_is_at_level(...)` call from `_same_level_neighbors` → the direct
  cross-level test goes red (verified: verdict flips False → True).
- delete the `state is None` + tombstone stub branch → test (a) goes red (verified: `[]` →
  `['tkt-target']`).
- delete the `state["status"] = tombstone_status` override → test (b) goes red (verified:
  `['tkt-target']` → `[]`).
- make `_read_tombstone_status`'s `except` return `None` instead of `"deleted"` → test (c)
  goes red (verified: `['tkt-target']` → `[]`).

Edge/negative coverage inside the new tests: an unreducible ticket dir, unparseable tombstone bytes, and a cross-level dep that must NOT be traversed. No new production behaviour, so there is no happy path beyond the existing suite, which must stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_cycles.py` contains a test asserting
      `check_cycle_at_level("task-M", "epic-B", "epic", tracker) is False` for an
      `epic-B depends_on task-M` tracker; checked by deleting the `_is_at_level` call from
      `_same_level_neighbors` and observing that exact test fail, then reverting.
- [x] `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_cycles.py` contains a test asserting
      `check_cycle_at_level("epic-A", "epic-B", "epic", tracker) is False` for an
      `epic-B depends_on task-M depends_on epic-A` chain, so a lower-level hop cannot
      reconnect two same-level nodes; checked by running that test against the unmodified
      tree and seeing it pass.
- [x] `tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py` contains a test that fails when the
      `state is None` + tombstone-present stub branch of `_load_states_with_tombstones` is
      deleted; checked by that deletion + `pytest` on the single test, then reverting.
- [x] `tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py` contains a test that fails when the
      `state["status"] = tombstone_status` override is deleted; checked the same way.
- [x] `tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py` contains a test that fails when
      `_read_tombstone_status`'s exception handler stops returning `"deleted"`; checked the
      same way.
- [x] `git diff --name-only origin/main` lists only the two test files — no `src/rebar` path.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0, and
      `pytest tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_cycles.py tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py`
      is green.
baseline.summary: Cover graph traversal seams surfaced by the loader/BFS refactor
