# 209 of 213 by-path test loaders are not cache-first, on keys shared by up to 9 files

## Provenance

Measured by AST walk over `tests/` while auditing bug 2bc7 (which repaired three files sharing the `"mutation"` key). The audit's scope was that key; this is the surface it revealed.

```
total by-path loaders under tests/  : 213
using sys.modules.setdefault        :   0   (the original 9f0b/2bc7 defect is eradicated)
cache-first (name AND __file__)     :   4
```

The four are `test_differ.py`, `test_differ_conflict_resolution.py`, `test_differ_quarantine_suppression.py` (2bc7's three) and `test_reconcile_filter.py::_stub_modules`. 2bc7 additionally fixed `test_differ_emits_probe.py` and `test_apply_list_of_mutations.py`.

## The collision surface

`sys.modules` keys registered by more than one test file:

```
outbound_differ   9 files        mutation    6 files
inbound_differ    8 files        reconcile   4 files
differ            5 files        applier     3 files
```

**None** of the loaders for `outbound_differ`, `inbound_differ`, `reconcile` or `applier` validates `__file__`. The original bug surfaced on `mutation` only because that is where a cross-file `isinstance` assertion happened to exist — the same latent coupling sits on keys with more registrants and no such assertion to expose it.

## Why this is latent rather than broken

pytest executes module-by-module, so a file that overwrites a shared key is self-consistent while its own tests run: its module-scoped fixture was built when its registration was current. The failure needs two things to coincide — a cross-file identity comparison, and an execution order that puts the other registrant first. 2bc7 was exactly that coincidence, and it presented as a macOS-only `isinstance` failure on an object that WAS of the asserted class.

## What 2bc7 deliberately did not attempt

A shared helper, so the loader exists once. It is the right fix and it is not mechanical: the registrants span `diffing/`, `mutate/`, `apply/`, `state/`, `fetch/`, `conflict/` and `orchestrate/`, and pytest puts only each test's OWN directory on `sys.path`, so a bare-name import does not resolve across them. Two workable shapes, both with costs:

* a module at the `tests/` root plus the `sys.path` plumbing `tests/_engine_path.py` already
  establishes — works for every caller including module-level constants;
* a conftest FIXTURE — inherited by subdirectories automatically, but cannot serve the call sites that
  load at module scope, and several do.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ONE cache-first by-path loader exists, reachable from every directory under `tests/` that needs
      it, with the `sys.path` mechanism it depends on documented at its definition
- [ ] every loader registering a key that MORE THAN ONE file registers is converted to it — the
      `outbound_differ`, `inbound_differ`, `differ`, `mutation`, `reconcile` and `applier` keys at
      minimum
- [ ] a guard test fails when a new by-path loader registers a SHARED key without validating
      `__file__`, so the count cannot regress silently (the audit above was a one-off scan; a scan
      nobody re-runs is not a guard)
- [ ] loaders that deliberately want an ISOLATED copy keep it, and say so — `test_mutation.py`
      returns an unregistered private copy and `test_differ.py` registers
      `mutation_for_diff_purity` under a distinct name; both are correct and must not be swept into
      the shared helper
- [ ] the full suite passes under a REVERSED collection order for the affected directories, not just
      the default alphabetical one

## Not urgent, and why

Nothing fails today. This is a latent-coupling cleanup whose value is that the next instance fails locally and deterministically instead of as a platform-specific surprise in CI.
baseline.summary: 209 of 213 by-path test loaders are not cache-first, on sys.modules keys shared by up to 9 files

# Jira Server / Data Center support via a Jira-family seam (not a forked second adapter)

## Context / Problem

CMS and similar federal clients run **self-hosted Jira Data Center**, which rebar cannot reconcile against. DC differs from Cloud on three axes: REST v2 with wiki-markup/plain-text bodies instead of v3 + ADF, Personal Access Token bearer auth instead of the ACLI subprocess, and name-based user identity instead of `accountId`.

GitHub PR #120 proposed a second adapter package for this. It rides ADR 0035's `Backend` port correctly, but it reaches into `adapters/jira/` privates (`_map_local_to_jira_fields`, `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS`, `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_PRIORITY`, `_sanitize_label`, `_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK`, `classify_probe_response`) and forks `map_fields_to_remote` as a verbatim copy of `adapters/jira/backend.py:42-72` with one line changed. That creates a de facto "Jira family" layer with no contract: `adapters/jira/` becomes simultaneously a concrete backend and a shared library, with nothing pinning what is shared and nothing stopping a Cloud change from breaking DC.

## Approach

Make the Jira family an **explicit sub-seam** rather than an accident, in an order that never puts the live-validated Cloud path at risk.

1. **Freeze Cloud first.** Extend the existing held-out characterization tests
   (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_characterization.py`) to pin the current outputs of every unit
   about to move, so any behavior change during extraction fails a pinned oracle.
2. **Extract a `adapters/jira_family/` shared layer** — and re-point the Cloud adapter at it. Cloud's ACLI
   transport is not touched at all.

   **Only non-location-pinned symbols may physically move.** ADR 0035 §(a) pins `adf.py`,
   `outbound_fields.py`, and `comment_limits.py` as **Jira-coupled *and* location-pinned**: they are loaded by
   filename relative to `_PACKAGE_DIR` (via `_loader.lazy_load(` / `_load_sibling_keyed(` /
   `spec_from_file_location(`), so physically moving them breaks the dynamic loader unless the loader is taught
   the new sub-package in the same change — deferred to ADR 0035's Phase 2, explicitly **out of scope here**.
   **Location-pinned means "cannot change path" — NOT "cannot be edited."** Editing a pinned module's
   *contents* (e.g. replacing a dict literal with an import) is safe and is how the pinned units get
   single-sourced; only *relocating* the file breaks the loader.

   **Move by SYMBOL, not by file.** `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py` cannot relocate wholesale: it imports
   `fit_text_to_adf_limit` from the pinned `adf.py` (used by `_sanitize_description`) and
   `truncate_comment_body` / `_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS` from the pinned `comment_limits.py` (used by
   `_sanitize_comment`). Moving the whole file would point `jira_family/` at `adapters/jira/` — the exact
   dependency inversion the import contract in §6 forbids. So the file is split by symbol, and the two coupled
   sanitizers are **parameterized by the contracts this epic already introduces** rather than importing a
   vendor module: `_sanitize_description` takes the `RichTextCodec` (its `fit_text_to_adf_limit` call *is* the
   rich-text seam), and comment truncation takes the vendor's comment-limit/truncation contract. Cloud
   constructs those contract objects in `adapters/jira/` from its pinned `adf.py` / `comment_limits.py`; DC
   constructs wiki-markup/plain-text equivalents. `jira_family/` imports neither.

   Concretely, of the six symbols PR #120 reached for:
   - **Movable to `jira_family/` in this epic:** `_sanitize_label`, `_sanitize_summary`, `InvalidLabelError`,
     and `_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK` (all in `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py`, not location-pinned and not
     ADF/limit-coupled), `classify_probe_response` (`adapters/jira/probe.py`, not location-pinned), and the new
     `RichTextCodec` / `UserIdentityModel` contract objects.
   - **Moves to `jira_family/` only in contract-parameterized form:** `_sanitize_description` and
     `_sanitize_comment` — same observable behavior, but the ADF/limit dependency arrives as an injected
     contract instead of a direct import of a pinned module.

   - **Stays put (path-wise):** `_map_local_to_jira_fields` in the pinned `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py`,
     and the ADF encoder in the pinned `adapters/jira/adf.py`. These are shared **by dependency-inverting
     instead of moving**: the pinned module is parameterized by the `jira_family` contracts (it imports *from*
     `jira_family/`, never the reverse), so DC reuses one implementation without any file relocating and
     without the loader changing. Any story that would *move* a pinned file must instead stop and record the
     blocker.

   One more unit needs parameterizing rather than sharing verbatim: `classify_probe_response` hardcodes
   `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES = frozenset({"Resolved", "Done", "Cancelled"})`. Those are Cloud/DIG workflow state
   names; a self-hosted DC workflow can name its resolved states anything. So the classifier moves to
   `jira_family/` taking the resolved-status set **as a parameter**, with Cloud passing today's frozenset
   (pinned unchanged by J1's oracle) and DC passing its own configured set. Sharing it with the Cloud names
   baked in would silently misclassify a DC issue as `PRESENT_FILTERED` when it is in fact resolved.
   The DC set is **operator-configured** via a `reconciler.resolved_statuses` config key (a list of workflow
   state names), defaulting to the same `{Resolved, Done, Cancelled}` when unset so an operator whose workflow
   uses the conventional names configures nothing. Cloud continues to pass its own frozenset, so Cloud is not
   made configurable by this change.

   **The value maps are a special case — they are ALREADY duplicated, and this epic must not preserve the
   duplication.** There are today **three** independently-referenced copies of the local→Jira status map (and
   two of the priority map):
   - `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py`: `_LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` / `_LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA` — read **only** by the
     ACLI transport (`acli.py:69-70,143,171`; `acli_cli_ops.py:34,343,354`).
   - `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` (pinned): `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` / `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_PRIORITY` — read by
     the `Backend` port via `backend.py`'s `map_fields_to_remote`.
   - `rebar_reconciler/config.py:37`: `local_to_jira_status` — the engine-level config copy.

   They have **already drifted**: `outbound_fields` and `config.py` both carry a `"deleted": "Done"` entry the
   `jira_fields` copy lacks. So simply moving the `jira_fields` copy to `jira_family/` would leave Cloud's
   backend still reading a second copy — the exact "two places" the epic exists to eliminate. This epic
   consolidates the two `adapters/` copies; `config.py`'s is folded in by bug `fe15` (its call sites are
   engine-level config, a wider blast radius than this epic's seam).

   **Resolution: `adapters/jira_family/` holds the ONE definition of each value map. Both current copies are
   deleted and replaced by imports from it** — `jira_fields.py` (whose map literals move out, the file itself
   staying put for its ADF/limit-coupled sanitizers) and `outbound_fields.py` (pinned, so it stays at its path
   but its dict literals become an import). After this,
   grep finds exactly one dict literal per map, reachable from the ACLI transport, the Cloud backend port, and
   the DC backend alike.

   The `deleted`-key drift **must be decided in J2**, because a single unified dict cannot preserve two
   callers that currently disagree. J2 adopts `"deleted": "Done"` — the value **two of the three** existing
   copies already use (`outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` and `config.py:37`'s `local_to_jira_status`).
   The ACLI-side omission produces `"Deleted"` via a `.title()` fallback, which is not a state in the live DIG
   workflow, so Jira would reject that transition: a latent bug, not behavior to preserve. This is the one
   declared observable change in an otherwise behavior-preserving extraction, pinned by its own test. Bug
   `fe15-3bc4-ed70-4b61` (`controlled-ornate-honeybee`) keeps the remainder: the missing ACLI-side
   characterization pins and folding `config.py`'s third copy into the single definition.
3. **Pin the two real axes of variation as contracts**: a `RichTextCodec` (ADF for Cloud, wiki/plain text for
   DC) and a `UserIdentityModel` (`accountId` for Cloud, `name` for DC). Cloud is parameterized by its existing
   behavior; DC is a different configuration, not a fork.
4. **DC transport builds on the maintained `pycontribs/jira` library**, gated behind a `[jira-datacenter]`
   extra and imported lazily, so the engine's `dependencies = []` contract and the battle-tested Cloud path are
   both untouched.
5. **Verify against a real Jira.** Atlassian stopped issuing DC trial licenses on 30 March 2026, so the oracle
   is the Jira 8.17.1 test instance the pycontribs/jira project uses, reachable at
   `http://localhost:2990/jira` — the same substrate that project validates itself against.

   **It is BUILT, not pulled — corrected against the registry.** An earlier version of this step said to
   `docker run -dit -p 2990:2990 pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1` and called it a pinned *pullable* image.
   That is false: `docker pull` returns "repository does not exist", the Docker Hub API returns
   `object not found`, and the `pycontribs` namespace publishes only seven OS base images. The tag is a LOCAL
   BUILD NAME — pycontribs/jira ships `docker/jira-test-image/Dockerfile` and its README's own instruction is
   `docker build -t pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1 docker/jira-test-image`. Its base,
   `addono/jira-software-standalone`, IS pullable and the digest pycontribs pins resolves. J5
   [rebar:c97f-90ae-4976-47c7] therefore vendors a small Dockerfile pinned to that base digest; the mechanism
   and its three load-bearing details (`-DskipAllPrompts=true`, the TTY requirement, 8.x-only) live there.

   Two consequences worth recording at epic level because they shape what this oracle can promise: the image
   does NOT contain Jira — `atlas-run` downloads it from `maven.atlassian.com` at first start, so egress to
   Atlassian is a hard runtime dependency and **pinning the image digest does not pin Jira itself** — and the
   base is `linux/amd64`, so an arm64 runner emulates it and starts far slower than upstream's quoted 3-5
   minutes. Jira 8.17.1 is ≥ 8.14, the release that introduced Personal Access Tokens, so PAT
   bearer auth is exercised for real. J5 [rebar:c97f-90ae-4976-47c7] owns the harness and records the
   version-drift limitation (8.17.1 is older than a client such as CMS is likely running, so it proves REST v2
   protocol semantics, not deployment-specific workflow/field/permission behavior — tracked separately as
   `9895-ac7d-4276-4f08`).
6. **Keep the new boundary structurally enforced, not conventional.** The drift this epic exists to prevent can
   recur the moment a contributor adds Cloud-specific logic to the shared layer. So the seam ships with a
   machine-checked import contract (an `import-linter` contract in `pyproject.toml`, or an equivalent CI grep
   check): only `adapters/jira/` and `adapters/jira_datacenter/` may import `adapters/jira_family/`, and
   `jira_family/` may import neither of them.
7. **Security posture for the DC connection.** Self-hosted DC is frequently served over plain HTTP inside
   corporate networks, which would put ticket bodies and the PAT on the wire in cleartext. The DC backend
   therefore **requires `https`** for `reconciler.base_url` and rejects a non-TLS URL unless an explicit
   `allow_insecure = true` override is set (which logs a warning). Operator docs state the least-privilege
   expectation: a **dedicated service account** whose PAT is scoped to only the projects rebar reconciles
   (Browse Projects / Create Issues / Edit Issues / Add Comments / Link Issues on those projects), never an
   admin-level token.

   **The PAT is env-only, never file-config.** Like Cloud's `JIRA_API_TOKEN`, the DC PAT is read from a
   `JIRA_PAT` environment variable and is NOT accepted from `[tool.rebar.jira]` in a committed config file, so
   the credential cannot be checked into a repo by accident. The DC transport never logs the token, and a
   missing `JIRA_PAT` raises a config error naming the variable rather than falling back to anonymous access.

   **Certificate verification stays ON.** Self-hosted DC commonly presents a self-signed or internal-CA
   certificate, and the tempting fix — disabling verification — turns the `https` requirement into theatre. So
   the DC transport never sets `verify=False`: an operator with an internal CA points rebar at their CA bundle
   (a `ca_bundle` config key / the standard `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` env var honoured by the underlying client), and
   a verification failure surfaces as a clear error naming the CA-bundle setting rather than being silently
   downgraded. `allow_insecure` governs the URL *scheme* only; it does NOT relax certificate checking.

   **The J5 harness is the intended `allow_insecure` case, not an exception to it.** The Dockerized Jira serves
   plain `http://localhost:2990/jira`, so every live test against it sets `allow_insecure = true` explicitly and
   asserts the warning is emitted. That is deliberate: it means the loopback-only test path exercises the
   override rather than bypassing the validator, and the validator's reject-by-default branch is covered by a
   unit test with a non-loopback `http://` URL. The override is **not** narrowed to loopback — an operator on a
   private network is a real use case — but the warning text names the cleartext risk.

**Provenance decision.** DC and Cloud share the single `jira` creation channel, `jira-` local-id prefix, and `jira_key` binding; deployments are disambiguated by the `RemoteRef.instance` field that ADR 0035 §(d) already defines for exactly this. They are the same vendor. Generalizing the store vocabulary is epic `be74`'s work, where a genuinely different vendor (GitHub) makes it necessary; doing it here would mean a store migration for no user-visible benefit.

**Alternative rejected: PR #120's separate adapter package.** Two copies of the field maps and sanitizers drift, and cross-adapter private imports are a dependency direction ADR 0035 never sanctioned.

**Alternative rejected: a hand-rolled stdlib REST client.** PR #120's client is competent, but pycontribs/jira already absorbs DC-vs-Cloud auth, pagination, and payload quirks that thousands of users have found. Confining it to an opt-in extra keeps the cost off every rebar install.

**Alternative rejected: `atlassian-python-api`.** It was surveyed in ADR 0004 and does support DC with PAT auth, but `pycontribs/jira` is the better fit here for two reasons: it ships the Dockerized-Jira-SDK test harness pattern this epic adopts as its verification oracle (its own `tests/conftest.py`), and its `JIRA(server=…, token_auth=…)` surface covers DC-vs-Cloud divergence behind one client object. Either would work; picking one and confining it to an opt-in extra is what matters.

**Alternative rejected: generalizing `jira_key` / the `jira-` prefix / the channel vocabulary now.** That is epic `be74`'s spine and touches 50+ binding-store sites; pulling it forward delays the CMS delivery for no behavioral gain.

**Alternative rejected: moving the location-pinned modules now.** Relocating `outbound_fields.py` / `adf.py` into `jira_family/` would be the tidier file layout, but it requires teaching the dynamic loader the new sub-package and re-targeting every `mock.patch("rebar_reconciler.<mod>.<attr>")` site in the suite (ADR 0035 §(a)–(b)). That is ADR 0035's Phase 2; doing it here would couple a live-Cloud-risking refactor to a delivery epic for no DC-visible benefit. Dependency inversion gets the same single-implementation guarantee at a fraction of the risk.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/` (new), `adapters/jira/`, `adapters/jira_datacenter/` (new).
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — widen `reconciler.backend` (**owned by J7**), add the TLS/`allow_insecure`
  validator and the `ca_bundle` + `resolved_statuses` keys (**owned by J6**). Split deliberately: J6 lands the
  DC connection settings with the transport that consumes them; J7 lands the backend-choice widening with the
  assembly that makes the choice valid.
- `pyproject.toml` — `[jira-datacenter]` extra, and the import contract.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_characterization.py`, `test_backend_contract.py`.
- A new ADR amending ADR 0035.
- **Out of scope:** relocating any location-pinned module (`adf.py`, `outbound_fields.py`,
  `comment_limits.py`) or touching `_loader.py` — ADR 0035 Phase 2 owns that.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] every child story is closed and its change is `Verified +1` on Gerrit
- [x] `test_backend_contract.py`'s backend fixture includes `jira-datacenter` and the suite passes for it
- [x] an ADR records the Jira-family sub-seam, the shared `jira` provenance identity, and the DC EOL horizon
- [x] [operator-attested] rebar reconciles bidirectionally against the Dockerized Jira SDK instance at
      `localhost:2990`, selected by `reconciler.backend = "jira-datacenter"` with `reconciler.base_url`
      pointing at that instance: at least one issue created in DC appears in the local store after an inbound
      pass, and one local edit appears on the DC issue after an outbound pass, with zero unhandled exceptions
      in the reconcile log
- [x] No SHARED mapping logic exists in two places, and each VARYING unit has exactly one shared CONTRACT:
      (a) the field/value maps, the label sanitizer, and the link-relation vocabulary
      each have exactly one implementation in `adapters/jira_family/`, imported by both backends (or, for
      the location-pinned modules, consumed parameterized by a `jira_family` contract); and (b) the
      rich-text codec and the user-identity model each have exactly one shared CONTRACT in
      `adapters/jira_family/` with one implementation PER DEPLOYMENT. `adapters/jira_datacenter/` defines no
      copy of any unit in (a). Cross-imports between `adapters/jira/` and `adapters/jira_datacenter/` are
      forbidden and machine-checked, failing CI on a violation.
      **AMENDED — the original wording required "exactly one implementation reachable by both backends" for
      ALL SIX units including the codec and the identity model. That prescribes an outcome that would be
      WRONG if achieved:** Cloud is ADF and DC is wiki/plain text; Cloud identifies users by `accountId`
      and DC by `name`. Two implementations of one pinned contract IS the correct design
      (`jira_family/rich_text.py:36 RichTextCodec` → `WikiTextCodec` / `AdfCodec`;
      `jira_family/identity_model.py:42 UserIdentityModel` → `NameIdentity` / `AccountIdIdentity`). Two
      further corrections folded in, both recorded in this epic's AC-verification comment: the create-path
      field map legitimately exists twice (`jira_datacenter/backend.py:53 _map_local_to_dc_fields`, because
      Cloud's version lazy-loads the location-pinned `adf.py` BY FILE PATH — a coupling DC must not carry),
      so the "defines none of its own" clause is scoped to the units in (a); and the enforcement clause is
      narrowed to what the checker actually does — it forbids cross-IMPORTS and pins one dict literal per
      value map, but cannot prevent a re-DEFINITION, so four of the six units rest on convention plus
      review. The substance was verified: cross-imports are empty on `gerrit/main`, the boundary checker
      fires on 11 forbidden edges and stays silent on 4 permitted ones, and the value-map single-sourcing
      is asserted by object IDENTITY (`... is LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA`), not equality
      **AMENDED AGAIN (task `f020-0960-2c42-4d61`, 2026-08-12) — the probe classifier
      (`classify_probe_response`) is REMOVED from the (a) list.** Bug `3b5f` removed every consumer of the
      inbound absence-probe chain, leaving the port dormant; `f020` deleted the port and the classifier
      together, so `adapters/jira_family/probe.py` no longer exists and neither backend imports it. The
      "one shared … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: Jira Server / Data Center support via a Jira-family seam (not a forked second adapter)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_provisioning.py:195` (`test_a_missing_epic_field_aborts_provisioning`) stubs `_request` so `/rest/api/2/field` returns a body with `Epic Name` but WITHOUT `Epic Link`, then calls `harness._assert_project_capabilities("RBTEST")`. The missing field is permanently absent under the stub, so the readiness poll can only expire — and it expires against the real PRODUCTION budget.

That budget is `scripts/jira_dc_field_readiness.py:114`, `FIELD_READY_BUDGET_S = 120.0`, polled every `FIELD_POLL_INTERVAL_S = 1.0` (line 95). `await_required_fields` (line 226) loops `request` -> `if monotonic() >= deadline: break` -> `sleep(interval)`, so the unit test performs ~120 stub reads and sleeps ~120 real seconds to learn something the stub decided up front. That matches the filed 120.39-121.03s.

The seam is already provided. `_assert_project_capabilities` (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py:580-581`) does NOT rely on the module constant: it computes `field_budget = _field_ready_timeout()` and passes `budget=field_budget` explicitly. `_field_ready_timeout()` (line 157) reads the `JIRA_DC_FIELD_READY_TIMEOUT` environment variable and only falls back to `FIELD_READY_BUDGET_S` when it is unset. And `await_required_fields` documents (line 252) that at least one attempt is always made "even with a zero or negative allowance — the answer must come from an observation, never from arithmetic".

## Approach

Set the readiness budget to zero for this one test through the environment variable the production code already honours, and assert the resulting poll count.

* `monkeypatch.setenv("JIRA_DC_FIELD_READY_TIMEOUT", "0")` inside the test.
  `monkeypatch` restores the environment at teardown, so no other test and no
  production path sees it; the committed `FIELD_READY_BUDGET_S` stays `120.0`.
  Going through the env var rather than rebinding `FIELD_READY_BUDGET_S` is what
  makes this deterministic: the caller passes `budget=` explicitly, so a constant
  rebind would be silently defeated whenever `JIRA_DC_FIELD_READY_TIMEOUT` is
  already set in the ambient environment, whereas `setenv` overrides it either way.
* With a zero budget the loop is fully DETERMINISTIC rather than merely fast: one
  attempt is made unconditionally, `monotonic() >= deadline` is then true, and the
  loop breaks BEFORE `sleep` is ever called. So the test asserts that the stub saw
  exactly ONE `/rest/api/2/field` read.

That single assertion is the required guard, and it is stronger than a timing budget: reaching a real sleep is only possible by going round the loop again, which necessarily produces a second field read and fails the count. It contains no wall-clock assertion.

`_stub_request` (line 72) already returns its recorded `(method, path, payload)` list, so the poll count is available without new plumbing.

This is the mechanism the sibling suite already uses — `tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_conftest.py:296` sets the same environment variable for the same reason — so it adds no new pattern to the tree. A fake `sleep`/`monotonic` pair was rejected: `await_required_fields` accepts them, but `_assert_project_capabilities` does not forward them, so injecting would mean changing a production signature to serve a test.

## Scope

* `tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_provisioning.py` — set the zero budget and assert the
  poll count in `test_a_missing_epic_field_aborts_provisioning`; note why in the
  test docstring.

No production change: `scripts/jira_dc_field_readiness.py` and `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py` are read but not modified.

## Testing

* Happy path — the test still raises `AssertionError` naming `Epic Link`, i.e. the
  existing assertion is untouched, and now also pins one field read.
* Failure/edge path — the guard is proven by seeding: temporarily removing the
  `setenv` is confirmed to make the poll-count assertion FAIL (many reads), not
  merely run slowly. Seed reverted, not committed.
* Ambient-environment check — the test is also run with
  `JIRA_DC_FIELD_READY_TIMEOUT=300` already exported, confirming the `setenv`
  overrides an ambient value rather than being defeated by it.
* Isolation check — the neighbouring readiness tests and the rest of the module
  still pass in the same session, confirming `monkeypatch` restored the env.
* Production-default check — `FIELD_READY_BUDGET_S` is still `120.0` in the
  committed tree, read directly from the source.
* Whole-suite regression — the CI pytest command is green.

No wall-clock or timing-budget assertion is added; savings go in ticket comments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `test_a_missing_epic_field_aborts_provisioning` still raises the same
      `AssertionError` naming `Epic Link` — verified by the unchanged
      `pytest.raises` plus substring assertion still passing.
- [x] The test asserts exactly one `/rest/api/2/field` read, which proves the
      expiry path ran without reaching `sleep` — verified by the new assertion
      passing and by the seeded-budget run failing it.
- [x] The test completes in under 2 seconds where it took ~120s — measured with
      `pytest --durations` and posted as a before/after ticket comment.
- [x] `scripts/jira_dc_field_readiness.py` and
      `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py` are byte-identical to `origin/main`,
      confirmed by an empty `git diff --stat origin/main -- <those paths>`, so
      production readiness defaults are unchanged.
- [x] The rest of `tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_provisioning.py` and
      `tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_conftest.py` pass in one session, showing the
      env override did not leak.
baseline.summary: Missing-field unit test burns the full 120-second Jira readiness budget

baseline.description:
# Inbound link removal never converges when a pair holds two relations (unlink is pair-scoped)

## Context / Problem

Links are WRITTEN keyed on `(target_id, relation)`: `graph/_links.py::add_dependency` is idempotent per `(target_id, relation)`, so one ordered pair CAN hold two net-active differently-related deps (e.g. `blocks` + `relates_to`). But removal is pair-scoped: `rebar.unlink(id1, id2)` takes no relation argument and `_commands/unlink.py::_get_link_info` returns "the most recent net-active link for target". Change 1276 (bug `2b16-9be0-a8f5-41d9`) therefore added guard G5 in `rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py::_inbound_unlink_one`, which declines + logs when the pair's net-active relation does not match the relation whose peer link vanished.

**How a remove record reaches G5 despite G4 (traced).** In a normal bidirectional pass, G4 (`inbound_differ.py::compute_inbound_mutations`, the action-aware same-pass link suppression) drops an inbound remove whenever the outbound differ emitted a link mutation for the same pair — and `outbound_links.py::_diff_links` usually re-emits an ADD for a still-local, peer-absent dep, so in THAT case the pair "converges" by outbound re-adding the peer-deleted link and G5 is never reached. But the outbound ADD is deduped **direction-agnostically on `(vendor_type, target_key)`** and "intentionally NOT deduped on `relation`" (`_diff_links` docstring + `already_present` check), while the inbound removal differ compares in per-relation LOCAL vocabulary (`link_direction.py`: `blocks` and `depends_on` BOTH map to vendor type `Blocks`). So when a local dep's vendor type collides with a remote link of the same vendor type in the OTHER direction — e.g. local dep `blocks → K` while the remote pair holds an inward `Blocks` link (which reads as `depends_on` in local vocabulary) — that remaining same-vendor-type remote link keeps the outbound ADD deduped (`already_present` → skip), outbound emits nothing for the pair, `ob_entry`'s `link_add_keys`/`link_remove_keys` are empty, and the inbound remove record survives to G5. The same holds for any pass where the outbound differ emits no link mutation for the pair (e.g. inbound-only application of records). In those G5-reached cases the decline IS permanent when the pair's most-recent net-active relation differs from the vanished one: the removal record re-emits and re-declines on every subsequent pass, so inbound link removal never converges for that double-related pair. This fix targets exactly that G5-reached path; the G4-suppressed path (outbound re-add wins) is out of scope and unchanged. (Verified at runtime in a scratch store: one ordered pair holds `blocks` + `relates_to` net-active simultaneously; `blocks` + `depends_on` on one ordered pair is rejected by the cycle guard; pair-scoped `rebar.unlink` removes the most-recent link.)

**Relation to 2b16's fail-safe ruling (removal-convergence is deliberately re-enabled).** The operator ratified converting the G5 decline into a relation-scoped removal (see the ratified-decision comment). The residual exposure — `managed_refs` marks a ref managed the instant it is created locally, so a managed-but-never-pushed local link whose outbound ADD is permanently deduped by the direction-agnostic vendor-type check is state-indistinguishable from a genuine peer deletion — is PRE-EXISTING, not introduced here: today, when such a never-pushed link is the pair's most-recent net-active link, G5's relation match PASSES and the pair-scoped unlink already removes it. This change only makes the outcome order-independent (the exactly-named relation is removed instead of "whichever is most recent, else decline forever"). It never removes a relation the record did not name, and a record naming a relation with no matching net-active local link removes nothing. The proper discriminator (persisted peer-link history distinguishing never-pushed from peer-deleted) is a design pass of its own, filed as ticket `a4bd-4ca8-c44f-49bb` (linked `discovered_from` this ticket) and deliberately out of scope here.

## Approach (operator-ratified 2026-08-04 — see comment)

Make removal symmetric with the write path, keyed on `(target_id, relation)`:

1. **Graph-layer relation-scoped removal seam** — `graph/_links.py` gains
   `remove_dependency(source_id, target_id, tracker_dir, relation)`, symmetric with
   `add_dependency`: validates the relation, finds the most recent net-active LINK with
   exactly that `(target_id, relation)`, writes the UNLINK event through the shared locked
   write seam, and removes the reciprocal link for `relates_to`. The net-active replay in
   `_commands/unlink.py::_get_link_info` gains an optional `relation=` filter (default `None`
   keeps pair-scoped behavior) so the seam and the CLI stay in lockstep on one replay.
2. **Reconciler convergence** — `_inbound_unlink_one` uses the relation-scoped removal, so
   the G5 decline case converges by removing exactly the mirrored relation. The safety
   invariant is preserved positively: when the named relation has NO net-active link locally,
   the removal is a logged no-op and no other relation's link is ever removed.
3. **CLI backward-compatible optional relation** — `rebar unlink <id1> <id2> [relation]`.
   With a relation, removal is relation-scoped; with no relation, the existing pair-scoped
   most-recent behavior is byte-for-byte UNCHANGED. `rebar.unlink` (library facade) gains the
   same optional `relation=None` keyword.

Strict TDD: RED behavioral tests first, then the implementation turns them GREEN.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/graph/_links.py` — add `remove_dependency` (relation-scoped removal seam) and an
  UNLINK event writer mirroring `_write_link_event`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/unlink.py` — optional relation on `_get_link_info`, `_write_unlink`,
  `unlink_core`, `unlink_cli`; usage text updated.
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` — `rebar.unlink(id1, id2, relation=None, ...)`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` — `_inbound_unlink_one`
  performs relation-scoped removal instead of the permanent G5 decline.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_link_removal_2b16.py` — the G5 mismatch
  test is revised to the new contract (still asserts the other relation's link survives and
  a mismatching removal with no matching local link removes nothing); a new test proves the
  double-related pair converges.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_unlink_relation_scoped_e39f.py` — new: two-relation pair
  behaviors for the seam, the facade, and the CLI (including no-relation backward compat).
- `src/rebar/_cli/help/unlink.txt` — the pinned `--help` text the CLI actually prints
  (served by `_cli/_help.py::subcommand_help`) gains the optional relation.
- `docs/cli-reference.md` — machine-generated from the help files under a CI drift gate;
  regenerated with `python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`.
- `docs/user-guide.md` — the one-line `rebar unlink` description gains the optional relation.

Out of scope (owned elsewhere): MCP `unlink_tickets` signature, binding_store.py, jira fetcher.py issuelinks merge, completion attestation/signing, show-command rendering.

## Testing

Behavioral, through public entry points:
- Happy path: pair holds `blocks` + `relates_to`; relation-scoped removal of `blocks` leaves
  `relates_to` net-active (and vice versa), asserted via `rebar.show_ticket` deps.
- Reconciler: a double-related pair whose peer dropped one relation converges — the mirrored
  relation's dep is gone after `_inbound_update_apply_links`, the other survives, and the
  apply is counted (`applied == 1`); re-apply is an idempotent no-op.
- Safety/negative: removal naming a relation with no net-active local link removes NOTHING
  (G5's invariant, asserted positively) and is a logged no-op; `unlink` with an invalid
  relation errors; `unlink` with no relation keeps the existing most-recent pair-scoped
  behavior (existing tests stay green unmodified except the revised G5 mismatch test).
- Edge: relation-scoped removal of `relates_to` also removes the reciprocal link.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A test proves a pair CAN hold two differently-related net-active deps (checked: the new
      lifecycle test creates `blocks` + `relates_to` on one pair and asserts both appear in
      `show_ticket` deps).
- [x] A peer deletion of ONE relation in a two-relation pair reaches a defined end state: the
      exactly-mirrored relation's link is removed and the reconcile converges (checked: new
      2b16-file test drives `_inbound_update_apply_links` and asserts the named relation's dep
      is gone, the other remains, and a second apply is a counted-zero no-op).
- [x] G5 never removes a link the peer still carries — asserted positively (checked: revised
      mismatch test shows a removal naming a relation with no matching net-active local link
      leaves the pair's other link intact and removes nothing).
- [x] `rebar unlink <id1> <id2>` with NO relation argument behaves exactly as before (checked:
      all pre-existing unlink tests pass unmodified; a new test pins most-recent pair-scoped
      removal).
- [x] Targeted tests, `make lint`, and `make typecheck` pass in the worktree venv (checked:
      command output recorded in ticket comments).
- [x] Mutation-checked: re-introducing the pair-scoped call in `_inbound_unlink_one` turns the
      convergence test RED; verdicts recorded on the ticket.
baseline.summary: Inbound link removal never converges when a pair holds two relations (unlink is pair-scoped)

baseline.description:
## Why

`docs/architecture.md:49-55` states the core invariant: **all mutations go through ONE locked append+commit path in `rebar._store`** (`event_append.py`, `push.py`, `sync.py`, `lock.py`). `graph/_links.py` violates this — it hand-rolls a second, divergent write path for LINK events. This is the single confirmed *structural* finding of the 2026-06-18 audit (HIGH; the adversarial validator searched for a justifying reason and found none). The risk is concrete: push policy, HLC semantics, lock semantics, and commit shaping now live in two places, so any change to `_store` silently fails to propagate to link writes, and the hand-rolled copy already carries defects (wrong author, zero env_id, weaker lock).

## What

Route link-event writes in `graph/_links.py` through the canonical `_store` write path (the same path `_commands/_seam.append_event` → `_store.event_append.write_and_push` uses), eliminating the duplicate lock+commit+push logic while preserving the pre-write cycle-check semantics.

## Scope

- In scope: `src/rebar/graph/_links.py` (`_write_link_event` / `add_dependency`),
  reusing `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`.
- Out of scope: changing link *semantics* (cycle rules, hierarchy promotion),
  the reconciler's grandfathered advisory lock, any non-link write.

## Context (citations)

- **The duplicate path:** `src/rebar/graph/_links.py:108-255` (`_write_link_event`).
  It builds the LINK envelope by hand, opens `.ticket-write.lock` with bare
  `fcntl.flock` (≈ lines 148-149), shells `git add` + `git commit --no-verify`,
  and runs its own retry/push/rebase/merge loop. It hardcodes
  `author="ticket-graph"` and `env_id="00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"`.
- **The canonical path it should use:** `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:143`
  (`write_and_push`) → `:77` (`stage_and_commit`), which writes via atomic
  temp+rename, locks through `_store.lock.write_lock(tracker, dual_window=True)`
  (the unified **dual-leg fcntl+mkdir** lock, `_store/lock.py:1-29`), and runs the
  rebase guard (`check_no_rebase_in_progress`).
- **How other writers do it correctly:** `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:151-187`
  (`append_event`) composes the envelope (real `author(...)`, real
  `env_id(tracker)`) and routes through the store path; `_commands/delete.py`
  writes UNLINK events this way.
- **Validator note:** the cycle checks (`_links.py:317-345`) run *before*
  `_write_link_event`, which already acquires its lock *internally* — so "check
  then write" is *already* non-atomic. A separate write path buys no atomicity;
  the differences are pure defects.

## Implementation plan

1. Read `_seam.append_event` (`_commands/_seam.py:151-187`) and
   `event_append.write_and_push` to confirm the envelope fields and return
   contract (exit code / event id).
2. **PREFER `_seam.append_event` over `write_and_push` directly.** The review
   confirmed `write_and_push(tracker, ticket_id, event)` takes a **pre-composed**
   event and does **NOT** tick HLC — so calling it directly would force `_links.py`
   to keep composing the envelope *and* ticking itself (the error-prone status quo).
   `_seam.append_event(source_id, "LINK", {"target_id":…, "relation":…}, tracker)`
   composes the envelope with real `author()`/`env_id(tracker)` **and** ticks HLC
   internally (`_seam.py:174`) — strictly cleaner. Replace `_write_link_event`'s
   body to call it, and **delete the existing `hlc.next_tick` call** (`_links.py:125`)
   so there is no double-tick.
3. Delete the now-dead inline `fcntl.flock` block, the `git add`/`commit`
   subprocess calls, and the bespoke push/rebase/merge retry loop.
4. Preserve the existing pre-call cycle-check / idempotency ordering in
   `add_dependency` exactly (do not move the check inside the lock — it is
   currently outside, and changing that is a separate design decision).
5. Verify the HLC tick source: `_links.py` currently calls
   `hlc.next_tick(...)`; confirm `write_and_push`/`stage_and_commit` performs the
   tick (or pass it through) so timestamps stay monotonic and no double-tick
   occurs.
6. Run the link/graph test suites (`tests/scripts/reducer/test_reducer_links.py`,
   `tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py`, any `tests/**/`*link* and
   `*graph*`), plus a two-clone convergence test if one exists, to confirm event
   shape and merge behavior are unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

- **Benefit:** one write path; push/HLC/lock policy evolves in exactly one place;
  the author/env_id/rebase-guard defects vanish for free.
- **Cost/risk:** the extraction must preserve the "cycle-check (outside lock) →
  append (inside lock)" ordering and idempotency, so it is *not* a mechanical
  move — review the atomicity assumptions in `add_dependency` carefully. If
  `write_and_push` ticks HLC internally, ensure the old explicit `hlc.next_tick`
  call is removed to avoid a double tick.
- **Behavioral change to note:** LINK events will now carry the real `author` and
  `env_id` instead of the sentinel values. This applies to **both** writes —
  the primary link AND the `relates_to` reciprocal (both go through
  `_write_link_event`, e.g. `_links.py:369`). Confirm no test asserts on
  `author == "ticket-graph"` or the zero-UUID env_id; update any that do (they
  were asserting on a defect).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `graph/_links.py` no longer opens `.ticket-write.lock` directly, no longer
  shells `git add`/`commit`, and no longer implements its own push loop; it routes
  LINK writes through `_store.event_append.write_and_push` (or the `_seam`).
- [ ] LINK events carry a real `author` and a real `env_id(tracker)` (no
  `"ticket-graph"` / zero-UUID sentinels).
- [ ] HLC timestamps remain monotonic (no double-tick) — verified by a reducer/HLC test.
- [ ] All existing link/graph/unblock tests pass; two-clone link convergence (if a
  test exists) is unchanged.
- [ ] `ruff check src tests` and the scoped mypy gate stay green.
</content>
baseline.summary: Route graph/_links.py link writes through the canonical _store write path

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`capabilities.py:330` defines a SINGLE global constant

    CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS = 4096

commented as the Opus floor, and applies it to every model. Anthropic's minimum cacheable prefix is MODEL-DEPENDENT, and two independent investigations in this epic measured real floors that the constant misdescribes.

## Measured evidence — two agents, two paths, neither trusting the other

MEASUREMENT A (via the overlap-judge path, `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`), bracketed two ways:
    bare API            922 tok -> no cache      1042 tok -> write 1035, read 1035
    real judge request  875 tok -> nothing       1250 tok -> write 1243, read 1243
  => sonnet-4-6 floor is ~1024, NOT 4096.

MEASUREMENT B (via a wrapped httpx transport, live A/B with identical marker and payload):
    haiku-4-5   1193 tok -> not cached
    haiku-4-5   2748 tok -> not cached
    haiku-4-5   4749 tok -> CACHED (w=4742 r=4742)
    sonnet-4-5   253 tok -> not cached
    sonnet-4-5  7930 tok -> CACHED (w=7923)
  => haiku-4-5's floor lies between 2748 and 4749; the sonnet-4-5 bracket is consistent with ~1024.

The two are not in conflict: they show the floor VARIES BY MODEL, which is exactly what a single global constant cannot express. A floor of 4096 is roughly right for haiku and roughly 4x too high for sonnet.

## Two distinct harms, both observed

1. FALSE NEGATIVE IN THE WARNING. `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` gates `warn_if_cache_ineffective`
   (`structured_run.py:417-422`). A genuine caching failure on a sonnet call site with a 900-3000
   token prefix is silently below the global floor and never warns — the exact blind spot bug 7a79
   introduced the floor to avoid over-warning about, now over-corrected in the other direction.
2. IT MISLEADS SIZING DECISIONS. Work on ticket 8415 hoisted a shared prefix to make it cacheable and
   landed at 846 tokens. Against the real 1024 floor that is a near miss (+5.8% input tokens, zero
   cache); against the documented 4096 it looks hopeless. The constant materially changes what an
   engineer concludes is worth doing.

## A second, separable defect in the same predicate

`warn_if_cache_ineffective` compares total `input_tokens` against the floor, but what governs caching is the size of the MARKED PREFIX, not the total request. A call with a 150-token marked prefix and a 7000-token unmarked user message clears the floor on totals and is uncacheable in fact. Bug f81d carries the detail; noted here because any fix to the constant should fix the compared quantity too, or the floor will still be measured against the wrong number.

## What is NOT established

The exact floor per model, from a documented source rather than bracketing. The measurements above are empirical brackets on three models on one date; Anthropic publishes per-model minimums and those should be the source of truth, with the measurements used to VERIFY rather than to define.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The cache floor is model-dependent rather than one global constant, sourced from documented
      per-model minimums and carried on the capability record alongside `prompt_cache_style`.
- [x] `warn_if_cache_ineffective` compares the MARKED PREFIX size against that model's floor, not the
      total `input_tokens`.
- [x] A test pins that a sub-floor prefix on a LOW-floor model (sonnet) now warns where it previously
      did not, and fails before the fix.
- [x] A test pins that the haiku floor is not lowered to sonnet's, so the fix does not reintroduce the
      over-warning bug 7a79 removed.
- [x] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
baseline.summary: CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS is a model-blind global: 4x too high for sonnet, so real caching failures never warn

baseline.description:
## Why
rebar is event-per-file-per-commit: every mutation = one git commit (closer to
git-issue, the documented high-bloat counterexample). Re-enabling stock gc (epic
minor-haste-ogle) fixes *reclaim* of object bloat, but the growth *rate* is set at
write time. The durable way to bound growth is to create fewer objects at the
source — exactly what git-bug does.

## What
Batch multiple mutations into a single git blob/commit per logical operation, the
git-bug `operationPack` pattern (multiple ops serialized into one blob -> one
commit per Commit()), instead of one commit per event. Must preserve the
append-only / merge-as-union (CRDT) convergence the store relies on, and the
globally-unique event identity used by replay/dedup.

Prior art (verifiable):
- git-bug operationPack: https://github.com/git-bug/git-bug/blob/master/entity/dag/operation_pack.go
- git-bug entity commit/merge: https://github.com/git-bug/git-bug/blob/master/entity/dag/entity.go

## Scope
In: a batched-write primitive + adoption on the highest-churn write paths (import,
reconciler apply, multi-event transactions). Out: changing the per-ticket event
schema or the union/replay semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A batch-commit primitive writes N events in one commit, preserving per-event identity, replay, and union-merge convergence
- [ ] Adopted on at least the bulk paths (import; reconciler batch apply)
- [ ] Object-count reduction demonstrated on a synthetic many-event run (before/after)
- [ ] No regression: replay, dedup, and cross-clone convergence tests green
baseline.summary: Write-time op batching: fewer commits per mutation (git-bug operationPack pattern)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Split out of bug 304e-9c0f-2068-4d0e (castoff-tigerseye-ammonite) to avoid widening that fix's scope; filed rather than fixed there.

`run_ensures()` (`src/rebar/_store/ensures.py:158`) calls `write_lock()` with the module defaults `_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT=30` x `_DEFAULT_ATTEMPTS=2` = a **60 second** acquisition budget, then treats a `LockTimeout` as a whole-sweep no-op (it does log a WARNING — it is not silent — but it has already burned the 60s by then).

304e fixed the *reclaimability* defect that made one particular lock unprovable forever, so that specific 60s stall is gone. The budget itself is untouched and is a standing fragility: ANY genuinely contended lock — a concurrent writer, a slow push, a genuinely foreign-host lock on a shared filesystem (which is correctly never reclaimed) — still stalls the ensure sweep for a full minute on a path that runs at boot. The review-bot's autodeploy health check is `HEALTH_TIMEOUT=30`, so a 60s budget on the boot path can fail a deploy on its own, with no orphaned lock involved.

`run_ensures`'s own docstring already anticipates this: "A caller that must not block (e.g. MCP boot) passes a SHORT budget so a contended lock skips the sweep rather than delaying it." The MCP boot path does; the review-bot startup path evidently does not.

## Approach

Audit `run_ensures` callers on startup paths and give the boot-time ones a short bounded budget (the sweep is idempotent and re-runs, so skipping it under contention is cheap and safe), or make a short budget the default for the ensure sweep and let the long budget be opt-in. Consider whether the boot path should surface the skip more loudly than a WARNING.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No startup/boot path can spend more than a few seconds acquiring the write lock for the ensure
      sweep; verified by a test that holds the lock and asserts the boot path returns promptly.
- [ ] A skipped sweep is still visible (logged) and still re-runs on the next boot.
- [ ] The fail-closed StoreIncompatibleError re-raise is unaffected.
- [ ] make lint, make typecheck, and the default suite exit zero.
baseline.summary: run_ensures uses the full 60s write-lock budget on the boot path, so any contended lock alone can blow a 30s deploy health timeout

# The gating pip-audit job fails on EVERY Gerrit patchset, blocking all Verified +1 votes

## Symptom

`build-and-test / pip-audit (dependency vulnerabilities)` fails on every patchset run observed today, so no change can reach `Verified +1`. Confirmed across five independent runs on different agents' patchsets: 30770494611, 30770603146, 30770604307, 30770971365, 30771122330, 30771131391. All share head sha 4214516f95 (`origin/main`), and the failures are identical, so this is a property of `main`, not of any one change.

## Root cause — a real advisory, NOT a network flake

From run 30770494611's job log (the audit step's own output):

    pip-audit attempt 1/3
    click 8.2.1   PYSEC-2026-2132   8.3.3   Pallets Click, versions 8.3.2 and below,
      contain a command injection vulnerability in the click.edit() function, allowing
      attackers to pass arbitrary OS commands from an unprivileged account.
    ##[error]pip-audit found dependency vulnerabilities (see output). Bump the pinned
      version, or add --ignore-vuln <ID> with justification if accepted.

It succeeded on attempt 1 — it REACHED the advisory DB and found a vulnerability. So the workflow's documented infra escape hatch does NOT apply: `_build-and-test.yml`'s failure policy reserves `recheck` for the case where all three attempts fail to reach the DB. Commenting `recheck` will not clear this.

`click` is a TRANSITIVE dependency pinned at 8.2.1 in the committed `uv.lock` (line 711); it is not pinned in `pyproject.toml`. The advisory appears to have been published after `ce5d: go uv-canonical with a committed lock` landed the lock, which is why a previously green gate went red with no code change.

## Remediation (one of)

1. Refresh the lock so `click` resolves to >= 8.3.3 (the fix version pip-audit names).
   Preferred: it removes the vulnerability rather than accepting it.
2. If 8.3.3 is not resolvable under the current constraint set, `--ignore-vuln
   PYSEC-2026-2132` with a written justification, per the failure policy's explicit
   provision for that (`_build-and-test.yml`, "Failure policy"). Note rebar does not call
   `click.edit()`, so the exploit path is plausibly not reachable — but that argument
   belongs IN the justification comment, reviewed, not assumed here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pip-audit` is green on a fresh patchset against `main`
- [ ] the fix is a lock/pin change or a justified, greppable `--ignore-vuln`, not a
      blanket skip of the job
- [ ] if option 2 is taken, the justification names why the vulnerable code path is
      unreachable from rebar

## Why this is filed separately

Discovered while landing story 79d5 (DC length convergence), whose diff is two new test files plus a source comment and touches no dependency pin. A lock refresh is a different change with a different blast radius, and `uv.lock` is outside that story's declared file impact.
baseline.summary: pip-audit gate is red on main: click 8.2.1 PYSEC-2026-2132

## Context / Problem
After S2, command identity/help and every handler grammar come from the registry/parser system, but real execution still traverses explicit intercept/dispatch ladders and policy frozensets. Leaving those selection authorities in parallel preserves the coordination defect RP-05 is intended to remove.

## Approach
Move core top-level execution to the selected registry route after the pre-operation help boundary. Resolve only the selected lazy handler reference and invoke it through a closed typed adapter-kind set matching existing call shapes. The router passes the original command remainder unchanged; the selected handler uses S2's shared argparse factory. The router must not parse command/nested options a second time.

Consume route metadata for:

- central best-effort mount eligibility;
- strict initialization `none`, `init_only`, or `full`, plus narrow pure selectors for genuinely conditional cases;
- position-independent confirmation/output extraction while preserving tokens after `--`;
- legacy output passthrough for `create`, `idea`, `transition`, `claim`, and `reopen`;
- exact handler adapter, argv, stdout/stderr, exit-code, and exception contracts.

Before cutover, compare registry-derived policies and selected handler/parser pairs to every existing set and arm. Any non-allowlisted delta fails shadow parity. Cut over one selection authority only after parity is exact; keep derived compatibility exports for S6 rollback.

This story covers core and bridge execution that does not change optional-capability posture. S4 owns selected optional mode/backend checks and may proceed from the same S2 contract without editing dispatch.

## Compatibility and Rollback
The positive rationale is a single validated selection/dispatch authority while preserving specialized parser-backed handlers. No signature introspection, middleware pipeline, eager parser-tree construction, or second parse is added. Rollback selects the derived compatibility exports; no event, ticket, bridge, or binding data changes.

## Testing
Use real CLI subprocess contracts rather than source greps. Extend mount/init, mutation confirmation, global output, bridge vocabulary, hidden alias, unknown, and exit-code suites. Add typed fake handlers for every adapter kind/selector. Include negative controls for tokens after `--`, malformed global flags, no-auto-mount commands, store-touching intercepts, handler exceptions, and a parser spy proving the selected handler parses exactly once while unrelated factories/handlers are not imported.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every core canonical command and compatibility spelling resolves exactly one lazy handler through a closed adapter kind, and only the selected handler/parser modules are imported.
- [ ] The top-level router preserves original remainder argv and the selected S2 factory parses it exactly once; no route-level option grammar exists.
- [ ] Registry-derived mount/init behavior matches the pre-cutover census for every route, including no-auto-mount and conditional cases.
- [ ] Confirmation, global output extraction, legacy JSON shapes, `--`, streams, exit codes, and exception propagation match existing behavioral tests.
- [ ] Bridge compatibility spellings and hidden `bridge-status` execute through approved adapters while `purge-bridge` remains unknown.
- [ ] Execution can switch back to derived compatibility exports without handler, generated-help, or persisted-data changes.
baseline.summary: RP-05 S3 — Dispatch core CLI execution through validated lazy routes

## Why
The diff-scope filter keeps a detector match only when `location.file` is EXACTLY equal to an entry in `changed_files` (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/detectors.py:74`, `if loc and loc in changed:`), with neither side normalized. A location and a changed-file entry that denote the SAME file with different spellings (`./app.py`, an absolute path under repo_root, `a//b.py` repeated separators, a unicode NFC/NFD variant) compare unequal, so a real high-severity security match is silently dropped. VALIDATED.

## Decision: normalize BOTH sides at this boundary
Add a small canonicalizer applied to `location.file` AND each `changed_files` entry before the membership test — a pure textual canonical form (no filesystem access, since diff-scope paths need not exist on disk):
1. If the path is absolute AND under `repo_root`, make it relative to `repo_root` (both sides
   then live in the same relative space; the upstream contract already intends repo-relative).
2. `os.path.normpath` — collapses `./`, repeated separators (`a//b` → `a/b`), and `..`.
3. `unicodedata.normalize("NFC", …)` — so a composed/decomposed unicode filename matches.
Symlink resolution (realpath) is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE: it requires the file to exist on disk, which a diff-scope path need not; this ticket canonicalizes spelling, not inode identity (noted in a code comment).

## What
1. `detectors.py`: add `_canonical_path(p, repo_root)` (relativize-under-repo_root → normpath →
   NFC) and apply it to both `loc` and every `changed_files` entry (build the `changed` set from
   canonicalized entries; canonicalize `loc` before the `in` test).
2. `tests/unit/test_code_review_ws5.py`: variant-path matching tests (RED-first — they fail
   against the current exact-match code, pass after canonicalization).

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/detectors.py` — canonicalize both sides of the diff-scope filter.
- `tests/unit/test_code_review_ws5.py` — variant-path-form tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `location.file` and `changed_files` are both canonicalized (relativize-under-repo_root +
      normpath + NFC) before the membership test.
- [ ] Tests: a match whose `location.file` is `./app.py`, an absolute path under repo_root,
      `a//b.py` (repeated separators), and an NFC/NFD unicode variant each STILL matches its
      changed-file entry `app.py` / `a/b.py` / the unicode name — the high-severity match is
      retained.
- [ ] A genuinely-different file (e.g. `other.py` not in `changed_files`) still does NOT match.
- [ ] `make test` green.
baseline.summary: Define and test the security-detector diff-scope path contract

baseline.description:
## Context
Discovered while implementing epic sonic-columned-sturgeon (op-certs). Children 4214 (merge-gate verify), ee0b (trusted-server producer), and 8f1d (HMAC→opcert migration) all depend on a shared primitive: **how an asymmetric op-cert (a DSSE envelope) is stored on a ticket and produced.** The epic decomposition treated this as implicit; it is a core event-sourcing change, so it gets its own ticket.

Today attestations are HMAC records. `reducer/_processors.py::process_signature` builds the `attestations[kind]` record from a FIXED field set (manifest/algorithm/signature/key_id/head_sha/ signed_at/author/kind) — it does NOT preserve an added `envelope`. Storing an op-cert DSSE envelope therefore requires a reducer change (runs on every ticket replay; the SNAPSHOT/compaction fold at `_processors.py:763` restores `attestations` verbatim, so op-cert fields survive compaction for free) plus a producer in `signing.py`.

## Selected design — Option A (DECIDED 2026-07-13 by Joe Oakhart; no further confirmation needed)
Extend the existing `SIGNATURE` event record — do NOT introduce a new event type. The *structural* choice (carry the new signature inside the existing event/record rather than a new event type) mirrors git signed commits (a `gpgsig` header on the existing commit object) and additive Protobuf/Avro schema evolution.

**Cross-version behavior (accurate — NOT tolerant-reader-transparent).** An op-cert `SIGNATURE` event carries the DSSE `envelope` and OMITS the HMAC `signature`/`algorithm`. So an OLD clone does not "ignore an unknown field and keep verifying": it reduces the event into a record with no HMAC and reads it as **UNSIGNED** — it cannot verify an op-cert because it lacks the asymmetric verifier. This is exactly the identity epic's SSHSIG-authorship rollout posture (older clones preserve the event append-only but cannot verify it) and the `TAG_DELTA` precedent: **op-cert events are preserved-but-unverifiable on pre-upgrade clones; upgrade the verify/reconcile hosts first.** What IS additive-transparent is the record *schema*: the new `envelope`/bound fields are present-only, so legacy HMAC `sign_manifest` records are byte-unchanged and existing HMAC verification is untouched.

Concretely:

- **Producer** (`signing.sign_opcert_manifest`, parallel to `sign_manifest`): builds a DSSE
  envelope via `opcert.sign_opcert(ticket_id, material_fingerprint, merged_log_commit,
  key_path=…, principal=…)`, then appends a `SIGNATURE` event whose record carries the signed
  `manifest` (first line `"<kind>: …"` so the reducer derives the kind), the encoded `envelope`
  (`dsse.encode`), the bound `material_fingerprint` + `merged_log_commit`, and `algorithm="sshsig"`
  — NO HMAC signature.
- **Reducer** (`process_signature`): additionally preserve `envelope`, `material_fingerprint`,
  `merged_log_commit` into the `attestations[kind]` record (read via `data.get(...)`, present-only).
  No change needed to the compaction fold (it restores `attestations` verbatim).
- **Read helper** (`opcert.opcert_from_record`): returns `(dsse.Envelope, {material_fingerprint,
  merged_log_commit})` when the record carries an `envelope`, else `None` (distinguishes an op-cert
  record from a legacy HMAC record).
- **Rollout:** op-cert events are preserved append-only by older clones but read as UNSIGNED
  there (no asymmetric verifier) — upgrade verify/reconcile hosts first, exactly as the SSHSIG
  authorship rollout and `TAG_DELTA` require. The record-schema extension itself is additive
  (legacy HMAC records unchanged).

(Considered and rejected: Option B — a new `OPCERT` event type + separate `opcerts` map — cleaner separation but larger change and its separation is moot once 8f1d removes HMAC.)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `signing.sign_opcert_manifest(...)` writes an envelope-bearing `SIGNATURE` event; a test
      asserts the ticket's reduced `attestations[<kind>]` record then carries the encoded
      `envelope` + bound `material_fingerprint`/`merged_log_commit`, and NO HMAC `signature`.
- [ ] `process_signature` preserves those fields through a full reduce AND through a
      compact-then-replay round-trip; a test asserts an op-cert survives compaction unchanged.
- [ ] `opcert.opcert_from_record(record)` returns `(envelope, bound_fields)` for an op-cert record
      and `None` for a legacy HMAC record (test both); the returned envelope, fed to
      `opcert.verify_opcert` with a pinned keyring, certifies (end-to-end test).
- [ ] The record-schema extension is additive (present-only): a test asserts a legacy HMAC
      `sign_manifest` record is byte-unchanged (no `envelope`/bound keys) and still HMAC-verifies,
      so existing HMAC attestations are untouched. Rollout note documented: op-cert events are
      preserved-but-unverifiable on pre-upgrade clones (read as unsigned) — upgrade verify/reconcile
      hosts first (as with SSHSIG authorship / `TAG_DELTA`).
- [ ] 4214 can read a stored op-cert to verify it over the merged log; ee0b/8f1d can produce op-certs
baseline.summary: op-cert storage + producer primitive (DSSE envelope on a ticket) — shared keystone for 4214/ee0b/8f1d
