# A shell-expanded comment body wrote live credentials into the ticket store; only GitHub push protection caught it

## What happened

An agent posted a ticket comment whose body quoted an upstream error message containing backtick-delimited text. The body was passed to `rebar comment` inside a DOUBLE-QUOTED shell argument, so zsh performed COMMAND SUBSTITUTION on the backticks. The backticked token happened to be `local`, a zsh builtin, which with no arguments prints every shell and environment variable. That dump was interpolated into the comment body and committed to the tickets store.

The resulting COMMENT event was 17,821 characters where the intended text was a few thousand, and contained live secrets read straight out of the environment:

* an Anthropic API key (`sk-ant-`, 108 chars)
* TWO GitHub personal access tokens (`ghp_`, 40 chars each)
* an OpenAI-style service key (`sk-svc-`, 167 chars)
* a Google-style API key and several base64 blobs

## Blast radius — nothing reached a remote, and the reason matters

GitHub secret-scanning PUSH PROTECTION rejected the push: "push declined due to repository rule violations ... To push, remove secret from commit(s)". Verified afterwards: the offending commit is on NO remote branch and is NOT an ancestor of origin/tickets. Every unpushed commit was scanned and exactly ONE commit / ONE file is affected.

So the credentials never left the machine. **The only control that stopped this was a third-party scanner on the far side of the push.** rebar itself accepted the body, signed it, committed it, and would have pushed it to a mirror of a real repository. That is the finding: there is no rebar-side control at all, and the one that saved us is outside the project.

A second consequence worth noting: because push protection blocks the whole ref update, the poisoned commit wedged 108 unrelated commits of legitimate ticket history behind it. A single bad body therefore also becomes an availability problem for the store's durability.

## Why this is rebar's problem and not merely operator error

The proximate cause is a quoting mistake by the caller, and callers will keep making it: agents routinely paste provider error text, log lines and code snippets into comments, and that text frequently contains backticks. The store's job is to persist what it is given, but it currently persists a credential dump silently and irreversibly (event files are append-only and signed), and the damage is only discoverable at push time, far from the cause.

Note also the asymmetry: rebar ALREADY understands that secrets must not be logged in some places, and the review-bot's own token exposure is tracked separately. There is no equivalent guard on the one surface that writes attacker-useful text to a git history.

## Scope

- the comment/description write path (whatever validates an event body before it is committed
  and signed) — a pre-write secret screen.
- optionally the CLI argument surface, so a body arriving with a shell-expanded variable dump is
  recognisable.
- documentation for agents on passing untrusted text to `rebar comment` safely.

## Approach

Two independent layers, and the first is the one that matters:

1. **Screen event bodies for high-confidence secret shapes before committing** — the same
   prefix families GitHub's scanner uses are cheap, low-false-positive anchors (an
   Anthropic/OpenAI key prefix, a GitHub token prefix, an AWS access-key id). On a hit, REFUSE
   the write with a clear error naming the matched family and offset. Refusing is correct rather
   than redacting: a body containing a live credential is almost never the body the author meant
   to write, so silently truncating it would hide the mistake that produced it.
2. **Make the shell hazard hard to hit** — document the safe invocation (write the body to a
   file and pass it via a form the shell does not re-scan) and prefer a stdin/file-based body
   argument over a positional string for long bodies.

Deliberately NOT proposed: scanning the whole store retroactively, or weakening the append-only event model. The guard belongs at the write boundary.

## Testing

- a body containing a synthetic token of each screened family is REFUSED, with the family named,
  and NO event file is written and NO commit is created. Verify RED by removing the screen.
- a body containing look-alike-but-harmless text (a hex string, the literal word 'sk-ant' with no
  key material, a base64 blob under the length floor) is ACCEPTED, so the screen does not become
  a nuisance that agents learn to work around.
- a body legitimately quoting backticked text is stored VERBATIM when passed by the documented
  safe path, proving the fix does not merely forbid the content that triggered the incident.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] an event body containing a high-confidence secret shape is refused at the write boundary,
      before any event file is written, signed, or committed — proven by a test verified RED.
- [ ] the refusal names the matched secret family and does not echo the secret value.
- [ ] look-alike benign text is not refused, evidenced by explicit negative cases, so the screen
      does not train agents to route around it.
- [ ] the safe way to pass untrusted or quoted text as a comment body is documented where agents
      will read it, with the failure mode named (shell command substitution on backticks).
- [ ] the incident is recorded with its blast radius, including that the only control which
      stopped it was outside the project.
baseline.summary: Ticket store persists shell-expanded credential dumps; only GitHub push protection caught a live PAT leak

baseline.description:
## Why
This is the convergence mechanism itself: reuse plan-review's novelty machinery to stop code review re-nagging carryover findings and to drop novel low-impact findings on UNCHANGED code, while ALWAYS raising novel findings on newly-changed code (the per-citation region gate is the deliberate divergence from plan-review's whole-artifact floor).

## What
- **Consume the reader.** Call `latest_code_review_result(key)` (revenued-thickset-dassie) for the
  current review's typed key to obtain prior SURFACED findings + the prior `deps` map. Key selection:
  `session:<id>` for local reviews (set on the verdict by paradoxal-balsamic-bubblefish),
  `change:<id>` for Gerrit.
- **REUSE unchanged kernel primitives (no fork):** the novelty SCORING CONTRACT
  (`review_kernel.verify.novelty_model` / `NOVELTY_SUBANSWERS`), the reshaper
  `review_kernel.verify.reshape_novelties`, the per-finding novelty math
  `review_kernel.decide.novelty`, and the drop predicate
  `review_kernel.decide.rising_floor_drop(priority, novelty, *, t_novel, floor)` — all verbatim. A
  thin `score_code_novelty` (mirroring plan-review's `_score_floor_novelty` runner wiring) drives
  the sub-call and, from `reshape_novelties`, surfaces BOTH the novelty float (for the drop) AND the
  `matched_prior_id` (for `carried_from`). NOTE: it does NOT reuse the kernel `score_novelty`
  wrapper verbatim — that returns only `{index: float}` and DISCARDS `matched_prior_id`, which the
  carryover-labeling AC needs; `score_code_novelty` reuses the same underlying primitives
  (reshape + decide.novelty) so the scoring is identical, just also returning the matched id.
- **NEW code-review novelty PROMPT + reviewer id.** Add `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code_review_novelty.md`
  (`outputs: code_review_novelty`, `execution_mode: single_turn`, `category: code-review-pass`) and a
  `code-novelty` reviewer id used in the sub-call's `RunRequest(reviewers=["code-novelty"])`. Wiring
  mirrors plan-review's `_score_floor_novelty` runner: the diff is the domain context and the prior
  SURFACED findings are appended to the instructions as a context block (NOT a `{{plan}}`/template
  var). Register the reused contract at `code_review/contracts.py::register_contracts()`
  (`contracts.register_contract("code_review_novelty", novelty_model)`, importing `novelty_model`
  from `review_kernel.verify`) — mirroring `plan_review/passes.py`; without it a
  `RunRequest(output_schema="code_review_novelty")` fails at runtime.
  - **cites_prior_location REDEFINED for code (critical).** `NOVELTY_SUBANSWERS` shares the field
    name `cites_prior_location`, whose kernel/plan meaning is "same PLAN location/section/AC line".
    The code prompt MUST firmly redefine it so the model does not anchor on the plan meaning:
    `cites_prior_location — does this finding point at the SAME source file AND approximately the
    same line region (within ~10 lines) as the prior finding? (not merely the same file — the same
    localized area)`. (This closes the epic-review advisory T1.)
- **NEW `region_gate.py`** (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/region_gate.py`) defining the region-state
  vocabulary + detector:
  - Constants: `REGION_UNCHANGED = "unchanged"`, `REGION_CHANGED = "changed"`, `REGION_UNKNOWN = "unknown"`.
  - **Citation basis:** a finding's cited region is derived from its `location` field (a `path` or
    `path:line`). The detector takes the finding's cited FILE path, hashes the current file
    (`attest._hash_file`), and compares to `prior_deps[path]`: equal → `UNCHANGED`; differ → `CHANGED`;
    path absent from `prior_deps`, OR the finding is multi-location / absence-evidence (no concrete
    file) / moved / renamed / any error → `UNKNOWN`. File-level in v1 (line-level deferred).
- **NEW `region_gated_floor`** (in `code_review/workflow_ops.py`, applied over the decided advisory
  set in the produce path before the sidecar emit — the code-review analogue of plan-review's
  `_maybe_apply_rising_floor`, which sits after the verdict and before emit):
  - A finding is DROPPED iff `rising_floor_drop(priority, novelty, t_novel, floor)` is true AND its
    region is `REGION_UNCHANGED`. `REGION_CHANGED` and `REGION_UNKNOWN` NEVER drop (both raise).
  - **Thresholds/activation (decided):** reuse the EXISTING config — `verify.novelty_drop_threshold`
    (t_novel), `verify.novelty_priority_floor` (floor), AND `verify.novelty_drop_active` as the
    activation/evidence gate. This introduces NO NEW config key (the epic's "no eval-gated
    activation flag" = no NEW flag): the code-review floor reuses plan-review's SAME three keys, so
    it is OFF by default and an operator opts in with evidence exactly as plan-review requires
    (preserving the opt-in-with-evidence discipline the reviewer flagged). On top of the flag, the
    floor also SELF-GATES: inert whenever there is no prior memory for the current key (first review,
    or a reader error → empty prior set). Both gates must be open to drop anything.
  - Dropped findings carry `drop_reason = "novelty-region"`.
  - **Carryover labeling:** a finding that matches a prior surfaced finding (low novelty) but is NOT
    dropped is stamped `carried_from` = the `matched_prior_id` returned by `score_code_novelty` for
    that finding (the prior finding's id; empty ⇒ not stamped). Data model: by the time the floor runs (post-decide, in the produce path), findings
    are plain dicts in the verdict's `advisory`/`blocking` lists — `carried_from` is added as a KEY
    on that dict (no Pydantic model change needed; the coach already ran in-workflow, so the floor
    strips coaching notes whose `finding_refs` point at a `carried_from`-stamped finding from the
    verdict's `coaching` list). The finding remains surfaced.
  - **FAIL-SAFE (full mirror of plan-review):** the whole floor is wrapped in try/except; any
    reader/hash/compare/novelty error returns the FULL unfiltered finding set (no drops). A finding
    with no novelty entry defaults to novelty 0.0 (carryover = kept).
- **Neutrality (ADR 0008 Invariant 1):** the Pass-1 finder NEVER receives prior findings; only the
  post-find novelty seam does.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py` (region_gated_floor + novelty sub-call wiring),
  `src/rebar/llm/code_review/region_gate.py` (NEW: vocab + detector),
  `src/rebar/llm/code_review/contracts.py` (register `code_review_novelty`),
  `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code_review_novelty.md` (NEW prompt),
  `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` (invoke the floor before emit).
- Depends on the reader/payload (revenued-thickset-dassie) and, for end-to-end LOCAL integration, on
  local persistence (paradoxal-balsamic-bubblefish). This story is reviewed/implemented AFTER c639
  (+3bff) are committed on the stack, so the reader (`latest_code_review_result`) + `deps` map exist
  in the tree; region_gated_floor UNIT tests run against a mocked reader.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A `code-novelty` reviewer prompt (`code_review_novelty.md`) + reviewer id exist, binding the
      reused novelty contract, with diff context + prior findings in the instructions block and
      `cites_prior_location` redefined for source-file/line regions.
- [ ] The `code_review_novelty` contract is registered in `contracts.register_contracts()`;
      `rising_floor_drop`, `reshape_novelties`, and `decide.novelty` are reused UNCHANGED (the thin
      `score_code_novelty` surfaces `matched_prior_id` for carryover; it does not reuse the
      `score_novelty` wrapper, which discards it).
- [ ] `region_gate.py` defines `REGION_UNCHANGED`/`REGION_CHANGED`/`REGION_UNKNOWN` used by the
      detector, which compares a cited file's current sha256 to the prior `deps` map.
- [ ] `region_gated_floor` drops a finding ONLY when novel AND low-priority AND `REGION_UNCHANGED`;
      `REGION_CHANGED` and `REGION_UNKNOWN` both raise; dropped findings carry
      `drop_reason = "novelty-region"`.
- [ ] Thresholds/activation reuse the EXISTING `verify.novelty_drop_threshold`,
      `verify.novelty_priority_floor`, and `verify.novelty_drop_active` (no NEW config key); the
      floor is OFF by default and additionally self-gates inert with no prior memory.
- [ ] Carryover findings are stamped `carried_from` = the matched prior finding's id (string, added
      as a dict key), have their coaching notes stripped from the verdict, but remain surfaced.
- [ ] Any reader/hash/compare/novelty error returns the full unfiltered finding set (no drops).
- [ ] The Pass-1 finder receives no prior findings; only the novelty seam does — asserted by a test
      that the finder/verifier pass inputs contain no prior-findings context (ADR 0008 Invariant 1).
- [ ] Tests (mocked reader): unchanged-region low-priority novel → dropped; changed-region novel →
      raised; absence/multi-location → UNKNOWN → raised; carryover → `carried_from` = matched id +
      coaching stripped; forced reader error → no drops; and a neutrality test that the Pass-1
      finder step receives no prior findings.
baseline.summary: region_gated_floor: content-addressed novelty convergence for code review

baseline.description:
A single failed Jira mutation (e.g. an unreachable workflow transition) aborts the entire reconciler pass mid-way, silently skipping all later mutations. The reconciler should isolate per-mutation failures: apply everything it can, then fail loud at the END with a non-zero exit and a report of what failed.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Have a local ticket whose mapped Jira status is not reachable via any available
   workflow transition on its Jira issue (e.g. a local `idea` before the Jira
   `IDEA` status/transitions are provisioned).
2. Run a reconcile pass that includes that ticket plus other tickets with valid
   mutations.
3. Observe the pass abort when it reaches the unreachable transition.

## Expected vs Actual

- Expected: the reconciler applies every other (valid) mutation in the pass,
  records the failed one, and at the END exits non-zero with a report naming the
  failed mutation(s) — no valid mutation is silently skipped.
- Actual: `transition_issue_by_name` raises an uncaught `RuntimeError` (no
  transition reaches the target), or the preflight raises `StatusMappingError`,
  aborting the whole pass mid-way; mutations for all subsequent tickets are skipped
  until the next scheduled run.

## Context

This is independent of the `idea` feature (it affects every transition), but it is the mechanism that makes the `idea → IDEA` create-drops-status convergence and the "Jira not yet configured" window tolerable instead of pass-aborting — see the `idea` epic and its "Jira `idea ↔ IDEA` mapping" story. Relevant code: the abort sites are the preflight in `reconcile.py` (`StatusMappingError`), the per-mutation error handling in `dispatch_one.py` (only HTTP-400 "illegal transition" currently degrades to a comment-fallback), and the `RuntimeError` in `acli.py::transition_issue_by_name` when no transition reaches the target.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A reconcile pass containing one unreachable-transition mutation still applies
      every other valid mutation in that pass (test-verified).
- [ ] The failed mutation is recorded and surfaced in the pass's end-of-run report.
- [ ] The pass exits non-zero when any mutation failed (fail loud), rather than
      exiting 0 or aborting mid-pass.
- [ ] A `RuntimeError` from `transition_issue_by_name` (no transition reaches the
      target) is caught per-mutation and does not abort the pass.
- [ ] The status-mapping preflight does not abort the whole pass for a single
      unmapped/unreachable status.
- [ ] `make lint` and the reconciler test suite pass.
baseline.summary: Reconciler aborts whole pass on one failed Jira transition; should isolate + fail loud at end

## Report

`tests/unit/test_path_injection_guards.py::test_rerun_502_body_has_no_exception_detail` FAILS on current `origin/main` (reproduced standalone at 43ecfa8f27, and independently at 9bdb22f5887 before that):

```
AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'headers'
src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:101: in _request_token
    header_token = request.headers.get(TOKEN_HEADER, "").strip()
```

## Mechanism (unconfirmed — for the investigation to prove)

`_request_token` (`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:101`) reads `request.headers` unconditionally. The header path was added for ticket 66af (accept the token via header, keeping the query param for legacy Gerrit webhooks whose `webhooks.config` has not been re-pushed). The test constructs its request as a `types.SimpleNamespace` that predates that change and carries no `headers` attribute, so the attribute read raises before any assertion runs.

Whether the correct fix is to make `_request_token` tolerate a header-less request object, or to update the test's fake to match the real request contract, is EXACTLY the question the investigation must answer — a header-less request may be a real shape in production (some ASGI/test clients) or may be purely a test artifact. Do not assume.

## Why it matters

This is red on main. It reds the `Verified` CI gate for anyone whose change touches this suite, and it is a SECURITY-adjacent guard: the test exists to prove a 502 body carries no exception detail (path-injection guard). A guard test that errors before asserting proves nothing — the guarantee it is supposed to pin is currently unverified.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The root cause is proven, with a cited mechanism, not guessed — the stale `types.SimpleNamespace` request double at tests/unit/test_path_injection_guards.py:163-166, left behind when ticket 66af (4e8c83c833) widened `_request_token` (src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:101) to read `request.headers` FIRST.
- [x] It is established and stated whether a header-less request is a REAL production shape or a test-only artifact, with evidence — **TEST ARTIFACT, not a real shape.** starlette's `HTTPConnection.headers` (requests.py:132-136) is an unconditional property; deleting `headers` from an ASGI scope raises `KeyError`, NEVER `AttributeError` — so the observed `AttributeError` is only producible by an object that is not a `Request` at all. A real request with zero caller headers still carries an empty `Headers`. FastAPI binds a `Request`-annotated param behind an `isinstance` gate (fastapi/dependencies/utils.py:711), whose only alternative is `WebSocket` — also an `HTTPConnection`, also with `.headers`. Full evidence in the Phase 1 RCA comment.
- [x] The test passes on a clean tree and actually exercises its original assertion (a 502 body containing no exception detail), not merely stops erroring — proven by defect-seeded mutation: adding `"detail": str(exc)` to the 502 body returns the test to RED, naming the leaked string in the failure output. The ORIGINAL test could not have caught that; it raised before its first assert.
- [x] A regression test fails against the pre-fix code and passes after — two mutations of the production path each return it to RED (leak the exception detail -> assertion diff; stub out the `X-Rebar-Token` header read -> 401), and it is GREEN with src/rebar/review_bot/app.py byte-identical to main. No production code changed.
- [x] The fix lands on main through Gerrit with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 — change 1481 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1481): LLM-Review+1 (PASS) and Verified+1 (Actions run 31167914711, SUCCESS), 0 unresolved comments, MERGED 2026-08-07 10:17:28 as origin/main aaf71639b8.
baseline.summary: test_rerun_502_body_has_no_exception_detail fails on main: _request_token reads request.headers on a header-less fake request

STATUS: TABLED — a sensitive reconciler-CORE change, deferred by decision. This idea is a resume pointer; the FULL raw record (measured facts, verified findings, 4 history dossiers on WHY the current design exists, options, open gates) is in session_log **bdc7-9256-ff48-4520** (felicific-hardheaded-elephant). Prior measured facts + cited prior-art research: session_log **b96a-15a5-1c0a-47c5**. Umbrella: **1270-b740**.

## Problem
The rebar tickets git store (.tickets-tracker, `tickets` branch) grows UNBOUNDEDLY: ~443 MB / ~178k objects for ~15k tickets, of which ~85% (~375 MB) is the reconciler's `.bridge_state/` Jira-sync cache — bindings.json (219 MB / ~987 versions) + prev_snapshot.json (155 MB / ~4450 versions). By packed size the repo is 95.7% blobs, so tree/sharding/active-archive splits are the WRONG lever. Every ephemeral CI job and local clone pays the full history on clone.

## Key findings (verified this session)
1. Nothing reads the git HISTORY of .bridge_state — only the current worktree copy. Its history's sole value is debugging.
2. prev_snapshot is NOT redundant (an earlier "delete it" hypothesis was disproven): its direction-arbitration role IS superseded by the per-binding baseline in bindings.json, but it remains the load-bearing EDGE-TRIGGER ancestor (run_differs.py:198 -> differ.py:299 inbound-create). It is, however, grossly OVER-PROVISIONED: its live consumers need only the SET of Jira keys, not the full ACLI payload -> can shrink 24 MB -> ~25 KB and stop churning every pass.
3. bindings.json's dominant growth driver is `baseline_advanced_at`, a WRITE-ONLY timestamp bumped unconditionally on ~92% of entries every pass (never read) — so the file rewrites a scattered delta every pass (~987 versions ~= ~987 passes). Content is 97% baseline, 86% of which is the description stored as full ADF dict.
4. Storage posture is settled (epic 6c9c): .bridge_state stays committed on-branch as a merge=ours derived cache; event-sourcing/re-homing it (WS-1) was explicitly dropped. Trust verification is ancestry-based (survives a consistent history rewrite) EXCEPT the absolute-SHA enforce_since pin (rebar.toml:105).

## Plan (tabled; implement in order)
1. prev_snapshot -> bare KEY-SET (dict {jira_key:{}}), after clearing the open gate G1. + dead-code cleanup of the fixture-only prev plumbing.
2. bindings.json: CHURN GUARD (drop/guard baseline_advanced_at + write-when-changed in set_baseline; collapses version count) THEN TEXT NORMALIZE (adf_to_text + .name, -66%, no migration). DIGEST (-92%) optional, higher-risk, only behind a dual-write-shadow rollout, and EXCLUDE assignee (one-to-many match = REB-532 risk).
3. DEBUG TRAIL: a separate bounded full-Jira-snapshot artifact, max 1/day, 15-day retention, on a dated disjoint path, never fail-closed.
4. ONE-TIME coordinated history reclaim (filter-repo strip old .bridge_state blobs): a reconciler-paused, all-clones-converged 8-step flag-day with lockstep enforce_since re-pin. Do LAST.

## Open gates (resolve before implementing) — see session log [10]
- G1 (blocks step 1): resolve whether differ._compute_mutations_emit_both reaches Jira with a key-set prev (null-ancestor field-clear risk) via a corpus mutation-diff. THE critical fence.
- G2 (blocks digest): normalization parity + extend direction-preservation property suite first.
- G3: coordinate with the ACTIVE reconciler session (epic 58b0 sync-correctness) — shared differ/field contract; ride the proven dual-write-shadow -> N-divergent=0 -> flip rollout template.
- G4: enforce_since re-pin + converge ALL auto-pushing clones or --allow-unrelated-histories drags the stripped blobs back.

## Decisions already made
Debug trail = 1/day x 15-day; existing 337 MB = one-time coordinated reclaim; bindings.json investigated now (folded in). .bridge_state stays committed (required for ephemeral CI + local consistency).
baseline.summary: Bound tickets-repo growth: shrink reconciler .bridge_state on-branch (prev->key-set + bindings churn-guard/normalize) + one-time history reclaim

# Cloud Markdown↔ADF functions (pure capability; AdfCodec untouched)

## Context / Problem
Jira Cloud stores rich text as ADF (structured JSON). The `RichTextCodec` seam (epic e369, story J3) routes Cloud rich text through `AdfCodec` (`adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py`), a pass-through over the pinned `adapters/jira/adf.py`. **`adf.py`'s encode is plain-text-structured, not Markdown-aware:** `text_to_adf` (`adf.py:275`) splits on blank lines and emits each block as one `paragraph`, so headings, list markers, fenced code and inline bold/strike/link are carried as **literal characters** and Cloud renders raw source. `adf_to_text` (`adf.py:26`) already emits Markdown-ish text on decode; the missing half is a Markdown-aware **encode**.

**Why pure functions, not a codec change.** On Cloud the codec ops are reachable on the LIVE send path (`AdfCodec.fit_outbound` fits the posted description; compare sites call `adf.py` directly), so repointing `AdfCodec` here would change live truncation and comparison — a cutover that must land with echo-safety in story 3388. This story adds the functions and tests only, leaving `AdfCodec` a plain pass-through (`rich_text_codec.py:25/29/33/37`). Nothing observable changes on merge.

## Engine: marklas as an OPTIONAL EXTRA, lazily imported (not vendored)
`marklas` (pure-Python, mistune-based; `github.com/byExist/marklas`) pinned EXACTLY at **0.8.6** as a new optional extra together with its transitive `mistune` 3.3.4. The pin is exact because this story depends on a specific API surface — encode `marklas.to_adf`, decode `marklas.to_md` — and on measured output shape. Licences: marklas is **MIT**, mistune is **BSD-3-Clause** (both OSI-approved, both permissive); the extra records each.

**Superseded plan + deviation record.** The earlier plan vendored marklas under `src/rebar/_vendor/marklas/`. A plan review BLOCKed that: marklas needs `mistune`, the engine importing `adf.py` is contractually dependency-free (`pyproject.toml:69`), and `src/rebar/_vendor/` is not importable from the reconciler subprocess. Chosen instead: **lazy-import inside the three function bodies, with `ImportError` routed to the plain-text `adf.py` fallback** — preserving the stdlib-only contract and mirroring the `agents`/`metrics`/`grounding` extras. Vendoring stays available later; this is the deviation record. The "tolerate a no-extras install" requirement belongs to story 3388's cutover and is recorded there.

## Measured evidence (re-measured here; the prior figures did not survive)
The prior plan quoted a 2026-08-03 export and `files/parity_*.py` artifacts. **None of that survives** — not on disk, not in git history; rebar has no attachment store. Re-measured against the live store (4,996 unique bodies): idempotence **reproduces** (99.65% claimed vs 99.75% measured); the "5,730 bodies" cardinality is **stale**; and structural richness does **NOT** reproduce (56.7% claimed vs 20.5% measured). AC bars are set from the committed fixture, not from the claims.

**Richness predicate (explicit):** a body is structurally rich iff its encoded ADF contains at least one non-paragraph BLOCK node — `heading`, `bulletList`, `orderedList`, `codeBlock`, `taskList`, `blockquote`, `rule`, `table` or `panel`. Inline marks alone do NOT qualify (that looser predicate yields 25.2%).

A full corpus cannot be committed: `check-added-large-files` caps files at 500 KB, there is no LFS, and `.gitignore` records a decision not to raise it. The fixture is a scrubbed, sharded sample from a committed generator, mirroring `scripts/capture_jira_fixtures.py` doctrine.

## Two defects the functions must handle (both reproduced here)
1. **Combined-mark 2-cycle.** `A **~~both~~** end` ⇄ `A ~~**both**~~ end` alternates
   forever under repeated round-trip — an exact 2-cycle. A deterministic
   **mark-order canonicalizer** in `adf_to_markdown` is required.
2. **HTML comments are dropped.** marklas removes them: `text <!-- x --> more`
   becomes `text  more`, and a lone marker becomes the empty string. rebar's own
   reconciler echo marker is an HTML comment. 8 of 4,996 live bodies carry one and
   3 of the first 8 lose it. **Mechanism:** `markdown_to_adf` self-verifies — it
   decodes its own result and, if any `<!-- … -->` present in the source is missing,
   returns the plain `text_to_adf(md)` encode for that body instead — so an engine
   quirk degrades richness rather than losing content. Exactly 1 of the 360
   committed corpus bodies carries an HTML comment, and it loses that comment
   without this mechanism.

## Approach (pure functions in `adf.py`)
Add three functions, **not referenced by any `AdfCodec` op or live send path here**:
1. `markdown_to_adf(md) -> dict` — Markdown-aware encode via `marklas.to_adf`, with
   the HTML-comment self-verification above.
2. `adf_to_markdown(doc) -> str` — decode via `marklas.to_md`, applying the
   mark-order canonicalizer.
3. `fit_markdown_to_adf_limit(md, *, limit=…) -> str` — length-fit measuring the
   `markdown_to_adf` serialization.
Plus a whole-codec **plain-text fallback helper** returning the existing plain `adf.py` functions as a set, which 3388 installs on conversion error — defined and unit-tested here, wired there. Existing plain functions stay untouched.

## Scope
- `adapters/jira/adf.py` — the three functions + canonicalizer + fallback helper.
- `pyproject.toml` — pinned optional extra (marklas + mistune); `src/rebar/_optional.py`
  — register it.
- `scripts/build_cloud_adf_corpus.py` (new) + `tests/fixtures/cloud_adf_corpus/` (new).
- **UNCHANGED:** `AdfCodec` and its four ops; the shared plain-text
  `inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text`; every live Cloud send/compare site.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `adf.markdown_to_adf` emits Markdown-aware ADF nodes (heading/list/code plus
  inline marks) rather than literal `#`/`-`/`**`; verified by
  `test_cloud_adf_roundtrip` asserting node types.
- [x] `adf.adf_to_markdown` returns the source Markdown for a structured body;
  verified by `test_cloud_adf_roundtrip` asserting decoded equality.
- [x] The combined strong+strikethrough 2-cycle is eliminated by the mark-order
  canonicalizer; verified by `test_cloud_mark_order_converges` pinning the measured
  `**~~x~~**` ⇄ `~~**x**~~` oscillation as a regression.
- [x] An HTML comment present in the source survives the round-trip, falling back to
  the plain encode when the engine would drop it; verified by
  `test_cloud_html_comment_survives`.
- [x] `adf.fit_markdown_to_adf_limit` measures the `markdown_to_adf` serialization
  rather than the plain encode; verified by
  `test_adf_fit_measures_the_serialized_document_not_the_plain_text`.
- [x] With marklas absent, importing `adf` succeeds and each of the three functions
  returns its plain-`adf.py` result rather than raising; verified by
  `test_cloud_functions_degrade_without_marklas` simulating the ImportError.
- [x] The plain-text fallback helper returns the existing plain `adf.py` functions
  as a set; verified by `test_cloud_plain_fallback_helper_returns_plain_functions`.
- [x] Over the committed `tests/fixtures/cloud_adf_corpus/`, the MD→ADF→MD
  round-trip reaches a fixed point after one pass for ≥99.6% of bodies (measured
  100.00% over 360 bodies, 0 conversion errors); verified by
  `test_cloud_corpus_idempotence`.
- [x] Over the same fixture, ≥15% of bodies encode to structurally rich ADF under
  the block-node predicate defined above (measured 15.6%); verified by
  `test_cloud_corpus_richness`.
- [x] The committed fixture cardinality is pinned at 360 bodies, so a silent
  regeneration fails; verified by `test_cloud_corpus_cardinality_is_pinned`.
- [x] The committed fixture carries no unscrubbed emails, tenant hostnames or URLs;
  verified by `test_cloud_corpus_carries_no_unscrubbed_secrets`.
- [x] `AdfCodec` and its four ops remain a plain pass-through; verified by the
  existing `test_adf_codec_is_a_pass_through_to_the_pinned_adf_module` staying green
  unmodified.
baseline.summary: Cloud ADF codec (marklas), truly bidirectional

baseline.description:
## Why
The plan-review calibration epic (6982) can cheaply measure DETECTION on KNOWN-seeded defects (E2) and
judge RELIABILITY via self-consistency (E6), and it can lean on the gate's own persisted sidecar
validity/impact. What it CANNOT currently produce is an **independent finding-level TP/FP gold set** — a
verdict on the gate's surface/drop decisions from a standard OTHER than the gate itself. That gold set is
the missing ingredient for measuring the gate's PRECISION on REAL plans (false-positive rate) and for
calibrating Pass-2's sub-question / impact-axis thresholds against ground truth rather than the gate's own
opinion. This idea parks that work, DESIGNED ENOUGH to resume, once human adjudication time is budgeted.

## Context — why the first attempt (E1's adjudication corpus) was invalidated
The E1 finding-adjudication corpus was labeled by a process WEAKER than the gate it judged and is invalid
(79% of labels contaminated). Two root causes, both to AVOID here:
1. The LLM rater saw a TRUNCATED plan (PLAN_CAP=6000 chars); production reviews the WHOLE plan + children.
2. The LLM rater ran single-pass with NO tools; production runs 16 criteria as AGENTIC finders that grep
   the codebase. The human adjudication inherited the flaw (dispute set selected by the faulty process,
   anchored on faulty rationales, not independently code-grounded). Re-running the gate's OWN grounded
   verifier to label is CIRCULAR (it just reproduces the sidecar). So the gold set MUST come from
   independent HUMAN judgment, made efficient by grounded evidence.

## What (design — hard-won constraints)
Build a stratified, review-time-faithful, human-adjudicated finding-level TP/FP gold set:
- **Sample:** reuse the surviving E1 finding SAMPLE (300 surfaced + 100 dropped, text-bearing, positionally
  bucketed by coverage.counts, stratified by criterion). Over-weight the code-grounded criteria
  (E4/G1G2/G3/G4/G6/G7/T1/T3/T5c/T8/T10/T11/T13/T14/A1/removal-rationale) and the surfaced/dropped boundary,
  where the gate is hardest to judge.
- **Adjudicator capability floor (non-negotiable):** the human must judge each finding with (a) the WHOLE
  plan + children (never truncated), and (b) the finding's cited code. Provide GROUNDED EVIDENCE via the
  already-prototyped reuse pipeline (harnesses/grounded_batch_adjudicate.py + verify_single_finding.yaml):
  it reruns production's plan-review-verifier-agentic (assemble_context + get_runner agentic + pai_tools
  codebase tools) to surface the cited code, the binary sub-answers, and the impact axes — so the human
  adjudicates efficiently, NOT from raw text. The human JUDGMENT stays independent of the gate (do not adopt
  the verifier's label as truth — use its evidence).
- **Review-time grounding (required):** ground each finding at the commit its review ran against. Recover it
  from the ticket's REVIEW_RESULT event timestamps -> the contemporaneous origin/main SHA (git rev-list -1
  --before). Current-HEAD grounding is biased (drift flips verdicts: e165 moved dropped->advisory).
- **Plan-version fidelity (required):** restrict to plan_matches_review=True tickets (~85%/165 of 195 in the
  E1 sample; compare the review round's material_fingerprint to the current one). Exclude drifted-plan
  tickets (the finding is about a plan that no longer exists) unless old-plan reconstruction is added.
- **Reliability:** double-adjudicate a stratified subset by a second human; report a prevalence-robust
  agreement (Gwet AC1 / raw agreement), NOT bare Cohen's kappa (TP-skew triggers the kappa paradox).
- **Deliverable:** a frozen gold JSONL {finding_id, ticket_id, review_sha, plan_matches_review, human_label
  (TP/FP), adjudicator, grounded_evidence_ref}, plus the gate's own sidecar call per finding, so the
  human-vs-gate DELTA localizes which Pass-2 sub-questions/axes miscalibrate.

## How it enriches epic 6982
- Gives E2/E3/R1 a real FP/TP standard to calibrate blocking thresholds + measure precision on REAL plans
  (complements E2's construct-valid seeded-defect detection ground truth).
- Turns E6 from self-consistency-only into self-consistency-vs-truth (does a stable judge also agree with the
  human gold?).
- The human-vs-verifier deltas are the direct refinement backlog for the Pass-2 verification questions.

## Cost / prerequisite
The BINDING constraint is human adjudication TIME (this is why it is deferred, not the LLM cost — the grounded
evidence pipeline is ~$0.30/finding). Budget/staff the human adjudication before promoting idea->open. The
machinery (sample, grounded evidence harness, review-time resolver) already exists from the E1 session.

## Acceptance Criteria (for when promoted idea -> open)
- [ ] A stratified human-adjudicated gold set of >= N findings (choose N by human budget) is committed, each
      row grounded at its review-time SHA with plan_matches_review=True and grounded evidence attached.
- [ ] A double-adjudicated subset reports prevalence-robust inter-adjudicator agreement (Gwet AC1 + raw).
- [ ] The gate's sidecar call is recorded beside each human label; the human-vs-gate delta table is produced
      and handed to the Pass-2-refinement stories.
- [ ] The adjudication protocol (whole-plan + code-grounded + review-time + independent human judgment) is
      documented so the gold set is reproducible and defensibly independent of the gate.
baseline.summary: Human-adjudicated finding-level TP/FP gold corpus (independent, grounded, review-time-faithful) — future enrichment for the plan-review calibration epic

# Release build fails: check_build_env_locked doesn't PEP 503-normalize package names

The hash-locked `--no-isolation` release build aborts because `scripts/check_build_env_locked.py` compares package names WITHOUT PEP 503 canonicalization, so a package whose `pip freeze` name uses `.`/`_` but whose lock entry uses `-` is falsely reported "installed but ABSENT from the lock", failing the build job and blocking every release.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Dispatch `release.yml` from `main` (v0.8.0 attempt, run 29467136412).
2. The `Build distributions (build-once)` job runs
   `python scripts/check_build_env_locked.py --lock .github/release-requirements.txt --freeze <(pip freeze)`.
3. It exits 1 with: `jaraco.classes==3.4.0: installed but ABSENT from the lock` (also
   `jaraco.context`, `jaraco.functools`, `pyproject_hooks`, `readme_renderer`).

Local repro: `python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts');import check_build_env_locked as m;print(set(m._parse_pins('jaraco-classes==3.4.0'))==set(m._parse_pins('jaraco.classes==3.4.0')))"` prints `False`.

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** `jaraco.classes` (from `pip freeze`) and `jaraco-classes` (in the
  pip-compile lock) are recognized as the SAME package (PEP 503: runs of `[-_.]`
  collapse to a single `-`), so the subset check passes and the build proceeds.
- **Actual:** the two spellings hash to different keys, so the installed package is
  judged absent from the lock and the build FAILS — even though it is pinned.

## Root cause

`_parse_pins` lowercases the name and strips an `[extra]` suffix but does not apply PEP 503 name normalization. `build`/`twine`'s transitive deps (`jaraco-classes/-context/ -functools`, `readme-renderer`, `pyproject-hooks`) are pinned in the lock with hyphens but reported by `pip freeze` with dots/underscores, so they never match. This is the first release through the new pinned build-once pipeline (08a8/6168 landed after v0.7.1), so the mismatch was never exercised.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `scripts/check_build_env_locked.py` canonicalizes every package name with PEP 503
  normalization (`re.sub(r"[-_.]+", "-", name).lower()`) on BOTH the lock and freeze
  sides before comparing (verify: the two spellings map to one key —
  `python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts');import check_build_env_locked as m;assert set(m._parse_pins('jaraco-classes==3.4.0'))==set(m._parse_pins('jaraco.classes==3.4.0'))"`).
- [ ] A regression test in `tests/unit/test_check_build_env_locked.py` fails before the
  fix and passes after: a lock with `jaraco-classes==3.4.0` and a freeze with
  `jaraco.classes==3.4.0` (and an `_`/`.` variant) is accepted as lock-consistent
  (`main([...]) == 0`), and a genuine version mismatch on a normalized name still fails.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass, and re-dispatching `release.yml`
  from `main` with `version=0.8.0` gets past the build's env-lock guard.
baseline.summary: Release build fails: check_build_env_locked missing PEP 503 name normalization

## Context / Problem
The reconcile-bridge-canary workflow carries ~200 lines of production logic in YAML run-blocks — staleness classification, two alert-ticket lifecycle state machines (heartbeat + binding-drift), each with find/open/comment/close steps. This is the highest-defect shell surface (449f: 7 recommendations), untestable and unlintable by ruff. The companion reconcile-bridge.yml push-back loop was ALSO a defect source (4c4f), but that loop's fix deliberately kept it in YAML under a verbatim-execution test — see Alternatives below.

## Alternatives / prior art
tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py (ticket 4c4f) established that CAS push loops on the hot tickets ref stay in workflow YAML and are tested VERBATIM (extracting them creates an untested-glue drift seam; the block contains zero ${{ }} expressions so the YAML itself is executable under test). This plan honors that decision: BOTH CAS push loops — reconcile-bridge.yml "Commit reconciler events back and push" (93L) and the canary's "Flush any unpushed ticket changes" (35L) — are OUT of scope and stay in YAML. What migrates is classification/alert-lifecycle logic, which differs from the push loops in kind: it has branchy decision logic (API-error vs zero-state vs stale; dedup-find vs open vs comment vs close), no git-ref CAS races, and it currently interleaves ${{ }} expressions with logic — exactly the shape that benefits from extraction + unit tests. The drift-seam risk the 4c4f rationale warns about is mitigated the same way the probe port (f1eb) mitigated it: an anti-rot unit test pins the thin YAML invocations (workflow parses, step invokes the canonical Python entry point with the expected env/args), and the extracted functions carry their own unit tests.

Deployment note: the f1eb executes-from-main trap does NOT apply here — gerrit-verify.yaml never runs the canary, and reconcile-bridge-canary.yml executes from main on schedule/workflow_dispatch only AFTER this change merges, so workflow edits and the new script deploy atomically; no transitional shim is needed.

The reconcile-bridge raw git write (the 93L commit-back loop) is NOT routed through the library write seam: it is workflow-only orchestration on a dedicated CI worktree, and the seam's own code warns a whole-index commit there races normal store writes. Instead, the raw-git-write lint child (d37e) allowlists the two verbatim-tested YAML loops as documented exceptions; this ticket records that contract in the migrated module's docstring.

## Approach
Strangler-fig on reconcile-bridge-canary.yml only: move the four logic families into one Python module invoked by thin YAML steps.
1. scripts/canary_bridge.py (new, single module, ~250-400 LOC): subcommands
   - check-heartbeat: GitHub API query (gh api via subprocess, injected runner seam) + classification {api-error->transient/no-alert, no-success-runs->stale(never), older-than-window->stale, fresh->ok}; emits GITHUB_OUTPUT keys (stale, last_run_ago, status_msg) exactly as today.
   - heartbeat-alert: the find/open/comment/close lifecycle against rebar CLI (find existing open alert by marker tag, open when stale+none, comment when still stale, close on recovery) — one function per transition, dedup pattern preserved. Error handling — PRESERVE each step's existing failure disposition (verified against the YAML), not a blanket rule: (a) alert-lifecycle WRITES (create/comment/transition close) have NO fallback in YAML today -> stay FAIL LOUD (non-zero exit -> red canary run; a silently swallowed alert-write failure would defeat the canary); (b) the dedup FINDs (`rebar list ... || echo ''`, YAML lines 218-219/341-342) deliberately degrade to empty -> the subcommand preserves fail-soft-to-not-found (treat CLI failure as 'no existing alert'); (c) check-binding-drift: `rebar bridge-fsck` exits 1 BY DESIGN when it finds drift (the signal the canary exists to detect; YAML line 316 `|| true`) -> the subcommand captures stdout regardless of exit code, parses JSON, and treats unparseable/empty output as empty drift data exactly as the YAML python block does today — exit 1 with valid JSON is DRIFT (alert path), never an error; unit tests cover each disposition: fsck-exit-1-with-drift-JSON -> drift reported; fsck-garbage-output -> empty drift; alert-write failure -> non-zero exit. DRY_RUN: the step-level `if: env.DRY_RUN == 'false'` gates stay in YAML, AND the subcommands re-check DRY_RUN from env and short-circuit all rebar writes when 'true' (defense in depth against a dropped `if:`).
   - check-binding-drift + binding-drift-alert: same two shapes for the second alert family.
2. Thin YAML: each replaced step becomes env + `python scripts/canary_bridge.py <subcommand>`; ${{ }} values pass via env, keeping logic expression-free.
3. Anti-rot test pins the wiring (canary workflow invokes scripts/canary_bridge.py subcommands; no logic-bearing run-blocks reappear beyond the allowlisted flush loop).
4. reconcile-bridge.yml is untouched except NO changes needed — its 13L exit-code case on "Run reconciler" is workflow-native annotation glue (::notice/::error) and stays.

## Scope
- .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml: 10 logic steps -> thin invocations (Check last successful run; Log canary result; Find/Open/Comment/Close heartbeat alert; Check binding-drift; Find/Open/Comment/Close drift alert). The flush loop and plumbing steps (mount, install, identity, signing key, seed, fail-on-stale) stay.
- scripts/canary_bridge.py: new module with the four subcommands.
- tests/scripts/test_canary_bridge.py: unit tests for classification + lifecycle transitions.
- tests/unit/test_probe_wired_into_ci.py or a sibling anti-rot test: pin the canary wiring.
- tests/unit/test_reconcile_bridge_canary_class.py: RE-POINT — it asserts every `rebar transition ... closed` in the canary YAML carries --class (bug 0e15/ed13 guard); the close-on-recovery commands move to Python, so the guard becomes an assertion on scripts/canary_bridge.py's close calls (the protection survives, relocated).
- Verified-unaffected consumers (enumerated; assertions target steps that STAY): tests/interfaces/store/test_reconcile_workflow_no_shallow_rebase.py (parametrizes over reconcile-bridge-canary.yml; asserts fetch-depth:0 + merge-not-rebase invariants — the checkout/merge plumbing stays in YAML untouched); tests/unit/workflow/test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py (mount->init->first-merge ordering + no manual ours-driver — plumbing and flush stay in YAML), tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone_workflows.py (checkout `with:` inputs — checkout untouched), tests/unit/test_workflow_names.py (workflow `name:` — unchanged), tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py (bridge file untouched).
- pyproject.toml: T201 per-file-ignore for the new operational script — matching the LANDED legitimate-print entries (scripts/capture_jira_fixtures.py, scripts/retarget_jira_project.py, scripts/check_server_manifest.py); f1eb's probe_rebar.py entry additionally lands before this via change 1275, stacked earlier in this epic.

## Testing
- Unit: classification matrix (api-error, never-succeeded, stale, fresh, malformed window input), each lifecycle transition (open-when-none, dedup-when-open, comment-when-still-stale, close-on-recovery, no-op paths), GITHUB_OUTPUT emission format, the rebar-error path (runner raises -> subcommand exits non-zero, loud), and a DRY_RUN=true case asserting ZERO rebar mutations. Runner seam injected (no live gh/rebar in unit tier).
- Anti-rot: workflow YAML parses; each replaced step invokes the module subcommand; flush loop still present verbatim (guard against accidental migration).
- Parity: trigger reconcile-bridge-canary.yml via workflow_dispatch in-session after merge; compare step outcomes/annotations to the last pre-migration scheduled run.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Canary logic steps reduced to env + single-command invocations; classification/lifecycle logic lives in scripts/canary_bridge.py with unit tests.
- [x] Both CAS push loops (bridge commit-back, canary flush) remain in YAML byte-identical to pre-change; test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py still passes.
- [x] Anti-rot test pins the canary wiring (invocations + no new logic-bearing run-blocks).
- [x] tests/scripts suite green; lint/typecheck green.
- [x] [operator-attested] One workflow_dispatch canary run post-merge shows parity (same stale/fresh classification and alert behavior as the preceding scheduled run); run id + outcome recorded in a ticket comment before close.

## File impact
- .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml (edit)
- scripts/canary_bridge.py (new)
- tests/scripts/test_canary_bridge.py (new)
- tests/unit/test_probe_wired_into_ci.py (edit, or sibling anti-rot module)
- pyproject.toml (edit: T201 ignore)

Four independent definitions of "this blocker no longer blocks", with three different memberships:

- `graph/_ready.py:26` `{"closed"}`
- `graph/_unblock.py:26` `{"closed", "deleted"}`
- `graph/_graph.py:107` `("closed", "deleted")`
- `_engine_support/next_batch.py:30` `{"closed", "done", "completed", "deleted"}`

`done` and `completed` are NOT in the status vocabulary (`types.py:21`, `schemas/common.schema.json:9`) — unreachable branches.

Reproduced empirically in a throwaway store: with a ticket blocked by a `deleted` ticket, `next-batch` offered it while `ready` withheld it. The ordinary path is safe because `delete` unlinks peers; only "link to an already-deleted ticket" triggers the split.

Scope clarified during approval. `ready` and `next-batch` answer DIFFERENT questions by design — `ready` has zero file-impact logic; `next-batch` adds conflict-aware batching keyed solely off declared `file_impact`. That difference is correct and documented. This ticket does NOT merge the two commands; it unifies the one predicate they both depend on.

Maintainer decision: the terminal set is `{closed, archived, deleted}` — each represents a terminal state. This CHANGES behaviour in three places: `ready` gains `archived` and `deleted`; `_unblock`/`_graph` gain `archived`; `next_batch` gains `archived` and loses the phantom values.

Note `_ready.py`'s docstring already says a blocker must be "closed (or tombstoned / missing)", which reads as though `deleted` should count — the code and its own docstring already disagree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] One shared terminal-state predicate, imported by all four sites
- [x] The phantom `done`/`completed` values are removed
- [x] A test asserts `ready` and `next-batch` agree on a ticket blocked by a deleted ticket
- [x] A test asserts the terminal set is a subset of the schema's status enum, so vocabulary drift fails fast
- [x] The `_ready.py` docstring matches the implemented rule
baseline.summary: Unify the terminal-state blocker predicate

Delete the dead `.gitattributes` migration arm that strips the retired `.reconciler-* merge=ours` line from an already-initialized tracker.

## Why it is dead

The reconciler pass-lock/phase-gate moved onto `refs/reconciler/*` (epic dust-troth-naval / C4), so the union-merge carve-out was retired. The arm is permanently unreachable here. Residual risk, accepted by the operator ruling: a clone that has not swept since 2026-07-05 would no longer be converged by `init`.

## Context
A completion close always dispatches the billable verifier after deterministic guards, even when the ticket already carries a cryptographically certified `completion-verifier` PASS bound to the exact immutable commit being closed. The existing signature verifier can authenticate the stored completion op-cert, but the close seam never consults it. A runtime probe created a certified same-ref completion record on an in-progress bug, then closed at that exact SHA: the provider spy was called once.

The earlier standalone `verify-completion` command returns a signable result but does not persist an attestation. Changing that command into a mutating producer is out of scope; reuse applies only when a genuine ticket-contained completion attestation already exists (for example, from the trusted op-cert producer). The closed Locust task concerns bounded retry of insufficiency-only FAILs and is not a duplicate.

## Proven root cause
`src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py::_completion_precheck` unconditionally calls `close_autoresume.verify_with_auto_resume` after its deterministic guards. `verify_with_auto_resume` immediately invokes `llm.verify_completion`; neither seam checks the ticket's existing `completion-verifier` attestation. The required verifier, SHA pin, and material fingerprint are already available from the signature and plan-material infrastructure.

## Repair plan
- Add a fail-safe reuse check at the close auto-resume seam before provider dispatch.
- Resolve the close target ref once and require the stored completion op-cert to certify cryptographically.
- Require an authenticated `completion-verifier: PASS` manifest.
- Require the authenticated `verified-at-sha` to equal the resolved close target SHA.
- Require the authenticated material fingerprint to equal the ticket's current material fingerprint.
- Reject attestations invalidated by a later reopen.
- Return a close-compatible reused PASS result so the normal close, durable verdict, and post-close signing path remain unchanged.
- Fall through to the existing verifier for every absent, malformed, unverifiable, stale, differently pinned, or otherwise ineligible record.

## Test contract card
- authoritative_contract: operator-approved same-ref attested-PASS reuse requirement on this ticket.
- trigger_preconditions: ticket is in progress; completion gate enabled; a completion-verifier op-cert is already stored; explicit --ref resolves to the op-cert SHA.
- production_path: transition -> close precheck -> close autoresume/reuse seam -> locked close -> completion signing.
- observable_postcondition: provider call count is zero and the ticket closes signed.
- negative_controls: different SHA, invalid signature, missing pin, stale material, and pre-reopen attestation each call the provider exactly once.
- test_tier: lifecycle integration over an ephemeral git repo and real ticket store, with only the provider replaced by a spy.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A close at the exact SHA of a valid stored completion PASS makes zero completion-provider calls.
- [x] A reused PASS still produces a signed closed ticket.
- [x] A reused PASS leaves durable completion evidence for the closed ticket.
- [x] A changed resolved ref forces a fresh completion verification.
- [x] A cryptographically invalid completion record forces a fresh completion verification.
- [x] A non-PASS or wrong-kind record forces a fresh completion verification.
- [x] An attestation without an authenticated SHA pin forces a fresh completion verification.
- [x] An attestation without an authenticated material fingerprint forces a fresh completion verification.
- [x] A material fingerprint mismatch forces a fresh completion verification.
- [x] An attestation invalidated by a later reopen forces a fresh completion verification.
- [x] Explicit CLI `--ref` reaches the reuse decision through the normal lifecycle path.
- [x] Focused tests pass.
- [x] `make lint` passes.
- [x] `make typecheck` passes.
baseline.summary: Reuse same-ref attested completion verification during close

# Authenticated identity — entity + authorship certification + provider-neutral user mapping

## Context
rebar has no real concept of **who** performed an operation: `author` is `git config user.name`, an unauthenticated free string anyone with push access to `origin/tickets` can forge. Two needs follow: (1) attribute ticket events to a **real person** so activity is auditable and non-repudiable, and (2) map that person to **external ticket-system users** (Jira now; GitHub Issues / Linear later) so sync assigns work to the right person. **Beneficiary:** projects syncing to external trackers (correct assignee/reporter attribution, wrong or lost today) and anyone auditing "who did this." This epic depends on the **asymmetric attestation foundation** for its signing substrate.

## Approach (and why)
Adopt **git-bug's** identity model on rebar's existing event machinery, filling its gaps:
- **Identity = a first-class entity** whose event log IS its version chain (rebar already has
  event-sourcing / replay / snapshot). Stable **opaque rebar id** as the handle — **not**
  self-certifying; the signing key provides tamper-evidence, not the id. Attributes: `name`, `email`,
  `{provider, external_id}` external mappings, and **public** keys only.
- **Attribution always** (name+email denormalized on every event, git-style) + an optional
  `author_id` reference + an optional **authorship signature** — a new attestation kind on the
  foundation's substrate (namespace `rebar.authorship.v1`).
- **Trust root = the identity's in-band public keys**, TOFU on the genesis key + **G2** (key add/
  rotate/revoke must be signed by a currently-valid key). Safe for authorship: low authority, cannot
  forge another person's signatures; the worst case from a bad TOFU binding is a display-name dispute.
- **Provider-neutral mapping.** `{provider, external_id}` keys on the provider's **opaque stable id**,
  never email. Jira is the **first adapter** behind a provider seam; an unmapped inbound user mints a
  **placeholder** that idempotently auto-upgrades.
- **Deliberate creation.** A normal write never auto-mints an identity **entity**; identities are
  created explicitly or as a mapping target (see the default-install invariant below).

## Mechanisms (concrete definitions — these resolve the load-bearing terms)
- **Private key material.** Authorship signing uses the developer's **existing SSH private key** via
  `ssh-agent` / `~/.ssh`; it is **never** stored in the repo or on the `tickets` branch. The identity
  entity stores only **public** keys, and a write-time guard rejects any attempt to place private-key
  material into an identity event.
- **Era (key-validity window) = position in the `tickets`-branch commit graph, refined by intra-commit
  index.** rebar's HLC is **per-ticket** (`hlc.next_tick(tracker, ticket_id)` in
  `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py`), so it gives no global cross-ticket sequence. Events reach the
  `tickets` branch either singly (`event_append.stage_and_commit`, one event per commit) or in bulk
  (`event_append.batch_stage_and_commit`, **N events in one commit**), so commit **ancestry** is the
  global merged order, **refined by a stable `intra_idx`** (an event's 0-based rank
  within its commit when that commit's event files are sorted by `(timestamp, uuid)` — a deterministic,
  insertion-independent order computed from the committed events themselves, not git's lexicographic
  tree order; 0 for single-event commits; nothing extra is stored). Each event therefore has a position `(commit, intra_idx)`, and
  the same commit-graph is what git-bug uses for `ValidKeysAtTime`. Each key record binds
  `{pubkey, added_at:(commit,intra_idx), revoked_at:(commit,intra_idx)?}`. Key K is **valid for** an
  event E iff E's position is **>= added_at and < revoked_at** (when set), where positions compare by
  commit ancestry first (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`) and, when two positions share a commit, by
  `intra_idx` — no wall-clock, no fabricated global sequence. Multi-clone reconcile yields one merged
  graph, so validity is deterministic once merged; the authoritative check runs on that merged branch.
- **Verification state — reuse the existing `verdict` enum (do not invent a parallel one).** The
  authorship result reuses the 4-value verdict enum already defined in
  `src/rebar/schemas/verify_signature_result.schema.json` — `certified`, `unsigned`, `foreign_key`,
  `mismatch` — **extended** with one new value `key_not_valid_at_era` (added to that same schema). The
  human-facing `show`/`fsck` display collapses these into a trichotomy: **verified** = `certified`;
  **unsigned** = `unsigned`; **unverified** = `foreign_key` | `mismatch` | `key_not_valid_at_era`.
  There is **no** separate reason field — the `verdict` value IS the reason.
- **The "merge gate" (the real control).** rebar's `tickets` branch auto-pushes to `origin/tickets`
  with no GitHub pre-receive hook, so enforcement is a **CI verification job** — a GitHub Actions
  workflow on the `tickets` branch that runs `rebar verify-identity` / `fsck` over the **merged** log
  and **fails the check** (non-zero exit + a structured per-event report → red commit status / alert)
  on any `unsigned`/`unverified` event **when** the project sets `identity.require_authenticated=true`.
  This is **detect-and-fail-on-the-merged-log**, not pre-receive rejection (the honest limitation of a
  hookless remote); the local write-gate is only a fast-fail UX affordance. Enforcement is scoped by a
  **cutover ref** `identity.enforce_since` (a `tickets`-branch commit recorded when the project first
  enables enforcement): the CI job runs `verify-identity --require-authenticated --since <enforce_since>`,
  so only events at/after the cutover can fail — pre-cutover events are **grandfathered** (reported,
  not failed). Deployment prerequisite: enable the workflow, set `identity.require_authenticated=true`,
  and record `identity.enforce_since` at the enabling commit.
- **Authorship attestation shape.** The DSSE envelope is `{payload, payloadType, signatures}` — DSSE
  has **no `subject` field** (that is an in-toto concept). The **payload** is an in-toto-style Statement
  whose `subject` binds the signed event as `{event_uuid, content_hash}`, with
  `payloadType = "application/vnd.rebar.authorship.v1+json"`; the signature covers
  `PAE(payloadType, payload)`. Because the binding lives in the Statement `subject`, a signature cannot
  be lifted to another event. If the signing key is unavailable at write time, the event is authored
  **unsigned** (Tier 0) — the write never blocks.
- **Placeholder create-path.** The identity create path supports **system-minted placeholders** (no
  user present, no keys, partial data): `create_placeholder(provider, external_id, display_name)`,
  owned by the entity child and consumed by the inbound-ghost child.
- **Modify-Reporter constraint.** Setting the Jira `reporter` field via REST requires the project's
  Jira role to hold the **"Modify Reporter"** permission; without it, reporter sync degrades to
  assignee-only (documented), never hard-fails.
- **Default-install invariant.** With zero identity configuration, behavior is byte-identical to
  pre-feature: a write succeeds with the denormalized git author (name+email — this is the git commit
  author, already public in commit metadata, so it is **not** new email exposure; the "no broadcast"
  property is specifically that **no identity entity with keys/mappings is auto-minted** by a normal
  write), and `list`/`ready`/gates behave identically.

- **`verify-identity` CLI (the enforcement tool).** `rebar verify-identity [--require-authenticated]
  [--since <ref>] [--format text|json]` scans events on the merged `tickets` log (optionally since a
  ref), computes each event's verification state, and emits one **report entry** per event (all events
  in `--format json`; only non-`verified` in text). **Exit code:** non-zero iff any `unsigned`/
  `unverified` event is found under `--require-authenticated`; `0` otherwise (advisory without the
  flag). The CI merge-gate job runs it with `--require-authenticated`.
- **Report-entry schema.** `{event_uuid, ticket_id, commit (tickets-branch SHA), author (name+email),
  author_id?, verdict: <a verify_signature_result verdict, incl. the new key_not_valid_at_era>,
  display: "verified"|"unverified"|"unsigned"}`. `fsck` embeds the same entries; the `verdict` is the
  single source of the failure reason (no separate reason field).
- **Compaction survival (concrete).** A SNAPSHOT records, per folded signed event, a verification tuple
  `{event_uuid, content_hash, signature, signer_pubkey, position:(commit,intra_idx)}`, so a compacted signed event
  re-verifies (signature checked against the recorded `content_hash`; era resolved by comparing the
  recorded event `position` against the signer key's `added_at`/`revoked_at`) without the original event
  object. `process_snapshot` surfaces these tuples; a
  round-trip test asserts a compacted signed event still returns `verified`.
- **TOFU genesis base case.** The genesis key-add is **self-signed** — signed by the very key it
  introduces — and its `added_at_commit` is the identity's genesis commit; it is valid for every event
  whose commit is a descendant of (or equal to) that genesis commit. This is the base case of the G2
  "signed by a currently-valid key" rule (the recursion bottoms out at the self-signed genesis = TOFU);
  every later key change must be signed by an already-valid key.
- **Jira bootstrap availability + fallback.** Seeding `accountId` from email via
  `GET /rest/api/3/user/search` requires the integration's Jira role to hold **"Browse users and
  groups"** and returns nothing when the target's email is privacy-hidden — so it is best-effort with
  an explicit fallback chain: (1) an operator-provided mapping (a config/CSV of `identity → accountId`);
  (2) resolve `accountId` from existing Jira data where the user is already assignee/reporter on synced
  issues; (3) else degrade to project-default assignee (`-1`)/unassigned and leave the mapping unset for
  later repair. Never hard-fail, never block a sync.

## Scope
- **In:** the `identity` entity (a new ticket-type on the `session_log` exemption pattern); event
  attribution fields; the authorship attestation kind on the foundation's substrate; the TOFU + G2 key
  chain with era-scoped validity; the provider-neutral mapping + Jira adapter + placeholder/auto-upgrade;
  reconciler outbound assignee/reporter + inbound ghost; opt-in enforcement (local write-gate + the CI
  merge-gate verify job + fsck marking); snapshot/compaction carrying folded identities + signatures;
  docs + ADR.
- **Out:** the signing substrate itself (foundation epic); operation-cert behavior (op-cert epic);
  DSSE transparency-log / keyless follow-ons; **actual** GitHub Issues / Linear sync (the adapter seam
  must not preclude them, but wiring them is separate).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A new `identity` ticket-type exists and is exempt from lifecycle / gates / graph / Jira-sync
      (mirrors `session_log`); a create path mints one carrying name, email, `{provider,external_id}`
      mappings, and **public** keys, and a `create_placeholder(provider, external_id, display_name)`
      path mints a keyless partial-data placeholder. Verified by creating both, asserting `show`
      renders the fields, and asserting exclusion from `ready`/`next_batch`/default `list`.
- [ ] Every mutating event carries a denormalized `author` name + email; an optional `author_id`
      references an identity. Regression test: existing events without `author_id`/email still replay
      to the same state.
- [ ] An `authorship` kind wraps an in-toto Statement payload (its `subject` binds `{event_uuid,
      content_hash}`) in a DSSE envelope (`payloadType application/vnd.rebar.authorship.v1+json`), signed
      via the foundation substrate over `PAE(payloadType, payload)`, and
      verifies offline against the identity's in-band keys; a test asserts an event signed by identity A
      does not verify against B, a tampered event fails, and an unavailable signing key yields an
      `unsigned` (Tier-0) write, never a blocked write.
- [ ] Each identity key record binds `{pubkey, added_at_commit, revoked_at_commit?}` (`tickets`-branch
      commit SHAs); key add/rotate/revoke is refused unless signed by a currently-valid key (G2). Using
      two fixture commits on the `tickets` branch, a test asserts the genesis key-add is accepted only when self-signed (TOFU base
      case), an unsigned non-genesis key-add is refused, an event whose commit is NOT a descendant of the key's `added_at_commit` (or IS a descendant of its
      `revoked_at_commit`) fails verification, and one that is a descendant of `added_at_commit` and not
      of `revoked_at_commit` passes.
- [ ] `{provider, external_id}` mappings key on the provider's opaque id; the reconciler resolves an
      outbound Jira assignee by `accountId`, bootstraps via `/user/search` best-effort (which needs the
      "Browse users and groups" permission and may return nothing), then falls back to an
      operator-provided mapping, then to existing Jira assignee/reporter data, and finally degrades to
      project-default (`-1`)/unassigned without hard-failing; reporter is set by `accountId` only when
      the Modify-Reporter permission is held, else assignee-only. Test with a
      fixture identity + stubbed `accountId`.
- [ ] An inbound Jira user with no mapping creates a placeholder via `create_placeholder`; re-running
      resolution after a real mapping is added idempotently upgrades it — a test asserts one identity
      results, not two.
- [ ] Enforcement is opt-in (`identity.require_authenticated`): with it on, a CI merge-gate job runs
      `rebar verify-identity --require-authenticated --since <identity.enforce_since>` over the merged
      log and **exits non-zero**, emitting one report entry (`{event_uuid, ticket_id, commit, author,
      verdict, display}`) per non-`certified` event at/after the cutover, while pre-cutover events are
      grandfathered (test asserts exit code, a report entry's fields, and grandfathering); the local write-gate fails fast but is documented UX-only. Replay never rejects
      (test: a bad-signature event still folds into state); `show`/`fsck` surface the display grouping (`verified`/`unverified`/`unsigned`) over the raw `verdict`.
- [ ] Default-install regression: with zero identity configuration, an integration test asserts a
      normal write succeeds unsigned, **no identity entity is minted**, and `list`/`ready`/gates behave
      identically to pre-feature (proves SC "default install unchanged").
- [ ] Snapshots (compaction) record the per-signed-event verification tuple `{event_uuid, content_hash,
      signature, signer_pubkey, position}` so compacted signed events still return `verified`
      without the original event object (round-trip test).
- [ ] Docs + ADR: identity model; the verdict enum (existing `verify_signature_result` verdicts + new `key_not_valid_at_era`) and its `verified/unverified/unsigned` display grouping; opt-in enforcement + the
      CI-merge-gate-is-the-control caveat + its detect-vs-reject limitation; Jira `accountId` mapping +
      the Modify-Reporter permission requirement; key-rotation / era (commit-ancestry: `added_at_commit`/`revoked_at_commit`);
      private-key storage (ssh-agent/`~/.ssh`, never committed); the provider-neutral seam.
- [ ] A person running rebar has a modeled identity; events attribute it (name+email always; an authorship
- [ ] An opt-in project can REQUIRE authenticated authorship: `unsigned`/`unverified` events are flagged by
- [ ] The identity provides a stable local↔`accountId` map the reconciler uses to set the Jira assignee
- [ ] Key rotation works: events verify against the keys whose validity-ancestry contains them (added_at_commit ancestor, revoked_at_commit not); a revoked key
- [ ] Default install is byte-identical to pre-feature; signing and enforcement are fully opt-in.

## Intended decomposition (children)
1. `identity` ticket-type + entity (attributes, **public**-key-only storage + private-key guard,
   exemptions, normal + `create_placeholder` paths, config pointer, default-install invariant).
2. Event attribution (name+email + `author_id`) + replay back-compat + default-install regression test.
3. Authorship attestation kind on the foundation substrate (DSSE subject binding; unsigned fallback).
4. TOFU genesis + G2 signed key-rotation chain + era (commit-ancestry) validity.
5. Provider-neutral mapping + Jira adapter (outbound assignee/reporter, Modify-Reporter degrade).
6. Inbound ghost/placeholder + idempotent auto-upgrade.
7. Opt-in enforcement: local write-gate + **CI merge-gate verify job** + fsck `verified/unverified/unsigned`
   marking + replay-never-rejects + snapshot carries identities/sigs.
8. Docs + ADR.

## Prior art / grounding
git-bug identity entity + `ValidKeysAtTime` (log-position key validity) + bridge metadata; SCIM `externalId`; OIDC `(iss,sub)` (email disqualified as key); Jira Cloud GDPR `accountId` (email null/hidden) + Modify-Reporter permission; Gitea/GitLab placeholder-user + auto-upgrade; git `.mailmap` (email as adopt-heuristic only). Depends on the asymmetric attestation foundation.
baseline.summary: Authenticated identity — entity + authorship certification + provider-neutral user mapping

## Summary
A work ticket carries a single cryptographic attestation slot (`state["signature"]`). Both the **plan-review attestation** (earned at claim time via `rebar review-plan`) and the **completion verdict** (signed at close by the completion verifier) are written as `SIGNATURE` events into that one slot. The reducer applies `SIGNATURE` as last-writer-wins, so the completion verdict signed on close **overwrites and destroys** the plan-review attestation. These two attestations are independent proofs of two different gates and should be **additive** — a closed ticket should retain BOTH.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Take a non-bug work ticket (e.g. a `story`) and earn a plan-review attestation: `rebar review-plan <id>` (PASS). `rebar show <id>` now shows `signature.manifest[0] == "plan-review: PASS"`.
2. Claim and complete the work, then close: `rebar transition <id> in_progress closed`. The completion verifier runs and signs a completion verdict.
3. `rebar show <id>` again.

**Expected:** the ticket retains both attestations — the plan-review PASS *and* the completion-verifier PASS (queryable independently).

**Actual:** the `signature` field now shows only `manifest[0] == "completion-verifier: PASS"`; the plan-review attestation is gone from compiled state. Observed live on story `3d3d-da49-c3f3-4298` (REB-522): `signature` was `["plan-review: PASS", ...]` while in_progress and became `["completion-verifier: PASS", ...]` after close.

## Root Cause
`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:376` `process_signature()` does `state["signature"] = {…}` — a single slot, last-writer-wins (see its own docstring, line 377). The compactor builds the SNAPSHOT `compiled_state` via this same reducer, so after compaction the earlier attestation is permanently lost from compiled state (the raw append-only SIGNATURE events still exist in the log, but `show`/MCP/`verify-signature`/the gates read the single compiled field). Both verdict kinds are already distinguishable by `manifest[0]` (`"plan-review: …"` vs `"completion-verifier: …"`), so they can be keyed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A ticket can simultaneously hold a plan-review attestation AND a completion verdict; signing one does not clobber the other (additive, not last-writer-wins across kinds).
- [ ] Within a single kind, last-writer-wins still applies (re-running plan-review replaces the prior plan-review attestation; re-closing replaces the prior completion verdict).
- [ ] `process_signature` (and the SNAPSHOT/compaction path that replays it) preserves all kinds across compaction.
- [ ] `verify-signature` can certify each attestation kind; the claim gate reads the plan-review attestation and the close gate reads/writes the completion verdict, each unaffected by the presence of the other.
- [ ] Backward compatible: tickets with a single legacy `signature` still verify; the change is forward/back-compat for older clones (new shape preserved-and-ignored, per the rollout convention).
- [ ] Tests cover: plan-review then close retains both; re-sign same kind replaces in place; round-trip through compaction; legacy single-signature ticket still reads/verifies.

## Affected Files (initial)
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` (`process_signature`)
- `src/rebar/signing.py` (`sign_manifest`, verify)
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py`, `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` (signing call sites)
- relevant SIGNATURE schema under `src/rebar/schemas/` and reducer/compaction tests
baseline.summary: Completion verdict signature clobbers the plan-review attestation (single signature slot is last-writer-wins; should be additive)
