# Extract interpret_failure() -- run()'s except spine

ADR 0056 decision 3, FIRST extraction. The ordering is deliberate and was corrected by adversarial review.

## Why this one first

An earlier draft ordered resolution first, claiming "every" recent commit touching runner.py was a pre-call resolution concern. Review disproved it -- at least five were not: 8e4d6a46d and 5144a9009 (usage/cost, post-call), 4291b9a56 (disposition classifier, in the except arm), 3938c7ed2 (gate posture, in preflight), c8aa1ecdd (refusal fail-closed, in the call section). The real figure is ~70%.

The except spine is also the DENSEST code region in the file: 75 lines at only 20% comment (58 code), versus the pre-call region's 50% comment (113 code across 254 lines). Per line extracted it returns the most headroom, and it is where several of the most recent growth commits actually landed.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:555-629` -> `interpret_failure(...)`.
  MEASURED on the cc33 base (commit ad5ced165): line 555 is the first `except UsageLimitExceeded as
  exc:` and line 629 is `raise provider_err from exc`, the last statement of the last arm. An earlier
  draft of this bullet said "507-581", which was wrong at BOTH ends: 507 is the `_call_label`
  observability setup that sits BEFORE the `try:`, and 581 stops inside the middle arm, omitting the
  entire broad `except Exception` arm (582-629) — the one carrying the load-bearing
  sampling-rejection ordering. Re-locate by content, not by these offsets, if the base moves.
- Destination: `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` — the run-execution cluster already split from
  runner.py (task 2682/3a98). NOT `failure.py`, which stays pure classification, and NOT a new file
  (AGENTS.md forbids creating one under 100 LOC by splitting).
- The `finally:` block at 630 STAYS in `run()`. It is teardown, not interpretation.
- tests/unit/

### Parameters the arms genuinely read (name them explicitly; no carrier unless >~6)

`exc`, `run_messages`, `req_limit`, `eff_max_iter`, `ran_model`, `_call_label`, `req.execution_mode`, and `_t0` (for the elapsed-time log). `ran_model` is required by BOTH the `translate_sampling_parameter_rejection` call and the `ClassifyContext`, so it is not optional. ADR 0056 permits a carrier above ~6 parameters; a small frozen context object holding the logging and counter fields is in-bounds here, since none of its fields is mutated after construction (the ADR's objection to `ResolvedCall` was that two of ITS fields were).

## Preserve the arm ORDER — it is the whole contract

Keep `UsageLimitExceeded`, then `LLMError`, then broad `Exception`; and within the broad arm try `translate_sampling_parameter_rejection` FIRST. Python's type lattice hides a regression here: `UsageLimitExceeded` and every `LLMError` are plain `Exception` subclasses, so a broad-first spine silently reclassifies a step-budget stop or a typed failure as a provider OUTAGE. And `LLMConfigError` is a SUBCLASS of `LLMUnavailableError`, so an `isinstance` assertion CANNOT distinguish a correctly-translated sampling rejection from the broad fallback — arm-ordering tests must assert `type(x) is`, never `isinstance`.

NOTE for the implementer: translate_sampling_parameter_rejection performs NO retry -- it inspects and reclassifies. An earlier architecture draft wrongly described it as rebuilding settings and retrying. It does not break the resolve-then-execute shape.

## Monkeypatch repoints: MEASURED ZERO for this child

None of the eight `monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, "...")` targets in the suite (`_import_pydantic_ai`, `_local_proxy_bypass_base_url`, `_pai_model`, `_pai_structured`, `cache_settings_for`, `capabilities_for`, `get_runner`, `ProviderSession`) lies in the except spine, so this extraction needs no repoints. That zero was MEASURED for this region and does NOT transfer to the sibling children.

## Pre-existing decay this ticket should tidy, not be blamed for

`tests/unit/test_llm_failure_matrix.py` carries 23 descriptive labels of the form `"CURRENT(runner.py:NNN): ..."` (e.g. `runner.py:346`, `runner.py:365`). They are the third element of test-case tuples — human-readable descriptions, NOT assertions, which is why the suite passes regardless. They were ALREADY WRONG before this ticket: they cite 346/365 while the spine actually sits at 555-629, so they date from a layout two splits ago. Since this extraction moves the code they describe, retarget them to name `structured_run.interpret_failure` WITHOUT a line number, so they cannot rot again. This is label text only — no assertion changes.

## Testing

Unit tier: pure given an exception and the counters. Plus one end-to-end assertion through the real `PydanticAIRunner.run()`, because a `run()` that stopped calling the seam would still pass every isolated unit test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a test asserts a sampling-parameter rejection is reclassified to the typed config error and NOT
      to LLMUnavailableError -- the arm-ordering property; it fails if the broad classification runs
      first. MUST assert `type(err) is LLMConfigError`, because LLMConfigError subclasses
      LLMUnavailableError and an isinstance check would pass vacuously
- [ ] a test asserts the raised TYPE is unchanged for each of the three arms, so every existing
      `except LLMUnavailableError` caller keeps working
- [ ] the classified disposition is still attached as METADATA without changing the raised type,
      asserted as: the raised error's `.outcome` is not None AND `type(err) is LLMUnavailableError`
- [ ] an end-to-end test drives the real `run()` with a failing model and asserts the sampling
      rejection still surfaces as the typed config error -- proving run() still routes through the seam
- [ ] runner.py's before/after LOC is recorded in the commit message, AND the resulting file is under
      the 700 headroom guard on THIS commit (parent 7f86 AC3: `Verified` is cast per patchset, so a
      red ancestor blocks the whole relation chain)
- [ ] any monkeypatch target that moved is repointed IN THE SAME COMMIT and named in the message with
      its reason (expected: none — see "MEASURED ZERO" above)
- [ ] no comment moved or rewritten in `run()` lost a measured number, a `file:line` citation, a
      bug/story/epic id, a named failure mode, or a stated invariant
baseline.summary: Extract interpret_failure() from run()'s except spine

Bring `resolve_event_commit` and `resolve_position_commit` in line with the bulk map builders, which already carry both flags. This is an authorship-correctness fix, unrelated to repo size. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
`authorship.py:152-168` (`resolve_event_commit`) and `:194-209` (`resolve_position_commit`) omit `--no-renames` and `-c log.showSignature=false`; the bulk builders at `:313-331` and `:383-401` carry both, and `:298-300` documents why. The missing `log.showSignature=false` is a **live latent bug**: on a host with `log.showSignature=true`, `gpg:` lines interleave into stdout and `lines[-1]` (`:172`, `:213`) returns a non-SHA.

`--no-renames` is behaviour-preserving: it can only convert `R` into `A`+`D`; both pathspecs match at most one path (positions are globally unique `{ts}-{uuid}`); and the only event-file renames are `.json` -> `.json.retired`, which no `*.json` pathspec matches. **Do not add `--no-merges`** — `authorship.py:294` documents that the fallback exists precisely to catch files added only inside merge commits.

Note: an earlier framing justified this as a partial-clone performance fix. That motivation is **not** established — pathspec limiting runs before diffcore rename detection, so these single-path resolvers likely never fault blobs. The correctness argument stands on its own.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With `log.showSignature=true` **and signed commits** in the fixture repo (a `gpg.program` /
      `gpg.format` shim suffices), both resolvers return a valid **40-hex SHA**. Tier: **unit**
      against a real temporary git repo. The signing is load-bearing: with `--format=%H` over
      *unsigned* commits the setting emits no extra lines, so an unsigned fixture makes this
      **vacuously green**.
- [ ] Both flags appear in the argv of both resolvers, and `--no-merges` does **not**. Tier: **unit**
      pinning the constructed command.
- [ ] Resolver output matches the bulk map builders' output over a sample of >=100 real events — the
      cross-check that the flags did not change semantics. Tier: **integration** against the store.

## Files
`src/rebar/attest/authorship.py`, tests

Scope: XS-S. No dependencies.
baseline.summary: B5: add --no-renames and -c log.showSignature=false to the two authorship resolvers

## Why
Agentic steps need a generalized output contract, a safe repo view at a caller-chosen git ref, scoped ticket access, and per-step model choice.

## What
- Generalize RunRequest with optional output_schema/mode; split findings-finalization into one
  strategy (backward-compatible with existing review_* callers).
- Hardened git-ref filesystem: rev-parse to a full SHA, `git archive` that SHA, hardened tar
  extract (read-only/no-git steps); handle export-ignore/subst/LFS/submodule/symlink; size
  guard; finally + TTL GC.
- Scoped rebar ticket tool (read + comment only). Multi-provider/model per step.
- Agent runtime hardening: create_agent v1, exact dependency pins, robust structured output.

## Scope
- In: runner generalization, git-ref snapshot (create + teardown + split trigger), scoped tool,
  per-step provider, agent runtime hardening.
- Out: gate security / provenance hardening (epic 8a1c).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] RunRequest output_schema/mode added; review_ticket/review_code/scan_spec unaffected.
- [ ] git archive snapshot bound to the resolved SHA; hardened extraction; documented export-ignore/submodule behavior.
- [ ] WS-D owns snapshot creation + finally-teardown and the fs_tools.py -> llm/workflow/snapshot.py split trigger.
- [ ] Scoped ticket tool grants read + comment only (no write/transition/sign).
- [ ] Per-step model/provider precedence documented (step > workflow > config > env > default).
- [ ] Built on create_agent v1 with exact-pinned langgraph/-prebuilt/-checkpoint (upgrades gated behind WS-G evals).
- [ ] Structured output: Pydantic v2 (all fields required), include_raw=True, branch on parsing_error/parsed-is-None with own retry+repair, non-empty invalid_tool_calls treated as retryable.
- [ ] Preserves AIMessage(tool_calls)<->ToolMessage pairing across WORKFLOW_STEP replay.
baseline.summary: WS-D: Agentic-step capabilities (runner generalization, git-ref snapshot, multi-provider)

# Workflow engine v2: declarative IR + thin interpreter + provider-agnostic runtime + visual editing

## Context

Split out of the remediation epic 6f2d (soupy-spool-revel) per the deep-design brainstorm (session log ad3f-2d99-6d41-40e6 "boom-demon-jug"). The brainstorm established that "remediation" is really a re-architecture of the workflow engine; THIS epic owns the BUILD. 6f2d retains remediation-on-top (docs, migrating existing reviewers onto this engine, prompts, eval coverage, cleanup, visual+eval review, intent-alignment) and depends_on this epic. Every decision is grounded in 4 deep-research rounds + codebase spikes + 3 passing de-risk POCs under docs/experiments/workflow-remediation-pocs/ (REFERENCE, not deliverables).

## What we are building (4 parts)

- **Declarative IR (git source of truth):** one YAML/JSON file per workflow; steps are deterministic
  (`uses:` an INTERNAL registered op) or agentic (`prompt:` an LLM step); control flow (conditional
  branches, bounded loops, map/fan-out) expressed as DATA; stable step ids. Evolves v1 GitHub-Actions YAML.
- **Thin synchronous interpreter (engine):** run-state on rebar's EVENT LOG (genuine reuse —
  WORKFLOW_RUN/WORKFLOW_STEP events on the target ticket, same reducer/commit/push); iteration-keyed
  idempotency markers; mandatory max_iterations; control-flow state derived from recorded outputs
  (replay-correctness discipline the engine POC proved). BOUNDED-CONCURRENT fan-out: parallel LLM calls,
  serialized commits (decision: included in v1).
- **Provider-agnostic agent runtime behind the existing Runner seam:** Pydantic AI, REPLACING
  LangChain/LangGraph (sole justification — native Langfuse tracing — is obsolete; Langfuse is OTel-native).
  Runs single-turn LLM calls AND tool-using agents (filesystem + MCP + custom rebar-op tools). Tracing via
  OTel -> Langfuse, dev/maintenance only (clients pay nothing).
- **Ephemeral visual editor:** bpmn-js (constrained BPMN metamodel — NOT draw.io's free-form canvas, which
  would allow edits that don't map back). A thin IR<->BPMN serializer (bpmn-moddle + a registered `rebar`
  moddle descriptor) projects the IR for editing and round-trips back; the visual format is NEVER committed
  (auto-layout on open).

## Structured-output reliability (output feeds deterministic steps — reliability is key)

Retire the second-interpreter LLM (a recognized anti-pattern). Layered stack (research-grounded):
1. Provider-native CONSTRAINED decoding / strict json_schema where supported (OpenAI strict ~100% vs <40%;
   Gemini responseSchema; **Anthropic native structured outputs now GA**) via Pydantic AI NativeOutput; else
   PromptedOutput cross-provider.
2. Deterministic tolerant parse of near-miss output (json-repair) — no LLM.
3. Pydantic validation + normalizing validators (numeric/length bounds HERE, not in the JSON Schema, to stay
   inside Anthropic's strict-grammar subset).
4. Bounded SAME-model retry feeding the validation error back (Pydantic AI retries={'output': 2}; raise the
   default budget of 1).
Handle Anthropic stop_reason in {refusal, max_tokens}; for steps needing extended thinking, SPLIT reasoning and structured extraction into two steps (thinking is a tradeoff vs forced structured output).

## Dependencies

- Reuse: event-sourced git store (run-state), git-canonical prompt library, Inspect AI eval seam, Runner seam.
- Add (runtime, light): pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,...] (~41 pkgs vs LangGraph ~80-110); provider SDKs;
  json-repair; OTel exporter ([tracing]) -> Langfuse.
- Drop: langchain, langgraph, langchain-mcp-adapters.
- Add (edit-time ONLY, out-of-process): bpmn-js (browser editor) + bpmn-moddle (MIT serializer). NOT runtime.
- Build (the only custom code): IR schema+linter (low risk); interpreter (moderate, justified by
  event-sourcing); Pydantic-AI Runner adapter (low); IR<->BPMN serializer (moderate, bounded — bpmn-moddle +
  one descriptor + round-trip fixtures; POC-validated).

## How it meets the invariants
- I1 human visual edit incl. loops/conditionals: bpmn-js (constrained metamodel) + round-trip serializer.
- I2 LLM edit+validate: lean schema'd IR; atomic id-keyed edit ops + schema + linter validation.
- I3 git-stored, clean diff NOT required: only the IR is committed; visual format ephemeral.
- I4 light runtime / heavy edit-deps OK: interpreter is stdlib; agent runtime lazy-loaded for agent steps;
  visual editor out-of-process.
- Cross-provider (hard req): Pydantic AI provider-agnostic, NO per-provider code; Anthropic-only rejected.
- Tool-using agents (FS+MCP+rebar ops): native to Pydantic AI (validated).
- Deterministic step logic INTERNAL-only (registry not exposed via CLI/MCP).
- Don't-build-unique-engine is EARNED: every off-the-shelf engine (DBOS/Restate/Spiff) owns its run-state and
  conflicts with event-sourcing; standard formats (BPMN/ASL) carry impedance > a lean IR.

## De-risk POCs (all PASS; docs/experiments/workflow-remediation-pocs/)
- engine_interpreter_poc.py: replay exactly-once across ALL crash points (deepest risk retired).
- runtime_pydanticai_poc.py: cross-provider integration validated; Claude thinking+structured-output 400
  reproduced AND mitigated (PromptedOutput); dep weight 41.
- visual_bpmn_roundtrip_poc.mjs: IR<->BPMN round-trip preserves ids / multi-instance / agent metadata.

## Known limitations
- We own/maintain the interpreter (replay correctness is subtle — POC found+fixed one bug; contained by the
  state-discipline rule + tests).
- IR<->BPMN serializer is bespoke and bounded by BPMN's vocabulary (our IR must map onto BPMN).
- Agent-step config richness in the canvas is limited (edit flow visually, prompts in text).
- Pydantic AI is young (2.0 beta incoming) — contained by the strict swappable Runner seam.
- OTel->Langfuse token/cost attribute mapping is a known soft spot (analytics, not span structure).
- Cross-provider COMPLETION proven on Anthropic; OpenAI/Google billing-blocked (integration validated).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] v2 IR JSON Schema + v1->v2 migrate shim + linter (cycles legal only via declared loop frames); coverage guard.
- [ ] Interpreter: conditionals/loops/map; iteration-keyed (run_id,step_id,iteration) markers; mandatory
      max_iterations; replay tests (kill mid-run -> replay from events -> no double effects).
- [ ] Bounded-concurrent fan-out: parallel agent calls + serialized event commits; deterministic replay
      preserved; Burr tripwire relaxed NARROWLY for the map path only (recorded).
- [ ] PydanticAIRunner behind the Runner seam; FS+MCP+custom tools; structured output via NativeOutput/
      PromptedOutput (NOT forced-tool ToolOutput); validate + bounded retry; parallel-run-and-diff vs the old
      LangGraph path to the DEFINED PARITY BAR (child 7d58: non-inferiority on the eval corpus — validity >= v1,
      per-criterion verdict-agreement >= 95% + zero decision flips, recall/false-accept within +/-2pp) before
      cutover; the bar gates the LangGraph drop.
- [ ] LangChain/LangGraph/langchain-mcp-adapters removed; tracing via [tracing] OTel->Langfuse, optional.
- [ ] Structured-output reliability layers 1-4 implemented; thinking+extraction split where needed;
      stop_reason handling; second-interpreter LLM removed.
- [ ] bpmn-js editor + IR<->BPMN serializer with a registered `rebar` moddle descriptor + round-trip fixtures
      (ids, agent metadata, multi-instance survive); visual format never committed.
- [ ] docs reference the 3 de-risk POCs.
- [ ] v2 declarative IR (steps + conditionals + loops + map) with a JSON Schema + linter, agent-editable.
- [ ] Thin interpreter executing it with run-state on the event log, deterministic resume/replay, and
- [ ] Agent runtime swapped to provider-agnostic Pydantic AI behind the Runner seam; LangGraph dropped.
- [ ] Structured-output reliability stack (native/strict + tolerant parse + validators + bounded retry); the
- [ ] Human visual view+edit via bpmn-js over an ephemeral IR<->BPMN projection.
baseline.summary: Workflow engine v2: declarative IR + thin interpreter + provider-agnostic runtime + visual editing

baseline.description:
## Symptom

An operator's local status change is silently reverted by the Jira reconciler, minutes later, with every OTHER field write from the same period left intact. Confirmed twice on 2026-08-07:

- `858c-786a-13be-4332` (REB-2500): reopened `closed -> open` at 10:09:14Z; reconciler wrote
  `open -> closed` at 10:17:58Z. The description rewrite from the same window SURVIVED.
- `556a-5a1f-adb3-4139` (REB-1504): moved `in_progress -> open` at 10:09:02Z; reconciler wrote
  `open -> in_progress` at 10:17:52Z.

Both events are authored `reconciler` / `env_id: reconciler`, e.g. `.tickets-tracker/858c-786a-13be-4332/1786097878273766164-d80fab3f-...-STATUS.json`: `{"author":"reconciler","env_id":"reconciler","data":{"current_status":"open","status":"closed"}}`.

The projection/reducer is NOT at fault: the reconciler event is genuinely the LATEST status event in the log. This is an inbound write, not a replay defect.

## Proven root cause — the baseline lags our own outbound push by exactly one pass

ADR 0026 Decision 1 makes the per-binding baseline the sole direction signal: `local == baseline` is taken to mean "local did not change, so a differing remote must be a Jira-side edit — stand down and let inbound mirror it" (`outbound_field_diff.py:323-334` `_suppressed_by_inbound`, applied to status at `:389-396`). Inbound has no arbitration of its own — it is pure value inequality (`inbound_differ.py:233-234`), and it only ever clobbers a field in a pass where outbound emitted nothing for that field (same-pass suppression, `inbound_differ.py:709-718`).

The baseline is advanced from the pass-START snapshot (`reconcile.py:595` calling `_advance_baselines`, `reconcile.py:514-531`, with `ctx.curr_snapshot` fetched at `reconcile.py:280` BEFORE the outbound apply). So in the pass where rebar itself pushes a status to Jira, the baseline is left holding the OLD value.

That makes the guard's premise false for one pass. A REOPEN is a revert to a previous value, so:

1. Pass N (run 31168795002): local `closed`/`in_progress` pushed outbound —
   `RECON: outbound_update key=REB-2500 changed=[description,status]` and
   `key=REB-1504 changed=[...,status]`. Jira now holds `Done` / `In Progress`.
   Baseline NOT advanced: `.bridge_state/bindings.json` at f0fe2ce9d4 (10:14:45Z) still records
   `baseline.status = 'To Do'` for BOTH bindings.
2. Operator reopens locally to `open` (10:09).
3. Pass N+1 (run 31169292024): local `open` == canonicalized baseline `To Do` -> `open`, so
   `_suppressed_by_inbound` fires and status is omitted from outbound —
   `RECON: outbound_update key=REB-2500 changed=[description]`, `key=REB-1504 changed=[]`.
   Inbound then reads Jira's `Done`/`In Progress` and overwrites local. Clobber.

This is the same omit-vs-clear asymmetry class recorded on `39c1-2a32-b564-4b4b` for the 2026-08-03 parent-clear incident (`ed5e-f176-3aea-41fd`).

### Runtime reproduction (the discriminating experiment)

Replaying the real pass-time inputs through `outbound_field_diff.compute_update_fields`, with the baseline as the ONLY variable:

    STALE baseline 'To Do' (the real pass-time value)
       -> outbound fields = {'description': 'NEW'}                     status_sent=False
    ADVANCED baseline 'Done' (what outbound had just pushed)
       -> outbound fields = {'description': 'NEW', 'status': 'To Do'}  status_sent=True

The stale-baseline row reproduces the observed `changed=[description]` exactly, including the operator's discriminating detail: the description was NOT equal to the baseline so it WAS sent, while status was suppressed. One variable flips the outcome.

## Why the description survived but the status did not

Not a revision rollback. Description differed from the (stale) baseline, so it was pushed outbound and inbound had nothing to say. Status EQUALLED the stale baseline, so outbound stood down and inbound won. The asymmetry is a direct consequence of the guard, not of event ordering.

## NOT a regression from 2026-08-07 changes

The clobbering pass is run 31169292024, started 10:14:54Z. Every suspect commit landed AFTER it: e7a9 `33d6d4ef7c` 12:16:01Z, 851e `17c31cf5c8` 12:25:19Z, 2876 `c390cef54a` 12:34:40Z, 65d7 `08dfbbc689` 13:13:44Z. None was in the deployed tree.

Independently: a tracker-wide sweep for `author: reconciler` STATUS events finds the SAME shape on 2026-07-20 15:21:03Z across 8 tickets (`0662-2b88-6fe3-4844`, `1416-b1bc-c8e9-477e`, `542e-fb17-6f5d-4ced`, `caed-6c07-2a14-4ef9`, `7cab-bb99-9803-4ccb`, `9f60-2767-9ca3-45b2`, `c03f-254f-014b-4cc7` open->closed, `6dac-d0d9-1a60-4998` in_progress->closed) — 18 days earlier. Pre-existing defect, exposed today because the Reconcile Bridge was re-enabled mid-session.

## Blast radius

Any local status change made in the window between rebar's own outbound push of a status and the next pass's baseline advance, where the new local value equals the pre-push baseline. Reopen and un-claim are exactly that shape, so operator corrections are the most exposed operation. Silent: the pass exits 0 and nothing is logged as a conflict.

## Approach (operator decision: OPTION A)

Restore ADR 0026's own definition of the baseline as the **last-SYNCED** value rather than the last-FETCHED one, by overlaying the values rebar itself just pushed onto the pass-start snapshot before `set_baseline` records it. Applied to all five `_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS` (summary/description/priority/status/assignee), because all five share the `_suppressed_by_inbound` guard and therefore share the ABA exposure.

**Per-mutation success is the gate, not the pass exit code.** The applier does not currently expose a per-mutation outcome the baseline advance can key off, so that plumbing is part of this change:

1. `dispatch_one._update_one_scalar_update` currently returns only the update result, which is
   `None` both when the call is skipped (parent-only mutation) and when the 400
   illegal-transition comment-fallback soft-fails. It will instead return
   `(result, fields_synced)` where `fields_synced` is the exact kwargs dict handed to
   `client.update_issue` **only when that call returned without raising**, and `{}` on the
   skip and soft-fail arms. This is deliberately conservative: any raise (including the
   `RuntimeError` from `acli.transition_issue_by_name` for an unreachable transition, the raw
   404, `AssigneeNotFoundError`, and any partial application inside `update_issue`) records
   NOTHING, so the baseline can only ever lag — never falsely lead.
2. `dispatch_one.update_one` gains a `fields_synced` out-parameter (same shape as the existing
   `subop_applied` out-parameter it already carries), filtered to the mirrored baseline fields.
3. `apply_handlers.handle_update` records that dict onto `BatchApplyContext.synced_fields`
   (the dataclass is defined in `apply_handlers.py:66`, not in `apply_base.py`)
   keyed by `local_id`. The 404 / assignee soft-fail arms return before the record, and the
   `record_backstop_failure` backstop never reaches it, so a soft-failed mutation contributes
   nothing.
4. `applier.apply` / `_apply_batch` accept a `synced_fields_out` dict out-parameter and copy
   `ctx.synced_fields` into it; `reconcile._apply_mutations` (reconcile.py:365, which calls
   `applier.apply` at lines 448/452) passes one in and stores it on the `_PassContext` for
   `_persist_and_log` -> `_advance_baselines` to consume.
5. `reconcile._advance_baselines` takes the synced map and, after `set_baseline` writes the
   pass-start snapshot, overlays the synced fields via a new
   `peer_state.merge_baseline` (a field-level overlay onto the existing baseline, as opposed to
   `set_baseline`'s whole-dict replace). The overlay also runs for a confirmed binding whose
   key was outside the fetch window, since our own push is fresh evidence even when the fetch
   was not.
6. **Observability for the deliberate non-advance.** A soft-failed mutation withholds its
   baseline advance silently today. `_advance_baselines` emits a single `RECON:
   baseline_overlay advanced=<n> fields=<n>` line to stderr per pass, and `handle_update`'s
   soft-fail arms already file a `bridge_alerts` entry — so an operator can tell "the baseline
   did not move because the push failed" from "the baseline did not move because there was
   nothing to push" without reading the manifest.

The mutation `fields` dict is already vendor-shaped at this point (post `OutboundFieldMapper.map_fields_to_remote`: local `title` -> `summary`, status/priority -> their Jira names, description ADF-fitted+normalized), which is exactly the shape `peer_state.set_baseline` / `normalize_baseline_value` consume for `summary`, `description`, `status` and `priority` — those four need no new mapping layer.

**`assignee` is the one field where that is NOT true, and it is handled deliberately rather than assumed away.** A snapshot's `assignee` is a Jira user OBJECT, which the inbound mapper canonicalizes into a display scalar plus an `assignee_identity` triple; the outbound mutation carries only the single RESOLVED value (a bare display/email string, or an accountId when the 264f fast path set `_assignee_is_account_id`). So:

* Bare string (no fast path): the pushed value IS the local assignee string, so it is overlaid
  directly and the `_assignee_matches` guard resolves it exactly like a fetched scalar.
* accountId (fast path): the overlay records `{"accountId": <value>}`. The canonicalized
  baseline then carries that accountId as its only identity, which will NOT match a local
  assignee held as an email/display name — so the guard does not suppress and the pass falls
  back to today's local-wins push. That is the SAFE direction (a baseline that lags can only
  cause a redundant outbound re-push; a baseline that leads is the silent divergence the
  operator decision forbids), and it is chosen over fabricating a displayName/email we never
  observed. The residual ABA exposure for accountId-resolved assignees is pinned by an explicit
  test so it is a recorded limitation, not an accident.

**Also in scope — close the coverage gap.** ADR 0026 mandates a direction-preservation regression cell and it exists for `title` only; the status equivalent (`test_inbound_field_sync_directionality.py::test_jira_side_status_change_suppressed`) drives `adapters/jira/outbound_fields._diff_fields`, which has **no production caller**. New cells are added on the LIVE `outbound_field_diff.diff_canonical_fields` path for every mirrored field, and the tests assert they executed the production path (an import-site assertion that the function under test is the one `compute_update_fields` calls) so they cannot degrade into the 599e / 24f7 "passing by not running" class.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py` — `_update_one_scalar_update` returns a
  per-call applied-fields dict; `update_one` gains the `fields_synced` out-parameter.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_handlers.py` — the `BatchApplyContext` dataclass
  (defined here at line 66) gains a `synced_fields` accumulator, and `handle_update` records
  into it on per-mutation success only.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py` — `apply` / `_apply_batch` `synced_fields_out`
  out-parameter.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py` — `_apply_mutations` collects the synced
  map onto `_PassContext`; `_persist_and_log` hands it to `_advance_baselines`, which overlays
  it after `set_baseline`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/peer_state.py` — new `merge_baseline` field-level overlay.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py` — thin `merge_baseline` delegate,
  matching the existing `set_baseline` delegate.
- `docs/adr/0026-reconciler-three-way-merge-baseline.md` — record that the baseline advance is
  last-synced (fetch overlaid with confirmed pushes), gated on per-mutation success.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — new ABA-oracle, held-firm, soft-fail, and live-path
  direction-preservation cells (files named in Testing below).

**Module-size cap.** `dispatch_one.py` is at 785/800 LOC and `binding_store.py` at 782/800, so the cap is a real constraint here. The `dispatch_one` change is written as an out-parameter on `_update_one_scalar_update` (which `update_one` already calls) rather than a returned tuple, keeping the delta to roughly ten lines. If it still crosses 800, the fallback is to extract the existing sub-op dispatch cluster — `_update_one_dispatch_labels` / `_update_one_dispatch_links` / `_update_one_dispatch_comments` (lines 662-785, ~124 LOC, called only from `update_one`) — into a new `dispatch_subops.py`. That is a pre-existing call-graph seam and clears >100 LOC, so it satisfies the split policy; it is NOT a mechanical line-count carve. New baseline logic goes in `peer_state.py` (the existing baseline home), never in `reconcile.py`.

## Testing

Assume the reconciler unit-test fakes (in-memory binding store + stub transport) are the harness; no live Jira.

- **ABA oracle (RED first)** — `test_baseline_advance_aba.py`: baseline `To Do`; local pushed to
  `closed` and the push succeeds; local reverted to `open` before the next pass; assert pass N+1
  emits `status` outbound and the inbound differ does NOT clobber. Run against unmodified `main`
  first and record the failure, then fix.
- **Held-firm** — a genuine Jira-side status edit with local unchanged since the (correctly
  advanced) baseline still suppresses outbound and flows inbound. This is the guard against the
  fix silently becoming the rejected option B.
- **Soft-fail** — a status transition that raises `RuntimeError` from
  `transition_issue_by_name` (the `applier.py` backstop path) and a 400 illegal-transition
  comment-fallback: assert the baseline is NOT advanced for the failed field, and that a
  same-mutation field applied by a *separate* successful call is likewise not recorded
  (conservative all-or-nothing per `update_issue` call).
- **All five fields** — the ABA oracle and the direction-preservation cell are parameterized
  over `summary`/`description`/`priority`/`status`/`assignee`. The assignee cell asserts BOTH
  halves of the caveat above: a bare-string assignee push DOES close the ABA hole, and an
  accountId-resolved push falls back to local-wins (asserted explicitly, so the limitation is
  pinned rather than silently regressed).
- **Live-path direction preservation** — cells driving
  `outbound_field_diff.diff_canonical_fields` (the function `compute_update_fields` actually
  calls), asserting for each mirrored field that `local == baseline` + differing remote
  suppresses the outbound emit. Each cell asserts the production reachability of the function it
  drives, so it cannot pass by not running.
- **Empty/edge** — no synced fields (a pass with zero outbound updates) leaves
  `_advance_baselines` byte-identical to today; an unbound/unconfirmed `local_id` in the synced
  map is a no-op; an out-of-window key still receives its overlay.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The baseline for a field is advanced to the value rebar itself just pushed outbound, so
      `local == baseline` no longer means "local unchanged" for one pass after our own write
      (or an equivalent fix that removes the false premise)
- [x] A test reproduces the ABA sequence end to end - baseline B, local pushed to A, local
      reverted to B before the next pass - and proves the status is NOT clobbered
- [x] A test pins that the deliberate ADR 0026 behaviour is NOT weakened: a genuine Jira-side
      status edit against an unchanged local status still flows inbound
- [x] The fix is applied to every inbound-mirrored field, or its restriction to status is stated
      with a reason (`_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS` = title, description, priority, status, assignee -
      all share the guard, so all share the ABA exposure)
baseline.summary: Reconciler reverts a local status change: the arbitration baseline lags rebar's own outbound push by one pass, so a reopen looks like 'local never changed'

## What
The new flags (REBAR_GATE_REF/SOURCE/TMPDIR/FREE_WATERMARK_BYTES/GRACE_SECONDS/MAX_AGE_SECONDS/REVERIFY_SECONDS/JANITOR_INTERVAL_SECONDS), the [snapshot] config table, the --ref/--source CLI flags, and REBAR_LLM_REPO_PATH's new precedence vs the gate code root are documented only in docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md, NOT in docs/config.md (the canonical config-key inventory). src/rebar/config.md path: docs/config.md.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] docs/config.md documents the [snapshot] section + all eight REBAR_GATE_* env vars with defaults + precedence.
- [ ] docs/config.md notes the gate code-root precedence in repo_path resolution.
- [ ] The doc-coverage test (or a new one) asserts these keys appear in docs/config.md so they cannot silently drift.

# rebar bug-trend analysis (2026-08-01, reviewed)

Data baseline: 344 bug tickets (77 Jun, 260 Jul, 7 Aug 1); 333 closed. Bug-close `--class` enum (regression | plan_defect | env_integration | flaky | preexisting | not_a_bug | duplicate | escalated | undetermined) became required ~07-19 (ed13); 214 closed bugs carry no class — ~207 predate the requirement, ~7 post-date it via then-unenforced close surfaces (the 376d class: MCP transition / NDJSON import). Of the 119 classified: preexisting 57, plan_defect 15, env_integration 14, duplicate 12, regression 12, not_a_bug 4, flaky 4, undetermined 1. Caveat: every classified close is a July/Aug-created bug (the June cohort closed pre-taxonomy), and the class is closer-self-reported, unaudited. Tags: 237/344 untagged, ad-hoc vocab. creation_channel: unknown 209 / cli 126 / jira 5 / python 4. file_impact set on 100/344. `rebar metrics` registry lenses: agent_process (attempts_per_ticket, first_pass_rate, reopen_recovery, revert_recovery, rework_within_7_days), code_health (churn, refactor_to_addition_ratio), gate_economics (cost_per_accepted_change, first_pass_verification, env_diagnosis_intervals); module-size metrics show `unavailable`. No bug lens exists.

Title-keyword clustering (overlapping, 261/344 matched): reconciler/Jira sync 77; concurrency/locking/git-store races 76; plan-review/attestation gate defects 55; CI/test flakiness+isolation 41; silent-failure/fail-open 39; infra/deploy 27; code-review gate 24; completion-verifier/close gate 22; config/env-var 19; truncation/pagination/limits 15; direction-inversion/asymmetry ~7.

Recurring same-class families (explicit in titles): unlocked raw git commits bypassing the canonical locked write seam (3a33, 3435, 4dd2, 3b4e); pagination truncation (9263, 1f3d, deac); link-direction inversion (3b86 → 4b59 → 32cc); asymmetric ADD-only differs (7f42, 908c); lock wedges/reclamation (620c, a4b2, 304e, ac26, 1a47, 9305, 449f — 449f documents 7 post-fix recurrences as residual, not regression); mtime-less cache staleness (1d76, e995, 908b); wall-clock perf assertions in tests (edfe, b228, 19d7, 5e94, 85c3); missing subprocess timeouts (c16f, d843, 747f); "exists on CLI only, not lib/MCP" parity (6e88, 1598, 5199, d21b; close --class rollout misses 0e15, 376d); unread config/env keys (281f, 9d7a; b00f is the adjacent scanner-blind-spot case).

---

## Q1 — Additional observability/traceability? YES, three low/zero-friction gaps.

What already exists and costs users nothing extra: bug-close `--class` (bounded enum, enforced); the **blame-hunt subsystem** — every bug close best-effort auto-derives a `caused_by` link to the culprit ticket (`src/rebar/metrics/blame.py`, `transition_close.py:490`, ticket 555e) with retroactive backfills (`scripts/backfill_caused_by.py`, `scripts/backfill_bug_class.py` — structural, no-LLM close_class backfill from reverts/REVIEW_RESULT/gate_error signals, ticket 5062); `discovered_from` links; tags; session logs; auto-filed canary tickets (binding-drift, heartbeat) with a find-existing-then-comment dedup pattern; the code-review FP ledger (`fp:code-review` bug tickets with a `root-cause:` enum, compiled into NO-FIRE eval cases); `rebar metrics` lenses.

Gaps:
1. **The close taxonomy captures relationship-to-work, not mechanism or escape channel.**
   `preexisting` (57/119) tells you it wasn't a regression; it does not tell you it was a
   concurrency bug that escaped because no gate looks at raw git writes. Recommendation:
   a **batch auto-classifier** extending the 5062 backfill pattern — structural signals
   where they suffice, the `rebar.llm` framework for the rest — writing bounded
   `mechanism:*` / `detected-by:*` tags to closed bugs on a schedule, spot-checked. Zero
   author burden. Do NOT add a second *required* close flag: the `--class` rollout itself
   broke every automated close surface (0e15 red main; 376d MCP/NDJSON gaps; the canary
   closes bugs programmatically — reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:300), and automation would
   stamp a constant value anyway, polluting the data.
2. **Nothing aggregates.** Answering "top bug mechanism this month" required re-mining 344
   titles by hand; the registry has agent_process/code_health/gate_economics lenses but no
   bug lens. Recommendation: a `bug_trends` metrics lens over data already in the store —
   close_class distribution over time, mechanism-tag distribution, open-bug age,
   `caused_by` fan-in (shared culprits), canary time-to-detect. Read-only; zero burden.
3. **Class-level recurrence is prose; only culprit-level links are structured.**
   `caused_by` gives queryable bug→culprit-ticket links, but "same class as the
   enrich-queue prune race", "sibling sweep of 5546", "9305 rec #1" live in titles —
   recurrence-of-a-mechanism across channels is unqueryable. Recommendation: a link/tag
   convention (`relates_to` to the anchor bug + a `class:<anchor>` tag) written by the
   debug skill automatically (see Q4), so recurrence rate per class becomes a query.
Also: extend the FP-ledger pattern (proven for code review) to plan-review false positives — a large fraction of the 55 plan-review bugs are FP/noise reports; making each a NO-FIRE eval case compounds precision. Anti-recommendation: no new mandatory fields at bug **create** time (canaries and agents must file cheaply), and no mandatory prose root-cause field (comments already carry it).

## Q2 — Fragility/decay trends? Mostly surface-expansion + latent-defect discovery, with four real structural weaknesses.

The July spike tracks new subsystem activation (review-bot, auto-lander, Bedrock cutover, Jira DC, live tiers); the June baseline was itself audit-driven (audit-2026-06-09 filed ~17 on 06-10; antipattern-audit). In the classified (July-created, self-reported) subsample, `preexisting` outnumbers `regression` 57:12 — consistent with latent-defect discovery rather than decay, though that subsample excludes the June cohort and is unaudited. Four structural fragility patterns are real and mitigable regardless:
1. **A bespoke concurrent database on git** (~76 bugs). Many writers (CLI, MCP, review-bot,
   reconcile-bridge, enrich queue, janitors, retention) re-discover the locking contract;
   failures: unlocked whole-index commits, auto-gc/maintenance corrupting the shared object
   DB, unreclaimable locks in containers. Mitigation: one canonical locked write seam
   (`run_git_write` exists; delete/txn/compact/init already route through it), **enforced
   deterministically in CI** — forbid raw `git commit`/index mutation outside an
   allowlisted seam, scoped to store-touching code AND workflows/scripts:
   reconcile-bridge.yml:283 does a raw `git commit` of ticket events in CI and is the live
   instance behind 449f's dominant failure mode; a src/rebar-only lint would miss it.
   Allowlist the seam files and test-fixture repos (eval_solver.py, criterion_preview.py).
   Plus the contention policy 9305 asks for.
2. **Hand-written per-field, per-direction reconciler differs** (~77). Asymmetric ADD-only
   differs, direction inversions, silent pagination truncation, untyped transport (cc77
   names the type gap as the root cause of a357's class). Mitigation: typed transport
   protocol (mypy-enforced port completeness — cc77), roundtrip/property invariants
   (inbound∘outbound identity, direction preservation), pagination-by-construction (one
   paged iterator, no raw page calls).
3. **The gates are themselves a top bug surface** (~100 across plan-review/code-review/
   verifier): attestation staleness/races, verdict non-determinism (620b, e458), token-cap
   INDETERMINATEs, FP classes. Meta-fragility: guardrail bugs erode trust and consume the
   bug budget. Mitigation: treat gate reliability as a product area (it is trending that
   way), keep the FP-ledger/eval loop growing, prefer deterministic pre-checks before LLM
   passes.
4. **Silent-failure default** (~39): fail-open checks, exit-0-on-error, unread env keys,
   integrations broken for weeks unnoticed (1630: 4119 mail errors since 06-30; 8070:
   canary red since 07-14). Mitigation: fail-loud policy for gate/infra code paths +
   auto-file tickets on canary red transitions (pattern already exists for binding-drift/
   heartbeat).

## Q3 — Gate levers, precision-first. Yes: mostly deterministic, narrowly-scoped ones.

Current posture is good: code review blocks only on security + secret/high-critical detectors; the rest is advisory; plan-review criteria carry applicability gates and ANTI-FP clauses; an FP ledger polices code-review noise. Levers, ranked by signal-to-noise:
1. **Deterministic CI lint: no raw git writes outside the canonical store seam** (catches
   the 3a33/3435/4dd2 class; low-FP *with* an allowlist for the seam itself and
   test-fixture repos, and scoped to include workflows/scripts — see Q2 §1 for why).
2. **Engine-layer enforcement rule as a code-review project criterion** (narrow): new
   validation/gates must live in the engine, not the CLI layer — catches the 0e15/376d and
   "CLI-only flag" parity class. Deterministic alternative: a parity test template.
3. **"Config key must be observably read" check** — for each new config/env key, require a
   test or a registry entry proving a behavioral effect; the env-registry drift gate
   already exists but checks documentation only (`scripts/gen_env_registry.py`), and b00f
   shows scanner blind spots.
4. **Auto-file P1 tickets on external/live canary red transitions** (8070 sat red for two
   weeks) — observability, but it closes the "merged broken, nobody looked" channel.
   Reuse the reconcile-bridge canary's find-existing-open-ticket→comment dedup pattern
   (reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:259-267) so it cannot spam; external-integration.yml has
   no such path today.
5. **Narrow advisory code-review criterion: absolute wall-clock assertions in tests**
   (edfe/b228/19d7/5e94/85c3 class) — textually detectable, low FP as a scoped rule.
6. **Extend the FP-ledger pattern to plan review** — precision lever for existing criteria
   rather than a new detector; build on the adjudication corpus + FP-proxy harness already
   in docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/.
7. Candidate only — needs a security design first: completion verifier executing a
   ticket's recorded `verify_commands` deterministically before the LLM pass would turn
   "AC satisfied" from pure judgment into judgment + executed evidence and catch
   proxy-validation escapes at close. But verify_commands are agent-authored arbitrary
   shell run in whichever environment closes the ticket: it needs sandboxing/allowlisting
   and a staleness story (plan-time commands vs post-merge tree) before it is a lever, not
   a liability.
Anti-levers: no new blocking LLM dimensions (T9/T5b stay advisory — concurrency/reliability review by LLM is FP-prone); no mutation-testing gate in CI (keep manual/scoped); no mandatory local review-code preflight (cost without vote).

## Q4 — rebar-debug: strong on single-bug rigor; four gaps for class-level closure.

The two-phase protocol, falsifiability, dynamic-proof rule, parsimony/exit gate, not-a-bug guard, and Step 7 sibling sweep are all present and good. Gaps vs "sibling issues, recurrence through different channels, residual fragility":
1. **No ticket-store writeback.** The skill never claims the bug ticket, records the proven
   root cause + experiment log as a comment, closes with the right `--class`, or files
   sibling/residual tickets with links. Note this is partly deliberate: the skill's
   Approval gate (SKILL.md:94-106) requires user approval before writing to "Jira or other
   trackers". So the fix must reconcile with that gate, not bypass it: add a "Record the
   outcome" section that treats the project's own rebar store as the sanctioned write
   surface when project guidance (AGENTS.md) mandates recording work there, keeping the
   approval gate for external trackers (Jira). Content: root-cause comment (mechanism,
   citations, experiments), close with the taxonomy class, siblings → tickets linked to
   the anchor bug, residual risks → tickets. This is also what makes Q1's recurrence
   observability free.
2. **Step 7 sweeps constructs, not channels.** It greps for the same code construct; the
   observed recurrences are the same *invariant* violated via a different surface (CLI vs
   MCP vs import; local vs CI — a4b2 fixed the local wedge, 449f documents the CI-side
   residue). Add: derive the sweep from the violated invariant, and enumerate parallel
   surfaces (CLI/lib/MCP/workflow/import/CI scripts) and other writers of the same state —
   "who else enforces or relies on this invariant?"
3. **Residual-fragility disposition.** Reporting covers bounded sweeps, but confirmed
   adjacent weaknesses from Phase 1 (dossier leads that weren't the root cause but are real)
   and known-uncovered residue of the fix have no required disposition. Add: a "residual
   risk" line in Reporting + file tickets for confirmed adjacent defects instead of
   dropping them (449f is the exemplar of why).
4. **No class-prevention hook.** When the cause is a repeatable pattern, Step 7 fixes live
   instances but never asks "can this class be made impossible or detectable?" (lint, type,
   constructor, CI gate, FP-ledger entry when a gate mis-fired). Add one paragraph: propose
   the structural guard as a ticket (not inline scope-creep).
Keep additions conditional (writeback only where a rebar store exists — the skill is cross-project) and short; the skill already warns against ceremony inflation.

## Q5 — rebar-implement: five escape-rate additions that don't duplicate gates.

Held-out TDD, RED-first, mutation/refactoring litmus, preflight, stacked landing are all in place; plan review owns plan quality, code review owns security/tests/scope advisories, the verifier owns AC satisfaction, CI owns lint/type/module-size/suite. Escaped classes that none of those own, addressable in the skill:
1. **Surface-parity enumeration in 4a.** When the behavior exists on multiple surfaces
   (CLI/lib/MCP), the spec must enumerate them and either cover each or explicitly file a
   follow-up ticket (create + link discovered_from). Targets the proven parity class
   (6e88/1598/5199/0e15/376d). No gate checks this today.
2. **"New config is read" oracle rule in 4b.** Any new config key/env var/flag gets one
   test proving behavior differs when it is set (kills 281f/b00f "parsed but read by
   nothing"). The CI env-registry gate checks documentation, not effect.
3. **Contention edge case in tier selection.** If a leaf mutates the ticket store or other
   shared state, the held-out edge set includes one second-writer/contention case —
   authored to test-design §7's deterministic-barrier discipline (multiple real processes,
   barrier/failpoint, no sleeps), else waived. The discipline matters: the repo's newest
   flaky-test close (08-01) is itself a contention test, and an undisciplined mandate here
   would feed the ~41-bug CI-flakiness cluster. Scoped to the store's dominant bug class,
   not a general mandate.
4. **Gate-finding → oracle upgrade loop in 4g.** On any post-push Verified -1 or LLM
   finding that is real, record in the session log which held-out test should have caught
   it and add that case before amending — converts every escape into a permanent oracle
   member.
5. **Residual-gap disposition at close.** If an edge/E2E case was deliberately descoped,
   file the ticket before closing the leaf (extends the existing discovered_from rule from
   "missing dependency" to "known untested residue").
Anti-additions: no mandatory local `review-code` preflight, no mutation-testing runs per leaf, no re-statement of module-size/lint (already in the 4d brief and CI).
baseline.summary: Bug-trend program: mechanism/escape observability, fragility mitigations, gate levers, and debug/implement skill upgrades (2026-08 retrospective)

baseline.description:
Block direct commits to `main`/`master` at commit time by enabling the pre-commit framework's built-in `no-commit-to-branch` hook, so the "never commit to main" rule this repo already enforces server-side (GitHub ruleset + Gerrit gates) also fails fast locally — at `git commit` instead of only at push/review.

## Why
CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md mandate that no change land on `main` except through Gerrit's two gates. Today nothing stops a local `git commit` while `HEAD` is on `main`; the mistake is only caught later at push. Catching it at commit time is cheaper and matches the repo's "errors happen early" posture.

## What
Add the packaged `no-commit-to-branch` hook (id from `pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks`, already pinned at `rev: v6.0.0` in this repo) to the existing hooks list in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, with an EXPLICIT `args: [--branch, main, --branch, master]`.

Rationale for explicit args (chosen over relying on the hook default): the tool default at v6.0.0 is `frozenset(args.branch or ('master', 'main'))` — verified by inspecting the installed hook source `pre_commit_hooks/no_commit_to_branch.py` — so a bare entry already protects `main`. But passing the branches explicitly (a) documents intent inline for the next reader, and (b) is robust to any future change of the upstream default. The cost is two lines; the robustness/clarity gain is worth it. Because the repo already depends on that pinned repo, this adds no new dependency and requires no `rev` bump.

## Scope
- One file: `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
- Add a single `- id: no-commit-to-branch` entry (with the explicit `args`) under the
  existing `- repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks` block (the one
  holding `check-yaml`, `check-toml`, etc.).
- No change to the `local` lint/typecheck hooks; no Makefile change (the hook is
  activated by the existing `pre-commit install` in `make hooks`).
- Non-goal: server-side enforcement (already covered by the GitHub ruleset + Gerrit);
  this is a local fail-fast convenience only, and remains bypassable with
  `git commit --no-verify` by design.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `.pre-commit-config.yaml` contains a `no-commit-to-branch` hook id with an
      explicit `args` listing both `main` and `master`, under the
      `pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks` repo block.
      Proving command: `grep -q 'no-commit-to-branch' .pre-commit-config.yaml && python -c "import yaml,sys; d=yaml.safe_load(open('.pre-commit-config.yaml')); hs=[h for r in d['repos'] for h in r['hooks'] if h['id']=='no-commit-to-branch']; a=hs[0].get('args',[]); sys.exit(0 if hs and 'main' in a and 'master' in a else 1)" && echo OK`
- [ ] The config still parses and the hook is registered; running it on the current
      (non-protected) working branch passes.
      Proving command: `pre-commit run no-commit-to-branch --all-files` prints
      `Passed` and exits 0 while `HEAD` is on the feature branch.
- [ ] A `git commit` attempted while `HEAD` is on a protected branch is rejected.
      Proving command (negative path, exit code asserted):
      `git switch -c __scratch_main main 2>/dev/null; git branch -f main; git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main; pre-commit run no-commit-to-branch --all-files; test $? -ne 0 && echo BLOCKED-OK` — i.e. the hook exits non-zero (prints `Failed`) when HEAD is `main`. Restore HEAD to the feature branch afterward. (Run manually in a scratch checkout; not a CI step.)
- [ ] Existing gates are unaffected: `make lint && make typecheck` stay green and the
      YAML hygiene hooks still pass.
      Proving command: `make lint && make typecheck && pre-commit run check-yaml --all-files`
      all exit 0.
baseline.summary: Block direct commits to main via pre-commit no-commit-to-branch hook

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
The operation-linked compaction sweep is not crash-atomic, and this is the root wedge-generator for the store (parent epic becoming-berserk-grunion; live wedges recorded on e72e-259d-5ee7-4e73 and 6ccc-0577-198c-44fa). rebar._commands.compact_trigger.maybe_compact() fires on the tail of every ticket CLOSE and spawns a DETACHED sweep worker (run_sweep → compact.compact_all_cli → compact_txn). The fold performs snapshot-write → retire-rename (tracked source → `*.retired`) → git commit as SEPARATE steps with no rollback. If the detached worker dies, is killed, or races a concurrent writer between the rename and the commit, the SHARED tracker working tree is left DIRTY: tracked deletions plus untracked `*-SNAPSHOT.json` / `*.retired` files. A dirty tree then aborts the next reconverge union merge ("local changes / untracked files would be overwritten"), stranding local ticket commits — the chronic wedge. Interim mitigation `[compact] trigger="off"` is active on the affected host and must be removable once this lands.

## Approach
Make the fold crash-atomic with an intent journal + rollback + startup recovery (the classic write-ahead-intent pattern):
1. **Intent journal**: before mutating anything, `_apply_fold` writes a journal record (ticket dir, snapshot path, sources to retire) to a store-local journal location; if the journal cannot be written, the fold REFUSES (logs, stderr Error, exit 1) without mutating the store.
2. **Ordered mutation + rollback**: perform snapshot-write, then renames, then ONE commit; on any failure after mutation begins, `_rollback_fold` reverse-renames and removes the uncommitted snapshot. If a reverse-rename itself fails (incomplete rollback), RETAIN the uncommitted snapshot rather than delete it — dropping it would lose folded events; the retained state is exactly what fsck reports as SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT and doctor can repair.
3. **Recovery**: compact_recovery.recover_abandoned_folds scans for journals with no matching commit at startup/next sweep entry, discriminating: journal + uncommitted artifacts present → revert (restore sources, remove snapshot, clear journal); journal whose snapshot already reached HEAD → clear journal (fold landed); journal whose snapshot is gone from disk (superseded or fsck-repaired) → clear journal without touching ticket files.
4. Transient-fault discipline: git probes used for discrimination must distinguish "object absent" from transient failures (index.lock contention, timeout) so recovery never mis-classifies a transient fault as "snapshot absent" and reverts a landed fold.
The journal lives with the store and is cleaned in the same locked scope as the fold; the sweep remains operation-linked (portable — no CI dependence).

## Scope
- src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py — intent journal write, ordered fold, `_rollback_fold` with the retain-on-incomplete-rollback guard.
- src/rebar/_commands/compact_recovery.py — abandoned-fold discrimination + recovery.
- src/rebar/_commands/compact.py — recovery invocation at sweep entry.
- tests/unit/test_compact_crash_atomicity.py (new) — kill-at-each-step coverage.
- tests/unit/test_lock_holder_labelling.py — lock label update.

## Testing
- Crash injection at each step boundary (after journal, after snapshot-write, after renames, before commit): the next sweep entry recovers to a clean tree (`git status --porcelain` empty) with no ticket events lost.
- Refusal path: journal write failure → exit 1, store untouched (zero mutations, zero commits).
- Incomplete rollback: a failing reverse-rename retains the uncommitted snapshot; assert the snapshot bytes survive and fsck reports the state.
- Recovery discrimination: landed-fold journal is cleared without reverting; superseded/fsck-repaired journal (snapshot gone from disk) is cleared without touching ticket files; transient git failure during the probe does NOT trigger a revert.
- Idempotence: recovery on a clean store makes zero changes; double recovery is safe.
- Manual mutation pass over journal/rollback/recovery branches; every mutant killed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A fold killed at ANY step boundary leaves a store that the next sweep entry converges to clean (no dirty tracked deletions, no stray snapshots, no lost events); checked by the crash-injection tests.
- [x] A fold that cannot journal refuses without mutating the store; checked by the refusal test.
- [x] Recovery never deletes folded-event bytes: incomplete rollback retains the snapshot, and landed/superseded journals are cleared without reverting ticket files; checked by the discrimination tests.
- [x] Transient git faults during recovery probes are not treated as "snapshot absent"; checked by the fault-injection test.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1) before close; after merge the `[compact] trigger="off"` mitigation is removed on the affected host.
baseline.summary: Defense-in-depth: make compaction crash-atomic — detached sweep that dies after write/retire but before commit leaves the tracker tree dirty (source of the untracked leftovers that wedge reconverge)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
The first proposal mixed forward validity with historical convention. Revise it to a small deterministic floor intended to have no false positives, then use accepted history only as an adversarial counterexample corpus.

## Approach
Test failure patterns rather than preferred prose style. A rule qualifies for the floor only when the detected state is structurally incompatible with an executable plan; otherwise it remains advisory. Search closed tickets carrying signed plan-review and completion evidence, inspect every matching candidate in context, and narrow or remove any rule with a legitimate match.

## Criteria Under Review
1. An Acceptance Criteria checkbox must contain non-whitespace text after the checkbox marker.
2. Two Acceptance Criteria items must not be exact duplicates after joining continuations and normalizing whitespace/case.
3. Active execution prose must not contain a bare unresolved sentinel (`TBD`, `TODO`, `FIXME`, or `???`) in Approach, Scope, Testing, or Acceptance Criteria; ignore fenced code, inline code, quotations, examples, explicit removal/prohibition assertions, and superseded/history sections.
4. Structured file-impact entries, when present, must have a nonempty path and nonempty reason; absence of file impact is allowed.
5. A `[rebar:<id>]` prerequisite citation used as plan evidence must resolve to a direct verified upstream dependency; ignore literal examples in code spans/fences.

## Scope
Read-only ticket-store analysis. The only mutation is the final findings comment on this ticket; no repository files or other ticket material will be changed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every criterion under review has a documented historical search and cited matching tickets, verified by the final findings comment.
- [ ] Every legitimate matching ticket is treated as a counterexample and causes the rule to be narrowed or rejected, verified by before/after detection wording in the final findings.
- [ ] The final recommendation clearly separates hard-floor rules from advisory signals, verified by a structured classification table in the final findings.
- [ ] If a rule has no historical match, the finding says that explicitly without claiming proof of soundness, verified by the final findings comment.
baseline.summary: Adversarially validate a revised deterministic clarity floor

baseline.description:
# Store accepts secret-bearing event bodies; leak blocked all tickets pushes

## Context / Problem

At 2026-08-03 19:13 an agent session posted a comment on ticket 129e containing a full zsh environment dump. The dump embedded SEVEN live credentials (Anthropic, 2x GitHub PAT, Gemini/Google, Jira/Atlassian, OpenAI service-account, PyPI). GitHub push protection then rejected `refs/heads/tickets` (GH013) on the Anthropic key, so EVERY session's store writes queued local-only — 153 commits at diagnosis. One comment caused a full store-sharing outage for all concurrent agents, and it presented as transient contention: the only symptom was `WARNING rebar._store.push: tickets branch push failed after 3 retries`.

This is urgent now because the store auto-pushes to a single shared ref, so any agent that pastes an environment dump into a comment wedges the branch for everyone until a human intervenes.

## Root cause

There is no content screening anywhere in the write path. `_store/event_append._validate_event` (`src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:126`) checks the envelope shape and `event_type` membership only, and never inspects `data`. Confirmed RED before any fix: `leaf.comment(<ticket>, "KEY=<live-shaped anthropic key>")` returns 0 and the COMMENT event lands on disk.

Corollary the original diagnosis got wrong, and which this plan corrects: `append_event` is NOT the single write seam. `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py:258-276` writes Jira-sourced COMMENT/EDIT bodies — untrusted EXTERNAL input — by calling the halves of `finalize_event` directly, deliberately bypassing `append_event` because that helper commits+pushes eagerly. The txn and delete cores bypass it too. A screen at `append_event` would therefore have left a credential pasted into a Jira comment able to reproduce this exact wedge.

## Approach

Add a deterministic, pure secret screen and enforce it at `_seam.finalize_event` (`src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:329`) — the one function `append_event` (`src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:405`), the txn/delete cores, and the reconciler's inbound translate all route through. Inbound translate is changed to call the seam rather than its halves, and a test pins that routing so it cannot regress into a bypass again.

On a match the write is REFUSED — the event does not land — per the operator decision recorded on this ticket (2026-08-07). Redaction was considered and rejected: silently rewriting a caller's payload makes the stored event differ from what the caller believes it wrote, and in an append-only store that divergence is unrecoverable after the fact. Refusal is loud, reversible, and leaves the caller in control. A force override (`--allow-secret-pattern=<reason>`) keeps a false positive from ever being a permanent hard block; it is the same escape-hatch shape as `--force-close`, is CLI-only (never exposed over MCP), and records who forced and why on the event itself so a forced write is auditable.

Refusal must be safe to leave ON by default, which drives two design constraints:

- It names WHICH family fired and WHERE (field + line), so using the override is an informed
  choice rather than a blind retry.
- It never echoes the secret. `SecretFinding` (`src/rebar/secret_screen.py:116`) carries
  family/field/line and structurally has NO value field, so the value cannot leak through the
  refusal message, logs, stderr, or the event on disk. Payload dict KEYS are redacted before
  they reach the printed field path, since a credential used as a key would otherwise leak
  through the path itself.

Detection is tuned by measurement against the live store rather than by argument. Patterns match a FIXED-WIDTH window rather than a greedy `{80,}` quantifier, so same-class padding appended after a real key (400 `-` characters — an ASCII rule in a log or env dump) cannot dilute the entropy average below the floor and make the screen miss a genuine credential. The PEM pattern is line-anchored, because a real paste puts the banner on its own line whereas prose enumerating banners does not.

`llm/workflow/lint.py` consumes the shared pattern table instead of keeping a second copy, which had already drifted — it lacked the Anthropic/OpenAI/Atlassian/PyPI families the incident actually carried.

## Scope

Recorded via `set-file-impact` (paths). New: `src/rebar/secret_screen.py` (pattern table, pure `scan_text`/`screen_event_data`, override audit record, refusal message) and `tests/unit/test_secret_screen_e7a9.py`. Modified: `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py` (enforce at `finalize_event`), `src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py` (parse the override above BOTH dispatch routes so every write verb honours it, not just `comment`), `src/rebar/_commands/leaf.py` and `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` (thread the override through), `src/rebar/llm/workflow/lint.py` (consume the shared table), `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py` (route through the seam), `docs/user-guide.md` (the command-substitution hazard + the screen/override).

Out of scope: surfacing the GH013 push-rejection detail. That was bug 2a76 and already landed on main (`tests/unit/test_push_rejection_surfacing.py`); AC5 below records it rather than duplicating it.

## Testing

- Fire: each of the families the incident dump carried is refused, asserted via the family name
  in the refusal. Credential-shaped fixtures are ASSEMBLED AT RUNTIME (`_fake_secret`,
  `_pem_banner`) so this repo never commits a live-shaped literal and the repo's own secret
  scanner stays fully armed on the test file.
- No-fire: the verbatim benign strings the live-store sweep found — a truncated placeholder
  (`sk-ant-api03-...`), a regex literal (`sk-ant-api03-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{93,}`), and prose
  enumerating PEM banners — all still write.
- Padding: a real key followed by 400 same-class padding characters is still refused (the
  fixed-width-window regression).
- No-echo: the secret value AND its head/tail fragments are absent from five channels — the
  exception message, stdout, stderr, the log records, and every byte on disk. The forced-write
  path is checked separately because it is the only path that logs, so asserting on log records
  in the refusal path alone would be vacuous. A positive control proves the on-disk assertion
  can actually observe a landed value.
- Bypass: a test pins that the reconciler's inbound translate routes through `finalize_event`,
  and another pins that the override is absent from the MCP surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A write whose event data matches a high-confidence credential pattern is REFUSED at
      `_seam.finalize_event` and the event file does not exist on disk afterwards — verified by
      a test that asserts the command's non-zero exit and the absence of the event.
- [x] The refusal names the matched secret family and the field+line, and does NOT echo the
      secret value — verified by asserting the value and its head/tail fragments are absent from
      the exception message, stdout, stderr, log records, and all on-disk bytes.
- [x] Benign look-alike text (truncated placeholders, regex literals, prose enumerating
      banners — the verbatim strings from the live-store sweep) still writes successfully, so
      the screen is safe to leave on by default — verified by explicit negative-case tests.
- [x] The screen covers writers that do NOT go through `append_event`, specifically the
      reconciler's inbound Jira translate — verified by a test asserting inbound translate
      routes through `finalize_event`.
- [x] `--allow-secret-pattern=<reason>` allows the refused write for every write verb, records
      the reason and bypassed families on the event, and is absent from the MCP tool surface —
      verified by tests over the CLI verbs and a test asserting MCP non-exposure.
- [x] The shell command-substitution hazard that produced the incident is documented in
      `docs/user-guide.md` with the exact wrong and right forms.
- [x] The incident is recorded on this ticket with its blast radius, including that the only
      control which actually stopped the leak (GitHub push protection) was outside this project.
- [x] Surfacing the GH013 push-rejection reason is confirmed ALREADY satisfied on main by bug
      2a76 (`tests/unit/test_push_rejection_surfacing.py`) and is not duplicated here.

## Absorbed from e4f4 (closed as duplicate)

e4f4-295b-2c03-44c4 described the same underlying defect (the store accepting secret-bearing event bodies) and was filed about 8 minutes apart from this ticket with no link between them. Its two ACs with no counterpart here — documenting the shell command-substitution hazard for agents, and recording the incident with its blast radius — are folded into the Acceptance Criteria above so nothing is lost by closing it.
baseline.summary: Store accepts secret-bearing event bodies; leak blocked all tickets pushes
