baseline.description:
## Reproduction Steps

1. Take epic `1386-5e7c-391d-4a74` (tearful-cleansable-gopher) and its children as authored.
2. Run `rebar review-plan` on the epic and on children `35bc-aef6-efd5-4df5` and
   `2aa6-726a-ea56-4d6c`.
3. Observe every one returns **PASS with 0 blocking findings** and signs a certified
   attestation. The epic's own signed manifest records `plan-review: PASS` / `blocking: 0` /
   `advisory: 11`.
4. Implement the tickets exactly as specified.
5. Observe that **seven acceptance criteria across the three tickets cannot be satisfied**, and
   that the contradictions are visible in the plan text itself — no implementation knowledge is
   needed to see them.

**Expected:** a plan whose acceptance criteria contradict each other, contradict their own
Scope, or contradict a sibling's acceptance criteria is not certifiable. Plan review should
either block or, at minimum, raise these as findings.

**Actual:** all three passed with zero blocking findings. Every contradiction surfaced later —
either mid-implementation or at the completion-verifier close gate, after the work was done.

## Why the plans were not completeable

Seven instances, in four distinct failure classes. All quotes are the ORIGINAL text as
reviewed; each has since been amended.

### Class A — an AC contradicts its OWN ticket's Scope or another AC in the SAME ticket

The strongest class: both halves of the contradiction sit in a single document the reviewer
read in full.

1. **Epic `1386` AC1 vs its own Scope.** AC1: *"No live source file under `src/rebar/` matches
   `Success Criteria` / `success criteria` / `success criterion` (case-insensitive)"*, granting
   exclusions only for frozen fixtures and the vendor bundle. Its own **OUT OF SCOPE** section,
   ~15 lines earlier, defers *"the `dod_uncertifiable` / 'definition-of-done' vocabulary in the
   verifier prompts"* — three live files under `src/rebar/` that therefore keep matching
   forever. AC1 could never pass.

2. **Story `2aa6` AC1 vs its own Scope AND its own AC6.** AC1 required
   `grep -rniE "success[ _-]criteri(a|on)" src/rebar/llm/reviewers/ ...` to return **no
   matches**. Its Scope has a section headed **"EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED"** naming
   `plan_review_T2.md:10`, and its **AC6** states that a grep on that same file *"still returns
   its one match"*. AC1 and AC6 are directly contradictory: one demands zero matches in a
   directory, the other demands one match in a file inside it.

3. **Story `2aa6` AC3 vs AC6.** AC3 required the generated criteria guide's SC grep to be
   *"empty"*. The guide is generated from the criteria registry and embeds each criterion's
   prompt verbatim, so T2's AC6-protected phrase necessarily echoes into it.

4. **Story `35bc` AC3 vs the epic's design.** AC3: *"No test file under
   `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/`, `tests/interfaces/store/` or
   `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py` contains `## Success Criteria`."* But
   sibling `5f4d`'s AC1 requires its reintroduction guard be *"proven by a test that injects
   one"*. The epic therefore REQUIRES a file containing the literal string, and the natural home
   is the contract test `35bc` itself adds. The completion verifier blocked the close on exactly
   this, twice.

### Class B — an AC contradicts a mechanical, checkable property of the artifact

5. **Epic `1386` AC5.** *"`docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is REGENERATED (not hand-edited)
   ... and contains no SC vocabulary."* The same criterion asserts the file is generated from
   the registry, and the registry contains T2's excluded prompt. The criterion contradicts
   itself in one sentence: regenerate from a source containing X, and contain no X.

### Class C — an AC hard-codes a count that the plan elsewhere says to recompute

6. **Epic `1386` AC4.** *"The **108** store tickets carrying `## Success Criteria` are
   migrated."* Child `0a8c`'s Scope explicitly says *"the migration recomputes the set rather
   than hard-coding it"*. The real number at run time was **106**. A literal reading of AC4 can
   never be satisfied, and a count in an AC is guaranteed to drift between authoring and
   execution.

### Class D — unowned scope: a parent AC that no child covers

7. **Epic `1386` AC1 vs the decomposition.** AC1 requires clearing SC vocabulary from every live
   file under `src/rebar/`, but `src/rebar/llm/completion.py:288` (*"its success criteria are met
   across children"*) was covered by **no child story**: `35bc` took the detectors, `2aa6` the
   reviewer prompts, `93d0` the eval specs, `44c7` the guides/docs. The union of children did not
   cover the parent's AC, so the epic could not close however perfectly each child was executed.
   This is notable because the criteria registry already contains **G3**, whose stated checklist
   is *"The union of children covers each parent acceptance/success criterion"* — the exact
   condition that was violated — and G3 routes at container scope. G3 ran and did not flag it.

## Cost of late detection

Each instance was found DURING implementation or at the close gate, not at review:

- `35bc` AC3 — the completion verifier refused the close twice. Resolution required amending the
  criterion, which invalidated the attestation as `stale-material` and forced a **full LLM
  re-review** before the ticket could close.
- `2aa6` AC1 and AC3 — found while implementing; same amend-plus-re-review cost.
- Epic AC1/AC4/AC5 and the unowned `completion.py` site — found only by hand-auditing the epic's
  AC against the real tree after three of six children were already closed and merged.

So the failure mode is not merely "a bad plan shipped": it is that **plan review certifies plans
that the completion verifier later refuses**, and the disagreement surfaces at the most expensive
possible moment — after the code is written, reviewed, and in `35bc`'s and `0a8c`'s case already
merged. Every correction also costs a re-review, because amending a description invalidates the
attestation.

## Signal that the reviewer CAN catch a neighbouring class

On re-review, `2aa6` was correctly **BLOCKED** for a stale cross-ticket factual claim (its plan
asserted prerequisite `1f32` *"has NOT yet merged"* when `show_ticket` showed it closed). So
cross-ticket fact-checking against live ticket state does fire. The seven failures above are a
different class — internal consistency between an AC and its own Scope, its sibling ACs, or the
decomposition — and none of them fired.

## Out of scope for this ticket

**Do not** analyse or redesign the plan-review process here. No investigation of criteria
prompts, routing, or detectors. This ticket exists to RECORD the evidence in detail; a follow-up
session owns the diagnosis and the fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] This ticket records all seven instances with the ORIGINAL criterion text, the specific
      text it contradicts, and the ticket each belongs to — enough for a follow-up session to
      reproduce the analysis without re-deriving it.
- [ ] The four failure classes (A: intra-ticket contradiction; B: contradiction with a mechanical
      property of a generated artifact; C: hard-coded count vs recompute-at-run-time; D: parent AC
      not covered by any child) are each named with at least one worked example.
- [ ] The evidence that these plans PASSED is recorded — epic `1386`'s signed manifest showing
      `plan-review: PASS`, `blocking: 0`, `advisory: 11`.
- [ ] The observation that G3 ("the union of children covers each parent acceptance/success
      criterion") exists, routes at container scope, ran, and did not flag the class-D gap is
      recorded as an observation only, with no diagnosis attached.
- [ ] The late-detection cost is recorded: which gate actually caught each instance
      (completion verifier / mid-implementation / manual audit) and that each fix forced a
      re-review via `stale-material`.
- [ ] No change is made to any plan-review prompt, criterion, routing entry or detector under
      this ticket.
baseline.summary: Plan review certified an epic whose acceptance criteria were mutually unsatisfiable

baseline.description:
## Why

Completion-verification is single-pass and, by contract, emits findings ONLY for FAILING criteria (`reconcile_verdict` flips a PASS-with-findings to FAIL). On a PASS it persists just signed counts via the attestation — no per-criterion record exists anywhere, and the FAIL-only sidecar never fires. So a successfully-closed ticket has no durable per-criterion completion audit, unlike its plan and code reviews.

## What

1. Extend the verifier's output contract with a positive per-criterion `criteria[]` array — one
   `{criterion, met, citation, kind}` entry per acceptance/success criterion evaluated (met
   status, a source-code or attestation citation, and its codebase-verifiable / operator-attested
   kind). This rides ALONGSIDE the failures-only `findings`; a PASS keeps `findings == []`.
2. Emit a completion sidecar on PASS (not only FAIL) persisting that array plus the verdict,
   runner, model, and material fingerprint.

Completion stays single-pass — this adds a per-criterion result list, NOT a four-pass structure.

## Schema-version strategy (explicit)

Do NOT bump the existing FAIL schema. Keep `SCHEMA_FAIL = "completion_verifier_fail_v1"` unchanged (so `latest_fail_verdict` and the existing FAIL-record tests are untouched). Add a SECOND constant `SCHEMA_PASS = "completion_verifier_pass_v1"` for PASS records; `build_payload` picks the schema by verdict. This keeps `test_fail_close_persists_durable_verdict` and `test_pass_close_leaves_no_fail_record` green (a PASS record is a different schema, so `latest_fail_verdict` still returns None on a PASS).

The `kind` field vocabulary is the CLOSED set `{"codebase-verifiable", "operator-attested"}` (matching ADR 0043's two criterion kinds); `met` is a bool; `citation` reuses the shared `Citation` shape (nullable).

## Scope (enumerated edit targets)

- `src/rebar/llm/contracts.py` — **load-bearing**: `CompletionVerdict` is a pydantic `BaseModel`
  with no `extra="allow"`, so pydantic v2 DROPS any `criteria[]` the agent emits unless it is a
  declared field. Add a `Criterion` sub-model (`{criterion: str, met: bool, citation: Citation |
  None, kind: str}`) and a `criteria: list[Criterion] = Field(default_factory=list)` field to
  `CompletionVerdict`.
- `src/rebar/schemas/completion_verdict.schema.json` — add the OPTIONAL `criteria[]` property
  (items `{criterion, met, citation, kind}`); `findings` stays required, `criteria` optional. The
  model↔schema PARITY test
  (`tests/interfaces/store/test_completion_verifier.py::test_completion_verdict_pins_to_schema`)
  asserts the model's field set equals the schema's property set, so it MUST be UPDATED in lockstep
  to include `criteria` (it will NOT pass unchanged) — this is an expected, in-scope test edit.
- `src/rebar/schemas/completion_reconcile_input.schema.json` — **required because this schema is
  `additionalProperties: false`**: add a `raw_criteria` (array) property, else the workflow's
  `completion_reconcile` step would reject/not-carry the criteria. (The verify step's `criteria`
  output must be threaded into the reconcile step — see the YAML edit below.)
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/completion-verification.yaml` — in the `completion_reconcile`
  step's `with:`, thread `raw_criteria: ${{ steps.verify.outputs.criteria }}` (alongside the
  existing `raw_verdict`/`raw_findings`), so the agent's positive array reaches the reconcile op.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py` — `completion_reconcile(ctx)` reads `raw_criteria` from
  `ctx.inputs` and sets `result["criteria"] = list(ctx.inputs.get("raw_criteria") or [])` on the
  reconciled verdict BEFORE `validate_structured`, so the workflow (close-gate) path carries
  `criteria[]` end-to-end — not only the bespoke `verify_completion` path.
- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md` — update the prompt: instruct the agent to
  emit `criteria[]` with one met-record per evaluated criterion (each with citation + kind).
  `findings` stays failures-only.
- `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` — `reconcile_verdict` must NOT flip a PASS that carries a
  populated `criteria[]` but empty `findings` (it keys the flip on `findings`; ensure `criteria[]`
  is not stripped and add the regression test).
- `src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py` — the existing constant is named `SCHEMA` (value
  `"completion_verifier_fail_v1"`). Do NOT rename it (that would churn the FAIL reader + its
  tests); keep `SCHEMA` as the FAIL schema and ADD a second constant
  `SCHEMA_PASS = "completion_verifier_pass_v1"`. `build_payload` branches on the verdict
  (PASS → `SCHEMA_PASS` + `criteria[]`; FAIL → unchanged `SCHEMA` + `findings`); add
  `latest_pass_record(ticket_id)` mirroring `latest_fail_verdict` but schema-guarded to
  `SCHEMA_PASS`. `latest_fail_verdict` (guarded to `SCHEMA`) is untouched, so a PASS record is
  invisible to it and the existing FAIL tests stay green.
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — on the PASS path (after the verdict is confirmed
  PASS, before `_verdict_manifest` signs), add a best-effort `completion_sidecar.emit(result,
  material=…, repo_root=repo_root)` (swallow its own errors — persistence is observability, never
  load-bearing on the close). Set `result.setdefault("ticket_id", resolved_id)` first.

## Compatibility & rollback

`criteria[]` is OPTIONAL — an older agent/response that omits it yields today's behavior (PASS counts only), and the failures-only `findings` invariant is unchanged, so nothing regresses. No backfill. Reverting stops the PASS-path emit and drops the field; existing FAIL records stay readable (their schema is untouched).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A completion PASS returns a `criteria[]` array with one met-record per evaluated criterion
      and `findings` stays empty. Oracle: a unit test on `reconcile_verdict` feeding a PASS
      verdict with a populated `criteria[]`, asserting it is NOT flipped to FAIL and the array
      survives; plus a test that the `CompletionVerdict` pydantic model round-trips `criteria[]`
      (proving it is not dropped).
- [ ] A completion PASS emits a `completion_verifier_pass_v1` sidecar persisting the per-criterion
      array. Oracle: an integration test that closes a ticket through the gate with a stub verifier
      returning the new PASS shape and asserts on the emitted event JSON (via the real sidecar
      emit path), plus that `latest_pass_record` reads it back.
- [ ] Live end-to-end: running the real completion verifier (`[agents]` extra + API key) on a
      fixture ticket whose criteria are met produces a PASS with a populated `criteria[]`
      persisted to the sidecar. Oracle: a live/E2E test exercising the real agent path, gated on
      LLM availability (skipped with a recorded reason otherwise).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: completion-verification lossless PASS capture (per-criterion record)

baseline.description:
Provide an explicit capture helper that lets agents record verbose session logs without hand-assembling `create` + `comment` calls — one call that creates a `session_log` on first use and appends an entry — available from all three interfaces.

## Why

Beyond plain `create` / `edit` / `comment`, agents benefit from a single convenience call that creates the session log (if needed) and appends activity to it, so verbose logging is low-friction and consistent. It is thin sugar over the existing shared write path, so it flows to library, CLI, and MCP uniformly.

## What

- A core helper that resolves/creates the current `session_log` (carrying a short
  work-summary title) and appends an entry as a COMMENT, via the existing
  `composer.create_core` + `leaf.comment` write path.
- Library: `rebar.append_session_log(entry, *, summary=None)`.
- CLI: `rebar session-log append "<entry>"` (and a `start --summary` to create the
  log explicitly).
- MCP: a write-gated `log_session(entry)` tool (no-op/refused under
  `REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1`).
- Allow optional `relates_to` / `discovered_from` links from the log to the work
  it documents.

## Scope

Explicit, agent-invoked capture helper only. Relies on the foundation (the type + write-path rules). An automatic per-session hook is **explicitly out of scope** for this epic (no honest cross-interface trigger — the CLI has no long-lived process — and it introduces write amplification).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A capture helper can create a `session_log` and append entries to it from the
      library, the CLI, and MCP, all through the single shared write path.
- [ ] First use creates exactly one log (with the summary title); subsequent calls
      append rather than recreating.
- [ ] Logs may carry `relates_to` / `discovered_from` links; blocking links remain
      refused.
- [ ] The MCP tool is refused/no-op under `REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1`.
- [ ] Tests cover create-then-append and the three-interface parity.
baseline.summary: Session-log capture helper (explicit, all three interfaces)

baseline.description:
## Context

`model_max_output_tokens` (`src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py`, `MODEL_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`) knows only the three Claude ladder models and falls back to `DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS` (16,000) for an unmapped model. Amazon Nova models on Bedrock accept at most 10,000 output tokens, so every review call that rides the "raise to model max" seam with a Nova model is rejected by Bedrock with `ValidationException: The maximum tokens you requested exceeds the model limit of 10000` before it runs — measured live during the 2026-08-11 model-comparison experiments (rebar ticket b902-18af-14ed-4da1), where the whole plan-review LLM phase collapsed to INDETERMINATE until the table was patched in-process. Nova Pro subsequently completed 8/8 end-to-end plan-review replays, so the ceiling entry is the only blocker to running these models through rebar.

## Plan

Add four entries to `MODEL_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`: `("nova-pro", 10_000)`, `("nova-2-lite", 10_000)`, `("nova-lite", 10_000)`, `("nova-micro", 10_000)`. The lookup is a plain substring match, and `nova-lite` is NOT a substring of `nova-2-lite` (the `-2-` breaks it), so both forms are listed explicitly; the full Bedrock inference-profile ids (`us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0` etc.) are covered by the same substring semantics. Values per the AWS Bedrock model documentation: Nova family max output tokens = 10,000. No behavior change for any currently-configured model: the table is consulted only when the resolved model matches an entry, and the existing conservative fallback stays for everything else.

Extend the existing unit coverage of `model_max_output_tokens` with the Nova ids (full Bedrock profile-id form and bare form).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `model_max_output_tokens("bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0")` returns 10000. Verify: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from rebar.llm.review_kernel.verify import model_max_output_tokens as f; assert f('bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0')==10000 and f('us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0')==10000 and f('claude-sonnet-4-6')==128000"` exits 0.
- [x] A unit test pins the Nova entries alongside the existing Claude entries. Verify: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_max_tokens_model_ceiling_1019.py -x` passes.
- [x] Unknown models still fall back to the configured default (existing behavior pinned by an assertion in the same test). Verify: same pytest run passes.
baseline.summary: Teach MODEL_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS the Amazon Nova output ceilings (10k) so Bedrock Nova calls stop 400ing

baseline.description: Parked from ticket b5f8-d3f9-39d9-4195 (bounded auto-resume for the completion close gate), whose resumption deliberately passes NO frontier. Steering a resumption away from already-searched places (or toward where credited evidence was found) requires an argument-level tool-call transcript that the verifier telemetry does not currently carry. This idea covers (1) the capability question — extending verifier telemetry to record tool-call arguments per evidence-search step — and (2) the extractor design on top of it that would digest a failed attempt's search frontier into a hint for the next attempt. Cache seeding alone proved sufficient in the live 8d74 re-run, so this is an optimization, not a correctness gap; it stays an idea until the telemetry capability question is answered.
baseline.summary: Search-frontier handoff for completion-verifier auto-resume (capability question)

baseline.description:
## What

Generate `docs/cli-reference.md` from the CLI's OWN help data, so the command reference cannot drift, and gate it in CI like `scripts/gen_env_registry.py`.

## Source of truth (verified — the CLI surface is two disjoint families)
1. **50 help-backed subcommands** — fully enumerable, RELIABLE help text:
   - `rebar._cli._help.known_subcommands() -> frozenset[str]` (returns 50).
   - `rebar._cli._help.subcommand_help(sub) -> str|None` — the full pinned usage text
     (package data under `rebar._cli.help/*.txt`). Reliable; use this for full help.
2. **16 intercept-arm commands** — handled in `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` main() before the
   `known_subcommands()` check (~lines 372-447), with NO `help/*.txt` and no overview row:
   `reconcile, review, review-code, scan-spec, verify-completion, review-plan, sign-review,
   enrich, explain, verify-commit-ticket, workflow, llm, jira-onboard, prompt, criteria,
   config`.

**Do NOT subprocess-capture `rebar <cmd> --help` for the intercepts.** Verified gotcha: `rebar enrich --help` has no argparse parser (`cmd_enrich()` in `rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py`) — it calls `drain()` and prints JSON with exit 0, so a "non-empty + exit 0" guard would silently store JSON garbage as "help". Subprocess capture across 16 heterogeneous commands is fragile. Instead: carry a hardcoded **curated one-line description** for each of the 16 intercept commands in the generator (`INTERCEPT_COMMANDS: dict[str,str]`), and DRIFT-GATE the dict's key set against the `if argv[0] == "..."` ladder in `_cli/__init__.py` so a newly-added intercept without a curated entry fails the generator loudly.

Total ~66 commands, all listed; the 50 with full pinned help, the 16 with a curated one-liner (marked as advanced/intercept commands, "see `rebar <cmd> --help`").

## Scope
- Add `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` (new): Family 1 via `_help.known_subcommands()` +
  `subcommand_help()`; Family 2 via the `INTERCEPT_COMMANDS` curated dict. Emit
  `docs/cli-reference.md` with a "Generated by … do not edit" header (mirror
  `gen_env_registry.py`), each command name rendered backtick-wrapped for exact matching.
- The generator asserts `set(INTERCEPT_COMMANDS) == <ladder set parsed from _cli/__init__.py>`
  and exits non-zero on mismatch (so a new/removed intercept is caught — no subprocess).
- `--check` mode: regenerate in memory, exit non-zero if committed file differs.
- Wire a drift gate into BOTH `.github/workflows/test.yml` AND
  `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` (the actual Verified gate; a parity test
  `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` ENFORCES every `scripts/*.py` in test.yml also
  appears in gerrit-verify.yaml — omitting the latter breaks `make test`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/cli-reference.md` is generated (marked generated) and lists BOTH families:
      every `known_subcommands()` entry (50) with its full help AND all 16 intercept
      commands with a curated one-liner.
- [ ] Completeness proof, EXACT backtick match (no substring false positives like
      `review` vs `review-plan`), prints nothing:
      `python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py && for c in $(python -c "from rebar._cli import _help; print(' '.join(sorted(_help.known_subcommands())))") reconcile review review-code scan-spec verify-completion review-plan sign-review enrich explain verify-commit-ticket workflow llm jira-onboard prompt criteria config; do grep -qF "\`$c\`" docs/cli-reference.md || echo "MISSING $c"; done`
- [ ] Intercept-drift guard: `set(INTERCEPT_COMMANDS)` equals the ladder set parsed from
      `_cli/__init__.py`; a mismatch makes the generator exit non-zero. DETERMINISTIC proof
      (prints `CAUGHT`): temporarily remove one key from the dict in memory and confirm the
      generator's self-check fails — covered by a held-out unit test that mutates the dict
      and asserts a non-zero/raise. (The generator runs this parity check on every run.)
- [ ] Drift gate works — a stale committed reference fails `--check` (prints `CAUGHT`):
      `python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py; printf '\nstale\n' >> docs/cli-reference.md; python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py --check >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo MISS || echo CAUGHT; python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`
- [ ] The gate is wired in BOTH CI files (prints nothing):
      `for f in .github/workflows/test.yml .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml; do grep -qF 'gen_cli_reference.py' "$f" || echo "NOT WIRED: $f"; done`
      and `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py -q` passes.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` stay green.

Files: `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` (new), `docs/cli-reference.md` (new/generated), `.github/workflows/test.yml`, `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`.
baseline.summary: P1: Generate the CLI command reference (generator + drift gate)

baseline.description:
Stop `rebar init` from silently creating an empty divergent store when it cannot obtain the configured tickets branch. This fixes P1 `01e8-302b`.

## Current mechanism

`_mount_or_create_branch` currently checks only local refs and the local remote-tracking ref. If both are absent, it immediately creates an orphan branch. A failed or timed-out fetch can therefore make an existing remote branch look like a genuine first init. `pending_init_attaches_to_existing` repeats the same ref-only predicate. Both `ensure_store_mounted_best_effort` and `_create_tracker` in `src/rebar/_cli/_init.py` consume that predicate, so every path must share one tri-state result and distinguish unreachable from genuinely absent.

The current code already bounds the cold materializing fetch with `_git_fetch` and `_FETCH_TIMEOUT = 300`. Preserve that behavior. Add a shorter bounded remote-advertisement probe through a shared network runner rather than duplicating the timeout wrapper. Use `git ls-remote --exit-code <remote> refs/heads/<branch>`: return code 0 means advertised, 2 means reachable but absent, and timeout or another failure means unreachable.

## Implementation plan

- Generalize the existing bounded Git-network seam so `_git_fetch` retains its 300-second cold-fetch contract and a new advertisement probe uses a short named timeout. Both convert `TimeoutExpired` to a descriptive `CompletedProcess(124)`.
- Add one shared tri-state remote-branch probe consumed by `_mount_or_create_branch`, `pending_init_attaches_to_existing`, `ensure_store_mounted_best_effort`, and `_create_tracker` whenever neither a local branch nor a local remote-tracking ref exists.
- Cache only the tri-state probe result for a short named TTL, keyed by resolved repo, remote, and branch. The first best-effort-mount probe and immediately following strict auto-init reuse one result, so an unreachable remote costs at most one probe timeout per CLI invocation. Inject the monotonic clock for a test that advances past the TTL and proves later calls re-probe.
- Preserve `ensure_store_mounted_best_effort` as a non-raising best-effort API. It treats unreachable as do-not-auto-mount and returns without error. Its `init_core` call continues to use `force_new_store=False`, supplied by the default or explicitly, and it never authorizes an override.
- Update `_create_tracker` to distinguish reachable-absent from unreachable. Unreachable fails closed with the remote diagnostic and never enters the interactive consent gate. The preceding best-effort path and strict path reuse the cached result.
- If the remote advertises the branch, attempt the existing bounded fetch. Mount only after the branch materializes. If fetch fails, return nonzero with an error naming the configured remote and branch plus fetch-and-retry remediation. Never create an orphan in this state.
- If the remote is reachable and does not advertise the branch, preserve legitimate first-init orphan bootstrap.
- If the probe cannot reach the remote or times out, fail closed with a distinct error naming the remote, branch, timeout where applicable, retry remediation, and explicit deliberate-bootstrap override. Never create an orphan unless the override was supplied.
- Add `--force-new-store` to explicit CLI init, thread `force_new_store=False` through `init_core`, and expose the equivalent keyword on `rebar.init_repo`. Auto-init and `ensure_store_mounted_best_effort` never supply the override; only an explicit CLI flag or library keyword can authorize bootstrap while reachability is unknown.
- The override applies only to unreachable. When the remote is reachable, warn that `--force-new-store` has no effect and continue normal behavior: reachable-absent bootstraps normally; advertised fetches and mounts or fails nonzero without orphaning.
- Update `src/rebar/_cli/help/init.txt` and regenerate `docs/cli-reference.md` for the new flag.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With a reachable remote advertising the configured tickets branch but no local remote-tracking ref, a simulated bounded fetch failure returns nonzero and creates no orphan branch. Tier: CLI subprocess with real temporary repositories.
- [ ] With a reachable remote that does not advertise the configured branch, init still bootstraps successfully. Tier: CLI subprocess negative control.
- [ ] With an unreachable or timing-out remote, explicit init and strict auto-init return nonzero within one probe bound, create no orphan branch, and emit an error distinct from advertised/fetch-failed. Strict auto-init does not enter the consent prompt. Proving command: `pytest tests/integration/test_init_fail_closed.py -k unreachable -v`.
- [ ] `ensure_store_mounted_best_effort` treats unreachable as do-not-auto-mount, returns without error, and never supplies `force_new_store=True`; the following strict path reuses the cached result and reports the actionable failure.
- [ ] `rebar init --force-new-store` and `rebar.init_repo(force_new_store=True)` permit deliberate bootstrap only when reachability cannot be established. Tier: CLI subprocess plus library interface test.
- [ ] With a reachable advertised branch, `--force-new-store` is ineffective: the command warns, attempts normal bounded fetch, and returns nonzero without an orphan if fetch fails. With reachable-absent, it warns and follows normal successful bootstrap. Tier: CLI subprocess negative controls.
- [ ] Failure messages name the configured remote, configured branch, timeout where applicable, and concrete fetch/retry or force-new-store remediation. Tier: unit assertions on stderr.
- [ ] An existing healthy store remains idempotent, does not invoke the advertisement probe, and is unaffected by the override default. Proving command: `pytest tests/integration/test_init_fail_closed.py -k idempotent -v`.
- [ ] `pending_init_attaches_to_existing` returns true when the remote advertises the branch despite no local remote-tracking ref, and false for reachable-absent and unreachable. Proving command: `pytest tests/unit/test_init_attach_predicate.py -v`.
- [ ] Behavioral wiring tests monkeypatch the one shared probe and prove `_mount_or_create_branch`, `pending_init_attaches_to_existing`, `ensure_store_mounted_best_effort`, and `_create_tracker` consume it; a second independent remote-existence predicate fails the tests.
- [ ] One CLI invocation performs at most one underlying advertisement probe on the unreachable path; advancing the injected monotonic clock past the short TTL causes a fresh probe. Tier: unit orchestration test.
- [ ] Existing timeout tests continue proving cold fetch retains its 300-second bound, while new tests prove the advertisement probe has its own positive short bound and folds timeout to return code 124.
- [ ] `rebar init --help` and generated `docs/cli-reference.md` both contain `--force-new-store` and its deliberate-bootstrap semantics. Proving commands: `rebar init --help | grep -- --force-new-store` and `grep -- --force-new-store docs/cli-reference.md`.

## Files

Production and docs: `src/rebar/_commands/init.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_init.py`, `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/help/init.txt`, and generated `docs/cli-reference.md`.

Tests: new `tests/integration/test_init_fail_closed.py` and `tests/unit/test_init_attach_predicate.py`; update existing direct-call and timeout coverage including `tests/unit/test_git_timeout_bounds_983f.py` and `tests/unit/test_sync_remote_config.py`, plus other directly affected init CLI/library tests discovered during the RED-first inventory.

Scope: S-M. No dependencies.
baseline.summary: B2: fail closed instead of orphan-bootstrapping an empty store when the tickets fetch fails (fixes P1 01e8-302b)

baseline.description:
## Reproduction Steps
1. Local ticket has a description long enough that its ADF representation exceeds Jira's ~32k limit (`_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT = 32000`).
2. Outbound sync truncates the description via `adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit` so it fits Jira (send-side only, by design).
3. Jira now stores the TRUNCATED description.
4. On the next inbound pass, `inbound_differ._diff_jira_vs_local` compares Jira's truncated description against local's full description.

**Expected:** Inbound recognises Jira's body as the truncated form of local and emits NO description change; the local description (and its plan-review fingerprint/signature) is untouched.

**Actual:** Inbound only `rstrip()`-compares, sees the truncated Jira body != full local body, and emits `changed["description"] = <truncated>`. The applier writes the truncated body into the local store, clobbering the full description and invalidating the plan-review attestation.

## Root Cause
Asymmetry between the two differs:
- Outbound (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_fields.py:436-437`) applies `fit_text_to_adf_limit(local_val)` before comparing, so it converges.
- Inbound (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_differ.py` `_diff_jira_vs_local`, ~L295-302) does NOT apply the same transform to the local value before comparison.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Inbound differ applies the identical `fit_text_to_adf_limit` transform to the local description before comparing to Jira, mirroring the outbound convergence fix.
- [ ] When Jira holds only the truncated form of an otherwise-identical local description, NO inbound description mutation is emitted (local store + fingerprint unchanged).
- [ ] A genuine Jira-side description edit (not merely truncation) STILL flows inbound (no regression to inbound field-sync).
- [ ] Unit test (RED→GREEN) in tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing covering the truncation-equal case and the genuine-edit case.
- [ ] E2E/integration test covering the full outbound-truncate → Jira-holds-truncated → inbound-pass round-trip asserting local description is unchanged.
baseline.summary: Inbound differ clobbers local description with Jira-truncated body, invalidating plan-review signature

baseline.description:
# Thread an explicit cap_override through run_pass1 -> shed_to_budget

## Problem (verified at origin/main cc69cc1179)

`ProductionBatchRunner.run` receives `req.usd_budget` as a per-plan cost cap override but cannot apply it. `run_pass1` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:425`) calls `_shed_to_budget` (`:453`, an alias for `sizing.shed_to_budget`), which computes the cap INTERNALLY at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py:605` — `cap = plan_budget_cap(ctx)` — with no injection point.

The two "overrides" available today are both wrong: `REBAR_PLAN_REVIEW_BUDGET` is read by `plan_budget_cap` (`sizing.py:120-130`) as the BASE and then centrality-scaled (`base * (1.0 + ctx.centrality)`), so it is not a cap override at all, and it is a process-global env var; the alternative is a parameter, which is exactly this ticket. So the runner currently JOURNALS the request and drops it (`production_batch_runner.py:142-149`: `coverage["requested_usd_budget"]`, `budget_override_applied = False`, a WARNING) and the computed cap is used.

## Approach

Add an OPTIONAL `cap_override` parameter along the existing call chain `ProductionBatchRunner.run` -> `run_pass1` -> `shed_to_budget`, defaulting to `None` (= today's behaviour, byte-identical).

`cap_override` is the FINAL cap in USD, used VERBATIM — NOT centrality-scaled. That is the whole point of the seam: the env var's base-then-scale semantics is precisely why it is "NOT a true cap override" per this ticket. `None` (not falsiness) selects the computed cap, so an explicit `0.0` is honourable as "shed everything sheddable".

The runner then passes `req.usd_budget` and flips its journal to `budget_override_applied = True`, dropping the WARNING. `coverage["budget"]` (`sizing.py:640-648`) gains a `cap_source` of `"override"` or `"computed"` so which cap governed a run stays observable.

**Scope honesty:** the plan-review gate YAML does NOT set `usd_budget` on its `finders` batch step today (only the v3 schema defines the key, `src/rebar/schemas/workflow.v3.schema.json:302`), so `req.usd_budget` is `None` on every live gate run and the live gate's behaviour is UNCHANGED. This ticket builds the seam and makes the request honourable; it deliberately does NOT start setting a budget in the gate YAML, which would be a separate cost-policy decision.

## Changes

1. `sizing.py:586` — `shed_to_budget(..., cap_override: float | None = None)`; at `:605`
   `cap = plan_budget_cap(ctx) if cap_override is None else float(cap_override)`. Record
   `cap_source` in the `coverage["budget"]` dict.
2. `pass1.py:425` — `run_pass1(..., cap_override: float | None = None)`, forwarded at `:453`.
3. `production_batch_runner.py:142-152` — pass `req.usd_budget` into `run_pass1`; journal
   `budget_override_applied = True` and drop the "no clean seam" WARNING. Update the D4
   docstring at `:22-26`, which names this ticket as the follow-up.

## Tests

- `shed_to_budget` with a `cap_override` BELOW the projected sheddable spend sheds criteria
  that the computed cap would have kept, and records `cap_usd` == the override with
  `cap_source: "override"`. Its companion: the same call with `cap_override=None` is unchanged.
- `cap_override` is NOT centrality-scaled: on a ctx with non-zero `centrality`, the recorded
  `cap_usd` equals the override exactly (the bug the seam exists to avoid).
- `cap_override=0.0` is honoured rather than treated as absent (the `is None` vs falsy trap).
- Through `ProductionBatchRunner`: a `BatchRunRequest` with `usd_budget` set produces
  `coverage["budget"]["cap_usd"]` == that value and `budget_override_applied` true.
- **Stub-arity population.** `run_pass1` is replaced via `monkeypatch.setattr` — invisible to
  Serena — so the population is enumerated by grepping the symbol as a STRING
  (`grep -rn 'run_pass1' tests/`). Exactly TWO 6-positional-arg stubs exist:
  `tests/unit/test_pass1_finder_model.py:96` and `tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py:136`
  (both `def _fake_run_pass1(ctx, cfg, runner, single, agent, coverage)`). Both must accept the
  new argument. Direct `sizing.shed_to_budget(...)` callers
  (`tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:1870,1873,1890`) pass 5 positional args and are unaffected by
  a defaulted trailing parameter.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `shed_to_budget(..., cap_override=X)` uses X as the cap verbatim, with no centrality
      scaling: on a ctx with centrality > 0, recorded `cap_usd` == X exactly.
- [x] `cap_override=0.0` is treated as a real cap, not as absent.
- [x] `cap_override=None` (and every existing 5-positional call) behaves exactly as today.
- [x] `run_pass1` forwards `cap_override` to `shed_to_budget`.
- [x] A `BatchRunRequest` carrying `usd_budget` yields `coverage["budget"]["cap_usd"]` equal to
      it and `coverage["budget_override_applied"]` true.
- [x] `coverage["budget"]["cap_source"]` is `"override"` when overridden and `"computed"`
      otherwise.
- [x] The `production_batch_runner.py` WARNING and D4 docstring naming this ticket are gone.
- [x] The plan-review gate YAML still sets NO `usd_budget`, so live-gate behaviour is unchanged.
- [x] NO 6-positional-arg `run_pass1` stub remains: `grep -rn 'run_pass1' tests/` shows both
      `test_pass1_finder_model.py` and `test_model_class_ladder.py` stubs accepting the new
      argument. This fails while ANY instance remains un-updated.
- [x] `make lint` passes.
- [x] `make typecheck` passes.
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/workflow tests/unit/test_plan_review.py tests/unit/test_pass1_finder_model.py tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py` passes.
baseline.summary: plan-review: explicit cap_override seam through run_pass1 -> shed_to_budget

# Revisit pandoc spawn cost on the DC render path (after `rich_sha` lands)

Deferred from `ashy-waterlog-hamadryas` (5c0e), where safe-run batching was DESCOPED by operator decision. Park this until the cutover story's change-gated `rich_sha` skip has landed and real spawn cost can be measured against it; the skip avoids rendering unchanged bodies entirely and may remove the problem outright.

## The hazard
The DC renderer spawns one pandoc process per renderable unit: ~0.3s/field flat spawn cost independent of body size, and a serial reconcile over many fields was measured blocking ~20 min of wall time on `fork+exec`.

## What was already measured (starting point — do not redo)
Against the landed renderer (merged `cf5155e528`) over the committed 178-body corpus in `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/`:
- 233 contiguous SAFE runs across 884 `_RENDER` units. Ceiling = 74% fewer spawns, but **106 of 233 runs (46%) are a single unit**, so it is unreachable.
- Run-level fallback (one bad fragment poisons the run): **63/178 bodies (35%) lose richness**.
- Verify-then-accept with per-unit fallback: 157/178 identical to per-unit, but only **12% fewer spawns**, because a failed batch pays for both attempts.
- **21/178 bodies render DIFFERENTLY even when a batch verifies.** pandoc parses block boundaries relative to surrounding content, so concatenating units into one commonmark document is not equivalent to rendering them separately. Suspected causes: setext-style headings, lazy continuation, reference-style links.

## Where to start if this is picked up
The 21 divergent bodies are the whole question. Characterise them first: if a document-assembly rule (for example forcing an unambiguous hard block separator between concatenated units, or normalising trailing blank lines) restores byte-equivalence, batching becomes a transparent optimization and the 74%-ceiling argument can be revisited. If it cannot, batching should stay descoped.

Any renewed attempt must keep the invariant this fleet already enforced once: rendered output must not change silently. Prove byte-equality against the per-unit path over the whole corpus before proposing it.
baseline.summary: Revisit pandoc spawn cost on the DC render path

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Reconciler parity bugs (3f04, 4b59, 32cc class: inverted link directions, asymmetric field handling) escape because per-field asymmetry POLICY lives scattered in code with no single declarative source: the should_propagate_removal gate (rebar.reducer._managed_refs) is imported at four separate reconciler sites, add-wins tag merging is an inline dedup in apply_inbound_records.py, and inbound_differ carries only a 2-entry field-NAME canonicalization map (_OUTBOUND_TO_INBOUND_FIELD). No enumerable "field contract" exists yet — this ticket CREATES it. The typed-transport half of this hardening already landed as bug cc77 (closed; Gerrit 1222-1225 merged) — do not duplicate it. Pagination-iterator consolidation was split out of this ticket into its own child (see discovered_from link) after plan review flagged the bundle.

## Approach
(1) MATERIALIZE the contract: new module src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_field_contract.py — a declarative registry enumerating each reconciled field with its symmetry class (bidirectional-roundtrip / add-wins / one-way-with-propagation-gate) plus references to its codec/gate (e.g. should_propagate_removal for managed refs, the tag dedup for add-wins). The module docstring records this as the cross-cutting registration contract for future fields, and a one-paragraph pointer is added to the reconciler section of docs/architecture.md so new call sites know to register (captures the new convention durably). (2) Property tests parameterized OFF the registry: tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_field_contract_properties.py. Coverage guard: the test module enumerates the reconciled fields handled by inbound_differ/apply_inbound_records and fails collection if any handled field lacks a registry entry (adding a field without declaring its class breaks the build). Per-class properties: roundtrip identity asserted ONLY for declared-bidirectional value codecs (status mapping, link inward/outward direction); add-wins fields get a merge-idempotence + no-removal property; one-way-gated fields get a gate-consulted property (behavior asserted consistent with should_propagate_removal through the real call path). (3) NO behavior refactor: the registry declares, tests assert code behavior MATCHES declarations. Rewiring call sites to import the registry is explicitly out of scope (follow-up candidate if drift recurs); this keeps the change additive and low-risk.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_field_contract.py (new, declarative registry)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_field_contract_properties.py (new)
- docs/architecture.md (one-paragraph registration-contract note in the reconciler section)
- OUT of scope: pagination iterators (split to sibling ticket), call-site rewiring, any transport work (cc77 landed).

## Testing
The property tests are the deliverable. Mutation check before push: flip one declared symmetry class in the registry — the named field's property test must fail; delete one registry entry — collection must fail via the coverage guard.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] _field_contract.py registry exists; every reconciled field handled by the differ/apply path has a declared symmetry class; docstring + docs/architecture.md note record the registration contract.
- [x] Coverage guard fails collection for a handled-but-undeclared field (proven by the deletion mutation).
- [x] Roundtrip identity asserted only for declared-bidirectional codecs; add-wins and gated classes have their class-specific properties asserted through real call paths.
- [x] relates_to link recorded to cc77 (typed transport, already landed/closed) and discovered_from link on the split-out pagination child.
baseline.summary: Reconciler: declared-asymmetry property tests + pagination iterator dedup

baseline.description:
# Code-review verdicts never record provider_provenance

## Context / Problem
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py:106` reads `verdict.get("provider_provenance")`, but the code-review verdict NEVER sets that key, so every signed code-review verdict records it as absent. This is the SAME defect that story 343b found and fixed for the plan-review and completion gates (343b gap 5); code review was left out of that change deliberately to keep it reviewable.

VERIFIED IN SOURCE at commit b872bc3c89:
- The terminal verdict is assembled by `code_review_coach`
  (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py:500-532`); its return dict carries
  verdict/blocking/advisory/coaching/coverage/dropped/indeterminate and no provenance.
- `finalize_code_review_verdict` then adds only cfg-derived fields:
  `verdict.setdefault("runner", runner_sel.name)` and `verdict.setdefault("model", cfg.model)`
  (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/finalize.py:244-245`). Exactly the cfg-derived shape 343b removed
  from plan-review.
- The outage path `_degraded_code_review_verdict` (`workflow/gate_dispatch.py:246-257`) sets
  `runner` only.

CONSEQUENCE: the epic's acceptance criterion "A signed verdict states which provider, endpoint host, and support tier produced it" holds for two of the three gates. A code-review verdict produced through Bedrock, or behind an OpenAI-compatible gateway, still records only a bare model string -- the misattribution the provenance record exists to remove. This matters most for the review bot, which is the S8 Bedrock cutover target.

## Approach
Mirror what 343b did, and reuse its mechanism rather than inventing a second one: `capabilities.provenance_for` assembles the record ONCE inside the runner (`src/rebar/llm/runner.py:388`) and `findings.finalize_outcome` stamps it onto every per-call result (`findings.py:312-313,343-344`). An AGENT step's outputs are the runner result VERBATIM (`workflow/runs.py:262`), and 343b made `_dispatch` default the key to None when no provider resolved, so `${{ steps.<agent>.outputs.provider_provenance }}` resolves for code review too.

So the shape is: wire the record from code review's own Pass-2 `verify` agent step through to whatever assembles the terminal verdict, and set the key only when it is present.

DO NOT recompute the record at the verdict site. `capabilities.provenance_for`'s docstring (`capabilities.py:295-300`) forbids it: a recomputed record can diverge from the one that actually drove the run, which is the prior regression it must not repeat.

DO NOT try to carry it through the usage aggregate. `sizing.usage_record` (`sizing.py:272-290`) builds each per-call record from the runner result's `_usage` SUB-DICT only, and the provenance lives at the result's TOP level, so it is dropped before aggregation. 343b established this dead end; do not re-derive it.

HONEST VALUE WHERE NOTHING RAN: `_degraded_code_review_verdict` is the outage path -- no model ran, so it must OMIT the key rather than synthesize one from cfg. 343b applies the same rule at its three no-record sites.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/finalize.py` (298 LOC) and/or
  `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py` -- whichever holds the assembly seam.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` -- the wire from the verify step.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:246-257` -- the outage path, comment only.
- a test file under `tests/unit/`.

## Testing
THE ORACLE MUST NOT HAND-BUILD A VERDICT. That is precisely why 343b gap 5 shipped broken: every test handed `build_payload` a verdict that already contained the key, proving the persist step and never the path. Model the tests on `tests/unit/test_verdict_provenance_wiring.py`:
- assert the gate YAML actually WIRES the record, from a step that is an AGENT step (only an agent
  step's outputs are the runner result verbatim; sourcing from a scripted op silently wires None);
- assert on a verdict produced by the REAL assembly path, then fed to the REAL sidecar payload
  builder;
- a control asserting the outage path omits the key rather than inventing one.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] a test asserts a code-review verdict produced by the real assembly path carries
      `provider_provenance`, and that the real sidecar payload built FROM that verdict records it
- [x] a test asserts `code-review.yaml` wires the record from an AGENT step, not a scripted op
- [x] a test asserts the degraded/outage code-review verdict OMITS the key rather than deriving one
      from cfg
- [x] `grep -n "setdefault(\"model\"" src/rebar/llm/code_review/finalize.py` is accompanied by a
      provenance assignment, i.e. the verdict no longer records a bare model string alone
- [x] every file touched stays at or under the 800-LOC cap in `.github/module-size-limit.txt`
baseline.summary: Code-review verdicts never record provider_provenance

baseline.description:
# Land dependabot PRs #129 + #130 as ONE Gerrit change (setup-uv v10 + uv-lock botocore/json-repair)

## Context / Problem

GitHub is a read-only mirror: dependabot PRs never merge there; content is re-applied locally and landed via Gerrit, then the PRs are commented/closed. Per operator directive these two open dependabot PRs are grouped into a SINGLE ticket and a SINGLE Gerrit change (one commit touching both the CI-action pin and the lockfile — the shared "dependency housekeeping" lane):

* PR #129 (`dependabot/github_actions/github-actions-fa3bf1173d`, github-actions
  group): `astral-sh/setup-uv` v9.0.0 (`c771a70e…`) -> v10.0.0 (`ae62891f…`),
  19 pinned-SHA references across 11 workflow files. VALIDITY: v10 is a major
  bump; its ONLY breaking change disables the cache for `enable-cache: auto` on
  `pull_request_target` / `workflow_run` / `release` events (cache-poisoning
  hardening, astral-sh/setup-uv#984). EVERY rebar usage passes
  `enable-cache: true` explicitly (never `auto`), so that change does not alter
  our behavior; the `version`/`version-file` additions are opt-in and unused.
  Dependabot pins the exact v10.0.0 commit SHA, so the bump is reproducible.

* PR #130 (`dependabot/uv/uv-lock-434831ba27`, uv-lock group): two lock-only
  patch bumps —
  - `botocore` 1.43.69 -> 1.43.70 (patch) — SAFE. Routine service-model update;
    consumed via lazy imports only (`bedrock_model.py`, `structured.py`,
    `remote_cert.py`). pyproject floor `botocore>=1.43.0` already admits it and
    boto3's botocore range (`<1.44`) accepts it, so boto3 need not move.
  - `json-repair` 0.63.0 -> 0.63.1 (patch) — SAFE. `src/rebar/llm/structured.py`
    calls `repair_json(cand, return_objects=True[, schema=…])`; the called API is
    unchanged across the patch. Floor `json-repair>=0.61` already admits it.
  The PR also carries uv's lockfile-format churn: `revision = 2 -> 3` and an
  httpcore2 marker simplification (dependabot ran a newer uv). Both are
  format/resolver byproducts, not dependency changes; `uv lock --check` on main
  already passes latest-uv, so revision is not load-bearing — but we reproduce
  the PR faithfully by regenerating with a recent uv.

## Approach

In a fresh worktree branched from `origin/main` (venv on PATH):

1. NO pyproject.toml edit — all bumps are admitted by existing constraints
   (setup-uv is a SHA pin in workflow YAML, not a pyproject dep; botocore /
   json-repair floors listed above; no exact pins exist for either).
2. setup-uv: replace every `astral-sh/setup-uv@c771a70e…  # v9.0.0` with
   `astral-sh/setup-uv@ae62891fec2bb8e7d6c99fc78c9fec3a63790f8d  # v10.0.0`
   across the 11 workflow files (19 sites) via an exact-string sed; verify 0
   remaining v9 SHAs and 19 v10 SHAs.
3. uv-lock: install a recent uv in the worktree, then
   `uv lock --upgrade-package botocore --upgrade-package json-repair`. If uv
   resolves PAST the PR's reviewed versions (per the #128 precedent it did),
   re-lock with exact `==1.43.70` / `==0.63.1` pins so the landed lock matches
   the certified scope; the newer patches arrive in the next dependabot round.
   Then `uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra agents` so gates run against the
   bumped tree. Verify `git diff uv.lock` moved only botocore/json-repair (plus
   uv's transitive/format bookkeeping) — no other version churn.
4. Gates: YAML-parse the 11 changed workflow files; `uv lock --check`;
   `make lint`; `make typecheck`; targeted usage-surface tests
   (`pytest tests/unit/test_structured.py tests/unit/test_silent_success.py`
   for json-repair; `tests/unit/test_llm_capabilities.py` for the botocore lazy
   import — run whichever exist). Full `pytest tests/unit` is CI's job; CI
   Verified +1 is the authoritative full-suite gate.
5. ONE commit (subject <=50 chars, body wrapped at 72) with trailer
   `rebar-ticket: <this ticket's full canonical id>` + DCO `-s`;
   `git push gerrit HEAD:refs/for/main`. Leave the ticket in_progress for the
   bots; the change is submitted only after LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1.
6. Comment on BOTH PR #129 and PR #130 pointing at the single Gerrit change and
   noting they were grouped; leave the PRs open for dependabot/operator to close
   once the mirror updates.

## STOP / defer rule (explicit fallback done-state)

If a package bump fails its targeted tests or lint/typecheck in step 4: drop ONLY that package (re-lock from a clean `git checkout uv.lock` with the remaining package), record the failure evidence as a ticket comment, and land the remaining safe content. If setup-uv v10 fails a workflow-parse or a real usage incompatibility surfaces, drop the actions bump and land the lock subset (or vice-versa) — the two halves are independent. The fallback done-state: the ticket closes legitimately with the landed subset, provided every dropped item has a recorded-on-ticket failure reason.

## Out of scope

* Any src/rebar or test code change — nothing in these deltas requires one.
* boto3 / mcp / any other dependency bump not in PR #129 or #130.
* pyproject.toml constraint edits and `.github/complexity-baseline.json`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: on the landed change, all 19 setup-uv references read the v10.0.0 SHA
  `ae62891fec2bb8e7d6c99fc78c9fec3a63790f8d` across the 11 workflow files, zero
  v9 SHAs remain, and all 11 changed workflow files still parse as valid YAML.
- [ ] AC2: `uv.lock` records botocore 1.43.70 and json-repair 0.63.1 (or a
  documented STOP-rule subset), pyproject.toml is unchanged, and
  `uv lock --check` exits 0.
- [ ] AC3: `make lint` + `make typecheck` exit 0 and the targeted usage-surface
  tests pass against the bumped tree.
- [ ] AC4: the change lands through Gerrit as a SINGLE change with a
  `rebar-ticket:` trailer for this ticket's full canonical id + DCO sign-off,
  after LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1.
- [ ] AC5: both PR #129 and PR #130 carry a comment pointing at the single
  grouped Gerrit change; both left open for the mirror/dependabot to close.
- [ ] AC6 (fallback): every item dropped under the STOP rule has a ticket
  comment recording the concrete failure evidence and the re-lock excluding it
  (vacuously satisfied when everything lands).
baseline.summary: Land dependabot PRs #129 + #130 as one Gerrit change (setup-uv v10 + uv-lock botocore/json-repair)

baseline.description:
Add the core built-in plan-review criterion T15 "overlay-derisk". Stack-agnostic; LLM-routed on plan content via `overlay_routing: llm`, dispatched by the review orchestrator exactly like T13/T14 (there is no ticket-tag routing). The full rubric is specified verbatim below so the artifact can be authored without resolving any other ticket.

Note on two distinct fields: the routing-entry `exec` uses the descriptor value "AGENT"; the rubric FRONT-MATTER `execution_mode` uses the prompt-loader enum value `agentic` (valid values are single_turn|agentic — "AGENT" is NOT valid front-matter and will fail the loader).

## Rubric to write verbatim into src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T15.md
YAML front-matter: `title: Overlay de-risk — prove risky mechanisms out-of-loop`, `category: plan-review-criterion`, `execution_mode: agentic`, `dimension: overlay-derisk`. `title:` is REQUIRED, not decorative: `build_descriptor` computes `name = prompt.title or cid`, so a rubric with no `title` degrades the criterion's rendered name to the bare id `T15` in both the guide header and `rebar explain T15`. AC #4 (which requires `rebar explain T15` to print the criterion name) would then pass only degenerately, and T15 would read differently from every sibling (T13 'Behavioral-prohibition consumer scan', T14 'CI-trigger / release-infrastructure coverage audit'). Body:

OVERLAY — apply only when ALL of the following hold; else PASS not-applicable.
- S1 Codified loop? the mechanism is delivered/validated by pushing through an automated pipeline or an environment/infrastructure apply, not by running or unit-testing code directly.
- S2 Slow or costly pass? one pass through that loop is slow (minutes-to-hours) or otherwise costly to run.
- S3 Runtime-only correctness? the change introduces behavior whose correctness only resolves when it actually runs in a realistic environment (boots, authenticates, connects, is authorized, passes readiness) — unreachable by static/unit checks.

When applicable, report a finding for each check not satisfied:
- (a) RISK NAMED — the plan identifies the specific mechanism(s) confirmable only by completing the full loop.
- (b) FAST OUT-OF-LOOP PROOF — for each named risk, the plan commits to proving it via the fastest feedback path available for that mechanism, outside the slow loop: running the unit locally/emulated where feasible, OR a manual experiment directly against the real target (an interactive call, a one-off CLI/console action, a probe script, a throwaway resource) where local reproduction isn't possible. The experiment is concrete and returns a verdict in minutes, not a delivery cycle. An unnamed "we'll verify" / "we'll check after deploy" does not satisfy it.
- (c) PROVE-THEN-CODIFY — the cheap experiment comes before committing the mechanism into the slow loop, so the loop validates an already-proven mechanism.
- (d) SCOPED CLEANUP — throwaway experiments are cleaned up afterward, with teardown that removes ONLY the artifacts the experiment itself created (the records a probe inserted, the scratch resource it spun up) and touches nothing pre-existing, shared, or persistent; a cleanup step that could delete, reset, or truncate a resource the experiment did not create (e.g. dropping an existing table or wiping a bucket to "reset" it) fails this check.

ANTI-FP: a manual experiment against the real target is a fully valid proof — never penalize choosing it over local reproduction; many stacks cannot be reproduced locally. A mechanism already proven elsewhere in the codebase needn't be re-proven.

## Routing entry to add to src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json (key "T15")
- `exec`: "AGENT"
- `facet`: "overlay-derisk"
- `overlay_routing`: "llm"  (orchestrator-dispatched content routing, as T13/T14)
- `applies_at`: { "suppress_types": ["bug"] }
- Posture/threshold: NOT set here — inherit the registry default (advisory). Advisory-vs-blocking is decided by the normal registry/review process, out of scope for this ticket.

## Implementation steps
1. Create src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T15.md with the front-matter (execution_mode: agentic) + body above.
2. Add the "T15" routing entry above to src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json.
3. Add "T15" to CANONICAL_LLM in src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py.
4. Regenerate the guide: `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` (updates docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md).

## Scope boundary
This ticket authors the criterion artifact + registration + regenerated guide only. Runtime routing/finder BEHAVIOR (does T15 fire on an infra plan and stay silent on an app-only plan) is proven by the eval-fixtures story 36ab-b649-b72b-4608, which depends on this ticket — not asserted here.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T15.md exists containing the S1-S3 gate, checks (a)-(d), and the ANTI-FP paragraph verbatim, with front-matter `execution_mode: agentic` and `dimension: overlay-derisk`. Verify: `python -c "import pathlib; s=pathlib.Path('src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T15.md').read_text(); assert 'execution_mode: agentic' in s and 'dimension: overlay-derisk' in s and all(k in s for k in ['S1','S2','S3','RISK NAMED','FAST OUT-OF-LOOP PROOF','PROVE-THEN-CODIFY','SCOPED CLEANUP','ANTI-FP'])"` exits 0.
- [x] Routing entry has the required field VALUES (not just the key). Verify: `python -c "import json; e=json.load(open('src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json'))['T15']; assert e['exec']=='AGENT' and e['facet']=='overlay-derisk' and e['overlay_routing']=='llm' and e['applies_at']['suppress_types']==['bug'], e"` exits 0.
- [x] `python -c "from rebar.llm.plan_review.registry import CANONICAL_LLM; assert 'T15' in CANONICAL_LLM"` exits 0.
- [x] `rebar explain T15` prints the criterion name, exec tier AGENT, facet overlay-derisk, and the rubric body (S1-S3 + checks a-d).
- [x] Registry validators pass. Verify: `python -c "from rebar.llm.plan_review.registry import check_registry_coverage, validate_packaged_routing, validate_criteria_guide; ok,missing=check_registry_coverage(); assert ok, missing; assert not validate_packaged_routing(); assert not validate_criteria_guide()"` exits 0.
- [x] The regenerated guide contains the full T15 section (heading + checks). Verify: `python -c "s=open('docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md').read(); assert '## T15' in s and all(k in s for k in ['RISK NAMED','FAST OUT-OF-LOOP PROOF','PROVE-THEN-CODIFY','SCOPED CLEANUP'])"` exits 0.
baseline.summary: Add T15 overlay-derisk criterion: rubric + routing + registry + regenerate guide

## Context

Designed under 475e-9b99-9085-4b2d (see its design comment for the full argument and Limits).

`llm/overlap/queue.py::_events_of` opens and `json.load`s EVERY matching event file, and `reduce_ticket` calls it three times per ticket. `enrich_drain.maybe_drain` calls `pending_enrichment` as its "cheap gate" on every write against a 20 ms budget (`overlap_drain_gate_budget_ms`). Measured on this repo's live tracker (3,727 ticket dirs): the gate does 11,181 `listdir` calls and 4,977 file opens per invocation, and logs `enrich drain gate check took 404.9 ms (> 20 ms budget)` on every rebar command (observed 404-654 ms). The opens term grows without bound as enrichment re-runs accumulate; the budget does not.

`digest_sidecar.latest_ticket_digest` is already bounded (sorts dirents, walks newest-first, returns on the first parseable payload) and needs no change. This ticket is the queue side only.

## Plan

Make the queue reduce read newest-first and lazily, changing no on-disk behaviour.

The event filename is `{timestamp}-{uuid}-{TYPE}.json` where the prefix is the same monotonic timestamp the reducer compares (`_store/event_append.py::event_filename`, built by `_prepare_event` from the validated event's own timestamp). Timestamps are fixed-width ns integers, so lexicographic filename order is timestamp order. Therefore:

- `_latest(dir, TYPE)` reads only the LAST matching dirent, falling back to the next-older on a
  parse failure - the same shape `latest_ticket_digest` already uses. 1 open per type per ticket.
- `claim()` arbitration needs only CLAIM events newer than the latest ENQUEUE, which are a
  contiguous suffix of the sorted names; walk newest-first and stop once a filename's timestamp
  prefix is `<=` the enqueue timestamp. Bounded by the contention window, not history.

This deletes nothing, renames nothing and writes nothing, so `docs/concurrency.md` invariant I1 and cross-clone union merges are untouched.

Also pin the implicit coupling the optimisation depends on: a test asserting that the filename timestamp prefix equals the event body's `timestamp` field for an appended event. Without it a future writer that names files differently would silently mis-reduce.

Scope note: this fixes the ASYMPTOTE (the opens term), not today's constant - `listdir` dominates at current scale, so the gate will still breach 20 ms. Do not claim the budget breach is resolved; that needs a separate lever (a store-level index, or a cheaper drain gate).

## Testing

- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py tests/unit/test_ticket_digest_store.py -q`
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py -q` (the two-clone union-merge regression from be8a0c0595 must stay green)
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint && env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `reduce_ticket` opens at most one file per event type per ticket in the no-corruption case, proven by a test that counts `open` calls against a ticket dir seeded with many ENQUEUE/CLAIM/DONE events.
- [x] `claim()` arbitration reads only CLAIM events newer than the latest ENQUEUE, proven by a test that seeds pre-enqueue CLAIM events and asserts they are not opened.
- [x] A corrupt newest event file falls back to the next-older one, proven by a test that writes invalid JSON as the newest file and asserts the reduce still resolves.
- [x] A test asserts the appended event's filename timestamp prefix equals its body `timestamp` field, pinning the ordering assumption the suffix read depends on.
- [x] Existing claim/drain semantics are unchanged: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py -q` passes.
- [x] No event file is deleted or renamed by this change, verified by the diff touching no `os.unlink`/`os.remove`/`os.rename` call.
baseline.summary: Bound the enrichment queue reduce read: newest-first suffix scan in overlap/queue.py

## Context / Problem
Most core ticket, store, read/write, config, import/export, maintenance, and gate commands parse argv imperatively. Adding docs-only argparse definitions would create the duplicate grammar RP-05 is meant to eliminate.

## Approach
Inventory every registered core grammar owned by `src/rebar/_commands/`, `src/rebar/_engine_support/`, and `src/rebar/_io/`. For each command:

1. Capture current production-path positive, negative, boundary, surplus/missing argument, option-space/equal, global-output, and `--` behavior from existing tests and focused additions.
2. Move the grammar into a side-effect-free factory using the S2a argparse contract, extracting shared argument-definition helpers where canonical and compatibility forms overlap.
3. Switch the runtime handler to parse with that same factory in the same change. Keep domain execution and initialization outside the parser module.
4. Preserve command-specific diagnostic text, stdout/stderr, and exit codes through the shared parser seam; do not accept an option merely because argparse can parse it.
5. Register the parser reference and prove only the selected parser/handler is resolved during execution.

Cover the leaf positional registry, reads/lookups/gates, create/edit/lifecycle, compaction/fsck/doctor/maintenance, config, import/export, metrics, identity-adjacent core store commands, and static reads. Split files only along existing command-family call graphs and respect module-size rules.

## Compatibility and Rollback
No help cutover occurs here. Accepted grammar and execution behavior are invariant unless this ticket records and receives approval for a specific delta. A parser family and its handler switch are one revertable unit; no stored data changes.

## Testing
Use the smallest production path crossing each parser. Pure parser tables may be unit-tested, but public oracles run real CLI subprocesses or existing interface tests and assert return code, exact relevant stream, parsed effect/persisted state, and unchanged state on refusal. Include nearest controls and verify tests run under `make test`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every registered core command runtime calls its S2a parser factory; no parallel imperative grammar remains for that command.
- [ ] Accepted/rejected argv matrices cover missing/surplus values, space/equal options, `--`, global confirmation/output extraction, and representative malformed input.
- [ ] Existing persisted effects, no-effect refusals, diagnostics, streams, and exit codes show no unapproved behavior delta.
- [ ] Parser construction imports no domain executor or optional dependency, and selected execution resolves no unrelated parser/handler.
- [ ] All touched modules meet module-size/complexity policy and each family can be reverted with its handler switch.
baseline.summary: RP-05 S2b — Migrate core command grammars to shared argparse factories
