# Model classes: trivial / standard / frontier as the universal LLM interface

## Context / Problem

rebar's gates deliberately run different model tiers per pass, but the selection is not expressible as configuration. It is INFERRED, and the inference inverts off the default provider:

- `review_kernel/verify.py:269` is `verifier_default if model == default_model else (model or
  verifier_default)`. Any model that is not the literal framework default — every Bedrock id — is
  read as an explicit operator choice, so the Pass-2/Pass-4 downgrade SILENTLY STOPS APPLYING.
- `completion.py:332` repeats the same equality test on a separate path, so the completion verifier
  loses its downgrade the same way.
- `workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` declares no `model:` on any step, so ALL FOUR of code review's
  passes take `cfg.model` and it never downgrades at all.
- `plan-review.yaml:62-65` sets `model_ladder` to BARE names (`claude-haiku-4-5`,
  `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-opus-4-8`), and `config.py:333-341` maps the prefix `claude` to
  provider `anthropic`. So on a Bedrock run the Pass-1 finders still resolve to DIRECT ANTHROPIC —
  a split-brain in the pass that does most of the work (MEASURED on a real review: 41 of 42 calls).

The root cause is one knob for four passes. `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is a single scalar, and a scalar cannot express a per-tier mapping. That is also why `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID` was deleted [rebar:281f-3336-c668-4979] — a second scalar does not help.

## Approach

Introduce THREE capability classes — `trivial`, `standard`, `frontier` — as the universal interface every rebar LLM call site resolves against. Each class is a config SLOT the operator fills with a model/provider/endpoint (and an optional fallback chain); rebar's internals reference the class, never a model id.

**Prior art (this shape is not invented).** LiteLLM's proxy config is exactly this: a `model_list` of `{model_name: <alias>, litellm_params: {model, api_base, api_key, ...}}` plus `router_settings.fallbacks` mapping alias -> [alias]. Callers reference the alias; deployment details and failover live in config. Aider solves the same problem role-wise (`--model` / `--weak-model` / `--editor-model`, with each main model carrying a default weak model). pydantic-ai supplies the runtime half but no config schema: `FallbackModel(default, *fallbacks, fallback_on=...)` takes model instances or `provider:model` strings, so rebar constructs one per class from config.

**Rebar already thinks in these tiers**, which is why the axis is right: `DEFAULT_MODEL` is the frontier model and `VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL` is documented in-code as "the decisive NON-FRONTIER model". This formalizes a distinction the code already makes implicitly.

**Alternative rejected — a second scalar (`REBAR_LLM_VERIFIER_MODEL`).** It fixes only the verifier half, leaves the Pass-1 ladder routing to Anthropic, and would be a config surface we ship and then deprecate once classes land. Rejected as knowingly short-lived.

**Alternative rejected — provider-qualifying the ladder in the gate YAML.** Most explicit, but it hard-codes one provider into the gate definition, which is exactly what makes today's ladder non-portable.

**Config shape.** The three names are SLOTS the client fills, not presets rebar ships and the client selects. Nothing requires the operator to know rebar's internal vocabulary beyond the three slot names:

    [tool.rebar.llm.frontier]
    model = "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8"
    provider = "bedrock"

    [[tool.rebar.llm.trivial.fallback]]
    model = "us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5"
    provider = "bedrock"

Secrets are NOT part of this structure. rebar's config layer deliberately keeps API keys env-only (`config.py:388-398` states secrets are not config-file keys); LiteLLM puts `api_key` inline in `litellm_params` and rebar must not copy that.

**Config discovery is unchanged**, with one addition: `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` names a file that LAYERS over the discovered config (pyproject `[tool.rebar.llm]` / `rebar.toml` / XDG). It layers rather than replaces so an environment overriding one key does not have to restate the whole config — duplication is the likelier source of drift than precedence subtlety. No new discovery path is invented; the pointer IS the escape hatch.

**The merge is DEEP over tables and REPLACING over arrays.** This is the decision, not a preference:

- **Tables merge recursively, leaf key wins.** Setting only `frontier.model` in the pointed-to file
  keeps the discovered `frontier.provider`, `frontier.endpoint` and `frontier.fallback`. Anything
  shallower defeats the stated purpose — a table-level replace would force CI to restate an entire
  class slot to change one field, which IS the duplication this pointer exists to avoid.
- **Arrays are replaced wholesale, never appended.** A `fallback` chain in the pointed-to file
  REPLACES the discovered chain; `fallback = []` explicitly disables fallbacks. Appending is
  rejected because a chain that can only grow can never be shortened, reordered, or cleared by an
  environment — CI could not pin "no fallback, fail loudly" over a project default.
- **Precedence, unchanged in shape:** CLI `-c` > env > `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` > discovered config
  file > built-in default. The pointer slots directly above the discovered file. Secrets stay
  env-only at every layer.

**This does NOT change `read_reserved_section`.** That helper's `merged.update(sub)` (`config.py:588-600`) is a SHALLOW merge shared by every reserved section, and deepening it would silently alter layering for unrelated consumers. The deep merge is implemented in the llm config resolver over the section dict it receives, leaving the shared helper's contract untouched. Any child that finds itself editing `read_reserved_section` has mis-scoped the change.

**`REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is DEPRECATED with a migration window** rather than kept as a permanent alias. There are few clients today and a single-scalar knob alongside a class model is precisely the ambiguity this work removes.

## Scope

This parent's contract, delivered by its children:

- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — the three class slots, their parsing from the existing layered config,
  and the class resolver.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` / `_config_sources.py` — the `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` pointer and its
  per-key layering.
- `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py`, `src/rebar/llm/completion.py`,
  `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` — the three verifier paths resolve `standard`
  instead of inferring from an equality test.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml` and the batch runners — the Pass-1 ladder is
  expressed in classes, not bare model names.
- `src/rebar/llm/` — per-class fallback chains constructed as pydantic-ai `FallbackModel`.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py`, `docs/` — the `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` deprecation, an ADR, and example configs
  per provider.

## Testing

Unit tier for resolution and layering (pure config, no model calls); contract tier for the gate paths (the observable is which model id each pass resolves to); and one live [operator-attested] run for the end-to-end claim. Per-child tiers are stated on each child.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] every child ticket is closed
- [ ] a test asserts the pointed-to file DEEP-merges tables: a file setting only `frontier.model`
      over a discovered config carrying `frontier.provider` + a `frontier.fallback` chain yields the
      overridden model AND the discovered provider and fallback chain (the shallow-merge failure
      mode drops them, so this test fails against `dict.update` semantics)
- [ ] a test asserts arrays REPLACE rather than append: a `fallback` chain in the pointed-to file
      yields exactly that chain, and `fallback = []` yields no fallbacks
- [ ] a test asserts `read_reserved_section`'s own shallow-merge behaviour is UNCHANGED for a
      non-llm reserved section, so the deep merge did not leak into shared config machinery
- [ ] a test asserts each of the three verifier paths (plan-review Pass-2/Pass-4, completion) resolves
      the `standard` class rather than inferring from an equality against the framework default
- [ ] a test asserts no bare `claude-*` id resolves to provider `anthropic` during a run whose classes
      are configured for another provider
- [ ] [operator-attested] a real gate run with classes configured across two providers records the
      per-pass model ids actually used, cited from the run's usage log in a comment
baseline.summary: Model classes: trivial/standard/frontier as the universal LLM interface

baseline.description:
# S8 — Cut the production review bot over to Bedrock Claude (dogfood, no cross-provider fallback)

## Context / Problem

The `LLM-Review` vote gates every landing on `main`, and today it runs against the direct Anthropic API. The epic's premise is that our clients will predominantly reach Claude through Bedrock, so the path rebar develops against is not the path rebar's users run; dogfooding closes that gap. State the premise honestly: it is an asserted product judgement, not a measured one — no survey or citation backs it anywhere in the epic. What IS measurable is the consequence: if Bedrock throttles, mis-caches, or returns differently shaped structured output, we find out on our own repo before a client does.

This ticket was written early in epic 061c and its original Scope and Approach have been overtaken by the epic's own deliverables. The rewrite below replaces them. What changed:

* the per-pass model split it worried about **now exists in code**, so the cutover is a configuration
  act rather than a design problem;
* the single `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` knob it named is **deprecated** [rebar:eb58-e71d-ec90-4b00] and cannot
  express a per-class mapping, so it is no longer the instrument;
* the `observability.sh` alarm it listed as a deliverable **already shipped** under S4b;
* the Anthropic-key retirement it promised is **not expressible** against the current `.env` layout
  and would break the kill switch it also promises.

## What is already established — do NOT re-measure or re-build

* **The per-pass class split has LANDED.** `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` now
  declares `base: model: frontier` (:74), `round_a`/`round_b`: `model_ladder: [frontier]` (:92, :130),
  `verify: model: standard` (:174) and `coach: model: standard` (:209); `plan-review.yaml` Pass-1 is
  `model_ladder: [frontier]` (:70-71) and the verifier paths resolve `standard`
  [rebar:172e-b207-4c18-4243, rebar:77ed-dea1-4997-4f74, rebar:7761-4b1a-e8c3-45a0,
  rebar:3768-789c-11ed-48be, rebar:cc33-13db-de48-4468]. The gate no longer reads a single
  `cfg.model` for all four passes. **The obsolete-plan hazard is therefore inverted from what this
  ticket used to say: the risk is no longer "one knob for four passes", it is choosing an instrument
  that COLLAPSES the split that now exists.**
* **No bare `claude-*` id survives on either gate's executed path.** The only remaining bare ids under
  `src/rebar/llm/workflow/` are `examples/review_skeleton.yaml:44` (an example, never executed by the
  bot) and JSX placeholders in `editor_assets/`. The split-brain this ticket previously warned about
  is closed.
* **Escalation no longer crosses providers.** `plan_review/sizing.py:400` `models_at_or_above` maps
  every at-or-above rung through its model class via `_rung_target`, which drops a rung it cannot name
  in the run's provider [rebar:7761-4b1a-e8c3-45a0]. A Bedrock-configured run escalates to Bedrock.
* **`pydantic_ai.exceptions.UserError` is now caught** (`src/rebar/llm/failure.py:250,271`), so a
  Bedrock client-construction failure reaches rebar's typed failure path instead of escaping every
  `except LLMError` handler [rebar:a574-7193-6a5b-48e9].
* **Both region variables are ALREADY SET in the review-bot service.**
  `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:151` `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION: "us-east-1"` and `:157`
  `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: "us-east-1"`. They are NOT interchangeable and both are required: rebar's own
  knob threads into `BedrockProvider` while botocore reads only `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`
  (`AWS_REGION` alone does not work on boto3/botocore 1.43.58), and IMDS supplies credentials but never
  a region [rebar:a574-7193-6a5b-48e9]. Verify, do not re-derive.
* **IAM is granted and exercised.** `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf` grants `bedrock:InvokeModel` +
  `InvokeModelWithResponseStream` on `*.anthropic.claude-*` inference profiles, scoped to the instance
  role, verified by a real call rather than the policy simulator
  [rebar:9249-1569-7be9-4f67].
* **The VOTER_ERROR alarm chain already exists and is live.** `review_bot/voter.py` `_voter_error()`
  writes a greppable line to journald; `infra/scripts/observability.sh` §4 (:113, :135) publishes
  `rebar/host:voter_errors`; `infra/terraform/monitoring_s4b.tf` declares
  `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.voter_errors` = `rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` (`period = 300`,
  `evaluation_periods = 1`, `threshold = 0`, :48-54); `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md:110` documents
  reading it. `describe-alarms` returns `StateValue: OK` with a fresh datapoint. **Nothing in
  `observability.sh` is a deliverable of this story** — an implementer who takes the old Scope at face
  value will rebuild it and may double-publish the metric.
* **Only INFERENCE PROFILES are invokable**, and caching works on them. Plain on-demand
  `anthropic.claude-*` ids return `ValidationException: … on-demand throughput isn't supported`;
  `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` measured `cache_write=4017` then read on the next attempt
  [rebar:2932-8a98-6d70-4550]. The verified id triple is checked in at
  `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml`.
* **All three local gates already run clean on Bedrock** — `review-plan` (27/27 Bedrock calls,
  `cache_read` 226,668), `review-code` (5/5 Bedrock, `cache_read` 18,292), `verify-completion`
  (1/1 Bedrock, `cache_read` 45,122), all with structured output validating and zero direct-Anthropic
  calls [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7]. This cutover is a confirmation, not a first contact.
* **The parity bar is cleared as the epic defines it** [rebar:0d76-ebbf-ee3a-48ac]: same payloads,
  same tools, provider-clean routing, both inference profiles invoke. The operator hold recorded on
  this ticket ("DO NOT claim until 0d76 records a cleared bar") is therefore RELEASED. Carry the
  nuance: the residual `gating_failures` are informational cross-model verdict comparisons, so the
  slots read `passed=False` while no acceptance criterion is unmet.

## Approach

Fill the review-bot's **model-class slots** with Bedrock inference-profile ids, in the service's own `environment:` block in `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`:

```yaml
      REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL: "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8"
      REBAR_LLM_STANDARD_MODEL: "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"
      REBAR_LLM_TRIVIAL_MODEL:  "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0"
```

These are the literal names in `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:105-115`. Because the gates name classes rather than model ids, filling the slots re-points Pass-1 onto the Bedrock opus profile and Pass-2/Pass-4 onto the Bedrock sonnet profile in one act, preserving the split that [rebar:77ed-dea1-4997-4f74] restored and the standing operator rule behind it (standard is the default for verification/judging; frontier needs justification). No `src/` change is expected. The ids are copied from `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml` so there is exactly one authoritative triple, and a test pins the two together so they cannot drift.

**The cutover is purely ADDITIVE and the kill switch is purely SUBTRACTIVE.** `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` appears nowhere under `infra/` today (verified: `grep -rn REBAR_LLM_MODEL infra/` returns nothing), so the bot currently runs on the built-in class defaults, which resolve to `anthropic:claude-*`. Deleting the three lines above and recreating the container therefore restores the Anthropic path with no other edit — the exact both-directions revert already proven token-free in [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7] AC7.

**THE IMAGE DOES NOT INSTALL THE BEDROCK PROVIDER PACKAGE — a second, non-config deliverable.** `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot:83` is `RUN uv sync --locked --no-dev --extra agents --extra reviewbot`, and `bedrock` is a **distinct extra** that is not in that list (`pyproject.toml:133-135`, `bedrock = ["pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]>=1,<2"]`). `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:60-66` imports `pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock` and raises `LLMConfigError` when it is absent, so — with no cross-provider fallback, deliberately — the class-slot flip ALONE would make the first Bedrock call fail and the `LLM-Review` gate would stop voting on every landing on `main`. The fix is one flag: add `--extra bedrock` to that `uv sync`.

*The gap is PARTIALLY masked, which is what defeats the obvious probe.* `pyproject.toml:93` is `reviewbot = ["fastapi", "uvicorn[standard]", "boto3"]`, so the container ALREADY has boto3, and both region vars and IMDS credentials are already in place. Any probe of the form "can this container reach Bedrock with boto3?" — including the boto3 region resolution that the provider builder itself pre-checks at `bedrock_model.py:76-79` — therefore SUCCEEDS on an image that still lacks the provider module. The dependency is partially satisfied, so the container reads as healthy right up to the first gate call. The pre-cutover check must probe the IMPORT, not AWS reachability.

*Why this was invisible:* [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7] proved all three gates clean on Bedrock (33 calls, zero direct-Anthropic) — but LOCALLY, in a dev env whose `[dev]` extra resolves `pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,bedrock,openai,retries]`. A local proof cannot see a container packaging gap.

*The lockfile does NOT need regenerating — checked, not assumed.* `uv.lock` already carries the bedrock extra fully resolved: the `nava-rebar` entry has `bedrock = [{ name = "pydantic-ai-slim", extra = ["bedrock"] }]`, and `pydantic-ai-slim` 1.107.1's own `bedrock` extra resolves to `boto3==1.43.62`, already locked. `uv lock --check` passes against the committed lock, and `uv sync --locked --no-dev --extra agents --extra reviewbot --extra bedrock --dry-run` resolves with no drift complaint — so `--locked` is satisfied by the existing lock and no `uv lock` regeneration is part of this story. One adjacency worth knowing: `uv.lock`'s `[conflicts]` declares `bedrock` mutually exclusive with `eval` (and `dev` with `eval`); the image installs neither `eval` nor `dev`, so adding `--extra bedrock` does not trip it.

**THE ANTHROPIC CREDENTIAL IS RETAINED. This story retires the DEFAULT USE, not the credential.** `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` is **out of scope and unchanged**, for two independent reasons:

1. *The kill switch needs it.* A recovery path that flips back to Anthropic without a key is a no-op,
   and it would be discovered at exactly the wrong moment. The credential must outlive the cutover.
2. *It is not per-container in the first place.* `fetch-secrets.sh:81` reads `anthropic-api-key` as a
   REQUIRED param and :116 writes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=` into ONE shared `.env`, which is `env_file` for
   both `review-bot` (docker-compose.yml:113-114) and `opcert` (:196-197); opcert consumes it for its
   own gate LLM ops (:193). "Retire the key for this container" is not expressible against that layout,
   and deleting the line breaks opcert.

So the post-cutover container still carries `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, deliberately, unused. The old acceptance criterion asserting the container env contains **no** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is **withdrawn**: it contradicted the kill switch, and it was the wrong oracle anyway. The property actually worth proving is positive and measurable — that no call on the Bedrock path reaches Anthropic — and `REBAR_USAGE_LOG`'s per-call tally proves it directly, as it did for all three local gates.

**No cross-provider fallback**, unchanged from the original plan and still the right call: a `FallbackModel` to direct Anthropic would mask exactly the failures this cutover exists to surface, and a persistently degraded Bedrock could run unnoticed behind it. Note the asymmetry that makes this coherent rather than dogmatic: the INTRA-provider fallback chain accepted in [rebar:cc33-13db-de48-4468] (`model_classes.py:388`) stays available; it is only the cross-provider hop that is refused.

**The transient-fault posture on Bedrock, stated accurately.** The original plan claimed "the existing tenacity transport retry absorbs transient faults". That is false on this path. `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:88` is `return BedrockProvider(region_name=region)` and its docstring says so explicitly: "No custom client/transport is opened here (unlike the retrying Anthropic path)". There is no `botocore.config.Config(retries=…)`, no `"adaptive"` mode and no `aws_read_timeout` anywhere in `src/rebar/llm/` — the tenacity envelope and `RetryConfig` live only in `anthropic_model.py:114-150`. So:

* Bedrock's transient-fault handling is **botocore's stock client defaults**, which do retry throttling
  and transient 5xx, but are NOT configured by rebar and are NOT driven by `llm_retry_max_attempts` or
  `timeout_s`.
* The epic's "first_class = full fidelity ⇒ equivalent retry and timeout per transport" is an **unmet
  intention, not a landed property**. This story does not claim it and does not fix it: closing it means
  changing the provider builder, which belongs in a `src/` ticket rather than inside a production
  cutover. It is filed as its own defect, linked `discovered_from` this ticket, and the posture is
  written into the runbook so an operator debugging a throttle is not looking for a retry envelope that
  does not exist.
* Related honesty correction: inference profiles are **not** a throttling mitigation, which is how the
  original Approach justified them. Zero throttle events were observed across ~1,400 parity requests,
  the 33 local gate calls, and a 19-call plan-review. The evidenced reason is simpler and stronger —
  on-demand ids are not invokable at all [rebar:2932-8a98-6d70-4550].

**Provenance oracle: `e951` is a hard prerequisite.** [rebar:343b-4fdc-6722-469b] delivered `provider_provenance` for the plan-review and completion gates only. The code-review gate — the one that produces the `LLM-Review` vote — still does not stamp it: `code_review/finalize.py:245` sets `model` and nothing sets `provenance`, while `code_review/sidecar.py:106` reads `verdict.get("provider_provenance")` and gets `None`. [rebar:e951-7df6-1851-4d5e] fixes exactly this and is already implemented and pushed as Gerrit change 1307, so depending on it is cheap. The `provider == "bedrock"` criterion below is gated on e951 landing; the `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` tally is an independent second observation that does not depend on it, so the cutover is not un-evidenced if e951 slips.

**Alternatives rejected**

* **`REBAR_LLM_MODEL` re-pointed at a Bedrock id** — the original plan's instrument. Rejected on three
  independent grounds: it is deprecated with a migration window [rebar:eb58-e71d-ec90-4b00,
  rebar:d23e-1012-6749-4181], its deprecation shim fans a single value out to ALL THREE classes, which
  collapses the Pass-1/Pass-2 split back into one model, and a scalar cannot express a per-class mapping
  at all. Concretely: sonnet-everywhere silently downgrades the Pass-1 finder; opus-everywhere loses the
  Pass-2 cost downgrade and renders the `temperature: 0` greedy pin at `code-review.yaml:185`
  inoperative, since Bedrock opus accepts only the default temperature. Both single-model outcomes are
  wrong, in opposite directions. A runbook naming it would also rot at v1.0.0.
* **`REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` pointed at `/app/.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml`** — genuinely
  attractive: it is the instrument [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7] proved end-to-end, it is what the CI
  provider matrix uses, and it makes the id triple single-sourced by construction. Rejected for the
  container specifically. The file is present in the image only incidentally —
  `Dockerfile.reviewbot:82` is `COPY . /app` and `.dockerignore` happens not to exclude `.github` — so a
  future context-trimming change would delete it and the pointer would fail at gate time in production,
  after the deploy that caused it. Env class slots also OUTRANK the file pointer in the precedence order
  (CLI > env > `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` > discovered file > default), so keeping both layers live invites
  two configurations that silently disagree. The single-sourcing benefit is recovered by the drift test
  instead of by indirection.
* **Per-service Anthropic key retirement via a `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ""` override in the review-bot
  `environment:` block** — technically expressible (compose `environment:` outranks `env_file`), and it
  would satisfy the old "no Anthropic credential in this container" criterion without touching opcert.
  Rejected because it disables the kill switch for the sake of a criterion we have withdrawn, and buys
  nothing: the credential is unused either way, and "unused" is what the usage-log tally proves.

## Scope

- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` — the three class-slot env vars in the `review-bot` service's
  `environment:` block, AND `REBAR_USAGE_LOG`. Region vars are already present and are not re-added.
  The usage-log var is IN SCOPE because THIS TICKET'S OWN acceptance criteria require a
  `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` per-call tally proving every call reached a Bedrock profile and none reached
  Anthropic — and that was unsatisfiable as written: recording is OPT-IN (`usage_log.record()` is
  a no-op with the var unset) and the var was set NOWHERE under `infra/`, so this container had
  never written a usage log. The Approach anticipates the need ("Write the usage log to a durable
  path outside the job workspace") without ever saying to enable it. So the earlier, narrower
  wording contradicted this ticket's own criteria; the scope-intent finding on change 1327 caught
  exactly that seam and this is the correction. The path sits on the bind-backed volume because
  auto-deploy recreates the container.
- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot` — add `--extra bedrock` to the `uv sync --locked` line (:83),
  so the image contains `pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock`. No `uv.lock` edit accompanies it (see
  Approach: the lock already resolves that extra and `--locked` is already satisfied).
- `infra/terraform/` — a Bedrock `InvokeModel` client-error alarm built on AWS/Bedrock NATIVE metrics via
  a `metric_query` metric-math expression, NOT a host-published custom metric. MEASURED in this account:
  the `AWS/Bedrock` namespace already publishes `InvocationClientErrors` and `Invocations`, dimensioned by
  `ModelId` (values include `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` from this epic's own traffic), so the rate is
  computable as `InvocationClientErrors / Invocations` with no publisher to add. THIS IS WHY
  `observability.sh` STAYS OUT OF SCOPE: the alternative — a `rebar/host` custom metric — would require a
  new publisher there and would re-open a scope claim this plan deliberately makes. It also means the
  DIMENSIONLESS-ON-BOTH-SIDES contract that `monitoring_s4b.tf` and `monitoring_s5.tf` document does not
  apply here: those are host-published custom metrics, whereas a native metric is dimensioned by AWS and
  the alarm must MATCH that dimensioning (`ModelId`) rather than avoid it. State the dimension explicitly
  in the resource so it cannot silently stop matching.
  This is the one signal the existing
  `rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` alarm cannot give: `voter_errors` fires only when the gate fails to vote
  at all, so a partially degraded Bedrock that still produces votes is invisible to it. Thresholds per
  the epic's criterion (client-error rate > 25% of invocations over a 15-minute window, 2 consecutive
  periods), with the alarm ARN and a forced test notification recorded on this ticket — the evidence
  gap the epic's AC has been carrying unresolved.
- `infra/runbooks/` — the kill-switch entry (class slots, not `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`), stating that the
  Anthropic credential is retained by design and why, and recording the actual Bedrock retry/timeout
  posture.
- a test pinning the compose class-slot values to `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml`.
- **NOT in scope:** `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` (see Approach), `infra/scripts/observability.sh`
  (already shipped under S4b), and any `src/rebar/llm/` change — including the botocore retry/timeout
  parity gap, which is filed separately.

## Testing

Live end-to-end, because this is a cutover of a production gate: the oracle is a real vote on a real change, not a local invocation. The drift test is the only unit-tier item.

- **container packaging, pre-cutover:** rebuild the review-bot image from the amended
  `Dockerfile.reviewbot` and run
  `docker compose exec review-bot python -c "import pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock"`, capturing the exit
  status and output. This runs BEFORE the class slots are set, so a missing provider package surfaces as
  a build-time finding rather than as a gate outage. What is probed is the IMPORT; a boto3/AWS
  reachability probe is not a substitute (see Approach).
- **safety net, pre-cutover:** induce a real `VOTER_ERROR` on the CURRENT Anthropic path and observe
  `rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` transition `OK → ALARM`. Access for this is confirmed (CloudWatch read
  plus SSM to the prod host). Design caveat: per [rebar:c943-1b38-d613-4013] a 409 "change is closed"
  deliberately does NOT emit `VOTER_ERROR`,  … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: S8 — cut the production review bot over to Bedrock Claude (dogfood, no fallback)

# Reduce the import-cycle SCC (facade-read reroute — parts 1 & 2 landed; this ticket now = part 3 / item 9.3)

## Context
A verified AST+Tarjan analysis found a large strongly-connected import component spanning the
facade, `_commands`, `signing`, and most of `llm`, held together by function-local lazy imports.
Layering was enforced only by docstrings. Three remediations were approved. **Two have already
shipped to `main`; this ticket now tracks ONLY the remaining part 3 (item 9.3).** The live baseline
(`.import-cycle-baseline.json`) records the current surface: `largest_scc_size = 36`,
11 cross-package cycle pairs, 49 modules-in-cycles. (The original "~69-module" figure predated the
part-1/part-2 landings; 36 is the current truth.)

## What
1. **[DONE — change 208]** Import-cycle CI strangler contract: `scripts/check_import_cycles.py` +
   `.import-cycle-baseline.json` + CI wiring (`.github/workflows/test.yml`) + `tests/unit/
   test_import_cycles.py`. Freezes the surface; fails only NEW cross-package cycles.

   the leaf `src/rebar/_ids.py`; `_engine_support/resolver.py` re-exports it; `reducer/_processors.py`
   imports from `rebar._ids` (no longer UP into `_engine_support`). Guarded by

   and make `rebar._reads` itself a leaf so the reroute measurably shrinks the SCC.

## Item 9.3 — concrete scope (grimp-verified in worktree janitor/item-9.3-facade-reads)

  `from rebar import RebarError` (line 45); `from rebar import config` is a submodule edge

- **Make `_reads` a leaf:** move `RebarError` + `ConcurrencyError` into a new stdlib-only leaf

- **Out of scope:** the larger 36→18 collapse needs routing WRITES through a leaf too — not a
  reads-only change; not attempted here.

- [x] Import-cycle CI contract in place; passes current state, fails a new cross-package cycle (change 208).
- [x] `reducer` no longer imports `_engine_support`; shared resolution in the leaf `rebar._ids`; reducer/replay tests green (change 205).
- [ ] `rebar._reads` no longer imports the `rebar` facade (`RebarError` sourced from the new leaf `rebar._errors`); `rebar._reads` is OUT of the largest SCC.

# Bridge publish fails on rejected refs: a GitHub 500 is misread as a stolen lease

## Premise correction (read first)

The original report described the witness failure as "a stale `--force-with-lease` expectation". **The raw run log disproves that.** It was never a stale lease — it was a GitHub **server-side error** that rebar's CAS classifier mistook for lease movement.

## Evidence

### Fault 1 — witness publication (run 31455622724, 2026-08-11T03:30Z)

```
WARNING rebar_reconciler._ref_lock: ref-lock: push to origin refs/reconciler/last-pass
  (expected oid 22cd71bd...) classified as CAS mismatch (lease moved) —
  stderr: remote: fatal error in commit_refs
 ! [remote rejected] 1e5caeb7... -> refs/reconciler/last-pass (failure)
WARNING rebar_reconciler._ref_lock: ref-lock: git push to origin refs/reconciler/last-pass
  failed (exit 1) — fail-closed: remote: Internal Server Error
ERROR: cannot publish reconciler last-pass witness: Command '[... --force-with-lease ...]'
```

Attempt 1 was `remote: fatal error in commit_refs` + `! [remote rejected] ... (failure)`. `_is_cas_mismatch_stderr` in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py` matched the broad `rejected` marker, found nothing in `_NON_CAS_REJECT_MARKERS`, and therefore reported **"classified as CAS mismatch (lease moved)"** — a false claim that another process stole the lease. Attempt 2 returned `Internal Server Error`, which *is* in the marker list, so it correctly fell through to fail-closed and killed the pass.

This is exactly the failure shape bug 4afc's subtractive classifier exists to prevent; the marker list simply does not know GitHub's `fatal error in commit_refs` or the bare `(failure)` ref-status. Misclassification is not cosmetic: a "stolen lease" verdict is a statement about **concurrency** that operators use to reason about racing passes.

### Fault 2 — tickets-branch delivery (run 31244501098, 2026-08-08T06:41Z)

```
final-push-rejected: To https://github.com/navapbc/rebar
 ! [remote rejected] HEAD -> tickets (cannot lock ref 'refs/heads/tickets':
   is at e45f61a9... but expected 9ecaaa40...)
 (6 unpushed commits on origin/tickets..HEAD)
```

This one **is** a genuine lost CAS race, and it *was* retried — `cannot lock ref` is correctly classified retriable, so the loop spent its budget. It still lost every time, because `src/rebar/_store/push.py` has **no backoff anywhere**: the retries fire back-to-back and keep colliding with the same concurrent `tickets` writer. Under the continuous-loop cadence this contention is routine.

## Plan

1. In `_ref_lock.py`, extend `_NON_CAS_REJECT_MARKERS` with the observed server-side
   failure signatures (`fatal error in commit_refs`, and the generic `(failure)`
   ref-status) so a server fault can no longer be reported as lease movement. Keep the
   subtractive shape and the fail-closed default: `stale info` stays conclusive for a
   genuine lease move, and ambiguity still fails closed.
2. In `push.py`, spend backoff between non-fast-forward / CAS retries, reusing the
   injectable backoff seam added for `subzero-locustal-junebug` (this change stacks on
   it), so a lost `cannot lock ref` race gets a real chance to converge instead of
   re-colliding immediately.

**Constraint that shapes step 1:** `_ref_lock.py` sits at exactly the repo's 800-LOC hard cap, so the markers are appended in a single `+=` statement (with the tuple annotated `tuple[str, ...]`) rather than added inline with a comment block. The file stays at the cap. A proper split of that module along a call-graph seam is owed but is deliberately NOT bundled into this bug fix — it is a refactor with its own risk profile (the reconciler loads siblings through a custom loader, and existing tests bind to module identity and logger names).

## Deliberate non-change (and why)

The ticket also asks "whether the last-pass witness failure should be fatal at all (it is a witness, not the payload)". **This change does NOT downgrade it.** Witness fatality is the fail-loud contract described in `docs/adr/0094-reconciler-last-pass-two-witness-status.md`, and the heartbeat canary is the downstream detector that depends on it; relaxing it is a user-visible alerting change, not a reliability fix, and belongs in its own ticket with an ADR amendment. This change fixes the **mechanism** that produced the failure (a misclassified server error, and unbacked-off retries) while leaving the contract intact.

## Scope / non-goals

- No change to `_is_cas_mismatch_stderr`'s subtractive shape, to the `stale info`
  conclusive marker, or to the fail-closed default.
- No change to `finalize_process`'s return contract in `last_pass.py`.
- No change to the CAS retry COUNT anywhere (`_MAX_RETRIES = 5`; the witness's 3 attempts).
- No new secrets, credentials, permissions, or infrastructure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1: A test proves the exact run-31455622724 stderr (`remote: fatal error in
  commit_refs` with `! [remote rejected] ... (failure)`) is **not** classified as a CAS
  mismatch, i.e. it is no longer reported as a stolen lease.
- [x] AC2: A test proves a genuine lease move (`stale info`) is **still** classified as a
  CAS mismatch — the bug 4afc contract is not weakened by the new markers.
- [x] AC3: A test proves the existing non-CAS markers (`hook declined`,
  `internal server error`, `rate limit`, `file exists`) still classify as non-CAS.
- [x] AC7: `_ref_lock.py` stays within the 800-LOC hard cap (the module-size gate is
  green), and the complexity ratchet reports no new debt.
- [x] AC4: A test proves a `cannot lock ref … is at X but expected Y` rejection sleeps
  between retry attempts (via the injected sleep seam) rather than retrying back-to-back,
  and that the number of push attempts is unchanged.
- [x] AC5: The existing ref-lock classification suite
  (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_ref_lock_push_classification.py`) and the push
  contract suite pass unchanged.
- [x] AC6: `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
baseline.summary: Reconcile Bridge delivery fails on rejected ref pushes (stale force-with-lease + lost tickets race)

baseline.description:
Own the **remediation-mode GATE**: the freshness-window + precondition check that decides
whether a re-review runs in floored (remediation) mode or as a normal full review, and wire
it parallel to `drift_refresh` in `_run_plan_review`. (This is the task-4 candidate-check; the
Pass-3 drop math it gates is task cc5b. Body/title were previously swapped with task 3689 —
this restores the epic's 6-task decomposition.)

## Preconditions (ALL required, else byte-identical full review)

- config enabled (`remediation_mode` key; see rollout note below)
- plan changed since the prior review
- **code UNCHANGED since baseline** — detected deterministically by comparing the gate's
  attested `verified_at_sha` (the origin/main snapshot SHA the gate signs into the prior
  review's manifest) against the current run's `verified_at_sha`. Equal ⇒ code unchanged;
  differ ⇒ code drifted. This reuses the already-signed snapshot ref — no new diff machinery.
- registry unchanged (criteria-routing material fingerprint equal to the prior review's)
- a prior `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar WITH finding text is available (task e344)
- the last review of ANY kind (full or partial) is within the window (default 60 min),
  measured from that last review and **reset on each review** so the loop persists across a
  series of edits and lapses to a normal full review only after the agent goes idle.

Code-changed / both-drifted → full review (`drift_refresh` path byte-unchanged, out of scope).

## Rollout (resolves the default-on advisory)

The `remediation_mode` config key ships **default-OFF** for one release (expand-contract:
ship off → validate on the dogfood corpus → flip the default on in a follow-up), so existing
consumers do not silently get a narrowed verdict on upgrade. Setting the key off (or absent)
restores byte-identical full-review behavior at any time — the back-out.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Candidate check enforces ALL preconditions; any failure → full review (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py`, `attest.py`)
- [ ] `remediation_mode` config key (default-OFF for v1) + window minutes (default 60) in `src/rebar/config.py`; key off/absent → byte-identical full review
- [ ] "code unchanged" is the `verified_at_sha` equality check (prior manifest vs current run); registry-unchanged is the routing material-fingerprint equality check
- [ ] Window measured from the last review of any kind, reset on each review
- [ ] both-drifted → full review; `drift_refresh` path byte-unchanged
- [ ] Wiring is parallel to `drift_refresh` in `_run_plan_review`; the Pass-3 drop math itself lives in cc5b (this task only decides remediation-mode eligibility)
baseline.summary: Remediation-mode gate: freshness window + preconditions + wiring

baseline.description:
# A tracker re-clone silently re-identifies the environment, invalidating every attestation

`.env-id` is git-ignored local state (tracker `.gitignore` lines 1, 13, 14 cover `.env-id`, `.opcert-key`, `.opcert-key.pub`) that is STAMPED INTO EVERY EVENT and is the `principal` of every op-cert attestation. Re-cloning the tracker without carrying it over mints a NEW environment identity, and every attestation signed by the old one becomes unverifiable.

## Context / Problem

Operators re-clone or rebuild the tickets tracker (this happened on 2026-08-09 while remediating bug 2fa6). A fresh clone carries the events but not the git-ignored local state, so `.env-id` is absent and rebar mints a new uuid with no signal at all. Hours later the claim gate reports `verdict: foreign_key` on a ticket that had already earned an attestation, and it reads as a per-ticket problem when it is store-wide. The prior session's handoff note warned about this in capitals and the operator still hit it, which is the argument for a mechanical signal at the moment of the act rather than more documentation.

## Observed

`.env-id` was regenerated at 20:39 (`b8a354e0-…`, replacing `ade0f2ef-…`) and a new `.opcert-key` at 20:50. Store scan: 2498 ticket directories carry material referencing the OLD env id, 7 carry both, 4 carry only the new one.

    rebar review-plan b2bb-fa81-e054-4fb5 --status
    verdict: foreign_key — "op-cert signed by a different environment
    (principal 'ade0f2ef-…'; this environment is 'b8a354e0-…')"

## Confirmed root cause

`rebar._commands.init._ensure_env_id_unit` (the `env-id` ensure-registry unit, run from every init entry point, the MCP boot path and `fsck --repair`) and `init._gen_local_files` both mint a fresh uuid whenever `.env-id` is absent, with NO check for whether the store already holds events written by a different environment. Event files carry the writing environment at the top level (`env_id`), so the prior identity IS discoverable on disk — nothing consults it.

## Why 'just accept both env ids' does NOT fix it

Verifying a signature made by the old environment needs THAT environment's op-cert public key, which is git-ignored, was never committed, and is gone. An accept-list would only move the failure from `foreign_key` to `mismatch`; making it PASS would mean accepting the principal WITHOUT verifying the signature, which defeats the gate. Publishing per-environment public keys is the principled fix and is OUT OF SCOPE — a trust-model change needing its own ADR (operator decision 2026-08-12). Full analysis in the comments.

## Approach

Operator decision (2026-08-12, B7): **warn loudly with an explicit override — do not refuse outright, do not silently migrate identities.**

1. Extract the environment-identity concern into a new leaf module
   `src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py`: read/mint, the bounded scan for env ids already in the
   store, the override, the warning text, the relocated `env-id` ensure unit, and the
   divergence report. A new module because `init.py` is already at the module-size cap.
2. Minting into a populated store WARNS loudly on stderr — naming the prior env id(s), the
   attestation consequence, and the git-ignored state to carry over — and still completes.
   It warns rather than refuses because a second clone mounting a shared tickets branch is a
   first-class workflow that legitimately needs its own identity, and the store cannot tell
   that from a re-clone; only the operator can.
3. `REBAR_ALLOW_ENV_REIDENTIFY=1` acknowledges it and quietens the warning. An env var, not a
   CLI flag, because the mint happens inside the ensure registry, which runs from the CLI, the
   MCP boot path and the library alike.
4. `rebar fsck` gains a counted `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` check, scoped by AUTHOR (this environment's
   own author also writing under another env id) so it does not fire on the healthy
   multi-clone topology. It reuses the pairs the authorship tally already collects.
5. Document the re-clone carry-over list and what breaks per file.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py` (new) — env-id read/mint/scan, override, warning text,
  divergence report, and the relocated `env-id` ensure unit.
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` — `_ensure_env_id_unit` moves out; `_gen_local_files` delegates
  its `.env-id` mint to the new module (net LOC decreases, keeping the module under the cap).
- `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py` — `_registry()` maps `env-id` to the relocated unit.
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py` — collect event `env_id`s during check 1 and emit the counted
  `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` line.
- `docs/concurrency.md` — the re-clone carry-over list (`.env-id`, `.opcert-key`,
  `.opcert-key.pub`, `.ensure-applied`) and what breaks per file.
- `tests/` — new tests for the guard, the override, and the fsck check.

Nothing else changes. Ticket history is NOT rewritten: events are append-only and correctly stamped with the environment that actually wrote them. No `.env-id` restoration and no identity migration.

## Testing

- Happy path: a store with events all carrying the CURRENT env id runs the ensure unit as `ok`
  and produces no `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` line from fsck.
- Guard path (held-out): a tracker with existing events stamped `E1` and NO `.env-id` — the
  ensure unit does not write `.env-id`, returns a non-`ok` outcome, and the message names `E1`
  and the override.
- Override path: the same fixture with `REBAR_ALLOW_ENV_REIDENTIFY=1` mints `.env-id` and still
  warns.
- Empty/edge: a store with NO events (genesis init) mints silently — no warning, no regression
  to first-time `rebar init`.
- Detector path: a tracker with events stamped `E1` and `.env-id` = `E2` makes `rebar fsck`
  emit a counted `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` issue naming both ids, present in `--output json`.
- Unreadable/garbage event files are skipped by the scan and never crash the ensure unit or
  fsck.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Minting `.env-id` into a store that already holds events from another environment is
      never silent: a stderr warning names the prior env id(s), the attestation consequence,
      the git-ignored files to carry over, and the override. Verified by a test asserting the
      message contains the prior id, `attestation`, `.opcert-key` and the override name.
- [x] The mint still COMPLETES, so a second clone mounting a shared tickets branch stays
      writable. Verified by a test that mints over a foreign-event store and then creates a
      ticket, and by the existing two-clone integration test staying green.
- [x] `REBAR_ALLOW_ENV_REIDENTIFY=1` acknowledges the situation and quietens the warning to a
      one-line note that still records what was written over. Verified by a test asserting no
      `WARNING` and the prior id present.
- [x] A store with no prior events (genesis `rebar init`) mints with no warning. Verified by a
      test on an emptied store.
- [x] `rebar fsck` emits a counted `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` issue, naming both ids and present in
      `--output json`, when THIS environment's author also wrote events under a different env
      id. Verified by a test over a fixture store.
- [x] That check does NOT fire on the healthy multi-clone topology (several env ids, different
      authors). Verified by a dedicated false-positive test.
- [x] `docs/concurrency.md` lists the local state a re-clone must carry over (`.env-id`,
      `.opcert-key`, `.opcert-key.pub`, `.ensure-applied`), what breaks per file, and why the
      guard warns rather than refuses. Verified by reading the rendered section.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the full `pytest` suite pass in the worktree.

## Provenance

Found when the claim gate blocked task b2bb during the store/signing remediation session.
baseline.summary: Tracker re-clone silently re-identifies the environment, voiding attestations

## Why

Audit Maintainability finding #1: `reconcile.py:697` (and the reconciler's `_loader` helper) loads sibling modules by file path (`_load("reconcile_run_differs", "run_differs.py")`) instead of normal package imports. This defeats every static tool the repo relies on — Pyright/Serena reference resolution, import-linter layering checks, IDE navigation, and the grounding oracle — in the repo's largest and most change-heavy subsystem (~40 modules, 5 of the 10 biggest files). The audit rated the reconciler the highest-onboarding-cost area partly because of this. The mechanism predates the reconciler shipping as a proper package; it is now pure legacy.

## What

Convert the `_engine/rebar_reconciler` path-based `_load()` calls to ordinary `from . import …` / `import rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler.…` package imports, delete the `_load()` helper once callerless, and let the existing lazy-import pattern (module-level function-local imports with rationale comments) handle any genuine circular-import seams the conversion surfaces.

## Scope

In: all `_load()` call sites under `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`, the loader helper itself, and any import-cycle untangling the conversion forces. Out: any behavioral change to reconciliation, module splits/renames (janitor epics own refactors — this story changes only *how modules are referenced*, which is why it rides this epic despite the scope boundary; flagged at creation).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Zero path-based `_load(` call sites remain under `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` (grep-verifiable)
- [ ] The `_load` helper is deleted outright — the file-path loader (`spec_from_file_location`-based `_load()` and the `_loader.py` `lazy_load` bootstrap) is removed once callerless, with no deprecation stub left behind (deletion is final; there is no future migration path to preserve)
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green; reconciler test suites (`tests/scripts/bridge/`, reconciler units) pass unchanged
- [ ] Pyright/Serena can resolve references into the converted modules (spot-check: find-references on a converted symbol returns its call sites)
- [ ] No new import cycles: `python -c "import rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler"` and the optionality guard stay green
baseline.summary: Reconciler: replace path-based _load() module loading with package imports

## Why
Humans and a future CI gate need to see/consume all attestations on a ticket.
## What
Render the `attestations` map in `show` and the MCP ticket-state response (omitted when
empty). NOTE: the HMAC-hex strip for `attestations.<kind>.signature` is implemented in 114f
(it introduces the two-level shape, so the strip lands with it — no leak window); this story
only ASSERTS the rendered output carries no hex for any kind. Document the model in
`docs/plan-review-gate.md` (a new attestations section): when each kind is emitted,
additive-across/replace-within semantics, immutable-record + `compute_validity` on read, the
legacy `signature` mirror (back-compat; its removal is the deferred follow-up
352b-5097-9971-4dc1), and how a future CI gate consumes `verify-signature --kind K`.
Document the HMAC symmetric-key constraint (a CI verifier needs `REBAR_SIGNING_KEY`) as
known follow-up; do NOT build a CI `gate-check` command here. SCOPE BOUNDARY: this story
owns the `attestations` field in the ticket-state MCP response; the `verify_signature` MCP
tool + schema are owned by cc1b.
## Scope
`src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py` / show path, `src/rebar/mcp_server.py` (ticket-state
response only), `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, `CLAUDE.md` attestations note.
## Depends on
Requires 114f (state shape + hex strip) and cc1b (verify surface) merged.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `show`/MCP render `attestations` (kind -> record); omitted when empty.
- [ ] Output carries NO HMAC hex for any kind (the strip itself lands in 114f; verified here).
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` documents emission per kind, semantics, `compute_validity`, the legacy mirror + its deferred removal (352b).
- [ ] CI-readiness (per-kind certified check) + the HMAC symmetric-key constraint documented as follow-up; no CI `gate-check` command added.

## Summary
`rebar show <id>` intermittently returns EMPTY stdout with an apparently-successful (zero) exit instead of the ticket JSON. Downstream consumers that pipe/redirect `show` into a parser receive empty input and crash. The store itself is intact — the same ticket `show`s correctly moments later, and `fsck` is clean — so this is a read-output bug, not data loss.

## Circumstances under which we observed it
Seen repeatedly during a session doing scripted read→transform→write loops on tickets (fetch a description with `rebar show`, edit it, push with `rebar edit --description`):
- It manifests during a BURST of rapid back-to-back rebar invocations — several `rebar edit` (writes) immediately
  followed by `rebar show` (reads) — with `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always` (the default), so each write spawns a
  background push to `origin/tickets`.
- The empty return correlates with those in-flight background pushes/git activity on the `tickets` worktree
  (`.tickets-tracker/`): a tight retry loop of `rebar show <id> > file` can fail on EVERY attempt (8/8) during the
  contention window, while a single `rebar show` after a multi-second quiet period succeeds.
- DECISIVE SIGNAL: setting `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off` for the read/write burst made `rebar show` succeed reliably every
  time (single piped call) — strongly implicating background-push / git-lock contention as the cause.
- During the same window, `rebar clarity-check <id>` and `rebar check-ac <id>` on the SAME id SUCCEED (a different
  read path), and `rebar fsck` reports "no issues found" — so the data is present; only `show`'s stdout comes back
  empty.
- Environment: macOS (darwin) / zsh; rebar over the `tickets` orphan branch (worktree `.tickets-tracker/`); an
  `origin` remote present; default `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always`.

## Reproduction Steps
1. With `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always` (default) and an `origin` remote, run a burst: `rebar edit` on several tickets,
   then immediately `rebar show <id> > out.json` (or `rebar show <id> | python3 -c "import sys,json;json.load(sys.stdin)"`).
2. Repeat in a tight loop.
3. Observe `out.json` intermittently empty / the parser failing with `Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)`,
   despite a success-looking exit.
4. Set `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off` and repeat → `rebar show` succeeds every time.

## Expected vs Actual
- EXPECTED: `rebar show` is read-consistent under concurrent background push — it returns the full ticket JSON,
  or on genuine failure exits NON-ZERO with a diagnostic on stderr. It must NEVER emit empty stdout with exit 0.
- ACTUAL: intermittently emits empty stdout with a success exit during background-push contention, silently
  breaking read→transform→write pipelines.

## Impact
- Silently breaks scripted pipelines that consume `rebar show`. It is also a latent DATA-LOSS vector in
  combination with `edit --description`: an empty `show` feeding an unguarded `edit --description "$(...)"` would
  erase content — the edit-side empty-value guard (bug `e78f-9f79`) mitigates the clobber, but the empty `show`
  is the upstream root cause and should be fixed directly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar show` never returns empty stdout on a zero exit; under read/push contention it returns the complete
      record or exits non-zero with a clear error to stderr.
- [ ] `show` reads a consistent snapshot (or retries internally) so a concurrent background push to
      `origin/tickets` cannot truncate its output; reproduced + fixed under `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always`.
- [ ] A regression test exercises the burst-of-writes-then-`show` pattern and asserts `show` output is always
      complete-or-erroring (never empty+exit0).
- [ ] Audit the other read paths (clarity-check/check-ac/fsck observed unaffected) for the same race; fix
      uniformly or document why only `show` is affected.
baseline.summary: rebar show intermittently returns empty stdout (exit 0) under concurrent background auto-push

# Make a silent, identity-less writer LOUD (scoped to AC2 + AC3)

Split out of bug beb1. **Operator decision 2026-08-12: implement AC2 and AC3 ONLY.** The original limb 1 ("review-bot CREATEs carry `creation_channel=null`") was **disproven by measurement** and is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE — see the re-measurement comment: production CREATEs carry `creation_channel="python"` (52/52 post-deploy, zero nulls store-wide for 25 days); the null reading came from reading a top-level key that lives in `event["data"]`. "Loud" here means **logged and counted**; `identity.require_authenticated` stays advisory per ADR-0045 — this ticket does NOT make any write fail.

## Why this matters

beb1 (a review bot writing ~8900 unsigned, `Unknown`-authored events) ran for a MONTH undetected because the failure was silent at two layers that this ticket closes: `_apply_authorship` returns with no log at all when no identity resolves, and `fsck`'s authorship line is a single store-wide tally, so one env writing 0% signed is invisible behind another env's healthy volume.

## Confirmed mechanism (read from the code, 2026-08-11)

- `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:327-359` — `_apply_authorship` signs only when
  `author_id AND signing_key`. When `signing_key` IS configured but `author_id` is falsy,
  control falls to the cannot-sign branch; with `require_authenticated` off (the default)
  it **returns silently**. Only the signing FAILURE path (line 341) logs.
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:111-122, 259-264` — the authorship tally is summed
  store-wide into one advisory, uncounted text line. There is no per-`env_id` breakdown,
  so the per-env signed-rate analysis that eventually found beb1 remains a one-off script.

## Measured baseline (live store, read-only, 2026-08-11)

18 envs. Four are 0%-signed (`a7f6c5e0` 6 events, `37a1e8e8` 5, `00000000-…` 4, `58e9f32e` 2) and **all four are dormant** — their last event predates the store's first signed event. No env is both 0%-signed and active after signing was adopted. So the adoption-gated rule below reports **zero** issues on today's store (no legacy noise), while beb1's env `b2b5c498` (0 signed, 8914 `Unknown`-authored, writing concurrently with the signing env `ade0f2ef`) WOULD have been reported.

## Acceptance Criteria

The approved subset only — AC1 (creation_channel) is out of scope, see below.

- [x] **AC2** — `fsck` reports, as a **counted** issue (`UNSIGNED_ENV:` line, `issue_count`
      and `--output json` `issues[]`), any `env_id` that has at least one event and either
      **0 signed events** or **every event authored `Unknown`/absent**, gated so it fires
      only when the store has adopted signing AND that env wrote at or after the store's
      earliest signed event. Dormant pre-signing envs are NOT reported.
- [x] **AC3** — `_apply_authorship` emits a `logger.warning` when signing is **SKIPPED**
      for lack of a resolvable identity (or a missing signing key under the gate), naming
      the event uuid, the ticket, and which of the two inputs was missing. It must remain
      best-effort: no write may start failing because of this ticket.
- [x] Held-out tests for each: an fsck test asserting a 0%-signed active env is counted AND
      that a dormant pre-signing env is not (the false-positive guard), and a `_seam` test
      asserting the skip path logs at WARNING with the reason and still writes the event.

## Implementation notes

`fsck.py` is 779 LOC against the hard 800 cap, so the tally lands in a new leaf module `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_authorship.py` (an `EnvAuthorshipTally` that `_scan` feeds from the JSON it ALREADY parses in Check 1 — no extra I/O pass) and `fsck.py` gains only the wiring. The new `unsigned_env` kind is deliberately NOT added to `_STRUCTURED_KINDS`: that set makes the transform parse the line head as a `ticket_id`, and this head is an `env_id`.

## Out of scope

creation_channel (disproven), backfilling the 166 legacy `unknown`-channel review CREATEs, and any change to `identity.require_authenticated` enforcement.
baseline.summary: No guard makes an unsigned, identity-less writer loud

# 59 of the 63 tickets orphaned by the 2026-08-03 reconcile incident are STILL parentless

The **code defect** that destroyed these edges is fixed (`88d9-fe42-e50f-4067`, landed `25ead49f3e`). The **data** was never restored. This ticket tracks that outstanding restoration backlog, which no open ticket currently owns.

## What happened (re-confirmed independently in this investigation)

Reconcile run **30828160906** (GitHub Actions, `workflow_dispatch`, `MODE: live`, 2026-08-03 15:37:59-15:38:10 UTC) wrote 63 `EDIT` events with `{"fields": {"parent_id": ""}}`, author `reconciler`, all in one commit `b8062b10e97b0c891deefbefa87934bb37c66d84` on the `tickets` branch.

**All 63 destroyed a real parent edge. Zero were no-ops.**

The mechanism, cited:
* `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_field_diff.py:138-139` - outbound
  **OMITS** the parent field whenever the local parent's `ticket_type != "epic"`,
  so Jira is never told about it.
* `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py` `diff_inbound_parent` - inbound
  then read Jira's honest "no parent", classified it `PARENT_NO_PARENT`, and **CLEARED**
  the local edge. Its only guard, `should_propagate_removal`, answers the *outbound*
  question (absent locally -> delete on peer) and structurally cannot answer the inbound
  one. `add_managed_ref` is folded by the **local** parent-set event
  (`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:87-90`, `:526-528`), so "managed" never proved Jira
  ever had the parent.
* Omit-vs-clear asymmetry is documented on `39c1-2a32-b564-4b4b`.

**Discriminating evidence (this investigation).** Of tickets holding a parent immediately before the run: **every one of the 63 lost parents is a `story` (62) or `bug` (1) - not one `epic`**; 600+ epic-parented children in the same pass were untouched. Story/bug-parented tickets that survived had **no Jira binding**, so the inbound differ never saw them. The rule is exact: `cleared <=> bound AND parent is not an epic`. No unexplained residual.

## Why it was never repaired

`8b86-cf7f-ae1c-4955` - 61 of the 63 prior parents are **closed**, and `rebar edit <child> --parent=<closed parent>` is refused by the `--parent` validation cascade. `5992-f317-e05e-42f7` (a dedicated `parent` verb with `--force`) is still an **`idea`**, so no repair route exists today.

## Current state (measured 2026-08-04)

* **59 of 63 still parentless**; 4 restored ad hoc.
* The full child -> lost-parent map is recoverable from the event log and is posted as a
  comment on this ticket.
* The `Reconcile Bridge` workflow is currently `disabled_manually` (last run
  2026-08-04 16:05 UTC), so nothing is re-clearing anything right now.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the recovered child -> lost-parent map is verified against the event log
- [ ] a supported write path exists for re-parenting onto a **closed** parent (depends on
      `5992-f317-e05e-42f7` / `8b86-cf7f-ae1c-4955`)
- [ ] all 59 remaining edges are restored, or each exception is recorded with a reason
- [ ] a post-restore sweep confirms 0 tickets from the incident set remain parentless
- [ ] restoration is done with the reconciler's peer-evidence fix in force, and a
      subsequent reconcile pass is confirmed not to re-clear them
baseline.summary: Restore the 59 tickets still orphaned by the 2026-08-03 reconciler parent-clear incident

Live capture (2026-08-06, closing c827-2a23-cd00-473e from the loop-breaker checkout, main at 9a27202837): the primary completion-verifier run looped and was correctly aborted by the c827 actuator (requests=119, distinct_ratio_window=0.5). Bounded recovery started, but the evidence agent for ONE criterion hit its own step budget with a perfectly HEALTHY profile — 'completion-verifier-evidence ... hit step budget (request_limit=20 max_iterations=40) requests=20 tool_calls=35 distinct=35 max_consecutive_repeat=1 distinct_ratio_window=1.0 top_repeats=[]' — and that single LLMBudgetExhaustedError propagated out of the per-criterion loop in CompletionAgentStep._recover (completion_recovery.py ~:519-536), discarding all evidence already gathered and failing the whole recovery. The gate then reported 'bounded evidence recovery also failed' and offered --force-close: the exact exhaustion-is-not-a-verdict trap this cluster removes, one layer down.

The defect: the per-criterion evidence loop treats a single criterion's budget exhaustion as fatal to the aggregate, when the bound is a per-criterion safeguard. Partial evidence must be preserved rather than discarded — the finalizer already renders per-criterion verdicts and can mark a criterion unverifiable-within-bounds.

Plan: catch LLMBudgetExhaustedError, RunawayToolLoopError, and token-exhaustion UnretryableOutputError (guarded by _is_token_exhaustion, mirroring run()) around the per-criterion runner.run in _recover; substitute a content-free placeholder evidence entry that names the failure class and its usage counters (from the exception diagnostic), mark the entry exhausted=true; continue with remaining criteria; recovery fails outright only if EVERY criterion's evidence run fails. Placeholder text must never be presentable as affirmative evidence — it must state that evidence could not be gathered within recovery bounds so the finalizer scores the criterion unmet/indeterminate, not met. Aggregate char bound and finalizer input bound stay as-is. CompletionRecoveryError raised only when zero criteria produced evidence, carrying counts {criteria_total, criteria_exhausted}.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A single criterion's LLMBudgetExhaustedError no longer aborts recovery: with N criteria and one evidence run exhausting, the finalizer still runs and receives N evidence entries, the exhausted one carrying an explicit could-not-gather-within-bounds placeholder (unit test, held-out oracle style).
- [x] A RunawayToolLoopError raised by an evidence run is handled the same way (unit test).
- [x] A token-exhaustion UnretryableOutputError from an evidence run is converted to the exhausted placeholder, mirroring the primary path; a NON-token UnretryableOutputError still propagates (unit test).
- [x] The placeholder is content-free (no exception prose interpolated beyond the failure class name and numeric usage counters) and can never read as affirmative evidence (unit test asserts wording).
- [x] If EVERY criterion's evidence run fails, recovery raises CompletionRecoveryError with diagnostic {criteria_total, criteria_exhausted} (unit test).
- [x] Successful-evidence behaviour is byte-identical: runs where no evidence agent fails produce the same finalizer input as before (unit test).
- [x] Live Bedrock proof before ship: a real gate-style recovery over multiple criteria where at least one evidence run exhausts completes with a verdict instead of failing whole (session experiment, not in unit suite).
- [x] make lint and mypy clean; full CI marker suite matches the pre-existing baseline.

## Testing
Held-out unit oracle in tests/unit/workflow/ (written before the fix, RED first): `python -m pytest tests/unit/workflow/ -q`. Mutation checks on the fix. Live Bedrock experiment (session artifact, not in unit suite) proving a multi-criterion recovery with one exhausted evidence run still reaches a verdict. `make lint` + `make typecheck` clean; full marker suite matches pre-existing baseline.
baseline.summary: Bounded recovery dies whole when one criterion's evidence run exhausts its budget

## Problem

The provider-parity corpus includes the `code-review-verify` spec, whose output carries NO decision polarity, so the two-bucket parity mapping cannot score it. Every verify case is therefore scored `advisory` regardless of its gold label, which makes the gold-block case `V-real-defect` a GUARANTEED recall miss on BOTH arms.

Confirmed empirically in the committed artifact `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json`: `V-real-defect` has `label: "block"` with `v1.decision == v2.decision == "advisory"`, `valid: true`, `errored: false`, on BOTH the standard and frontier slots. Both verify cases sit inside the scored gold set (30 records, `n_gold` 28; the two excluded are the `G3-*` container fixtures).

Mechanism: `fidelity_spot_eval._verdict_decision` (imported by `provider_parity.py:52` so the two cannot drift) keys only on `verdict == "FAIL"` or a non-empty `findings`. The verifier emits neither — its output vocabulary is `{verifications: [...]}` — so it falls through to `advisory`.

## Why the obvious fix is WRONG

"Treat a non-empty `verifications` list as `block`" looks right and is not. `code-review-verify.eval.yaml` states the contract twice:
  - header: "Per the T8-advisory contract it is scored on PRESENCE of verifications, NOT a FAIL/BLOCK
    verdict ... either way the verifier must emit a graded answer set."
  - dataset: "the gating scorer is presence-based, so the verifier must emit verifications for both."
BOTH cases — `V-real-defect` (gold block) and `V-clean-rename` (gold advisory) — are REQUIRED to emit a non-empty list. Mapping presence to `block` would fix the recall miss and simultaneously score the clean case as a block, manufacturing a FALSE ACCEPT. The arm has no polarity to read; no adapter can invent one.

## Approach

EXCLUDE `code-review-verify` from the parity corpus, for a reason DISTINCT from the existing `AGENTIC_SOLVERS` exclusion (that one excludes agentic ops; this one excludes a polarity-free scorer). Keep the two reasons separately named so a future reader does not collapse them.

## Impact on the recorded run

Excluding both verify cases takes `n_gold` 28 -> 26, still above `MIN_GOLD_ITEMS = 20`. It removes one guaranteed miss from each arm, so recall rises on both. The miss was SYMMETRIC, so no gating verdict flips — the v2-vs-v1 noninferiority comparison is unaffected and false-accept is untouched (the affected case is a gold-block case, not a safe one). This corrects measurement ACCURACY, not a pass/fail outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `code-review-verify` is excluded from the parity corpus by a named, separate mechanism from
      `AGENTIC_SOLVERS`, with the reason (no decision polarity) stated at the definition.
- [x] A test asserts NO case from a polarity-free spec is eligible, and that the exclusion reason is
      distinct from the agentic exclusion — i.e. removing the agentic set does not silently cover this.
- [x] A test pins the SPECIFIC failure this fixes: a `{verifications: [...]}` output does NOT map to
      `block`, AND a gold-block verify case is no longer scored as a live miss because it is excluded
      rather than mis-scored. It must fail before the fix.
- [x] The recorded artifact is RE-SCORED OFFLINE with zero model calls; the new `n_gold` and recall are
      recorded, and it is stated explicitly whether any GATING verdict changed (expected: none).
- [x] The gold floor still holds after exclusion (`n_gold >= MIN_GOLD_ITEMS`), asserted by a test so a
      future corpus shrink cannot silently drop below it.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code, the default selection is green, and the
      config-read and env-drift gates pass.
baseline.summary: Parity corpus scores the polarity-free code-review-verify arm, guaranteeing a recall miss

## Reproduction Steps

1. Open a PR; CI runs the default pytest suite across the matrix (ubuntu/macos × py3.11/3.12).
2. On a loaded runner (observed on `macos-latest, py3.12`), `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_perf.py` fails on absolute wall-clock assertions even though the code is unchanged.

Observed failures (PR #108 run 28505746020):
- `test_graph_perf.py:59` — `build_dep_graph took 3.192s for 1,000-ticket chain (limit: 2.0s)`
- `test_graph_perf.py:327` — `9 cross-tier add_dependency calls took 8.65s (limit: 5.0s)`

Both passed on all ubuntu runners in the same PR; a manual re-run of the macOS job passed. So the failures are runner-load-dependent, not a code regression.

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** perf tests gate against genuine algorithmic regressions and are stable across CI runners.
- **Actual:** they assert against fixed absolute-time thresholds (`< 2.0s`, `< 5.0s`) that a slow/loaded shared runner (esp. macOS) blows past, producing false-failure PR blocks that require manual re-runs.

## Impact

Flaky red on unrelated PRs → wasted re-runs + eroded trust in the gate (a green PR gets blocked by an infra hiccup). This blocked epic 3156's final merge (PR #108) until a manual re-run.

## Root cause

Absolute wall-clock budgets are sensitive to shared-runner contention. A perf test should measure a *relative* signal (scaling / ratio vs a baseline op on the same machine) or run in an isolated, non-gating, retried context — not a raw seconds ceiling.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_perf.py` no longer false-fails under runner load: either (a) assert on a RELATIVE metric (e.g. per-op time scaled to a same-machine baseline, or big-O scaling ratio between N and 2N) instead of an absolute seconds ceiling, or (b) mark the wall-clock assertions with a bounded retry (e.g. `flaky`/rerun) AND widen the ceilings with generous headroom, or (c) move the raw-timing assertions to a dedicated NON-gating perf job (still run, reported, not merge-blocking) while keeping a correctness-only assertion in the gating suite.
- [ ] The chosen approach still catches a real >2x algorithmic regression (a deliberately O(n^2) reintroduction fails the test) — documented in the test.
- [ ] No absolute single-run wall-clock ceiling remains in the gating path for these two tests.
baseline.summary: Flaky graph perf tests (absolute wall-clock limits) fail on loaded CI runners

# New-gate CI steps fail pre-gate changes: workflow from target branch, tree from change

## Summary

Gerrit's verify job takes the **workflow definition from the target branch** but **checks out the change's tree**. A newly landed gate step that runs a repo script (`python scripts/check_X.py`) therefore hard-fails every open change whose base predates the gate-introducing commit: the step runs, but the script does not exist in the checked-out tree.

Observed in production: changes 1332/1333 (based before d37e's 6739ea54fa landed) failed Verified with `python: can't open file '.../scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py': [Errno 2] No such file or directory`. The just-merged wall-clock-assert gate (1e95, 9af88c3ada, scripts/check_wall_clock_asserts.py) has the identical window. Immediate recovery for 1332/1333 was a server-side rebase:chain — but every future gate-script landing re-opens this window for all in-flight changes.

## Root cause

The two new gate steps in .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml invoke their script unconditionally. The workflow definition and the checked-out tree can legitimately diverge (definition-from-target-branch is Gerrit CI's model), so a gate step must tolerate a tree that predates its script.

## Fix plan

Guard both new gate steps with an existence check that SKIPS (with an explanatory log line) when the script is absent from the checked-out tree:

    - name: raw-git-write gate
      run: |
        if [ -f scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py ]; then
          python scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py
        else
          echo "scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py not in checked-out tree (change predates the gate) — skipping"
        fi

Same shape for the wall-clock-assert gate step. Include an inline workflow comment stating the idiom and WHY (definition-from-target-branch vs change tree skew), so future gate authors copy the guard along with the step. Deleting a gate script in a change silently skips that gate for that change — acceptable: such a deletion is itself visible in review, and the gate re-enforces on every post-merge change.

Older gate steps (comment-hygiene, module-size, commit wrap) predate all open changes; leave them unguarded to keep the diff minimal — the documented idiom covers any future script.

## Verification

- actionlint via make lint passes on the edited workflow.
- Shell logic locally exercised both branches: script present -> runs detector (exit propagates); script absent (temp dir) -> skip message, exit 0.
- CI on the change itself (which HAS both scripts) still runs both gates — Verified +1 proves the present-branch path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Both new gate steps (raw-git-write, wall-clock-assert) skip with an explanatory message when their script is absent from the checked-out tree, and run it when present.
- [x] The skew rationale + copy-me idiom is documented inline in the workflow at the gate steps.
- [x] make lint (actionlint) passes; both branches of the guard exercised locally.

## File impact

- .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml (edit)
baseline.summary: New-gate CI steps fail pre-gate changes: workflow from target branch, tree from change
