## Context / Scope Correction
This ticket originally tracked a loose-object ENOENT/write-tree failure. When Gerrit 1827 later failed with a batched-empty / narrow-success signature, the ticket was reopened under the assumption that it was the same failure class. Investigation refuted that assumption: deleting the previously implicated loose blob left both broad and narrow history walks healthy. The unresolved ENOENT symptom is preserved separately in previous-quelled-nutria, linked discovered_from this ticket and blocked on recurrence evidence. Historical comments below remain the audit trail; the current scope is only the distinct Gerrit 1827 recurrence.

## Problem
In Gerrit 1827 run 31961655783, tests/unit/test_authorship_batched_ticket_map_7084.py called build_ticket_position_commit_map once and required a complete map. That optimization helper explicitly fails closed to an empty map on any Git nonzero result, empty output, or process exception; production callers then preserve attribution with per-event fallback. The fixture equivalence assertion incorrectly treated the optimization boundary as guaranteed to succeed on its first environmental attempt. The observed sequence was an empty batched result followed immediately by a successful narrow read in the unchanged repository.

## Approach
- Prove the recurrence boundary with the real temporary Git topology and first-attempt injections for rc 128 with empty output, rc 0 with empty output, and BlockingIOError(EAGAIN).
- Add fixture-only bounded recovery that repeats the exact batched resolver call, returns only a complete map, and stops after five attempts with existing object-store diagnostics.
- Route both direct equivalence assertions and the optimization-count assertion through the same fixture helper.
- Keep src/rebar fail-closed and per-event fallback behavior unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The prior loose-object ENOENT class is refuted for this recurrence: deleting the implicated blob leaves both broad and narrow history reads successful; the residual ENOENT work is tracked in previous-quelled-nutria.
- [x] First-attempt rc 128/empty, rc 0/empty, and BlockingIOError(EAGAIN) injections each reproduce the observed empty-batched then successful-identical-replay sequence against the real fixture repository.
- [x] Fixture-only recovery makes at most five exact batched attempts, returns on the first complete map, and raises persistent diagnostics containing fsck and count-objects evidence; no src/rebar behavior changes.
- [x] Both fixture equivalence assertions and the optimization-count assertion use the recovery seam without weakening exact position-to-commit expectations.
- [x] Held-out TDD evidence is recorded: four behavioral cases were RED before the repair, GREEN afterward, and returned to RED under the exact omitted-recovery mutation; the in-file optimization sibling was independently RED then GREEN.
- [x] [operator-attested] Focused tests (12 passed), adjacent suites (27 passed), lint, typecheck, and the full local suite (13,522 passed, 60 skipped, 289 deselected) are green; Gerrit 1828 earned LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 with zero unresolved comments, merged as commit 29448f61c095c4f63afb9291ae156a4e0163d843, and CI run 31967631562 completed with 17 green jobs including Ubuntu/Python 3.11.
  provenance: environment=local worktree and Gerrit CI; principal=RebarBotNava and rebar CI bot; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — commands, votes, merge state, and CI run were observed directly and recorded in the final repair comment.

## Context
The generated artifacts from a rebar-janitor session were lost. Reconstruct the recoverable results from `~/Downloads/ChatGPT-Rebar janitor analysis-20260816-0915.md`. Decisions 1-6 require the deepest research and analysis. This is a no-code recovery: preserve evidence, distinguish transcript facts from present-day corroboration, and make uncertainty explicit.

The current skill names `.rebar-janitor/`, but this repository’s historical local-only artifact convention is `.joe-janitor/`, evidenced by tracked `.joe-janitor/tools.md` and tracker record `naive-bigheaded-wildcat`. Other git-excluded files visible in one checkout are opportunistic corroboration only: the plan does not assume that `known-fine.md` or prior `report-*.md` files survive. baseline.description:
## Why

Today a plan-review criterion is inert unless it is in the hardcoded `CANONICAL_LLM` frozenset
(`plan_review/registry.py:70`) AND the packaged `criteria_routing.json`; `_routing_index()` /
`load_criteria()` are `@lru_cache`d with no `repo_root` key. So a project cannot add a criterion at
all. This story opens the vocabulary and adds the project overlay — the **dependency root + MVP
slice** for the whole epic (`3156`). It is NOT blocked on `b744` (extends plan-review directly).

## What

- `effective_criteria(repo_root)` = `CANONICAL_LLM` ∪ activated project ids; route it through
  **every** plan-review vocabulary site: `load_criteria`, `check_registry_coverage`, and the
  workflow Pass-1 batch vocab in `workflow_ops` (`plan_review_assemble_criteria`). The
  `include_<id>` output key must sanitize the `project.<name>` id (`.`→`_`) at BOTH the assemble
  and consume sites (keep the rule co-located).
- `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` overlay: gate-keyed (`{plan_review: {...}, activate: [...]}`),
  reusing the packaged routing schema; `project.<name>` namespace; an un-prefixed built-in id =
  re-tune/disable; a `project.`-id colliding with a built-in, or a duplicate, is **rejected at
  load** (located error). A criterion runs only if in `activate`.
- Cache isolation: keep `_routing_index()` cached for the packaged index; add
  `effective_routing(repo_root)` (uncached, or keyed by `(repo_root, overlay mtime)` — note mtime
  granularity, prefer content hash if flaky); extend `prompt_library._invalidate_caches()`.
- Routing validation: load-time (invalid routing = located error, not silent skip) + a CI
  drift/parity gate mirroring `reviewers/index.json`.

## Scope

- Files: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py`, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py`,
  `src/rebar/llm/prompt_library.py`, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` (schema doc).
- MVP end-to-end: activate ONE project LLM criterion from the overlay → it runs in plan-review
  Pass-1 → surfaces a finding. (Attestation invalidation is story `#4`; unify is story `#6`.)
- Out: code-review side (story `#6`, b744-blocked); DET consumer (story `#2`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `effective_criteria(repo_root)` loads activated project criteria and is routed through
      `load_criteria`, `check_registry_coverage`, and the workflow Pass-1 batch vocab; an activated
      project LLM criterion fans out and runs in plan-review Pass-1.
- [ ] `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` overlay per schema: gate-keyed, `project.<name>` namespace,
      explicit `activate` list, load-time collision/rebind rejection (located error).
- [ ] `include_<id>` key sanitization (`.`→`_`) applied at both assemble + consume sites.
- [ ] Overlay merge is cache-isolated per repo (packaged index stays cached; overlay is not);
      a RED test proves no cross-repo routing leakage in the long-lived MCP server.
- [ ] Routing validation: invalid overlay routing is a located error + a CI drift/parity gate.
- [ ] An ADR documents the unified-registry + overlay merge/activation contract.
- [ ] MVP slice demonstrated end-to-end (activate one criterion → runs → surfaces a finding).

## Backward-compatibility, fan-out mechanism & cache strategy (remediation, run 1)

### Expand-contract / backward-compatibility (clears T4)
Every signature change is **additive** with a `repo_root=None` default that preserves
today's behaviour, so no existing caller breaks:
- `registry.load_criteria(repo_root=None)`, `registry.by_id(repo_root=None)`,
  `registry.check_registry_coverage(repo_root=None)`, `registry._descriptor_from_prompt(cid,
  *, repo_root=None, routing_index=None)`, and the NEW `effective_criteria(repo_root=None)` /
  `effective_routing(repo_root=None)` all default `repo_root=None`.
- `repo_root=None` resolves to `config.repo_root()` (the same root `get_prompt` already
  resolves `.rebar/prompts/` overrides against) — so an **overlay-absent** repo yields
  **exactly** today's packaged-only vocabulary/routing (no behaviour change, no churn).
- **Call sites updated** (enumerated): `orchestrator.route_criteria` (passes the ctx
  repo_root), `workflow_ops.plan_review_assemble_criteria` (uses `ctx.repo_root`),
  `attest.registry_version`/`plan_review.__init__` coverage (story #4 threads repo_root;
  this story keeps the no-arg default working), and the tests. Bare `load_criteria()` /
  `check_registry_coverage()` keep working unchanged.
- **Rollback:** delete `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` (overlay-absent ⇒ packaged behaviour),
  or revert the additive params (all default `None`).

### Dynamic Pass-1 fan-out mechanism (clears G6/T1/T3 — schema-safe, NO v3 change)
The v3 `batch` step schema (`workflow.v3.schema.json`) is IMMUTABLE + version-pinned with
`additionalProperties:false` on `$defs/batch`, and the gate validates its OWN document at run
time — so a new `batch` field (e.g. `extra_criteria`) is impossible without a v4 schema+shim
(out of MVP scope). Instead, project criteria fan out through the **rebar-specific
`ProductionBatchRunner`** (`production_batch_runner.py`), NOT a new doc field:
- built-in criteria keep fanning out via the STATIC `criteria:` list in `gates/plan-review.yaml`
  (each gated by its `include_<ID>` key — byte-identical to today);
- the runner, after `assemble_context`, calls `route_criteria(ctx)` (which now returns the FULL
  effective set) and appends ONLY the `project.<name>`-prefixed descriptors — already past the
  SAME `applies()`/overlay filter the built-ins use — to the finder's tier-split set, deduped
  against the built-ins. `assemble` still emits sanitized `include_project_<name>` booleans
  (`.`→`_`) as the coverage/routing record. `gates/plan-review.yaml` and the immutable schema
  are UNTOUCHED. (Probe-mode caveat: route_criteria has no probe notion, so a project criterion
  is also evaluated during a drift probe — harmless, documented follow-up.)

### Cache strategy — content-hash, not mtime (clears E2/G6/T8/T9)
`effective_routing`/`load_criteria` are memoized in repo-keyed module dicts keyed by
`(repo_root, sha256(overlay-bytes))` — a **content signature**, NOT mtime (mtime
granularity is coarse/flaky), so editing the overlay auto-invalidates the memo. The
packaged `_routing_index()` stays `@lru_cache`d (immutable per binary). Stale-entry
growth is bounded: `prompt_library._invalidate_caches()` clears both memos + the lru_caches
(the RED cross-repo-leak test proves repo A's routing never serves repo B).

### Sanitization inverse & missing-prompt fallback (clears T8)
The `.`→`_` map is one-directional at the workflow-key layer only; the criterion id and
prompt id retain the dotted form, so no inverse un-sanitization is needed (the
`project_criteria` entry carries the real dotted `prompt` id directly). An activated
project id whose prompt file is absent/malformed surfaces as a **located `RegistryError`**
from `load_criteria` (same as a missing built-in prompt) — fail-loud at load, never a
silent skip.

### ADR contents (clears E1/AC6)
`docs/adr/0015-project-supplied-criteria.md` documents: the `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`
overlay schema (gate-keyed, `project.<name>` namespace, `activate` list); the merge +
collision/rebind rules; `effective_criteria`/`effective_routing` as the vocabulary seam;
the content-hash cache-isolation contract; and the runner-side (schema-free) project fan-out.

### Scope clarification (clears E5/T8/G5)
Files also touched: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py` (project fan-in) and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py` (`route_criteria` threads repo_root). MVP end-to-end exercises ONE activated project **LLM** criterion (`exec: 1-TURN`). Project
`exec: DET` criteria (the prompt-less descriptor branch) are story #2; the shared
`rebar.llm.criteria` unification is story #6. The CI drift/parity gate here is a
**validation** gate (the packaged `criteria_routing.json` stays schema-valid and in parity
with `CANONICAL_LLM` + the prompt files), not a generator, since the routing is
hand-authored judgement (thresholds/applies_at) with no derivation source.

## Acceptance Criteria (remediation additions)

- [ ] All new/changed registry signatures are additive with a `repo_root=None` default that
      preserves packaged-only behaviour (overlay-absent repo == today); rollback = delete the
      overlay.
- [ ] The dynamic Pass-1 fan-out for a project criterion is runner-side (`ProductionBatchRunner`
      appends the `project.` subset of `route_criteria`), leaving the immutable v3 `batch` schema
      and `gates/plan-review.yaml` UNCHANGED.

- [ ] An activated project criterion with a missing/malformed prompt file raises a LOCATED
      `RegistryError` from `load_criteria` (fail-loud, no silent skip); a test asserts it.
- [ ] Overlay mis-authoring is covered by named tests: collision/rebind rejection, un-namespaced
      net-new id, activated-without-routing, invalid routing schema, malformed JSON — each a
      located `RegistryError`.
- [ ] `prompt_library._invalidate_caches()` clears the new overlay-merged caches (proven: an
      overlay edit is picked up for the same repo_root without a process restart).
baseline.summary: Criteria registry: open the vocabulary + .rebar/ routing overlay + activation + cache isolation (plan-review MVP root)

# DELETE the dormant inbound absence-probe port

**Decision (operator ruling, recorded on this ticket): DELETE.** This ticket is no longer an open delete-vs-re-home question; it executes the deletion. Option 2 (re-home the port to `binding_walk`) is a REJECTED alternative, retained below only so the rejection is legible.

## What is being deleted, and why it is safe

Bug `3b5f-1b21-ee14-4bdf` removed every consumer of the `(inbound, probe)` chain — the producer `differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes`, the dispatch arm `_run_differs_inbound_probe_dispatch`, and `reconcile_helpers.route_inbound_probe`. What remained is a capability with **zero callers**:

* `_backend.SupportsAbsenceProbe` (Protocol) and the three `probe_remote` implementations
  (`adapters/jira/backend.py`, `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py`,
  `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py`)
* the neutral vocabulary module `inbound_probe.py` (`ProbeBranch`, `ProbeResult`,
  `ProbeConfigError`)
* the Cloud probe `adapters/jira/probe.py` and the shared classifier
  `adapters/jira_family/probe.py` (`classify_probe_response`), whose only callers are the
  `probe_remote` implementations above

This is a **pure deletion with no behavior change**: nothing in a reconcile pass reaches any of it. Deletion detection is NOT affected — it lives OUTBOUND, in `outbound_differ._safe_get_issue` + `binding_walk`, and the separate **outbound** probe leaf (`_apply_outbound_probe`, the `(outbound, probe)` dispatch arm) is live and is NOT touched by this ticket.

## Why option 2 (re-home to `binding_walk`) is rejected

* The port must NOT be used to restore same-pass re-creation — an earlier operator ruling
  on `3b5f` is that a confirmed-deleted issue is never resurrected. That removes the
  port's original purpose.
* Its stated motivation was false: `binding_walk` already takes the direct-GET as an
  INJECTED `probe_get: Callable`, with `outbound_differ._safe_get_issue` as a lazy default
  only — there is no hardcoded private reach for the port to fix.
* It would re-cross an ownership boundary ADR 0028 deliberately draws: absence-vs-deletion
  discrimination is OUTBOUND-owned. Re-homing an INBOUND port there re-splits what `3b5f`
  just consolidated.
* The vocabularies are incompatible in an unsafe direction: `ProbeBranch` has no
  confirmed-404 branch, and its `ARCHIVED_OR_MOVED` conflates deletion with a
  still-alive MOVE — routing it to `binding_walk`'s tombstone could tombstone a live
  moved issue.

## Explicitly OUT of scope (follow-up, not this change)

Deleting the classifier orphans the operator-facing `jira.resolved_statuses` / `reconciler.resolved_statuses` config keys and the DC transport's `_resolved_statuses` plumbing. Removing DOCUMENTED config keys is a user-visible surface change needing its own deprecate-vs-remove decision, so it is deliberately deferred to a follow-up ticket linked `discovered_from` this one — the same reasoning by which `3b5f` deferred this ticket. The keys keep their current behavior here (they simply have no reader), so this change stays behavior-neutral.

## Every file that must change (the deletion's full blast radius)

**Source — deleted outright:** `rebar_reconciler/inbound_probe.py`, `adapters/jira/probe.py`, `adapters/jira_family/probe.py`.

**Source — edited:** `_backend.py` (drop `SupportsAbsenceProbe`), `adapters/jira/backend.py` + `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` (drop `probe_remote`), `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` (drop `probe_remote` + the classifier import), `adapters/jira_family/__init__.py` (drop `classify_probe_response` from the imports, `__all__` and the docstring), `reconcile_helpers.py` (stale docstring), `adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py` (comment reference), `pyproject.toml` (comment reference).

**Tests — deleted outright** (they exist only to exercise the deleted units): `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_probe_capability.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_probe_capability_heldout.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_probe_resolved_statuses_config.py`.

**Tests — edited** (they import or assert the deleted units and would hard-break): `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/backend_support.py` (the `probe_remote` stub), `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_characterization.py` (`test_classify_probe_response_pins_every_branch`, the `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES` pin), `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_backend_characterization.py` (the DC probe characterization block and its mutation-log comments), `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py` (`SupportsAbsenceProbe` isinstance + `probe_remote` delegation), `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_dc_config_settings.py` (the probe-based `resolved_statuses` assertion), `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_family_seam.py` (the `classify_probe_response` seam tests), `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_transport.py` (the live `probe_remote` test).

**Tests — edited because they pin the deleted units BY NAME as invariants** (these fail as assertions, not merely as imports, so they are called out separately): `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py` (`inbound_probe.py` is an entry in `_ZERO_ADAPTER_IMPORT_SCALAR_CORE`) and `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py` (its boundary example string names `from rebar_reconciler.inbound_probe import ProbeBranch`).

**Docs:** ADR 0028 (dormant-port Consequences), ADR 0035 (module list), ADR 0055 (shared probe-classifier unit).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] no live caller of the port remains, proven by a Serena semantic search AND
      independently by a plain string grep (per AGENTS.md an empty semantic result alone is
      not trustworthy)
- [x] that proof is recorded as a comment on this ticket
- [x] `SupportsAbsenceProbe` and all three `probe_remote` implementations are deleted
- [x] `inbound_probe.py`, `adapters/jira/probe.py` and `adapters/jira_family/probe.py` are
      deleted, and `classify_probe_response` is dropped from the `jira_family` package
      exports
- [x] the **outbound** probe leaf (`_apply_outbound_probe`, the `(outbound, probe)`
      dispatch arm) is untouched, proven by the existing suite staying green
- [x] epic `e369`'s AC5 is amended to drop the probe classifier from its "one shared
      implementation imported by both backends" clause, with the amendment recorded on
      `e369` and this ticket linked to it
- [x] the dormancy notes in `inbound_probe.py`, `SupportsAbsenceProbe` and ADR 0028 are
      removed along with the code they describe, and ADR 0035 / ADR 0055 no longer list
      the deleted units as shared
- [x] the stale `reconcile_helpers.py` docstring claim that it by-path loads
      `inbound_probe.py` is corrected (no such runtime load exists)
- [x] a follow-up ticket for the orphaned `resolved_statuses` config keys is filed and
      linked `discovered_from` this ticket
- [x] every test file listed above is deleted or updated, so no test imports or asserts a
      deleted unit
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and `make test` are green in the worktree
- [x] the change is `Verified +1` on Gerrit before the ticket is closed

## Execution record

Landed as Gerrit change 1645, merged to `main` as `b95c097fd4` (`LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`); 30 files, +79 / -1040. Two deviations from the plan above — ADR 0035 is now `docs/adr/0083-...`, and the config-read gate turned the deferred `resolved_statuses` orphan into a hard CI blocker (resolved with the gate's own ticket-pointing marker rather than by removing the key). Both, plus the provenance of AC1's two proof halves, are recorded in this ticket's comments.

`docs/exit-codes.md` declares itself "the single source of truth" (`:5`) covering "each public dispatcher arm" (`:69`). It has 41 table rows against 75 real commands — independently re-derived from `_cli/_help.known_subcommands()` union `_cli/__init__._INTERCEPTS`. The 34 omissions include `review-plan`, `review-code`, and `verify-completion`, whose exit-11 semantics the same document defines four lines into its own codes table.

Grounding found worse: codes **75** (`RebaseGuard`/`EXIT_RESCHEDULE`) and **78** (`StoreIncompatibleError`) reach the process exit status via `_seam.py:419` → `_commands/__init__.py:160` and appear nowhere in the document. 75 is the one code a CI workflow actually branches on. Codes 3, 4, 12 and `validate`'s 0-4 severity bucket are also undocumented.

The doc's own scope note is stale: it says only five commands validate unknown options, but `metrics`, `doctor`, `composer` and `fsck` all exit 2 on unknown options today.

A separate candidate finding — "define an exit-code vocabulary and standardise usage" — was run through the pipeline and FAILED both floors (impact 0.415). The one exit-code defect in this repo's history (`show`/`list` returning 1 instead of 2) was caught by writing the doc and a conformance test, not by constants. That is the mitigation already in place, and this ticket extends it rather than replacing it. Do not add a named exit-code enum.

Full generation was assessed and rejected: the command list is derivable, but per-command *semantics* have no machine-readable source, and exit 11 is produced at the CLI layer (`_cli/_llm_commands.py:129-171`), not in `_commands/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Rows exist for all 75 dispatcher arms
- [x] Codes 3, 4, 12, 75 and 78 are documented with their meanings
- [x] The stale "only five commands validate options" note is corrected
- [x] A CI check asserts every dispatcher arm has a row, so a new command without one fails
- [x] The document carries a forward-compatibility sentence: an unknown non-zero code MUST be treated as failure
baseline.summary: Make docs/exit-codes.md complete and keep it that way

baseline.description:
## Why

The deterministic decision math (Pass-3) is the most divergence-dangerous part of the four-pass
framework: if two gates compute "what blocks" differently, the gate guarantee silently forks.
`pass3_decide` + `pass3_over_findings` already live in `plan_review/orchestrator.py`/`passes.py`
and are *already* shared across the (former) bespoke and workflow paths — this lifts them into a
named shared kernel module as the framework's single decision core, with per-criterion thresholds
parameterized so a consuming gate can set its own posture without forking the math.

## What

- Create the kernel package (e.g. `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/`) and move the deterministic
  Pass-3 core into it: `pass3_decide` (validity = graded fraction of the binary sub-answers;
  impact = mean of ordinal-mapped severity attributes; priority = validity×impact; the
  conditional cited-reference veto; block/advisory against per-criterion thresholds) +
  `pass3_over_findings`.
- Parameterize the per-criterion `block_threshold` / posture so consumers pass their own
  thresholds; keep plan-review's current defaults intact.
- Rewire the plan-review workflow's `plan_review_decide` op to call the kernel (no behavior
  change). Keep a thin re-export from `plan_review` if needed for back-compat.

## Scope

In scope: the Pass-3 decision function + math + the binary→validity / attrs→impact maps, moved to
the kernel; plan-review consumes it. Out of scope: Pass-2 verify (WS2), the coach (WS3), the seam
doc + evals (WS4), and threshold *calibration* (deferred). Touches
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py`/`passes.py`, the new kernel module, and
`workflow_ops.py` (the decide op).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A kernel module exists and houses `pass3_decide` + `pass3_over_findings` + the
      validity/impact/veto math; per-criterion thresholds are a parameter, not hardcoded.
- [ ] The plan-review `plan_review_decide` op consumes the kernel; an offline test asserts the
      decided partition (blocking/advisory/dropped/indeterminate) is unchanged vs before.
- [ ] No second copy of the decision math remains; any `plan_review` references are thin
      re-exports, not duplicated logic.
- [ ] `make lint` + `make check` + the full test suite pass.
baseline.summary: WS1: Extract Pass-3 deterministic decision into the shared review kernel

## What
The release workflow `.github/workflows/release.yml` publishes `nava-rebar` to PyPI on a `vX.Y.Z` tag but never creates a **GitHub Release**. The v0.2.0/v0.3.0 GitHub Releases were created by hand and that manual step lapsed, so github.com/navapbc/rebar shows **v0.3.0 as Latest** while tags and all three channels (PyPI, Homebrew, MCP Registry) advanced to **v0.6.0**. `docs/releasing.md` does not mention the GitHub Release channel at all.

## Why
GitHub's Releases page is the human-facing "what's the latest version" surface. It being 3 versions stale is misleading to users and contributors.

## Fix (two parts)
- **Backfill (ops):** create GitHub Releases for the missing tags `v0.4.0`, `v0.5.0`, `v0.5.1`, `v0.5.2`, `v0.6.0` with auto-generated notes so `Latest` points at v0.6.0 now.
- **Process (code, via Gerrit):** add a job/step to `.github/workflows/release.yml` that creates a GitHub Release on every `v*` tag push (auto-generated notes, marked latest), and document the channel in `docs/releasing.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] GitHub Releases exist for v0.4.0, v0.5.0, v0.5.1, v0.5.2, v0.6.0 and `gh release list` shows v0.6.0 as `Latest`.
- [ ] `.github/workflows/release.yml` creates a GitHub Release automatically on a `v*` tag push (with `contents: write` on that job and auto-generated notes).
- [ ] `docs/releasing.md` documents the GitHub Release channel/step.
- [ ] Change lands on main through Gerrit (both LLM-Review and Verified votes green).
baseline.summary: Automate GitHub Release creation in release.yml + backfill v0.4.0–v0.6.0

# S10 — external integration tests cover MULTIPLE live providers

## Context / Problem

The external integration suite is the only place rebar exercises a REAL provider end to end, and it runs on ONE provider. `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` gates every live job on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (lines 46, 124, 185, 247; the `OPENAI_API_KEY` fallback appears only in the guard message, not as a matrix arm), and `prompt-eval.yml` likewise. So the provider seam this epic built — first-class Anthropic AND Bedrock, best-effort OpenAI-compatible — has exactly one arm under live test. A Bedrock-only regression (throttling shape, a `cachePoint` envelope change, an inference-profile id that stops resolving, structured output degrading) cannot be caught by CI today. It can only be caught by a human running the gates locally, which is what S7b makes possible and is NOT a substitute for automation.

This is the THIRD of the three permanent provider switches, the other two being the repo config / local environment [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7] and the AWS review bot [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a]. It is deliberately NOT "flip CI to Bedrock": the goal is live-grounded confidence across every provider we hold credentials for, so a MATRIX, not a switch. Flipping the single arm from Anthropic to Bedrock would trade one blind spot for another.

## Approach

Make provider a MATRIX DIMENSION of the external suite rather than an ambient default. Run the live jobs once per credentialed provider — Anthropic, Bedrock, and OpenAI where a key exists — and have each arm SKIP LOUDLY when its credential is absent, so a missing secret is visible as a skip rather than indistinguishable from a green run.

SELECT THE PROVIDER THROUGH `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE`, the layered config-file pointer, rather than bespoke per-arm CI wiring. Each matrix arm writes a small config file setting only `[llm.model_classes]` and points the env var at it. This is the right instrument for three reasons: it is the mechanism rebar already documents for exactly this purpose (`docs/local-dev-env.md`, landed by S7b), it DEEP-MERGES over the discovered config instead of replacing it so the arm overrides provider and model and nothing else, and it means CI DOGFOODS the same override path a developer uses — so the pointer itself gets live coverage on every run instead of being exercised only by hand. The deprecated bare `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is explicitly not the instrument: it cannot express per-class models.

Bedrock authenticates from the AWS credential chain, not an API key, so the matrix cannot key on "an API key secret exists"; the Bedrock arm needs its own credential presence check.

THE S7 PRECEDENT DOES NOT TRANSFER, and an earlier draft of this plan wrongly said it did. S7 [rebar:9249-1569-7be9-4f67] grants an EC2 INSTANCE ROLE reached via IMDS from inside `compose-review-bot-1` (caller identity `assumed-role/rebar-gerrit-instance-role/<instance-id>`). The external suite runs on `ubuntu-latest` (`external-integration.yml:32`) — a GitHub-hosted runner with no instance role and no IMDS path to that host. So the CI arm needs its OWN credential mechanism, named explicitly: OIDC federation — `permissions: id-token: write` plus `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` assuming a dedicated, scoped Bedrock role modelled on S7's POLICY (reuse the policy shape, not the delivery path). Static long-lived keys in a secret are the rejected alternative: they would put a durable AWS credential in CI to save a one-time role setup.

REGION MUST BE SET EXPLICITLY, and the `[llm.model_classes]` file cannot carry it. Bug [rebar:a574] established by measurement that IMDS does NOT supply a region and that Bedrock hard-fails with `NoRegionError` at client construction when none resolves — and that rebar's own `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` alone was insufficient, `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` was also required. The Bedrock arm therefore sets BOTH as job env. This is a real trap, not a hypothetical: it already broke a Bedrock cutover once.

Cost is the real constraint: N providers multiplies the live spend of a suite that already runs weekly. Decide and record whether every provider runs on every trigger, or whether non-default providers run on a reduced cadence or a reduced case subset.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The external suite runs its live jobs for MORE THAN ONE provider, with provider as an explicit
      matrix dimension rather than an ambient default read from whichever key happens to be set.
- [x] Anthropic and Bedrock are both covered. OpenAI is covered where a credential exists, or its
      absence is recorded as a deliberate decision with the reason.
- [x] Each arm selects its provider via `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` pointing at a config file that sets
      ONLY `[llm.model_classes]`, NOT via the deprecated bare `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`. A test or CI assertion
      pins that the override changes provider/model and leaves the rest of the discovered config intact.
- [x] An arm whose credential is ABSENT skips LOUDLY and is distinguishable in the run output from an arm
      that ran and passed — a missing secret must never read as green.
- [x] The Bedrock arm obtains credentials by a NAMED mechanism valid on a GitHub-hosted runner — OIDC
      role assumption via `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` to a dedicated scoped role (the S7 EC2
      instance-role path is NOT reachable from `ubuntu-latest`) — and a test or CI assertion pins that it
      does not silently fall back to `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- [x] The Bedrock arm resolves an AWS region explicitly, setting BOTH `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` and
      `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` as job env, and FAILS LOUDLY with the typed configuration error (per
      [rebar:a574]) when no region resolves — it must never skip silently or read as green.
- [x] The per-trigger COST of the matrix is measured and recorded, and the cadence decision (every
      trigger vs reduced cadence/subset per provider) is stated with its rationale.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code; the default selection is green; the config-read
      and env-drift gates pass.
baseline.summary: S10 — external integration tests cover MULTIPLE live providers, not just Anthropic

# E — Force measurement provenance into `[operator-attested]` evidence

## Context / Problem

`[operator-attested]` (ADR-0043) is a deliberate trust escape hatch, and the criteria guide states its evidence contract three separate times in the same shape:

> treat a criterion … as sufficiently specified when its 'done' evidence lives outside the codebase and is a
> concrete attestation recorded on the ticket (**a change id / vote outcome / timestamp**)

That contract demands provenance of the **attestation event**. It demands nothing about provenance of the **measurement**: which environment it was taken in, under which principal, at what privilege relative to production. The gate asks *"is there an attestation?"* — never *"was it taken somewhere that could have exhibited the failure?"*

Two escapes in the `061c-ecd1-8967-4a76` run went through exactly that hole, both recorded with attestations that satisfied the contract as written:

- **Wrong environment.** Bedrock caching / model-availability measurements taken in account `579718921998` /
  `us-east-2` were recorded as settled fact for work targeting `896586841071` / `us-east-1` (the account named
  by the Terraform backend `rebar-tfstate-896586841071` and by `infra/terraform/`). Caught by a human asking
  "is that this project's account?", not by any gate.
- **Privilege that cannot fail.** Live `bedrock:Converse` calls were offered as validation of a scoped IAM
  grant, made under an identity holding `bedrock:*`. Evidence generated under broader privilege than
  production is structurally unable to fail, so its success carries zero information. Role-scoped
  `simulate-principal-policy` later proved the planned `bedrock:InvokeModel` grant would have `implicitDeny`-ed
  `Converse` in production — feeding a cutover story (`eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a`) that has no fallback.

Neither is a calibration miss. `verified_at_sha` pins the code world completely and the outside world not at all; plan-review runs before the evidence exists, and the completion-verifier accepts attested evidence on trust by design. One gate cannot audit it; the other is designed not to.

## Approach

Do **not** try to make a gate observe the world. Force the measurement's context into the record as text, then let the existing repo-grounded machinery find contradictions in it.

**1. Extend the attested-evidence contract with measurement-provenance fields.** An `[operator-attested]` criterion whose evidence comes from an external system must declare, alongside the existing change-id / vote / timestamp:

- `environment` — the concrete identifier (AWS account id, cluster, tenant, endpoint host);
- `principal` — the identity the measurement ran as;
- `privilege_posture` — one of `production-equivalent` / `broader` / `narrower`, plus a one-line justification
  of why that posture can exhibit the failure the criterion rules out;
- `instrument` — one of `live-call` / `simulation` / `static-analysis`: what KIND of instrument produced the
  measurement. REQUIRED, and checked independently of `privilege_posture` (see 1a for why).

**1a. The declaration's exact textual form and location (pinned — both checks depend on it).** The four fields are NOT a second inline tag. They live on a **continuation line indented under the owning `[operator-attested]` checkbox item**, in one canonical single-line form:

```
- [ ] [operator-attested] <the criterion text, as today>
      provenance: environment=<value>; principal=<value>; privilege_posture=<production-equivalent|broader|narrower>; instrument=<live-call|simulation|static-analysis> — <one-line justification>
```

Rules, stated once so the DET check and the AGENT rubric cannot diverge:

- **Location**: the first line after the checkbox item that is (a) more-indented than the checkbox marker and
  (b) begins with the literal case-insensitive key `provenance:`. It binds to the NEAREST preceding
  `- [ ]` item — that is what associates a declaration with its owning AC.
- **Form**: FOUR `key=value` pairs separated by `;`, keys exactly `environment`, `principal`,
  `privilege_posture`, `instrument`; `privilege_posture` must be one of the three literals
  `production-equivalent` / `broader` / `narrower`; `instrument` must be one of the three literals
  `live-call` / `simulation` / `static-analysis`; the justification follows an em-dash.
- **Why `instrument` is a REQUIRED fourth field, not a nice-to-have.** The parent epic 3147 records this
  as a design decision on its final state: the contract "should capture not only WHERE and UNDER WHAT
  PRIVILEGE a measurement was taken, but what KIND of instrument produced it (simulation / static analysis
  / live call) — because a simulation and a live call are not interchangeable evidence for an authorization
  claim, and the current attestation shape cannot tell them apart." This is escape **2b**, the epic's
  self-described sharpest case: `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` returned a confident and WRONG
  authorization conclusion that only a real from-instance call refuted. `privilege_posture` cannot
  distinguish those two instruments — both can honestly be `production-equivalent` — so without
  `instrument` the epic's sharpest escape stays invisible in the record. Epic 3147 has exactly ONE child
  (this story), so no sibling can deliver it.
- **The justification IS checked, for presence and non-placeholder only.** The text after the em-dash is a
  REQUIRED part of the declaration, not optional prose: the DET check requires it to be present and
  non-placeholder by the same rule as the four values below (empty / `TBD` / `TODO` / `N/A` / `?` / `-` /
  angle-bracketed => treated as ABSENT, so the declaration is incomplete and is flagged). The DET check
  makes NO judgement about whether the justification is *adequate* or *true* — that stays with the
  AGENT-tier criterion, consistent with the DET-vs-AGENT ownership split above. Rationale: a declaration
  whose justification is `— TBD` records the posture without the reasoning that makes it reviewable, which
  is precisely the "confidence outrunning method" failure this story exists to close.
- **Placeholder rejection** (what "non-placeholder" means, concretely): a value is a PLACEHOLDER if, after
  trimming, it is empty, or is one of `TBD` / `TODO` / `N/A` / `?` / `-` (case-insensitive), or is wrapped in
  angle brackets (`<account>`). A placeholder is treated as ABSENT.
- **Consequence for the implementation**: `det_operator_attested.ac_item_lines` returns ONLY `- [` checkbox
  lines and so cannot see a continuation line. The new module therefore needs its own line scanner that
  retains each checkbox item WITH its following continuation lines. It still imports
  `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` from `det_operator_attested` for the "is this item tagged?" decision, so the
  tag matcher stays single-sourced; only the multi-line association is new.

**2. Enforce presence deterministically — zero LLM.** A `det_`-style check mirroring `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py` (which already owns the canonical tag matcher). Presence and shape of the declaration is a string/structure question, so it belongs in the Layer-1 deterministic floor, consistent with this repo's DET-first doctrine. It asserts the fields EXIST and are non-placeholder; it makes no judgement about whether they are *right*.

**3. Let an LLM criterion judge the declaration against repo facts.** Once provenance exists as text, the wrong-account escape becomes a **repo-checkable contradiction**: a reviewer that can read `infra/` can flag "the plan attests measurements from account X, but `infra/terraform/versions.tf`'s backend and the IaC name account Y". That is exactly the kind of grounded probe the gate's strongest criteria (E4, G1G2, T3, T10) already perform — it simply had nothing to read before.

**4. Add the generalized rule as a criterion**, shaped as declaration-completeness rather than world-observation:

> Evidence produced under broader privilege, or in a different environment, than the thing being tested is not
> evidence.

Structurally this is the same shape as T5c's undeclared-access-posture hunt, aimed at **verification plans** instead of designs. It is the world-grounded generalization of E4's "cached knowledge is not a substitute for a probe", and of what mutation testing does to a vacuous test.

**Calibration:** per ADR-0054, it enters **advisory**; corpus replay decides promotion to blocking. It must not ship blocking on first landing.

## Explicitly rejected

- **Making the completion-verifier re-run world measurements.** Expensive, flaky, and recursive — the
  verifier's own credentials carry the same privilege-masking problem, so it would validate using the
  instrument under suspicion. The cheap, honest lever is forcing provenance into the record.
- **Treating "reported green while typecheck was red" as a gate gap.** That is reporting discipline, already
  covered by the orchestration rule that agents report gate output faithfully rather than narrating success.
  Filing it here would be mis-attribution and would dilute this story's scope.
- **Wording changes to the existing contract.** The rule was followed and still failed; emphasis is not the
  defect (see the parent epic's framing).
- **Catching a FALSE declaration (the honest-declaration limit, G6).** This mechanism closes the
  **undeclared** hole, not the **lying** one. `environment` is refutable against repo facts (the IaC
  backend names an account), so a wrong-account declaration becomes a repo-checkable contradiction.
  `principal` and `privilege_posture` are NOT repo-refutable: an author who runs under `bedrock:*` and
  writes `privilege_posture: production-equivalent` is not caught, and nothing in a repo-grounded gate
  could catch them. That class is scoped OUT by ADR-0043's trust boundary and this story INHERITS it
  deliberately rather than claiming to close it. What the fields buy for the non-refutable two is
  narrower and still real: they make the posture claim **explicit, attributable and reviewable by a
  human**, converting a silent omission into a recorded assertion someone can challenge. The story's
  prose must not overclaim beyond that.

## Scope

**Concrete names pinned by this plan** (no placeholders — every proving command below runs as written):

- new criterion id: **`project.measurement-provenance`**
- new deterministic check module: **`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py`**

**In scope**

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py` — a NEW `det_`-style deterministic
  presence/shape check for the provenance fields, a pure leaf alongside `det_operator_attested.py`
  (which keeps sole ownership of the canonical `[operator-attested]` tag matcher; the new module
  IMPORTS that matcher rather than restating it, so "tagged" stays single-sourced).
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` — surface the new lint through `p6_ac_quality`, exactly as
  the sibling operator-attested lint is surfaced. `p6_ac_quality` is ADVISORY and never blocks.
- `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` — define and activate `project.measurement-provenance` at
  `default_posture: "advisory"`, using the SAME overlay mechanism the existing `project.*` criteria use,
  and pinned at **`"exec": "AGENT"`** with a deterministic **`trigger`** so an ~85x-cost AGENT-tier
  criterion does not route on EVERY plan reaching Pass-1: it fires only on plans whose text actually
  carries the `[operator-attested]` tag, i.e. `"trigger": [{"text_all": ["\\[operator-attested\\]"]}]`,
  the same `trigger` MECHANISM `project.engine-layer-enforcement` already uses. (Cited for the trigger
  mechanism ONLY: that criterion is `exec: "1-TURN"`, not AGENT — it is not a precedent for the tier.) The tier is load-bearing, not cosmetic: `AGENT` is the only
  tool-using tier (`registry.AGENT_TIER`, "one tool-using agent loop each"), and the criterion's whole job
  is to READ an in-repo anchor (`infra/terraform/versions.tf`) and compare it to the declared
  `environment`. At `1-TURN` it would have no filesystem tooling and the contradiction probe could not run.
- **`.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md` — a NEW rubric prompt file.** This is
  REQUIRED, not optional: `registry.build_descriptor` resolves every activated non-DET `project.<name>`
  criterion's rubric body via `criterion_prompt_id()` -> `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-<name>.md`,
  and the routing entry's `checklist` is empty for every existing project criterion. Without this file the
  criterion raises `PromptNotFound` and the LLM half of the mechanism cannot load at all. The rubric must
  state the FOUR decision rules in one place: (a) declared `environment` vs the in-repo IaC anchor —
  MISMATCH is a finding; (b) NO comparable anchor in the repo — NO finding (see the no-anchor case);
  (c) `privilege_posture: broader` on a criterion verifying a scoped permission — a finding;
  `production-equivalent` / `narrower` — no finding; **(d) the instrument-vs-authorization rule (escape 2b):
  on a criterion whose claim is an AUTHORIZATION claim (a permission / grant / policy / role / access
  decision), `instrument=simulation` or `instrument=static-analysis` is a finding EVEN WHEN
  `privilege_posture=production-equivalent`, because a simulator answers "is the action NAMED in the
  policy?" and not "which action does the API actually CHECK?"; `instrument=live-call` is no finding.**

**Which component produces which judgement (assigned explicitly, so no rule is left mechanism-less).** The split follows the DET-first doctrine — deterministic where the question is string/structure, LLM only where it needs semantics:

- **The DET check (`det_measurement_provenance.py`) owns**: presence of all four keys, non-placeholder
  values, and membership of the two enum fields in their allowed literal sets. It makes NO judgement about
  whether a value is *correct* or *appropriate* — in particular it does NOT decide whether a criterion makes
  an "authorization claim", which is a semantic question no lexicon can answer reliably.
- **The AGENT-tier criterion `project.measurement-provenance` owns**: rules (a) environment-vs-repo-anchor,
  (b) the no-anchor fallback, (c) the privilege-posture judgement, and (d) the instrument-vs-authorization
  judgement. Rule (d) is LLM work precisely because "is this an authorization claim?" is a reading task.
  Rule (d) is therefore the mechanism that catches escape 2b, and it is advisory on first landing like the
  rest of the criterion. It follows the FILE SHAPE of the three existing
  `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-*.md` files (YAML frontmatter: `schema_version`, `title`,
  `description`, `execution_mode`, `category`) but MUST differ from all three in one load-bearing field:
  they all declare `execution_mode: single_turn` (the tool-less mode), whereas this prompt MUST declare
  **`execution_mode: agentic`**. `registry.py` is explicit that "agentic tooling (filesystem + rebar) is
  granted by a prompt's `execution_mode`, not per criterion-id" — so copying the neighbours verbatim would
  ship a criterion that CANNOT read `infra/terraform/versions.tf`, silently defeating the contradiction
  probe. Every existing code-reading criterion (E4/T1/T10/T5c/G6) carries `execution_mode: agentic`.
- `docs/adr/` — an ADR recording the amended evidence contract, citing ADR-0043 as the shape it changes.
- Tests + corpus/replay fixtures for the ADR-0054 calibration.

**Explicitly OUT of scope — the shipped contract text is NOT edited** (this is the correction that keeps AC-6 honest). The three `OPERATOR-ATTESTED RULE` statements do NOT live in the docs: they are shipped reviewer prompts at `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_F1.md`, `plan_review_E2.md` and `plan_review_E6.md`, with a fourth contract-text site at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py` (coach move `14`). `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is GENERATED from the registry and parity-gated (`registry.validate_criteria_guide`), so it cannot be hand-edited independently. Editing any of those four sites would change the contract for EVERY rebar client — the exact outcome AC-6 forbids. Therefore this story amends the contract in the ADR + the project overlay ONLY, and leaves all four shipped sites byte-identical. Rolling the requirement into the shipped default set is a SEPARATE, later decision that ADR-0054 corpus replay must justify first.

## Testing

- **Deterministic check, unit tier**: an attested criterion WITHOUT provenance fields is flagged; one WITH them
  passes; a placeholder value (`TBD`, `<account>`, empty) is flagged. No LLM in the loop.
- **Contradiction detection, contract tier**: a plan declaring account X against a repo whose Terraform backend
  names account Y produces a finding. **This is the regression test for the actual escape** — build the fixture
  from the real one (`579718921998` declared, `896586841071` in `infra/terraform/versions.tf`).
- **Contrast case**: a plan whose declared environment MATCHES the repo's IaC produces no finding — otherwise
  the criterion is noise on every correctly-attested ticket.
- **Privilege-posture case**: a criterion verifying a *scoped* permission while declaring
  `privilege_posture: broader` is flagged; `production-equivalent` or `narrower` is not. This is the
  `bedrock:*` escape in miniature.
- **No-anchor fallback case (T8)**: a plan whose declared `environment` has NO comparable in-repo anchor —
  a repo with no Terraform/IaC backend, or a non-AWS identifier (cluster / tenant / endpoint host) with no
  in-repo counterpart — produces NO finding. Absence of an anchor is NOT a contradiction; the criterion
  fires only on an actual declared-vs-repo MISMATCH. Without this the criterion would nag every repo that
  has no IaC.
- **Grandfathering case (T4)**: an EXISTING `[operator-attested]` criterion predating this contract (no
  provenance fields at all) is surfaced as an advisory coaching string and does NOT block a claim or a
  close. This is the regression test that the contract change ships without a migration break.
- **Calibration**: corpus replay per ADR-0054 measuring false-positive rate before any promotion from advisory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] an `[operator-attested]` criterion lacking any of `environment` / `principal` / `privilege_posture` /
      `instrument` is flagged by a DETERMINISTIC check (no LLM), and a test asserts the check makes no
      judgement about correctness — only presence, non-placeholder shape, and (for the two enum fields)
      membership of the allowed literal set
- [x] the criterion rides the `.rebar/` project overlay, not the shipped default criteria set:
      `grep -rn 'project.measurement-provenance' src/rebar/` prints nothing (exit 1), while the overlay
      carries BOTH the definition and the activation — asserted structurally (not by line-counting, which
      a compact JSON layout would defeat):
      `python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('.rebar/criteria_routing.json'));c='project.measurement-provenance';assert c in d['plan_review'];assert 'plan_review' in d['activate'][c];assert d['plan_review'][c]['default_posture']=='advisory';assert d['plan_review'][c]['exec']=='AGENT'"`
      exits 0 — no other rebar client gains a new BLOCKING criterion
- [x] the shipped contract text is untouched, proving no cross-client behaviour change:
      `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_F1.md
      src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_E2.md src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_E6.md

## Summary
Two related gaps in the workflow reference-linter (`workflow/lint_refs.py`), surfaced reviewing the code-review gate (epic b744 / WS3):
1. `check_string` is routed over a step's `with:` values + the `if:` guard, but NOT over a `batch:` step's `criteria[].when` expressions (lint_refs.py ~378-407). So a typo'd `${{ steps.X.outputs.include_typo }}` in a batch criterion's `when:` is NEVER name-checked — it only surfaces at runtime.
2. `_output_fields_map` (lint_refs.py ~547) reads only `schema.properties.keys()`, ignoring `patternProperties`. So an output whose dynamic keys live in `patternProperties` (e.g. `overlay_union_output`'s `include_<overlay>` keys, or `plan_review_assemble_criteria_output`'s `include_<ID>`) is invisible to the reference check.

## Impact
The code-review gate (gates/code-review.yaml) leans on 22 `${{ steps.triggers/union.outputs.include_<overlay> }}` refs in batch `when:` clauses; none are linted. A typo would pass `rebar workflow validate` and only fail/misbehave at runtime (silently skipping an overlay). Pre-existing (plan-review's include_<ID> refs have the same blind spot); not introduced by b744.

## Reproduction Steps
1. In a v3 workflow, add a batch criterion `{prompt: X, when: '${{ steps.s.outputs.nonexistent_key }}'}`.
2. `rebar workflow validate <file>` → passes (no 'output not produced' finding), despite the bogus ref.
Expected: the linter flags the unknown output ref (as it does for `with:`/`if:`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `lint_refs` walks `batch.criteria[].when` expressions through `check_string` (same as `if:`/`with:`).
- [ ] `_output_fields_map` consults `patternProperties` (a ref matching a pattern is considered produced), so dynamic-keyed outputs aren't falsely flagged AND a non-matching typo IS flagged.
- [ ] A test: a typo'd batch `when:` ref fails `workflow validate`; a valid `include_<overlay>` ref passes.

## Notes
Discovered reviewing WS3 (8855) of the code-review epic (b744). Not fixed there (linter is shared infra; out of scope for the gate). Workaround: the code-review gate's offline test exercises the real `when:` resolution, catching typos at test time.
baseline.summary: Workflow linter doesn't name-check batch.criteria[].when refs + is patternProperties-blind

Same class as [rebar:a371-fb42-32c5-48bd] (an `importorskip`-masked test that is broken the moment its extra IS installed). Found while running the full unit suite with the `[ui]` extra installed to verify a371's fix.

`tests/unit/test_path_injection_guards.py:147` `test_rerun_502_body_has_no_exception_detail` builds a fake request as:

    req = types.SimpleNamespace(
        app=types.SimpleNamespace(state=types.SimpleNamespace(config=cfg)),
        query_params={"token": "tok", "change": "12345"},
    )
    resp = asyncio.run(rerun(req))

`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:101` reads `request.headers.get(TOKEN_HEADER, "").strip()`, and the fake has no `headers`, so the test dies with:

    AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'headers'

Reproduced deterministically at origin/main (c89a2ddcc4), py3.12, with `--extra ui` installed (which pulls fastapi):

    pytest tests/unit/test_path_injection_guards.py -q -p no:randomly
      -> 1 failed, 54 passed

Line 148 is `pytest.importorskip("fastapi")  # the reviewbot extra; absent in the lean CI suite`, so the lean CI suite skips it and the breakage is invisible. As with a371, the test reads as covering the `/rerun` 502-body containment barrier while providing no coverage in any environment where the extra is present.

Presumably the fake request stopped matching `app.rerun` when header-token auth was added to that handler; the fake needs a `headers` mapping (and whatever else the current handler reads).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_path_injection_guards.py` passes with the reviewbot/ui extra
      installed
- [ ] The test still asserts the same containment barrier (502 body carries no exception or
      stack-trace detail) -- do not weaken it to make it pass
- [ ] Sweep the other `importorskip`-guarded tests for the same rot, since none of them run in
      the lean CI suite
baseline.summary: importorskip-masked: test_rerun_502_body_has_no_exception_detail fails when the reviewbot extra IS installed

## Context / Problem
probe-rebar.sh accumulated stale assertions (08ce: 3 stale asserts against removed flags/keysets). Its missing 'set -e' is DELIBERATE harness design (continue past failures, report all) — a naive port or hardening pass would break it.

## Approach
Port to a Python probe harness (scripts/probe_rebar.py) preserving the continue-on-failure design (collect results, report all, exit non-zero if any failed — the same contract, now explicit). Assertion-parity review required: every current assertion enumerated and carried over or retired with a reason (the 08ce class came from silent drift). Do NOT add set -e semantics.

Shell deletion and consumer re-pointing happen in the SAME change, after the side-by-side parity run: every consumer that hard-wires the shell path is re-pointed to the Python entry point in this change, so CI and the anti-rot gate track the new harness atomically.

## Scope
- scripts/probe-rebar.sh -> scripts/probe_rebar.py (port; the shell path is retained as a 7-line transitional exec shim because gerrit-verify.yaml executes from MAIN's workflow definition, whose golden-path step still invokes the shell path until this change lands — discovered on patchset 1, Verified-1 exit 127; deletion is follow-up d772-6007-5d04-4101)
- Consumers re-pointed in the same change (enumerated by grep for 'probe-rebar'):
  - .github/workflows/test.yml:128 — 'bash scripts/probe-rebar.sh </dev/null' -> python invocation
  - .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml:209 — same re-point
  - .github/workflows/external-integration.yml:54 — comment mentioning the path; update wording
  - tests/unit/test_probe_wired_into_ci.py — _PROBE_JOBS asserts substring 'scripts/probe-rebar.sh' in golden-path jobs; update the pinned substring to the Python entry point so the anti-rot gate keeps guarding
  - docs/releasing.md:401,405,407 — invocation examples -> Python equivalents
  - CHANGELOG.md + docs/experiments corpus jsonl are historical records — NOT touched.
- Assertion inventory table in the change description (commit message).

## Testing
Self-test: inject one failing probe -> harness continues, reports it, exits non-zero. Parity: run both harnesses against the same build before deletion, identical pass/fail verdict per assertion. tests/unit/test_probe_wired_into_ci.py green against the updated substring.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Python harness replaces the shell probe with continue-on-failure preserved.
- [x] Assertion-parity table: every shell assertion mapped to ported/retired-with-reason.
- [x] Side-by-side run shows identical verdicts; shell path reduced to a transitional exec shim (full deletion tracked in d772-6007-5d04-4101, required because gerrit-verify.yaml executes from main's workflow definition) with ALL enumerated consumers (workflows, anti-rot test, docs) re-pointed to the Python entry point.

## 2026-08-08 resolved-report consolidation

Resolved report: `08ce-0e74-07f6-414e` (the three stale shell-probe assertions were incorporated into this port).

Fresh resolution experiment on current `origin/main`: `python scripts/probe_rebar.py` ran the full isolated end-to-end CLI probe and reported `PROBE RESULT: 140 passed, 0 failed`. This re-exercises the exact edit/tag, priority, and show/list projection assertions from the original report, so none remains stale.

## Why

PyPI/wheel installs have no rebar git checkout, so live-git SHA resolution
(story 1) yields version-only there. Baking the release commit SHA at build time
gives consistent gate-code provenance across dev/editable and PyPI installs
(epic jira-reb-596).

## What

- Add `hatch_build.py` at the **repo root** implementing `BuildHookInterface`; it
  runs `git rev-parse --short HEAD` at wheel/sdist build and writes a generated,
  git-ignored `src/rebar/_build_info.py` (`COMMIT = "<sha>"`, or `COMMIT = None`
  when built outside a git tree).
- Register it in `pyproject.toml` with a `[tool.hatch.build.hooks.custom]` stanza
  (WITHOUT this, hatchling silently skips the hook and the baked SHA never ships).
- Add `src/rebar/_build_info.py` to `.gitignore` AND to the `artifacts` glob under
  `[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]` (git-based source discovery drops git-ignored
  files from the wheel otherwise — the baked SHA would never reach PyPI).
- Extend the story-1 resolver fallback to **live-git-first, build-baked-second,
  omit-last**: with no live checkout, import `_build_info.COMMIT`.
- Keep package version STATIC (`pyproject.toml` `version`); do NOT adopt hatch-vcs.

## Scope

Build-time SHA capture + fallback wiring only. Depends on story 1's resolver.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `hatch_build.py` writes `src/rebar/_build_info.py` with the build-time short
      SHA; a non-git build writes `COMMIT = None` (graceful).
- [ ] `[tool.hatch.build.hooks.custom]` is registered AND `_build_info.py` is in
      the wheel `artifacts` glob and `.gitignore`.
- [ ] Resolver falls back to the baked SHA on a non-git install, still preferring
      the live checkout SHA when one exists.
- [ ] Package version remains static (no hatch-vcs).
- [ ] Tests: baked-fallback resolves the SHA when live git is absent; version-only
      when both absent; a built wheel actually contains `_build_info.py` with a SHA.
baseline.summary: Bake release commit SHA at build time for non-git installs

# WS8 — Harden Gerrit auth (replace DEVELOPMENT_BECOME_ANY_ACCOUNT with GitHub OAuth)

## Why
The live Gerrit (`rebar.solutions.navateam.com`, 3.14) runs `auth.type =
DEVELOPMENT_BECOME_ANY_ACCOUNT` — a dev-only mode where anyone can impersonate any account (no
real IdP). It CANNOT be the sole gate on production GitHub `main` (WS7) until real auth is in
place. **Confirmed strategy (2026-07-01): GitHub OAuth via the `gerrit-oauth-provider` plugin
(GitHub backend), no reverse-proxy org gate** — access curated via a short account roster + Gerrit
ACLs. Precedent: GerritHub authenticates its whole user base this way; the plugin is actively
maintained (3.13.x, tracks the Gerrit release train). Blocks WS7.

## Config (the target state)
`infra/compose/gerrit.config`:
```ini
[auth]
    type = OAUTH
    gitBasicAuthPolicy = HTTP        # bots + git-over-HTTP keep working via HTTP passwords
[plugin "gerrit-oauth-provider-github-oauth"]
    root-url = "https://github.com/"
    client-id = "<GitHub OAuth App client id>"     # non-secret; from SSM
```
`etc/secure.config` (secrets, NOT committed — materialized from SSM like the S5 deploy key):
```ini
[plugin "gerrit-oauth-provider-github-oauth"]
    client-secret = "<GitHub OAuth App client secret>"
```
Plus: install the pinned `gerrit-oauth-provider` jar into `$GERRIT_SITE/plugins`, and remove ALL
`DEVELOPMENT_*` auth.

## Deliverables — split by access boundary
### In-repo (committed; applied on a fresh redeploy) — DELIVERABLE THIS SESSION
- A runbook `infra/runbooks/gerrit-auth-hardening.md`: the full procedure (OAuth App, plugin,
  gerrit.config/secure.config, SSM params, redeploy, bot HTTP-password provisioning, account
  migration, verification, rollback).
- `gerrit-oauth-provider` pinned-jar provenance in `infra/gerrit/plugins/README.md` +
  install-plugins scaffolding.
- The `[auth]` block comment in `infra/compose/gerrit.config` points at the runbook + WS8 (the
  live flip to `type = OAUTH` lands with the plugin+secrets chain, per the runbook — flipping it
  in isolation would break a fresh Gerrit boot).

### Access-gated (needs org admin + working AWS) — HANDOFF
- Create the **GitHub OAuth App** on `navapbc` (callback `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/oauth`)
  → client-id/secret. (Needs GitHub org admin via the web UI; this session's token lacks `admin:org`.)
- Put client-id/secret in **SSM** under the Gerrit secret prefix; add the params to `infra/terraform/ssm.tf`.
- **Apply to the live host** (AWS SSM/SSH — this session's AWS session is EXPIRED): install the
  plugin, seed the OAuth config into the live `site/etc/gerrit.config` + `secure.config`, remove
  become-any-account, restart Gerrit.
- **Provision bot credentials BEFORE cutover**: give the `rebar-review-bot` service account an HTTP
  password (dev-mode required none), so its git/REST access survives the auth change.

## Acceptance Criteria
### In-repo (this session)
- [ ] `infra/runbooks/gerrit-auth-hardening.md` documents the complete GitHub-OAuth hardening procedure (OAuth App → plugin → gerrit.config/secure.config → SSM → redeploy → bot passwords → account migration → verify → rollback).
- [ ] The `gerrit-oauth-provider` jar is pinned + provenance-documented (plugins/README.md) and wired into the plugin install path.
- [ ] `infra/compose/gerrit.config` `[auth]` comment points at the runbook + WS8 (records that the live flip to OAUTH lands with the plugin+secrets chain).
### Live (access-gated)
- [ ] GitHub OAuth App created; client-id/secret in SSM; `ssm.tf` params added.
- [ ] Live Gerrit switched to `auth.type = OAUTH` (become-any-account removed); Gerrit restarts healthy; a human logs in via GitHub OAuth.
- [ ] `rebar-review-bot` has an HTTP password; its REST/git access verified post-cutover.

## Dependencies
- Blocks WS7 (the Gerrit-only cutover must not precede real auth).
- Live steps need `navapbc` GitHub org admin + working AWS access to the Gerrit host (d251 infra).
baseline.summary: WS8: Harden Gerrit auth (GitHub OAuth, replace DEVELOPMENT_BECOME_ANY_ACCOUNT)

# S1 — extract the retry/error cluster out of `transport.py` (behaviour-preserving)

## Context / Problem

Split out of [rebar:b586-2fda-8a15-4260], whose plan hit BLOCK ten times. The round-by-round record is on that ticket; the structural finding is that it carried TWO independent changes — a mechanical relocation and a new 429 policy — and every round found new surface because a fix to one re-opened the other. Rounds 6-7 were about THIS half's mechanics; rounds 1, 4, 8, 9, 10 were about the policy half (now S2). Splitting is the same move that turned J9's eight BLOCKs into a first-try PASS as J10.

This story is the mechanical half and is **forced by the module-size cap, not by taste**: `transport.py` is **789 lines on `origin/main`** against the LOCKED 800-line cap (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), so there are ELEVEN lines of headroom and the 429 policy cannot be added in place. (Recording the measurement because this file's LOC has been misquoted twice in epic e369: the earlier "792 vs 789" disagreement was a pre-/post-9263 base difference, and now that 9263 is merged both readings agree at 789.)

## Approach

**Relocate, do not redesign.** Move the retry/error cluster from `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` into a new `adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py`, changing no behaviour. The cluster is `_connection_retry_exceptions`, `_jira_http_error_types`, `_as_backend_http_error`, `TlsVerificationError`, `_tls_verification_error`, and `_with_connection_retry`.

**`TlsVerificationError` MUST move with the rest.** `_tls_verification_error` returns it, so leaving the class behind in `transport.py` makes `retry.py` import from `transport.py` while `transport.py` imports `_with_connection_retry` from `retry.py` — a circular import. The class and its factory are one unit.

**Re-export from `transport.py` so existing importers keep working.** `test_jira_dc_config_settings.py` imports `TlsVerificationError` from the transport module; that test must pass UNEDITED, because editing it to chase the move would convert a regression signal into a rubber stamp.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py` — NEW; the moved cluster.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` — cluster deleted,
  cluster imported, names re-exported.

**NOT in scope:** any behaviour change, and specifically any 429 / `Retry-After` handling — that is S2. If this story changes what any call does, it has failed.

## Testing

The oracle for a pure relocation is that the EXISTING suite passes unedited — a new test asserting the code moved would only restate the diff.

* `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` DC transport tests pass with NO edits.
* `test_jira_dc_config_settings.py` passes with NO edits (proves the re-export works).
* The module-size gate passes, and `transport.py` is measurably smaller.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `retry.py` exists and contains all six named members, and `transport.py` no longer defines
      them
- [ ] `TlsVerificationError` lives in `retry.py` WITH `_tls_verification_error`, and a test or a
      clean `python -c "import ..."` proves there is no circular import between the two modules
- [ ] `transport.py` re-exports the moved names, and `test_jira_dc_config_settings.py` passes
      **with zero edits to that file** — asserted by `git diff --exit-code` on it
- [ ] the full DC transport unit suite passes with zero test edits; if any test needed an edit,
      this story is not behaviour-preserving and must be reworked rather than the test adjusted
- [ ] `transport.py` is under the 800-line cap with headroom for S2, and the measured before/after
      line counts are recorded on this ticket
- [ ] NO diff hunk changes control flow, retry counts, backoff values, or exception types — a
      reviewer can confirm the change is a move by reading the diff alone
baseline.summary: S1 — extract the retry/error cluster out of transport.py (behaviour-preserving)

# BUG: code-review vote renders a fail-closed DET detector match as "BLOCK — finding / 0 blocking issues"

## Reproduction Steps
1. Push a change touching a file that a fail-closed DET detector (gitleaks secret-detection) matches on.
2. The 4-pass LLM gate returns PASS (no LLM blocking findings), but apply_failclosed forces BLOCK.
3. The Gerrit vote is LLM-Review-1 tagged "[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]" with message "rebar code review found 0 blocking issue(s):" — and NO robot comment names the match.

Root cause: src/rebar/llm/code_review/detectors.py:123-151 apply_failclosed sets
verdict["verdict"]="BLOCK" on a match but never appends the match to verdict["blocking"]
(it only records it under coverage.security_detectors). review_bot/adapter.py then counts
len(verdict["blocking"])==0 and renders "found 0 blocking issue(s)"; adapter.py:183-191 tags
it "finding". voter.py posts only the message. So a genuine detector block is unnamed and
non-actionable — and a REAL leaked secret is hidden from the author identically.

Expected: a fail-closed detector match is surfaced as a named, counted blocking finding.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] apply_failclosed appends a kernel-shaped finding (criterion + file + remediation hint) to verdict["blocking"] when blocking_enabled and there is a match; the finalize invariant holds.
- [ ] Gerrit message reads "found N blocking issue(s):" (N>=1) and names the match; review_code CLI/MCP render it too.
- [ ] RED-first regression tests: test_failclosed_forces_block_on_detector_match asserts verdict["blocking"] non-empty + names the criterion; an adapter-seam test asserts the message never reads "found 0".
- [ ] make lint + code-review suites green; commit carries a rebar-ticket trailer.
baseline.summary: BUG: code-review vote renders a DET detector match as 'BLOCK — finding / 0 blocking issues'

baseline.description:
## Why

Surfaced by the plan-v4 divergence-grading calibration (story doggish-nonorganic-tsetsefly), from the same plan-v3 sidecar corpus (18,085 verified findings).

`undecomposed` fires on **12 of 18,085 findings (0.07%)** — two orders of magnitude below every other axis — while holding full HARD-OVERRIDE power (any non-none grade floors impact at 0.85 and auto-blocks). Comparison across the seven axes on plan-v3:

| axis | non-none |
|---|---|
| vague_directive | 31.03% |
| ac_unverifiable | 15.79% |
| internal_conflict | 10.17% |
| divergent_implementation | 7.72% (fixed in plan-v4) |
| dod_uncertifiable | 5.36% |
| irreversible_without_rationale | 1.97% |
| **undecomposed** | **0.07%** |

Two candidate explanations, both worth confirming before touching anything:

1. **Working as intended / correctly suppressed.** The axis's own prompt text says a deterministic
   signal (G5) already suppresses false 'flat plan' findings on tickets that HAVE children, and
   most reviewed tickets do have children. If so, 0.07% is the correct residual and the axis
   simply has a narrow true population — no change needed, just documentation.
2. **Mis-specified / unreachable.** The grading instruction may be so hedged ('Grade ONLY a
   genuine gap') that verifiers never assign it, in which case a real class of flat-plan defects
   is scoring 0.0 the same way the divergence class did before plan-v4.

## What

Investigate, do not pre-commit to a fix:

- Pull the 12 firing findings from the corpus and read them — are they genuine flat-plan defects,
  and did they block?
- Determine how often the G5 deterministic suppressor fires, to separate 'correctly suppressed'
  from 'never assigned'.
- Look for the inverse population: findings whose TEXT describes an undecomposed/flat plan but
  which scored the axis `none` (the same ~90%-missed analysis that motivated plan-v4's
  divergence grading).
- Only if (2) is confirmed, propose a change — and note that any impact-model shape change costs
  an IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION bump that closes the plan-v4 cohort, so batch it per ADR 0054 §4.

## Testing / Verification

This is an analysis ticket: the deliverable is a recorded finding, so verification is read-only replay over the persisted sidecar corpus plus source reads. No code changes, no new eval suite, no bulk re-review sweep (ADR 0054 §4).

- Locate the corpus and count its records with an asserting command, e.g.
  `test -n "$(find .rebar -name '*sidecar*' -o -name '*.jsonl')" && echo CORPUS_PRESENT || echo CORPUS_ABSENT`,
  then a `python3 -c` record count over whatever sidecar/journal path is found. If no corpus is
  reachable from this checkout, that absence is itself recorded as a limit and the analysis is
  scoped to source-level evidence.
- Read the axis definition and the G5 suppressor at source:
  `rg -n 'undecomposed|G5' src/rebar/llm/` — the root must be `src/rebar/llm/`, not
  `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/`, because `decide.py` and `verify_models.py` live under the
  sibling `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/`. Files to read: `plan_review/det_floor.py`,
  `plan_review/det_lint.py`, `plan_review/pass1.py`, `review_kernel/decide.py`,
  `review_kernel/verify_models.py`, and the two reviewer prompts.
- Distinguish the TWO separate 'undecomposed' mechanisms before measuring anything: (a) the
  PASS-1 finder-side deterministic veto `veto_undecomposed_g5` (`plan_review/det_lint.py`,
  invoked from `plan_review/pass1.py`), which suppresses G5-criterion FINDER findings on tickets
  that have children; and (b) the review_kernel VERIFIER severity axis `undecomposed`

  report the count of matching findings whose `undecomposed` axis grade is `none`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Method is ADR-0054-compliant: driven off the persisted sidecar corpus at zero marginal LLM
