# live_jira_dc harness exhausts Jira DC's 10-PAT-per-user cap

## Context / Problem

The live Jira DC harness tier dies at SETUP, so no live acceptance evidence can be produced at all — and every remaining story in epic e369 (notably J11, the epic's headline live proof) runs on this harness. Reproduced across two independent CI runs (30604756524, 30623000498), same signature:

    ERROR at setup of test_add_label_and_the_links_surface_against_a_real_instance
    AssertionError: PAT creation failed: 403
      {'exception': 'com.atlassian.pats.exception.UserTokenLimitExceededException',
       'error': "You can't create more than 10 tokens."}

`jira_dc_pat` (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py:355`) is declared `@pytest.fixture` with NO scope, so it is FUNCTION-scoped: every test that requests it mints a brand new Personal Access Token via `POST /rest/pat/latest/tokens` and never deletes it. Jira Data Center caps a user at 10 PATs. Consumption therefore grows as O(tests) while the budget is fixed at 10.

Two properties make this expensive to diagnose, and both are reasons to fix it properly rather than by trimming test count:

* **It mis-attributes.** The ERROR surfaces at setup of a test in `test_transport.py` — a module
  nobody touched — because that is merely the test that happened to run once the budget was
  spent. The cause is session-wide.
* **It looks flaky but is deterministic.** The fixture mints with `expirationDuration=1`, so
  tokens self-clear after a day. Whether a run fails depends on how recently the instance was
  used, not on chance.

## Approach

**Make `jira_dc_pat` SESSION-scoped**, turning PAT consumption from O(tests) into O(1).

This is the fix that scales, and scaling is the actual requirement: J11 adds substantially more live tests to this tier, so any fix whose budget is still proportional to test count merely moves the cliff. Every consumer needs only *a* valid PAT — no test in this tier asserts per-token behaviour (verified: the fixture's only assertions are on `rawToken`, and its sole consumers use it as a bearer credential) — so one token per run is behaviourally identical to one per test.

**Rejected: per-test teardown via `DELETE /rest/pat/latest/tokens/{id}`.** It preserves per-test isolation that nothing here needs, costs an API call per test, and — decisively — it is not verified to be implementable: the creation response is only asserted to carry `rawToken`, and whether it also returns an `id` has NOT been confirmed against a live instance. Choosing it would make the fix depend on an unverified response field. Session scope depends on nothing new.

**Complementary: sweep leftover `rebar-j5-harness-*` tokens at session start**, mirroring `_leaked_scratch_projects()` (`conftest.py:181`), which already does exactly this for scratch PROJECTS left by interrupted runs. Session scope alone fixes consumption WITHIN a run; it does not help a run that starts against an instance already holding 10 tokens from a crashed predecessor. Both layers are required for the ACs below, and they address different failures.

The sweep uses the same defensive posture the project fixture already establishes: read the token list from its direct REST endpoint and, if it cannot be enumerated, **return empty rather than invent a failure** — a sweep that cannot see is not evidence of cleanliness, and the harness-readiness assertion remains authoritative for usability. Deleting a leftover token is likewise best-effort: a failed delete is reported, not fatal, because the session-scoped mint that follows is the real test of whether headroom exists.

**Raw `urllib` REST is correct here and is not a divergence from "never hand-roll REST".** That rule governs the DC *transport*, which must go through `pycontribs/jira`. This conftest deliberately speaks raw REST v2 with stdlib `urllib` only (see its module docstring) so the harness does not depend on the client library the harness exists to validate. The sweep reuses the existing `_request` helper.

## Scope

- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py` — change `jira_dc_pat` to `scope="session"`,
  document the 10-token cap in its docstring, and add a `_leaked_harness_tokens()` helper plus
  its invocation from the existing session-scoped `_jira_dc_harness_ready` autouse fixture.
- `tests/unit/` — unit coverage for the sweep helper's parsing and its
  cannot-enumerate/failed-delete degradation, exercised against a stubbed `_request` so it runs
  in the normal (non-live) tier.

No production `src/rebar` code changes: this is a test-harness defect.

## Testing

The live tier cannot run on this workstation (its base image is linux/amd64 only and this is Apple Silicon — `tests/external/live_jira_dc/README.md:54-73`), so the split is deliberate:

* **Unit (runs everywhere, in CI on every change):** the sweep helper returns the leftover
  token names/ids from a well-formed list response; returns EMPTY when the endpoint errors or
  returns a non-list (the cannot-enumerate path); ignores tokens not carrying the
  `rebar-j5-harness-` prefix (so it never deletes a human's unrelated PAT — the failure mode
  that would make this fix worse than the bug); and does not raise when a DELETE fails.
* **Live (GitHub Actions `jira DC harness smoke` job):** the acceptance evidence. The full
  `tests/external/live_jira_dc` suite completes with no `UserTokenLimitExceededException`.
  Because session scope makes consumption O(1), one token is consumed regardless of test count,
  which is what supplies headroom rather than a coincidence of the current count.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `jira_dc_pat` is `scope="session"`, verified by reading the fixture declaration, so a run
      mints exactly ONE PAT no matter how many tests request it
- [ ] the full `tests/external/live_jira_dc` suite runs in the GitHub Actions
      `jira DC harness smoke` job with ZERO `UserTokenLimitExceededException`, confirmed by
      reading that job's log — not the overall run status
- [ ] headroom is structural, not coincidental: because consumption is O(1) in test count, the
      run above passes with MORE live tests present than the count that first triggered the cap
- [ ] a leftover `rebar-j5-harness-*` token from a crashed run is deleted at session start, so
      it does not break the next run — covered by a unit test against a stubbed `_request`
- [ ] the sweep never deletes a token lacking the `rebar-j5-harness-` prefix, asserted by unit
      test
- [ ] the sweep degrades safely: a non-200/non-list list response yields an empty result rather
      than an exception, and a failed DELETE does not abort the session — both unit-tested
- [ ] the 10-token cap and the session-scope decision are documented in the `jira_dc_pat`
      docstring, since the cap is a non-obvious Jira DC limit
baseline.summary: live_jira_dc harness exhausts Jira DC's 10-PAT-per-user cap; jira_dc_pat is function-scoped

# Hard-remove the deprecated `resolved_statuses` config keys

Removal half of task [rebar:549c-032f-6cb0-4258], which decided DEPRECATE-not-remove and executed the deprecation half (change 1670). It was blocked on operator sign-off because removing a documented operator-facing config key is a user-visible surface change.

**OPERATOR SIGN-OFF IS GIVEN** (2026-08-12, verbatim: "delete the old config settings is approved"; provenance recorded in the first comment on this ticket). This is the fourth change of the pre-1.0 breaking window that also landed tickets 97d4 and 6cc4.

## Background

`jira.resolved_statuses` fed the inbound absence probe (`adapters/jira/probe.py:: _resolve_resolved_statuses`), reachable as recently as shipped v0.10.1; the probe went with task f020 and 549c removed the write-only transport plumbing. Both keys are now **inert** — accepted, coerced and validated, read by nothing. Resolved/unresolved discrimination is outbound-owned (ADR 0028), so there is **no replacement setting**: operators simply delete the line.

## Plan (line numbers against origin/main @ abf3817187)

### 1. `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — delete the fields and coercers

* Delete `ReconcilerConfig.resolved_statuses` (L465) with its 5-line DEPRECATED comment
  block and `# read-via:` marker (L460-464).
* Delete `JiraConfig.resolved_statuses` (L489) with its 5-line comment block and
  `# read-via:` marker (L484-488).
* Delete the two `_as_str_list` coercer entries: `reconciler` section L696, `jira`
  section L706.
* Check `_as_str_list` for other callers; if this removes its last one, delete the helper
  too rather than leave a dead coercer.

### 2. `src/rebar/_deprecations.py` — swap deprecation rows for tombstones

* Delete the two `_scheduled("cfg", …)` rows (L106-107) and the 549c comment block that
  introduces them (L91-105).
* Append a historical NOTE in the "removed scheduled surfaces" block recording
  **operator-approved removal, 2026-08-12**, matching the wording pattern of the
  neighbouring 97d4 / 6cc4 NOTEs.
* Add to `_TOMBSTONE_REGISTRY`, in the existing `cfg, warn` group:
  `_tomb("cfg", "jira.resolved_statuses", "", "warn")` and
  `_tomb("cfg", "reconciler.resolved_statuses", "", "warn")`.
* Add the auto-derived env twins to the `env, warn` group:
  `_tomb("env", "REBAR_JIRA_RESOLVED_STATUSES", "", "warn")` and
  `_tomb("env", "REBAR_RECONCILER_RESOLVED_STATUSES", "", "warn")` — env names derive
  generically as `REBAR_<SECTION>_<KEY>` (config.py L273), so both were real usable inputs.
  This follows the `REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ENABLED` precedent.

**Tombstone class is `warn`, deliberately.** `_deprecations.py` codifies the rule: `error` for an operationally load-bearing removed input (store location, write/sync gate, auth, security, lifecycle policy), `warn` for an inert one. These keys are inert — nothing reads them and the behaviour they configured no longer exists — so a still-set key must not abort the command. This matches every comparable cfg precedent (`code_health.enabled`, `code_health.analyzers`, `reconciler.lock_backend`, `reconciler.lock_max_retries`). It deliberately does NOT follow 6cc4's `error` choice for `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`, whose stated rationale — "silently ignoring a still-set model id would quietly change which model every operation runs" — is a load-bearing argument that does not transfer to an inert key.

### 3. Tests

* `tests/unit/test_config_resolved_statuses_deprecation.py` — the whole module asserts the
  deprecation semantics that no longer exist. Replace it with a removal module (mirroring
  6cc4's `test_llm_model_env_deprecation.py` -> `test_llm_model_env_removal.py` rename)
  asserting: the fields are gone from both dataclasses; a config still carrying either key
  loads and warns rather than raising; the key is dropped from the parsed config; and the
  env twins warn.
* `tests/scripts/test_check_config_reads_heldout.py` L318-331 — the docstring and the
  `assert all("resolved_statuses" in r for r in reports)` assertion both encode the
  now-deleted `# read-via:` markers. Retarget to whatever the config-read gate reports once
  the markers are gone (expected: an empty report for these keys).
* `tests/unit/test_deprecation_registry.py` L41 — comment references the 549c rows; update.

### 4. Docs

* `docs/config.md` — delete the `resolved_statuses` line (L285) and its 9-line DEPRECATED
  comment block (L276-284) from the `[tool.rebar.jira]` sample.
* `docs/user-guide.md` — delete the `resolved_statuses` row (L510) from the DC settings table.
* `docs/release-notes.md` + `CHANGELOG.md` — add the removal entry alongside the sibling
  pre-1.0 pass #3 entries.

### 5. Gates

Run the full local CI gate set from the worktree venv: the ten `check_*` gates, the six generators (regenerate all generated registries and commit the diff), and CI's pytest invocation. Two specific risks: the **config-read gate** may flag orphaned `# read-via:` bookkeeping once the markers go, and the **module-size gate** — `_config_schema.py` sits at 798/800, so this removal should pull it down; verify it does rather than assuming.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] operator sign-off for the removal is recorded on this ticket
- [x] both schema fields and their `_as_str_list` coercers are deleted
- [x] both keys are tombstoned warn-class, so an existing config still loads with a warning
- [x] the auto-derived env twins are tombstoned warn-class
- [x] the deprecation registry rows are gone and a historical NOTE records the
      operator-approved 2026-08-12 removal
- [x] the `# read-via:` markers are gone and the heldout marker test matches
- [x] neither key is documented any more
- [x] all ten `check_*` gates, the six generators, `make lint`, `make typecheck` and CI's
      pytest invocation are green; `Verified +1` before close
baseline.summary: Remove the deprecated resolved_statuses config keys (needs operator sign-off)

Ticket bb9b landed the contributor-triggerable re-review (comment `recheck-review` on a change; merged as Gerrit change 1243, live in production), and docs/review-policy.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and the review-bot runbook were updated with it — but the packaged guide was missed: lines 112–114 still tell the contributor a coverage-gap BLOCK requires "a maintainer re-triggers; re-pushing the same commit or pinging the maintainer is the move". That is now wrong (self-service exists) and it is the single most discoverable surface, so the stale text actively misdirects contributors to ping maintainers.

## What

baseline.description:
## Report

`rebar transition <id> in_progress closed` can print an error to stderr **with exit code 0**, ~60s AFTER the close is durably committed, silently downgrading the ticket to closed-WITHOUT-signature. Seen in the field: an agent reported its final `rebar transition` failed with a lock error; re-reading showed the transition had LANDED.

## Premise verified in current `origin/main` (cc69cc1179)

In `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py`, `close_ticket` (line **263**): the STATUS event commits and releases the lock BEFORE the signing tail runs. Line **433** calls `sign_completion_verdict(...)`, whose append takes a fresh 60s `write_lock` via `write_and_push` -> `event_append`. Line **434** catches `_signing.SigningError`; lines **439-445** write `Warning: closed <id> WITHOUT a completion signature — <exc.message>` to stderr and fall through, so `close_ticket` returns its normal success payload (lines **492-498**: `ticket_id`, `from`, `to`, `newly_unblocked`, `noop`) and the command exits **0**. That payload carries **no field at all** about the signature outcome, so no library, MCP or CLI consumer can detect the loss programmatically. The sibling drift refusal (lines **421-429**) lands unsigned the same way, likewise unreported.

The `except` comment (lines **435-438**) justifies the exit-0 degrade for a *missing ssh-keygen* — permanent and operator-fixable — which does not transfer to the **transient lock timeout** the field incident hit; the appended `exc.message` ("flock: could not acquire lock after 60s") reads as the CLOSE failing when it succeeded. Zebrafish (cc69cc1179) added bounded retry there, mitigating frequency but not the reporting shape.

## Direction

Make the loss **machine-readable and honestly worded** for the caller that suffered it, without changing the process exit code.

1. **Payload marker.** `close_ticket` returns an additional
   `completion_signature: {"signed": bool, "cause": str, "error": str}`, mirroring the
   machine-branchable `PlanReviewAttestation.as_dict()` idiom used for this same problem at
   `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/resign.py:457`, so callers branch on `cause` without parsing
   English. The `cause` vocabulary is **closed and total** over the close path, and `error` is
   empty wherever there is no failure text:

   | outcome | `signed` | `cause` | `error` |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | signature persisted | `True` | `signed` | `""` |
   | `SigningError` at line 434 | `False` | `sign_failed` | `exc.message` |
   | drift refusal at line 421 | `False` | `material_drifted` | `""` |
   | `--force` close (signing deliberately skipped) | `False` | `force_bypassed` | `""` |

   The key is present only where a completion signature is in play: **absent** for a non-close
   transition, and absent for `idea -> closed`, which line **325**
   (`target_status == "closed" and current_status != "idea"`) excludes from the signing block
   entirely — a REJECT/DROP of an undesigned idea is not a completion, so it has no signature
   outcome and inventing a `cause` would misreport a deliberate non-event. Consumers treat the
   key as optional, absence meaning "not a completion close".

   `sign_failed` deliberately covers BOTH the transient lock timeout and the permanent
   missing-`ssh-keygen` degrade: they differ in remedy but not in the fact reported, and the
   distinguishing text is carried verbatim in `error`. Splitting it would make this layer
   classify `SigningError`s it does not construct — that belongs with the signing layer.

   **Consumers that must forward it.** The payload is re-projected field by field at two
   boundaries that would otherwise silently strip the new key, so both are in the edit set:
   `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:414-419` (public `rebar.transition()`) and
   `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:580-591` (CLI `--output json`). MCP `transition_ticket`
   (`src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:190-195`) forwards the library result and inherits it once
   `_lib_writes` does — asserted, not assumed. The shared
   `src/rebar/schemas/transition_result.schema.json` gains `completion_signature` as an
   OPTIONAL property (out of `required`: `reopen` shares the schema and has no close path);
   it already sets `additionalProperties: true`, so this is additive. The `TransitionResult`
   TypedDict at `src/rebar/types.py:205-213` mirrors that schema field by field and is the
   declared return type of public `transition()`, so it gains the same key as `NotRequired` in
   this change — otherwise the typed and JSON contracts disagree and mypy rejects the new key
   at the `_lib_writes` return.
2. **Honest message.** The stderr text leads with the close having **LANDED** and only the
   signature having failed, then names the recovery — rather than appending a bare lock error
   that describes the succeeded operation as failed.
3. **No durable read-side record here — split out.** The first draft proposed a best-effort
   audit comment. That is unsound: it appends through the SAME `event_append` -> `write_lock`
   path whose 60s timeout produced the `SigningError`, so under the contention that causes
   this bug it fails too, and the record would be missing in exactly the case it exists for.

   The sound mechanism is to record the EXPECTATION at close time in the same locked write
   that already commits the STATUS event (line **377** `txn.transition_core`, which already
   carries `close_class` and `force_close_reason`), so a reader can compare "a signature was
   expected" against "a valid completion attestation exists". That is an event-schema addition
   (schema + reducer + `docs/event-schema.md`) — materially more cross-cutting than this
   reporting fix — so it is tracked as its own bug, **mechanical-coherent-wolverine**
   (`23b2-1a94-6a01-466b`), linked `discovered_from` this one, rather than hand-waved here.

   This ticket therefore makes the loss visible to the CALLER that suffered it, across all
   three public surfaces. Making it visible to an unrelated LATER reader is wolverine's job.

### Why NOT a nonzero exit code (deliberate, recorded)

The report offers "a nonzero exit **or at minimum** a machine-readable failure marker"; the exit path is rejected here. `docs/exit-codes.md` declares the contract **frozen** as of the 2026-06-09 window, pinned by `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_exit_codes.py`, with the table at `docs/exit-codes.md:158` fixing `transition` at 0/1/10 — a NEW code is additive-only in a future window, a release decision rather than an implementation one. Reusing exit **1** would be actively harmful: agents read 1 as "the transition failed" and re-run it, which then exits **10** (already closed), trading a silent loss for a louder wrong answer. The marker route meets the reporting need within the frozen contract; a new code is out of scope here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A close whose signature append raises `SigningError` returns
      `completion_signature.signed == False` with `cause == "sign_failed"` — verified by a
      test that forces the append to fail
- [x] A successful close returns `completion_signature` `{signed: True, cause: "signed",
      error: ""}` — verified by a test
- [x] A `--force` close returns `signed == False`, `cause == "force_bypassed"` — test
- [x] The marker survives to all three public consumers: `rebar.transition()` returns it,
      `rebar transition … --output json` prints it, and MCP `transition_ticket` carries it —
      verified by a test per surface
- [x] The stderr text on that failure states the close LANDED and only the signature did not,
      and does not present the lock error as the close failing — verified by a test asserting
      the message text
- [x] `idea -> closed` returns no `completion_signature` key — verified by a test
- [x] The material-drift refusal path reports `signed == False` with
      `cause == "material_drifted"` — verified by a test
- [x] Exit code is unchanged (0) throughout — verified by a test pinning that decision
baseline.summary: transition close reports a lock error with exit 0 after the close landed, silently dropping the completion signature

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Operator directive (verbatim, 2026-08-13): 'One source of contention for CI runners in this project is the reconciler bridge job and canary. let's double the time between runs for both jobs and for both fallback and the chained reconciler invocation.'

The operator names the reconciler bridge job and canary as a source of CI-runner contention on navapbc's shared GitHub Free pool (20 concurrent jobs org-wide). Attribution must be stated honestly: dotted-uncheery-dunnart measured the 2026-08-12/13 run mix as 609 `main|workflow_dispatch` (the Gerrit Verified lane, one dispatch per patchset) and 169 `main|schedule`, and that Verified-lane starvation is a SEPARATE open ticket this change does not address. The bridge and canary sit in the 169 scheduled runs, plus a near-continuous dispatch stream whenever the opt-in `RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS` chain is enabled. Halving every bridge/canary lever cuts that share of the pool; it is a reduction in this pair's footprint, not a fix for the Verified lane.

**Honest cost of lever 2.** The paced chain sleeps inside its own job: it halves chained runs and dispatch events but does not release the runner slot during the pause. Freeing the slot outright means turning `RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS` off — a repo Variable, not a code change, and out of scope.

## Approach
Four cadence levers, all doubled:

1. **Bridge cron backstop** — `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` `schedule:` goes from `*/20 * * * *` to a **uniform 40-minute** cadence. Cron cannot express 40 min in one entry, so use the three-entry 2-hour cycle GitHub accepts under one `schedule:` key: `0 0-23/2 * * *`, `40 0-23/2 * * *`, `20 1-23/2 * * *` (fires :00, :40, 1:20, 2:00, … — gaps uniformly 40 min).
2. **Chain pacing** — the "Re-dispatch to sustain the continuous loop (opt-in)" step calls `gh workflow run` immediately, so the chain's inter-invocation period equals exactly **one** pass duration (~7 min here, per `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`). No delay knob exists. Add one that is self-tuning rather than a repo-specific literal, since this file is a client-copied TEMPLATE: a new early step records `PASS_STARTED_EPOCH` into `$GITHUB_ENV`, and the re-dispatch step sleeps for the pass's own elapsed duration before dispatching. Period becomes **two** pass durations — doubled at any pass duration, for any adopter. Three plain-literal bounds, no new repo Variable:
   - **Unset guard.** The step runs under `set -euo pipefail`, and `test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py::_run_redispatch` runs the step body in isolation with `env={PATH, MODE}` only — no `PASS_STARTED_EPOCH`. So the step reads `started="${PASS_STARTED_EPOCH:-}"` and, when empty or not all-digits, **skips pacing entirely** (prints a note, dispatches immediately). Arithmetic never sees an empty string, `-u` cannot abort the step, and the disabled-422 test passes unchanged.
   - **Cap.** The sleep is capped at a literal **900 s (15 min)**.
   - **Skip threshold.** Pacing is skipped once elapsed >= 1800 s (30 min): such a pass already paces itself, and the remaining `timeout-minutes: 60` budget must stay free.
   Pacing lives inside the step's existing `RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS` gate, so the template default (chain off) is unaffected.
3. **Canary schedule** — `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` `0 * * * *` (hourly) -> `0 */2 * * *` (2-hourly).
4. **Canary staleness window** — the canary header states the window rationale as "3x cadence"; at 40 min that floor rises 1h -> 2h, equalling today's default window, so leaving it would alarm on healthy-but-late runs. Double the default `ALERT_WINDOW_HOURS` 2 -> 4 (workflow `env:` default plus the `alert_window_hours` input default/description), preserving the same 2x margin. `scripts/canary_bridge.py` reads the value from the environment with no hard-coded default, so only its ticket-body string "(cron: */20)" changes.

**Jenkins parity.** `Jenkinsfile` spells the backstop `cron('H/20 * * * *')`. Jenkins `H/40` gives non-uniform 40/20 gaps, so mirror the three-entry cycle as a multi-line `cron('''...''')`. `.gitlab-ci.yml` has no cron (GitLab schedules are server-side) — no edit.

**Truthfulness.** Every comment naming `*/20` or "hourly" is rewritten: the bridge header, re-dispatch comments and `::warning::` text; the canary header staleness paragraph; `canary_bridge.py`'s alert body; `jira-sync-setup.md`'s cadence table, its "…20-minute floor" heading (plus three anchor links), bullets and exit-75 row; the `test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py` docstring.

**Latency note.** Worst-case reconcile latency doubles (20 -> 40 min) and canary detection latency doubles (1h -> 2h poll, 2h -> 4h window). Recorded in `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` beside the cadence table — the authoritative cadence home. `docs/ci-provider-matrix.md` covers the external LLM suite's provider cadence, not the bridge, so it is deliberately untouched.

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` — schedule, new pass-start step, paced re-dispatch, comments.
- `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` — schedule, `ALERT_WINDOW_HOURS` defaults, header.
- `Jenkinsfile` — mirrored 40-minute backstop.
- `scripts/canary_bridge.py` — alert-body cadence string.
- `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` — cadence table, continuous-loop section + anchors, latency note.
- `tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_push_policy.py` — `_UNCHANGED_CRONS` pin + uniformity assertion.
- `tests/unit/test_ci_main_push_policy.py` — `test_reconcilers_keep_their_own_schedules_and_never_cancel`.
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_bridge_provider_wrappers_heldout.py` — `test_github_schedule_and_continuous_redispatch_remain_compatible`.
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py` — docstring + paced re-dispatch branches.

## Testing
- **Happy path:** the three cadence pins named in Scope each compare against the full three-entry list.
- **Uniformity:** a new assertion in `tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_push_policy.py` derives the fire times of the three cron entries over one 2-hour cycle and asserts every consecutive gap is exactly 40 minutes — the property the three-entry spelling exists to satisfy, which a literal-only pin would not catch.
- **Edge / failure path:** extend `_run_redispatch` in `tests/unit/workflow/test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py` to exercise (a) a short elapsed time (sleep taken, cap not hit), (b) elapsed past the 1800 s skip threshold (no sleep, dispatch still issued), and (c) `PASS_STARTED_EPOCH` absent — the harness's existing default env — asserting exit 0, no sleep, and a dispatch. (a)/(b) stub `sleep` on `PATH` so the test records the requested duration instead of waiting. The pre-existing disabled-workflow-422 benign-no-op test must still pass unchanged; case (c) is exactly its guard.
- **Gates:** `make lint`, `make typecheck`, actionlint/zizmor, and the CI unit selection.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `reconcile-bridge.yml` `schedule:` holds exactly `0 0-23/2 * * *`, `40 0-23/2 * * *`, `20 1-23/2 * * *`, and a test asserts consecutive fire-time gaps are uniformly 40 minutes.
- [x] `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` schedule is `0 */2 * * *` and its `ALERT_WINDOW_HOURS` default (env + input) is `4`.
- [x] The re-dispatch step sleeps for the pass's own elapsed duration before dispatching, capped at a literal 900 s, skipped above 1800 s elapsed, and skipped when `PASS_STARTED_EPOCH` is unset or non-numeric (no new repo Variable); tests assert the sleeping branch, the elapsed-skip branch, and the unset-guard branch.
- [x] `Jenkinsfile` carries the same three-entry 40-minute backstop.
- [x] `grep -rn '\*/20' .github/workflows/ Jenkinsfile scripts/ docs/jira-sync-setup.md` returns no hits, and no comment or doc still calls the canary "hourly" or the window 2h.
- [x] [operator-attested] The tests named in Scope pass against the new literals, and `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the CI unit selection are green. Gate runs are process evidence, not repository artifacts; output is in the CHECKPOINT comment here.
baseline.summary: Halve reconciler bridge and canary run cadence

## Context
Absence grace, retirement/tombstone behavior, explicit unretire, and append-only comment identity remain embedded in the facade after core identity extraction. Their fail-open/fail-closed boundaries are hard-won compatibility behavior.

## Outcome
Move these state transitions into `BindingLifecycle` without changing thresholds, stored shape, corruption disposition, or facade signatures.

## Plan
1. Add table tests for confirmed 404 grace, successful-read reset, three-404 retirement, tombstone suppression, explicit unretire, corrupt retired/live data, alert-write failure, and changed/unchanged comment IDs.
2. Extract the existing absence, retirement, suppression, unretire, and comment-map call clusters.
3. Keep three confirmed 404s as the retirement threshold; preserve retired corruption and alert-write fail-open behavior and live corruption fail-closed behavior.
4. Keep comment IDs append-only/change-gated and read old records without eager rewrite.

## Testing
Reload through the repository after transitions and assert bytes, alerts, tombstones, counters, and facade results.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Three confirmed 404s retire an issue, while a successful read resets absence state.
- [ ] Tombstones suppress recreation with an alert until explicit unretire.
- [ ] Retired corruption and alert-write failures remain fail-open, while live corruption remains fail-closed.
- [ ] Comment IDs append only when changed and old records without the field remain readable without rewrite.
- [ ] No lifecycle threshold, stored field, or public method signature changes.

## Out of scope
Interrupted-retirement recovery and production rich-emission cutover.

baseline.description:
## Context / Outcome
Current Jira writes can cross dispatch, Cloud ACLI/REST, or DC SDK/wrapper retries. A timeout can multiply writes or leave acceptance ambiguous. Prove one provider-neutral budget by setting an exact summary through Cloud and DC. Because Jira has no Rebar idempotency key, recovery observes desired state before replay. S1 establishes ADR 0100; S3 owns cutover/outcome consumption; S5 finalizes it after all operation families migrate.

## Approach
1. Define an operation/outcome contract: stable logical id, desired postcondition, invocation/request counts, disposition, failure scope, replay safety, provider delay, `retry_not_before`, and bounded redacted diagnostics. An operation carries at most eight chronological diagnostic entries; every diagnostic message is redacted first and then capped at 512 Unicode code points.
2. One physical invocation is one executor call to a write or observation; raw requests are counted separately. Allow at most three invocations and 15 seconds cumulative sleep. Use `2**(attempt+1) + U[0,1)`: [2s,3s), then [4s,5s). Provider `Retry-After`, parsed by `_errors.parse_retry_after`, is a lower bound.
3. Add a constructor-injected internal route selector at dispatch. It defaults to legacy in S1; tests explicitly select the executor. It is not config or an environment variable. Only exact `{"summary"}` is eligible; mixed fields remain one legacy call. No dual-send. S3 owns venue-gated validation and default-on cutover.
4. Cloud makes one ACLI process per write and preserves existing POSIX/non-POSIX cleanup. Decode sanitized exit/stdout/stderr; unknown shapes fail loud. Recovery uses primary-store `get_issue_by_rest`, never ACLI JQL. Add a per-call policy to `acli_rest._rest_urlopen_with_retry`; summary recovery alone selects one attempt/no sleep. All existing callers retain three attempts with 2s/5s waits.
5. Build the dedicated DC executor with the Jira 3.10.5 public `jira.JIRA(..., max_retries=0)` seam, then fail fast unless the constructed client's `_session.max_retries == 0`. The legacy client keeps current SDK retry. Selected pre-read/write/read-back calls use `_with_connection_retry` under a per-call one-attempt/no-sleep policy; legacy callers keep current behavior.
6. A DC summary-write invocation is GET -> PUT -> GET, with no hidden repeats. Failure ends that invocation. Successful read-back is authoritative. After ambiguous PUT, a separate GET observation consumes the next invocation.
7. Desired summary observed after timeout means recovered success. Conclusive old state may replay within the remaining budget. Failed, rate-limited, or inconclusive observation returns non-replaying `commit_unknown`. An authoritative delay that cannot fit returns `retry_not_before` without sleeping. Auth, TLS, permission, invalid request, and permanent failures do not retry; eligible network, 429, and retryable 5xx failures use the shared schedule.
8. Preserve the `update_one` / `apply_handlers.handle_update` boundary while S1 is test-only. `dispatch_one` maps success/recovered success to the legacy result and fills `_fields_synced` only after conclusive success; `_comment_errors` and `_subop` keep their shapes. `commit_unknown`/`retry_not_before` map to a tagged internal result. `handle_update` records exactly one redacted per-mutation error/disposition message capped at 512 Unicode code points, leaves `_fields_synced` empty, advances no baseline or set-field provenance, persists no deferral in S1, and lets the batch continue. S3 maps terminal dispositions to pass/fuse control and durable deferral, then retires the bridge.
9. Emit exactly one redacted completion log for every terminal/exhausted outcome or cleanup failure. It contains only logical id, disposition, invocation count, request count, cleanup status, `retry_not_before`, and one redacted message capped at 512 Unicode code points; the complete serialized log is capped at 1,024 Unicode code points.
10. ADR 0100 records the retry owner, Jira idempotency limit, observe-before-replay, budget, lifecycle owners, rollback, and deltas from ADR 0084/0087 and desired-state ADRs 0004/0026/0029. The 15-second cumulative limit supersedes ADR 0084 only on selected routes.

## Scope
- Core: `operation_outcome.py`, `retry_budget.py`, `dispatch_one.py`, `dispatch_apply_phases.py`, `apply_handlers.py`.
- Cloud: `acli.py`, `acli_subprocess.py`, `acli_rest.py`, backend; preserve unrelated REST retry defaults.
- DC: `transport.py`, `retry.py`, `_issues.py`, backend; dedicated executor client and per-call policy preserve legacy defaults.
- ADR 0100; budget/outcome, handler, historical ACLI, cleanup, and DC request tests.

## Testing
Fake-clock/stateful tests cover schedules, deadlines, request order, ambiguity, recovery, failure classes, and no real sleep. Poison tests reject hidden retry or extra ACLI processes; neighbor tests preserve unselected behavior. Handler tests prevent false state advance. Historical triples pin decoding, real processes pin cleanup, and output tests pin bounds/redaction. S3 owns venue-gated evidence; S5 owns final live confirmation.

## Compatibility / Rollback
Production stays on legacy through the internal selector. Rollback selects legacy before a call; there is no config/env surface or dual-send. S3 changes the default after validation. Selected routes use the new budget, long-delay deferral, fail-loud unknown ACLI shapes, and non-replaying inconclusive recovery; other callers retain current behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Cloud and DC summary routes produce one provider-neutral outcome schema; tests assert every field.
- [ ] Repeated invocations preserve one logical id.
- [ ] No selected operation exceeds three invocations or 15 seconds cumulative sleep.
- [ ] Each selected DC write invocation is exactly GET/PUT/GET with no hidden repeats.
- [ ] Cloud recovery performs one primary-store REST request with no sleep; neighbor tests preserve existing REST retry.
- [ ] Executor-selected exact `{"summary"}` bypasses generic `_call_with_retry`.
- [ ] The constructor selector defaults to legacy, adds no config/env key, and tests explicitly enable it.
- [ ] Mixed fields stay one unsplit legacy call.
- [ ] Confirmed outcomes preserve legacy result, `_fields_synced`, `_comment_errors`, and `_subop` shapes.
- [ ] Every terminal outcome records exactly one redacted per-mutation message capped at 512 Unicode code points, with no baseline/provenance advance or S1 deferral.
- [ ] ADR and contract name S3 as sole cutover, fuse/deferral consumer, and bridge-retirement owner.
- [ ] The Jira 3.10.5 executor passes `max_retries=0` and fails fast unless `_session.max_retries == 0`; legacy SDK retry is unchanged.
- [ ] Selected DC wrapper calls are one-attempt/no-sleep; legacy wrapper behavior is unchanged.
- [ ] Fallback sleeps remain [2s,3s), then [4s,5s).
- [ ] Over-budget provider delay returns `retry_not_before` without sleep.
- [ ] Permanent failures use one invocation; eligible transient failures use the schedule.
- [ ] Satisfied observation returns recovered success without another write.
- [ ] Conclusive old state permits only remaining-budget replay.
- [ ] Failed/inconclusive observation returns non-replaying `commit_unknown`.
- [ ] ACLI cleanup passes for POSIX groups and non-POSIX children.
- [ ] Historical ACLI triples decode deterministically; unknown triples do not retry.
- [ ] Operation outcomes hold at most eight diagnostics, with each redacted message capped at 512 Unicode code points.
- [ ] Every terminal/exhausted outcome or cleanup failure emits exactly one completion log containing only logical id, disposition, invocation/request counts, cleanup status, `retry_not_before`, and one redacted message capped at 512 Unicode code points; the whole log is at most 1,024 Unicode code points.
- [ ] ADR 0100 records contract, ownership, compatibility deltas, rollback, and prior art; index checks pass.
baseline.summary: RP-03 S1 — Execute one Jira postcondition through a single retry budget

## The file

`src/rebar/signing.py` is 798 LOC against the 800 hard cap — two lines of headroom. Deferred from `cinderlike-lucky-akitainu` (which took `pass1.py` and `_store/push.py` instead) because this one cut cannot be made without editing a test, a different risk profile from those two.

## Concern map (measured on origin/main @ 2af5a4c773)

| concern | LOC | symbols |
|---|---|---|
| A manifest vocabulary + gate provenance | 158 | `SigningError`, `parse_manifest`, `VERIFIED_AT_SHA_PREFIX`, `verified_at_sha_step`, `verified_at_sha_from_manifest`, `verified_at_sha_subject`, `REBAR_VERSION_PREFIX`, `rebar_version_step`, `rebar_version_from_manifest`, `_gate_source_dir`, `_baked_commit_sha`, `_gate_commit_sha`, `gate_code_version`, `head_sha` |
| B legacy symmetric HMAC scheme | 231 | `ALGORITHM`, `PAYLOAD_VERSION`, `_NO_KEY`, `signing_key`, `_generate_key_file`, `key_fingerprint`, `_canonical_payload`, `compute_signature`, `verify_record`, `_hmac_opcert_not_certified` |
| C CLI arms | 103 | `sign_cli`, `verify_signature_cli` |
| D dispatch + sign/verify paths | 194 | `OPCERT_KINDS`, `verify_attestation_record`, `_sign_manifest_under_lock`, `sign_manifest`, `_resolve_and_reduce`, `most_recent_attestation`, `_record_for_kind`, `verify_signature`, `verify_attestations` |

Proposed: sibling modules (NOT a package — the cap is per-file either way, and `_opcert_signing.py` is the established precedent, split out of this same module in story 8d8e). `_signing_manifest.py` ~198, `_signing_hmac.py` ~276, `signing.py` ~377. Direction `signing -> _signing_hmac -> _signing_manifest`, acyclic. An optional third cut (`_signing_cli.py` ~133) would take `signing.py` to ~245 but requires the CLI arms to import `rebar.signing` IN-FUNCTION, never at module level, or the eight `verify_signature` and one `sign_manifest` monkeypatches bind pre-patch and silently no-op.

## Why it needs a test edit — the blocker

`_baked_commit_sha` is monkeypatched on the `signing` module at `test_attestation_signing.py:139,151,162`, and its consumer `_gate_commit_sha` calls it as a BARE GLOBAL in the same file (`:308,:312`). Move both into `_signing_manifest.py` and `_gate_commit_sha` resolves `_baked_commit_sha` from `_signing_manifest.__dict__`, so the patch becomes a NO-OP. Two of the three tests fail loudly; `:162` (`assert "STALEBAKED" not in got`) passes VACUOUSLY — it silently stops testing the live-over-baked precedence it was written to prove. That third one is the dangerous one.

Remedies, in order: (1) re-point the three patches at `"rebar._signing_manifest._baked_commit_sha"` — legitimate, the symbol is private with zero src consumers outside the family; (2) keep the whole gate-provenance sub-family (69 LOC) in `signing.py`, costing ~69 LOC on the entry module and shrinking `_signing_manifest.py` to ~129; (3) NOT an in-function `from rebar.signing import _baked_commit_sha` — that is a back-edge and a cycle.

## Other constraints found

- `docs/reuse-surface.md` documents `sign_manifest`, `verify_signature`, `verify_attestations`,
  `verify_record`, `head_sha`; `tests/unit/test_reuse_surface_doc.py` introspects NINE
  `signing.*` callables with `inspect.signature`. Six of the nine move — the re-export must
  carry them with unchanged parameter lists. That test is the CI tripwire.
- Six PRIVATE names must be re-exported despite the underscore: `_gate_commit_sha` (imported by
  `llm/build_drift.py:127`), `_baked_commit_sha`, `_NO_KEY`, `_generate_key_file`,
  `_canonical_payload`, `_hmac_opcert_not_certified`.
- Silent-behaviour flag: `verify_record` and `_hmac_opcert_not_certified` call
  `verified_at_sha_from_manifest` / `rebar_version_from_manifest` as bare globals. After the cut
  they resolve in `_signing_hmac`'s globals, so a patch on `signing` no longer reaches them. No
  test depends on that today, but it is a real semantic change and should be stated in the
  commit.
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` has ZERO keys for `signing.py` — the `--lock` gate is not a
  constraint here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `signing.py` <= 500 LOC; every new module in [100, 500].
- [ ] All nine `signing.*` callables in `test_reuse_surface_doc.py` reachable with unchanged
      signatures; the six private names re-exported.
- [ ] The `_baked_commit_sha` hazard resolved by remedy (1) or (2), stated explicitly, with the
      `:162` vacuous-pass risk addressed rather than left latent.
- [ ] Full-suite test-count parity; `make lint`, `make typecheck`, module-size contract green.

baseline.description:
# Bridge git delivery is abandoned after ONE transport failure (TLS/DNS/timeout)

## Impact, stated first

Two Reconcile Bridge runs **converged the reconcile** and then lost the delivery to `origin/tickets`, leaving unpushed commits on the runner that die with it:

- run 31535962079: `push-transport-failed: fatal: unable to access
  'https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/': server certificate verification failed. CAfile:
  none CRLfile: none` → `(3 unpushed commits on origin/tickets..HEAD)` →
  `Bridge delivery failed (exit 1)`.
- run 31420498173: `merge-recovery-blocked: fatal: ... server certificate verification
  failed` plus `fatal: could not fetch 983800f2 from promisor remote` →
  `(2 unpushed commits)`.

A converged pass whose events never reach `origin/tickets` is silently lost work; the heartbeat canary is the only detector.

## Confirmed root cause

`src/rebar/_store/push.py` retries **only** a genuine non-fast-forward. Every other non-zero push is terminal on the FIRST failure:

```python
if not _is_non_fast_forward(stderr):
    reason = (
        "push-policy-declined" if _is_policy_decline(stderr) else "push-transport-failed"
    )
    _raise_if_strict(strict, reason, stderr, base_path, remote_ref)
    return  # non-retriable class — best-effort
```

The comment justifying "terminal" is about **permanent rule violations** ("hitting the remote twice more cannot change a permanent rule violation") — true for a policy decline, **false** for a transport fault. But both land in the same branch, so a TLS handshake blip, a DNS failure, or the 30 s `_GIT_TIMEOUT` (which surfaces as returncode 124 / `git timed out after 30s`) all get **zero** retries.

There is also **no backoff anywhere** in this loop; the existing non-FF retries fire back-to-back.

`CAfile: none CRLfile: none` points at the runner's CA bundle not resolving — a hosted runner infra flake, not a rebar bug. The `filter: blob:none` partial clone widens the blast radius: on-demand promisor fetches during merge recovery hit the network too. rebar cannot fix the runner's CA store, but abandoning a converged pass after ONE transient blip is rebar's defect and is squarely fixable.

## Plan

1. Add a transport-retriable classifier in `src/rebar/_store/push.py` that recognises the
   transient transport signatures observed in CI and their close relatives (TLS/certificate
   verification, could-not-resolve-host, connection reset/timed out, the synthetic
   `git timed out after 30s`, early EOF / RPC failures, promisor-remote fetch failure).
   It must be **subtractive** in the same shape already proven for `_is_non_fast_forward`
   (bug 2a76) and `_ref_lock` (bug 4afc): a policy decline can never be transport-retriable,
   and ambiguity resolves to TERMINAL rather than to a retry loop that cannot converge.
2. Add a bounded, injectable sleep helper. **Declared budget: 3 transport attempts total
   per leg, with an attempt-indexed backoff of 0.5 s then 2.0 s** (the last delay repeats
   if a leg ever gains more attempts). Small on purpose: ride out a blip, never sit on a
   real outage while commits pile up.
3. In the push loop, when the failure is transport-retriable and the transport-retry budget
   is not spent, sleep and retry rather than raising. Keep the budget small and explicit.
4. When the transport budget IS spent, raise exactly today's `push-transport-failed` reason
   with the same detail + unpushed-commit summary, so the strict contract and the existing
   reason vocabulary are unchanged.
5. Leave `push-policy-declined` strictly terminal — unchanged, zero retries.
6. Cover BOTH recovery legs, which fail with **different** reasons and must be named
   separately:
   - the **explicit fetch** in `_recover_non_fast_forward`, which raises
     `push-transport-failed` (not `merge-recovery-blocked`); and
   - the **promisor on-demand fetch that fires inside `git merge` itself** in
     `_merge_remote_under_lock` — this is the leg that produced run 31420498173's
     `merge-recovery-blocked: ... server certificate verification failed` together with
     `could not fetch ... from promisor remote`, because the checkout is a `blob:none`
     partial clone.
   Both legs run the SAME subtractive transport classifier. A genuine merge conflict is
   never transport-retriable and stays terminal on its first failure, still raising
   `merge-recovery-blocked`.

7. **Required structural consequence:** `src/rebar/_store/push.py` already sits at 786 of
   the repo's 800-LOC hard cap, so this fix cannot land without a split. Move the
   push-failure **classification, backoff and strict-reporting** cluster to a new
   `src/rebar/_store/push_classify.py` along the seam those functions already form — they
   answer "what KIND of failure is this, how long do we wait, and how is it reported", and
   none of them shells out to git or touches the worktree. The dependency is one-way
   (`push.py` imports `push_classify.py`), and the moved code is otherwise unchanged, so
   most of this change's line count is relocation rather than new logic.

## Scope / non-goals

- **No** change to the reason vocabulary (`push-transport-failed`,
  `push-policy-declined`, `final-push-rejected`, `merge-recovery-blocked` all keep their
  spelling and meaning) — only *when* they are raised.
- **No** change to `_MAX_RETRIES = 5` for the non-fast-forward path.
- No new secrets, credentials, permissions, or infrastructure; no CI runner changes. Fixing
  the runner's CA bundle is explicitly out of scope — this ticket makes rebar survive the
  flake, and is deliberately a reliability-only change.
- Does not touch the ref-lock CAS classifier (`freeborn-dizzy-raven`) or the workflow
  re-dispatch step (`callous-wavy-kite`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1: A test proves a push failing with the exact CI TLS stderr (`server certificate
  verification failed. CAfile: none CRLfile: none`) is retried and then **succeeds**,
  where today it raises on the first failure.
- [x] AC2: A test proves the transport retry budget is bounded — a persistently failing
  transport push stops after exactly **3** attempts and raises `push-transport-failed`,
  carrying the git stderr and the unpushed-commit summary.
- [x] AC3: A test proves a policy decline (`pre-receive hook declined` / `GH013`) is still
  terminal after exactly ONE push attempt and still raises `push-policy-declined` — the
  bug 2a76 contract is not weakened.
- [x] AC4: A test proves retries sleep between attempts (via the injected sleep seam),
  i.e. they are not back-to-back.
- [x] AC5: The existing push contract tests still pass, including
  `tests/unit/test_push_strict.py::test_five_rejections_spend_one_terminal_push_and_earlier_success_does_not`
  (the 6-push non-FF budget) and the transport/policy reason parametrisation. ONE assertion
  is deliberately updated: the strict path's stdout/stderr SILENCE no longer holds for the
  transport class, because a retry announces itself before the terminal raise. Policy
  declines still assert exact silence; the retry count moves to `caplog`. See comments.
- [x] AC7: A test proves the **merge** leg retries a transport fault — a recovery merge
  failing with the run-31420498173 TLS + `could not fetch ... from promisor remote` stderr
  is retried and then succeeds, where today it raises `merge-recovery-blocked` on the
  first failure.
- [x] AC8: A test proves a genuine merge conflict is NOT retried as a transport fault —
  it stops after ONE merge and still raises `merge-recovery-blocked`.
- [x] AC6: `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass, the complexity ratchet reports no new
  debt, and every `src/rebar` module stays under the 800-LOC hard cap.
baseline.summary: Reconcile Bridge git delivery fails on TLS 'server certificate verification failed'

## Summary
The scheduled **Live External Integration** run on 2026-08-17 (run 32000764439, job "jira DC harness smoke (real Jira Data Center, ephemeral)") failed `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_multi_project_rehearsal.py::test_unknown_project_fails_closed` with:

```
E   Failed: DID NOT RAISE RebarError
```

The scenario maps an unknown project key — `rebar.bridge_projects_set(unknown, ["rebar-ghost"], repo_root=str(work))` — and then previews/syncs it, expecting the bridge to **fail closed** (RAISE `RebarError`) rather than silently no-op on an unknown mapped key. Against the live DC instance it did **not** raise.

## Regression window
This is a NEW regression, not a long-standing failure:
- 2026-08-15 run 31879125045 (jira DC job 94999114642): **73 passed, 1 xfailed, 0 failed**.
- 2026-08-17 run 32000764439: **2 failed, 71 passed, 1 xfailed** — this test is one of the two new failures.

So a change landed between 2026-08-15 and 2026-08-17 that broke the fail-closed guard for an unknown bridge-project key. Candidate areas to bisect: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/projects_store.py` (`resolve_project` / `compute_snapshot`), `bridge_projects_set`, and the multi-project preview/sync path (cf. related bug 3b87 `resolve_project` tri-state collapse, and epic 0e68 / story 368f which delivered this behavior).

## Impact
The multi-project bridge's fail-closed safety guarantee is not holding against a real Jira DC instance: an unknown mapped project key produces a silent empty fetch/sync instead of an error. Correctness/safety of the many-to-many bridge.

## The regression escaped because only a LIVE test covered it
Per triage guidance: a live-external regression must be reproducible by a NON-external test so CI catches it without the (slow, credentialed) live suite. Today the only coverage is the live DC rehearsal.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A **RED** non-external test (unit or fake-transport integration, no live DC/creds) reproduces the regression: setting an unknown bridge-project mapping and running preview/sync RAISES `RebarError` (fail-closed) — asserted to FAIL against current `main` before the fix.
- [ ] Root cause identified (the change between 2026-08-15 and 2026-08-17 that dropped the fail-closed behavior) and fixed so an unknown mapped project key fails closed.
- [ ] The new non-external test passes after the fix.
- [ ] The live rehearsal `test_unknown_project_fails_closed` passes in the next Live External Integration run.

## Evidence
- Failing run: https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/32000764439 (job: jira DC harness smoke)
- Test: `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_multi_project_rehearsal.py::test_unknown_project_fails_closed`
- Delivered by story 368f (gasolinic-microbian-puffin), epic 0e68 (outrageous-uncultured-wildebeast).
baseline.summary: Live Jira DC rehearsal: unknown bridge project no longer fails closed (test_unknown_project_fails_closed — DID NOT RAISE RebarError)

## Context

Operator-attested completion evidence is currently easy to misread as evidence that only a human operator may provide. The original ADR defines the category by where evidence lives: outside the codebase, with a concrete attestation recorded in the ticket. Comments are non-material plan history; changing the criterion tag in the description is material.

## Decision

Operator-attested describes evidence location, not actor identity. An agent may freely record truthful, concrete external evidence it observed. The author must classify the criterion with `[operator-attested]` before plan review. Concrete evidence may then be added as a ticket comment without invalidating the review. Existing exact-tag, specificity, and prompt-injection safeguards remain unchanged.

## Approach

Clarify the existing contract in ADR 0043 and the author-facing plan guide. Documentation is the fitting mechanism because the implementation already treats comments as non-material and judges evidence without requiring human authorship; no gate behavior needs to change.

## Plan

- Add the exact sentence `Operator-attested describes the evidence location, not the identity of the actor` to ADR 0043, followed by an explicit statement that agents may provide truthful, concrete evidence they observed.
- Add the exact ordering sentence `Classify the criterion before plan review by adding the [operator-attested] tag to its checkbox text.` to the plan-writing guide.
- Add the exact sentence `Record that evidence in a ticket comment; comments are non-material` to the same guide.
- Preserve the current exact-tag, concrete-specificity, and command-versus-attestation safeguards in ADR 0043.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] ADR 0043 contains `Operator-attested describes the evidence location, not the identity of the actor`, verified with `rg -nF "Operator-attested describes the evidence location, not the identity of the actor" docs/adr/0043-operator-attested-completion-evidence.md`.
- [x] ADR 0043 explicitly permits agent-authored evidence, verified with `rg -nF "Agents may freely record truthful, concrete operator-attested evidence they observed." docs/adr/0043-operator-attested-completion-evidence.md`.
- [x] The guide teaches classification before review, verified with `rg -nF "Classify the criterion before plan review by adding the [operator-attested] tag to its checkbox text." src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md`.
- [x] The guide explains evidence comments and materiality, verified with `rg -nF "Record that evidence in a ticket comment; comments are non-material" src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md`.
- [x] Existing safeguards remain present, verified with `rg -nF "Matching is **exact and case-insensitive** on" docs/adr/0043-operator-attested-completion-evidence.md`, `rg -nF "An operator-attested criterion is **MET** only if an attestation names" docs/adr/0043-operator-attested-completion-evidence.md`, and `rg -nF "a **command** tries to control the verdict" docs/adr/0043-operator-attested-completion-evidence.md`.

## Testing

Run every exact `rg -nF` command above and `git diff --check`.
baseline.summary: Clarify operator-attested comments and agent authorship

baseline.description:
## Context

Parent epic `a4bd-4ca8-c44f-49bb`; depends on S1 (`248f-ac00-18db-4259`, closed). S3 (`47a0-7019-da4b-40e0`) makes the inbound removal path decline removals of links carrying no peer-confirmation record. Without a backfill, the FIRST post-upgrade pass would find an empty store and decline EVERY legitimate peer deletion — a regression worse than the blind spot being fixed. The epic states it directly: "Backfill grandfathers existing managed links as confirmed-at-upgrade (marked as such) so the first post-upgrade run does not decline every legitimate removal."

This story must land BEFORE S3 turns the decline on.

## Scope

- `peer_confirmations.py` — add `DIRECTION_BACKFILL = "backfill"` beside the existing
  `DIRECTION_OUTBOUND` / `DIRECTION_SNAPSHOT`. `SOURCE_BACKFILL` already exists; the direction
  vocabulary must stay a closed, named set rather than gaining a bare string literal.
- `peer_confirmations.py` — the loader records whether the store file was ABSENT at open (a
  `was_absent` attribute set in `PeerConfirmationStore._load`). Backfill runs on "file was
  absent" (a fresh upgrade), NOT on "store is empty": an operator who legitimately emptied the
  store must not silently have it re-populated.
- `peer_confirmations.py` — add
  `backfill_from_managed_refs(store, local_tickets, binding_store, pass_id) -> int`.
  For each local ticket, read its managed refs via
  `rebar.reducer._managed_refs.managed_ref_set(ticket)` — its kinds are already constrained to
  `MANAGED_REF_KINDS`, so no extra kind filter is needed or wanted. For each `(kind, target)`
  whose `target` resolves to a BOUND peer key via `binding_store.get_jira_key(target)`, write a
  record keyed `(ticket_local_id, target, kind)` with `source_kind=SOURCE_BACKFILL`,
  `direction=DIRECTION_BACKFILL`, `link_id=None`, `confirmed_pass=pass_id`.

**The no-downgrade guard is explicit, because `record()` will not provide it.** S1's landed `PeerConfirmationStore.record()` overwrites its key UNCONDITIONALLY — it reads the previous entry only to preserve `first_confirmed_at`. So backfill MUST check first and write ONLY when `store.get(source, target, kind) is None`. Any existing record (`push` or `snapshot`) is strictly stronger evidence than a grandfather assumption and must be left untouched. This read-before-write skip is the entire mechanism behind AC5's no-downgrade half; the upgrade half needs no new code, since a later `push`/`snapshot` `record()` call overwrites a backfilled entry by the same unconditional behaviour.

- `reconcile.py::_confirm_peer_links` — **one store instance for the whole evidence step.**
  As landed by S2 this helper calls `open_store(ctx.repo_root)` itself and saves only when it
  wrote records. If backfill opened a SECOND instance, two things break: (a) backfilled records
  would be invisible to snapshot confirmation's fresh disk load, so the same-pass provenance
  upgrade could not happen; and (b) worse, the two instances would race a LOST UPDATE — each
  loaded a pre-write copy, so whichever saves last silently discards the other's records.
  So this story restructures the helper into the single evidence step it should have been:
  open the store ONCE, run `backfill_from_managed_refs` FIRST, then `confirm_from_snapshot` on
  that SAME instance, then `store.save()` once if either wrote. Ordering inside one instance is
  what makes the upgrade work — snapshot's `record()` overwrites the backfilled entry in memory.
  Keep the existing fail-open `try/except Exception` wrapper and the `if persist:` gate exactly
  as they are; no second call site is added to `_persist_and_log`.

- A backfilled record is treated as confirmed by `is_confirmed()`. Distinguishing backfill from
  proof at the DECISION point is deliberately NOT done — that would re-open the blind spot for
  every pre-upgrade link, which is exactly what grandfathering exists to avoid.
- `managed_refs` monotonicity is unchanged; nothing is pruned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1 On a store whose file was absent, every managed ref with a bound target gets a record
      with `source="backfill"` and `direction="backfill"`; the store is then non-empty and
      persisted. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k fresh_upgrade`.
- [x] AC2 A managed ref whose target is UNBOUND gets no record. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k unbound`.
- [x] AC3 Backfill does NOT run when the store file existed but is empty. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k existing_empty`.
- [x] AC4 Backfill does not re-run once the file exists — a second pass adds zero records. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k second_pass`.
- [x] AC5 Provenance never downgrades: backfill SKIPS a key already carrying a `push` or
      `snapshot` record (asserted by inspecting `source` after backfill runs over it), while a
      later snapshot confirmation DOES overwrite a backfilled key's `source` to `"snapshot"`.
      Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k provenance`.
- [x] AC6 `is_confirmed()` returns True for a backfilled record. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k confirmed`.
- [x] AC7 In no-write mode (`persist` False) no backfill is written, and a raising backfill does
      not break the pass. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k "nowrite or fail_open"`.
- [x] AC8 The evidence step uses a SINGLE store instance: a record backfilled this pass is
      visible to snapshot confirmation in the SAME pass (its `source` becomes `"snapshot"`), and
      no record written by either half is lost after the single save (lost-update regression).
      Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k "ordering or lost_update"`.
- [x] AC9 Every edited module stays under the 800-line cap. Proof: `bash -c 'git archive HEAD |
      tar -xO src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py | wc -l'` per edited file, < 800.
- [x] AC10 Gates green. Proof: `make lint` exit 0, `make typecheck` exit 0,
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` exit 0.

## Testing

- New suite `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py` covering the
  fresh-upgrade backfill, unbound-target skip, existing-but-empty non-run, one-shot behaviour
  across two passes, both halves of the provenance rule, `is_confirmed` acceptance, the no-write
  and fail-open paths, and the backfill-before-snapshot ordering.
- Regression: `make lint && make typecheck && pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler`.

## Out of scope

The removal decline (S3). No pruning of `managed_refs`. No change to its monotonicity or to `record()`'s unconditional-overwrite contract.
baseline.summary: Backfill existing managed links as confirmed-at-upgrade

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Live completion-gate captures show agentic runs wasting 40-70% of their request budget on DUPLICATE tool calls: one run repeated an identical search_files call 144x, another looped 62x on an honest "(no matches)" result. The shipped windowed distinct-ratio actuator (agent_call.py) correctly ABORTS pathological runs, but abortion is the backstop — nothing today prevents the waste before the trip point, and every duplicate re-executes the tool and re-pays the round-trip. Research across agent harnesses (OpenHands StuckDetector, smolagents max_steps) found detect-and-terminate everywhere but no harness that memoizes the duplicate and steers the model back on course — graduated nudge-then-abort is the recommended pattern.

## Approach

Add a memoize+nudge toolset wrapper at the shared agent-call seam (src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py), the module that already arms every tool-bearing Agent call: wrapper order runaway guard OUTERMOST -> memo -> steering (guard :68, steering :45; the guard's call_tool observes the signature before the memo short-circuits, so the actuator's window math is unchanged).

- Key: the EXISTING usage_log tool-call signature (identical normalization to the actuator — same signature means same dedup semantics).
- Behavior: first repeat of a signature returns the cached result plus a static templated nudge line; further repeats return the cached result plus a stronger static nudge; the distinct-ratio actuator remains the abort backstop. Static text only — a templated nudge keeps message content byte-stable for provider prompt caching.
- Non-memoization predicate (keyed on how the allowlisted tools ACTUALLY signal, pai_tools.py): these tools NEVER raise into the agent loop — they return strings. An ERROR result is one whose text begins with the "Error:" prefix (read_file/list_directory/search_files/show_ticket all return f"Error: {exc}" on ValueError/OSError). Error results are NOT memoized and NOT nudged: the identical call re-executes on retry, because a transient/again-different outcome is possible. By contrast the deterministic "sentinel-empty" results — "(no matches)" (search_files), "(empty)" (list_directory), "(empty range)" (read_file) — are HONEST, stable answers and ARE memoized+nudged: memoizing "(no matches)" is precisely the 62x-loop waste this ticket eliminates. (The "UNRESOLVED" resolve_symbol sentinel is moot here — resolve_symbol is not in the allowlist below.)
- Read-only allowlist: only read_file, search_files, list_directory, and show_ticket are memoized (all four exist in the verifier toolset, pai_tools.py:243); write or non-deterministic tools — including the banked-verification sibling's record_criterion_verdict — are exempt.
- No manifest / in-context awareness in THIS ticket: the FULL/skeleton "already in context" nudge depends on the pre-loading sibling's manifest, whose shape, marker vocabulary, and accessor are not yet defined and ship AFTER this change. This ticket therefore adds NO manifest coupling: every allowlisted read_file executes normally on first sight and returns the real content; duplicates get memoization plus the generic repeat nudge only. The manifest-aware FULL-branch nudge is deferred to the pre-loading ticket, which will layer it on this seam.

## Scope

- src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py — the memo wrapper + wrapper-order wiring (guard -> memo -> steering).
- tests/unit/test_agent_call_memo_nudge.py — new: memo semantics, wrapper order, allowlist, error passthrough (Error:-prefixed strings re-execute), sentinel-empty memoization ("(no matches)" cached), nudge escalation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A duplicate allowlisted call returns the cached result without re-executing the tool; the wrapped tool function runs exactly once for N identical calls (unit test with a counting stub).
- [x] Nudge escalation: first repeat carries the level-1 static nudge, subsequent repeats the level-2 text; both byte-stable across runs (unit test).
- [x] The runaway guard still observes memoized duplicates: the distinct-ratio window sees every duplicate signature, and a synthetic loop still trips the actuator at the same call index with the memo active (unit test against the existing guard tests' fixtures).
- [x] Error results are not memoized: an allowlisted call whose return begins with "Error:" re-executes on the next identical call (counting stub returning an "Error:"-prefixed string, then a success), and carries no nudge (unit test).
- [x] Deterministic sentinel-empty results ARE memoized: a search_files-style stub returning "(no matches)" runs exactly once for N identical calls and the duplicate carries the repeat nudge (unit test) — the core waste case.
- [x] Only allowlisted read-only tools are memoized; record_criterion_verdict and any non-allowlisted tool always execute (unit test).
- [x] Live Bedrock capture recorded on this ticket: a run demonstrating either a nudge-broken loop (duplicate signature followed by a different next call) or a nudge->actuator escalation, with usage-log figures, backed by a durable in-repo artifact under docs/experiments/.
- [x] make lint and make typecheck pass; the existing runaway-guard unit suite (tests/unit/test_agent_call_runaway_guard_c827.py) passes unchanged.

## Testing

Unit suite in tests/unit/test_agent_call_memo_nudge.py per the acceptance criteria (counting stubs, wrapper-order assertion, guard-interaction fixture reuse, Error:-prefix passthrough, "(no matches)" memoization). Run: python -m pytest tests/unit/test_agent_call_memo_nudge.py tests/unit/test_agent_call_runaway_guard_c827.py -q. Live Bedrock capture per the live AC recorded as a durable artifact under docs/experiments/ plus a ticket comment. make lint + make typecheck.
baseline.summary: Memoize and nudge duplicate read-only tool calls at the shared agent-call seam
