## Context / Problem

Four guards in `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py` each call `_run_request_sites()` (line 467), which re-derives the SAME immutable analysis of the whole `src/rebar` tree: `test_the_provenance_analysis_can_see_the_sites_it_judges` (line 487), `test_no_run_request_inherits_the_raw_config_model` (line 495), `test_every_unfollowable_site_is_registered_with_a_reason` (line 515) and `test_neither_registry_has_stale_entries` (line 524). CI recorded 30.10s, 32.27s, 31.02s and 32.50s for them in one contended run.

The analysis is expensive twice over, and the second reason is not in the ticket title. `_run_request_sites` walks `_SRC.rglob("*.py")` and parses every file that mentions `RunRequest(`. For each site it calls `_verdict`, whose parameter-provenance branch (lines 448-450) re-walks `sorted(_SRC.rglob("*.py"))` and calls `ast.parse(caller_path.read_text())` on EVERY file in the tree, once per site it has to follow — which is why a single scan was profiled at ~8,033 parses over a tree with far fewer files. So the repetition is both across the four tests and inside each one.

The analysis is a pure function of the committed source: no test mutates `src/rebar`, and the module's only autouse fixture (`class_table`, line 60) patches `llm_config._read_llm_file_table`, which the AST scan never consults.

## Approach

Compute the analysis once per test process, and stop the inner scan re-reading the tree.

* Add a session-scoped fixture `run_request_sites` that calls `_run_request_sites()`
  once and returns its list; the four guards take it as a parameter instead of
  calling the function. A pytest fixture is bounded by the session that created it,
  so the cached value cannot outlive the run or be served to a later session — the
  staleness requirement is satisfied by construction rather than by an
  invalidation rule that could itself be wrong. `_run_request_sites` stays a plain
  function so the fixture, and any future caller, can still invoke it directly.
* Memoise the per-path parse behind a module-level
  `_parsed(path) -> ast.Module` keyed on the path, used by `_run_request_sites`,
  `_functions` (line 355) and `_verdict`'s caller scan (line 450). Within one
  process each file is then read and parsed at most once, which removes the inner
  repetition the four tests were each paying in full.

Both halves are caching only: the same `(key, expr, verdict)` tuples are produced, in the same order, and every assertion, offender message and registry check is untouched. Deriving the analysis once is the smallest change that removes the repetition without weakening what the guards inspect — the alternative of narrowing the scan (fewer files, cheaper heuristics) would trade coverage for time, and these guards exist precisely because a vacuous scan is the failure mode (`test_the_provenance_analysis_can_see_the_sites_it_judges` guards the guard).

## Scope

* `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py` — add `_parsed`, route the three
  parse sites through it, add the session-scoped `run_request_sites` fixture, and
  change the four guards to take it.

No production change: `src/rebar` is READ by the scan and not modified.

## Testing

* Happy path — all four guards still pass and still see the real tree:
  `test_the_provenance_analysis_can_see_the_sites_it_judges` continues to assert
  `>= 15` sites with a non-empty `config=` on each, which is what makes the other
  three non-vacuous.
* Equivalence check — the analysis produced through the fixture and the parse memo
  is compared element-by-element against the result of the pre-change code on the
  same tree, and must be identical.
* Failure/edge path — a defect is seeded by adding a `RunRequest(config=cfg, ...)`
  site to a real `src/rebar` module and confirming
  `test_no_run_request_inherits_the_raw_config_model` FAILS naming that site
  through the cached path. Seed reverted, not committed.
* Whole-suite regression — the CI pytest command is green.

No wall-clock or timing-budget assertion is added; savings go in ticket comments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `_run_request_sites` is invoked exactly once per test process when the four
      guards run, verified by counting invocations with a temporary wrapper during
      a focused run and reporting the count in a ticket comment.
- [x] The four guards' assertions, offender messages and both registry checks are
      unchanged in meaning — verified by `git diff` showing no edit to any assert
      body or message, only the parameter each test receives.
- [x] The list of `(key, expr, verdict)` tuples is byte-identical before and after
      the change, verified by capturing it on `origin/main` and on the change and
      comparing.
- [x] A seeded raw-config `RunRequest` site is still caught by
      `test_no_run_request_inherits_the_raw_config_model`, with the offender key in
      the failure message — evidence in a ticket comment, seed reverted.
- [x] The cache is a pytest session fixture plus a process-local parse memo, with
      no on-disk artifact, so nothing survives the pytest session — verified by
      `git diff` showing no file is written.
- [x] Before/after durations for the four guards are measured with
      `pytest --durations` and posted as a ticket comment.
baseline.summary: Four model-provenance guards repeat the same whole-tree AST analysis

## Context / Problem
The automated-quality audit found approved maintainability ratchets that cannot be enabled wholesale without first accounting for existing diagnostics. This epic stages blocking enforcement for function complexity, four safe Mypy settings, Ruff ASYNC/DTZ, and Ruff RUF hygiene. It explicitly defers disallow_any_generics, disallow_untyped_defs, Ruff security-family S rules, and Semgrep expansion.

## Approach
Deliver independently reviewed stories into a short-lived Gerrit feature branch, then merge the completed branch atomically to main. Stories that edit pyproject.toml execute in this order: d9f5-baa5-9fc3-451d, then 28cd-d8f8-4456-482c, then 125d-ee6f-7af0-4200. The 28cd story creates and owns tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py; 125d depends on 28cd and extends that file. The complexity story does not share pyproject.toml and may proceed independently when next-batch reports no file-impact conflict.

Rejected: one large cleanup change, because it would mix distinct tools, obscure regressions, and make rollback difficult.

## Child Decomposition
- c9f7-d6df-bce0-4b77: add a symbol-level shrink-only C901 baseline at threshold 15 and wire it into the canonical lint gate.
- d9f5-baa5-9fc3-451d: enable no_implicit_optional, strict_equality, warn_redundant_casts, and warn_unused_ignores after revalidating the measured diagnostics.
- 28cd-d8f8-4456-482c: make the three DTZ sites timezone-explicit, enable ASYNC/DTZ, create the shared Ruff ratchet test, and run the integration pytest tier.
- 125d-ee6f-7af0-4200: clear RUF100 and other approved RUF diagnostics, extend the shared Ruff ratchet test, and continue to defer RUF001, RUF002, and RUF003.

## Verification Checkpoints
After each story, its focused commands and Gerrit labels are recorded on that child ticket. After all children merge to the server-side feature branch, the integration worktree runs each command in the Acceptance Criteria independently.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every direct child is closed; `rebar list --parent=facb-44c3-2ada-41ee --status=open,in_progress` returns an empty JSON array (no open or in_progress direct child).
- [x] make lint exits 0 from the integrated feature worktree.
- [x] make typecheck exits 0 from the integrated feature worktree.
- [x] config-check exits 0 from the integrated feature worktree.
- [x] pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q exits 0 from the integrated feature worktree.
- [x] pytest -m integration -q exits 0 from the integrated feature worktree.
- [x] [operator-attested] Every story change has LLM-Review +1 in Gerrit.
- [x] [operator-attested] Every story change has Verified +1 in Gerrit.
- [x] [operator-attested] Every story change has zero unresolved Gerrit comments.
- [x] [operator-attested] The final no-ff merge-back change has LLM-Review +1 in Gerrit.
- [x] [operator-attested] The final no-ff merge-back change has Verified +1 in Gerrit.
- [x] [operator-attested] The final no-ff merge-back change has zero unresolved Gerrit comments.
- [x] [operator-attested] The final no-ff merge-back change is submitted to main.
- [x] After fetching origin, git merge-base --is-ancestor for every child rebar-ticket commit against origin/main exits 0.

<!-- green-on-origin-main AC -->
- [x] Before the final merge-back lands, `git fetch origin` is run and every gate newly enforced by this epic (the C901 complexity wrapper, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `config-check`) exits 0 against the **current** `origin/main` tip — no gate is landed while it reports a failure on current `origin/main`.
- [x] Every pre-existing diagnostic in an enforced ratchet family (C901, the four Mypy flags, Ruff ASYNC/DTZ, Ruff RUF) that is present on the **current** `origin/main` at land time — including any introduced by `origin/main` drift after each story's measured baseline commit — is resolved (or, for C901, captured in the shrink-only baseline) before the corresponding gate is landed.

baseline.description:
## Context
On the Gerrit `Verified` gate, `tests/unit/test_opcert_service_app.py` intermittently crashes its pytest-xdist worker (`worker gwN crashed`; `[gwN] node down: Not properly terminated`), failing the whole matrix job and producing a spurious `Verified -1`. The failure is a hard worker-process death (not an assertion), lands on a RANDOM matrix shard per run (~1 of 4), and is timing/platform-dependent. Observed 4+ consecutive times on 2026-08-08 blocking change 1545 (ticket ad16), whose diff is markdown/comment-only and cannot touch `opcert_service`. Reproduction is CI-only (never locally).

## Root cause
The background worker offloads each job with `asyncio.to_thread(jobs.run_job, ...)` (`src/rebar/opcert_service/app.py` ~line 77), which runs on the **event loop's global default `ThreadPoolExecutor`**. The lifespan teardown (`app.py` ~55-59) cancels and awaits the worker *asyncio task*, but `asyncio.to_thread` exposes no handle to the underlying OS thread, and that thread's disposal is tied to the loop's `shutdown_default_executor()`. When the `TestClient` anyio portal tears the fixture down under xdist, the loop/portal can close without deterministically disposing the default executor, so a leftover default-executor thread is still unwinding when the worker process exits -> `[gwN] node down: Not properly terminated`. The previously-proposed "make the `with TestClient(...) as c:` exit guaranteed" change is a no-op (the fixture at :44-49 already uses a `with` block).

## Constraint: this must stay consistent with ADR-0067
`review_bot/app.py`, which this service mirrors, DELIBERATELY keeps `asyncio.to_thread` and accepts the un-force-cancellable orphan thread; ADR-0067 ("review-bot bounded shutdown") explicitly **rejects an unbounded `await`/join at teardown** because a genuinely hung `run_job` would hang shutdown forever. So the fix must NOT introduce a blocking `executor.shutdown(wait=True)` join (that reopens ADR-0067's rejected alternative). The change below is additive: it preserves the bounded/abandon-in-flight property and only makes the executor's per-loop disposal DETERMINISTIC.

## Plan (app-owned executor, bounded disposal — `src/rebar/opcert_service/app.py`)
- In `lifespan` startup, create an app-owned executor:
  `app.state.executor = concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=WORKER_COUNT, thread_name_prefix="opcert-job")`.
- In `_worker`, replace `asyncio.to_thread(jobs.run_job, ...)` with
  `loop.run_in_executor(app.state.executor, functools.partial(jobs.run_job, ...))` (same call, same
  `asyncio.wait_for(..., job_timeout_seconds)` wrapper, same result/timeout semantics — no request/response
  behavior change).
- In the lifespan `finally`, AFTER the existing bounded task cancel/await, dispose the app-owned executor with a
  BOUNDED, NON-blocking shutdown: `app.state.executor.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)`. This cancels
  queued futures and lets idle worker threads exit on the sentinel, WITHOUT blocking on an in-flight job
  (ADR-0067-consistent: abandon in-flight, the process is exiting). Because the executor is owned by the app and
  disposed INSIDE the lifespan shutdown (which `TestClient` runs before it closes the loop/portal), its threads
  are handled deterministically at teardown instead of leaking onto the loop's global default executor.

Explicitly REJECTED alternatives (documented so they are not re-litigated):
- `@pytest.mark.xdist_group` co-location — INERT here: the default suite that runs this unit module uses
  `--dist worksteal` (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:653-654`); `xdist_group` only groups under
  `--dist loadgroup`, which CI uses ONLY for the `-m integration` tier (line 668). Switching the unit lane's
  dist-mode edits contended CI config, which is out of this epic's non-overlapping scope.
- `executor.shutdown(wait=True)` blocking join — reopens ADR-0067's rejected unbounded-shutdown alternative.

## Testing
Deterministic, in-session-evaluable checks (no probabilistic CI dependence, no undeclared tooling):
- Teardown disposes the app-owned executor (the actual end-state that removes the orphan): a unit test enters the
  `TestClient` context, exercises a job round-trip, exits the context, then asserts the app-owned executor is
  shut down (`app_module.app.state.executor._shutdown is True`) and no thread whose name starts with
  `opcert-job` remains alive
  (`[t for t in threading.enumerate() if t.name.startswith("opcert-job") and t.is_alive()] == []`).
- The offload no longer uses the loop's global default executor:
  `grep -n "asyncio.to_thread" src/rebar/opcert_service/app.py` returns `0` matches, and
  `grep -n "run_in_executor\|ThreadPoolExecutor\|executor.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)" src/rebar/opcert_service/app.py`
  shows the app-owned executor, its use, and its bounded disposal.
- Existing HTTP-plumbing tests still pass: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_opcert_service_app.py -q`.
- CI corroboration (monitored, NOT the acceptance oracle since it is probabilistic): the `Verified` matrix shows
  no `worker gwN crashed` / `node down` line for this module after the change.

## Resolution (2026-08-11 re-measurement — defect already fixed; original ACs void, closed `duplicate`)

The crash is **fixed**, but not by the plan below — and the plan's root-cause hypothesis was falsified before this ticket was written. This ticket duplicates [rebar:2207-2917-e21b-42bd] ("py3.11 xdist worker crash: opcert test_matching_guard_is_accepted", closed `flaky`) — same test, same symptom — whose RCA proved the real mechanism and whose fix, commit `8c9bf5d78d` (2026-08-08 21:38), repaired it.

### The proven mechanism (from 2207's RCA)

**CPython issue 86296**: on Python 3.11, `asyncio.wait_for` *consumes* an external cancellation when its child completes in the same event-loop turn. The worker then loops back to `queue.get()` with `cancelling()==1` while lifespan awaits it forever; pytest-timeout kills the worker, surfacing as `worker gwN crashed` / `node down: Not properly terminated`. Python 3.12+ is unaffected — which is why the failure was CI-only and shard-random (only the 3.11 matrix leg is susceptible).

`8c9bf5d78d` replaced `asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.to_thread(...), timeout=…)` with `async with asyncio.timeout(...): await asyncio.to_thread(...)`, restoring correct cancellation semantics, and added two regression tests.

### Differential evidence (2026-08-11)

Note first that **the repo `.venv` is Python 3.12.13**, so any local run in it is non-discriminating for a 3.11-only defect. A dedicated 3.11 venv was built for this measurement.

Running the regression oracle `8c9bf5d78d` added, on py3.11, against pre-fix vs current `app.py`:

    PRE-FIX (43e822a83f = 8c9bf5d78d^)   RUN 1: rc=124  HUNG (killed at 120s)
                                          RUN 2: rc=1    1 failed, 7 passed
                                          RUN 3: rc=124  HUNG (killed at 120s)
    HEAD                                  RUN 1: rc=0    8 passed in 0.69s
                                          RUN 2: rc=0    8 passed in 0.70s
                                          RUN 3: rc=0    8 passed in 1.02s

Verbatim from the pre-fix failure:

    assert worker.done(), "worker ignored shutdown cancellation and returned to queue"
    E   AssertionError: worker ignored shutdown cancellation and returned to queue
    E    +  where False = <Task cancelling name='Task-26'
             coro=<_worker() running at .../prefix/src/rebar/opcert_service/app.py:70>>.done
    FAILED tests/unit/test_opcert_service_app.py::test_worker_cancellation_survives_job_completion_race

`Task cancelling`, parked at `app.py:70` (`queue.get()`) — exactly the RCA's mechanism. The two `rc=124` hangs ARE the CI symptom (CI's guard kills the worker at 300s; a 120s cap caught it sooner). 3/3 hang-or-fail pre-fix, 3/3 clean at HEAD.

Supporting non-discriminating runs, all green at HEAD: `pytest tests/unit -k opcert -p xdist -n 4` = 134 passed x3 on py3.12 and x3 on py3.11; the ticket's own Testing command (`pytest tests/unit/test_opcert_service_app.py -q`) = 8 passed x3 on py3.12 and x3 on py3.11.

### CI corroboration (the signal this ticket designates as monitored)

Trawled `Gerrit Verified Gate` logs for the crash signatures (`node down: Not properly terminated`, `worker gwN crashed`, `INTERNALERROR`, `replacing crashed worker`, `test_matching_guard_is_accepted`). Fix ancestry was established per-run with `git merge-base --is-ancestor 8c9bf5d78d <run headSha>` rather than by wall-clock, which matters: `8c9bf5d78d` is 2026-08-08 21:38 -0700 = **2026-08-09 04:38 UTC**, so several runs dated 08-09 do not actually contain it.

**Positive control (proves the search detects the thing).** Both pre-fix runs named in this ticket's own comment light up verbatim — run 31244604695, `pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.11)`:

    [gw3] node down: Not properly terminated
    [gw3] linux -- Python 3.11.15 /home/runner/work/rebar/rebar/.venv/bin/python
    worker 'gw3' crashed while running 'tests/unit/test_opcert_service_app.py::test_matching_guard_is_accepted'

Run 31266912051 is byte-identical. Four further runs (31292427797, 31291608135, 31290743251,
31289893832) also match and are confirmed **NOT** fix-ancestors — so the true pre-fix count is **six
consecutive occurrences, not four**, all on the `ubuntu-latest, py3.11` leg. One of them crashed **gw1**, not gw3, confirming the crash is not worker-pinned.

**Post-fix: zero.** 0 of 21 genuine fix-containing runs match any signature; all 21 returned usable logs. The zero is meaningful because **13 of the 21 ran the suite to 11,561-11,862 passes** — past the ~11,435-pass point where the crash used to fire. The remaining 8 failed at a pre-pytest gate (module-size / docs-staleness / lint) so pytest never collected and they are evidentially neutral. A fully-green post-fix run (31455407940) was spot-checked with complete `--log`: also zero matches.

All 12 real post-fix test failures were unrelated and individually distinct (store-lock, complexity baseline, py3.14 transport drift, `_resolve_conflicted_pop`, git contention 9305, S3 doctor, import-convention gate, lock-steal). None is an xdist worker death.

### Why the original Acceptance Criteria are VOID rather than met

They are recorded here rather than left as unreachable checkboxes. ACs 1-3 encode the **app-owned-`ThreadPoolExecutor`** hypothesis — that an orphaned default-executor thread from `asyncio.to_thread` survives portal teardown. **2207's RCA investigated and explicitly rejected that hypothesis** ("Executor alternative rejected for this incident"). Measured against current `src/rebar/opcert_service/app.py`:

- **AC1 — FAIL, and correctly so.** `grep -n "asyncio.to_thread"` returns line 77 (AC demanded 0
  matches). No `run_in_executor`, no `ThreadPoolExecutor`, no `app.state.executor`.
- **AC2 — FAIL.** `grep -n "executor.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)"` returns 0 matches.
- **AC3 — FAIL.** No teardown test asserting `app.state.executor._shutdown`; the attribute does not
  exist.
- **AC4 — PASS.** 8 passed, verified 6x (3x py3.12, 3x py3.11).
- **AC5 — vacuously satisfied.** No unbounded join was added; ADR-0067's bounded-shutdown property
  is intact, since the fix never touched the offload strategy.

Implementing ACs 1-3 as written would be work against an already-falsified hypothesis, and would churn a code path that ADR-0067 deliberately keeps aligned with `review_bot/app.py`. That is why this closes as `duplicate` of the ticket that carries the proven root cause, not as "criteria met".

## Testing

    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_opcert_service_app.py -q
baseline.summary: Flaky CI: pytest-xdist worker crash on test_opcert_service_app::test_matching_guard_is_accepted

## Context / Problem
Nested pytest sessions that execute tests requiring temporary fixtures without a private --basetemp join pytest's user-global numbered root and may delete unrelated cleanup-eligible trees at session finish. The parent pytest process owns the temporary lifetime, so each affected nested child must use a unique basetemp under its parent's tmp_path. This bug was discovered from grindable-deviant-angwantibo after its runtime RCA confirmed that cleanup mechanism.

## Complete nested-pytest inventory
Direct subprocess launch constructs:
- tests/_store_isolation.py:32-48 is safe: it passes tmp_path / nested-pytest as --basetemp.
- tests/unit/test_external_isolation.py:62-78 is safe: it passes tmp_path / bt as --basetemp.
- tests/unit/test_ci_snapshot_fixture_cleanup.py:13-31 is safe: it passes tmp_path / nested-basetemp as --basetemp.
- tests/unit/test_git_version_floor.py:143-178 is non-applicable: --collect-only exits during configuration under the fake under-floor Git and never allocates TempPathFactory._basetemp.
- tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:826-848 is non-applicable: its --collect-only children instantiate no fixtures and never allocate TempPathFactory._basetemp.
- tests/unit/test_tests_import_convention.py:82-116 is non-applicable: its --collect-only children instantiate no fixtures and never allocate TempPathFactory._basetemp.
- tests/unit/test_engine_dir.py:148-204 is confirmed unsafe: it executes the selected reducer test under repository conftest autouse fixtures, allocating the shared numbered root without --basetemp.
- tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py:142-178 is confirmed unsafe: it executes the standalone reproduction module under repository conftest autouse fixtures, allocating the shared numbered root without --basetemp.

Pytester's managed launches are already safe: six pytester.runpytest_subprocess calls in tests/unit/test_caplog_coverage_integrity.py:180-264 receive the helper's native numbered --basetemp, and four pytester.runpytest calls in tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py:158-215 pass through Pytester._ensure_basetemp. The literal pytest occurrences in tests/scripts/test_summarize_ci_failures.py:134 and tests/unit/grounding/test_deps.py:286-298 are test data, not launch sites.

The non-applicable classification follows pytest 9.1's _pytest.tmpdir.TempPathFactory contract inspected in the installed locked dependency: pytest_configure constructs the factory without allocating a root; pytest_sessionfinish returns immediately while _basetemp is None; getbasetemp is what creates and registers cleanup for the numbered root. Therefore a collect-only child that resolves no temporary fixture cannot execute this defect. A repository-wide AST/literal search plus a pytester.runpytest search found no other nested pytest launch sites. Pinned evidence: uv.lock:2403-2404 locks pytest 9.1.1; pytest 9.1.1 upstream src/_pytest/tmpdir.py lines 145-229 show getbasetemp creates the numbered root and registers cleanup, lines 244-254 show pytest_configure only constructs the factory, and lines 315-340 show pytest_sessionfinish returns while _basetemp is None (https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/9.1.1/src/_pytest/tmpdir.py).

## Approach
Add tmp_path to each of the two confirmed unsafe outer tests and pass a distinct child path through --basetemp. This follows the already-green ownership pattern in tests/_store_isolation.py:32-48 and tests/unit/test_external_isolation.py:62-78, keeps cleanup local to the parent fixture, and preserves each child's interpreter or console-script entrypoint, cwd, selectors, plugins, and assertions. The three collect-only launchers remain unchanged because runtime control flow cannot reach the cleanup mechanism; changing them would not repair a demonstrated defect.

Extend the existing behavior-level real-subprocess regression in tests/unit/test_test_suite_store_isolation.py for the two executing sites, reusing assert_nodes_do_not_mutate_external_store from tests/_store_isolation.py. A seed child allocates an isolated PYTEST_DEBUG_TEMPROOT; the test then creates enough unlocked numbered directories to make the seed sentinel cleanup-eligible. The outer subprocess receives its own --basetemp so it cannot touch the shared root. It drives one affected outer test, whose nested child crosses the real numbered-root cleanup seam. The sentinel's exact bytes distinguish the broken and repaired behavior without timing sleeps or source-text assertions.

## Scope
- tests/unit/test_engine_dir.py: parent-owned basetemp for the mixed-module child.
- tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py: parent-owned basetemp for the standalone bare-pytest child.
- tests/unit/test_test_suite_store_isolation.py: held-out real-subprocess regression for both confirmed cleanup sites.

No production module, dependency, configuration key, or public API changes.

## Testing
- RED oracle: seed an isolated shared numbered root, prove the sentinel is cleanup-eligible, run each affected outer test with an outer --basetemp, and assert its nested child deletes the sentinel before repair.
- GREEN oracle: apply the repair and assert each exact sentinel byte payload remains unchanged.
- Contrast/control: require each driven outer test to return success, preserving its existing entrypoint, cwd, selection, plugin, and assertion contract.
- Mutation: remove one repaired --basetemp pair to restore the exact defect and confirm that site's held-out case returns RED, then restore it.
- Focused: run the new regression plus tests/unit/test_engine_dir.py and tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py.
- Broad: run the CI default unit selection, make lint, and make typecheck.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The inventory classifies every direct and pytester-managed nested pytest launch; verified by repository AST, literal, and pytester.runpytest searches.
- [ ] The engine-directory nested child leaves its cleanup-eligible sentinel byte-for-byte unchanged; verified by its parametrized case in tests/unit/test_test_suite_store_isolation.py.
- [ ] The standalone import-convention nested child leaves its cleanup-eligible sentinel byte-for-byte unchanged; verified by its parametrized case in tests/unit/test_test_suite_store_isolation.py.
- [ ] Existing nested entrypoint, cwd, selector, plugin, and child assertions remain green; verified by focused execution of both affected modules.
- [ ] Removing a repaired --basetemp makes the corresponding held-out behavior case fail; verified by the exact-defect mutation run.
- [ ] The CI default unit selection exits zero.
- [ ] make lint exits zero.
- [ ] make typecheck exits zero.
baseline.summary: Nested pytest meta-tests still clean the user-global numbered temp root

## Problem / opportunity

The source process audit found 49.0% first-pass plan review and a p90 of eight attempts. That is meaningful churn, but the project already has a mature deterministic pre-LLM floor: current code implements P1-P11. A proposal framed as "add deterministic preflight" would duplicate existing architecture and risk promoting noisy heuristics.

## Prior decisions that constrain this idea

elfin-floor-gouge established the deterministic tier as the default blocking layer and semantic LLM review as the architecture/context layer. depleted-lethal-brownbear promoted P10/P11 only after pass/block backtests demonstrated discrimination and low false-positive rates; it rejected spec-by-example and riskiest-assumption blockers because they did not discriminate. childsafe-bizarre-lorikeet found that criterion-skipping on revised plans is unsafe: 37% of 894 revisions blocked on a criterion absent from the first block. It separately identified identical-material re-reviews as a quality-neutral optimization target.

This idea must extend the existing floor rather than build a parallel preflight or weaken semantic review.

## Outcome hypothesis

Persisted plan-review and completion sidecars can reveal a small Pareto set of recurrent, mechanically decidable failure classes. Replay-tested candidates may reduce avoidable LLM churn without increasing false blocks or hiding cross-cutting findings.

## Guardrails

- Candidate checks must be mechanically decidable from evidence available before the LLM review.
- Unsupported or uncertain grounding fails open and records coverage.
- No criterion-skipping based only on unchanged-looking plan sections.
- No promotion directly from intuition to blocking; use offline replay and an advisory observation period.
- Preserve semantic review for architecture, failure modes, portability, testing strategy, and tradeoffs.
- Optimize total review quality/cost, not PASS rate in isolation.

## Questions before promotion

- What is the Pareto distribution of blocking findings by normalized failure class and remediation?
- Which classes can be decided deterministically with pre-review material?
- What pass/block cohorts and sampling method establish a false-positive ceiling?
- What precision/recall and minimum support thresholds justify advisory rollout and later blocking?
- How will abstention, unsupported stacks, and stale grounding be represented?
- Which identical-material rerun causes can be eliminated without changing review coverage?
- What guard metrics ensure completion quality and defect signals do not worsen?

## Evidence

Discovered from unpleasing-hairy-yellowlegs; source audit bleakish-stational-cob. Prior work: elfin-floor-gouge, depleted-lethal-brownbear, papyral-scarlet-malamute, childsafe-bizarre-lorikeet, big-mammalian-bronco.
baseline.summary: Mine review history for the next low-false-positive deterministic plan checks

## Summary

The integration test
`tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py::test_reconcile_dry_run_against_live_jira`
**fails (does not skip)** in an environment where `acli` is on PATH but no live Jira project is
configured for the test's fixture repo. Observed while running the full unit+integration suite
locally during the commit-ticket-gate work (ticket `263d-e96c-80b4-4c84`). NOT caused by that
change (which does not touch reconcile / Jira), and it is excluded from the default CI gate
(`-m "not integration and not external"`), so the Gerrit `Verified` gate is unaffected.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Have `acli` on PATH (so the test's `shutil.which("acli") is None` skip guard does NOT fire).
2. Do NOT configure a live Jira project for the fixture (`JIRA_PROJECT` unset; the fresh
   `rebar_repo` fixture has no `[jira] project`).
3. Run: `pytest tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py::test_reconcile_dry_run_against_live_jira`
   (or the whole integration tier: `pytest -m integration`).

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** the test skips (no live Jira env) or asserts a routed, non-mutating dry-run.
- **Actual:** `rebar reconcile` raises and exits non-zero; the assertion
  `'"mode": "dry-run"' in out or '"no_write": true' in out or returncode == 0` fails:
  ```
  ERROR: reconcile_once raised: inbound fetch requires a valid jira.project key
  (JIRA_PROJECT / [jira] project); got ''. Refusing to search Jira unscoped.
  ```

## Analysis

The reconciler's inbound-fetch guard (refuse an unscoped Jira search when `jira.project` is
empty) is correct, pre-existing behaviour. The bug is in the TEST's precondition: its skip
guard checks only for `acli` on PATH, not for a configured Jira project — so on a machine where
`acli` is installed but the fixture repo has no `jira.project`, the test runs and trips the
guard. Test brittleness / missing precondition, not a reconciler regression.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The test SKIPS (not fails) when a live Jira project is not configured — e.g. also gate on
      `os.environ.get("JIRA_PROJECT")` (or a configured `[jira] project`), or set `jira.project`
      in the fixture repo before invoking `rebar reconcile`.
- [ ] With `acli` present AND a valid Jira project, the test still exercises the dry-run path.
- [ ] `pytest -m integration tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py` passes or skips cleanly in
      both configurations (project set / unset).
baseline.summary: test_reconcile_dry_run_against_live_jira fails (not skips) when acli is present but fixture has no jira.project

## Context / Problem
The shared git-backed tickets store has chronically wedged under parallel multi-session writes. Proven chain (RCA on 6ccc-0577-198c-44fa, live recurrence on e72e-259d-5ee7-4e73): the operation-linked compaction sweep (rebar._commands.compact_trigger.maybe_compact -> detached worker -> compact_txn._compact_locked) mutates the worktree (SNAPSHOT write, *.retired renames, .archived deletions) BEFORE its git commit, with no rollback on worker death. The leftover dirty tree then makes rebar._store.sync._union_merge's `git merge origin/tickets` abort in two variants: (a) untracked files origin wants to create (recovered by Gerrit change 1757, ticket small-delicious-loris), and (b) tracked-file deletions/modifications ("Your local changes ... would be overwritten") — unhandled. The abort strands local ticket commits off origin (P0 data-loss risk) and the dirty tree breaks every plan-review/close attestation (strict `git status --porcelain` head check). Root residue: 119 `*/.archived` and 126 `*/.write.lock` runtime markers are TRACKED in HEAD (committed before their gitignore patterns existed; gitignore never un-tracks), so routine marker churn shows as tracked dirt forever. Interim mitigation active: user-config compact.trigger=off (recorded on e72e-259d-5ee7-4e73).

This epic makes the store wedge-PROOF (the dirty state is never produced), SELF-HEALING (sync and push recover the known abort classes in place), OPERATOR-REPAIRABLE (fsck detects the class, doctor repairs it under the write lock), and SCALABLE (store-wide scans default to active tickets, with an override flag reaching archived ones).

## Child decomposition (responsibilities, dependency-ordered)
- **Untrack per-ticket runtime markers** (`*/.archived`, `*/.write.lock`) from the tickets branch via an idempotent ensure unit, and make the reader self-heal a missing marker cache — removes the tracked-dirt class at its source; first because every later recovery then only faces untracked artifacts.
- **Crash-atomic compaction fold** (bug compulsory-pernickety-mantis): the fold commits as one unit with rollback on failure, plus a sweep-start crash-recovery preamble that reverts an abandoned partial fold under the write lock — the dirty tree is never produced. Discrimination of the two half-fold states is by an INTENT JOURNAL (a commit-pending sentinel): before its first worktree mutation the fold writes an intent record (ticket id, snapshot path, folded source list) OUTSIDE the worktree (under the tracker's git dir, so the sentinel itself can never be tree dirt), and removes it on every completed outcome — after the fold's commit succeeds, AND on the `_retire_folded_sources` failure paths (both the clean-rollback return and the intentionally-retained SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT state it keeps for `fsck --repair-snapshots`). The recovery preamble therefore reverts ONLY when it finds a live journal whose recorded snapshot is still uncommitted (rename `*.retired` sources back, unlink the uncommitted snapshot, unstage the ticket dir); a journal whose snapshot is already in HEAD means the crash hit between commit and journal removal, so recovery just discards the journal; and the retained SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT state has NO journal by construction, so the preamble never touches it — `fsck --repair-snapshots` remains its sole owner.
- **Reconverge tracked-artifact recovery** (variant b): `_union_merge` also recovers the "local changes would be overwritten" abort for store-artifact paths (restore worktree-deleted tracked files from HEAD, quarantine modified ones), retry once — depends on change 1757's untracked-path quarantine landing (ticket small-delicious-loris).
- **Push-recovery parity** (bug sulfuryl-suicidal-osprey): the non-fast-forward push recovery path gets the same untracked-collision + tracked-deletion recovery as reconverge.
- **fsck detection + doctor repair**: `rebar fsck` reports the dirty-tree/stale-lock class (tracked deletions, untracked regenerable leftovers, orphaned locks, orphaned .tmp-event-*); `rebar doctor --repair` heals what is safe under the write lock (restore, quarantine, reclaim), never touching `.tmp-event-*` content.
- **Active-only scan scoping**: store-wide walks (fsck scan, compact-all sweep) default to non-archived tickets and accept `--include-archived` to reach the full store, so scan cost tracks the ACTIVE working set as the store grows.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A compaction fold interrupted at any point between its first worktree mutation and its commit leaves the tracker tree clean after the next sweep or doctor run; proxy: kill-mid-fold unit test asserts `git status --porcelain` is empty post-recovery.
- [x] A reconverge facing EITHER abort variant on regenerable store artifacts completes the union merge keeping both parents, with no local commit orphaned; proxy: RED->GREEN tests for both variants in tests/unit.
- [x] `git ls-files '*/.archived' '*/.write.lock'` in the tracker returns empty after the ensure unit runs, and marker add/remove churn no longer appears in `git status`; proxy: ensure-unit test on a fixture store seeded with tracked markers.
- [x] `rebar fsck` names each dirty-tree/stale-lock finding class and `rebar doctor --repair` heals a seeded wedge end-to-end; proxy: integration test seeds all classes and asserts clean status + converged merge afterward.
- [x] [operator-attested] `rebar fsck` and `rebar compact-all` default to active tickets and reach archived ones only with `--include-archived`; proxy: tests/unit/test_scan_scoping.py (merged 39de64871c) — test_fsck_default_skips_archived_and_flag_restores, test_ticket_dirs_defaults_to_active_only, and the compact-all sweep tests count visited dirs both ways on an archived+active fixture.
- [x] [operator-attested] The interim user-config `compact.trigger=off` mitigation is removed once the crash-atomicity child closes; proxy: comment recorded on e72e-259d-5ee7-4e73 (AC-20 proxy record) — no compact.trigger key remains in any config and compact-sweep.stamp shows sweeps at defaults.
baseline.summary: Wedge-proof tickets store: crash-atomic compaction, self-healing sync recovery, marker untracking, fsck/doctor repair, active-only scan scoping

# Extend the survived-LLM-step-failure tally to review-code and verify-completion

## Context (verified at origin/main cc69cc1179)

`eclectic-industrial-argali` landed a run-scoped sink (`src/rebar/llm/step_failures.py`) that counts LLM step calls which fail but do NOT fail the run, surfaced on the plan-review verdict as `coverage.llm_step_failures`. It was scoped to `review-plan` only. The recording site is already universal: every LLM call funnels through `PydanticAIRunner.run`'s except block (`src/rebar/llm/runner.py:595`), which calls `step_failures.record(...)` unconditionally. So both remaining gates start counting the moment a scope is active around them — this ticket is scope activation plus a drain.

Reference shape, plan-review: activation `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:163` (`collect_step_failures()`), drain `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:526-528` (present ONLY when non-empty).

## review-code (wiring only)

It already has a `coverage` object (`src/rebar/schemas/code_review_verdict.schema.json`) and an exact structural twin to copy: the contract-violation drain at `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py:521-523`.

1. Activate the sink in the code-review run scope —
   `gate_dispatch.py:480`, currently
   `with gate_source.gate_read_root(handle), review_kernel.collect_contract_violations():`.
2. Drain into that gate's coverage beside the violations drain
   (`code_review/workflow_ops.py:521-523`), same present-only-when-non-empty posture.
3. Declare `coverage.llm_step_failures` in `code_review_verdict.schema.json`, mirroring the
   `plan_review_verdict.schema.json` block verbatim (`required: [total, by_step]`, `total`
   integer minimum 1, `by_step` object of integers minimum 1).

## verify-completion (needs the placement decision)

`completion_verdict.schema.json` has NO `coverage` object — its properties are `verdict`, `findings`, `criteria`, `summary`, `remediation`, `target`, `reviewers`, `certifiable`, `runner`, `model`, `trace_id`. The parent ticket explicitly left the placement open (its closing comment: "verify-completion has no coverage object at all, so it needs a placement decision first"), and nothing in either ticket's recorded context decides it.

**Decision: `coverage.llm_step_failures`, mirroring the other two gates**, with `coverage` created ONLY when the tally is non-empty. Rationale, recorded because it is a judgement call:

- One JSON path (`coverage.llm_step_failures`) then works across all three gates, so a caller
  reads the tally the same way everywhere. A bespoke top-level key on this one gate would make
  the tally gate-specific for no gain.
- Creating `coverage` only when non-empty keeps a clean run's verdict byte-identical, so no
  empty container appears on the overwhelmingly common path. This matters more here than
  elsewhere: the completion verdict is SIGNED, and byte-identity on clean runs is the
  attestation-safety posture the parent established.

Wiring:

4. Activate the sink in the completion run scope — `gate_dispatch.py:696`
   (`with gate_config(cfg):`), so it covers the whole `run_workflow` call.
5. Drain in `completion_reconcile` (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py:251` — the registered step
   function, no leading underscore), the op that assembles the verdict, immediately before its
   `return findings.validate_structured(result, _OUTPUT_SCHEMA)` at `:319`. The deterministic
   `completion_passthrough` arm makes no LLM call, so its tally is empty and its verdict is
   unchanged.
6. Declare `coverage` (object, with the same `llm_step_failures` sub-block) in
   `completion_verdict.schema.json`. The schema is `additionalProperties: true`, so this
   documents the key rather than unblocking it.

## Constraints (same as the parent)

Observability only: never changes a verdict, an exit code, a signature, or a provenance stamp, and no swallow site changes behaviour. Present ONLY when non-empty.

## Tests

- review-code: with a sink scope active and a recorded failure, the code-review coach op puts
  `coverage.llm_step_failures` on the verdict; with no failure the key is ABSENT.
- verify-completion: same pair through `completion_reconcile` — and on the clean run assert
  `"coverage" not in verdict`, i.e. no empty container is created.
- The drained shape validates against each gate's schema (`total` + `by_step`).
- Both gate run scopes actually activate the sink, asserted at the dispatch level rather than
  only on the op, so a drain that can never receive anything is caught.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `review-code`: a survived LLM step failure appears at `coverage.llm_step_failures` on the
      code-review verdict.
- [x] `review-code`: a clean run's verdict has NO `llm_step_failures` key.
- [x] `verify-completion`: a survived LLM step failure appears at `coverage.llm_step_failures`
      on the completion verdict.
- [x] `verify-completion`: a clean run's verdict has NO `coverage` key at all (no empty
      container).
- [x] The code-review run scope (`gate_dispatch.py:480`) activates `collect_step_failures()`.
- [x] The completion run scope (`gate_dispatch.py:696`) activates `collect_step_failures()`.
- [x] `code_review_verdict.schema.json` declares `coverage.llm_step_failures` with
      `required: [total, by_step]`.
- [x] `completion_verdict.schema.json` declares `coverage.llm_step_failures` with
      `required: [total, by_step]`.
- [x] No verdict string, exit code, or signature changes on any run: the only observable
      difference is the added key.
- [x] Every touched file stays under the 800-LOC module-size cap (`gate_dispatch.py` is 721 and
      `gate_ops.py` 340 at origin/main, so this must not push either over).
- [x] The placement rationale for `verify-completion` is recorded as a comment on this ticket.
- [x] `make lint` passes.
- [x] `make typecheck` passes.
- [x] `pytest tests/unit` passes.
baseline.summary: Tally survived LLM step failures in review-code and verify-completion

## Context
Gerrit Verify run 31846417650 dynamically attributed the recurring macOS long pole: `socket.getfqdn` consumed 35.013s inside `ThreadingHTTPServer` construction for the loopback editor fixture; constructor and fixture setup were 35.014s/35.020s. TCP bind was below the 1s instrumentation threshold. The test contract needs a real loopback HTTP server but does not consume `server_name`, so reverse DNS changes no asserted behavior. This violates the operator requirement that individual tests remain negligible and that average Verify duration stay within 20–30 minutes without reducing coverage. pip explicitly bypasses the same ~30s HTTPServer reverse-DNS path; aiohttp and urllib3 likewise bind literal loopback/raw sockets.

## Proven root cause
CPython `HTTPServer.server_bind` calls `socket.getfqdn(host)` after binding. On GitHub macOS runners, reverse resolution of numeric `127.0.0.1` repeatedly waits about 35 seconds. The editor workflow constructs `ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), ...)`, so every affected test worker pays a network-environment-dependent lookup even though only loopback bind/address behavior is contractual.

## Plan
- Inventory existing editor-server tests and freeze a held-out behavioral oracle: editor workflow starts a real loopback server even when `socket.getfqdn` raises, and still publishes the literal bound address/port needed by clients.
- Prove the oracle RED against current main for the expected reverse-DNS reason.
- With the oracle held out from the fixer, introduce a local ThreadingHTTPServer subclass whose bind path delegates to `socketserver.TCPServer.server_bind` and derives `server_name`/`server_port` from the already-bound literal address, matching the established pip pattern without adding a dependency.
- Restore the oracle and prove GREEN; defect-seed the original HTTPServer bind path to return it to RED, then restore the fix.
- Run focused editor tests, lint, typecheck, and applicable workflow/action guards.
- Land through Gerrit, then use a full macOS Verify run to confirm the 35-second span disappears while real editor behavior remains covered.

## Caller safety
Expected post-fix behavior: all editor-workflow callers receive the same localhost URL, token, request handling, and shutdown behavior; only an unused reverse-DNS-derived `server_name` value becomes the literal bound host. Before repair, sweep all `ThreadingHTTPServer` and editor workflow callers up to three levels for any dependency on reverse-resolved `server_name`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A behavioral oracle is observed RED first because current server construction invokes `socket.getfqdn`.
- [ ] Editor workflow starts and serves over real loopback without invoking reverse DNS.
- [ ] Bound address/ephemeral port, request handling, authentication, and shutdown coverage remain intact.
- [ ] No new dependency, external call, skip, xfail, or weakened assertion is introduced.
- [ ] The defect-seeded original bind path makes the held-out oracle RED again.
- [ ] Focused tests, lint, typecheck, and applicable CI policy gates pass.
- [ ] Gerrit LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 precede merge.
- [ ] A post-fix macOS Verify observation records the removed span and wall-clock effect.
baseline.summary: Avoid reverse DNS in loopback editor test server

baseline.description:
`pyproject.toml:375` omits the `ARG*` family from `select`, so nothing detects a parameter that is accepted and never read. `ruff check --select ARG src/rebar` reports **72** (56 ARG001, 14 ARG002, 2 ARG005). This backlog concealed three real accepted-then-dropped values, which is the defect class that motivated this run's unwired-functionality sweep.

**Scope: a one-off sweep. No permanent gate is enabled by this ticket** — see "Revisit" below.

## Classification (a decision procedure covering every violation)

`ruff check --select ARG src/rebar` currently reports **64** (48 ARG001, 14 ARG002, 2 ARG005) — down from the 72 measured when this ticket was written, because `c61a` ("Retire dead bridge verbs") landed on `main` and deleted `purge_bridge.py`/`bridge.py`. Rather than a fixed count that drifts, EVERY violation is dispositioned by the procedure below, applied site-by-site with `ruff check --select ARG src/rebar` as the completeness oracle. Each of the 64 falls into exactly one bucket, and each bucket names a concrete action, so no violation is left without a disposition:

1. **Tracked real defect — EXCLUDED, left in place.** An accepted-then-silently-dropped value that
   *should* be consumed is a real bug, tracked separately and NOT fixed in this sweep. Exactly
   three are known: `timeout_s` (`7504-a127-e9b0-42bb`), the discarded close reason
   (`3803-8e04-7c32-4b80`, CLOSED), and the `acli_cmd` bug. Their residual ARG sites —
   `close_precheck.py:166` `_completion_precheck(*, reason)` (keyword-only, body never reads it)
   and `txn.py:189` `force_close_reason` — belong to the close-reason defect's surface; leave the
   violation in place (do not `_`-prefix or `# noqa` it). **If execution surfaces a NEW
   accepted-then-dropped value that looks like a genuine defect, do not fold its fix into this
   sweep:** `create` a ticket, `link <new> fc0c-e218-8b34-4858 discovered_from`, and leave that
   violation in place.
2. **Cluster-1 — reconciler leaf handlers (10 sites), normalize to `**_kwargs`** (see below).
3. **Cluster-2 — `OutboundMapper` Protocol conformance (7 sites), `# noqa: ARG002`** (see below).
4. **Rename UNSAFE (keyword-passed, string-referenced, or keyword-only) — resolve with
   `# noqa: ARG00x` + a one-line reason, never a bare rename.** The parameter is passed by keyword
   at a call site, referenced by string name (`getattr`/`setattr`/`monkeypatch.setattr`/
   `sig.parameters`/`**kwargs` unpacking), or declared keyword-only (after `*`), so `_`-prefixing
   it breaks a caller. Each such site must name the keyword call site or string reference that
   makes it unsafe. (Confirmed example: `_completion_precheck(*, reason)` is keyword-only — but it
   is bucket 1, excluded.)
5. **Interface/Protocol/callback-registry unused, dispatched POSITIONALLY — safe to `_`-prefix.**
   The parameter is pinned by a shared signature (e.g. the eval-scorer registry `case`, the
   reducer `_processors` `event`, the provider-factory `provider_name`, dispatch-table callbacks)
   but unused in this implementation, and every dispatch site calls positionally. `_`-prefix it.
6. **Plain mechanical (SAFE-RENAME) — `_`-prefix the parameter (zero-touch).** No keyword call
   site, no string reference, not keyword-only, not interface-pinned. Where the value is genuinely
   dead and the parameter is purely local, delete the parameter and its call site(s) instead.

The load-bearing safety check is the bucket-4 test: a rename is applied ONLY after confirming with `grep` (not semantic search alone — Serena omits string references) that the name is neither passed by keyword nor referenced as a string. The executor records the final per-bucket counts and the irreducible `# noqa`/excluded total on this ticket (see AC).

### CLUSTER-1 — reconciler leaf handlers (10 violations)

`apply_inbound.py:135,177,205,224` and `apply_outbound.py:92,127,168,190,215`, all dispatched from `_LEAVES` in `typed_dispatch.py:56-70` and invoked at `:142` as `handler(mutation, **_leaf_kwargs)`.

Two hazards that make a naive rename unsafe:

- `client` is passed **unconditionally** (`typed_dispatch.py:137`: `_leaf_kwargs = {"client": client}`).
  Renaming it to `_client` is an immediate runtime `TypeError`, caught by no type checker.
- `repo_root` is gated by **runtime string introspection** (`typed_dispatch.py:128`:
  `accepts_repo_root = "repo_root" in sig.parameters or _has_var_kw`). Renaming flips this to
  `False` and the dispatcher silently stops passing it — a cosmetic lint fix changing dispatch
  behaviour through a string comparison.

**Preferred resolution: normalize the leaves to `**_kwargs`.** This removes all 10 violations without a rename and decouples dispatch from parameter spelling. Decide once for all ten; do not rename piecemeal.

**Normalize only the UNUSED parameters — keep the ones the body reads.** "Normalize to `**_kwargs`" does not mean stripping every named parameter: several leaves DO read `client` (e.g. `apply_outbound.py` create/conflict) or `repo_root`, and those must stay as explicit named parameters (keeping them named is itself rename-free and ARG-clean because they are used). The `**_kwargs` catch-all replaces only the parameters that are accepted-but-unused in that leaf, so each leaf ends as `def _leaf(mutation, *, client=..., **_kwargs)` or `def _leaf(mutation, **_kwargs)` depending on what its body actually consumes. The invariant to preserve: every parameter the body reads is still delivered (the dispatcher passes client unconditionally and repo_root/binding_store by the string-introspection gate), and every unused one is absorbed by `**_kwargs`.

**Third string-introspected kwarg — `binding_store`.** `typed_dispatch.py` gates a THIRD kwarg by the identical runtime string check: `accepts_binding_store = "binding_store" in sig.parameters or _has_var_kw` (`:129`), and per ticket 1577 only leaves that explicitly declare `binding_store` receive it. Normalizing a leaf to `**_kwargs` sets `_has_var_kw=True`, so `accepts_binding_store` flips to `True` and EVERY normalized leaf now also receives `binding_store` (and `repo_root`). This is behaviour-preserving because the leaf body ignores the extra keyword — but it IS a change in what the dispatcher passes, so it must be pinned by a test (see AC): the observable reconciler result is identical, and a leaf that previously did not receive `binding_store` still produces the same events/effects when it now does.

### CLUSTER-2 — `OutboundMapper` Protocol conformance (7 violations)

`adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:89,90,91,93` and `adapters/jira_family/outbound_mapper.py:44,45,46`. Names are pinned by the Protocol at `_backend.py:370-392`, implemented by two backends, and call sites pass **by keyword** (`outbound_field_diff.py:285-287,346-348`). Renaming is a contract break across a Protocol, two backends and two keyword call sites. `suppressed_out` (`jira_datacenter/backend.py:93`) is documented as accepted-and-ignored on purpose (ticket 8390) and the Protocol docstring at `_backend.py:379-383` mandates that behaviour.

**Resolution: `# noqa: ARG002` with a Protocol reference.** This is correct code that ARG cannot model — ruff concedes the general case is blocked on type inference (astral-sh/ruff#15952, open).

## Why no gate

`_`-prefixing is NOT a universally safe remediation here, contrary to a common assumption. Ruff's lead maintainer, astral-sh/ruff#10409: *"You could change `name: str` to `_name: str`, but that also carries some risk, since it will break for users that pass keyword arguments."* This codebase proves it: Cluster-1 renames break runtime dispatch, Cluster-2 renames break keyword call sites.

A survey of ~15 major Python projects found **no project that adopted ARG and later reverted** — but also that the exclusion is near-universal and always added in the same commit that first enabled ruff (attrs: `"ARG",  # unused arguments are normal when implementing interfaces`; pythondotorg: `# Django views/signals/admin methods have required unused args by framework contract`; Home Assistant: `# generic callbacks and setup methods create a lot of warnings`). Counter-examples exist and matter: beancount/fava runs ARG fully enabled with no exemptions at all, PlasmaPy for 3+ years.

Enabling ARG here would require carrying roughly **17 permanent inline `# noqa: ARG00x`** — a discretionary per-site exception mechanism, which this project has ruled against in favour of restrictions that are absolute or bounded by an invariant. If Cluster-1 is normalized to `**_kwargs` the irreducible count drops to about 7, which may change that calculus.

## Revisit

Record the irreducible exception count after the sweep. **The next rebar-janitor run must revisit whether to enable an ARG gate**, using that measured count rather than an estimate. That count and the revisit note are recorded as a `comment` on THIS ticket (`fc0c-e218-8b34-4858`) — the durable, queryable home for janitor findings — not in an out-of-tree scratch file. (An earlier draft cited `.joe-janitor/tools.md`, which does not exist in the repo; the ticket comment supersedes it.)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every one of the 64 `ARG` violations is dispositioned by the Classification decision
      procedure — each into exactly one of buckets 1-6, with the bucket-appropriate action applied.
      After the sweep, `ruff check --select ARG src/rebar` reports ONLY the deliberately-retained
      set: the bucket-4 `# noqa`'d sites and the bucket-1 tracked-defect sites (no unclassified
      residual remains).
- [x] Every rename (buckets 5-6) is verified safe against keyword call sites AND against the
      parameter name appearing **as a string** (`getattr`, `setattr`, `monkeypatch.setattr`,
      `sig.parameters`, `**kwargs`), using `grep`, not semantic search alone.
- [x] Every bucket-4 (rename-unsafe) site carries a `# noqa: ARG00x` with a one-line reason that
      names the keyword call site or string reference making a rename unsafe.
- [x] Cluster-1 is resolved by one decision covering all ten leaves; with `**_kwargs`
      normalization, `typed_dispatch.py`'s `accepts_repo_root` introspection still selects the
      right handlers, and a test pins it.
- [x] The `binding_store` side effect of `**_kwargs` normalization is pinned: a test proves that a
      Cluster-1 leaf which (pre-change) did NOT receive `binding_store` now receives it yet
      produces an identical observable result (the extra keyword is inert), so `accepts_binding_store`
      flipping to `True` is behaviour-preserving.
- [x] Cluster-2 carries justified `# noqa: ARG002` referencing the Protocol, or an equivalent that
      does not break the Protocol contract or its keyword call sites.
- [x] The three real defects are NOT folded into this sweep — they remain tracked as
      `7504-a127-e9b0-42bb` (`timeout_s`), `3803-8e04-7c32-4b80` (`close_reason`), and the
      `acli_cmd` bug; any NEW possible-defect surfaced during the sweep is filed as a ticket linked
      `discovered_from fc0c-e218-8b34-4858` and its violation left in place, not fixed here.
- [x] `ARG` is **not** added to `select` in `pyproject.toml` by this ticket.
- [x] The post-sweep per-bucket counts and the irreducible `# noqa`/excluded total are recorded as
      a comment on this ticket.
- [x] No behaviour change: the reconciler dispatch and the outbound mapping produce identical
      results (a test exercises the real dispatch/mapping paths, asserting observable output).
baseline.summary: One-off ARG sweep of src/: 43 mechanical fixes plus two cluster decisions, no gate

## Context / Problem
After S1, persistence has a cohesive owner but `BindingStore` still embeds forward/reverse identity transitions, pending/confirmed state, numeric-ID re-key, comment identity, absence grace, tombstones, and unretire policy. Production rich-text convergence also reaches through shallow `all_bindings()` and mutates an inner dictionary, bypassing any future policy seam.

## Outcome
Extract lifecycle decisions into a private policy owner operating on the repository original dictionaries, with the public facade retaining every existing method/signature. Add a narrow facade operation for rich-text emission state. Preserve shallow `all_bindings()` compatibility, but make the narrow operation the supported production mutation seam for the later caller cutover.

## Plan
1. Move cohesive forward/reverse, pending/confirmed, immutable-ID re-key, comment-map, absence/retirement, tombstone, suppression, and unretire call clusters into `binding_lifecycle.py`.
2. Keep the facade authoritative: it coordinates the lifecycle owner and repository unit-of-work; no adapter or reconciler caller receives a writable repository object.
3. Use open typed views over the same dictionaries. Unknown and legacy fields remain present and writable only through named policy operations.
4. Add `BindingStore.note_rich_emit(local_id, wire)` (or an equivalently narrow name) that preserves the current counter/hash behavior and missing-binding fail-open result. Do not change `all_bindings()` copy depth.
5. Preserve exact current failure choices: confirmed 404 grace/reset, moved-key repair, retired corruption fail-open, live corruption fail-closed, append-only comment identity, tombstone suppression, and explicit unretire.

## Testing (RED → GREEN)
- Direct policy tests exercise both-index transitions and reload through the real repository after each state change.
- Table-driven tests cover duplicate bind, stale reverse cleanup, missing/corrupt forward state, three-404 retirement, 200 reset, numeric-ID move, legacy no-ID behavior, tombstone suppression/unretire, and changed/unchanged comment IDs.
- A narrow-operation test compares rich-emission hashes/counters and save behavior to the existing production sequence.
- Signature and shallow-query regression tests pin the facade compatibility surface.

## Compatibility / rollback
Facade delegates can be moved back without changing bytes or callers. This slice adds the narrow mutation operation but does not yet modify RP-04-owned apply files. No lifecycle thresholds, corruption disposition, copy-depth, stored schema, or identity-marker writer changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Given valid and corrupt forward/reverse combinations, every lifecycle operation preserves at-most-one identity, removes stale reverse entries when required, and safety-aborts ambiguous double binds.
- [ ] Three confirmed 404s retire, a successful read resets absence, immutable numeric-ID lookup re-keys instead of retiring, and legacy entries retain current behavior.
- [ ] Tombstoned issues suppress recreate with an alert until explicit unretire; retired corruption and alert-write failures retain their current fail-open boundaries.
- [ ] Comment IDs remain append-only/change-gated and old records without the field remain readable without rewrite.
- [ ] The narrow rich-emission operation matches current hash/counter/save behavior while missing bindings remain nonfatal.
- [ ] Existing facade signatures and shallow `all_bindings()` semantics remain unchanged; no production adapter obtains direct repository mutation access.
baseline.summary: RP-02 S2 — Extract binding lifecycle policy and narrow mutation operations

baseline.description:
## Problem
7-day store mining (2026-08-07..14) found 33 FORCE_CLOSE audit records, ~25 of them ADMINISTRATIVE closes — duplicate, obsolete, wontfix, stale-premise — where completing the described work is not the intent, so the completion verifier can never PASS them and operators reach for --force. A narrow attested-disposition path exists but is doubly scoped down: (a) class set — `close_disposition.DISPOSITION_CLASSES` = {duplicate, not_a_bug, escalated} only; (b) ticket type — close_precheck.py:64 gates the path to bugs, so an obsolete task/story/epic has NO truthful exit today. And the completion-FAIL message never mentions the path that exists: "it offered only 'complete the work' or '[operator-attested]' — attesting would have been a FALSE claim" (9b70). This is the single largest FORCE_CLOSE class.

## Fix (extends the EXISTING --class mechanism; no new flag)
1. Vocabulary: add obsolete (premise no longer holds; reason required), superseded (replaced by a named live ticket), wontfix (deliberate decision; reason required) to the single-sourced `CLOSE_CLASSES` (txn.py:168). Enumerated co-edits: common.schema.json#/$defs/close_class enum+description (same order), ticket_state.schema.json close_class description (:196-198), `close_disposition.DISPOSITION_CLASSES` AND `close_precheck._NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES` (both gain the three; their equality drift-guard tests/unit/test_close_disposition_attestation_738a.py:26 updated), the `transition.py` parser (existing `--class` gains the values; NO new --disposition flag), and `types.py` CloseClass.
2. Administrative subset, single-sourced: a new frozenset `close_disposition.ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES = {duplicate, obsolete, superseded, wontfix}` — the classes valid on NON-BUG closes (not_a_bug/escalated stay bug-only vocabulary). Drift-guarded by a test asserting ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES < DISPOSITION_CLASSES and exact membership.
3. Write-side enforcement (gate-independent — cannot be skipped by --force or a disabled completion gate): extend `txn.transition_core`'s close-class guard (txn.py:260, today `ticket_type == "bug"`-gated) so (a) a non-bug close MAY carry --class only from ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES (anything else refused naming the allowed values — the enforcement point for not_a_bug/escalated staying bug-only); (b) obsolete/wontfix REQUIRE a reason (refusal when missing). The reason REUSES the existing `--reason` flag (transition.py:152-158) — today force-only, with an active refusal on plain transitions ("--reason is only meaningful with --force", transition.py:549-554): that guard is AMENDED to also admit `--reason` WITHOUT `--force` when the close carries a reason-capable administrative class (obsolete/wontfix; unchanged refusal otherwise). On a non-force administrative close the reason persists as a NEW `close_reason` key on the close STATUS event (present-only, mirroring close_class at txn.py:287; NOT force_close_reason, which stays the --force channel's fold). Threading co-edits: transition_core (and transition_compute) gain a `close_reason` parameter threaded from close_ticket/the CLI parse; reducer fold `_fold_close_metadata` (reducer/_processors_status.py:49) folds it; types.py ticket-state TypedDict (:138 area) + ticket_state.schema.json declare it.
4. Verification skip for administrative closes: a NEW explicit `_completion_precheck` branch — a close whose class is a reason-only ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASS (obsolete/wontfix, no replacement link) skips the AC/file-impact/billable-verifier checks and returns the disposition verdict (widening `_has_live_replacement_link`'s type-gate at close_precheck.py:64 alone would NOT route them: that function detects replacement links, which reason-only classes lack). Replacement-bearing classes route through the widened :64 gate; `_ensure_duplicate_close_is_linked` (close_precheck.py:139, called at :508) widens from duplicate-only to {duplicate, superseded} so both demand a live replacement link (existing `find_replacement`, close_disposition.py:47); the plan-review claim gate is untouched.
5. Attestation for reason-only classes: `close_disposition.verdict()` (:92) today returns None unless find_replacement resolves a live ticket, and `decorate_manifest` (:114) signs that replacement — so obsolete/wontfix as-written would close UNSIGNED (the 738a trap). Extend both signatures: verdict() gains a `close_reason: str = ""` parameter (threaded from its precheck call site) and mints the reason-only verdict from (class + close_reason); decorate_manifest signs a `disposition: <class> reason: <text>` line for reason-only classes; replacement-bearing classes unchanged.
6. Discoverability: the close refusal surface is `close_precheck`'s CommandError assembly, which HAS ticket context — it appends the applicable-class enumeration (`--class` values valid for THIS ticket_type) to the completion-FAIL/refusal message; the static COMPLETION_REMEDIATION_GUIDANCE constant stays generic (no per-ticket data in a module constant). The 9b70 incident is the RED oracle: a wontfix-shaped ticket's failure message must present a truthful exit.
7. Migration: existing FORCE_CLOSE records stay as-is; new administrative closes should have no reason to use --force.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] The three new classes appear in every single-sourced consumer — txn.CLOSE_CLASSES, common.schema.json + ticket_state.schema.json, DISPOSITION_CLASSES, _NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES, types.py CloseClass — with the 738a equality drift-guard updated; ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES exists in close_disposition with exact membership {duplicate, obsolete, superseded, wontfix} and a subset drift-guard test.
- [x] Non-bug tickets (task/story/epic fixture each) close with an administrative class without completion verification — reason-only classes via the new explicit precheck branch returning the disposition verdict; a non-bug close with not_a_bug/escalated (or any non-administrative class) is REFUSED in txn.transition_core naming allowed values; bug closes keep today's behavior.
- [x] obsolete/wontfix demand a reason (write-side refusal when missing, enforced in transition_core even with the completion gate off); the transition.py:549-554 "--reason only with --force" guard admits --reason WITHOUT --force for these classes (refusal unchanged otherwise); the reason threads close_ticket -> transition_core/transition_compute, persists as close_reason on the close event (distinct from force_close_reason), folds via _fold_close_metadata into reduced state, and typechecks (types.py); superseded/duplicate demand a live replacement link (_ensure_duplicate_close_is_linked widened); store-event tests per class.
- [x] A reason-only disposition close mints a SIGNED disposition attestation whose manifest carries the class+reason line; replacement-bearing closes keep the replacement line; an unsigned close for a valid disposition is RED.
- [x] The close_precheck refusal/FAIL message enumerates the applicable --class values for the ticket's type; message test asserts the 9b70 wontfix scenario is offered a truthful exit; --force on an administrative-shaped close hints the disposition alternative.
- [x] `make lint`/`make typecheck` clean (CI gate ran them on the merged change).
- [x] [operator-attested] Lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
  provenance: environment=Gerrit+GitHub Actions; principal=session operator (git-credential REST); privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — /a/changes/1794/detail showed LLM-Review +1, Verified +1; MERGED as 9844f6de35 on origin/main.

# OSS v1.0.0 community front door — contribution intake, governance, and release artifacts

## Context

rebar is technically near-1.0 (PyPI Trusted Publishing + PEP 740 attestations, immutable releases, `docs/api-stability.md` stability matrix, event-schema forward-compat) but the public contribution funnel is closed: GitHub (navapbc/rebar) is a read-only mirror with Issues and Discussions disabled (verified via API 2026-07-09: `has_issues: false`), and while CONTRIBUTING.md already documents an external Gerrit path (§1–§3), there is no GitHub-side intake, no governance/DCO/review-policy artifacts, and no user-facing changelog. Three converging assessments (internal repo audit; an external deep-research report; peer research across Go, Chromium, Qt, LibreOffice, Wikimedia, OpenStack, Eclipse) identify public intake + written governance as the only blockers to a credible v1.0.0.

Peer convergence establishes the design: KEEP Gerrit — Wikimedia reversed its GitLab migration in June 2024 over the review model (https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/GitLab/Migration_status), JGit/EGit migrated TO GerritHub rather than accept PRs (https://gitenterprise.me/2023/11/21/14-years-of-jgit-egit-code-reviews-migrated-to-gerrithub/) — and pair the wall with a ramp: bot-answered PRs (LibreOffice/Wikimedia pattern), a first-change tutorial, a shepherded-patch fallback, GitHub Issues as zero-friction intake (Go's model), DCO enforced at the Gerrit server (OpenStack TC resolution 2025-05-20, https://governance.openstack.org/tc/resolutions/20250520-replace-the-cla-with-dco-for-all-contributions.html), and skipped non-convergent ceremony (CODEOWNERS, GPG-signed tags, RC trains — each a recorded non-goal with rationale in a child).

Stars/forks/contributor counts are explicitly OUT of scope; success is artifact completeness and funnel quality.

Cross-child protocols (binding on all children):
- **Vote-semantics single source:** `docs/review-policy.md` (child wrathful-preregal-blobfish) is the sole authoritative DOCUMENT for Gerrit vote semantics; its table's content is transcribed from the code enums (`_TAG_SUFFIXES` in adapter.py + the merge-path tags in voter.py) — document-of-record and source-of-truth are distinct and both are named. Every other doc links to it rather than duplicating the table. Until it lands, CONTRIBUTING.md §2c remains the interim authority.
- **Ownership inversion for cross-links:** a child that CREATES a doc never forward-links to a sibling's not-yet-existing doc; the sibling that creates the later doc owns adding links into earlier docs. Dependency edges: PR-posture and review-policy each depend_on the onboarding tutorial (their artifacts link it).
- **Decisions live in the repo**, not only on tickets: design decisions are recorded as ADRs under `docs/adr/` or in the owning doc (e.g. `docs/releasing.md`), with a ticket comment pointing at the artifact.
- **Shepherded-patch DCO interplay:** a shepherded contribution needs the ORIGINAL author's `Signed-off-by` (contributor runs `git commit -s` before `git format-patch`) plus the shepherd's own sign-off added on amend — the OpenStack two-trailer convention; documented in both the DCO and PR-posture children.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All nine child stories closed: GitHub intake; PR posture; onboarding tutorial + CONTRIBUTING; README front door; DCO; governance docs; review policy; CHANGELOG; release hygiene / 1.0 declaration.
- [ ] The four pre-flight experiments (E1 fork-side UX with has_pull_requests=false; E2 Gerrit Forge Author ACL; E3 PR-event dependency audit; E4 rebar-ticket trailer policy for shepherded patches) are executed AND each dependent child's design is updated or explicitly confirmed against the outcome (outcome-framed: an experiment that invalidates an assumption must change the affected child before that child is worked). E3-discovered breakage is fixed (or ticketed via discovered_from) by the PR-posture child.
- [ ] The `docs/api-stability.md` pre-1.0 caveat flip and the Development Status classifier bump are staged for the v1.0.0 release change (release-hygiene child names the landing vehicle).
- [ ] Final consistency audit (epic-level, before epic close, owned by the epic executor): re-read CONTRIBUTING.md, CLAUDE.md, SUPPORT.md, README.md, and all new docs as one set; verify no artifact contradicts the Gerrit-primary workflow or another artifact (including the vote-semantics single-source rule); record the audit result as an epic comment.
- [ ] Cross-link completeness: `docs/release-notes.md` carries a pointer to CHANGELOG.md (owned by the changelog child); every new doc is reachable from CONTRIBUTING.md or README.md.
- [ ] GitHub intake works and is self-explanatory: Issues enabled with structured forms; an issue can be filed with no Gerrit account, no local checkout, and no knowledge beyond the form itself (verifiable from the rendered chooser, not a timing claim).
- [ ] The path from GitHub to a merged Gerrit change is documented end-to-end in one tutorial an outsider can follow with zero Nava-internal knowledge (measured by concrete checks in the onboarding child, e.g. no references to internal-only groups/layouts on the happy path).
- [ ] A no-Gerrit patch fallback is published. Authorship preservation via `git am` is promised only if experiment E2 confirms Gerrit's Forge Author permission is (or can be) granted; if E2 fails, the documented fallback is `Co-authored-by:` credit and the policy text says so (go/no-go, not an unconditional promise).
- [ ] Governance, review policy, DCO, and maintainer info are published, each grounded in a named peer convention (curl/CNCF, Chromium-CQ/Zuul, OpenStack/moby — URLs in the children).
- [ ] Release artifacts (CHANGELOG, dependabot, README front door, 1.0 declaration mechanics) match documented 2026 Python-tool convergence.
baseline.summary: OSS v1.0.0 community front door — contribution intake, governance, and release artifacts
