## Context
Before merged Change 1847, at the parent of commit 034e17209c, tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_review_drain.py constructed `env = dict(os.environ)` and returned that mapping inside the `box` fixture value. A deliberate nested-pytest RED probe against that pre-fix revision placed a synthetic sentinel before PATH and observed pytest default-long traceback rendering print it; no real credential value was used or recorded. Commit 034e17209c repaired that defect: the current file at lines 149-165 now constructs a narrow PATH-plus-harness allowlist. This ticket records and verifies the already-landed repair; it does not claim the current fixture still copies the full environment. The performance ticket must not absorb this unrelated security fix.

## Plan
- Reproduce on the pre-fix revision with a synthetic first-position sentinel in the ambient environment and a deliberate assertion failure.
- Change the fixture boundary to pass only required environment variables while preserving the real bash subprocess environment needed by the tests.
- Audit sibling subprocess fixtures for the same `dict(os.environ)`-inside-rendered-fixture shape.
- Prove on the repaired revision that the synthetic sentinel never appears in pytest default-long failure output while the autodeploy suite remains behaviorally green.

## Scope and alternative rationale
The construct sweep separates two runtime carriers rather than deferring equivalent leaks. This parent and child dumbstruck-wonderful-xiphosuran own the eight decorated fixtures whose returned values pytest renders as function arguments; explicit allowlists are correct there because minimal-parent runs prove their consumers need only declared harness values. The remaining broad mappings are test-local or helper values exposed only when subprocess startup itself raises. Some intentionally forward the invoking pytest environment or environment-only live-service credentials, so applying the fixture allowlist would break their contract. Follow-up antiutopic-toadyish-goldfinch owns all 103 of those sites as one atomic shared representation-safe mapping migration, with a repository guard and exact child-value preservation test. A repo-wide allowlist was rejected because it would drop required values; independent per-file wrappers were rejected because they would duplicate the same diagnostic boundary without enforcement. Pytest `--tb=short` was a useful negative control but was rejected as remediation because it globally reduces debugging detail and only masks this traceback carrier; the repaired fixture boundary remains safe under the default long traceback. ADR 0041 governs durable LLM diagnostic fields rather than pytest fixture representations; its fail-closed allowlist posture is nevertheless followed for these decorated fixtures.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] [operator-attested] A deterministic regression test fails on the pre-fix revision because a synthetic ambient secret appears in captured pytest failure rendering.
  provenance: environment=sanitized-red-probe-034e17209c; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=narrower; instrument=simulation — real nested pytest default-long traceback with first-position synthetic sentinel
- [x] The synthetic secret is absent from failure output after the fix.
- [x] Required PATH and autodeploy environment behavior remains covered through the real bash subprocess.
- [x] Sibling occurrences are inventoried and either fixed or linked as follow-ups.
- [x] [operator-attested] Repository gates and Gerrit votes pass before closure.
  provenance: environment=gerrit-ci-run-32101886011; principal=rebar-ci-bot; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=static-analysis — canonical Gerrit Verified and LLM-Review gates for merged change 1847
baseline.summary: Prevent autodeploy test failures from printing ambient credentials

## Why
Epic 88ab (elfish-chair-lug) S1. The feature-branch pattern needs Gerrit-side changes: vote-carry for re-merges after main advances (MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE), an explicitly pinned submit type (currently unset/inherited — FF-only or cherry-pick would defeat atomic merge-back), and a bounded write path for merge commits + feature branches.

## What
- `infra/gerrit/project.config`: LLM-Review `copyCondition = changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE OR changekind:MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE`; Verified copyCondition UNCHANGED (re-run posture — rationale in the ADR).
- Record the CURRENT effective inherited submit type (ssh/REST query, noted on this ticket) BEFORE pinning `[submit] action = merge if necessary` + `mergeContent = true`; apply in a quiet window (no open changes targeting main).
- ACLs: `Create Reference` + `Delete Reference` on `refs/heads/feature/*`; `Push Merge Commit` on `refs/for/refs/heads/main` + `refs/for/refs/heads/feature/*`; ALL bound to a new named group `feature-branch-drivers`.
- `infra/gerrit/setup-project.sh`: extend the managed-groups `want` dict (~line 57, currently Administrators + Service Users only) so the group is created/resolved declaratively and idempotently.
- ADR amending ADR-0013 (+ the 1fa8 Verified ADR): merge-change gate design, label-divergence rationale, group membership policy.
- `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` gate/ACL sections.

Inherited plan-review findings (run 3): membership policy must be constrained in the ADR — initial members = repo admins + named operating agents; changes via admin-approved setup-project.sh edit (f8e6233f). Back-out wording: "no label/gate changes REQUIRED" — the copyCondition addition is inert absent merge changes (MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE cannot match a non-merge patchset) and may be left or reverted (f51eb171/f90d5449).

## Scope
Gerrit config + setup script + ADR + setup docs only. No bot code (S2), no CI/g2p (S3), no contributor docs (S4).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] copyCondition change applied declaratively (refs/meta/config) and accepted by the running Gerrit 3.14.1
- [ ] Current inherited submit type recorded on this ticket BEFORE the [submit] pin lands; pin applied in a quiet window
- [ ] `feature-branch-drivers` group exists holding exactly the three ACLs; `setup-project.sh` converges it idempotently on re-run
- [ ] ADR merged: gate design, Verified/LLM-Review divergence rationale, membership policy (initial members + change process), copyCondition back-out note
- [ ] `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` updated
- [ ] Live negative checks: merge push by a non-member is refused; feature/* branch creation outside the group is refused
baseline.summary: S1: Gerrit gate + ACL config — merge-carry copyCondition, submit-type pin, feature/* + pushMerge ACLs

baseline.description:
## Why

MCP tools carry no behavior annotations, so clients cannot present safe UI or
confirmation flows. rebar already has the semantic information internally —
reads are separate from writes, writes are hidden under `REBAR_MCP_READONLY`,
Jira-live and LLM tools are call-gated — but none of it is exposed as the MCP
`ToolAnnotations` hints (`readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`,
`openWorldHint`) that the spec defines for exactly this purpose.

## What

Annotate every registered tool via `FastMCP.tool(annotations=ToolAnnotations(...))`
across the three registrars (`register_read_tools` in `_mcp_reads.py`,
`register_llm_tools` in `_mcp_llm.py`, `register_write_tools` in `_mcp_writes.py`).
Confirmed feasible: `mcp` 1.28.1 exposes `ToolAnnotations` with all four hint
fields and `FastMCP.tool` accepts `annotations`.

Mapping policy:

- **Read tools** -> `readOnlyHint: true`.
- **Additive writes** (create/comment/tag/link/edit/claim/transition/set_*) ->
  `readOnlyHint: false`, `destructiveHint: false`; `idempotentHint: true` where
  the op is idempotent (e.g. tag/untag).
- **Destructive/irreversible** (archive/delete/compact, reconcile-live) ->
  `destructiveHint: true`.
- **Outward-reaching** (LLM review/verify, Jira reconcile, `run_workflow`) ->
  `openWorldHint: true`.

## Scope

`src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py`, `_mcp_llm.py`, `_mcp_writes.py`. Annotations are hints
only — no behavior change. Add/adjust a parity test if the interface suite pins
tool metadata.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every `@mcp.tool()` in the three registrars carries a `ToolAnnotations`
  consistent with the mapping policy above.
- [ ] Read tools are `readOnlyHint: true`; delete/archive/reconcile-live are
  `destructiveHint: true`; LLM/Jira/workflow tools are `openWorldHint: true`.
- [ ] The server still builds and starts; existing MCP/interface tests pass.
- [ ] No functional behavior of any tool changes.
baseline.summary: Annotate MCP tools with behavior hints (read-only/destructive/idempotent/open-world)

baseline.description:
## Purpose

`rebar metrics`'s structural metrics need three analyzers: **lizard** (Python, complexity), **scc** (Go, size) and **jscpd** (Node, duplication). They have reported `unavailable` in this repository since they shipped, so rebar has never dogfooded its own code-health metrics.

Operator request 2026-08-05: install them on this machine AND make new venvs in this project get them.

## Corrected premise -- VERIFIED against the tree, replacing the original assumption

The ticket was written assuming *no bootstrap path installs lizard*. **That is false**, and the correction reshapes the whole ticket:

- `pyproject.toml` `dev` extra self-references `nava-rebar[agents,metrics]`, and
  `metrics = ["lizard>=1.23"]`. So `uv sync --locked --extra dev` and `pip install -e '.[dev]'`
  **already** pull lizard transitively.
- Proven empirically: a worktree provisioned by `make worktree` on **unmodified `main`** imports
  `lizard` 1.23.0 successfully. AC "a fresh venv can import lizard" **already passes on `main`**.
- `uv.lock` already pins lizard 1.23.0 (`uv.lock`, `name = "lizard"` / `1.23.0`), reached via the
  `metrics` extra marker. So no lock update is needed and `uv lock --check` cannot drift.

The lizard half of this ticket is therefore **not a fix but a hardening**: the `dev` extra pulls metrics *incidentally*, and its own comment says it is there so optional-capability tests RUN in CI. That is a CI-testing rationale, not a "dev envs get the analyzers" rationale -- so if that self-reference is ever trimmed, local venvs would silently lose lizard and `rebar metrics` would regress to `unavailable` with nothing to catch it. Naming the extra explicitly in the two bootstrap paths pins the intent independently of the CI rationale.

## What this ticket changes

1. `Makefile` `install`: `uv sync --locked --extra dev` -> `uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra
   metrics`. Behaviour-preserving today (metrics already arrives via `dev`); the value is that
   the dev bootstrap now states the dependency itself. Extend the existing uv-locked comment
   (ticket ce5d) with this rationale -- do not overwrite it.
2. `Makefile` `install-unlocked`: `pip install -e '.[dev]'` -> `'.[dev,metrics]'`, same rationale.
   `make worktree` delegates to `make install`, so worktree venvs are covered by change 1 with no
   separate edit -- confirm by reading the target, do not duplicate the change.
3. Document the two NON-Python analyzers in `docs/local-dev-env.md`. They cannot come from a
   Python extra, so a documented install step is the only route. Use exactly the commands proven
   on this machine: `brew install scc` (Go) and `npm install -g jscpd` (Node). State plainly that
   they are **optional** and that their absence degrades to a clean `Unavailable` in
   `rebar metrics`, never a hard failure.

## End state / scope boundary

Post-change, a dev venv can run the **lizard-backed complexity** and **jscpd-backed duplication** metrics. The **scc-backed size metrics still return a confident zero** -- blocked on sibling bug `c5b3-1b8a-08dd-40af` (the adapter omits `--by-file`). This ticket does not claim to make `rebar metrics` complete; it makes the toolchain installable and documented.

## CI impact -- checked

CI does **not** call `make install`. Every workflow invokes `uv sync --locked --extra ...` (or `pip install -e .`) directly, so no `Makefile` edit here can reach CI. CI also already receives lizard transitively via `dev`. CI is unaffected; no workflow change is needed.

## Explicitly NOT in scope

- Adding a `[code_health]` section to `rebar.toml` (scan_roots / size_cap). That is real
  dogfooding config and must follow the scc bug being fixed, otherwise it would enshrine the
  broken zero.
- `code_health.enabled` is INERT (bug a573-00ea-2bf6-4eb1) -- do not set it expecting an effect.
- Installing scc/jscpd automatically, or gating any target on their presence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `Makefile` `install` names `--extra metrics` and `install-unlocked` names `.[dev,metrics]`,
      with the existing uv-locked rationale comment preserved and extended, not replaced.
- [x] `make worktree` is confirmed by inspection to delegate to `make install` (no second edit).
- [x] A venv provisioned by the edited `make install` imports `lizard` 1.23.0.
- [x] `uv lock --check` passes on the change (no lock drift), proving the metrics extra was
      already locked.
- [x] `docs/local-dev-env.md` documents `brew install scc` and `npm install -g jscpd`, marks both
      optional, and states that absence degrades to `Unavailable` rather than failing.
- [x] PROVEN, not asserted: with `scc` and `jscpd` made unresolvable on `PATH`, `make install`,
      `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the test suite all still succeed, and `rebar metrics`
      reports `unavailable` for the affected lenses instead of erroring. Evidence recorded as a
      ticket comment.
- [x] CI is unaffected -- confirmed by showing no workflow invokes `make install`.
baseline.summary: Make the metrics analyzer toolchain explicit in dev bootstrap and document the non-Python analyzers (scc, jscpd)

baseline.description:
Standardize the CLI write-command argument parsing: retire the hand-rolled manual loop for Python's stdlib argparse, WITHOUT changing observable behavior.

## Context / Problem
Today the CLI parses write-command args with a hand-rolled loop (src/rebar/_commands/claim.py _parse_force/_parse_assignee, and src/rebar/_commands/transition.py _parse_flags) carrying bespoke semantics not reflected in any schema: --assignee ABSENT is a None sentinel (=> ticket.default_assignee fallback) while explicit --assignee "" CLEARS the assignee. This is tech-debt: flags and --help can silently drift from actual behavior.

## Dependency / sequencing
Depends on blusterous-earthly-kitten, which normalizes the force surface (removes `force_close`, makes `transition`'s `--force[=<reason>]` a reason-carrying param matching `claim`, and drops the `--reason`-as-force-note fallback). This is a behavior-preserving MECHANICAL refactor that must preserve the POST-blusterous CLI surface, so it runs AFTER that semantic change to avoid re-encoding a soon-to-change flag and to avoid a conflicting edit on the same parser files.

## Approach
Refactor the CLI write-command parsing onto Python's stdlib argparse. argparse is the chosen default: zero new runtime dependency, portable, and it generates accurate --help; we do NOT adopt Click or Typer, to avoid adding a runtime dependency. This is a behavior-preserving ADAPTER REFACTOR, orthogonal to the parity oracle. Respect the module-size (<=800 LOC) and per-function complexity ratchets by extracting along existing call-graph seams rather than inflating a single function.

## Contract preservation (must not regress, relative to the post-blusterous surface)
Flag spellings, exit-code 10 (ConcurrencyError), the `--force[=<reason>]` reason-carrying bypass (bare `--force` -> "(no reason given)"; `--force=<reason>` -> that reason; `--reason` is NOT the force note), and the --assignee None-vs-empty-string distinction must be preserved exactly.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_commands/claim.py — replace the _parse_force/_parse_assignee hand loop with argparse, preserving the sentinel semantics.
- src/rebar/_commands/transition.py — replace _parse_flags with argparse; same treatment.
- Lib and MCP surfaces are OUT OF SCOPE (this is an adapter-local change).

## Testing
- Existing CLI interface tests pass unchanged (tests/interfaces).
- `--force[=<reason>]` supplies the audit note inline (bare -> "(no reason given)"); `--reason` is admitted only as close_reason, never as the force note (test, consistent with blusterous).
- --assignee absent => default_assignee fallback; --assignee "" => cleared (test asserts both).
- A ConcurrencyError still exits 10.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CLI write-command parsing goes through argparse and `--help` is generated (verified by running the command's --help and confirming it lists the flags).
- [ ] The `--force[=<reason>]` reason-carrying form is preserved (bare -> "(no reason given)", `--force=<reason>` -> that reason); `--reason` is not repurposed as the force note (test).
- [ ] The --assignee None-vs-empty-string distinction is preserved: absent => default_assignee fallback, "" => cleared (test asserts both).
- [ ] Exit code 10 on ConcurrencyError is preserved (existing CLI interface tests pass).
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` are green; module-size and complexity ratchets respected.
baseline.summary: Standardize CLI write-command arg parsing (retire hand-rolled loop for a std framework)

baseline.description:
# Bounded completion recovery is unreachable for a step-budget exhaustion

## Context / Problem

Discovered while root-causing [rebar:bf31-fd55-d28d-4b7a].

`CompletionAgentStep.run` (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:426`) catches ONLY `UnretryableOutputError`, and only when `_is_token_exhaustion(exc)` holds. A step-budget exhaustion raises `LLMRunnerError` (`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:95` builds it as `budget_err` with a `.diagnostic` attached), and per `src/rebar/llm/errors.py` `LLMRunnerError` is a strict ANCESTOR of `UnretryableOutputError` — so it never matches and the recovery never engages.

Confirmed by experiment, with a control: a synthetic budget `LLMRunnerError` fed to `CompletionAgentStep.run` PROPAGATED and left `failure_diagnostic is None`; the control, an `UnretryableOutputError` truncation, ENTERED recovery.

This matters because bounded recovery is exactly the mechanism the failure needs. It isolates each explicit criterion in a FRESH agentic history (so a loop cannot persist across criteria), converges the evidence run at 16 run steps, and finishes with a tool-free structured finalizer — see `docs/llm-framework.md`. The error message printed to the operator says "narrow the task", and this is the machinery that does exactly that, sitting unreachable one `except` clause away.

## Approach

Two small pieces, per the design review on this ticket's plan:

1. **A dedicated typed exception.** `interpret_failure`'s budget branch (`structured_run.py:95`)
   currently raises a bare `LLMRunnerError`. Diagnostic-shape sniffing CANNOT identify that branch:
   `interpret_failure` attaches the SAME `usage_log.failure_usage(...)` dict (same key set) to
   EVERY exception it raises — typed `LLMError`s, sampling rejections, and `LLMUnavailableError`
   alike — so "carries requests/tool_calls/request_limit keys" is true of all of them. Add
   `LLMBudgetExhaustedError(LLMRunnerError)` to `src/rebar/llm/errors.py` and raise it from the
   budget branch. Every existing `except LLMRunnerError` / `except LLMError` site keeps catching
   (strict subclass = backward compatible), and the budget stop becomes identifiable **purely by
   type** — no message sniffing, no shape sniffing.
2. **The missing entry edge.** Extend the `except` clause in `CompletionAgentStep.run` to catch
   `LLMBudgetExhaustedError` and route it to the existing `_recover(...)`. The truncation path
   keeps its exact current behaviour: `UnretryableOutputError` + `_is_token_exhaustion` still
   routes to the same `_recover`. `_recover`'s own fail-closed guarantees are untouched — this
   ticket only adds the missing entry edge. The budget diagnostic is preserved onto
   `self.failure_diagnostic` before recovery so that if recovery ALSO fails,
   `raise_completion_workflow_failure` has the loop-vs-breadth counters (the surfacing of those
   counters is [rebar:8b97-a0ca-82a4-4d4e]'s subject).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/errors.py` — new `LLMBudgetExhaustedError(LLMRunnerError)`.
- `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` — the budget branch of `interpret_failure` raises the subclass
  (message and `.diagnostic` unchanged).
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py` — the `except` spine of
  `CompletionAgentStep.run` catches the subclass and routes to `_recover`.
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_token_recovery.py` — the tests below (extends the existing
  suite for this class).

Out of scope: what `tool_step_limit` does inside the evidence runs ([rebar:e1b1-859e-a7b4-48f2]); the runaway detector/actuator ([rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e]); sidecar emission ([rebar:8b97-a0ca-82a4-4d4e]).

## Testing

    pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_token_recovery.py -q

Happy path: an `LLMBudgetExhaustedError` from the primary step enters recovery and produces a verdict. Edge: a plain `LLMRunnerError` (not the subclass) still propagates (negative control); the truncation path is regression-pinned. Failure path: recovery that cannot produce full criterion coverage still fails closed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `LLMBudgetExhaustedError(LLMRunnerError)` exists in `src/rebar/llm/errors.py` and
      `interpret_failure`'s budget branch raises it with the same message and `.diagnostic` as
      today; verified by a unit test on `interpret_failure` asserting the raised type, message, and
      diagnostic keys, and by every existing `except LLMRunnerError`-based test passing unmodified
- [x] a step-budget exhaustion (`LLMBudgetExhaustedError`) routes into the
      bounded per-criterion recovery instead of propagating; verified by a test driving it end to end
      through `CompletionAgentStep.run` with a fake runner and asserting recovery ran and produced a
      verdict
- [x] a plain `LLMRunnerError` that is NOT the budget subclass still propagates unchanged (the catch
      is purely typed — no message or diagnostic-shape sniffing); verified by a negative-control test
- [x] the truncation path keeps its current behaviour exactly (`UnretryableOutputError` +
      `_is_token_exhaustion` -> recovery; non-exhaustion `UnretryableOutputError` propagates);
      regression-pinned by the existing tests passing unmodified
- [x] recovery still fails CLOSED when it cannot produce full criterion coverage — this must never
      become a route to an unearned PASS; verified by a test where recovery's preconditions fail and
      the step still raises
- [x] when recovery also fails, the original budget diagnostic is preserved on
      `self.failure_diagnostic` (not lost); verified by a test asserting the diagnostic's
      `requests`/`tool_calls` counters survive
baseline.summary: Bounded completion recovery is unreachable for a step-budget exhaustion (LLMRunnerError is not UnretryableOutputError)

## Corrected account (post-RCA): NOT A BUG
Original premise (stale link read) REFUTED by rebar-debug investigation — see the RCA comment for full evidence.

What actually happened: after `rebar link viral-peppy-lowchen creatable-foldable-arthropods discovered_from`, the LINK event persisted immediately (event f30a6c94, 16:06:52.581) and `rebar show` DID return it in the same read that showed the later STATUS event — under the documented `deps` key (docs/ticket-model.md §"Direction and visibility": `deps` = outgoing, `inbound_deps` = inbound). The observing agent queried a nonexistent `links` key and misread the empty default as a missing write.

Per-hypothesis verdicts:
- H1 show omits LINK: refuted — misunderstanding (edge present in `deps`; no contract promises `links`).
- H2 silent success: intended-behavior — Unix convention across comment/tag/unlink/transition (only create/revert print, they return generated ids).
- H3 silent idempotent re-link: intended-behavior — add_dependency docstring pins the idempotent no-op; guard has bug-fix pedigree (f5a8). An "already linked" notice would be a feature request.
- H4 enrich-drain WARNING masking stdout: refuted — logs are stderr; success stdout is empty by design.

Disposition: closed not_a_bug. No code change warranted; 3 of the original 4 acceptance criteria are already satisfied by current behavior.
baseline.summary: rebar show omits persisted outbound links: LINK event not reflected while later STATUS event is

# Pin `config.local_to_jira_status` against the canonical Jira-family map

## Context / Problem

**This ticket's original scope is already delivered; what remains is one specific residue, and this plan has been rewritten to that residue.** Filed during J1 as "the local->Jira maps exist in two drifted copies inside `adapters/jira/`". Story J2 [rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743] consolidated those two into a single definition and resolved the drift. Verified against the tree, not assumed:

* `adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py` now holds the SOLE adapter-side definition
  (`LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA`, `LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA`).
* The ACLI transport reads it (`acli.py:73,75`; `acli_cli_ops.py:35`) and so does the Backend port
  (`outbound_fields.py:35-36`), both via an alias to the old private names.
* The `deleted` drift is decided: the unified map adopts `"deleted": "Done"`, and
  `test_acli_status_resolution_heldout.py` pins it
  (`test_deleted_now_resolves_to_done_instead_of_the_invalid_deleted`).

So original ACs 1-3 are met. The residue is the **THIRD copy**, which J2 deliberately left out of its scope and named this ticket for, in `value_maps.py`'s own module docstring: "``rebar_reconciler/ config.py``'s separate third copy is deliberately out of this story's scope — see bug fe15-3bc4-ed70-4b61."

## Evidence — the residue is a REAL unpinned gap, measured

`config.local_to_jira_status` (`config.py:24-38`) is a key-for-key **independent literal**. Today it is content-identical to `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` (compared programmatically: `==` is True), so there is no drift *yet* — but nothing prevents one.

MUTATION EXPERIMENT (the same method that originally exposed this bug class): setting `config.local_to_jira_status["deleted"] = "Archived-MUTANT"` — a value that is NOT a state in the live DIG workflow ({To Do, In Progress, In Review, Done}) — left **59 passed, 0 failed** across `state/test_config.py`, `test_acli_status_resolution_heldout.py`, `test_jira_family_seam.py`, and `test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py`. Nothing catches divergence. That is precisely the failure mode this ticket reported, surviving in the one copy J2 did not touch.

Note the partial existing cover, so this plan does not re-add it: `test_config.py`'s `test_idea_maps_to_jira_idea_across_all_status_maps` already pins the `idea -> IDEA` entry across all three maps. It is ONE key. The other six are unpinned, which is why the mutation above went unseen.

## Approach — a parity test, NOT a shared import

**Do not make `config.py` import the canonical map.** `config.py` currently imports nothing but `__future__` — it is a deliberately zero-dependency core module — and `adapters/jira_family/` is a VENDOR package whose `__init__` states its dependency direction is one-way ("Concrete backends import this package; it never imports them back"). Having core `config` import a Jira adapter would invert that layering. It would also put the operator-override surface and the documented empty-dict kill-switch (`test_config.py:91-98`) behind an adapter import.

**Use the idiom this file already established for exactly this problem.** `config.jira_to_local_status` is a second literal of `inbound_differ._JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS`, and the codebase keeps the two honest with a PARITY TEST plus a lock-step comment — see the comment at `config.py:50-51` ("Must stay in lock-step with inbound_differ._JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS (parity is enforced by tests/.../test_config.py)") and `test_jira_to_local_status_parity_with_inbound_differ`. Mirror that, one layer over.

`test_config.py` already has the mechanism: `_load_attr(module_file, attr)` loads a constant **from a file path** via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`, so the test reads the adapter's map WITHOUT importing the adapter package into core's test context — and it is already called with `"adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py"` today. No new machinery is needed.

## Scope

- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_config.py` — ONE new parity test.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/config.py` — a lock-step COMMENT above
  `local_to_jira_status`, mirroring the one already above `jira_to_local_status`. No code change.

**NOT in scope:** any change to a map's VALUES (they already agree; changing one would be a behaviour change this ticket does not need); any production import between core and the adapter layer; the priority map (`config.py` has NO priority copy — verified: no priority attribute exists on the module, so there is no third priority literal to pin).

## Testing

The oracle is the parity test itself, and it must be shown to have teeth rather than asserted to: re-run the mutation above and confirm the new test goes RED, then revert and confirm GREEN. A parity test that passes against a divergent map is worse than none.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a test in `state/test_config.py` asserts `config.local_to_jira_status` equals
      `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` loaded from `adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py` via the existing
      `_load_attr` helper — full-dict equality, not a per-key spot check
- [ ] MUTATION-CHECKED: with `config.local_to_jira_status["deleted"]` changed to a non-workflow value
      the new test FAILS, and with it reverted the test PASSES; both verdicts recorded on this ticket
- [ ] `config.py` carries a lock-step comment naming the canonical map and the enforcing test, in the
      same form as the existing `jira_to_local_status` comment
- [ ] `config.py` still imports nothing outside `__future__` — asserted by reading the diff; no
      production dependency from core onto `adapters/`
- [ ] the empty-dict kill-switch and operator-override behaviour are unchanged — the existing
      `test_config.py` suite passes with ZERO edits to its existing tests (`git diff` shows only an
      ADDED test)
- [ ] `state/test_config.py`, `test_acli_status_resolution_heldout.py`, `test_jira_family_seam.py`
      and `test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py` all pass
baseline.summary: config.local_to_jira_status is an unpinned third copy of the canonical Jira-family status map

# e2e editor test `test_editor_batch_library_select_and_author` fails on main (authored criterion not referenced)

## Reproduction Steps
1. From a checkout of `main` (verified at `d42afd880`), with Node/npm available locally:
2. `python -m pytest tests/e2e/test_editor_batch_library.py::test_editor_batch_library_select_and_author`

## Expected vs Actual
- **Expected:** after the editor's batch AUTHOR flow creates a new criterion (`my-new-crit`),
  the batch step's first criterion references it: `authored["batch"]["criteria"][0]["prompt"] == "my-new-crit"`.
- **Actual:** the step still references the pre-existing criteria — `[{'prompt': 'tests'},
  {'prompt': 'ticket-quality', 'when': ...}]`; assertion fails `'tests' == 'my-new-crit'`
  (`tests/e2e/test_editor_batch_library.py:99`).

## Notes
- **Pre-existing on `main`** — reproduces identically with and without the item-15 llm reorg
  (change 238), so it is NOT caused by that change. Discovered while running the full suite for
  ITEM 15 (toll-clock-tier).
- Does not block the gating Gerrit CI (the `not integration and not external` default suite): the
  `e2e` tier self-skips when Node/npm is absent, so the CI image does not exercise it (which is
  how it reached `main`). It DOES fail locally where Node is present.
- Likely in the editor-server batch-author path (`llm/workflow/editor_server.py` /
  `prompt_library` write + criterion-reference wiring), not the prompt reorg.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root-cause why the authored criterion id is not written onto the batch step's first criterion.
- [ ] `test_editor_batch_library_select_and_author` passes locally (with Node present) and in CI.
- [ ] Confirm the `e2e` tier's CI skip behavior is intended (or wire Node into the gate so e2e regressions are caught).
baseline.summary: e2e editor batch-author test fails on main: authored criterion not referenced

## Problem
The .bridge_state/projects.json write path is a HAND-ROLLED client that bypasses the authoritative shared store seams and thereby violates the tickets-branch invariant (every mutation runs under the unified write lock AND auto-commits+publishes). projects_store._write_record hand-rolls tempfile+os.replace instead of the shared fsutil.atomic_write, and projects_store.set_project/remove_project never take the lock, commit, or push. This forced the ad-hoc hand-commits behind incident 05b8-4efe-8d58-4c27 (LEG/ONE/TWO/ZERO leak).

## Scope: CONVERT the hand-rolled client to the authoritative shared seams ONLY
Reuse the existing seams exactly as-is. Do NOT modify any seam and do NOT build a facade over them (that would be additional, separately-approved scope):
- rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write — the shared crash-atomic file write.
- rebar._store.lock.write_lock — the unified tickets write lock (context manager).
- rebar._store.push.commit_and_push_tickets_branch(tracker, *, message=...) — commits all
  pending tracker changes UNDER THE WRITE LOCK (+ rebase guard) then pushes.

## Approach (pure conversion)
1. projects_store._write_record: replace the hand-rolled mkstemp/fdopen/os.replace block
   with `fsutil.atomic_write(path, json.dumps(record, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")`.
   Behavior-preserving: the on-disk bytes stay byte-identical, and the existing
   `path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` is KEPT before the call (atomic_write
   requires the parent dir to already exist), so first-write still creates .bridge_state.
   The module's read path stays stdlib-only standalone; the write path lazily imports the
   rebar._store seams (only ever reached from the _lib_ops library layer, never from the
   engine reconciler's read-only importers), and the module docstring is updated to state
   this read-path-standalone / write-path-uses-seams split so the swap does not contradict
   the documented invariant.
2. Run the mutation under the lock AND publish it, both through existing seams, from the
   single _lib_ops entry point that BOTH the CLI and the library route through
   (bridge_projects_set / bridge_projects_remove -> set_project / remove_project): hold
   `lock.write_lock(tracker)` around the read-modify-write call to set_project/remove_project
   (so the RMW itself runs under the lock — no lost-update race), release it, then call
   `push.commit_and_push_tickets_branch(tracker, message="bridge: update projects mapping")`
   (which re-acquires the same lock for the commit+push). No ad-hoc git; the read path
   (load_mapping / read_projects) is untouched.
3. Record the invariant (explicitly requested): add the two-part invariant to
   docs/concurrency.md "Mutating the tracker" section — EVERY tickets-branch mutation runs
   under write_lock AND auto-commits+publishes.

## Explicitly OUT of scope (separate tickets)
- Write-time project-key VALIDATION — separate ticket 209b (a distinct behavior addition,
  not a seam conversion).
- Any change to resolve_project / legacy_default (ticket a011).
- Any modification of the shared seam or a new facade/helper over it (needs separate
  approval).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] projects_store._write_record uses `fsutil.atomic_write` (not hand-rolled
      mkstemp/os.replace) and keeps the `path.parent.mkdir(...)`; serialized bytes are
      byte-identical to today, pinned by a RED-first test in
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_projects_store_happy.py`.
- [x] A projects.json mutation runs its read-modify-write under `lock.write_lock` and is
      then committed + pushed via `push.commit_and_push_tickets_branch(tracker, ...)` with no
      ad-hoc git; verified by a seam-patched regression guard in
      `tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_projects_happy.py`.
- [x] `docs/concurrency.md` "Mutating the tracker" section states the two-part invariant:
      EVERY tickets-branch mutation runs under write_lock AND auto-commits+publishes.
- [x] No new commit/push/lock/atomic-write helper or facade is introduced; the existing
      seams are used as-is (checked: `git diff` shows only inline seam call-sites added).

## Testing
- `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_projects_store_happy.py tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_projects_store_heldout.py tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_projects_happy.py -q`
- `make lint`
- `make typecheck`

## Sequencing
Edits projects_store.py + docs/concurrency.md (+ tests); reuses push/fsutil/lock (no edit). Disjoint from A/C/D. Ticket 209b (key validation) and ticket E (parity conversion) both edit projects_store.py / the reconciler commit path and are sequenced AFTER this one.
baseline.summary: Bridge-state writes: adopt shared write_lock + commit+push + atomic_write seams (tickets-branch invariant)

baseline.description:
RISK 1 (cross-session duplication). Two independently-authored modules each define their OWN `RetryExhaustedError` with a DIFFERENT base class, each raised by a separate retry loop and re-exported from a different public surface. A caller writing `except RetryExhaustedError` against one import silently MISSES the one raised by the other path — exception identity drives control flow, so this is a latent reliability bug, not cosmetic.

## Why
Verified ground truth: `acli_subprocess.py:124` → `class RetryExhaustedError(RuntimeError)` (re-exported via `acli.py`); `batch_dispatch.py:39` → `class RetryExhaustedError(Exception)` (re-exported via `applier.py`). So `acli.RetryExhaustedError is not applier.RetryExhaustedError`. `JiraAPIError` has ONE body (`batch_dispatch.py:31`) re-exported through both surfaces — only the re-export, not the class, is duplicated. The `acli` raise site chains (`raise ... from last_error`); the `batch_dispatch` site does NOT (`raise RetryExhaustedError(str(last_exc))` — drops the cause).

## What — OSS-informed design (requests/urllib3/httpx/tenacity + PEP 3134)
Consensus: one package-level base in a dedicated errors module; subclass `Exception` (or the single most-derived stdlib type a caller already catches); carry the last failure; chain the cause. `_errors.py` already exists (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_errors.py`, ~67 LOC) — ADD the unified types there:
- `class ReconcilerError(Exception)` — the catch-all base seam (per requests `RequestException` / urllib3 `HTTPError`).
- `class RetryExhaustedError(ReconcilerError, RuntimeError)` — MRO `RetryExhaustedError→ReconcilerError→RuntimeError→Exception` is consistent and is caught by BOTH existing `except RuntimeError` (acli path) AND `except Exception` (batch path) sites, so NO call-site breaks. `__init__(self, message="", *, last_exception=None, attempts=None)` — message-first keeps both current `RetryExhaustedError("…")` call sites working; the optional fields mirror tenacity `RetryError.last_attempt` / urllib3 `MaxRetryError.reason`. Do NOT list `(RuntimeError, Exception)` literally (redundant/duplicate base — pylint E0241).
- `class JiraAPIError(ReconcilerError)` — move the single body from `batch_dispatch.py:31` here, keeping `__init__(self, message, status_code)` verbatim.
Then delete both `RetryExhaustedError` bodies and `import` the canonical one (`from rebar_reconciler._errors import RetryExhaustedError`); leave the `acli.py`/`applier.py` `__all__` re-exports (they now re-export the SAME object). Fix the chaining gap at `batch_dispatch.py:137`: `raise RetryExhaustedError("…", last_exception=last_exc, attempts=max_retries+1) from last_exc`.

## Scope
In: unify the two exception types in `_errors.py`, repoint both modules, fix the missing `from` chain. FOLLOW-ON (separate, not this ticket): consolidate the 5 HTTP/subprocess retry LOOPS (push/batch_dispatch/acli_subprocess×2/acli_rest) onto one `retry(fn, *, attempts, backoff, retry_on)` helper — linked as discovered_from.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `from rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler.acli import RetryExhaustedError` and `from ...applier import RetryExhaustedError` resolve to the SAME object (`is` identity test).
- [ ] A `RetryExhaustedError` raised by either retry loop is caught by `except RuntimeError`, `except Exception`, AND `except ReconcilerError`.
- [ ] Both raise sites chain the cause (`__cause__` is the last underlying exception); `last_exception`/`attempts` populated.
- [ ] `JiraAPIError` defined once in `_errors.py`, `__init__(message, status_code)` unchanged; both surfaces import it.
- [ ] Tests cover the cross-path `except` identity + chaining; existing reconciler tests pass.
baseline.summary: Risk 1: unify reconciler exception taxonomy + chaining (OSS-informed)

# BUG: child-certification check fails OPEN on a store read error

## Reproduction Steps

2. `completion.py:73-76` catches and returns `([], [])` → `certifiable=True` → parent closes SIGNED over the uncertified child.

baseline.description:
## Context

Rebar is a reusable ticket, reconciliation, and review-gate system consumed through several harnesses and deployed into projects with very different stacks, repository shapes, platforms, and execution environments. Development of rebar itself happens primarily in a Python repository on macOS through current agent harnesses, which creates a risk that a technically plausible plan silently bakes rebar-project assumptions into reusable behavior.

Representative failures include a core `rebar landing` command that encodes this repository Gerrit policy, Python-only review rules that fail to apply to a Next.js client, macOS-specific dependencies, and operations that assume the process starts inside a local project checkout. The review must catch concrete incompatibilities without requiring every plan to contain generic portability prose.

## Why

Rebar maintainers need an early, high-recall warning when a proposed plan would break a supported client shape. Downstream clients need project-specific policy to remain in project configuration while reusable mechanisms remain usable across harnesses, target projects, platforms, execution venues, and project-location models. Dogfooding the existing project-criterion and project-coaching seams also provides a real example for client authors.

## What

Add one activated project plan-review criterion, `project.portability`, through `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` and `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md`. It runs in Pass 1 at both container and leaf scope. It does not adjudicate validity, impact, severity, or disposition; existing Pass 2 and Pass 3 do that without modification.

The finder may emit a portability finding only when it supplies all four elements:

- a citation to the explicit plan detail or mechanism carrying the assumption;
- a materially different supported client shape;
- the causal mechanism by which that shape fails; and
- a specific, observable breakage scenario that Pass 2 can verify.

The compatibility counterexample matrix is:

- Harness: Python library, CLI, and remote MCP clients, without assumptions specific to Claude Code, Codex, or another development harness.
- Target project: Ruby, Python, Java, Next.js, .NET, and atypical layouts such as Terraform subprojects inside a monorepo.
- Platform and venue: macOS, Windows, Linux, and BSD across CI, servers, and developer workstations.
- Project location and access: in-checkout current working directory, explicitly located workspace, and server execution outside the target checkout without assuming unrestricted local filesystem access.

Silence about portability is not a finding. If the reviewer cannot construct the cited, concrete counterexample, it emits no finding. Project-specific behavior is allowed when it remains project configuration rather than leaking into reusable core behavior.

Add one project-specific Pass-4 move in `.rebar/plan_review_moves.json`, applicable only when `project.portability` survives review:

- id: `project-portability`
- name: `restore rebar portability`
- applies_when: `["project.portability"]`
- template: `Rework {subject} so it remains portable across supported rebar client shapes; keep project-specific behavior in project configuration or an explicit extension boundary.`

The existing Pass-4 applicability filter, move picker, subject validator, and deterministic renderer remain unchanged. No generic core coaching move is added.

## Approach and sequencing

The fresh-worktree experiment is complete and recorded on this epic. It mechanically proved criterion activation for leaf and container plans, `ProductionBatchRunner` project fan-in, project move loading, criterion-scoped applicability, and deterministic rendering against current `origin/main`. The temporary experiment files were removed; implementation remains outstanding.

Delivery is decomposed into four bounded children:

1. `immune-floury-toad` activates and integrates the Pass 1 finder.
2. After the finder lands, `truthful-specified-silverfish` adds project-scoped Pass 4 coaching while `indigoid-unmystic-serpent` independently calibrates the live criterion against balanced positive and negative cases.
3. After coaching and calibration land, `taurine-catchable-kakarikis` documents the final project extension pattern and runs repository-wide regression gates.

This approach uses the existing project extension seams instead of changing the generic four-pass kernel. It directly demonstrates the intended boundary, gives live semantics a separate calibration gate, limits blast radius, and preserves Pass 2 and Pass 3 behavior.

## Child delivery map

- `immune-floury-toad` — owns routing, activation, prompt resolution, leaf/container fan-in, rubric structure, false-positive instructions, and overlay-absent integration coverage.
- `truthful-specified-silverfish` — owns only the `project-portability` move, its criterion-scoped applicability, deterministic rendering, and proof that no generic core move changes.
- `indigoid-unmystic-serpent` — owns the balanced live eval corpus, four-part positive findings, must-not-fire boundaries, and repeat-run thresholds. If the first complete run meets every threshold, it makes no prompt edit. On a threshold miss, it may reword finder instructions or contrast examples only in `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md`; criterion id, routing, output schema, Pass 2, and Pass 3 remain unchanged.
- `taurine-catchable-kakarikis` — owns the client-facing dogfood documentation, parser-safe placement outside the built-in move table, and final lint/typecheck/test verification.
- The completed worktree experiment remains parent-level operator evidence because it de-risks the whole decomposition and is not remaining implementation work.

The dependency graph is `immune-floury-toad -> {truthful-specified-silverfish, indigoid-unmystic-serpent} -> taurine-catchable-kakarikis`.

## Scope

In scope:

- Rebar-project Pass-1 criterion configuration, prompt, and activation.
- Rebar-project Pass-4 move configuration restricted to `project.portability`.
- Offline wiring experiment in a fresh worktree.
- Focused positive, negative, leaf, container, routing, and rendering tests.
- A balanced live evaluation corpus with repeat-run release thresholds.
- Documentation of the project configuration as an example for clients.

Out of scope:

- Remediating existing portability debt discovered by the criterion.
- Adding `rebar landing` or other rebar-project workflow policy to reusable core.
- A generic built-in coaching move.
- Changes to Pass 2 validity/impact adjudication or Pass 3 deterministic decisions.
- Guaranteeing that every existing rebar feature already supports every matrix cell.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `immune-floury-toad` activates `project.portability` with `exec: 1-TURN`, `facet: project-invariants`, `applies_at.scope: [container, leaf]`, `default_posture: blocking`, and `block_threshold: 0.9`. Verify: `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py -k criterion_activation`
- [ ] `immune-floury-toad` proves the resolved rubric contains the finding threshold plus the exact silence and project-configuration non-finding rules. Verify: `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py -k "prompt_resolution or finding_threshold or omission_guard or project_configuration_guard"`
- [ ] `immune-floury-toad` proves both leaf and container plans route through production project fan-in. Verify: `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py -k "leaf_routing or container_routing or production_fan_in"`
- [ ] `indigoid-unmystic-serpent` proves the corpus contains exactly `PORT-F1` through `PORT-F4`, each with a gold four-part note: plan citation, alternate client shape, causal mechanism, plus observable breakage. Verify: `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k "balanced_corpus or finding_contract"`
- [ ] `indigoid-unmystic-serpent` proves a plan with no portability discussion is a must-not-fire case. Verify: `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k negative_boundaries`
- [ ] `indigoid-unmystic-serpent` proves specialization behind project configuration or an explicit extension boundary is a must-not-fire case. Verify: `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k negative_boundaries`
- [ ] [operator-attested] `indigoid-unmystic-serpent` records three live eval runs over `PORT-F1`–`PORT-F4` plus `PORT-N1`–`PORT-N4` with recall `1.0`, false-accept rate `0.0`, agreement `1.0`, per-case stability of at least two of three, and Cohen kappa of at least `0.70`. Verify: `.venv/bin/rebar criteria eval project.portability --runs 3 --output json`
- [ ] `truthful-specified-silverfish` proves the `project-portability` move applies only when `project.portability` survives review. Verify: `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_coaching.py -k "applies_to_portability or ignores_empty_triggers or ignores_unrelated_findings"`
- [ ] `truthful-specified-silverfish` proves the move deterministically renders the locked project template and does not add a generic core move. Verify: `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_coaching.py -k "deterministic_render or project_owned_only"`

### P1 — The implementation is a cyclic modular monolith, not the documented layering
An AST-level package dependency analysis, including lazy imports, produced one 13-package strongly connected component spanning `_cli`, `_commands`, `_store`, `graph`, `llm`, `signing`, `audit`, `attest`, and supporting packages.
Concrete inversions include:
- Storage imports command-layer fsck logic ([gitutil.py (line 106)](/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:106)).
- Graph mutation code imports command orchestration ([graph/_links.py (line 110)](/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/src/rebar/graph/_links.py:110)).
- A command imports CLI help presentation ([transition.py (line 500)](/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:500)).
- The canonical storage write path directly invokes optional LLM enrichment ([event_append.py (line 450)](/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:450)).
- Transition and claim maintain their own commit implementation rather than using the documented canonical primitive ([txn.py (line 10)](/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:10)).
This conflicts with the “thin interfaces” and “one locked append+commit path” architecture narrative ([architecture.md (line 28)](/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/docs/architecture.md:28), [architecture.md (line 46)](/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/docs/architecture.md:46)). Lazy imports avoid runtime import failures but do not remove architectural coupling.

- `ports`: repository, synchronization, clock, signer, enrichment interfaces.
- `adapters`: Git, Jira, CLI, MCP, LLM, Gerrit.

baseline.description:
Our goal is to integrate self improvement into rebar's review process so that friction during development, bugs after release, and user observations flow into improvements to the review process without the need for dedicated epics and design by users. Our intent is to provide 3 options for the feature: off (no auto improvement), suggestion (improvements require user approval), and fully autonomous (improvements happen automatically).
During brainstorming, start with the following information gathering. These steps should be completed as part of brainstorming, not as part of the epic implementation.
1. Look at this project's history of improving the review process, specifically at criteria additions or modifications. 
2. Research skills, prompts, and agentic development systems that involve self-improvement. How do they gather information during the development workflow? How do they decide what guidance to preserve? How do they handle growth of guidance over time to avoid unbounded context usage? What gotchas have they encountered?
3. Search for research on self-improving agentic systems from 2026, focusing on those with data or code to support their conclusions. How do they solve the problem of unreliable agentic judgment when determining what improvements are worth making? How do they prevent new improvements from causing regression? What other problems are will documented in self-improving systems?
Consider whether we should implement shadow criteria to evaluate self improvement before they are visible to users. Shadow criteria would be evaluated in pass 1 and 2 of the review process as normal, with the results recorded in a tracking file, but would always be dropped by pass 3. This could allow us to gather data to support the value of a new criteria before promoting it to normal use. We would want to limit the number of shadow criteria at a time to avoid excessive token use and wall clock costs.

baseline.description:
Attestation manifests (plan-review and completion-verifier) should record the
**version of rebar that produced the certification**, for audit/provenance —
*not* for enforcement. `regver` (criteria-registry version) already owns
version-skew invalidation; this stamp is never read by `compute_validity` and
never auto-invalidates an attestation.

## Context

- Signed manifests are built by `build_manifest` (plan-review) and
  `_verdict_manifest` (completion-verifier) in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py`.
- The manifest already carries a `regver:` line (enforced skew stamp) and, for
  plan-review, `verified_at_sha` (the **target** repo SHA). The new stamp is a
  distinct axis: which **rebar gate code** signed the attestation.
- Package version is **static** (`pyproject.toml` `version = "0.6.0"`, hatchling,
  no VCS) — coarse, so version alone can't answer "what code certified this?".
  Hence version **+ short commit SHA of the gate-code checkout**.

## What gets recorded

One additive manifest line, e.g. `rebar-version: 0.6.0 (gc1a2b3c4-dirty)`:
- **Version**: `rebar.__version__` (static package version).
- **Commit SHA** of the **rebar source (gate code)** checkout — NOT the target
  repo — resolved **live-first, baked-second**:
  1. live git checkout of the rebar source -> `git -C <dir of rebar.__file__>
     rev-parse --short HEAD` (dev/editable: the live truth, wins over any baked
     value which goes stale as you commit);
  2. else -> SHA **baked at build time** into a generated, git-ignored
     `src/rebar/_build_info.py` (PyPI/wheel install);
  3. else -> omit the SHA, keep the version.
- **`-dirty` marker** on the live-checkout path when the working tree has
  uncommitted changes (`git status --porcelain`), so a mid-edit signer can't
  stamp a clean SHA that doesn't match the running gate code. Release builds are
  clean.

## Scope / non-goals

- No enforcement / no auto-invalidation on version mismatch (that stays with
  `regver`).
- Version stays static; do NOT switch to hatch-vcs — only add SHA capture.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `build_manifest` (plan-review) and `_verdict_manifest`
      (completion-verifier) both append a `rebar-version:` line carrying the
      static version + short gate-code commit SHA.
- [ ] A SHA-resolution helper implements live-git-first, build-baked-second,
      omit-last, with a `-dirty` suffix when the live checkout is dirty.
- [ ] A hatchling build hook (`BuildHookInterface`) captures the commit SHA at
      wheel/sdist build into a generated, git-ignored `src/rebar/_build_info.py`;
      absent-git build omits it gracefully.
- [ ] A `manifest_rebar_version()` parser (mirroring `manifest_regver()`)
      extracts the stamp; returns `None` for pre-stamp manifests.
- [ ] `compute_validity` is unchanged and never reads the stamp; old manifests
      without the line still validate byte-identically.
- [ ] The stamp is surfaced in `show` (attestation block) and returned by
      `verify_signature`.
- [ ] Tests: both manifests carry the line; live-checkout resolution (incl.
      `-dirty`); baked fallback for non-git install; graceful omit; parser
      round-trip + pre-stamp `None`; no validity impact.
- [ ] An auditor reading a signed attestation can determine the exact rebar version
- [ ] Zero behavior change to gate validity: the stamp never affects claim/close.
baseline.summary: Certifications need to include the version of rebar they were certified against

baseline.description:
Oscillation and The Cross-Boundary Problem
The most significant risk inherent in automated convergence loops is the threat of infinite oscillation, a phenomenon most frequently triggered by the Cross-Boundary Problem.
This occurs when a defect identified in the reviewed code is actually a symptom of a root cause located in a different architectural domain. For instance, a reviewer agent analyzing a frontend component might correctly identify an error handling flaw, but the true fix requires a structural change to a backend server API. An unsophisticated prompt will cause the reviewer to flag the frontend code and demand a client-side workaround. The autonomous fixer applies the workaround, but upon re-review, the reviewer agent flags the workaround as a negative architectural "code smell," demanding it be removed. This initiates an endless, costly cycle of applying and reverting the exact same mitigation. 
To resolve this, advanced prompt schemas force the reviewer model to output a bo[span_100](start_span)[span_100](end_span)undary_owner field alongside its finding. By evaluating the architectural boundaries, the LLM determines which service should genuinely own the fix. If the boundary_owner does not match the currently reviewed service, the finding is formally logged for human architectural review but is explicitly excluded from the automated convergence check, cleanly severing the oscillation loop and allowing the PR to proceed.
baseline.summary: Oscillation and The Cross-Boundary Problem

baseline.description: When an  agent fixes a problem in a prompt, they have a tendency to over-fit the prompt to the problem they've encountered. They as overly long and verbose explanatory text around the problem. They confuse the prompt with historical documentation. They reorient the entire prompt around a narrow edge case rather than adding a small clarification. We need to apply the lens: what is the minimal prompt change that accomplishes our goal? Does the prompt include historical or explanatory text beyond what is strictly necessary for the agent? Does the change maintain the general focus of the prompt or shift primary focus to an edge case that should be a footnote? We should ensure prompt changes include AC that enforce these principles in plan review's overlay related to LLM prompts and that code review's overlay related to LLM prompts evaluates these issues.
baseline.summary: Catch the failure mode of overly specific, verbose guidance
